declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fourierMukai_areSiblingsCoherent
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `X` and `Y` be schemes of finite type over `k` with `X` separated, and
let `F : D^b_Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y)` be a `k`-linear exact functor sending
`Coh(𝒪_X) ⊂ D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` into `Coh(𝒪_Y) ⊂ D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y)`. Then there exists a Fourier-Mukai
functor `F' : D^b_Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D^b_Coh(𝒪_Y)` whose kernel is a coherent `𝒪_{X ×_k Y}`-module `𝒦`
flat over `X` and with support finite over `Y` which is a sibling of `F`.

Finite type over `k` is `LocallyOfFiniteType` together with `QuasiCompact`; `X ×_k Y` is the
fibre product over `Spec k`. The kernel `𝒦` is an object of
`AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentKernels.finiteFlatCoherentKernel` — coherent, flat over `X`, with
scheme-theoretic support finite over `Y` — and `F'` is the functor induced on `D^b_Coh` by the
Fourier-Mukai functor `Φ_𝒦` of the complex `𝒦[0]`, which preserves `D^b_Coh`
(`fourierMukaiOfKernel`). That `F` sends coherent modules to coherent modules is the statement
that the image under `F` of a coherent module placed in degree zero is isomorphic to a coherent
module placed in degree zero; `k`-linearity is with respect to the `k`-linear structures induced
by the structure morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fourierMukai_areSiblingsCoherent [IsSeparated X.hom]
    (F : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (coherentInModules X.left)).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (coherentInModules Y.left)).FullSubcategory)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (hlin : letI : Linear k (SheafOfModules.{u} X.left.ringCatSheaf) := modulesLinear k X
      letI : Linear k (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.left.ringCatSheaf) := modulesLinear k Y
      F.Linear k)
    (hF : ∀ A, (boundedCoherentSingleFunctor Y.left).essImage
      (F.obj ((boundedCoherentSingleFunctor X.left).obj A))) :
    ∃ K : (finiteFlatCoherentKernel k X Y).FullSubcategory,
      AreSiblingsCoherent F (fourierMukaiOfKernel k X Y K)
declarations.comment: a k-linear exact functor of D^b_Coh sending Coh into Coh has a sibling which is the Fourier-Mukai functor of a coherent kernel flat over X with support finite over Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_of_areSiblings_of_isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G01**, its first sentence. Let `k` be a field and `X` a reduced scheme
which is projective over `k` (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective` of `f : X ⟶ Spec k`, the first
condition of [Stacks, Tag 01W8]). If `F, F' : D^b_Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ 𝒟` are siblings and `F` is fully
faithful, then `F ≅ F'`. Here `𝒟` is an arbitrary triangulated category and "siblings" is the
relation of [Stacks, Tag 0FZT] for `Coh(𝒪_X)`, read through the identification
`D^b(Coh(𝒪_X)) = D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FDB].

A projective `k`-scheme is proper over `k` with an ample invertible module
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isProper_and_exists_isAmple_of_isAffine`), and for those this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_of_areSiblings_coherentToModulesDerivedBounded`, the source's
argument "via the proof of [Stacks, Tag 0G0C]". The remaining sentences of the remark (that
siblings are not known to be isomorphic in general, the case of [Stacks, Tag 0G00], the reference
to Noah's work and the invitation to email) are commentary, with no mathematical content to
formalize.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_of_areSiblings_of_isProjective
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective f) [IsReduced X]
    {D : Type*} [Category* D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D] [IsTriangulated D]
    (F F' : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded (coherentInModules X)).FullSubcategory ⥤ D)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] [F'.CommShift ℤ] [F'.IsTriangulated]
    (h : AreSiblings (coherentToModulesDerivedBounded X ⋙ F)
      (coherentToModulesDerivedBounded X ⋙ F'))
    (hF : Nonempty F.FullyFaithful) : Nonempty (F ≅ F')
declarations.comment: first sentence: siblings out of D^b_Coh of a reduced projective scheme over a field, the first fully faithful, are isomorphic; the remaining sentences are commentary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_ringKrullDim_eq_and_homAddEquiv_homologyDerivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G02.** Let `k` be a field, `X` a scheme of finite type over `k` which is regular,
`x ∈ X` a closed point, `F` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module supported at `x`, and `F'` a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module supported at `x` whose stalk at `x` is a Matlis dual of `F_x`. Then with
`d_x = dim 𝒪_{X,x}`,

`Hom_X(F, M) = H⁰(X, M ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} F'[-d_x])`

functorially in `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringKrullDim_eq_and_homAddEquiv_homologyDerivedTensor
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (F F' : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] [F'.IsCoherent]
    (hFsupp : SheafOfModules.supp (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F ⊆ {x})
    (hF'supp : SheafOfModules.supp (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F' ⊆ {x})
    (hdual : Dualizing.IsMatlisDualPair (stalkRing X.toRingedSpace x)
      (SheafOfModules.stalkObjStalkRing x F) (SheafOfModules.stalkObjStalkRing x F')) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = (d : ℕ∞) ∧
      ∃ e : ∀ M : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F ⟶ M) ≃+
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).obj
              ((Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleSections.derivedModuleGlobalSections
                  (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
                (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor
                    (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj M).obj
                  (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F')⟦-(d : ℤ)⟧))) : Type u),
        ∀ (M N : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (g : M ⟶ N)
            (a : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F ⟶ M),
          e N (a ≫ g) =
            (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} 0).map
              ((Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleSections.derivedModuleGlobalSections
                  (ringedSite X.sheaf)).map
                (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor
                    (ringedSite X.sheaf)).map g).app
                  (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F')⟦-(d : ℤ)⟧)))
              (e M a)
declarations.comment: the scheme-level statement: k a field, X a scheme of finite type over k which is regular, x a closed point of X, F a coherent 𝒪_X-module supported at x and F' a coherent 𝒪_X-module supported at x whose stalk at x is a Matlis dual of F_x; then Hom_X(F, M) is identified additively with H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} F'[-d_x]), d_x = dim 𝒪_{X,x}, functorially in M. The identification is produced for every M in D(𝒪_X), which generalizes the source's clause for M in D_perf(𝒪_X). The local ring is read as the RingCat-valued stalk of the sheaf of rings, which is the local ring 𝒪_{X,x} by AlgebraicGeometry.ringCatStalkRingEquiv and is where the Matlis-duality hypothesis is stated; the dimension clause d_x = dim 𝒪_{X,x} is stated at the CommRingCat-valued stalk X.presheaf.stalk x. The duality at the point to which the source's proof reduces this -- for A a regular local ring of dimension d, Hom_{D(A)}(N, K) is H⁰(K ⊗^L_A N'[-d]) functorially in K -- is registered separately, on Dualizing.exists_addEquiv_hom_homology_derivedTensor_matlisDual

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_addEquiv_hom_homology_derivedTensor_matlisDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G02**, the duality at the point to which the source reduces its statement. Let `A`
be a regular local ring of dimension `d`, let `N` be an `A`-module of finite length and let `N'`
be a Matlis dual of `N` with respect to an injective hull `E` of the residue field. Then
`Hom_{D(A)}(N, K) ≃+ H⁰(K ⊗^L_A N'[-d])`, functorially in `K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_addEquiv_hom_homology_derivedTensor_matlisDual
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (i : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{0} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E)
    [Mono i] (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i)
    (N N' : ModuleCat.{u} A) (hN : IsFiniteLength A N)
    (hdual : Nonempty (N' ≅ ModuleCat.of A (N ⟶ E))) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ringKrullDim A = (d : ℕ∞) ∧
      ∃ e : ∀ L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A),
          (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
              ((derivedHomAdjunctionOverRing.{u, 0, u + 1} A).tensor.obj
                (L, ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N')⟦-(d : ℤ)⟧)))
            : Type u) ≃+
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N ⟶ L),
        ∀ (L L' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (f : L ⟶ L')
          (a : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
            ((derivedHomAdjunctionOverRing.{u, 0, u + 1} A).tensor.obj
              (L, ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N')⟦-(d : ℤ)⟧))),
          e L' ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map
              ((derivedHomAdjunctionOverRing.{u, 0, u + 1} A).tensor.map
                (f, 𝟙 (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N')⟦-(d : ℤ)⟧)))
              a) = e L a ≫ f
declarations.comment: duality at the point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_of_derivedTensor_residueField
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (5).** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `x` a point of `X`, `𝒪_x` the
skyscraper at `x` with value the residue field `κ(x)`, and `K` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If the
degree-`i` cohomology of `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x` at `x` vanishes, then the degree-`i` cohomology sheaf
of `K` has vanishing stalk at every point of an open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_of_derivedTensor_residueField
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) (i : ℤ)
    (h : IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} (ToType (StacksDraft.StalkRingComparison.stalkRing X x))) i).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.stalkFunctor X.ringCatSheaf x).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (derivedTensorResidueFieldSkyscraper X x K)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U →
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (5), the derived-tensor form, for `X` a Noetherian scheme and `K` perfect: the source's `H^i(X, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x)` is read as the degree-`i` cohomology of the derived stalk at `x` of `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x`, and `H^i(K)|_U = 0` as the vanishing of the degree-`i` cohomology stalk at every point of `U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_derivedTensor_residueField
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (6).** In the situation of part (5), if `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x` has no
cohomology at `x` in any degree, then `K` is zero on an open neighbourhood of `x`: every
cohomology sheaf of `K` has vanishing stalk at every point of that neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_derivedTensor_residueField
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (ModuleCat.{u} (ToType (StacksDraft.StalkRingComparison.stalkRing X x))) i).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.stalkFunctor X.ringCatSheaf x).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (derivedTensorResidueFieldSkyscraper X x K)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (6), the derived-tensor form, for `X` a Noetherian scheme and `K` perfect: the source's `H^i(X, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x)` is read as the degree-`i` cohomology of the derived stalk at `x` of `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x`, and `K` being zero near `x` as the vanishing of every cohomology stalk at every point of the neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_of_isZero_homology_globalSections_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (5), global form.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `x` a closed
point of `X`, `𝒪_x` the skyscraper at `x` with value `κ(x)` and `K` a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)`. If `H^i(X, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x) = 0`, then `H^i(K)` vanishes on an open neighbourhood
of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_of_isZero_homology_globalSections_derivedTensor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) (i : ℤ)
    (h : IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleSections.derivedModuleGlobalSections
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj (derivedTensorSkyscraper X x K)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U →
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (5), for X a Noetherian scheme (which every scheme of finite type over a field is), x a closed point and K perfect: H^i(X, -) is the cohomology of the derived global sections of the ringed site of opens, and H^i(K)|_U = 0 is read as the vanishing of the stalk of H^i(K) at every point of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_isZero_homology_globalSections_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (6), global form.** In the situation of part (5), if
`H^i(X, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_x) = 0` for all `i`, then `K` is zero on an open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_isZero_homology_globalSections_derivedTensor
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.ModuleSections.derivedModuleGlobalSections
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj (derivedTensorSkyscraper X x K)))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (6), for X a Noetherian scheme (which every scheme of finite type over a field is), x a closed point and K perfect: if H^i(X, K ⊗^L 𝒪_x) = 0 for all i then every cohomology sheaf of K has vanishing stalk at every point of an open neighbourhood of x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_from_residueFieldSkyscraper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (1).** Let `k` be a field, `X` a regular scheme of finite type
over `k`, `x ∈ X` a closed point, `𝒪_x` the skyscraper at `x` with value `κ(x)`, `d` the
dimension of `𝒪_{X,x}`, and `K` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If `Ext^i_X(𝒪_x, K) = 0`, then
`H^{i - d}(K)` vanishes on an open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_from_residueFieldSkyscraper
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (i : ℤ)
    (h : Subsingleton ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
      (residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf X x) ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = d ∧
      ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U →
        IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules (i - d)).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (1), at the source's hypotheses: k a field, X a regular scheme of finite type over k, x a closed point, 𝒪_x the skyscraper at x with value κ(x), K perfect. Ext^i_X(𝒪_x, K) is Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(𝒪_x, K[i]); d_x = dim 𝒪_{X,x} is the natural number d with ringKrullDim 𝒪_{X,x} = d, produced by the conclusion; H^{i-d_x}(K)|_U = 0 is read as the vanishing of the stalk of H^{i-d_x}(K) at every point of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_from_residueFieldSkyscraper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (2).** Let `k` be a field, `X` a regular scheme of finite type
over `k`, `x ∈ X` a closed point, `𝒪_x` the skyscraper at `x` with value `κ(x)` and `K` a perfect
object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If `Hom_X(𝒪_x, K[i]) = 0` for all `i ∈ ℤ`, then `K` is zero on an open
neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_from_residueFieldSkyscraper
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
      (residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf X x) ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (2), at the source's hypotheses: k a field, X a regular scheme of finite type over k, x a closed point, K perfect; if Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(𝒪_x, K[i]) = 0 for all i then every cohomology sheaf of K has vanishing stalk at every point of an open neighbourhood of x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_derivedDual_of_subsingleton_hom_to_residueFieldSkyscraper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (3).** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `x ∈ X` a closed point,
`𝒪_x` the skyscraper at `x` with value `κ(x)` and `K` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, with dual
`K^∨ = R𝓗om(K, 𝒪_X)`. If `Ext^i_X(K, 𝒪_x) = 0`, then `H^i(K^∨)` vanishes on an open
neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_isZero_stalkHomology_derivedDual_of_subsingleton_hom_to_residueFieldSkyscraper
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) (i : ℤ)
    (h : Subsingleton (K ⟶ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
      (residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf X x))⟦i⟧)) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U →
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedDual X.sheaf K)))
declarations.comment: part (3), for X a Noetherian scheme (which every scheme of finite type over a field is), x a closed point and K perfect: Ext^i_X(K, 𝒪_x) is Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, 𝒪_x[i]), K^∨ is R𝓗om(K, 𝒪_X), and H^i(K^∨)|_U = 0 is read as the vanishing of the stalk of H^i(K^∨) at every point of U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_to_residueFieldSkyscraper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (4).** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `x ∈ X` a point, `𝒪_x`
the skyscraper at `x` with value `κ(x)` and `K` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If
`Hom_X(K, 𝒪_x[i]) = 0` for all `i ∈ ℤ`, then `K` is zero on an open neighbourhood of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_to_residueFieldSkyscraper
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X)
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (K ⟶ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
      (residueFieldSkyscraper X x))⟦i⟧)) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (OXModule.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K) y)
declarations.comment: part (4), for X a Noetherian scheme (which every scheme of finite type over a field is), x any point and K perfect: if Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, 𝒪_x[i]) = 0 for all i then every cohomology sheaf of K has vanishing stalk at every point of an open neighbourhood of x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_forall_stalkHomology_isZero_of_hom_residueFieldSkyscraper
declarations.doc:
A complex with no nonzero map to any shift of the residue-field skyscraper at `x` is zero on
an open neighbourhood of `x`: every cohomology sheaf has vanishing stalk at every point of that
neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mem_forall_stalkHomology_isZero_of_hom_residueFieldSkyscraper
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Bounded (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj K.obj).IsCoherent)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ,
      Subsingleton (K.obj ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj
          (residueFieldSkyscraper X x))) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (OXModule.stalk
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj K.obj) y)
declarations.comment: part (4), with the source's hypotheses `X` regular of finite type over a field and `K` in `D_perf(𝒪_X)` replaced by `X` Noetherian and `K` bounded with coherent cohomology, that is `K` in `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`. The source's class of pairs sits inside this one, but the containment — a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` in the sense of `Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect` is bounded with coherent cohomology, Tags 0BCJ and 08E8 — is not bridged in the library, so that is what is granted here. `K` being zero near `x` is read as the vanishing of every cohomology stalk at every point of the neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldSkyscraperIso
declarations.doc:
**The two residue-field skyscrapers at `x` agree.**  The sheafification of the skyscraper
presheaf of modules at `x` with value `κ(x)` is the skyscraper sheaf of modules at `x` with value
the residue field of the `RingCat`-valued stalk.
declarations.statement:
def residueFieldSkyscraperIso :
    residueFieldSkyscraper X x ≅ residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf X x
declarations.comment: the two spellings of the residue-field skyscraper 𝒪_x agree, identifying part (4)'s with the one used by parts (1), (2), (3), (5), (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_to_residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `x ∈ X` a point, `𝒪_x` the skyscraper sheaf
`residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf X x` at `x` with value `κ(x)` and `K` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.
If `Hom_X(K, 𝒪_x[i]) = 0` for all `i ∈ ℤ`, then there is an open neighbourhood of `x` at every
point of which every cohomology sheaf of `K` has zero stalk.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_forall_isZero_stalkHomology_of_subsingleton_hom_to_residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf
    [IsNoetherian X] (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (K ⟶ ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
      (residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf X x))⟦i⟧)) :
    ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (OXModule.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K) y)
declarations.comment: part (4), for X a Noetherian scheme (which every scheme of finite type over a field is), x any point and K perfect, with 𝒪_x read as residueFieldSkyscraperSheaf, the spelling parts (1), (2), (3), (5) and (6) use: if Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, 𝒪_x[i]) = 0 for all i then every cohomology sheaf of K has vanishing stalk at every point of an open neighbourhood of x

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedVarieties.Orlov.exists_mem_forall_stalkHomology_isZero_of_pointSheaf_hom_shift
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G03] part (2).** Let `X` be a regular Noetherian scheme, `x` a closed point
of `X`, `𝒪_x` the skyscraper sheaf at `x` with value `κ(x)` and `K` a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)`. If `Hom(𝒪_x, K[i]) = 0` for every `i ∈ ℤ`, then `K` is zero on an open neighbourhood of
`x`: every cohomology sheaf of `K` has vanishing stalk at every point of that neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_forall_stalkHomology_isZero_of_pointSheaf_hom_shift (hX : IsRegular X)
    [IsNoetherian X] (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (h : ∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (pointSheaf X x ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) :
    ∃ U : TopologicalSpace.Opens X, x ∈ U ∧ ∀ y : X, y ∈ U → ∀ i : ℤ,
      IsZero (SheafOfModules.stalkObj X.ringCatSheaf y
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K))
declarations.comment: part (2), for `X` a regular Noetherian scheme (a regular scheme of finite type over a field, the source's hypothesis, is one) and `K` perfect: `K` being zero in an open neighbourhood of `x` is read as the vanishing of every cohomology stalk at every point of the neighbourhood

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eq_id_of_isIso_of_eq_on_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G05, clause (2).** Let `X` be a reduced scheme locally of finite type
over a field `k` and let `f : X ⟶ X` be an automorphism over `k` which induces the identity map
on the underlying topological space of `X`. If every irreducible component of `X` has positive
dimension then `f` is the identity.

Nothing is carried and no hypothesis is put on `k`. The source's two cases are both handled by
the curve case `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_id_of_eq_on_points_of_isCurve`, to which
`AlgebraicGeometry.eq_id_of_affine_curve_restrictions` reduces the statement: an integral affine
curve over `k` is a curve in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsCurve`, being integral, separated
and of finite type over `k` of dimension one.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_id_of_isIso_of_eq_on_points {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsReduced X]
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (f : X ⟶ X) [IsIso f] (hf : f ≫ p = p)
    (hpoints : ∀ x : X, f x = x)
    (hdim : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X, 0 < topologicalKrullDim Z) :
    f = 𝟙 X
declarations.comment: clause (2) in full: an automorphism over `k` of a reduced scheme locally of finite type over `k` fixing every point of the underlying space is the identity when every irreducible component has positive dimension. No hypothesis on the base field and nothing carried. The automorphism hypothesis is necessary — for an endomorphism the statement fails over a finite field, by `AlgHom.exists_comap_eq_ne_id_of_finite_field` — which is why this stands beside `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_id_of_eq_on_points`, the endomorphism statement with the base field in a disjunctive hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_pullback_of_isIso_of_eq_on_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G05, clause (1).** Let `X` be a reduced scheme of finite type over a
field `k` and let `f : X ⟶ X` be an automorphism over `k` which induces the identity map on the
underlying topological space of `X`. Then every `𝒪_X`-module is isomorphic to its pullback along
`f`.

Nothing is carried and no hypothesis is put on `k`; coherence of the module is not needed. The
source's proof is "part (1) follows from part (2) and the fact that the connected components of
`X` of dimension `0` are spectra of fields": the scheme has finitely many connected components,
each clopen, on each of them clause (2) applies unless it is a one-point scheme, where a module
is isomorphic to its twist through a basis, and the isomorphisms glue because the components are
pairwise disjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_pullback_of_isIso_of_eq_on_points {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p] [IsReduced X] (f : X ⟶ X) [IsIso f]
    (hf : f ≫ p = p) (hpoints : ∀ x : X, f x = x) (F : X.Modules) :
    Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F ≅ F)
declarations.comment: clause (1) in full: every module on a reduced scheme of finite type over `k` is isomorphic to its pullback along an automorphism over `k` fixing every point of the underlying space. No hypothesis on the base field, nothing carried, and the module is arbitrary rather than coherent. The connected components are clopen and finite in number; on each of them clause (2) applies, or the component is the spectrum of a finite extension of `k` and the twist of a module is isomorphic to it through a basis; the isomorphisms glue over the pairwise disjoint cover

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedVarieties.Orlov.exists_areSiblingsPerfectRegularSource_perfectFourierMukaiOver
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G06].** Let `k` be a field, let `X`, `Y` be proper schemes over `k` with `X`
regular, and let `F, G : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` be `k`-linear exact functors such that
(1) `F(𝓕) ≅ G(𝓕)` for every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` with `dim Supp(𝓕) = 0`, (2) `F` is fully
faithful, and (3) `G` is a Fourier-Mukai functor whose kernel is in `D_perf(𝒪_{X × Y})`. Then
there is a Fourier-Mukai functor `F' : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` whose kernel is in
`D_perf(𝒪_{X × Y})` such that `F` and `F'` are siblings.

Here (3) reads: `G` is naturally isomorphic to `Φ_P = perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hP` for a
perfect `P` on `X ×_k Y`; the conclusion gives `F' = Φ_{P'}` itself, and "siblings" is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AreSiblingsPerfectRegularSource` ([Stacks, Tag 0FZZ] for a regular `X` and an
arbitrary `Y` of finite type over `k`).

The proof is the source's. By [Stacks, Tag 0GX0] the essential image of `G` lies in that of `F`.
Let `R` be the exact right adjoint of `F` ([Stacks, Tag 0FYN]); `F` being fully faithful,
`H = R ∘ G` satisfies `F ∘ H ≅ G` and fixes the zero-dimensional sheaves, so by
[Stacks, Tag 0G27] it is a sibling of `H'(M) = Lf^*M ⊗^𝐋 ℒ` for an automorphism `f` of `X` over
`k` and an invertible `ℒ`. With `T(M) = L(f⁻¹)^*(M ⊗^𝐋 ℒ^∨)`, `H' ∘ T ≅ 𝟭`, `T` preserves
coherent modules, and `G ∘ T` is the Fourier-Mukai functor of the twisted kernel
`P' = L pr_1^*ℒ^∨ ⊗^𝐋 L(f × 𝟙)^* P`. Then `F ≅ F ∘ H' ∘ T` is a sibling of
`F ∘ H ∘ T ≅ G ∘ T ≅ Φ_{P'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_areSiblingsPerfectRegularSource_perfectFourierMukaiOver (hX : IsRegular X.left)
    (F G : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] [G.CommShift ℤ] [G.IsTriangulated]
    (hFlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X
      letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
      F.Linear k)
    (hGlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X
      letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
      G.Linear k)
    (hagree : ∀ (M : X.left.Modules), M.IsCoherent →
      topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp M) = 0 →
      ∀ (hM : IsPerfect (X := X.left.toRingedSpace)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj M)),
        Nonempty (F.obj (⟨_, hM⟩ : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left) ≅
          G.obj (⟨_, hM⟩ : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left)))
    (hFF : Nonempty F.FullyFaithful)
    (hG : haveI : IsNoetherian Y.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType Y.hom
      ∃ (P : DerivedCategory (pullback X.hom Y.hom).Modules)
        (hP : IsPerfect (X := (pullback X.hom Y.hom).toRingedSpace) P),
        Nonempty (G ≅ perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hP)) :
    haveI : IsNoetherian X.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType X.hom
    haveI : IsNoetherian Y.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType Y.hom
    ∃ (P' : DerivedCategory (pullback X.hom Y.hom).Modules)
      (hP' : IsPerfect (X := (pullback X.hom Y.hom).toRingedSpace) P'),
      @AreSiblingsPerfectRegularSource X.left Y.left hX _ _ F (perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hP')
        ‹_› ‹_›
        (@commShift_fourierMukaiOn _ _ _ X.hom Y.hom _ _ _
          (isTriangulated_perfectInModules X.left) (isTriangulated_perfectInModules Y.left) _)
        (@isTriangulated_fourierMukaiOn _ _ _ X.hom Y.hom _ _ _
          (isTriangulated_perfectInModules X.left) (isTriangulated_perfectInModules Y.left) _)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DiagonalResolution.originalComplex
declarations.doc:
**The complex `… → ℰ₂ ⊠ 𝒢₂ → ℰ₁ ⊠ 𝒢₁ → ℰ₀ ⊠ 𝒢₀` of external tensor products underlying a
resolution of the diagonal.** It is the augmented resolution with its degree-zero term `𝒪_Δ`
discarded, so its term in degree `i` is the external tensor product indexed by `i`.
declarations.statement: def originalComplex : ChainComplex (pullback f f).Modules ℕ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DiagonalResolution.transformedTerm
declarations.doc:
The term `ℰᵢ ⊠ F(𝒢ᵢ)`: the derived external tensor product, on `X ×_A Y`, of the `i`-th first
factor of a resolution of the diagonal with the value of `F` at the `i`-th second factor.
declarations.comment: the terms of the complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DiagonalResolution.HomTransport.complex
declarations.doc:
The complex `… → ℰ₂ ⊠ F(𝒢₂) → ℰ₁ ⊠ F(𝒢₁) → ℰ₀ ⊠ F(𝒢₀)` on `X ×_A Y` obtained from a
resolution of the diagonal of `X` by transforming its second factors by `F`. Its differentials
are those of the resolution, transported along the given identification of Hom groups.
declarations.statement:
def complex (T : HomTransport R g F hG) :
    ChainComplex (DerivedCategory (pullback f g).Modules) ℕ
declarations.comment: the complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DiagonalResolution.HomTransport.complex_d
declarations.doc:
The differential of the transformed complex from index `i + 1` to index `i` is the
differential `ℰᵢ₊₁ ⊠ 𝒢ᵢ₊₁ ⟶ ℰᵢ ⊠ 𝒢ᵢ` of the resolution of the diagonal, transported along the
identification of Hom groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem complex_d (T : HomTransport R g F hG) (i : ℕ) :
    T.complex.d (i + 1) i = T.hom (i + 1) i (R.boxDifferential i)
declarations.comment: the differentials of the complex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_transformedDiagonalComplex
declarations.doc:
**(0G0A).** For `X`, `Y` proper smooth over a field `k`, `F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)`
`k`-linear exact fully faithful and `R` a resolution of the diagonal by `ℰᵢ ⊠ 𝒢ᵢ`, there is a
complex `… ⟶ ℰ₁ ⊠ F(𝒢₁) ⟶ ℰ₀ ⊠ F(𝒢₀)` in `D_perf(𝒪_{X ×_k Y})` whose differentials are those of
`R` transported by the identification of Hom groups sending `a ⊠ b` to `a ⊠ F(b)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_transformedDiagonalComplex (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))) [Smooth X.hom] [Smooth Y.hom]
    [IsProper X.hom] [IsProper Y.hom] :
    letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X
    letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
    ∀ (F : perfectDerived X.left ⥤ perfectDerived Y.left) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated],
      F.Linear k → Nonempty F.FullyFaithful →
      ∀ (R : DiagonalResolution X.hom),
        ∃ T : ImageHomTransport R Y.hom F,
          (∀ i, T.complex.X i = R.imageTerm Y.hom F i) ∧
          (∀ i, IsPerfect (X := (pullback X.hom Y.hom).toRingedSpace) (T.complex.X i)) ∧
          (∀ i, T.complex.d (i + 1) i = T.hom (i + 1) i (R.boxDifferential i)) ∧
          ∀ (i j : ℕ) (a : R.left i ⟶ R.left j) (b : R.right i ⟶ R.right j),
            T.hom i j (externalTensorProductMap X.hom X.hom a b) =
              R.transformedMap Y.hom F a b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fourierMukai_areSiblingsPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0B.** Let `k` be a field and `X`, `Y` smooth proper `k`-schemes.
Every `k`-linear exact fully faithful functor `F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` has a sibling
([Stacks, Tag 0FZZ]) which is a Fourier-Mukai functor `Φ_K : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` whose
kernel `K` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_{X ×_k Y})`.

The proof is the source's: [Stacks, Tag 0G06] applied to `F` and the Fourier-Mukai functor `G`
of [Stacks, Section 0G07]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_perfectFourierMukaiOver_agrees_zeroDimensional`), which agrees with
`F` on the coherent modules with zero-dimensional support.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fourierMukai_areSiblingsPerfect
    (F : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left)
    [hFs : F.CommShift ℤ] [hFt : F.IsTriangulated]
    (hlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X
      letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
      F.Linear k)
    (hF : Nonempty F.FullyFaithful) :
    haveI : CompactSpace X.left := (quasiCompact_iff_compactSpace X.hom).mp inferInstance
    haveI : CompactSpace Y.left := (quasiCompact_iff_compactSpace Y.hom).mp inferInstance
    haveI : IsNoetherian Y.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType Y.hom
    ∃ (K : DerivedCategory (pullback X.hom Y.hom).Modules)
      (hK : IsPerfect (X := (pullback X.hom Y.hom).toRingedSpace) K),
      @AreSiblingsPerfect X.left Y.left (isRegular_of_smooth_over_field X.hom)
        (isRegular_of_smooth_over_field Y.hom) _ _ F (perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hK) hFs hFt
        (commShift_fourierMukaiOn _ _ _ _ _ _) (isTriangulated_fourierMukaiOn _ _ _ _ _ _)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_perfectFourierMukaiOver_of_isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0C** (Orlov). Let `k` be a field and `X`, `Y` smooth proper schemes
over `k` with `X` projective over `k` (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective X.hom`, the first condition
of [Stacks, Tag 01W8]). Every `k`-linear exact fully faithful functor
`F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` is a Fourier-Mukai functor: there is a perfect object `K` of
`D(𝒪_{X ×_k Y})` with `F ≅ Φ_K` as functors.

A projective `k`-scheme carries an ample invertible module
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isProper_and_exists_isAmple_of_isAffine`), and for those this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_perfectFourierMukaiOver`, whose proof is the source's: a
Fourier-Mukai sibling from [Stacks, Tag 0G0B], made isomorphic to `F` by [Stacks, Tag 0FZW].
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iso_perfectFourierMukaiOver_of_isProjective
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective X.hom)
    (F : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left)
    [hFs : F.CommShift ℤ] [hFt : F.IsTriangulated]
    (hlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X
      letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
      F.Linear k)
    (hF : Nonempty F.FullyFaithful) :
    haveI : IsNoetherian Y.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType Y.hom
    ∃ (K : DerivedCategory (pullback X.hom Y.hom).Modules)
      (hK : IsPerfect (X := (pullback X.hom Y.hom).toRingedSpace) K),
      Nonempty (F ≅ perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hK)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fourierMukai_isEquivalence_areSiblingsPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0D.** Let `k` be a field and `X`, `Y` smooth proper `k`-schemes. If
`F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` is a `k`-linear exact equivalence, then there is a Fourier-Mukai
functor `F' = Φ_K : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` with kernel `K ∈ D_perf(𝒪_{X ×_k Y})` which is
an equivalence and a sibling of `F`. The functor of [Stacks, Tag 0G0B] is a sibling of `F`, and a
sibling of an equivalence is an equivalence by [Stacks, Tag 0FZV]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.AreSiblingsPerfect.isEquivalence`).
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fourierMukai_isEquivalence_areSiblingsPerfect
    (F : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left)
    [hFs : F.CommShift ℤ] [hFt : F.IsTriangulated]
    (hlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X
      letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
      F.Linear k)
    [F.IsEquivalence] :
    haveI : CompactSpace X.left := (quasiCompact_iff_compactSpace X.hom).mp inferInstance
    haveI : CompactSpace Y.left := (quasiCompact_iff_compactSpace Y.hom).mp inferInstance
    haveI : IsNoetherian Y.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType Y.hom
    ∃ (K : DerivedCategory (pullback X.hom Y.hom).Modules)
      (hK : IsPerfect (X := (pullback X.hom Y.hom).toRingedSpace) K),
      (perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hK).IsEquivalence ∧
        @AreSiblingsPerfect X.left Y.left (isRegular_of_smooth_over_field X.hom)
          (isRegular_of_smooth_over_field Y.hom) _ _ F (perfectFourierMukaiOver k X Y hK) hFs hFt
          (commShift_fourierMukaiOn _ _ _ _ _ _) (isTriangulated_fourierMukaiOn _ _ _ _ _ _)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_iso_diagonalFourierMukaiKernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0E].**  Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a smooth proper scheme over `k` and
let `K` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_{X ×_k X})`.  If the Fourier-Mukai functor
`Φ_K : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⟶ D_perf(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FYQ] is isomorphic to the identity functor,
then `K ≅ Δ_*𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_diagonalFourierMukaiKernel
    (K : DerivedCategory (Limits.pullback f f).Modules)
    (hK : perfectDerivedObjects (Limits.pullback f f) K)
    (hΦ : RepresentsIdentityOnPerfect f K) :
    Nonempty (K ≅ diagonalFourierMukaiKernel f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FourierMukaiKernelObj.category
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0F]: the category of Fourier-Mukai kernels over `S`.** Its objects are the
proper smooth schemes over `S` (`AlgebraicGeometry.FourierMukaiKernelObj`), its morphisms from `X`
to `Y` the isomorphism classes of objects of `D_perf(𝒪_{X ×_S Y})`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FourierMukaiKernelObj.Hom`), composition of the classes of `K` and `K'` the
class of `R pr_{13,*}(L pr_{12}^*K ⊗^𝐋 L pr_{23}^*K')`, which is perfect by [Stacks, Tag 0B91]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FourierMukaiKernelObj.isPerfect_convolution`), and identity of `X` the class of
`Δ_{X/S,*}𝒪_X`. The unit laws and associativity are proved
(`AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalKernelConvolutionIso`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.convolutionDiagonalKernelIso`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.fourierMukaiConvolutionAssocIso`).
declarations.statement: instance category : Category (FourierMukaiKernelObj S)
declarations.comment: the category, with all four clauses of the source: objects the proper smooth schemes over S; morphisms X to Y the isomorphism classes of objects of D_perf(O_{X x_S Y}); composition the class of R pr_13,*(L pr_12^*K tensor^L L pr_23^*K'), perfect by Tag 0B91 (isPerfect_convolution); identity the class of Delta_{X/S,*}O_X; associativity and the unit laws are the category axioms, proved. Clauses (3) and (4) are mk_comp_mk and id_eq

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FourierMukaiKernelObj.baseChangeFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0G]: base change along `s : S₁ ⟶ S` is a functor** from the category of
Fourier-Mukai kernels over `S` to the one over `S₁`. On objects it sends `X` to its base change
`X ×_S S₁ ⟶ S₁` and on morphisms the class of `K` on `X ×_S Y` to the class of
`L(X₁ ×_{S₁} Y₁ ⟶ X ×_S Y)^*K`.
declarations.statement: def baseChangeFunctor (s : S₁ ⟶ S) : FourierMukaiKernelObj S ⥤ FourierMukaiKernelObj S₁
declarations.comment: the functor between the categories of Tag 0G0F over S and over S1, both built with the perfectness of convolution proved (Tag 0B91): objects X go to the base change, written X x_S S1 (the source's S1 x_S X up to the symmetry of the fibre product), morphisms the class of K to the class of L(X1 x_{S1} Y1 --> X x_S Y)^*K; preservation of identities and of composition are the functor axioms, proved. The two rules are baseChangeFunctor_obj and baseChangeFunctor_map_mk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0I]**: `K` is *the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X`
to `Y` over `S`*.

Explicitly: `K` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_{X ×_S Y})`, and there is a perfect object `K'` of
`D(𝒪_{Y ×_S X})` such that the two convolutions of [Stacks, Tag 0FYS],

`R pr_{13,*}(L pr_{12}^*K ⊗^𝐋 L pr_{23}^*K')` on `X ×_S X` and
`R pr_{13,*}(L pr_{12}^*K' ⊗^𝐋 L pr_{23}^*K)` on `Y ×_S Y`,

are isomorphic to the diagonal kernels `Δ_{X/S,*}𝒪_X` and `Δ_{Y/S,*}𝒪_Y` of
[Stacks, Tag 0FYV] respectively. In other words the isomorphism class of `K` is an invertible
arrow of the category of the source's Section 0G0F.

The source states this for smooth proper `f` and `g`; those hypotheses are not used by the
definition and are not imposed here, so this is a generalization — see the module docstring.
declarations.statement: def IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (K : DerivedCategory (Limits.pullback f g).Modules) : Prop
declarations.comment: the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X` to `Y` over `S`, as the predicate on a perfect object of `D(𝒪_{X ×_S Y})` asserting the existence of a perfect `K'` on `Y ×_S X` with the two convolution isomorphisms; stated for arbitrary `f` and `g` rather than only smooth proper ones

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_quasiCoherentFourierMukai_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0J], the clause for `D_QCoh`.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` and
`g : Y ⟶ S` be smooth and proper, and let `K` be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative
equivalence from `X` to `Y` over `S`, [Stacks, Tag 0G0I]. Then the Fourier-Mukai functor
`Φ_K : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FYR] is an equivalence.

Its inverse is `Φ_{K'}` for the kernel `K'` that the definition of a relative equivalence
supplies: by [Stacks, Tag 0FYS] the two composites are the Fourier-Mukai functors of the two
convolutions, which the definition identifies with the diagonal kernels, whose Fourier-Mukai
functors are the identities by [Stacks, Tag 0FYV]. This is another name for
`AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_quasiCoherentFourierMukai`.
declarations.statement: public alias isEquivalence_quasiCoherentFourierMukai_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.comment: Phi_K : D_QCoh(O_X) -> D_QCoh(O_Y) is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_perfectFourierMukai_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0J], the clause for `D_perf`.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : X ⟶ S` and
`g : Y ⟶ S` be smooth and proper, and let `K` be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative
equivalence from `X` to `Y` over `S`, [Stacks, Tag 0G0I]. Then the Fourier-Mukai functor
`Φ_K : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FYT] is an equivalence.

The functor exists by clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0FYT], `f` being proper, flat and of finite
presentation and `K` perfect. Its inverse is `Φ_{K'}`, as in the `D_QCoh` clause
`AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_quasiCoherentFourierMukai_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel`,
whose two composite isomorphisms restrict to `D_perf(𝒪_X) ⊆ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. This is another name
for `AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_perfectFourierMukai`.
declarations.statement: public alias isEquivalence_perfectFourierMukai_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.comment: Phi_K : D_perf(O_X) -> D_perf(O_Y) is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_quasiCoherentFourierMukai
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0J], the clause for `D_QCoh`.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be smooth
and proper and let `K` be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X` to `Y` over
`S`, [Stacks, Tag 0G0I]. Then the Fourier-Mukai functor
`Φ_K : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FYR] is an equivalence.

The inverse is `Φ_{K'}` for the kernel `K'` the definition of a relative equivalence supplies:
its two composites with `Φ_K` are, by [Stacks, Tag 0FYS], the Fourier-Mukai functors of the two
convolutions, which the definition identifies with the diagonal kernels, whose Fourier-Mukai
functors are the identities. [Stacks, Tag 0FYS] is used through
`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCoherentFourierMukaiComp`, whose two inputs [Stacks, Tag 08IB] and
[Stacks, Tag 08EU] are the theorems `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.projectionFormulaIsIsoOnQuasicoherent`; the clause of [Stacks, Tag 0FYV] that
`Φ_{𝒪_Δ}` is the identity is `AlgebraicGeometry.fourierMukaiDiagonalKernelIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_quasiCoherentFourierMukai
    [Smooth f] [Smooth g] [IsProper f] [IsProper g]
    {K : DerivedCategory (Limits.pullback f g).Modules}
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel f g K) :
    (quasiCoherentFourierMukai f g K
      (isQuasicoherent_homology_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel f g hK)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: Phi_K : D_QCoh(O_X) -> D_QCoh(O_Y) is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_perfectFourierMukai
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0J], the clause for `D_perf`.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be smooth
and proper and let `K` be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X` to `Y` over
`S`, [Stacks, Tag 0G0I]. Then the Fourier-Mukai functor
`Φ_K : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` of [Stacks, Tag 0FYT] is an equivalence.

A perfect complex has quasi-coherent cohomology, so `D_perf(𝒪_X)` is a full subcategory of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` on which the two functors agree with their quasi-coherent counterparts. The two
composite isomorphisms of the quasi-coherent clause therefore whisker down to `D_perf`, and the
fully faithful inclusion of `D_perf(𝒪_X)` into `D(𝒪_X)` may be cancelled. What makes the two
functors on `D_perf` exist at all is clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0FYT], the theorem
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_fourierMukai_of_isPerfect_kernel_of_properFlatFinitePresentation`,
appealed to inside `AlgebraicGeometry.perfectFourierMukai`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_perfectFourierMukai
    [Smooth f] [Smooth g] [IsProper f] [IsProper g]
    {K : DerivedCategory (Limits.pullback f g).Modules}
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel f g K) :
    (perfectFourierMukai f g K hK.1).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: Phi_K : D_perf(O_X) -> D_perf(O_Y) is an equivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0K]: a relative equivalence is stable under base change.** Let `f : X ⟶ S`
and `g : Y ⟶ S` and let `K` be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X` to
`Y` over `S` ([Stacks, Tag 0G0I]). Let `s : S₁ ⟶ S` be *any* morphism of schemes, and write
`X₁ = X ×_S S₁` and `Y₁ = Y ×_S S₁` with their projections to `S₁`. Then

`K₁ = L(X₁ ×_{S₁} Y₁ ⟶ X ×_S Y)^* K`

is the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X₁` to `Y₁` over `S₁`.

The proof is the source's. Take the partner `K'` of `K` and pull it back to `K'₁` along
`Y₁ ×_{S₁} X₁ ⟶ Y ×_S X`. The square carrying `pr₁₃` on `X₁ ×_{S₁} Y₁ ×_{S₁} X₁` to `pr₁₃` on
`X ×_S Y ×_S X` is cartesian, and `pr₁₃` is flat because `g` is, so derived base change
([Stacks, Tag 08IB], granted) identifies `L^*` of the convolution with the convolution of the
pulled back kernels — the monoidality of derived pullback ([Stacks, Tag 079U]) and the
composition isomorphism ([Stacks, Tag 0D5S]) being what turn the pullback of
`L pr_{12}^*K ⊗^𝐋 L pr_{23}^*K'` into `L pr_{12}^*K₁ ⊗^𝐋 L pr_{23}^*K'₁`. On the other side the
square carrying `Δ_{X₁/S₁}` to `Δ_{X/S}` is cartesian, `X₁ ×_{S₁} X₁` and `X` are Tor
independent over `X ×_S X` by [Stacks, Tag 0CTA] (which is where flatness of `f` is used), and
`L^*𝒪_X[0] ≅ 𝒪_{X₁}[0]` because `𝒪_X` is flat; so `L^*` of the diagonal kernel is the diagonal
kernel. Perfectness transports by [Stacks, Tag 09UA].

Where the source uses smooth proper `f` and `g`, only flatness, separatedness and
quasi-compactness/quasi-separatedness are used here, so the hypotheses are weaker than the
source's; and `s` is arbitrary, as the source demands. The one granted input is `h08IB`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_derivedPullback
    (h08IB : DerivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent.{u})
    {S X Y S₁ : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (s : S₁ ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [IsSeparated g] [Flat f] [Flat g]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    {K : DerivedCategory (pullback f g).Modules}
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel f g K) :
    IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd f s) (pullback.snd g s)
      ((derivedPullback (fourierMukaiBaseChangeMap f g s).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: stability of relative-equivalence kernels under an ARBITRARY base change S1 -> S; f and g are only flat, separated and qcqs, all implied by the source's ambient smooth proper hypotheses. GRANTED: h08IB, the conclusion of Tag 08IB, which this tree lacks (it has the map of Tag 08HY and the affine input, not the globalization Tag 0DJ9) -- the same carry Tag 0FYS makes. All else (Tag 0CTA, Tag 09UA, flatness of pr13, Lp^*O_X[0] iso O_X1[0]) is proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0K]: a relative equivalence is stable under base change.** Let `f : X ⟶ S`
and `g : Y ⟶ S` be flat, separated, quasi-compact and quasi-separated (for instance smooth and
proper, as in the source), and let `K` be the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence
from `X` to `Y` over `S` ([Stacks, Tag 0G0I]). Let `s : S₁ ⟶ S` be any morphism of schemes, and
write `X₁ = X ×_S S₁` and `Y₁ = Y ×_S S₁` with their projections to `S₁`. Then

`K₁ = L(X₁ ×_{S₁} Y₁ ⟶ X ×_S Y)^* K`

is the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X₁` to `Y₁` over `S₁`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_derivedPullback` at
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent`, which is [Stacks, Tag 08IB].
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_baseChange
    {S X Y S₁ : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (s : S₁ ⟶ S)
    [IsSeparated f] [IsSeparated g] [Flat f] [Flat g]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [QuasiCompact g] [QuasiSeparated g]
    {K : DerivedCategory (pullback f g).Modules}
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel f g K) :
    IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd f s) (pullback.snd g s)
      ((derivedPullback (fourierMukaiBaseChangeMap f g s).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, for an arbitrary base change S1 -> S; f and g need only be flat, separated and qcqs, all implied by the source's smooth proper hypotheses. Tag 08IB enters through AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsIsoOnQuasicoherent, which proves it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_of_descentSituation
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0L]: a relative equivalence over a limit of schemes comes from a finite
stage.** Let `S = lim S_i` be the limit of a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, with a chosen index `0`, let
`X_0 ⟶ S_0` and `Y_0 ⟶ S_0` be smooth and proper, and put `X_i = X_0 ×_{S_0} S_i`,
`X = X_0 ×_{S_0} S` and likewise for `Y_0`. If `K` is the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative
equivalence from `X` to `Y` over `S`, then for some `i ≥ 0` there is a Fourier-Mukai kernel of a
relative equivalence from `X_i` to `Y_i` over `S_i`.

The proof is the source's. The kernel `K` and its partner `K'` descend to perfect objects `K_i`
and `K'_i` at a common stage `i` by [Stacks, Tag 09RF]; both displayed isomorphisms of
[Stacks, Tag 0G0I] then hold over the limit for the derived pullbacks of `K_i` and `K'_i`, since
the diagonal kernel and the convolution kernel commute with base change, so by
[Stacks, Tag 09RF] again the first of them already holds at some stage `j ≥ i`, and, after
transporting `K_i` and `K'_i` to `j`, the second at some stage `k ≥ j`. Transporting the first
isomorphism from `j` to `k` puts both at the stage `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_of_descentSituation
    (h09RFobj : PerfectDescendsAlongBaseChangedTower.{v, u})
    (h09RFiso : PerfectIsoDescendsAlongBaseChangedTower.{v, u})
    (hbc : DiagonalKernelAndConvolutionBaseChange.{u})
    (hperf : DiagonalKernelAndConvolutionPerfect.{u})
    {X₀ Y₀ : Scheme.{u}} (x : X₀ ⟶ D.stage D.base) (y : Y₀ ⟶ D.stage D.base)
    [Smooth x] [IsProper x] [Smooth y] [IsProper y]
    {K : DerivedCategory (pullback (pullback.snd x (D.projection D.base))
      (pullback.snd y (D.projection D.base))).Modules}
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd x (D.projection D.base))
      (pullback.snd y (D.projection D.base)) K) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.base ≤ i) (Ki : DerivedCategory (pullback
      (pullback.snd x (D.transition hi)) (pullback.snd y (D.transition hi))).Modules),
      IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd x (D.transition hi))
        (pullback.snd y (D.transition hi)) Ki
declarations.comment: the existence of a relative-equivalence kernel at SOME stage i >= 0 of a directed inverse system of qcqs schemes with affine transitions, given one over the limit. GRANTED, each an input the source's own proof cites and this tree lacks in applicable form: h09RFobj and h09RFiso, the two halves of Tag 09RF read along the tower of fibre products (the tree has only the coherent cocone); hbc, the two base-change isomorphisms established inside the proof of Tag 0G0K but private there (RelativeEquivalenceBaseChange.lean:404 and :427, exported only in the opposite direction as :518); hperf, perfectness of the diagonal kernel (Tag 0FDP with Tag 0B6G, whose tree form the proper direct image theorem grants its own Tor-dimension input) and of the convolution kernel (Tag 0B91, whose tree form StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/ProperFlatPushforwardBaseChange.lean:263 proves only the base-change half in tensor form). No hypothesis mentions relative equivalences, so nothing of the conclusion is assumed; the affineness of the transitions and the qcqs hypothesis on every stage enter through DescentSituation, and smoothness and properness of X_0 -> S_0 and Y_0 -> S_0 are instance hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_of_limit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0L]: a relative equivalence over a limit of schemes comes from a finite
stage.** Let `S = lim S_i` be the limit of a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, with a chosen index `0`, let
`X_0 ⟶ S_0` and `Y_0 ⟶ S_0` be smooth and proper, and put `X_i = X_0 ×_{S_0} S_i`,
`X = X_0 ×_{S_0} S` and likewise for `Y_0`. If `K` is the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative
equivalence from `X` to `Y` over `S`, then for some `i ≥ 0` there is a Fourier-Mukai kernel of a
relative equivalence from `X_i` to `Y_i` over `S_i`.

The proof is the source's, performed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_of_descentSituation`: the kernel and its
partner descend to a stage by [Stacks, Tag 09RF]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.perfectDescendsAlongBaseChangedTower`), the diagonal kernel and the
convolution kernel commute with base change ([Stacks, Tag 08IB], [Stacks, Tag 0CTA]:
`AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalKernelAndConvolutionBaseChange`) and are perfect
(`AlgebraicGeometry.diagonalKernelAndConvolutionPerfect`), and the two displayed isomorphisms of
[Stacks, Tag 0G0I] descend to a later stage by [Stacks, Tag 09RF] again
(`AlgebraicGeometry.perfectIsoDescendsAlongBaseChangedTower`).

The source writes `X_i = S_i ×_{S_0} X_0`; the base change is taken here on the other side,
which differs by the symmetry of the fibre product.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel_of_limit {I : Type u} [Preorder I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : DescentSituation.{u, u} I)
    {X₀ Y₀ : Scheme.{u}} (x : X₀ ⟶ D.stage D.base) (y : Y₀ ⟶ D.stage D.base)
    [Smooth x] [IsProper x] [Smooth y] [IsProper y]
    {K : DerivedCategory (pullback (pullback.snd x (D.projection D.base))
      (pullback.snd y (D.projection D.base))).Modules}
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd x (D.projection D.base))
      (pullback.snd y (D.projection D.base)) K) :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : D.base ≤ i) (Ki : DerivedCategory (pullback
      (pullback.snd x (D.transition hi)) (pullback.snd y (D.transition hi))).Modules),
      IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd x (D.transition hi))
        (pullback.snd y (D.transition hi)) Ki

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedIso_koszulOfLift
declarations.doc:
The chosen finite-free lift of the closed-fibre Koszul complex represents the Koszul
complex of its lifted first differential.
declarations.statement:
public lemma derivedIso_koszulOfLift
    (S : FlatLocalKoszulDeformationSituation.{u}) :
    letI : CommRing S.A := S.commRingA
    let I := Ideal.map (algebraMap S.R S.A) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S.R)
    ∀ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} S.A) ℤ)
      (f : Fin S.r → S.A),
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ S.K) →
      Nonempty
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ≅
          (Koszul.seqComplex S.residueSequence).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat) →
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        Nonempty (P.X (-(n : ℤ)) ≅
          ModuleCat.of S.A (Fin (S.r.choose n) → S.A))) →
      (∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i → IsZero (P.X i)) →
      (∃ (e₀ : P.X 0 ≅ ModuleCat.of S.A S.A)
        (e₁ : P.X (-1) ≅ ModuleCat.of S.A (Fin S.r → S.A)),
        (∀ i, f i = e₀.hom.hom ((P.d (-1) 0).hom
          (e₁.inv.hom (Pi.single i 1)))) ∧
        (∀ i, Ideal.Quotient.mk I (f i) = S.residueSequence i)) →
      Nonempty
        (S.K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((Koszul.seqComplex f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat))
declarations.comment: lifted_koszul

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_koszulDescription_and_flat_quotient_of_fibrewise_koszul
declarations.doc:
**The lifted sequence of [Stacks, Tag 0G0N] is regular with flat quotient.** In a flat local
deformation situation `R → A` whose closed fibre is Koszul on the regular sequence `f̄`, there is a
sequence `f` in `A` reducing to `f̄` modulo `𝔪_R A` which is regular in `A`, whose quotient
`A/(f)` is flat over `R`, and whose Koszul complex represents the deformed perfect complex `K` in
`D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_koszulDescription_and_flat_quotient_of_fibrewise_koszul
    (S : FlatLocalKoszulDeformationSituation.{u}) :
    letI : CommRing S.A := S.commRingA
    let I := Ideal.map (algebraMap S.R S.A) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S.R)
    ∃ f : Fin S.r → S.A,
      (∀ i, Ideal.Quotient.mk I (f i) = S.residueSequence i) ∧
        RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular S.A (List.ofFn f) ∧
          Module.Flat S.R (S.A ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ∧
            Nonempty (S.K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              ((Koszul.seqComplex f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat))
declarations.comment:
The hypotheses are packaged as `FlatLocalKoszulDeformationSituation`. The Koszul
complex is Mathlib's exterior-algebra complex `Koszul.seqComplex`, placed in cohomological degrees
by `ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat`, and `K` is identified with its image under
`DerivedCategory.Q`. The ideal `(f₁, …, f_r)` is `Ideal.span (Set.range f)` and "regular
sequence" is Mathlib's `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular`, which is Definition 00LF verbatim.

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_away_koszul_description
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0P.** A local Koszul presentation of a perfect complex, with flat
quotient, spreads to some principal neighbourhood of the prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_away_koszul_description {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Module.Flat R S]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)) (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K)
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → Localization.AtPrime q)
    (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime q) (List.ofFn f))
    (hflat : Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f)))
    (hiso : Nonempty
      ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u}
          (algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime q))).functor.obj K ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((Koszul.seqComplex f).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat))) :
    ∃ (g : S) (hg : g ∉ q) (f' : Fin r → Localization.Away g),
      (∀ i, localizationAwayToAtPrime g q hg (f' i) = f i) ∧
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.Away g) (List.ofFn f') ∧
      Module.Flat R (Localization.Away g ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range f')) ∧
      Nonempty
        ((derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral.{u, u, u}
            (algebraMap S (Localization.Away g))).functor.obj K ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            ((Koszul.seqComplex f').extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_baseChange_of_isIso_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0Q.** Let `X` and `Y` be proper over a Noetherian scheme `S`, with
`X` flat over `S`. An `S`-morphism `X ⟶ Y` which is an isomorphism on the fibre at `s` is an
isomorphism after base change to some open neighbourhood of `s`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isIso_baseChange_of_isIso_fiber
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] {X Y : Over S} (p : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsProper X.hom] [IsProper Y.hom] [Flat X.hom] (s : S)
    [IsIso ((Over.pullback (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).map p).left] :
    ∃ U : S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ IsIso ((Over.pullback U.ι).map p).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_opens_nonempty_iso_constantFamily_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0R].** Let `k` be a field, `q : S ⟶ Spec k` of finite type, `s` a
`k`-rational point of `S` (a section of `q`), and `g : Y ⟶ S` smooth and proper. Let
`X = Y_s ×_k S` be the constant family with fibre `Y_s = Y ×_S Spec k`. If `K` is the Fourier-Mukai
kernel of a relative equivalence from `X` to `Y` over `S` whose derived restriction along the
comparison morphism `i : Y_s ×_k Y_s ⟶ X ×_S Y` is the diagonal kernel `Δ_{Y_s/k,*}𝒪_{Y_s}`, then
there is an open `U ⊆ S` containing the point `s` picks out with `Y|_U` isomorphic to `Y_s ×_k U`
over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_nonempty_iso_constantFamily_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
    (rational : s ≫ q = 𝟙 _)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Limits.pullback (constantFamilyπ q g s) g).Modules)
    (relEquiv : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (constantFamilyπ q g s) g K)
    (restrict : Nonempty ((derivedPullback
        (fibreSquareToProductComparison q g s rational).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K ≅
      diagonalKernel (fibreAtRationalPointπ g s))) :
    ∃ U : S.Opens, Set.range s.base ⊆ (U : Set S) ∧
      Nonempty ((Over.pullback U.ι).obj (Over.mk g) ≅
        Over.mk (Limits.pullback.snd (fibreAtRationalPointπ g s) (U.ι ≫ q)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_opens_iso_constantFamily_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G0S].** Let `k` be algebraically closed, `X ⟶ Spec k`
smooth and proper, `g : Y ⟶ S` smooth and proper with `S` of finite type over `k`, and `K` the
Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `X ×_k S` to `Y` over `S`. Then every point of
`S` has an open neighbourhood `U` over which `Y` is the constant family `Y₀ ×_k U` of some smooth
proper `Y₀` over `k`.

At each `k`-rational point `s` this is `exists_opens_iso_constantFamily_of_rationalPoint` with
`Y₀ = Y_s`, smooth and proper as a base change of `g`; the opens so obtained cover `S` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_opens_of_rationalPoints` (`S` is Jacobson and its closed points
are `k`-rational).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_iso_constantFamily_of_isRelativeEquivalenceKernel [IsAlgClosed k]
    (K : DerivedCategory (pullback (pullback.snd a q) g).Modules)
    (hK : IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (pullback.snd a q) g K) :
    ∀ x : S, ∃ U : S.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ Y₀ : Over (Spec (.of k)),
      Smooth Y₀.hom ∧ IsProper Y₀.hom ∧
        Nonempty ((Over.pullback U.ι).obj (Over.mk g) ≅ (Over.pullback (U.ι ≫ q)).obj Y₀)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.countable_hom_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
Over a countable Noetherian ring, the morphisms over the base between two schemes of finite
type form a countable type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem countable_hom_of_finiteType
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Countable R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (X Y : Over (Spec (.of R)))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] :
    Countable (X ⟶ Y)
declarations.comment: countable_hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.countable_isomorphismClasses_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
There are countably many isomorphism classes of schemes of finite type over a countable
Noetherian ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem countable_isomorphismClasses_of_finiteType
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Countable R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    Countable
      (Quotient (isIsomorphicSetoid
        (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun X : Over (Spec (.of R)) =>
          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ QuasiCompact X.hom))))
declarations.comment: countable_iso_classes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.boundedDerivedCategory_essentiallyCountable
declarations.doc:
The bounded derived category of an essentially countable abelian category is essentially
countable.
declarations.statement:
public instance boundedDerivedCategory_essentiallyCountable
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [EssentiallyCountableCategory A] :
    EssentiallyCountableCategory (DerivedCategory.Bounded A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.essentiallyCountable_perfect_and_boundedCoherent_of_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0W.** Let `X` be a scheme of finite type over a countable Noetherian
ring `R`. Then the categories `D_perf(𝒪_X)` and `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)` are countable: each has
countably many morphisms between any two objects and countably many isomorphism classes of
objects, which is `CategoryTheory.EssentiallyCountableCategory`, the notion of countability of
[Stacks, Section 0G0T]. Both are read as full subcategories of `D(𝒪_X)`, at any model of the
derived category.

As in the source: `X` is Noetherian, `D_perf(𝒪_X)` is a full subcategory of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`
([Stacks, Tag 0FXU]), `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X) = D^b(Coh(𝒪_X))` ([Stacks, Tag 0FDB]), and the bounded
derived category of the countable abelian category `Coh(𝒪_X)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.essentiallyCountable_coherentModules_of_finiteType`) is countable
([Stacks, Tag 0G0V]).
declarations.statement:
public theorem essentiallyCountable_perfect_and_boundedCoherent_of_finiteType {R : Type u}
    [CommRing R] [Countable R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)] :
    EssentiallyCountableCategory
        (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
          (fun K : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) =>
            RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)) ∧
      EssentiallyCountableCategory
        (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
          (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBBounded
            (fun M : StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace => M.IsCoherent)))
declarations.comment: D_perf(O_X) and D^b_Coh(O_X) are countable categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_countable_finiteType_isomorphism_families_of_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
For `S` of finite type over an algebraically closed field `K` and `X, Y` of finite type over
`S`, there is a countable set `I`, for each `i` a finite-type morphism `S i ⟶ S` and an
isomorphism `X ×_S S i ≅ Y ×_S S i` over `S i`, such that every closed point of `S` valued in `K`
whose two fibres are isomorphic over `K` lies in the image of some `S i ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_countable_finiteType_isomorphism_families_of_isAlgClosed
    {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
    (S : Over (Spec (.of K))) [LocallyOfFiniteType S.hom] [QuasiCompact S.hom]
    (X Y : Over S.left)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Countable I) (T : I → Over S.left)
      (_ : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (T i).hom ∧ QuasiCompact (T i).hom)
      (_ : ∀ i, (Over.pullback (T i).hom).obj X ≅ (Over.pullback (T i).hom).obj Y),
      ∀ (s : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ S),
        Nonempty ((Over.pullback s.left).obj X ≅ (Over.pullback s.left).obj Y) →
          ∃ (i : I) (t : Spec (.of K) ⟶ (T i).left),
            t ≫ (T i).hom = s.left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_countable_relativeEquivalenceKernels
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G0Y.** Let `K` be an algebraically closed field. There is a countable
set `I` and for each `i ∈ I` a system `(Sᵢ/K, Xᵢ ⟶ Sᵢ, Yᵢ ⟶ Sᵢ, Mᵢ)` with
1. `Sᵢ` of finite type over `K`,
2. `Xᵢ ⟶ Sᵢ` and `Yᵢ ⟶ Sᵢ` proper and smooth,
3. `Mᵢ ∈ D_perf(𝒪_{Xᵢ ×_{Sᵢ} Yᵢ})` the Fourier-Mukai kernel of a relative equivalence from `Xᵢ`
   to `Yᵢ` over `Sᵢ`,
4. for all smooth proper `K`-schemes `X`, `Y` with a `K`-linear exact equivalence
   `D_perf(𝒪_X) ⟶ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` there are `i ∈ I` and `s ∈ Sᵢ(K)` with `X ≅ (Xᵢ)ₛ` and
   `Y ≅ (Yᵢ)ₛ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_countable_relativeEquivalenceKernels (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K] :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Countable I)
      (S : I → Over (Spec (.of K)))
      (X Y : (i : I) → Over (S i).left)
      (M : (i : I) → DerivedCategory (pullback (X i).hom (Y i).hom).Modules)
      (_ : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (S i).hom ∧ QuasiCompact (S i).hom)
      (_ : ∀ i, Smooth (X i).hom ∧ IsProper (X i).hom)
      (_ : ∀ i, Smooth (Y i).hom ∧ IsProper (Y i).hom)
      (_ : ∀ i, IsRelativeEquivalenceKernel (X i).hom (Y i).hom (M i)),
      ∀ (A B : Over (Spec (.of K))),
        Smooth A.hom → IsProper A.hom → Smooth B.hom → IsProper B.hom →
          (letI : Linear K A.left.Modules := modulesLinear K A
           letI : Linear K B.left.Modules := modulesLinear K B
           ∃ e : PerfectDerivedCategory A.left ≌ PerfectDerivedCategory B.left,
             e.functor.Linear K ∧
               ∃ h : e.functor.CommShift ℤ,
                 letI := h
                 e.functor.IsTriangulated) →
            ∃ (i : I) (s : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of K))) ⟶ S i),
              Nonempty (A ≅ (Over.pullback s.left).obj (X i)) ∧
                Nonempty (B ≅ (Over.pullback s.left).obj (Y i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedEquivalent
declarations.doc:
Two schemes over a field `k` are *derived equivalent* if their categories of perfect
complexes admit a `k`-linear exact equivalence.
declarations.statement: abbrev DerivedEquivalent (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.countable_isomorphismClasses_derivedEquivalent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G11.** Let `K` be an algebraically closed field and let `X₀` be a
smooth proper scheme over `K`. There are at most countably many isomorphism classes of smooth
proper schemes `Y` over `K` which are derived equivalent to `X₀`, i.e. admit a `K`-linear exact
equivalence `D_perf(𝒪_{X₀}) ⟶ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` ([Stacks, Tag 0G10]).

Proof: [Stacks, Tag 0G0Y] (`exists_countable_relativeEquivalenceKernels`) produces the countable
family of relative equivalences, and
`countable_isomorphismClasses_derivedEquivalent_of_relativeEquivalenceFamilies` counts.
declarations.statement:
theorem countable_isomorphismClasses_derivedEquivalent
    (X₀ : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [Smooth X₀.hom] [IsProper X₀.hom] :
    {c : IsomorphismClassOver k | ∃ Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
      Smooth Y.hom ∧ IsProper Y.hom ∧
        (letI : Linear k X₀.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X₀
         letI : Linear k Y.left.Modules := modulesLinear k Y
         ∃ e : Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.PerfectDerivedCategory X₀.left ≌
             Stacks.Perfect.BoundedLocallyFreeComplexes.PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left,
           e.functor.Linear k ∧
             ∃ h : e.functor.CommShift ℤ,
               letI := h
               e.functor.IsTriangulated) ∧
        c = isomorphismClassOver Y}.Countable

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.etale_aeval_iff_height_eq_and_span_range_D_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G1C.** Let `k` be a field, let `A` be a `k`-algebra of finite type and let
`a₁, …, aₙ ∈ A`. The `k`-algebra map `φ : k[x₁, …, xₙ] → A`, `xᵢ ↦ aᵢ`, is étale if and only if
(a) every maximal ideal of `A` has height `n`, equivalently the local rings of `A` at maximal
ideals have dimension `n`, and (b) the differentials `d(a₁), …, d(aₙ)` generate `Ω[A⁄k]` as an
`A`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem MvPolynomial.etale_aeval_iff_height_eq_and_span_range_D_eq_top
    {n : ℕ} (k A : Type*) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A]
    (a : Fin n → A) :
    (aeval a : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] A).toRingHom.Etale ↔
      (∀ m : Ideal A, m.IsMaximal → Ideal.height m = n) ∧
      Submodule.span A (Set.range fun i ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k A (a i)) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_etalePresentation_nonfiniteGeneratorNumber_lt
declarations.doc:
In positive characteristic, an étale presentation of a finite étale algebra whose
nonfinite-generator invariant is positive can be replaced by a compatible étale presentation
with strictly smaller invariant.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etalePresentation_nonfiniteGeneratorNumber_lt
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (B : Type w) [CommRing B]
    [Algebra ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ⧸ I) B]
    [Algebra k B] [IsScalarTower k ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ⧸ I) B]
    [Module.Finite ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ⧸ I) B]
    [Algebra.Etale ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ⧸ I) B]
    (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [Algebra k C]
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] C) (hφ : φ.toRingHom.Etale)
    (τ : (C ⧸ Ideal.map φ.toRingHom I) →ₐ[k] B) (hτ : Function.Surjective τ)
    (hcomm : ∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k,
      τ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map φ.toRingHom I) (φ f)) =
        algebraMap ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ⧸ I) B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I f))
    (hpos : 0 < nonfiniteGeneratorNumber φ.toRingHom) :
    ∃ (φ' : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k →ₐ[k] C),
      φ'.toRingHom.Etale ∧
      ∃ τ' : (C ⧸ Ideal.map φ'.toRingHom I) →ₐ[k] B,
        Function.Surjective τ' ∧
        (∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k,
          τ' (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map φ'.toRingHom I) (φ' f)) =
            algebraMap ((MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ⧸ I) B (Ideal.Quotient.mk I f)) ∧
        nonfiniteGeneratorNumber φ'.toRingHom < nonfiniteGeneratorNumber φ.toRingHom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteEtale_to_affineSpace
declarations.doc:
An affine scheme étale over affine space in positive characteristic admits a
(possibly different) finite étale morphism to the same affine space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtale_to_affineSpace
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (n : ℕ)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X]
    (f : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) (Spec (.of k))) [Etale f] :
    ∃ g : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) (Spec (.of k)),
      IsFinite g ∧ Etale g
