      (renumberedCanonicalExtSpectralSequence S)
declarations.comment: canonical_convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.renumberedCanonicalExtSpectralSequence_convergesToExt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, convergence after renumbering.** For `M ∈ D⁻(A)` and
`K ∈ D⁺(A)`, the renumbered canonical Ext spectral sequence converges to
`Ext^(i+j)(M, K)`, with filtration index `j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem renumberedCanonicalExtSpectralSequence_convergesToExt
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    {M K : DerivedCategory A} {M' : CochainComplex A ℤ}
    {e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M' ≅ M}
    (S : CanonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M' e)
    (hM : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).minus M)
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).plus K) :
    let E := renumberedCanonicalExtSpectralSequence S
    ∃ hF : ∀ n : ℤ, Monotone (canonicalExtFiltration S n),
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ canonicalExtFiltration S n a = ⊥ ∧
        canonicalExtFiltration S n b = ⊤) ∧
      (∀ i j : ℤ, E.HasPageInfinityAt (i, j)) ∧
      ∀ i j : ℤ, Nonempty
        (E.pageInfinity (i, j) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (canonicalExtFiltration S (i + j) j)
            (canonicalExtFiltration S (i + j) (j + 1)) (hF (i + j) (by omega))))
declarations.comment: canonical_convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isBounded_canonicalExtSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, boundedness of the canonical Ext spectral sequence.** For `M ∈ D⁻(A)` and
`K ∈ D⁺(A)`, the Ext spectral sequence of the canonical truncation filtration
`F^p M^• = τ_{≤ -p} M^•` of a complex `M^•` representing `M` is bounded.  This is
`canonicalExtSpectralSequence_isBounded` at the filtration itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isBounded_canonicalExtSpectralSequence
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (M K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M' ≅ M)
    (hM : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).minus M)
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).plus K) :
    IsBounded (canonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M' e).spectralSequence
declarations.comment: canonical_convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.convergesToExt_canonicalExtSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, convergence of the canonical Ext spectral sequence.** For `M ∈ D⁻(A)` and
`K ∈ D⁺(A)`, the Ext spectral sequence of the canonical truncation filtration
`F^p M^• = τ_{≤ -p} M^•` of a complex `M^•` representing `M` converges to `Ext^{p+q}(M, K)`,
with filtration index `-p`.  This is `canonicalExtSpectralSequence_convergesToExt` at the
filtration itself.
declarations.statement:
public theorem convergesToExt_canonicalExtSpectralSequence
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (M K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M' ≅ M)
    (hM : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).minus M)
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).plus K) :
    let S := canonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M' e
    let E := S.spectralSequence
    ∃ hF : ∀ n : ℤ, Monotone (canonicalExtFiltration S n),
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ canonicalExtFiltration S n a = ⊥ ∧
        canonicalExtFiltration S n b = ⊤) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, E.HasPageInfinityAt (p, q)) ∧
      ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
      (E.pageInfinity (p, q) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (canonicalExtFiltration S (p + q) (-p))
            (canonicalExtFiltration S (p + q) (-p + 1)) (hF (p + q) (by omega))))
declarations.comment: canonical_convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.stupidExtSpectralSequence_isBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, boundedness of the brutal-truncation Ext spectral sequence.** If
`K ∈ D⁺(A)` and the cochain complex `M^•` is bounded above, the Ext spectral sequence of the
filtration `F^p M^• = σ_{≥ p} M^•` is bounded.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stupidExtSpectralSequence_isBounded
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).plus K)
    (hM : CochainComplex.minus A M') :
    IsBounded (stupidExtSpectralSequence K M')
declarations.comment: stupid_convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.stupidExtSpectralSequence_convergesToExt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, convergence of the brutal-truncation Ext spectral sequence.** If
`K ∈ D⁺(A)` and the cochain complex `M^•` is bounded above, the Ext spectral sequence of the
filtration `F^p M^• = σ_{≥ p} M^•` converges to `Ext^{p+q}(M^•, K)`, the Ext groups of the
object `M` of the derived category represented by `M^•`, with filtration index `-p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stupidExtSpectralSequence_convergesToExt
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (hK : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := A)).plus K)
    (hM : CochainComplex.minus A M') :
    let E := stupidExtSpectralSequence K M'
    ∃ hF : ∀ n : ℤ, Monotone
        (extQuotientFiltration K (CochainComplex.stupidTruncationFiltration M') n),
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧
        extQuotientFiltration K (CochainComplex.stupidTruncationFiltration M') n a = ⊥ ∧
        extQuotientFiltration K (CochainComplex.stupidTruncationFiltration M') n b = ⊤) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, E.HasPageInfinityAt (p, q)) ∧
      ∀ p q : ℤ, Nonempty
        (E.pageInfinity (p, q) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE
            (extQuotientFiltration K
              (CochainComplex.stupidTruncationFiltration M') (p + q) (-p))
            (extQuotientFiltration K
              (CochainComplex.stupidTruncationFiltration M') (p + q) (-p + 1))
            (hF (p + q) (by omega))))
declarations.comment: stupid_convergence

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.canonicalExtSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, the canonical truncation filtration.** Let `A` be a Grothendieck abelian
category and let `M, K ∈ D(A)`.  Every cochain complex representing `M`, filtered by
`F^p M^• = τ_{≤ -p} M^•`, gives a cohomological spectral sequence whose first page is
`E₁^{p,q} = Ext^{2p+q}(H^p(M), K)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalExtSpectralSequence
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (M K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M' ≅ M) :
    CanonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M' e
declarations.comment: canonical_e1

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_canonicalExtSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, the canonical truncation filtration.** Let `A` be a Grothendieck abelian
category and let `M, K ∈ D(A)`.  Every cochain complex representing `M`, filtered by
`F^p M^• = τ_{≤ -p} M^•`, gives a cohomological spectral sequence whose first page is
`E₁^{p,q} = Ext^{2p+q}(H^p(M), K)`.  This is `canonicalExtSpectralSequence` forgetting the
construction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_canonicalExtSpectralSequence
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (M K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M' ≅ M) :
    Nonempty (CanonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M' e)
declarations.comment: canonical_e1

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.stupidExtSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, the brutal truncation filtration.** The Ext spectral sequence of the
filtration `F^p M^• = σ_{≥ p} M^•` of a cochain complex `M^•`, a cohomological spectral sequence
`(E_r, d_r)_{r ≥ 1}`.  It is definitionally the construction of Tag 0G1Z applied to that filtered
complex, so every page, differential and page-turning isomorphism is specified.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stupidExtSpectralSequence
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ) :
    CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{w} 1
declarations.comment: stupid_e1

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.stupidExtSpectralSequenceE₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G20, the brutal truncation filtration.** The first page of the Ext spectral
sequence of the filtration `F^p M^• = σ_{≥ p} M^•` is `E₁^{p,q} = Ext^q(M^{-p}, K)`.

The index is `-p`, not `p`: the first page at `(p, q)` is `Ext^{p+q}` of the graded piece
`gr^{-p}M^• = M^{-p}[p]`, and the shift moves `p + q` down to `q`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stupidExtSpectralSequenceE₁
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A]
    (K : DerivedCategory A) (M' : CochainComplex A ℤ) (p q : ℤ) :
    ((stupidExtSpectralSequence K M').page 1).X (p, q) ≅
      AddCommGrpCat.of (DerivedCategory.Ext
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A 0).obj (M'.X (-p))) K q)
declarations.comment: stupid_e1

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.canonicalExtSpectralSequence_iso
declarations.doc:
The canonical-truncation Ext spectral sequence is independent of the choice of complex
representing `M`, as a spectral sequence from `E₁` onward.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalExtSpectralSequence_iso
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A] (M K : DerivedCategory A)
    (M₁ M₂ : CochainComplex A ℤ)
    (e₁ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M₁ ≅ M) (e₂ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj M₂ ≅ M)
    (S₁ : CanonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M₁ e₁)
    (S₂ : CanonicalExtSpectralSequence M K M₂ e₂) :
    Nonempty (S₁.spectralSequence ≅ S₂.spectralSequence)
declarations.comment: representative_independence

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.extensionByZero_unit_hom_coproduct_bijective
declarations.doc:
Extension by zero of the unit module on `U` is compact with respect to
bounded-below direct sums, provided cohomology on `U` commutes with direct sums.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extensionByZero_unit_hom_coproduct_bijective
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, r}) (U : X.C)
    (hsums :
      letI : EnoughInjectives (SheafOfModules.{max u v r m}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :=
        enoughInjectives_of_ringedSite.{u, v, r, m} X
      letI : (SheafOfModules.evaluation.{max u v r m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
          (op U)).Additive :=
        evaluation_additive_of_ringedSite.{u, v, r, m} X U
      ∀ (p : ℕ) (I : Type w),
      PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
        ((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{max u v r m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            (op U)).rightDerived p))
    (I : Type w) [DecidableEq I]
    (M : I → DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r m}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) [HasCoproduct M]
    (hM : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
      (C := SheafOfModules.{max u v r m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))).plus
          (∐ M)) :
    let K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r m}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :=
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{max u v r m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
        (extensionByZeroUnit.{v, u, r, m} X.J (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U))
    Function.Bijective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid (β := fun i : I => K ⟶ M i) (γ := K ⟶ ∐ M)
        fun i => Preadditive.rightComp K (Limits.Sigma.ι M i))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.extensionByZero_unit_hom_coproduct_bijective_of_hasIntersectionsIn
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site with a cofinal collection of finite coverings closed under finite
intersections, extension by zero of the unit module over `U` is compact with respect to
bounded-below coproducts.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extensionByZero_unit_hom_coproduct_bijective_of_hasIntersectionsIn
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (B : Set X.C) (Cov : ∀ U : X.C, Set (PreZeroHypercover.{c} U))
    (hCov : ∀ (U : X.C) (E : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U), Cov U E → E.sieve₀ ∈ X.J U)
    (hfinite : ∀ (U : X.C) (E : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U), Cov U E →
      HasIntersectionsIn B E)
    (hcofinal : ∀ (U : X.C), B U → ∀ S ∈ X.J U,
      ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U, Cov U E ∧ E.sieve₀ ≤ S)
    (U : X.C) (hU : B U)
    (I : Type i) [DecidableEq I]
    (M : I → DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct M]
    (hM : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))).plus (∐ M)) :
    let K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :=
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
        (extensionByZeroUnit.{u, u, u, u} X.J (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U))
    Function.Bijective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid (β := fun j : I => K ⟶ M j) (γ := K ⟶ ∐ M)
        fun j => Preadditive.rightComp K (Limits.Sigma.ι M j))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_of_bijective_on_spanning_set
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G24.** Let `F : C ⥤ D` be an exact functor of
pre-triangulated categories which has both adjoints. If a set `S` detects zero objects by maps
from and to all shifts of its members, and `F` induces bijections on all shifted Hom sets between
members of `S`, then `F` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fullyFaithful_of_bijective_on_spanning_set
    {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{v'} D]
    [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    [F.IsLeftAdjoint] [F.IsRightAdjoint] (S : Set C)
    (h_from : ∀ K : C,
      (∀ E : C, E ∈ S → ∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (E ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) → IsZero K)
    (h_to : ∀ K : C,
      (∀ E : C, E ∈ S → ∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (K ⟶ E⟦i⟧)) → IsZero K)
    (h_bijective : ∀ E : C, E ∈ S → ∀ E' : C, E' ∈ S → ∀ i : ℤ,
      Function.Bijective (fun f : E ⟶ E'⟦i⟧ ↦
        F.map f ≫ (F.commShiftIso i).hom.app E')) :
    Nonempty F.FullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedVarieties.Orlov.fullyFaithful_iff_bijective_ext_perfectPointSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G25].** Let `k` be a field and let `X`, `Y` be proper schemes over `k` with
`X` regular. A `k`-linear exact functor `F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` is fully faithful if and
only if for all closed points `x, x' ∈ X` the maps
`F : Ext^i_X(𝒪_x, 𝒪_{x'}) ⟶ Ext^i_Y(F(𝒪_x), F(𝒪_{x'}))` are isomorphisms for all `i ∈ ℤ`. Here
`𝒪_x` is the skyscraper sheaf at `x` with value `κ(x)` (`perfectPointSheaf`), and
`Ext^i(A, B) = Hom(A, B[i])`, the map being `f ↦ F(f)` followed by the commutation of `F` with the
shift.

The proof is the source's: `F` has both adjoints ([Stacks, Tag 0FYN]), so the criterion of
[Stacks, Tag 0G24] applies to the closed-point skyscrapers, its hypotheses (2) and (3) being
[Stacks, Tag 0G03] parts (2) and (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_iff_bijective_ext_perfectPointSheaf (hX : IsRegular X.left)
    (F : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] [F.Linear k] :
    Nonempty F.FullyFaithful ↔
      ∀ (x x' : X.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X.left))
        (hx' : IsClosed ({x'} : Set X.left)) (i : ℤ),
        haveI : IsNoetherian X.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType X.hom
        Function.Bijective (fun f : perfectPointSheaf X.left hX x hx ⟶
            (perfectPointSheaf X.left hX x' hx')⟦i⟧ =>
          F.map f ≫ (F.commShiftIso i).hom.app (perfectPointSheaf X.left hX x' hx'))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedVarieties.Orlov.fullyFaithful_of_fixes_zeroDimensional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G26].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme over `k` which is
regular, and let `F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_X)` be a `k`-linear exact functor. Assume that for
every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` with `dim Supp(𝓕) = 0` there is an isomorphism `𝓕 ≅ F(𝓕)`. Then
`F` is fully faithful.

Here `𝓕` is read in `D_perf(𝒪_X)` placed in degree zero (it is perfect, `X` being regular, and the
hypothesis is asked for every proof of that); the isomorphism is taken in `D(𝒪_X)`, which is the
same as one in the full subcategory `D_perf(𝒪_X)`. "Exact" is a triangulated functor, and
`k`-linearity is for the structure induced by the structure morphism
(`AlgebraicGeometry.modulesLinear`). By [Stacks, Tag 0G25] it suffices that `F` is bijective on
`Ext` between closed-point skyscrapers, which is
`bijective_map_shift_perfectPointSheaf_of_fixes_zeroDimensional`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_of_fixes_zeroDimensional (hX : IsRegular X.left)
    (F : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory X.left) [F.CommShift ℤ]
    [F.IsTriangulated]
    (hlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X; F.Linear k)
    (hfix : ∀ (𝓕 : X.left.Modules), 𝓕.IsCoherent →
      topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp 𝓕) = 0 →
      ∀ h𝓕 : IsPerfect (X := X.left.toRingedSpace)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj 𝓕),
        Nonempty ((F.obj ⟨_, h𝓕⟩).obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj 𝓕)) :
    Nonempty F.FullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedVarieties.Orlov.exists_areSiblingsPerfect_of_fixes_zeroDimensional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G27].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme over `k` which is
regular, and let `F : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_X)` be a `k`-linear exact functor. Assume that for
every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` with `dim Supp(𝓕) = 0` there is an isomorphism `𝓕 ≅ F(𝓕)`. Then
there exist an automorphism `f : X ⟶ X` over `k` which induces the identity on the underlying
topological space and an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ` such that `F` and
`F'(M) = Lf^*M ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} ℒ` are siblings.

Here `F'` is `perfectPullbackDerivedTensor f.hom ℒ` and "siblings" is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AreSiblingsPerfect` ([Stacks, Tag 0FZZ]: siblings as functors on
`D_perf = D^b_Coh`, `X` being regular). `F` is fully faithful by [Stacks, Tag 0G26] and essentially
surjective by [Stacks, Tag 0GX0], and the rest of the source's proof is
`exists_areSiblingsPerfect_of_fullyFaithful_of_essSurj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_areSiblingsPerfect_of_fixes_zeroDimensional (hX : IsRegular X.left)
    (F : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory X.left) [F.CommShift ℤ]
    [F.IsTriangulated]
    (hlin : letI : Linear k X.left.Modules := modulesLinear k X; F.Linear k)
    (hfix : ∀ (𝓕 : X.left.Modules), 𝓕.IsCoherent →
      topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp 𝓕) = 0 →
      ∀ h𝓕 : IsPerfect (X := X.left.toRingedSpace)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj 𝓕),
        Nonempty ((F.obj ⟨_, h𝓕⟩).obj ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj 𝓕)) :
    haveI : IsNoetherian X.left := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType X.hom
    ∃ (f : X.left ≅ X.left) (L : X.left.Modules)
      (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.left.presheaf X.left.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
      f.hom ≫ X.hom = X.hom ∧ (∀ x : X.left, f.hom x = x) ∧
      @AreSiblingsPerfect X.left X.left hX hX _ _ F
        (perfectPullbackDerivedTensor f.hom L (isPerfect_single_of_isInvertible hX L hL))
        ‹_› ‹_›
        (show (perfectPullbackDerivedTensor f.hom L
          (isPerfect_single_of_isInvertible hX L hL)).CommShift ℤ from inferInstance)
        (show (perfectPullbackDerivedTensor f.hom L
          (isPerfect_single_of_isInvertible hX L hL)).IsTriangulated from inferInstance)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedLowerShriekUnbounded
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G29] (2).** Let `Λ` be a torsion ring and let
`Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, Λ)` be the derived lower shriek of a
compactification `f = f̄ ∘ j`. Then `Rf_!` commutes with direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedLowerShriekUnbounded
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (hΛ : ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ (m : Λ) = 0)
    (I : Type (max (u + 1) r)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, r} f j Λ)
declarations.comment: (2) for Λ a torsion ring in any universe, on D(X_étale, Λ): Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ j_! commutes with direct sums. The base declarations of (2) assume the proper case (Tag 0F0D); here it is proved

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimit_derivedLowerShriek_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G29] (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type separated morphism of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, let `Λ` be a ring, in any universe, and let
`Rf_! = R(fbar)_* ∘ j_!` be the derived lower shriek of a compactification `j` of `f`, on bounded
below derived categories. Let `K : I → D⁺(X_étale, Λ)` be a family of objects and `a : ℤ` such
that `H^n(K i) = 0` for `n < a` and all `i`. Then `Rf_!(⨁ i, K i) = ⨁ i, Rf_!(K i)`.

The source states this for `K i` in `D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`; no torsion hypothesis is used, so it is
stated for all of `D⁺(X_étale, Λ)`. The three inputs of the source's proof are proved: the
adjunction `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` ([Stacks, Tag 08FJ],
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleModuleDerivedExtensionByZeroAdj`), that `j_!` preserves the lower
bound (a right derived functor does), and [Stacks, Tag 0GIW] for the proper morphism `fbar`
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimit_etaleModuleDerivedDirectImage_of_isGE`, whose input
[Stacks, Tag 09Z1] is
`preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_rightDerived_etaleModuleDirectImage_univ`).
declarations.comment: (1) Rf_!(⨁ K_i) = ⨁ Rf_! K_i for a family of D⁺(X_étale, Λ) with common lower bound a, Λ a ring in any universe; the base declaration of (1) assumes Tags 08FJ, 03S5 and 0GIW, here they are proved

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedUpperShriek.preservesColimit_derivedLowerShriek_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G29] (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type separated morphism of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, let `Λ` be a ring, let `j` be a compactification of
`f` and let `Rf_! = R(fbar)_* ∘ j_!` be the derived lower shriek it determines.  Let
`K : I → D⁺(X_étale, Λ)` be a family of objects and let `a : ℤ` be such that `H^n(K i) = 0`
for `n < a` and all `i`, that is `(K i).IsGE a`.  Then
`Rf_!(⨁ i, K i) = ⨁ i, Rf_!(K i)`.

The three inputs are the ones the source cites.  `adjImmersion` is the adjunction
`j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` of [Stacks, Tag 08FJ]; from it, and not from any further hypothesis, `j_!`
commutes with the direct sum.  `hShriekGE` is exactness of extension by zero,
[Stacks, Tag 03S5], in the form that `j_!` preserves the lower bound, so that
[Stacks, Tag 0GIW] applies to the family `j_! (K i)`.  `hProper` is [Stacks, Tag 0GIW] itself
for the proper — hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated — morphism `fbar = j.toBase`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimit_derivedLowerShriek_of_isGE {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    {I : Type w} (K : I → DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X))
    (a : ℤ) (hK : ∀ i, (K i).IsGE a)
    {Uj : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ j.space) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X)}
    (adjImmersion : etaleModuleDerivedExtensionByZero.{u, r} Λ j.immersion ⊣ Uj)
    (hShriekGE : ∀ (b : ℤ) (M : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X)), M.IsGE b →
      ((etaleModuleDerivedExtensionByZero.{u, r} Λ j.immersion).obj M).IsGE b)
    (hProper : ∀ L : I → DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ j.space),
      (∀ i, (L i).IsGE a) →
      PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor L)
        (etaleModuleDerivedDirectImage.{u, r} Λ j.toBase)) :
    PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor K) (derivedLowerShriek.{u, r} f j Λ)
declarations.comment: (1) Rf_!(⨁ K_i) = ⨁ Rf_! K_i for a family with common lower bound a

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedUpperShriek.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G29] (2).** Let `Λ` be a torsion ring and let
`Rf_! = R(fbar)_* ∘ j_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, Λ)` be the derived lower shriek of a
compactification `f = fbar ∘ j` of a finite type separated morphism of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes.  Then `Rf_!` commutes with direct sums of every shape.

The two inputs are the ones the source cites: `adjImmersion` is the adjunction `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}`
of [Stacks, Tag 08FJ] for the open immersion `j`, and `hProper` is [Stacks, Tag 0F0D], that
`R(fbar)_*` commutes with direct sums for a torsion coefficient ring.  That a left adjoint
commutes with direct sums, and that the composite therefore does, is proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedLowerShriek {DU : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} DU]
    {DX : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} DX] {DY : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} DY]
    {shriek : DU ⥤ DX} {Uj : DX ⥤ DU} (adjImmersion : shriek ⊣ Uj)
    (pushforwardFbar : DX ⥤ DY) (I : Type w)
    (hProper : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) pushforwardFbar) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (shriek ⋙ pushforwardFbar)
declarations.comment: (2) for Λ torsion, Rf_! = R(fbar)_* ∘ j_! commutes with direct sums

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedUpperShriek.CompactificationData.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G29] (2) for the derived lower shriek of a `CompactificationData`.**  The
functor `Rf_! = R(fbar)_* ∘ j_!` read off a compactification commutes with direct sums of
every shape, given the adjunction `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` of [Stacks, Tag 08FJ] and
[Stacks, Tag 0F0D] for `R(fbar)_*`.

This is the form that discharges the hypothesis of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedUpperShriek.CompactificationData.isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriek`,
which is [Stacks, Tag 0G2C].
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedLowerShriek {DU : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} DU]
    {DX : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} DX] {DY : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} DY]
    (data : CompactificationData DU DX DY) {Uj : DX ⥤ DU} (adjImmersion : data.shriek ⊣ Uj)
    (I : Type w)
    (hProper : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) data.pushforwardFbar) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) data.derivedLowerShriek
declarations.comment: (2) for a CompactificationData: Rf_! commutes with direct sums

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.preservesColimitsOfSize_derivedExtensionByZero
declarations.doc:
**The open immersion case of the proof of [Stacks, Tag 0G29].** On the unbounded derived
categories of sheaves of modules over a ringed site, extension by zero along the localization
at an object commutes with direct sums — indeed with all colimits — because it is a left
adjoint of restriction, which is [Stacks, Tag 08FJ],
`Stacks.Cohomology.Localization.derivedExtensionByZeroRestrictionAdjunction`.

The source of [Stacks, Tag 0G29] reduces the commutation of `Rf_!` with direct sums to this
statement for an open immersion and to [Stacks, Tag 0GIW] or [Stacks, Tag 0F0D] for a proper
morphism; this is the half of the reduction that is available outright.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfSize_derivedExtensionByZero (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (U : X.C) :
    PreservesColimitsOfSize.{w, w'}
      (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
        (𝟙 (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).over U))).mapDerivedCategory
declarations.comment: the open immersion case of the proof: j_! commutes with direct sums

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_bounded_derivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G2A].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes with `Y` quasi-compact,
`j` a compactification of `X` over `Y` (through which `Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_!` is defined), and `Λ`
a ring. There is an integer `N` such that for `E ∈ D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`, and, when `Λ` is
torsion, for `E ∈ D(X_étale, Λ)`:

1. `Hⁱ(Rf_!(τ_{≤ a} E)) ⟶ Hⁱ(Rf_! E)` is an isomorphism for `i ≤ a`;
2. `Hⁱ(Rf_! E) ⟶ Hⁱ(Rf_!(τ_{≥ b - N} E))` is an isomorphism for `i ≥ b`;
3. if `Hⁱ(E) = 0` for `i ∉ [a, b]` then `Hⁱ(Rf_! E) = 0` for `i ∉ [a, b + N]`; stated as the two
   implications `E ≥ a ⇒ Rf_! E ≥ a` and `E ≤ b ⇒ Rf_! E ≤ b + N`, which together are part (3)
   for all `-∞ ≤ a ≤ b ≤ ∞`.

[Stacks, Tag 0G2A] assumes `f` separated of finite type and `X`, `Y` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated; here the compactification `j` is given, and only quasi-compactness of `Y` is
used.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bounded_derivedLowerShriek [CompactSpace Y] :
    ∃ N : ℕ,
      (∀ E : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X), isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X E →
        (∀ a i : ℤ, i ≤ a → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).map
            ((derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f j Λ).map
              ((DerivedCategory.Plus.TStructure.t.truncLEι a).app E)))) ∧
          (∀ b i : ℤ, b ≤ i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ i).map
            ((derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f j Λ).map
              ((DerivedCategory.Plus.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (b - N)).app E)))) ∧
          (∀ a : ℤ, E.IsGE a → ((derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f j Λ).obj E).IsGE a) ∧
          ∀ b : ℤ, E.IsLE b →
            (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj ((derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f j Λ).obj E)).IsLE
              (b + N)) ∧
      ((∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ (m : Λ) = 0) → ∀ E : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X),
        (∀ a i : ℤ, i ≤ a → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map
            ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ).map
              ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι a).app E)))) ∧
          (∀ b i : ℤ, b ≤ i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).map
            ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ).map
              ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (b - N)).app E)))) ∧
          (∀ a : ℤ, E.IsGE a → ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ).obj E).IsGE a) ∧
          ∀ b : ℤ, E.IsLE b →
            ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ).obj E).IsLE (b + N))
declarations.comment: all three parts, for E in D+_tors(X, Lambda) (Rf_! = derivedLowerShriek on D+) and, when Lambda is torsion, for E in D(X, Lambda) (Rf_! = derivedLowerShriekUnbounded), with one N for both; part (3) is the conjunction of its lower and upper bound halves, which is the source's statement for all -infinity <= a <= b <= infinity

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedUpperShriek.isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
Let `Λ` be a coefficient ring, let `A` be the Grothendieck abelian category of sheaves of
`Λ`-modules on `X_étale`, and let `Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ j_!` be the derived lower shriek of a
compactification `f = f̄ ∘ j`, with `j_!` and `Rf̄_*` exact. If `Rf_!` commutes with direct sums —
which is [Stacks, Tag 0G29] when `f` is a separated finite-type morphism of quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes and `Λ` is torsion — then `Rf_!` has a right adjoint
`Rf^! : D(Y_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(X_étale, Λ)`.
declarations.statement: theorem isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriek : (shriek ⋙ pushforwardFbar).IsLeftAdjoint
declarations.comment: Rf_! = Rf̄_*j_!, with its commutation with direct sums (Tag 0G29) assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.DerivedUpperShriek.CompactificationData.isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
The functor `Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ j_!` read off a `CompactificationData` has a right adjoint as soon
as it commutes with direct sums, which is [Stacks, Tag 0G29].
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriek
    (data : CompactificationData (DerivedCategory A) DX DY)
    [data.shriek.CommShift ℤ] [data.shriek.IsTriangulated]
    [data.pushforwardFbar.CommShift ℤ] [data.pushforwardFbar.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ J : Type (max w u v),
      PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) data.derivedLowerShriek] :
    data.derivedLowerShriek.IsLeftAdjoint
declarations.comment: for a CompactificationData; the commutation with direct sums (Tag 0G29) assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriekUnbounded_of_compactification
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G2C].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite type separated morphism of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated schemes and let `Λ` be a torsion ring, in any universe. The functor
`Rf_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, Λ)` has a right adjoint
`Rf^! : D(Y_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(X_étale, Λ)`.

Here `Rf_!` is `Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_!` for a compactification `f = f̄ ∘ j`, as in [Stacks, Tag 0F7H]: such
a compactification exists ([Stacks, Tag 0F41]), and for every one of them `Rf_!` is a left
adjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriekUnbounded_of_compactification (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] [CompactSpace Y]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] (hΛ : ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ (m : Λ) = 0) :
    (∃ j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f), QuasiCompact j.immersion) ∧
      ∀ j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f),
        (derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, r} f j Λ).IsLeftAdjoint
declarations.comment: Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_! on D(X_étale, Λ), Λ a torsion ring in any universe, for every compactification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isIntegralHom_isPullback_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2D.** Let `j : V ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact open immersion of algebraic spaces over
a scheme `S` and let `π : Z ⟶ V` be an integral morphism. Then there is an integral morphism
`ν : Y' ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` such that `Z` is `V`-isomorphic to the inverse image
of `V` in `Y'`: the square formed by `π`, `j`, `ν` and the canonical morphism `Z ⟶ Y'` is
cartesian.

`Y'` is the normalization of `Y` in `Z`, and the cartesian square is obtained from the
chart description of that normalization by the cancellation of Tag 07VZ along a surjective étale
chart of `V`; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIntegralHom_isPullback_of_isOpenImmersion
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hV : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (j : V ⟶ Y) (hj : IsOpenImmersion B S hS j)
    (hjqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS j) (π : Z ⟶ V) (hπ : IsIntegralHom B S hS π) :
    ∃ (Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (ν : Y' ⟶ Y) (f' : Z ⟶ Y'),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y' ∧ IsIntegralHom B S hS ν ∧ IsPullback f' π ν j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_pushforward_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2E.** If `i : Z ⟶ X` is a perfect closed immersion of schemes then `i_*𝒪_Z` is a
perfect `𝒪_X`-module, that is, a perfect object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_pushforward_structureSheaf {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [Perfect i]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)] :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace) 0).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_countable_dense_subset
declarations.doc:
An infinite dense subset of a Noetherian scheme contains a countable dense
subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_countable_dense_subset (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S]
    (T : Set S) (_hT_infinite : T.Infinite) (hT_dense : Dense T) :
    ∃ E : Set S, E ⊆ T ∧ E.Countable ∧ Dense E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DeligneSystem.isIso_restrictionNatTrans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G2H.** Let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open immersion of Noetherian schemes and
let `(K_n)` be a Deligne system with value `K` on `U`. Then the canonical restriction
transformation

`colim_n Mor_X(K_n, -) ⟶ Mor_U(K, (-)|_U)`

is an isomorphism: `colim_n Hom_X(K_n, L) = Hom_U(K, L|_U)` for every `L` in
`D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.DeligneSystem.isIso_restrictionNatTrans_of_core` with its hypothesis
`hcore` supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.DeligneSystem.restrictionLifting_truncGELE`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_restrictionNatTrans (K : BoundedCoherentDerived U)
    (e : D.system ⋙ restrictBoundedCoherent j ≅
      (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj ((boundedCoherentDerived U).ι.obj K)) :
    IsIso (D.restrictionNatTrans K e)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.exists_firstOrderThickening_without_localRetraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2J.** If an object `x` of a category fibred in groupoids with (RS*) over the big
fppf site of a locally Noetherian scheme is not versal at a finite type point `u` of an affine
scheme `U` of finite type, then `x` extends to an object `y` over a first order thickening
`U ⟶ T` with ideal `κ(u)` which has no retraction to `x` over any open neighbourhood of `u`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_firstOrderThickening_without_localRetraction
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : Type v} [Category.{w} F]
    (p : F ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hRS : Deformation.Artin.SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp)
    (U : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : F)
    (hx : p.obj x = U)
    [IsAffine ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U).hom]
    (u₀ : ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U).left)
    (_hu₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u₀)
    (hnot : ¬ Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt
      ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj U) (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion)
      u₀ x (congrArg (Over.post B.inclusion).obj hx)) :
    ∃ (T : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : U ⟶ T)
      (y : F) (hy : p.obj y = T) (r : x ⟶ y),
      let V := AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS
      let iS := V.map i
      (p.map r = eqToHom hx ≫ i ≫ eqToHom hy.symm) ∧
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening iS ∧
      Epi (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit iS.toRingCatSheafHom) ∧
      Nonempty (kernel (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
        iS.toRingCatSheafHom) ≅
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward ((V.obj T).fromSpecResidueField (iS u₀))).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit
            (Spec ((V.obj T).residueField (iS u₀))).ringCatSheaf)) ∧
      (∀ (W : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS) (j : W ⟶ T)
          (w₀ : V.obj W) (_ : V.map j w₀ = iS u₀)
          (_ : IsOpenImmersion (V.map j))
          (z : F) (hz : p.obj z = W) (s : z ⟶ y)
          (_ : p.map s = eqToHom hz ≫ j ≫ eqToHom hy.symm)
          (_ : p.IsCartesian (p.map s) s),
        ¬ ∃ (β : z ⟶ x) (x' : F) (a : x' ⟶ x) (b : x' ⟶ z),
          p.IsCartesian (p.map a) a ∧
          p.IsCartesian (p.map b) b ∧
          IsPullback
            (V.map (p.map a ≫ eqToHom hx))
            (V.map (p.map b ≫ eqToHom hz)) iS (V.map j) ∧
          a ≫ r = b ≫ s ∧ b ≫ β = a)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isVersalAt_of_specializes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2K.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `𝒳` a category fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces,
which satisfies (RS*) and which is limit preserving. Let `x` be an object of `𝒳` over a scheme
`U` locally of finite type over `S`, and let `u ⤳ u₀` be a specialization of points of `U` with
`u₀` of finite type. If `x` is versal at `u₀`, then `x` is versal at `u`.

The source asks `U` to be of finite type over `S` and `u` to be a finite type point; neither is
used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVersalAt_of_specializes [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hΔ : AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasRepresentableDiagonal B S hS 𝒳)
    (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS 𝒳.val.p 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hlim : IsLimitPreserving.{u, u, u, w, v} B S hS 𝒳)
    (x : 𝒳.val.obj) [LocallyOfFiniteType ((𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x).hom]
    (u u₀ : ((𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x).left)
    (hu₀ : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint u₀) (hspec : u ⤳ u₀)
    (hversal : IsVersalAt ((𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x)
      (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ x rfl) :
    IsVersalAt ((𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x)
      (𝒳.val.p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u x rfl

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
A 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` *is quasi-finite*
when it is locally quasi-finite (**Stacks 06PU**) and quasi-compact (**Stacks 050U**).
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiFinite {𝒳 𝒴 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiFinite_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2N.** A composite of quasi-finite 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is
quasi-finite: local quasi-finiteness composes by **Stacks 06UD** and quasi-compactness by
**Stacks 050W**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFinite_comp
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hg : IsQuasiFinite B S hS g) :
    IsQuasiFinite B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiFinite_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2P.** A base change of a quasi-finite 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks
over `S` is quasi-finite: the first projection of any 2-fibre product of the cospan `(g, f)` is
quasi-finite as soon as `f` is.

Quasi-finiteness is local quasi-finiteness together with quasi-compactness, and the two conjuncts
are inherited by **Stacks 06UB** and **Stacks 050V** respectively.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFinite_baseChange {𝒳 𝒴 𝒴' : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴' ⟶ 𝒴)
    (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq g f)
    (hP : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P)
    (hf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiFinite B S hS P.fst

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasiFinite_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiDM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2Q.** If a composite of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` is quasi-finite
and its second factor is quasi-separated and quasi-DM, then its first factor is quasi-finite.

Quasi-finiteness is local quasi-finiteness together with quasi-compactness, and the source's
proof combines the cancellation of each conjunct: local quasi-finiteness cancels against the
quasi-DM second factor by **Stacks 06UG** and quasi-compactness cancels against the
quasi-separated second factor by **Stacks 050Y**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFinite_of_comp_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_isQuasiDM
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵)
    (hfg : IsQuasiFinite B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hgQuasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS g)
    (hgQuasiDM : IsQuasiDM B S hS g) :
    IsQuasiFinite B S hS f

declarations.name: maximalPoints
declarations.doc: The points of `T` which admit no nontrivial generalization belonging to `T`.
declarations.statement: def maximalPoints {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (T : Set X) : Set X
declarations.comment: the set of maximal points

declarations.name: specialization_eq_of_mem_maximalPoints
declarations.doc: There is no nontrivial specialization between maximal points of a subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem specialization_eq_of_mem_maximalPoints
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] {T : Set X} {x y : X}
    (hx : x ∈ maximalPoints T) (hy : y ∈ maximalPoints T)
    (hxy : x ⤳ y) : x = y
declarations.comment: part (a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_maximalPoint_specializes
declarations.doc:
Every point of a subset of a Noetherian scheme is a specialization of a maximal point
of that subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_maximalPoint_specializes
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ T) :
    ∃ y ∈ maximalPoints T, y ⤳ x
declarations.comment: part (b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.closure_maximalPoints
declarations.doc:
The maximal points of a subset of a Noetherian scheme have the same closure as the
subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem closure_maximalPoints
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (T : Set X) :
    closure (maximalPoints T) = closure T
declarations.comment: part (c)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.exists_sequence_firstOrderThickenings_without_localRetraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G2S.** Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over the big
fppf site of a locally Noetherian scheme `S`, satisfying (RS*), and let `x` be an object of
`𝒳` over an affine scheme `U` of finite type over `S`. Let `u 0, u 1, …` be finite type
points of `U` with no specializations between distinct ones, at none of which `x` is versal.
Then there are morphisms `x ⟶ x₁ ⟶ x₂ ⟶ …` of `𝒳` over `U ⟶ U₁ ⟶ U₂ ⟶ …` over `S` such
that each `U ⟶ Uₙ₊₁` is a first order thickening, the ideal of `Uₙ ⟶ Uₙ₊₁` is the residue
field `κ(u n)`, and `x ⟶ xₙ₊₁` admits no retraction over any open neighbourhood of `u n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sequence_firstOrderThickenings_without_localRetraction
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F : Type v} [Category.{w} F]
    (p : F ⥤ AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp)
    (U : Over S) [IsAffine U.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom] [QuasiCompact U.hom]
    (x : F) (hx : (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x = U)
    (u : ℕ → U.left)
    (hfinite : ∀ n, AlgebraicGeometry.IsFiniteTypePoint (u n))
    (hincomparable : ∀ n m, n ≠ m → ¬ (u n ⤳ u m))
    (hnonversal : ∀ n,
      ¬ Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt U (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) (u n) x hx) :
    let q : F ⥤ Over S := p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion
    ∃ (xs : ℕ → F)
      (step : ∀ n, xs n ⟶ xs (n + 1))
      (fromX : ∀ n, x ⟶ xs n),
      ∃ hzero : xs 0 = x,
        fromX 0 = eqToHom hzero.symm ∧
        (∀ n, fromX (n + 1) = fromX n ≫ step n) ∧
        (let j : ∀ n, U.left ⟶ (q.obj (xs n)).left :=
          fun n ↦ eqToHom (congrArg Over.left hx).symm ≫ (q.map (fromX n)).left
        ∀ n,
          Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening (j (n + 1)) ∧
          (let i : (q.obj (xs n)).left ⟶ (q.obj (xs (n + 1))).left :=
              (q.map (step n)).left
           Epi (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit i.toRingCatSheafHom) ∧
           Nonempty (kernel (SheafOfModules.unitToPushforwardObjUnit
               i.toRingCatSheafHom) ≅
             (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
                 ((q.obj (xs (n + 1))).left.fromSpecResidueField (j (n + 1) (u n)))).obj
               (SheafOfModules.unit (Spec ((q.obj (xs (n + 1))).left.residueField
                 (j (n + 1) (u n)))).ringCatSheaf))) ∧
          (∀ (y : F) (r : y ⟶ xs (n + 1)),
            IsOpenImmersion (q.map r).left →
            (∃ z : (q.obj y).left,
              (q.map r).left z = j (n + 1) (u n)) →
            ∀ (z : F) (t : z ⟶ x) (s : z ⟶ y),
              IsPullback (q.map t).left (q.map s).left
                (q.map (fromX (n + 1))).left (q.map r).left →
              ¬ ∃ β : y ⟶ x,
                s ≫ β = t ∧ t ≫ fromX (n + 1) = s ≫ r))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd.hasColimit
declarations.doc: (ind, part 1) An essentially constant `M` has a colimit.
declarations.statement: theorem hasColimit {M : I ⥤ C} (h : IsEssentiallyConstantInd M) : HasColimit M

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd.exists_retraction_colimit
declarations.doc:
(ind, part 2) The colimit cocone realizes `IsEssentiallyConstantInd M` with value
`colimit M`: some `i₀` admits a retraction `b` of `colimit.ι M i₀` through which every
`colimit.ι M j` factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_colimit {M : I ⥤ C} (h : IsEssentiallyConstantInd M) [HasColimit M] :
