declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd.hasLimit_of_op
declarations.doc: (pro, part 1) If `M` is essentially constant as a pro-object, `M` has a limit.
declarations.statement: theorem hasLimit_of_op {M : I ⥤ C} (h : IsEssentiallyConstantInd M.op) : HasLimit M

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.IsEssentiallyConstantInd.exists_retraction_op_limit
declarations.doc:
(pro, part 2) The (opposite) limit cone realizes `IsEssentiallyConstantInd M.op` with value
`op (limit M)`: some `i₀` admits a retraction `b` of `(limit.π M i₀.unop).op` through which every
`(limit.π M j.unop).op` factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_op_limit {M : I ⥤ C} (h : IsEssentiallyConstantInd M.op)
    [HasLimit M] :
    ∃ (i₀ : Iᵒᵖ) (b : op (limit M) ⟶ M.op.obj i₀),
      IsEssentiallyConstantWith M.op (limit.cone M).op i₀ b

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pro.homEquiv
declarations.doc:
A morphism of pro-systems from `F` to `G` is the same thing as a transformation of functors
`t : B ⟶ A`, where `A(X) = colim_i Mor(F i, X)` and `B(X) = colim_j Mor(G j, X)`. The bijection
sends `t` to the family of images under `t` of the classes of the identities `id_{G j}`; see
`component_homEquiv`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def homEquiv : (coyonedaColim G ⟶ coyonedaColim F) ≃ Hom F G

declarations.name: irreducibleComponents_eq_range_of_irredundant_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G2Y**.
Given an irredundant finite covering of `X` by irreducible closed subsets `T i` (`i : Fin n`),
the set of irreducible components of `X` is exactly the image of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleComponents_eq_range_of_irredundant_cover
    {n : ℕ} (T : Fin n → Set X)
    (hcov : ⋃ i, T i = (Set.univ : Set X))
    (hirr : ∀ i, IsIrreducible (T i))
    (hcl : ∀ i, IsClosed (T i))
    (hmin : ∀ i, ¬ T i ⊆ ⋃ j ∈ ({j | j ≠ i} : Set (Fin n)), T j) :
    irreducibleComponents X = Set.range T

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible.trans
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a geometrically irreducible field extension and let `S` be a geometrically
irreducible `K`-algebra. Then `S` is geometrically irreducible over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible.trans (k K S : Type u) [Field k] [Field K]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra k K] [Algebra K S] [Algebra k S] [IsScalarTower k K S]
    [Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k K] [Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible K S] :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIrreducible.iff_ratFunc
declarations.doc:
An extension of fields `K/k` is geometrically irreducible if and only if the induced extension
`K(X)/k(X)` of purely transcendental extensions in one variable is geometrically irreducible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIrreducible.iff_ratFunc (k K : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ↔
      GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k⟮X⟯ K⟮X⟯)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_specMap_adjoin_of_transcendental
declarations.doc:
Let `K/L/M` be a tower of fields with `L` geometrically irreducible over `M`, and let
`x : K` be transcendental over `L`. Then `L(x)` is geometrically irreducible over `M(x)`,
where `M(x) = M⟮x⟯` and `L(x)` is the `M⟮x⟯`-subfield of `K` generated by the image
of `L`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIrreducible_specMap_adjoin_of_transcendental
    {M L K : Type u} [Field M] [Field L] [Field K] [Algebra M L] [Algebra M K] [Algebra L K]
    [IsScalarTower M L K]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap M L)))]
    {x : K} (hx : Transcendental L x) :
    GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (algebraMap ↥M⟮x⟯ ↥(adjoin ↥M⟮x⟯ (Set.range (algebraMap L K))))))

declarations.name: separableClosure.eq_bot_iff_geometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be an extension of fields. The separable closure of `k` in `K` is trivial — every
element of `K` separably algebraic over `k` lies in `k` — if and only if `K` is geometrically
irreducible over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem separableClosure.eq_bot_iff_geometricallyIrreducible (k K : Type u) [Field k]
    [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    separableClosure k K = ⊥ ↔ GeometricallyIrreducible (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k K)))

declarations.name: deRham_isDiffOpOfOrder_one
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a ring map and `i ≥ 0`. The de Rham differential `d : Ωⁱ_{B/A} → Ωⁱ⁺¹_{B/A}`,
an additive map that is `A`-linear (`hAlin`) and satisfies
`d (b₀ · db₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ dbᵢ) = db₀ ∧ db₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ dbᵢ` (`hChar`), is a differential operator of order `1`
relative to `A → B`: for every `b ∈ B` the map `ω ↦ d (b · ω) - b · d ω` is `B`-linear.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRham_isDiffOpOfOrder_one (i : ℕ)
    (d : (⋀[B]^i (Ω[B⁄A])) →+ (⋀[B]^(i + 1) (Ω[B⁄A])))
    (hAlin : IsALinear A B d)
    (hChar : ∀ b : Fin (i+1) → B, d (deRhamGen i b) = deRhamTop i b) :
    IsDiffOpLE A B 1 d

declarations.name: isDiffOpLE_succ_of_comm_isDiffOpLE_on_generators
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `(g i)`
generate `B` as an `A`-algebra, let `M, N` be `B`-modules and `D : M →+ N` an
`A`-linear map. Fix `k ≥ 1` (written `k + 1` here). If for every `i` the commutator
`diffOpComm (g i) D` is a differential operator of order `≤ k`, then `D` is a
differential operator of order `≤ k + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiffOpLE_succ_of_comm_isDiffOpLE_on_generators
    {ι : Type*} (g : ι → B)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin A (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B M] [Module B N]
    (D : M →+ N) (hD : IsALinear A B D) (k : ℕ)
    (hcomm : ∀ i : ι, IsDiffOpLE A B k (diffOpComm (g i) D)) :
    IsDiffOpLE A B (k + 1) D

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.existsUnique_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G36.** Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` and `N` be `S`-modules and let `T ⊆ S` be
a multiplicative subset. A differential operator `D : M → N` of order at most `k` relative to
`R → S` extends uniquely to a differential operator of order at most `k` relative to
`R → T⁻¹S` on the localizations: there is a unique `R`-linear map `E : T⁻¹M → T⁻¹N` which is a
differential operator of order at most `k` and satisfies `E ∘ f = g ∘ D` for the localization
maps `f : M → T⁻¹M` and `g : N → T⁻¹N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_extension {k : ℕ} {D : M →ₗ[R] N}
    (hD : D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k) (T : Submonoid S) [IsLocalization T S']
    (f : M →ₗ[S] M') (g : N →ₗ[S] N') [IsLocalizedModule T f] [IsLocalizedModule T g] :
    ∃! E : M' →ₗ[R] N', E.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S' k ∧
      E ∘ₗ f.restrictScalars R = g.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ D
declarations.comment:
Stated for abstract localizations `IsLocalization T S'`, `IsLocalizedModule T f`,
`IsLocalizedModule T g` rather than for `Localization T` and `LocalizedModule T`. The order of
the extension is relative to `R → S'`, as in the source's proof. `extends` is spelled as the
equation `E ∘ₗ f.restrictScalars R = g.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ D`, so the source's canonical maps
are pinned; the case `k = 0` is `IsLocalizedModule.lift`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.rTensorB
declarations.doc:
**The operator `D ⊗ id_N`.** The tensor product of an `R`-linear map `D : M →ₗ[R] M'` with the
identity of a `B`-module `N`, as a `B`-linear map `M ⊗[R] N → M' ⊗[R] N`. Its underlying `R`-linear
map is `LinearMap.rTensor N D`; the content of the definition is the `B`-linearity, `B` acting
through `algebraMap B (A ⊗[R] B) b = 1 ⊗ₜ b` on the factor `N` that `D ⊗ id_N` leaves alone. Here
`hsmul` and `hsmul'` say that `A ⊗[R] B` acts on the tensor products by
`(a ⊗ b) • (m ⊗ n) = (a • m) ⊗ (b • n)`, and `halg` that `B → A ⊗[R] B` is `b ↦ 1 ⊗ b`.
declarations.statement:
public def rTensorB
    (halg : ∀ b : B, algebraMap B (A ⊗[R] B) b = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] b)
    (hsmul : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M) (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (hsmul' : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M') (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (D : M →ₗ[R] M') : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[B] M' ⊗[R] N
declarations.comment:
the operator `D ⊗ id_N` itself; `rTensorB_tmul` is its values on pure tensors,
`order_rTensorB` the order bound and `eq_rTensorB` its uniqueness. The `B`-algebra structure on
`A ⊗[R] B` and the actions on `M ⊗[R] N`, `M' ⊗[R] N` are hypotheses because Mathlib has no such
instances; `halg`, `hsmul` and `hsmul'` pin them to the canonical ones. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.rTensorB_tmul
declarations.doc: `D ⊗ id_N` sends `m ⊗ n` to `D m ⊗ n`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma rTensorB_tmul
    (halg : ∀ b : B, algebraMap B (A ⊗[R] B) b = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] b)
    (hsmul : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M) (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (hsmul' : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M') (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (D : M →ₗ[R] M') (m : M) (n : N) :
    rTensorB halg hsmul hsmul' D (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = D m ⊗ₜ[R] n
declarations.comment: the values of `rTensorB` on pure tensors

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.order_rTensorB
declarations.doc:
If `D` is a differential operator of order at most `k` relative to `R → A`, then `D ⊗ id_N` is
one of order at most `k` relative to `B → A ⊗[R] B`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma order_rTensorB {k : ℕ} {D : M →ₗ[R] M'}
    (hD : D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE A k)
    (halg : ∀ b : B, algebraMap B (A ⊗[R] B) b = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] b)
    (hsmul : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M) (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (hsmul' : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M') (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n)) :
    (rTensorB halg hsmul hsmul' D).IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE (A ⊗[R] B) k
declarations.comment: the order bound on `rTensorB`

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.eq_rTensorB
declarations.doc: `D ⊗ id_N` is the only `B`-linear map `M ⊗[R] N → M' ⊗[R] N` carrying `m ⊗ n` to `D m ⊗ n`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma eq_rTensorB {D : M →ₗ[R] M'}
    (halg : ∀ b : B, algebraMap B (A ⊗[R] B) b = 1 ⊗ₜ[R] b)
    (hsmul : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M) (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (hsmul' : ∀ (a : A) (b : B) (m : M') (n : N),
      (a ⊗ₜ[R] b) • (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ[R] (b • n))
    (D' : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[B] M' ⊗[R] N)
    (hD' : ∀ (m : M) (n : N), D' (m ⊗ₜ[R] n) = D m ⊗ₜ[R] n) :
    D' = rTensorB halg hsmul hsmul' D
declarations.comment: uniqueness of `rTensorB`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.isEssentiallyConstant_op_iff_exists_iso_const_biprod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G39**. An inverse system `A : J ⥤ 𝒟` in a pre-triangulated category, indexed by a
cofiltered category `J`, is essentially constant as a pro-object (Stacks 05PU for `A.op`) if and
only if there are an index `i`, an object `X` and an inverse system `Z : Over i ⥤ 𝒟` on the
indices `j ≥ i` such that

* `A_j ≅ X ⊞ Z_j` naturally in `j ≥ i` — so the transition morphisms respect the decomposition
  and are the identity on `X` — and
* for every `j ≥ i` there are `j' ≥ j` and a transition morphism `Z_{j'} ⟶ Z_j` equal to zero.

The value of the essentially constant system is then `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEssentiallyConstant_op_iff_exists_iso_const_biprod [IsCofiltered J] (A : J ⥤ D) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd A.op ↔
      ∃ (i : J) (X : D) (Z : Over i ⥤ D)
        (_ : Over.forget i ⋙ A ≅ (Functor.const (Over i)).obj X ⊞ Z),
        ∀ j : Over i, ∃ (j' : Over i) (u : j' ⟶ j), Z.map u = 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.isEssentiallyConstant_op_π₂_and_exists_limit_triangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3A**. Let `T : J ⥤ Triangle 𝒟` be an inverse system of distinguished triangles
`A_j ⟶ B_j ⟶ C_j ⟶ A_j[1]` in a pre-triangulated category, indexed by a cofiltered category `J`.
If `(A_j)` and `(C_j)` are essentially constant as pro-objects (Stacks 05PU for the opposite
diagrams), then so is `(B_j)`, and there are an index `n`, a distinguished triangle
`S = (A ⟶ B ⟶ C ⟶ A[1])` of the values and a morphism of triangles `φ : T_n ⟶ S` which induces
an isomorphism `lim_{j ≥ n} A_j ⟶ A`, and similarly for `B` and `C`: for each of the three terms
there is a limit cone on the system restricted to the indices `j ≥ n` (the objects of `Over n`)
whose apex is that term of `S` and whose leg at `n` is split by the corresponding component of
`φ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEssentiallyConstant_op_π₂_and_exists_limit_triangle [IsCofiltered J]
    (T : J ⥤ Triangle D) (hT : ∀ j, T.obj j ∈ distTriang D)
    (h₁ : IsEssentiallyConstantInd (T ⋙ Triangle.π₁).op)
    (h₃ : IsEssentiallyConstantInd (T ⋙ Triangle.π₃).op) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd (T ⋙ Triangle.π₂).op ∧
      ∃ (n : J) (S : Triangle D) (_ : S ∈ distTriang D) (φ : T.obj n ⟶ S)
        (πA : (Functor.const (Over n)).obj S.obj₁ ⟶ Over.forget n ⋙ T ⋙ Triangle.π₁)
        (πB : (Functor.const (Over n)).obj S.obj₂ ⟶ Over.forget n ⋙ T ⋙ Triangle.π₂)
        (πC : (Functor.const (Over n)).obj S.obj₃ ⟶ Over.forget n ⋙ T ⋙ Triangle.π₃),
        (πA.app (Over.mk (𝟙 n)) ≫ φ.hom₁ = 𝟙 S.obj₁ ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ πA))) ∧
        (πB.app (Over.mk (𝟙 n)) ≫ φ.hom₂ = 𝟙 S.obj₂ ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ πB))) ∧
        (πC.app (Over.mk (𝟙 n)) ≫ φ.hom₃ = 𝟙 S.obj₃ ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ πC)))

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.isEssentiallyConstant_op_and_exists_limit_cone_of_homology
declarations.doc:
Let `A : J ⥤ D(𝒜)` be an inverse system in the derived category of an abelian category, indexed
by a cofiltered category `J`. Assume `H^i(A_j) = 0` for every `j` and every `i` outside an interval
`[a, b]`, and that each inverse system `(H^i(A_j))_j` of `𝒜` is essentially constant (Stacks 05PU
for the opposite diagram). Then `(A_j)` is essentially constant: besides
`IsEssentiallyConstantInd A.op`, there are an index `n`, an object `X`, a morphism `φ : A_n ⟶ X`
and a limit cone with apex `X` on the system restricted to the indices `j ≥ n` (the objects of
`Over n`) whose leg at `n` is split by `φ`; and for every `i` the image of that cone under `H^i` is
again a limit cone, i.e. `H^i(X)` is the value of the essentially constant system `(H^i(A_j))_j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEssentiallyConstant_op_and_exists_limit_cone_of_homology
    [IsCofiltered J] (A : J ⥤ DerivedCategory 𝒜) (a b : ℤ)
    (hA : ∀ (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i → ∀ j : J, IsZero ((homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).obj (A.obj j)))
    (hH : ∀ i : ℤ, IsEssentiallyConstantInd (A ⋙ homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).op) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd A.op ∧
      ∃ (n : J) (X : DerivedCategory 𝒜) (φ : A.obj n ⟶ X)
        (π : (Functor.const (Over n)).obj X ⟶ Over.forget n ⋙ A),
        π.app (Over.mk (𝟙 n)) ≫ φ = 𝟙 X ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X π)) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, Nonempty (IsLimit ((homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).mapCone (Cone.mk X π)))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_proInverse_mor₁_of_proZero_π₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3C**. Let `T : J ⥤ Triangle 𝒟` be an inverse system of distinguished triangles
`A_j ⟶ B_j ⟶ C_j ⟶ A_j[1]` in a pre-triangulated category, indexed by a cofiltered category `J`.
If the inverse system `(C_j)` of third terms is pro-zero, i.e. every index admits an arrow along
which the transition morphism of third terms vanishes, then the morphisms `A_j ⟶ B_j` determine
an isomorphism of pro-objects between `(A_j)` and `(B_j)`: for every index `j` there are an arrow
`f : k ⟶ j` and a morphism `s : B_k ⟶ A_j` such that `A_k ⟶ B_k ⟶ A_j` is the transition morphism
`A_k ⟶ A_j` and `B_k ⟶ A_j ⟶ B_j` is the transition morphism `B_k ⟶ B_j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_proInverse_mor₁_of_proZero_π₃ [IsCofiltered J]
    (T : J ⥤ Triangle D) (hT : ∀ j, T.obj j ∈ distTriang D)
    (h₃ : ∀ j : J, ∃ (k : J) (f : k ⟶ j), (T.map f).hom₃ = 0) (j : J) :
    ∃ (k : J) (f : k ⟶ j) (s : (T.obj k).obj₂ ⟶ (T.obj j).obj₁),
      (T.obj k).mor₁ ≫ s = (T.map f).hom₁ ∧ s ≫ (T.obj j).mor₁ = (T.map f).hom₂

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.exists_proInverse_of_proInverse_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3D**. Let `α : A ⟶ B` be an inverse system of maps `A_j ⟶ B_j` of the derived
category of an abelian category, indexed by a cofiltered category `J`. Assume `H^i(A_j) = 0` and
`H^i(B_j) = 0` for every `j` and every `i` outside an interval `[a, b]`, and that for every `i`
the maps `H^i(A_j) ⟶ H^i(B_j)` are an isomorphism of pro-objects of `𝒜`, i.e. every index `j`
admits an arrow `f : k ⟶ j` and a morphism `H^i(B_k) ⟶ H^i(A_j)` whose two round trips are the
transition morphisms. Then the maps `A_j ⟶ B_j` determine an isomorphism of pro-objects between
`(A_j)` and `(B_j)`: for every index `j` there are an arrow `f : k ⟶ j` and a morphism
`s : B_k ⟶ A_j` such that `A_k ⟶ B_k ⟶ A_j` is the transition morphism `A_k ⟶ A_j` and
`B_k ⟶ A_j ⟶ B_j` is the transition morphism `B_k ⟶ B_j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_proInverse_of_proInverse_homology [IsCofiltered J]
    {A B : J ⥤ DerivedCategory 𝒜} (α : A ⟶ B) (a b : ℤ)
    (hA : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → ∀ j : J, IsZero ((homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).obj (A.obj j)))
    (hB : ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → ∀ j : J, IsZero ((homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).obj (B.obj j)))
    (hH : ∀ (i : ℤ) (j : J), ∃ (k : J) (f : k ⟶ j)
      (s : (homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).obj (B.obj k) ⟶ (homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).obj (A.obj j)),
      (homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).map (α.app k) ≫ s = (homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).map (A.map f) ∧
        s ≫ (homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).map (α.app j) = (homologyFunctor 𝒜 i).map (B.map f))
    (j : J) :
    ∃ (k : J) (f : k ⟶ j) (s : B.obj k ⟶ A.obj j),
      α.app k ≫ s = A.map f ∧ s ≫ α.app j = B.map f

declarations.name: DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletion_isReflection
declarations.doc:
Derived completion with respect to a finitely generated ideal is the reflection into the
derived-complete objects: it takes derived-complete values, and its unit `K ⟶ K̂` induces a
bijection from maps out of `K̂` to maps out of `K` whenever the target is derived complete.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedCompletion_isReflection (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → A)
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))] :
    (∀ K, IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span (Set.range f))
      ((derivedCompletionFunctor A f).obj K)) ∧
    ∀ (K E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)),
      IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) E →
        Function.Bijective
          (fun g : (derivedCompletionFunctor A f).obj K ⟶ E ↦
            (derivedCompletionUnit A f).app K ≫ g)

declarations.name: PrincipalScaledVariable.scaledVariableCompletionCokernel_isDerivedComplete_not_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3F.** Let `p` be prime. The cokernel of the map between the `p`-adic
completions of `ℤ_[p][X]` induced by `X ↦ pX` is derived complete but not adically complete.
The image of `1 + pX + p²X² + ⋯` is a nonzero element belonging to every `p^n M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem scaledVariableCompletionCokernel_isDerivedComplete_not_isAdicComplete
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    let A := ℤ_[p]
    let I : Ideal A := Ideal.span {(p : A)}
    let φ : Polynomial A →ₗ[A] Polynomial A :=
      (Polynomial.aeval ((p : A) • Polynomial.X)).toLinearMap
    let φhat := AdicCompletion.map I φ
    let M := HasQuotient.Quotient (AdicCompletion I (Polynomial A))
      (LinearMap.range (φhat.restrictScalars A))
    letI : HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ModuleCat A) :=
      moduleCat_hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete A ℕ
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A M) ∧
      ¬ IsAdicComplete I M ∧
      ∃ z : AdicCompletion I (Polynomial A),
        (∀ n : ℕ, z.val n =
          Submodule.Quotient.mk
            (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (p : A) ^ i • (Polynomial.X : Polynomial A) ^ i)) ∧
        Submodule.Quotient.mk z ≠ (0 : M) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, Submodule.Quotient.mk z ∈ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)

declarations.name: PrincipalCompletionKernel.iInf_principal_powers_annihilates_ker_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3G.** Let `J` be the intersection of all powers of the principal ideal `(f)`.
If `M` is derived complete with respect to `f`, then `J` annihilates the kernel of the canonical
map from `M` to its `f`-adic completion. In particular, if `A` is derived complete with respect
to `f`, then `J` is square-zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iInf_principal_powers_annihilates_ker_adicCompletion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    let I := Ideal.span ({f} : Set A)
    let J := ⨅ n : ℕ, I ^ n
    (IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A M) →
      J • (AdicCompletion.of I M).ker = ⊥) ∧
    (IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A A) →
        J ^ 2 = ⊥)

declarations.name: PrincipalHenselianPair.henselianPair_of_isDerivedCompleteModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3H.** A commutative ring derived complete with respect to an ideal forms a
henselian pair with that ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_of_isDerivedCompleteModule
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_nat
    IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A A) → HenselianPair A I

declarations.name: PrincipalCompletionNilpotent.iInf_powers_pow_two_pow_eq_bot_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3I.** If a commutative ring is derived complete with respect to an ideal `I`
generated by `r` elements, then the `2 ^ r`-th power of the intersection of all powers of `I`
is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem iInf_powers_pow_two_pow_eq_bot_of_isDerivedComplete
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_nat
    IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A A) →
      (⨅ n : ℕ, I ^ n) ^ (2 ^ r) = ⊥

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.Homology.homologyIdealPowers_proIsomorphic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3K.** The homology of the complex of ideal powers is canonically
pro-isomorphic to the ideal powers of the homology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homologyIdealPowers_proIsomorphic
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {K : Type v} {L : Type w} {M : Type x}
    [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A K] [Module A L] [Module A M]
    [Module.Finite A K] [Module.Finite A L] [Module.Finite A M]
    (I : Ideal A) (α : K →ₗ[A] L) (β : L →ₗ[A] M)
    (_hβα : β.comp α = 0) :
    let P : ℕ → Submodule A L := fun n =>
      LinearMap.ker β ⊓ (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A L))
    let D : (n : ℕ) → Submodule A (P n) := fun n =>
      Submodule.comap (P n).subtype
        (Submodule.map α (I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A K)))
    let H : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => (P n) ⧸ D n
    let Q : ℕ → Type _ := fun n =>
      ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0)))
    ∃ (τ : ∀ (m n : ℕ), n ≤ m → H m →ₗ[A] H n),
      (∀ n, τ n n (le_refl n) = LinearMap.id) ∧
      (∀ (k m n : ℕ) (hkm : m ≤ k) (hmn : n ≤ m),
        (τ m n hmn).comp (τ k m hkm) = τ k n (hmn.trans hkm)) ∧
      (∀ (m n : ℕ) (hmn : n ≤ m) (y : P m),
        ∃ z : P n, z.1 = y.1 ∧
          τ m n hmn (Submodule.Quotient.mk y : H m) =
            (Submodule.Quotient.mk z : H n)) ∧
      ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧
        ∃ (ρ : ∀ (n : ℕ), c ≤ n → H n →ₗ[A]
              ↥(I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0))))
          (ψ : ∀ (n : ℕ), c ≤ n →
              ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0))) →ₗ[A] H (n - c)),
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : c ≤ n) (z : H n),
            ((ρ n hn z : ↥(I ^ (n - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0)))) : H 0) =
              τ n 0 (Nat.zero_le n) z) ∧
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : c ≤ n)
            (z : ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0)))) (y : P n),
            y.1 ∈ I ^ n • LinearMap.ker β →
            (z : H 0) = τ n 0 (Nat.zero_le n) (Submodule.Quotient.mk y : H n) →
            ψ n hn z = τ n (n - c) (Nat.sub_le n c)
              (Submodule.Quotient.mk y : H n)) ∧
          (∀ (m n : ℕ) (hmn : n ≤ m) (hm : c ≤ m) (hn : c ≤ n)
            (z : ↥(I ^ m • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0))))
            (z' : ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0)))),
            (z' : H 0) = z →
            τ (m - c) (n - c) (Nat.sub_le_sub_right hmn c) (ψ m hm z) =
              ψ n hn z') ∧
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 * c ≤ n)
            (z : ↥(I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0)))),
            (((ρ (n - c) (by omega) (ψ n (by omega) z) :
                ↥(I ^ ((n - c) - c) • (⊤ : Submodule A (H 0)))) : H 0) = z.1)) ∧
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 * c ≤ n) (z : H n),
            ψ (n - c) (by omega) (ρ n (by omega) z) =
              τ n ((n - c) - c) (by omega) z) ∧
          -- The standard explicit witness that the two inverse systems are
          -- isomorphic as pro-objects, using the cofinal shift `n ↦ n + c`.
          ∃ (forward : ∀ m : ℕ, H (m + c) →ₗ[A] Q m)
              (backward : ∀ m : ℕ, Q (m + c) →ₗ[A] H m),
            (∀ (m m' : ℕ) (h : m ≤ m') (z : H (m' + c)),
              ((forward m (τ (m' + c) (m + c) (by omega) z) : Q m) : H 0) =
                (forward m' z : H 0)) ∧
            (∀ (m m' : ℕ) (h : m ≤ m') (z : Q (m' + c)) (z' : Q (m + c)),
              (z' : H 0) = z →
                backward m z' = τ m' m h (backward m' z)) ∧
            (∀ (m : ℕ) (z : H ((m + c) + c)),
              backward m (forward (m + c) z) =
                τ ((m + c) + c) m (by omega) z) ∧
            (∀ (m : ℕ) (z : Q ((m + c) + c)),
              ((forward m (backward (m + c) z) : Q m) : H 0) = z)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.ExtIdealPowerRestriction.ext_ideal_power_restriction_factors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G3L.** Restriction on positive-degree Ext from a finite module to a sufficiently
high ideal power factors through Ext into a shifted ideal power of the second module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ext_ideal_power_restriction_factors
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Small.{v} A]
    {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A M]
    (I : Ideal A) (p : ℕ) (_hp : 0 < p) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
      let P : Submodule A M := I ^ n • ⊤
      let Q : Submodule A N := I ^ (n - c) • ⊤
      ∃ lift : Ext (ModuleCat.of A M) (ModuleCat.of A N) p →+
          Ext (ModuleCat.of A P) (ModuleCat.of A Q) p,
        ((Ext.mk₀ (ModuleCat.ofHom Q.subtype)).postcomp
            (ModuleCat.of A P) (add_zero p)).comp lift =
          (Ext.mk₀ (ModuleCat.ofHom P.subtype)).precomp
            (ModuleCat.of A N) (zero_add p)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.KoszulIdealPower.idealPowerSystem_proIso_koszulIdealComplexSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G3M.** Over a Noetherian ring, the inverse system of positive
powers of the ideal generated by a finite sequence and the inverse system of shifted,
positive-degree Koszul complexes on its positive powers are pro-isomorphic in the derived
category. The comparison is induced by the Koszul differential into the corresponding ideal
power; the displayed identities express a two-sided inverse after cofinal refinement.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idealPowerSystem_proIso_koszulIdealComplexSystem
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) :
    let I := Ideal.span (Set.range f)
    ∃ (ε : ∀ n : ℕ,
        koszulIdealComplex (fun i ↦ f i ^ (n + 1)) ⟶
          (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A ↥(I ^ (n + 1))))
      (e : koszulIdealComplexSystem f ⟶ idealPowerSystem I),
      (∀ n,
        (ε n).f 0 ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (I ^ (n + 1)).subtype =
          (koszulIdealComplexXIso (fun i ↦ f i ^ (n + 1)) 0).hom ≫
            (Koszul.seqComplex (fun i ↦ f i ^ (n + 1))).d 1 0 ≫
            ModuleCat.ofHom
              (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv A (Fin r → A)).toLinearMap) ∧
      (∀ n,
        e.app (op n) = DerivedCategory.Q.map
          (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (ε n) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m)
        (s : (idealPowerSystem I).obj (op m) ⟶
          (koszulIdealComplexSystem f).obj (op n)),
        e.app (op m) ≫ s =
            (koszulIdealComplexSystem f).map (homOfLE h).op ∧
          s ≫ e.app (op n) =
            (idealPowerSystem I).map (homOfLE h).op

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.IdealPowerTensorComparison.derivedTensor_idealPowers_proIsomorphic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G3N.** For a bounded complex of finite modules over a Noetherian
ring, the inverse system of maps `Iⁿ ⊗ᴸ M → Iⁿ M` formed from the canonical derived tensor
product is an isomorphism of pro-objects in the derived category. The displayed identities are
the two-sided inverse identities after cofinal refinement.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensor_idealPowers_proIsomorphic {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (M.X i))
    (hfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i)) :
    ∃ (t : ∀ n, idealPowerComplex M I (n + 1) ⟶ idealPowerComplex M I n)
      (_ht : ∀ n, t n ≫ image.ι (idealPowerMultiplication M I n) =
        image.ι (idealPowerMultiplication M I (n + 1)))
      (α : derivedTensorIdealSystem (DerivedTensorData.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A)
          (DerivedTensorData.canonicalSymmetry A) M I ⟶ idealPowerSystem M I t),
      (∀ n, α.app (op n) = derivedToIdealPowerMap
        (DerivedTensorData.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A)
        (DerivedTensorData.canonicalSymmetry A) M I n) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m)
        (s : (idealPowerSystem M I t).obj (op m) ⟶
          (derivedTensorIdealSystem (DerivedTensorData.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A)
            (DerivedTensorData.canonicalSymmetry A) M I).obj (op n)),
        α.app (op m) ≫ s =
            (derivedTensorIdealSystem (DerivedTensorData.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A)
              (DerivedTensorData.canonicalSymmetry A) M I).map (homOfLE h).op ∧
          s ≫ α.app (op n) = (idealPowerSystem M I t).map (homOfLE h).op

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PrincipalParts.principalPartsSheafification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G3U**, which read as a statement about the sheaf of principal parts
is **Tag 09CV**. Let `φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂` be a morphism of presheaves of
commutative rings on a site and let `F` be a presheaf of `O₂`-modules. Then the sheaf of
principal parts of order `k` of `F^#` relative to `O₂^# / O₁^#` is the sheaf associated to
the presheaf `X ↦ Pᵏ_{O₂(X)/O₁(X)}(F X)` of sectionwise modules of principal parts, and the
sectionwise universal operators are compatible with restriction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def principalPartsSheafification [HasWeakSheafify J CommRingCat.{u}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective CommRingCat.{u}]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u u₁ v₁ v}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u u₁ v₁ v}] {O₁ O₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}}
    (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{max u u₁ v₁ v} (O₂ ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}))
    (k : ℕ) :
    Σ' P : PresheafOfModules.{max u u₁ v₁ v}
        (O₂ ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}),
      Σ' D : F.presheaf ⟶ P.presheaf,
        Σ' _e : (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialOperatorsFunctor.{v₁, u₁, u,
            max u u₁ v₁ v}
            ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
              (associatedCommRingSheafMap J φ))
            ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂)).obj F)
            k).coreprX (hF :=
              AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialOperatorsFunctor_isCorepresentable
                ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
                  (associatedCommRingSheafMap J φ))
                ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂)).obj F) k) ≅
          (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂)).obj P,
        ∀ X : Cᵒᵖ,
          letI : Algebra (O₁.obj X) (O₂.obj X) := (φ.app X).hom.toAlgebra
          letI : Module (O₁.obj X) (F.obj X) :=
            Module.compHom (F.obj X) (φ.app X).hom
          letI : Module (O₁.obj X) (P.obj X) :=
            Module.compHom (P.obj X) (φ.app X).hom
          letI : IsScalarTower (O₁.obj X) (O₂.obj X) (F.obj X) :=
            IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
          letI : IsScalarTower (O₁.obj X) (O₂.obj X) (P.obj X) :=
            IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
          ∃ d : F.obj X →ₗ[O₁.obj X] P.obj X,
            (∀ x, d x = (D.app X).hom x) ∧
              d.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE (O₂.obj X) k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.nonempty_principalPartsSequence_opens
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G3V.** For a homomorphism `φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂` of sheaves of commutative
rings on a topological space, the sheaves of first principal parts of the sheaves of
`O₂`-modules assemble into a functor sitting in a short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ Ω_{O₂/O₁} ⊗_{O₂} F ⟶ P¹_{O₂/O₁}(F) ⟶ F ⟶ 0`

natural in `F`, with its two arrows determined by their values on universal differential
operators.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomEvaluation_isIso_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G40.** Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space and let `K`, `L`, `M` be objects of
`D(O_X)` with `K` perfect. The evaluation morphism

`RSheafHom(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_X} K ⟶ RSheafHom(RSheafHom(K, L), M)`

of Stacks 0A8U is an isomorphism, for every `L` and `M`.

This reads off the ringed-site statement

of the space, for the canonical derived tensor product and the derived internal Hom of the ringed
space; the two notions of perfection agree because the predicate used here *is* the site-level
one of Stacks 08G5.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomEvaluation_isIso_of_isPerfect
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    (hK : (ringedSite Rc).IsPerfect K) :
    IsIso (derivedSheafHomEvaluation Rc K L M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isUniversallyCatenary_iff_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme is universally catenary if and only if its reduced
irreducible components are universally catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_iff_irreducibleComponents
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    IsUniversallyCatenary S ↔
      ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents S,
        let I : S.IdealSheafData := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
          ⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩
        let : IsLocallyNoetherian I.subscheme :=
          LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian I.subschemeι
        IsUniversallyCatenary I.subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineDiffOp.globalDiffOpEquiv
declarations.doc:
On an affine scheme, taking global sections gives a bijection from differential operators
of order at most `k` between sheaves to differential operators of order at most `k` between the
corresponding modules. The source sheaf is required to be quasi-coherent; the target sheaf is
arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def globalDiffOpEquiv
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (F G : (Spec (.of A)).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (k : ℕ) :
    letI _modAF : Module A Γ(F, ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom _ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom
    letI _modAG : Module A Γ(G, ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom _ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom
    letI _modRF : Module R Γ(F, ⊤) := Module.compHom _ (algebraMap R A)
    letI _modRG : Module R Γ(G, ⊤) := Module.compHom _ (algebraMap R A)
    letI _towerF : IsScalarTower R A Γ(F, ⊤) := IsScalarTower.of_compHom R A _
    letI _towerG : IsScalarTower R A Γ(G, ⊤) := IsScalarTower.of_compHom R A _
    {e :
      {D : DiffOp.GlobalOp F G //
        DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeStructureSheafMap
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R A)))) k D} ≃
        {D : Γ(F, ⊤) →ₗ[R] Γ(G, ⊤) //
          D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE A k} //
      ∀ D x, (e D).1 x = D.1 (.op ⊤) x}

declarations.name: Stacks.FibreProductAffineChart.Chart.diffOpEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Differential operators on an affine chart of a fibre product.** The differential operators
of order at most `k` on `X ×_S Y / Y` between two modules on `X ×_S Y`, defined over the opens
contained in a chart, are the differential operators of order at most `k` relative to
`Γ(Y, V) ⟶ Γ(X, U) ⊗_{Γ(S, W)} Γ(Y, V)` between the two modules of sections on the chart.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def diffOpEquiv (M M' : (pullback a b).Modules)
    [(Scheme.Modules.restrict M ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι)).IsQuasicoherent] (k : ℕ) :
    letI _modAF : Module (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right))
        Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom _ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso
        (.of (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right)))).inv.hom
    letI _modAG : Module (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right))
        Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M' ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom _ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso
        (.of (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right)))).inv.hom
    letI _modRF : Module Γ(Y, c.right)
        Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(Y, c.right)
        (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right)))
    letI _modRG : Module Γ(Y, c.right)
        Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M' ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(Y, c.right)
        (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right)))
    letI _towerF : IsScalarTower Γ(Y, c.right) (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right))
        Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) :=
      IsScalarTower.of_compHom _ _ _
    letI _towerG : IsScalarTower Γ(Y, c.right) (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right))
        Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M' ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) :=
      IsScalarTower.of_compHom _ _ _
    {D : DiffOp.RawOp M M' c.ι.opensRange //
        DiffOp.IsDiffOpOfOrder (pullback.snd a b).relativeStructureSheafMap k D} ≃
      {D : Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) →ₗ[Γ(Y, c.right)]
          Γ(Scheme.Modules.restrict M' ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι), ⊤) //
        D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE
          (Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right)) k}
declarations.comment: the affine-chart reduction step of the proof: over an affine chart of `X ×_S Y`, the differential operators of order at most `k` on `X ×_S Y / Y` are the differential operators of order at most `k` relative to `B ⟶ A ⊗_R B` on the chart's sections. Neither the construction of `D'` nor its characterisation on pure tensors is included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.globalDiffOp_ext_of_chart_sections
declarations.doc:
**A differential operator on a fibre product is determined by its action on the affine
charts.** Two differential operators of order at most `k` on `X ×_S Y / Y`, out of a
quasi-coherent module, which agree on the sections over every affine chart of `X ×_S Y`, are
equal.
declarations.statement:
theorem globalDiffOp_ext_of_chart_sections {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S) (b : Y ⟶ S) (k : ℕ)
    {M M' : (pullback a b).Modules} [M.IsQuasicoherent] (D E : DiffOp.GlobalOp M M')
    (hD : DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder (pullback.snd a b).relativeStructureSheafMap k D)
    (hE : DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder (pullback.snd a b).relativeStructureSheafMap k E)
    (hagree : ∀ (c : Chart a b) (s : Γ(M, c.ι.opensRange)),
      D (op c.ι.opensRange) s = E (op c.ι.opensRange) s) :
    D = E
declarations.comment: the local-global step of the proof: a differential operator of order at most `k` on `X ×_S Y / Y` out of a quasi-coherent module is determined by its action on the sections over the affine charts. This is not the uniqueness clause of the tag, which is uniqueness among the operators satisfying the characterisation on pure tensors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_globalDiffOp_externalTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Base change of a differential operator.** Let `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` be morphisms of
schemes, let `F`, `F'` be quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module
and let `D : F ⟶ F'` be a differential operator of order at most `k` on `X/S`. There is a unique
differential operator of order at most `k` on `X ×_S Y / Y` from `pr₁^*F ⊗ pr₂^*G` to
`pr₁^*F' ⊗ pr₂^*G` which carries, for all local sections `s` of `F` and `t` of `G`, the section
attached to `s` and `t` to the section attached to `D s` and `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_globalDiffOp_externalTensorProduct {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ S)
    (b : Y ⟶ S) (F F' : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F'.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (k : ℕ)
    (D : DiffOp.GlobalOp F F')
    (hD : DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder a.relativeStructureSheafMap k D) :
    ∃! E : DiffOp.GlobalOp (externalTensorProduct a b F G) (externalTensorProduct a b F' G),
      DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder (pullback.snd a b).relativeStructureSheafMap k E ∧
        ∀ (U' : X.Opens) (V' : Y.Opens) (s : Γ(F, U')) (t : Γ(G, V'))
          (W : (pullback a b).Opens) (hW₁ : W ≤ pullback.fst a b ⁻¹ᵁ U')
          (hW₂ : W ≤ pullback.snd a b ⁻¹ᵁ V'),
          E (op W) (externalTensorSection a b F G s t W hW₁ hW₂) =
            externalTensorSection a b F' G (D (op U') s) t W hW₁ hW₂

declarations.name: Stacks.FibreProductAffineChart.Chart.existsUnique_boxDiffOp
declarations.doc:
**The affine-chart base change of a differential operator (Tag 0G45 on a chart).** Let
`D : F ⟶ F'` be a differential operator of order at most `k` on `X/S` between quasi-coherent
modules and let `G` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Y`-module. Over the opens of an affine chart of
`X ×_S Y` there is exactly one differential operator of order at most `k` on `X ×_S Y / Y` from
`F ⊠ G` to `F' ⊠ G` which, read through the identification of the sections of a box product on the
chart with `Γ(Spec Γ(X, U), F) ⊗_{Γ(S, W)} Γ(Spec Γ(Y, V), G)`, carries `s ⊗ t` to `D s ⊗ t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_boxDiffOp (F' : X.Modules) [F'.IsQuasicoherent] (k : ℕ)
    (D : DiffOp.GlobalOp F F')
    (hD : DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder a.relativeStructureSheafMap k D) :
    ∃! E : {E : DiffOp.RawOp (externalTensorProduct a b F G) (externalTensorProduct a b F' G)
          c.ι.opensRange //
        DiffOp.IsDiffOpOfOrder (pullback.snd a b).relativeStructureSheafMap k E},
      ∀ (s : Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback c.fromSpecLeft).obj F, ⊤))
        (t : Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback c.fromSpecRight).obj G, ⊤)),
        (c.boxDiffOpTensorEquiv hl hr F G F' k E).1 (s ⊗ₜ[Γ(S, c.base)] t) =
          (c.leftDiffOpEquiv hl F F' k
              ⟨D.restrict c.fromSpecLeft.opensRange, hD c.fromSpecLeft.opensRange⟩).1 s
            ⊗ₜ[Γ(S, c.base)] t
declarations.comment: the affine-chart step of the construction of `D'`: over ONE affine chart of `X ×_S Y` this gives the existence of `D'`, its order bound, its characterisation on pure tensors and its uniqueness, all read through the identification of the sections of `F ⊠ G` on the chart with `Γ(Spec A, F) ⊗_R Γ(Spec B, G)`. The global operator on `X ×_S Y` is NOT constructed: the chart-wise operators are not glued, and the characterisation is not expressed on the sections of `F ⊠ G` attached to a pair of local sections of `F` and of `G`

declarations.name: Stacks.FibreProductAffineChart.Chart.boxHom_boxSectionOfTensor
declarations.doc:
**The affine description of the box product on morphisms.** Read on the sections of `F ⊠ G`
over the image of a chart, through the identification of those sections with
`Γ(Spec A, F) ⊗_R Γ(Spec B, G)`, the operator `D ⊠ E` is the tensor product `D ⊗ E` of the
operator attached to `D` on `Γ(Spec A, F)` and the operator attached to `E` on
`Γ(Spec B, G)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem boxHom_boxSectionOfTensor
    (z : Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback c.fromSpecLeft).obj F.module, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)]
      Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback c.fromSpecRight).obj G.module, ⊤)) :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.boxHom D E).1
        (op (((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι) ''ᵁ ⊤))
        (c.boxSectionOfTensor hl hr F.module G.module z) =
      c.boxSectionOfTensor hl hr F'.module G'.module
        (TensorProduct.map
          (c.leftDiffOpEquiv hl F.module F'.module k
            ⟨D.1.restrict c.fromSpecLeft.opensRange, hD c.fromSpecLeft.opensRange⟩).1
          (c.rightDiffOpEquiv hr G.module G'.module l
            ⟨E.1.restrict c.fromSpecRight.opensRange, hE c.fromSpecRight.opensRange⟩).1 z)
declarations.comment: the MORPHISM half of the affine description of the remark: on an affine chart of `X ×_S Y`, and so in particular for `X = Spec A`, `Y = Spec B`, `S = Spec R` and the chart whose three opens are everything, the operator `D ⊠ E` read on the sections of `F ⊠ G` through the identification of those sections with `M ⊗_R N` is `D ⊗ E`. Carries a chosen order bound for each of the two operators (`hD`, `hE`), which exists for every morphism of the category. The OBJECT half `(M, N) ↦ M ⊗_R N` is `Chart.boxSectionsEquiv`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.boxHom_add_left
declarations.doc: **The box product is additive in its first argument.**
declarations.comment: half of the bilinearity on morphisms asserted by the remark: the box product `D ⊠ E` is additive in the operator `D` on `X/S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.boxHom_add_right
declarations.doc: **The box product is additive in its second argument.**
declarations.comment: the other half of the bilinearity on morphisms asserted by the remark: the box product `D ⊠ E` is additive in the operator `E` on `Y/S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.boxProductFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The box-product bifunctor of [Stacks, Tag 0G46].** The external tensor product on objects
and the box product of two differential operators on morphisms form a functor from the product
of the categories of finite-order differential operators on `X/S` and on `Y/S` to the category
of finite-order differential operators on `X ×_S Y / S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boxProductFunctor (a : X ⟶ S) (b : Y ⟶ S) :
    FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory a × FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory b ⥤
      FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory (pullback.fst a b ≫ a)
declarations.comment: the box product bifunctor of the remark: `(F, G) ↦ F ⊠ G` on objects and `(D, E) ↦ D ⊠ E` on morphisms, with both functor laws. NOT the notation `F ⊠ G`, and NOT the affine description `(M, N) ↦ M ⊗_R N`, `(D, D') ↦ D ⊗ D'`, which is covered by `Chart.boxSectionsEquiv` and `Chart.boxHom_boxSectionOfTensor`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.boxHom
declarations.doc:
**The box product `D ⊠ E` of two finite-order differential operators.** For morphisms
`D : F ⟶ F'` of the category of finite-order differential operators on `X/S` and `E : G ⟶ G'` of
the category on `Y/S`, the composite `(1 ⊠ E) ∘ (D ⊠ 1) : F ⊠ G ⟶ F' ⊠ G'` of the category of
finite-order differential operators on `X ×_S Y / S`.
declarations.comment: the assignment on morphisms of the box product of the remark: for `D : F ⟶ F'` on `X/S` and `E : G ⟶ G'` on `Y/S` the operator `D ⊠ E = (1 ⊠ E) ∘ (D ⊠ 1)`, a morphism `F ⊠ G ⟶ F' ⊠ G'` of the category of finite-order differential operators on `X ×_S Y / S`. The FUNCTOR of the remark is not constructed HERE: `map_id`, `map_comp` and the bilinearity on morphisms are proved in `BoxProductFunctor`, and the affine description `(M, N) ↦ M ⊗_R N`, `(D, D') ↦ D ⊗ D'` in `BoxProductAffineDescription`

declarations.name: Stacks.FibreProductAffineChart.Chart.boxSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The sections of a box product on a chart.** The module of sections of `F ⊠ G` on a chart is
the tensor product over `Γ(S, W)` of the sections of `F` on `Spec Γ(X, U)` and of `G` on
`Spec Γ(Y, V)`, linearly over `Γ(X, U) ⊗_{Γ(S, W)} Γ(Y, V)`, which acts on the tensor product by
`(f ⊗ g) • (s ⊗ t) = (f • s) ⊗ (g • t)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def boxSectionsEquiv :
    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback ((c.specIso hl hr).inv ≫ c.ι)).obj
        (externalTensorProduct a b F G), ⊤)
      ≃ₗ[Γ(X, c.left) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)] Γ(Y, c.right)]
      (Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback c.fromSpecLeft).obj F, ⊤) ⊗[Γ(S, c.base)]
        Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback c.fromSpecRight).obj G, ⊤))
declarations.comment: the OBJECT half of the affine description of the remark: on an affine chart of `X ×_S Y`, and so in particular for `X = Spec A`, `Y = Spec B`, `S = Spec R` and the chart whose three opens are everything, the module of sections of `F ⊠ G` is `M ⊗_R N`, linearly over the ring `A ⊗_R B` of the chart. NOT the morphism half `(D, D') ↦ D ⊗ D'`, which is `Chart.boxHom_boxSectionOfTensor`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.externalTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
The external tensor product of an `O_X`-module and an `O_Y`-module on the fibre
product of two schemes `X` and `Y` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev externalTensorProduct {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) : (pullback f g).Modules
declarations.comment: external_tensor_product_of_modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module, regarded as an object of the category of finite-order
differential operators on `X/S`.
declarations.statement: structure FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory (a : X ⟶ S)
declarations.comment: category_of_finite_order_differential_operators

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.Hom
declarations.doc: Morphisms in the category of finite-order differential operators.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev Hom (F G : FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory a)
declarations.comment: category_of_finite_order_differential_operators

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.instCategory
declarations.doc:
Composition of finite-order differential operators makes quasi-coherent modules
into a category.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instCategory :
    Category (FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory a)
declarations.comment: category_of_finite_order_differential_operators

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.instPreadditive
declarations.doc:
The pointwise addition of finite-order differential operators is compatible with
composition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instPreadditive :
    Preadditive (FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory a)
declarations.comment: category_of_finite_order_differential_operators

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.divisor
declarations.doc:
**The divisor `H_w = Z(ψ(w))`** cut out on `X` by a vector of the linear system, as a
quasi-coherent ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement: def divisor (w : D.V) : D.X.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the divisor of a vector of the linear system

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G47.** The standing situation of the Bertini theorems: a field `k`,
a scheme `X` over `k`, an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L`, a finite dimensional `k`-vector space
`V` with a chosen basis `v₁, …, v_r`, and a `k`-linear map `ψ : V → Γ(X, L)`.
declarations.statement: structure FamilyDivisors
declarations.comment: the standing situation

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.universalSection
declarations.doc:
**The universal section** `s_univ = Σᵢ xᵢ ψ(vᵢ)` of `pr₂^* L` on `𝔸^r_k ×_k X`, where
`x₁, …, x_r` are the coordinates of the parameter affine space.
declarations.statement:
def universalSection :
    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback D.parameterProjection).obj D.L, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the universal section

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.universalDivisor
declarations.doc:
**The universal divisor** `H_univ = Z(s_univ) ⊂ 𝔸^r_k ×_k X`, the zero scheme of the
universal section.
declarations.statement: def universalDivisor : D.parameterSpace.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the universal divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.specializedSection
declarations.doc:
**The section `ψ(v) = Σᵢ aᵢ ψ(vᵢ)`** of `L|_{X_{k'}}` attached to the vector
`v = Σᵢ aᵢ vᵢ` of `V ⊗_k k'` with coordinate tuple `a` over a field extension `k'/k`.
declarations.statement:
def specializedSection (a : Fin (Module.finrank D.k D.V) → K) :
    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.baseChangeToX K)).obj D.L, ⊤)
declarations.comment: the section attached to a vector over an extension field

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.specializedDivisor
declarations.doc:
**The divisor `H_v = Z(ψ(v))`** on `X_{k'}` attached to the vector of `V ⊗_k k'` with
coordinate tuple `a`, as the zero scheme of the section it determines.
declarations.statement:
def specializedDivisor (a : Fin (Module.finrank D.k D.V) → K) :
    (D.baseChange K).IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the divisor attached to a vector over an extension field

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.specializedDivisor_eq_comap
declarations.doc:
**`H_v = H_{univ, v}`.** The divisor attached to a vector of `V ⊗_k k'` is the fibre of
the universal divisor over the corresponding `k'`-point of `𝔸^r_k`, as quasi-coherent sheaves
of ideals on `X_{k'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem specializedDivisor_eq_comap (a : Fin (Module.finrank D.k D.V) → K) :
    D.specializedDivisor K a = D.universalDivisor.comap (D.fibreParameterMap K a)
declarations.comment: the fibre of the universal divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.ForGeneral
declarations.doc:
**A property of vectors holds for general `v`** when there is one nonempty open
`U ⊂ 𝔸^r_k` such that `P` holds at every vector of `V ⊗_k k'` whose coordinate tuple gives a
`k'`-point of `U`, for every field extension `k'/k`.
declarations.statement:
def ForGeneral
    (P : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra D.k K], TensorProduct D.k D.V K → Prop) : Prop
declarations.comment: holding for general vectors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.essSurj_coherentDerivedBoundedRestrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G48].** On a Noetherian scheme, restriction to an open subscheme is
essentially surjective as a functor `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D^b_Coh(𝒪_U)`: every bounded complex of
`𝒪_U`-modules with coherent cohomology is the restriction of one on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essSurj_coherentDerivedBoundedRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (U : X.Opens) :
    (coherentDerivedBoundedRestrict U).EssSurj

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical
declarations.doc:
**The global Künneth map for two module sheaves at the canonical global cup product.**

`RΓ(X, ℱ) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, 𝒢) ⟶ RΓ(W, p^*ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_W} q^*𝒢)`

in `D(A)` for `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`, where `p ≫ a = f = q ≫ b`; the source takes `W = X ×_S Y` with
its two projections.  It is `Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethMapOfSheaves` at the
canonical global cup product of Section 0FKU.
declarations.statement:
def kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical (F : Modules X.sheaf) (G : Modules Y.sheaf) :
    ((tensorBase S).obj ((sectionsOverBase a).obj (singleD F))).obj
        ((sectionsOverBase b).obj (singleD G)) ⟶
      (sectionsOverBase f).obj
        (singleD (sheafTensorObj ((modulePullback p).obj F) ((modulePullback q).obj G)))
declarations.comment: the map, at the A-linear global cup product `globalCupProductCanonical` of Section 0FKU on the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical_eq_kunnethGlobalMapCanonical
declarations.doc:
The Künneth map for two module sheaves at the canonical global cup product is the derived
Künneth map `kunnethGlobalMapCanonical` at the two sheaves placed in degree zero, followed by
derived global sections of the canonical comparison from the derived tensor product of the derived
pullbacks to the ordinary tensor product of the ordinary pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical_eq_kunnethGlobalMapCanonical (F : Modules X.sheaf)
    (G : Modules Y.sheaf) :
    kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical a b p q f hp hq F G =
      kunnethGlobalMapCanonical a b p q f hp hq (singleD F) (singleD G) ≫
        (sectionsOverBase f).map (externalTensorComparison p q F G)
declarations.comment: the map is the derived map at the sheaves in degree zero: both sides are at the canonical global cup product, the right-hand side being `kunnethGlobalMapCanonical` of Tag 0G7V

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical_naturality_derived
declarations.doc:
The derived Künneth map `kunnethGlobalMapCanonical` at sheaves placed in degree zero, the
first factor of `kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical`, is natural in the two sheaves `ℱ` and `𝒢`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethMapOfSheavesCanonical_naturality_derived
    {F F' : Modules X.sheaf} {G G' : Modules Y.sheaf} (φ : F ⟶ F') (ψ : G ⟶ G') :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
          ((sectionsOverBase a).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules X.sheaf) 0).map φ)) ×ₘ
            (sectionsOverBase b).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y.sheaf) 0).map ψ))) ≫
        kunnethGlobalMapCanonical a b p q f hp hq (singleD F') (singleD G') =
      kunnethGlobalMapCanonical a b p q f hp hq (singleD F) (singleD G) ≫
        (sectionsOverBase f).map
          ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
            ((derivedPullback p).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
                ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules X.sheaf) 0).map φ)) ×ₘ
              (derivedPullback q).map (DerivedCategory.Q.map
                ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (Modules Y.sheaf) 0).map ψ))))
declarations.comment: naturality inherited from the derived map, at the canonical global cup product

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethMapOfSheavesSchemeCanonical
declarations.doc:
**The global Künneth map at the fibre product of two schemes, at the canonical global cup
product.** For schemes `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` over a base, `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`, an
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` and an `𝒪_Y`-module `𝒢`, the canonical map

`RΓ(X, ℱ) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, 𝒢) ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Y, p^*ℱ ⊗_{𝒪_{X ×_S Y}} q^*𝒢)`

in `D(A)`, where `p` and `q` are the two projections of `X ×_S Y` and the target is the external
tensor product of Tag 0G46 placed in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
def kunnethMapOfSheavesSchemeCanonical (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) :
    ((tensorBase S.toRingedSpace).obj
          ((sectionsOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (singleD F))).obj
        ((sectionsOverBase b.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (singleD G)) ⟶
      (sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (singleD (externalTensorProduct a b F G))
declarations.comment: the map at X ×_S Y, at the global cup product `globalCupProductCanonical` on the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethMapOfSheavesSchemeCanonical_eq_kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical
declarations.doc:
At the fibre product of two schemes, the Künneth map for two module sheaves at the canonical
global cup product is the derived Künneth map `kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical` at the two sheaves
placed in degree zero, followed by derived global sections of `externalTensorComparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethMapOfSheavesSchemeCanonical_eq_kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) :
    kunnethMapOfSheavesSchemeCanonical a b F G =
      kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical a b (singleD F) (singleD G) ≫
        (sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).map
          (externalTensorComparison (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom
            (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom F G)
declarations.comment: the map at the fibre product is the derived map at the sheaves in degree zero: both sides are at the canonical global cup product, the right-hand side being `kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical` of Tag 0G7V

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxProductObj_module
declarations.doc:
**`𝓕 ⊠ 𝓖 = p^*𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_{X ×_S Y}} q^*𝓖`**, the definition [Stacks, Section 0G4A] opens with:
the tensor product, on `X ×_S Y`, of the two pullbacks along the projections.  The tensor product
is the **nonderived** one, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorStalkRingedSpace.tensorSheaf`; the
section says explicitly that, contrary to a later section, the nonderived product is meant.
declarations.statement:
theorem boxProductObj_module (F : FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory a)
    (G : FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory b) :
    (boxProductObj F G).module =
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨(((pullback a b).toRingedSpace)).presheaf, (((pullback a b).toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj
            (((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst a b)).obj F.module))).obj
        (((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd a b)).obj G.module)))
declarations.comment: the display `F ⊠ G = p^*F ⊗_{O_{X ×_S Y}} q^*G` that opens the section, including that the tensor product is the nonderived one; the bifunctoriality of `⊠` is Tag 0G46, `AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory.boxProductFunctor`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxDoubleComplex
declarations.doc:
**The double complex `𝓕^i ⊠ 𝓖^j` of [Stacks, Section 0G4A]**: the bicomplex obtained by
applying the box product of [Stacks, Tag 0G46] to two `ℤ`-indexed complexes of quasi-coherent
modules with finite-order differential operators as differentials, by the construction of
[Stacks, Tag 0A5J].  Its horizontal differential is `d_1 = d_𝓕 ⊠ 1` and its vertical one is
`d_2 = 1 ⊠ d_𝓖`; both are morphisms of the category of finite-order differential operators on
`X ×_S Y / S`, which is the section's assertion that the maps of the diagram are differential
operators of finite order there.
declarations.statement:
abbrev boxDoubleComplex :
    HomologicalComplex₂ (FiniteOrderDifferentialOperatorCategory (pullback.fst a b ≫ a))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
declarations.comment: the double complex displayed in the section: the bicomplex `(i, j) ↦ F^i ⊠ G^j` of finite-order differential operators on `X ×_S Y / S`. No boundedness is needed for the double complex itself; its total complex, `Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotal`, needs both factors strictly bounded below

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxDoubleComplex_X_X
declarations.doc: **The term of the double complex in degree `(i, j)` is `𝓕^i ⊠ 𝓖^j`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem boxDoubleComplex_X_X (i j : ℤ) :
    ((boxDoubleComplex a b K L).X i).X j = boxProductObj (K.X i) (L.X j)
declarations.comment: the entries of the displayed double complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxDoubleComplex_d_f
declarations.doc:
**The horizontal differential of the double complex is `d_1^{i, j} = d^i_𝓕 ⊠ 1`**, the first
of the two formulas written out in [Stacks, Section 0G4A].  There is no sign: the signs of
[Stacks, Tag 012Z] enter only in the total complex, where
`Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotal_d` records them.
declarations.statement:
theorem boxDoubleComplex_d_f (i i' j : ℤ) :
    ((boxDoubleComplex a b K L).d i i').f j = boxHom (K.d i i') (𝟙 (L.X j))
declarations.comment: the display `d_1^{i, j} = d^i_F ⊠ 1`, the horizontal differential of the double complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxDoubleComplex_X_d
declarations.doc:
**The vertical differential of the double complex is `d_2^{i, j} = 1 ⊠ d^j_𝓖`**, the second
of the two formulas written out in [Stacks, Section 0G4A], again with no sign.
declarations.statement:
theorem boxDoubleComplex_X_d (i j j' : ℤ) :
    ((boxDoubleComplex a b K L).X i).d j j' = boxHom (𝟙 (K.X i)) (L.d j j')
declarations.comment: the display `d_2^{i, j} = 1 ⊠ d^j_G`, the vertical differential of the double complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxDoubleComplex_comm
declarations.doc:
**The squares of the diagram displayed in [Stacks, Section 0G4A] commute**: boxing with the
identity in one variable is natural in the other, so `(1 ⊠ d_𝓖) ∘ (d_𝓕 ⊠ 1)` and
`(d_𝓕 ⊠ 1) ∘ (1 ⊠ d_𝓖)` agree as operators `𝓕^i ⊠ 𝓖^j ⟶ 𝓕^{i'} ⊠ 𝓖^{j'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem boxDoubleComplex_comm (i i' j j' : ℤ) :
    boxHom (K.d i i') (𝟙 (L.X j)) ≫ boxHom (𝟙 (K.X i')) (L.d j j') =
      boxHom (𝟙 (K.X i)) (L.d j j') ≫ boxHom (K.d i i') (𝟙 (L.X j'))
declarations.comment: commutativity of the squares of the displayed diagram, i.e. that `(i, j) ↦ F^i ⊠ G^j` with those two differentials really is a double complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotal_eq_total
declarations.doc:
**`Tot(𝓕^• ⊠ 𝓖^•)` is the total complex of the double complex `𝓕^i ⊠ 𝓖^j`**, which is what
the notation means in [Stacks, Section 0G4A].  `Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotal` is formed
as `HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor`, the total complex of the bicomplex obtained by applying the
box product; this identifies the two.
declarations.statement:
theorem boxTotal_eq_total
    [HomologicalComplex.HasMapBifunctor K L (boxProductCurried a b) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] :
    boxTotal a b K L n₁ n₂ = (boxDoubleComplex a b K L).total (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
declarations.comment: the sentence fixing the notation `Tot(F^• ⊠ G^•)` as the total complex of the displayed double complex; the sign convention of that total complex is Tag 012Z, recorded by `Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotal_d`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.isQuasicoherent_boxTotal_X
declarations.doc:
**The terms of `Tot(𝓕^• ⊠ 𝓖^•)` are quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X ×_S Y}`-modules**, the first of the
two closing assertions of the paragraph of [Stacks, Section 0G4A] that fixes the notation.  In
degree `n` the term is a finite biproduct of the `𝓕^i ⊠ 𝓖^j` with `i + j = n`, and the external
tensor product of two quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_externalTensorProduct`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_boxTotal_X (n : ℤ) :
    ((boxTotal a b K L n₁ n₂).X n).module.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the assertion that `Tot(F^• ⊠ G^•)` has quasi-coherent terms

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.exists_isGlobalDiffOpOfOrder_boxTotal_d
declarations.doc:
**The differentials of `Tot(𝓕^• ⊠ 𝓖^•)` are differential operators of finite order on
`X ×_S Y / S`**, the second of the two closing assertions of the paragraph of
[Stacks, Section 0G4A] that fixes the notation: for each pair of degrees there is a `k` for which
the differential is a global differential operator of order `≤ k` relative to the structure map
of `X ×_S Y / S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGlobalDiffOpOfOrder_boxTotal_d (n m : ℤ) :
    ∃ k, DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).relativeStructureSheafMap k
      ((boxTotal a b K L n₁ n₂).d n m).1
declarations.comment: the assertion that the differentials of `Tot(F^• ⊠ G^•)` are differential operators of finite order on `X ×_S Y / S`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.relativeBoxKunnethMap
declarations.doc:
**The relative Künneth map of the box product**

`Ra_*(𝓕^•) ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_S} Rb_*(𝓖^•) ⟶ Rf_*(Tot(𝓕^• ⊠ 𝓖^•))`,

for `𝓕^•` on `X/S` and `𝓖^•` on `Y/S` complexes of quasi-coherent modules with differentials
differential operators of finite order, both strictly bounded below, and `f` the structure
morphism of `X ×_S Y`. It is the Künneth map of [Stacks, Tag 0FLP] for the inverse-image ringed
spaces, followed by `Rf_*` of steps (4) and (5).
declarations.statement:
def relativeBoxKunnethMap :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor.{u, u + 1} (SheafedSpace.sheaf S.toRingedSpace)).obj
          ((derivedPushforward.{u, u + 1, u + 1} (inverseImageBaseProjection a)).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (leftComplex a K)))).obj
        ((derivedPushforward.{u, u + 1, u + 1} (inverseImageBaseProjection b)).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (rightComplex b L))) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
          (inverseImageBaseProjection (pullback.fst a b ≫ a))).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (boxTotalModules a b K L n₁ n₂))
declarations.comment:
the map, corrected: `Tot(F ⊠ G)` is formed under strict boundedness below of both
  complexes, without which it does not exist in the category of finite-order differential
  operators; and steps (1) to (3) are taken with the derived inverse image `Lp^*`, the canonical
  comparison `Lp^*F ⟶ p^{-1}F` being inserted into step (4); the step-(5) comparison
  `Tot(p^{-1}F ⊗ q^{-1}G) ⟶ Tot(F ⊠ G)` is `Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.boxTotalComparison`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.BoxKunneth.relativeBoxKunnethMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**The relative map is the three-step map of [Stacks, Tag 0FLP] followed by the last two
steps.** Steps (1) to (3), the two pullback maps and the relative cup product, are the Künneth
map of [Stacks, Tag 0FLP] for the projections of `(W, f^{-1}𝒪_S)` to `(X, a^{-1}𝒪_S)` and
`(Y, b^{-1}𝒪_S)`; steps (4) and (5) are `boxTotalDerivedComparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeBoxKunnethMap_eq :
    relativeBoxKunnethMap a b K L n₁ n₂ =
      Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedKunneth.kunnethMap (inverseImageBaseProjection a)
          (inverseImageBaseProjection b) (fstProjection a b) (sndProjection a b)
          (inverseImageBaseProjection (pullback.fst a b ≫ a))
          (fstProjection_comp a b) (sndProjection_comp a b)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (leftComplex a K)) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (rightComplex b L)) ≫
        (derivedPushforward (inverseImageBaseProjection (pullback.fst a b ≫ a))).map
          (boxTotalDerivedComparison a b K L n₁ n₂ (boxTotalComparison a b K L n₁ n₂))
declarations.comment:
the map is the Künneth map of Tag 0FLP for the inverse-image ringed spaces, which
  is steps (1) to (3) with `Lp^*` for `p^{-1}`, followed by `Rf_*` of steps (4) and (5)

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_adjoin_linearCombination
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a finitely generated geometrically irreducible extension and let `Ω` be generated
over `K` by algebraically independent elements `x₁, …, xₙ`. If `x₁, …, xₙ`, `∑ gᵢxᵢ` and
`∑ cᵢgᵢ` are algebraically independent over `k`, then `Ω` is geometrically irreducible over the
subfield generated over `k` by the `xᵢ` and `∑ gᵢxᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_adjoin_linearCombination
    (k K Ω : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Field Ω]
    [Algebra k K] [Algebra K Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsScalarTower k K Ω]
    (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Ω) (g : Fin n → K)
    (hgen : IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range x) = ⊤)
    (hx : AlgebraicIndependent K x)
    (hK : Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k K)
    (hfg : (⊤ : IntermediateField k K).FG)
    (c : Fin n → k)
    (hind : AlgebraicIndependent k
      (Sum.elim x (Bool.rec
        (∑ i, algebraMap K Ω (g i) * x i)
        (∑ i, algebraMap K Ω ((algebraMap k K (c i)) * g i))))) :
    let ξ : Ω := ∑ i, algebraMap K Ω (g i) * x i
    let F : IntermediateField k Ω :=
      IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range x ∪ {ξ})
    letI : Algebra F Ω := F.toSubalgebra.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible F Ω

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_algebraicIndependent_linearCombinations
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a domain of finite type over a field `k`, let
`n ≥ 2` and let `g : Fin n → A`. If the common zero locus of `g 0` and `g 1` has an irreducible
component of dimension `dim A - 2`, then there are `c : Fin n → k` for which the variables
`x₁, …, xₙ`, the linear combination `∑ gᵢxᵢ` and the constant `∑ cᵢgᵢ` are algebraically
independent over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_algebraicIndependent_linearCombinations
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [Algebra k A]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k A] {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (g : Fin n → A)
    (hcodim : ∃ p : Ideal A,
      p ∈ (Ideal.span {g ⟨0, by omega⟩, g ⟨1, by omega⟩}).minimalPrimes ∧
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p) + 2 = ringKrullDim A) :
    ∃ c : Fin n → k,
      AlgebraicIndependent k
        (Sum.elim (MvPolynomial.X : Fin n → MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
          (fun j : Fin 2 =>
            if j = 0 then
              ∑ i : Fin n, MvPolynomial.C (g i) * MvPolynomial.X i
            else
              MvPolynomial.C (∑ i : Fin n, algebraMap k A (c i) * g i)))

declarations.name: Algebra.algebraicIndependent_linearCombination_of_codimTwo
declarations.doc:
**The variables and their linear combination are algebraically independent over the base
field.** Let `A` be a domain of finite type over `k`, `n ≥ 2` and `g : Fin n → A` such that
`V(g₁, g₂)` has an irreducible component of codimension two in `Spec A`. Then the `n + 1` elements
`x₁, …, xₙ` and `ξ = ∑ gᵢxᵢ` of `Ω` are algebraically independent over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraicIndependent_linearCombination_of_codimTwo
    [IsDomain A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] [IsFractionRing A K]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (x : Fin n → Ω) (hx : AlgebraicIndependent K x) (g : Fin n → A)
    (hcodim : ∃ p : Ideal A,
      p ∈ (Ideal.span {g ⟨0, by omega⟩, g ⟨1, by omega⟩}).minimalPrimes ∧
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p) + 2 = ringKrullDim A) :
    AlgebraicIndependent k
      (Sum.elim x fun _ : Unit => ∑ i, algebraMap K Ω (algebraMap A K (g i)) * x i)
declarations.comment: the variables and their linear combination, read in the ambient field

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.Hypotheses.exists_ringKrullDim_quotient_add_two_eq_reducedChart
declarations.doc:
On a trivializing affine chart meeting `Z`, the reduced chart ring `A` is a domain of finite
type over `k`, and some minimal prime `p` over the ideal generated by the images of the functions
of `v₂` and `v₃` satisfies `dim (A ⧸ p) + 2 = dim A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringKrullDim_quotient_add_two_eq_reducedChart (c : D.Chart)
    (hZ : ((c.U : Set D.X) ∩ (h.Z : Set D.X)).Nonempty) :
    letI := reducedChartAlgebra c.U
    ∃ p : Ideal (reducedChartRing c.U),
      p ∈ (Ideal.span {Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (chartFunction c.triv h.v₂),
        Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (chartFunction c.triv h.v₃)}).minimalPrimes ∧
        ringKrullDim (reducedChartRing c.U ⧸ p) + 2 = ringKrullDim (reducedChartRing c.U)
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) as the codimension datum of the chart statements

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_universalDivisorChart_of_linearSubst
declarations.doc:
The function field of the universal divisor over a chart is geometrically irreducible over
the field generated by the parameters. This is
`Algebra.isGeometricallyIrreducible_universalDivisorChart` with the parameters indexed by an
arbitrary finite set `σ` and its hypotheses imposed not on `f` itself but on the image `g` of `f`
under an invertible `k`-linear transformation `b` of the parameters.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyIrreducible_universalDivisorChart_of_linearSubst (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (g : Fin (n + 1) → A) (hg : ∀ i, g i = ∑ j, algebraMap k A (b i j) * f j)
    {w : A} (hw : w * g 0 = 1)
    (hcompat : ∀ a : A, algebraMap K Ω (algebraMap A K a) =
      universalDivisorChartMap A Ω f (C a))
    (hK : Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible k K)
    (hcodim : ∃ p : Ideal A,
      p ∈ (Ideal.span {g ⟨1, by omega⟩, g ⟨2, by omega⟩}).minimalPrimes ∧
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p) + 2 = ringKrullDim A) :
    letI F : IntermediateField k Ω :=
      IntermediateField.adjoin k
        (Set.range fun j : σ => universalDivisorChartMap A Ω f (X j))
    letI : Algebra F Ω := F.toSubalgebra.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyIrreducible F Ω
declarations.comment: the generic fibre over a chart, for distinguished vectors of an arbitrary basis

declarations.name: Algebra.algebraicIndependent_universalDivisorChartMap_X_of_linearSubst
declarations.doc:
The parameters of a chart are algebraically independent over the base field. This is
`Algebra.algebraicIndependent_universalDivisorChartMap_X` with the parameters indexed by an
arbitrary finite set and its hypotheses imposed on the image of `f` under an invertible
`k`-linear transformation of the parameters.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraicIndependent_universalDivisorChartMap_X_of_linearSubst (hn : 2 ≤ n)
    (g : Fin (n + 1) → A) (hg : ∀ i, g i = ∑ j, algebraMap k A (b i j) * f j)
    {w : A} (hw : w * g 0 = 1)
    (hcompat : ∀ a : A, algebraMap K Ω (algebraMap A K a) =
      universalDivisorChartMap A Ω f (C a))
    (hcodim : ∃ p : Ideal A,
      p ∈ (Ideal.span {g ⟨1, by omega⟩, g ⟨2, by omega⟩}).minimalPrimes ∧
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ p) + 2 = ringKrullDim A) :
    AlgebraicIndependent k fun j : σ => universalDivisorChartMap A Ω f (X j)
declarations.comment: the dominance over the parameter space, for an arbitrary basis

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.Hypotheses.exists_mem_minimalPrimes_height_eq_two
declarations.doc:
On a trivializing affine chart `U` that meets `Z`, the prime of `Γ(U, ⊤)` cutting out `Z ∩ U`
is a minimal prime over the ideal generated by the functions `g₂, g₃` of `v₂, v₃`, and its height
is exactly two.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_minimalPrimes_height_eq_two (c : D.Chart)
    (hZ : ((c.U : Set D.X) ∩ (h.Z : Set D.X)).Nonempty) :
    ∃ p : Ideal Γ(c.U.toScheme, ⊤),
      p ∈ (Ideal.span {chartFunction c.triv h.v₂, chartFunction c.triv h.v₃}).minimalPrimes ∧
        p.height = 2
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) read on a chart meeting Z, as an exact height

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.Hypotheses.exists_chart_isUnit_and_height_eq_two
declarations.doc:
There is a trivializing affine chart on which the function of `v₁` is a unit and on which
some minimal prime over the ideal generated by the functions of `v₂` and `v₃` has height exactly
two.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_chart_isUnit_and_height_eq_two :
    ∃ c : D.Chart, IsUnit (chartFunction c.triv h.v₁) ∧
      ∃ p : Ideal Γ(c.U.toScheme, ⊤),
        p ∈ (Ideal.span {chartFunction c.triv h.v₂, chartFunction c.triv h.v₃}).minimalPrimes ∧
          p.height = 2
declarations.comment: hypothesis (3) on a single chart: an invertible first function and an exact height

declarations.name: Stacks.Bertini.FamilyDivisors.Hypotheses.v₁_notMem_span
declarations.doc: The vector `v₁` is not in the span of `v₂` and `v₃`.
declarations.statement: theorem v₁_notMem_span : h.v₁ ∉ Submodule.span D.k {h.v₂, h.v₃}
declarations.comment: v₁ is independent from v₂ and v₃
