declarations.comment: the maps K'_n = (𝓘')^n 𝓕^• ⟶ 𝓘^n 𝓕^• = K_n of the explicit construction, induced by the inclusions (𝓘')^n ⊆ 𝓘^n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerComplexSystem.compareHom_comp_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y] is the inclusion, read inside `𝓕^•`.** Composing
`K'_n ⟶ K_n` with the inclusion of `K_n` into `𝓕^•` gives the inclusion of `K'_n`. Since the
inclusions are termwise monomorphisms, this characterises the comparison map.
declarations.comment: the maps K'_n ⟶ K_n of the explicit construction are the inclusions read inside 𝓕^•, which is what pins them down

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerComplexSystem.compareHom_comp_transition
declarations.doc:
**The comparison maps of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y] form a map of inverse systems.** They commute
with the transitions `K'_{n+1} ⟶ K'_n` and `K_{n+1} ⟶ K_n` of the two ideal-power
filtrations.
declarations.comment: the maps K'_n ⟶ K_n of the explicit construction commute with the transitions, so they are a map of the inverse systems (K'_n) ⟶ (K_n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G50.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of `FTS_S`. The functor `Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_!` of [Stacks, Section 0G4Z]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriek`) is, up to isomorphism, independent of the choice of the
compactification `j : X ⟶ X̄` of `X` over `Y`.

The proof is the source's. Two compactifications `X̄₁`, `X̄₂` are dominated by a third, the
scheme-theoretic closure `X̄₃` of `X` in `X̄₁ ×_Y X̄₂`
(the closure of `AlgebraicGeometry.compactificationPairMap`; that `X ⟶ X̄₃` is an open immersion is
because `X ⟶ X̄₁ ×_Y X̄₂` is a quasi-compact immersion), which is cofilteredness of the category of
compactifications for these two objects; and a morphism `g : X̄₃ ⟶ X̄ᵢ` of compactifications gives
`Rf̄ᵢ_* ∘ Rjᵢ_! ≅ Rf̄ᵢ_* ∘ Rg_* ∘ Rj₃_! ≅ Rf̄₃_* ∘ Rj₃_!` by [Stacks, Tag 0G4X]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekIsoOfFactor`).
declarations.statement: public def lowerShriekIso : lowerShriek f c₁ ≅ lowerShriek f c₂

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Compactification.shriekImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G50.** The functor `Rf_!` is, up to isomorphism, independent of the
choice of the compactification.

The compactifications of `X` over `Y` are the objects of a cofiltered category `𝒦`, each carrying
the data of a `CategoryTheory.Compactification`, and each morphism of `𝒦` induces an isomorphism
of the attached functors `Rf_!` — the isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0G4X], produced by
`CategoryTheory.Compactification.shriekImageIsoOfMorphism`. Any two compactifications are then
dominated by a third, and the two isomorphisms to it compose to one between them.
declarations.statement:
public def shriekImageIso {𝒦 : Type w₁} [Category.{w₂} 𝒦] [IsCofiltered 𝒦] {ℳ : 𝒦 → Type u₃}
    [∀ c, Category.{v} (ℳ c)] (C : ∀ c, Compactification 𝒞 𝒟 (ℳ c))
    (e : ∀ {c c' : 𝒦}, (c ⟶ c') → ((C c').shriekImage ≅ (C c).shriekImage)) (c c' : 𝒦) :
    (C c).shriekImage ≅ (C c').shriekImage
declarations.comment: the per-compactification data, the cofilteredness of the category of compactifications, and the isomorphisms attached to its morphisms by Tag 0G4X, supplied as data

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.CompactificationData.shriekImageIso
declarations.doc:
The functor `Rf_!` is, up to isomorphism, independent of the choice of the compactification.

The compactifications of `X` over `Y` are the objects of a cofiltered category `𝒦`, each carrying
the data of a `CategoryTheory.CompactificationData`, and each morphism of `𝒦` induces an
isomorphism of the attached functors `Rf_!`, that of Stacks, Tag 0G4X. The isomorphism between the
functors of `c` and `c'` is the composite of the isomorphisms to the functor of a compactification
dominating both.
declarations.statement:
public def shriekImageIso {𝒦 : Type w₁} [Category.{w₂} 𝒦] [IsCofiltered 𝒦] {ℳ : 𝒦 → Type u₃}
    [∀ c, Category.{v} (ℳ c)] (C : ∀ c, CompactificationData 𝒞 𝒟 (ℳ c))
    [∀ c (A : ℳ c ⥤ Type v), (C c).direct.HasLeftKanExtension A]
    (e : ∀ {c c' : 𝒦}, (c ⟶ c') → ((C c').shriekImage ≅ (C c).shriekImage)) (c c' : 𝒦) :
    (C c).shriekImage ≅ (C c').shriekImage
declarations.comment: the per-compactification data, the cofilteredness of the category of compactifications, and the isomorphisms attached to its morphisms by Tag 0G4X, supplied as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekHomIso
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of `FTS_S`. Then `Rf_!` and
`f^!` are adjoint in the following sense: for `K` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` and `L` in
`D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)`

`Hom_X(K, f^! L) = Hom_{Pro-D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)}(Rf_! K, L)`,

bifunctorially in `K` and `L`: an isomorphism of functors
`D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_Y) ⥤ Type`, with components
`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekHomEquiv`. Here `Rf_!` and `f^!` are computed at an arbitrary
compactification `c` of `X` over `Y`, `Rf_! K` is viewed in `Pro-D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)` through
`D^b_{Coh} ⊆ D^+_{Coh}`, and `f^! L` is read at the standard model of `D(𝒪_X)`
(`Stacks.Duality.UpperShriekDuality.upperShriekStd`).
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriekHomIso :
    (lowerShriek f c ⋙ ProSeq.map (boundedCoherentToPlusCoh Y₁.left)).op ⋙ coyoneda ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj ProSeq.const ≅
      (boundedCoherentDerived X₁.left).ι.op ⋙ coyoneda ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj (upperShriekStd f c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_shriekImage_distTriang_system
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of `FTS_S` and let

`K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ K[1]`

be a distinguished triangle of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`. Then there is an inverse system of distinguished
triangles

`K_n ⟶ L_n ⟶ M_n ⟶ K_n[1]`

of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)` such that the pro-systems `(K_n)`, `(L_n)` and `(M_n)` give `Rf_! K`,
`Rf_! L` and `Rf_! M`.

Here `Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_!` is `AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriek f c`, the functor of
[Stacks, Section 0G4Z] attached to a compactification `c`, `j : X ⟶ X̄`, of `X` over `Y` with
structure morphism `f̄ : X̄ ⟶ Y`: `Rj_!` is the extension by zero of [Stacks, Tag 0G4N] and `Rf̄_*`
is the derived direct image `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_{X̄}) ⥤ D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)`, applied termwise to
pro-objects. The statement holds for every compactification; by [Stacks, Tag 0G50] the functor
does not depend on it.

The proof is the source's. [Stacks, Tag 0G4M] for `j`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.DeligneTriangle.exists_extensionByZero_distTriang`) gives an inverse system of
distinguished triangles `K̄_n ⟶ L̄_n ⟶ M̄_n ⟶ K̄_n[1]` of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_{X̄})` whose vertex systems
give `Rj_! K`, `Rj_! L` and `Rj_! M`; the system `K_n = Rf̄_* K̄_n`, and likewise for `L_n` and
`M_n`, works by the very definition of `Rf_!`
(`CategoryTheory.CompactificationData.exists_shriekImage_distTriang_system`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shriekImage_distTriang_system (f : X₁ ⟶ Y₁)
    (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (T : Triangle (BoundedCoherentDerived X₁.left))
    (hT : T ∈ distTriang (BoundedCoherentDerived X₁.left)) :
    ∃ TY : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Triangle (BoundedCoherentDerived Y₁.left),
      (∀ n, TY.obj n ∈ distTriang (BoundedCoherentDerived Y₁.left)) ∧
      Nonempty (ProSeq.of (TY ⋙ Triangle.π₁) ≅ (lowerShriek f c).obj T.obj₁) ∧
      Nonempty (ProSeq.of (TY ⋙ Triangle.π₂) ≅ (lowerShriek f c).obj T.obj₂) ∧
      Nonempty (ProSeq.of (TY ⋙ Triangle.π₃) ≅ (lowerShriek f c).obj T.obj₃)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pro.exists_diagonalRepresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G53 (diagonal representation).** A countable inverse
system of pro-objects, each represented by an inverse sequence, has a diagonal
inverse-sequence representation.  Equivalently, naturally in `N`,
`colim_i colim_n Hom(M_{i,n}, N)` is `colim_k Hom(D_k, N)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_diagonalRepresentation {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (P : Functor ℕ (Functor C (Type v))) (M : ℕ → Functor ℕᵒᵖ C)
    (e : ∀ i, P.obj i ≅ Pro.coyonedaColim (liftedInverseSequence (M i))) :
    Nonempty (DiagonalRepresentation P M e)
declarations.comment: diagonal_representation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pro.diagonalRepresentation_uniqueUpToIso
declarations.doc:
The diagonal inverse sequence is uniquely pro-isomorphic to any other representation `G` of
the same functor of points: there is a unique pro-morphism to `G` compatible with the comparison
isomorphisms, and it has a two-sided inverse.
declarations.statement:
public theorem diagonalRepresentation_uniqueUpToIso {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (P : Functor ℕ (Functor C (Type v))) (M : ℕ → Functor ℕᵒᵖ C)
    (e : ∀ i, P.obj i ≅ Pro.coyonedaColim (liftedInverseSequence (M i)))
    (r : DiagonalRepresentation P M e) {I : Type v} [Category.{v} I]
    (G : Functor I C) (eG : colimit P ≅ Pro.coyonedaColim G) :
    ∃! φ : Pro.Hom (liftedInverseSequence r.system) G,
      (∃ ψ : Pro.Hom G (liftedInverseSequence r.system),
        (Pro.homEquiv G (liftedInverseSequence r.system)).symm ψ ≫
            (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r.system) G).symm φ =
          𝟙 (Pro.coyonedaColim (liftedInverseSequence r.system)) ∧
        (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r.system) G).symm φ ≫
            (Pro.homEquiv G (liftedInverseSequence r.system)).symm ψ =
          𝟙 (Pro.coyonedaColim G)) ∧
      eG.hom ≫ (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r.system) G).symm φ =
        r.comparison.hom
declarations.comment: diagonal_uniqueness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pro.exists_compositionRepresentation
declarations.doc:
The composition of two compactly supported direct images: the termwise image under `G` of an
inverse sequence `M` is represented by an inverse sequence in the target category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_compositionRepresentation {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C] {D : Type u}
    [Category.{v} D] (G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D ⥤ Type v) (S : C → ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ D)
    (e : ∀ L : C, G.obj (op L) ≅ Pro.coyonedaColim (liftedInverseSequence (S L)))
    (M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ C) : Nonempty (CompositionRepresentation G M)
declarations.comment: the composition, for pro-object-valued functors with countable-index representations supplied as data

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pro.CompositionRepresentation.homColimitIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G54**, the displayed formula: for every object `L`, the colimit over
`n` of `Hom(G (M n), L)` is the colimit over `k` of `Hom(system_k, L)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def CompositionRepresentation.homColimitIso {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C]
    {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] {G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D ⥤ Type v} {M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ C}
    (r : CompositionRepresentation G M) (L : D) :
    colimit ((M.rightOp ⋙ G) ⋙ (evaluation D (Type v)).obj L) ≅
      colimit ((liftedInverseSequence r.system).op ⋙ coyoneda ⋙
        (evaluation D (Type v)).obj L)
declarations.comment: the Hom-colimit formula, for pro-object-valued functors with countable-index representations supplied as data

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pro.compositionRepresentation_uniqueUpToIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G54**, uniqueness: two inverse sequences representing the termwise
image of `M` under `G` are uniquely pro-isomorphic over their comparison isomorphisms. The
pro-morphism and its inverse are expressed through Stacks 0G2X.
declarations.statement:
public theorem compositionRepresentation_uniqueUpToIso {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C]
    {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] (G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D ⥤ Type v) (M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ C)
    (r r' : CompositionRepresentation G M) :
    ∃! φ : Pro.Hom (liftedInverseSequence r.system) (liftedInverseSequence r'.system),
      (∃ ψ : Pro.Hom (liftedInverseSequence r'.system) (liftedInverseSequence r.system),
        (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r'.system)
              (liftedInverseSequence r.system)).symm ψ ≫
            (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r.system)
              (liftedInverseSequence r'.system)).symm φ =
          𝟙 (Pro.coyonedaColim (liftedInverseSequence r.system)) ∧
        (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r.system)
              (liftedInverseSequence r'.system)).symm φ ≫
            (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r'.system)
              (liftedInverseSequence r.system)).symm ψ =
          𝟙 (Pro.coyonedaColim (liftedInverseSequence r'.system))) ∧
      r'.comparison.hom ≫ (Pro.homEquiv (liftedInverseSequence r.system)
          (liftedInverseSequence r'.system)).symm φ = r.comparison.hom
declarations.comment: uniqueness up to pro-isomorphism, for pro-object-valued functors with countable-index representations supplied as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G54**, the definition. In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be composable morphisms of `FTS_S`, with compactifications `cf` of `X`
over `Y` and `cg` of `Y` over `Z` defining `Rf_!` and `Rg_!` ([Stacks, Section 0G4Z],
`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriek`). For `K` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`, `Rf_! K` is given by an inverse
system `(M_n)` of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekObjIso`), `(Rg_! M_n)` is an
inverse system of `Pro-D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Z)`, and `Rg_! Rf_! K` is the pro-object of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Z)`
given by [Stacks, Tag 0G53] with

`Hom(Rg_! Rf_! K, L) = colim_n Hom(Rg_! M_n, L)`

for every `L` (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekCompPointsIso`); it is unique up to pro-isomorphism
(`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_lowerShriekComp_iff`) and does not depend on the inverse system
`(M_n)` chosen. Functoriality in `K` is omitted, as in the source.
declarations.comment: the definition of Rg_! Rf_! K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekCompPointsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G54**, the defining property: for every inverse system `(M_n)` of
`D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)` giving `Rf_! K`,

`Hom(Rg_! Rf_! K, L) = colim_n Hom(Rg_! M_n, L)`

naturally in `L` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Z)`.
declarations.comment: Hom(Rg_! Rf_! K, L) = colim_n Hom(Rg_! M_n, L) for every inverse system (M_n) giving Rf_! K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekCompHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G54**, the displayed formula with `Hom`-sets of pro-objects: for every
inverse system `(M_n)` giving `Rf_! K` and every `L` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Z)`,

`Hom_{Pro}(Rg_! Rf_! K, L) = colim_n Hom_{Pro}(Rg_! M_n, L)`.
declarations.comment: Hom_Pro(Rg_! Rf_! K, L) = colim_n Hom_Pro(Rg_! M_n, L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_lowerShriekComp_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G54**, uniqueness: for an inverse system `(M_n)` giving `Rf_! K`, an
inverse system `(N_k)` of `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Z)` satisfies `Hom((N_k), L) = colim_n Hom(Rg_! M_n, L)`
naturally in `L` if and only if it gives `Rg_! Rf_! K`; so `Rg_! Rf_! K` is the unique
pro-isomorphism class with that property.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_lowerShriekComp_iff (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (cf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (cg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g.left))
    (K : BoundedCoherentDerived X.left) {M : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ BoundedCoherentDerived Y.left}
    (e : ProSeq.of M ≅ (lowerShriek f cf).obj K) (N : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ BoundedCoherentDerived Z.left) :
    Nonempty ((ProSeq.of N).points ≅
        colimit (M.rightOp ⋙ ProSeq.pointsFunctor (lowerShriek g cg))) ↔
      Nonempty (ProSeq.of N ≅ lowerShriekComp f g cf cg K)
declarations.comment: uniqueness up to pro-isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekCompIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G55.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`g : Y ⟶ Z` be composable morphisms of `FTS_S`. With notation as in [Stacks, Tag 0G54] we have
`Rg_! ∘ Rf_! = R(g ∘ f)_!`: for `K` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` the composition `Rg_! Rf_! K`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekComp`) is isomorphic to `R(g ∘ f)_! K`, for arbitrary
compactifications `cf`, `cg` and `cfg` computing `Rf_!`, `Rg_!` and `R(g ∘ f)_!`.

The proof is the source's: both pro-objects have the functor of points
`L ↦ Hom_X(K, (g ∘ f)^! L)` on `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Z)`, by [Stacks, Tag 0G51] for `g`, `f` and `g ∘ f`
and `f^! ∘ g^! = (g ∘ f)^!` ([Stacks, Tag 0ATX]); a pro-object is determined by its functor of
points ([Stacks, Tag 0G2X]).
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriekCompIso (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (cf : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (cg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g.left))
    (cfg : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g).left)) (K : BoundedCoherentDerived X.left) :
    lowerShriekComp f g cf cg K ≅ (lowerShriek (f ≫ g) cfg).obj K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G56.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of `FTS_S`, let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open immersion and `g = f ∘ j = f|_U`. Then there is a
canonical morphism

`Rg_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rf_! K`,

functorial in `K` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`. This is the third construction of the source: for `L` in
`D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)`,

`Hom(Rf_! K, L) = Hom_X(K, f^! L) ⟶ Hom_U(K|_U, (f^! L)|_U) = Hom_U(K|_U, g^! L)
  = Hom(Rg_!(K|_U), L)`,

by [Stacks, Tag 0G51] twice and `g^! = j^* ∘ f^!` (the construction of the upper shriek
functors, `Stacks.Duality.UpperShriekDuality.upperShriekStdPrecompOpenIso`), and the
functoriality in `L` gives the morphism of pro-objects by [Stacks, Tag 0G2X]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekMapOfHom`). `Rf_!` and `Rg_!` are computed at arbitrary
compactifications `c` and `cU`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification_eq_lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap
declarations.doc:
The agreement of constructions (2) and (3). In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y`
be a morphism of `FTS_S`, `i : U ⟶ X` an open immersion, `g = f ∘ i`, and `j : X ⟶ X̄` a
compactification of `X` over `Y` with `f̄ : X̄ ⟶ Y`. The canonical map `Rg_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rf_! K` given
by `Rf̄_*` applied to the map `Rj'_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rj_! K` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y], `j' = j ∘ i`
(construction (2), `AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification`), is the map
induced by `Hom(Rf_! K, L) = Hom_X(K, f^! L) ⟶ Hom_U(K|_U, f^! L|_U)`
`= Hom_U(K|_U, g^! L) = Hom(Rg_!(K|_U), L)` (construction (3),
`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap`), with `Rg_!` computed at the compactification
`j'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification_eq_lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (i : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion i.left] :
    lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification f c i =
      lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap f c i (c.precompOpen i.left)
declarations.comment: constructions (2) and (3) give the same arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G56], construction (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of `FTS_S`,
`i : U ⟶ X` an open immersion, `c` a compactification `j : X ⟶ X̄` of `X` over `Y` with structure
morphism `f̄ : X̄ ⟶ Y`, and `j' = j ∘ i` the induced compactification of `U` over `Y`. With
`Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj_!` and `Rg_! = Rf̄_* ∘ Rj'_!` for `g = f ∘ i`, the canonical map
`Rg_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rf_! K`, functorial in `K` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`, is `Rf̄_*` applied to the map
`Rj'_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rj_! K` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y].
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (i : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion i.left] :
    restrictBoundedCoherentLift i.left ⋙ lowerShriek (i ≫ f) (c.precompOpen i.left) ⟶
      lowerShriek f c
declarations.comment: construction (2): Rf̄_* applied to the map Rj'_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rj_! K of Tag 0G4Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of `FTS_S`, `i : U ⟶ X` an
open immersion and `g = f ∘ i`. The canonical map `Rg_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rf_! K`, functorial in `K` in
`D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`, obtained from `Rg_! = Rf_! ∘ Ri_!` ([Stacks, Tag 0G55]) and `Rf_!` applied to the
map `Ri_!(K|_U) ⟶ K` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y] (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionCompMap`),
with `Ri_!` computed at the compactification `X` of `U` over `X` and `Rg_!` at the
compactification restricted from the compactification `c` of `f`.
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left))
    (i : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion i.left] :
    restrictBoundedCoherentLift i.left ⋙ lowerShriek (i ≫ f) (c.precompOpen i.left) ⟶
      lowerShriek f c
declarations.comment: construction (1): Rf_! applied to the map Ri_!(K|_U) ⟶ K of Tag 0G4Y, through Rg_! = Rf_! ∘ Ri_! of Tag 0G55, functorial in K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition_eq_lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap
declarations.doc:
`Rf_!` applied to the map `Ri_!(K|_U) ⟶ K` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y] through `Rg_! = Rf_! ∘ Ri_!`
is the map induced by
`Hom(Rf_! K, L) = Hom_X(K, f^! L) ⟶ Hom_U(K|_U, g^! L) = Hom(Rg_!(K|_U), L)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition_eq_lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (i : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion i.left] :
    lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition f c i =
      lowerShriekOpenImmersionMap f c i (c.precompOpen i.left)
declarations.comment: constructions (1) and (3) give the same arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition_eq_lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification
declarations.doc:
`Rf_!` applied to the map `Ri_!(K|_U) ⟶ K` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y] through `Rg_! = Rf_! ∘ Ri_!`
is `Rf̄_*` applied to the map `Rj'_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rj_! K` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y], for the
compactification `j : X ⟶ X̄`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition_eq_lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (i : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion i.left] :
    lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfComposition f c i =
      lowerShriekOpenImmersionMapOfCompactification f c i
declarations.comment: constructions (1) and (2) give the same arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekEtaleMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G57.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let

`U --h--> X --f--> Y`,  `g = f ∘ h`

be a commutative diagram of `FTS_S` with `h` étale. Then there is a canonical morphism

`Rg_!(h^* K) ⟶ Rf_! K`,

functorial in `K` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`, defined by the sequence of maps

`Hom(Rf_! K, L) = Hom_X(K, f^! L) ⟶ Hom_U(h^* K, h^*(f^! L)) = Hom_U(h^* K, h^! f^! L)
  = Hom_U(h^* K, g^! L) = Hom(Rg_!(h^* K), L)`

for `L` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)`: [Stacks, Tag 0G51] twice, `h^* = h^!` ([Stacks, Tag 0FWI]) and
`h^! ∘ f^! = g^!` ([Stacks, Tag 0ATX]); the functoriality in `L` gives the morphism of
pro-objects by [Stacks, Tag 0G2X] (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekMapOfHom`). `Rf_!` and `Rg_!` are
computed at arbitrary compactifications `c` and `cU`, and `h^!` at the compactification of `h`
obtained from them (`Stacks.Duality.CompCompactification.restrictCompactification`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekFlatQuasiFiniteMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G58.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] let

`U --h--> X --f--> Y`,  `g = f ∘ h`

be a commutative diagram of `FTS_S` with `h` flat and quasi-finite. Then there is a canonical
transformation

`Rg_! ∘ h^* ⟶ Rf_!`

of functors on `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)`, constructed as in [Stacks, Tag 0G57] from the transformation
`h^* ⟶ h^!` on `D^+_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` (`Stacks.Duality.pullbackToUpperShriekOfFlatQuasiFinite`) given by
`h^! K = h^* K ⊗ ω_{U/X}`, `ω_{U/X} = h^! 𝒪_X` the relative dualizing module of `h`
([Stacks, Tag 0B6U], [Stacks, Tag 0BV7], [Stacks, Tag 0BVG], [Stacks, Tag 0BUL]), and the trace
element `τ_{U/X} : 𝒪_U ⟶ ω_{U/X}` ([Stacks, Tag 0BVJ]): for `L` in `D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_Y)`,

`Hom(Rf_! K, L) = Hom_X(K, f^! L) ⟶ Hom_U(h^* K, h^* f^! L) ⟶ Hom_U(h^* K, h^! f^! L)
  = Hom_U(h^* K, g^! L) = Hom(Rg_!(h^* K), L)`,

by [Stacks, Tag 0G51] twice and `h^! ∘ f^! = g^!` ([Stacks, Tag 0ATX]); the functoriality in `L`
gives the morphism of pro-objects by [Stacks, Tag 0G2X] (`AlgebraicGeometry.lowerShriekMapOfHom`).
Quasi-finiteness is `LocallyQuasiFinite`, morphisms of `FTS_S` being quasi-compact. `Rf_!` and
`Rg_!` are computed at arbitrary compactifications `c` and `cU`, and `h^!` at the
compactification of `h` obtained from them
(`Stacks.Duality.CompCompactification.restrictCompactification`).
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriekFlatQuasiFiniteMap (f : X ⟶ Y) (c : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left))
    (h : U ⟶ X) [Flat h.left] [LocallyQuasiFinite h.left] (g : U ⟶ Y) (w : h ≫ f = g)
    (cU : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g.left)) :
    boundedCoherentPullback h.left ⋙ lowerShriek g cU ⟶ lowerShriek f c

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportDualityEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5A.** Let `p : U ⟶ Spec k` be separated of finite type over a field
`k` and `ω_{U/k}^• = p^!𝒪_{Spec k}`. For `K ∈ D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_U)` and `i ∈ ℤ` there is a canonical
isomorphism of topological `k`-vector spaces

`Hom_k(H^i(U, K), k) ≃ H^{-i}_c(U, R𝓗om(K, ω_{U/k}^•))`,

for the topology of pointwise convergence on the dual (the limit topology over the finite
dimensional subspaces, `Module.Dual.limitTopology_eq_iInf_finiteDimensional`) and the limit
topology of [Stacks, Section 0G59] on compactly supported cohomology. It is functorial in `K`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportDualityEquiv_naturality`). Here `p^!` and `H^*_c` are computed
at an arbitrary compactification `c` of `U` (one exists by [Stacks, Tag 0F41]).
declarations.statement:
def compactSupportDualityEquiv (K : BoundedCoherentDerived U) (i : ℤ) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard U.Modules
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} k)
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType p
    letI := Module.Dual.limitTopology k ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) i).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver p).obj K.obj))
    Module.Dual k ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) i).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver p).obj K.obj)) ≃L[k]
      compactSupportCohomology c
        (openDualObj (standardUpperShriekDualizingComplex p c)
          (isDualizingComplex_standardUpperShriekDualizingComplex p c) K) (-i)
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of topological k-vector spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportDualityEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5A, functoriality.** The isomorphisms of
`AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportDualityEquiv` are functorial in `K`: for `α : K ⟶ K'` and a
linear form `l` on `H^i(U, K')`, the image of `l ∘ H^i(α)` is the image of `l` under the map
`H^{-i}_c(U, D_U K') ⟶ H^{-i}_c(U, D_U K)` induced by `D_U α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSupportDualityEquiv_naturality {K K' : BoundedCoherentDerived U} (α : K ⟶ K')
    (i : ℤ) (l :
      letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard U.Modules
      letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} k)
      Module.Dual k ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) i).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver p).obj K'.obj))) :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard U.Modules
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} k)
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType p
    compactSupportDualityEquiv p c K i
        (l ∘ₗ ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) i).map
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver p).map α.hom)).hom) =
      compactSupportCohomologyMap c
        (openDualMap (standardUpperShriekDualizingComplex p c)
          (isDualizingComplex_standardUpperShriekDualizingComplex p c) α) (-i)
        (compactSupportDualityEquiv p c K' i l)
declarations.comment: functoriality in K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportDualityEquiv_restrict
declarations.doc:
Let `p : U ⟶ Spec k` be separated of finite type over a field `k`, with a compactification
`c : U ⊆ X` at which `p^!` and `H^*_c` are computed, as in [Stacks, Tag 0G5A]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportDualityEquiv`), and let `V ⊆ U` be an open, with the induced
compactification `V ⊆ U ⊆ X` (`AlgebraicGeometry.compactificationOpen`). Then the square

`Hom_k(H^i(U, K), k)       ⟶  H^{-i}_c(U, R𝓗om(K, ω_{U/k}^•))`
`        ↑                                  ↑`
`Hom_k(H^i(V, K|_V), k)    ⟶  H^{-i}_c(V, R𝓗om(K|_V, ω_{V/k}^•))`

commutes, for every `K ∈ D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_U)` and `i ∈ ℤ`: for every linear form `l` on
`H^i(V, K|_V)`, the image of `l ∘ res` under the duality isomorphism of `U` is the image under the
right vertical arrow of the image of `l` under the duality isomorphism of `V`. Here the horizontal
arrows are the isomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0G5A], the left vertical arrow is the contragredient
of the restriction map `res : H^i(U, K) ⟶ H^i(V, K|_V)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyRestrict`),
and the right vertical arrow is the map of [Stacks, Remark 0G56]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.compactSupportOpenDualMap`): `Rq_*` of the canonical map
`Rj'_!(L|_V) ⟶ Rj_! L` of [Stacks, Tag 0G4Y], read through the canonical identification of
`R𝓗om(K|_V, ω_{V/k}^•)` with `R𝓗om(K, ω_{U/k}^•)|_V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSupportDualityEquiv_restrict (K : BoundedCoherentDerived U) (i : ℤ) :
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType p
    haveI := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType (V.ι ≫ p)
    ∀ l : Module.Dual k ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) i).obj
      ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver (V.ι ≫ p)).obj ((restrictBoundedCoherentLift V.ι).obj K).obj)),
    compactSupportDualityEquiv p c K i (l ∘ₗ cohomologyRestrict p V K i) =
      compactSupportOpenDualMap p c V K i
        (compactSupportDualityEquiv (V.ι ≫ p) (compactificationOpen p c V)
          ((restrictBoundedCoherentLift V.ι).obj K) i l)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.degreeZeroCompactSupportMap_injective_and_range
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a proper scheme over a field `k`. Let
`K ∈ D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_X)` with `H^i(K) = 0` for `i < 0`, and set `𝓕 = H^0(K)`. Let `Z ⊆ X` be closed
with complement `U = X ∖ Z`. Then

`H^0_c(U, K|_U) ⊂ H^0(X, 𝓕)`

is given by those global sections of `𝓕` which vanish in an open neighbourhood of `Z`.

Here `H^0_c(U, K|_U)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.degreeZeroCompactSupport`: the morphisms
`𝒪_{Spec k} ⟶ Rg_!(K|_U)` in `Pro-D^b_{Coh}(𝒪_{Spec k})`, for `g : U ⟶ Spec k` and the functor
`Rg_! = Rp_* ∘ Rj_!` of [Stacks, Section 0G4Z] attached to the compactification `j : U ⟶ X`
(which is `lim_n H^0(X, K_n)` for a Deligne system `(K_n)` with value `K|_U`,
[Stacks, Section 0G59]); the map `H^0_c(U, K|_U) ⟶ H^0(X, 𝓕)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.degreeZeroCompactSupportMap`, induced by the map `Rg_!(K|_U) ⟶ Rp_* K` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G56] for `X` its own compactification and `H^0(X, K) = Γ(X, H^0(K))`. The statement
is that this map is injective with exactly that image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem degreeZeroCompactSupportMap_injective_and_range {k : Type u} [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper p] (K : BoundedCoherentDerived X)
    (hK : ∀ i < 0, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K.obj))
    (Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X) :
    letI : IsNoetherian X := @IsNoetherian.mk X (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian p)
      (QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace p)
    Function.Injective (degreeZeroCompactSupportMap p Z.compl K
        ((DerivedCategory.isGE_iff K.obj 0).2 hK)) ∧
      Set.range (degreeZeroCompactSupportMap p Z.compl K
        ((DerivedCategory.isGE_iff K.obj 0).2 hK)) =
        {σ | ∃ V : X.Opens, (Z : Set X) ⊆ V ∧
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules 0).obj K.obj).presheaf.map
            (homOfLE (le_top : V ≤ ⊤)).op σ = 0}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Lichtenbaum.le_topologicalKrullDim_and_isProper_of_not_isZero_rightDerived
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G5E].** Let `U` be a variety over a field `k` and let `F` be a coherent
`𝒪_U`-module. If `H^d(U, F)` is nonzero, then `dim(U) ≥ d`, and if equality holds, then `U` is
proper over `k`.

Here `H^d(U, F)` is the `d`-th right derived functor of global sections on `Mod(𝒪_U)`, and
`dim(U)` is the topological Krull dimension. The proof is the source's. The bound is
Grothendieck's vanishing theorem ([Stacks, Tag 02UZ]). If `dim U = d`, choose an integral scheme
`X` proper over `k` containing `U` as an open subscheme ([Stacks, Tag 0F41],
[Stacks, Tag 0A9Z]); then `dim X = d`, and if `U` is not proper then `U ≠ X`, so
`H^d(U, F) = 0` by duality ([Stacks, Tag 0G5A]) and the vanishing of
`H^{-d}_c(U, R𝓗om(F, ω_U^•))`
(`Stacks.Duality.Lichtenbaum.isZero_rightDerived_of_nonempty_compl`).
declarations.statement:
theorem le_topologicalKrullDim_and_isProper_of_not_isZero_rightDerived (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {U : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] (F : U.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (d : ℕ) (h : ¬ IsZero (((moduleGlobalSections U).rightDerived d).obj F)) :
    (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim U ∧ (topologicalKrullDim U = d → IsProper f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Lichtenbaum.tfae_isZero_cohomologyOverField
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G5F].** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a field `k`, of
dimension `d` (so `X` is nonempty). The following are equivalent:

1. `H^d(X, F) = 0` for all coherent `𝒪_X`-modules `F`,
2. `H^d(X, F) = 0` for all quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules `F`, and
3. no irreducible component `X' ⊆ X` of dimension `d`, viewed as an integral closed subscheme
   through its reduced induced structure, is proper over `k`.

Here `H^d(X, F)` is the `k`-vector space `AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverField k f F d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isZero_cohomologyOverField (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d) :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent], IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f F d),
       ∀ (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent], IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f F d),
       ∀ Z : irreducibleComponents X,
        let C := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (X := X)
          ⟨Z.1, isClosed_of_mem_irreducibleComponents Z.1 Z.2⟩
        topologicalKrullDim C.subscheme = d → ¬ IsProper (C.subschemeι ≫ f)]

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5G, the first canonical map.** The canonical map
`b^*Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ Ω^a_{L/S}` of the commutative square

```
L → X
↓   ↓
S = S
```

attached to the coordinate blowup; this is the general construction of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialFormsMap`, that is, of Section 50.2 of the
source.

This is the **first** of the two canonical maps asserted by Stacks 0G5G, in that tag's own
Situation: `coordinateAmbient` is the tag's `X`, `coordinateBlowup` is the tag's global `L`,
and the affine blowup charts `A[I/yᵢ]` enter only in the proof of the second map. The second
map and the identification of the composite are not available yet, so only this clause of the
tag is claimed here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def blowupFormsPullbackMap (a : ℕ) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (coordinateBlowupToAmbient R m n)).obj
        (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (coordinateAmbientToBase R m n) a) ⟶
      Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (coordinateBlowupToBase R m n) a
declarations.comment: the first canonical map b^*Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ Ω^a_{L/S}

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsTwistedComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5G, the second canonical map.** The map
`Ω^a_{L/S} ⟶ b^*Ω^a_{X/S} ⊗_{𝒪_L} 𝒪_L((n-1)E)`.

This is `Stacks.Divisors.twistedRetraction` at the effective Cartier divisor `(n-1)E` and the
monomorphism `Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsPullbackMap`: the pole bound
`Stacks.DeRham.exceptionalPoleBound` says that `ℐ_{(n-1)E} · Ω^a_{L/S} ⊆ b^*Ω^a_{X/S}`, which
lets the ideal sheaf act on `Ω^a_{L/S}` with values in `b^*Ω^a_{X/S}`, and untwisting that action
by the evaluation pairing of `𝒪_L((n-1)E)` with `ℐ_{(n-1)E}` gives a map into the twist.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def blowupFormsTwistedComparison (a : ℕ) :
    Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (coordinateBlowupToBase R m n) a ⟶
      blowupFormsExceptionalTwist R m n a
declarations.comment: the second canonical map Ω^a_{L/S} ⟶ b^*Ω^a_{X/S} ⊗_{𝒪_L} 𝒪_L((n-1)E)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsPullbackMap_comp_twistedComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5G, the composite of the two canonical maps.** The composite of
`Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsPullbackMap` with `Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsTwistedComparison` is the
map induced by the inclusion `𝒪_L ⊆ 𝒪_L((n-1)E)`.

That induced map is `Stacks.DeRham.blowupFormsCanonicalSection`, multiplication by the canonical
section of `𝒪_L((n-1)E)`; the identity is `Stacks.Divisors.comp_twistedRetraction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowupFormsPullbackMap_comp_twistedComparison (a : ℕ) :
    blowupFormsPullbackMap R m n a ≫ blowupFormsTwistedComparison R m n a =
      blowupFormsCanonicalSection R m n a
declarations.comment: the composite of the two maps is induced by the inclusion 𝒪_L ⊆ 𝒪_L((n-1)E)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.isIso_coordinateBlowupTwistDerivedMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5H.** Let `b : L ⟶ X = 𝐀^{m+n}_R` be the blowing up of affine space
along the coordinate subspace `𝐀^m_R`, `n ≥ 1`, with exceptional divisor `E`. For every locally
free `𝒪_X`-module `ℰ`, of any rank, and every `0 ≤ i ≤ n - 1` the canonical map
`ℰ ⟶ Rb_*(b^*ℰ ⊗ 𝒪_L(iE))` is an isomorphism in `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coordinateBlowupTwistDerivedMap (hn : 1 ≤ n) (i : ℕ) (hi : i ≤ n - 1)
    (E : (coordinateAmbient R m n).Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.{u, u, u} E] :
    IsIso (TwistDerived.twistDerivedMap (coordinateBlowupToAmbient R m n)
      (coordinateExceptional R m n ^ i) E)

declarations.name: Stacks.RegularSequence.subsingleton_ext_pushforward_of_isRegularClosedImmersionOfCodim
declarations.doc:
Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes which is regular of codimension `c`, let
`F` be an arbitrary `𝒪_Z`-module and let `E` be a locally free `𝒪_X`-module. Then
`Ext^q_{𝒪_X}(i_*F, E) = 0` for every `q < c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_ext_pushforward_of_isRegularClosedImmersionOfCodim {Z X : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (c : ℕ) (hi : IsRegularClosedImmersionOfCodim i c)
    (F : Z.Modules) (E : X.Modules) (hE : Scheme.Modules.IsLocallyFree E)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : q < c) :
    Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj F) E q)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.existsUnique_blowUpFormsRetraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5J**, granted its two inputs.  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth, let
`I` cut out a closed subscheme of `X` smooth over `S`, and let `b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of
`X` along it.  For `a ≥ 0` there is exactly one arrow `Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ Ω^a_{X/S}` in `D(𝒪_X)`
whose composition with the canonical `Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S}` is the identity, provided:

* `hcone`:  the third term `Z` of a distinguished triangle on the canonical map admits no
  nonzero morphism to `Ω^a_{X/S}`.  This is the hypothesis discharged in the source by
  [Stacks, Tag 0FUU] part (3), [Stacks, Tag 0E7D] and [Stacks, Tag 0G5I].
* `hv`:  an invertible factorization of the canonical map.  This is the hypothesis discharged in
  the source by the twist isomorphism of [Stacks, Tags 0G5G and 0G5H].

The two smoothness hypotheses are those of the setting of [Stacks, Tag 0FUT] and are not used by
the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_blowUpFormsRetraction [Smooth f] [Smooth (I.subschemeι ≫ f)] (a : ℕ)
    {Z : DerivedCategory X.Modules}
    {p : blowUpFormsObj f I (a : ℤ) ⟶ Z} {q : Z ⟶ (formsSingle f (a : ℤ))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (hT : Triangle.mk (blowUpFormsDerivedDirectImage f I (a : ℤ)) p q ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (hcone : ∀ g : Z ⟶ formsSingle f (a : ℤ), g = 0)
    {D : DerivedCategory X.Modules} (v : blowUpFormsObj f I (a : ℤ) ⟶ D)
    (hv : IsIso (blowUpFormsDerivedDirectImage f I (a : ℤ) ≫ v)) :
    ∃! r : blowUpFormsObj f I (a : ℤ) ⟶ formsSingle f (a : ℤ),
      blowUpFormsDerivedDirectImage f I (a : ℤ) ≫ r = 𝟙 (formsSingle f (a : ℤ))
declarations.comment: both clauses reduced to the two inputs the source uses, for the canonical map Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} in D(𝒪_X) constructed here. NOT proved: either input. `hcone` is the source's Tag 0FUU (3) + 0E7D + 0G5I vanishing, and Tag 0FUU is not proved here; `hv` is its twist isomorphism of Tags 0G5G and 0G5H, proved only for the coordinate model

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.existsUnique_blowUpFormsRetraction_blowUpToBase
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G5J], in corrected form.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be smooth, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a
closed immersion with `Z` smooth over `S` and with image of empty interior in `X`, and let
`b : X' ⟶ X` be the blowing up of `X` along `Z`.  For every `a ≥ 0` there is exactly one arrow
`Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ Ω^a_{X/S}` in `D(𝒪_X)` whose composite with the canonical map
`Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S}` is the identity.

The hypothesis on the interior corrects the source: for `S = X = Z = Spec k` the blowup is empty
and `𝒪_X ⟶ 0` has no retraction
(`Stacks.DeRham.exists_smooth_not_isIso_formsDirectImageComparison_blowUpToBase`,
`Stacks.DeRham.isEmpty_blowUp_bot`).  The proof is the source's.  Existence: the canonical map
followed by `Rb_*` of the second map of [Stacks, Tag 0G5G] is the twist map of
[Stacks, Tag 0G5H] for `𝒟 = Σ_c (c - 1)E_c`, an isomorphism.  Uniqueness: by
[Stacks, Tag 0FUU] (3) the higher direct images are pushed forward from the centre, and
[Stacks, Tags 0E7D and 0G5I] kill every map from the cone to `Ω^a_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_blowUpFormsRetraction_blowUpToBase [IsClosedImmersion i] [Smooth f]
    [Smooth (i ≫ f)] (hint : interior (Set.range i.base) = ∅) (a : ℕ) :
    ∃! r : blowUpFormsObj f i.ker (a : ℤ) ⟶ formsSingle f (a : ℤ),
      blowUpFormsDerivedDirectImage f i.ker (a : ℤ) ≫ r = 𝟙 (formsSingle f (a : ℤ))
declarations.comment: corrected form: for f smooth and i : Z ⟶ X a closed immersion of a scheme smooth over S whose image has EMPTY INTERIOR in X, and b = blowUpToBase i.ker, for every a ≥ 0 there is a unique arrow Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} ⟶ Ω^a_{X/S} in D(𝒪_X) whose composite with the canonical Ω^a_{X/S} ⟶ Rb_*Ω^a_{X'/S} is the identity. The interior hypothesis is a correction: as stated the lemma is false when Z contains a nonempty open of X — for S = X = Z = Spec k the blowup is empty (Stacks.DeRham.isEmpty_blowUp_bot) and 𝒪_X ⟶ 0 has no retraction (counterexample of 0FUU: Stacks.DeRham.exists_smooth_not_isIso_formsDirectImageComparison_blowUpToBase)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.iterate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5M**.
The `n`-fold composite `Y ∘ … ∘ Y` of an endofunctor `Y : C ⥤ C` with itself, with
`Y.iterate 0 = 𝟭 C` and `Y.iterate (n + 1) = Y.iterate n ⋙ Y`, so that the copy of `Y` added at
each step is the outermost one. On objects it is the `n`-fold iterate of `Y.obj`, whence the name.
Godement's `X_n`, a composite of `n + 1` copies of `Y`, is `Y.iterate (n + 1)`, and his `X_{-1}` is
`Y.iterate 0`.
declarations.statement: public def iterate (Y : C ⥤ C) : ℕ → C ⥤ C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.iterate_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5M**.
The powers of an endofunctor are additive: `Y^{m+n} = Y^m ∘ Y^n` in `⋙`-order, i.e.
`Y.iterate (m + n) = Y.iterate m ⋙ Y.iterate n`. This is the observation `X_{n+m+1} = X_n ∘ X_m`,
where `X_n = Y.iterate (n + 1)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iterate_add (Y : C ⥤ C) (m n : ℕ) :
    Y.iterate (m + n) = Y.iterate m ⋙ Y.iterate n

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Godement.face
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5M**.
The face `d^n_j : X_n ⟶ X_{n-1}` attached to a transformation `d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C`, for `n ≥ 0` and
`0 ≤ j ≤ n`: it whiskers `d` into the `j`-th of the `n + 1` copies of `Y` in
`X_n = Y.iterate (n + 1)`, counted from the left, i.e. from the outside, so that
`d^n_j = 1_{X_{j-1}} ⋆ d ⋆ 1_{X_{n-j-1}}`. It is defined by the recursion `d^n_0 = d ⋆ 1_{X_{n-1}}`
and `d^{n+1}_{j+1} = 1_Y ⋆ d^n_j`; in particular `face d 0 0 = d : X_0 = Y ⟶ 𝟭 C` is the
augmentation. No compatibility between `d` and a comultiplication is assumed.
declarations.statement:
public def face (d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C) :
    (n : ℕ) → Fin (n + 1) → (Y.iterate (n + 1) ⟶ Y.iterate n)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Godement.degeneracy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5M**.
The degeneracy `s^n_j : X_n ⟶ X_{n+1}` attached to a transformation `s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y`, for `n ≥ 0`
and `0 ≤ j ≤ n`: it whiskers `s` into the `j`-th of the `n + 1` copies of `Y` in
`X_n = Y.iterate (n + 1)`, counted from the left, i.e. from the outside, so that
`s^n_j = 1_{X_{j-1}} ⋆ s ⋆ 1_{X_{n-j-1}}`. It is defined by the recursion `s^n_0 = s ⋆ 1_{X_{n-1}}`
and `s^{n+1}_{j+1} = 1_Y ⋆ s^n_j`. No compatibility between `s` and a counit is assumed.
declarations.statement:
public def degeneracy (s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y) :
    (n : ℕ) → Fin (n + 1) → (Y.iterate (n + 1) ⟶ Y.iterate (n + 2))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Godement.exists_augmented_standardResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5N**.
Let `Y : C ⥤ C` be an endofunctor with transformations `d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C` and `s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y` satisfying
the counit identities `1_Y = (d ⋆ 1_Y) ∘ s = (1_Y ⋆ d) ∘ s` and coassociativity
`(s ⋆ 1_Y) ∘ s = (1_Y ⋆ s) ∘ s`, i.e. let `(Y, d, s)` be a comonad on `C`. Then the powers
`X_n = Y.iterate (n + 1)`, with the faces `Godement.face d` and the degeneracies
`Godement.degeneracy s`, are a simplicial object of the category `C ⥤ C` of endofunctors of `C`,
augmented over `X_{-1} = Y.iterate 0 = 𝟭 C` by `face d 0 0 = d : X_0 = Y ⟶ 𝟭 C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_augmented_standardResolution {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {Y : C ⥤ C}
    (d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C) (s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y)
    (left_counit : s ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft Y d = 𝟙 Y)
    (right_counit : s ≫ Functor.whiskerRight d Y = 𝟙 Y)
    (coassoc : s ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft Y s = s ≫ Functor.whiskerRight s Y) :
    ∃ (X : SimplicialObject.Augmented (C ⥤ C))
      (h : ∀ n : ℕ, X.left.obj (op ⦋n⦌) = Y.iterate (n + 1)) (hX : X.right = 𝟭 C),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)),
        X.left.δ j = eqToHom (h (n + 1)) ≫ face d (n + 1) j ≫ eqToHom (h n).symm) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)),
        X.left.σ j = eqToHom (h n) ≫ degeneracy s n j ≫ eqToHom (h (n + 1)).symm) ∧
      X.hom.app (op ⦋0⦌) = eqToHom (h 0) ≫ face d 0 0 ≫ eqToHom hX.symm

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Godement.exists_augmented_standardResolution_whisker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5P**.
Let `Y : C ⥤ C` be an endofunctor with transformations `d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C` and `s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y` satisfying
the counit identities `1_Y = (d ⋆ 1_Y) ∘ s = (1_Y ⋆ d) ∘ s` and coassociativity
`(s ⋆ 1_Y) ∘ s = (1_Y ⋆ s) ∘ s`, i.e. let `(Y, d, s)` be a comonad on `C`, and let `F : A ⥤ C` and
`G : C ⥤ B` be functors. Then the conjugated powers `G ∘ X_n ∘ F = F ⋙ Y.iterate (n+1) ⋙ G`, with
the faces `1_G ⋆ d^n_j ⋆ 1_F` and degeneracies `1_G ⋆ s^n_j ⋆ 1_F` obtained from `Godement.face d`
and `Godement.degeneracy s` by whiskering with `F` and `G`, are a simplicial object of the category
`A ⥤ B` of functors from `A` to `B`, augmented over `G ∘ F = F ⋙ G` by `1_G ⋆ d ⋆ 1_F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_augmented_standardResolution_whisker
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B]
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {Y : C ⥤ C}
    (d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C) (s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y) (F : A ⥤ C) (G : C ⥤ B)
    (left_counit : s ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft Y d = 𝟙 Y)
    (right_counit : s ≫ Functor.whiskerRight d Y = 𝟙 Y)
    (coassoc : s ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft Y s = s ≫ Functor.whiskerRight s Y) :
    ∃ (X : SimplicialObject.Augmented (A ⥤ B))
      (h : ∀ n : ℕ, X.left.obj (op ⦋n⦌) = F ⋙ Y.iterate (n + 1) ⋙ G)
      (hX : X.right = F ⋙ G),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)),
        X.left.δ j = eqToHom (h (n + 1)) ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F (face d (n + 1) j)) G ≫
            eqToHom (h n).symm) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)),
        X.left.σ j = eqToHom (h n) ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F (degeneracy s n j)) G ≫
            eqToHom (h (n + 1)).symm) ∧
      X.hom.app (op ⦋0⦌) = eqToHom (h 0) ≫
        Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F (face d 0 0)) G ≫ eqToHom hX.symm

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Augmented.exists_section_of_comp_hom_app_zero_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5Q**.
Let `X` be an augmented simplicial object of `D`, with augmentation
`ε = X.hom : X.left ⟶ const X.right`, and let `h₀ : X.right ⟶ X_0` satisfy `ε_0 ∘ h₀ = 1`. Then
there is a morphism of simplicial objects `h : const X.right ⟶ X.left` restricting to `h₀` in
degree `0` and satisfying `ε ∘ h = 1`; necessarily `h_n = u_n ∘ h₀` with `u_n : X_0 ⟶ X_n` induced
by the unique morphism `⦋n⦌ ⟶ ⦋0⦌`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_section_of_comp_hom_app_zero_eq_id {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D]
    (X : SimplicialObject.Augmented D) (h₀ : X.right ⟶ X.left.obj (op ⦋0⦌))
    (hh₀ : h₀ ≫ X.hom.app (op ⦋0⦌) = 𝟙 X.right) :
    ∃ h : (SimplicialObject.const D).obj X.right ⟶ X.left,
      h.app (op ⦋0⦌) = h₀ ∧ h ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 ((SimplicialObject.const D).obj X.right)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Godement.exists_homotopy_hcomp_hcomp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5R**.
Let `Y : C ⥤ C` be an endofunctor with transformations `d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C` and `s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y`, let `F`,
`F' : A ⥤ C` and `G`, `G' : C ⥤ B` be functors, and let `Z`, `Z'` be the augmented simplicial
objects `G ∘ X ∘ F` and `G' ∘ X ∘ F'` of `A ⥤ B` obtained by conjugating the powers
`X_n = Y.iterate (n + 1)`. Let `(a_n) : G ∘ X ⟶ G' ∘ X` and `(b_n) : X ∘ F ⟶ X ∘ F'` be morphisms
of simplicial objects, i.e. families commuting with the faces `Godement.face d` and degeneracies
`Godement.degeneracy s`, compatible via the augmentations with `a : G ⟶ G'` and `b : F ⟶ F'`. Then
the two horizontal composites `a ⋆ (b_n)` and `(a_n) ⋆ b` are morphisms `Z ⟶ Z'` of augmented
simplicial objects with component `a ⋆ b` over the augmentations, and they are homotopic: there is
a simplicial homotopy from `(a_n) ⋆ b` to `a ⋆ (b_n)`, given by `h_{n, i} = a_{i-1} ⋆ b_{n-i}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_hcomp_hcomp
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B]
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {Y : C ⥤ C}
    (d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C) (s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y) (F F' : A ⥤ C) (G G' : C ⥤ B)
    (a : G ⟶ G') (b : F ⟶ F')
    (an : (n : ℕ) → (Y.iterate (n + 1) ⋙ G ⟶ Y.iterate (n + 1) ⋙ G'))
    (bn : (n : ℕ) → (F ⋙ Y.iterate (n + 1) ⟶ F' ⋙ Y.iterate (n + 1)))
    (han_face : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)),
      an (n + 1) ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (face d (n + 1) j) G' =
        Functor.whiskerRight (face d (n + 1) j) G ≫ an n)
    (han_degeneracy : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)),
      an n ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (degeneracy s n j) G' =
        Functor.whiskerRight (degeneracy s n j) G ≫ an (n + 1))
    (han_aug : an 0 ≫ Functor.whiskerRight (face d 0 0) G' =
      Functor.whiskerRight (face d 0 0) G ≫ a)
    (hbn_face : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)),
      bn (n + 1) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft F' (face d (n + 1) j) =
        Functor.whiskerLeft F (face d (n + 1) j) ≫ bn n)
    (hbn_degeneracy : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)),
      bn n ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft F' (degeneracy s n j) =
        Functor.whiskerLeft F (degeneracy s n j) ≫ bn (n + 1))
    (hbn_aug : bn 0 ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft F' (face d 0 0) =
      Functor.whiskerLeft F (face d 0 0) ≫ b)
    (Z Z' : SimplicialObject.Augmented (A ⥤ B))
    (hZ : ∀ n : ℕ, Z.left.obj (op ⦋n⦌) = F ⋙ Y.iterate (n + 1) ⋙ G)
    (hZr : Z.right = F ⋙ G)
    (hZδ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)), Z.left.δ j = eqToHom (hZ (n + 1)) ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F (face d (n + 1) j)) G ≫ eqToHom (hZ n).symm)
    (hZσ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)), Z.left.σ j = eqToHom (hZ n) ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F (degeneracy s n j)) G ≫
        eqToHom (hZ (n + 1)).symm)
    (hZhom : Z.hom.app (op ⦋0⦌) = eqToHom (hZ 0) ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F (face d 0 0)) G ≫ eqToHom hZr.symm)
    (hZ' : ∀ n : ℕ, Z'.left.obj (op ⦋n⦌) = F' ⋙ Y.iterate (n + 1) ⋙ G')
    (hZr' : Z'.right = F' ⋙ G')
    (hZδ' : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)), Z'.left.δ j = eqToHom (hZ' (n + 1)) ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F' (face d (n + 1) j)) G' ≫ eqToHom (hZ' n).symm)
    (hZσ' : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)), Z'.left.σ j = eqToHom (hZ' n) ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F' (degeneracy s n j)) G' ≫
        eqToHom (hZ' (n + 1)).symm)
    (hZhom' : Z'.hom.app (op ⦋0⦌) = eqToHom (hZ' 0) ≫
      Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.whiskerLeft F' (face d 0 0)) G' ≫ eqToHom hZr'.symm) :
    ∃ α β : Z ⟶ Z',
      (∀ n : ℕ, α.left.app (op ⦋n⦌) = eqToHom (hZ n) ≫
        NatTrans.hcomp (F := F ⋙ Y.iterate (n + 1)) (bn n) a ≫ eqToHom (hZ' n).symm) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, β.left.app (op ⦋n⦌) = eqToHom (hZ n) ≫
        NatTrans.hcomp b (an n) ≫ eqToHom (hZ' n).symm) ∧
      α.right = eqToHom hZr ≫ NatTrans.hcomp b a ≫ eqToHom hZr'.symm ∧
      β.right = eqToHom hZr ≫ NatTrans.hcomp b a ≫ eqToHom hZr'.symm ∧
      Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy β.left α.left)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Godement.exists_homotopy_whiskerLeft_whiskerRight
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5S**.
Let `Y : C ⥤ C` be an endofunctor with transformations `d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C` and `s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y`, and let
`X` be an augmented simplicial object of the category `C ⥤ C` of endofunctors of `C` whose terms
are the powers `X_n = Y.iterate (n + 1)`, whose faces and degeneracies are `Godement.face d` and
`Godement.degeneracy s`, and whose augmentation has target `𝟭 C`. Let `f : 𝟭 C ⟶ 𝟭 C` be an
endomorphism of the identity functor. Then the two whiskerings `f ⋆ 1_{X_n}` and `1_{X_n} ⋆ f` of
`f` onto the terms of `X` are morphisms of simplicial objects, compatible with `f` through the
augmentation `ε : X ⟶ 𝟭 C`, i.e. they are endomorphisms of `X` in the category of augmented
simplicial objects with component `f` over `𝟭 C`. Moreover they are homotopic: there is a
simplicial homotopy from `1_X ⋆ f` to `f ⋆ 1_X`, given by `h_{n, i} = 1_i ⋆ f ⋆ 1_{n + 1 - i}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopy_whiskerLeft_whiskerRight {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {Y : C ⥤ C} (d : Y ⟶ 𝟭 C) (s : Y ⟶ Y ⋙ Y) (f : 𝟭 C ⟶ 𝟭 C)
    (X : SimplicialObject.Augmented (C ⥤ C))
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ, X.left.obj (op ⦋n⦌) = Y.iterate (n + 1)) (hX : X.right = 𝟭 C)
    (hδ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)),
      X.left.δ j = eqToHom (h (n + 1)) ≫ face d (n + 1) j ≫ eqToHom (h n).symm)
    (hσ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 1)),
      X.left.σ j = eqToHom (h n) ≫ degeneracy s n j ≫ eqToHom (h (n + 1)).symm) :
    ∃ α β : X ⟶ X,
      (∀ n : ℕ, α.left.app (op ⦋n⦌) =
        eqToHom (h n) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft (Y.iterate (n + 1)) f ≫ eqToHom (h n).symm) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, β.left.app (op ⦋n⦌) =
        eqToHom (h n) ≫ Functor.whiskerRight f (Y.iterate (n + 1)) ≫ eqToHom (h n).symm) ∧
      α.right = eqToHom hX ≫ f ≫ eqToHom hX.symm ∧
      β.right = eqToHom hX ≫ f ≫ eqToHom hX.symm ∧
      Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy β.left α.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicTopology.homotopyEquivalences_forget_iff_quasiIso_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5T**.
Let `R` be a ring and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of simplicial `R`-modules which is surjective
in each degree. Then the underlying morphism of simplicial sets `X ⋙ forget ⟶ Y ⋙ forget` is a
homotopy equivalence — it admits a morphism of simplicial sets back whose two composites with it
are homotopic to the identities — if and only if the induced morphism `s(X) ⟶ s(Y)` of associated
chain complexes of `R`-modules is a quasi-isomorphism. Applied to the augmentation `X(M) ⟶ M` of
the standard resolution of an `R`-module `M` by free modules, whose underlying augmentation of
simplicial sets is a homotopy equivalence, this says that `M` is the only nonzero homology group of
the complex associated to `X(M)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyEquivalences_forget_iff_quasiIso_of_surjective {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {X Y : SimplicialObject (ModuleCat.{v} R)} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective (f.app n).hom) :
    SimplicialObject.homotopyEquivalences (Type v)
        (Functor.whiskerRight f (forget (ModuleCat.{v} R))) ↔
      QuasiIso ((alternatingFaceMapComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R)).map f)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.free_standardResolution_face_degeneracy_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5U**.
Let `R` be a ring, `M` an `R`-module and `R[N]` the free `R`-module on the underlying set of an
`R`-module `N`, with `[n] = ModuleCat.comonadMk n` and `∑ᵢ f nᵢ rᵢ = ModuleCat.comonadSum ξ f` for
`ξ = ∑ᵢ rᵢ[nᵢ]`. For the simplicial `R`-module `X(M)` with `X₁(M) = R[R[M]]` and
`X₂(M) = R[R[R[M]]]`, and a typical element `ξ = ∑ᵢ rᵢ[∑ⱼ r_ij[m_ij]]` of `X₁(M)`, the two faces
`d₀, d₁ : R[R[M]] → R[M]` — the counit of the free-forgetful adjunction contracting the outer,
resp. the inner, bracket — are given by `d₀(ξ) = ∑_{i,j} rᵢr_ij[m_ij]` and
`d₁(ξ) = ∑ᵢ rᵢ[∑ⱼ r_ij m_ij]`, and the two degeneracies `s₀, s₁ : R[R[M]] → R[R[R[M]]]` — its
comultiplication doubling the outer, resp. the inner, bracket — by `s₀(ξ) = ∑ᵢ rᵢ[[∑ⱼ r_ij[m_ij]]]`
and `s₁(ξ) = ∑ᵢ rᵢ[∑ⱼ r_ij[[m_ij]]]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem free_standardResolution_face_degeneracy_apply {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (ξ : ((adj R).toComonad.obj ((adj R).toComonad.obj M) : Type u)) :
    (adj R).toComonad.ε.app ((adj R).toComonad.obj M) ξ = comonadSum ξ (fun x r => r • x) ∧
      (adj R).toComonad.map ((adj R).toComonad.ε.app M) ξ =
        comonadSum ξ (fun x r => r • comonadMk (comonadSum x (fun m c => c • m))) ∧
      (adj R).toComonad.δ.app ((adj R).toComonad.obj M) ξ =
        comonadSum ξ (fun x r => r • comonadMk (comonadMk x)) ∧
      (adj R).toComonad.map ((adj R).toComonad.δ.app M) ξ =
        comonadSum ξ (fun x r =>
          r • comonadMk (comonadSum x (fun m c => c • comonadMk (comonadMk m))))

declarations.name: PrincipalCompletionNilpotent.isAdicComplete_of_isReduced_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G5V.** A reduced commutative ring which is derived complete with respect to a
finitely generated ideal is adically complete with respect to that ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicComplete_of_isReduced_of_isDerivedComplete
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsReduced A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_nat
    IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A A) → IsAdicComplete I A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openProjAlgebra
declarations.doc: The subalgebra of `A[T]` generated by `A` and all `f Tⁿ` with `D(f) ⊆ U`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def openProjAlgebra (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) :
    Subalgebra A (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) A)
declarations.comment: the graded subring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openProjGrading
declarations.doc: The degree-`n` piece of the indicated subalgebra, inherited from polynomial degree.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def openProjGrading (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) (n : ℕ) :
    Submodule A (openProjAlgebra U)
declarations.comment: the homogeneous components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openProjGradedRing
declarations.doc: The polynomial-degree decomposition restricts to the algebra of the open.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def openProjGradedRing (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) :
    GradedRing (openProjGrading U)
declarations.comment: the grading

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openProjDegreeZeroEquiv
declarations.doc: The canonical identification of the degree-zero part with the coefficient ring.
declarations.comment: the degree-zero ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openProjDegreeZeroEquiv_apply
declarations.doc: The degree-zero identification sends a coefficient to its image in the subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem openProjDegreeZeroEquiv_apply (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) (a : A) :
    letI := openProjGradedRing U
    ((openProjDegreeZeroEquiv U a : openProjGrading U 0) : openProjAlgebra U) =
      algebraMap A (openProjAlgebra U) a
declarations.comment: the canonical degree-zero identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projOpenIso
declarations.doc: The projective spectrum of the indicated algebra is the chosen open subscheme.
declarations.comment: the isomorphism with the open subscheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.projOpenIso_hom_comp
declarations.doc: Under the isomorphism, the canonical morphism to `Spec A` is inclusion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem projOpenIso_hom_comp (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) :
    letI := openProjGradedRing U
    Proj.toSpecZero (openProjGrading U) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (openProjDegreeZeroEquiv U).toRingHom) =
        (projOpenIso U).hom ≫ U.ι
declarations.comment: compatibility with the structure morphism

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_homotopy_frobeniusEndo_squareEndo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G5Y.** Let `A → B` be a ring map with `p = 0` in `A` for a prime `p`,
and let `P_•` be the standard resolution of `B` over `A`. The endomorphism of `P_•` induced by
the commutative square of Frobenius maps `F_A` and `F_B` is homotopic to the endomorphism given
by Frobenius on each term `P_n`. The homotopy produced here runs from the termwise Frobenius to
the square-induced map; the source states the relation without an orientation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_homotopy_frobeniusEndo_squareEndo (hp : p.Prime) (A : Type u)
    [CommRing A] (B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A) (hA : (p : A) = 0) :
    Nonempty (SimplicialObject.Homotopy
      (frobeniusEndo.{u, v} p hp A B hA) (squareEndo.{u, v} p hp A B hA))

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.nonempty_homotopy_squareCotangentComplexMap_frobeniusSquare
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime, let `A → B` be a ring map with `p = 0` in `A`, and let `F_A` and `F_B` be
the Frobenius endomorphisms. The endomorphism of the cotangent complex `L_{B/A}` induced by the
commutative square `(F_A, F_B)` — the map of Section 08QL, namely the `complexMap` field of
`CommAlgCat.squareFunctoriality` at `CommAlgCat.frobeniusSquare` — is homotopic to zero.

The target is the cotangent complex read over `B` along `F_B`: the induced map is semilinear over
`F_B`, not `B`-linear. Restriction of scalars leaves the underlying complex of abelian groups and
its differentials unchanged, so a null homotopy of this map is a null homotopy of the endomorphism
`L_{B/A} → L_{B/A}`.

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isZero_cotangentComplexDerived_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime number, let `A → B` be a ring homomorphism with `p = 0` in `A`, and assume
that `A` and `B` are perfect. Then `L_{B/A}` is zero in `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_cotangentComplexDerived_of_perfect [PerfectRing A p]
    [PerfectRing (B : Type u) p] :
    IsZero (cotangentComplexDerived.{u, u} A B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.isPrime_iff_eq_infiniteSquareZeroVariableIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G62.** The ideal generated by the square-zero variables is the unique prime ideal
of `S k = k[x₀, x₁, …]/(x₀², x₁², …)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPrime_iff_eq_infiniteSquareZeroVariableIdeal (k : Type*) [Field k]
    (P : Ideal (S k)) : P.IsPrime ↔ P = infiniteSquareZeroVariableIdeal k
declarations.comment: unique_prime

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.uniquePrimeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G62.** The spectrum of `S k = k[x₀, x₁, …]/(x₀², x₁², …)` has exactly one
point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance uniquePrimeSpectrum (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    Unique (PrimeSpectrum (S k))
declarations.comment: singleton_spectrum

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.noetherianSpace_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G62.** The spectrum of `S k = k[x₀, x₁, …]/(x₀², x₁², …)` is a Noetherian
topological space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance noetherianSpace_primeSpectrum (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace (PrimeSpectrum (S k))
declarations.comment: noetherian_underlying_space

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.infiniteSquareZeroVariableIdeal_not_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G62.** The ideal generated by the variables of
`S k = k[x₀, x₁, …]/(x₀², x₁², …)` is not finitely generated; in particular `S k` is not a
Noetherian ring even though its spectrum is a Noetherian space.
declarations.statement:
theorem infiniteSquareZeroVariableIdeal_not_fg (k : Type*) [Field k] :
    ¬ (infiniteSquareZeroVariableIdeal k).FG

declarations.name: ManyMonomial.subalgebra

declarations.name: ManyMonomial.localization_away_x_equiv_laurentPolynomial
declarations.doc: Inverting `x` gives Laurent polynomials in `x` over `k[y]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_away_x_equiv_laurentPolynomial :
    ∃ e : Localization.Away (x k) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial (Polynomial k),
      (∀ c : k,
        e (algebraMap (subalgebra k) (Localization.Away (x k))
          (algebraMap k (subalgebra k) c)) =
        LaurentPolynomial.C (Polynomial.C c)) ∧
      e (algebraMap (subalgebra k) (Localization.Away (x k)) (x k)) =
        LaurentPolynomial.T 1 ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ,
        e (algebraMap (subalgebra k) (Localization.Away (x k))
          (xyPowIn k i)) =
        LaurentPolynomial.T 1 * LaurentPolynomial.C (Polynomial.X ^ i))
declarations.comment: localization description

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.flat_formallyUnramified_adicCompletion_and_not_formallyEtale
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local ring of prime characteristic `p` with
`[κ : κᵖ] < ∞`. Then the canonical map `A → A^∧` to the `𝔪`-adic completion is flat and
formally unramified; if moreover `A` is regular but not excellent, it is not formally étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_formallyUnramified_adicCompletion_and_not_formallyEtale
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    [CharP A p]
    [Module.Finite (frobenius (ResidueField A) (ringExpChar (ResidueField A))).fieldRange
      (ResidueField A)] :
    Module.Flat A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) ∧
      Algebra.FormallyUnramified A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) ∧
      (IsRegularLocalRing A → ¬ IsExcellent A →
        ¬ Algebra.FormallyEtale A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A))

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.formallyEtale_adicCompletion_of_isExcellent
declarations.doc:
The forward implication of Stacks `0G68`: for a regular local ring of characteristic
`p > 0` whose residue field has finite imperfection degree, excellence makes the canonical map
to the maximal-ideal-adic completion formally étale.

This needs none of Lemma `0G66`: excellence makes the map regular, Néron–Popescu writes the
completion as a filtered colimit of smooth algebras, and formal unramifiedness upgrades that to
formal smoothness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallyEtale_adicCompletion_of_isExcellent
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP A p]
    [Module.Finite (frobenius (ResidueField A) (ringExpChar (ResidueField A))).fieldRange
      (ResidueField A)] (excellent : IsExcellent A) :
    Algebra.FormallyEtale A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)
declarations.comment: the forward implication, with no carried hypotheses; see the module docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.isExcellent_iff_formallyEtale_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
A regular local ring of characteristic `p > 0` whose residue field has finite imperfection
degree is excellent if and only if the canonical map to its maximal-ideal-adic completion is
formally étale.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isExcellent_iff_formallyEtale_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsRegularLocalRing A] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP A p]
    [Module.Finite (frobenius (ResidueField A) (ringExpChar (ResidueField A))).fieldRange
      (ResidueField A)] :
    IsExcellent A ↔ Algebra.FormallyEtale A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)
declarations.comment: both directions, with no carried hypotheses

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6A**, second point: a homotopy between maps `f, g` of bicomplexes regarded as
complexes of rows, i.e. between the flipped maps, induces a homotopy between `Tot(f)` and `Tot(g)`;
on the summand `(i₁, i₂)` it is `ε₂ (i₁, c₂.prev i₂) • h.hom i₂ (c₂.prev i₂)`, which for

declarations.statement: noncomputable def totalMapHomotopy₂ : Homotopy (total.map f c₁₂) (total.map g c₁₂)

  homotopic; any shapes

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₂.ιTotal_totalMapHomotopy₂_hom

lemma ιTotal_totalMapHomotopy₂_hom (i₁ : I₁) (i₂ i₂' : I₂) (j j' : I₁₂)

    K.ιTotal c₁₂ i₁ i₂' j hj ≫ (totalMapHomotopy₂ h₂ c₁₂).hom j j' =
      ComplexShape.ε₂ c₁ c₂ c₁₂ (i₁, i₂) • (h₂.hom i₂' i₂).f i₁ ≫ L.ιTotalOrZero c₁₂ i₁ i₂ j'
declarations.comment: the tag's `h'`: `(-1)^p h^{p, q}` on the summand `A^{p, q}`, as `ε₂`

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₂.ιTotal_totalMapHomotopy₁_hom
declarations.doc:
The homotopy `totalMapHomotopy₁ h` on the summand `(i₁', i₂)`: it is `h.hom i₁' i₁` into the
summand `(i₁, i₂)`, `i₁ = c₁.prev i₁'`, up to the sign `ε₁ (i₁, i₂)`; for `ℤ`-cochain shapes this

declarations.statement:
lemma ιTotal_totalMapHomotopy₁_hom (i₁ i₁' : I₁) (i₂ : I₂) (j j' : I₁₂)

      ComplexShape.ε₁ c₁ c₂ c₁₂ (i₁, i₂) • (h.hom i₁' i₁).f i₂ ≫ L.ιTotalOrZero c₁₂ i₁ i₂ j'
