declarations.name: HomotopyCategory.exists_trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**A distinguished triangle of `K(𝒜)` is the triangle of a degreewise split short exact
sequence of complexes, after changing its middle term.** Let `𝒜` be an additive category and
let `(A^•, B, C^•, a, b, c)` be a distinguished triangle of `K(𝒜)` whose outer terms are the
complexes `A^•` and `C^•`. Then there are a complex `(B')^•` and maps `f : A^• ⟶ (B')^•`,
`g : (B')^• ⟶ C^•` with `f ≫ g = 0` whose degreewise evaluations
`0 → A^n → (B')^n → C^n → 0` are split short exact sequences, and an isomorphism
`e : B ≅ (B')^•` in `K(𝒜)` with `a ≫ e = f`, `e ≫ g = b` and such that `c` is the connecting
morphism of the sequence, i.e. `(𝟙, e, 𝟙)` is an isomorphism of distinguished triangles from
`(A^•, B, C^•, a, b, c)` to `(A^•, (B')^•, C^•, f, g, c)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit_of_distinguished
    {𝒜 : Type u} [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Preadditive 𝒜] [HasZeroObject 𝒜] [HasBinaryBiproducts 𝒜]
    {A C : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ} {B : HomotopyCategory 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)}
    (a : (quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj A ⟶ B)
    (b : B ⟶ (quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj C)
    (c : (quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj C ⟶
      ((quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj A)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hT : Triangle.mk a b c ∈ distTriang (HomotopyCategory 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    ∃ (B' : CochainComplex 𝒜 ℤ) (f : A ⟶ B') (g : B' ⟶ C) (w : f ≫ g = 0)
      (σ : ∀ n, ((ShortComplex.mk f g w).map (eval 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting)
      (e : B ≅ (quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj B'),
      a ≫ e.hom = (quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f ∧
        e.hom ≫ (quotient 𝒜 (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map g = b ∧
        c = (trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit (.mk f g w) σ).mor₃

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.bifunctor_homotopy_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**The general reduction (Derived Categories, Remark 13.10.9 / tag 0G6E).**
For additive categories `A, B, D` with `D` having the countable direct sums
needed to form the relevant total complexes, and any functor `F : A ⥤ B ⥤ D`
additive (bilinear on morphisms) in each variable, fixing one complex variable
`G^•` and taking `Tot` of the resulting double complex yields an exact functor of
homotopy categories `K(B) ⥤ K(D)` (here the fixed complex is the LEFT factor).
Statements 1 and 2 are the instances `A = B = D = Mod(O)`, `F = ⊗_O = sheafTensor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bifunctor_homotopy_isTriangulated
    {A B D : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Category D]
    [Preadditive A] [Preadditive B] [Preadditive D]
    [HasZeroObject A] [HasZeroObject B] [HasZeroObject D]
    [HasBinaryBiproducts A] [HasBinaryBiproducts B] [HasBinaryBiproducts D]
    (F : A ⥤ B ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [∀ X, (F.obj X).Additive]
    [∀ (K₁ : HomologicalComplex A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        (K₂ : HomologicalComplex B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)),
        K₁.HasMapBifunctor K₂ F (ComplexShape.up ℤ)]
    (G : HomologicalComplex A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    ∃ (Φ : HomotopyCategory B (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤ HomotopyCategory D (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      (ξ : Φ.CommShift ℤ),
      Φ.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (HomotopyCategory.quotient B (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ Φ ≅
          (F.map₂HomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj G ⋙
            HomotopyCategory.quotient D (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
          (letI := ξ; Φ.IsTriangulated)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.bifunctor_homotopy_flip_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6E (2).** The right-variable version of
`bifunctor_homotopy_isTriangulated`: fixing a complex of `B` and totalizing in the `A`
variable gives an exact functor `K(A) ⟶ K(D)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bifunctor_homotopy_flip_isTriangulated
    {A B D : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Category D]
    [Preadditive A] [Preadditive B] [Preadditive D]
    [HasZeroObject A] [HasZeroObject B] [HasZeroObject D]
    [HasBinaryBiproducts A] [HasBinaryBiproducts B] [HasBinaryBiproducts D]
    (F : A ⥤ B ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [∀ X, (F.obj X).Additive]
    [∀ (K₁ : HomologicalComplex A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        (K₂ : HomologicalComplex B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)),
        K₁.HasMapBifunctor K₂ F (ComplexShape.up ℤ)]
    (G : HomologicalComplex B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    ∃ (Φ : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤
        HomotopyCategory D (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
      (ξ : Φ.CommShift ℤ),
      Φ.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ Φ ≅
          (F.map₂HomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).flip.obj G ⋙
            HomotopyCategory.quotient D (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
          (letI := ξ; Φ.IsTriangulated)

declarations.name: ExtendedAlternatingCech.cechd_comp_cechd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6G**.
For consecutive integer degrees `i, j, k`, the composition `d_{j,k} ∘ d_{i,j}` of the
differentials of the extended alternating Čech complex vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechd_comp_cechd (i j k : ℤ) (hij : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel i j)
    (hjk : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel j k) :
    CategoryStruct.comp (cechd f M i j) (cechd f M j k) = 0

declarations.name: ExtendedCech.termTensorEquiv_comm_d
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Lemma 15.30.2 (Tag 0G6H).** The degreewise canonical isomorphisms
`termTensorEquiv` (induced by `M ⊗_R R_g ≅ M_g`) commute with the Čech
differentials, the differential of `M ⊗_R Č•(R)` being
`id_M ⊗ d_R = LinearMap.lTensor M (Cech.cechD f R p)`.  Together with
`termTensorEquiv` this exhibits the extended alternating Čech complex of `M` as
`M ⊗_R Č•(R)`, an isomorphism of cochain complexes of `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem termTensorEquiv_comm_d (p : ℕ) :
    (termTensorEquiv f M (p + 1)).toLinearMap.comp (cechD f M p)
      = (LinearMap.lTensor M (cechD f R p)).comp (termTensorEquiv f M p).toLinearMap

declarations.name: Stacks.CechBaseChange.exists_cechComplexBaseChange_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6I**.
Let `R → S` be a ring map, `g_i` the image of `f_i` in `S` and `N = S ⊗_R M`. There is an
isomorphism of cochain complexes of `S`-modules `e : C^•(f; M) ⊗_R S ≅ C^•(g; N)` (the
target lifted to the universe of the source) whose degree-`p` component, after lowering
the lift, is `termBaseChangeS f M S p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cechComplexBaseChange_iso :
    ∃ e : cechComplexBaseChange f M S ≅ cechComplexBaseChangeTarget f M S,
      ∀ p : ℕ, ULift.moduleEquiv.toLinearMap.comp (e.hom.f p).hom =
        termBaseChangeS f M S p

declarations.name: Stacks.CechContractible.cechComplex_nullHomotopic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6J**.
If some `f i` is a unit in `R`, then the extended alternating Čech complex of `M` is homotopy
equivalent to `0`: the identity chain map is chain homotopic to the zero chain map.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechComplex_nullHomotopic
    (hunit : ∃ i : Fin r, IsUnit (f i)) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy (𝟙 (cechComplex f M)) 0)

declarations.name: Cech.cechComplex_homology_torsion_support_vanishes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6K.** The cohomology of the extended alternating Čech complex is
concentrated in degrees `0, …, r`; every chosen element acts locally nilpotently
on every cohomology class; its support lies in the common zero locus of the chosen
elements; and all cohomology vanishes when an element of their generated ideal
acts invertibly on the coefficient module.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechComplex_homology_torsion_support_vanishes
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R)
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (q : ℤ) :
    let K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ :=
      (Cech.cechComplex f M).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat
    ((q < 0 ∨ (r : ℤ) < q) → Subsingleton (K.homology q)) ∧
      (∀ (i : Fin r) (x : K.homology q),
        ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ f i ^ n • x = 0) ∧
      Module.support R (K.homology q) ⊆
        PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Ideal.span (Set.range f) : Set R) ∧
      ((∃ g ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range f),
          IsUnit (algebraMap R (Module.End R M) g)) →
        Subsingleton (K.homology q))

declarations.name: Cech.cechComplex_homology_isZero_of_isKoszulRegular
declarations.doc:
The extended alternating Čech complex of a Koszul-regular sequence has zero cohomology in
every degree other than the length of the sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cechComplex_homology_isZero_of_isKoszulRegular
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) (hf : Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f)
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p ≠ r) :
    CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero ((Cech.cechComplex f R).homology p)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.KFlat.exists_kFlat_factorization_up_to_homotopy
declarations.doc:
A morphism from a K-flat complex factors up to homotopy through another K-flat complex
which maps to the target by a quasi-isomorphism. When the source has flat terms, the intermediate
complex can be chosen with flat terms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kFlat_factorization_up_to_homotopy
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ} (a : K ⟶ L)
    (hK : K.KFlat) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (b : K ⟶ N) (c : N ⟶ L),
      N.KFlat ∧
        QuasiIso c ∧
        Nonempty (Homotopy a (b ≫ c)) ∧
        ((∀ n : ℤ, Module.Flat R (K.X n)) → ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Flat R (N.X n))

declarations.name: Stacks.SupportedSectionsCounterexample.exists_epi_not_epi_supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
The functor `H_Z : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_X|_Z)` of sections supported on a closed subset does not
preserve epimorphisms in general: on the two-point Sierpinski space with `Z` the closed point,
the skyscraper at the open point surjects onto the skyscraper at the closed point, `H_Z` of the
source is zero and `H_Z` of the target is not.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_not_epi_supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor_map :
    ∃ (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
      (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (φ : F ⟶ G),
      Epi φ ∧ ¬ Epi ((supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ).map φ)
declarations.comment: H_Z does not preserve epimorphisms in general

declarations.name: Stacks.SupportedSectionsCounterexample.exists_not_preservesFiniteColimits_supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor `H_Z : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_X|_Z)` of sections supported on a closed subset is left
exact
(`Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits`)
but is *not* exact in general: it does not preserve finite colimits, since a functor preserving
finite colimits preserves epimorphisms, which `H_Z` does not.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_preservesFiniteColimits_supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor :
    ∃ (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z),
      ¬ PreservesFiniteColimits (supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ)
declarations.comment: H_Z is not exact in general

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
`H_Z` preserves finite limits. It is right adjoint to pushforward along the inclusion of
`Z` (Stacks 0G6P), and a right adjoint preserves all limits.
declarations.statement:
instance supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ)
declarations.comment: left exactness of H_Z

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedSectionsOnClosedForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6N, abelian compatibility.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X`.
Taking the sections of an `𝒪_X`-module supported on `Z`, realized as a sheaf of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules
on `Z`, and then forgetting the module structure, is the same as forgetting the module structure
first and then taking the sections of the resulting abelian sheaf supported on `Z`, realized as
an abelian sheaf on `Z`. The identification is natural in the `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
def supportedSectionsOnClosedForgetIso (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ ⋙
        _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)) ≅
      _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙
        ClosedImmersionSheaves.supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor Z hZ
declarations.comment: abelian compatibility

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6N.** The functor `H_Z : Mod(𝒪_X) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_X|_Z)` of sections supported on a
closed subset `Z`, realized as a sheaf of modules on `Z`. It is characterised, up to the
natural isomorphism `supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor_comp_modulePushforward_iso`, by the
property that its pushforward to `X` is the supported-sections subsheaf.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X) ⥤
      _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (RingedSpace.inverseImage X
        (ClosedImmersionSheaves.closedSubsetInclusion Z)))
declarations.comment: H_Z as a functor Mod(O_X) ⥤ Mod(O_X|_Z)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.supportedSectionsSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of sections of `F` supported on `Z`, equipped with its canonical inclusion into
`F`. On each open set the inclusion is injective and its range is precisely the set of
sections whose support is contained in `Z ∩ U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def supportedSectionsSheaf {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    Σ G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X),
      {ι : G ⟶ F //
        (∀ U, Function.Injective (ι.val.app U)) ∧
          ∀ (U : (Opens X.carrier)ᵒᵖ) (s : F.val.obj U),
            s ∈ Set.range (ι.val.app U) ↔
              (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleSheafOfModules F).suppSection (unop U) s ⊆
                Z ∩ ((unop U : Opens X.carrier) : Set X.carrier)}
declarations.comment: the sheaf of sections supported on Z

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.supportedSectionsSheafι_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6N.** The sections supported on `Z` form a *submodule* sheaf of `F`: their
inclusion is a monomorphism of sheaves of modules.
declarations.comment: the supported sections form a submodule sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.supportedSectionsSheaf_supp_subset
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0G6N.** The sheaf of sections supported on `Z` is itself supported on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedSectionsSheaf_supp_subset {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleSheafOfModules
      (supportedSectionsSheaf Z F).1).supp ⊆ Z
declarations.comment: the subsheaf is supported on Z

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.hom_to_supportedSectionsSheaf_of_supp_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6N.** Maximality of the subsheaf of sections supported on `Z`: any morphism
into `F` from a sheaf of modules which is supported on `Z` factors through it. The
factorisation is unique because `supportedSectionsSheafι` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_to_supportedSectionsSheaf_of_supp_subset {X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (i : G ⟶ F)
    (hG : (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleSheafOfModules G).supp ⊆ Z) :
    ∃ j : G ⟶ (supportedSectionsSheaf Z F).1,
      j ≫ supportedSectionsSheafι Z F = i
declarations.comment: maximality of the subsheaf among subsheaves supported on Z

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.modulePushforward_supportedSectionsOnClosed_adjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6P.** For a closed subset `Z` of a ringed space `X`, with the restricted
structure sheaf `𝒪_X|_Z`, pushforward of modules along the inclusion `i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ X` is
left adjoint to the functor `H_Z` of sections supported on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforward_supportedSectionsOnClosed_adjunction (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    modulePushforward (RingedSpace.inverseImageProjection X
        (ClosedImmersionSheaves.closedSubsetInclusion Z)) ⊣
      supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatTensor.isFlat_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G6Q.** The tensor product of two flat sheaves of
modules is flat.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFlat_tensor {O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (G F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{z} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hG : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat G)
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat F) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, z, z} O).flip.obj F).obj G)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.shortExact_map_pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G6R.**  Let `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` be a morphism of
ringed topoi and let `0 → F → G → H → 0` be a short exact sequence of sheaves of `O_D`-modules
with `H` a flat `O_D`-module.  Then `0 → f^*F → f^*G → f^*H → 0` is short exact.

The pullback of Stacks 03D6 part (2) is the inverse image of Stacks 03D2 followed by extension
of scalars along `f♯`.  The inverse image is exact (Stacks 04JC) and carries `H` to a flat
`f⁻¹O_D`-module (Stacks 05VD), and extension of scalars keeps a short exact sequence with flat
third term short exact (Stacks 03EX).
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_pullbackModules
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := Y.O) S.X₃) :
    (S.map (f.pullbackModules)).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.exists_shortExact_map_pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G6R.**  For a morphism of ringed topoi
`(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` and a short exact sequence of sheaves of `O_D`-modules
whose final term is flat, the pullback sequence `0 ⟶ f^*F₁ ⟶ f^*F₂ ⟶ f^*F₃ ⟶ 0` is short exact.

The pullback is the one of Stacks 03D6 part (2), `O_C ⊗_{f⁻¹O_D} f⁻¹(-)`.  The composite-is-zero
witness is carried in the statement, so that the statement does not mention preservation of zero
morphisms by the pullback, which is not part of that functor's public interface.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_map_pullbackModules (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (O := Y.O) S.X₃) :
    ∃ h : (f.pullbackModules).map S.f ≫ (f.pullbackModules).map S.g = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk ((f.pullbackModules).map S.f)
        ((f.pullbackModules).map S.g) h).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
morphisms of ringed topoi, with the source ringed topos's site small in the
universe of its sections and the target's section universe equal to the max of its object and
morphism universes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.cechComplex_augment_homotopyEquiv_zero_of_eq
declarations.doc:
If a family of open subsets of `U` contains `U`, its extended Čech complex is homotopy
equivalent to zero. The existential proof is precisely the fact that the canonical augmentation
squares to zero; the resulting augmented complex is independent of that proof by proof
irrelevance.
declarations.statement:
lemma cechComplex_augment_homotopyEquiv_zero_of_eq
    (X : TopCat.{u}) (F : TopCat.Presheaf Ab.{u} X)
    {I : Type u} {U : Opens X} (V : I → Opens X) (hV : ∀ i, V i ≤ U)
    (i : I) (hi : V i = U) :
    ∃ (w : cechAugmentation X F V hV ≫
        ((cechComplexFunctor V).obj F).d 0 1 = 0),
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv
        (((cechComplexFunctor V).obj F).augment
          (cechAugmentation X F V hV) w)
        (HomologicalComplex.zero : CochainComplex Ab.{u} ℕ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.alternatingCechComplex_augment_homotopyEquiv_zero_of_eq
declarations.doc:
If a family of opens contained in `U` contains `U`, its extended alternating Čech complex is
homotopy equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma alternatingCechComplex_augment_homotopyEquiv_zero_of_eq
    (X : TopCat.{u}) (F : TopCat.Presheaf Ab.{w} X)
    {I : Type v} {U : Opens X} (V : I → Opens X) (hV : ∀ i, V i ≤ U)
    (i : I) (hi : V i = U) :
    ∃ (w : alternatingCechAugmentation X F V hV ≫
        (alternatingCechComplex V F).d 0 1 = 0),
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv
        ((alternatingCechComplex V F).augment
          (alternatingCechAugmentation X F V hV) w)
        (HomologicalComplex.zero : CochainComplex Ab.{max v w} ℕ))
declarations.comment: alternating complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.orderedCechComplex_augment_homotopyEquiv_zero_of_eq
declarations.doc:
For any ordering, if a family of opens contained in `U` contains `U`, its extended ordered
Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedCechComplex_augment_homotopyEquiv_zero_of_eq
    (X : TopCat.{u}) (F : TopCat.Presheaf Ab.{w} X)
    {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] {U : Opens X} (V : I → Opens X) (hV : ∀ i, V i ≤ U)
    (i : I) (hi : V i = U) :
    ∃ (w : orderedCechAugmentation X F V hV ≫
        (orderedCechComplex V F).d 0 1 = 0),
      Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv
        ((orderedCechComplex V F).augment
          (orderedCechAugmentation X F V hV) w)
        (HomologicalComplex.zero : CochainComplex Ab.{max v w} ℕ))
declarations.comment: ordered complex

registrations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isKFlat_two_out_of_three
registrations.comment: ringed space case of the ringed site statement

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isKFlat_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0G6V.** A map `a : K^• ⟶ L^•` of complexes of `O`-modules with `K^•` K-flat factors,
up to homotopy, through a K-flat complex `N^•` which maps to `L^•` by a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isKFlat_factorization
    {K L : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ}
    (a : K ⟶ L) (hK : IsKFlat X.O K) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ)
      (b : K ⟶ N) (c : N ⟶ L),
      IsKFlat X.O N ∧ QuasiIso c ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy a (b ≫ c))
declarations.comment: the K-flat factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isKFlat_isFlat_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0G6V, second half.** If in addition the terms of `K^•` are flat `O`-modules, then the
intermediate complex of the factorization can be chosen with flat terms as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isKFlat_isFlat_factorization
    {K L : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ}
    (a : K ⟶ L) (hK : IsKFlat X.O K)
    (hKflat : ∀ i : ℤ,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (K.X i)) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ)
      (b : K ⟶ N) (c : N ⟶ L),
      IsKFlat X.O N ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ,
          AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (N.X i)) ∧
        QuasiIso c ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy a (b ≫ c))
declarations.comment: the factorization with flat terms

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.cupWithClassCanonical
declarations.doc:
**The map `ξ ∪ -` at the canonical global cup product.** For a class `ξ ∈ Hⁱ(X, K)` it is the
morphism

`ξ ∪ - : RΓ(X, M)[-i] ⟶ RΓ(X, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} M)`

in `D(A)` for `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, namely the composition of the identification
`RΓ(X, M)[-i] = A[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(X, M)`, of `ξ ⊗ 1` for the morphism representing `ξ`, and of the
global cup product `μ` of Section 0FKU, `globalCupProductCanonical`.
declarations.statement:
def cupWithClassCanonical (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (i : ℤ) (ξ : ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X) ⟶ cohomologyModule K i) :
    ((baseSections X).obj M)⟦-i⟧ ⟶
      (baseSections X).obj (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M)
declarations.comment: the construction of the map ξ ∪ - : RΓ(X, M)[-i] ⟶ RΓ(X, K ⊗^L M) attached to a class ξ ∈ H^i(X, K), the first clause of the remark, at the global cup product μ of Section 0FKU, `globalCupProductCanonical`, on an arbitrary ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.homologyFromSingle_cupWithClassCanonical
declarations.doc:
On cohomology the map `ξ ∪ -` at the canonical global cup product is the cup product with `ξ`:
for `ξ ∈ Hⁱ(X, K)` and `η ∈ Hʲ(X, M)`, the map `Hⁱ⁺ʲ(ξ ∪ -)` carries the class of `η`, read in
`Hⁱ⁺ʲ(RΓ(X, M)[-i])` through the identifications `A[-i-j] = A[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A A[-j]` and
`A[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(X, M) = RΓ(X, M)[-i]`, to the class of the cup product `ξ ∪ η` in the composition
shape of Section 0FKU and Tag 0FP2.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyFromSingle_cupWithClassCanonical
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (i j : ℤ)
    (ξ : ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X) ⟶ cohomologyModule K i)
    (η : ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X) ⟶ cohomologyModule M j)
    (χ : baseShift X (i + j) ⟶ ((tensorBase X).obj (baseShift X i)).obj (baseShift X j)) :
    DerivedCategory.homologyFromSingleLinearEquiv (ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X))
          (((baseSections X).obj M)⟦-i⟧) (i + j) (baseRing X)
          (χ ≫ ((tensorBase X).obj (baseShift X i)).map (classRepresentative M j η) ≫
            (baseShiftTensorIso X i ((baseSections X).obj M)).hom) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X)) (i + j)).map
          (cupWithClassCanonical X K M i ξ) =
      DerivedCategory.homologyFromSingleLinearEquiv (ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X))
        ((baseSections X).obj (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M)) (i + j)
        (baseRing X)
        (χ ≫ ((tensorBase X).map (classRepresentative K i ξ)).app (baseShift X j) ≫
          ((tensorBase X).obj ((baseSections X).obj K)).map (classRepresentative M j η) ≫
            (globalCupProductCanonical X).app (K, M))
declarations.comment: the second clause of the remark: on cohomology ξ ∪ - is the cup product with ξ, for the global cup product `globalCupProductCanonical`. The cup product of two classes is in the composition shape of Section 0FKU and Tag 0FP2, A[-i-j] ⟶ A[-i] ⊗ᴸ A[-j] ⟶ RΓ(X, K) ⊗ᴸ RΓ(X, M) ⟶ RΓ(X, K ⊗ᴸ M), for every identification χ of A[-i-j] with A[-i] ⊗ᴸ A[-j]

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.homologyFromSingle_cupWithClassCanonical_cupPairing
declarations.doc:
On cohomology, `Hⁱ⁺ʲ(ξ ∪ -)` at the canonical global cup product carries the class of `η` to
`ξ ∪ η` as `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.cupPairing` defines it for the canonical
global cup product, the source's identification `A[-i-j] = A[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A A[-j]` being
`pinnedSplitting`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyFromSingle_cupWithClassCanonical_cupPairing
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (i j : ℤ)
    (ξ : ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X) ⟶ cohomologyModule K i)
    (η : ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X) ⟶ cohomologyModule M j) :
    DerivedCategory.homologyFromSingleLinearEquiv (ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X))
          (((baseSections X).obj M)⟦-i⟧) (i + j) (baseRing X)
          (pinnedSplitting X i j ≫
            ((tensorBase X).obj (baseShift X i)).map (classRepresentative M j η) ≫
              (baseShiftTensorIso X i ((baseSections X).obj M)).hom) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X)) (i + j)).map
          (cupWithClassCanonical X K M i ξ) =
      (λ_ (ModuleCat.of (baseRing X) (baseRing X))).inv ≫ (ξ ⊗ₘ η) ≫
        cupPairing (globalCupProductCanonical X) K M i j
declarations.comment: the second clause of the remark, with the cup product of two classes read against the cohomology-level pairing `cupPairing` of Section 0FKU at the global cup product `globalCupProductCanonical`: the tensoring of classes of Tag 068H followed by H^{i+j}(μ), which is how the source defines ∪. The source's identification A[-i-j] = A[-i] ⊗ᴸ A[-j] is `pinnedSplitting`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LinearCupProductTriangle.linearCupProductMayerVietoris
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6X.**  Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space, `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, and let
`X = U ∪ V` be a union of two open subsets.  For a choice of resolutions of two complexes `K`
and `M` of `𝒪_X`-modules there is a map of distinguished triangles in `D(A)` from the
Mayer--Vietoris triangle of `RΓ(X, K) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(-, M)` to the Mayer--Vietoris triangle of
`RΓ(-, K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} M)` whose three vertical maps are the cup products over `X`, over `U` and
`V`, and over `U ∩ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearCupProductMayerVietoris (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤) :
    cupSourceTriangle U V d hUV ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) ∧
      cupTargetTriangle U V d hUV ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) ∧
        (tensorRepresentative d).map
              (DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverFirstComplex X U V d.inj)) ≫
            derivedCupMiddle U V d =
          derivedCupMap d ⊤ ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverFirstComplex X U V d.tgt) ∧
        (tensorRepresentative d).map
              (DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverSecondComplex X U V d.inj)) ≫
            derivedCupMap d (U ⊓ V) =
          derivedCupMiddle U V d ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverSecondComplex X U V d.tgt) ∧
        cupBoundary U V d hUV ≫
            (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) (1 : ℤ)).map
              (derivedCupMap d ⊤) =
          derivedCupMap d (U ⊓ V) ≫
            DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ (shortExact_cupTarget U V d hUV)
declarations.comment: the map of triangles, with the vertices read on the chosen representatives

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LinearCupProductTriangle.exists_cupData_linearCupProductMayerVietoris
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6X for arbitrary complexes.**  Every complex `K` of `𝒪_X`-modules admits a
quasi-isomorphism into a complex carrying a choice of resolutions, so that the map of
Mayer--Vietoris triangles above exists for every object of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cupData_linearCupProductMayerVietoris (hUV : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    (K M : CochainComplex (Modules X) ℤ) :
    ∃ (K' : CochainComplex (Modules X) ℤ) (e : K ⟶ K') (d : CupData X K' M), QuasiIso e ∧
      cupSourceTriangle U V d hUV ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) ∧
        cupTargetTriangle U V d hUV ∈
            distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) ∧
          (tensorRepresentative d).map
                (DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverFirstComplex X U V d.inj)) ≫
              derivedCupMiddle U V d =
            derivedCupMap d ⊤ ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverFirstComplex X U V d.tgt) ∧
          (tensorRepresentative d).map
                (DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverSecondComplex X U V d.inj)) ≫
              derivedCupMap d (U ⊓ V) =
            derivedCupMiddle U V d ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (coverSecondComplex X U V d.tgt) ∧
          cupBoundary U V d hUV ≫
              (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing X))) (1 : ℤ)).map
                (derivedCupMap d ⊤) =
            derivedCupMap d (U ⊓ V) ≫
              DerivedCategory.triangleOfSESδ (shortExact_cupTarget U V d hUV)
declarations.comment: for arbitrary complexes, after replacing K by a K-injective resolution

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.isKInjective_supportedSectionsOnClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G6Z.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion. If `I` is a K-injective complex of
`𝒪_X`-modules, then the complex `H_Z(I)` of sections supported on `Z` is a K-injective complex
of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules.

theorem isKInjective_supportedSectionsOnClosed (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) (I : CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] :
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor
        X Z hZ).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LocalToGlobalSupport.derivedSectionsWithSupportIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G70.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion.  Then `RΓ(Z, -) ∘ RH_Z = RΓ_Z(X, -)` as functors
`D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X(X))`: for every right derived functor `RΓ(Z, -)` of global sections on `Z` and
every right derived functor `RΓ_Z(X, -)` of global sections supported on `Z`, there is a
canonical natural isomorphism from the composite of `RH_Z` with `RΓ(Z, -)` to `RΓ_Z(X, -)`.  It
is canonical by uniqueness of right derived functors: it is the unique transformation compatible
with the comparisons to the underived functors, by
`derivedSectionsWithSupportIso_hom_fac` together with
`derivedSectionsWithSupportIso_hom_unique`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSectionsWithSupportIso
    [RΓZ'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αΓ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ClosedModuleSheaves X Z) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RΓZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor αZ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ ⋙ RΓZ' ≅ RΓZ

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.LocalToGlobalSupport.derivedSectionsWithSupportIso_hom_fac
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G70, the normalization that makes the isomorphism the canonical one.** The
isomorphism of Stacks 0G70 carries the comparison `localToGlobalUnit` of `RΓ(Z, -) ∘ RH_Z` to
the comparison `αZ` of `RΓ_Z(X, -)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSectionsWithSupportIso_hom_fac
    [RΓZ'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αΓ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ClosedModuleSheaves X Z) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RΓZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor αZ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    localToGlobalUnit X Z hZ RΓZ' αΓ ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh
        (derivedSectionsWithSupportIso X Z hZ RΓZ' αΓ RΓZ αZ).hom =
      αZ
declarations.comment: the comparison is the canonical one
