declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SectionsWithSupport.canonicalSectionsWithSupportTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 0G71.**  Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`U = X ∖ Z`.  The triangle
`RΓ_Z(X, K) ⟶ RΓ(X, K) ⟶ RΓ(U, K) ⟶ RΓ_Z(X, K)[1]`
is distinguished in `D(O_X(X))`, functorially in `K` in `D(O_X)`.  The three functors are
the total right derived functors constructed above, the two forward arrows are the canonical
ones, and the connecting morphism is a natural transformation independent of `K`; nothing is
quantified over.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalSectionsWithSupportTriangle_distinguished
    (K : DerivedModuleSheaves X) :
    canonicalSectionsWithSupportTriangle X Z hZ K ∈ distTriang (DerivedGlobalModules X)
declarations.comment:
the distinguished triangle RΓ_Z(X,K) → RΓ(X,K) → RΓ(U,K) → RΓ_Z(X,K)[1] in
D(O_X(X)), at the three constructed derived functors, functorial for K in D(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SectionsWithSupport.derivedSectionsWithSupportTriangle
declarations.doc:
Derived sections with support, global derived sections, and derived
sections on the open complement form a distinguished triangle, naturally in the object of
the unbounded derived category.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedSectionsWithSupportTriangle
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (RΓZ RΓ RΓU : DerivedModuleSheaves X ⥤ DerivedGlobalModules X)
    (aZ : homotopyToDerived X (sectionsWithSupport X Z hZ) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓZ)
    (aX : homotopyToDerived X
      (SheafOfModules.evaluation (structureSheafRing X) (op ⊤)) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓ)
    (aU : homotopyToDerived X (sectionsOnComplement X Z hZ) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓU)
    [RΓZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor aZ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RΓ.IsRightDerivedFunctor aX
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RΓU.IsRightDerivedFunctor aU
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    SectionsWithSupportTriangleData X RΓZ RΓ RΓU
      (derivedSupportInclusion X Z hZ RΓZ RΓ aZ aX)
      (derivedRestrictionToComplement X Z hZ RΓ RΓU aX aU)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedSupportedSectionsTriangleδ
declarations.doc:
**The connecting map of Stacks 0G72, as a term.** For chosen right derived functors `RH` of
`ℱ ↦ i_* ℋ_Z(ℱ)` and `RJ` of `ℱ ↦ j_*(ℱ|_U)`, this is the natural transformation
`δ : RJ ⟶ RH⟦1⟧` completing the two canonical maps `RH ⟶ 𝟭` and `𝟭 ⟶ RJ` to a distinguished
triangle, by `derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle_distinguished`.

The existence statement `exists_derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle` is this map with the quantifier
in front: the connecting map is constructed by
`Stacks.Cohomology.RestrictionCover.derivedTriangleOfShortExactOnInjectives` as the connecting
map of the short exact sequence of complexes obtained by applying the three functors to the
functorial K-injective resolution, descended along the localization.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedSupportedSectionsTriangleδ :
    RJ ⟶ RH ⋙ shiftFunctor
      (DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (1 : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the connecting morphism δ of the triangle, as a term

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G72.** The triangle of `derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle` is distinguished at every
object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle_distinguished
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle X Z hZ RH RJ aH aJ K ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
declarations.comment: the triangle i_*RℋZ(K) ⟶ K ⟶ Rj_*(K|_U) ⟶ [1] is distinguished

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.exists_derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G72.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and `j : U = X ∖ Z ⟶ X`
the inclusion of the complement.  For arbitrary right derived functors `RH` of
`ℱ ↦ i_* ℋ_Z(ℱ)` and `RJ` of `ℱ ↦ j_*(ℱ|_U)` on the unbounded derived category of
`𝒪_X`-modules, the two canonical maps `RH ⟶ 𝟭` and `𝟭 ⟶ RJ` extend to a connecting map `δ`
making `RH(K) ⟶ K ⟶ RJ(K) ⟶ RH(K)⟦1⟧` a distinguished triangle for every `K`.  All three maps
are natural transformations of functors, so the triangle is functorial in `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedSupportedSectionsTriangle (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (RH RJ : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (aH : (supportedSectionsFunctor X Z).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RH)
    (aJ : (restrictPush (structureSheafRing X) (openComplement Z hZ)).mapHomotopyCategory
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RJ)
    [RH.IsRightDerivedFunctor aH
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RJ.IsRightDerivedFunctor aJ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    ∃ δ : RJ ⟶ RH ⋙ shiftFunctor
        (DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) (1 : ℤ),
      ∀ K, Triangle.mk ((derivedSupportedSectionsToId X Z RH aH).app K)
          ((idToDerivedRestrictPush X Z hZ RJ aJ).app K) (δ.app K) ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.SupportedSections.isZero_derivedSupportedSections_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G73.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`j : (U, 𝒪_X|_U) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion of an open subset with `U ∩ Z = ∅`. Then
`R H_Z(Rj_* K) = 0` for every `K` in `D(𝒪_U)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedSupportedSections_derivedPushforward
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (U : Opens X.carrier)
    (hUZ : (U : Set X.carrier) ∩ Z = ∅)
    (Rj : DerivedCategory
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (αj : (modulePushforward (X.ofRestrict U.isOpenEmbedding)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rj)
    [Rj.IsRightDerivedFunctor αj (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (RH : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (RingedSpace.inverseImage X
        (ClosedImmersionSheaves.closedSubsetInclusion Z)))))
    (αH : (supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RH)
    [RH.IsRightDerivedFunctor αH (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)))) :
    IsZero (RH.obj (Rj.obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.GysinAbelianSquare.pushforwardLocalCohomologyForgetIso
declarations.doc:
The underlying sheaf of abelian groups of `i_*ℋ ⁿ_T(ℱ[0])`, with the local cohomology sheaf
taken as the degree-`n` cohomology sheaf of `R𝓗_T(ℱ[0])` in the unbounded derived category — the
spelling of the target of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.gysinMap` — is the abelian direct image of
the abelian local cohomology sheaf `ℋ ⁿ_T(ℱ_ab)`, naturally in `ℱ`.
declarations.comment: part (2) at the GYSIN MAP'S TARGET: the underlying abelian sheaf of i_*H^n_T(F) is i_*^ab H^n_T(F_ab), naturally in F, which is what lets H^n_T act on a morphism that is additive but not O_X-linear. No hypotheses beyond IsClosed T

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.localCohomologySheafForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G74, part (2): the canonical map.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space
`X`, let `RH` be a right derived functor of the sections supported on `Z` of sheaves of
`𝒪_X`-modules and `RHab` one of the sections supported on `Z` of abelian sheaves. This is the
canonical map `RH_Z(K)_ab ⟶ RH_Z(K_ab)` in `D(Ab(Z))`, natural in `K`, induced through the
universal property of `RH` by the underived comparison of supported sections.

This map is an isomorphism: `isIso_localCohomologySheafForgetComparison_of_isRightDerivedFunctor`
in `UnderlyingAbelianLocalCohomologyInvertible.lean` proves it, for `aHab` the derivation unit of
a right derived functor of abelian supported sections.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologySheafForgetComparison
    [RH.IsRightDerivedFunctor aH
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    RH ⋙ underlyingDerivedSheaf (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)) ⟶
      underlyingDerivedSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙ RHab
declarations.comment: part (2), the canonical map; invertibility is proved in isIso_localCohomologySheafForgetComparison_of_isRightDerivedFunctor

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.localCohomologySheafFunctorForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G74, part (2), on cohomology sheaves in every degree.** Let `Z` be a closed subset
of a ringed space `X` and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules with underlying abelian sheaf
`ℱ_ab`. For every `n : ℕ` the degree-`n` local cohomology sheaf `ℋ ⁿ_Z(ℱ)`, an `𝒪_X|_Z`-module
on `Z`, has underlying abelian sheaf the degree-`n` local cohomology sheaf `ℋ ⁿ_Z(ℱ_ab)` of the
abelian sheaf `ℱ_ab`, naturally in `ℱ`.

Both sides are Mathlib's `ℕ`-indexed `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived`, of supported
sections of `𝒪_X`-modules on the left and of abelian sheaves on the right. This is the statement
a consumer needs in order to let `ℋ ⁿ_Z` act on a morphism of sheaves which is additive but not
`𝒪_X`-linear — a de Rham differential, say: the morphism has no image under the module-level
functor at all, but its underlying morphism of abelian sheaves has one under the abelian functor,
and this isomorphism transports the result back.

The proof passes from each `ℕ`-indexed derived functor to the degree-`n` cohomology of a total
right derived functor on the unbounded derived category, where Stacks 0G74 part (2) applies, and
back again; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologySheafFunctorForgetIso (n : ℕ) :
    localCohomologySheafFunctor X Z hZ n ⋙
        _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)) ≅
      _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙
        ClosedImmersionSheaves.localCohomologySheafFunctor Z hZ n
declarations.comment: part (2) degreewise: ℋ ⁿ_Z(ℱ)_ab ≅ ℋ ⁿ_Z(ℱ_ab)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.isIso_localCohomologySheafForgetComparison_of_isRightDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G74, part (2).** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X`, let `RH` be a
right derived functor of the sections supported on `Z` of sheaves of `𝒪_X`-modules and let
`RHab` be one of the sections supported on `Z` of abelian sheaves. The canonical map

`RH_Z(K)_ab ⟶ RH_Z(K_ab)`

of `localCohomologySheafForgetComparison` is an **isomorphism** in `D(Ab(Z))`, in all degrees.

The proof is the source's. It is enough to check invertibility at the image of a K-injective
complex `K` of `𝒪_X`-modules, and a K-injective resolution of `K` with injective terms has the
same image in the derived category, so one may take the terms of `K` injective. There the
derivation unit of `RH` is invertible because `K` is K-injective, and the transported unit is
invertible by `abelianSupportedUnit_isIso_at_underlying_kInjective` — which is where flasqueness
enters: the underlying abelian sheaf of an injective `𝒪_X`-module is flasque (Stacks 09SX), and
supported sections of a flasque abelian sheaf are the kernel of a *surjection* between sections
over two opens, so `K_ab` computes the derived functor even though it is neither K-injective nor
a complex of injectives. The defining factorization
`localCohomologySheafForgetComparison_fac` then forces the comparison itself to be
invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_localCohomologySheafForgetComparison_of_isRightDerivedFunctor
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (RHab : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (TopCat.of Z)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}))
    (aHab : (abelianSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RHab)
    [RHab.IsRightDerivedFunctor aHab
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
        (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (RH : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z))))
    (aH : (supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RH)
    [RH.IsRightDerivedFunctor aH
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    IsIso (localCohomologySheafForgetComparison X Z hZ RHab aHab RH aH)
declarations.comment: part (2), invertibility of the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.localCohomologySheafFunctorZeroForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G74, part (2), in degree zero.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X`
and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules with underlying abelian sheaf `ℱ_ab`. The degree-zero
local cohomology sheaf `ℋ ⁰_Z(ℱ)`, an `𝒪_X|_Z`-module on `Z`, has underlying abelian sheaf the
degree-zero local cohomology sheaf `ℋ ⁰_Z(ℱ_ab)` of `ℱ_ab`, naturally in `ℱ`.

In degree zero both sides are the supported-sections functor itself, `H_Z` being left exact, so
this is `supportedSectionsOnClosedForgetIso` read through the two degree-zero
identifications.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologySheafFunctorZeroForgetIso (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    localCohomologySheafFunctor X Z hZ 0 ⋙
        _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)) ≅
      _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙
        ClosedImmersionSheaves.localCohomologySheafFunctor Z hZ 0
declarations.comment: part (2) in degree 0 only; the comparison in higher degrees is not proved here, see isIso_localCohomologySheafForgetComparison_of_isRightDerivedFunctor for the derived form

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnderlyingAbelianSectionsWithSupport.sectionsWithSupportForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G74, part (1): the canonical map.**  Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space
`X`, let `RΓZ` be a right derived functor of sections with support in `Z` of sheaves of
`O_X`-modules and `RΓZab` one of sections with support in `Z` of abelian sheaves.  This is the
canonical map `RΓ_Z(X, K) ⟶ RΓ_Z(X, K_ab)` in `D(Ab)`, natural in `K`, induced through the
universal property of `RΓZ` by the underived comparison of sections with support.
declarations.statement:
def sectionsWithSupportForgetComparison
    [RΓZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor aZ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RΓZab.IsRightDerivedFunctor aZab
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (AbelianSheavesOnSpace X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    RΓZ ⋙ underlyingDerivedGlobalModules X ⟶
      underlyingDerivedSheaf (structureSheafRing X) ⋙ RΓZab
declarations.comment: part (1), the canonical map, for given right derived functors of sections with support

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.UnderlyingAbelianSectionsWithSupport.sectionsWithSupportForgetComparison_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G74, part (1).**  Let `(X, O_X)` be a ringed space, `Z ⊆ X` a closed subset and
`K` an object of `D(O_X)` with image `K_ab` in `D(ℤ_X)`.  The canonical map
`RΓ_Z(X, K) ⟶ RΓ_Z(X, K_ab)` is an isomorphism in `D(Ab)`, naturally in `K`.
declarations.statement:
instance sectionsWithSupportForgetComparison_isIso
    [RΓZ.IsRightDerivedFunctor aZ
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleSheaves X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [RΓZab.IsRightDerivedFunctor aZab
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (AbelianSheavesOnSpace X) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    IsIso (sectionsWithSupportForgetComparison X Z hZ RΓZab aZab RΓZ aZ)
declarations.comment: part (1), the map is an isomorphism, for given right derived functors of Gamma_Z

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedTensorMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G75.** For `K` and `M` in `D(𝒪_X)` and `i : Z ⟶ X` the inclusion of
a closed subset, the canonical map `K|_Z ⊗^L_{𝒪_X|_Z} R𝓗_Z(M) ⟶ R𝓗_Z(K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} M)` in
`D(𝒪_X|_Z)`: the map corresponding to `supportedTensorMateMap` under the adjunction
`i_* ⊣ R𝓗_Z` of Tag 0A3B.
declarations.statement:
def supportedTensorMap
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z).sheaf).obj
        ((derivedPullback (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).obj K)).obj
        ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj M) ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `K|_Z ⊗^L R𝓗_Z(M) ⟶ R𝓗_Z(K ⊗^L M)`; not functoriality in either complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedTensorMap_mate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G75.** The adjunction equation characterizing the canonical map:
pushing it forward and composing with the counit of Tag 0A3B gives the displayed composite.
This is what "by adjointness of `i_*` and `R𝓗_Z`" means in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedTensorMap_mate
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (supportedTensorMap X Z hZ K M) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X Z hZ).counit.app
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M) =
      supportedTensorMateMap X Z hZ K M
declarations.comment: the adjunction equation characterizing the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G76.** The cup product of a class `ξ` on `X` with a class `η`
supported on `Z`: restrict `ξ` to `Z`, tensor the two on `Z`, and follow with the map of
Tag 0G75. Reading `W = 𝒪_Z[-a-b]`, `U = 𝒪_X[-a]` and `V = 𝒪_Z[-b]`, and reading morphisms
out of `𝒪_Z[-n]` into `R𝓗_Z(-)` as classes in `H^n_Z(X, -)` by Tag 0G70, this is the source's
`H^a(X, K) × H^b_Z(X, M) ⟶ H^{a+b}_Z(X, K ⊗^L M)`. The source's identification
`𝒪_Z[-a-b] = (𝒪_X[-a])|_Z ⊗^L 𝒪_Z[-b]` is the morphism `χ`.
declarations.comment: the cup product `H^a(X, K) × H^b_Z(X, M) ⟶ H^(a+b)_Z(X, K ⊗^L M)`, as the source's four-step composite over an arbitrary presentation of the three groups by corepresenting objects; the source's own presentation by shifted structure sheaves is `supportedCupProductOfClasses`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedCupProductOfClasses
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G76.** The cup product of a class `ξ ∈ H^a(X, K)` and a class
`η ∈ H^b_Z(X, M) = H^b(Z, R𝓗_Z(M))`, landing in
`H^{a+b}_Z(X, K ⊗^L M) = H^{a+b}(Z, R𝓗_Z(K ⊗^L M))`: restrict `ξ` to `Z`, tensor the two classes
on `Z` and follow with the map of Tag 0G75, after the identification
`𝒪_Z[-a-b] = (𝒪_X[-a])|_Z ⊗^L 𝒪_Z[-b]` of the corepresenting objects.
declarations.statement:
def supportedCupProductOfClasses
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (a b : ℤ)
    (ξ : shiftedStructureSheaf X a ⟶ K)
    (η : shiftedStructureSheaf (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z) b ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj M) :
    shiftedStructureSheaf (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z) (a + b) ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M)
declarations.comment: the cup product `H^a(X, K) × H^b_Z(X, M) ⟶ H^(a+b)_Z(X, K ⊗^L M)` on classes represented by morphisms out of shifted structure sheaves, in the source's degrees

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.forgetSupport_supportedCupProduct_square
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G77.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `(X, 𝒪_X)` and let
`K`, `M` be objects of `D(𝒪_X)`. The square

```
H^a(X, K) × H^b_Z(X, M) -----> H^{a+b}_Z(X, K ⊗^L M)
    |                                  |
    v                                  v
H^a(X, K) × H^b(X, M) -------> H^{a+b}(X, K ⊗^L M)
```

commutes, where the top arrow is the cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0G76], the bottom arrow is the
cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0FP2] and the verticals forget support. A class of `H^a(X, K)` is a
morphism `ξ : 𝒪_X[-a] ⟶ K` and a class of `H^b_Z(X, M) = H^b(Z, R𝓗_Z(M))` is a morphism
`η : 𝒪_Z[-b] ⟶ R𝓗_Z(M)` ([Stacks, Tag 0G70]); forgetting support is precomposition with the
comparison `𝒪_X[-p] ⟶ i_*𝒪_Z[-p]` followed by the counit `i_*R𝓗_Z(-) ⟶ -` of
[Stacks, Tag 0A3B].
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetSupport_supportedCupProduct_square (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) (a b : ℤ) (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (ξ : shiftedUnitObject X a ⟶ K)
    (η : shiftedUnitObject (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z) b ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj M) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    shiftedUnitToPushforward Z (a + b) ≫
        (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (supportedCupProductOfClasses X Z hZ K M a b ξ η) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X Z hZ).counit.app
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M) =
      (shiftedUnitTensorIso X a b).hom ≫
        ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).map ξ).app (shiftedUnitObject X b) ≫
        ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).map
          (shiftedUnitToPushforward Z b ≫
            (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory.map η ≫
            (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X Z hZ).counit.app M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_cohomologySupportedOn
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0G78] is an isomorphism at a complex supported on `Z`.**
If every cohomology sheaf of `K` is supported on `Z` then the adjunction map
`ε_K : i_* R𝓗_Z(K) ⟶ K` is itself an isomorphism, by [Stacks, Tag 0AEF] part (2), so the
hypothesis of `isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_isIso_map_counit` is immediate.

No hypothesis on `f` is used. This is the special case of the invertibility of Tag 0G78 that
the library's Tag 0AEF already supplies, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces; for an open
immersion and an arbitrary `K` see `isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_isOpenImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_cohomologySupportedOn
    (hZ' : IsClosed (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn (structureSheafRing X) Z K) :
    IsIso (supportedPullbackMap f Z hZ hZ' K)
declarations.comment: the canonical map is an isomorphism when K has cohomology sheaves supported on Z, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G78] along an open immersion, unconditionally.**  For an open immersion of
ringed spaces `f : X' ⟶ X`, a closed `Z ⊆ X` and `Z' = f^{-1}(Z)`, the canonical map

`L(f|_{Z'})^* R𝓗_Z(K) ⟶ R𝓗_{Z'}(Lf^* K)`

of [Stacks, Tag 0G78] is an isomorphism for every `K` in `D(𝒪_X)`.

Nothing is assumed beyond `f` being an open immersion and `Z` being closed.  The proof is
`isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_natIso` applied to
`derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosedPullbackNatIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_supportedPullbackMap_of_isOpenImmersion (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (hZ' : IsClosed (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z)
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) hZ'
    IsIso (supportedPullbackMap f Z hZ hZ' K)
declarations.comment: the canonical map is an isomorphism along an open immersion of ringed spaces, unconditionally

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.isIso_supportedPullbackBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G78]: the map of functors of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] is an isomorphism in this
case**, for every object of `D(𝒪_X|_Z)`. The
base-change transformation of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] for the square of the restriction,

`Lf^*(Ri_*M) ⟶ Ri'_*(L(f|_{Z'})^*M)`,

is an isomorphism for every `M`, in particular at `M = R𝓗_Z(K)`.

This is the essential-image half of [Stacks, Tag 0AEF] part (2) applied twice. The base-change
map is, by [Stacks, Tag 08HY]'s adjoint characterization, the unit of `Li'^* ⊣ Ri'_*` at
`Lf^*(Ri_*M)` followed by `Ri'_*` of a composite of three isomorphisms: the two composition
isomorphisms of [Stacks, Tag 0D5S], and the derived counit `Li^*(Ri_*M) ⟶ M`, which is
invertible because `Ri_*` is fully faithful for a closed-subset inclusion. So only the unit is
in question, and the unit of an adjunction with fully faithful right adjoint is invertible
exactly on the essential image of that right adjoint. The source `Lf^*(Ri_*M)` lies there:
`Ri_*M` has its cohomology supported on `Z`, derived pullback carries that to support on
`Z' = f^{-1}(Z)` by `cohomologySupportedOn_derivedPullback`, and [Stacks, Tag 0AEF] part (2)
puts every `Z'`-supported complex in the essential image of `Ri'_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_supportedPullbackBaseChangeMap
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)))) :
    IsIso (supportedPullbackBaseChangeMap f Z M)
declarations.comment: the Remark's own assertion that the map of functors Lf^* i_* -> i'_* L(f|Z')^* of Remark 20.28.3 (Tag 08HY) is an isomorphism in this case, proved for every M in D(O_X|Z), in particular at M = RHZ(K); the source's stalkwise justification is replaced by the essential-image half of Tag 0AEF part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedPullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G78].** Let `f : (X', 𝒪_{X'}) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be a morphism of ringed spaces,
let `Z ⊆ X` be closed and let `Z' = f^{-1}(Z)`. For `K` in `D(𝒪_X)` the canonical map

`L(f|_{Z'})^* R𝓗_Z(K) ⟶ R𝓗_{Z'}(Lf^* K)`

in `D(𝒪_{X'}|_{Z'})`: the map corresponding to `supportedPullbackMateMap` under the adjunction
`i'_* ⊣ R𝓗_{Z'}` of [Stacks, Tag 0A3B] part (1).
declarations.statement:
def supportedPullbackMap (hZ' : IsClosed (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    (derivedPullback (closedSubsetRestriction f Z)).obj
        ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj K) ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) hZ').obj
        ((derivedPullback f).obj K)
declarations.comment: the canonical map and the adjunction equation characterizing it; the invertibility of the base-change transformation of Tag 08HY, which is the stalkwise step of the source, is isIso_supportedPullbackBaseChangeMap above

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedPullbackMap_mate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G78], the adjunction equation characterizing the canonical map.** Pushing the
canonical map forward from `Z'` and composing with the adjunction map
`i'_* R𝓗_{Z'}(Lf^* K) ⟶ Lf^* K` of [Stacks, Tag 0A3B] gives the displayed composite. This is the
unique factorization that the source obtains from part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0AEF].
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPullbackMap_mate (hZ' : IsClosed (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    (modulePushforward
            (closedSubsetInclusion X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (supportedPullbackMap f Z hZ hZ' K) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) hZ').counit.app
          ((derivedPullback f).obj K) =
      supportedPullbackMateMap f Z hZ K
declarations.comment: the factorization of the pulled-back adjunction map through the adjunction map on the preimage

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedPullbackMap_unique
declarations.doc:
The adjunction equation determines the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0G78]: no other
morphism of that type satisfies it. Together with `supportedPullbackMap_mate` this says the map
is the unique solution of the characterization, so the construction is not under-determined.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPullbackMap_unique (hZ' : IsClosed (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (g : (derivedPullback (closedSubsetRestriction f Z)).obj
        ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj K) ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) hZ').obj
        ((derivedPullback f).obj K))
    (hg : (modulePushforward
              (closedSubsetInclusion X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))).mapDerivedCategory.map g ≫
          (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) hZ').counit.app
            ((derivedPullback f).obj K) =
        supportedPullbackMateMap f Z hZ K) :
    g = supportedPullbackMap f Z hZ hZ' K
declarations.comment: the uniqueness the Remark asserts: 'we find that the south-east arrow factors UNIQUELY over the south-west arrow'. This is the half of the universality of Tag 0AEF part (3) that supportedPullbackMap_mate does not state, and it is what makes the canonical map canonical -- neither the zero map nor the negative of it satisfies the characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.supportedPullbackMap_triangle
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G78], the commutative triangle of the source.** Composing the base-change
transformation of [Stacks, Tag 08HY] with the pushforward from `Z'` of the canonical map and the
adjunction map `i'_* R𝓗_{Z'}(Lf^* K) ⟶ Lf^* K` gives the derived pullback along `f` of the
adjunction map `i_* R𝓗_Z(K) ⟶ K`.

This is `supportedPullbackMap_mate` with the inverse of the base-change transformation cleared
from the statement, so it is the triangle of the source read literally: the diagonal arrow out
of `Lf^*(i_* R𝓗_Z(K))` factors through the adjunction map on the preimage.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedPullbackMap_triangle (hZ' : IsClosed (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    supportedPullbackBaseChangeMap f Z ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj K) ≫
          (closedPushforwardComparison X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z)).inv.app _ ≫
          (modulePushforward
              (closedSubsetInclusion X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))).mapDerivedCategory.map
            (supportedPullbackMap f Z hZ hZ' K) ≫
          (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) hZ').counit.app
            ((derivedPullback f).obj K) =
      (derivedPullback f).map ((closedPushforwardComparison X Z).inv.app _) ≫
        (derivedPullback f).map ((derivedPushforwardAdjunction X Z hZ).counit.app K)
declarations.comment: the commutative triangle, with the base-change transformation of Tag 08HY on the left

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.forgetSupport_pullbackSupportedClass_preimage_shiftedUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G79, at the canonical corepresenting objects.** The four groups are
corepresented by the shifted structure sheaves of [Stacks, Tag 0G70] — `𝒪_X[-p]`, `𝒪_{X'}[-p]`,
`𝒪_Z[-p]`, `𝒪_{Z'}[-p]` with `Z' = f^{-1}(Z)` — and the four comparisons between them are the
canonical ones: `ρ`, `ρ'` are `shiftedUnitToPushforward`, and `c`, `d` are the identifications
`Lf^*(𝒪_X[-p]) ≅ 𝒪_{X'}[-p]` of `Stacks.RingedSpace.derivedPullbackShiftedUnitIso`.

Those four identifications agree across the square — that is the
*pseudofunctoriality of the structure-sheaf comparison* of [Stacks, Tag 01CD] with respect to
the composition isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0D5S], in which no derived pushforward, no
base-change transformation of [Stacks, Tag 08HY], no `R𝓗_Z` and no adjunction map occur. It is
proved in degree `0`
(`StacksDraft.UnitPullbackComposition.derivedPullbackCompIsoCanonical_hom_app_singleUnit`), in
an arbitrary degree `p`
(`StacksDraft.UnitPullbackComposition.derivedPullbackCompIsoCanonical_hom_app_shiftedUnit`,
which also needed the first `CategoryTheory.NatTrans.CommShift` for the composition comparison
of [Stacks, Tag 0D5S],
`StacksDraft.UnitPullbackComposition.commShift_derivedPullbackCompComparisonCanonical`), and
around the square in the spelling this statement needs
(`StacksDraft.UnitPullbackComposition.shiftedUnitIso_square_left`), which is what is supplied
below.
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetSupport_pullbackSupportedClass_preimage_shiftedUnit (p : ℤ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (η : shiftedUnitObject (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z) p ⟶
      (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).obj K) :
    shiftedUnitToPushforward (X := X') (closedSubsetPreimage f Z) p ≫
        (modulePushforward
            (closedSubsetInclusion X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z))).mapDerivedCategory.map
          ((derivedPullbackShiftedUnitIso (closedSubsetRestriction f Z) p).inv ≫
            (derivedPullback (closedSubsetRestriction f Z)).map η ≫
            supportedPullbackMap f Z hZ (isClosed_closedSubsetPreimage f Z hZ) K) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X' (closedSubsetPreimage f Z)
            (isClosed_closedSubsetPreimage f Z hZ)).counit.app ((derivedPullback f).obj K) =
      (derivedPullbackShiftedUnitIso f p).inv ≫ (derivedPullback f).map
        (shiftedUnitToPushforward Z p ≫
          (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory.map η ≫
          (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X Z hZ).counit.app K)
declarations.comment: the commuting square for the canonical map of Tag 0G78 itself, at the canonical corepresenting objects: the four groups are corepresented by the shifted structure sheaves of Tag 0G70, the four comparisons between them are the canonical ones, and their agreement across the square -- the pseudofunctoriality of the structure-sheaf comparison of Tag 01CD with respect to the composition isomorphism of derived pullbacks of Tag 0D5S -- is StacksDraft.UnitPullbackComposition.shiftedUnitIso_square_left. The binders are the degree p, the complex K and the class eta, which are the data of a class in H^p_Z(X, K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomEvaluation.tensorMap_pushforwardSheafHomMap_sheafHomEval
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7A.**  For a morphism of ringed spaces `f : (X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y, 𝒪_Y)` and objects
`K, M` of `D(𝒪_X)` the square

`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, M) ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*K ⟶ Rf_*(R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, M) ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} K) ⟶ Rf_*M`,
`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, M) ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*K ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*K, Rf_*M) ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*K ⟶ Rf_*M`

commutes: the map of Stacks 0B69 tensored with the identity of `Rf_*K` followed by the
evaluation on `Y` agrees with the relative cup product of Stacks 0B68 followed by the derived
pushforward of the evaluation on `X`.

That the bijection of Stacks 08DI on `Y` evaluates, which is the content of the square, is
`tensorEquivIsEvaluation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorMap_pushforwardSheafHomMap_sheafHomEval
    (K M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.sheaf))) :
    tensorMap Y (pushforwardSheafHomMap f M K) (𝟙 ((derivedPushforward f).obj K)) ≫
        sheafHomEval Y ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj M) =
      Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedRelativeCupProduct.relativeCupProduct f (sheafHomObj X K M) K ≫
        (derivedPushforward f).map (sheafHomEval X K M)
declarations.comment: the square commutes, for every morphism of ringed spaces f and all K, M; this is the whole of the remark. The source states it for `K, M ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, which is a slip — the diagram applies both `R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}` and `Rf_*` to `K` and `M`, so the arrows type-check only for `K, M ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, and that is the form here

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isKFlat_two_out_of_three
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7B.** In a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves of modules on a ringed
site whose third term has flat terms, if two out of the three complexes are K-flat, so is the
third.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKFlat_two_out_of_three
    (h : (IsKFlat X.O S.X₁ ∧ IsKFlat X.O S.X₂) ∨ (IsKFlat X.O S.X₁ ∧ IsKFlat X.O S.X₃) ∨
      (IsKFlat X.O S.X₂ ∧ IsKFlat X.O S.X₃)) :
    IsKFlat X.O S.X₁ ∧ IsKFlat X.O S.X₂ ∧ IsKFlat X.O S.X₃

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatTwoOutOfThree.kFlat_left_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7B, left complex.**  In a short exact sequence of complexes of `O`-modules whose
right complex has flat terms, K-flatness of the middle and of the right complex implies
K-flatness of the left complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_left_of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) (S.X₃.X i))
    (h₂ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₂) (h₃ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₃)
      :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₁
declarations.comment: left complex

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatTwoOutOfThree.kFlat_middle_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7B, middle complex.**  In a short exact sequence of complexes of `O`-modules
whose right complex has flat terms, K-flatness of the two outer complexes implies K-flatness of
the middle complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_middle_of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) (S.X₃.X i))
    (h₁ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₁) (h₃ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₃)
      :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₂
declarations.comment: middle complex

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatTwoOutOfThree.kFlat_right_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7B, right complex.**  In a short exact sequence of complexes of `O`-modules whose
right complex has flat terms, K-flatness of the left and of the middle complex implies
K-flatness of the right complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_right_of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) (S.X₃.X i))
    (h₁ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₁) (h₂ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₂)
      :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat R S.X₃
declarations.comment: right complex

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatCycles.isFlat_kernel_d_of_kFlat_of_acyclic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0G7C.**  Let `K` be a K-flat, acyclic complex of `O`-modules on a ringed site
whose terms are flat.  Then the kernel of `d^n : K^n ⟶ K^{n + 1}` is a flat `O`-module.

The hypothesis is K-flatness in the sense of Tag 06YN (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat`, which
is `Iff.rfl` to the bifunctor-relative predicate written here).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_kernel_d_of_kFlat_of_acyclic
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, v, w} R)) ℤ)
    (hK : CochainComplex.KFlatBifunctor.KFlat
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} R) K)
    (hacyclic : K.Acyclic)
    (hflat : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R) (K.X i))
    (n : ℤ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{v, u, w, w} (O := R)
      (kernel (K.d n (n + 1)))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isKFlat_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0G6V.** A map `a : K^• ⟶ L^•` of complexes of `O`-modules with `K^•` K-flat factors,
up to homotopy, through a K-flat complex `N^•` which maps to `L^•` by a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isKFlat_factorization
    {K L : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ}
    (a : K ⟶ L) (hK : IsKFlat X.O K) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ)
      (b : K ⟶ N) (c : N ⟶ L),
      IsKFlat X.O N ∧ QuasiIso c ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy a (b ≫ c))
declarations.comment: the K-flat factorization

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isKFlat_isFlat_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0G6V, second half.** If in addition the terms of `K^•` are flat `O`-modules, then the
intermediate complex of the factorization can be chosen with flat terms as well.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isKFlat_isFlat_factorization
    {K L : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ}
    (a : K ⟶ L) (hK : IsKFlat X.O K)
    (hKflat : ∀ i : ℤ,
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (K.X i)) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O)) ℤ)
      (b : K ⟶ N) (c : N ⟶ L),
      IsKFlat X.O N ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ,
          AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.O) (N.X i)) ∧
        QuasiIso c ∧ Nonempty (Homotopy a (b ≫ c))
declarations.comment: the factorization with flat terms

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isFlat_componentModulesRestrictionComplex_X
declarations.doc:
**The flat-terms clause of Stacks 0G7E at `g_n`.** The restriction to a component of a
complex of `O`-modules with flat terms has flat terms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_componentModulesRestrictionComplex_X
    (K : CochainComplex (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules ℤ)
    (hflatK : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
      (O := (S.totalRingedTopos O).O) (K.X i)) (i : ℤ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
      (O := (S.componentRingedTopos O n).O)
      (((S.componentModulesRestrictionComplex O n).obj K).X i)
declarations.comment: the flat-terms clause, for restriction to a simplicial component

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.kFlat_componentModulesRestrictionComplex
declarations.doc:
**The K-flatness clause of Stacks 0G7E at `g_n`.** The restriction to a component of a
K-flat complex of `O`-modules with flat terms is K-flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem kFlat_componentModulesRestrictionComplex
    (K : CochainComplex (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules ℤ)
    (hK : Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat (S.totalRingedTopos O).O K)
    (hflatK : ∀ i : ℤ, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u}
      (O := (S.totalRingedTopos O).O) (K.X i)) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlat.KFlat (S.componentRingedTopos O n).O
      ((S.componentModulesRestrictionComplex O n).obj K)
declarations.comment: the K-flatness clause, for restriction to a simplicial component

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.pullbackModules_preservesZeroMorphisms
declarations.doc:
Pullback of sheaves of modules along a morphism of ringed topoi preserves zero
morphisms: it is a left adjoint by Stacks 03D7, and a left adjoint between categories with
zero morphisms carries zero morphisms to zero morphisms. This is what lets `f^*` be applied
degreewise to a complex of modules, as in Stacks 0G7E.
declarations.statement:
instance pullbackModules_preservesZeroMorphisms (f : RingedToposHom X Y) :
    (f.pullbackModules).PreservesZeroMorphisms
declarations.comment: degreewise pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullback.pullbackTopos_preservesZeroMorphisms
declarations.doc:
Pullback of sheaves of modules preserves zero morphisms, being additive.  This is what
makes the degreewise pullback functor on complexes available.
declarations.statement:
instance pullbackTopos_preservesZeroMorphisms
    (f : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposSiteHom X Y) :
    (show SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) from
        f.pullbackTopos).PreservesZeroMorphisms
declarations.comment: degreewise pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.DerivedPullback.KFlatPullbackOfToposHom.isKFlat_pullbackMapHomotopy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7E for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, on the homotopy category.**
Degreewise pullback along `f` carries the class of K-flat complexes of `O`-modules with flat
terms into the same class for `O'`.

Nothing happens on passage to the homotopy category: the underlying complex of `K(f^*)K` is `f^*`
of the underlying complex of `K`.  The K-flatness clause is `kFlat_pullbackComplex` and the
flat-terms clause is `isFlat_pullbackComplex_X`, i.e. Stacks 05VD alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKFlat_pullbackMapHomotopy (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{w'} (SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction.IsKFlat (Y := Y) K) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackPushforwardAdjunction.IsKFlat (Y := X)
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.pullbackMapHomotopy f).obj K)
declarations.comment: K-flat with flat terms is preserved, for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedQuasicoherent.quasiCoherentSupported_derivedSupportedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7G (1).** Let `X` be a scheme, let `T ⊆ X` be a closed subset whose open
complement `X ∖ T` is retrocompact, and let `i : T → X` be the inclusion. For `E` in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the complex `i_* R𝓗_T(E)` lies in `D_{QCoh, T}(𝒪_X)`: its cohomology sheaves
are quasi-coherent and supported on `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiCoherentSupported_derivedSupportedPushforward (hTc : IsRetrocompact Tᶜ)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) E) :
    Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentSupported X T
      ((derivedSupportedPushforward X.toRingedSpace T hT).obj E)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedQuasicoherent.quasiCoherentSupportedInclusionAdj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7G (2).** Let `X` be a scheme, let `T ⊆ X` be a closed subset whose open
complement is retrocompact, and let `i : T → X` be the inclusion. The functor
`i_* ∘ R𝓗_T : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is right adjoint to the inclusion functor
`D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

The adjunction is the restriction of the ambient adjunction `i_* ⊣ R𝓗_T` of Stacks 0A3B along
the two fully faithful inclusions: on the left `R𝓗_T` identifies `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` with a full
subcategory of `D(𝒪_X|_T)`, because the counit `i_* R𝓗_T(A) ⟶ A` is invertible there, and on
the right `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is a full subcategory of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
def quasiCoherentSupportedInclusionAdj (hTc : IsRetrocompact Tᶜ) :
    quasiCoherentSupportedInclusion X T ⊣ quasiCoherentDerivedSupport X T hT hTc
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme and let `T ⊆ X` be a closed subset such that `X ∖ T` is a retrocompact
open of `X`.  Then for a family `Eᵢ`, `i ∈ I`, of objects of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` we have
`R𝓗_T(⊕ Eᵢ) = ⊕ R𝓗_T(Eᵢ)`: the derived functor `R𝓗_T` of sections supported on `T`, restricted
to `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, preserves `I`-indexed direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed
    (hTc : IsRetrocompact (Tᶜ : Set X)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
      ((quasicoherentDerivedProperty X).ι ⋙
        derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X.toRingedSpace T hT)
declarations.comment: for families indexed by a type of the scheme universe, the only index universe at which `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` has direct sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.acyclic_on_equationsComplement
declarations.doc:
The extended alternating Čech complex is acyclic off the common zero locus
of the global equations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem acyclic_on_equationsComplement
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules) :
    (((Scheme.Modules.pullback (⨆ i, X.basicOpen (f i)).ι).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (data f F).complex).Acyclic

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechLocalCohomology.cohomologySupportedOn_extendedAlternatingCech
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7K**, as a support statement.  The cohomology sheaves of the
extended alternating Čech complex of the equations `f₁, …, f_c` are supported on their common
zero locus: the complex is acyclic on the complement, which is the union of the principal opens
of the equations.

This is the hypothesis under which [Stacks, Tag 0AEF] part (2) applies to the complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologySupportedOn_extendedAlternatingCech :
    AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)
      (equationsClosedSet f)
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((data f F).complex.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat))
declarations.comment: the cohomology sheaves are supported on the common zero locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Cech.extendedCechComplex_acyclic_restrict_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7K for an arbitrary ringed space.** Let `Y` be a ringed space, let
`g 0, …, g (c-1)` be global sections of its structure sheaf, let `Z` be their common zero
locus and let `F` be a sheaf of `𝒪_Y`-modules. Then the extended alternating Čech complex of
`F` for the opens `Y.basicOpen (g i)` restricts to an acyclic complex over `Y ∖ Z`, which is
the open `⨆ i, Y.basicOpen (g i)` by `Stacks.Cech.coe_iSup_basicOpen`.

The proof is `Stacks.Cech.sectionComplex_acyclic`: over an open contained in one of the
`Y.basicOpen (g i)` the complex of sections is the extended ordered Čech complex of a covering
one of whose members is the whole open, hence is contractible by Stacks 0G6T; exactness of a
complex of sheaves of modules is checked on stalks, and every point of `Y ∖ Z` has arbitrarily
small neighbourhoods inside some `Y.basicOpen (g i)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem extendedCechComplex_acyclic_restrict_basicOpen
    (F : OXMod.{u, u} Y) :
    (((restrictModules.{u, u, u} Y (⨆ i, Y.basicOpen (g i))).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
      (extendedCechComplex (fun i => Y.basicOpen (g i)) F)).Acyclic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.augmentation
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the extended alternating Čech complex to its
degree-zero module, in the unbounded derived category.
declarations.statement:
public def augmentation (F : X.Modules) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((data f F).complex.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ⟶
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F
declarations.comment: augmentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.augmentation_natural
declarations.doc: The canonical augmentation is natural in the coefficient module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem augmentation_natural {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map
        (HomologicalComplex.extendMap ((functor f).map φ)
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ≫
      augmentation f G =
      augmentation f F ≫ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ
declarations.comment: augmentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.ExtendedAlternatingCech.Augmentation.augmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7L.** The canonical map from the extended alternating Čech complex
to its coefficient module placed in degree `0`, in the unbounded derived category.
declarations.statement:
public def augmentation (F : X.Modules) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((extendedAlternatingCech f F).complex.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ⟶

declarations.comment: augmentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.ExtendedAlternatingCech.Augmentation.augmentation_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7L.** The canonical augmentation is natural in the coefficient
module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem augmentation_natural {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map
        (HomologicalComplex.extendMap ((extendedAlternatingCechFunctor f).map φ)
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ≫
      augmentation f G =
    augmentation f F ≫ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ
declarations.comment: augmentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.cohomologySupportedOn_cech
declarations.doc:
**The extended alternating Čech complex is supported on the common zero locus.** Every
cohomology sheaf of `𝓕^•` has vanishing stalks outside the common zero locus of the equations,
because `𝓕^•` restricted to the union of the principal opens is acyclic (Stacks 0G7K).

This is the first assertion of Remark 0G7L, `𝓕^• ∈ D_Z(𝒪_X)`: `CohomologySupportedOn` is the
property cutting out `D_Z(𝒪_X)` inside `D(𝒪_X)`, so membership in the supported derived category
*is* this statement, and it is what makes the adjunction of Stacks 0AEF applicable to `𝓕^•` in
the rest of the remark.  The remark deduces it from Stacks 0G7K, whose own carrier is
`cohomologySupportedOn_extendedAlternatingCech`; what is registered here is the deduction, at
the derived-category spelling that the remark's diagram and the comparison
`cechToDerivedSupport` below are stated at.  No hypothesis beyond the remark's is carried: `ℱ`
is an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module and the equations are arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomologySupportedOn_cech :
    AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)
      (equationsClosedSet e)
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((cplx e F).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat))
declarations.comment:
the first assertion of the remark: the cohomology sheaves of 𝓕^• are supported on
the common zero locus, hence 𝓕^• is an object of D_Z(𝒪_X).  Deduced from Stacks 0G7K, stated at
the derived-category spelling the remark's diagram uses, for an arbitrary 𝒪_X-module ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.cechToDerivedSupport
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison of Stacks 0G7L**, `𝓕^• ⟶ i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ)`.

It is the inverse of the counit `i_* R𝓗_T(𝓕^•) ⟶ 𝓕^•`, invertible by
`isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsToId_cech`, followed by `i_* R𝓗_T` applied to the augmentation
`𝓕^• ⟶ ℱ[0]` of Stacks 0G7L.  This is the map whose degree-`c` cohomology sheaf Stacks 0G7Q
uses to define `c_{f₁,…,f_c}`.

As in the source, `ℱ` is an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module: the counit is invertible at `𝓕^•` because
`𝓕^•` is supported on the common zero locus of the equations, which is Stacks 0G7K and holds
for every `ℱ`.  Quasi-coherence enters only later, in Stacks 0G7M, where the *other* leg of the
triangle — `i_* R𝓗_T` applied to the augmentation — is shown to be invertible.
declarations.comment:
the canonical comparison 𝓕^• ⟶ i_*RℋT(ℱ), built from the counit of Stacks 0G72
and the augmentation, for an arbitrary 𝒪_X-module ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.cechToDerivedSupport_comp_derivedSupportedSectionsToId
declarations.doc:
**The commuting triangle of Stacks 0G7L**, in the shape the remark displays:

`𝓕^• ⟶ ℱ`, `𝓕^• ⟶ i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ)` and `i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ) ⟶ ℱ`

commute, the third edge being the counit of Stacks 0G72 at `ℱ[0]`.  So the canonical map
`𝓕^• ⟶ ℱ` of the remark — the augmentation, coming from the equality `𝓕^0 = ℱ` — factors
through `i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ)`, which is what the adjunction of Stacks 0A3B provides and what the remark
asserts.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cechToDerivedSupport_comp_derivedSupportedSectionsToId
    (hTe : equationsClosedSet e ⊆ T) :
    cechToDerivedSupport e F hT hTe ≫
        (supportPushCounit hT).app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F) =
      augmentation e F
declarations.comment:
the commuting triangle 𝓕^• ⟶ ℱ, 𝓕^• ⟶ i_*RℋT(ℱ), i_*RℋT(ℱ) ⟶ ℱ of the remark's
diagram, for an arbitrary 𝒪_X-module ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechComparison.augmentation_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7L.** The augmentations of the two constructions of the extended
alternating Čech complex correspond under the comparison isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem augmentation_eq :
    AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.augmentation f F =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (extendBridge f F).hom ≫
        Stacks.Perfect.ExtendedAlternatingCech.Augmentation.augmentation f F
declarations.comment: the augmentations of the two constructions agree

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.derivedSupportedSectionsToId_single_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The edge `i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ) ⟶ ℱ` of the diagram of Stacks 0G7L is natural in the coefficient
module.**  It is the counit of Stacks 0G72 evaluated at `ℱ[0]`, hence a component of a natural
transformation, so its naturality square is `NatTrans.naturality`; it is stated here because the
remark asserts its diagram functorial in `ℱ`, and that assertion is the naturality of all three
edges.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedSupportedSectionsToId_single_naturality {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T)
    {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    (supportPush hT).map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ) ≫
        (supportPushCounit hT).app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj G) =
      (supportPushCounit hT).app ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ
declarations.comment: functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ, the edge i_*RℋT(ℱ) ⟶ ℱ of the diagram

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.Q_map_extendMap_cplxMap_comp_cechToDerivedSupport
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison `𝓕^• ⟶ i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ)` of Stacks 0G7L is natural in the coefficient
module.**  Both sides become, after the invertible counit of Stacks 0G72, the functor
`i_* R𝓗_T` applied to a naturality square for the augmentation.

This is the second of the three edges of the remark's diagram; with
`Q_map_extendMap_cplxMap_comp_augmentation` for the edge `𝓕^• ⟶ ℱ` and
`derivedSupportedSectionsToId_single_naturality` for the edge `i_* R𝓗_T(ℱ) ⟶ ℱ` it is the
remark's closing clause, that the diagram is "functorial in the `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`".

As in the source, `φ` is a morphism of arbitrary `𝒪_X`-modules: quasi-coherence is nowhere used,
the counit being invertible at the extended alternating Čech complex of any module by
Stacks 0G7K.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Q_map_extendMap_cplxMap_comp_cechToDerivedSupport {m : ℕ} (e : Fin m → Γ(X, ⊤))
    {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) {T : Set X}
    (hT : IsClosed T) (hTe : equationsClosedSet e ⊆ T) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (cplxMap e φ)
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ≫ cechToDerivedSupport e G hT hTe =
      cechToDerivedSupport e F hT hTe ≫
        (supportPush hT).map ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).map φ)
declarations.comment: functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ, the edge 𝓕^• ⟶ i_*RℋT(ℱ) of the diagram

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedSupportedSectionsLift
declarations.doc:
**The canonical factorization of Stacks 0G7L.** A map `i_* L ⟶ K` in `D(𝒪_X)` out of a
complex pushed forward from `Z` has a canonical lift `L ⟶ RH_Z(K)`, its adjoint transpose under
`derivedPushforwardAdjunction`. Pushing the lift forward and composing with the counit
`i_* RH_Z(K) ⟶ K` returns the original map, by
`modulePushforward_map_derivedSupportedSectionsLift_comp_counit`: this is the commutative
triangle of Stacks 0G7L, for the chosen adjunction.
declarations.comment: the canonical factorisation through derived supported sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.modulePushforward_map_derivedSupportedSectionsLift_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**The triangle of Stacks 0G7L commutes.** The canonical lift of `u : i_* L ⟶ K` through
`i_* RH_Z(K)`, pushed forward and followed by the counit of the adjunction, is `u` again.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePushforward_map_derivedSupportedSectionsLift_comp_counit
    {L : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)))}
    {K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    (u : letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
      letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
      (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory.obj L ⟶ K) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (derivedSupportedSectionsLift X Z hZ u) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardAdjunction X Z hZ).counit.app K = u
declarations.comment: the commuting triangle of the factorisation

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechLocalCohomology.pushforwardLocalCohomologyIso
declarations.doc:
**The extended alternating Čech complex computes the local cohomology sheaves.**  For a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` and the common zero locus `Z` of the equations, the direct image
of the local cohomology sheaf `𝓗 ⁿ_Z(F)` along the inclusion of `Z` is the degree-`n` cohomology
sheaf of the extended alternating Čech complex of `F`.

In the top degree the right-hand side is the cokernel of the last Čech differential, the module
in which the fraction class of [Stacks, Tag 0G7Q] takes its values.
declarations.statement:
def pushforwardLocalCohomologyIso [F.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
      (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)
    (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f))).obj
        (localCohomologySheafOfComplex X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
          (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) (n : ℤ)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)) ≅
      (data f F).complex.homology n
declarations.comment: the complex computes the local cohomology sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.isIso_map_augmentation_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7M**, the step of the proof that uses the quasi-coherence of the
coefficient module.  With `X`, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `F` as in Stacks 0G7I, and `F`
quasi-coherent, **a derived functor `R𝓗_Z` of sections supported on the common zero locus `Z` of
the equations inverts the augmentation `𝓕^• ⟶ F[0]` of Stacks 0G7L**.

The augmentation is the comparison between the extended alternating Čech complex and its
coefficient module, so this says that the complex and the module have the same derived sections
with support on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_map_augmentation_of_isQuasicoherent (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (RH : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
        (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)))))
    (αH : (schemeSupportedSectionsFunctor X (equationsClosedSet f)
        (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RH)
    (hRH : RH.IsRightDerivedFunctor αH
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    IsIso (RH.map (Stacks.Perfect.ExtendedAlternatingCech.Augmentation.augmentation f F))
declarations.comment: the derived sections with support invert the augmentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.nonempty_cechIso_derivedSupportedSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7M.**  With `X`, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `F` as in Stacks 0G7I
and `F` quasi-coherent, the extended alternating Čech complex `𝓕^•` **represents
`i_* R𝓗_Z(F)`**, the comparison being the augmentation `𝓕^• ⟶ F[0]` of Stacks 0G7L.

Two halves combine.  The augmentation is inverted by `R𝓗_Z`, which is
`isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed_map_augmentation` and is where quasi-coherence is used;
and `𝓕^•` is its own derived sections with support, which is
`Stacks.Perfect.CechSupportRepresentation.nonempty_pushforwardDerivedSupportCechIso` and is
where the acyclicity of Stacks 0G7K is used.  The K-injective resolution entering the second
half is not canonical, so the conclusion is stated as the existence of the isomorphism, in the
form the neighbouring existence statements of Stacks 0A3B take.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_cechIso_derivedSupportedSections (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
      (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)
    Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((Stacks.Perfect.ExtendedAlternatingCech.extendedAlternatingCech f F).complex.extend
            ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) ≅
        (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace
            (equationsClosedSet f))).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
              (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)))
declarations.comment: the extended alternating Čech complex represents i_*RℋZ(F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsToId_cech
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G7M, the acyclicity half, with the comparison as a canonical term.** The counit
`i_* R𝓗_T(𝓕^•) ⟶ 𝓕^•` of Stacks 0G72 is invertible at the extended alternating Čech complex of
a family of equations whose common zero locus is contained in `T`: the complex is supported
there, so the third vertex `Rj_*(𝓕^•|_U)` of the triangle vanishes.

This is the content of `nonempty_pushforwardDerivedSupportCechIso`, with the isomorphism being
the canonical map rather than one produced on a chosen K-injective resolution; only the
invertibility is asserted, and invertibility is a proposition, so nothing is chosen.
declarations.comment:
the canonical counit i_*RℋT(𝓕^•) ⟶ 𝓕^• of Stacks 0G72 is invertible at the
extended alternating Čech complex, for every closed T containing the common zero locus of the
equations.  The theorem nonempty_pushforwardDerivedSupportCechIso asserts the same isomorphism
without naming it, because it is produced on a chosen K-injective resolution; here only
invertibility of the canonical map is asserted, and invertibility is a proposition, so nothing
is chosen

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechComparison.isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed_map_augmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7M.** With `X` a scheme, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` global functions,
`Z` their common zero locus and `F` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, the chosen derived functor of
sections supported on `Z` inverts the augmentation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.data`.

This is `Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed_map_augmentation`
for the construction of the complex on which [Stacks, Tag 0G7K] and the well-definedness of the
fraction class of [Stacks, Tag 0G7Q] are stated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed_map_augmentation [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsIso ((Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed
      X.toRingedSpace (Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.equationsClosedSet f)
      (Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)).map
        (AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.augmentation f F))
declarations.comment: the derived sections with support invert the augmentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.LocalCohomologyDegrees.isZero_homology_derivedSupportedSections_of_locallyCutOut
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7N.**  Let `X` be a scheme and let `T ⊆ X` be a closed subset which
can locally be cut out by `c` elements of the structure sheaf.  Then the local cohomology sheaves
of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module vanish above degree `c`:

`ℋ ^i_T(ℱ) = 0` for `i > c`.

The hypothesis is that every point has an open neighbourhood `U` on which the part of `T` lying
in `U` is the common zero locus of `c` functions on `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_homology_derivedSupportedSections_of_locallyCutOut {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (c : ℕ)
    (hcut : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ f : Fin c → Γ(U.toScheme, ⊤),
      U.ι ⁻¹' T = Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.equationsClosedSet f)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (i : ℤ) (hi : (c : ℤ) < i) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X.toRingedSpace T))) i).obj
      ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X.toRingedSpace T hT).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)))
declarations.comment: stated for the closed subset T; the source writes ℋ^i_Z for it, a slip

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.LocalCohomologyDegrees.isZero_homology_derivedSupportedSections_of_locallyKoszulRegular_of_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7P.**  Let `X` be a scheme.  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subset which can
locally be cut out by a Koszul-regular sequence having `c` elements.  Then

`ℋ ^i_Z(ℱ) = 0` for `i ≠ c`

for every flat, quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`.

Above degree `c` this is Stacks 0G7N, which needs neither the Koszul-regularity of the equations
nor the flatness of `ℱ`
(`isZero_homology_derivedSupportedSections_of_locallyKoszulRegular`); below degree `c` it needs
both and is
`isZero_homology_derivedSupportedSections_of_locallyKoszulRegular_of_lt`.

"Locally" is read with affine open neighbourhoods, which by Stacks 063G is the same condition as
the source's; see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_homology_derivedSupportedSections_of_locallyKoszulRegular_of_ne
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (c : ℕ)
    (hcut : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧
      ∃ f : Fin c → Γ(U.toScheme, ⊤), Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f ∧
        U.ι ⁻¹' Z = equationsClosedSet f)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
      (C := TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toTopCat)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (O := X.sheaf) F)
    (i : ℤ) (hi : i ≠ (c : ℤ)) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X.toRingedSpace Z))) i).obj
      ((derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X.toRingedSpace Z hZ).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)))
declarations.comment:
the whole statement: for a closed subset locally cut out by a Koszul-regular
sequence of c elements and a flat quasi-coherent module, the vanishing of the local cohomology
sheaf in every degree other than c; exactly the source's conditions, with locally read
over affine open neighbourhoods, which Stacks 063G shows is the same condition

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.GysinLocalCohomology.fractionClassOnClosed
declarations.doc:
With `X` a scheme, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `Z ⊆ X` the closed subscheme they cut out,
the canonical map `c_{f₁, …, f_c} : i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules on `Z`, as a natural
transformation of functors of the `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`: from `ℱ ↦ i^*(ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ)`, the inverse
image along the inclusion of `Z` of the cokernel of `(f₁, …, f_c) : ℱ^{⊕c} ⟶ ℱ`, to
`ℱ ↦ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`. Its component at `ℱ` is the transpose under `i^* ⊣ i_*` of the component of
`fractionClassPushTrans`.
declarations.statement:
public def fractionClassOnClosed {d : ℕ} (f : Fin (d + 1) → Γ(X, ⊤)) :
    equationsQuotientFunctor f ⋙
        modulePullback (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0 ⋙
        derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
            (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the remark's conclusion: the canonical O_X|_Z-linear map c_{f₁,…,f_c} : i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ) on Z, together with its functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ, as a natural transformation of the two functors of ℱ into 𝒪_X|_Z-modules; obtained from the transformation on X by the remark's last step, the transposition along i^* ⊣ i_* that full faithfulness of i_* provides

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.eq_of_eq_mod_equations_empty
declarations.doc:
For no equations, the fraction is just the numerator itself, and the
quotient by the zero ideal changes nothing.
declarations.statement:
public lemma eq_of_eq_mod_equations_empty
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Fin 0 → Γ(X, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules) (V : X.Opens)
    (s t : Γ(F, V))
    (x y : Γ((data f F).complex.X 0, V))
    (hmod : s - t = ∑ i : Fin 0,
      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top : V ⟶ ⊤).op (f i)) •
        (0 : Γ(F, V)))
    (hx : ((data f F).zeroIso.hom).app V x = s)
    (hy : ((data f F).zeroIso.hom).app V y = t) :
    x = y
declarations.comment: fraction_class_well_defined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.cokernel_π_app_eq_of_eq_mod_equations
declarations.doc:
Fractions with congruent numerators have the same class in the final
Čech cokernel.
declarations.statement:
public lemma cokernel_π_app_eq_of_eq_mod_equations
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {c : ℕ} {ι : Type*} (f : Fin (c + 1) → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (F : X.Modules) (V : X.Opens) (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, U i ≤ V) (hcover : ⨆ i, U i = V)
    (s t : Γ(F, V))
    (x y : Γ((data f F).complex.X (c + 1), V))
    (a : ∀ j : ι, Fin (c + 1) → Γ(F, U j))
    (hmod : ∀ j,
      (Scheme.Modules.presheaf F).map (homOfLE (hU j)).op (s - t) =
        ∑ i, (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top : U j ⟶ ⊤).op (f i)) • a j i)
    (hx : ∀ q : CechCochains.OrdIndex (I := Fin (c + 1)) c,
      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top :
        CechCochains.inter (fun i => V ⊓ X.basicOpen (f i)) q.1 ⟶ ⊤).op
        (∏ i, f i)) •
        ((data f F).sectionsIso c V x q) =
      (Scheme.Modules.presheaf F).map
        (homOfLE (show
          CechCochains.inter (fun i => V ⊓ X.basicOpen (f i)) q.1 ≤ V from
            (iInf_le _ (0 : Fin (c + 1))).trans inf_le_left)).op s)
    (hy : ∀ q : CechCochains.OrdIndex (I := Fin (c + 1)) c,
      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE le_top :
        CechCochains.inter (fun i => V ⊓ X.basicOpen (f i)) q.1 ⟶ ⊤).op
        (∏ i, f i)) •
        ((data f F).sectionsIso c V y q) =
      (Scheme.Modules.presheaf F).map
        (homOfLE (show
          CechCochains.inter (fun i => V ⊓ X.basicOpen (f i)) q.1 ≤ V from
            (iInf_le _ (0 : Fin (c + 1))).trans inf_le_left)).op t) :
    (cokernel.π ((data f F).complex.d c (c + 1))).app V x =
      (cokernel.π ((data f F).complex.d c (c + 1))).app V y
declarations.comment: fraction_class_well_defined

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.classMapToPushforward_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q, functoriality in `ℱ`**, in the spelling of `i_*ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)` with the
direct image outside: `classMapToSupport_natural`, with its carried numerator hypothesis
discharged by `fracTermTop_naturality`, carried across the comparison of the two spellings, which
is natural.
declarations.statement:
public theorem classMapToPushforward_natural {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) {F G : X.Modules}
    (φ : F ⟶ G) {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hTf : equationsClosedSet f ⊆ T) :
    φ ≫ classMapToPushforward f G hT hTf =
      classMapToPushforward f F hT hTf ≫ (localCohomologyPushforwardFunctor hT (c : ℤ)).map φ
declarations.comment:
functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ, with the direct image taken outside the
cohomology sheaf, for an arbitrary 𝒪_X-module and any number of equations

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.quotientClassMapToPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q, for an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module.**  The `𝒪_X`-module map

`i_*i^*ℱ = ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)`

carrying the class of a local section `s` of `ℱ` to the class of the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`.
The remark builds exactly this map and then descends it along the fully faithful `i_*`; here the
descent is `fractionClassAnyModule`.

No quasi-coherence and no hypothesis on the number of equations: the class of the fraction lands
in the degree-`c` cohomology sheaf of the extended alternating Čech complex, which the comparison
of [Stacks, Tag 0G7L] carries into `i_*ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)` for every `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`.
declarations.comment:
i_* of the remark's map c_{f₁,…,f_c}, between its two presentations, for an
arbitrary 𝒪_X-module ℱ and any number of equations

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.cokernelπ_comp_quotientClassMapToPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.**  The map out of the quotient sends the class of a local section
`s` of `ℱ` to the class of the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cokernelπ_comp_quotientClassMapToPushforward {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (F : X.Modules) {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hTf : equationsClosedSet f ⊆ T) :
    cokernel.π (equationsMap f F) ≫ quotientClassMapToPushforward f F hT hTf =
      classMapToPushforward f F hT hTf
declarations.comment:
the value on the class of a local section is the class of its fraction, for an
arbitrary 𝒪_X-module ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.quotientClassMapToPushforward_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q, functoriality in `ℱ` of the map out of the quotient.**  The
square commutes for every morphism `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` of `𝒪_X`-modules, the left vertical arrow being
`i_*i^*φ` in the presentation `equationsQuotientMap`.

The projection onto the quotient is an epimorphism, so this is
`classMapToPushforward_natural`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotientClassMapToPushforward_natural {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤))
    {F G : X.Modules} (φ : F ⟶ G) {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTf : equationsClosedSet f ⊆ T) :
