    equationsQuotientMap f φ ≫ quotientClassMapToPushforward f G hT hTf =
      quotientClassMapToPushforward f F hT hTf ≫
        (localCohomologyPushforwardFunctor hT (c : ℤ)).map φ
declarations.comment:
functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ of i_* of the remark's map, for an arbitrary
𝒪_X-module ℱ and any number of equations

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClassAnyModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q, for every `𝒪_X`-module.**  The canonical `𝒪_X|_T`-linear map

`c_{f₁, …, f_c} : i^*(ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ) ⟶ ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)`

on a closed subset `T` containing the common zero locus of `f₁, …, f_c`, for an **arbitrary**
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` and an arbitrary number of equations.  It is the transpose, under the adjunction
`i^* ⊣ i_*` between inverse image and direct image along the inclusion of `T`, of the map
`quotientClassMapToPushforward` carrying the class of a local section `s` of `ℱ` to the class of
the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`.

This is the remark's own construction: the `𝒪_X`-module map `i_*i^*ℱ ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)` followed by
the descent along `i_*`.  Only the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 0G7L] is used, and that holds for
every `𝒪_X`-module; `Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClass` is this map on a quasi-coherent
module, by `fractionClassAnyModule_eq`.
declarations.statement:
public def fractionClassAnyModule {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules) {T : Set X}
    (hT : IsClosed T) (hTf : equationsClosedSet f ⊆ T) :
    (modulePullback (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace T)).obj (equationsQuotient f F) ⟶
      localCohomologySheafOfComplex X.toRingedSpace T hT (c : ℤ)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map c_{f_1, …, f_c}, for an arbitrary 𝒪_X-module ℱ and any number of
equations

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.homEquiv_fractionClassAnyModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.**  The map `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` is the transpose of the map
`i_*i^*ℱ ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)` out of the quotient by the equations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homEquiv_fractionClassAnyModule {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules)
    {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hTf : equationsClosedSet f ⊆ T) :
    homEquiv (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace T) _ (equationsQuotient f F)
        (fractionClassAnyModule f F hT hTf) =
      quotientClassMapToPushforward f F hT hTf
declarations.comment:
c_{f_1, …, f_c} is the transpose of the map out of the quotient, for an arbitrary
𝒪_X-module ℱ

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClassAnyModule_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q, functoriality in `ℱ` of `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` itself.**  For every
morphism `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` of `𝒪_X`-modules the square

`i^*(ℱ/(f)ℱ) ⟶ ℋ ᶜ_T(ℱ)`, `i^*(𝒢/(f)𝒢) ⟶ ℋ ᶜ_T(𝒢)`

commutes, the vertical arrows being `i^*` of `equationsQuotientMap` and `ℋ ᶜ_T(φ)`.  This is the
functoriality the remark asserts, read on `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` rather than on its direct image.

It is `quotientClassMapToPushforward_natural` transposed: both sides become maps out of
`ℱ/(f)ℱ` under the bijection of the adjunction `i^* ⊣ i_*`, by its naturality in each variable,
and there the square is the one already proved.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fractionClassAnyModule_natural {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) {F G : X.Modules}
    (φ : F ⟶ G) {T : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hTf : equationsClosedSet f ⊆ T) :
    (modulePullback (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace T)).map (equationsQuotientMap f φ) ≫
        fractionClassAnyModule f G hT hTf =
      fractionClassAnyModule f F hT hTf ≫
        (localCohomologySheafOfComplexFunctor X.toRingedSpace T hT (c : ℤ)).map φ
declarations.comment:
functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ of c_{f_1, …, f_c} itself, for an arbitrary
𝒪_X-module ℱ and any number of equations

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClassAnyModule_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q: the quasi-coherent construction is this one specialised.**  On a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module the map `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` built here through [Stacks, Tag 0G7L] alone
is `Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClass`, which is built through [Stacks, Tag 0G7M].  Both
are transposes along `i^* ⊣ i_*`, and their transposes agree by
`quotientClassMapToPushforward_eq`.
declarations.comment:
the quasi-coherent construction of c_{f_1, …, f_c} is the arbitrary-module one
specialised

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.smulHom_comp_classMap
declarations.doc:
**The fraction class only depends on the numerator modulo the equations.** Multiplying the
numerator by one of the equations kills the class of the fraction, because the result is the image
of a cochain under the last Čech differential. An equation to multiply by is itself a witness
that there is at least one, which is what the descent of the product needs.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smulHom_comp_classMap (j : Fin c) :
    smulHom (f j) F ≫ classMap f F = 0
declarations.comment: the class of the fraction depends only on the numerator modulo the equations

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.cokernelπ_comp_quotientClassMap
declarations.doc: The map out of the quotient sends the class of a section to the class of its fraction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cokernelπ_comp_quotientClassMap :
    cokernel.π (equationsMap f F) ≫ quotientClassMap f F = classMap f F
declarations.comment: the value on the class of a local section is the class of its fraction

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.** The canonical map
`c_{f₁, …, f_c} : i^{-1}(ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ) ⟶ 𝓗ᶜ_Z(ℱ)`
of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules on the common zero locus `Z` of `f₁, …, f_c`, for a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`: it is the transpose, under the adjunction between inverse image and direct
image along the inclusion of `Z`, of the map carrying the class of a local section `s` of `ℱ` to
the class of the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)` in the degree-`c` cohomology sheaf of the extended
alternating Čech complex of the equations, which is the direct image of `𝓗ᶜ_Z(ℱ)`.
declarations.statement:
public def fractionClass [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (modulePullback (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f))).obj
        (equationsQuotient f F) ⟶
      localCohomologySheafOfComplex X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)
        (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) (c : ℤ)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)
declarations.comment: the canonical map c_{f_1, …, f_c}

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.pushforwardFractionClass_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.** The map to the direct image of the local cohomology sheaf is
the fraction class followed by the two identifications: the comparison of the two constructions
of the extended alternating Čech complex, and the identification of the degree-`c` cohomology
sheaf of that complex with the direct image of `𝓗ᶜ_Z(ℱ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pushforwardFractionClass_eq [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    pushforwardFractionClass f F =
      (quotientClassMap f F ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (Stacks.Perfect.CechComparison.complexIso f F).inv c) ≫
        (Stacks.Perfect.CechLocalCohomology.pushforwardLocalCohomologyIso f F c).inv
declarations.comment: the fraction class followed by the identifications

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.homEquiv_fractionClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.** The map `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` is the transpose of the map from the
quotient `ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ` to the direct image of the degree-`c` local cohomology sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homEquiv_fractionClass [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    homEquiv (closedSubsetInclusion X.toRingedSpace (equationsClosedSet f)) _
        (equationsQuotient f F) (fractionClass f F) =
      pushforwardFractionClass f F
declarations.comment: c_{f_1, …, f_c} is the transpose of the fraction class

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.supportedFractionClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q**, the class of the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`.  With `X`,
`f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `ℱ` as in Tag 0G7I, this is the map

`Coker((f₁, …, f_c) : ℱ^{⊕c} ⟶ ℱ) ⟶ Coker(⨁ᵢ ℱ_{1…î…c} ⟶ ℱ_{1…c})`

carrying the class of a local section `s` of `ℱ` to the class of the fraction
`s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`, by `supportedFractionClass_mk`.  It is the direct image along the closed
immersion `i : Z → X` of the map `c_{f₁,…,f_c} : i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` of the remark: its source is
`i_* i^*ℱ`, presented as the cokernel of `(f₁, …, f_c)` as the remark does, and its target is
`i_* ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`, presented as the cokernel of the last differential of the extended alternating
Čech complex as the remark does, the two being identified by Tag 0G7M.
declarations.statement:
public def supportedFractionClass {d : ℕ} (f : Fin (d + 1) → Γ(X, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules) :
    cokernel (equationsMultiplication f F) ⟶ cokernel (lastDif f F)
declarations.comment: i_* of the remark's map c_{f₁,…,f_c}, between its two presentations; no descent

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.supportedFractionClass_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.**  The class map sends the class of a local section `s` of `ℱ`
to the class of the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)` in the cokernel of the last differential of the
extended alternating Čech complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedFractionClass_mk {d : ℕ} (f : Fin (d + 1) → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (F : X.Modules) (V : X.Opens) (s : Γ(F, V)) :
    (supportedFractionClass f F).app V
        ((cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication f F)).app V s) =
      (cokernel.π (lastDif f F)).app V ((fractionHom f F d).app V s)
declarations.comment: the value of the class map on the class of a section

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.fractionClassTrans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7Q.**  With `X` a scheme, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` global functions
and `Z ⊆ X` the closed subscheme they cut out, there is a canonical map

`c_{f₁, …, f_c} : i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`

of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules, functorial in the `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`.  Here it is that functoriality: a
natural transformation between the two functors of `ℱ`, from `ℱ ↦ i_*i^*ℱ`
(`equationsQuotientFunctor`, the cokernel of `(f₁, …, f_c) : ℱ^{⊕c} ⟶ ℱ`, which is how the remark
presents the source) to `ℱ ↦ i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` (`supportCohomologySheafFunctor`).  Both functors are
direct images along the inclusion of `Z`, which is fully faithful, so the transformation is the
map of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules of the statement — this is the last step of the remark's construction and
the form in which Stacks 0G7T states the analogous twisted map
(`Stacks.Perfect.ConormalClass.conormalTwistClass`).

Its component at `ℱ` is the map `supportedFractionClass` of the remark, between the two
presentations, followed by the canonical identification `General.cokernelLastDifToSupport` of its
target with `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`; on the class of a local section `s` of `ℱ` it is the class of the
fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`, by `cokernelπ_comp_fractionClassTrans_app`.  As in Remark 0G7I, which
fixes the setting of this remark, `ℱ` is an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module and the morphisms of the
naturality square are arbitrary morphisms of `𝒪_X`-modules: quasi-coherence is used neither by
the map nor by its functoriality, which is why the two factors and the naturality square are
taken from the namespace `General` above, and the source adds it only in Stacks 0G7S and
Stacks 0G7U.

The target is the spelling of `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` in which Stacks 0G7Q and Stacks 0G7S are stated here,
with the direct image taken before the cohomology sheaf.  The other spelling, with the cohomology
sheaf taken on `Z` first — the one `Stacks.Perfect.FractionClass.fractionClass` lands in — is
identified with this one, naturally in `ℱ` and with no hypothesis on `ℱ`, by
`Stacks.Perfect.GysinLocalCohomology.supportCohomologySheafFunctorIso`.
declarations.comment: the canonical map c_{f₁,…,f_c} : i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ) together with its functoriality in the 𝒪_X-module ℱ, as a natural transformation between the two functors of ℱ: from ℱ ↦ i_*i^*ℱ, the cokernel of (f₁,…,f_c) as the remark presents it, to ℱ ↦ i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ); read on X along the fully faithful i_*, as the remark's last step and as Stacks 0G7T does for the twisted map

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.AffineFractionClass.supportedFraction_eq_conj
declarations.doc:
**Clause 3 of Tag 0G7R.**  Let `A` be a commutative ring, let `f₁, …, f_c ∈ A` be a finite
nonempty family and let `M` be an `A`-module.  The map `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` of Tag 0G7Q for
`X = Spec A` and `ℱ = M~`, in the cokernel-to-cokernel presentation
`Coker((f₁,…,f_c) : ℱ^{⊕c} ⟶ ℱ) ⟶ Coker(lastDif)` of
`Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.supportedFractionClass`, read on global sections through the
two canonical isomorphisms

`M/(f₁,…,f_c)M ≅ Γ(Spec A, Coker((f₁,…,f_c) : (M~)^{⊕c} ⟶ M~))`  (`affineSourceEquiv`) and
`Coker(⨁ᵢ M_{f₁⋯f̂ᵢ⋯f_c} ⟶ M_{f₁⋯f_c}) ≅ Γ(Spec A, Coker(lastDif))`  (`targetEquiv`),

**is** the map `Cech.supportedFraction` by which the example describes it.  Both comparisons are
isomorphisms (`bijective_affineSourceComparison` and `bijective_targetComparison`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedFraction_eq_conj (f : Fin (d + 1) → R) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    Cech.supportedFraction f (M : Type u) =
      (targetEquiv f M).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ
        ((moduleSpecΓFunctor.map (supportedFractionClass (specFun f) (tilde M))).hom ∘ₗ
          (affineSourceEquiv f M).toLinearMap)
declarations.comment: the description itself: Γ(Spec A, -) of Tag 0G7Q's map c_{f₁,…,f_c} for ℱ = M~, conjugated by the two canonical isomorphisms affineSourceEquiv and targetEquiv, IS the map Cech.supportedFraction of Tag 0G7R

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.AffineFractionClass.targetEquiv_symm_Γ_supportedFractionClass_affineSourceEquiv_mk
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0G7R.**  Let `A` be a commutative ring, let `f₁, …, f_c ∈ A` and let `M` be an
`A`-module.  Take `X = Spec A` and `ℱ = M~`.  Then the map `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` of Tag 0G7Q, read on
global sections through the two canonical `A`-linear isomorphisms

`M/(f₁,…,f_c)M ≅ Γ(Spec A, Coker((f₁,…,f_c) : ℱ^{⊕c} ⟶ ℱ))`  (`affineSourceEquiv`) and
`Coker(⨁ᵢ M_{f₁⋯f̂ᵢ⋯f_c} ⟶ M_{f₁⋯f_c}) ≅ Γ(Spec A, Coker(lastDif))`  (`targetEquiv`),

is the map `M/(f₁,…,f_c)M ⟶ Coker(⨁ᵢ M_{f₁⋯f̂ᵢ⋯f_c} ⟶ M_{f₁⋯f_c})` carrying the class of
`s ∈ M` to the class of the fraction `s/(f₁⋯f_c)`.

This is the example's description, source and target modules, map and formula together, in one
statement, for a nonempty family; the empty family is
`Stacks.Perfect.AffineFractionClassEmpty.targetIsoEmpty_inv_Γ_quotientClassMap_sourceIsoEmpty`.
The classes of sections exhaust `M/(f₁,…,f_c)M`, so the formula below determines the
conjugated map; the map-level equality is `supportedFraction_eq_conj` and the formula alone is
`Cech.supportedFraction_mk`.

The ring and the module are taken in a *single* universe, as `tilde` requires, whereas
`Cech.supportedFraction` itself is stated for a ring and a module in independent universes.
That is a restriction of spelling only: a ring and a module in independent
universes are moved into a common universe by `ULift`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem targetEquiv_symm_Γ_supportedFractionClass_affineSourceEquiv_mk
    (f : Fin (d + 1) → R) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (s : M) :
    (targetEquiv f M).symm
        ((moduleSpecΓFunctor.map (supportedFractionClass (specFun f) (tilde M))).hom
          (affineSourceEquiv f M (Submodule.Quotient.mk s))) =
      Submodule.Quotient.mk
        (DirectSum.lof R {t : Finset (Fin (d + 1)) // t.card = d + 1}
          (fun t => Cech.cechMod f (M : Type u) t.1) ⟨Finset.univ, Finset.card_fin _⟩
          (LocalizedModule.mk s ⟨∏ i, f i, Submonoid.mem_powers _⟩))
declarations.comment: the example in one statement: for X = Spec A and ℱ = M~, Tag 0G7Q's map c_{f₁,…,f_c} on global sections, conjugated by the canonical isomorphisms affineSourceEquiv and targetEquiv, sends the class of s ∈ M to the class of the fraction s/(f₁⋯f_c) in Coker(⨁ᵢ M_{f₁⋯f̂ᵢ⋯f_c} ⟶ M_{f₁⋯f_c})

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.AffineFractionClassEmpty.targetIsoEmpty_inv_Γ_quotientClassMap_sourceIsoEmpty
declarations.doc:
For the empty family (`c = 0`), let `A` be a commutative ring, let `M` be an `A`-module and
take `X = Spec A`, `ℱ = M~` and the empty family of equations. Then the map `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` of
Tag 0G7Q, read on global sections through the canonical isomorphisms
`M/(f₁, …, f_c)M ≅ Γ(Spec A, ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ)` (`sourceIsoEmpty`) and
`M_{f₁⋯f_c} ≅ Γ(Spec A, H⁰(ℱ^•))` (`targetIsoEmpty`), sends the class of `s ∈ M` to the fraction
`s/(f₁⋯f_c)`; here `f₁⋯f_c = 1`, the cokernel of the map out of the empty direct sum is
`M_{f₁⋯f_c}` itself, and the map is `s ↦ s/1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem targetIsoEmpty_inv_Γ_quotientClassMap_sourceIsoEmpty (s : M) :
    (targetIsoEmpty f M).inv
        ((moduleSpecΓFunctor.map (quotientClassMap (specFunEmpty f) (tilde M))).hom
          ((sourceIsoEmpty f M).hom (Submodule.Quotient.mk s))) =
      LocalizedModule.mk s ⟨∏ i, f i, Submonoid.mem_powers _⟩
declarations.comment: the case c = 0: for X = Spec A, ℱ = M~ and the empty family, Tag 0G7Q's map on global sections, conjugated by the canonical isomorphisms sourceIsoEmpty and targetIsoEmpty, sends the class of s ∈ M to s/(f₁⋯f_c) = s/1

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.supportedFractionClass_eq_det_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7S**, the determinant identity as a single equation in a common
target.

With `X`, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `ℱ` as in Stacks 0G7I, let `a_{ji} ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and
`g_j = ∑_i a_{ji} f_i`, let `ℱ` be quasi-coherent and let `g₁, …, g_c` cut out the same closed
subset `Z` as `f₁, …, f_c`.  Then

`c_{f₁,…,f_c} = det(a_{ji}) c_{g₁,…,g_c}`

as maps into the single object `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`.

The two class maps `supportedFractionClass f F` and `supportedFractionClass g F` of Stacks 0G7Q
land in the cokernels of the last differentials of the `f`- and the `g`-complex.  Each of those
cokernels is identified with `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` by `cokernelLastDifToSupport`, the composite of
`cokernelLastDifIsoHomology` (the cokernel of the last differential is the degree-`c` cohomology
of the complex) with the degree-`c` cohomology of the canonical comparison `cechToDerivedSupport`
of Stacks 0G7L; both identifications are isomorphisms, which is the first two conjuncts and is
Stacks 0G7M.  Both class maps are then read on the common source `ℱ` through the canonical
epimorphisms `cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication f F)` and
`cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication g F)` presenting `i_* i^*ℱ` in the two ways the remark does;
since those are epimorphisms, the displayed equation is equivalent to the equality of the class
maps themselves, and no choice of isomorphism between the two presentations of `i_* i^*ℱ` is
needed.

The proof is the source's: both sides are the image of the single degree-`c` cohomology class of
the mixed cocycle `mixedFractionHom` on the complex of the `2c` equations `f₁, …, f_c, g₁, …, g_c`
(`subfamily_comp_cokernelπ_comp_cokernelLastDifToSupport` applied to the two projections
`mixedFractionHom_subfamilyProd_castAdd` and `mixedFractionHom_subfamilyProd_natAdd`).

The hypothesis `hZ` replaces the source's "`g₁, …, g_c` cut out `Z` scheme theoretically" by the
equality of the two common zero loci as closed *subsets*.  That is implied by the
scheme-theoretic condition, so the statement is a generalisation of the source's and not a
weakening of it.  It suffices because `R𝓗_T` depends only on the closed subset `T`: no scheme
structure on `Z` enters the identification of the two targets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedFractionClass_eq_det_smul {d : ℕ} (f g : Fin (d + 1) → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (a : Matrix (Fin (d + 1)) (Fin (d + 1)) Γ(X, ⊤)) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hg : ∀ j, g j = ∑ i, a j i * f i)
    (hZ : equationsClosedSet g = equationsClosedSet f) :
    IsIso (cokernelLastDifToSupport f F (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) subset_rfl) ∧
      IsIso (cokernelLastDifToSupport g F (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) hZ.le) ∧
      cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication f F) ≫ supportedFractionClass f F ≫
          cokernelLastDifToSupport f F (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) subset_rfl =
        globalSmul a.det F ≫ cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication g F) ≫
          supportedFractionClass g F ≫
            cokernelLastDifToSupport g F (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) hZ.le
declarations.comment:
the determinant identity c_{f₁,…,f_c} = det(a_{ji})·c_{g₁,…,g_c} as ONE equation
of maps into the common target i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ), together with the invertibility of the two
identifications it is read through.  The 0G7Q class maps of the f- and the g-complex are composed
with cokernelLastDifToSupport -- cokernel of the last differential ≅ H^c of the complex ≅
i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ), the last step by the canonical comparison of Stacks 0G7L and its invertibility,
which is Stacks 0G7M -- and are read on the common source ℱ through the two canonical
epimorphisms ℱ ↠ i_*i^*ℱ; those are epimorphisms, so this is equivalent to the equality of the
class maps and needs no chosen isomorphism between the two presentations of i_*i^*ℱ.  The
hypothesis used in place of the source's 'g₁,…,g_c cut out Z scheme theoretically' is the weaker
set-level equality of the two common zero loci, so this is a GENERALIZATION and not a weakening:
it suffices because RℋT depends only on the closed set T, so no scheme structure on Z enters the
identification of the two targets

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.mixedFractionHom_projections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7S**, the determinant identity on the mixed extended alternating
Čech complex.

With `X`, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and `ℱ` as in Stacks 0G7I, let `a_{ji} ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` and
`g_j = ∑_i a_{ji} f_i`.  Write `𝓕''^•` for the extended alternating Čech complex of the mixed
family `f₁, …, f_c, g₁, …, g_c` of `2c` equations, which is the complex the source's proof
introduces.  Projecting away the components involving a `g`, respectively an `f`, gives the two
morphisms of complexes `𝓕''^• ⟶ 𝓕^•` and `𝓕''^• ⟶ (𝓕')^•` of the source, both the identity in
degree `0` (`subfamilyCplxMap`, whose degree-`(c)` component is `subfamilyProd`).

The content of the lemma is the explicit degree-`c` cocycle `σ = mixedFractionHom` of the
source, whose component at an increasing `c`-tuple `q` of the `2c` indices is
`det(minor of (a_{ji}) selected by q) · s / (product of the equations of q)`:

* `σ` is a cocycle;
* its projection to `𝓕^•` is `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`, i.e. `c_{f₁,…,f_c}`;
* its projection to `(𝓕')^•` is `det(a_{ji}) s / (g₁ ⋯ g_c)`, i.e. `det(a_{ji}) c_{g₁,…,g_c}`.

What is **not** carried out here is the last step of the source's proof: passing from these
two projections of `σ` to the single equation `c_{f₁,…,f_c} = det(a_{ji}) c_{g₁,…,g_c}` of
sheaf maps `i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`.  That step is the identification of the degree-`c` cohomology of
each of the three complexes with `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`, which is Stacks 0G7M and **is** available in
this library — `Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedSupport.isIso_map_augmentation_of_isQuasicoherent`
for the half that uses the quasi-coherence of `ℱ`, and
`isIso_derivedSupportedSectionsToId_cech` above for the canonical form of the other half.  What
is missing is only the bookkeeping that composes the two statements below with those
identifications: the comparison `cechToDerivedSupport` of Stacks 0G7L above, its degree-`c`
cohomology sheaf, and the identification of `H^c` of each complex with the cokernel of its last
differential.  The hypothesis that `g₁, …, g_c` cut out `Z` scheme theoretically is likewise
needed only for that step — it is what makes the two identifications land in the same
`i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` — and so does not appear below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mixedFractionHom_projections (hg : ∀ j, g j = ∑ i, a j i * f i) :
    mixedFractionHom (mixedEquations f g) a F ≫ difSucc (mixedEquations f g) F d = 0 ∧
      mixedFractionHom (mixedEquations f g) a F ≫
          subfamilyProd (mixedEquations f g) (Fin.castAddOrderEmb (d + 1) :
            Fin (d + 1) ↪o Fin ((d + 1) + (d + 1))) F d ≫
          prodTermCongr (mixedEquations_comp_castAdd f g) F d =
        fractionHom f F d ∧
      mixedFractionHom (mixedEquations f g) a F ≫
          subfamilyProd (mixedEquations f g) (Fin.natAddOrderEmb (d + 1) :
            Fin (d + 1) ↪o Fin ((d + 1) + (d + 1))) F d ≫
          prodTermCongr (mixedEquations_comp_natAdd f g) F d =
        globalSmul a.det F ≫ fractionHom g F d
declarations.comment:
the source's own construction: the explicit degree-c cocycle on the mixed
extended alternating Čech complex of f₁,…,f_c,g₁,…,g_c is a cocycle, and projects to
s/(f₁⋯f_c) and to det(a)·s/(g₁⋯g_c).  Stated at the level of the complexes, i.e. before the
identification of the degree-c cohomology of the three complexes with i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ); that
identification is Stacks 0G7M, and composing it with this statement to obtain the single
equation c_{f₁,…,f_c} = det(a_{ji})·c_{g₁,…,g_c} is carried out in this module, in
supportedFractionClass_eq_det_smul

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.mixedFractionHom_comp_cokernelπ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7S**, read on the classes of Stacks 0G7Q.

The class map `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` of Stacks 0G7Q is `supportedFractionClass f F`, carrying the class
of a local section `s` to the class of `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)` in the cokernel of the last differential
of the extended alternating Čech complex of `f₁, …, f_c`.  Both `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` and
`det(a_{ji}) c_{g₁,…,g_c}` are the image of the single degree-`c` class `σ` of the mixed complex
under the two projections.  This is the equality in the form the source proves it, with the two
sides still living in the cokernels of the last differentials of the `f`- and the `g`-complex
rather than in a common `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`; the identification of those two cokernels with
`i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` is Stacks 0G7M, and composing it with this statement to obtain the single
equation is `supportedFractionClass_eq_det_smul` below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mixedFractionHom_comp_cokernelπ (hg : ∀ j, g j = ∑ i, a j i * f i) :
    mixedFractionHom (mixedEquations f g) a F ≫
          subfamilyProd (mixedEquations f g) (Fin.castAddOrderEmb (d + 1) :
            Fin (d + 1) ↪o Fin ((d + 1) + (d + 1))) F d ≫
          prodTermCongr (mixedEquations_comp_castAdd f g) F d ≫
          cokernel.π (lastDif f F) =
        cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication f F) ≫ supportedFractionClass f F ∧
      mixedFractionHom (mixedEquations f g) a F ≫
          subfamilyProd (mixedEquations f g) (Fin.natAddOrderEmb (d + 1) :
            Fin (d + 1) ↪o Fin ((d + 1) + (d + 1))) F d ≫
          prodTermCongr (mixedEquations_comp_natAdd f g) F d ≫
          cokernel.π (lastDif g F) =
        globalSmul a.det F ≫
          cokernel.π (equationsMultiplication g F) ≫ supportedFractionClass g F
declarations.comment:
the same identity read on the two class maps c_{f₁,…,f_c} and c_{g₁,…,g_c} of
Stacks 0G7Q, with the two sides in the cokernels of the last differentials of the two complexes
rather than in a common i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ); the identification of those cokernels with i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ) is
Stacks 0G7M, and composing it with this statement to obtain the single equation is
supportedFractionClass_eq_det_smul in this module

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.ConormalClass.conormalTwistClass
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `⋀^c(𝒞_{Z/X})^∨ ⊗_{𝒪_Z} i^*ℱ ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`, functorial in `ℱ`, for a closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of finite presentation whose conormal sheaf `𝒞_{Z/X}` is finite locally
free of rank `c`.  The source is `i_*` of the tensor product over `𝒪_Z` (Stacks 01CA) of the dual
`SheafHom(⋀^c 𝒞_{Z/X}, 𝒪_Z)` of the `c`-th exterior power of the conormal sheaf with `i^*ℱ`, and
the target is `ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` read on `X`; the direct image along `i` is fully faithful, so this is the
map of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules of the statement.  On a chart it is the map of
`conormalTwistClass_app_tmul`.
declarations.statement:
def conormalTwistClass :
    twistFunctor i c ⟶ supportCohomologySheafFunctor (isClosed_zeroLocus i) (c : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the canonical map, as a natural transformation of functors of the module F; its value on a chart is conormalTwistClass_app_tmul

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.ConormalClass.conormalTwistClass_app_tmul
declarations.doc:
The value of `conormalTwistClass` on a chart.  Let `W ⊆ X` be an open on which
`f₁, …, f_c` generate the ideal sheaf of `Z`, let `U ⊆ W` be open, `λ` a local section of
`(⋀^c 𝒞_{Z/X})^∨` over `Z ∩ U`, `s` a local section of `ℱ` over `U` and `r` a function on `U`
restricting on `Z ∩ U` to `λ(f₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ f_c)`.  Then `c(λ ⊗ s)`, read in `ℋ^c_{T}(ℱ)` for the
closed subset `T ⊇ Z` of the chart (over `W` the change of support `ℋ^c_Z ⟶ ℋ^c_T` is an
isomorphism), is the class `c_{f₁, …, f_c}(r s)` of the fraction `r s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)` of
Stacks 0G7Q.  In particular the map does not depend on the chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalTwistClass_app_tmul {W : X.Opens} {f : Fin c → Γ(X, W)}
    (hgen : IsGeneratedByOn X.toRingedSpace (definingIdealOfHom i) W f) (U : X.Opens) (hU : U ≤ W)
    (lam : (dualSheaf Z.toRingedSpace (line i c)).val.obj (op (i ⁻¹ᵁ U))) (s : Γ(F, U))
    (r : Γ(X, U))
    (hr : (i.app U).hom r = dualEval Z.toRingedSpace (line i c) lam
      ((line i c).presheaf.map (homOfLE (i.preimage_mono hU)).op
        (wedge i f (app_chart_eq_zero W f hgen)))) :
    (supportChangeH (isClosed_zeroLocus i) (isClosed_chartSupport W (chartEq W f))
        (zeroLocus_subset_chartSupport W f hgen) F (c : ℤ)).app U
        (((conormalTwistClass i c).app F).app U
          (tensorObjTmul Z.toRingedSpace (dualModule (line i c)) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj F)
            (op (i ⁻¹ᵁ U)) lam
            (((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction i).unit.app F).app U s))) =
      (topClass W F (isClosed_chartSupport W (chartEq W f)) (chartEq W f) subset_rfl).app U
        (r • s)
declarations.comment: canonicity: on every chart the map is the twisted fraction class of Stacks 0G7Q, λ ⊗ s ↦ c_{f₁, …, f_c}(λ(f₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ f_c) s)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechBaseChangeCounterexample.isEmpty_iso_cplx
declarations.doc:
**No isomorphism at all between the extended alternating Čech complexes**
`g^*(ℱ^•)` and `(g^*ℱ)^•` of the counterexample: their degree-one terms are a single
`g^*(j_*(ℱ|_U))`, resp. `j'_*((g^*ℱ)|_{U'})`, and these are not isomorphic
(`isEmpty_iso_restrictedModule`).  This refutes the note `(ℱ')^• = g^*ℱ^•` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G7U] for non-quasi-coherent `ℱ` in its strongest reading, with no comparison map
fixed in advance.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmpty_iso_cplx :
    IsEmpty (((Scheme.Modules.pullback (diag k)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (cplx (eqns k) (coeff k)) ≅
      cplx (fun j => (diag k).appTop (eqns k j)) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (diag k)).obj
        (coeff k)))
declarations.comment: refutes the note `(F')^• = g^*F^•` for a non-quasi-coherent `F`: for the diagonal `A^1 → A^2`, `f_1 = x` and `F` the extension by zero of `O` from `D(y)`, the two complexes are not isomorphic at all; the quasi-coherent form is `isIso_cplxBaseChange`

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechBaseChangeCounterexample.not_isIso_cplxBaseChange_f_one
declarations.doc:
**The base-change comparison of complexes of [Stacks, Tag 0G7U] is not an isomorphism for
the non-quasi-coherent module `ℱ = coeff k`**, already in degree `1`.  Here `k` is any field,
`g : 𝔸¹_k ⟶ 𝔸²_k` is the diagonal, the single equation is `x`, and `ℱ` is the sheaf of functions
with vanishing germ at the generic point of the line `y = 0` (the extension by zero of `𝒪` from
`D(y)`).  So the note `(ℱ')^• = g^*ℱ^•` of the remark, read through the comparison map
`cplxBaseChange`, is false for an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module; for quasi-coherent `ℱ` it holds
(`Stacks.Perfect.CechBaseChange.isIso_cplxBaseChange`).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isIso_cplxBaseChange_f_one :
    ¬ IsIso ((cplxBaseChange (diag k) (eqns k) (coeff k)).f 1)
declarations.comment: refutes the note `(F')^• = g^*F^•` for a non-quasi-coherent `F`: the comparison `cplxBaseChange` is not an isomorphism in degree 1 for the diagonal `A^1 → A^2`, `f_1 = x` and `F` the extension by zero of `O` from `D(y)`; the quasi-coherent form is `isIso_cplxBaseChange`

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDegreeCBaseChange.supportedFractionSource_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**The first diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0G7U]**: the class map `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G7Q], read on the coefficient module and in `i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`, commutes with base
change.  The inverse image of the class map for `f` and `ℱ`, followed by the degree-`c`
comparison `degreeCBaseChange`, is the class map for the pulled-back equations `f'` and the
inverse-image module `ℱ'`.

Unfolding both class maps, the inverse of the identification of [Stacks, Tag 0G7M] sitting in
`degreeCBaseChange` cancels against its occurrence in the class map, and what is left is the
class of the fraction `s / (f₁ ⋯ f_c)`: the characterizing property of the preserved-cokernel
comparison turns the inverse image of the class of a top-degree cochain into the class of its
inverse image, and the remaining identity is the compatibility of the fraction with base change,
`Stacks.Perfect.CechFractionBaseChange.cplxBaseChange_comp_fracTermTop`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedFractionSource_baseChange [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map
          (supportedFractionSource f F (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) le_rfl) ≫
        degreeCBaseChange g f F =
      supportedFractionSource (fun j => g.appTop (f j)) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F)
        (isClosed_equationsClosedSet (fun j => g.appTop (f j))) le_rfl
declarations.comment: the first diagram of the remark: the class map c_{f_1,...,f_c} of Tag 0G7Q commutes with base change, for quasi-coherent F, read on X in i_*H^c_Z(F) -- the spelling supportedFractionSource, which is the one Tag 0G7Q is itself registered at in SupportedFractionMap. Its top horizontal arrow IS the map of Cohomology Remark 0G78 on cohomology sheaves in degree c, which the remark's own sentence asserts: that identification is degreeCBaseChange_eq_homology_zeroG78 below, prefixed by the comparison the remark suppresses

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDegreeCBaseChange.degreeCBaseChange_eq_homology_zeroG78
declarations.doc:
**The top arrow of the first diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0G7U] is the map of [Stacks, Tag 0G78]
read on cohomology sheaves in degree `c`.**  This is what the remark asserts verbatim: the top
horizontal arrow of its first diagram "is the map of Cohomology, Remark 0G78 on cohomology
sheaves in degree `c`".

The arrow of [Stacks, Tag 0G78] is the upper route
`Stacks.Perfect.SupportedDerivedBaseChange.supportedPullbackRoute` of the remark's derived
diagram — its left-hand equal sign followed by its top horizontal arrow — followed by
`i'_* R𝓗_{Z'}` of the down arrow `Lg^*ℱ ⟶ ℱ'`; it is the whole left-to-right passage of the
derived diagram above the Čech complexes, and it is the composite that stands to the left of
`Lg^*` of the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 0G7L] in
`Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeSquare_cech`.  Its degree-`c` cohomology
starts at `ℋ^c(Lg^* i_* R𝓗_Z(ℱ))`, not at `g^*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` where `degreeCBaseChange` starts, so the
canonical comparison `derivedPullbackDegreeCComparison` of the two is prefixed; and it ends at
`i'_*ℋ^c_{Z'}(ℱ')` spelled at the preimage `g^{-1}(Z)`, so the identification
`supportCohomologySheafPullbackIso` of the two spellings of `Z'` is appended.

The proof is the source's own: take the degree-`c` cohomology of the derived diagram
`derivedBaseChangeSquare_cech`, and cancel `ℋ^c(Lg^*(ℱ^• ⟶ i_* R𝓗_Z(ℱ)))`, which is invertible
because the comparison of [Stacks, Tag 0G7L] is ([Stacks, Tag 0G7M], as
`Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.isIso_cechToSupport`).  What is left on the other side is
`ℋ^c` of the lower horizontal arrow `Lg^*(ℱ^•) ⟶ (ℱ')^•` followed by `ℋ^c` of the comparison of
[Stacks, Tag 0G7L] for `f'` and `ℱ'`, and that is `cokernelLastDifBaseChange` followed by the
identification of [Stacks, Tag 0G7M] — which is `degreeCBaseChange` — by
`homologyMap_extendBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem degreeCBaseChange_eq_homology_zeroG78 [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    derivedPullbackDegreeCComparison g f F ≫ degreeCBaseChange g f F =
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X'.Modules ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)).map
          (supportedPullbackRoute g.toLRSHom.toShHom (equationsClosedSet f)
              (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F) ≫
            (supportPush (isClosed_equationsClosedSet_pullback g f)).map
              (derivedPullbackSingleObj g.toLRSHom.toShHom F)) ≫
        (supportCohomologySheafPullbackIso g f F).hom
declarations.comment: the top horizontal arrow of the first diagram is the map of Cohomology Remark 0G78 on cohomology sheaves in degree c: the degree-c cohomology of the upper route of the derived diagram, preceded by the canonical comparison of H^c(Lg^*(-)) with g^*H^c(-) that the remark leaves implicit

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDegreeCBaseChange.fractionClassTrans_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**The first diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0G7U], with all four of its arrows**, read on `X'` along
the fully faithful direct image `i'_*` along the inclusion of `Z'`: for a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` the square

```
g^*(i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ))  --degreeCBaseChange-->  i'_*ℋ^c_{Z'}(ℱ')
      ^                                          ^
 g^*(c_{f₁,…,f_c})                         c_{f'₁,…,f'_c}
      |                                          |
g^*(i_*i^*ℱ)  --equationsQuotientBaseChange-->  i'_*(i')^*ℱ'
```

commutes, where the vertical arrows are the components at `ℱ` and at `ℱ' = g^*ℱ` of the natural
transformation `Stacks.Perfect.SupportedFraction.fractionClassTrans` that [Stacks, Tag 0G7Q] is
registered at — `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` read on `X` along the fully faithful `i_*`, with source the
quotient `ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ = i_*i^*ℱ` that the remark presents it on — the bottom arrow is the
comparison of the two quotients, and the top arrow is the degree-`c` comparison, which is the map
of Cohomology, Remark 0G78 on cohomology sheaves in degree `c` by
`degreeCBaseChange_eq_homology_zeroG78`.

**Why this is the remark's diagram.**  The remark's diagram lives on `Z'`, with corners
`h^*i^*ℱ`, `(i')^*ℱ'`, `(i')^{-1}𝒪_{X'} ⊗_{h^{-1}i^{-1}𝒪_X} h^{-1}ℋ^c_Z(ℱ) = h^*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)` and
`ℋ^c_{Z'}(ℱ')`.  Applying the fully faithful `i'_*` does not change whether it commutes, and
`i'_*h^* = g^*i_*` for the cartesian square `Z' = Z ×_X X'` of the setting
(`AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.isPullback_equationsClosedSubscheme`) carries its
left-hand corners to `g^*(i_*i^*ℱ)` and `g^*(i_*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ))`; this is the form in which the library
states the class map of [Stacks, Tag 0G7Q] itself.

The proof cancels the epimorphism `g^*` of the projection `ℱ ⟶ i_*i^*ℱ` and is then
`supportedFractionSource_baseChange`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fractionClassTrans_baseChange [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).map ((fractionClassTrans f).app F) ≫
        degreeCBaseChange g f F =
      equationsQuotientBaseChange g f F ≫
        (fractionClassTrans (fun j => g.appTop (f j))).app
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F)
declarations.comment: the first diagram of the remark with all four arrows, for quasi-coherent F: the components of the Tag 0G7Q transformation c_{f_1,...,f_c} at F and at F' = g^*F on the quotients i_*i^*F = F/(f_1,...,f_c)F, the comparison of the two quotients as bottom arrow, and the degree-c comparison (the Tag 0G78 map in degree c) as top arrow; read on X' along the fully faithful i'_*

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDegreeCBaseChangeOnClosed.fractionClassOnClosed_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G7U], the first diagram, on the closed subscheme `Z'`.**  Let `g : X' ⟶ X` be
a morphism of schemes, `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, `f'ⱼ = g^♯(fⱼ)`, `Z ⊆ X` and `Z' ⊆ X'` the
closed subsets cut out by them, made into ringed spaces `(Z, i^{-1}𝒪_X)` and
`(Z', (i')^{-1}𝒪_{X'})`, and `h : Z' ⟶ Z` the induced morphism (`closedRestriction`).  For a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, with `ℱ' = g^*ℱ`, the diagram

```
h^*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)   --topArrow-->   ℋ^c_{Z'}(ℱ')
     ^                              ^
h^*c_{f₁,…,f_c}               c_{f'₁,…,f'_c}
     |                              |
h^*i^*ℱ      --bottomArrow-->   (i')^*ℱ'
```

commutes.  Here `c_{f₁,…,f_c}` and `c_{f'₁,…,f'_c}` are the components at `ℱ` and at `ℱ'` of
`Stacks.Perfect.GysinLocalCohomology.fractionClassOnClosed`, the map of [Stacks, Tag 0G7Q] on the
closed subset, with source the remark's presentation `i^*(ℱ/(f₁, …, f_c)ℱ)` of `i^*ℱ`; the
left-hand top corner is `h^*ℋ^c_Z(ℱ) = (i')^{-1}𝒪_{X'} ⊗_{h^{-1}i^{-1}𝒪_X} h^{-1}ℋ^c_Z(ℱ)`, the
inverse image of modules along the morphism of ringed spaces `h`; the bottom arrow is the
canonical comparison `h^*i^*ℱ ≅ (i')^*g^*ℱ = (i')^*ℱ'`; and the top arrow is the one determined by
the degree-`c` comparison `degreeCBaseChange`, which is the map of Cohomology, Remark 0G78 on
cohomology sheaves in degree `c`
(`Stacks.Perfect.CechDegreeCBaseChange.degreeCBaseChange_eq_homology_zeroG78`).

The proof is the remark's: the diagram read on `X'` is
`Stacks.Perfect.CechDegreeCBaseChange.fractionClassTrans_baseChange`, and `comp_transposeTop`
descends it to `Z'`, the comparison of inverse images being conjugate to the comparison of direct
images by `Stacks.Cohomology.conjugateEquiv_pullbackCompSquare`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fractionClassOnClosed_baseChange [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (modulePullback (closedRestriction g f)).map ((fractionClassOnClosed f).app F) ≫
        topArrow g f F =
      bottomArrow g f F ≫
        (fractionClassOnClosed (fun j => g.appTop (f j))).app
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F)
declarations.comment: the first diagram of the remark on the closed subscheme Z', for quasi-coherent F: h^*c_{f_1,...,f_c} followed by the top arrow h^*H^c_Z(F) -> H^c_{Z'}(F') equals the canonical h^*i^*F -> (i')^*F' followed by c_{f'_1,...,f'_c}, with c the Tag 0G7Q map on the closed subset

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechDerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeSquare_cech
declarations.doc:
**The derived diagram of [Stacks, Tag 0G7U] commutes**, for the lower horizontal arrow and
the down arrow the remark itself writes down.  This is
`Stacks.Perfect.SupportedDerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeSquare` instantiated at
`cechDerivedBaseChange` and `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpaceThickening.derivedPullbackSingleObj`,
whose compatibility with the augmentations of [Stacks, Tag 0G7L] is
`cechDerivedBaseChange_comp_augmentation`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedBaseChangeSquare_cech :
    (derivedPullback g.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
          (cechToDerivedSupport f F (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) le_rfl) ≫
        supportedPullbackRoute g.toLRSHom.toShHom (equationsClosedSet f)
            (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f)
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F) ≫
        (supportPush (isClosed_equationsClosedSet_pullback g f)).map
          (derivedPullbackSingleObj g.toLRSHom.toShHom F) =
      cechDerivedBaseChange g f F ≫
        cechToDerivedSupport (fun j => g.appTop (f j)) ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj F)
          (isClosed_equationsClosedSet_pullback g f) (equationsClosedSet_pullback_subset g f)
declarations.comment: the derived diagram of the remark, with the remark's own lower horizontal arrow Lg^*F^bullet -> g^*F^bullet -> (F')^bullet and its own down arrow induced by Lg^*F -> g^*F = F', for an arbitrary O_X-module F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.isPullback_equationsClosedSubscheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7U**, the assertion `Z' = Z ×_X X'` of the setting: the closed
subscheme cut out by the pulled-back equations `f'ᵢ = g^♯(fᵢ)` is the base change along `g` of
the closed subscheme cut out by `f₁, …, f_c`, the induced morphism of schemes being
`equationsClosedSubschemeBaseChange`.

The set-theoretic form of the same assertion, which is the shape [Stacks, Tag 0G78] and hence
the remark's diagrams are stated at, is
`Stacks.Perfect.SupportedDerivedBaseChange.equationsClosedSet_pullback`.
declarations.comment: Z' = Z ×_X X' of the setting, as a pullback square of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendedAlternatingCech.equationsClosedSubschemePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G7U**, the identification `Z' = Z ×_X X'` of the setting, as an
isomorphism of schemes.
declarations.comment: the identification Z' ≅ Z ×_X X' of the setting

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.CechBaseChange.isIso_cplxBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of the two extended alternating Čech complexes is an isomorphism for
quasi-coherent `ℱ`.** This is the corrected form of the note `(ℱ')^• = g^*ℱ^•` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G7U], as an isomorphism of complexes rather than only a morphism — which is what
the remark's first diagram needs, and what lets its top arrow be identified with the
[Stacks, Tag 0G78] map in degree `c` rather than with a Čech-level comparison.

The remark states the note for an arbitrary `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, and in that generality it is
false: `Stacks.Perfect.CechBaseChangeCounterexample.not_isIso_cplxBaseChange_f_one` takes `k` a
field, `g : 𝔸¹_k ⟶ 𝔸²_k` the diagonal, the single equation `x`, and `ℱ` the extension by zero
of `𝒪` from `D(y)`, and shows that this comparison is not an isomorphism in degree `1`
(`Stacks.Perfect.CechBaseChangeCounterexample.isEmpty_iso_cplx`: the two complexes are not
isomorphic by any isomorphism).  The quasi-coherence hypothesis is therefore needed here; it is
the hypothesis under which the remark's first diagram is asserted.

A morphism of complexes is invertible as soon as every component is
(`HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components`); here the degree-`0` component is the identity and
the rest is `isIso_prodTermBaseChange`. No flatness on `g`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_cplxBaseChange (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsIso (cplxBaseChange g f F)
declarations.comment: the note `(F')^• = g^*F^•`, corrected to quasi-coherent `F` and read through the comparison map; for an arbitrary `F` it is false, see `CechBaseChangeCounterexample.not_isIso_cplxBaseChange_f_one`

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethGlobalMapCanonical
declarations.doc:
**The global Künneth map of Tag 0G7V, with no parameter.**

`RΓ(X, K) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, M) ⟶ RΓ(W, Lp^*K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_W} Lq^*M)`

in `D(A)` for `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`, where `p ≫ a = f = q ≫ b`; the source takes `W = X ×_S Y` with its
two projections.  It is defined for arbitrary `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and `M ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, over an arbitrary
base, and it is built from the canonical global cup product of Section 0FKU on the base together
with the relative Künneth map of Tag 0FLP and the Leray isomorphism of Tag 0D5W.
declarations.statement:
def kunnethGlobalMapCanonical (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))) :
    ((tensorBase S).obj ((sectionsOverBase a).obj K)).obj ((sectionsOverBase b).obj M) ⟶
      (sectionsOverBase f).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj ((derivedPullback p).obj K)).obj
          ((derivedPullback q).obj M))
declarations.comment: the map, for arbitrary K ∈ D(𝒪_X) and M ∈ D(𝒪_Y) over an arbitrary base

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethGlobalMapCanonical_naturality
declarations.doc: **The global Künneth map with no parameter is natural in both complexes jointly.**
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethGlobalMapCanonical_naturality
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))}
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))} (k : K ⟶ K') (m : M ⟶ M') :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
          ((sectionsOverBase a).map k ×ₘ (sectionsOverBase b).map m) ≫
        kunnethGlobalMapCanonical a b p q f hp hq K' M' =
      kunnethGlobalMapCanonical a b p q f hp hq K M ≫
        (sectionsOverBase f).map
          ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
            ((derivedPullback p).map k ×ₘ (derivedPullback q).map m))
declarations.comment: naturality in both complexes, with no parameter

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical
declarations.doc:
**The global Künneth map of Tag 0G7V at the fibre product of two schemes, with no
parameter.**  For schemes `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` over a base and `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`, the
canonical map

`RΓ(X, K) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, M) ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Y, Lp^*K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_{X ×_S Y}} Lq^*M)`

in `D(A)`, where `p` and `q` are the two projections of `X ×_S Y`.  The base scheme is arbitrary
and `K`, `M` are arbitrary; quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, quasi-coherence and
Tor-independence enter only in Tag 0FLQ, which asserts that this map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (M : DerivedCategory Y.Modules) :
    ((tensorBase S.toRingedSpace).obj ((sectionsOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)).obj
        ((sectionsOverBase b.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M) ⟶
      (sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (pullback a b).toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
            ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj K)).obj
          ((derivedPullback (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M))
declarations.comment: the map at X ×_S Y, for arbitrary K and M over an arbitrary base scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalKunneth.kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The global Künneth map at the fibre product of two schemes, with no parameter, is natural in
both complexes.**
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical_naturality {K K' : DerivedCategory X.Modules}
    {M M' : DerivedCategory Y.Modules} (k : K ⟶ K') (m : M ⟶ M') :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S.toRingedSpace)).map
          ((sectionsOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom).map k ×ₘ
            (sectionsOverBase b.toLRSHom.toShHom).map m) ≫
        kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical a b K' M' =
      kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical a b K M ≫
        (sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).map
          ((Functor.uncurry.obj
              (derivedTensorProductFunctor (pullback a b).toRingedSpace.sheaf)).map
            ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).map k ×ₘ
              (derivedPullback (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).map m))
declarations.comment: naturality at the fibre product of two schemes, with no parameter

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.KunnethCupWithClass.kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical_cupWithClass
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0G7W.**  Let `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` be morphisms of schemes, let
`p : X ×_S Y ⟶ X` and `q : X ×_S Y ⟶ Y` be the projections, and set `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`.  Let
`𝒢, ℱ ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and `ℰ ∈ D(𝒪_Y)` — for instance quasi-coherent modules placed in degree
zero — and let `ξ ∈ Hⁱ(X, 𝒢)`, with pullback `p^*ξ ∈ Hⁱ(X ×_S Y, Lp^*𝒢)`, represented by the
morphism `A[-i] ⟶ RΓ(X, 𝒢)` representing `ξ` followed by the pullback map
`p^* : RΓ(X, 𝒢) ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Y, Lp^*𝒢)` (that this represents the class `Hⁱ(p^*)(ξ)` is
`Stacks.Cohomology.KunnethCupWithClass.classOverBase_comp_homology`).  Then the square

```
RΓ(X, ℱ)[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, ℰ) --ξ ⊗ 1--> RΓ(X, 𝒢 ⊗ ℱ) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, ℰ)
           |                                            |
           v                                            v
RΓ(X ×_S Y, Lp^*ℱ ⊗ Lq^*ℰ)[-i] --p^*ξ--> RΓ(X ×_S Y, Lp^*(𝒢 ⊗ ℱ) ⊗ Lq^*ℰ)
```

commutes in `D(A)`.  The horizontal arrows are cup product with a class, Remark 0G6W, for the
`A`-linear global cup products of Section 0FKU on `X` and on `X ×_S Y`; the vertical arrows are
the global Künneth map of Equation 36.23.0.2, `kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical` (Tag 0G7V),
shifted by `[-i]` through the source's identification `M[-i] = A[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A M`.  Nothing is a
parameter: the cup products, the pullback map, the associativity constraint `baseAssociator`
of `⊗^𝐋_A` (that of `D({*}, A)` read through `D(A) = D({*}, A)`, as in Section 0FKU) and that
of `⊗^𝐋_{𝒪}` (Tag 0FPB) are all canonical.  The two identifications the source makes silently in
the bottom-right corner, `Lp^*(𝒢 ⊗ ℱ) = Lp^*𝒢 ⊗ Lp^*ℱ` (Tag 079U) and the rebracketing, are
the last two arrows of the right-hand route.  No quasi-coherence, affineness or finiteness
hypothesis is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical_cupWithClass
    (𝒢 ℱ : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (ℰ : DerivedCategory Y.Modules) (i : ℤ)
    (ξ : ModuleCat.of (baseRing S.toRingedSpace) (baseRing S.toRingedSpace) ⟶
      cohomologyModuleOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom 𝒢 i) :
    ((tensorBase S.toRingedSpace).map
          (cupWithClassOverBase (sectionsOverBaseComparison a.toLRSHom.toShHom) 𝒢 ℱ i
            (classOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom 𝒢 i ξ))).app
          ((sectionsOverBase b.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ) ≫
        kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical a b
            (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj 𝒢).obj ℱ) ℰ ≫
          (sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).map
              ((Functor.uncurry.obj
                  (derivedTensorProductFunctor (pullback a b).toRingedSpace.sheaf)).map
                (pullbackTensorComparisonApp (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom 𝒢 ℱ ×ₘ
                  𝟙 ((derivedPullback (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ))) ≫
            (sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).map
              (derivedAssociator (pullback a b).toRingedSpace
                ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj 𝒢)
                ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℱ)
                ((derivedPullback (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ)) =
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S.toRingedSpace)).map
          ((baseShiftTensorIso S.toRingedSpace i
              ((sectionsOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℱ)).inv ×ₘ
            𝟙 ((sectionsOverBase b.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ)) ≫
        baseAssociator S.toRingedSpace (baseShift S.toRingedSpace i)
            ((sectionsOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℱ)
            ((sectionsOverBase b.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ) ≫
          ((tensorBase S.toRingedSpace).obj (baseShift S.toRingedSpace i)).map
              (kunnethGlobalMapSchemeCanonical a b ℱ ℰ) ≫
            (baseShiftTensorIso S.toRingedSpace i
              ((sectionsOverBase (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
                (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (pullback a b).toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
                  ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℱ)).obj
                    ((derivedPullback (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ)))).hom ≫
              cupWithClassOverBase
                (sectionsOverBaseComparison (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom)
                ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj 𝒢)
                (((derivedTensorProductFunctor (pullback a b).toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
                    ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℱ)).obj
                  ((derivedPullback (pullback.snd a b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj ℰ)) i
                (classOverBase a.toLRSHom.toShHom 𝒢 i ξ ≫
                  pullbackSections a.toLRSHom.toShHom (pullback.fst a b).toLRSHom.toShHom
                    (pullback.fst a b ≫ a).toLRSHom.toShHom rfl 𝒢)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.kunnethOverBase_cupWithClassOverBase
declarations.doc:
**Remark 0G7W.**  Let `a : X ⟶ S` and `b : Y ⟶ S` be spaces over a base, let `p : W ⟶ X`,
`q : W ⟶ Y` and `f : W ⟶ S` with `p ≫ a = f = q ≫ b`, and set `A = Γ(S, 𝒪_S)`.  For
`𝒢, ℱ ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, `ℰ ∈ D(𝒪_Y)` and a class `ξ ∈ Hⁱ(X, 𝒢)` represented by a morphism
`A[-i] ⟶ RΓ(X, 𝒢)`, the square

```
RΓ(X, ℱ)[-i] ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, ℰ) --ξ ⊗ 1--> RΓ(X, 𝒢 ⊗^𝐋 ℱ) ⊗^𝐋_A RΓ(Y, ℰ)
           |                                            |
           v                                            v
RΓ(W, Lp^*ℱ ⊗^𝐋 Lq^*ℰ)[-i] --p^*ξ--> RΓ(W, Lp^*(𝒢 ⊗^𝐋 ℱ) ⊗^𝐋 Lq^*ℰ)
```

commutes in `D(A)`, the horizontals being cup product with a class as in Remark 0G6W and the
verticals the global Künneth map of Equation 36.23.0.2.  The right-hand route is continued by
the pullback–tensor comparison of Tag 079U and the associativity constraint, the two
identifications the source makes silently in its bottom-right corner.
declarations.statement:
theorem kunnethOverBase_cupWithClassOverBase
    (aA : ∀ P Q Z : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing S)),
      ((tensorBase S).obj (((tensorBase S).obj P).obj Q)).obj Z ⟶
        ((tensorBase S).obj P).obj (((tensorBase S).obj Q).obj Z))
    (aB : ∀ U V Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing W)),
      ((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj U).obj V)).obj Z ⟶
        ((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj U).obj
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj V).obj Z))
    (haA : ∀ {P P' Q Q' Z Z' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing S))} (k : P ⟶ P')
        (l : Q ⟶ Q') (m : Z ⟶ Z'),
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
            ((Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map (k ×ₘ l) ×ₘ m) ≫ aA P' Q' Z' =
        aA P Q Z ≫
          (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
            (k ×ₘ (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map (l ×ₘ m)))
    (haB : ∀ {U U' V V' Z Z' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing W))}
        (k : U ⟶ U') (l : V ⟶ V') (m : Z ⟶ Z'),
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
            ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map (k ×ₘ l) ×ₘ m) ≫
          aB U' V' Z' =
        aB U V Z ≫
          (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
            (k ×ₘ (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map (l ×ₘ m)))
    (hα : ∀ P Q Z : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (baseRing S)),
      κW.tensorComparison.app ((Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).obj (P, Q), Z) ≫
          (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
              (κW.tensorComparison.app (P, Q) ×ₘ 𝟙 (κW.pullback.obj Z)) ≫
            aB (κW.pullback.obj P) (κW.pullback.obj Q) (κW.pullback.obj Z) =
        κW.pullback.map (aA P Q Z) ≫
          κW.tensorComparison.app (P, (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).obj (Q, Z)) ≫
            (Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
              (𝟙 (κW.pullback.obj P) ×ₘ κW.tensorComparison.app (Q, Z)))
    (hπ : CupProductPullbackCompatible κX κW π)
    (ξ : baseShift S i ⟶ (sectionsOverBase a).obj 𝒢) :
    ((tensorBase S).map (cupWithClassOverBase κX 𝒢 ℱ i ξ)).app
            ((sectionsOverBase b).obj ℰ) ≫
        kunnethOverBase κW π ρ (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj 𝒢).obj ℱ) ℰ ≫
          (sectionsOverBase f).map
              ((Functor.uncurry.obj (derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf)).map
                (pullbackTensorComparisonApp p 𝒢 ℱ ×ₘ 𝟙 ((derivedPullback q).obj ℰ))) ≫
            (sectionsOverBase f).map
              (aB ((derivedPullback p).obj 𝒢) ((derivedPullback p).obj ℱ)
                ((derivedPullback q).obj ℰ)) =
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBase S)).map
          ((baseShiftTensorIso S i ((sectionsOverBase a).obj ℱ)).inv ×ₘ
            𝟙 ((sectionsOverBase b).obj ℰ)) ≫
        aA (baseShift S i) ((sectionsOverBase a).obj ℱ) ((sectionsOverBase b).obj ℰ) ≫
          ((tensorBase S).obj (baseShift S i)).map (kunnethOverBase κW π ρ ℱ ℰ) ≫
            (baseShiftTensorIso S i
              ((sectionsOverBase f).obj
                (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj
                  ((derivedPullback p).obj ℱ)).obj ((derivedPullback q).obj ℰ)))).hom ≫
              cupWithClassOverBase κW ((derivedPullback p).obj 𝒢)
                (((derivedTensorProductFunctor W.sheaf).obj ((derivedPullback p).obj ℱ)).obj
                  ((derivedPullback q).obj ℰ)) i (ξ ≫ π 𝒢)
declarations.comment: the commutativity of the square, for A-linear cup products built from a one-point comparison on X and on W (the parameters `κX`, `κW`, as for Section 0FKU in this development), for the pullback map `π` on derived global sections with its compatibility `hπ` with the two cup products (Cohomology, Lemma 0FP6, which this development cannot transport onto them), and for associativity constraints `aA`, `aB` with their naturality `haA`, `haB` and the compatibility `hα` of the comparison with them, all universally quantified; the source's suppressed identifications p^*(G ⊗ F) = p^*G ⊗ p^*F of Tag 079U and the rebracketing are the last two arrows of the right-hand route

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Fibres.extendsOverNeighbourhood_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G7X].**  An idempotent global function on a fibre of a proper morphism is the
restriction of a section of the structure sheaf over the inverse image of an open neighbourhood
of the base point;  equivalently, it lies in the image of the stalk `(f_* 𝒪_X)_s`.  Nothing is
assumed on the base:  its locally Noetherian case is
`Stacks.FormalFunctions.extendsOverNeighbourhood_of_isLocallyNoetherian`, and the general case
follows from it by the approximation argument above.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extendsOverNeighbourhood_of_isProper {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    (s : S) (e : Γ(f.fiber s, ⊤)) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
    ExtendsOverNeighbourhood f s e

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.GeomReducedFibre.exists_open_finiteEtale_and_derivedPushforward_splitting
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G7Y].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper, flat and of finite presentation and let
`s ∈ S` be a point whose fibre `X_s` is geometrically reduced. Then there is an affine open
neighbourhood `U` of `s` such that

* `f_*𝒪_X` is a finite etale `𝒪_S`-algebra over `U`: for every affine open `V ⊆ U` the ring
  map `Γ(S, V) → Γ(X, f⁻¹V)` is finite and etale;
* `Rf_*𝒪_X ≅ f_*𝒪_X ⊕ P` in `D(𝒪_U)` with `P` perfect of Tor amplitude in `[1, b]` for some `b`
  (so in `[1, ∞)`), at every model of the derived categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_finiteEtale_and_derivedPushforward_splitting {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hfp : FinitePresentation f) [IsProper f] [Flat f] (s : S)
    (hred : GeometricallyReduced (f.fiberToSpecResidueField s)) :
    ∃ U : S.Opens, s ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧
      (∀ V : S.affineOpens, V.1 ≤ U →
        letI : Algebra Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) := (f.app V.1).hom.toAlgebra
        Module.Finite Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) ∧ Algebra.Etale Γ(S, V.1) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ V.1)) ∧
      ∃ b : ℤ, 1 ≤ b ∧ ∀ (hX : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.Modules)
        (hU : HasDerivedCategory.{w} U.toScheme.Modules),
        letI := hX
        letI := hU
        letI : HasDerivedCategory.{w}
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.toSheafedSpace)) := hX
        letI : HasDerivedCategory.{w}
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing U.toScheme.toSheafedSpace)) := hU
        ∃ P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules,
          @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect U.toScheme.toRingedSpace hU P ∧
          @Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitude U.toScheme.toRingedSpace hU P 1 b ∧
          Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor U.toScheme.Modules 0).obj
              ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (f ∣_ U)).obj
                (Scheme.unitModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)) ⊞ P ≅
            (Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward
              (f ∣_ U).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.Modules 0).obj
                (Scheme.unitModule (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_isZero_naiveCotangentHomology
declarations.doc:
**Étale morphisms by the naive cotangent complex.** A morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is
étale if and only if it is locally of finite presentation and both cohomology sheaves
`H⁻¹(NL_{X/S})` and `H⁰(NL_{X/S})` of its naive cotangent complex vanish.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_iff_locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_isZero_naiveCotangentHomology (f : X ⟶ S) :
    Etale f ↔
      (LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧
        IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology (-1)) ∧
        IsZero ((Scheme.naiveCotangentComplex f).homology 0))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.of_comp_of_etale
declarations.doc:
Let `X → Y → Z` be morphisms of schemes. If `X → Z` is smooth and `Y → Z` is étale, then
`X → Y` is smooth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Smooth.of_comp_of_etale {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [Smooth (f ≫ g)] [Etale g] : Smooth f

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_homEquiv_symm_relativeCupProduct_comp_trace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G81.** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and
`f : X ⟶ Y` a proper, flat morphism of finite presentation; let `a` be the right adjoint of
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E], `ω^•_{X/Y} = a(𝒪_Y)` the relative
dualizing complex and `Tr_{f, 𝒪_Y} : Rf_*ω^•_{X/Y} ⟶ 𝒪_Y` the trace of [Stacks, Tag 0B6S]. Let
`K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and `M ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `M` pseudo-coherent, and let
`φ : K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} M ⟶ ω^•_{X/Y}` be a map whose transpose `K ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(M, ω^•_{X/Y})` under
the tensor–internal-Hom bijection of [Stacks, Tag 08DI] is an isomorphism. Then the map
`Rf_*K ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*M, 𝒪_Y)` corresponding under that bijection on `Y` to

`Rf_*K ⊗^L_{𝒪_Y} Rf_*M ⟶ Rf_*(K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} M) ⟶ Rf_*ω^•_{X/Y} ⟶ 𝒪_Y`

(the relative cup product of [Stacks, Tag 0B68], `Rf_*φ` and `Tr_{f, 𝒪_Y}`) is an isomorphism.

The source asks `K` to lie in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`; that is not used. The instance arguments
`CompactSpace X` and `QuasiSeparatedSpace X` restrict nothing: they hold for every proper `f` over
a quasi-compact quasi-separated `Y` (`AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated`), and are arguments only because
the right adjoint `a` of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E] at this model is found by instance search from them.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homEquiv_symm_relativeCupProduct_comp_trace (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (M : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (hM : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) M.obj)
    (φ : ((derivedTensorProductFunctor X.sheaf).obj K).obj M.obj ⟶
      (relativeDualizingComplex f (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
        (derivedStructureSheafInDegree Y 0)).obj)
    (hφ : IsIso (((derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf)).homEquiv
      K M.obj (relativeDualizingComplex f
        (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
        (derivedStructureSheafInDegree Y 0)).obj).symm φ)) :
    IsIso (((derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf)).homEquiv
      ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ((derivedPushforward f).obj M.obj)
      (derivedStructureSheafInDegree Y 0).obj).symm
        (relativeCupProduct f.toLRSHom.toShHom K M.obj ≫ (derivedPushforward f).map φ ≫
          (ι _).map (relativeDualizingComplexTrace f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
            (derivedStructureSheafInDegree Y 0))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.gysinMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G83: the Gysin map.** Let `π : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let
`f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`, and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be the closed subscheme they cut
out, that is, let the ideal sheaf of `i` be generated by `f₁, …, f_c`. The Gysin map

`γ^p_{f₁, …, f_c} : Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})`

is the unique morphism whose value on the restriction `ω̃|_Z` of a local `p`-form `ω̃` on `X` is
`c_{f₁, …, f_c}(ω̃|_Z) ∧ d f₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d f_c`. Both sheaves are read on `X` through the direct image
along `i`, which is faithful; `ℋ^c_Z` is the local cohomology sheaf and `c_{f₁, …, f_c}` the
canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0G7Q].

**The content is well-definedness**, that is, independence of the chosen lift `ω̃`: the map
`gysinFormulaHom` kills the kernel of restriction to `Z`, because a lift is determined up to
`∑ f_j ω'_j + ∑ ω''_j ∧ d f_j` — that is
`formKernelGeneratedByEquations_of_isCutOutByEquations`, where the hypothesis on `Z` enters —
and both kinds of term go to zero, the first by `smulHom_comp_gysinFormulaHom`, the second by
`exactFormWedgeHom_comp_gysinFormulaHom`. The map is then the descent of `gysinFormulaHom` along
the epimorphism `formRestriction`, taken constructively with
`CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiDesc`.
declarations.statement:
def gysinMap (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (π : X ⟶ S) {c : ℕ}
    (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) (p : ℕ)
    (hcut : Stacks.Gysin.IsCutOutByEquations i f) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (relativeDifferentialForms (i ≫ π) (p : ℤ)) ⟶
      pushforwardLocalCohomology f
        (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the Gysin map γ^p_{f_1, …, f_c}, for the closed subscheme cut out by the equations: no hypothesis beyond the source's own, that the ideal sheaf of i is generated by f_1, …, f_c.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.formRestriction_comp_gysinMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G83: the formula for the Gysin map.** On the restriction `ω̃|_Z` of a
local `p`-form `ω̃` on `X`, the Gysin map takes the value
`c_{f₁, …, f_c}(ω̃|_Z) ∧ d f₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d f_c`. This is the equation of the source, and it determines
`gysinMap` because restriction to `Z` is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem formRestriction_comp_gysinMap (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (π : X ⟶ S) {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) (p : ℕ)
    (hcut : Stacks.Gysin.IsCutOutByEquations i f) :
    formRestriction i π (p : ℤ) ≫ gysinMap i π f p hcut = gysinFormulaHom π f (p : ℤ)
declarations.comment: the formula γ^p(ω) = c_{f_1, …, f_c}(ω̃|_Z) ∧ d f_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ d f_c, for the closed subscheme cut out by the equations, with no hypothesis beyond the source's own.

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.gysinMap
registrations.comment: the displayed map γ^p_{f_1, …, f_c} : Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ ℋ^c_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S}) of Remark 0G83, with both sheaves read on X through their direct images, that is as i_*Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*ℋ^c_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S}); both direct images are faithful, and no descent of either sheaf to Z is available, source and target being modules over different rings on Z. No hypothesis beyond the source's own, that the ideal sheaf of i is generated by f_1, …, f_c.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.gysinMapCommutesWithDeRham
declarations.doc:
The Gysin map of [Stacks, Tag 0G83] is compatible with the de Rham differentials on
`Ω^•_{X/S}` and `Ω^•_{Z/S}`: the square

`i_*Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})`,  `i_*Ω^{p+1}_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_Z(Ω^{p+c+1}_{X/S})`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.GysinMapCommutesWithDeRham` commutes.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.gysinMap_comm_deRham
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G85.**  The Gysin map `γ^p_{f₁, …, f_c}` of [Stacks, Tag 0G83] is
compatible with the de Rham differentials on `Ω^•_{X/S}` and `Ω^•_{Z/S}`, for **every** number
`c ≥ 0` of equations: the square

`i_*Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})`,  `i_*Ω^{p+1}_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*ℋ ᶜ_Z(Ω^{p+c+1}_{X/S})`

commutes, whose horizontal arrows are `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.gysinMap` in degrees `p` and
`p + 1` (read on underlying abelian sheaves, the second followed by the canonical identification of
the degrees `(p + 1) + c = p + c + 1`), whose left vertical arrow is the de Rham differential of
`Z/S` pushed forward along `i`, and whose right vertical arrow is the action of `i_*ℋ ᶜ_Z` on the
de Rham differential of `X/S` given by [Stacks, Tag 0G74] part (2).

The square is checked after precomposition with the epimorphism of restriction of forms to `Z`,
where the Gysin map becomes the Gysin formula, and there it is
`abelianSheaf_map_gysinFormulaHom_comm`.
The hypotheses are exactly those of `gysinMap`: `i` a closed immersion cut out by
`f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)`, with `c` arbitrary — `c = 0` included.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinMap_comm_deRham (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (π : X ⟶ S) {c : ℕ}
    (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤)) (p : ℕ) (hcut : Stacks.Gysin.IsCutOutByEquations i f) :
    (abelianSheaf X).map (gysinMap i π f p hcut) ≫
        pushforwardLocalCohomologyAbelianMap (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) c
          (deRhamDifferentialAbHom π (p + c)) =
      pushforwardDeRhamDifferentialAbHom i π p ≫
        (abelianSheaf X).map (gysinMap i π f (p + 1) hcut ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg
            (fun k : ℤ => pushforwardLocalCohomology f (relativeDifferentialForms π k))
            (gysinAnyTargetDegree_eq c p)))

registrations.name: Stacks.Perfect.AbelianCechCokernelPassage.map_cokernelLastDifToSupport_abelian_square
