declarations.name: Stacks.Gysin.existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G86: the canonical Gysin map of a closed immersion.**  Let
`π : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed immersion of finite presentation
whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank `c`.  Then there is **one** map

`γ^p : i_*Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ i_*ℋ^c_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})`

which, over every open contained in an open on which `c` functions generate the ideal of `Z`, is
the Gysin map `γ^p_{f₁, …, f_c}` of [Stacks, Tag 0G83] of those functions, and it is the only map
with that property.

**The rank is an arbitrary natural number.**  [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] says `c ≥ 0` explicitly, so
`c = 0` is part of the statement and not a degenerate exclusion; it is the case in which `Z` is a
*clopen* piece of `X`, by `Stacks.Gysin.isClopen_range_base_of_conormalRank_zero`, and in which a
chart carries the empty family of equations.  The hypotheses are exactly the tag's: no bound on
`c`, and in particular neither `c ≠ 0` nor a rank of the form `d + 1`.

The proof splits on `c` and nothing else does:

* for `c = d + 1`, `Stacks.Gysin.existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank_succ`, the chart route
  through `Stacks.Gysin.GysinChartData` — the charts then cover `X`, because away from the closed
  subscheme the equations may be taken to generate the unit ideal;
* for `c = 0`, `existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank_zero`, where the charts cover only the
  image and the gluing is run on the family augmented by its complement.

The charts are *all* the equation charts of `Stacks.Gysin.EquationChart`, which is what makes the
conclusion quantify over every local family of `c` equations cutting out `Z` and not only over a
chosen covering family.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i] (π : X ⟶ S) {c : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (hE : ConormalRank i c) :
    ∃! φ : pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ) ⟶ gysinTarget i π c p,
      ∀ (a : EquationChart i c) (V : X.Opens) (hV : V ≤ a.ambient)
        (x : Γ(pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ), V)),
        φ.app V x =
          chartLoc i π p a.ambient a.equations
            (isCutOutByEquationsOn_of_isGeneratedByOn i a.gen a.vanish)
            (equationsClosedSet_restrictEquations i a.ambient
              (isCutOutByEquationsOn_of_isGeneratedByOn i a.gen a.vanish)) V hV x

declarations.name: Stacks.Gysin.gysinHom_comm_deRham_of_conormalRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G87: the Gysin map is compatible with the de Rham differentials.**

Let `π : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `i : Z ⟶ X` a closed immersion of finite
presentation whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank `c` — the hypotheses of
[Stacks, Tag 0G86], and nothing more.  Let `γ` and `γ'` be the Gysin maps of [Stacks, Tag 0G86]
in the degrees `p` and `p + 1`, each characterised as that tag characterises it: over every open
contained in an equation chart it is the Gysin map `γ^p_{f₁, …, f_c}` of [Stacks, Tag 0G83] of
that chart's equations.  Then the square

`ℋ ᶜ_Z(d_{X/S}) ∘ γ^p = γ^{p+1} ∘ d_{Z/S}`

commutes, on the sections over every open of `X`.  The left vertical arrow is the relative de
Rham differential of `Z/S` (`Stacks.Gysin.pushforwardDeRham`), the right one the action of
`i_*ℋ ᶜ_Z` on the relative de Rham differential of `X/S` given by [Stacks, Tag 0G74] part (2)
(`Stacks.Gysin.gysinTargetDeRhamHom`).

**The rank is an arbitrary natural number**, as [Stacks, Tag 0G86] states it and as
[Stacks, Tag 0G8A] says explicitly (`c ≥ 0`).  In particular `c = 0` — the case in which `Z` is a
*clopen* piece of `X`, by `Stacks.Gysin.isClopen_range_base_of_conormalRank_zero`, and in which
an equation chart carries the empty family — is part of the statement and not a degenerate
exclusion; neither `c ≠ 0` nor a rank of the form `d + 1` is assumed.

Both maps `γ`, `γ'` with these properties exist and are unique at every rank, by
`Stacks.Gysin.existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank`, the registration of [Stacks, Tag 0G86]; the
characterisations are stated here verbatim as they are there.

The proof splits on `c` and nothing else does:

* for `c = d + 1`, `gysinHom_comm_deRham_of_conormalRank_succ`, the chart route — the charts then
  cover `X`, and the square at one chart family is `gysinHom_comm_deRham_charts`;
* for `c = 0`, `Stacks.Gysin.gysinHom_comm_deRham_of_conormalRank_zero`, where the charts cover
  only the image of `i` and the square is glued on the family augmented by its complement.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHom_comm_deRham_of_conormalRank (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i] (π : X ⟶ S) {c : ℕ} (p : ℕ)
    (hE : ConormalRank i c)
    (γ : pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ) ⟶ gysinTarget i π c p)
    (γ' : pushforwardRelativeForms i π ((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ⟶ gysinTarget i π c (p + 1))
    (hγ : ∀ (a : EquationChart i c) (V : X.Opens) (hV : V ≤ a.ambient)
      (x : Γ(pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ), V)),
      γ.app V x =
        chartLoc i π p a.ambient a.equations
          (isCutOutByEquationsOn_of_isGeneratedByOn i a.gen a.vanish)
          (equationsClosedSet_restrictEquations i a.ambient
            (isCutOutByEquationsOn_of_isGeneratedByOn i a.gen a.vanish)) V hV x)
    (hγ' : ∀ (a : EquationChart i c) (V : X.Opens) (hV : V ≤ a.ambient)
      (x : Γ(pushforwardRelativeForms i π ((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ), V)),
      γ'.app V x =
        chartLoc i π (p + 1) a.ambient a.equations
          (isCutOutByEquationsOn_of_isGeneratedByOn i a.gen a.vanish)
          (equationsClosedSet_restrictEquations i a.ambient
            (isCutOutByEquationsOn_of_isGeneratedByOn i a.gen a.vanish)) V hV x)
    (V : X.Opens) (x : Γ(pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ), V)) :
    abSectionsHom (gysinTargetDeRhamHom i π c p) V (γ.app V x) =
      γ'.app V (pushforwardDeRham i π p V x)

declarations.name: Stacks.Gysin.conormalGysin_formRestriction_cupDegreeZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G88 at the canonical Gysin maps of [Stacks, Tag 0G86], with nothing
assumed.**  The only hypotheses are the tag's own: `i` a closed immersion of finite presentation
whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank `c`.

**`c` is an arbitrary natural number**, as [Stacks, Tag 0G86] states it and as [Stacks, Tag 0G8A]
says explicitly (`c ≥ 0`): the case `c = 0`, in which `Z` is a *clopen* piece of `X` by
`Stacks.Gysin.isClopen_range_base_of_conormalRank_zero` and in which a chart carries the empty
family of equations, is part of the statement and not a degenerate exclusion.

The maps are `Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.conormalGysinHom`, the `γ^p` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G86] itself, whose characterisation is
`Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.conormalGysinHom_app`; the degree comparison is the canonical
transport, whose one equation is `Stacks.Gysin.eqToHom_app_gysinWedgeOn_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalGysin_formRestriction_cupDegreeZero [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i]
    (hE : ConormalRank i c) (q : ℕ) :
    (_root_.Hfunctor X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ q).map (formRestriction i π (p : ℤ)) ≫
        (_root_.Hfunctor X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ q).map
          (Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.conormalGysinHom i π p hE) =
      Stacks.Cohomology.cupDegreeZero X.ringCatSheaf (conormalWedgePair i π c p)
        (conormalUnitClass i π
          (eqToHom (congrArg (relativeDifferentialForms π) (natCast_zero_add c)))
          (Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.conormalGysinHom i π 0 hE)) q

declarations.name: Stacks.Gysin.GysinBaseChange.gysinHom_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G89.** For a transverse cartesian square the Gysin maps of
[Stacks, Tag 0G86] on the two closed immersions fit into a commutative square: the base-change
map on the targets applied to `γ^p` agrees with `γ^p` applied to the pullback of relative
differential forms.

The commutativity is checked locally, which is what the source does: on a covering of the open by
opens inside an equation chart over which the form lifts to the ambient scheme, it is
`gysinHom_baseChange_subschemeFormPullback`; the target is a sheaf, so it holds over the open
itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHom_baseChange (V : X.Opens) (x : Γ(pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ), V)) :
    B.tgt V (D.gysinHom.app V x)
      = D'.gysinHom.app (g ⁻¹ᵁ V) (subschemeFormBaseChange i i' h g π π' t left_comm right_comm
          (p : ℤ) V x)
declarations.comment: the Gysin square of a transverse cartesian square commutes, for the Gysin maps GysinChartData.gysinHom of Stacks 0G86; granted the right vertical arrow of Stacks 0G78 descended to degree c by the vanishing of Stacks 0G7N as the hypothesis B.tgt with B.tgt_res, the class-map base-change square of Stacks 0G7U as the hypothesis B.tgt_cls, hypotheses (2) and (3) of the statement -- the left square cartesian and the conormal comparison of Stacks 01R4 an isomorphism -- as the chart correspondence B.chart with B.chart_ambient and B.chart_equations, and the local liftability of relative forms coming from the conormal sequence of Stacks 01UZ as the hypothesis B.lift; none of these four is proved in this library

declarations.name: Stacks.Gysin.conormalGysinHom_comp_gysinBaseChangeTargetHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G89.**  Let `c ≥ 0` and let
```
Z' ⟶ X' ⟶ S'
↓h    ↓g    ↓t
Z  ⟶ X  ⟶ S
```
be a commutative diagram of schemes such that

1. `i : Z ⟶ X` and `i' : Z' ⟶ X'` satisfy the assumptions of [Stacks, Tag 0G86]: closed
   immersions of finite presentation whose conormal sheaves are locally free of rank `c`
   (`hE`, `hE'`);
2. the left square is cartesian (`hcart`);
3. the map `h^*𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z'/X'}` of [Stacks, Tag 01R4] is an isomorphism (`_hconormal`).

Then the Gysin maps `γ^p` of [Stacks, Tag 0G86] commute with the pullback of differential forms
on the left and the base change arrow of [Stacks, Cohomology, Remark 0G78] on the right,
descended to degree `c` by the vanishing of [Stacks, Tag 0G7N].  The square is stated on `X`:
the left vertical arrow `gysinBaseChangeSourceHom` is the transpose of `h^*Ω^p_{Z/S} ⟶ Ω^p_{Z'/S'}`
pushed forward, and the right vertical arrow `gysinBaseChangeTargetHom` is the transpose along
`g^* ⊣ g_*` of the source's right vertical arrow, whose source is `g^*` of `i_*ℋ^c_Z(Ω^{p+c})`.

**On hypothesis (3).**  It is the source's hypothesis and is kept as the binder `_hconormal`,
but the proof does not consume it: given (2), the map of (3) is surjective (the ideal of `Z'` is
generated by the pullback of the ideal of `Z`), and given (1) both sides are locally free of the
same finite rank `c`, so a surjection between them is an isomorphism; in other words (3) is
implied by (1) and (2).  What the proof uses of the transversality is that the pulled-back
equations `g^♯f₁, …, g^♯f_c` of an equation chart of `Z` cut out `Z'` over the preimage chart,
`Stacks.Gysin.EquationChart.ofIsPullback`, which needs only (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalGysinHom_comp_gysinBaseChangeTargetHom (hcart : IsPullback h i' i g)
    (right_comm : g ≫ π = π' ≫ t) {c : ℕ} (p : ℕ) (hE : ConormalRank i c)
    (hE' : ConormalRank i' c)
    (_hconormal : IsIso (Stacks.Immersion.immersionConormalSheafMap i' i h g
      (congrArg (fun k => k.toLRSHom.toShHom) hcart.w.symm))) :
    (conormalGysinHom i π p hE ≫ (conormalGysinTargetIso i π c p).hom) ≫
        gysinBaseChangeTargetHom i i' h g π π' t hcart right_comm p hE =
      gysinBaseChangeSourceHom i i' h g π π' t hcart.w right_comm (p : ℤ) ≫
        (modulePushforward g.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
          (conormalGysinHom i' π' p hE' ≫
            (conormalGysinTargetIso i' π' c p).hom)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G8A.**  Let `π : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `i : Z ⟶ X` a
closed immersion of finite presentation whose conormal sheaf is locally free of rank `c`
— the hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0G86].  Let `p ≥ 0` and assume

`ℋ^j_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S}) = 0` for `j = 0, …, c - 1`.

Then there is a map

`γ^{p, q} : H^q(Z, Ω^p_{Z/S}) ⟶ H^{q + c}(X, Ω^{p + c}_{X/S})`

for every `q`, obtained exactly as the source obtains it: the `γ^p` of [Stacks, Tag 0G86]
followed by the passage `ℋ^c_Z(ℱ) = R𝓗_Z(ℱ)[c]`, the identification `H^q(Z, -) = H^q(X, i_*-)`
and the adjunction map `i_*R𝓗_Z(ℱ) ⟶ ℱ`.

The sheaf-level map is `conormalGysinHom`, the `γ^p` of [Stacks, Tag 0G86] itself — glued from the
Gysin maps of [Stacks, Tag 0G83] of the local families of equations, not built from one global
family — and the three remaining steps are `gysinHodgeFormsMap`, which performs them for an
arbitrary sheaf-level Gysin map.  The one identification in between is
`conormalGysinTargetIso`, between two spellings of `i_*ℋ^c_Z(Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})` that agree because
the direct image along the inclusion of a closed subset is exact.

Nothing is assumed: both hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 0G86] are consumed where the source consumes
them, by `Stacks.Gysin.existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank`, the quasi-coherence of
`Ω^p_{Z/S}` needed by [Stacks, Tag 089W] is proved inside `gysinHodgeFormsMap`, and `hvan` is the
source's own vanishing hypothesis.  The sufficient condition of [Stacks, Tag 0G7P] is not
available here and is not used.

**The rank is an arbitrary natural number**, as the tag states it: [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] says
`c ≥ 0` explicitly.  Nothing here needs `c ≠ 0`, because
`Stacks.Gysin.existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank` supplies `γ^p` at every rank — it splits on
`c`, the chart route of `Stacks.Gysin.exists_gysinCharts` handling `c = d + 1` and
`Stacks.Gysin.existsUnique_gysinHom_of_conormalRank_zero` handling `c = 0`, where the local
families of equations are empty and the charts cover the image rather than `X`.

`hvan` is retained because it is the source's own hypothesis, not an artefact of the rank: at
`c = 0` it is vacuous in content — the degrees `j < 0` carry none, by
`Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.isZero_localCohomologySheafOfComplex_of_neg` — and the
construction consumes it uniformly.

**What rank `0` forces, and what it does not.**  `ConormalRank i 0` says exactly that the
conormal sheaf of `i` vanishes, so the ideal sheaf vanishes on an affine neighbourhood of every
point of `Set.range i.base` —
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ConormalEquations.exists_affineOpen_equations_of_conormalRank`, read at
`c = 0`, returns such a neighbourhood and it carries no hypothesis on `c`.  Hence `i` is an
isomorphism onto an open subscheme, which being also closed has *clopen* range.  It does **not**
force that range to be the whole of `X`: the identity satisfies `ConormalRank i 0`, and so does
the inclusion of a proper clopen piece.  The equations of the chapter cannot see the latter, by
`Stacks.Gysin.equationsClosedSet_eq_range`: an empty family cutting out `i` in the sense of
`Stacks.Gysin.IsCutOutByEquations` makes `Set.range i.base` the whole of `X`.  That is why the
`c = 0` branch of [Stacks, Tag 0G86] is glued on the charts together with the complement of the
image instead of on a `Stacks.Gysin.GysinChartData`.
declarations.statement:
def gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i] (π : X ⟶ S) {c : ℕ} (p : ℕ)
    (hE : ConormalRank i c)
    (hvan : ∀ j : ℤ, j < (c : ℤ) →
      IsZero (localCohomologySheafOfComplex X.toRingedSpace (Set.range i.base)
        i.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range j ((singleFunctor _ (0 : ℤ)).obj
          (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ))))))
    (q : ℕ) :
    Hgroup Z.ringCatSheaf ⊤ q (relativeDifferentialForms (i ≫ π) (p : ℤ)) ⟶
      Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ (q + c)
        (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamKoszul.koszulGysinCohomologyMap_comm_deRham
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G8B.**  Let `π : X ⟶ S` be a *smooth* morphism of schemes and let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be as in [Stacks, Tag 0G86] — a closed immersion of finite presentation whose
conormal sheaf is finite locally free of rank `c` — and *Koszul-regular*.  The
cohomological Gysin maps `γ^{p, q} : H^q(X, i_*Ω^p_{Z/S}) ⟶ H^{q + c}(X, Ω^{p + c}_{X/S})` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G8A] attached to the glued `γ^p` of [Stacks, Tag 0G86] are compatible with the de
Rham differentials on `Ω^•_{X/S}` and `Ω^•_{Z/S}`: the square

```
H^q(X, i_*Ω^p_{Z/S}) ----γ^{p, q}----→ H^{q+c}(X, Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})
        ↓ d                                     ↓ d
H^q(X, i_*Ω^{p+1}_{Z/S}) --γ^{p+1, q}→ H^{q+c}(X, Ω^{p+c+1}_{X/S})
```

commutes, the verticals being the arrows the de Rham differentials induce on cohomology through
`Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRham.abelianHgroupMap`.

The square itself is
`Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamConormal.conormalGysinCohomologyMap_comm_deRham`, which
assumes the vanishing of [Stacks, Tag 0G8A]; here that vanishing is
`supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms`, derived from the hypotheses of this tag through
[Stacks, Tag 0G7P], so that nothing beyond them is assumed.  That the map the square is about is
the tagged `γ^{p, q}` of [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] and not a second construction is
`Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamConormal.gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank_eq`.

**The rank is an arbitrary natural number**, as [Stacks, Tag 0G86] states it and
[Stacks, Tag 0G8A] says explicitly (`c ≥ 0`); neither `c ≠ 0` nor a rank of the form `d + 1` is
assumed.  Both inputs are already general: the vanishing
`supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms` handles `c = 0` separately — in degrees `j < 0`
there is nothing to vanish — and the square
`Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamConormal.conormalGysinCohomologyMap_comm_deRham` rests on
[Stacks, Tag 0G87] at an arbitrary rank,
`Stacks.Gysin.gysinHom_comm_deRham_of_conormalRank`.
declarations.statement:
theorem koszulGysinCohomologyMap_comm_deRham (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i] (π : X ⟶ S) [Smooth π]
    (hkos : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) {c : ℕ} (p q : ℕ)
    (hE : ConormalRank i c) :
    gysinCohomologyMap (Set.range i.base) (isClosed_range_base i) c
          (pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ))
          (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
          (supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms i π hkos c hE p)
          (conormalGysinHom i π p hE ≫ (conormalGysinTargetIso i π c p).hom) q ≫
        abelianHgroupMap X.toRingedSpace (0 : ℤ) ((q : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)) (q + c)
          (by omega) (ambientDeRhamShiftAbHom π c p) =
      abelianHgroupMap X.toRingedSpace (c : ℤ) ((q : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)) q
          (by omega) (pushforwardDeRhamDifferentialAbHom i π p) ≫
        gysinCohomologyMap (Set.range i.base) (isClosed_range_base i) c
          (pushforwardRelativeForms i π ((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
          (relativeDifferentialForms π (((p + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
          (supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms i π hkos c hE
            (p + 1))
          (conormalGysinHom i π (p + 1) hE ≫
            (conormalGysinTargetIso i π c (p + 1)).hom) q

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.GysinProjection.equationGysinCohomologyMap_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**The cohomological projection formula for the Gysin map of a family of equations.**  Let
`π : X ⟶ S`, let `f₁, …, f_c ∈ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` with `c = n + 1` and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be the closed
subscheme they cut out.  Then the composite

`H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S}) --(restriction to Z)--> H^q(X, i_*Ω^p_{Z/S}) --γ^{p,q}--> H^{q+c}(X, Ω^{p+c})`

is the composite

`H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S}) --(Gysin formula)--> H^{q+c}_Z(X, Ω^{p+c}) --(forget support)--> H^{q+c}(X, …)`,

the first arrow of the second composite being induced by the morphism of sheaves carrying a local
`p`-form `ω̃` to the class of `ω̃ ∧ d f₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d f_c` divided by `f₁ ⋯ f_c`.

**This is the cohomological content of [Stacks, Tag 0G88]** for the Gysin map of a family of
equations, which is items (1), (2) and (4) of the source's proof of [Stacks, Tag 0G8C]: the
sheaf-level projection formula is the formula clause of [Stacks, Tag 0G83],
`formRestriction_comp_gysinMapOfFormKernel`, and the two factorisations are
`cohomologyMapOfModuleHom_comp` and `gysinCohomologyMap_eq`.  Nothing is assumed beyond the
hypotheses `hker` and `hvan` that [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] already carries.
declarations.statement:
theorem equationGysinCohomologyMap_comp_eq (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (π : X ⟶ S) {n : ℕ}
    (f : Fin (n + 1) → Γ(X, ⊤)) (p : ℕ)
    [(relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))).IsQuasicoherent]
    (hker : FormKernelGeneratedByEquations i π f (p : ℤ))
    (hvan : EquationSupportVanishes π f p) (q : ℕ) :
    cohomologyMapOfModuleHom X.toRingedSpace _ _ (n + 1) q (formRestriction i π (p : ℤ)) ≫
        equationGysinCohomologyMap i π f p hker hvan q =
      cohomologyMapOfModuleHom X.toRingedSpace _ _ (n + 1) q (gysinFormulaHom π f (p : ℤ)) ≫
        forgetSupportCohomology (equationsClosedSet f) (isClosed_equationsClosedSet f) (n + 1)
          (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))) hvan q
declarations.comment: the cohomological content of the proof, items (1), (2) and (4) of the source's list, for the Gysin map of a family of equations: gamma^{p,q} of the restriction of alpha to Z is the class with support of alpha wedge df_1 wedge ... wedge df_c over f_1 ... f_c with its support forgotten, proved with no hypothesis beyond the hker and hvan that Tag 0G8A already carries; the remaining identification of that class with alpha cup gamma^{0,0}(1) is Cohomology Tags 0G77 and 0G76 in the Hgroup presentation of the groups, which is absent here

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.GysinCupHodge.gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank_hodgeRestriction
declarations.doc:
**The Gysin map and the cup product** [Stacks, Tag 0G8C]. Let `π : X ⟶ S` be smooth and
`i : Z ⟶ X` a Koszul regular closed immersion of finite presentation whose conormal sheaf is
locally free of rank `c` (`hE`). For `α ∈ H^q(X, Ω^p_{X/S})`,
`γ^{p,q}(α|_Z) = (-1)^{qc} α ∪ γ^{0,0}(1)` in `H^{q+c}(X, Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})`.

Here `α|_Z` is `hodgeRestriction i π p q α`, `γ^{a,b}` is the Gysin map
`gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank` of Tag 0G8A, whose vanishing hypothesis is proved from the
smoothness of `π` and the Koszul regularity of `i` (`supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms`,
Tag 0G7P), `1 ∈ H^0(Z, Ω^0_{Z/S})` is `oneFormCohomologyClass`, and `∪` is the cup product
`hodgeCupStructureSheaf` of Cohomology, Section 0FKU. The cup product is stated on the modules
`H^m(RΓ(X, -))`, so both sides are read through the bridge `hgroupModuleShiftIso`, an
isomorphism.

The sign `(-1)^{qc}` comes from the identification `H^q(X, A) ≅ H^{q+c}(RΓ(X, A[-c]))` of the
bridge, which is sign-free, where the source uses the Koszul-signed identification; it appears
at `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedGlobalCupProduct.totalCupPairing_shift₂`. Under the Koszul-signed
identification this is the source's formula `γ^{p,q}(α|_Z) = α ∪ γ^{0,0}(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank_hodgeRestriction (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i] (π : X ⟶ S) [Smooth π] {c : ℕ} (hE : ConormalRank i c)
    (hK : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i) (p q : ℕ)
    (α : Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ q (relativeDifferentialForms π (p : ℤ))) :
    (hgroupModuleShiftIso (X := X.toRingedSpace) (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
        0 (q + c) ((q : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)) (by push_cast; ring)).hom
      ((Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank i π p hE
        (Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamKoszul.supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms
          i π hK c hE p) q).hom
        ((hodgeRestriction i π p q).hom α)) =
    ((q : ℤ) * (c : ℤ)).negOnePow •
      (hodgeCupStructureSheaf π p c q c).hom
        ((hgroupModuleShiftIso (X := X.toRingedSpace) (relativeDifferentialForms π (p : ℤ)) 0 q q
          (by simp)).hom α ⊗ₜ
        (hgroupModuleShiftIso (X := X.toRingedSpace) (relativeDifferentialForms π (c : ℤ)) 0 (0 + c)
          c (by push_cast; ring)).hom
          ((Hfunctor X.ringCatSheaf ⊤ (0 + c)).map
            (eqToHom (congrArg (relativeDifferentialForms π) (by push_cast; ring)))
            ((Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank i π 0 hE
              (Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamKoszul.supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms
                i π hK c hE 0) 0).hom
              (Stacks.DeRham.GysinProjection.oneFormCohomologyClass (i ≫ π)))))
declarations.comment: the full statement, at the source's hypotheses (pi smooth, i a Koszul regular closed immersion of finite presentation with conormal sheaf locally free of rank c), with the cup product of Cohomology Section 0FKU constructed and nothing assumed; stated with the sign: gamma^{p,q}(alpha|_Z) = (-1)^{qc} alpha cup gamma^{0,0}(1). The sign comes from this library's sign-free identification H^q(X, A) = H^{q+c}(R Gamma(X, A[-c])) of the bridge hgroupModuleShiftIso, where the source uses the Koszul-signed identification; it appears at totalCupPairing_shift₂. Under the Koszul-signed identification the formula is the source's gamma^{p,q}(alpha|_Z) = alpha cup gamma^{0,0}(1)

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyBaseChange.conormalGysinCohomologyMap_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G8D.** Let `c ≥ 0` and let

```
Z' → X' → S'
↓h   ↓g    ↓t
Z  → X  → S
```

satisfy the assumptions of [Stacks, Tag 0G89]: `Z → X` and `Z' → X'` are closed immersions of
finite presentation whose conormal sheaves are locally free of rank `c`, the left square is
cartesian and `h^*𝒞_{Z/X} → 𝒞_{Z'/X'}` is an isomorphism.  Assume in addition that `X → S`,
`X' → S'` are smooth and `Z → X`, `Z' → X'` are Koszul regular immersions.  Then

```
H^q(Z, Ω^p_{Z/S})  ----γ^{p,q}---→ H^{q+c}(X, Ω^{p+c}_{X/S})
       ↓                                    ↓
H^q(Z', Ω^p_{Z'/S'}) --γ^{p,q}---→ H^{q+c}(X', Ω^{p+c}_{X'/S'})
```

commutes, `γ^{p,q}` being the Gysin map of [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] at the `γ^p` of
[Stacks, Tag 0G86].

The cohomology of the closed subschemes is read on the ambient schemes, `H^q(X, i_*Ω^p_{Z/S})`,
which is how [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] constructs `γ^{p,q}` (and how the registered [Stacks, Tag 0G8B]
reads it); the vertical maps are the pullback maps on cohomology of [Stacks, Tag 01F9] built from
the canonical comparisons `CohomologyPullbackComparison.canonical` of [Stacks, Tag 01F8] and
[Stacks, Tag 01EZ], at the `g`-maps of relative differential forms — on the left the pullback of
forms along `h`, read on `X` (`Stacks.Gysin.gysinBaseChangeSourceHom`), on the right
functoriality of `Ω^{p+c}` (`Stacks.Gysin.formsBaseChangeHom`).  Both are the standard pullback
maps, with the module placed in degree `0`; that the placement degree does not matter is
`pullbackHgroup_canonical_eq`.

Nothing is assumed beyond the source: the vanishing that [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] needs is derived
from smoothness and Koszul regularity by [Stacks, Tag 0G7P]; the sheaf square is
[Stacks, Tag 0G89] (`Stacks.Gysin.conormalGysinHom_comp_gysinBaseChangeTargetHom`, whose
binder `_hconormal` is hypothesis (3) as the source states it); and the compatibility of the
Gysin edge morphisms with pullback, [Stacks, Tag 0G78] and
[Stacks, Tag 0G79], is `gysinEdge_baseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalGysinCohomologyMap_pullback (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (h : Z' ⟶ Z)
    (g : X' ⟶ X) (π : X ⟶ S) (π' : X' ⟶ S') (t : S' ⟶ S)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i]
    [IsClosedImmersion i'] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation i']
    {c : ℕ} (hE : ConormalRank i c) (hE' : ConormalRank i' c)
    (hcart : IsPullback h i' i g) (right_comm : g ≫ π = π' ≫ t)
    (hconormal : IsIso (Stacks.Immersion.immersionConormalSheafMap i' i h g
      (congrArg (fun k => k.toLRSHom.toShHom) hcart.w.symm)))
    [Smooth π] [Smooth π'] (hkos : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i)
    (hkos' : IsKoszulRegularImmersion i') (p q : ℕ) :
    gysinCohomologyMap (Set.range i.base) (isClosed_range_base i) c
          (pushforwardRelativeForms i π (p : ℤ))
          (relativeDifferentialForms π ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
          (Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamKoszul.supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms
            i π hkos c hE p)
          (conormalGysinHom i π p hE ≫ (conormalGysinTargetIso i π c p).hom) q ≫
        pullbackHgroup (CohomologyPullbackComparison.canonical g.toLRSHom.toShHom) (0 : ℤ)
          ((q : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)) (q + c) (by omega)
          (formsBaseChangeHom g π π' t right_comm ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
      = pullbackHgroup (CohomologyPullbackComparison.canonical g.toLRSHom.toShHom) (0 : ℤ)
          (q : ℤ) q (by omega)
          (gysinBaseChangeSourceHom i i' h g π π' t hcart.w right_comm (p : ℤ)) ≫
        gysinCohomologyMap (Set.range i'.base) (isClosed_range_base i') c
          (pushforwardRelativeForms i' π' (p : ℤ))
          (relativeDifferentialForms π' ((p : ℤ) + (c : ℤ)))
          (Stacks.DeRham.GysinCohomologyDeRhamKoszul.supportVanishing_relativeDifferentialForms
            i' π' hkos' c hE' p)
          (conormalGysinHom i' π' p hE' ≫ (conormalGysinTargetIso i' π' c p).hom) q

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRham.CohomologicalGysin.gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank_oneClass_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G8E].** Let `k` be a field and `X` an irreducible smooth proper scheme over
`k` of dimension `d`. Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be the reduced closed subscheme consisting of a single
`k`-rational point, i.e. a closed immersion with `Z ≅ Spec k` over `k`. Then the image of
`1 ∈ k = H^0(Z, 𝒪_Z) = H^0(Z, Ω^0_{Z/k})` under the Gysin map
`H^0(Z, Ω^0_{Z/k}) ⟶ H^d(X, Ω^d_{X/k})` of [Stacks, Tag 0G8A] is nonzero. The identification
`ω_X^• ≅ Ω^d_{X/k}[d]` the argument uses is [Stacks, Tag 0FVV], part (7).
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank_oneClass_ne_zero (d : ℕ) [IsProper π] [Smooth π]
    [IrreducibleSpace X] (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = d) [IsIso (i ≫ π)] :
    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension d π := smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_equidimensional k π
      (TopologicalSpace.Equidimensional.of_preirreducibleSpace X) d hd
    haveI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation i := locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_comp i π
    gysinHodgeFormsMapOfConormalRank i π (c := d) 0 (conormalRank_of_formallyUnramified i π d)
      (supportVanishing_of_formallyUnramified i π d 0) 0 (oneClass π i) ≠ 0
declarations.comment: for X irreducible smooth proper over a field k of dimension d and Z the reduced closed subscheme of a k-rational point, the Gysin map H^0(Z, Omega^0_{Z/k}) -> H^d(X, Omega^d_{X/k}) of 0G8A sends 1 to a nonzero class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDualitySituation
declarations.doc:
A proper smooth morphism over a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, with all fibres
nonempty and equidimensional of dimension `n`.
declarations.statement: structure RelativeDualitySituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDualitySituation.structureSheafDirectImage
declarations.doc:
In the relative duality situation `f : X ⟶ S`:

1. `f_*𝒪_X` is a finite étale `𝒪_S`-algebra: the structure morphism of its relative spectrum
   is finite and étale;
2. locally on `S`, `Rf_*𝒪_X ≅ f_*𝒪_X ⊕ P` in `D(𝒪_S)` with `P` perfect of Tor amplitude in
   `[1, ∞)`: every point of `S` has an open neighbourhood `U` over which this holds in `D(𝒪_U)`;
3. the map `d : f_*𝒪_X ⟶ f_*Ω_{X/S}` is zero: the degree-zero de Rham differential vanishes on
   sections over `f⁻¹V` for every open `V` of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem structureSheafDirectImage (D : RelativeDualitySituation.{u}) :
    (letI := isQuasicoherent_pushforwardAlgebra_of_quasiCompact D.f;
      IsFinite (relativeSpecToBase (pushforwardAlgebra D.f)) ∧
        Etale (relativeSpecToBase (pushforwardAlgebra D.f))) ∧
    (∀ s : D.S, ∃ (U : D.S.Opens) (_ : s ∈ U)
      (P : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u}
        (D.S.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))),
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect P ∧
      Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeGE
        (D.S.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding) P 1 ∧
      Nonempty ((RingedSpace.derivedRestrictModules D.S.toRingedSpace U).obj
          ((derivedPushforward D.f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
            (structureSheafDegreeZeroObj D.X)) ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((RingedSpace.restrictModules D.S.toRingedSpace U).obj
            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward D.f).obj (Scheme.unitModule D.X))) ⊞ P)) ∧
    (∀ V : D.S.Opens, ((Scheme.Hom.deRhamComplex D.f).d 0 1).val.app (op (D.f ⁻¹ᵁ V)) = 0)
declarations.comment: the three assertions: (1) f_*O_X is a finite étale O_S-algebra (its relative Spec is finite étale over S); (2) locally on S, Rf_*O_X = f_*O_X ⊕ P in D(O_S) with P perfect of tor amplitude in [1, ∞); (3) d : f_*O_X → f_*Ω_{X/S} is zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDualitySituation.existsUnique_isRelativePoincareTrace
declarations.doc:
In the situation of relative Poincaré duality ([Stacks, Tag 0G8G]), `f : X ⟶ S` proper and
smooth over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base, all of whose fibres are nonempty and
equidimensional of dimension `n`, there is an `𝒪_S`-module map
`t : Rf_*Ω^n_{X/S}[n] ⟶ 𝒪_S` such that for all `p` the pairing
`Rf_*Ω^p_{X/S} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω^{n-p}_{X/S}[n] ⟶ 𝒪_S` given by the relative cup product composed with
`t` is a perfect pairing of perfect complexes, and `t` is unique up to precomposing with
multiplication by a unit of `H^0(X, 𝒪_X)`: the maps with this property are exactly the
`t ∘ u` for `u` a unit of `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isRelativePoincareTrace :
    ∃ t : (Stacks.Duality.derivedPushforward D.f).obj ((D.f.formsInDegreeZero D.n)⟦(D.n : ℤ)⟧) ⟶
        (Stacks.Duality.derivedStructureSheafInDegree D.S 0).obj,
      D.IsRelativePoincareTrace t ∧ ∀ t', D.IsRelativePoincareTrace t' ↔
        ∃ u : (Γ(D.X, ⊤))ˣ, t' = D.f.formsShiftSMul D.n u ≫ t
declarations.comment: relative Poincaré duality trace: there is t : Rf_*Omega^n[n] -> O_S, unique up to a unit of H^0(X, O_X), all of whose pairings Rf_*Omega^p (x)^L Rf_*Omega^{n-p}[n] -> O_S are perfect pairings of perfect complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilDeRham.higherDirectImage_map_deRham_d_top_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G8J.** In the situation of relative Poincaré duality
([Stacks, Tag 0G8G]) — `S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `f : X ⟶ S` proper and smooth, all
fibres nonempty and equidimensional of dimension `n` — the map
`d : Rⁿf_*Ω^{n-1}_{X/S} ⟶ Rⁿf_*Ωⁿ_{X/S}` induced by the de Rham differential is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDirectImage_map_deRham_d_top_eq_zero (D : RelativeDualitySituation.{u}) :
    (Stacks.Cohomology.AbelianSheaf.higherDirectImage D.f.base D.n).map
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).map (D.f.deRhamComplex.d (D.n - 1) D.n)) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDualitySituation.existsUnique_deRhamPoincareTrace
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0G8K].** In the situation of relative Poincaré duality ([Stacks, Tag 0G8G]):
`S` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `f : X ⟶ S` proper and smooth, all of whose fibres are
nonempty and equidimensional of dimension `n`. There is an `𝒪_S`-module map
`t : R^{2n}f_*Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ 𝒪_S` such that the pairing
`Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S}[2n] ⟶ 𝒪_S`, `(ξ, ξ') ↦ t(ξ ∪ ξ')`, is a perfect pairing of
perfect complexes (`IsDeRhamPoincareTrace`, read through the identification
`Hom(Rf_*(Ω^•[2n]), 𝒪_S) ≃ Hom(R^{2n}f_*Ω^•, 𝒪_S)` of `deRhamTraceEquiv`, which holds as
`Rf_*(Ω^•[2n])` has no cohomology in positive degrees), and `t` is unique up to precomposing with
multiplication by a unit of `H^0(X, 𝒪_X)`: the maps with this property are exactly the
`t ∘ u` for `u` a unit of `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_deRhamPoincareTrace :
    ∃ t : D.deRhamTopCohomology ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit D.S.ringCatSheaf,
      D.IsDeRhamPoincareTrace (D.deRhamTraceEquiv.symm t) ∧
      ∀ t' : D.deRhamTopCohomology ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit D.S.ringCatSheaf,
        D.IsDeRhamPoincareTrace (D.deRhamTraceEquiv.symm t') ↔
          ∃ u : (Γ(D.X, ⊤))ˣ, t' = D.deRhamTopCohomologySMul (u : Γ(D.X, ⊤)) ≫ t
declarations.comment: relative Poincaré duality for de Rham cohomology: there is t : R^{2n}f_*Omega^. -> O_S, unique up to a unit of H^0(X, O_X), such that (xi, xi') |-> t(xi cup xi') is a perfect pairing Rf_*Omega^. (x)^L Rf_*Omega^.[2n] -> O_S of perfect complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedSubgroupScheme_iff_factor
declarations.doc: The factorization criterion for a closed subscheme to be a subgroup scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedSubgroupScheme_iff_factor {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Grp (Over S)) {H : Over S} (j : H ⟶ G.X)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion j.left] :
    (∃ K : ClosedSubgroupScheme G,
      ∃ e : H ≅ K.carrier.X, j = e.hom ≫ K.ι.hom.hom) ↔
      ((∃ e : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ H, e ≫ j = η[G.X]) ∧
       (∃ m : H ⊗ H ⟶ H, m ≫ j = (j ⊗ₘ j) ≫ μ[G.X]) ∧
       (∃ i : H ⟶ H, i ≫ j = j ≫ ι[G.X]))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenSubgroupScheme_iff_factor
declarations.doc: The factorization criterion for an open subscheme to be a subgroup scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubgroupScheme_iff_factor {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : Grp (Over S)) {H : Over S} (j : H ⟶ G.X)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion j.left] :
    (∃ K : OpenSubgroupScheme G,
      ∃ e : H ≅ K.carrier.X, j = e.hom ≫ K.ι.hom.hom) ↔
      ((∃ e : 𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ H, e ≫ j = η[G.X]) ∧
       (∃ m : H ⊗ H ⟶ H, m ≫ j = (j ⊗ₘ j) ≫ μ[G.X]) ∧
       (∃ i : H ⟶ H, i ≫ j = j ≫ ι[G.X]))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Module.FinitenessViaHomColimit.finite_iff_comparisonMap_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0G8N.** An `R`-module `N` is finite (finitely generated) if and
only if for every filtered colimit `M = colim_i M_i` of `R`-modules the canonical
comparison map `Θ_N : colim_i Hom_R(N, M_i) → Hom_R(N, M)` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_iff_comparisonMap_injective (N : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    Module.Finite R N ↔ InjectiveForAllFilteredColimits R N

declarations.name: finitePresentation_iff_comparisonMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0G8P.** An `R`-module `N` is finitely presented if and only if for
every directed (filtered) system of `R`-modules the canonical comparison map
`Φ : colim_i Hom_R(N, M_i) → Hom_R(N, colim_i M_i)` is bijective.

We quantify over index types `ι` and module families `G` in the universe `u` of `R` and `N`.
The forward direction holds for directed systems in any universe. The converse uses the system
of finitely generated submodules of `N`, which lives in the universe of `N`, and the system of
quotients `(Fin n →₀ R) ⧸ S Q`, which lives in the universe of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_iff_comparisonMap_bijective
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] :
    Module.FinitePresentation R N ↔
      ∀ {ι : Type u} [Preorder ι] [DecidableEq ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
        (G : ι → Type u) [(i : ι) → AddCommGroup (G i)] [(i : ι) → Module R (G i)]
        (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i →ₗ[R] G j)
        [DirectedSystem G (fun i j h => f i j h)],
        Function.Bijective (homColimComparison (R := R) (N := N) (ι := ι) G f)

declarations.name: Ideal.range_eq_affineBlowup_and_ker_eq_saturation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G8S.** Let `R` be a ring, let `I = (a, bᵢ : i ∈ ι)` be an ideal of
`R` generated by `a` together with a family `b : ι → R`, and let `Rₐ` be the
localization of `R` at `a`.  Let `φ : R[xᵢ : i ∈ ι] → Rₐ` be the `R`-algebra map
with `φ xᵢ = bᵢ/a`.  Then the range of `φ` is the affine blowup algebra
`R[I/a] = {x/aⁿ : x ∈ Iⁿ}`, and `φ f = 0` if and only if `aⁿ f` lies in the ideal
of relations `(a xᵢ - bᵢ)` for some `n`; that is, `φ` induces a surjection
`R[xᵢ]/(a xᵢ - bᵢ) → R[I/a]` whose kernel is the `a`-power torsion of the
source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Ideal.range_eq_affineBlowup_and_ker_eq_saturation
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {ι : Type*} {Rₐ : Type*} [CommRing Rₐ] [Algebra R Rₐ]
    {a : R} {b : ι → R} {I : Ideal R} [IsLocalization.Away a Rₐ]
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (insert a (Set.range b)))
    (φ : MvPolynomial ι R →ₐ[R] Rₐ)
    (hφ : ∀ i, φ (X i) * algebraMap R Rₐ a = algebraMap R Rₐ (b i)) :
    Set.range φ =
        {y : Rₐ | ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ x ∈ I ^ n, y * algebraMap R Rₐ a ^ n = algebraMap R Rₐ x} ∧
      ∀ f : MvPolynomial ι R, φ f = 0 ↔
        ∃ n : ℕ, a ^ n • f ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range fun i ↦ C a * X i - C (b i))

declarations.name: projective_of_ext_one_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag 0G8T (Lemma 10.77.3): a finite module `P` over a Noetherian ring `R` is
projective as soon as `Ext¹_R(P, M)` vanishes for every finite `R`-module `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_of_ext_one_eq_zero {R : Type} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (P : Type) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.Finite R P]
    (h : ∀ (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M],
      Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext (C := ModuleCat R) (ModuleCat.of R P) (ModuleCat.of R M) 1)) :
    Module.Projective R P

declarations.name: finiteType_of_isNilpotent_quotient_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0G8U (Lemma 10.126.8).** Let `R` be a ring, let `I` be a nilpotent ideal
of `R`, and let `S` be an `R`-algebra such that the induced ring map `R ⧸ I → S ⧸ IS` is
of finite type. Then the structure map `R → S` is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteType_of_isNilpotent_quotient_finiteType
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (S : Type*) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hI : IsNilpotent I)
    (hft : Algebra.FiniteType (R ⧸ I) (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S))) :
    Algebra.FiniteType R S

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.colimit_ext_comparison_isIso_of_lt_and_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G8W.** If `K` is `m`-pseudo-coherent, then the canonical map from the
filtered colimit of `Extⁿ(K, Mᵢ)` to `Extⁿ(K, colim Mᵢ)` is an isomorphism for
`n < -m`, and is a monomorphism for `n = -m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem colimit_ext_comparison_isIso_of_lt_and_mono
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] {ι : Type v} [Category.{v} ι] [IsFiltered ι]
    (M : ι ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m) :
    let extFunctor (n : ℤ) :=
      DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0 ⋙
        shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) n ⋙
        preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)
    (∀ n : ℤ, n < -m →
      IsIso (colimit.desc (M ⋙ extFunctor n)
        ((extFunctor n).mapCocone (colimit.cocone M)))) ∧
      Mono (colimit.desc (M ⋙ extFunctor (-m))
        ((extFunctor (-m)).mapCocone (colimit.cocone M)))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_colimit_ext_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G8X.** A cohomologically bounded-above object `K` is `m`-pseudo-coherent if and
only if, for every filtered diagram of modules, the canonical map from the filtered colimit of
`Extⁿ(K, -)` to its value on the colimit is an isomorphism for `n < -m` and a monomorphism for
`n = -m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_colimit_ext_comparison
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsLE n) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom K m ↔
      ∀ (ι : Type v) [Category.{v} ι] [IsFiltered ι]
        (M : ι ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R),
        let extFunctor (n : ℤ) :=
          DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0 ⋙
            shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) n ⋙
            preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)
        (∀ n : ℤ, n < -m →
          IsIso (colimit.desc (M ⋙ extFunctor n)
            ((extFunctor n).mapCocone (colimit.cocone M)))) ∧
          Mono (colimit.desc (M ⋙ extFunctor (-m))
            ((extFunctor (-m)).mapCocone (colimit.cocone M)))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.exists_finitelyPresented_module_mono_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G8Y.** For every degree `i`, the degree-`i` cohomology of a pseudo-coherent
object of `D(R)` embeds in a finitely presented `R`-module, and the embedding is induced by a
morphism from the object to that module placed in degree `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitelyPresented_module_mono_homology {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (hK : IsPseudoCoherent K) (i : ℤ) :
    ∃ (M : ModuleCat.{v} R), Module.FinitePresentation R M ∧
      ∃ f : K ⟶ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj M,
        Mono ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).map f ≫
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso
            (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).hom.app M)

declarations.name: factorsThroughProj_iff_free
declarations.doc:
A linear map factors through a projective module if and only if it factors through a free
module.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsThroughProj_iff_free
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [CommRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    FactorsThroughProj φ ↔ FactorsThroughFree φ

declarations.name: FactorsThroughProj.submodule
declarations.doc:
The `R`-linear maps `M →ₗ[R] N` which factor through a projective `R`-module form an
`R`-submodule of `M →ₗ[R] N`.

declarations.name: FactorsThroughProj.comp_comp
declarations.doc:
Factoring through a projective module is stable under precomposition and postcomposition by
arbitrary linear maps.

declarations.name: Module.exists_finite_projective_factorization
declarations.doc:
A linear map out of a *finite* module which factors through a projective module already
factors through a *finite* projective module.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_finite_projective_factorization
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} {N : Type w}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) (hφ : FactorsThroughProj φ) :
    ∃ (P : Type (max u v w)) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module R P)
      (_ : Module.Finite R P) (_ : Module.Projective R P)
      (α : M →ₗ[R] P) (β : P →ₗ[R] N), φ = β ∘ₗ α

declarations.name: Module.isIProjective_iff_free
declarations.doc:
`M` is `I`-projective if and only if for every `a ∈ I` the multiplication-by-`a`
endomorphism of `M` factors through a free `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.isIProjective_iff_free (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.IsIProjective R I M ↔ ∀ a ∈ I, FactorsThroughFree ((LinearMap.lsmul R M) a)

declarations.name: Module.isIProjective_iff_ext_annihilated
declarations.doc: `M` is `I`-projective if and only if `I` annihilates `Ext¹_R(M, N)` for every `R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.isIProjective_iff_ext_annihilated (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    Module.IsIProjective R I M ↔
      ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
        I ≤ Module.annihilator R
          (Abelian.Ext (ModuleCat.of R M) (ModuleCat.of R N) 1)

declarations.name: Module.IsIProjective
declarations.doc:
An `R`-module `M` is *`I`-projective*, for an ideal `I` of `R`, if for every `a ∈ I` the
multiplication-by-`a` endomorphism `m ↦ a • m` of `M` factors through a projective
`R`-module.
declarations.statement:
def Module.IsIProjective (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : Prop

declarations.name: Module.isIProjective_of_smul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
If `M` is annihilated by the ideal `I`, that is `a • m = 0` for all `a ∈ I` and `m : M`, then
`M` is `I`-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.isIProjective_of_smul_eq_zero {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (h : ∀ a ∈ I, ∀ m : M, a • m = 0) :
    Module.IsIProjective R I M

declarations.name: Module.isIProjective_of_injective_of_exact
declarations.doc:
Given a short exact sequence `0 → K →[i] P →[p] M → 0` of `R`-modules with `M` `I`-projective
and `P` projective, the module `K` is `I`-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.isIProjective_of_injective_of_exact {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    {K P M : Type u} [AddCommGroup K] [Module R K] [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Projective R P] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (i : K →ₗ[R] P) (p : P →ₗ[R] M)
    (hi : Function.Injective i) (hp : Function.Surjective p)
    (hexact : LinearMap.range i = LinearMap.ker p)
    (hM : Module.IsIProjective R I M) :
    Module.IsIProjective R I K

declarations.name: Module.IsIProjective.dual
declarations.doc:
If `M` is a finite `I`-projective `R`-module, then its dual `M^∨ = Hom_R(M, R)` is
`I`-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.IsIProjective.dual (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type v)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (hM : Module.IsIProjective R I M) :
    Module.IsIProjective R I (Module.Dual R M)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveAmplitude.existsUnique_iso_biprod_truncations_of_ext_map_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G97.** Let `K` be a bounded above object of `D(R)` and let `a` be an integer.
Assume that for every injective `R`-module map `M ⟶ M'` the induced map
`Ext^{-a}(K, M) ⟶ Ext^{-a}(K, M')` is injective. Then `τ_{≥ a + 1}K` has projective amplitude in
`[a + 1, b]` for some `b`, and there is a *unique* direct sum decomposition
`K ≅ τ_{≤ a}K ⊞ τ_{≥ a + 1}K` compatible with the two canonical truncation maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_biprod_truncations_of_ext_map_injective
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) (a : ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsLE n)
    (hExt : ∀ (M M' : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (f : M ⟶ M'), Mono f →
      Function.Injective (fun x : DerivedCategory.Ext K
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) 0).obj M) (-a) ↦
        x.comp (ShiftedHom.mk₀ 0 rfl
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) 0).map f)) (zero_add _))) :
    ∃ b : ℤ,
      HasProjectiveAmplitude
          ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (a + 1)).obj K) (a + 1) b ∧
        ∃! e : K ≅
            ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE a).obj K ⊞
              (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (a + 1)).obj K),
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι a).app K ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ∧
            (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (a + 1)).app K =
              e.hom ≫ biprod.snd

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveAmplitude.existsUnique_iso_biprod_truncations_of_ext_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G98.** Let `K` be a bounded above object of `D(R)` and let `a` be an integer.
Assume `Ext^{-a}(K, M) = 0` for every `R`-module `M`. Then `τ_{≥ a + 1}K` has projective
amplitude in `[a + 1, b]` for some `b`, and there is a *unique* direct sum decomposition
`K ≅ τ_{≤ a - 1}K ⊞ τ_{≥ a + 1}K` compatible with the two canonical truncation maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_biprod_truncations_of_ext_vanishing
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) (a : ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ n : ℤ, K.IsLE n)
    (hExt : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R,
      Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) 0).obj M) (-a))) :
    ∃ b : ℤ,
      HasProjectiveAmplitude
          ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (a + 1)).obj K) (a + 1) b ∧
        ∃! e : K ≅
            ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE (a - 1)).obj K ⊞
              (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (a + 1)).obj K),
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLEι (a - 1)).app K ≫ e.hom = biprod.inl ∧
            (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (a + 1)).app K =
              e.hom ≫ biprod.snd

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveAmplitude.hasProjectiveAmplitude_iff_perfect_iff_ext_vanishing
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProjectiveAmplitude_iff_perfect_iff_ext_vanishing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) (a b : ℤ) :
    let moduleObject := fun N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R ↦
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) 0).obj N
    let projectiveAmplitude := HasProjectiveAmplitude K a b
    let perfectTorAmplitude := Perfect.IsPerfect K ∧ Perfect.HasFlatRepresentative K a b
    let extOutsideVanishes := ∀ N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.FinitePresentation R N →
      ∀ i : ℤ, i ∉ Set.Icc (-b) (-a) →
        Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) i)
    let upperVanishing :=
      (∀ n : ℤ, b < n →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) n).obj K)) ∧
        ∀ N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.FinitePresentation R N →
          ∀ i : ℤ, -a < i → Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) i)
    let endpointVanishing :=
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ∉ Set.Icc (a - 1) b →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) n).obj K)) ∧
        ∀ N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R, Module.FinitePresentation R N →
          Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) (-a + 1))
    (projectiveAmplitude ↔ perfectTorAmplitude) ∧
      (perfectTorAmplitude ↔ extOutsideVanishes) ∧
      (extOutsideVanishes ↔ upperVanishing) ∧
      (upperVanishing ↔ endpointVanishing)

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.projective_homology_iff_ext_one_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9C.** For a derived object with cohomology concentrated in degrees `-1` and `0`,
vanishing of degree-one Ext against every module is equivalent to vanishing of degree-minus-one
cohomology and projectivity of zero-th cohomology. If the ring is Noetherian and these two
cohomology modules are finite, the same condition can be tested on finite modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem projective_homology_iff_ext_one_vanishing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) :
    let moduleObject := fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R ↦
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N
    let projectiveHomology :=
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).obj K) ∧
        Module.Projective R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj K)
    let extVanishes := ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R,
      Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) 1)
    let finiteExtVanishes := ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R, Module.Finite R N →
      Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) 1)
    (projectiveHomology ↔ extVanishes) ∧
      (IsNoetherianRing R →
        Module.Finite R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).obj K) →
        Module.Finite R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj K) →
        (projectiveHomology ↔ finiteExtVanishes))

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.smooth_and_formallySmooth_iff_ext_one_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9D.** A ring map is smooth if and only if it is of finite presentation and
degree-one Ext from its naive cotangent complex to every module vanishes. It is formally smooth
if and only if the same Ext groups vanish, without a finite-presentation condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smooth_and_formallySmooth_iff_ext_one_vanishing
    {R : Type u'} {S : Type v'} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    let naiveCotangentObject : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u' v'} S) :=
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (HomologicalComplex.double
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Algebra.Generators.self R S).toExtension.cotangentComplex)
          (show (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel (-1) 0 from rfl))
    let extOneVanishes := ∀ N : ModuleCat.{max u' v'} S,
      Subsingleton
        (DerivedCategory.Ext naiveCotangentObject
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u' v'} S) 0).obj N) 1)
    (f.Smooth ↔ f.FinitePresentation ∧ extOneVanishes) ∧
      (f.FormallySmooth ↔ extOneVanishes)

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.exists_twoTerm_representative_free_zero_and_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9E.** A derived object with cohomology only in degrees `-1` and `0` has a
two-term representative whose degree-zero term is free. If the ring is Noetherian and both
cohomology modules are finite, it also has such a representative with finite degree-minus-one
term and finite free degree-zero term.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_twoTerm_representative_free_zero_and_finite
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) :
    (∃ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
      L.IsStrictlyGE (-1) ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE 0 ∧
        Module.Free R (L.X 0) ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K)) ∧
    (IsNoetherianRing R →
      Module.Finite R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).obj K) →
      Module.Finite R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj K) →
      ∃ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
        L.IsStrictlyGE (-1) ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE 0 ∧
          Module.Finite R (L.X (-1)) ∧ Module.Finite R (L.X 0) ∧
            Module.Free R (L.X 0) ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K))

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.ext_one_annihilated_iff_twoTerm_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9F.** For a derived object with cohomology concentrated in degrees `-1` and `0`,
the first Ext groups are annihilated by an ideal exactly when multiplication by every element of
the ideal factors through the differential of a suitable free two-term representative, or of
every projective two-term representative. Under Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses these are
also equivalent to testing only finite modules and to the existence of a finite representative.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ext_one_annihilated_iff_twoTerm_factorization
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (I : Ideal R)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) :
    let moduleObject := fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R ↦
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N
    let extAnnihilated := ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (a : R), a ∈ I →
      ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) 1, a • ξ = 0
    let hasFreeRepresentative := ∃ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
      L.IsStrictlyGE (-1) ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE 0 ∧ Module.Free R (L.X 0) ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K) ∧
        ∀ (a : R), a ∈ I → ∃ h : L.X 0 ⟶ L.X (-1),
          L.d (-1) 0 ≫ h = a • 𝟙 (L.X (-1))
    let everyProjectiveRepresentative := ∀ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
      L.IsStrictlyGE (-1) → L.IsStrictlyLE 0 → Module.Projective R (L.X 0) →
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K) →
        ∀ (a : R), a ∈ I → ∃ h : L.X 0 ⟶ L.X (-1),
          L.d (-1) 0 ≫ h = a • 𝟙 (L.X (-1))
    let finiteExtAnnihilated := ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R), Module.Finite R N →
      ∀ (a : R), a ∈ I → ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) 1, a • ξ = 0
    let hasFiniteFreeRepresentative := ∃ L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ,
      L.IsStrictlyGE (-1) ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE 0 ∧ Module.Finite R (L.X (-1)) ∧
        Module.Finite R (L.X 0) ∧ Module.Free R (L.X 0) ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K) ∧
        ∀ (a : R), a ∈ I → ∃ h : L.X 0 ⟶ L.X (-1),
          L.d (-1) 0 ≫ h = a • 𝟙 (L.X (-1))
    (extAnnihilated ↔ hasFreeRepresentative) ∧
      (hasFreeRepresentative ↔ everyProjectiveRepresentative) ∧
      (IsNoetherianRing R →
        Module.Finite R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).obj K) →
        Module.Finite R
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj K) →
        (extAnnihilated ↔ finiteExtAnnihilated) ∧
          (finiteExtAnnihilated ↔ hasFiniteFreeRepresentative))

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.twoTermBaseChange_iso_truncGE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9G.** Termwise base change of a two-term representative whose degree-zero term
is flat represents the truncation in degrees at least `-1` of the derived base change: the
canonical comparison, transported along the representative isomorphism `e`, factors through
`truncGEπ (-1)` by an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem twoTermBaseChange_iso_truncGE
    {R : Type u} {R' : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    (φ : R →+* R') :
    letI : (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max v (max u w)} φ).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      ModuleCat.instIsLeftAdjointExtendScalars.{u, v, max u w} φ
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R))
      (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) ℤ)
      (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K)
      (_hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
        Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) i).obj K))
      (_hL : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 → Limits.IsZero (L.X i))
      (_hflat : Module.Flat R (L.X 0))
      (derivedBaseChange : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R'))
      (comparison : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedBaseChange ⟶
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max v (max u w)} φ).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      [derivedBaseChange.IsLeftDerivedFunctor comparison
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))],
      ∃ f : ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} R')).truncGE (-1)).obj
          (derivedBaseChange.obj K) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max v (max u w)} φ).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L),
        ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} R')).truncGEπ (-1)).app
          (derivedBaseChange.obj K) ≫ f = derivedBaseChange.map e.inv ≫ comparison.app L ∧
        IsIso f

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.ext_one_annihilated_truncGE_derivedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9H.** If an ideal annihilates every degree-one Ext group from a two-term derived
object, then the extended ideal has the same property for its derived base change truncated in
degrees at least `-1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ext_one_annihilated_truncGE_derivedBaseChange
    {R : Type u} {R' : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing R']
    (I : Ideal R) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) i).obj K))
    (φ : R →+* R')
    (hI : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (a : R), a ∈ I →
      ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) 0).obj N) 1,
        a • ξ = 0)
    (derivedBaseChange : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R'))
    (comparison : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ derivedBaseChange ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q)
    [derivedBaseChange.IsLeftDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    let K' := ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := ModuleCat.{max u v} R')).truncGE (-1)).obj
      (derivedBaseChange.obj K)
    ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R') (a : R'), a ∈ Ideal.map φ I →
      ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K'
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R') 0).obj N) 1,
        a • ξ = 0

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.smul_id_eq_zero_of_two_term_homology_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9I.** Let `α : K ⟶ K'` be a morphism of `D(R)` between objects with cohomology in
degrees `-1` and `0` such that `H⁰(α)` is an isomorphism and `H⁻¹(α)` is surjective. If
multiplication by `f : R` is zero on `K`, then it is zero on `K'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smul_id_eq_zero_of_two_term_homology_map
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)} (α : K ⟶ K')
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K))
    (hK' : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K'))
    (hα0 : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).map α))
    (hαneg : Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).map α))
    (f : R) (hf : f • 𝟙 K = 0) :
    f • 𝟙 K' = 0

declarations.name: TwoTermComplexExt.ext_one_annihilated_of_homology_iso_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9J.** Let `K ⟶ K'` be a morphism of derived objects whose cohomology is
concentrated in degrees `-1` and `0`. If it induces an isomorphism in degree `0` and an
epimorphism in degree `-1`, then ideal annihilation of every first Ext group for `K` implies
the same ideal annihilation for `K'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ext_one_annihilated_of_homology_iso_epi
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)}
    (α : K ⟶ K')
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K))
    (hK' : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K'))
    [IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).map α)]
    [Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).map α)]
    (h : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (a : R), a ∈ I →
      ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N) 1,
        a • ξ = 0) :
    ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (a : R), a ∈ I →
      ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K'
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N) 1,
        a • ξ = 0

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.exists_power_ext_one_annihilated_iff_cohomology_conditions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9K.** For a two-term derived object, some power of an ideal annihilates all
first Ext groups if and only if some power annihilates degree-minus-one cohomology and makes
degree-zero cohomology relatively projective. Under Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses these
are also equivalent to the corresponding finite-module Ext condition and to projectivity of
degree-zero cohomology after localization on a finite cover of the complement of the ideal's
vanishing locus.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_power_ext_one_annihilated_iff_cohomology_conditions
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] (I : Ideal R)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K)) :
    let Hneg := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) (-1)).obj K
    let Hzero := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj K
    let moduleObject := fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R ↦
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N
    let extAnnihilatedBySomePower := ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (a : R),
      a ∈ I ^ c → ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) 1, a • ξ = 0
    let cohomologyCondition := ∃ c : ℕ,
      (∀ (a : R), a ∈ I ^ c → ∀ x : Hneg, a • x = 0) ∧
        Module.IsIProjective R (I ^ c) Hzero
    let finiteExtAnnihilatedBySomePower := ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R),
      Module.Finite R N → ∀ (a : R), a ∈ I ^ c →
        ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) 1, a • ξ = 0
    let localizedProjectiveOnNeighborhood :=
      IsIPowerTorsion R Hneg I ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R),
        I.radical ≤ (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).radical ∧
          ∀ i, Module.Projective (Localization.Away (f i))
            (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) Hzero)
    let localizedProjectiveOnCover :=
      IsIPowerTorsion R Hneg I ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R),
        (∀ i, f i ∈ I) ∧ (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).radical = I.radical ∧
          ∀ i, Module.Projective (Localization.Away (f i))
            (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) Hzero)
    let localizedProjectiveOnEveryCover :=
      IsIPowerTorsion R Hneg I ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R),
        (∀ i, f i ∈ I) → (Ideal.span (Set.range f)).radical = I.radical →
          ∀ i, Module.Projective (Localization.Away (f i))
            (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i)) Hzero)
    (extAnnihilatedBySomePower ↔ cohomologyCondition) ∧
      (IsNoetherianRing R → Module.Finite R Hneg → Module.Finite R Hzero →
        (extAnnihilatedBySomePower ↔ finiteExtAnnihilatedBySomePower) ∧
        (finiteExtAnnihilatedBySomePower ↔ localizedProjectiveOnNeighborhood) ∧
        (localizedProjectiveOnNeighborhood ↔ localizedProjectiveOnCover) ∧
        (localizedProjectiveOnCover ↔ localizedProjectiveOnEveryCover))

declarations.name: Matrix.Q_map_detSmul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0G9L**.
The morphism `det(A) : K → K` is the zero morphism in the derived category `D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Q_map_detSmul_eq_zero :
    (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat R)).map (detSmul A) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.DerivedReductionProIso.derivedReduction_proIsomorphic_adicReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9M.** Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` and let `M` be a
bounded complex of finite `A`-modules.  Then `M` admits a bounded-above resolution `p : P -> M`
by finite free modules, and the canonical comparison from the derived reductions of `P` modulo
the positive powers of `I` to the degreewise reductions of `M` is compatible with the
transition maps and is an isomorphism of pro-objects in the derived category: each level
acquires a two-sided inverse after passing to a later level.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedReduction_proIsomorphic_adicReduction
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i)) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (p : P ⟶ M),
      (∃ b : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Free A (P.X i)) ∧
      IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map p) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ,
        adicReductionTransition I P (Nat.le_succ n) ≫ adicReductionComparison I p n =
          adicReductionComparison I p (n + 1) ≫
            adicReductionTransition I M (Nat.le_succ n)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m)
          (s : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((reduceComplex (I ^ (m + 1))).obj M) ⟶
            DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((reduceComplex (I ^ (n + 1))).obj P)),
          adicReductionComparison I p m ≫ s =
              adicReductionTransition I P h ∧
            s ≫ adicReductionComparison I p n =
              adicReductionTransition I M h

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_to_rightDerived_of_termwise_acyclic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9N.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-separated and quasi-compact
morphism of schemes and let `K` be a complex of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules each of which is
right acyclic for `f_*`. Then `f_* K` represents `Rf_* K` in `D(𝒪_S)`: the canonical comparison
from the termwise direct image to any right derived direct image is an isomorphism at `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_to_rightDerived_of_termwise_acyclic
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (K : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hqc : ∀ n, (K.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hacyclic : ∀ n, (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightAcyclic (K.X n))
    (Rf : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory S.Modules)
    (α : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf)
    [Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    IsIso (α.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pushforwardComparisonQ_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**`Q(f_*C^•) ⟶ Rf_*(QC^•)` is invertible along an affine morphism of schemes**, for a
cochain complex `C^•` of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules and with no boundedness hypothesis.

The comparison is the unit of the derived direct image with the two comparisons between `Q` and
`Qh ∘ quotient` inserted at either end.  Those are isomorphisms for every morphism, and the unit
is invertible at a complex of quasi-coherent modules along an affine morphism by
[Stacks, Tag 0G9N], `AlgebraicGeometry.AnyModel.isIso_derivedPushforwardUnit_app_of_isAffineHom`.

This is the input that the source's proof of [Stacks, Tag 0B55] gets from [Stacks, Tag 08KS] for
a closed embedding, and it is what the affine case of [Stacks, Tag 08I9] needs in its place.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pushforwardComparisonQ_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f]
    (C : CochainComplex
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules X.toRingedSpace) ℤ)
    (hqc : ∀ n : ℤ, (C.X n : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf).IsQuasicoherent) :
    IsIso (pushforwardComparisonQ f.toLRSHom.toShHom C)
declarations.comment: the comparison Q(f_*C) ⟶ Rf_*(QC) at the Q spelling: it is invertible for an affine morphism of schemes and a complex of quasi-coherent modules, with no boundedness hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_to_derivedGlobalSections_of_termwise_acyclic
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-separated and quasi-compact scheme and let `K` be a complex of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules each of which is right acyclic for `Γ(X, -)`. Then `Γ(X, K)`
represents `RΓ(X, K)` in `D(Γ(X, 𝒪_X))`: the canonical comparison from termwise global sections
to any right derived global-sections functor is an isomorphism at `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_to_derivedGlobalSections_of_termwise_acyclic (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hqc : ∀ n, (K.X n).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hacyclic : ∀ n, (sectionsFunctor X ⊤).rightAcyclic (K.X n))
    (RΓ : DerivedCategory X.Modules ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (α : (sectionsFunctor X ⊤).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RΓ)
    [RΓ.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    IsIso (α.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hypercohomologySpectralSequence_isBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9Q.** The hypercohomology spectral sequence of an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is bounded: in each total degree only
finitely many second-page terms are nonzero.

The second page in bidegree `(i, j)` is `H^i(X, H^j(K))`, and `H^j(K)` is quasi-coherent, so by
the uniform vanishing of the cohomology of quasi-coherent modules the term is zero unless
`0 ≤ i ≤ N - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hypercohomologySpectralSequence_isBounded (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    IsBounded (hypercohomologySpectralSequence X.toRingedSpace K.obj).spectralSequence
declarations.comment: boundedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hypercohomologySpectralSequence_abutsTo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9Q.** The hypercohomology spectral sequence of an object `K` of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme converges to the hypercohomology of `K`:
there is a finite decreasing filtration of each `H^n(X, K)` whose graded pieces are the terms of
the infinity page.

The two hypotheses of the convergence statement of [Stacks, Tag 0BKK] are supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isZero_hypercohomology_filtration_obj` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_hypercohomologyMap_filtration_ι`; what that statement delivers is
the abutment of the unrenumbered spectral sequence to the hypercohomology of the underlying
complex of the filtration, which is transported to `K` along the representative and then along
the two renumberings.
declarations.statement:
theorem hypercohomologySpectralSequence_abutsTo (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    (hypercohomologySpectralSequence X.toRingedSpace K.obj).spectralSequence.AbutsTo
      (fun n => (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u} ((structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj
          (op (⊤ : Opens X.carrier)))) n).obj
        ((hypercohomologySpectralSequence X.toRingedSpace K.obj).truncation.RΓ.obj K.obj))
declarations.comment: convergence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pushforwardToRightDerived_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9R.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of schemes and let `K`
be a complex of quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules. Then `f_* K = Rf_* K`: the right derived direct
image is defined at `K` and the canonical map from the termwise direct image to it is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pushforwardToRightDerived_of_isAffine
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    [HasDerivedCategory Y.Modules]
    (K : HomologicalComplex X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
    (hK : ∀ i, (K.X i).IsQuasicoherent) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh).ComputesRightDerived
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient X.Modules (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)

declarations.name: factor_through_free_of_tor_one_map_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9T.** A map from a finitely presented module which induces the zero
map on `Tor₁` with every module factors through a free module.
declarations.statement:
lemma factor_through_free_of_tor_one_map_eq_zero
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M M' : ModuleCat.{u} R} (f : M ⟶ M')
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M]
    (hf : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).map f).app N = 0) :
    FactorsThroughFree f.hom

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_shortExact_pushout
declarations.doc:
The pushout of the left-hand map in a short exact sequence is again a short exact sequence,
with the same right-hand object.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_pushout
    {C : Type u} [Category C] [Abelian C]
    {K P M K' : C} {i : K ⟶ P} {p : P ⟶ M}
    (hip : i ≫ p = 0) (h : (ShortComplex.mk i p hip).ShortExact) (a : K ⟶ K') :
    ∃ (E : C) (j : P ⟶ E) (i' : K' ⟶ E) (q : E ⟶ M)
      (hi'q : i' ≫ q = 0),
      IsPushout i a j i' ∧ j ≫ q = p ∧ (ShortComplex.mk i' q hi'q).ShortExact

declarations.name: exists_uniform_tor_transition_eq_zero_of_pow_smul_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G9X.** For a fixed power `I ^ m` and a positive Tor degree, there is
a uniform shift such that the transition from `A / I ^ n` to `A / I ^ (n - c)` induces the zero
map on Tor against every module annihilated by `I ^ m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_tor_transition_eq_zero_of_pow_smul_eq_bot
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (m i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A),
      I ^ m • (⊤ : Submodule A M) = ⊥ → ∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
        ((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj M).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
            (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))) = 0
