declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_affineBlowupAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Uniform annihilation of the high `Tor` modules of an affine blowup algebra.**
Let `I = (a₁, …, a_t)` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`, let `a = a₁`, and let `B = A[I/a]`
be the affine blowup algebra. There is a `c > 0` such that `Iᶜ` annihilates `Torᴬᵢ(B, M)` for
every `A`-module `M` and every `i ≥ t`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_affineBlowupAlgebra
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {n : ℕ} (g : Fin (n + 1) → A)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g))
    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra A S] [IsLocalization.Away (g 0) S] :
    ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i : ℕ), n + 1 ≤ i →
      I ^ c ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A ↥(affineBlowupAlgebra I (g 0) S))).obj M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_threshold_nonempty_derivedGlobalSectionsTwistedPullback_iso_derivedTensorIdealPow
declarations.doc:
**Cohomology of the twisted derived pullback along the affine blowup, unconditionally.** Let
`A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `p : X ⟶ Spec A` the blowup of `Spec A` in `I`.
There is a `q₀` such that for every `n ≥ q₀` and **any** `A`-module `M`,

`RΓ(X, Lp^*(M̃) ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(n)) ≅ M ⊗^𝐋_A Iⁿ`  in `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_threshold_nonempty_derivedGlobalSectionsTwistedPullback_iso_derivedTensorIdealPow
    [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    ∃ q₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, q₀ ≤ n →
      ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of A),
        Nonempty ((AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsOver (toSpec I)).obj
            (((Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.derTensor (blowUpRingedSpace I)).tensor.obj
                ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
                  (toSpecRingedSpace I)).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (tildeComplex
                    ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of A)) 0).obj
                      M))))).obj
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (BlowUpModules I) 0).obj
                  (blowUpTwist I (n : ℤ))))) ≅
          ((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A).tensor.obj
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj M))).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
                (ModuleCat.of A (I ^ n : Ideal A)))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Blowup.exists_pow_le_annihilator_homology_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA0.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `I = (a₀, …, a_n) ⊆ A` an
ideal with `t = n + 1` generators, and let `p : X ⟶ Spec A` be the blowup of `Spec A` in `I`,
that is `X = Proj(⨁_{m ≥ 0} Iᵐ)`. There is an integer `c > 0`, depending only on `A` and `I`,
such that for every `A`-module `M` the cohomology sheaves `H^j(Lp^*M̃)` are annihilated by `Iᶜ`
for all `j ≤ -t`.

Annihilation is expressed on sections: an element `r ∈ Iᶜ`, viewed as a global section of `X`
through `p` and restricted to an open `U`, kills every section of `H^j(Lp^*M̃)` over `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_le_annihilator_homology_derivedPullback {n : ℕ} (g : Fin (n + 1) → A)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of A)) (j : ℤ), j ≤ -((n : ℤ) + 1) →
      ∀ (U : (blowUpSpec I).Opens) (r : A), r ∈ I ^ c →
        ∀ s : Γ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (blowUpSpec I).Modules j).obj
            ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
              (toSpecRingedSpace I)).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (tildeComplex
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (CommRingCat.of A)) 0).obj M)))), U),
          (blowUpSpec I).presheaf.map (homOfLE (show U ≤ ⊤ from le_top)).op
            ((toSpec I).appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv r)) • s = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow_blowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA1.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and let `I = (g 0, …, g (t-1))` be
an ideal of `A` generated by at most `t` elements, as in the Situation of [Stacks, Tag 0G9W].
There is an integer `m`, depending only on `A` and `I`, such that for *every* `A`-module `M` the
modules `Tor_i^A(M, A/I^q)` are annihilated by `I^m` for all `i > t` and all `q ≥ 0`.

Nothing is assumed. The spectral sequence the source's proof runs on is produced by
`Stacks.Blowup.exists_hypercohomologySpectralSequence_abutsTo_tor_idealPow` on the blowup of
`Spec A` in `I`, and the step from it to the filtration of `Tor_i^A(M, Iᑫ)` that
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow` asks for is
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII`
`.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow_of_abutsTo_restrictScalars`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow_blowup [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    {t : ℕ} (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i q : ℕ), t < i →
      I ^ m ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj M).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ q)))

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA1.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and let `I = (g 0, …, g (t-1))` be
an ideal of `A` generated by at most `t` elements, as in the Situation of [Stacks, Tag 0G9W].
There is an integer `m`, depending only on `A` and `I`, such that for *every* `A`-module `M` the
modules `Tor_i^A(M, A/I^q)` are annihilated by `I^m` for all `i > t` and all `q ≥ 0`.

The hypothesis `hfilt` is the geometric input of the source's proof, which is not formalized
here: for all `i ≥ t` and all `q ≥ q₀`, the module `Tor_i^A(M, I^q)` carries a filtration
`⊤ = F 0, …, F d = ⊥` in `d` steps whose graded pieces are annihilated by `Iᶜ`. The source
produces it from the hypercohomology spectral sequence [Stacks, Tag 0G9Q] of
`Lp^*M̃(q)` on the blowup `p : X ⟶ Spec A` of `Spec A` in `I`, with `q₀ = q(A, I)`, with `d = t`
by the vanishing [Stacks, Tag 071L] for the cover of `X` by the `t` affine charts, and with
`c = c(A, I)` the exponent of [Stacks, Tag 0GA0]; the identification of the abutment with
`Tor_i^A(M, I^q)` is [Stacks, Tag 0G9Z].

Given `hfilt`, the exponent `m = max (d * c) q₀ + 1` works: above the threshold the filtration
gives `I^{dc} • Tor_i^A(M, I^q) = 0` for `i ≥ t`, which the sequence `0 → I^q → A → A/I^q → 0`
shifts to `A/I^q` for `i > t`, and for the remaining `q ≤ m` already `I^m ≤ I^q` annihilates
`A/I^q` and hence `Tor_i^A(M, A/I^q)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ}
    (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) (q₀ d c : ℕ)
    (hfilt : ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i q : ℕ), t ≤ i → q₀ ≤ q →
      ∃ F : ℕ → Submodule A
          (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj M).obj (ModuleCat.of A ↥(I ^ q))),
        F 0 = ⊤ ∧ F d = ⊥ ∧ ∀ k, I ^ c • F k ≤ F (k + 1)) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i q : ℕ), t < i →
      I ^ m ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj M).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ q)))

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow_of_card_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA1 for an ideal generated by at most one element.** Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring and let `I = (g 0, …, g (t-1))` be an ideal generated by at most `t ≤ 1` elements.
There is an integer `m`, depending only on `A` and `I`, such that for *every* `A`-module `M` the
modules `Tor_i^A(M, A/I^q)` are annihilated by `I^m` for all `i > t` and all `q ≥ 0`. Nothing is
assumed: the geometric input of `exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow` is not needed here.

For `t = 1` and `I = (a)` take `m = q₀`, an index at which the ascending chain of annihilators
`ann(a) ⊆ ann(a²) ⊆ ⋯` stabilizes. For `q ≤ q₀` already `I^{q₀} ≤ I^q` annihilates `A/I^q`. For
`q > q₀` the ideal `I^q = (a^q)` is the cyclic module `A ⧸ ann(a^q)` with `ann(a^q) = ann(a^{q₀})`
annihilated by `a^{q₀}`, so one dimension shift gives `a^{q₀} · Tor_i^A(M, I^q) = 0` for `i ≥ 1`
and a second, along `0 → I^q → A → A/I^q → 0`, gives the claim for `i > 1`. The case `t = 0`,
where `I = 0`, is the degenerate case of `exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow_of_card_le_one [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ} (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) (ht : t ≤ 1) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i q : ℕ), t < i →
      I ^ m ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj M).obj (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ q)))
declarations.comment: for an ideal generated by at most one element

declarations.name: exists_uniform_tor_transition_eq_zero_of_pow_le_annihilator_tor'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA2.** Let `I = (g 0, …, g (t - 1))` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring
`A` generated by at most `t` elements. There are `N` and `c`, depending only on `A`, `I` and `t`,
such that the surjection `A / I ^ n ↠ A / I ^ (n - c)` induces the zero map
`Tor_{t+1}^A(M, A/I^n) → Tor_{t+1}^A(M, A/I^{n-c})` for *every* `A`-module `M` and every
`n ≥ N`. That `N` and `c` are produced before the module is seen is the whole content of the
source's lemma.

The power `I ^ c₁` annihilating `Tor_i^A(M, A/I^q)` for all `M`, all `i > t` and all `q`, which
the source's induction starts from, is [Stacks, Tag 0GA1],
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_pow_le_annihilator_tor_quotient_pow_blowup`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_tor_transition_eq_zero_of_pow_le_annihilator_tor'
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ}
    (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ N c : ℕ, ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (n : ℕ), N ≤ n →
      ((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (t + 1)).obj M).map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_uniform_torMapVanishesAtSucc_quotientFactor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA3, condition (7) of Tag 0G9V.** Let `I = (g 0, …, g (t - 1))` be an
ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` generated by at most `t` elements. There are `N` and `c`,
depending only on `A`, `I` and `t`, such that for every `n ≥ N` the transition
`A / I ^ n ↠ A / I ^ (n - c)` induces the zero map on `Tor _ (t + 1)` against every module.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0GA2], `exists_uniform_tor_transition_eq_zero_of_pow_le_annihilator_tor'`,
read through the braiding of the two models of `Tor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_torMapVanishesAtSucc_quotientFactor [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ} (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ N c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      TorMapVanishesAtSucc
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))) t
declarations.comment: condition (7) of Tag 0G9V

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_uniform_extMapVanishesAbove_quotientFactor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA3, condition (3) of Tag 0G9V.** Let `I = (g 0, …, g (t - 1))` be an
ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` generated by at most `t` elements. There are `N` and `c`,
depending only on `A`, `I` and `t`, such that for every `n ≥ N` the transition
`A / I ^ n ↠ A / I ^ (n - c)` induces the zero map
`Ext ^ i (A / I ^ (n - c), M) → Ext ^ i (A / I ^ n, M)` for every module `M` and every `i > t`.

As `A` is Noetherian and `A / I ^ n` is a finite `A`-module, all seven conditions of
[Stacks, Tag 0G9V] are equivalent for the transition (`tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite`), so
this is the assertion that the transition satisfies them; it is obtained from condition (7),
`exists_uniform_torMapVanishesAtSucc_quotientFactor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_extMapVanishesAbove_quotientFactor [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ} (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ N c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      ExtMapVanishesAbove
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))) t
declarations.comment: condition (3) of Tag 0G9V

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_uniform_hasLiftVanishingAbove_quotientFactor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA3, condition (1) of Tag 0G9V.** Let `I = (g 0, …, g (t - 1))` be an
ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` generated by at most `t` elements. There are `N` and `c`,
depending only on `A`, `I` and `t`, such that for every `n ≥ N` and every choice of projective
resolutions of `A / I ^ n` and of `A / I ^ (n - c)`, the transition `A / I ^ n ↠ A / I ^ (n - c)`
lifts to a map of resolutions whose components vanish in all homological degrees above `t`.

It is obtained from condition (7), `exists_uniform_torMapVanishesAtSucc_quotientFactor`, by the
equivalence of the conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0G9V] for a finite module over a Noetherian ring,
`tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_hasLiftVanishingAbove_quotientFactor [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ} (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ N c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      ∀ {P P' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ}
        (p : P ⟶ singleComplex (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ n)))
        (p' : P' ⟶ singleComplex (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ (n - c))))
        [CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution p]
        [CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution p'],
        HasLiftVanishingAbove p p'
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
            (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))) t
declarations.comment: condition (1) of Tag 0G9V

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_uniform_vanishingConditions_quotientFactor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA3.** Let `I = (g 0, …, g (t - 1))` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring
`A` generated by at most `t` elements. There are `N` and `c`, depending only on `A`, `I` and `t`,
such that for every `n ≥ N` and every choice of projective resolutions of `A / I ^ n` and of
`A / I ^ (n - c)`, the transition `A / I ^ n ↠ A / I ^ (n - c)` satisfies all seven conditions of
[Stacks, Tag 0G9V] with `e = t`, in the order of the source: (1) a lift vanishing in all degrees
above `t`, (2) a lift vanishing in degree `t + 1`, (3) the zero map on `Ext ^ i` for all `i > t`,
(4) the zero map on `Ext ^ (t + 1)`, (5) the canonical class of degree `t + 1` pulls back to zero,
(6) the zero map on `Tor _ i` for all `i > t`, (7) the zero map on `Tor _ (t + 1)`.

All seven follow from condition (7), `exists_uniform_torMapVanishesAtSucc_quotientFactor`, by
`tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_vanishingConditions_quotientFactor [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} {t : ℕ} (g : Fin t → A) (hg : I = Ideal.span (Set.range g)) :
    ∃ N c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      ∀ {P P' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ}
        (p : P ⟶ singleComplex (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ n)))
        (p' : P' ⟶ singleComplex (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ (n - c))))
        [CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution p]
        [CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution p'],
        let α := ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))
        HasLiftVanishingAbove p p' α t ∧ HasLiftVanishingAtSucc p p' α t ∧
          ExtMapVanishesAbove α t ∧ ExtMapVanishesAtSucc α t ∧
          CanonicalExtClassPullbackVanishes p p' α t ∧ TorMapVanishesAbove α t ∧
          TorMapVanishesAtSucc α t
declarations.comment: all seven conditions of Tag 0G9V at e = t

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.exists_uniform_vanishingConditions_quotientFactor_of_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA4.** Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring of Krull dimension `d` and
let `I` be an ideal of `A`. There are `N` and `c` such that for every `n ≥ N` and every choice of
projective resolutions of `A / I ^ n` and of `A / I ^ (n - c)`, the transition
`A / I ^ n ↠ A / I ^ (n - c)` satisfies all seven conditions of [Stacks, Tag 0G9V] with `e = d`,
in the order of the source: (1) a lift vanishing in all degrees above `d`, (2) a lift vanishing in
degree `d + 1`, (3) the zero map on `Ext ^ i` for all `i > d`, (4) the zero map on
`Ext ^ (d + 1)`, (5) the canonical class of degree `d + 1` pulls back to zero, (6) the zero map on
`Tor _ i` for all `i > d`, (7) the zero map on `Tor _ (d + 1)`.

This is the conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 0GA3] with `e = t` replaced by `e = dim A`; no bound on
the number of generators of `I` enters the statement. All seven conditions follow from condition
(7), `exists_uniform_torMapVanishesAtSucc_quotientFactor_of_ringKrullDim`, by
`tfae_of_isNoetherianRing_of_finite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_vanishingConditions_quotientFactor_of_ringKrullDim
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (I : Ideal A) (d : ℕ) (hdim : ringKrullDim A = d) :
    ∃ N c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
      ∀ {P P' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ}
        (p : P ⟶ singleComplex (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ n)))
        (p' : P' ⟶ singleComplex (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I ^ (n - c))))
        [CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution p]
        [CochainComplex.IsProjectiveResolution p'],
        let α := ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.factor (p := I ^ n) (p' := I ^ (n - c))
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c)))
        HasLiftVanishingAbove p p' α d ∧ HasLiftVanishingAtSucc p p' α d ∧
          ExtMapVanishesAbove α d ∧ ExtMapVanishesAtSucc α d ∧
          CanonicalExtClassPullbackVanishes p p' α d ∧ TorMapVanishesAbove α d ∧
          TorMapVanishesAtSucc α d
declarations.comment:
Tag 0GA3 with e = dim A for a local ring: all seven conditions of Tag 0G9V; the
cd(A, I) question the remark raises is open in the source and is not stated

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.nonempty_strictProIso_systemFour_systemOne
declarations.doc:
**If `P` is Noetherian, the system (4) is strictly pro-isomorphic to the system (1).**
Let `φ : P → A` be a ring map of Noetherian rings, `J ⊆ P` an ideal, `I = JA`, and `M` a
bounded complex of finite `A`-modules. Then the inverse system `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ⁺¹` in `D(A)` is
isomorphic, in the strict pro-category of `D(A)`, to the system `n ↦ M/Iⁿ⁺¹M`. An isomorphism
of the strict pro-category is in particular an isomorphism of pro-objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_strictProIso_systemFour_systemOne [IsNoetherianRing P] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (J : Ideal P) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = J.map φ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i)) :
    Nonempty (proObj (systemFour φ M J) ≅
      proObj (Stacks.AdicSystem.DerivedReductionProIso.reductionComplexSystem I M ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q))
declarations.comment: if `P` is Noetherian, the system (4) is strictly pro-isomorphic to the system (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.nonempty_proIso_systemFour_systemOne
declarations.doc:
**If `P` is Noetherian, the system (4) is pro-isomorphic to the system (1).**
Let `φ : P → A` be a ring map of Noetherian rings, `J ⊆ P` an ideal, `I = JA`, and `M` a bounded
complex of finite `A`-modules. Then the inverse systems `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ⁺¹` and `n ↦ M/Iⁿ⁺¹M`
in `D(A)` are pro-isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_proIso_systemFour_systemOne [IsNoetherianRing P] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (J : Ideal P) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = J.map φ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i)) :
    Nonempty (_root_.InverseSequence.ProIso (systemFour φ M J)
      (Stacks.AdicSystem.DerivedReductionProIso.reductionComplexSystem I M ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q))
declarations.comment: if `P` is Noetherian, the system (4) is pro-isomorphic to the system (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.isZero_tor_quotient_pow_idealOfVars
declarations.doc:
`A[x₁, …, x_r]/(x₁, …, x_r)ⁿ` has Tor dimension at most `r` for all `n`: for every module `N`
over `R = A[x₁, …, x_r]` and every `p > r`, `Tor_p^R(R/(x₁, …, x_r)ⁿ, N) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_tor_quotient_pow_idealOfVars (n : ℕ) (N : ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))
    {p : ℕ} (hp : r < p) :
    IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)) p).obj
      (ModuleCat.of _ (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A ⧸ idealOfVars (Fin r) A ^ n))).obj N)
declarations.comment: in the standard example, `A[x₁, …, x_r]/(x₁, …, x_r)ⁿ` has tor dimension at most `r` for all `n`

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.polynomialSystemFourIso
declarations.doc:
**`M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ = M ⊗ᴸ_{A[x]} A[x]/(x)ⁿ`.**  Let `P = R₀[x₁, …, x_r]` (the source takes
`R₀ = ℤ`; at a universe `u` other than `0` one takes `R₀ = ULift ℤ`), let `P → A` send `xᵢ` to
`gᵢ`, and `J = (x₁, …, x_r)`.  Then the system (4) `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ⁺¹` is isomorphic, as an
inverse system in `D(A)`, to the system `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_{A[x]} A[x]/(x)ⁿ⁺¹`, i.e. to the system (4)
for `A[x] → A`, `xᵢ ↦ gᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def polynomialSystemFourIso :
    systemFour (polyEval R₀ g) M (MvPolynomial.idealOfVars (Fin r) R₀) ≅
      systemFour (polyEvalBase g) M (MvPolynomial.idealOfVars (Fin r) A)
declarations.comment: the standard example: `M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ = M ⊗ᴸ_{A[x]} A[x]/(x)ⁿ` for `P = ℤ[x₁, …, x_r]`

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.nonempty_proIso_polynomialSystemFour_systemTwo
declarations.doc:
In the situation of `polynomialSystemFourIso`, with `A` Noetherian and `I = (g₁, …, g_r)`,
the system (4) `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ⁺¹` for `P = R₀[x₁, …, x_r]` is strictly pro-isomorphic to the
system (2) `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_A A/Iⁿ⁺¹`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_proIso_polynomialSystemFour_systemTwo [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    Nonempty (proObj (systemFour (polyEval R₀ g) M (MvPolynomial.idealOfVars (Fin r) R₀)) ≅
      proObj (systemTwo (polyEval R₀ g) M (Ideal.span (Set.range g))))
declarations.comment: the standard example `P = ℤ[x₁, …, x_r]`: the system (4) is strictly pro-isomorphic to the system (2), by reduction to the finite map `A[x] → A`

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.isIso_proHom_derivedReductionComparison
declarations.doc:
**The natural map from system (2) to system (1) is a strict pro-isomorphism.** Let `I` be an
ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`, let `M` be a bounded complex of finite `A`-modules and
`p : P ⟶ M` a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded above complex of finite flat modules, so that
`P/IⁿP` computes `M ⊗ᴸ_A A/Iⁿ`. Then the natural map from the inverse system `n ↦ P/I^(n+1)P` to
the inverse system `n ↦ M/I^(n+1)M` in `D(A)` is an isomorphism in the strict pro-category of
`D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_proHom_derivedReductionComparison [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i))
    {P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ} (p : P ⟶ M) (hPbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hPfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Flat A (P.X i))
    (hp : IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map p)) :
    IsIso (proHom (⟨0, Functor.whiskerRight (reductionComplexSystemMap I p) DerivedCategory.Q⟩ :
      StrictProHomRep (reductionComplexSystem I P ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
        (reductionComplexSystem I M ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)))
declarations.comment: the natural map from (2) to (1) is a strict pro-isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.derivedReductionComparison_hasEventualInverses
declarations.doc:
**The systems (1) and (2) are pro-isomorphic.** Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`,
let `M` be a bounded complex of finite `A`-modules and `p : P ⟶ M` a quasi-isomorphism from a
bounded above complex of finite flat modules, so that `P/IⁿP` computes `M ⊗ᴸ_A A/Iⁿ`. Then the
natural map from the system (2) `n ↦ P/I^(n+1)P` to the system (1) `n ↦ M/I^(n+1)M` in `D(A)` is
a pro-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedReductionComparison_hasEventualInverses [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i))
    {P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ} (p : P ⟶ M) (hPbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hPfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Flat A (P.X i))
    (hp : IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map p)) :
    NoetherianAdicCompletion.HasEventualInverses
      (Functor.whiskerRight (reductionComplexSystemMap I p) DerivedCategory.Q)
declarations.comment: the systems (1) and (2) are pro-isomorphic, via Lemma 15.102.3

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.proIso_koszulToAdic
declarations.doc:
**The two systems are isomorphic as pro-objects.** The comparison `koszulToAdic` admits, at
every level `n`, a two-sided inverse defined on a later level `m`: both triangles it forms with
the transition maps commute.
declarations.statement:
public theorem proIso_koszulToAdic {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : n ≤ m)
      (s : (AdicCompletionTor.idealPowerQuotientModuleSystem
              (Ideal.span (Set.range f))).obj (op m) ⟶
        (Koszul.powQuotientSystem f).obj (op n)),
      (koszulToAdic f).app (op m) ≫ s = (Koszul.powQuotientSystem f).map (homOfLE h).op ∧
        s ≫ (koszulToAdic f).app (op n)
          = (AdicCompletionTor.idealPowerQuotientModuleSystem
              (Ideal.span (Set.range f))).map (homOfLE h).op
declarations.comment: the pro-isomorphism, in the category of modules, between the system `H⁰(Kₙ) = A/(f₀ⁿ, …, f_{r-1}ⁿ)` and the system `A/Iⁿ`, which is the comparison the remark makes by comparing with Koszul complexes and whose strictness the remark then denies

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.not_annihilator_pow_mul_pred
declarations.doc:
In `ℤ[x₀, …, x_{r-1}]` the module
`H⁰(Kₙ) = ℤ[x]/(x₀ⁿ, …, x_{r-1}ⁿ)` is not annihilated by `I^{r(n-1)}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_annihilator_pow_mul_pred (r n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ¬ (monomialIdeal r ^ (r * (n - 1)) ≤
        Module.annihilator (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)
          (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ ⧸
            Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ) ^ n)))
declarations.comment: the computation the remark performs on its example: for `A = ℤ[x₀, …, x_{r-1}]` and `f i = x i`, the module `H⁰(Kₙ) = A/(x₀ⁿ, …, x_{r-1}ⁿ)` is not annihilated by `I^{r(n-1)}`, witnessed by the monomial `x₀^(n-1) ⋯ x_{r-1}^(n-1)`

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.not_strictProIso_monomial
declarations.doc:
**Failure of strictness.** For `r ≥ 2` the inverse system
`H⁰(Kₙ) = ℤ[x]/(x₀ⁿ, …, x_{r-1}ⁿ)` of the Koszul complexes on the powers of the variables and
the adic system `ℤ[x]/Iⁿ` of the ideal `I = (x₀, …, x_{r-1})` they generate are *not* strictly
pro-isomorphic: there is no pair of strict pro-morphisms between them, in either direction,
whose composite is eventually the identity of the Koszul system.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_strictProIso_monomial (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    ¬ ∃ (φ : StrictProHomRep
          (AdicCompletionTor.idealPowerQuotientModuleSystem
            (Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ))))
          (Koszul.powQuotientSystem fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)))
        (ψ : StrictProHomRep
          (Koszul.powQuotientSystem fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ))
          (AdicCompletionTor.idealPowerQuotientModuleSystem
            (Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ))))),
      (ψ.comp φ).Equivalent
        (StrictProHomRep.id (Koszul.powQuotientSystem fun i : Fin r =>
          (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the failure of strictness the remark asserts for systems (1) and (3) at `M = A[0]`: the system `H⁰(Kₙ) = A/(x₀ⁿ, …, x_{r-1}ⁿ)` over `A = ℤ[x₀, …, x_{r-1}]` admits no strict pro-isomorphism with the system `A/Iⁿ`, proved as the negation it is

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.not_nonempty_iso_proObj_monomial
declarations.doc:
**Failure of strictness, in the strict pro-category.**  For `r ≥ 2` the inverse sequence
`A/Iⁿ` and the inverse sequence `H⁰(Kₙ) = A/(x₀ⁿ, …, x_{r-1}ⁿ)` over `A = ℤ[x₀, …, x_{r-1}]`
are not isomorphic as objects of the strict pro-category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_nonempty_iso_proObj_monomial (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    ¬ Nonempty
      (proObj (AdicCompletionTor.idealPowerQuotientModuleSystem
          (Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)))) ≅
        proObj (Koszul.powQuotientSystem fun i : Fin r =>
          (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the failure of strictness for systems (1) and (3) at `M = A[0]`, stated as non-isomorphism of the two inverse sequences in the strict pro-category itself

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.not_nonempty_iso_proObj_derived_monomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GA5, failure of strictness for (1) and (3), in `D(A)`.**  Let
`A = ℤ[x₀, …, x_{r-1}]` with `r ≥ 2`, `fᵢ = xᵢ` and `I = (x₀, …, x_{r-1})`.  For `M = A[0]` the
system (1) is `n ↦ (A/I^(n+1))[0]` and the system (3) is `n ↦ A ⊗ᴸ K_{n+1} = K_{n+1}`, the
Koszul complex on `x₀^(n+1), …, x_{r-1}^(n+1)`.  These two inverse systems of `D(A)` are not
isomorphic in the strict pro-category of `D(A)`.

Applying `H⁰` to an isomorphism of the strict pro-category gives one between the systems
`A/I^(n+1)` and `H⁰(K_{n+1}) = A/(x₀^(n+1), …, x_{r-1}^(n+1))` of modules, which
`not_nonempty_iso_proObj_monomial` rules out.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_nonempty_iso_proObj_derived_monomial {r : ℕ}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{0} (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ))] (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    ¬ Nonempty
      (proObj (AdicCompletionTor.idealPowerQuotientModuleSystem
          (Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ))) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} (MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)) 0) ≅
        proObj (Koszul.powDerivedSystem fun i : Fin r => (X i : MvPolynomial (Fin r) ℤ)))
declarations.comment: systems (1) and (3) are not strictly pro-isomorphic, even for `M = A[0]`: the example `A = ℤ[x₁, …, x_r]`, `fᵢ = xᵢ`, read in the strict pro-category of `D(A)`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.StrictProCategory
declarations.doc:
The strict pro-category of `C`. Its objects are inverse sequences in `C`; its morphisms are
uniformly shifted compatible maps modulo eventual agreement after passing to a common shift.
declarations.statement: abbrev StrictProCategory (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]
declarations.comment: strict_pro_category

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.derivedTensorKoszulSystem_hasEventualInverses
declarations.doc:
**Systems (2) and (3) are pro-isomorphic.**  For an ideal `I = (f₀, …, f_{r-1})` of a
Noetherian ring `A`, the inverse system `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ K_{n+1}` of derived tensor products with the
Koszul complexes on the positive powers of the generators is pro-isomorphic to the inverse
system `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ A/Iⁿ⁺¹`, via the derived tensor product with `M` of the comparison
`Kₙ → A/Iⁿ` of [Stacks, Tag 0921].
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensorKoszulSystem_hasEventualInverses
    [IsNoetherianRing A] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (T : CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.DerivedTensorProduct A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) :
    NoetherianAdicCompletion.HasEventualInverses
      (Functor.whiskerRight (NoetherianAdicCompletion.koszulIdealPowerComparison f I hI)
        (T.tensor.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)))
declarations.comment: the pro-isomorphism between the systems (2) and (3), via Lemma 15.96.1

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.derivedTensorKoszulSystem_hasEventualInverses_canonical
declarations.doc:
`derivedTensorKoszulSystem_hasEventualInverses` for the canonical derived tensor product
of [Stacks, Tag 0BYI].
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedTensorKoszulSystem_hasEventualInverses_canonical
    [IsNoetherianRing A] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) :
    NoetherianAdicCompletion.HasEventualInverses
      (Functor.whiskerRight (NoetherianAdicCompletion.koszulIdealPowerComparison f I hI)
        ((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct A).tensor.obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)))
declarations.comment: the pro-isomorphism between the systems (2) and (3), for the canonical derived tensor product

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.isIso_proHom_systemFourToTwo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GA5: if `P → A` is finite, system (4) is strictly pro-isomorphic to system
(2).**  Let `P` be Noetherian, `f : P → A` a finite ring map, `J ⊆ P` an ideal with `I = JA`,
and `M` a complex of `A`-modules.  Then the comparison from the system `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_P P/Jⁿ⁺¹` to
the system `n ↦ M ⊗ᴸ_A A/Iⁿ⁺¹` is an isomorphism of the strict pro-category of `D(A)`.

The source states the remark for a bounded complex `M` of finite modules over a Noetherian
ring `A`; neither hypothesis is used here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_proHom_systemFourToTwo [IsNoetherianRing P] (hf : f.Finite) (J : Ideal P)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = J.map f) :
    IsIso (proHom (⟨0, systemFourToTwo f M J I hI⟩ :
      StrictProHomRep (systemFour f M J) (systemTwo f M I)))
declarations.comment: if `P → A` is finite, the system (4) is strictly pro-isomorphic to the system (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityII.hasUniformInverses_systemTwoToOne
declarations.doc:
**The natural map from (2) to (1) is a strict pro-isomorphism**, for the derived-tensor model
of (2). Let `I` be an ideal of a Noetherian ring `A` and `M` a bounded complex of finite
`A`-modules. The counits `M ⊗ᴸ_A A/Iⁿ⁺¹ ⟶ M/Iⁿ⁺¹M` have inverses over a shift independent of
`n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasUniformInverses_systemTwoToOne [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i)) :
    HasUniformInverses (systemTwoToOne f M I)
declarations.comment: the natural map from (2) to (1) is a strict pro-isomorphism, for (2) formed with the derived tensor product

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.DerivedReductionProIso.derivedReduction_exists_uniform_inverse
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GA5], explicitly.**  In the situation of
`derivedReduction_hasUniformInverses`, there is a shift `c` such that for all `n + c ≤ m` the
comparison maps `adicReductionComparison` acquire an inverse from level `m` to level `n` whose
two round trips are the transition maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedReduction_exists_uniform_inverse [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hMbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, M.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ M.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hMfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (M.X i))
    {P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ} (p : P ⟶ M) (hPbounded : ∃ b : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hPfinite : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Flat A (P.X i))
    (hp : IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map p)) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n m : ℕ, n + c ≤ m →
      ∃ (h : n ≤ m) (s : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((reduceComplex (I ^ (m + 1))).obj M) ⟶
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((reduceComplex (I ^ (n + 1))).obj P)),
        adicReductionComparison I p m ≫ s = adicReductionTransition I P h ∧
          s ≫ adicReductionComparison I p n = adicReductionTransition I M h
declarations.comment: the natural map from (2) to (1) is a strict pro-isomorphism: inverses over a uniform shift

declarations.name: AssociatedGraded.dInvariant
declarations.doc:
**The invariant `d(S) = d(Gr_I(A))`**: the maximum of the dimensions of the fibres of
`Proj(S) → Spec(S₀)`, a fibre with empty underlying space contributing `0`.

This is clause (2) of the paragraph of [Stacks, Tag 0GA6] that introduces `d`; see the
implementation notes for its relation to the paragraph's primary phrasing in terms of the
blowup.
declarations.statement: def dInvariant : ℕ∞
declarations.comment: the invariant d(S) of the associated graded ring S = Gr_I(A), as the maximum of the dimensions of the fibres of Proj(S) → Spec(S₀), which is clause (2) of the paragraph defining d; the equality with the maximum of the fibre dimensions of the blowup p : X → Spec(A), the paragraph's primary phrasing, is not proved here

declarations.name: AssociatedGraded.qInvariant
declarations.doc:
**The invariant `q(S) = q(Gr_I(A))`**: the smallest `q₀ ≥ 0` such that
`AssociatedGraded.IsRegularDegree` holds at every `q ≥ q₀`.

That the set of such `q₀` is nonempty is Cohomology of Schemes, Lemmas [Stacks, Tag 0AG6] and
[Stacks, Tag 0AG7], which are not available in this generality; it is therefore a hypothesis of
`AssociatedGraded.isRegularDegree_of_qInvariant_le` and not proved here.
declarations.statement: def qInvariant : ℕ
declarations.comment: the invariant q(S) of the associated graded ring S = Gr_I(A), as the smallest q(S) ≥ 0 such that for all q ≥ q(S) one has Hⁱ(Y, 𝒪_Y(q)) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ d(S) and H⁰(Y, 𝒪_Y(q)) = I^q/I^{q+1} for Y = Proj(S); the appeal to Cohomology of Schemes Lemmas 0AG6 and 0AG7 that makes the set of such bounds nonempty is not proved here, and is carried as a hypothesis by isRegularDegree_of_qInvariant_le

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.blowupHmod_of_qS_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GA7]**: with `q₀ = q(S)` (`qS I`, the least integer such that for all
`q ≥ q₀` one has `Hⁱ(Y, 𝒪_Y(q)) = 0` for `i ≥ 1` and `H⁰(Y, 𝒪_Y(q)) = Iᑫ/I^{q+1}`), for a
Noetherian ring `A` and any ideal `I`, on the blowup `X` of `Spec A` in `I`:

1. for `n ≥ 1`, `q ≥ q₀` and `i > 0`, `Hⁱ(X, 𝒪_{Yₙ}(q)) = 0`;
2. for `n ≥ 1` and `q ≥ q₀`, the canonical map `Iᑫ/I^{q+n} → H⁰(X, 𝒪_{Yₙ}(q))` is an
   isomorphism — stated as the bijectivity of `cdivMod I m q`, whose source is `Iᑫ/I^{q+m+1}`
   and whose target is `H⁰(X, 𝒪_{Y_{m+1}}(q))`, for every `m`, i.e. at `n = m + 1`;
3. for `q ≥ q₀` and `i > 0`, `Hⁱ(X, 𝒪_X(q)) = 0`;
4. for `q ≥ q₀`, the canonical map `Iᑫ → H⁰(X, 𝒪_X(q))` is an isomorphism.

The cohomology is `A`-module-valued, the source's identifications being isomorphisms of
`A`-modules. The integer `d = d(S)` the tag names enters only through the definition of `q(S)`,
where it bounds the degrees in which vanishing is asked; see `IsBaseThreshold`,
`isBaseThreshold_iff_of_vanishing_gt` and `exists_qS_isLeast_isBaseThresholdUpTo`.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowupHmod_of_qS_le [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    (∀ n i q : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → 1 ≤ i → qS I ≤ q →
        Subsingleton (blowupHmod I i (thickeningTwist I n q))) ∧
      (∀ n q : ℕ, qS I ≤ q → Function.Bijective (cdivMod I n q)) ∧
      (∀ i q : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → qS I ≤ q → Subsingleton (blowupHmod I i (blowupTwist I q))) ∧
      (∀ q : ℕ, qS I ≤ q → Function.Bijective (ambientSectionsMod I q))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exceptionalIdeal_pow_le_annihilator_kernel
declarations.doc:
In a short exact sequence over `A ⧸ I ^ n` whose quotient is finite and
`I ^ c / I ^ n`-projective, the kernel of the pulled-back first map is
annihilated by the ideal of the `c`-th exceptional thickening.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exceptionalIdeal_pow_le_annihilator_kernel
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (n c : ℕ) (_hcn : c ≤ n)
    (K L M : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n))
    (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M) (w : f ≫ g = 0)
    (hExact : (ShortComplex.mk f g w).ShortExact)
    [Module.Finite (A ⧸ I ^ n) M]
    (hM : Module.IsIProjective (A ⧸ I ^ n)
      (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n)) (I ^ c)) M) :
    (exceptionalIdeal (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom I))) ^ c ≤
      Scheme.Modules.annihilatorIdeal
        (kernel ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
          (blowUpToBase (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
            (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom I)))).map
              ((tilde.functor (.of A)).map
              ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).map f))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.schemeTheoreticSupport_iff_exceptionalTwistContraction_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GA9.** A quasi-coherent module of finite type on the blowup of a
scheme in a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals is scheme theoretically supported on the `c`-fold
thickening `Y_c` of the exceptional divisor if and only if the canonical map `𝓕(c) ⟶ 𝓕`
vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_iff_exceptionalTwistContraction_eq_zero
    (F : (blowUp ℐ).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] :
    exceptionalIdeal ℐ ^ c ≤ Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport F ↔
      exceptionalTwistContraction ℐ c F = 0
declarations.comment: corrected: the canonical map runs 𝓕(c) ⟶ 𝓕, since 𝒪(1) is the ideal sheaf of Y

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.ModuleSituation.subsingleton_H_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAA, clause (1).** For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M`, in the case
`i = d ≥ 1` and `q ≥ q₀` we have `H^d(X, p^*M(q)) = 0`.

The long exact sequence of `0 → 𝒢 → (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r} → p^*M → 0` sits `H^d(X, p^*M(q))` between
`H^d(X, (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r}(q))`, which vanishes by Tag 0GA7(1), and `H^{d+1}(X, 𝒢(q))`, which
vanishes because `d` bounds the fibre dimensions.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_H_top (M : ANCModule I n c) {q : ℤ}
    (hd : 1 ≤ S.d) (hq : (S.q₀ : ℤ) ≤ q) : Subsingleton (S.H M S.d q)
declarations.comment: clause (1), H^d(X, p^*M(q)) = 0 for i = d ≥ 1 and q ≥ q₀

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.ModuleSituation.subsingleton_H_next
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAA, clause (2).** For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M`, in the case
`i = d - 1 ≥ 1` and `q ≥ q₀` we have `H^{d-1}(X, p^*M(q)) = 0`.

The long exact sequence of `0 → 𝒢 → (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r} → p^*M → 0` sits `H^{d-1}(X, p^*M(q))`
between `H^{d-1}(X, (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r}(q))`, which vanishes by Tag 0GA7(1) since `d - 1 ≥ 1`, and
`H^d(X, 𝒢(q))`, which vanishes by `subsingleton_HG_top`.

The hypothesis `i = d - 1` is written `i + 1 = d` to avoid a truncated subtraction.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_H_next (M : ANCModule I n c) {i : ℕ} {q : ℤ}
    (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hid : i + 1 = S.d) (hq : (S.q₀ : ℤ) ≤ q) : Subsingleton (S.H M i q)
declarations.comment: clause (2), H^{d-1}(X, p^*M(q)) = 0 for i = d - 1 ≥ 1 and q ≥ q₀

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.TwistedModuleSituation.Htr_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAA, clause (3).** For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M`, in the case
`d - 1 > i > 0` and `q ≥ q₀ + (d - 1 - i)c` the map
`Hⁱ(X, p^*M(q)) → Hⁱ(X, p^*M(q - (d - 1 - i)c))` is zero.

The case distinction `d - 1 > i > 0` is written `1 ≤ i` together with `i + k + 1 = d` and
`1 ≤ k`, which fixes `k = d - 1 - i`; the target twist `q - kc` is carried as a parameter `r`
with `r + kc = q`. The proof reduces the statement to `HGtr_eq_zero`, whose induction it is.
declarations.statement:
theorem Htr_eq_zero (M : ANCModule I n c) {i k : ℕ} {q r : ℤ} (h : r ≤ q)
    (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hik : i + k + 1 = S.d) (hr : r + k * c = q)
    (hq : (S.q₀ : ℤ) + k * c ≤ q) : S.Htr M i q r h = 0
declarations.comment: clause (3), Hⁱ(X, p^*M(q)) → Hⁱ(X, p^*M(q-(d-1-i)c)) is zero for d-1 > i > 0

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.TwistedModuleSituation.surjective_secM
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAA, clause (4).** For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M`, in the case
`i = 0`, `d ∈ {0, 1}` and `q ≥ q₀` the canonical map `I^q ⊗_A M → H⁰(X, p^*M(q))` is
surjective.

The long exact sequence of `0 → ℱ → p^*K → 𝒢 → 0` makes `H¹(X, p^*K(q)) → H¹(X, 𝒢(q))`
surjective, since `H²(X, ℱ(q)) = 0` for `d ≤ 1`; its source vanishes, by clause (1) if `d = 1`
and because `d` bounds the fibre dimensions if `d = 0`. So `H¹(X, 𝒢(q)) = 0` and the long exact
sequence of `0 → 𝒢 → (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r} → p^*M → 0` makes `H⁰(X, (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r}(q)) → H⁰(X, p^*M(q))`
surjective; for `q ≥ q₀` the source is `(I^q/I^{q+n})^{⊕r}` by Tag 0GA7(2), and the composite
with it factors through `I^q ⊗_A M` by `ANCPresentation.freeTensor_surjective`.

The Stacks Project writes the source `I^qM`. Read as the submodule `I^q·M` of `M` the clause
is false: for `A = ℤ`, `I = (2)` (so the blowing up is an isomorphism, `d = 0`, `q₀ = 0`),
`n = 1`, `c = 0` and `M = A ⧸ I`, at `q = 1` that submodule is `0` while Tag 0GA7(2) gives
`H⁰(X, p^*M(1)) = H⁰(X, 𝒪_{Y₁}(1)) = I/I² ≅ ℤ/2`. What the proof produces, and what is
formalized, is the surjection out of `I^q ⊗_A M = (I^q/I^{q+n}) ⊗_A M`, which agrees with
`I^q/I^{q+n}` for `M = A ⧸ Iⁿ` as Tag 0GA7(2) demands.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_secM (M : ANCModule I n c) {q : ℕ} (hd : S.d ≤ 1) (hq : S.q₀ ≤ q) :
    Function.Surjective (S.secM M q)
declarations.comment: clause (4), surjectivity onto H⁰(X, p^*M(q)) for i = 0, d ≤ 1, q ≥ q₀; corrected: the source is I^q ⊗_A M, not the submodule I^qM, for which this is false

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.TwistedModuleSituation.range_Htr_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAA, clause (5).** For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M`, in the case
`i = 0`, `d > 1` and `q ≥ q₀ + (d - 1)c` the image of
`H⁰(X, p^*M(q)) → H⁰(X, p^*M(q - (d - 1)c))` is contained in the image of the canonical map
`I^{q - (d-1)c} ⊗_A M → H⁰(X, p^*M(q - (d - 1)c))`, the map of clause (4); as there, the source
is the tensor product and not the submodule `I^{q-(d-1)c}M` of `M`.

The case `d > 1` is written `k + 1 = d` with `1 ≤ k`, which fixes `k = d - 1`; the target
twist `q - kc` is carried as a natural number `r` with `r + kc = q`, which is no restriction
since `q ≥ q₀ + kc` forces `q - kc ≥ q₀ ≥ 0`. Arguing as in clause (4)
it suffices that the image lie in the image of `H⁰(X, (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r}(q - (d-1)c))`, which by the
long exact sequence of `0 → 𝒢 → (𝒪_{Yₙ})^{⊕r} → p^*M → 0` holds as soon as the boundary in
`H¹(X, 𝒢(q))` dies in `H¹(X, 𝒢(q - (d-1)c))`; that is `HGtr_eq_zero` at `i = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_Htr_le (M : ANCModule I n c) {k r : ℕ} {q : ℤ} (h : (r : ℤ) ≤ q)
    (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hkd : k + 1 = S.d) (hr : (r : ℤ) + k * c = q)
    (hq : (S.q₀ : ℤ) + k * c ≤ q) :
    LinearMap.range (S.Htr M 0 q (r : ℤ) h) ≤ LinearMap.range (S.secM M r)
declarations.comment: clause (5), H⁰(p^*M(q)) → H⁰(p^*M(q-(d-1)c)) lands in the image of the canonical map out of I^{q-(d-1)c} ⊗_A M; corrected as in clause (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.PullbackDual.dualModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
The dual `F^∨ = SheafHom_O(F, O)` of a sheaf of modules on a ringed site: the internal Hom
of Tag 03EM out of `F` into the structure sheaf, the structure sheaf being read as a module
over itself.  This is the `(-)^∨` of Tag 0GAB.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualModuleSheaf (Z : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf Z.O)) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf Z.O)
declarations.comment: the dual F^∨ = SheafHom(F, O), for a sheaf of modules on a ringed site

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.moduleDual
declarations.doc:
The dual `M^∨ = Hom_R(M, R)` of an `R`-module, as a functor contravariant in `M`: on
morphisms it is `LinearMap.dualMap`, that is, precomposition. For `R = A/Iⁿ` this is the `M^∨`
of Tag 0GAB; no finiteness of `M` is needed to form it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def moduleDual : (ModuleCat.{u} R)ᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R
declarations.comment: the dual M^∨ = Hom_{A/Iⁿ}(M, A/Iⁿ) of a module over A/Iⁿ, and its functoriality

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.IsANCModule.exists_finFree_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAB.** For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M` and `a ∈ I^c` the
multiplication-by-`a` endomorphism of `M` factors through a *finite free* `A/Iⁿ`-module.

This is the step the remark's proof of clause (4) opens with. By `IsANCModule` the map factors
through a projective module; since `M` is finite it factors through a finite projective module
by Tag 0G91, and a finite projective module is a retract of a finite free one.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsANCModule.exists_finFree_factorization {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    {n c : ℕ} {M : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)} (hM : IsANCModule I n c M)
    {a : A ⧸ I ^ n} (ha : a ∈ Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n)) (I ^ c)) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (α : M ⟶ finFreeModule (A ⧸ I ^ n) r)
      (β : finFreeModule (A ⧸ I ^ n) r ⟶ M), α ≫ β = a • 𝟙 M
declarations.comment: for a ∈ I^c the map a : M → M factors through a finite free A/Iⁿ-module

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.pullbackModuleDualMap
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GAB, the canonical map `can : p^*(M^∨) ⟶ (p^*M)^∨`.**  For a morphism of ringed sites
`f : X ⟶ Spec R` and an `R`-module `M`, with `p^*N = f^*(N~)`: the pullback of the comparison
`(M^∨)~ ⟶ (M~)^∨`, followed by the canonical map `f^*((M~)^∨) ⟶ (f^*(M~))^∨` of
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.PullbackDual.pullbackDualMap`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackModuleDualMap (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    (ringedSitePullback f).obj ((specTilde R).obj ((moduleDual R).obj (op M))) ⟶
      dualModuleSheaf X ((ringedSitePullback f).obj ((specTilde R).obj M))
declarations.comment: the canonical map can : p^*(M^∨) ⟶ (p^*M)^∨

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.pullbackModuleDualMap_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GAB, the construction of `can` is functorial in `M`.**  For `g : M ⟶ N` the square
formed by `can` at `M` and at `N`, by `p^*(g^∨)` and by `(p^*g)^∨` commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackModuleDualMap_naturality {M N : ModuleCat.{u} R} (g : M ⟶ N) :
    (ringedSitePullback f).map ((specTilde R).map ((moduleDual R).map g.op)) ≫
        pullbackModuleDualMap f M =
      pullbackModuleDualMap f N ≫
        dualModuleSheafMap X ((ringedSitePullback f).map ((specTilde R).map g))
declarations.comment: the construction of can is functorial in M

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.isIso_pullbackModuleDualMap_finFree
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GAB: `can` is an isomorphism at a finite free module `R^{⊕r}`.**  The comparison is
invertible there, `R^{⊕r}` being of finite presentation, and so is the sheaf-level `can` at
`(R^{⊕r})~`, `M ↦ M~` being additive with `R~ = 𝒪`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackModuleDualMap_finFree (r : ℕ) :
    IsIso (pullbackModuleDualMap f (finFreeModule R r))
declarations.comment: can is an isomorphism at a finite free A/Iⁿ-module

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.IsANCModule.kernel_map_pullbackModuleDualMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GAB, the kernel of `can`.**  Let `M` be an `(A, n, c)`-module, `a ∈ I^c` and
`f : X ⟶ Spec(A/Iⁿ)` any morphism of ringed sites.  Then `a` annihilates the kernel of
`can : p^*(M^∨) ⟶ (p^*M)^∨`: the endomorphism of `ker(can)` induced by multiplication by `a` on
`p^*(M^∨)` and on `(p^*M)^∨` is zero.  The source's reason is the proof: `a : M → M` factors
through a finite free `A/Iⁿ`-module (`IsANCModule.exists_finFree_factorization`), at which
`can` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsANCModule.kernel_map_pullbackModuleDualMap_eq_zero {X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}}
    (f : RingedSite.Hom X (specRingedSite (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))))
    {M : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)} (hM : IsANCModule I n c M) {a : A ⧸ I ^ n}
    (ha : a ∈ Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n)) (I ^ c)) :
    letI := specLinear (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))
    kernel.map (pullbackModuleDualMap f M) (pullbackModuleDualMap f M)
        ((ringedSitePullback f).map (a • 𝟙 ((specTilde (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))).obj
          ((moduleDual (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))).obj (op M)))))
        (dualModuleSheafMap X ((ringedSitePullback f).map
          (a • 𝟙 ((specTilde (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))).obj M))))
        (pullbackModuleDualMap_smul_naturality f M a) = 0
declarations.comment: for an (A,n,c)-module M, every a ∈ I^c annihilates the kernel of can

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.IsANCModule.cokernel_map_pullbackModuleDualMap_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GAB, the cokernel of `can`.**  For an `(A, n, c)`-module `M`, `a ∈ I^c` and any
morphism of ringed sites `f : X ⟶ Spec(A/Iⁿ)`, `a` annihilates the cokernel of
`can : p^*(M^∨) ⟶ (p^*M)^∨`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsANCModule.cokernel_map_pullbackModuleDualMap_eq_zero {X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}}
    (f : RingedSite.Hom X (specRingedSite (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))))
    {M : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)} (hM : IsANCModule I n c M) {a : A ⧸ I ^ n}
    (ha : a ∈ Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n)) (I ^ c)) :
    letI := specLinear (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))
    cokernel.map (pullbackModuleDualMap f M) (pullbackModuleDualMap f M)
        ((ringedSitePullback f).map (a • 𝟙 ((specTilde (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))).obj
          ((moduleDual (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))).obj (op M)))))
        (dualModuleSheafMap X ((ringedSitePullback f).map
          (a • 𝟙 ((specTilde (CommRingCat.of (A ⧸ I ^ n))).obj M))))
        (pullbackModuleDualMap_smul_naturality f M a) = 0
declarations.comment: for an (A,n,c)-module M, every a ∈ I^c annihilates the cokernel of can

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.DualSituation.exists_sum_powQuotSmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAC.** With `q₀ = q(S)` and `d = d(S)`, let `M` be an
`(A, n, c)`-module and `φ : M → Iⁿ/I^{2n}` an `A`-linear map. Write `D = max(d, 1)` and assume
`n ≥ q₀ + (1 + D)c` and `n ≥ (2 + D)c`. Then the composition

`M --φ--> Iⁿ/I^{2n} → I^{n-(1+D)c}/I^{2n-(1+D)c}`

is of the form `∑ aᵢψᵢ` with `aᵢ ∈ I^c` and `ψᵢ : M → I^{n-(2+D)c}/I^{2n-(2+D)c}`.

The levels are carried as parameters so that no truncated subtraction appears in a type:
`k + 1 = D`, `g + c = f`, `f + kc = e` and `e + 2c = n`, so that `f = n - (1 + D)c`,
`g = n - (2 + D)c` and `e = n - 2c`; the two numerical hypotheses of the source are the
existence of `g` as a natural number (`n ≥ (2 + D)c`) and `q₀ ≤ f` (`n ≥ q₀ + (1 + D)c`).

**Deviation from the source, at `d = 0`.** The source writes `d` where this statement writes
`D = max(d, 1)`, and adds for `d = 0` the hypothesis `n ≥ q₀ + 2c`. For `d ≥ 1` the two agree
exactly. For `d = 0` the source's own argument does not reach the level it asserts: it produces
`σ'` at level `n - 2c` — the cost of factoring through `can : p^*(M^∨) → (p^*M)^∨`, whose
kernel and cokernel are supported on `Y_c`, and which is independent of `d` — and then applies
clause (4) of Tag 0GAA at that level, which gives no further drop, so the argument ends at
`n - 2c` while the statement asserts `n - (1 + 0)c = n - c`, a discrepancy of `c` in the wrong
direction. The source's extra hypothesis `n ≥ q₀ + 2c` for `d = 0` is precisely what makes
clause (4) applicable at `n - 2c`, which corroborates that `n - 2c` is the level reached. So
for `d = 0` the levels stated here are the ones the argument supports, namely the `d = 1`
numbers `2c` and `3c`; the hypothesis `n ≥ 3c` this needs is not implied by the source's `d = 0`
hypotheses and is therefore part of `n ≥ (2 + D)c` above. Twisting the identity proved here
down by `c` recovers the source's numbering, so the source's `d = 0` form is strictly stronger
than what its argument establishes.

**The one open input.** The level-`(n - 2c)` section `σ'` is a hypothesis, not a conclusion:
producing it is the duality step of the source, which rests on the kernel and cokernel of `can`
being scheme-theoretically supported on `Y_c` — a statement about the blowup situation that
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.PullbackDual` (Tag 0GAB) explicitly does not prove. Everything after it
is derived: the `(d-1)c` drop is Tag 0GAA clause (5) for `d ≥ 2` and clause (4) for `d ≤ 1`
(`exists_ev_secM_eq`), and the passage from the resulting element of `I^f ⊗_A M^∨` to the sum
`∑ aᵢψᵢ` is `ev_secM_mem_divisibleMaps`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sum_powQuotSmul (M : ANCModule I n c)
    (φ : resModule I n M.1 →ₗ[A] powQuot I n n) {g f e k : ℕ}
    (hgf : g + c = f) (hk : max S.d 1 = k + 1) (he : f + k * c = e) (hen : e + 2 * c = n)
    (hq : S.q₀ ≤ f) (σ' : S.H M.dual 0 (e : ℤ))
    (hσ : S.ev M e (hq.trans (Nat.le.intro he)) σ' =
      (powQuotLe I (Nat.le.intro hen)).comp φ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → A) (ha : ∀ i, a i ∈ I ^ c)
      (ψ : Fin N → (resModule I n M.1 →ₗ[A] powQuot I g n)),
      (powQuotLe I ((Nat.le.intro he).trans (Nat.le.intro hen))).comp φ =
        ∑ i, (powQuotSmul I (ha i) hgf).comp (ψ i)
declarations.comment: with max(d, 1) in place of d, since at d = 0 the source's own argument reaches only level n - 2c while the source states n - c; its one open input is the level-(n-2c) section σ' of p^*(M^∨) produced by factoring through can, hypothesis `hσ`

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.exists_sum_powQuotSmul_blowup
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `q₀ = q(S)` and `d = d(S)` the integers
attached to the blowing up of `Spec(A)` in `I` (`qS I` and `fibreDim I`), `M` an
`(A, n, c)`-module and `φ : M → Iⁿ/I^{2n}` an `A`-linear map. If `n ≥ q₀ + (1 + d)c` and
`n ≥ (2 + d)c`, then the composition `M → Iⁿ/I^{2n} → I^{n-(1+d)c}/I^{2n-(1+d)c}` is of the
form `∑ aᵢψᵢ` with `aᵢ ∈ I^c` and `ψᵢ : M → I^{n-(2+d)c}/I^{2n-(2+d)c}`. No hypothesis
`n ≥ q₀ + 2c` is imposed when `d = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sum_powQuotSmul_blowup {n c : ℕ} (M : ANCModule I n c)
    (φ : resModule I n M.1 →ₗ[A] powQuot I n n)
    (hn₁ : qS I + (1 + fibreDim I) * c ≤ n) (hn₂ : (2 + fibreDim I) * c ≤ n) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (a : Fin N → A) (ha : ∀ i, a i ∈ I ^ c)
      (ψ : Fin N → (resModule I n M.1 →ₗ[A] powQuot I (n - (2 + fibreDim I) * c) n)),
      (powQuotLe I (Nat.sub_le n ((1 + fibreDim I) * c))).comp φ =
        ∑ i, (powQuotSmul I (ha i) (show n - (2 + fibreDim I) * c + c =
          n - (1 + fibreDim I) * c by
            have := two_add_mul_eq (fibreDim I) c; omega)).comp (ψ i)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.UniformityIII.ext_one_powQuot_map_eq_zero_blowup
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, and `q₀ = q(S)`, `d = d(S)` the integers
attached to the blowing up of `Spec(A)` in `I` (`qS I` and `fibreDim I`). Let `c ≥ 0` and
`n ≥ q₀ + (1 + d)c`, and let `K` be an object of `D(A/Iⁿ)` with `Hⁱ(K) = 0` for `i ≠ -1, 0`, with
`H⁻¹(K)` and `H⁰(K)` finite, and such that `Ext¹_{A/Iⁿ}(K, N)` is annihilated by `I^c` for every
finite `A/Iⁿ`-module `N`. Then the map

`Ext¹_{A/Iⁿ}(K, Iⁿ/I^{2n}) ⟶ Ext¹_{A/Iⁿ}(K, I^{n-(1+d)c}/I^{2n-2(1+d)c})`

induced by the canonical map of coefficients is zero.

The target is written `powQuot I f f = I^f/I^{f+f}` with `f = n - (1 + d)c`, as an
`A/Iⁿ`-module (`powQuotObjOfLe`); the map is the one induced by `Iⁿ ⊆ I^f` (`powQuotToOfLe`).
declarations.statement:
theorem ext_one_powQuot_map_eq_zero_blowup {n c : ℕ}
    (hn : qS I + (1 + fibreDim I) * c ≤ n)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)) i).obj K))
    (hfin₁ : Module.Finite (A ⧸ I ^ n)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)) (-1)).obj K))
    (hfin₀ : Module.Finite (A ⧸ I ^ n)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)) 0).obj K))
    (hann : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)), Module.Finite (A ⧸ I ^ n) N →
      ∀ a ∈ Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n)) (I ^ c),
      ∀ ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)) 0).obj N) 1, a • ξ = 0)
    (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext K
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)) 0).obj (powQuotObj I n n)) 1) :
    ξ ≫ (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n))) (1 : ℤ)).map
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⧸ I ^ n)) 0).map
          (powQuotToOfLe I (Nat.sub_le n ((1 + fibreDim I) * c)) (by omega)
            (Nat.sub_le n ((1 + fibreDim I) * c)))) = 0

declarations.name: Rig.completedNaiveCotangentComplex_homotopyEquiv
declarations.doc:
The completed naive cotangent complexes associated to two completed polynomial
presentations of the same `I`-adically complete algebra are homotopy equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem completedNaiveCotangentComplex_homotopyEquiv
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P Q : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    Nonempty (HomotopyEquiv
      (Rig.completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).cochainComplex
      (Rig.completedNaiveCotangentComplex B Q).cochainComplex)

declarations.name: Rig.surjective_completedPresentationMap
declarations.doc:
The completion `α^ : A[x₁, …, xₙ]^ → B^` of a presentation `α : A[x₁, …, xₙ] → B` of a finite
type algebra over a Noetherian ring is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_completedPresentationMap (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B)
    (hα : Function.Surjective α) : Function.Surjective (completedPresentationMap I α)
declarations.comment: B^ = A[x₁, …, xₙ]^ / J^: the completed presentation is surjective

declarations.name: Rig.ker_completedPresentationMap
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the completion `α^` of a presentation `α` with kernel `J` is the ideal
`J^ = J · A[x₁, …, xₙ]^` generated by `J` in the completed polynomial ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ker_completedPresentationMap (α : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B)
    (hα : Function.Surjective α) :
    RingHom.ker (completedPresentationMap I α).toRingHom =
      (RingHom.ker α.toRingHom).map
        (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) (adicCompletionMvPolynomial I n))
declarations.comment: B^ = A[x₁, …, xₙ]^ / J^: the kernel of the completed presentation is J^

declarations.name: Rig.differential_conormalComparison
declarations.doc:
**The square of differentials commutes**: both ways round, the class of `g ∈ J` goes to the
tuple of the images in `B^` of the partial derivatives `∂g/∂xᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem differential_conormalComparison (x : G.toExtension.Cotangent) :
    (completedComplex I G).differential (conormalComparison I G x) =
      fun i ↦ algebraMap B (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier
        (presentationDifferential G x i)
declarations.comment: the comparison commutes with the differentials

declarations.name: Rig.completionComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison of complexes `NL(α) ⊗_B B^ → NL^∧_{B^/A}`: in degree `-1` it is the
`B^`-linear extension of the map `J / J² → J^ / (J^)²` and in degree `0` it is `dxᵢ ↦ dxᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
public def completionComparison :
    NaiveCotangent.ChainMap
      (baseChangedTwoTerm (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier (presentationDifferential G))
      (completedComplex I G).twoTerm
declarations.comment: the comparison of complexes NL(α) ⊗_B B^ → NL^∧_{B^/A}

declarations.name: Rig.bijective_completionComparison_f₀
declarations.doc: The comparison `NL(α) ⊗_B B^ → NL^∧_{B^/A}` is bijective in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_completionComparison_f₀ :
    Function.Bijective (completionComparison I G).f₀
declarations.comment: the comparison is bijective in degree 0

declarations.name: Rig.bijective_completionComparison_f₁
declarations.doc:
The comparison `NL(α) ⊗_B B^ → NL^∧_{B^/A}` is bijective in degree `1`, that is
`B^ ⊗_B (J / J²) = J^ / (J^)²`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_completionComparison_f₁ :
    Function.Bijective (completionComparison I G).f₁
declarations.comment: the comparison is bijective in degree 1

declarations.name: Rig.bijective_completionComparison
declarations.doc:
`NL^∧_{B^/A} = NL(α) ⊗_B B^` as complexes: the comparison of two-term complexes is bijective
in both degrees and commutes with the two differentials.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_completionComparison :
    Function.Bijective (completionComparison I G).f₁ ∧
      Function.Bijective (completionComparison I G).f₀ ∧
      (completedComplex I G).twoTerm.d ∘ₗ (completionComparison I G).f₁ =
        (completionComparison I G).f₀ ∘ₗ
          (baseChangedTwoTerm (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier
            (presentationDifferential G)).d
declarations.comment: NL^∧_{B^/A} = NL(α) ⊗_B B^ as complexes

declarations.name: Rig.completedNaiveCotangentDerivedTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAF, second clause.** `NL^∧_{B^/A} = NL_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B^` in `D(B^)`, for the
canonical derived tensor product along `B → B^` with the unit complex `B^` in degree `0`.
declarations.statement:
public def completedNaiveCotangentDerivedTensorIso :
    (CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorChangeOfRings
        (algebraMap B (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier)
        ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
          (ModuleCat.{max u v} (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier
            (ULift.{u} (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier)))).F.obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (naiveCotangentCochain A B)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (completedComplex I G).cochainComplex
declarations.comment: NL^∧_{B^/A} = NL_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B^ in D(B^)

declarations.name: Rig.bijective_limitComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAF, the `lim` form of the first clause.** `lim NL(α) = NL(α) ⊗_B B^` as
complexes: the comparison is bijective in both degrees and commutes with the differentials.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_limitComparison :
    Function.Bijective (limitComparison I G).f₁ ∧
      Function.Bijective (limitComparison I G).f₀ ∧
      (adicLimitTwoTerm I G).d ∘ₗ (limitComparison I G).f₁ =
        (limitComparison I G).f₀ ∘ₗ
          (baseChangedTwoTerm (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)).carrier
            (presentationDifferential G)).d
declarations.comment: lim NL(α) = NL(α) ⊗_B B^ as complexes

declarations.name: Rig.bijective_limitCompletionComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAF, first clause in its `lim` form.** `NL^∧_{B^/A} = lim NL(α) ⊗_B B^` as
complexes: the comparison from the degreewise `I`-adic completion of `NL(α)` to the completed
naive cotangent complex of the completed presentation is bijective in both degrees and commutes
with the differentials.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_limitCompletionComparison :
    Function.Bijective (limitCompletionComparison I G).f₁ ∧
      Function.Bijective (limitCompletionComparison I G).f₀ ∧
      (completedComplex I G).twoTerm.d ∘ₗ (limitCompletionComparison I G).f₁ =
        (limitCompletionComparison I G).f₀ ∘ₗ (adicLimitTwoTerm I G).d
declarations.comment: NL^∧_{B^/A} = lim NL(α) ⊗_B B^ as complexes

declarations.name: Rig.baseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison map `NL^∧_{B₁/A₁} ⊗_{B₁} B₂ → NL^∧_{B₂/A₂}`, for the presentation of
`B₁` cut out by a generating family `g` of `B₁` modulo `I₁` and the compatible presentation of the
base change `B₂` in the same variables.

In degree `-1` it is the `B₂`-linear extension of the map `J₁ / J₁² → J₂ / J₂²` induced by the
base-change map of completed polynomial algebras, and in degree `0` it is `dxᵢ ↦ dxᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
public def baseChangeComparison :
    NaiveCotangent.ChainMap
      (baseChangedTwoTerm B₂.carrier
        (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B₁ (ofGenerators B₁ r g hI₁ hgen)).differential)
      (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B₂
        (baseChangePresentation (B₁ := B₁) hI₂ hc hmap hspan r g hgen)).twoTerm
declarations.comment: the comparison map

declarations.name: Rig.bijective_onH₀_baseChangeComparison_of_completedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `(A₁, I₁) → (A₂, I₂)` be as in Stacks Remark 0AL5 — a map of Noetherian pairs carrying a
positive power of `I₁` into `I₂` — let `B₁` be adically of finite type over `(A₁, I₁)`, and let
`B₂` be its completed base change `(B₁ ⊗_{A₁} A₂)^∧_{I₂}`. Then the canonical comparison map
`NL^∧_{B₁/A₁} ⊗_{B₁} B₂ → NL^∧_{B₂/A₂}` of `Rig.baseChangeComparison` induces an isomorphism on
`H⁰`. The identification of `B₂` with `(B₁ ⊗_{A₁} A₂)^∧_{I₂}` is the data `e`, `heA`, `heB`.
declarations.comment: isomorphism on H⁰

declarations.name: Rig.surjective_onH₁_baseChangeComparison_of_completedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
In the situation of
`Rig.bijective_onH₀_baseChangeComparison_of_completedBaseChange` — `(A₁, I₁) → (A₂, I₂)` as in
Stacks Remark 0AL5 with both rings Noetherian, and `B₂` the completed base change of `B₁` —
the canonical comparison map `NL^∧_{B₁/A₁} ⊗_{B₁} B₂ → NL^∧_{B₂/A₂}` induces a surjection on
`H⁻¹`.
declarations.comment: surjection on H⁻¹

declarations.name: Rig.IsRigSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAI.** Rig-smoothness of an adically finite type `A`-algebra over
`(A, I)`: some uniform power of `I` annihilates `Ext¹` from its completed naive cotangent
complex to every `B`-module.
declarations.statement: public def IsRigSmooth (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) : Prop

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_iff_cotangentCohomologyCondition
declarations.doc:
Rig-smoothness is equivalent to the cohomological criterion for the completed naive
cotangent complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_iff_cotangentCohomologyCondition
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    Rig.IsRigSmooth B ↔ HasCotangentCohomologyCondition B P
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_iff_cotangentFactorization
declarations.doc:
Rig-smoothness is equivalent to uniform factorization of powers of the ideal of
definition through the differential of a chosen completed naive cotangent complex.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_iff_cotangentFactorization
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    Rig.IsRigSmooth B ↔ HasCotangentFactorization B P
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_iff_hasJacobianCover
declarations.doc:
Rig-smoothness is equivalent to a finite Jacobian cover away from the ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_iff_hasJacobianCover
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    Rig.IsRigSmooth B ↔ HasJacobianCover B P
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (4)

declarations.name: Rig.isElementPowerTorsion_hneg_of_jacobianChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAJ, inside the proof of (4) ⟹ (2).**  Let `b` carry a Jacobian chart: a
subset `T` of `m` of the variables and `m` elements `f₁, …, fₘ` of the presentation ideal `J`
whose Jacobian minor along `T` divides `b`, with `b J ⊆ (f₁, …, fₘ) + J²`.  Then
`H⁻¹(NL^∧_{B/A})` is `b`-power torsion; in fact `b²` already annihilates it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isElementPowerTorsion_hneg_of_jacobianChart
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) (b : P.completedPolynomialRing)
    {m : ℕ} (T : Fin m ↪ Fin P.variableCount) (f : Fin m → P.ker)
    (hdet : P.toAlgHom
      (Matrix.det fun i j : Fin m ↦
        (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).partialDeriv (T i) (f j : P.completedPolynomialRing)) ∣
        P.toAlgHom b)
    (hrelations : ∀ x : P.completedPolynomialRing, x ∈ P.ker →
      b * x ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range fun j : Fin m ↦ (f j : P.completedPolynomialRing)) +
        P.ker ^ 2) :
    IsElementPowerTorsion B.carrier (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).Hneg
      (P.toAlgHom b)
declarations.comment: the proof of (4) ⟹ (2): H⁻¹(NL^∧) is b_l-power torsion

declarations.name: Rig.free_localized_hzero_of_jacobianChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAJ, inside the proof of (4) ⟹ (2).**  Let `b` carry a Jacobian chart: a subset
`T` of `m` of the variables and `m` elements `f₁, …, fₘ` of the presentation ideal `J` whose
Jacobian minor along `T` divides `b`, with `b J ⊆ (f₁, …, fₘ) + J²`.  Then `H⁰(NL^∧_{B/A})`
becomes finite free after inverting `b`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem free_localized_hzero_of_jacobianChart
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) (b : P.completedPolynomialRing)
    {m : ℕ} (T : Fin m ↪ Fin P.variableCount) (f : Fin m → P.ker)
    (hdet : P.toAlgHom
      (Matrix.det fun i j : Fin m ↦
        (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).partialDeriv (T i) (f j : P.completedPolynomialRing)) ∣
        P.toAlgHom b)
    (hrelations : ∀ x : P.completedPolynomialRing, x ∈ P.ker →
      b * x ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range fun j : Fin m ↦ (f j : P.completedPolynomialRing)) +
        P.ker ^ 2) :
    Module.Free (Localization.Away (P.toAlgHom b))
        (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (P.toAlgHom b))
          (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).Hzero) ∧
      Module.Finite (Localization.Away (P.toAlgHom b))
        (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (P.toAlgHom b))
          (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).Hzero)
declarations.comment: the proof of (4) ⟹ (2): H⁰(NL^∧) is finite free after inverting b_l

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_adicCompletionObj_of_smoothAwayFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAK (1).** If `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is smooth over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`, then the
`I`-adic completion `B^` is rig-smooth over `(A, I)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_adicCompletionObj_of_smoothAwayFrom (h : SmoothAwayFrom A I B) :
    IsRigSmooth (adicCompletionObj I (B := B))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Rig.exists_sub_one_mem_and_smoothAwayFrom_of_isRigSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAK (2).** If the `I`-adic completion `B^` is rig-smooth over `(A, I)`, then there
is `g ∈ 1 + IB` such that `Spec(B_g) → Spec(A)` is smooth over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sub_one_mem_and_smoothAwayFrom_of_isRigSmooth
    (h : IsRigSmooth (adicCompletionObj I (B := B))) :
    ∃ g : B, g - 1 ∈ I.map (algebraMap A B) ∧ SmoothAwayFrom A I (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Rig.smul_ext_one_completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAL.**  Let `(A₁, I₁) → (A₂, I₂)` be as in Stacks Remark 0AL5 — a
ring map `A₁ → A₂` of Noetherian rings with ideals `I₁ ⊆ A₁`, `I₂ ⊆ A₂` such that `I₁ ^ c`
maps into `I₂` for some `c ≥ 1` — let `B₁` be adically of finite type over `(A₁, I₁)` (Stacks
0AL4), let `B₂ = (B₁ ⊗_{A₁} A₂)^∧` be its base change, the value at `B₁` of the completed
base-change functor `Rig.completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing` of Remark 0AL5, and let
`f₂ ∈ B₂` be the image of `f₁ ∈ B₁`, that is of `f₁ ⊗ 1` (`Rig.CompletedBaseChange.scalar`).
If `f₁` annihilates `Ext¹_{B₁}(NL^∧_{B₁/A₁}, N₁)` for
every `B₁`-module `N₁`, then `f₂` annihilates `Ext¹_{B₂}(NL^∧_{B₂/A₂}, N₂)` for every
`B₂`-module `N₂`.

The completed cotangent complexes are computed from arbitrary completed polynomial
presentations `P₁` and `P₂`, on which they do not depend (Stacks 0GAE).
declarations.statement:
public theorem smul_ext_one_completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing
    (hpow : ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ (I₁ ^ c).map (algebraMap A₁ A₂) ≤ I₂)
    (B₁ : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u₁, v} A₁ I₁)
    (P₁ : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I₁ B₁)
    (P₂ : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I₂
      ((completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing hpow).functor.obj B₁))
    (f₁ : B₁.carrier)
    (h : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u₁ v} B₁.carrier)
      (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext (derivedCompletedNaiveCotangentComplex B₁ P₁)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u₁ v} B₁.carrier) 0).obj N) 1),
      f₁ • ξ = 0) :
    ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u₂ v}
        ((completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing hpow).functor.obj B₁).carrier)
      (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext
        (derivedCompletedNaiveCotangentComplex
          ((completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing hpow).functor.obj B₁) P₂)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u₂ v}
          ((completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing hpow).functor.obj B₁).carrier) 0).obj N) 1),
      (completedBaseChangeOfIsNoetherianRing hpow).scalar B₁ f₁ • ξ = 0

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_completedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAM.** Rig-smoothness is preserved by completed base change along a
map of Noetherian rings whose source and target ideals define the same closed subset of the
target spectrum.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_completedBaseChange
    (hV : (I₁.map (algebraMap A₁ A₂)).radical = I₂.radical)
    (C : CompletedBaseChange (A₁ := A₁) (A₂ := A₂) (I₁ := I₁) (I₂ := I₂))
    (B₁ : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u₁, v} A₁ I₁) (hB₁ : IsRigSmooth B₁) :
    IsRigSmooth (C.functor.obj B₁)

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_completedBaseChangedAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GAM.** Let `A₁ → A₂` be a map of Noetherian rings and let
`I₁ ⊆ A₁`, `I₂ ⊆ A₂` be ideals with `V(I₁ A₂) = V(I₂)`.  If `B₁` is rig-smooth over
`(A₁, I₁)`, then its base change `B₂ = (B₁ ⊗_{A₁} A₂)^`, the `I₂`-adic completion of Remark
0AL5, is rig-smooth over `(A₂, I₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_completedBaseChangedAlgebra
    (hV : (I₁.map (algebraMap A₁ A₂)).radical = I₂.radical)
    (B₁ : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u₁, v} A₁ I₁) (hB₁ : IsRigSmooth B₁) :
    IsRigSmooth (I := I₂)
      (⟨CommAlgCat.of A₂ (completedBaseChangedAlgebra (I₂ := I₂) B₁),
        isAdicComplete_and_finiteType_completedBaseChangedAlgebra hV B₁⟩ :
        AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u₂, max v u₂} A₂ I₂)

declarations.name: Rig.exists_perturbed_continuousAlgHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GAP**, the lifting claim, in the principal case.

Let `I = (a)`, let `C` be an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra on which `a` is a nonzerodivisor,
and let `J` be an ideal of `A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩` satisfying the obstruction relation
`a ^ c · g ≡ ∑ i (∂g/∂xᵢ) γᵢ` modulo `J²` for a fixed family `γ₁, …, γ_r ∈ J`. Then a continuous
`A`-algebra map `ψ : A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ → C` with `ψ(J) ⊆ aⁿC` can be perturbed to a continuous
`ψ'` with `ψ'(J) ⊆ a^{2(n-c)}C`, the perturbation taking values in `a^{n-c}C`.

The perturbation is `xᵢ ↦ ψ(xᵢ) - δᵢ` where `a ^ c δᵢ = ψ(γᵢ)`; the two conclusions are the
first-order expansion of Stacks 0AK3 applied to it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_perturbed_continuousAlgHom (a : A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = Ideal.span {a})
    {C : Type w} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C]
    (ha : IsRegular (algebraMap A C a))
    {r : ℕ} (Jid : Ideal (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin r))) (c n : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n)
    (γ : Fin r → RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin r)) (hγ : ∀ i, γ i ∈ Jid)
