   with each `Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ` corresponding to a flat map of Noetherian adic topological rings;
4. there are an affine étale covering `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` and factorizations `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Y` through
   affine formal algebraic spaces representable étale over `Y` with each `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ`
   corresponding to a flat map of Noetherian adic topological rings.

As in the source, (1) and (2) agree by Definition 0GCC, and (2), (3), (4) are the three
conditions of the Noetherian variant of Stacks 0ANG (Remark 0ANI) for flatness, a local property
of arrows of `WAdm^{Noeth}` by Stacks 0GC9.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsFlat B S hS f,
        HasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic TopologicalRing.IsFlatHom f,
        HasPropertyAfterTargetCover B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic TopologicalRing.IsFlatHom f,
        HasPropertyAfterSourceCover B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic TopologicalRing.IsFlatHom f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFlat_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductions_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCE, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of locally
Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` is flat (Definition 0GCC) and the morphism
of reductions `g_red : Z_red ⟶ Y_red` is locally of finite type, then the base change
`X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is flat.

Flatness of arrows of `WAdm^{Noeth}` is stable under base change by arrows of finite type on
reductions (Stacks 0GCA, part (1)); the hypothesis on `g_red` gives that property on every affine
étale chart map of `g` by the implication (4) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0GC7, and Stacks 0GBG transfers
flatness to the second projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductions_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductions B S hS g) :
    IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFiniteType_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCE, part (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of locally
Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` is flat (Definition 0GCC) and locally of
finite type (Stacks 0AM4), then the base change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is flat and locally of finite
type.

Flatness together with being adic and topologically of finite type is stable under arbitrary
base change of arrows of `WAdm^{Noeth}` (Stacks 0GCA, part (2)); the hypotheses on `f` give that
property on every affine étale chart map of `f` (Stacks 0GC0 read at `WAdm^{Noeth}`), Stacks 0GBF
transfers it to the second projection, and flatness is read off its first conjunct. The second
conclusion is Stacks 0AQ5, which needs neither flatness nor the Noetherian hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_and_isLocallyOfFiniteType_pullback_snd {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f g) ∧ IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFlat_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductions'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCE, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of locally
Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` is flat in the sense of Definition 0GCC and
the morphism of reductions `g_red : Z_red ⟶ Y_red` is locally of finite type, then the base
change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is flat.

Flatness of arrows of `WAdm^{Noeth}` is stable under base change by arrows of finite type on
reductions by part (1) of Stacks 0GCA, which the library proves outright; Remark 0GBG transfers
that to the second projection of the fibre product, on the two inputs `h31` and `hcover` it
carries — the invariance of flatness under isomorphism of targets is read off the locality
field of the stability bundle, whose first axiom it is; and the hypothesis on `g_red` becomes the chart condition the transfer
consumes by the implication (4) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0GC7, on the two inputs `hbridge` and
`hredsquare`. Nothing about flatness is assumed in any of the five.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductions'
    (h31 : SourceCoverImpliesEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
      TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic TopologicalRing.IsFlatHom)
    (hbridge : ChartPropertyIsFiniteTypeOnReductions B S hS)
    (hredsquare : IsLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductionsOnEveryAffineEtaleSquare B S hS)
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hcover : HasBaseChangeCoverOverPullbackSnd B S hS f g)
    (hZ : IsLocallyCountablyIndexed B S hS Z) (hY : IsLocallyCountablyIndexed B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteTypeOnReductions B S hS g) :
    IsFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: part (1), on the 0GBG transfer inputs and the 0GC7 (4) implies (1) inputs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyOfFiniteType_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCE, part (2), locally of finite type.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be
morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` is locally of finite
type in the sense of Stacks 0AM4, then the base change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is locally of finite type.

The second projection of the fibre product is a base change of `f`, and a base change of a
morphism locally of finite type is locally of finite type by **Stacks 0AQ5**, which the library
proves outright as `IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_isPullback`. Nothing else is needed, so neither
flatness of `f` nor the locally Noetherian hypotheses of the source nor the inputs of the
transfer of Remark 0GBF appear: the conclusion holds at every morphism of fppf sheaves, which is
at least as general as part (2) of the source.
declarations.comment: part (2), locally of finite type, from Stacks 0AQ5 alone -- the second projection is a base change of `f`. No input of Remark 0GBF and no comparison of Stacks 0GC0 is used, and flatness of `f` is not used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFlat_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCF.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` are flat morphisms of locally Noetherian
formal algebraic spaces over `S`, then `g ∘ f` is flat.

Flatness is condition (1) of Stacks 0ANG for Noetherian adic rings and flat ring maps, a local
property stable under composition (Stacks 0GCB), so Remark 0GBK applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsFlat B S hS f) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g) :
    IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFlat_of_hasPropertyULift_flatPropertyULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCG.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and flat in the Bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ is flat in the
sense of Definition 0GCC.

On an affine representable étale square over `f`, the homomorphism `φ` presenting the chart map
is taut because `f` is representable. Bootstrap flatness of `f` makes `φ` flat modulo every
weak ideal of definition of its source, and Stacks 0912 concludes that `φ` is flat. The source
assumes `X` and `Y` locally Noetherian; the proof does not use this.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_hasPropertyULift_flatPropertyULift {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (hflat : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS (Space.flatPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS)
      f.hom hrep) :
    IsFlat B S hS f

declarations.name: Rig.isRigSmooth_iff_forall_idealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCI.** Rig-smoothness of a finite-type morphism of Noetherian
weakly admissible rings does not depend on the ideal of definition of its source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigSmooth_iff_forall_idealOfDefinition
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (_hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (_hφ : Continuous φ) (hft : FiniteTypeAdicAlgebraForEveryIdeal φ) :
    (∃ (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I),
      IsRigSmooth (adicFiniteTypeAlgebra φ hft I hI)) ↔
      (∀ (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I),
        IsRigSmooth (adicFiniteTypeAlgebra φ hft I hI))

declarations.name: RingHom.IsRigSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCJ.** A continuous homomorphism of Noetherian adic topological
rings is *rig-smooth* when it is adic of topologically finite type — condition (6) of Tag 0GBW
— and makes its target rig-smooth over some ideal of definition of its source.  By Tag 0GCI the
choice of that ideal is immaterial.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsRigSmooth {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: Rig.rigSmooth_isLocalNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCK.** Rig-smoothness is a local property of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth`: it ascends
along a completed étale localization diagram, descends along one whose target-side horizontal
map is faithfully flat, and is preserved by finite products of targets.

declarations.name: Rig.rigSmooth_isLocalNoetherian'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCK.** Rig-smoothness is a local property of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth`: it is
independent of the presentations of its source and target, ascends along a completed étale
localization diagram, descends along one whose target-side horizontal map is faithfully flat,
and is preserved by finite products of targets.

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.rigSmooth_completedTensorProduct_of_isAdic
declarations.doc:
Rig-smoothness (Tag 0GCJ) is stable under base change by adic morphisms (Tag 0GBR) in the
sense of Remark 0GBG: if `B → A` is rig-smooth and `B → C` is adic, both arrows of
`WAdm^{Noeth}`, then the completed tensor product `A ⊗̂_B C` is again Noetherian adic and
rig-smooth over `C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigSmooth_completedTensorProduct_of_isAdic
    {B A C : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C]
    [IsLinearTopology C C] [Algebra B A] [Algebra B C] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B) (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsAdic C)
    (hBA : Continuous (algebraMap B A)) (hBC : Continuous (algebraMap B C))
    (hP : RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow (algebraMap B A))
    (hQ : RingHom.IsAdic (algebraMap B C)) :
    TopologicalRing.IsAdic (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := B) (M := A) (N := C)) ∧
      IsNoetherianRing (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := B) (M := A) (N := C)) ∧
      RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow
        (algebraMap C (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := B) (M := A) (N := C)))

declarations.name: Rig.rigSmooth_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCM.**  Rig-smoothness of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth` is stable under
composition: if `f : B →+* A` and `g : C →+* B` are continuous rig-smooth homomorphisms of
Noetherian adic topological rings, then so is `f ∘ g`.

Condition (6) of Stacks 0GBW for the composite is
`Rig.finiteTypeAdicAlgebraForEveryIdeal_comp`.  For rig-smoothness over an ideal of definition
`I ⊆ C`, Stacks 0GCI moves both hypotheses onto `I` and onto `I B`, Stacks 0ALM presents `A`
over `(C, I)` by combining the two presentations, and
`Rig.hasCotangentFactorization_combinedPresentation` multiplies the two factorizations of
condition (3) of Stacks 0GAJ.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigSmooth_comp
    {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C]
    [IsLinearTopology C C]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A ∧ IsNoetherianRing A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B ∧ IsNoetherianRing B)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsAdic C ∧ IsNoetherianRing C)
    (f : B →+* A) (g : C →+* B) (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g)
    (hPf : RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow f) (hPg : RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow g) :
    RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow (f.comp g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCP.** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *rig-smooth* when every
morphism between affine, representable, étale charts of its source and target is induced by a
rig-smooth continuous homomorphism of adic Noetherian topological rings.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRigSmooth (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_iff_hasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCQ, conditions (1) and (2).** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is
rig-smooth exactly when rig-smoothness as a property of arrows of `WAdm^{Noeth}` holds on every
affine étale diagram over it: the two conditions are the same, which is what Definition 0GCP
says.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_iff_hasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS f ↔
      HasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
        (fun R ↦ TopologicalRing.IsAdic R ∧ IsNoetherianRing R)
        (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
          [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
          RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCQ.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S`, the following are equivalent: `f` is rig-smooth (Definition 0GCP); every commutative
square with affine formal algebraic spaces `U`, `V` and representable étale maps `U ⟶ X`,
`V ⟶ Y` has `U ⟶ V` given by a rig-smooth arrow of `WAdm^{Noeth}`; there are an affine étale
covering `{Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` and, for each `j`, an affine étale covering `{Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ ×_Y X}` with every
`Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ` given by a rig-smooth arrow of `WAdm^{Noeth}`; and there is an affine étale covering
`{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` with factorizations `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Y` through affine formal algebraic spaces
representable étale over `Y` with every `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ` given by a rig-smooth arrow of
`WAdm^{Noeth}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_tfae {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigSmooth B S hS f,
        HasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic
          (fun φ ↦ RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f,
        HasPropertyAfterTargetCover B S hS TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic
          (fun φ ↦ RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f,
        HasPropertyAfterSourceCover B S hS TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic
          (fun φ ↦ RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCQ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S`. The following are equivalent:

1. `f` is rig-smooth (Definition 0GCP);
2. for every commutative square with `U`, `V` affine formal algebraic spaces and `U ⟶ X`,
   `V ⟶ Y` representable by algebraic spaces and étale, the morphism `U ⟶ V` corresponds to a
   rig-smooth map in `WAdm^{Noeth}`;
3. there exist a covering `{Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM and for each `j` a covering
   `{Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ ×_Y X}` as in Definition 0AIM such that each `Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ` corresponds to a
   rig-smooth map in `WAdm^{Noeth}`;
4. there exist a covering `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` as in Definition 0AIM and for each `i` a factorization
   `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Y` where `Yᵢ` is an affine formal algebraic space, `Yᵢ ⟶ Y` is representable by
   algebraic spaces and étale, and `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ` corresponds to a rig-smooth map in
   `WAdm^{Noeth}`.

In (2), (3) and (4) "corresponds to a rig-smooth map in `WAdm^{Noeth}`" is
`CorrespondsToNoetherianMap` for rig-smoothness: source and target are formal spectra of
Noetherian adic rings and the map is the formal spectrum of a rig-smooth homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigSmooth B S hS f,
        CorrespondsToNoetherianMapOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
          (fun φ ↦ RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f,
        CorrespondsToNoetherianMapAfterTargetCover B S hS (fun φ ↦ RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f,
        CorrespondsToNoetherianMapAfterSourceCover B S hS
          (fun φ ↦ RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ) f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` is rig-smooth and `g` is adic, then the base change
`X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is rig-smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_pullback_snd {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z) (hf : IsRigSmooth B S hS f)
    (hg : IsAdicMorphism B S hS g) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` and `g` are rig-smooth, then so is `g ∘ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsRigSmooth B S hS f) (hg : IsRigSmooth B S hS g) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: Rig.rigEtaleOver_iff_forall_idealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCU.** For an adic morphism of topologically finite type between
Noetherian adic rings, rig-étaleness over one ideal of definition is equivalent to
rig-étaleness over every ideal of definition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigEtaleOver_iff_forall_idealOfDefinition
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (_hφ : Continuous φ)
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A) (_hB : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B) :
    (FiniteTypeAdicAlgebraForEveryIdeal φ ∧
      ∃ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧ IsRigEtaleOver φ I) ↔
    (FiniteTypeAdicAlgebraForEveryIdeal φ ∧
      ∀ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I → IsRigEtaleOver φ I)

declarations.name: RingHom.IsRigEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCV.** A continuous homomorphism of Noetherian adic topological
rings is *rig-étale* when it is adic of topologically finite type — condition (6) of Tag 0GBW
— and makes its target rig-étale over some ideal of definition of its source.  By Tag 0GCU the
choice of that ideal is immaterial.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsRigEtale {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.rigEtale_completedTensorProduct_of_isAdic
declarations.doc:
Rig-étaleness (Tag 0GCV) is stable under base change by adic morphisms (Tag 0GBR) in the
sense of Remark 0GBG: if `B → A` is rig-étale and `B → C` is adic, both arrows of
`WAdm^{Noeth}`, then the completed tensor product `A ⊗̂_B C` is again Noetherian adic and
rig-étale over `C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigEtale_completedTensorProduct_of_isAdic
    {B A C : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C]
    [IsLinearTopology C C] [Algebra B A] [Algebra B C] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B) (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsAdic C)
    (hBA : Continuous (algebraMap B A)) (hBC : Continuous (algebraMap B C))
    (hP : RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow (algebraMap B A))
    (hQ : RingHom.IsAdic (algebraMap B C)) :
    TopologicalRing.IsAdic (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := B) (M := A) (N := C)) ∧
      IsNoetherianRing (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := B) (M := A) (N := C)) ∧
      RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow
        (algebraMap C (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := B) (M := A) (N := C)))

declarations.name: Rig.rigEtale_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCX.**  Rig-étaleness of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth` is stable under
composition in the sense of Formal Spaces Remark 0GBK: if `f : B →+* A` and `g : C →+* B` are
continuous rig-étale homomorphisms of Noetherian adic topological rings, then so is `f ∘ g`.

Condition (6) of Stacks 0GBW for the composite is
`Rig.finiteTypeAdicAlgebraForEveryIdeal_comp`.  For rig-étaleness over an ideal of definition
`I ⊆ C`, Stacks 0GCU moves both hypotheses onto `I` and onto `I B`, Stacks 0ALM presents `A`
over `(C, I)` by combining the two presentations, and the two exactness statements of its
six-term sequence at the middle complex `NL^∧_{A/C}` multiply the two annihilating ideals of
condition (3) of Stacks 0AJU.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigEtale_comp
    {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C] [IsLinearTopology C C]
    [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A) (hB : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsAdic C)
    (f : B →+* A) (g : C →+* B) (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g)
    (hPf : RingHom.IsRigEtale f) (hPg : RingHom.IsRigEtale g) :
    RingHom.IsRigEtale (f.comp g)

declarations.name: Rig.rigEtale_hasNoetherianCancellationProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GCY.**  Rig-étaleness on arrows of `WAdm^Noeth` has the
cancellation property of Formal Spaces Remark 0GBP: for `f : B →+* A` and `g : C →+* B`
continuous homomorphisms of Noetherian adic topological rings, rig-étaleness of `g` and of
`f ∘ g` implies rig-étaleness of `f`.

Unlike the base-change bundle of Tag 0GCL and the composition bundle of Tag 0GBK, the
cancellation predicate `TopologicalRing.HasNoetherianCancellationProperty` carries no locality
field, so this bundle is exactly what Remark 0GBP defines and exactly what 0GCY asserts; the
tag therefore sits on it.  Its content is `Rig.rigEtale_cancel`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GCZ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S`. The following are equivalent:

1. `f` is rig-étale (Definition 0AQM);
2. for every commutative square with `U`, `V` affine formal algebraic spaces and `U ⟶ X`,
   `V ⟶ Y` representable by algebraic spaces and étale, the morphism `U ⟶ V` corresponds to a
   rig-étale map in `WAdm^{Noeth}`;
3. there exist a covering `{Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM and for each `j` a covering
   `{Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ ×_Y X}` as in Definition 0AIM such that each `Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ` corresponds to a
   rig-étale map in `WAdm^{Noeth}`;
4. there exist a covering `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` as in Definition 0AIM and for each `i` a factorization
   `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Y` where `Yᵢ` is an affine formal algebraic space, `Yᵢ ⟶ Y` is representable by
   algebraic spaces and étale, and `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ` corresponds to a rig-étale map in
   `WAdm^{Noeth}`;
5. for every commutative square as in (2), every presentation of `U ⟶ V` by Noetherian adic rings
   is rig-étale.

Conditions (1) to (4) are the source's. In (2) the charts `U` and `V` are formal spectra of
Noetherian adic rings and `U ⟶ V` is the formal spectrum of a rig-étale homomorphism. Condition
(5) is the library's reading of Definition 0AQM, the form condition (2) takes in
`isRigEtale_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`; it is recorded so that this statement contains that
one. Conditions (2) and (5) agree by `correspondsToRigEtaleMapOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram_iff`,
which uses Stacks 0AKX, and the remaining implications are those of
`isRigEtale_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigEtale B S hS f,
        CorrespondsToRigEtaleMapOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS f,
        CorrespondsToRigEtaleMapAfterTargetCover B S hS f,
        CorrespondsToRigEtaleMapAfterSourceCover B S hS f,
        HasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS IsNoetherianAdic IsRigEtaleHom f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_of_isRigEtale
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0GD0.** A rig-étale morphism of formal algebraic spaces is rig-smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_of_isRigEtale (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S`. If `f` is rig-étale and `g` is adic, then the base change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is
rig-étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_pullback_snd_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f) (hg : IsAdicMorphism B S hS g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_pullback_snd_of_isAdicMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD1.** The base change of a rig-étale morphism of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S` by an adic morphism is rig-étale: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is rig-étale and
`g : Z ⟶ Y` is adic, then `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is rig-étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_pullback_snd_of_isAdicMorphism (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hcond : TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian.{u}
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        Rig.RigEtaleCondition φ))
    (hiso : PropertyIsInvariantUnderTargetIso.{u}
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    (h31 : SourceCoverImpliesEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
      (fun R ↦ TopologicalRing.IsAdic R ∧ IsNoetherianRing R)
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hcover : HasBaseChangeCoverOverPullbackSnd B S hS f g)
    (_hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (_hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (_hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f)
    (hg : IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramNoetherian B S hS g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: granting the locality of the cohomology-annihilation half of rig-étaleness, which is the hypothesis hcond and the only input of Stacks 0AQL, together with the three inputs of Remark 0GBG that the library leaves open: the covering of X ×_Y Z by fibre products of charts of Stacks 0GBD and 0AN0 (hcover), the implication (3) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0ANG (h31), and the invariance of rig-étaleness under isomorphism of targets implied by Stacks 0ANI (hiso)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` and `g` are rig-étale, then so is `g ∘ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z) (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f)
    (hg : IsRigEtale B S hS g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `g ∘ f` and `g` are rig-étale, then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z) (hfg : IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hg : IsRigEtale B S hS g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD3.** Rig-étaleness of morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S` cancels on the right: if `g ∘ f` and `g` are rig-étale, for `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`g : Y ⟶ Z`, then `f` is rig-étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_of_comp (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hcond : TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian.{u}
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        Rig.RigEtaleCondition φ))
    (htransfer : TransfersCancellationOnAffineEtaleDiagrams B S hS)
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (_hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (_hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (_hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hfg : IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hg : IsRigEtale B S hS g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS f
declarations.comment: granting the locality of the cohomology-annihilation half of rig-étaleness, which is the hypothesis hcond and the only input of Stacks 0AQL, and the transfer to formal algebraic spaces of Remark 0GBP, which is the hypothesis htransfer

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD4.** For a closed immersion `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian formal algebraic
spaces over `S`, rig-smoothness of `f` (Definition 0GCP), rig-étaleness of `f`
(Definition 0AQM), and the condition that on every affine representable étale chart `V ⟶ Y` of
the target the fibre product `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` be given by a surjection of `WAdm^{Noeth}` whose
kernel `J` has `J / J²` annihilated by an ideal of definition of the source, are all equivalent.

The implication (2) ⟹ (1) is Stacks 0GD0.  The implications (1) ⟹ (3) and (3) ⟹ (2) rest on
the computation of the completed naive cotangent complex of a surjection, for which both
rigidity notions reduce to the annihilation of the conormal module.  The hypotheses `hAQI` and
`hGCZ` carry Stacks 0AQI — that the fibre product chart map is a surjection which is adic of
topologically finite type — and Stacks 0GCZ in the form in which the source's proof uses it,
that rig-étaleness need only be checked on the ring maps appearing in (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (_hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f)
    (hAQI : HasAdicQuotientOnPullbackCharts B S hS f)
    (hGCZ : HasRigEtaleOnPullbackCharts B S hS f → IsRigEtale B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigSmooth B S hS f, IsRigEtale B S hS f,
        HasAnnihilatedConormalOnPullbackCharts B S hS f]
declarations.comment: the full equivalence of the three conditions, with Stacks 0AQI (the fibre product chart map being a surjection of WAdm^Noeth which is adic of topologically finite type) and Stacks 0GCZ (rig-étaleness need only be checked on the ring maps appearing in condition (3)) carried as the hypotheses `hAQI` and `hGCZ`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD4.** For a closed immersion `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian formal algebraic
spaces over `S`, rig-smoothness of `f` (Definition 0GCP), rig-étaleness of `f`
(Definition 0AQM), and the condition that on every affine representable étale chart `V ⟶ Y` of
the target the fibre product `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` be given by a surjection of `WAdm^{Noeth}` whose
kernel `J` has `J / J²` annihilated by an ideal of definition of the source, are all equivalent.

The implication (2) ⟹ (1) is Stacks 0GD0. The implication (1) ⟹ (3) uses the surjectivity of
the fibre product chart homomorphism, `surjective_of_isClosedImmersion_chart`, and the
computation of the completed naive cotangent complex of a surjection. The implication
(3) ⟹ (2) is `isRigEtale_of_hasAnnihilatedConormalOnPullbackCharts`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (_hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigSmooth B S hS f, IsRigEtale B S hS f,
        HasAnnihilatedConormalOnPullbackCharts B S hS f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_iff_hasAnnihilatedKerPowOnPullbackCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD5**, both directions, carrying three hypotheses. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a closed
immersion of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S`. Then `f` is rig-surjective
exactly when on every affine representable étale chart `V ⟶ Y` of the target the fibre product
`X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is given by a surjection of `WAdm^{Noeth}` some ideal of definition of whose
source annihilates a positive power of its kernel.

The hypothesis `hAQI` is Stacks 0AQI in the chart form of Stacks 0GD4, `hAQV` is the
equivalence of rig-surjectivity of `f` with rig-surjectivity of its chart base changes
(Stacks 0AQS forwards, Stacks 0AQV backwards), and `hAR0` is Stacks 0AR0 for the chart maps,
read through the full faithfulness of `Spf`. The passage from the factorisation criterion to
the annihilation condition is the algebraic equivalence proved here, which uses
**Stacks 00PH**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_iff_hasAnnihilatedKerPowOnPullbackCharts {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (_hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (_hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (_hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f)
    (hAQI : HasAdicQuotientOnPullbackCharts B S hS f)
    (hAQV : IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ HasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts B S hS f)
    (hAR0 : HasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts B S hS f ↔
      HasDvrFactorizationOnPullbackCharts B S hS f) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ HasAnnihilatedKerPowOnPullbackCharts B S hS f
declarations.comment: both directions, carrying three hypotheses: Stacks 0AQI in the chart form of Stacks 0GD4, that the chart homomorphism is a surjection of WAdm^Noeth which is adic of topologically finite type (hAQI); the equivalence of rig-surjectivity of f with rig-surjectivity of its chart base changes, which is Stacks 0AQS forwards and Stacks 0AQV backwards (hAQV); and Stacks 0AR0 for the chart maps, read through the full faithfulness of Spf of Stacks 0AN0, identifying rig-surjectivity of a chart map with the factorisation of its adic discrete valuation points (hAR0). The algebraic equivalence joining the factorisation criterion to the annihilation condition, which is what the source's two implications come down to and which uses Stacks 00PH, is proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_iff_hasAnnihilatedKerPow_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD5.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. Then `f` is rig-surjective if and only if for every affine formal
algebraic space `V` and every morphism `V ⟶ Y` which is representable by algebraic spaces and
étale, the base change `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` corresponds to a surjection `B → A` of `WAdm^{Noeth}`
whose kernel `J` satisfies `I J ^ n = 0` for some ideal of definition `I` of `B` and some
`n ≥ 1`.

Condition (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAnnihilatedKerPowOnPullbackCharts`, asked
of every presentation of the base change by Noetherian rings with adic topologies. The
equivalence of condition (2) with rig-surjectivity of every chart map is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAnnihilatedKerPow_iff_hasRigSurjective_of_isClosedImmersion`
(Stacks 0AQI, 0AR0 and 00PH). Rig-surjectivity of `f` gives that of the chart maps by
Stacks 0AQS, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts_of_isRigSurjective`,
and conversely by Stacks 0AQV,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_of_hasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_iff_hasAnnihilatedKerPow_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ HasAnnihilatedKerPowOnPullbackCharts B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_and_isRigSurjective_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD6.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. Then the following are equivalent: (1) `f` is rig-smooth and
rig-surjective; (2) `f` is rig-étale and rig-surjective; (3) on every affine representable étale
chart `V ⟶ Y` of the target the fibre product `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is given by a surjection of
`WAdm^{Noeth}` whose kernel is annihilated by some ideal of definition of the source.

The equivalence of the two rigidity notions is Stacks 0GD4, the identification of
rig-surjectivity with the annihilation of a power of the kernel is Stacks 0GD5, and the
passage from "a power of `J` is annihilated and `J / J ^ 2` is annihilated" to "`J` is
annihilated" is `Rig.exists_idealOfDefinition_mul_eq_bot`, the ring-theoretic step whose proof
the source omits.

The hypotheses `hAQI`, `hGCZ`, `hAQV` and `hAR0` are precisely the ones the library's
Stacks 0GD4 and Stacks 0GD5 carry: Stacks 0AQI in chart form, Stacks 0GCZ as the proof of
Stacks 0GD4 uses it, the equivalence of rig-surjectivity of `f` with rig-surjectivity of its
chart base changes (Stacks 0AQS forwards, Stacks 0AQV backwards), and Stacks 0AR0 for the chart
maps read through Stacks 0AN0.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_and_isRigSurjective_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f)
    (hAQI : HasAdicQuotientOnPullbackCharts B S hS f)
    (hGCZ : HasRigEtaleOnPullbackCharts B S hS f → IsRigEtale B S hS f)
    (hAQV : IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ HasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts B S hS f)
    (hAR0 : HasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts B S hS f ↔
      HasDvrFactorizationOnPullbackCharts B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigSmooth B S hS f ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS f,
        IsRigEtale B S hS f ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS f,
        HasAnnihilatedKerOnPullbackCharts B S hS f]
declarations.comment: all three conditions and every implication between them, carrying exactly the four hypotheses which this library's Stacks 0GD4 and Stacks 0GD5 already carry and nothing more: Stacks 0AQI in the chart form of Stacks 0GD4, that the chart homomorphism is a surjection of WAdm^Noeth which is adic of topologically finite type (hAQI), whose library carrier covers only the countably indexed case, which the Noetherian charts here are not; Stacks 0GCZ read as the proof of Stacks 0GD4 reads it, that rig-etaleness of f need only be checked on the ring maps appearing in condition (3) (hGCZ); the equivalence of rig-surjectivity of f with rig-surjectivity of its chart base changes, Stacks 0AQS forwards and Stacks 0AQV backwards (hAQV), undischargeable because Tag 0AJG, IsEtaleULift implies IsLocallyOfFiniteTypeULift, has no carrier in this library; and Stacks 0AR0 for the chart maps read through the full faithfulness of Spf of Stacks 0AN0 (hAR0), undischargeable because its substantial direction rests on the EXISTENCE half of Tag 0AQD, whose carriers supply uniqueness only. No carried hypothesis is an implication of this lemma. The combination the source calls trivial is proved, including the ring-theoretic observation the source omits: I * J ^ n = 0 together with I * J <= J ^ 2 forces I ^ n * J = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_and_isRigSurjective_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD6.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. Then the following are equivalent: (1) `f` is rig-smooth and
rig-surjective; (2) `f` is rig-étale and rig-surjective; (3) on every affine representable étale
chart `V ⟶ Y` of the target the fibre product `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is given by a surjection of
`WAdm^{Noeth}` whose kernel is annihilated by some ideal of definition of the source.

The equivalence of the two rigidity notions with the annihilation of the conormal module
`J / J ^ 2` is Stacks 0GD4, the identification of rig-surjectivity with the annihilation of a
power of the kernel is Stacks 0GD5, and the passage from "a power of `J` is annihilated and
`J / J ^ 2` is annihilated" to "`J` is annihilated" is `Rig.exists_idealOfDefinition_mul_eq_bot`,
applied chart by chart in `hasAnnihilatedKer_of_hasAnnihilatedConormal_of_hasAnnihilatedKerPow`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_and_isRigSurjective_tfae_of_isClosedImmersion' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigSmooth B S hS f ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS f,
        IsRigEtale B S hS f ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS f,
        HasAnnihilatedKerOnPullbackCharts B S hS f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_flat_isClosedImmersion_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD8.** Let `A` be a complete discrete valuation ring and let `X` be a locally
Noetherian formal algebraic space over `S` with a structure morphism `p : X ⟶ Spf A`. Then
there is a closed immersion `ι : X' ⟶ X` of formal algebraic spaces with `X'` locally
Noetherian and flat over `A` such that every morphism `q : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` a locally
Noetherian formal algebraic space flat over `A` factors through `ι`.

The atlas of `X` supplied by the locally Noetherian hypothesis is turned into a family of
affine flat parts by `hpart`; those are mutually compatible, since the universal property of
one of them applies to any Noetherian affine formal algebraic space flat over `A` mapping to
the corresponding chart, so they glue by `hdesc` to a closed immersion `ι : X' ⟶ X` whose
sources form an affine étale covering of `X'`. That covering exhibits `X'` as locally
Noetherian, and reading condition (4) of Stacks 0GCD on it gives flatness of `X'` over `A`.
For the universal property, `hrefine` covers a test object `Y` by Noetherian affine formal
algebraic spaces which are flat over `A` and map to the charts of `X`; each of them factors
through the corresponding flat part and hence through `X'`, and `hfac` glues those
factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flat_isClosedImmersion_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (_hAadic : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (_hAcomplete : IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)
    (hSpfAaffine : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D))
    (hSpfA : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D))
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (p : X ⟶ formalSpectrum D)
    (hpart : HasAffineFlatParts B S hS D p)
    (hdesc : FlatPartsDescend B S hS D p)
    (hfac : FactorizationDescendsAlongAffineEtaleCover B S hS)
    (hrefine : HasFlatAffineCoverOfFlat B S hS D p)
    (hloc : FlatnessLocalityInputs B S hS D) :
    ∃ (X' : FppfSheaf B S hS) (ι : X' ⟶ X),
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS ι ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X' ∧
        IsFlat B S hS (ι ≫ p) ∧
        ∀ (Y : FppfSheaf B S hS) (q : Y ⟶ X), IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y →
          IsFlat B S hS (q ≫ p) → ∃ r : Y ⟶ X', r ≫ ι = q
declarations.comment: both halves of the conclusion — the closed immersion with `X'` flat over `A`, and the factorization of every locally Noetherian `Y ⟶ X` flat over `A` through it — with the five inputs this library does not carry as named hypotheses. `hpart` is the affine half as a statement about formal spectra: its ring-theoretic content, that the quotient of the presenting ring by its `A`-torsion is flat over `A` and receives every homomorphism into a flat `A`-algebra, is proved here as `Algebra.exists_flat_quotient_of_isDiscreteValuationRing`, while its geometric realization needs the adic Noetherian quotient topology, a `QuotientSystem` for the quotient, Stacks 0ANP for a closed immersion out of a surjective presenting homomorphism and Stacks 0GCD for flatness out of a flat one, none of which this library carries. `hdesc` is the gluing step, Stacks 02WW with Bootstrap 046J and Spaces 03KD, carried in this library only as the quotient sheaf of a relation with the étale-equivalence-relation hypothesis undischarged, 046J only conditionally on Stacks 0AMP and Stacks 0421, and 03KD only for presheaves of `Type u`. `hfac` is the descent of a factorization through a closed immersion along an affine étale covering, Stacks 03KD with the monomorphism property of Stacks 0AQB. `hrefine` is the covering of a test object by the charts of the fibre products with the atlas, which is Stacks 0AJ3, the refinement of Stacks 0AJ2, Stacks 0AQ8 and Stacks 0GCG. `hloc` bundles the four hypotheses of `isFlat_tfae`, this library's Stacks 0GCD, namely Stacks 0AJ3, the refinement of Stacks 0AJ2 and the locality axioms of Stacks 0GC9 read through Stacks 0AN8 and Stacks 0AN9. Completeness of `A` is carried for faithfulness; the source's argument uses only that `A` is a discrete valuation ring, and the ring-theoretic half proved here needs only that it is a Bézout domain

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_flatPart_of_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD8.** Let `A` be a complete discrete valuation ring, carrying its `𝔪`-adic
topology, and let `X` be a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space over `S` with a structure
morphism `p : X ⟶ Spf A`. Then there is a closed immersion `ι : X' ⟶ X` of formal algebraic
spaces with `X'` locally Noetherian and flat over `A` such that every morphism `q : Y ⟶ X` with
`Y` a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space flat over `A` factors through `ι`.

The members `Uᵢ` of a Noetherian atlas of `X` carry affine flat parts `Zᵢ ⟶ Uᵢ`, the formal
spectra of the quotients by the `A`-torsion of their presenting rings; these glue to `ι`, the
`Zᵢ` forming an atlas of `X'`, on which flatness of `X'` over `A` is read off by Remark 0ANI.
A test object `Y` is covered by Noetherian affine charts flat over `A` mapping to the `Uᵢ`;
each factors through the corresponding `Zᵢ`, and the factorizations descend along the
covering because `ι` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flatPart_of_isLocallyNoetherian_of_isAdicComplete
    [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (hA : _root_.IsAdic (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))
    (hAc : IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (p : X ⟶ formalSpectrum D) :
    ∃ (X' : FppfSheaf B S hS) (ι : X' ⟶ X),
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS ι ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X' ∧
        IsFlat B S hS (ι ≫ p) ∧
        ∀ (Y : FppfSheaf B S hS) (q : Y ⟶ X), IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y →
          IsFlat B S hS (q ≫ p) → ∃ r : Y ⟶ X', r ≫ ι = q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isIso_or_isInitial_flatPart_of_isRigEtale_of_isRigSurjective_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GD9.** Let `A` be a complete discrete valuation ring, carrying its `𝔪`-adic
topology, let `X` be a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space over `S` with a structure
morphism `p : X ⟶ Spf A` locally of finite type, and let `ι : X' ⟶ X` be as in Stacks 0GD8: a
closed immersion with `X'` flat over `A` through which every morphism `Y ⟶ X` from a locally
Noetherian formal algebraic space flat over `A` factors. If the relative diagonal
`X ⟶ X ×_{Spf A} X` is rig-étale and rig-surjective, then `X' = Spf A` or `X' = ∅`: the
structure morphism `ι ≫ p` of `X'` is an isomorphism, or `X'` is initial.

`X'` is locally Noetherian, being locally of finite type over `X` (Stacks 0AQ7). The relative
diagonal of `ι ≫ p` is the base change of that of `p` along the adic comparison
`X' ×_{Spf A} X' ⟶ X ×_{Spf A} X`, `ι` being a monomorphism, so it is rig-étale (Stacks 0GD1) and
rig-surjective (Stacks 0AQS), and
`isIso_or_isInitial_of_isFlat_of_isRigEtale_of_isRigSurjective_diagonal` applies to `ι ≫ p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_or_isInitial_flatPart_of_isRigEtale_of_isRigSurjective_diagonal
    [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (hAadic : _root_.IsAdic (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))
    (hAc : IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)
    {X X' : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (p : X ⟶ formalSpectrum D)
    (hp : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p) (ι : X' ⟶ X) (hιclosed : IsClosedImmersion B S hS ι)
    (hX'flat : IsFlat B S hS (ι ≫ p))
    (_hX'univ : ∀ (Y : FppfSheaf B S hS) (q : Y ⟶ X), IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y →
      IsFlat B S hS (q ≫ p) → ∃ r : Y ⟶ X', r ≫ ι = q)
    (hdiagE : IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.diagonal p))
    (hdiagS : IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal p)) :
    IsIso (ι ≫ p) ∨ Nonempty (IsInitial X')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints_of_rigEtaleDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDA**, the substantial direction, carrying five hypotheses. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` locally Noetherian, `f` locally of finite
type and `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` rig-étale and rig-surjective. If `f` is rig-surjective then every
adic morphism `Spf R ⟶ Y`, with `R` a complete discrete valuation ring, lifts to `X` over `R`
itself.

Rig-surjectivity provides an extension `R ⊂ R'` of complete discrete valuation rings and a
lift `Spf R' ⟶ X` of the point `p`. In the fibre product `W = Spf R ×_Y X` the projection
`p₁ : W ⟶ Spf R` is locally of finite type by Stacks 0AQ5 and `W` is locally Noetherian by
`h0AQ8`, which is Stacks 0AQ8; the relative diagonal `Δ_{p₁}` is a base change of `Δ_f` along
the comparison morphism `W ×_{Spf R} W ⟶ X ×_Y X`, which is a base change of `p` and hence
representable by algebraic spaces, so `Δ_{p₁}` is rig-étale by `h0GD1`, which is Stacks 0GD1,
and rig-surjective by Stacks 0AQS. Hence `h0GD9`, which is Stacks 0GD9 together with Stacks
0GD8, gives the flat part `ι : W' ⟶ W` of `W` over `R` and the dichotomy. The lift
`Spf R' ⟶ W` is flat over `R` by `hextFlat`, which is Stacks 0GCD, and `Spf R'` is locally
Noetherian by `hSpfNoeth`, which is Stacks 0AKY, so the lift factors through `W'` and the
second alternative of the dichotomy is impossible. Therefore `ι ≫ p₁` is an isomorphism and
`inv (ι ≫ p₁) ≫ ι ≫ p₂` is the factorisation wanted.

Local Noetherianity of `Y` is a hypothesis of Stacks 0GDA and is kept as `_hY`; the proof does
not use it, obtaining local Noetherianity of `X ×_Y X` from that of `X` instead.
declarations.statement:
theorem factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints_of_rigEtaleDiagonal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (_hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hdiagEtale : IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hdiagSurj : IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (h0AQ8 : FibreProductIsLocallyNoetherian B S hS)
    (h0GD1 : RigEtaleIsStableUnderRepresentableBaseChange B S hS)
    (hSpfNoeth : FormalSpectrumOfCompleteDvrIsLocallyNoetherian B S hS)
    (hextFlat : FormalSpectrumMapOfDvrExtensionIsFlat B S hS)
    (h0GD9 : FlatPartOfRigEtaleDiagonalIsBaseOrPointless B S hS)
    (hrig : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) :
    FactorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints B S hS f
declarations.comment: the complete discrete valuation ring lifting criterion is necessary for rig-surjectivity, granting Stacks 0AQ8, Stacks 0GD1 read through Stacks 0AQ3, Stacks 0AKY for the formal spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring, Stacks 0GCD for an extension of such rings, and Stacks 0GD9 with Stacks 0GD8; see the module docstring for each

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_iff_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDA**, carrying five hypotheses. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` and `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` locally of finite type and
the relative diagonal `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` rig-étale and rig-surjective. Then `f` is
rig-surjective if and only if every adic morphism `Spf R ⟶ Y`, with `R` a complete discrete
valuation ring, lifts to a morphism `Spf R ⟶ X`.

The direction the source calls trivial is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_of_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints`, which needs
none of the hypotheses. The five carried hypotheses are used by the other direction only; see
the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_iff_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints_of_diagonal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hdiagEtale : IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hdiagSurj : IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (h0AQ8 : FibreProductIsLocallyNoetherian B S hS)
    (h0GD1 : RigEtaleIsStableUnderRepresentableBaseChange B S hS)
    (hSpfNoeth : FormalSpectrumOfCompleteDvrIsLocallyNoetherian B S hS)
    (hextFlat : FormalSpectrumMapOfDvrExtensionIsFlat B S hS)
    (h0GD9 : FlatPartOfRigEtaleDiagonalIsBaseOrPointless B S hS) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ FactorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints B S hS f
declarations.comment: granting Stacks 0AQ8, Stacks 0GD1 read through Stacks 0AQ3, Stacks 0AKY for the formal spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring, Stacks 0GCD for an extension of such rings, and Stacks 0GD9 with Stacks 0GD8, all five used by the forward implication only; see the module docstring for each

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_iff_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints_of_rigEtale_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDA.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` with `X`
and `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` locally of finite type, and the relative diagonal
`Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` rig-étale and rig-surjective. Then `f` is rig-surjective if and only if
every adic morphism `Spf R ⟶ Y`, with `R` a complete discrete valuation ring, lifts to a
morphism `Spf R ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_iff_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints_of_rigEtale_diagonal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hdiagEtale : IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hdiagSurj : IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ FactorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDC.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `T`
be a set of points of `X`. If `f` is a closed immersion, then the induced morphism of
completions `X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is a closed immersion of formal algebraic spaces: it is
representable by algebraic spaces and each of its base changes along a scheme-valued point of
its target is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isProper_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `T` be a set of points
of `X`. If `f` is proper, then the induced morphism of completions
`X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsProper B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompact_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDE.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `T`
be a set of points of `X`. If `f` is quasi-compact, then the induced morphism of completions
`f_{/T} : X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is quasi-compact: it is representable by algebraic spaces
and each of its base changes along a scheme-valued point of its target is a quasi-compact
morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    ∃ hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.quasiCompactPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS)
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T).hom hrep
declarations.comment: quasi-compactness of `f_{/T}` in the form of Bootstrap, Definition 03XZ: `f_{/T}` is representable by algebraic spaces and each of its base changes along a scheme-valued point of its target is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces. For a morphism representable by algebraic spaces this is the quasi-compactness of Stacks 0AJC by Stacks 0AM2, whose proof needs the agreement of the two notions of a quasi-compact space on an algebraic space, `QuasiCompactSpaceAgreesOnAlgebraicSpaces`, which this library does not carry; `isQuasiCompact_completionSheafMap_of_agreesOnAlgebraicSpaces` is the conclusion in the form of Stacks 0AJC granted that agreement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_completionSheafPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDF.** The completion of a fibre product is the fibre product of the
completions: for morphisms `f : X' ⟶ X` and `g : Y ⟶ X` of presheaves on the big fppf site of
`S` and a set `T` of points of `X`, the square formed by `(X' ×_X Y)_{/T''}`, the two
completions `X'_{/T'}` and `Y_{/T₂}` and `X_{/T}` is cartesian, so that
`X'_{/T'} ×_{X_{/T}} Y_{/T₂} = (X' ×_X Y)_{/T''}` as subobjects of the ambient sheaf of
`X' ×_X Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_completionSheafPullback (f : X' ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) :
    IsPullback (completionSheafPullbackFst B S hS f g T)
      (completionSheafPullbackSnd B S hS f g T)
      (completionSheafMap B S hS f T) (completionSheafMap B S hS g T)
declarations.comment: fibre product of completions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSheafDiagonal_comp_completionSheafInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDF.** The diagonal of the completed morphism is the diagonal of the original
morphism, read inside the ambient sheaf of `X' ×_X X'`: this is the equality
`Δ_{f_{/T}} = (Δ_f)_{/T''}` of morphisms of subobjects of `X' ×_X X'`, the inclusion of a
completion into the ambient sheaf being a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem completionSheafDiagonal_comp_completionSheafInclusion (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) :
    completionSheafDiagonal B S hS f T ≫
        completionSheafInclusion B S hS (pullback f f) (pullbackPoints B S hS f f T) =
      completionSheafInclusion B S hS X' (pointsMap B S hS X' f ⁻¹' T) ≫
        sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (pullback.diagonal f)
declarations.comment: diagonals agree over the fibre product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSheafDiagonal_eq_completionSheafMap_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDF.** The diagonal of the completed morphism is the completion of the diagonal:
`Δ_{f_{/T}} = (Δ_f)_{/T''}` as morphisms `X'_{/T'} ⟶ (X' ×_X X')_{/T''}`. The `eqToHom`
transports the source of `(Δ_f)_{/T''}`, the completion of `X'` along the inverse image of
`T''` under the diagonal, to the completion of `X'` along `T'`; the two sets of points are
equal by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap_diagonal_preimage_pullbackPoints`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completionSheafDiagonal_eq_completionSheafMap_diagonal (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) :
    completionSheafDiagonal B S hS f T =
      eqToHom (congrArg (completionSheaf B S hS X')
          (pointsMap_diagonal_preimage_pullbackPoints B S hS f T).symm) ≫
        completionSheafMap B S hS (pullback.diagonal f) (pullbackPoints B S hS f f T)
declarations.comment: equality of diagonals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSeparatedMorphism_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDG, the separatedness clause.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` and let `T` be a set of points of `X`. If `f` is separated, then the induced
morphism of completions `f_{/T} : X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is separated: its relative diagonal
is the completion of the relative diagonal of `f`, which is a closed immersion by Stacks
0GDC.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedMorphism_completionSheafMap
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsSeparatedMorphism B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)
declarations.comment: separated: the completion of a separated morphism of algebraic spaces along a set of points of its target is a separated morphism of formal algebraic spaces, separatedness of the completion read as the separatedness axiom of Stacks 0ARN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiSeparatedMorphism_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDG, the quasi-separatedness clause.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` and let `T` be a set of points of `X`. If `f` is quasi-separated, then the
induced morphism of completions `f_{/T} : X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` has quasi-compact relative
diagonal: that relative diagonal is the completion of the relative diagonal of `f`, which is
quasi-compact by Stacks 0GDE.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedMorphism_completionSheafMap
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiSeparatedMorphism B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)
declarations.comment: quasi-separated: the completion of a quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces along a set of points of its target has quasi-compact relative diagonal. Quasi-compactness of the diagonal is read as `IsQuasiSeparatedMorphism`, that is, as `Space.IsQuasiCompactULift`: every base change of the diagonal along a morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic space has quasi-compact source. The implementation notes of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.SeparatedMorphism` record that condition as a priori stronger than the source's quasi-compactness of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces, so the conclusion delivered is a priori stronger than the source's; the hypothesis is the source's quasi-separatedness of Stacks 03HL, part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDH.** In the situation of Stacks 0GDB, if `X` is locally Noetherian, `f` is
locally of finite type and `U' → U` is smooth, then `f_{/T}` is rig-smooth.

Granted the reduction to the affine case, the lemma is part (1) of Stacks 0GAK applied to the
affine data that reduction produces, exactly as in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_completionSheafMap {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hX : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hf : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hsm : Space.IsSmooth B S hS (Space.openComplementRestriction B S hS f T))
    (hred : ChartSquareReducesToSmoothAwayFrom B S hS f T) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)
declarations.comment: the affine case, which is part (1) of Stacks 0GAK (`Rig.isRigSmooth_adicCompletionObj_of_smoothAwayFrom`), applied through the reduction to the affine case carried as the hypothesis `hred`: granted the three hypotheses of the lemma it produces, for each affine representable étale square over `f_{/T}`, the Noetherian ring `A₀`, the ideal `I₀` and the finite type `A₀`-algebra `C₀` smooth over `Spec A₀` minus `V(I₀)` of the source's proof, together with the comparison of rig-smoothness of `C₀` completed with rig-smoothness of the arrow of `WAdm^{Noeth}` presenting the square. The source assembles that reduction from Properties of Spaces, Lemma 03FX, the cartesian completion squares of Stacks 0APV, the identification of a chart of the completion with a formal spectrum in the proof of Stacks 0AQ1, and the étale locality of local finite type, of smoothness and of local Noetherianity, none of which this library carries in that combination

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_completionSheafMap_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDH.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`T ⊆ |X|` be closed, and let `U ⊆ X` be the open complement of `T` and `U' = f⁻¹U` (the
situation of Stacks 0GDB). If `X` is locally Noetherian, `f` is locally of finite type and
`U' → U` is smooth, then the completion `f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X_{/T}` is rig-smooth.

The proof is the source's: compatible étale atlases of `X` and `X'` by spectra of rings
(Properties of Spaces, Lemma 03FX; `exists_compatible_affineOver_atlases`), condition (4) of
Stacks 0GCQ for `f_{/T}` from them
(`correspondsToNoetherianMapAfterSourceCover_isRigSmoothArrow_completionSheafMap`: the reduction
to the affine case and the affine case by Stacks 0GAK and Stacks 0GAM), and the implication
(4) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0GCQ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_completionSheafMap_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T)
    (hXN : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hf : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hsm : Space.IsSmooth B S hS (Space.openComplementRestriction B S hS f T)) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_diagonal_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDI.** In the situation of Stacks 0GDB, let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a separated morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `T` be a closed set of points of `X`, and let the restriction
`U' ⟶ U` of `f` to the open complements of `T` and of `T' = |f|⁻¹ T` be a monomorphism. Then
the diagonal `Δ_{f_{/T}} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X'_{/T'} ×_{X_{/T}} X'_{/T'}` of the completed morphism
is rig-surjective.

By Stacks 0GDF it is the completion of `Δ_f : X' ⟶ X' ×_X X'` along the set of points over
`T`, up to isomorphisms; `Δ_f` is a closed immersion, hence proper, and is surjective over the
complement of `T`, so Stacks 0AQW applies. The source's hypotheses that `X` be locally
Noetherian and `f` locally of finite type are not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_diagonal_completionSheafMap {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T) (hf : Space.IsSeparated B S hS f)
    (hmono : Mono ((Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).fromPreimage f)) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFormalModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDK.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over
`S` is a *formal modification* when (1) `f` is proper, (2) `f` is rig-étale, (3) `f` is
rig-surjective, and (4) the relative diagonal `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` is rig-surjective. The
hypothesis that `X` and `Y` be locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces is recorded in the
first two fields, so the condition is stated for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves on the
big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: structure IsFormalModification {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.artinConditions_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDL.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`, and compare the conditions of Artin's Definition 1.7 of a formal
modification — (i) the Jacobian and the Cramer ideal of `f` each contain an ideal of definition
of `X`, (ii) the ideal of the relative diagonal `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` is annihilated by an ideal
of definition of `X ×_Y X`, (iii) every adic morphism `Spf R ⟶ Y` with `R` a complete discrete
valuation ring lifts to `X` — with those of Definition 0GDK:

* Ad (i): condition (i) holds if and only if `f` is rig-étale;
* Ad (ii): if `f` is rig-étale, then `Δ_f` is rig-étale, and condition (ii) holds if and only
  if `Δ_f` is rig-surjective;
* Ad (iii): if conditions (i) and (ii) hold, condition (iii) holds if and only if `f` is
  rig-surjective.

Conditions (i) and (ii) are read on the affine étale charts of `f` and of `X ×_Y X`, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasJacobianCramerIdealOfDefinition` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAnnihilatedKerOnPullbackCharts`.
declarations.statement:
theorem artinConditions_comparison {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f) :
    (HasJacobianCramerIdealOfDefinition B S hS f ↔ IsRigEtale B S hS f) ∧
      (IsRigEtale B S hS f →
        IsRigEtale B S hS (pullback.diagonal f) ∧
          (HasAnnihilatedKerOnPullbackCharts B S hS (pullback.diagonal f) ↔
            IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))) ∧
      (HasJacobianCramerIdealOfDefinition B S hS f →
        HasAnnihilatedKerOnPullbackCharts B S hS (pullback.diagonal f) →
          (FactorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints B S hS f ↔ IsRigSurjective B S hS f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalModification_of_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDL.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper rig-étale morphism of locally Noetherian
formal algebraic spaces over `S` whose relative diagonal `Δ_f : X ⟶ X ×_Y X` is rig-surjective.
If every adic morphism `Spf R ⟶ Y` with `R` a complete discrete valuation ring factors through
`f` over `R` itself, then `f` is a formal modification in the sense of Definition 0GDK: such a
factorisation is in particular one over the trivial extension of `R`, so `f` is
rig-surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalModification_of_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hproper : IsProper B S hS f) (hetale : IsRigEtale B S hS f)
    (hdiagSurj : IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hlift : FactorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints B S hS f) :
    IsFormalModification B S hS f
declarations.comment: the implication of Ad (iii) that needs no further input: Artin's condition (iii), a lift of every adic point over the complete discrete valuation ring itself, implies rig-surjectivity, which asks only for a lift over an extension of that ring. Together with the remaining conditions of Artin's Definition 1.7 in the translated form the remark gives them — properness, rig-étaleness for condition (i) by Ad (i), and rig-surjectivity of the relative diagonal for condition (ii) by Ad (ii) — this is the comparison with Definition 0GDK. Not covered: the converse implication of Ad (iii), which the remark obtains from Stacks 0GDA; the two implications of Ad (ii), which it obtains from Stacks 0GD1, Stacks 0GD3 and Stacks 0GD6; and Ad (i), whose equivalence of condition (i) with rig-étaleness is part (7) of Lemma 0AJU, that is Stacks 0AJY, and whose Cramer and Jacobian ideals of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces this library does not have

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalModification_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDM.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|`
be closed and let `U ⊆ X` be the open subspace with `|U| = |X| ∖ T`. If `X` is locally
Noetherian, `f` is proper and `U' = f⁻¹U ⟶ U` is an isomorphism, then
`f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X_{/T}` is a formal modification.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalModification_completionSheafMap {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXN : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) (hf : Space.IsProper B S hS f)
    (hfU : IsIso (pullback.snd f (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι)) :
    IsFormalModification B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalModification_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDN.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a formal modification of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S` and let `g : Z ⟶ Y` be an adic morphism, `Z` locally Noetherian.
Then the base change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` of `f` along `g` is a formal modification.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalModification_pullback_snd
    (hcond : TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian.{u}
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        Rig.RigEtaleCondition φ))
    (hiso : PropertyIsInvariantUnderTargetIso.{u}
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    (h31 : SourceCoverImpliesEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
      (fun R ↦ TopologicalRing.IsAdic R ∧ IsNoetherianRing R)
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    (hcover : ∀ {X₀ Y₀ Z₀ : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (g₀ : Z₀ ⟶ Y₀),
      HasBaseChangeCoverOverPullbackSnd B S hS f₀ g₀)
    (h0AQ8 : FibreProductIsLocallyNoetherian B S hS)
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hg : IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramNoetherian B S hS g)
    (hgft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hdiag : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hf : IsFormalModification B S hS f) :
    IsFormalModification B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: granting Stacks 0AQ8 as h0AQ8 and the four open inputs of Stacks 0GD1 as hcond, hiso, h31, hcover; see the module docstring for these and for hgft, hdiag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalModification_pullback_snd_of_isAdicMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDN.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S` which is a formal modification. Then for any adic morphism `g : Z ⟶ Y` of locally
Noetherian formal algebraic spaces, the base change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is a formal modification.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalModification_pullback_snd_of_isAdicMorphism {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hg : IsAdicMorphism B S hS g) (hf : IsFormalModification B S hS f) :
    IsFormalModification B S hS (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionModificationFunctorBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDQ.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|` be
closed with open complement `U`, and let `g : X₁ ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces with `X₁`
locally Noetherian; write `T₁ = |g|⁻¹T` and `U₁ = g⁻¹U`. Then the square
```
  C_{X,T}   ⟶  C_{X_{/T}}
     ↓              ↓
  C_{X₁,T₁} ⟶  C_{X_{1,/T_1}}
```
commutes, where the horizontal arrows are the functors of Stacks 0AR5, the left vertical arrow is
base change along `g` and the right vertical arrow is base change along `X_{1, /T_1} ⟶ X_{/T}`.
