Base change being defined by a universal property, commutativity is a natural isomorphism of the
two composite functors.

The proof is the source's: the completion functor `(h : Y ⟶ X) ↦ Y_{/T}` commutes with fibre
products.
declarations.statement:
def completionModificationFunctorBaseChangeIso {X₁ X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (g : X₁ ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hX₁sp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁) (hXsp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hX₁ : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X₁) (hX : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) :
    Space.finiteTypeBaseChangePointsFunctor hX₁sp hXsp g T ⋙
        completionModificationFunctor (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T)
          (hT.preimage (Space.continuous_pointsMap B S hS g)) hX₁sp hX₁ ≅
      completionModificationFunctor T hT hXsp hX ⋙
        rigEtaleOverCompletionPullback g T hT hX₁sp hXsp hX₁ hX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctorBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**The square of Stacks 0GDQ**, for the categories of Stacks 0AS2 and 0AR5 and conditional
on its right vertical arrow. Base change along `g : X₁ ⟶ X` on finite-type modifications
followed by the functor of Stacks 0AR5 for `X₁` and `T₁ = |g|⁻¹T` agrees with the functor of
Stacks 0AR5 for `X` and `T` followed by any functor restricting base change along
`X_{1, /T_1} ⟶ X_{/T}`.

The commutativity is the one the source's proof gives: the completion functor
`(h : Y ⟶ X) ↦ Y_{/T}` commutes with fibre products, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionBaseChangeIso` and, after restriction to the two
subcategories, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictedCompletionBaseChangeSquareIso`.
declarations.statement:
def completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctorBaseChangeIso
    {X₁ X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (g : X₁ ⟶ X)
    (hX₁sp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁) (hXsp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hX : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (h0AIZ : IsFormalAlgebraicSpaceCompletionSheaf B S hS X T)
    (hnoeth : IsLocallyNoetherianCompletionSheaf B S hS X T)
    (hred : ChartSquareReducesToIsEtaleOutsideModifications T)
    (hX₁ : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X₁)
    (h0AIZ₁ : IsFormalAlgebraicSpaceCompletionSheaf B S hS X₁
      (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T))
    (hnoeth₁ : IsLocallyNoetherianCompletionSheaf B S hS X₁
      (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T))
    (hred₁ : ChartSquareReducesToIsEtaleOutsideModifications
      (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T))
    {D : RigEtaleOverCompletion B S hS X T ⥤
      RigEtaleOverCompletion B S hS X₁ (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T)}
    (hD : D ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (fun W : Over (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X₁
            (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T)) =>
          IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS W.left ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS W.left ∧
            IsRigEtale B S hS W.hom) ≅
      ObjectProperty.ι (fun W : Over (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T) =>
          IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS W.left ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS W.left ∧
            IsRigEtale B S hS W.hom) ⋙
        Over.pullback (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS g T)) :
    Space.finiteTypeBaseChangePointsFunctor hX₁sp hXsp g T ⋙
        completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctor (Space.pointsMap B S hS X₁ g ⁻¹' T)
          (hT.preimage (Space.continuous_pointsMap B S hS g)) hX₁ h0AIZ₁ hnoeth₁ hred₁ ≅
      completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctor T hT hX h0AIZ hnoeth hred ⋙ D
declarations.comment: the commutativity of the square, as an isomorphism of the two composite functors rather than an equality, the two completion functors being defined by a sheafification; and conditional on the right vertical arrow, which is the hypothesis `D` together with `hD` saying that `D` restricts base change along `X_{1, /T_1} ⟶ X_{/T}`: the categories of Stacks 0AS2 are realized here as full subcategories of an over-category, and base change on them is not available in this repository without the fibre products of formal algebraic spaces that Stacks 0AS2 provides

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor_map_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDR.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, `T ⊆ |X|`
closed and `U ⊂ X` the open subspace with `|U| = |X| ∖ T`. Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type and an isomorphism over `U`, and let
`g : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism with `Y` a locally Noetherian algebraic space. Then completion along
`T` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor`, the completion of Section 0GDB used in
Stacks 0AR5) is a bijection from the morphisms `Y ⟶ X'` over `X` to the morphisms
`Y_{/T} ⟶ X'_{/T}` over `X_{/T}`.

Injectivity is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor_map_injective`; surjectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_completionOverFunctor_map_eq_of_affineCompletionLiftProperty`
applied to its affine case `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.affineCompletionLiftProperty`. The
consequence that the functor of Stacks 0AR5 is fully faithful is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.finiteTypeModificationCompletionFullyFaithful`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completionOverFunctor_map_bijective {X X' Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsClosed T) {f : X' ⟶ X}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hfU : IsIso (pullback.snd f (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι)) (g : Y ⟶ X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian V)) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun a : Over.mk g ⟶ Over.mk f => (completionOverFunctor B S hS T).map a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.finiteTypeModificationCompletionFullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDR, the consequence: the functor of Stacks 0AR5 is fully faithful.** For a
locally Noetherian algebraic space `X` and a closed `T ⊆ |X|`, completion along `T` is fully
faithful on the morphisms `X' ⟶ X` locally of finite type which are an isomorphism over the
open subspace with points `|X| ∖ T`. The functor of Stacks 0AR5,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctor`, is this functor with
its values regarded in the full subcategory of rig-étale morphisms with locally Noetherian
formal source (`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctor_comp_ι`).
Fullness and faithfulness are the two halves of the bijection
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor_map_bijective`, applied to a finite-type
modification `M` as the locally Noetherian source: `M` is locally Noetherian because it is
locally of finite type over `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteTypeModificationCompletionFullyFaithful
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXnoeth : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) :
    (finiteTypeModificationCompletion (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) T).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: in particular: the functor of Stacks 0AR5 is fully faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isProper_completion_iso_of_isFormalModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDU, existence.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let
`T ⊆ |X|` be closed, `U ⊂ X` the open subspace with `|U| = |X| ∖ T`, and let
`𝔣 : 𝔛' ⟶ X_{/T}` be a formal modification (Definition 0GDK). Then there is a proper morphism
`f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces which is an isomorphism over `U` and whose completion `f_{/T}`
is isomorphic to `𝔣` over `X_{/T}`.

By Stacks 0ARB (`isEquivalence_completionModificationFunctor`), `𝔣`, an object of the
right-hand category of Stacks 0AR5, is the completion of a finite-type modification `f`; by
Stacks 0ARX (`isProper_iff_isFormalModification_of_iso`) `f` is proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_completion_iso_of_isFormalModification
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hXsp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hX : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    {W : FppfSheaf B S hS} {𝔣 : W ⟶ Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T}
    (h𝔣 : IsFormalModification B S hS 𝔣) :
    ∃ (X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (f : X' ⟶ X),
      Space.IsProper B S hS f ∧ IsIso (pullback.snd f (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι) ∧
        Nonempty ((Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).obj (Over.mk f) ≅ Over.mk 𝔣)
declarations.comment: existence: a proper f : X' ⟶ X, isomorphism over U, with f_{/T} ≅ 𝔣 over X_{/T}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_completionOverFunctor_map_comp_eq_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDU, uniqueness.** In the situation of
`exists_isProper_completion_iso_of_isFormalModification`, let `f₁ : X₁ ⟶ X` and `f₂ : X₂ ⟶ X`
be proper morphisms of algebraic spaces which are isomorphisms over `U`, with isomorphisms
`e₁ : f₁_{/T} ≅ 𝔣` and `e₂ : f₂_{/T} ≅ 𝔣` over `X_{/T}`. Then there is exactly one morphism
`φ : X₁ ⟶ X₂` over `X` whose completion is compatible with `e₁` and `e₂`, and it is an
isomorphism. So `f` is unique up to unique isomorphism.

This is Stacks 0GDR (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor_map_bijective`), which holds
because a proper morphism is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_completionOverFunctor_map_comp_eq_of_isProper
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hXsp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hX : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    {W : FppfSheaf B S hS} (𝔣 : W ⟶ Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
    {X₁ X₂ : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX₁ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₁)
    (hX₂ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₂) {f₁ : X₁ ⟶ X} {f₂ : X₂ ⟶ X}
    (hf₁ : Space.IsProper B S hS f₁) (hf₂ : Space.IsProper B S hS f₂)
    (hU₁ : IsIso (pullback.snd f₁ (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι))
    (hU₂ : IsIso (pullback.snd f₂ (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι))
    (e₁ : (Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).obj (Over.mk f₁) ≅ Over.mk 𝔣)
    (e₂ : (Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).obj (Over.mk f₂) ≅ Over.mk 𝔣) :
    ∃! φ : Over.mk f₁ ⟶ Over.mk f₂,
      (Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).map φ ≫ e₂.hom = e₁.hom ∧ IsIso φ
declarations.comment: uniqueness: any two such proper f₁, f₂ are isomorphic over X by a unique isomorphism compatible with the identifications of f₁_{/T} and f₂_{/T} with 𝔣

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isProper_completionOverFunctor_iso_of_isFormalModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDV.** Let `f : 𝔛' ⟶ 𝔛` be a formal modification (Definition 0GDK) of locally
Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S`. Let `A` be an adic Noetherian topological ring and
let `g : Spf A ⟶ 𝔛` be an adic morphism, `Spf A` being a formal algebraic space over `S` through
the quotient system `D`. Then there are a proper morphism `p : X ⟶ Spec A` of algebraic spaces
and an isomorphism `Spf A ×_𝔛 𝔛' ≅ X_{/Z}` over `Spf A` of the base change of `f` with the formal
completion of `X` along its closed fibre `Z = X ×_{Spec A} Spf(A)_red`.

Algebraic spaces with no base are algebraic spaces over `Spec ℤ`, the terminal scheme, and the
base change, a formal algebraic space over `S`, is viewed over `Spec ℤ` by the change of base of
Stacks 04SG (`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.smallerBaseSheafFunctor`). The closed fibre is the
inverse image under `p` of the zero locus `V(I)` of an ideal of definition `I`, which is the
closed subset of `Spec A` underlying `Spf(A)_red`; the completion along it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor`, and the isomorphism is one over the completion of
`Spec A` along `V(I)`, which is `Spf A`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumCompletionIso`).
The statement holds for every ideal of definition `I`.

As in the source: the base change `Spf A ×_𝔛 𝔛' ⟶ Spf A` is a formal modification by Stacks
0GDN, and Theorem 0GDU applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isProper_completionOverFunctor_iso_of_isFormalModification
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic A) (hAB : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    {X' X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X' ⟶ X) (hf : IsFormalModification B S hS f)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (g : formalSpectrum D ⟶ X) (hg : IsAdicMorphism B S hS g) :
    ∃ (Y : (BigFppfOver B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ Y)
      (p : Y ⟶ yoneda.obj (specOverTerminal B hZ hAB)),
      Space.IsProper B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ p ∧
        Nonempty ((Space.completionOverFunctor B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ
            (zeroLocusPoints B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hAB (terminal.from _) I)).obj (Over.mk p) ≅
          Over.mk ((Ψ).map (pullback.snd f g) ≫
            (formalSpectrumCompletionIso B hZ S hS hAB hA I hI D).hom))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isCoveringSheaf_extension_of_isStandardAffineSheafOnSubcategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDW.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `𝒞` be a full subcategory of `Sch/S` satisfying
conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 0EUW and let `F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Set` satisfy conditions (a), (b) and
(c). Then the extension `F' = AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.extension` of `F` to `Sch/S` is
a sheaf for each of the five topologies — Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf.

This is the unconditional form of
`AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isCoveringSheaf_extension`, whose hypothesis `hstd` is
supplied by `AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isStandardAffineSheaf_extension`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringSheaf_extension_of_isStandardAffineSheafOnSubcategory (τ : CoveringTopology)
    (P : ObjectProperty (Over S)) (F : P.FullSubcategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1)))
    (hP1 : HasAffineOpens P) (hP2 : HasFinitePresentationAffines P)
    (haF : IsZariskiSheafOnSubcategory P F) (hbF : PreservesAffineLimitsOnSubcategory P F)
    (hcF : IsStandardAffineSheafOnSubcategory.{max w (u + 1), u, v} τ P F) :
    IsCoveringSheaf.{max w (u + 1), u, v} τ (extension P F)
declarations.comment:
the extension of a functor satisfying conditions (a), (b) and (c) from a full
subcategory satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of Tag 0EUW is a sheaf for every τ-covering of
Sch/S, for each of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isCoveringSheaf_of_isStandardAffineSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The reduction of Stacks 0GDW to the standard affine case.** A Zariski sheaf on `Sch/S`
which satisfies the sheaf condition for the standard `τ`-coverings of the affine objects lying
over an affine open of `S` satisfies the sheaf condition for every `τ`-covering.

This is the general case of the proof of the source. An object of `Sch/S` is covered by its
affine opens lying over affine opens of `S`; over each of them the given covering is refined by a
standard `τ`-covering, which produces a local section
(`AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.exists_section_of_isStandardAffineSheaf`); the local
sections agree on the pairwise intersections because both restrictions are computed by the given
family over the base change of the covering to the intersection, and they glue by the Zariski
sheaf condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringSheaf_of_isStandardAffineSheaf (τ : CoveringTopology)
    {G : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (haG : IsZariskiSheaf G)
    (hG : IsStandardAffineSheaf.{w, u, v} τ G) : IsCoveringSheaf.{w, u, v} τ G
declarations.comment:
the general case of the source's proof: a Zariski sheaf on Sch/S which is a sheaf
for the standard τ-coverings of the affine objects lying over an affine open of the base is a
sheaf for every τ-covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isCoveringSheaf_extension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GDW, the general case of the source's proof, at the extension.** Let `S` be a
scheme, let `𝒞` be a full subcategory of `Sch/S` satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks
0EUW and let `F : 𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Set` satisfy condition (a). Then the extension
`F' = AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.extension` of `F` to `Sch/S` satisfies the sheaf
condition for every `τ`-covering as soon as it satisfies the sheaf condition for the standard
`τ`-coverings of the affine objects of `Sch/S` lying over an affine open of `S`.

The source deduces the latter from its condition (c) by writing such an affine object as a
directed limit of affines of finite presentation over an affine open of `S` (Stacks 00QN),
descending the standard covering to a stage of that limit (Stacks 049N) and passing to the
filtered colimit; that deduction is not formalized here, so the restricted sheaf condition is
carried as the hypothesis `hstd`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoveringSheaf_extension (τ : CoveringTopology) (P : ObjectProperty (Over S))
    (F : P.FullSubcategoryᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1))) (hP1 : HasAffineOpens P)
    (hP2 : HasFinitePresentationAffines P) (haF : IsZariskiSheafOnSubcategory P F)
    (hstd : IsStandardAffineSheaf.{max w (u + 1), u, v} τ (extension P F)) :
    IsCoveringSheaf.{max w (u + 1), u, v} τ (extension P F)
declarations.comment:
the general case: the extension is a sheaf for every τ-covering once it is one for
the standard τ-coverings of the affine objects lying over an affine open of the base, which is
carried as a hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation_full_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GDX, clauses (1)–(4), with the two morphisms `Spec κ(s) ⟶ T` identified.**
Let `fX : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type with `S`
locally Noetherian, let `gY : Y ⟶ T` be locally of finite type with `T` of finite type over `ℤ`,
let `x ∈ X` lie over `s ∈ S` with `𝒪_{S, s}` a G-ring, and let
`σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` be a local homomorphism. Let `yσ` be a point of
`Y ×_T Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` lying over `y ∈ Y` and over the closed point, and let
`φ : 𝒪^∧_{X, x} ≅ 𝒪^∧_{Y ×_T Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}, yσ}` be an isomorphism of `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras.
Then there are an elementary étale neighbourhood `V` of `(S, s)`, a morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` carrying
the marked point to `t`, a point `yτ` of `Y ×_{T, τ} V` over `y` and over the marked point of
`V`, and an elementary étale neighbourhood `W` of `(Y ×_{T, τ} V, yτ)` together with a morphism
`F : W ⟶ X` carrying the marked point to `x` which is étale, trivial on residue fields, and
compatible with the structure morphisms to `S`; moreover the canonical section
`Spec κ(s) ⟶ Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` followed by `Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s} ⟶ T` agrees with the canonical
section `Spec κ(s) ⟶ V` followed by `τ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation_full_section
    {S T X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (fX : X ⟶ S) (gY : Y ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType fX] [LocallyOfFiniteType gY]
    (hT : LocallyOfFiniteType (specULiftZIsTerminal.{u}.from T))
    (x : X) (s : S) (hfx : fX x = s) (t : T) (y : Y)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (σ : T.presheaf.stalk t →+* AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s))
      (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hσ : IsLocalHom σ)
    (yσ : ↥(pullback gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t)))
    (hyσ₁ : pullback.fst gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t) yσ = y)
    (hyσ₂ : pullback.snd gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t) yσ =
      closedPoint _)
    (φ : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≃+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal ((pullback gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫
          T.fromSpecStalk t)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
        ((pullback gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
    (hbase : (pullback.snd gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t) ≫
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)))) ≫
      S.fromSpecStalk s) yσ = s)
    (hφ : φ.toRingHom.comp ((algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))).comp
          (fX.stalkHomAt hfx)) =
      (algebraMap ((pullback gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫
            T.fromSpecStalk t)).presheaf.stalk yσ)
          (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal ((pullback gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫
              T.fromSpecStalk t)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
            ((pullback gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫
              T.fromSpecStalk t)).presheaf.stalk yσ))).comp
        ((pullback.snd gY (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t) ≫
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
            (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)))) ≫
          S.fromSpecStalk s).stalkHomAt hbase)) :
    ∃ V : EtaleNeighborhood S s, ∃ hVel : V.IsElementary,
      ∃ (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T) (_ : τ V.point = t),
        specResidueFieldSection (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (S.presheaf.stalk s)
              (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s)))) ≫
            S.fromSpecStalk s) (specCompletedStalkToBase_closedPoint s)
            (isIso_residueFieldMap_specCompletedStalkToBase s) ≫
            (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom σ) ≫ T.fromSpecStalk t) =
          specResidueFieldSection V.toBase V.map_point
            ((EtaleNeighborhood.isElementary_iff V).mp hVel) ≫ τ ∧
        ∃ yτ : ↥(pullback gY τ),
          pullback.fst gY τ yτ = y ∧ pullback.snd gY τ yτ = V.point ∧
          ∃ W : EtaleNeighborhood (pullback gY τ) yτ, W.IsElementary ∧
            ∃ (F : W.scheme ⟶ X) (_ : F W.point = x),
              Etale F ∧ IsIso (F.residueFieldMap W.point) ∧
                F ≫ fX = W.toBase ≫ pullback.snd gY τ ≫ V.toBase
declarations.comment: clauses (1), (2), (3) and (4) of the conclusion, together with the commutativity of the source's diagram: (1) the elementary étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)`; (2) the morphism `F : W ⟶ X` with `F(w) = x`, étale and trivial on residue fields at `w`, i.e. an elementary étale neighbourhood `(W, w) → (X, x)`; (3) `τ(v) = t`; and (4) the elementary étale neighbourhood `(W, w) → (Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ)`. HOW `y_τ` IS SPECIFIED -- the one part of the source's sentence that is NOT proved: the source takes for `y_τ` the point corresponding to `y_σ` under the identification `(Y_σ)_s = (Y ×_T V)_v`. Here `y_τ` is specified by lying over `y` and over `v`, together with the equality of the two morphisms `Spec κ(s) ⟶ T` -- one through `Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` and `σ`, one through `V` and `τ` -- which IS that identification of the two fibres as one and the same scheme. That `y_τ` and `y_σ` are the same point OF that common fibre is not established. NO hypothesis beyond the source's is carried: Theorem 07QZ in particular is not, being proved as `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.localApproximationProperty`, so Tags 0CAU, 0CAV, 07GC, 07PS, 01ZC, 01ZM, 07RP and 057G that this rests on are unconditional. Two of the source's hypotheses are WEAKENED, so what is proved is stronger there: `T` of finite type over `Spec ℤ` is only required to be LOCALLY of finite type, and `φ` is only required to be a map of `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras rather than of `𝒪^∧_{S, s}`-algebras

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GDX, clauses (1) and (3).** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme,
let `T` be locally of finite type over `Spec ℤ`, let `t ∈ T` and `s ∈ S`, assume `𝒪_{S, s}` is a
G-ring, and let `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` be a local homomorphism. Then for every `N ≥ 1`
there are an elementary étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)` and a morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` with
`τ v = t`; moreover the square relating `σ` to `τ^♯_v` commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N`, which is the
extra conclusion that Tag 0CAW records as its clause (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (hT : LocallyOfFiniteType (specULiftZIsTerminal.{u}.from T))
    (t : T) (s : S) (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (σ : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hσ : IsLocalHom σ) :
    ∃ V : EtaleNeighborhood S s, V.IsElementary ∧
      ∃ (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T) (hτ : τ V.point = t),
        ∀ a : T.presheaf.stalk t,
          V.completionMap (σ a) -
              algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)) (τ.stalkHomAt hτ a) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point) ^ N)
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (3) of the conclusion: the elementary étale neighbourhood `(V, v)` of `(S, s)` and the morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` with `τ(v) = t`. What is proved is STRONGER than those two clauses: it carries in addition the congruence that Tag 0CAW records as its clause (3), namely that the square relating `σ` to `τ^♯_v` commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N`, which is why this registration is kept; and the source's `T` of finite type over `Spec ℤ` is weakened to LOCALLY of finite type. None of `X`, `Y`, `φ`, `y_σ` enters this statement, so it says nothing about clauses (2) and (4) — the elementary étale neighbourhood `(W, w)` of `(X, x)` which is simultaneously one of `(Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ)`. THOSE ARE PROVED ELSEWHERE, twice over and independently, and both of those statements carry a registration for the whole conclusion: all four clauses are `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation_full_section` in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.EtaleNeighbourhood.AbsoluteApproximationFull`, and also `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_common_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation` in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.EtaleNeighbourhood.RelativeMapApproximation`. NO hypothesis beyond the source's is carried: the library's Tag 0CAU behind this deduction is unconditional, Theorem 07QZ being proved as `StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.localApproximationProperty`

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.exists_common_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GDX.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `s ∈ S` have a
G-ring local ring, let `T` be locally of finite type over `Spec ℤ`, let `p : X ⟶ S` and
`q : Y ⟶ T` be locally of finite type, let `x ∈ X` lie over `s` and `y ∈ Y` over `t ∈ T`, and
let `σ : 𝒪_{T, t} → 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` be a local homomorphism. Write
`Y_σ = Y ×_{T, σ} Spec 𝒪^∧_{S, s}` and let `y_σ ∈ Y_σ` lie over `y` and over the closed point.
An isomorphism `φ : 𝒪^∧_{X, x} ≅ 𝒪^∧_{Y_σ, y_σ}` of `𝒪_{S, s}`-algebras is then induced, after
elementary étale changes, by a morphism of schemes: there are an elementary étale neighbourhood
`(V, v)` of `(S, s)`, a morphism `τ : V ⟶ T` with `τ v = t`, and an elementary étale
neighbourhood `(W, w)` of `(X, x)` which is simultaneously an elementary étale neighbourhood of
`(Y ×_{T, τ} V, y_τ)`, where `y_τ` corresponds to `y_σ` under the identification of the closed
fibres `(Y_σ)_s = (Y ×_T V)_v`.

The identification of the closed fibres is given explicitly: an isomorphism `e` of the residue
fields of the two bases compatible with their maps to `S` and to `T`, and an isomorphism of the
scheme-theoretic fibres compatible with the two maps to `Y` and with `e`, carrying the point
above `y_σ` to the point above `y_τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_common_elementaryEtaleNeighborhood_absoluteApproximation
    {X S Y T : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ T)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [LocallyOfFiniteType q]
    (hT : LocallyOfFiniteType (specULiftZIsTerminal.{u}.from T))
    {x : X} {s : S} {y : Y} {t : T} (hx : p x = s) (hy : q y = t)
    (hG : IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
    (σ : T.presheaf.stalk t →+*
      AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (S.presheaf.stalk s)) (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hσ : IsLocalHom σ)
    (yσ : (pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) : Scheme.{u}))
    (hyσY : pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) yσ = y)
    (hyσZ : pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) yσ =
      specCompletedStalkPoint S s)
    (φ : AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≃+*
      AdicCompletion
        (maximalIdeal
          ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
        ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
    (hφ : φ.toRingHom.comp ((algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x))).comp
        (p.stalkHomAt hx)) =
      (algebraMap ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ)
          (AdicCompletion
            (maximalIdeal
              ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))
            ((pullback q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).presheaf.stalk yσ))).comp
        (((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).stalkHomAt hyσZ).comp
          ((specCompletedStalkTo S s).stalkHomAt
            (specCompletedStalkTo_specCompletedStalkPoint S s)))) :
    ∃ (V : EtaleNeighborhood S s) (τ : V.scheme ⟶ T) (hτ : τ V.point = t)
      (yτ : (pullback q τ : Scheme.{u}))
      (_ : pullback.fst q τ yτ = y) (hyτV : pullback.snd q τ yτ = V.point)
      (W : EtaleNeighborhood X x) (g : W.scheme ⟶ pullback q τ)
      (hgPoint : g W.point = yτ) (_ : Etale g),
      V.IsElementary ∧ W.IsElementary ∧
        IsIso (((pullback q τ).residueFieldCongr hgPoint).inv ≫
          g.residueFieldMap W.point) ∧
        g ≫ pullback.snd q τ ≫ V.toBase = W.toBase ≫ p ∧
        (∀ b : T.presheaf.stalk t,
          V.completionMap (σ b) -
              algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)) (τ.stalkHomAt hτ b) ∈
            Ideal.map
              (algebraMap (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)
                (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point))
                  (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point)))
              (maximalIdeal (V.scheme.presheaf.stalk V.point) ^ N)) ∧
        ∃ (eBase : (specCompletedStalk S s).residueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≅
            V.scheme.residueField V.point)
          (eFiber : (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiber
              (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≅
            (pullback.snd q τ).fiber V.point),
          (Spec.map eBase.inv ≫ V.scheme.fromSpecResidueField V.point ≫ V.toBase =
            (specCompletedStalk S s).fromSpecResidueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              specCompletedStalkTo S s) ∧
          (Spec.map eBase.inv ≫ V.scheme.fromSpecResidueField V.point ≫ τ =
            (specCompletedStalk S s).fromSpecResidueField (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ) ∧
          (eFiber.hom ≫ (pullback.snd q τ).fiberι V.point ≫ pullback.fst q τ =
            (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberι
                (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫
              pullback.fst q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)) ∧
          (eFiber.hom ≫ (pullback.snd q τ).fiberToSpecResidueField V.point =
            (pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberToSpecResidueField
                (specCompletedStalkPoint S s) ≫ Spec.map eBase.inv) ∧
          (eFiber.hom (((pullback.snd q (relativeBaseChangeMorphism s σ)).fiberHomeo
              (specCompletedStalkPoint S s)).symm ⟨yσ, hyσZ⟩) =
            ((pullback.snd q τ).fiberHomeo V.point).symm ⟨yτ, hyτV⟩)
declarations.comment: What is proved is STRONGER than the source in two respects, both inherited from the first stage of Tag 0CAW which replaces the étale slice of Tag 057G here: the pair `(V, τ)` satisfies in addition the congruence that Tag 0CAW records as its clause (3), namely that the square relating `σ` to `τ^♯_v` commutes modulo `𝔪_v ^ N` for the given `N ≥ 1`; and the source's `T` of finite type over `Spec ℤ` is weakened to LOCALLY of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyLimitPreserving_pullback
declarations.doc:
Relative limit preservation is stable under a fibre product of presheaves
over a common intermediate presheaf.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleSheaf_of_smooth_surjection
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B` and let `F` be a
presheaf on the common underlying category `Sch_α/S` of the big fppf and the big étale site of
`S`. Assume

1. `F` is a sheaf for the étale topology, and
2. there are an algebraic space `U` over `S` and a morphism `f : U ⟶ F` which is representable
   by algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth.

Then `F` is an algebraic space over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleSheaf_of_smooth_surjection
    {F U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigEtaleOver.topology (associatedBigEtaleSite B) S hS) F)
    (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U) (f : U ⟶ F)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f)
    (hsurj : HasProperty B S hS (surjectiveMorphismProperty B S hS) f hf)
    (hsmooth : HasProperty B S hS (smoothMorphismProperty B S hS) f hf) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of the big site over `S` with `f` locally of

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyNoetherianOver.not_hasPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE2, first assertion.** *The site `(Noetherian/S)_τ` does not have fibre
products*, here for `τ = fppf` and `S = Spec k` with `k` a countable field.

The diagram without a fibre product is `Spec K ⟶ S ⟵ Spec K` for `K = k(u₀, u₁, u₂, …)`. A
fibre product would be a locally Noetherian scheme receiving, compatibly, the square-zero
extensions `Spec (K ⊕ Kⁿ)` with their two maps to `Spec K`; all of these meet it in one point,
whose local ring would have to dominate maximal ideals of unbounded embedding dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_hasPullbacks (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (baseField : Type u) [Field baseField]
    [Countable baseField] (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of baseField))) :
    ¬ HasPullbacks (LocallyNoetherianOver B (Spec (.of baseField)) hS)
declarations.comment: the first assertion, for tau = fppf and S the spectrum of a countable field

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyNoetherianOver.not_isMorphismOfSites_toBigFppfOver
registrations.comment: the second assertion, for tau = fppf and S = Spec F_p: the example of Examples, Section 0GE8 that the remark defers to

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isEquivalence_limitPreservingRestriction_noetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE3.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `τ` be one of the five
topologies — Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf. Restriction along the inclusion of the
full subcategory of locally Noetherian objects of `Sch/S` is an equivalence from the category of
limit preserving sheaves on `(Sch/S)_τ` to the category of limit preserving sheaves on the site
`(Noetherian/S)_τ`.

Faithfulness is the sharp uniqueness statement of Stacks 0EUW, essential surjectivity is the
existence statement of Stacks 0EUW together with the sheaf property of the extension supplied by
Stacks 0GDW, and fullness is the functoriality of that extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_limitPreservingRestriction_noetherian (τ : CoveringTopology)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] :
    (limitPreservingRestriction (P := IsLocallyNoetherianOver (S := S)) τ
      (hasCoveringPullbacks_isLocallyNoetherianOver τ)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_limitPreserving_yoneda
declarations.doc:
A limit-preserving representable functor on the locally Noetherian site
represents a scheme locally of finite presentation over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_of_limitPreserving_yoneda
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : LocallyNoetherianOver B S hS)
    (hX : LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u}
      (LocallyNoetherianOver.toScheme B S hS) (yoneda.obj X)) :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map X.1.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.relativelyRepresentable_restriction_of_limitPreservingSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE5, implication (1) ⇒ (2).** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `τ` be
one of the five topologies — Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf — and let `F'`, `G'` be
limit preserving sheaves on `(Sch/S)_τ`. If a transformation `a' : F' ⟶ G'` is representable, in
the sense of Categories Definition 001X, then so is its restriction `a` to the full subcategory of
locally Noetherian objects: for every locally Noetherian object `V` over `S` and every map
`V ⟶ G` the fibre product `F ×_G V` is represented by a locally Noetherian object over `S`.

Only limit preservation of `F'` and `G'` enters the proof; the sheaf condition and the topology
are carried because the source states them, and the sharper statement is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.relativelyRepresentable_restriction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_restriction_of_limitPreservingSheaf
    (τ : CoveringTopology) [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    {F' G' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1))} (a' : F' ⟶ G')
    (hF' : IsLimitPreservingSheaf τ F') (hG' : IsLimitPreservingSheaf τ G')
    (h1 : (uliftYoneda.{max w (u + 1)}).relativelyRepresentable a') :
    (uliftYoneda.{max w (u + 1)}).relativelyRepresentable
      (Functor.whiskerLeft (IsLocallyNoetherianOver (S := S)).ι.op a')
declarations.comment: implication (1) ⇒ (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.isRepresentableOnAffineFiniteType_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE5, implication (2) ⇒ (3).** If the restriction of `a'` to the locally Noetherian
objects over `S` is representable, then it is representable at every test object which is affine
of finite type over `S` and maps into an affine open of `S`: criterion (3) is criterion (2) with
its test object restricted.
declarations.comment: implication (2) ⇒ (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.relativelyRepresentable_of_isRepresentableOnAffineFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE5, implication (3) ⇒ (1).** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `τ` be one
of the five topologies — Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf — and let `F'`, `G'` be limit
preserving sheaves on `(Sch/S)_τ`. If the restriction `a` of a transformation `a' : F' ⟶ G'` to the
locally Noetherian objects over `S` is representable at every test object which is affine of finite
type over `S` and maps into an affine open of `S`, then `a'` itself is representable, in the sense
of Categories Definition 001X.

For an arbitrary object `T` of `Sch/S` and a section of `G'` over it, the fibre product is
represented over every member of the basis of opens of `T` which are affine and lie over an affine
open of `S`; those representing objects glue by Stacks 01LH, the local sections of `F'` glue
because `F'` is a Zariski sheaf, and the glued object has the universal property of the fibre
product at every object of `Sch/S`, both the existence and the uniqueness being local on that
object.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_of_isRepresentableOnAffineFiniteType
    (τ : CoveringTopology) [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    {F' G' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1))} (a' : F' ⟶ G')
    (hF' : IsLimitPreservingSheaf τ F') (hG' : IsLimitPreservingSheaf τ G')
    (h3 : IsRepresentableOnAffineFiniteType.{w}
      (Functor.whiskerLeft (IsLocallyNoetherianOver (S := S)).ι.op a')) :
    (uliftYoneda.{max w (u + 1)}).relativelyRepresentable a'
declarations.comment: implication (3) ⇒ (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ExtendingFunctors.relativelyRepresentable_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE5.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `τ` be one of the five
topologies — Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf — and let `F'`, `G'` be limit preserving
sheaves on `(Sch/S)_τ`. For a transformation `a' : F' ⟶ G'` with restriction `a` to the full
subcategory of locally Noetherian objects over `S`, the following are equivalent:

1. `a'` is representable;
2. `a` is representable;
3. `a` is representable at every test object which is affine of finite type over `S` and maps into
   an affine open of `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_tfae (τ : CoveringTopology) [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    {F' G' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w (u + 1))} (a' : F' ⟶ G')
    (hF' : IsLimitPreservingSheaf τ F') (hG' : IsLimitPreservingSheaf τ G') :
    List.TFAE
      [(uliftYoneda.{max w (u + 1)}).relativelyRepresentable a',
       (uliftYoneda.{max w (u + 1)}).relativelyRepresentable
         (Functor.whiskerLeft (IsLocallyNoetherianOver (S := S)).ι.op a'),
       IsRepresentableOnAffineFiniteType.{w}
         (Functor.whiskerLeft (IsLocallyNoetherianOver (S := S)).ι.op a')]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyNoetherianOver.existsUnique_isAlgebraicSpace_restriction_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE7.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `F` be a set-valued functor
on the locally Noetherian étale site `(Noetherian/S)_étale`. If the diagonal
`Δ : F ⟶ F × F` is representable (Categories 001X), `F` satisfies Artin's axioms `[-1]`,
`[0]`, `[1]`, `[2]`, `[3]`, `[4]`, `[5]` in the form of Section 0GE6, and the local rings of
`S` at its finite type points are G-rings, then there is a limit preserving algebraic space `F'`
on the big fppf site `(Sch/S)_fppf` whose restriction to `(Noetherian/S)_étale` is `F`, and it is
unique: two such are identified by a unique isomorphism compatible with the identifications of
their restrictions with `F`.

The extension is the one of Stacks 0GE3, its diagonal is representable by Stacks 0GE5, the
axioms `[-1]`, `[2]`, `[3]`, `[4]`, `[5]` pass to it because they only involve locally Noetherian
test objects, and Stacks 07Y1 shows it is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isAlgebraicSpace_restriction_iso [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (F : (LocallyNoetherianOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hdiag : (yoneda (C := LocallyNoetherianOver B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable (diag F))
    (hax : SatisfiesArtinAxioms B S hS F)
    (hG : ∀ s : S, IsFiniteTypePoint s → IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)) :
    (∃ F' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F' ∧
        LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) F' ∧
        Nonempty ((LocallyNoetherianOver.toBigFppfOver B S hS).op ⋙ F' ≅ F)) ∧
      ∀ (F₁ F₂ : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F₁ → IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F₂ →
        LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) F₁ →
        LimitPreserving.{u, u, u, u, u + 1, u} (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS) F₂ →
        ∀ (e₁ : (LocallyNoetherianOver.toBigFppfOver B S hS).op ⋙ F₁ ≅ F)
          (e₂ : (LocallyNoetherianOver.toBigFppfOver B S hS).op ⋙ F₂ ≅ F),
        ∃! e : F₁ ≅ F₂,
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft (LocallyNoetherianOver.toBigFppfOver B S hS).op e ≪≫ e₂ = e₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyNoetherianOver.not_isMorphismOfSites_toBigFppfOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GE9.** *With `S = Spec 𝐅_p` the inclusion functor
`(Noetherian/S)_{fppf} ⟶ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` does not define a morphism of sites.*

Its pushforward on sheaves of sets has no left exact left adjoint. Both sites are subcanonical,
so a left exact `u_s` would identify the two Yoneda embeddings and force the inclusion to
preserve monomorphisms, which by
`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyNoetherianOver.not_preservesMonomorphisms_toBigFppfOver` it does
not.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_isMorphismOfSites_toBigFppfOver
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} (ZMod p))))) :
    ¬ IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1}
      (toBigFppfOver B (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} (ZMod p)))) hS)
      (fppfTopology B (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} (ZMod p)))) hS)
      (BigFppfOver.topology B (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} (ZMod p)))) hS)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isEquivalence_toFamilyDescentDatum_of_homOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEA.**
Let `𝒱 = {V j ⟶ U} ⟶ 𝒰 = {U i ⟶ U}` be a morphism of families of morphisms with fixed target
given by `𝟙 U`, a reindexing `α : J → I` and morphisms `V j ⟶ U (α j)`, and let `p` be a fibred
category. Assume that the fibre products `U i₁ ×_U U i₂`, `U i ×_U V j` and
`U i₁ ×_U U i₂ ×_U V j` exist, that `𝒮_U ⟶ DD(𝒱)` is an equivalence, that `𝒮_{U i} ⟶ DD(𝒱_i)`
is fully faithful for every `i`, and that `𝒮_{U i₁ ×_U U i₂} ⟶ DD(𝒱_{i₁i₂})` is faithful for
every `i₁, i₂`, where `𝒱_i` and `𝒱_{i₁i₂}` are the base changes of `𝒱`. Then `𝒮_U ⟶ DD(𝒰)` is
an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toFamilyDescentDatum_of_homOver {p : 𝒳 ⥤ C} [p.IsFibered] {U : C}
    {𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{w} U} {𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{w'} U} (Φ : 𝒱.HomOver 𝒰 (𝟙 U))
    [∀ i₁ i₂, HasPullback (𝒰.f i₁) (𝒰.f i₂)]
    [∀ i j, HasPullback (𝒰.f i) (𝒱.f j)]
    [∀ i₁ i₂ j, HasPullback (pullback.fst (𝒰.f i₁) (𝒰.f i₂) ≫ 𝒰.f i₁) (𝒱.f j)]
    (h₂ : (toFamilyDescentDatum p 𝒱).IsEquivalence)
    (h₃ : ∀ i, Nonempty (toFamilyDescentDatum p (𝒱.pullback₁ (𝒰.f i))).FullyFaithful)
    (h₄ : ∀ i₁ i₂, (toFamilyDescentDatum p
      (𝒱.pullback₁ (pullback.fst (𝒰.f i₁) (𝒰.f i₂) ≫ 𝒰.f i₁))).Faithful) :
    (toFamilyDescentDatum p 𝒰).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: Module.Flat.baseChange_of_map_maximalIdeal_eq_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEB.** Let `S ← R → R'`, `S → S'`, `R' → S'` be a commutative diagram of local
rings and local homomorphisms, let `M` be a finite `S`-module and let `f : M → M'` realize `M'` as
the base change `M ⊗_S S'`. Assume the horizontal arrows `R → R'` and `S → S'` are flat, that `M`
is flat over `R`, that `𝔪_R R' = 𝔪_{R'}` and that `R'` and `S'` are Noetherian. Then `M'` is flat
over `R'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChange_of_map_maximalIdeal_eq_maximalIdeal
    {R S R' S' M M' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [CommRing S']
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing R'] [IsLocalRing S']
    [IsNoetherianRing R'] [IsNoetherianRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S'] [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S']
    [IsScalarTower R S S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S']
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R' S')]
    [Module.Flat R R'] [Module.Flat S S']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [Module.Finite S M] [Module.Flat R M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module S M'] [Module R' M'] [Module S' M']
    [IsScalarTower S S' M'] [IsScalarTower R' S' M']
    (hm : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R R') = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R')
    (f : M →ₗ[S] M') (hf : IsBaseChange S' f) :
    Module.Flat R' M'
declarations.comment:
The commutative square is presented by the two scalar towers into `S'`, `M ⊗_S S'`
by `IsBaseChange S' f` as in the sibling 00MO, and `𝔪_R R'` by
`Ideal.map (algebraMap R R') (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)`. The source's unused hypotheses `S`
local, `R → S` local and `S → S'` local are dropped, and `R → R'` local is implied by `hm`. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_mem_nonZeroDivisors_not_isUnit
declarations.doc:
For a finite type algebra `S` over a field `k` with `0 < dim S`, some element of `S` is
simultaneously a nonzerodivisor and a nonunit.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_nonZeroDivisors_not_isUnit {k : Type*} [Field k] {S : Type*} [CommRing S]
    [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (h : 0 < ringKrullDim S) :

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.PerfectClassicalGenerator.triangEnvelope_eq_perfectObjects_of_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEF**. Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let `G` be a perfect
object of `D(𝒪_X)` lying in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and generating it, in the sense that an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` receiving only zero morphisms from the shifts of `G` is zero. Then `G` is a classical
generator of `D_perf(𝒪_X)`: the smallest strictly full triangulated subcategory of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
closed under direct summands and containing `G` is exactly the subcategory of perfect objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangEnvelope_eq_perfectObjects_of_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (G : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (hG : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) G.obj)
    (hgen : (ObjectProperty.singleton G).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator) :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton G).triangEnvelope = perfectObjects X
declarations.comment: for X quasi-compact and quasi-separated and G a perfect object generating D_QCoh(O_X), G is a classical generator of D_perf(O_X): the triangulated envelope of G is exactly the perfect objects

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.SupportedClassicalGenerator.hasCoproducts_and_exists_perfect_generator_and_triangEnvelope_eq_perfectSupported
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Remark 0GEG].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let
`T ⊆ X` be a closed subset such that `X ∖ T` is quasi-compact. Then

1. `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` has direct sums;
2. there is a perfect object `G` of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` which is a generator for
   `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` (by [Stacks, Tag 0A9A]);
3. every such `G` is a classical generator for `D_{perf,T}(𝒪_X)`: the smallest strictly full,
   saturated, triangulated subcategory of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` containing `G` is the subcategory
   `perfectSupported X T` of objects perfect in `D(𝒪_X)`.

Generators are weak generators in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 09SJ](3) and the classical
generation is equality with `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.triangEnvelope`. Everything is stated
at an arbitrary model of the derived category. The direct sums are indexed by the universe of
`𝒪_X`-modules; the source's argument uses them, with [Stacks, Tag 0A9B] and
[Stacks, Tag 09SR], at the locally small model, where the morphisms of `D(𝒪_X)` lie in that
universe too.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCoproducts_and_exists_perfect_generator_and_triangEnvelope_eq_perfectSupported
    (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact (Tᶜ : Set X)) :
    HasCoproducts.{u} (QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T) ∧
      (∃ G : QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T,
        perfectSupported X T G ∧ (ObjectProperty.singleton G).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator) ∧
      ∀ G : QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T, perfectSupported X T G →
        (ObjectProperty.singleton G).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator →
          (ObjectProperty.singleton G).triangEnvelope = perfectSupported X T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyBoundedBelow_of_isPerfectRelativeTo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEH, condition (1) implies the first clause of condition (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
flat and locally of finite presentation. An object of `D(𝒪_X)` perfect relative to `S` is locally
bounded below.

Relative perfectness gives an open covering of `X` on each member of which `E`, read over
`f⁻¹𝒪_S`, has Tor amplitude in some interval `[a, b]`. The structure sheaf of the inverse-image
ringed space is the unit of its tensor product, so that interval already bounds the cohomology
of `E|_U` read over `f⁻¹𝒪_S`, and restriction of scalars along `f⁻¹𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X` leaves the
underlying sheaves unchanged.

The derived tensor product is a family of certificates, one on each open subspace of the
inverse-image ringed space, pinned by the hypothesis that its underived tensor product is the
genuine `- ⊗_{f⁻¹𝒪_S} -`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyBoundedBelow_of_isPerfectRelativeTo {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (OXMod.{u, u} (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base))]
    [∀ U : Opens (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{d'}
        (OXMod.{u, u} ((RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).restrict
          U.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (D : ∀ U : Opens (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).carrier,
      RingedSpace.CertifiedDerivedSheafTensoring.{d', u}
        ((RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
    (hD : ∀ U : Opens (RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).carrier,
      (D U).tensor = Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ((RingedSpace.inverseImage S.toRingedSpace f.base).restrict U.isOpenEmbedding).sheaf)
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hE : f.IsPerfectRelativeTo D E) :
    RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow X.toRingedSpace E
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies the first clause of condition (2): an `S`-perfect object is locally bounded below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfectRelativeTo_iff_isLocallyBoundedBelow_and_fibres
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEH.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite
presentation, and let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`. The following are equivalent:

1. `E` is `S`-perfect (Stacks 0DI0);
2. `E` is locally bounded below and for every point `s ∈ S` the derived fibre `L(X_s ⟶ X)^*E` of
   `D(𝒪_{X_s})` is locally bounded below, where `X_s = X ×_S Spec κ(s)`.

Relative perfectness is read at the canonical certificate family
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily`, the genuine
derived tensor product over `f⁻¹𝒪_S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeTo_iff_isLocallyBoundedBelow_and_fibres
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    f.IsPerfectRelativeTo (RingedSpace.canonicalCertifiedDerivedSheafTensoringFamily _) E ↔
      RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow X.toRingedSpace E ∧
        ∀ s : S, RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow
          (pullback f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).toRingedSpace
          ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
            E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isRelativelyPerfect_of_isLocallyBoundedBelow_of_fibres
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEH, condition (2) implies condition (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be flat and locally of
finite presentation and let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`. If `E` is locally
bounded below and for every point `s` of `S` the derived pullback `L(X_s ⟶ X)^*E` of `E` to the
fibre `X_s = X ×_S Spec κ(s)` is locally bounded below, then `E` is `S`-perfect.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRelativelyPerfect_of_isLocallyBoundedBelow_of_fibres
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hpc : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow X.toRingedSpace E)
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow
      (Limits.pullback f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).toRingedSpace
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (Limits.pullback.fst f (S.fromSpecResidueField s)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)) :
    f.IsRelativelyPerfect E
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1): for f flat and locally of finite presentation and E pseudo-coherent, if E is locally bounded below and every derived fibre L(X_s ⟶ X)^*E is locally bounded below, then E is S-perfect

declarations.name: Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.truncGE_restriction_of_hom_koszul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEJ], the implication "Koszul orthogonality implies truncated
restriction".** Let `f₁, …, f_r ∈ A`, let `U = ⋃ᵢ D(f_i) ⊆ Spec A`, let `j : U ⟶ Spec A` be the
inclusion and let `K` be the sheafified Koszul complex of the sequence. Let `E` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec A})`. If every morphism `K⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E` vanishes for `n ≥ a`, then the canonical map
`E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` becomes invertible after truncation in degrees `≥ a`.

This is condition (2) of the source implying condition (1), at the source's own index: the
premise is at `a` and the conclusion at `a`.

The cone `N` of the unit restricts to zero on `U`, receives no morphism from `K⟦-n⟧` for
`n ≥ a - 1`, and has quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves — the last because `E` does and `Rj_*`
preserves quasi-coherent cohomology along a quasi-compact open immersion ([Stacks, Tag 08D5]).
The graded detection statement
`Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.isZero_homology_of_forall_hom_koszulObject_eq_zero` then kills the
homology of `N` in degrees `≥ a - 1`, which is what makes the truncated map invertible. That is
where the commutative algebra of the source sits: the Koszul power triangles of
[Stacks, Tag 062C], the lifting lemma of [Stacks, Tag 08E3] and the affine comparison
`D(A) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec A})` of [Stacks, Tag 06Z0]. The two other inputs of the source are
proved too: the Koszul object restricts to zero on `U` by
`Stacks.Koszul.OpenComplement.isZero_derivedRestrict_koszulObject`, and `Rj_*` is fully faithful
by the instance
`Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.isIso_derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction_counit_app`.
declarations.statement:
theorem truncGE_restriction_of_hom_koszul_eq_zero
    (E : DerivedCategory (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules) (hE : qcohSpec A E) (a : ℤ)
    (h : ∀ n : ℤ, a ≤ n → Subsingleton ((koszulObject f)⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E)) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).map
      ((derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction (openComplement f).ι).unit.app E))
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.hom_koszul_eq_zero_of_truncGE_restriction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEJ], the implication "truncated restriction implies Koszul orthogonality
`r` degrees up".** In the situation above, if the canonical map `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` is invertible
after truncation in degrees `≥ a`, then every morphism `K⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E` vanishes for `n ≥ a + r`.

The argument spends the window
`Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.subsingleton_hom_koszulObject_shift_of_isLE`, which is the perfectness
of `K`: `K` is a bounded complex of finite free modules in degrees `-r, …, 0`, so `Hom(K⟦-m⟧, M)`
sees only the homology of `M` in the `r + 1` degrees `m - r, …, m`. It is applied to
`τ_{≤a-1}E` and to `τ_{≤a-1}(Rj_*(E|_U))`, both of which have quasi-coherent cohomology
sheaves — and quasi-coherence is not a convenience here, the window being false without it.

**The index is `a + r`, and the `a + 1` of the published statement of the tag is false for
`r ≥ 2`.** This is an approved erratum of the Stacks Project, recorded against the tag; the
Stacks source text is left as published. The module documentation gives the counterexample
over `k[x, y]`, where `a + r` is sharp.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_koszul_eq_zero_of_truncGE_restriction
    (E : DerivedCategory (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules) (hE : qcohSpec A E) (a : ℤ)
    (h : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).map
      ((derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction (openComplement f).ι).unit.app E))) :
    ∀ n : ℤ, a + (r : ℤ) ≤ n → Subsingleton ((koszulObject f)⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E)
declarations.comment:
(1) implies (2) with a replaced by a + r, not the published a + 1, which is false
for r ≥ 2 — see the module docstring for the counterexample over k[x,y]

declarations.name: Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.truncLE_restriction_of_hom_koszul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `f₁, …, f_r ∈ A`, let `U = ⋃ᵢ D(f_i) ⊆ X = Spec A`, let `j : U ⟶ X` be the inclusion and
let `K` be the sheafified Koszul complex of the sequence. Let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`,
that is one whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. If every morphism `K⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E` vanishes
for `n ≤ a + 1`, then the canonical map `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` is invertible after truncation in
degrees `≤ a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem truncLE_restriction_of_hom_koszul_eq_zero
    (E : DerivedCategory (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).ringCatSheaf) E)
    (a : ℤ)
    (h : ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ a + 1 → Subsingleton ((koszulObject f)⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E)) :
    IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE a).map
      ((derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction (openComplement f).ι).unit.app E))
declarations.comment:
(2) at a+1 implies (1) at a, for E in D_QCoh. This is the corrected reverse
implication; the published '(2) at a implies (1) at a' is false: for A = k[x], f = (x),
E = 𝒪_X and a = 0 condition (2) holds and (1) fails, see the module documentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.hom_koszul_eq_zero_of_truncLE_restriction_sub_one
declarations.doc:
Let `f₁, …, f_r ∈ A`, let `U = ⋃ᵢ D(f_i) ⊆ X = Spec A`, let `j : U ⟶ X` be the inclusion and
let `K` be the sheafified Koszul complex of the sequence. Let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`,
that is one whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. If the canonical map `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` is
invertible after truncation in degrees `≤ a`, then every morphism `K⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E` vanishes for
`n ≤ a - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_koszul_eq_zero_of_truncLE_restriction_sub_one
    (E : DerivedCategory (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
    (_hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).ringCatSheaf) E)
    (a : ℤ)
    (h : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE a).map
      ((derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction (openComplement f).ι).unit.app E))) :
    ∀ n : ℤ, n ≤ a - 1 → Subsingleton ((koszulObject f)⟦-n⟧ ⟶ E)
declarations.comment:
(1) implies (2) with a replaced by a-1, at the source's own index, for E in
D_QCoh

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncGE_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEL].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let `P` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and let `a` be an integer. Then

1. `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦-i⟧, E) = 0` for `i ≫ 0`

if and only if

2. `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦-i⟧, τ_{≥a}E) = 0` for `i ≫ 0`,

where `τ_{≥a}` is the canonical truncation of `D(𝒪_X)` and vanishing of a Hom-group is
subsingletonness of the morphism type, the derived category being additive.

Both implications are the truncation triangle
`τ_{≤a-1}E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥a}E ⟶ (τ_{≤a-1}E)⟦1⟧`: a morphism `P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E` which dies in `τ_{≥a}E`
factors through `τ_{≤a-1}E`, and a morphism `P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ τ_{≥a}E` which dies in `(τ_{≤a-1}E)⟦1⟧`
factors through `E`. So each direction needs only that `τ_{≤a-1}E` and `(τ_{≤a-1}E)⟦1⟧` receive
no nonzero morphism from `P⟦-i⟧` for `i` large; both of them lie in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and are bounded
above, by `a - 1` and `a - 2`, and
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.exists_threshold_subsingleton_hom_negShift_of_isPerfect` kills both from
`i ≥ a - 1 + c` on, with `c` the threshold that perfectness of `P` supplies through
[Stacks, Tag 09M4].
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncGE_of_isPerfect
    (P E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hP : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) P)
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules j).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (a : ℤ) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i →
        Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncLE_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEM].** Let `X` be a scheme, let `P` and `E` be objects of `D(𝒪_X)` with `P`
bounded above by `nP`, and let `a` be an integer. Then `Hom(P⟦-i⟧, E) = 0` for `i ≪ 0` if and only
if `Hom(P⟦-i⟧, τ_{≤a}E) = 0` for `i ≪ 0`.

The source states this for `P` perfect on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and `E` in
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`; the argument consumes only boundedness above of `P`, which those hypotheses imply,
so the statement here is strictly more general and a consumer holding the source's hypotheses may
restrict. The vanishing that makes the truncation triangle harmless is pure t-structure
orthogonality: `P⟦-i⟧` is `≤ nP + i`, while `τ_{>a}E` is `≥ a + 1`, and `nP + i < a + 1` for
`i ≪ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncLE_of_isLE
    (P E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (nP : ℤ) (hP : P.IsLE nP) (a : ℤ) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ N → Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ N →
        Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE a).obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tfae_minus_of_isPerfect_generator
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_minus_of_isPerfect_generator
    (hqc : CompactSpace X) (hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (G E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (hgen : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ K), f = 0) → IsZero K)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    List.TFAE
      [(DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := StructureSheafModules X.sheaf)).minus E,
        ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (G⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E),
        ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext G E i),
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).minus
          ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
            (((globalDerivedHom X.sheaf).obj (op G)).obj E)),
        ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i, N ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
            (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G)).obj E))),
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).minus
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
            (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G)).obj E)),
        ∀ P : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf), (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect P →
          ((∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ∧
            (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext P E i)) ∧
            (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).minus
              ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
                (((globalDerivedHom X.sheaf).obj (op P)).obj E))) ∧
          (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i, N ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
            ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
              (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj P).obj E)))) ∧
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).minus
            ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
              (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj P).obj E))]

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ExtensionByZeroClosedSupport.isPerfect_jShriek_of_closedSupport_and_restrict
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_jShriek_of_closedSupport_and_restrict
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (U : Opens X) (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTU : T ⊆ (U : Set X))
    (Rj : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U (structureSheafRing X))) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)))
    (αj : (jPush U (structureSheafRing X)).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rj)
    (hRj : Rj.IsRightDerivedFunctor αj
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U (structureSheafRing X)))
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U (structureSheafRing X))))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding) E)
    (hET : AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn (resRing U (structureSheafRing X))
      ((fun x : Usp U ↦ x.1) ⁻¹' T) E) :
    IsIso ((extensionByZeroToDerivedPushforward (structureSheafRing X) U Rj αj).app E) ∧
      RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X)
        ((jShriek U (structureSheafRing X)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn (structureSheafRing X) T
        ((jShriek U (structureSheafRing X)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) ∧
      Nonempty ((jStar U (structureSheafRing X)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((jShriek U (structureSheafRing X)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) ≅ E)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.eventually_subsingleton_shiftedHom_iff_ext
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEQ, conditions (2) and (3).** For a perfect generator `G` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` on a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and an object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the groups
`Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(G⟦-i⟧, E)` vanish for `i ≪ 0` exactly when the groups `Ext^i_X(G, E)` do.

The two conditions hold of the same `i`, because `⟦-i⟧` is left adjoint to `⟦i⟧`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_subsingleton_shiftedHom_iff_ext
    (_hqc : CompactSpace X) (_hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (G E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (_hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (_hgen : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ K), f = 0) → IsZero K)
    (_hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (G⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext G E i)
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3): eventual vanishing of Hom(G[-i], E) and of Ext^i(G, E)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.plus_derivedGlobalSections_derivedTensor_derivedDual_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEQ, conditions (5) and (6).** For a perfect generator `G` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` on a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and an object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the cohomology groups
`H^i(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` vanish for `i ≪ 0` exactly when `RΓ(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` lies in
`D⁺(ℤ)`.

This is the description of the bounded-below derived category by its cohomology, applied to the
single object `RΓ(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` of `D(AddCommGrpCat)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem plus_derivedGlobalSections_derivedTensor_derivedDual_iff
    (_hqc : CompactSpace X) (_hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (G E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (_hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (_hgen : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ K), f = 0) → IsZero K)
    (_hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).plus
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
          (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G))) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n ≤ N, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
          (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G))))
declarations.comment:
conditions (5) and (6): eventual vanishing of H^i(X, G^vee ⊗ E) and membership
of RGamma(X, G^vee ⊗ E) in D^+(Z)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.eventually_subsingleton_ext_iff_isZero_homology_derivedTensorDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEQ, conditions (3) and (5).** For a perfect generator `G` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` on a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme and an object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the groups
`Ext^i_X(G, E)` vanish for `i ≪ 0` exactly when the cohomology groups
`H^i(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` do, granted that the canonical map
`E⟦i⟧ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} G^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(G, E⟦i⟧)` of Stacks 08I1 is invertible for every `i`.

The two conditions hold of the same `i`, because `Ext^i_X(G, E)` and `H^i(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)`
are the same group: Stacks 08DQ identifies `H⁰(X, M ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} G^∨)` with `Hom(G, M)`, and at
`M = E⟦i⟧` the left side becomes `H^i(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` because tensoring with `G^∨` and
`RΓ(X, -)` are triangulated, hence commute with the shift, and `H⁰` of an `i`-fold shift is
`H^i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_subsingleton_ext_iff_isZero_homology_derivedTensorDual
    (_hqc : CompactSpace X) (_hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (G E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (_hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (_hgen : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ K), f = 0) → IsZero K)
    (_hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (h08I1 : ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X.sheaf G (E⟦i⟧))) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext G E i)) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ n ≤ N, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} n).obj
        ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
          (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G))))
declarations.comment:
conditions (3) and (5): eventual vanishing of Ext^i(G, E) and of
H^i(X, G^vee ⊗ E), granted the 08I1 map E[i] ⊗ G^vee ⟶ RSheafHom(G, E[i]) invertible for all i

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tfae_plus_of_isPerfect_generator
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_plus_of_isPerfect_generator
    (hqc : CompactSpace X) (hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (G E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (hgen : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ K), f = 0) → IsZero K)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) :
    List.TFAE
      [(DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := StructureSheafModules X.sheaf)).plus E,
        ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (G⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E),
        ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext G E i),
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).plus
          ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
            (((globalDerivedHom X.sheaf).obj (op G)).obj E)),
        ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
            (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G)).obj E))),
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).plus
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
            (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj (derivedDual X.sheaf G)).obj E)),
        ∀ P : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf), (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect P →
          ((∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ∧
            (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext P E i)) ∧
            (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).plus
              ((RingedSite.underlyingDerivedGroup (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
                (((globalDerivedHom X.sheaf).obj (op P)).obj E))) ∧
          (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} i).obj
            ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
              (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj P).obj E)))) ∧
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u})).plus
            ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
              (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj P).obj E))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPseudoCoherent_of_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_tensor_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GES].** Let `A` be a ring, let `X` be a scheme separated and of finite
presentation over `A`, with structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec A`, and let `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. If
`RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` is a pseudo-coherent object of `D(A)` for every perfect object `E` of
`D(𝒪_X)`, then `K` is pseudo-coherent relative to `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_of_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_tensor_isPerfect
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hpc : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E →
        StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj K))) :
    f.IsPseudoCoherent K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_subsingleton_ext_of_derivedGlobalSections_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GET, the vanishing that the hypothesis produces.** Let `A` be a ring, let `X` be a
scheme separated, of finite presentation and flat over `A`, let `G` be a perfect generator of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose dual `G^∨` is perfect, and let `K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. If
`RΓ(X, K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` is a perfect object of `D(A)` for every perfect object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)`,
then `Ext^i_X(G, K)` and `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(G⟦-i⟧, K)` vanish for `i ≪ 0`.

Perfectness of `G^∨` is Stacks 08DQ, and is a hypothesis here rather than a consequence of
`hG`; see the implementation notes. It makes the hypothesis on perfect twists apply to `G^∨`,
so that `RΓ(X, K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} G^∨)` is the underlying complex of abelian groups of a perfect
object of `D(A)`. A perfect object of `D(A)` has vanishing cohomology in all sufficiently
negative degrees and the forgetful functor to abelian groups is exact, so
`H^i(X, G^∨ ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} K)` vanishes for `i ≪ 0`; that is condition (5) of Stacks 0GEQ, whose
equivalence with conditions (3) and (2) gives the two assertions.

`Spec(A)`-perfectness of `K` is not proved; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eventually_subsingleton_ext_of_derivedGlobalSections_isPerfect
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f] [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hqc : CompactSpace X) (hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
