    (G K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (hGdual : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect (derivedDual X.sheaf G))
    (hgen : ∀ L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj L).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (g : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ L), g = 0) → IsZero L)
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent)
    (h08I1 : ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X.sheaf G (K⟦i⟧)))
    (hperf : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect E →
        ∃ M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect M ∧
          Nonempty ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
              (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj K).obj E) ≅
            (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} A) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext G K i)) ∧
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (G⟦-i⟧ ⟶ K)
declarations.comment: ONLY the vanishing the tag's hypothesis produces: `Ext^i_X(G, K)` and `Hom(G⟦-i⟧, K)` vanish for `i ≪ 0`. That `K` is `Spec(A)`-perfect is NOT proved here; it needs Stacks 0GES, the implication (2) ⇒ (1) of Stacks 0GEH, and condition (1) of Stacks 0GEQ, none of which the library carries. See the implementation notes for what is carried.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_subsingleton_ext_of_derivedGlobalSections_isPerfect'
declarations.doc:
**The vanishing of Stacks 0GET, with the duality inputs proved.** Let `A` be a ring, let `X`
be a scheme separated, of finite presentation and flat over `A`, let `G` be a perfect generator
of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, and let `K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. If `RΓ(X, K ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} E)` is a
perfect object of `D(A)` for every perfect object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)`, then `Ext^i_X(G, K)` and
`Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(G⟦-i⟧, K)` vanish for `i ≪ 0`.

This is `eventually_subsingleton_ext_of_derivedGlobalSections_isPerfect` with its two arguments
about `G` discharged by [Stacks, Tag 08DQ]: the dual `G^∨` is perfect by the first assertion,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isPerfect_derivedDual`, and the map of [Stacks, Tag 08I1] out of
`K⟦i⟧ ⊗^L G^∨` is invertible for every `i` by the third,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_derivedTensorDualToSheafHom_of_isPerfect`.

That `K` is `Spec(A)`-perfect, the conclusion of the source, is not proved; the implementation
notes of `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/RelativelyPerfectDetectedByGlobalSections.lean`
list the three results it rests on.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eventually_subsingleton_ext_of_derivedGlobalSections_isPerfect'
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f] [Flat f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (hqc : CompactSpace X) (hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X)
    (G K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hG : (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G)
    (hgen : ∀ L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj L).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (g : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ L), g = 0) → IsZero L)
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hperf : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect E →
        ∃ M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A), StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect M ∧
          Nonempty ((derivedModuleGlobalSections (ringedSite X.sheaf)).obj
              (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj K).obj E) ≅
            (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} A) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapDerivedCategory.obj M)) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext G K i)) ∧
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i ≤ N, Subsingleton (G⟦-i⟧ ⟶ K)
declarations.comment: ONLY the vanishing the tag's hypothesis produces: `Ext^i_X(G, K)` and `Hom(G⟦-i⟧, K)` vanish for `i ≪ 0`, for a perfect generator `G`, with perfectness of the dual and invertibility of the Stacks 08I1 map proved by Stacks 08DQ. That `K` is `Spec(A)`-perfect is NOT proved here; it needs Stacks 0GES, the implication (2) ⇒ (1) of Stacks 0GEH, and condition (1) of Stacks 0GEQ.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isRelativelyPerfect_of_isPerfect_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GET.** Let `A` be a ring and let `X` be a scheme separated, of finite presentation
and flat over `A`, with structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec A`. Let `K` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. If `RΓ(X, E ⊗^L K)` is a perfect object of `D(A)` for every perfect object `E` of
`D(𝒪_X)`, then `K` is `Spec(A)`-perfect.

`RΓ(X, -)` is the `A`-linear derived global sections `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedGlobalSectionsOver`,
perfectness in `D(A)` is `StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect`, perfectness of `E` is Stacks 08CM on the
ringed space of `X`, and `Spec(A)`-perfectness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsRelativelyPerfect` (Stacks 0DI0). Of finite presentation is
`[QuasiCompact f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]` together with quasi-separatedness, which
separatedness implies.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.isRelativelyPerfect_of_isPerfect_derivedGlobalSectionsOver_tensor
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [Flat f]
    (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj K).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hperf : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E →
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect
          ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj E).obj K))) :
    f.IsRelativelyPerfect K

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.AffineLine.uncoheratedTrace_example
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEU].** Let `Y = Spec R`, `X = 𝐀¹_R` and `f : X ⟶ Y` the structure morphism,
and take `L = 𝒪_X`, `K = 𝒪_Y` in the trace map `Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`.

1. The left hand side is in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`: this holds for `Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(𝒪_X, M)` for every
   `M` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, so for `M = a(K)` whatever the right adjoint `a`.
2. The right hand side is isomorphic to `∏_{n ≥ 0} 𝒪_Y` placed in degree zero.
3. `∏_{n ≥ 0} 𝒪_Y` is quasi-coherent exactly when every `t ∈ R` satisfies an equation
   `t^j = t^{j+1} b`.
4. So when some `t ∈ R` satisfies no such equation, the right hand side is not in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`,
   it is not isomorphic to the left hand side, and the trace map is not an isomorphism
   (`Stacks.Duality.AffineLine.not_isIso_sheafyTrace`).

The source asserts in (3) that the product is not quasi-coherent for an arbitrary `R`. That is
false for a field (`Stacks.Duality.isQuasicoherent_piStructureSheaf_of_isField`), and (3) is the
corrected form: the product fails to be quasi-coherent precisely for the rings with an element
`t` admitting no equation `t^j = t^{j+1} b`, such as `ℤ` (`uncoheratedTrace_example_int`).
declarations.statement:
theorem uncoheratedTrace_example :
    (∀ M : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory (affineLine R),
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)
        (traceSource R M.obj)) ∧
    Nonempty (traceTarget R ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Spec R).Modules 0).obj
      (∏ᶜ (fun _ : ℕ ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (Spec R).ringCatSheaf))) ∧
    ((∏ᶜ (fun _ : ℕ ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).IsQuasicoherent ↔
      ∀ t : R, ∃ (j : ℕ) (b : R), t ^ j = t ^ (j + 1) * b) ∧
    ((∃ t : R, ∀ (j : ℕ) (b : R), t ^ j ≠ t ^ (j + 1) * b) →
      ¬ DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf) (traceTarget R) ∧
      ∀ M : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory (affineLine R),
        IsEmpty (traceSource R M.obj ≅ traceTarget R))
declarations.comment: the full example in corrected form: the left side is in D_QCoh, the right side is the product of copies of the structure sheaf, which is quasi-coherent exactly when every t satisfies t^j = t^(j+1) b (false over Z, true over a field), and then no isomorphism exists

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_coherator_homEquiv_sheafyTrace_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEV], erasing `DQ_Y` on the left.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, `L ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. If
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K))` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the map
`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ DQ_Y(R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K))` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` adjoint to the trace of
[Stacks, Tag 0B6H] is an isomorphism. All derived categories are at the standard model.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coherator_homEquiv_sheafyTrace_of_qcqs :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard X.Modules
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard Y.Modules
    ∀ (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
      (hsrc : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj
          ((twistedInverseImage f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj K).obj)),
      IsIso ((Adjunction.ofIsLeftAdjoint (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := Y.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)).ι).homEquiv
        ⟨_, StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f ⟨_, hsrc⟩⟩ _
        (sheafyTrace f
          (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf))
          (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf))
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
          (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)) L K))
declarations.comment: if RHom(L, a(K)) is in D_QCoh, erase DQ_Y on the left hand side of the arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_coherator_counit_comp_sheafyTrace_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEV], erasing `DQ_Y` on the right.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, `L ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. If
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, the map
`DQ_Y(Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K))) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`, the counit of the coherator followed by
the trace of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H], is an isomorphism. All derived categories are at the standard
model.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coherator_counit_comp_sheafyTrace_of_qcqs :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard X.Modules
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard Y.Modules
    ∀ (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
      (_htgt : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := Y.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj
          (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj)),
      IsIso ((Adjunction.ofIsLeftAdjoint (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := Y.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)).ι).counit.app _ ≫
        sheafyTrace f
          (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf))
          (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf))
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
          (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)) L K)
declarations.comment: if RHom(Rf_*L, K) is in D_QCoh, erase DQ_Y on the right hand side of the arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_derivedCategoryB_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEV], both sides in `D_QCoh`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, `L ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. If
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K))` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, the
trace `Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H] is an isomorphism.
All derived categories are at the standard model.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafyTrace_of_derivedCategoryB_of_qcqs :
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard X.Modules
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard Y.Modules
    ∀ (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
      (_hsrc : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj
          ((twistedInverseImage f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj K).obj))
      (_htgt : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := Y.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj
          (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj)),
      IsIso (sheafyTrace f
          (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf))
          (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf))
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
          (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
            (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)) L K)
declarations.comment: if both RHom's are in D_QCoh, then the map of Tag 0B6H is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_derivedCategoryB
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEV], the quasi-coherence criterion.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
schemes along which `Rf_*` preserves quasi-coherence of cohomology, let `a` be a right adjoint
of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, let `DQ_Y` be a right adjoint of the inclusion
`D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D(𝒪_Y)`, and let `L` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. If
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K))` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`,
then the sheafy trace map

`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`

of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H] is an isomorphism.

Both sides then lie in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` — the left one because `Rf_*` preserves quasi-coherence of
cohomology, which is the content of the source's `DQ_Y ∘ Rf_* = Rf_* ∘ DQ_X` — so the counit of
the coherator adjunction is invertible at both, and the trace is an isomorphism because
[Stacks, Tag 0A9Q] makes it one after `DQ_Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafyTrace_of_derivedCategoryB
    (hsrc : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj (a.obj K).obj))
    (htgt : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj
        (op ((derivedPushforward f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj))
    (h0A9Q : IsIso (DQY.map (sheafyTrace f DX DY hpush adj L K))) :
    IsIso (sheafyTrace f DX DY hpush adj L K)
declarations.comment: the quasi-coherence criterion: the trace is an isomorphism once both derived internal Homs have quasi-coherent cohomology, granted Tag 0A9Q (the trace is an isomorphism after the coherator) as the explicit hypothesis h0A9Q, and the coherator of Tag 0CR0 as data

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEV] (1), the perfect case.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_derivedCategoryB`, the sheafy trace map

`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`

is an isomorphism whenever `L` and `Rf_*L` are perfect.

Since `a(K)` and `K` have quasi-coherent cohomology, the part of [Stacks, Tag 0A6H] for a
perfect first argument puts `R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K))` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`
in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, and the quasi-coherence criterion applies. No hypothesis on `K` beyond
quasi-coherence of its cohomology is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafyTrace_of_isPerfect
    (h0A6HX : ∀ (M N : DerivedCategory X.Modules),
      RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) M →
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) N →
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op M)).obj N))
    (h0A6HY : ∀ (M N : DerivedCategory Y.Modules),
      RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace) M →
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf) N →
      DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op M)).obj N))
    (h0A9Q : IsIso (DQY.map (sheafyTrace f DX DY hpush adj L K))) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) L.obj →
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
      ((quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f hpush).obj L).obj →
    IsIso (sheafyTrace f DX DY hpush adj L K)
declarations.comment: clause (1), the perfect case, granted Tag 0A9Q as the explicit hypothesis h0A9Q, the perfect half of Tag 0A6H as h0A6HX and h0A6HY, and the coherator of Tag 0CR0 as data

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GEV] (2), the bounded-below pseudo-coherent case.** In the situation of
`Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_derivedCategoryB`, the sheafy trace map

`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)`

is an isomorphism whenever `K` is bounded below and `L` and `Rf_*L` are pseudo-coherent.

The right adjoint `a` carries bounded-below complexes to bounded-below complexes by
[Stacks, Tag 0A9I], so `a(K)` lies in `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)`; part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0A6H], for a
pseudo-coherent first argument and a bounded-below second argument, then puts
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K))` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, and the
quasi-coherence criterion applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafyTrace_of_isPseudoCoherent
    (h0A9I : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj →
      DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow (a.obj K).obj)
    (h0A9Q : IsIso (DQY.map (sheafyTrace f DX DY hpush adj L K))) :
    DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj →
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) L.obj →
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
      ((quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f hpush).obj L).obj →
    IsIso (sheafyTrace f DX DY hpush adj L K)
declarations.comment: clause (2), the bounded-below pseudo-coherent case, granted Tag 0A9Q as the explicit hypothesis h0A9Q, Tag 0A9I as h0A9I, and the coherator of Tag 0CR0 as data

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.sheafyTrace_quasiCoherent_criteria
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GEV.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated
schemes, `a` the right adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, `DQ_X`, `DQ_Y` the
coherators, `L ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then
`DQ_Y(Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K))) ≅ Rf_*DQ_X(R𝓗om(L, a(K)))` ([Stacks, Tag 0CR1]), and the map
`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H] is an isomorphism if
(1) `L` and `Rf_*L` are perfect, or (2) `K` is bounded below and `L` and `Rf_*L` are
pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafyTrace_quasiCoherent_criteria (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    Nonempty ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := Y.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)).ι.rightAdjoint.obj
          ((derivedPushforward f).obj (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj
            (op L.obj)).obj ((twistedInverseImage f
              (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj K).obj)) ≅
        (quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj
          ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).ι.rightAdjoint.obj
              (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj (op L.obj)).obj
                ((twistedInverseImage f
                  (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj K).obj))) ∧
    (RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) L.obj →
      RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj L).obj →
      IsIso (sheafyTrace f
        (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf))
        (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf))
        (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
        (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)) L K)) ∧
    (DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj →
      RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) L.obj →
      RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)).obj L).obj →
      IsIso (sheafyTrace f
        (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf))
        (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf))
        (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
        (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
          (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)) L K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isIso_sheafyTrace_of_isProper_of_derivedCategoryBMinus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GEW.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of Noetherian schemes, let
`L ∈ D^-_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `K ∈ D^+_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then the map
`Rf_*R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*L, K)` of [Stacks, Tag 0B6H], for `a` the right
adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafyTrace_of_isProper_of_derivedCategoryBMinus [IsProper f] [IsNoetherian X]
    [IsNoetherian Y] (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus (fun N : X.Modules => N.IsCoherent) L.obj)
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj) :
    IsIso (sheafyTrace f
      (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf))
      (derivedTensorHomAdjunction (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Y.sheaf))
      (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)
      (twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
        (StandardModel.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward f)) L K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_section
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GEY.** The canonical small étale sheaf descent functor for a morphism of schemes
admitting a section is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_section
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (s : Y ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_integral
declarations.doc: An integral surjection is an effective descent morphism for small étale sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_integral
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] [IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (devissage : ∀ {X' Y' Z' : B.Scheme} (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Z' ⟶ Y'),
      Surjective (B.inclusion.map g') → IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map g') →
      (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B (pullback.snd f' g')).IsEquivalence →
      (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B
        (pullback.snd f' (pullback.fst g' g' ≫ g'))).IsEquivalence →
      (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f').IsEquivalence) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
conditional.  Carried as the hypothesis `devissage`: the integral branch of the
base-change criterion [Stacks, Tag 0GF1], namely that descent along a morphism is effective once
it is effective after base change along a surjective integral morphism `g` and after base change
along `pullback.fst g g ≫ g`.  Proved here: an integral surjection `f` satisfies every hypothesis
of that criterion for the covering `g = f`, because the two base changes of `f` that occur there
are split -- by the diagonal and by the graph of the first projection -- so that descent is
effective along them.  NOT proved: that the source's equalizer construction is a quasi-inverse.
The construction itself is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDescentSheaf`, with its comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDescentComparison`, and the stalkwise criterion [Stacks, Tag 03PU]
is available as `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_bijective_etaleStalkMap`; what is missing is the
compatibility of the construction with base change [Stacks, Tag 0EYP], which the library carries
only conditionally on a presentation of an integral morphism by finite ones.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_integral_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a surjective integral morphism of a big étale site. The functor from sheaves
of sets on the small étale site of `Y` to descent data for `{X ⟶ Y}` is an equivalence of
categories.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_integral_unconditional
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] [IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctorGeneral B f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_proper_of_section
declarations.doc:
A proper surjection admitting a section is an effective descent morphism for small étale
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_proper_of_section
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] [IsProper (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (s : Y ⟶ X) (hs : s ≫ f = 𝟙 Y) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
the case of a proper surjection admitting a section, proved unconditionally.  This
case is degenerate: the conclusion for a split morphism is already [Stacks, Tag 0GEY], so neither
surjectivity nor properness enters the proof.  No other case of the source statement is proved
unconditionally.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_proper
declarations.doc: A proper surjection is an effective descent morphism for small étale sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_surjective_proper
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] [IsProper (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (devissage : ∀ {X' Y' Z' : B.Scheme} (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Z' ⟶ Y'),
      Surjective (B.inclusion.map g') → IsProper (B.inclusion.map g') →
      (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B (pullback.snd f' g')).IsEquivalence →
      (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B
        (pullback.snd f' (pullback.fst g' g' ≫ g'))).IsEquivalence →
      (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f').IsEquivalence) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
conditional.  Carried as the hypothesis `devissage`: the proper branch of the
base-change criterion [Stacks, Tag 0GF1], namely that descent along a morphism is effective once
it is effective after base change along a surjective proper morphism `g` and after base change
along `pullback.fst g g ≫ g`.  Proved here: a proper surjection `f` satisfies every hypothesis of
that criterion for the covering `g = f`, because the two base changes of `f` that occur there are
split -- by the diagonal and by the graph of the first projection -- so that descent is effective
along them.  NOT proved: the source's own argument for this lemma, that is the proof of
[Stacks, Tag 0GEZ] rerun with the proper base-change theorem [Stacks, Tag 0A3U] in place of
[Stacks, Tag 0EYP].

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_isProper_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Effective descent of small étale sheaves along a proper surjection.** For a surjective
proper morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of a big étale site, the functor sending a sheaf of sets on the small
étale site of `Y` to its canonical descent datum for `{X ⟶ Y}` is an equivalence of
categories.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_isProper_of_surjective
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] [IsProper (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Descent of small étale sheaves along `f : X ⟶ Y` is effective as soon as it is effective
along the structure morphism `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Y` of the base change of `f` along a morphism
`g : Z ⟶ Y` admitting a section.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_baseChange
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y Z : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (s : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hs : s ≫ g = 𝟙 Y)
    (hXZ : (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B (pullback.fst f g ≫ f)).IsEquivalence) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
only the case of a `g` admitting a section, and with the two hypotheses of the
source -- effectivity over `Z` and over `Z ×_Y Z` -- replaced by effectivity of descent along
the base change `X ×_Y Z` read along its structure morphism to `Y` rather than along its
projection to `Z`. The surjective integral and the surjective proper cases, where the content of
the source lemma lies (these are the cases in which 0GEZ resp. 0GF0 supplies effective descent
along `g`), are NOT proved here; neither is the passage from effectivity over `Z` and over
`Z ×_Y Z` to effectivity over `Y` of the base change.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_baseChange_id
declarations.doc:
Descent of small étale sheaves along `f : X ⟶ Y` is effective as soon as it is effective
along the projection `X ×_Y Y ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_baseChange_id
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hZ : (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B (pullback.snd f (𝟙 Y))).IsEquivalence) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
the case `Z = Y`, `g = 𝟙 Y` of the source statement, with the hypothesis in the
shape the source gives it, namely effectivity along the projection `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z`.  The hypothesis
over `Z ×_Y Z` is not needed in this case.  No other case of the source statement is proved.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_baseChange_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Descent of small étale sheaves, tested after a surjective integral or proper base
change.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of a big étale site, with `g` surjective
and either integral or proper. If the functors from sheaves on the small étale sites of `Z` and
of `Z ×_Y Z` to descent data for `{X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z}` and for `{X ×_Y (Z ×_Y Z) ⟶ Z ×_Y Z}` are
equivalences of categories, then so is the functor from sheaves on the small étale site of `Y`
to descent data for `{X ⟶ Y}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_baseChange_of_surjective
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y Z : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map g)]
    (hg : IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map g) ∨ IsProper (B.inclusion.map g))
    (hZ : (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B (pullback.snd f g)).IsEquivalence)
    (hZZ : (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B
      (pullback.snd f (pullback.fst g g ≫ g))).IsEquivalence) :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor B f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_fppf_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GF2].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of a big étale site which is
surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then the canonical functor from sheaves on
the small étale site of `Y` to descent data for `{X ⟶ Y}` is an equivalence of categories.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0GF3] for the one-member fppf covering `{f}`,
`smallEtaleSheafFamilyDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_fppfCovering_unconditional`, whose
proof is the source's proof of this lemma: the problem is local on `Y`, which reduces it to a
quasi-compact quasi-separated base; there [Stacks, Tag 0CP0] supplies a finite surjective
`Z ⟶ Y` with an open covering of `Z` factoring through `X`, the dévissage of [Stacks, Tag 0GF1]
replaces `Y` by `Z` and `Z ×_Y Z`, and over those `f` has sections Zariski locally, which is
[Stacks, Tag 0GEY] after localizing once more.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_fppf_unconditional
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X Y : B.Scheme} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)]
    [Flat (B.inclusion.map f)] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (smallEtaleSheafDescentFunctorGeneral B f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSheafFamilyDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_fppfCovering_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GF3].** Let `{f i : X i ⟶ Y}` be a family of morphisms of a big étale site
whose underlying family of morphisms of schemes is an fppf covering. Then the canonical functor
from sheaves on the small étale site of `Y` to descent data for small étale sheaves with respect
to the covering is an equivalence of categories.

The base is covered by affine opens `V k`; each `V k ×_Y V l` and each `V k ×_Y V l ×_Y V m` is
an open subscheme of the affine `V k`, hence quasi-separated, so the quasi-separated case
`smallEtaleSheafFamilyDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_fppfCovering_of_quasiSeparated`
applies to the base change of the covering to each of them, and descent is local on the base
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_toDescentData_smallEtaleSheafPullbackSystem_of_openCover`).
The quasi-separated case is reduced in the same way to the quasi-compact quasi-separated case,
which is the source's argument for [Stacks, Tag 0GF2] run for a family: [Stacks, Tag 0CP0], the
integral branch of [Stacks, Tag 0GF1], and sections Zariski locally. The source instead applies
[Stacks, Tag 0GF2] to the single morphism `∐ X i ⟶ Y`; the family is treated directly here.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtaleSheafFamilyDescentFunctor_isEquivalence_of_fppfCovering_unconditional
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {I : Type t} {X : I → B.Scheme} {Y : B.Scheme} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ B.inclusion.obj (X i)) (fun i ↦ B.inclusion.map (f i)) ∈
      Scheme.fppfPrecoverage (B.inclusion.obj Y)) :
    (smallEtaleSheafFamilyDescentFunctorGeneral B f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isEquivalence_smallEtaleSheafToCategoricalPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GF4.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a proper morphism of schemes, `i : Z ⟶ X`
a closed immersion and `E = Z ×_X X'` with projections `j : E ⟶ X'` and `g : E ⟶ Z`. If `f` is
an isomorphism over the open complement `U` of `Z`, the functor
`Sh(X_étale) ⥤ Sh(X'_étale) ×_{Sh(E_étale)} Sh(Z_étale)`, `F ↦ (f⁻¹ F, i⁻¹ F, c)` with `c` the
canonical isomorphism `j⁻¹ f⁻¹ F ≅ g⁻¹ i⁻¹ F`, is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_smallEtaleSheafToCategoricalPullback (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set X) = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ) [IsIso (f ∣_ U)] :
    (smallEtaleSheafToCategoricalPullback.{u, 0} f i j g sq.w).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigHOver.isStackInGroupoids_etaleSheafGroupoid
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GF5.** The category fibred in groupoids over the big h site `(Sch/S)_h` whose fibre
over `U` is the category of sheaves on the small étale site of `U` is a stack in groupoids.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.sheafGivesSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `Y` be an algebraic space over `S` and `𝓕` a sheaf of sets on its small étale site,
satisfying the set-theoretic condition of the source's proof. Write `G` for the corresponding
sheaf on the spaces-étale site (Stacks 03G1) and `X` for the functor
`T ↦ {(y, s) | y : T → Y, s ∈ Γ(T, y⁻¹ 𝓕)}` on `(Sch/S)_fppf`. Then

1. `X` is an algebraic space;
2. the map `X → Y`, `(y, s) ↦ y`, is étale;
3. via `Sh(Y_étale) = Sh(Y_{spaces,étale})`, `𝓕 ≅ h_X`, where `h_X(U)` is the set of
   morphisms `U → X` over `Y` of functors on `(Sch/S)_fppf`;
4. `X` is the (universe-lifted) functor of points of an algebraic space `X'`, under which the
   map `X → Y` is an étale morphism `f : X' → Y`; the inverse image `f_small⁻¹` has a left
   adjoint `f_{small,!}` (Stacks 03LP), and for every such left adjoint `𝓕 ≅ f_{small,!} *`,
   where `*` is the terminal sheaf on `X'_étale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafGivesSpace (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hF : SheafGivesSpace.SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS Y F) :
    IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (sheafPairsFunctor B S hS ((smallEtaleToposEquiv B S hS Y).inverse.obj F)) ∧
      IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (sheafPairsFunctorToBase B S hS ((smallEtaleToposEquiv B S hS Y).inverse.obj F)) ∧
      Nonempty (((smallEtaleToposEquiv B S hS Y).inverse.obj F).obj ≅
        sheafPairsHom B S hS ((smallEtaleToposEquiv B S hS Y).inverse.obj F)) ∧
      ∃ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : X' ⟶ Y) (_ : IsEtale B S hS f.hom)
        (ι : sheafPairsFunctor B S hS ((smallEtaleToposEquiv B S hS Y).inverse.obj F) ≅
          X'.obj ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1}),
        sheafPairsFunctorToBase B S hS ((smallEtaleToposEquiv B S hS Y).inverse.obj F) =
            ι.hom ≫ Functor.whiskerRight f.hom uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ∧
          (∃ L : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X'.1) (Type (u + 1)) ⥤
              Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (Type (u + 1)),
            Nonempty (L ⊣ (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage)) ∧
          ∀ (L : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X'.1) (Type (u + 1)) ⥤
              Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (Type (u + 1)))
            (_ : L ⊣ (smallToposMorphism B S hS f).inverseImage),
            Nonempty (F ≅ L.obj (⊤_ (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X'.1) (Type (u + 1)))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_and_supportOfSheaf_eq_univ_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
finite and surjective, with `X` locally Noetherian.  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion, let
`i' : Z' ⟶ Y` be the inverse image of `Z`, and let `f' : Z' ⟶ Z` be the induced morphism.  Then
`𝒢 = f'_*𝒪_{Z'}` is a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module whose support is all of `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_and_supportOfSheaf_eq_univ_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage
    {Z Z' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X) (i : Z ⟶ X) {i' : Z' ⟶ Y} {f' : Z' ⟶ Z}
    (sq : IsPullback i' f' f i) (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    IsCoherent B S hS Z.1 Z.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS f').obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z'))) ∧
      supportOfSheaf B S hS Z.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
        ((modulePushforward B S hS f').obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z')))) = Set.univ
declarations.comment: the whole statement: for f finite and surjective with X locally Noetherian and i : Z -> X a closed immersion, the direct image f'_* O_{Z'} along the induced morphism of the inverse image is a coherent O_Z-module, and its support is all of Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage
declarations.doc:
**The coherence assertion of Stacks 0GF7, granted the chart case `hchart`.**  Let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` locally Noetherian, let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion, and let `f' : Z' ⟶ Z` be the base change of `f` along `i`.
Then `𝒢 = f'_*𝒪_{Z'}` is a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module.

`Z` is locally Noetherian by Stacks 06ED and 04ZK, `f'` is finite by Stacks 03ZS, `Z'` is
locally Noetherian for the same reason as `Z`, and `𝒪_{Z'}` is then coherent by Stacks 07UB; so
this is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isFinite`, whose hypothesis
`hchart` is the étale-site form of Stacks 01Y6, that is Stacks 03DW, which this development
does not carry.  Surjectivity of `f` is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage (f : Y ⟶ X) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    {i' : Z' ⟶ Y} {f' : Z' ⟶ Z} (sq : IsPullback i' f' f i)
    (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (V : SmallEtale B S hS Z.1) (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS V.1.hom)
    (hchart : IsFinite B S hS (chartBaseChangeProjection B S hS f' V).hom →
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS
        ((SpacesEtale.toSpaces B S hS Z).obj ((comparisonFunctor B S hS Z).obj V)).1
        (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) →
      IsCoherent B S hS Z'.1 Z'.2 (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z')) →
      ((chartLocalizedModulePushforward B S hS f' V).obj
        ((moduleChartBaseChangeRestriction B S hS f' V).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z')))).IsCoherentOnSite) :
    IsCoherent B S hS Z.1 Z.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS f').obj
      (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z')))
declarations.comment: coherence of the direct image, granted the chart case hchart of Stacks 03DW which Tag 07UH already carries

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**The support assertion of Stacks 0GF7.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a surjective morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be any morphism and let `f' : Z' ⟶ Z` be the base
change of `f` along `i`.  Then the support of `𝒢 = f'_*𝒪_{Z'}` is all of `Z`.

Surjectivity is stable under base change by Stacks 03MH, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_eq_univ`.  Neither the
finiteness of `f`, nor the local Noetherianity of `X`, nor the closedness of the immersion `i`
is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage_eq_univ (f : Y ⟶ X) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    {i' : Z' ⟶ Y} {f' : Z' ⟶ Z} (sq : IsPullback i' f' f i)
    (hf : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS Z.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
        ((modulePushforward B S hS f').obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z')))) = Set.univ
declarations.comment: the support of the direct image is all of Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**The coherence assertion of Stacks 0GF7.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` locally Noetherian, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion,
and let `f' : Z' ⟶ Z` be the base change of `f` along `i`.  Then `𝒢 = f'_*𝒪_{Z'}` is a
coherent `𝒪_Z`-module.

`Z` is locally Noetherian by Stacks 06ED and 04ZK, `f'` is finite by Stacks 03ZS, `Z'` is
locally Noetherian for the same reason as `Z`, and `𝒪_{Z'}` is then coherent by Stacks 07UB; so
this is Stacks 07UH,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isFinite'`.
Surjectivity of `f` is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_modulePushforward_structureSheaf_preimage_of_isLocallyNoetherian (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) {i' : Z' ⟶ Y} {f' : Z' ⟶ Z} (sq : IsPullback i' f' f i)
    (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom) :
    IsCoherent B S hS Z.1 Z.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS f').obj
      (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z')))
declarations.comment: coherence of the direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealSmul_pushforward_eq_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GF8.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent sheaf on `Y` and let `I` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals on `X`.  If `f` is affine then

`I · f_*F = f_*((f⁻¹I) · F)`

as subsheaves of `f_*F`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealSmul_pushforward_eq` with quasi-coherence, rather than
the equivalent cartesian condition on affine charts, as the hypothesis of the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealSmul_pushforward_eq_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (hI : I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    Stacks.Sites.idealSmul (O := structureSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2)
        I (⊤ : ((smallBaseChangeModulePushforward B S hS f
          (relativelyRepresentable_hom_of_isAffineHom B S hS f haff)).obj F).Submodule) =
      pushforwardSubmodule B S hS f
        (relativelyRepresentable_hom_of_isAffineHom B S hS f haff) F
        (Stacks.Sites.idealSmul (O := structureSheaf B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
          (pullbackIdealSubsheaf B S hS f
            (relativelyRepresentable_hom_of_isAffineHom B S hS f haff) I) (⊤ : F.Submodule))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_isAmple_of_isProper_toAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFA.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space proper over a Noetherian ring `R` — here an
affine object `V` of the site with `Γ(V, 𝒪_V) = R` Noetherian and a proper `f : X ⟶ h_V` — and let
`𝓛` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module.  The following are equivalent:

1. `X` is a scheme and `𝓛` is ample on it: there are an object `U` of the site and an
   isomorphism `e : h_U ≅ X` for which the restriction of `𝓛` to `U` is an invertible and ample
   module;
2. for every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` there is an `n₀ ≥ 0` with `H ᵖ(X, 𝓕 ⊗ 𝓛^{⊗ n}) = 0` for
   all `n ≥ n₀` and `p > 0`;
3. for every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` there is an `n ≥ 1` with `H¹(X, 𝓕 ⊗ 𝓛^{⊗ n}) = 0`.

(1) ⟹ (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isZero_rightDerived_twistStep_of_isAmple` (Serre's
vanishing theorem on the scheme, Stacks 0B5T), (2) ⟹ (3) is immediate, and (3) ⟹ (1) is Stacks
0D2W (`exists_isAmple_of_forall_isCoherent_isZero_rightDerived_one_twistStep`), `X` being
Noetherian as it is proper over a Noetherian affine scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isAmple_of_isProper_toAffine
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    [IsNoetherianRing Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V, ⊤)]
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace V) (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS X.1)
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).property L] :
    have := enoughInjectives_modules B S hS X.1 X.2
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (eX : yoneda.obj U ≅ X.1)
        (_ : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
          (baseChangeModule B S hS L U eX.hom)),
        Stacks.Ample.IsAmple ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
          (baseChangeModule B S hS L U eX.hom),
      ∀ F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F →
        ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n → ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p →
          IsZero (((globalSectionsFunctor.{u + 1, u, u, u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O)).rightDerived p).obj
              (twistStep B S hS X.1 X.2 L n F)),
      ∀ F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F →
        ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ IsZero (((globalSectionsFunctor.{u + 1, u, u, u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
              (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O)).rightDerived 1).obj
            (twistStep B S hS X.1 X.2 L n F))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAmple_iff_exists_isAmple_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFB.**  Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `X` an algebraic space proper over `R` — a
proper `pX : X ⟶ h_V` with `V` affine and `Γ(V, 𝒪_V) = R` — and `f : Y ⟶ X` a finite surjective
morphism of algebraic spaces.  Let `𝓛` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module.  Then `X` is a scheme and `𝓛`
is ample on it if and only if `Y` is a scheme and `f^*𝓛` is ample on it.

A scheme is an object `U` of the site with an isomorphism `h_U ≅ X`, and `𝓛` is ample on it when
its restriction to `U` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangeModule`) is invertible and ample.  The
source also assumes `Y` proper over `R`; that follows, a finite morphism being proper.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_iff_exists_isAmple_modulePullback
    (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V)]
    [IsNoetherianRing Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V, ⊤)]
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (pX : X ⟶ schemeSpace V) (hpX : IsProper B S hS pX.hom)
    (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom) (hfs : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom)
    (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS X.1)
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O).property L] :
    (∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (eX : yoneda.obj U ≅ X.1)
      (_ : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
        (baseChangeModule B S hS L U eX.hom)),
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
        (baseChangeModule B S hS L U eX.hom)) ↔
    ∃ (U' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (eY : yoneda.obj U' ≅ Y.1)
      (_ : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U')
        (baseChangeModule B S hS ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj L) U' eY.hom)),
      Stacks.Ample.IsAmple ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U')
        (baseChangeModule B S hS ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj L) U' eY.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangEnvelope_eq_isPerfect_of_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFC.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, and
let `G` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` which is a generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. Then `G` is a
classical generator of `D_perf(𝒪_X)`: the triangulated envelope of `G` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` — its
closure under shifts, finite direct sums, extensions and direct summands — is exactly the property
of being perfect.

The source combines [Stacks, Tag 08F3] (direct sums in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`), [Stacks, Tag 09M8]
(compact equals perfect) and [Stacks, Tag 09SR] (a compact generator classically generates the
compact objects). Such a `G` exists by [Stacks, Tag 09IY]; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_triangEnvelope_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangEnvelope_eq_isPerfect_of_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (G : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hG : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect G.obj)
    (hgen : (ObjectProperty.singleton G).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator) :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton G).triangEnvelope =
      fun E => (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect E.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_triangEnvelope_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFC, the existence clause.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space
`X` over `S` there is a perfect object `G` of `D(𝒪_X)` which is a generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
([Stacks, Tag 09IY]), and every such `G` is a classical generator of `D_perf(𝒪_X)`: its
triangulated envelope in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is the property of being perfect. The generator is the
compact generator of `exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_qcqs`, perfect by
[Stacks, Tag 09M8], exactly as in the proof of `exists_isPerfect_generator`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_triangEnvelope_eq
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1) :
    ∃ G : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect G.obj ∧
        (ObjectProperty.singleton G).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator ∧
          (ObjectProperty.singleton G).triangEnvelope =
            fun E => (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect E.obj
declarations.comment: the existence of a perfect generator G of D_QCoh(O_X), by 09IY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.triangEnvelope_singleton_eq_isPerfect_of_supported
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, and
`T ⊆ |X|` a closed subset such that `|X| ∖ T` is quasi-compact. Let `G` be a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)` lying in `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` (quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves supported on `T`) which is
a generator of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)`: an object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` supported on `T` with
`Hom(G[n], E) = 0` for all `n ∈ ℤ` is zero. Then `G` is a classical generator of
`D_{perf,T}(𝒪_X)`: the triangulated envelope of `G` in `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` — the smallest strictly
full, saturated, triangulated subcategory containing `G` — is exactly the property of being
perfect in `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangEnvelope_singleton_eq_isPerfect_of_supported (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ)
    (G : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hG : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect G)
    (hGq : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O))) G)
    (hGs : CohomologySupportedOn B S hS X.1 X.2 T G)
    (hgen : ∀ E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
      CohomologySupportedOn B S hS X.1 X.2 T E.obj →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (g : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj), g = 0) → IsZero E.obj) :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton
        (⟨⟨G, hGq⟩, hGs⟩ : (quasicoherentDerivedSupportedOn X T).FullSubcategory)).triangEnvelope =
      fun K => (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect K.obj.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncGE_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GFF].**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S`, let `P` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, let `E` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and let `a` be an integer.  Then

1. `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦-i⟧, E) = 0` for `i ≫ 0`

if and only if

2. `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦-i⟧, τ_{≥a}E) = 0` for `i ≫ 0`,

where `τ_{≥a}` is the canonical truncation of `D(𝒪_X)` and vanishing of a Hom-group is
subsingletonness of the morphism type, the derived category being additive.

Both implications are the truncation triangle
`τ_{≤a-1}E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥a}E ⟶ (τ_{≤a-1}E)⟦1⟧`: a morphism `P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E` which dies in `τ_{≥a}E`
factors through `τ_{≤a-1}E`, and a morphism `P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ τ_{≥a}E` which dies in `(τ_{≤a-1}E)⟦1⟧`
factors through `E`.  So each direction needs only that `τ_{≤a-1}E` and `(τ_{≤a-1}E)⟦1⟧` receive
no nonzero morphism from `P⟦-i⟧` for `i` large; both lie in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and are bounded above,
by `a - 1` and `a - 2`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_threshold_subsingleton_hom_negShift_of_isPerfect` kills both from
`i ≥ a - 1 + c` on, with `c` the threshold that perfectness of `P` supplies through
[Stacks, Tag 09MB].
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncGE_of_isPerfect
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)]
    (P E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPerfect P)
    (hE : ∀ j : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) j).obj
      E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (a : ℤ) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i →
        Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncLE_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GFG].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space over `S`, let `P` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, let `E` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and let `a` be an integer. Then

1. `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦-i⟧, E) = 0` for `i ≪ 0`, and
2. `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦-i⟧, τ_{≤a}E) = 0` for `i ≪ 0`

are equivalent.

A perfect object on a quasi-compact algebraic space is bounded above
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLE_of_isPerfect`), and for a `P` bounded above the equivalence
is t-structure orthogonality against the truncation triangle
`τ_{≤a}E ⟶ E ⟶ τ_{≥a+1}E ⟶`, which is
`Stacks.DerivedTruncation.eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncLE`. Quasi-separatedness of `X` and
quasi-coherence of the cohomology sheaves of `E` are hypotheses of the source that this argument
does not read.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_subsingleton_hom_iff_truncLE_of_isPerfect
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (_hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPerfect P)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (_hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) i).obj
      E).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (a : ℤ) :
    (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ N → Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E)) ↔
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ N →
        Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE a).obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_isLE_of_isPerfect_generator
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isLE_of_isPerfect_generator (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (G : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hG : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect G)
    (hgen : ∀ E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
      (∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (G⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj)) → IsZero E.obj)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ a : ℤ, E.obj.IsLE a,
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (G⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E.obj),
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (G ⟶ E.obj⟦i⟧),
      ∃ a : ℤ, ((derivedModuleGlobalSectionsSmallEtaleAtModel B S hS X.1 X.2).obj
        (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op G)).obj E.obj)).IsLE a,
      ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (globalSectionRingSmallEtale B S hS X.1 X.2)) i).obj
          ((derivedModuleGlobalSectionsSmallEtaleAtModel B S hS X.1 X.2).obj
            (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B S hS X).obj
              (smallEtaleDerivedDual B S hS X G)).obj E.obj))),
      ∃ a : ℤ, ((derivedModuleGlobalSectionsSmallEtaleAtModel B S hS X.1 X.2).obj
          (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B S hS X).obj
            (smallEtaleDerivedDual B S hS X G)).obj E.obj)).IsLE a,
      ∀ P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
        (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect P →
          (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (P⟦-i⟧ ⟶ E.obj)) ∧
          (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → Subsingleton (P ⟶ E.obj⟦i⟧)) ∧
          (∃ a : ℤ, ((derivedModuleGlobalSectionsSmallEtaleAtModel B S hS X.1 X.2).obj
            (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op P)).obj E.obj)).IsLE a) ∧
          (∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (globalSectionRingSmallEtale B S hS X.1 X.2)) i).obj
              ((derivedModuleGlobalSectionsSmallEtaleAtModel B S hS X.1 X.2).obj
                (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B S hS X).obj P).obj E.obj)))) ∧
          (∃ a : ℤ, ((derivedModuleGlobalSectionsSmallEtaleAtModel B S hS X.1 X.2).obj
              (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B S hS X).obj P).obj E.obj)).IsLE a)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_of_isPseudoCoherent_derivedSections_tensor_perfect
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space separated and of finite presentation over `A` and
`K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` pseudo-coherent over `A` for every perfect `E`. Then `K`
is pseudo-coherent relative to `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPseudoCoherent_of_isPseudoCoherent_derivedSections_tensor_perfect
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) hA}
    (hsep : IsSeparated B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X).hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X).hom)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B _ hA X.1 X.2)) (hK : QcohDerived B _ hA X K)
    (h : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B _ hA X.1 X.2),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B _ hA X.1 X.2).IsPerfect E →
        StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
          ((representedAffineDerivedSections B _ hA (baseSiteObj B _ hA)).obj
            ((derivedModulePushforward B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X)).obj
              (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B _ hA X).obj E).obj K)))) :
    IsRelativelyPseudoCoherent B _ hA X.1 X.2 (toBase B _ hA X).hom
      (isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation B _ hA hfp.1) ⟨K, hK⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPerfectRelativeToCanonical_iff_isLocallyBoundedBelow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFK.** Let `f : X ⟶ T` be a morphism from an algebraic space to a scheme which is
flat and locally of finite presentation, and let `E ∈ D(𝒪_X)` be pseudo-coherent. Then `E` is
`T`-perfect exactly when `E` is locally bounded below and, for every point `s ∈ T`, the derived
pullback `L(X_s ⟶ X)^*E` to the fibre `X_s = X ×_T Spec κ(s)` is locally bounded below.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfectRelativeToCanonical_iff_isLocallyBoundedBelow (f : X ⟶ representedSpace T)
    (hfl : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (hlfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f.hom)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPseudoCoherent E) :
    IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS f hfl hlfp E ↔
      IsLocallyBoundedBelow X E ∧ ∀ s : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T,
        IsLocallyBoundedBelow (residueFibre f s)
          ((smallEtaleDerivedModulePullback B S hS (residueFibreι f s)).obj E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.isPerfectRelativeToCanonical_of_isPerfect_derivedSections
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a ring and `X` an algebraic space separated, of finite presentation and flat over
`A`. Let `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. If `RΓ(X, E ⊗^𝐋 K)` is perfect in `D(A)` for every perfect
`E ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, then `K` is `Spec(A)`-perfect.

Here `K` is an object of the full subcategory `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` of `D(𝒪_X)` (Stacks 071X), and
`RΓ(X, -)` with values in `D(A)` is `RΓ(Spec A, Rf_*(-))` for the structure morphism
`f : X ⟶ Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.isPerfectRelativeToCanonical_of_isPerfect_derivedSections
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) hA}
    (hsep : IsSeparated B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X).hom)
    (hfp : IsFinitePresentation B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X).hom)
    (hfl : IsFlat B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X).hom)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B _ hA X.1 X.2)
    (h : ∀ E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B _ hA X.1 X.2),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B _ hA X.1 X.2).IsPerfect E →
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect
          ((representedAffineDerivedSections B _ hA (baseSiteObj B _ hA)).obj
            ((derivedModulePushforward B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X)).obj
              (((smallEtaleDerivedTensor B _ hA X).obj E).obj K.obj)))) :
    IsPerfectRelativeToCanonical.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B _ hA (toBase B _ hA X) hfl hfp.1 K.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isColimit_of_separated_etale_descent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFP.** Let `B` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `D` be a diagram of
algebraic spaces separated over `B`, with a colimit `c` in the category of algebraic spaces
separated over `B`. Assume that the members of the diagram jointly cover the vertex on points,
that every separated étale algebraic space over the vertex is the colimit of its base changes
to the members of the diagram, and that every compatible family of separated étale algebraic
spaces over the members of the diagram arises as the family of base changes of a separated
étale algebraic space over the vertex. Then `c` is a colimit of the diagram in the category of
*all* algebraic spaces over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isColimit_of_separated_etale_descent
    (D : I ⥤ SeparatedOver site S hS B) (c : Cocone D) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (hcover : ∀ x : points site S hS c.pt.obj.left.obj,
      ∃ i : I, ∃ y : points site S hS (D.obj i).obj.left.obj,
        pointsMap site S hS (D.obj i).obj.left.obj (c.ι.app i).hom.left.hom y = x)
    (hbase : ∀ (E : I ⥤ SeparatedOver site S hS B) (p : E ⟶ D) (d : Cocone E)
      (q : d.pt ⟶ c.pt), IsEtaleSeparated site S hS q →
      (∀ i : I, IsPullback (p.app i).hom.left (d.ι.app i).hom.left
        (c.ι.app i).hom.left q.hom.left) → IsColimit d)
    (hdesc : ∀ (E : I ⥤ SeparatedOver site S hS B) (p : E ⟶ D),
      (∀ i : I, IsEtaleSeparated site S hS (p.app i)) →
      (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsPullback (E.map f).hom.left (p.app i).hom.left
        (p.app j).hom.left (D.map f).hom.left) →
      ∃ (d : Cocone E) (q : d.pt ⟶ c.pt), IsEtaleSeparated site S hS q ∧
        ∀ i : I, IsPullback (p.app i).hom.left (d.ι.app i).hom.left
          (c.ι.app i).hom.left q.hom.left) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit ((separatedOverInclusion site S hS B).mapCocone c))
declarations.comment: all five hypotheses; (1) carried by the diagram landing in the separated spaces over B, (2) by IsColimit of the cocone there, (3) stated as joint surjectivity on points, (4) and (5) stated with cartesian comparison squares

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isColimit_of_fpqc_local
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GFQ].** Let `T` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` of a big fppf site
and let `D` be a diagram of algebraic spaces over `T` with a cocone `c`. Suppose given an fpqc
covering `f a : (d a).pt ⟶ c.pt` of the vertex such that

* every `d a` is a cocone on a diagram `E a` whose squares over `D` are cartesian, and `d a` is
  a colimit; and
* every pairwise overlap `d₂ a b` of the covering is likewise a cocone on a cartesian diagram
  `E₂ a b` over `D` and is a colimit.

Then `c` is a colimit of `D` in the category of algebraic spaces over `T`.

The base algebraic space is the source's `B`; it is called `T` here because `B` names the big
fppf site throughout this library.
declarations.statement:
theorem isColimit_of_fpqc_local
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {T : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] (D : I ⥤ Over T) (c : Cocone D)
    {A : Type t}
    (E : A → I ⥤ Over T) (d : ∀ a, Cocone (E a))
    (p : ∀ a, E a ⟶ D)
    (f : ∀ a, (d a).pt ⟶ c.pt)
    (hcover : IsFpqcCovering B S hS fun a => ((f a).left).hom)
    (hbase : ∀ (a : A) (i : I),
      IsPullback ((p a).app i).left ((d a).ι.app i).left (c.ι.app i).left (f a).left)
    (hlocal : ∀ a, Nonempty (IsColimit (d a)))
    (E₂ : A → A → I ⥤ Over T)
    (d₂ : ∀ a b, Cocone (E₂ a b))
    (p₂ : ∀ a b, E₂ a b ⟶ D)
    (toFirst : ∀ a b, (d₂ a b).pt ⟶ (d a).pt)
    (toSecond : ∀ a b, (d₂ a b).pt ⟶ (d b).pt)
    (hoverlap : ∀ a b, IsPullback (toFirst a b).left (toSecond a b).left (f a).left (f b).left)
    (hbaseOverlap : ∀ (a b : A) (i : I),
      IsPullback ((p₂ a b).app i).left ((d₂ a b).ι.app i).left
        (c.ι.app i).left (toFirst a b ≫ f a).left)
    (hoverlapColimit : ∀ a b, Nonempty (IsColimit (d₂ a b))) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SpacesEtale.isEquivalence_toDescentData_smallEtaleSheafSystem_of_isEtaleCovering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_isEtaleCovering
declarations.doc:

étale covering. If
spaces-étale sheaves on `Y i` are equivalent, via the canonical descent datum, to descent data
for the base change `X ×_Y Y i ⟶ Y i` of `f`, and likewise over each pairwise overlap
`Y i ×_Y Y j`, then spaces-étale sheaves on `Y` are equivalent to descent data for `f`

declarations.statement:

      (fun _ : Unit => (spacesChosenPullback B S hS f (g i)).p₂)).IsEquivalence)
    (hYY : ∀ i j, ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData
      (fun _ : Unit => (spacesChosenPullback B S hS f
        (spacesChosenPullback B S hS (g i) (g j)).p).p₂)).IsEquivalence) :

      (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: for the pseudofunctor of spaces-étale inverse images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_surjective_integral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFU, the surjective integral case.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` which is representable by schemes, surjective and integral. Then spaces-étale
sheaves on `Y` are equivalent, via the canonical descent datum, to descent data for the covering
`{X ⟶ Y}`, granted the same assertion for a morphism with representable target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_surjective_integral
    (hsch : SpacesEtaleDescentOverRepresentable B S hS
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} ⊓ @AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegralHom.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom)
    (hint : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegralHom.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the surjective integral case, for the pseudofunctor of spaces-étale inverse images, granted the case of a representable target as the hypothesis `hsch`. Proved here: the étale-local reduction of the source, that is, that the conclusion for an arbitrary algebraic space `Y` follows from the case in which the target is a scheme -- a scheme atlas of `Y` is a one-member étale covering (Tag 025Y), the two base changes of `f` named by Tag 0GFT have representable target, and the representable surjective integral morphisms are stable under base change (Tag 02WE). NOT proved, and carried by `hsch`: the case of a scheme target, which the source deduces from Etale Cohomology Tag 0GEZ; that lemma is not in this library and rests in turn on the devissage of Tag 0GF1 and on the base-change theorem of Tag 0EYP. The other two cases of the source statement are separate declarations with their own hypothesis.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_surjective_proper
