declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_surjective_proper
    (hsch : SpacesEtaleDescentOverRepresentable B S hS
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} ⊓ @AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom)
    (hproper : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the surjective proper case, for the pseudofunctor of spaces-étale inverse images, granted the case of a representable target as the hypothesis `hsch`. Proved here: the étale-local reduction of the source, that is, that the conclusion for an arbitrary algebraic space `Y` follows from the case in which the target is a scheme -- a scheme atlas of `Y` is a one-member étale covering (Tag 025Y), the two base changes of `f` named by Tag 0GFT have representable target, and the representable surjective proper morphisms are stable under base change (Tag 02WE). NOT proved, and carried by `hsch`: the case of a scheme target, which the source deduces from Etale Cohomology Tag 0GF0; that lemma is not in this library and rests in turn on the devissage of Tag 0GF1 and on the proper base-change theorem of Tag 0A3U. The other two cases of the source statement are separate declarations with their own hypothesis.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_surjective_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFU, the surjective flat locally finitely presented case.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by schemes, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation. Then spaces-étale sheaves on `Y` are equivalent, via the
canonical descent datum, to descent data for the covering `{X ⟶ Y}`, granted the same assertion
for a morphism with representable target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_surjective_flat_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    (hsch : SpacesEtaleDescentOverRepresentable B S hS
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u} ⊓ @AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.{u} ⊓
          @AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom)
    (hflat : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom)
    (hlfp : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFinitePresentation.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f.hom) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the surjective flat locally-of-finite-presentation case, for the pseudofunctor of spaces-étale inverse images, granted the case of a representable target as the hypothesis `hsch`. Proved here: the étale-local reduction of the source, that is, that the conclusion for an arbitrary algebraic space `Y` follows from the case in which the target is a scheme -- a scheme atlas of `Y` is a one-member étale covering (Tag 025Y), the two base changes of `f` named by Tag 0GFT have representable target, and the representable surjective flat morphisms locally of finite presentation are stable under base change (Tag 02WE). NOT proved, and carried by `hsch`: the case of a scheme target, which the source deduces from Etale Cohomology Tag 0GF2; that lemma is not in this library and rests in turn on the devissage of Tag 0GF1 and on the finite domination of an fppf covering of Tag 0CP0. The other two cases of the source statement are separate declarations with their own hypothesis.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable (by
schemes) and is surjective and integral, or surjective and proper, or surjective, flat and locally
of finite presentation. Then the functor from sheaves on the spaces-étale site of `Y` (that is,
`Sh(Y_étale)`, Stacks 03G1) to descent data for étale sheaves with respect to `{X ⟶ Y}` is an
equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_relativelyRepresentable
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f.hom)
    (hf : IsSurjectiveIntegralProperOrFlatLfp B S hS f) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_representable_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFV for the pseudofunctor of spaces-étale inverse images.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `π : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces.
If the composite `π ≫ f` is representable by schemes and is surjective and integral, surjective
and proper, or surjective and flat and locally of finite presentation, then spaces-étale sheaves
on `Y` are equivalent, via the canonical descent datum, to descent data for the singleton family
`{X ⟶ Y}`. No hypothesis is placed on `f` itself.

The conclusion of Stacks 0GFU is granted as `h0GFU`; see the implementation notes of the file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_representable_comp
    (h0GFU : ∀ {X₀ Y₀ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀),
      yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f₀.hom →
      IsSurjectiveIntegralProperOrFlatLfp B S hS f₀ →
      ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData
        (fun _ : Unit => f₀)).IsEquivalence)
    {X' X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (π : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (π ≫ f).hom)
    (hcov : IsSurjectiveIntegralProperOrFlatLfp B S hS (π ≫ f)) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData
      (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: granted `h0GFU`, the conclusion of Stacks 0GFU: that for EVERY morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by schemes and is surjective and integral, surjective and proper, or surjective and flat and locally of finite presentation, spaces-étale sheaves on its target are equivalent to descent data for the singleton family it generates. That is the special case `π = 𝟙 X` of this statement, in which the morphism carrying the hypotheses is the morphism of the descent problem itself, so it is NOT the universally quantified form of this conclusion: this conclusion asks for descent along `f` while the hypotheses are carried by `π ≫ f`, and `f` itself is neither representable nor surjective in any instance of the grant. The implication runs one way only — the grant is an instance of this conclusion, and getting this conclusion back out of the grant is exactly the refinement step. That step, Stacks 0GEA, is proved and not granted: `CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.isEquivalence_toDescentData_of_homOver` of this file restates the library's `CategoryTheory.Functor.isEquivalence_toFamilyDescentDatum_of_homOver` at an arbitrary pseudofunctor, and its fibre-product and base-change obligations are discharged here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_relativelyRepresentable_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `π : X' ⟶ X` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces. Assume that `π ≫ f` is representable (by schemes) and is surjective
and integral, or surjective and proper, or surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation.
Then the functor from sheaves on the spaces-étale site of `Y` to descent data for étale sheaves

declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_relativelyRepresentable_comp
    {X' X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (π : X' ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (π ≫ f).hom)
    (hcov : IsSurjectiveIntegralProperOrFlatLfp B S hS (π ≫ f)) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_isSurjectiveIntegralProperOrFlatLfp
declarations.doc:

surjective and proper, or surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Then the functor
from sheaves on the spaces-étale site of `Y` to descent data for étale sheaves with respect to
`{X ⟶ Y}` is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_isSurjectiveIntegralProperOrFlatLfp
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_isSurjectiveDescentMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GFW for the pseudofunctor of spaces-étale inverse images.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is surjective and integral, or surjective and
proper, or surjective and flat and locally of finite presentation. Then sheaves on the
spaces-étale site of `Y` are equivalent, through the canonical descent datum, to descent data
for the one-member family `{f}`.

All three cases are stated. The integral and the flat case are proved from `hGFV`, which is
Stacks 0GFV; the proper case is the hypothesis `hproper`, carried whole.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_singleton_of_isSurjectiveDescentMorphism
    (hGFV : DescentEffectiveAlongRepresentablePrecomposition B S hS)
    (hproper : DescentEffectiveAlongProperSurjective B S hS)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsSurjectiveDescentMorphism B S hS f.hom) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData (fun _ : Unit => f)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: all three cases stated; the integral and flat cases are proved from Stacks 0GFV, carried as a hypothesis, and the proper case is carried whole as a hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_toDescentData_of_isFppfCovering
declarations.doc:

`S`. Then the functor from sheaves on the spaces-étale site of `Y` (that is, `Sh(Y_étale)`) to
descent data for étale sheaves with respect to `{f i : X i ⟶ Y}` is an equivalence of
categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_toDescentData_of_isFppfCovering {I : Type v}
    {X : I → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun i => (X i).1) (fun i => (f i).hom)) :
    ((spacesEtalePseudofunctor B S hS).toDescentData f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesModificationRestriction_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GFY].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a proper morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion, and let `E = Z ×_X Y` with
projections `j : E ⟶ Y` and `g : E ⟶ Z`. Suppose `f` is an isomorphism over the open complement
`u : X ∖ Z ⟶ X` of `Z`: the projection `fU : V ⟶ X ∖ Z` of a fibre product
`V = (X ∖ Z) ×_X Y` is an isomorphism. Then the functor
`Sh(X_étale) ⥤ Sh(Y_étale) ×_{Sh(E_étale)} Sh(Z_étale)`, `F ↦ (f⁻¹F, i⁻¹F)`, is an equivalence
of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_spacesModificationRestriction_of_isProper
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (sq : IsPullback j g f i)
    {V : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (w' : V ⟶ Y)
    (fU : V ⟶ closedImmersionComplement B S hS i hi) [IsIso fU]
    (sqU : IsPullback w' fU f (closedImmersionComplementHom B S hS i hi)) :
    (spacesModificationRestriction B S hS f i j g sq.w).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffective_homDescentData_of_isEtale_of_isProper_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG0.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper surjective morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S`. A descent datum relative to `f` whose underlying space is étale over `X` is effective;
more precisely, it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of an algebraic space over `Y`
which is étale over `Y`.

Two statements of the source are carried as hypotheses rather than proved: `hproperCase` is the
proper case of Stacks 0GFW, which is the case Stacks 0GG0 appeals to, and `hbridge` is the
translation between descent data of spaces and descent data of spaces-étale sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_homDescentData_of_isEtale_of_isProper_isSurjective
    (hproperCase : DescentEffectiveAlongProperSurjective B S hS)
    (hbridge : EtaleSpaceDescentEffectiveOfSheafDescent B S hS)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (D : Descent.HomDescentData.{u, 0} f.hom Y.property X.property)
    (hD : IsEtale B S hS (D.obj PUnit.unit).hom) :
    Descent.HomDescentData.IsEffective.{u, 0} D ∧
      ∃ V : Descent.AlgebraicSpacesOver (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) Y.1,
        IsEtale B S hS V.obj.hom ∧
          Nonempty ((Descent.canonicalDescentFunctor.{u, 0} f.hom Y.property
            X.property).obj V ≅ D)
declarations.comment: both the effectivity and the sharper form naming an étale V ⟶ Y, stated in the library's vocabulary for descent data of spaces; the translation between descent data of spaces and of étale sheaves and the proper case of Stacks 0GFW are carried as hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffective_and_exists_isEtale_iso_of_isProper_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG0.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper surjective morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S`. Any descent datum `(U/X, φ)` relative to `f` (Stacks 0ADG) with `U` étale over `X` is
effective (Stacks 0ADQ). More precisely, there exists an algebraic space `V` over `Y`, étale
over `Y`, whose canonical descent datum is isomorphic to `(U/X, φ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_and_exists_isEtale_iso_of_isProper_isSurjective
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) (hproper : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (D : Descent.HomDescentData.{u, 0} f.hom Y.property X.property)
    (hD : IsEtale B S hS (D.obj PUnit.unit).hom) :
    Descent.HomDescentData.IsEffective.{u, 0} D ∧
      ∃ V : Descent.AlgebraicSpacesOver (B := B) (S := S) (hS := hS) Y.1,
        IsEtale B S hS V.obj.hom ∧
          Nonempty ((Descent.canonicalDescentFunctor.{u, 0} f.hom Y.property
            X.property).obj V ≅ D)
declarations.comment: both the effectivity and the sharper form naming an étale V ⟶ Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEquivalence_spacesEtaleModificationRestriction_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GG1].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a proper morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion, and let `E = Z ×_X Y` with
projections `j : E ⟶ Y` and `g : E ⟶ Z`. Suppose `f` is an isomorphism over the open complement
`u : X ∖ Z ⟶ X` of `Z`: the projection `fU : V ⟶ X ∖ Z` of a fibre product
`V = (X ∖ Z) ×_X Y` is an isomorphism. Then the functor
`X_{spaces,étale} ⥤ Y_{spaces,étale} ×_{E_{spaces,étale}} Z_{spaces,étale}`,
`V ↦ (V ×_X Y, V ×_X Z)`, is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_spacesEtaleModificationRestriction_of_isProper
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hi : IsClosedImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (sq : IsPullback j g f i)
    {V : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (w' : V ⟶ Y)
    (fU : V ⟶ closedImmersionComplement B S hS i hi) [IsIso fU]
    (sqU : IsPullback w' fU f (closedImmersionComplementHom B S hS i hi)) :
    (spacesEtaleModificationRestriction B S hS f i j g sq.w).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.UncoheratedTrace.coherator_cannot_be_dropped
declarations.statement:
theorem coherator_cannot_be_dropped (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (t : Γ(S, ⊤))
    (ht : ∀ (j : ℕ) (b : Γ(S, ⊤)), t ^ j ≠ t ^ (j + 1) * b) :
    (IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS).1 ∧
      IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS).1 ∧
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (affineBaseSpace B S hS).1 ∧
        IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (affineBaseSpace B S hS).1) ∧
    PreservesQuasicoherentDerived Rf ∧
    quasicoherentDerivedProperty (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS)
      (structureSheafDerived B S hS (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS)) ∧
    quasicoherentDerivedProperty (affineBaseSpace B S hS)
      (structureSheafDerived B S hS (affineBaseSpace B S hS)) ∧
    (∀ M : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS).1
      (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS).2),
      quasicoherentDerivedProperty (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS) M →
        quasicoherentDerivedProperty (affineBaseSpace B S hS) (traceSource B S hS Rf M)) ∧
    Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ 0).obj (traceTarget B S hS Rf) ≅
      piUnit (affineBaseSpace B S hS).2) ∧
    ¬ (piUnit (affineBaseSpace B S hS).2).IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
    ¬ quasicoherentDerivedProperty (affineBaseSpace B S hS) (traceTarget B S hS Rf) ∧
    ∀ (a : QuasicoherentDerivedCategoryOfModel (affineBaseSpace B S hS) ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategoryOfModel (affineLineAlgebraicSpace B S hS))
      (_ : liftQuasicoherentDerived Rf (preservesQuasicoherentDerived B S hS Rf α) ⊣ a)
      (φ : traceSource B S hS Rf
          (a.obj ⟨structureSheafDerived B S hS (affineBaseSpace B S hS),
            structureSheafDerived_mem B S hS (affineBaseSpace B S hS)⟩).obj ⟶
        traceTarget B S hS Rf),
      ¬ IsIso φ
declarations.comment: the counterexample of 0GEU on algebraic spaces: for f : A^1_S -> S with S affine carrying t with no t^j = t^(j+1) b (S = Spec Z, t = 2), L = O_X, K = O_Y, the left side of the 0E57 map lies in D_QCoh, the right side has H^0 the non-quasi-coherent product of copies of O_Y, and no map between them is an isomorphism, for every right adjoint a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coheratorPushforwardSheafHomIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG4, the identification of the coherators.** For right adjoints `DQ_X`, `DQ_Y` of
the inclusions `D_QCoh ⟶ D`, `DQ_Y(Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K))) ≅ Rf_*DQ_X(R𝓗om(L, a(K)))` (Stacks 0CR5).
declarations.statement:
def coheratorPushforwardSheafHomIso
    {DQX : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2}
    {DQY : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2}
    (adjX : (QcohDerived B S hS X).ι ⊣ DQX) (adjY : (QcohDerived B S hS Y).ι ⊣ DQY)
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) :
    DQY.obj ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj
        (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op L.obj)).obj
          ((quasicoherentDerivedRightAdjoint hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs).obj K).obj)) ≅
      (quasicoherentDerivedPushforward B S hS f
          (isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiCompactSpace B S hS hZ Y.2 hYqs hXqc f.hom)
          (isQuasiSeparated_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_source B S hS hZ X.2 hXqs f.hom)).obj
        (DQX.obj (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op L.obj)).obj
          ((quasicoherentDerivedRightAdjoint hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs).obj K).obj))
declarations.comment: the identification of the coherators by Stacks 0CR5

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_coherator_counit_pushforward_sheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG4, erasing the coherator on the source.** If `R𝓗om(L, a(K))` has
quasi-coherent cohomology, then `DQ_Y(Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K))) ⟶ Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K))` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coherator_counit_pushforward_sheafHom
    {DQ : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2}
    (adjQ : (QcohDerived B S hS Y).ι ⊣ DQ)
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (h : QcohDerived B S hS X (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op L.obj)).obj
      ((quasicoherentDerivedRightAdjoint hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs).obj K).obj)) :
    IsIso (adjQ.counit.app ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj
      (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op L.obj)).obj
        ((quasicoherentDerivedRightAdjoint hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs).obj K).obj)))
declarations.comment: erasing the coherator on the source of the map of Stacks 0E58

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_coherator_counit_sheafHom_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG4, erasing the coherator on the target.** If `R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` has
quasi-coherent cohomology, then `DQ_Y(R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)) ⟶ R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coherator_counit_sheafHom_pushforward
    {DQ : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) ⥤
      QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2}
    (adjQ : (QcohDerived B S hS Y).ι ⊣ DQ)
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (h : QcohDerived B S hS Y (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS Y).obj
      (op ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj)) :
    IsIso (adjQ.counit.app (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS Y).obj
      (op ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj))
declarations.comment: erasing the coherator on the target of the map of Stacks 0E58

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_qcohDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG4, the quasi-coherence criterion.** If `R𝓗om(L, a(K))` and `R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` both
have quasi-coherent cohomology, then the map `Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` of
Stacks 0E57 is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_qcohDerived
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hA : QcohDerived B S hS X (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS X).obj (op L.obj)).obj
      ((quasicoherentDerivedRightAdjoint hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs).obj K).obj))
    (hB : QcohDerived B S hS Y (((smallEtaleDerivedSheafHom B S hS Y).obj
      (op ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj L.obj))).obj K.obj)) :
    IsIso (smallEtalePushforwardTrace hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs L K)
declarations.comment: the map of Stacks 0E57 is an isomorphism if both sides have quasi-coherent cohomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG4 (1).** If `L` and `Rf_*L` are perfect, then the map
`Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` of Stacks 0E57 is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_isPerfect
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hL : RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) L.obj)
    (hfL : RingedSite.IsPerfect (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
      ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj L.obj)) :
    IsIso (smallEtalePushforwardTrace hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs L K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG4 (2).** If `K` is bounded below and `L` and `Rf_*L` are pseudo-coherent, then
the map `Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` of Stacks 0E57 is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_isPseudoCoherent
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj)
    (hL : RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2) L.obj)
    (hfL : RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
      ((derivedModulePushforward B S hS f).obj L.obj)) :
    IsIso (smallEtalePushforwardTrace hZ f hXqc hXqs hYqs L K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GG5.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of Noetherian algebraic spaces over
`S`, `L` in `D^-_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `K` in `D^+_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then the map
`Rf_*R𝓗om(L, a(K)) ⟶ R𝓗om(Rf_*L, K)` of Stacks 0E57 is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtalePushforwardTrace_of_isProper (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom)
    (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1) (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus (isCoherent.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) L)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS Y.1 Y.2).O))) K) :
    IsIso (smallEtalePushforwardTrace hZ f hX.1 hX.2.1 hY.2.1
      ⟨L, fun i => (hL.2 i).toIsQuasicoherentOnSite⟩ ⟨K, hK.2⟩)

declarations.name: Rig.isFiniteTypeOnReductions_iff_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
An adic homomorphism into a Noetherian weakly admissible ring is of finite type on
reductions if and only if it is topologically of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteTypeOnReductions_iff_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ) :
    IsFiniteTypeOnReductions φ hφ ↔
      TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ

declarations.name: Rig.rigPoint_tfae
declarations.doc:
The eight equivalent characterizations of a rig point in a Noetherian adic
topological ring.
declarations.statement:
public lemma rigPoint_tfae {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [@CompleteSpace A (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A)] [T2Space A]
    (_hadic : ∃ I : Ideal A, IsAdic I) (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime] :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∃ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧
          Ideal.IsMaximalAmongPrimesAvoiding I q,
        ∃ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧
          Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom I q,
        ∀ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I →
          Ideal.IsMaximalAmongPrimesAvoiding I q,
        ∀ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I →
          Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom I q,
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ q) = 1 ∧
          ∃ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧ ¬ I ≤ q,
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ q) = 1 ∧
          ∀ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I → ¬ I ≤ q,
        ringKrullDim (A ⧸ q) = 1 ∧ ¬ DiscreteTopology (A ⧸ q),
          Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition q ]

declarations.name: Rig.Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition
declarations.doc:
The local description in condition (8) of the rig-point criterion.  The
topology and completeness on the quotient are the ones induced from `A`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime] : Prop
declarations.comment: rig-closed, via condition (8) of the rig-point criterion

declarations.name: Rig.Ideal.IsRigClosed
declarations.doc:
A prime `q` of a topological ring is *rig-closed* if some ideal of definition is not
contained in `q` and `q` is maximal among the primes not containing it.
declarations.statement:
public def Ideal.IsRigClosed {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    (q : Ideal A) : Prop

declarations.name: Rig.exists_residueFieldMap_finiteType_of_rigPoint
declarations.doc:
The residue field at a rig-closed point is of finite type over the quotient
of the source by its ideal of topologically nilpotent elements.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_residueFieldMap_finiteType_of_rigPoint
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition q)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hfiniteType : (Ideal.quotientMap (I := topologicalNilradical A)
      (topologicalNilradical B) φ
      (by
        intro x hx
        exact IsTopologicallyNilpotent.map hφ
          (IsTopologicallyNilpotent.mem_topologicalNilradical_iff.mp hx))).FiniteType) :
    let _ : IsLocalRing (B ⧸ q) := hq.choose
    ∃ ψ : (A ⧸ topologicalNilradical A) →+* IsLocalRing.ResidueField (B ⧸ q),
      ψ.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (topologicalNilradical A)) =
        (IsLocalRing.residue (B ⧸ q)).comp ((Ideal.Quotient.mk q).comp φ) ∧
      ψ.FiniteType

declarations.name: Rig.rigPoint_relative_tfae
declarations.doc:
For an adic, topologically finite type morphism of Noetherian weakly
admissible rings, a rig-closed prime upstairs satisfies the relative
rig-closed point criterion.
declarations.statement:
public lemma rigPoint_relative_tfae {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical B) q) :
    let a := topologicalNilradical A
    let p := q.comap φ
    List.TFAE
      [ ∃ hlocal : IsLocalRing (B ⧸ q),
          letI : IsLocalRing (B ⧸ q) := hlocal
          ∃ ψ : (A ⧸ a) →+* IsLocalRing.ResidueField (B ⧸ q),
            ψ.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) =
                (IsLocalRing.residue (B ⧸ q)).comp
                  ((Ideal.Quotient.mk q).comp φ) ∧
              ψ.Finite,
        Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom a p,
        (Ideal.quotientMap (I := p) q φ le_rfl).Finite ]

declarations.name: Rig.isRigPointLocalCondition_comap_of_isJacobsonRing_quotient
declarations.doc:
Under a Jacobson reduction of the source, the inverse image of a rig-closed
prime along an adic topologically finite type morphism is rig-closed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigPointLocalCondition_comap_of_isJacobsonRing_quotient
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition q)
    (hJacobson : ∃ I : Ideal A,
      TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧ IsJacobsonRing (A ⧸ I)) :
    Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition (q.comap φ)

declarations.name: Rig.rigPoint_lifts_iff_maximalIdeal_mem_specialFibre_image
declarations.doc:
A rig-closed prime lifts along a flat adic map of topologically finite type
if and only if the closed point of its quotient is in the image on special
fibres.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigPoint_lifts_iff_maximalIdeal_mem_specialFibre_image
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical A) p) :
    ( (∃ hlocal : IsLocalRing (A ⧸ p),
          letI : IsLocalRing (A ⧸ p) := hlocal
          ∃ r : Ideal B, r.IsPrime ∧
            topologicalNilradical B ≤ r ∧
            r.comap φ = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (A ⧸ p)).comap
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk p)) ↔
      (∃ q : Ideal B, ∃ hqprime : q.IsPrime,
        letI : q.IsPrime := hqprime
        Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
          (topologicalNilradical B) q ∧ q.comap φ = p) )
declarations.comment: lifting criterion

declarations.name: Rig.rigPoint_residueFieldMap_finite_of_lift
declarations.doc:
At a rig-closed lift, the induced map from the reduction of `A` to the
residue field of `B / q` is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigPoint_residueFieldMap_finite_of_lift
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical A) p)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical B) q)
    (hqp : q.comap φ = p) :
    ∃ hlocal : IsLocalRing (B ⧸ q),
      letI : IsLocalRing (B ⧸ q) := hlocal
      ∃ ψ : (A ⧸ topologicalNilradical A) →+*
          IsLocalRing.ResidueField (B ⧸ q),
        ψ.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (topologicalNilradical A)) =
            (IsLocalRing.residue (B ⧸ q)).comp
              ((Ideal.Quotient.mk q).comp φ) ∧ ψ.Finite
declarations.comment: relative residue-field finiteness

declarations.name: Rig.rigPoint_quotientMap_finite_of_lift
declarations.doc:
At a rig-closed lift, the induced map on the quotients by the two primes
is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rigPoint_quotientMap_finite_of_lift
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical A) p)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical B) q)
    (hqp : q.comap φ = p) :
    (Ideal.quotientMap (I := p) q φ (by simpa only [← hqp] using le_rfl)).Finite
declarations.comment: relative quotient finiteness

declarations.name: Rig.exists_completedAway_algEquiv_of
declarations.doc:
The completed principal localization is independent of the ideal of definition used to
form it: for ideals of definition `I` and `J` the `I`-adic and `J`-adic completions of `A[1/f]`
are isomorphic as `A`-algebras, compatibly with the maps from `A[1/f]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_completedAway_algEquiv_of {I J : Ideal A}
    (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (hJ : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition J) (f : A) :
    ∃ e : CompletedAway I f ≃ₐ[A] CompletedAway J f, ∀ x : Localization.Away f,
      e (AdicCompletion.of _ (Localization.Away f) x) =
        AdicCompletion.of _ (Localization.Away f) x
declarations.comment: independence of the ideal of definition

registrations.name: CompletedAway
registrations.comment: the completed principal localization, along a chosen ideal

declarations.name: Rig.tensorProduct_equiv_extendedIdeal
declarations.doc:
Extension of scalars of `p` to the completed principal localization is canonically its
extended ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorProduct_equiv_extendedIdeal
    (I p : Ideal A) (f : A) [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    ∃ e : (CompletedAway I f ⊗[A] p) ≃ₗ[CompletedAway I f] extendedIdeal I p f,
      ∀ (x : p) (c : CompletedAway I f),
        ((e (c ⊗ₜ[A] x) : extendedIdeal I p f) : CompletedAway I f) =
          algebraMap A (CompletedAway I f) (x : A) * c
declarations.comment: tensor-product description

declarations.name: Rig.adicCompletion_localizedIdeal_equiv_extendedIdeal
declarations.doc:
Completing the localized ideal `p A[1/f]` gives its extension to the completed principal
localization, compatibly with the canonical maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_localizedIdeal_equiv_extendedIdeal
    (I p : Ideal A) (f : A) [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    let A_f := Localization.Away f
    let J := I.map (algebraMap A A_f)
    let p_f := p.map (algebraMap A A_f)
    ∃ e : AdicCompletion J p_f ≃ₗ[A_f] extendedIdeal I p f,
      ∀ x : p_f,
        ((e (AdicCompletion.of J p_f x) : extendedIdeal I p f) : CompletedAway I f) =
          algebraMap A_f (CompletedAway I f) (x : A_f)
declarations.comment: completion description

declarations.name: Rig.extendedIdeal_isPrime
declarations.doc: The extension of `p` to the completed principal localization is prime.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extendedIdeal_isPrime
    (I p : Ideal A) (f : A) [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (hp : p.IsPrime)
    (hf : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk p f)) :
    (extendedIdeal I p f).IsPrime
declarations.comment: primality

declarations.name: Rig.quotient_extendedIdeal_equiv
declarations.doc:
Quotienting the completed principal localization by the extended prime canonically recovers
`A / p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotient_extendedIdeal_equiv
    (I p : Ideal A) (f : A) [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (hf : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk p f)) :
    ∃ e : (A ⧸ p) ≃+* (CompletedAway I f ⧸ extendedIdeal I p f),
      ∀ a : A,
        e (Ideal.Quotient.mk p a) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (extendedIdeal I p f)
            (algebraMap A (CompletedAway I f) a)
declarations.comment: quotient

declarations.name: Rig.exists_isClosedPointAwayFrom_completedAway_comap
declarations.doc:
After a suitable completed principal localization, the prime below a
rig-closed point is rig-closed as well.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isClosedPointAwayFrom_completedAway_comap
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      (topologicalNilradical B) q) :
    let I := hadic.choose
    let J := I.map φ
    ∃ f : A,
      IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk q (φ f)) ∧
        (let A_f := CompletedAway I f
         let B_f := CompletedAway J (φ f)
         let ψ : A_f →+* B_f := RingHom.completedAwayMap φ I f
         let I_f := I.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f))
         let J_f := J.map (algebraMap B (Localization.Away (φ f)))
         let I_hat := I_f.map (algebraMap (Localization.Away f) A_f)
         let J_hat := J_f.map (algebraMap (Localization.Away (φ f)) B_f)
         let q' := extendedIdeal J q (φ f)
         let p' := q'.comap ψ
         ψ.comp (algebraMap A A_f) = (algebraMap B B_f).comp φ ∧
           (∃ hqprime : q'.IsPrime,
             letI : q'.IsPrime := hqprime
             ∃ hpprime : p'.IsPrime,
               letI : p'.IsPrime := hpprime
               Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom J_hat q' ∧
                 Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom I_hat p'))

declarations.name: Rig.adicCompletionMap_localRingHom_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian adic topological ring, complete for an ideal of definition `I`, and
let `q` be a prime of the restricted power series ring `A{x_σ}` in finitely many variables.  If
`q` is rig-closed and so is its contraction to `A`, then the canonical map from the local ring of
the polynomial ring at `q ∩ A[x_σ]` to the local ring of `A{x_σ}` at `q` induces a bijection on
the completions at the maximal ideals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletionMap_localRingHom_bijective
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : IsAdic I) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (σ : Type*) [Finite σ]
    (q : Ideal (RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom (I.map (coefficientRingHom I σ)) q)
    (hp : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom I (q.comap (coefficientRingHom I σ))) :
    let f := polynomialRingHom I σ
    let q' := q.comap f
    let l := Localization.localRingHom q' q f rfl
    Function.Bijective
      (adicCompletionMap l
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q'))
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
        (IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_le l))

declarations.name: Rig.map_comap_eq_map_of_rigPoint_of_etale_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGI.** Let `φ : A → B` be an adic morphism of Noetherian weakly admissible
topological rings which is topologically of finite type and flat and whose reduction modulo an
ideal of definition `I ⊆ A` is étale.  If `q ⊆ B` is a rig-closed prime whose contraction to `A`
is rig-closed as well, then the extension of that contraction to the local ring of `B` at `q` is
the extension of `q` itself.
declarations.statement:
public lemma map_comap_eq_map_of_rigPoint_of_etale_quotient
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hadic : RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (_hft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (hetale : (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map).Etale)
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (_hq : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition q)
    (hp : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition (q.comap φ)) :
    (q.comap φ).map ((algebraMap B (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp φ) =
      q.map (algebraMap B (Localization.AtPrime q))

declarations.name: Rig.restrictedPowerSeriesBaseChangeEquiv
declarations.doc:
Base change of a restricted power series ring by a rig-closed quotient is
canonically the restricted power series ring over that quotient.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def restrictedPowerSeriesBaseChangeEquiv
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (I : Ideal A) (_hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (_hp : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition p)
    (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    letI : Algebra (A ⧸ p)
      (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A] (A ⧸ p)) :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A] (A ⧸ p)) ≃ₐ[A ⧸ p]
      RestrictedPowerSeries (I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p)) (Fin n)
declarations.comment: regular_map

declarations.name: Rig.restrictedPowerSeriesBaseChangeEquiv_coefficientProjection
declarations.doc:
At every finite level, the base-change identification reduces a series
coefficientwise modulo `p`. The polynomial `g` is any lift of that level's
coefficient polynomial, so the equation also asserts independence of lifts.
declarations.statement:
public lemma restrictedPowerSeriesBaseChangeEquiv_coefficientProjection
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition p)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (k : ℕ)
    (f : RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n))
    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
    (hg : RestrictedPowerSeries.coefficientProjection I (Fin n) k f =
      MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ k)) g) :
    letI : Algebra (A ⧸ p)
      (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A] (A ⧸ p)) :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    RestrictedPowerSeries.coefficientProjection
      (I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p)) (Fin n) k
      (restrictedPowerSeriesBaseChangeEquiv hA I hI p hp n hn
        ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom :
            RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) →+*
              (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A] (A ⧸ p))) f)) =
      MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk
        ((I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p)) ^ k))
        (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk p) g)
declarations.comment: regular_map

declarations.name: Rig.isRegularRingHom_baseChange_of_rigPoint
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the rig-closed quotient to the base-changed
restricted power series ring is regular.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isRegularRingHom_baseChange_of_rigPoint
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (I : Ideal A) (_hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (_hp : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition p)
    (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    letI : Algebra (A ⧸ p)
      (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A] (A ⧸ p)) :=
      Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    IsRegularRingHom (algebraMap (A ⧸ p)
      (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A] (A ⧸ p)))
declarations.comment: regular_map

declarations.name: Rig.isGeometricallyRegular_fibre
declarations.doc:
The fibre of a restricted power series algebra at a rig-closed prime is
geometrically regular over the residue field.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isGeometricallyRegular_fibre
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A)
    (I : Ideal A) (_hI : IsAdic I)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (_hp : Ideal.IsRigPointLocalCondition p)
    (n : ℕ) (_hn : 0 < n) :
    letI : Algebra p.ResidueField
      (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A]
        p.ResidueField) := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular p.ResidueField
      (RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin n) ⊗[A]
        p.ResidueField)
declarations.comment: geometrically_regular_fibre

declarations.name: Rig.naivelyRigFlat_tfae
declarations.doc:
For an adic morphism of weakly admissible adic topological rings with
finitely generated ideals of definition, flatness after localization may be
tested on topologically nilpotent elements of either ring, on all primes away
from an ideal of definition, or on rig-closed primes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem naivelyRigFlat_tfae
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    (phi : A →+* B) (_hphi_continuous : Continuous phi)
    (_hA_weaklyAdmissible : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (_hB_weaklyAdmissible : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (_hA_adicStar : ∃ I : Ideal A, IsAdic I ∧ I.FG)
    (_hB_adicStar : ∃ J : Ideal B, IsAdic J ∧ J.FG)
    (_hphi_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic phi) :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∀ f : A, IsTopologicallyNilpotent f →
          _root_.RingHom.Flat
            ((algebraMap B (Localization.Away (phi f))).comp phi),
        ∀ g : B, IsTopologicallyNilpotent g →
          _root_.RingHom.Flat
            ((algebraMap B (Localization.Away g)).comp phi),
        ∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime],
          (∃ J : Ideal B, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition J ∧ ¬ J ≤ q) →
            _root_.RingHom.Flat
              ((algebraMap B (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp phi),
        ∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime],
          (∃ J : Ideal B, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition J ∧
            Rig.Ideal.IsMaximalAmongPrimesAvoiding J q) →
              _root_.RingHom.Flat
                ((algebraMap B (Localization.AtPrime q)).comp phi) ]

declarations.name: Rig.RingHom.IsNaivelyRigFlat
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism `φ : A →+* B` is naively rig-flat if it is adic, topologically of finite
type, and `B[1 / φ(f)]` is flat over `A` for every topologically nilpotent `f : A`.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsNaivelyRigFlat {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [TopologicalSpace B] (φ : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: Rig.exists_isNaivelyRigFlat_not_isNaivelyRigFlat_completedAwayMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGN.** Naive rig-flatness is not preserved by passing to completed principal
localizations: there is a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain `A`, complete for a principal
ideal `(a)`, and `f ∈ 𝔪 ∖ (a)`, such that the reduction `B` of the completed localization
`C = (A_f)^∧` receives a naively rig-flat adic map `φ : A → B` of topological finite type —
presented by the restricted power series ring `A{x}` with `x ↦ 1/f` — while the induced map `ψ`
of completed principal localizations of `φ` at `f` is not naively rig-flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isNaivelyRigFlat_not_isNaivelyRigFlat_completedAwayMap :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : IsLocalRing A)
      (_ : IsNoetherianRing A) (a f : A),
      ringKrullDim A = 2 ∧
        IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {a}) A ∧
        f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧
        f ∉ Ideal.span {a} ∧
        (let I : Ideal A := Ideal.span {a}
         let Af := Localization.Away f
         let If : Ideal Af := I.map (algebraMap A Af)
         let C := AdicCompletion If Af
         let B := C ⧸ nilradical C
         let φ : A →+* B := (Ideal.Quotient.mk (nilradical C)).comp (algebraMap A C)
         letI : TopologicalSpace A := I.adicTopology
         letI : TopologicalSpace B := (I.map φ).adicTopology
         (¬ IsReduced (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a))) ∧
           (∃ θ : RestrictedPowerSeries I (Fin 1) →+* B,
             Function.Surjective θ ∧
               (∀ x : A,
                 θ (RestrictedPowerSeries.polynomialRingHom I (Fin 1) (MvPolynomial.C x)) =
                   φ x) ∧
               θ (RestrictedPowerSeries.polynomialRingHom I (Fin 1) (MvPolynomial.X 0)) =
                 Ideal.Quotient.mk (nilradical C)
                   (algebraMap Af C (IsLocalization.Away.invSelf (S := Af) f))) ∧
           (∀ q : Ideal B, q.IsPrime → φ a ∉ q → q.comap φ = ⊥) ∧
           RingHom.IsNaivelyRigFlat φ ∧
             (let B_f := Localization.Away (φ f)
              let J_f := (I.map φ).map (algebraMap B B_f)
              let I_hat := If.map (algebraMap Af C)
              let J_hat := J_f.map (algebraMap B_f (AdicCompletion J_f B_f))
              letI : TopologicalSpace C := I_hat.adicTopology
              letI : TopologicalSpace (AdicCompletion J_f B_f) := J_hat.adicTopology
              let ψ := RingHom.completedAwayMap φ I f
              (∃ e : AdicCompletion J_f B_f ≃+* B,
                (∀ b : B, e ((algebraMap B_f (AdicCompletion J_f B_f))
                  (algebraMap B B_f b)) = b) ∧
                (∀ c : C, e (ψ c) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (nilradical C) c)) ∧
              let a_hat : C := algebraMap Af C (algebraMap A Af a)
              (¬ _root_.RingHom.Flat (IsLocalization.Away.map (Localization.Away a_hat)
                (Localization.Away (ψ a_hat)) ψ a_hat)) ∧
                (¬ RingHom.IsNaivelyRigFlat ψ)))

declarations.name: Rig.RingHom.IsRigFlat
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism is rig-flat if it is adic and topologically of finite
type, and all the induced maps between completed principal localizations are
naively rig-flat.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsRigFlat {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [TopologicalSpace B] (φ : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: Rig.RingHom.isRigFlat_of_isNaivelyRigFlat_of_isJacobsonRing_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGQ.** A naively rig-flat arrow of `WAdm^Noeth` whose source has a Jacobson
reduction modulo an ideal of definition is rig-flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigFlat_of_isNaivelyRigFlat_of_isJacobsonRing_quotient
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (_hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hJacobson : ∃ I : Ideal A,
      TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧ IsJacobsonRing (A ⧸ I))
    (hflat : IsNaivelyRigFlat φ) :
    IsRigFlat φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigFlat_completedTensorProduct_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGR.**  Let `A → B` and `A → C` be arrows of `WAdm^Noeth`.  If `A → B` is rig-flat
and `A → C` is adic and topologically of finite type, then `C → B ⊗̂_A C` is rig-flat.

The naive form is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.naiveRigFlatBaseChangeByAdicFiniteType`, the
second to fifth paragraphs of the proof; the first paragraph upgrades it to rig-flatness through
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.rigFlat_completedTensorProduct_of_naive`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigFlat_completedTensorProduct_baseChange
    {A B C : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C]
    [IsLinearTopology C C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing C]
    (h₀ : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A) (h₁ : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B)
    (h₂ : TopologicalRing.IsAdic C) (hc₁ : Continuous (algebraMap A B))
    (hc₂ : Continuous (algebraMap A C)) (hP : Rig.RingHom.IsRigFlat (algebraMap A B))
    (hQ : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic (algebraMap A C) ∧
      TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType (algebraMap A C)) :
    Rig.RingHom.IsRigFlat (algebraMap C
      (CompletedTensorProduct (R := A) (M := B) (N := C)))

declarations.name: Rig.flat_atPrime_completedTensorProduct_restrictedPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
**Flatness of `A{σ} → B ⊗̂[A] A{σ}` at a rig-closed point.**  Let `A → B` be a continuous
adic and naively rig-flat homomorphism of Noetherian adic topological rings, complete along an
ideal of definition `I` of `A` and its extension to `B`, and let `C = A{σ}` be the restricted
power series ring on a finite set of variables.  If `q` is a rig-closed prime of the
identification `B{σ}` of `B ⊗̂[A] C` whose contraction to `A` is rig-closed, then
`C → B ⊗̂[A] C` is flat after localizing at the prime `q` cuts out.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_atPrime_completedTensorProduct_restrictedPowerSeries
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : _root_.IsAdic I) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (hJ : _root_.IsAdic (I.map (algebraMap A B)))
    [IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A B)) B]
    (σ : Type u) [Finite σ]
    (hcont : Continuous (algebraMap A B))
    (hflat : RingHom.IsNaivelyRigFlat (algebraMap A B))
    (q : Ideal (RestrictedPowerSeries (I.map (algebraMap A B)) σ)) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom
      ((I.map (algebraMap A B)).map (coefficientRingHom (I.map (algebraMap A B)) σ)) q)
    (hpA : Ideal.IsClosedPointAwayFrom I
      ((q.comap (TopologicalRing.restrictedPowerSeriesMap (B := B) I σ)).comap
        (coefficientRingHom I σ))) :
    letI : IsLinearTopology (RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) (RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      RestrictedPowerSeries.isLinearTopology_restrictedPowerSeries I
        (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) σ
    letI : TopologicalSpace (B ⊗[A] RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      tensorProductTopology (R := A) (M := B) (N := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)
    letI : UniformSpace (B ⊗[A] RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      tensorProductUniformSpace (R := A) (M := B) (N := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)
    letI : IsTopologicalRing (B ⊗[A] RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      tensorProduct_isTopologicalRing (R := A) (A := B) (B := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)
    letI : IsUniformAddGroup (B ⊗[A] RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      tensorProduct_isUniformAddGroup (R := A) (M := B) (N := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)
    let e := completedTensorProductRestrictedEquiv I (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I) σ hJ
    let ι : RestrictedPowerSeries I σ →+*
        CompletedTensorProduct (R := A) (M := B) (N := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      (UniformSpace.Completion.coeRingHom).comp
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := A) (A := B)
          (B := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)).toRingHom
    letI : (q.comap e.toRingHom).IsPrime := Ideal.comap_isPrime _ _
    _root_.RingHom.Flat
      ((algebraMap (CompletedTensorProduct (R := A) (M := B) (N := RestrictedPowerSeries I σ))
        (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap e.toRingHom))).comp ι)
declarations.comment: the last step only: for `C` the restricted power series ring `A{σ}` on a finite set of variables rather than an arbitrary adic `A → C` of topologically finite type, and flatness of `C → B ⊗̂_A C` localized at one rig-closed prime whose contraction to `A` is also rig-closed, rather than rig-flatness of `C → B ⊗̂_A C`

declarations.name: Rig.isRigFlat_of_flat_etale_square
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGS.** Rig-flatness ascends across the flat horizontal maps of a commutative
square of adic homomorphisms of topological finite type between Noetherian weakly admissible
rings whose lower map is étale modulo an ideal of definition: if `φ` is rig-flat, so is `φ'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigFlat_of_flat_etale_square
    {A A' B B' : Type u}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing B']
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace A'] [IsTopologicalRing A'] [IsLinearTopology A' A']
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [TopologicalSpace B'] [IsTopologicalRing B'] [IsLinearTopology B' B']
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A']
    [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B']
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (_hA' : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A')
    (_hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (_hB' : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B')
    (φ : A →+* B) (φ' : A' →+* B')
    (α : A →+* A') (β : B →+* B')
    (hsquare : φ'.comp α = β.comp φ)
    (hφ_cont : Continuous φ) (_hφ'_cont : Continuous φ')
    (hα_cont : Continuous α) (_hβ_cont : Continuous β)
    (hφ_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic φ)
    (hφ'_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic φ')
    (hα_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic α)
    (_hβ_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic β)
    (hφ_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (hφ'_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ')
    (hα_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType α)
    (hβ_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType β)
    (hα_flat : α.Flat) (hβ_flat : β.Flat)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    (hφ_rigFlat : RingHom.IsRigFlat φ)
    (hα_etale : (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map α) α Ideal.le_comap_map).Etale) :
    RingHom.IsRigFlat φ'

declarations.name: Rig.RingHom.isRigFlat_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGT.** Rig-flatness descends in a commutative square of adic homomorphisms of
topological finite type between Noetherian weakly admissible rings whose lower horizontal map is
flat and whose upper horizontal map is faithfully flat: if `φ'` is rig-flat, so is `φ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigFlat_of_faithfullyFlat
    {A A' B B' : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing A'] [CommRing B] [CommRing B']
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace A'] [IsTopologicalRing A'] [IsLinearTopology A' A']
    [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [TopologicalSpace B'] [IsTopologicalRing B'] [IsLinearTopology B' B']
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A'] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B']
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (_hA' : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A')
    (_hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B) (_hB' : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B')
    (φ : A →+* B) (α : A →+* A') (β : B →+* B') (φ' : A' →+* B')
    (hcomm : β.comp φ = φ'.comp α)
    (_hφ_cont : Continuous φ) (_hα_cont : Continuous α)
    (_hβ_cont : Continuous β) (_hφ'_cont : Continuous φ')
    (hφ_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic φ) (hα_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic α)
    (_hβ_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic β) (hφ'_adic : _root_.RingHom.IsAdic φ')
    (hφ_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ)
    (_hα_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType α)
    (_hβ_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType β)
    (_hφ'_ft : TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ')
    (hα_flat : α.Flat) (hβ_ff : β.FaithfullyFlat)
    (hφ'_rigFlat : Rig.RingHom.IsRigFlat φ') :
    Rig.RingHom.IsRigFlat φ

declarations.name: Rig.rigFlat_isLocalNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Rig-flatness is a local property of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth`** (Stacks 0GGU): it ascends
along completed étale localization diagrams, descends along faithfully flat ones, and is
preserved by finite products of targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem rigFlat_isLocalNoetherian :
    TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigFlat φ)

declarations.name: Rig.rigFlat_isLocalNoetherian'
declarations.doc:
**Rig-flatness is a local property of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth`**: it is
independent of the presentations of its source and target, ascends along completed étale
localization diagrams, descends along faithfully flat ones, and is preserved by finite products
of targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem rigFlat_isLocalNoetherian' :
    TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian'
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigFlat φ)

declarations.name: Rig.rigFlat_isStableUnderCompositionNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Rig-flatness is stable under composition on `WAdm^Noeth`** (Stacks 0GGV). Adicness and
topological finite type of the composite are Stacks 0GBZ; naive rig-flatness of the induced map
of completed principal localizations is `Rig.RingHom.isNaivelyRigFlat_comp` applied to the two
factors, transported along the functoriality `Rig.completedAwayMap_comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rigFlat_isStableUnderCompositionNoetherian :
    TopologicalRing.PropertyIsStableUnderCompositionNoetherian
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigFlat φ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGX.** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *rig-flat* when every
morphism between affine, representable, étale charts of its source and target is induced by a
rig-flat continuous homomorphism of adic Noetherian topological rings.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRigFlat (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasRigFlatSourceCovering_of_hasRigFlatTargetCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGY, (3) ⟹ (4).** A target covering witnessing rig-flatness on charts yields a
source covering witnessing it: the two coverings of condition (3) compose into one covering of
the source, and each of its members factors through the chart of the target covering it lies
over.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRigFlatSourceCovering_of_hasRigFlatTargetCovering
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : HasRigFlatTargetCovering B S hS f) :
    HasRigFlatSourceCovering B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigFlat_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGY.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S`, the following are equivalent: `f` is rig-flat (Definition 0GGX); every commutative
square whose verticals are affine formal algebraic spaces representable étale over `X` and `Y`
carries a rig-flat arrow of `WAdm^Noeth` on its top side; there are an affine étale covering of
`Y` and affine étale coverings of the fibre products of its members with `X` whose members map
to the corresponding chart of `Y` by rig-flat maps of `WAdm^Noeth`; there is an affine étale
covering of `X` whose members factor through affine formal algebraic spaces representable étale
over `Y` by rig-flat maps of `WAdm^Noeth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigFlat_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsRigFlat B S hS f,
        HasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS TopologicalRing.IsNoetherianAdic
          (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
            [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
            Rig.RingHom.IsRigFlat φ) f,
        HasRigFlatTargetCovering B S hS f,
        HasRigFlatSourceCovering B S hS f]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigFlat_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GGZ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` is rig-flat and `g` is locally of finite type, then the base
change `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is rig-flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigFlat_pullback_snd {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z) (hf : IsRigFlat B S hS f)
    (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) :
    IsRigFlat B S hS (pullback.snd f g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigFlat_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH0.** A composite of rig-flat morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic
spaces is rig-flat: if `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` are rig-flat, then so is `g ∘ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigFlat_comp (htransfer : TransfersCompositionOnAffineEtaleDiagrams B S hS)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hf : IsRigFlat B S hS f) (hg : IsRigFlat B S hS g) :
    IsRigFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the composite is rig-flat, with the geometric half of Stacks 0GBK as a hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigFlat_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH0.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `f` and `g` are rig-flat, then so is `g ∘ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigFlat_comp_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z) (hf : IsRigFlat B S hS f) (hg : IsRigFlat B S hS g) :
    IsRigFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: Rig.isRigFlat_and_exists_isRegular_of_isRigSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GH1.**  Let `φ : A → B` be an arrow of `WAdm^{Noeth}` — a continuous
homomorphism of Noetherian adic topological rings — which is rig-smooth.  Then `φ` is rig-flat,
and for every presentation `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_n⟩ / J` (over an ideal of definition `I` of `A`) and
every prime `J ⊆ 𝔮 ⊆ A⟨x⟩` not containing an ideal of definition, the ideal `J_𝔮` of `A⟨x⟩_𝔮` is
generated by a regular sequence.

Rig-flatness asks naive rig-flatness of every map `A_{\{f\}} → B_{\{f\}}`, which is
`Rig.isNaivelyRigFlat_completedAwayMap_of_isRigSmooth`; the regular sequences are
`Rig.exists_isRegular_ofList_eq_map_presentationIdeal`.  Both rest on the reduction of the
source's proof to a rig-closed prime lying over a rig-closed prime, through the completed
principal localization of Stacks 0GGG, where the Jacobian criterion on the regular fibre
(Stacks 0GGJ, 0GEE, 00MG) concludes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigFlat_and_exists_isRegular_of_isRigSmooth
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdic A) (hB : TopologicalRing.IsAdic B)
    (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ) (hsm : _root_.RingHom.IsRigSmooth φ) :
    RingHom.IsRigFlat φ ∧
      ∀ (hft : FiniteTypeAdicAlgebraForEveryIdeal φ) (I : Ideal A)
        (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
        (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I (adicFiniteTypeAlgebra φ hft I hI))
        (q : Ideal P.completedPolynomialRing) [q.IsPrime],
        ¬ I.map (algebraMap A P.completedPolynomialRing) ≤ q → P.ideal ≤ q →
        ∃ fs : List (Localization.AtPrime q),
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime q) fs ∧
            Ideal.ofList fs =
              P.ideal.map (algebraMap P.completedPolynomialRing (Localization.AtPrime q))

declarations.name: Rig.CompletedPolynomialPresentation.exists_pow_adicIdeal_le_annihilator_ker_onH₁_chainMapInl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GH2.**  Let `A → B → C` be morphisms of (0AL4), so that `B` and `C`
are adic and topologically of finite type over `A`, and suppose `B → C` is rig-smooth, i.e. `C`
is rig-smooth over `(B, I B)` (Stacks 0GAI, 0GCJ).  Then the kernel of the first map
`H⁻¹(NL^∧_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H⁻¹(NL^∧_{C/A})` of the six-term sequence of Stacks 0ALM is annihilated
by a power of the ideal of definition `I C`.

The presentations are the given ones: `P` of `B` over `A`, the presentation `ψ` of `C` over
`B`, and the combined presentation of `C` over `A` they define.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pow_adicIdeal_le_annihilator_ker_onH₁_chainMapInl
    (KB : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex P)
    (KC : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex
      (P.combinedPresentation s (ψ.restrictScalars A) hψ))
    (hBC : IsRigSmooth (AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.overBase (B := B) (C := C))) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, C.adicIdeal ^ n ≤ Module.annihilator C.carrier
      (LinearMap.ker (NaiveCotangent.chainMapInl _
        (P.combinedDifferential_comp_innerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KB KC)).onH₁)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigFlat_of_isRigSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH3.** A rig-smooth morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over
`S` is rig-flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigFlat_of_isRigSmooth (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsRigSmooth B S hS f) : IsRigFlat B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isAdicMorphism_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH4.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `g ∘ f` is rig-étale and `g` is an adic monomorphism, then `f` is
rig-étale: as `g` is a monomorphism, `f` is the base change of `g ∘ f` along `g`, and the base
change of a rig-étale morphism along an adic morphism is rig-étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isAdicMorphism_of_mono (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hcond : TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian.{u}
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] (φ : B →+* A) ↦
        Rig.RigEtaleCondition φ))
    (hiso : PropertyIsInvariantUnderTargetIso.{u}
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    (h31 : SourceCoverImpliesEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
      (fun R ↦ TopologicalRing.IsAdic R ∧ IsNoetherianRing R)
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hcover : HasBaseChangeCoverOverPullbackSnd B S hS (f ≫ g) g)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hfg : IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g))
    (hgadic : IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramNoetherian B S hS g) (hgmono : Mono g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS f
declarations.comment: granting the locality of the cohomology-annihilation half of rig-étaleness, which is the hypothesis hcond and the only input of Stacks 0AQL, together with the three inputs of Remark 0GBG that the library leaves open and that Stacks 0GD1, the sole cited input of this tag, is itself carried with: the covering by fibre products of charts of Stacks 0GBD and 0AN0 (hcover), the implication (3) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0ANG (h31), and the invariance of rig-étaleness under isomorphism of targets implied by Stacks 0ANI (hiso)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isAdicMorphism_of_mono_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces
over `S`. If `g ∘ f` is rig-étale and `g` is an adic monomorphism, then `f` is rig-étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isAdicMorphism_of_mono_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hfg : IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hgadic : IsAdicMorphism B S hS g) (hgmono : Mono g) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.of_comp_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH5.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces over `S` which are locally of finite type. If `g ∘ f` is rig-surjective and
`g` is a monomorphism, then `f` is rig-surjective.

As `g` is a monomorphism, the square with sides `𝟙 X` and `f` over `g ∘ f` and `g` is
cartesian, so `f` is the base change of `g ∘ f` along `g`; and the base change of a
rig-surjective morphism locally of finite type along a morphism locally of finite type is
rig-surjective, by Stacks 0AQS.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRigSurjective.of_comp_of_mono {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hsfg : IsRigSurjective B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hgmono : Mono g) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH6**, the rig-smooth case, carrying four hypotheses. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S`. If `g` is locally of finite type,
`f` is rig-smooth and rig-surjective, and `f ≫ g` is rig-smooth, then `g` is rig-smooth.

Rig-smoothness of `g` is tested on affine étale chart squares over it, by conditions (1) and
(2) of Stacks 0GCQ. At such a square the three hypotheses produce exactly the data the source's
argument consumes: the chart morphism `t` is locally of finite type, the base change
`X ×_Y V ⟶ V` of `f` along the chart of `Y` is rig-surjective and rig-smooth on charts, and its
composite with `t ≫ b` — that is, its composite with `g ∘ f` through the projection to `X` — is
rig-smooth on charts.

The hypotheses carried are `hlocal`, which is Stacks 0GCK; `htransfer`, the transfer of Remark
0GBG to formal algebraic spaces; `hetaleAdic` and `hetaleFiniteType`, that a representable étale
morphism is adic and locally of finite type; and `hdescent`, the chart-level argument of the
source. Local finiteness of type of `f`, which Definition 0AQQ presupposes, is the hypothesis
`hfft`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective
    (hlocal : TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian.{u}
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ))
    (htransfer : TransfersBaseChangeOnAffineEtaleDiagrams B S hS)
    (hetaleAdic : ∀ {U V : FppfSheaf B S hS} (w : U ⟶ V),
      IsRepresentableEtale B S hS w →
        IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramNoetherian B S hS w)
    (hetaleFiniteType : ∀ {U V : FppfSheaf B S hS} (w : U ⟶ V),
      IsRepresentableEtale B S hS w → IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS w)
    (hdescent : HasRigSurjectiveChartDescent B S hS
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigSmoothArrow φ))
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hgft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (hfft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hf : IsRigSmooth B S hS f) (hfs : IsRigSurjective B S hS f)
    (hgf : IsRigSmooth B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS g
declarations.comment: the rig-smooth case, assuming Stacks 0GCK (hlocal), the transfer of Remark 0GBG to formal algebraic spaces (htransfer), that a representable étale morphism is adic and locally of finite type (hetaleAdic, hetaleFiniteType), and the chart-level argument of the source's proof (hdescent)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH6**, the rig-étale case, carrying four hypotheses. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and
`g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S`. If `g` is locally of finite type,
`f` is rig-étale and rig-surjective, and `f ≫ g` is rig-étale, then `g` is rig-étale.

The proof is the proof of the rig-smooth case with rig-smoothness of arrows of `WAdm^{Noeth}`
replaced by rig-étaleness throughout: conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 0GCZ replace those of
Stacks 0GCQ, and Stacks 0GCW replaces Stacks 0GCL as the base-change input. The hypotheses are
the same four, with `hlocal` now Stacks 0AQL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective
    (hlocal : TopologicalRing.PropertyIsLocalNoetherian.{u}
