      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    (htransfer : TransfersBaseChangeOnAffineEtaleDiagrams B S hS)
    (hetaleAdic : ∀ {U V : FppfSheaf B S hS} (w : U ⟶ V),
      IsRepresentableEtale B S hS w →
        IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramNoetherian B S hS w)
    (hetaleFiniteType : ∀ {U V : FppfSheaf B S hS} (w : U ⟶ V),
      IsRepresentableEtale B S hS w → IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS w)
    (hdescent : HasRigSurjectiveChartDescent B S hS
      (fun {R₁ R₂ : Type u} [CommRing R₁] [TopologicalSpace R₁] [IsTopologicalRing R₁]
        [CommRing R₂] [TopologicalSpace R₂] [IsTopologicalRing R₂] (φ : R₁ →+* R₂) ↦
        RingHom.IsRigEtaleArrow φ))
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hgft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (hfft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f) (hfs : IsRigSurjective B S hS f)
    (hgf : IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS g
declarations.comment: the rig-étale case, assuming Stacks 0AQL (hlocal), the transfer of Remark 0GBG to formal algebraic spaces (htransfer), that a representable étale morphism is adic and locally of finite type (hetaleAdic, hetaleFiniteType), and the chart-level argument of the source's proof (hdescent)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSmooth_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH6**, the rig-smooth case. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` locally Noetherian. If `g` is locally of finite type, `f` is
rig-smooth and rig-surjective, and `g ∘ f` is rig-smooth, then `g` is rig-smooth.

The source also assumes `Y` and `Z` locally Noetherian and `f` locally of finite type; none of
these is used, see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSmooth_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hgft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (hf : IsRigSmooth B S hS f)
    (hfs : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) (hgf : IsRigSmooth B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsRigSmooth B S hS g
declarations.comment: the rig-smooth case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH6**, the rig-étale case. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` locally Noetherian. If `g` is locally of finite type, `f` is
rig-étale and rig-surjective, and `g ∘ f` is rig-étale, then `g` is rig-étale.

The source also assumes `Y` and `Z` locally Noetherian and `f` locally of finite type; none of
these is used, see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_of_comp_of_isRigSurjective_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hgft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f)
    (hfs : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) (hgf : IsRigEtale B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS g
declarations.comment: the rig-étale case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH8.** The standing situation of Artin's theorem on contractions: a locally
Noetherian base scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site `B`, an algebraic space `X'` locally
of finite type over `S`, a closed subset `T' ⊆ |X'|`, a locally Noetherian formal algebraic
space `W` over `S` with reduction `W_red` locally of finite type over `S`, and a formal
modification `g : X'_{/T'} ⟶ W` from the completion of `X'` along `T'` to `W`.

The open subspace `U' ⊆ X'` with `|U'| = |X'| ∖ T'` is not a field: it is constructed from
`T'` as `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.U'`.

The reduction of `W` is carried as data rather than constructed; see the module
documentation.
declarations.statement: structure ContractionSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
declarations.comment: the standing data S, X', T', W, W_red and g; the reduction of `W`, its inclusion and the witness that the inclusion exhibits it as the reduction are carried as the fields `Wred`, `WredInclusion` and `isReduction_WredInclusion` rather than constructed. That costs no generality: Stacks 0AIN supplies these for every formal algebraic space, and a reduction is unique up to unique isomorphism by its universal property, so the requirement that the reduction be locally of finite type over `S` does not depend on which one is supplied

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.U'
declarations.doc:
The open subspace `U' ⊆ X'` of the situation of Stacks 0GH8, the one with
`|U'| = |X'| ∖ T'`: the subfunctor of `X'` cut out by the complement of `T'` under the
correspondence of Stacks 03BZ. Its two defining properties are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.isOpenSubspace_U'` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.range_pointsMap_ι_U'`.
declarations.statement: def U' : Subfunctor c.X'
declarations.comment: the open subspace U' ⊆ X' with |U'| = |X'| ∖ T', which is determined by T' and therefore constructed rather than carried as a field of the situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.LocalRingsAreGRings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GH9.** The hypothesis the remark announces for the situation of Stacks 0GH8:
every local ring of the base scheme `S` is a G-ring in the sense of Stacks 07GH.
declarations.statement: def LocalRingsAreGRings (_c : ContractionSituation B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: the standing hypothesis the remark announces, that the local rings of S are G-rings, as a predicate on Situation 0GH8. The remark's two other sentences — that the source therefore does not prove its theorem for every Situation 0GH8, and the invitation to a reader who can prove the general case or supply a counterexample — assert no mathematics and are not formalized

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.contractionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHA.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8 the rule `F` that sends a locally
Noetherian scheme `V` over `S` to the set of triples `(Z, u', x̂)` satisfying the
compatibility condition, and that sends a morphism `φ : V₂ ⟶ V₁` of locally Noetherian
schemes over `S` to the map `F(φ) : F(V₁) ⟶ F(V₂)` sending `(Z₁, u'₁, x̂₁)` to
`(Z₂, u'₂, x̂₂)` with `Z₂` the inverse image of `Z₁` under `φ`, with `u'₂` the composition
of `u'₁` and `φ|_{V₂ ∖ Z₂}`, and with `x̂₂` the composition of `x̂₁` and `φ_{/Z₂}`, is a
contravariant functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def contractionFunctor (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) :
    (LocallyNoetherianOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the functor F, its values on objects and morphisms and the two functor laws, unconditionally; adicness of the third component of a triple is the defining condition of Stacks 0AQ3, that the morphism be representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.Solution.contractionFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHB, corrected.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, a solution
`(f : X' ⟶ X, T, a)` whose open subspace `U` is the complement of `T`, `|U| = |X| ∖ T`, gives a
functorial bijection `F(V) = Mor_S(V, X)` on the category of locally Noetherian schemes `V` over
`S`, where `F` is Artin's functor of Stacks 0GHA: `x : V ⟶ X` corresponds to
`(x⁻¹T, x|_{V ∖ Z}, a ∘ x_{/Z})`.

The source states this for every solution, but its notion of solution (the prose after
Situation 0GH8, `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.Solution`) does not ask
`|U| = |X| ∖ T`, and without that the statement is false:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.not_forall_nonempty_iso_of_solution`. The source's
proof uses `u' : V ∖ Z ⟶ U' = U` as the restriction of `x` to `V ∖ Z = x⁻¹(|X| ∖ T)`, which is
the condition added here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def contractionFunctorIso :
    contractionFunctor c ≅ morOnLocallyNoetherian B S hS X
declarations.comment: corrected: the solution is assumed to satisfy |U| = |X| ∖ T (the open subspace U of condition (2) is the complement of T), as the source's proof uses (u' : V ∖ Z → U' = U is the restriction of x to V ∖ Z = x⁻¹(X ∖ T)); for the literal notion of solution of Situation 0GH8 the printed statement is false, see AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.not_forall_nonempty_iso_of_solution

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.nonempty_iso_morOnLocallyNoetherian_of_solution_and_not_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHB, corrected.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, over a locally Noetherian scheme
`S`:

1. for every solution `(f : X' → X, T, a)` whose open subspace `U` of condition (2) is the open
   subspace of `X` with `|U| = |X| ∖ T` — the solutions the source's proof works with, since it
   takes `u' : V ∖ Z → U' = U` to be the restriction of `x` to `V ∖ Z = x⁻¹(|X| ∖ T)` — there is
   a functorial bijection `F(V) = Mor_S(V, X)` on the category of locally Noetherian schemes `V`
   over `S`, where `F` is Artin's functor of Stacks 0GHA; and
2. for the literal notion of solution of the prose after Situation 0GH8, which lets `U` be any
   open subspace of `X` onto which `f` maps `U'` isomorphically, the statement as printed fails
   as soon as `S` is nonempty: the situation `(X' = ∅, T' = ∅, W = ∅, g = id)` has the solution
   `X = S` (with `U = ∅ ≠ S = X ∖ T`), and `F(S) = ∅ ≠ Mor_S(S, S)`.

The bijection of (1) is `x ↦ (x⁻¹T, x|_{V ∖ Z}, a ∘ x_{/Z})`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.Solution.contractionFunctorIso`); its inverse comes
from the existence half of Stacks 0GI3 and its injectivity from the uniqueness of Stacks 0GI1.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_morOnLocallyNoetherian_of_solution_and_not_forall
    (hSN : IsLocallyNoetherian S) :
    (∀ (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (s : Solution c X), s.U = Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X s.Tᶜ →
          Nonempty (contractionFunctor c ≅ morOnLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)) ∧
      (Nonempty S → ¬ ∀ (c : ContractionSituation B S hS)
        (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), Solution c X →
          Nonempty (contractionFunctor c ≅ morOnLocallyNoetherian B S hS X))
declarations.comment: erratum: as printed the lemma is false for the literal notion of solution of Situation 0GH8 (part 2, over any nonempty S); it holds for the solutions whose open subspace U is the complement X ∖ T, the reading of condition (2) the source's proof uses (part 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.nonempty_solution_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHC.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, if there exist an algebraic space `X`
locally of finite type over `S` and a functorial bijection `F(V) = Mor_S(V, X)` on the category of
locally Noetherian schemes `V` over `S`, then `X` is a solution: there are a proper morphism
`f : X' ⟶ X`, a closed subset `T ⊆ |X|` and an isomorphism `a : X_{/T} ≅ W` such that `T'` is the
inverse image of `T`, `f` maps `U'` isomorphically onto an open subspace `U` of `X`, and
`g = a ∘ f_{/T}`.

The functorial bijection is `α : F ≅ Mor_S(-, X)` with `F` Artin's functor of Stacks 0GHA.

The source's paragraph constructing `f` from a transformation `h_{X'} ⟶ F` is incorrect as
written: its compatibility witness `x' = x̃ ∘ (V' ⟶ V)` restricts on `V'_{/Z}` to the wrong
projection of `V_{/Z} ×_W X'_{/T'}` (already for `V = X'`, `x̃ = id` and `g` the completion of the
blow-up of the affine plane in the origin). The proof takes a corrected route: Stacks 0GDU over `X`
algebraizes the base change of `g` along `a` to `h : X'' ⟶ X`, the witnesses supplied by `α` give
`x'' : X'' ⟶ X'`, Stacks 0GDR over `X'` inverts `x''`, and `f = h ∘ x''⁻¹`. The solution produced
has `U = X ∖ T`, recorded in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.exists_solution_of_iso_range_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_solution_of_iso
    (α : contractionFunctor c ≅ morOnLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hft : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (terminal.from X)) : c.IsSolution X
declarations.comment: the source's construction of f via h_{X'} → F uses the compatibility witness x' = x̃ ∘ (V' → V), which is incorrect: it restricts to the wrong projection of V_{/Z} ×_W X'_{/T'} (already for g the completion of the blow-up of the plane in the origin, V = X', x̃ = id). The proof takes a corrected route through X: 0GDU over X algebraizes the base change of g along a, the α-supplied witnesses give X'' → X', and 0GDR over X' inverts it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.range_pointsMap_toBase_inter_union_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, assertion (1): the image of `E' ⟶ V` meets `Z₁ ∪ Z₂` only inside
`Z = Z₁ ∩ Z₂`.

A field-valued point of `E'` lying over `Z₁` is carried by `x'₁` into `T'`, and if it did not
lie over `Z₂` it would be carried by `x'₂` outside `T'`; but the two images agree, `E'` being
the equalizer. The argument is symmetric in the two indices.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_toBase_inter_union_subset :
    Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS d.eqz d.toBase) ∩ (d.t₁.Z ∪ d.t₂.Z) ⊆ d.Z
declarations.comment: assertion (1), in full: that Im(E' → V) ∩ (Z₁ ∪ Z₂) is contained in Z = Z₁ ∩ Z₂, for the fibre product V' = V'₁ ×_V V'₂ and the equalizer E' ⟶ V' that this file constructs from two elements of F(V) and a chosen compatibility witness for each. Proved with no hypothesis on V beyond its being an object of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is the special case V := V.obj for a locally Noetherian object V of that site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.mono_pullbackSnd_offCenter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, first half of assertion (2): the morphism
`E' ×_V (V ∖ Z) ⟶ V ∖ Z` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem mono_pullbackSnd_offCenter : Mono (pullback.snd d.toBase d.offCenter.ι)
declarations.comment: assertion (2), the monomorphism half in full: that the morphism E' ×_V (V ∖ Z) → V ∖ Z is a monomorphism. The other half of the assertion, that this morphism is the equalizer of the restrictions of u'₁ and u'₂ to V ∖ (Z₁ ∪ Z₂), is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.exists_isLimit_fork_offCenter`. Proved with no hypothesis on V beyond its being an object of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.exists_isLimit_fork_offCenter
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, second half of assertion (2): the morphism
`E' ×_V (V ∖ Z) ⟶ V ∖ Z` *is* the equalizer of the restrictions of `u'₁` and `u'₂` to
`V ∖ (Z₁ ∪ Z₂)`, in the sense that it factors through `V ∖ (Z₁ ∪ Z₂)` by a morphism which is
a limiting fork for those two restrictions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_fork_offCenter :
    ∃ e : pullback d.toBase d.offCenter.ι ⟶ d.offBoth.toFunctor,
      e ≫ Subfunctor.homOfLe d.offBoth_le_offCenter =
          pullback.snd d.toBase d.offCenter.ι ∧
        ∃ he : e ≫ d.restrictedMap₁ = e ≫ d.restrictedMap₂,
          Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι e he))
declarations.comment: assertion (2), the equalizer half in full: that the morphism E' ×_V (V ∖ Z) → V ∖ Z factors through the open subspace V ∖ (Z₁ ∪ Z₂) by a morphism which is a limiting fork for the restrictions of u'₁ and u'₂ to V ∖ (Z₁ ∪ Z₂), that being what it is for the morphism to be equal to their equalizer. The other half of the assertion, that the morphism is a monomorphism, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.mono_pullbackSnd_offCenter`. Proved with no hypothesis on V beyond its being an object of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isSeparated_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, first half of the sentence "observe that `E' → V` is separated and
locally of finite type": the morphism `E' ⟶ V` is separated.

It is the composite of the equalizer inclusion `E' ⟶ V'`, which is a monomorphism, of the
projection `V' ⟶ V'₁`, which is a base change of the proper morphism `V'₂ ⟶ V`, and of the
proper morphism `V'₁ ⟶ V`.
declarations.statement: theorem isSeparated_toBase : Space.IsSeparated B S hS d.toBase
declarations.comment: the sentence `Observe that E' → V is separated and locally of finite type', the separatedness half in full: that the morphism E' ⟶ V is separated. The local-finite-type half is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isLocallyOfFiniteType_toBase`. The remainder of that sentence, that E_W is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space separated over V, is not claimed here; its separatedness half is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isSeparatedMorphism_EW`. Proved with no hypothesis on V beyond its being an object of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isLocallyOfFiniteType_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, second half of the sentence "observe that `E' → V` is separated and
locally of finite type": the morphism `E' ⟶ V` is locally of finite type.

It is the composite of the equalizer inclusion `E' ⟶ V'`, which is a base change of the
diagonal of `X'` and so locally of finite type by Stacks 02X4, of the projection
`V' ⟶ V'₁`, which is a base change of the proper morphism `V'₂ ⟶ V`, and of the proper
morphism `V'₁ ⟶ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_toBase :
    Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS d.toBase
declarations.comment: the sentence `Observe that E' → V is separated and locally of finite type', the local-finite-type half in full: that the morphism E' ⟶ V is locally of finite type. The separatedness half is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isSeparated_toBase`. The remainder of that sentence, that E_W is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space separated over V, is not claimed here; its separatedness half is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isSeparatedMorphism_EW`. Proved with no hypothesis on V beyond its being an object of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.mapTriple_eq_iff_factorsOffCenter_and_factorsEW
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, assertion (5): given a morphism `φ : A ⟶ V`, the two triples
`(Z₁, u'₁, x̂₁)` and `(Z₂, u'₂, x̂₂)` restrict to the same element of `F(A)` if and only if
`A ∖ φ⁻¹(Z) ⟶ V ∖ Z` factors through `E' ×_V (V ∖ Z)` and `A_{/φ⁻¹(Z)} ⟶ V_{/Z}` factors
through `E_W`.

The restriction of a triple along `φ` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.mapTriple`, which is the value on `φ` of Artin's
functor `F` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.contractionFunctor`) when `A` and `V` are locally
Noetherian. The two conditions of (b) are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.FactorsOffCenter` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.FactorsEW`; `E_W` is the equalizer of the two
morphisms `V_{/Z} ⟶ W` in the category of fppf sheaves, which is where formal algebraic spaces
over `S` live, so factoring through it is factoring through the remark's `E_W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mapTriple_eq_iff_factorsOffCenter_and_factorsEW :
    mapTriple c φ d.t₁ = mapTriple c φ d.t₂ ↔ d.FactorsOffCenter φ ∧ d.FactorsEW φ
declarations.comment: assertion (5), in full: for a morphism φ : A ⟶ V, the two triples restrict to the same element of F(A) if and only if A ∖ φ⁻¹(Z) → V ∖ Z factors through E' ×_V (V ∖ Z) and A_{/φ⁻¹(Z)} → V_{/Z} factors through E_W. Proved for an arbitrary morphism φ of the big fppf site over S, local Noetherianness of A and V being used nowhere, so the tag's own statement, for a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes, is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isPullback_completedToSituation_completedToEW
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, assertion (3): the morphism `E'_{/Z} ⟶ V_{/Z}` factors through `E_W`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.completedToEW`, and the square formed by
`E'_{/Z} ⟶ X'_{/T'}`, `E'_{/Z} ⟶ E_W`, the formal modification `g : X'_{/T'} ⟶ W` and the
morphism `E_W ⟶ V_{/Z} ⟶ W` is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_completedToSituation_completedToEW :
    d.completedToEW ≫ equalizer.ι d.xhat₁ d.xhat₂ = d.completedToBase ∧
      IsPullback d.completedToSituation d.completedToEW c.g
        (equalizer.ι d.xhat₁ d.xhat₂ ≫ d.xhat₁)
declarations.comment: assertion (3), the factorization and the cartesian square in full: that E'_{/Z} → V_{/Z} factors through E_W and that the square E'_{/Z} → X'_{/T'}, E_W → W over g is cartesian, in the category of fppf sheaves where formal algebraic spaces over S live. The closing sentence of (3), that E'_{/Z} → E_W is then a formal modification as a base change of g, is Stacks 0GDN applied to this square and is not claimed here. Proved for an arbitrary object V of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isSeparatedMorphism_EW
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD**, the separatedness half of the sentence "`E_W` is a locally Noetherian
formal algebraic space separated over `V`": the morphism `E_W ⟶ V` is separated, its relative
diagonal being an isomorphism because `E_W ⟶ V_{/Z}` and `V_{/Z} ⟶ V` are monomorphisms.
declarations.statement: theorem isSeparatedMorphism_EW : FormalSpace.IsSeparatedMorphism B S hS d.EWToBase
declarations.comment: the sentence `E_W is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space separated over V', the separatedness half in full: that E_W ⟶ V is separated, i.e. that its relative diagonal is a closed immersion. The other half, that E_W is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space, is not claimed here. Proved for an arbitrary object V of the big fppf site over S, so the tag's own hypothesis that V be a locally Noetherian scheme over S is a special case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.morIsoDiagonalFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD, the final conclusion.** For the data of Stacks 0GHD over a locally Noetherian
scheme `V`, a solution `E ⟶ V` of the situation of assertion (4) whose open subspace `U` is the
complement of `T` (the notion of solution for which Stacks 0GHB holds) represents the fibre
`F ×_{Δ, F × F} V` on the category of locally Noetherian schemes over `V`: there is an
isomorphism of functors `Mor_V(-, E) ≅ F ×_{Δ, F × F} V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def morIsoDiagonalFibre
    {E : (BigFppfOver B V.left.obj V.left.property)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (s : Solution (d.situation hVN) E)
    (hU : Set.range (Space.pointsMap B V.left.obj V.left.property s.U.toFunctor s.U.ι) =
      s.Tᶜ) :
    morOnLocallyNoetherian B V.left.obj V.left.property E ≅ d.diagonalFibre
declarations.comment: final conclusion (with the corrected notion of solution, see 0GHB: the open subspace U of the solution is the complement of T): a solution E → V of the triple of (4) represents F ×_{Δ, F × F} V on locally Noetherian schemes over V, by corrected 0GHB for the situation of (4) and the identification of its functor with F ×_{Δ, F × F} V through (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.nonempty_iso_diagonalFibre_of_solution_and_not_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD, final conclusion, corrected.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, over a locally
Noetherian scheme `S`, let `V` be a locally Noetherian scheme over `S` and `d` the data of Stacks
0GHD over `V` (two elements of `F(V)` with chosen compatibility witnesses):

1. for every solution `(f : E' → E, T, a)` of the triple of (4) whose open subspace `U` of
   condition (2) is the open subspace of `E` with `|U| = |E| ∖ T` — the solutions the source's
   proof of 0GHB works with, since it takes `u' : V ∖ Z → U' = U` to be the restriction of `x` to
   `V ∖ Z = x⁻¹(|X| ∖ T)` — `E` represents `F ×_{Δ, F × F} V` on the category of locally
   Noetherian schemes over `V`; and
2. for the literal notion of solution of the prose after Situation 0GH8, which lets `U` be any
   open subspace of `E` onto which `f` maps `U'` isomorphically, the statement as printed fails
   as soon as `S` is nonempty: for the situation `(S ⨿ S, ∅, (S ⨿ S)_{/∅}, id)` and the triples
   of the two inclusions `S ⟶ S ⨿ S` over `V = S`, the triple of (4) is `(∅, ∅, ∅ → ∅)`, which
   has the solution `E = V` (with `U = ∅ ≠ V = E ∖ T`), and `Mor_V(V, V) ∋ id` while
   `F ×_{Δ, F × F} V` has no element over `V`.

The isomorphism of (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.morIsoDiagonalFibre`:
corrected Stacks 0GHB for the situation of (4), followed by the identification of its functor with
`F ×_{Δ, F × F} V` through assertion (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_diagonalFibre_of_solution_and_not_forall
    (hSN : IsLocallyNoetherian S) :
    (∀ (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (d : ContractionEqualizer c V) (hVN : IsLocallyNoetherian V.left.obj)
        (E : (BigFppfOver B V.left.obj V.left.property)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (s : Solution (d.situation hVN) E),
        s.U = Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B V.left.obj V.left.property E s.Tᶜ →
          Nonempty (morOnLocallyNoetherian B V.left.obj V.left.property E ≅ d.diagonalFibre)) ∧
      (Nonempty S → ¬ ∀ (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (d : ContractionEqualizer c V) (hVN : IsLocallyNoetherian V.left.obj)
        (E : (BigFppfOver B V.left.obj V.left.property)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
        Solution (d.situation hVN) E →
          Nonempty (morOnLocallyNoetherian B V.left.obj V.left.property E ≅ d.diagonalFibre))
declarations.comment: erratum: the final conclusion, that a solution E → V of the triple of (4) represents F ×_{Δ, F × F} V on locally Noetherian schemes over V, is false as printed for the literal notion of solution of Situation 0GH8 (part 2, over any nonempty S); it holds for the solutions whose open subspace U is the complement E ∖ T, the reading of condition (2) the source's proof of 0GHB uses (part 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isLocallyNoetherian_EW
declarations.doc:
**`E_W` is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space**, half of the sentence of Stacks 0GHD
"`E_W` is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space separated over `V`": `E_W ⟶ V_{/Z}` is
locally of finite type (a base change of the diagonal of `W`, Stacks 0AIP) and `V_{/Z}` is locally
Noetherian (Stacks 0AQ1), so this is Stacks 0AQ8.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_EW (hVN : IsLocallyNoetherian V.left.obj) :
    FormalSpace.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS d.EW
declarations.comment: the sentence `E_W is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space separated over V', the locally Noetherian half in full, for V a locally Noetherian scheme over S; the separatedness half is AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isSeparatedMorphism_EW

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.isFormalModification_completedToEW
declarations.doc:
**`E'_{/Z} ⟶ E_W` is a formal modification**, the closing sentence of Stacks 0GHD (3): by
assertion (3) it is the base change of the formal modification `g : X'_{/T'} ⟶ W` along the
adic morphism `E_W ⟶ W` from the locally Noetherian `E_W`, so this is Stacks 0GDN.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalModification_completedToEW (hVN : IsLocallyNoetherian V.left.obj) :
    IsFormalModification B S hS d.completedToEW
declarations.comment: assertion (3), the closing sentence in full: E'_{/Z} → E_W is a formal modification, as the base change of g along E_W → W, for V a locally Noetherian scheme over S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionEqualizer.situation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHD, assertion (4).** For `V` a locally Noetherian scheme over `S`, the algebraic
space `E'` with its morphism to `V`, the closed subset `(E' ⟶ V)⁻¹ Z ⊆ |E'|` and the morphism
`E'_{/Z} ⟶ E_W` form a situation as in Stacks 0GH8 with base scheme `V`: through the change of
base of Stacks 04SG they become an algebraic space `E'_V` locally of finite type over `V`
(`ContractionSituation.X'`), the closed subset `T'` of `|E'_V|` corresponding to
`(E' ⟶ V)⁻¹ Z` (`ContractionSituation.T'`), the locally Noetherian formal algebraic space `W_V`
attached to `E_W ⟶ V` (`ContractionSituation.W`) and the formal modification attached to
`E'_{/Z} ⟶ E_W` (`ContractionSituation.g`); the reduction of `W_V` is locally of finite type over
`V`. The components are recorded by `situation_space`, `situation_closedSubset`, `situation_W` and
`smallerBaseSheafFunctor_map_situation_g`.
declarations.statement:
def situation (hVN : IsLocallyNoetherian V.left.obj) :
    ContractionSituation B V.left.obj V.left.property
declarations.comment: assertion (4), in full: E', (E' → V)⁻¹Z and E'_{/Z} → E_W form a situation as in Situation 0GH8 with base scheme the locally Noetherian scheme V, the objects over S lying over V being moved to the big fppf site of V by Stacks 04SG. The inputs are proved: E_W is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space (isLocallyNoetherian_EW, by 0AIP and 0AQ8), E'_{/Z} → E_W is a formal modification (isFormalModification_completedToEW, by assertion (3) and 0GDN along the adic morphism E_W → W), and the reduction of E_W over V is locally of finite type over V (isLocallyOfFiniteTypeULift_of_isReduction)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.exists_solution_of_isClosedImmersion_and_not_forall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHE, decided.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, over a locally Noetherian scheme
`S`:

1. if `X' → S` is proper and `Z ⊆ |S|` is a closed subset such that the inverse image of `Z` in
   `X'` is `T'`, the morphism `u : U' → S ∖ Z` is a closed immersion and the morphism
   `w : W → S_{/Z}` is a closed immersion, then there exists a solution `(f : X' → X, T, a)`, and
   moreover `X → S` is a closed immersion (the solution produced also has `|U| = |X| ∖ T`); and
2. without the hypothesis that `X' → S` is proper, the statement fails as soon as `S` has a
   closed subset which is not open (for instance `S = 𝔸¹_k`, with the closed point `0`): for an
   open `O ⊆ S` which is not closed, the situation `(X' = O, T' = ∅, W = X'_{/T'}, g = id)` with
   `Z = S ∖ O` satisfies the three conditions, but has no solution with `X → S` a closed
   immersion, since such a solution would make `X' → S` proper and hence `O` closed in `S`.

Part 1 is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.exists_solution_of_isClosedImmersion`;
part 2 is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.not_exists_solution_openSituation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solution_of_isClosedImmersion_and_not_forall (hSN : IsLocallyNoetherian S) :
    (∀ (c : ContractionSituation B S hS), Space.IsProper B S hS (terminal.from c.X') →
      ∀ (Z : Set (Space.points B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)))), IsClosed Z →
      Space.pointsMap B S hS c.X' (terminal.from c.X') ⁻¹' Z = c.T' →
      ∀ (u : c.U'.toFunctor ⟶
        (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) Zᶜ).toFunctor),
        Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS u →
      ∀ (w : c.W ⟶ Space.completionSheaf B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) Z),
        FormalSpace.IsClosedImmersion B S hS w →
      ∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (s : c.Solution X),
        Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS s.U.toFunctor s.U.ι) = s.Tᶜ ∧
        Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (terminal.from X)) ∧
    ((∃ Z : Set S, IsClosed Z ∧ ¬ IsOpen Z) →
      ¬ ∀ (c : ContractionSituation B S hS)
        (Z : Set (Space.points B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)))), IsClosed Z →
        Space.pointsMap B S hS c.X' (terminal.from c.X') ⁻¹' Z = c.T' →
        ∀ (u : c.U'.toFunctor ⟶
          (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) Zᶜ).toFunctor),
          Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS u →
        ∀ (w : c.W ⟶ Space.completionSheaf B S hS (⊤_ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)) Z),
          FormalSpace.IsClosedImmersion B S hS w →
        ∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : c.Solution X),
          Space.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (terminal.from X))
declarations.comment: erratum: as printed online the lemma is false without the hypothesis that X' → S is proper (part 2, over any S with a closed subset that is not open, e.g. S = 𝔸¹_k, Z = {0}, X' = 𝔾_m, T' = ∅); with that hypothesis, which the source's proof uses, it holds (part 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.relative_isClosedImmersion_diag_contractionFunctor
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, if `X' ⟶ S` and `W ⟶ S` are separated, then the diagonal
`Δ : F ⟶ F × F` of the functor `F` of Stacks 0GHA is representable by closed immersions: for every
locally Noetherian scheme `V` over `S` and every morphism `h_V ⟶ F × F`, the fibre product with `Δ`
is represented by a locally Noetherian scheme over `S` whose morphism to `V` is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_isClosedImmersion_diag_contractionFunctor (c : ContractionSituation B S hS)
    (hX' : Space.IsSeparated B S hS (terminal.from c.X'))
    (hW : FormalSpace.IsSeparatedMorphism B S hS (terminal.from c.W)) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@IsClosedImmersion.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (LocallyNoetherianOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (uliftYoneda.{u + 1} (C := LocallyNoetherianOver B S hS)) (diag (contractionFunctor c))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.satisfiesEtaleSheafProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHG.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8 the functor `F` of Stacks 0GHA satisfies
the sheaf property for every étale covering of locally Noetherian schemes over `S`: a
compatible family of triples on such a covering has a unique amalgamation.

Existence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.exists_mapTriple_eq` and uses the
two carried inputs; uniqueness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.eq_of_mapTriple_eq` and uses neither.
**The two carried inputs, and why neither is equivalent to the conclusion.**

`h0ADV` is the locality on the base of the compatibility condition of [Stacks, Tag 0GHA].  It is
the form in which [Stacks, Tag 0ADV], étale descent for algebraic spaces, enters the source's
argument: a witness over `V` is glued from the algebraic spaces `V'_i` and the morphisms
`p_i, j_i, x̂'_i, x'_i` of the witnesses over the `V_i`, out of a descent datum whose comparison
isomorphisms come from the uniqueness part of the main theorem on dilatations.  This library has
neither Tag 0ADV for algebraic spaces nor that uniqueness statement.

`hadic` is the locality on the base of the adicness condition of [Stacks, Tag 0AQ2].  It does not
follow from [Stacks, Tag 0APY] and [Stacks, Tag 0APV], the two facts about adicness the functor
`F` is built from: both are closure rules, so every derivation from them concludes adicness of a
composite built from restrictions, never of a factor.

Each is stated for an arbitrary situation of [Stacks, Tag 0GH8], an arbitrary covering family of
the big fppf site over `S`, and an arbitrary candidate datum over its base; each constrains one
already-given datum.  Neither mentions the étale site of locally Noetherian schemes, the family of
triples, or the existence of an amalgamation, so neither contains the conclusion.  The source's
proof of this lemma is omitted — the hint is only that morphisms may be defined étale locally — so
neither is a named citation of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesEtaleSheafProperty (c : ContractionSituation B S hS)
    (h0ADV : CompatibilityIsLocalOnBase B S hS)
    (hadic : AdicIsLocalOnBase B S hS) :
    SatisfiesEtaleSheafProperty c
declarations.comment: both the existence and the uniqueness of the amalgamation, granting the locality on the base of the compatibility condition of Stacks 0GHA as h0ADV (the form in which Stacks 0ADV enters the source's argument) and of the adicness condition of Stacks 0AQ2 as hadic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.contractionFunctor_satisfiesEtaleSheafProperty
declarations.doc:
In a contraction situation the functor `F` of triples satisfies the sheaf property for all
étale coverings of locally Noetherian schemes over `S`: a compatible family of triples on such a
covering has a unique amalgamation.
declarations.statement:
theorem contractionFunctor_satisfiesEtaleSheafProperty (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) :
    SatisfiesEtaleSheafProperty c

declarations.name: exists_nonreduced_adicCompletion_localization_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHI.** There is a local Noetherian two-dimensional domain `B`, complete with
respect to a principal ideal `I = (b)`, and an element `f` of its maximal ideal outside `I`, such
that the `I`-adic completion `C = (B_f)^` of the principal localization `B_f` is nonreduced, and
even such that `C[1/b]` is nonreduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonreduced_adicCompletion_localization_away :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : IsDomain B) (_ : IsLocalRing B)
      (_ : IsNoetherianRing B) (b f : B),
      ringKrullDim B = 2 ∧
        IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {b}) B ∧
        f ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ∧
        f ∉ Ideal.span {b} ∧
        (let C := AdicCompletion
            ((Ideal.span {b}).map (algebraMap B (Localization.Away f)))
            (Localization.Away f);
          (¬ IsReduced C) ∧
            (¬ IsReduced (Localization.Away (algebraMap B C b))))

declarations.name: PseudoCoherence.isRelativelyPerfect_iff_isBoundedBelow_and_fibres_isBoundedBelow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHJ.** Let `R → A` be a flat ring map of finite presentation and let `K` be a
pseudo-coherent object of `D(A)`. Then `K` is perfect relative to `R` if and only if `K` is
bounded below and, for every prime `p` of `R`, the derived fibre `K ⊗_R^L κ(p)` is bounded
below.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyPerfect_iff_isBoundedBelow_and_fibres_isBoundedBelow
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Module.Flat R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (comparison : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M) ⟶
        (StacksDraft.TorAmplitude.tensorModuleRight M).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison M)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K) :
    IsRelativelyPerfect.{u, u, u} derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived K ↔
      (∃ a : ℤ, K.IsGE a) ∧
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ a : ℤ,
          ((CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, u}
              (algebraMap R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)).functor.obj
            ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R A)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)).IsGE a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_adicFibreMap_eq_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHK, the separated case.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to
an ideal `I`, `S = Spec A`, `S_n = Spec (A / I^{n+1})`, and let `X`, `Y` be algebraic spaces over
`S` with `X ⟶ S` proper and `Y ⟶ S` separated and locally of finite type. A compatible system
of morphisms `g_n : X_n ⟶ Y_n` over the `S_n` between the adic fibres is the system of adic
fibres of exactly one morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` over `S`.

Remark 0GHK asks whether Stacks 0A4Z survives with `Y ⟶ S` only locally of finite type. This
declaration formalizes the remark's assertion that the answer is yes when `Y ⟶ S` is separated,
by the remark's reduction to a quasi-compact open of `Y` containing the image of `g_1` (here
`g 0`); uniqueness is included, as in Stacks 0A4Z. The remark's statement "we don't know the
answer in general" is an open question, not a mathematical assertion, and is not formalized.
The remark's further assertion for `Y ⟶ S` only quasi-separated is not formalized: the remark
gives no proof inside the Stacks project, deferring to Bhatt's algebraization theorem for
`D_perf` and to Hall–Rydh's coherent Tannaka duality, papers outside the project.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_adicFibreMap_eq_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete I A] (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B _ hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B _ hS Y)
    (fX : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject A B hS)) (fY : Y ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseObject A B hS))
    (hpX : IsProper B _ hS fX) (hsY : IsSeparated B _ hS fY)
    (hlY : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B _ hS fY)
    (g : ∀ n, adicFibre A I B hS hSn fX n ⟶ adicFibre A I B hS hSn fY n)
    (hg : ∀ n, g n ≫ pullback.snd fY (yoneda.map (adicThickeningMap A I B hS hSn n)) =
      pullback.snd fX (yoneda.map (adicThickeningMap A I B hS hSn n)))
    (hgc : ∀ n, adicFibreSucc A I B hS hSn fX n ≫ g (n + 1) =
      g n ≫ adicFibreSucc A I B hS hSn fY n) :
    ∃! φ : X ⟶ Y, ∃ hφ : φ ≫ fY = fX, ∀ n, adicFibreMap A I B hS hSn φ hφ n = g n
declarations.comment: the separated case: `Y ⟶ S` separated and locally of finite type; the quasi-separated case rests on Bhatt and Hall–Rydh, outside the Stacks project, and the open general question is not a statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isColimit_of_etale_local_affine_descent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHL.** Let `B` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `D` be a diagram of algebraic
spaces over `B` and let `c` be a cocone on `D`. If base change along the cocone legs is an
equivalence from the small étale site of the vertex onto the limit of the small étale sites of
the members, and if every cocone of morphisms from the base changes of an affine étale
realization to an affine space over an affine étale base descends uniquely, then `c` is a
colimit of `D` in the category of algebraic spaces over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isColimit_of_etale_local_affine_descent
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I]
    {B : AlgebraicSpaces site S hS} {D : I ⥤ Over B}
    (c : Cocone D)
    (h₁ : EtaleComparisonIsEquivalence site S hS c)
    (h₂ : ∀ (B' : AlgebraicSpaces site S hS) (b : B' ⟶ B),
      IsAffineSpace site S hS B'.1 →
      IsEtale site S hS b.hom →
      ∀ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces site S hS) (z : Z ⟶ B'),
        IsAffineSpace site S hS Z.1 →
        ∀ (E : CompatibleEtaleDiagram site S hS D)
          (r : EtaleRealization site S hS c E),
          IsAffineSpace site S hS r.U.1 →
          ∀ (u : r.U ⟶ B'),
            r.toX ≫ c.pt.hom = u ≫ b →
            ∀ (fᵢ : E.U ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj Z),
              (∀ i, fᵢ.app i ≫ z = r.baseChange.app i ≫ u) →
              ∃! f : r.U ⟶ Z,
                (f ≫ z = u) ∧
                  (∀ i, r.baseChange.app i ≫ f = fᵢ.app i)) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_finiteOrderThickening_presentation_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHM.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space over `S`. Then
`X = colim X_n` for a system `X_0 ⟶ X_1 ⟶ X_2 ⟶ ⋯` of finite-order thickenings of locally
Noetherian algebraic spaces over `S`, where `X_0 = X_red` and `X_n` is the `n`th infinitesimal
neighbourhood of `X_0` in `X_m` for all `m ≥ n`.

The stages are indexed from zero, so the stage `n` is the source's `X_{n+1}`. In detail: every
`X_n` is an algebraic space whose étale atlases are locally Noetherian; every transition morphism
`X_n ⟶ X_m` is representable and an `m`th-order thickening on every represented base change; on
every represented base change along a section of `X_m`, the ideal sheaf of `X_n` is the
`(n + 1)`st power of the ideal sheaf of `X_0`; and `X` is the colimit of the `X_n`, its colimit
leg at `0` exhibiting `X_0` as the reduction of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteOrderThickening_presentation_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) :
    ∃ E : ℕ ⥤ FppfSheaf B S hS,
      (∀ n, Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS (E.obj n).obj) ∧
      (∀ n, Space.HasEtaleLocalPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS (E.obj n).obj
        (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian T)) ∧
      (∀ ⦃n m : ℕ⦄ (f : n ⟶ m), Space.HasSchemePropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ k ↦ Stacks.Thickenings.IsNthOrderThickening m k) (E.map f).hom) ∧
      (∀ (n m : ℕ) (hnm : n ≤ m) {a b c : BigFppfOver B S hS}
        (g : uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj a ⟶ (E.obj m).obj)
        {fst₀ : uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj b ⟶ (E.obj 0).obj} {snd₀ : b ⟶ a}
        (_ : IsPullback fst₀ (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.map snd₀)
          (E.map (homOfLE (Nat.zero_le m))).hom g)
        {fstₙ : uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj c ⟶ (E.obj n).obj} {sndₙ : c ⟶ a}
        (_ : IsPullback fstₙ (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.map sndₙ) (E.map (homOfLE hnm)).hom g),
        ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map snd₀).ker ^ (n + 1) =
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map sndₙ).ker) ∧
      ∃ e : X ≅ colimit E, IsReduction B S hS X (E.obj 0) (colimit.ι E 0 ≫ e.inv)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_finiteOrderThickening_presentation_formalSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHM**, for a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space. Let `A` be a Noetherian
topological ring whose topology is adic. Then the formal spectrum of `A` is the colimit of a
sequence `X_0 → X_1 → X_2 → ⋯` of affine schemes over `S` whose transition morphisms are
finite-order thickenings, whose terms are all locally Noetherian, whose first term `X_0` is
reduced, and in which `X_n` is the `n`th infinitesimal neighbourhood of `X_0` inside `X_m` for
every `m ≥ n` — the last clause in the form of the equality
`(X_0 ⟶ X_m).ker ^ (n + 1) = (X_n ⟶ X_m).ker` of ideal sheaves on `X_m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteOrderThickening_presentation_formalSpectrum
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} (hI : _root_.IsAdic I) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    ∃ E : ℕ ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS,
      IsReduced ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (E.obj 0)) ∧
      (∀ n, IsLocallyNoetherian ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (E.obj n))) ∧
      (∀ ⦃n m : ℕ⦄ (f : n ⟶ m), Stacks.Thickenings.IsFiniteOrderThickening
        ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (E.map f))) ∧
      (∀ (n m : ℕ) (hnm : n ≤ m),
        ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (E.map (homOfLE (Nat.zero_le m)))).ker ^ (n + 1) =
          ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (E.map (homOfLE hnm))).ker) ∧
      Nonempty (formalSpectrum D ≅ colimit (E ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)))
declarations.comment: Noetherian affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSurjective_iff_isSurjectiveULift_red
declarations.doc:
Surjectivity on points of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is the condition
of Stacks 0GHP on it: the morphism between any two reductions of its source and target
compatible with it is a surjective morphism of algebraic spaces exactly when the morphism
itself is surjective on points.
declarations.comment: the definition, identified with the source's condition on the morphism of underlying reduced algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSurjective.comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of two surjective morphisms of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is
surjective.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSurjective.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a surjective morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is
surjective.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSurjective.hasSurjectiveFormalAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHS, condition (1) implies condition (4).** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is surjective and `Y`
is a formal algebraic space over `S`, then the atlas of `Y` furnished by Stacks 0AIM is a
covering `{Y_j ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM along which every base change of `f` is
surjective.
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSurjective_of_hasSurjectiveFormalAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHS, condition (4) implies condition (1).** If a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of fppf
sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` admits a covering `{Y_j ⟶ Y}` of its target as in
Definition 0AIM along which every base change of `f` is surjective, then `f` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_of_hasSurjectiveFormalAtlas {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h : HasSurjectiveFormalAtlas B S hS f) : IsSurjective B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (4) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSurjective_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_tfae {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsSurjective B S hS f,
        IsSurjectiveOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f,
        IsSurjectiveOnAffineBaseChanges B S hS f,
        HasSurjectiveFormalAtlas B S hS f,
        HasSurjectiveFormalCover B S hS f]
declarations.comment: conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of two monomorphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a
monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_comp {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
    (hf : Mono f) (hg : Mono g) : Mono (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Mono.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a monomorphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a monomorphism: in
the cartesian square with `f` on the right and `p` on the left, if `f` is a monomorphism then so
is `p`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_tfae {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [Mono f,
        IsMonoOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f,
        IsMonoOnAffineBaseChanges B S hS f,
        HasMonoFormalAtlas B S hS f,
        HasMonoLocallySurjectiveFamily B S hS f]
declarations.comment: conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_tfae'
declarations.doc:
For an arbitrary morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`,
conditions (1), (2), (3) and (5) of `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_tfae` are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_tfae' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [Mono f,
        IsMonoOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f,
        IsMonoOnAffineBaseChanges B S hS f,
        HasMonoLocallySurjectiveFamily B S hS f]
declarations.comment: conditions (1), (2), (3) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_tfae_flatCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHV**, its condition (6) together with the conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5).
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of formal algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y` a formal algebraic
space, the following are equivalent:

1. `f` is a monomorphism;
2. for every scheme `T` over `S` in the site and every `T ⟶ Y` the projection
   `X ×_Y T ⟶ T` is a monomorphism;
3. the same for every affine scheme `T` over `S` in the site;
4. there is a covering `{Y_j ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM such that each `X ×_Y Y_j ⟶ Y_j` is a
   monomorphism;
5. there is a family `{Y_j ⟶ Y}` with `∐ Y_j ⟶ Y` a surjection of sheaves such that each
   `X ×_Y Y_j ⟶ Y_j` is a monomorphism;
6. there is a morphism `Z ⟶ Y` of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by
   algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation such that
   `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` is a monomorphism.

The equivalence of the first five conditions is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_tfae`; condition (6) is absorbed into it by the identity of
`Y`, which is such a cover, and by the fact that such a cover is a surjection of sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_tfae_flatCover {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [Mono f,
        IsMonoOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f,
        IsMonoOnAffineBaseChanges B S hS f,
        HasMonoFormalAtlas B S hS f,
        HasMonoLocallySurjectiveFamily B S hS f,
        HasMonoFlatCover B S hS f]
declarations.comment: condition (6), and its equivalence with the conditions (1), (2), (3), (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_comp
declarations.doc:
A composite of two closed immersions of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_comp {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) (hg : IsClosedImmersion B S hS g) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a closed immersion of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed
immersion: in a cartesian square of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` whose right-hand
column `f` is a closed immersion, the left-hand column `snd` is a closed immersion.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_iff_forall_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2): a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed immersion if and only if for every scheme `T`
over the big fppf site of `S` and every morphism `T ⟶ Y` the projection `X ×_Y T ⟶ T` is a
closed immersion. As with the definition of a closed immersion, no hypothesis that `X` and `Y`
are formal algebraic spaces is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_forall_scheme {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f ↔
      ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yonedaSheaf B S hS T ⟶ Y),
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_of_locallySurjectiveFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, the descent step along a surjection of sheaves: a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is a closed immersion as soon as there is a family
`{Y_i ⟶ Y}` whose induced map from the coproduct is a surjection of sheaves with every base
change `X ×_Y Y_i ⟶ Y_i` a closed immersion.

A scheme-valued point of `Y` lies, locally on the point, in the image of a single member of the
family; over that covering sieve the base change of `f` is a base change of one of the given
closed immersions, so the base change of `f` along the point is a closed immersion by effective
fppf descent of closed immersions.

Representability of `f` by algebraic spaces is **not** assumed: it is part of the conclusion,
and it is produced by the same descent. The base change of `f` along a point of `Y` is a sheaf,
and being represented by a closed immersion of the site after a covering sieve of that point
already makes it pointwise `u`-small, which is all the descent step needs; the representing
objects it returns then exhibit the base changes as algebraic spaces.

This is the sufficiency in both descent conditions of the source. For condition (4) the family
is the étale atlas of the target, and Definition 0AIM asks of it exactly that it be a surjection
of sheaves, so this *is* condition (4) implies condition (1):
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_iff_exists_affineEtaleCover`. For condition (5)
the family has one member, but the source asks only that it be surjective *on points*, so the
hypothesis must be upgraded first; that is done in
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_of_hasFlatClosedImmersionCover`, which is
condition (5) implies condition (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_locallySurjectiveFamily {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (I : Type (u + 1)) (Yi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (c : ∀ i, Yi i ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
        Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc c))
    (hci : ∀ i, IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f (c i))) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: the descent step along a surjection of sheaves, which is the sufficiency in conditions (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_iff_forall_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (3): a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed immersion if and only if for every *affine*
scheme `T` over the big fppf site of `S` and every morphism `T ⟶ Y` the projection
`X ×_Y T ⟶ T` is a closed immersion. As with the definition of a closed immersion, no
hypothesis that `X` and `Y` are formal algebraic spaces is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_forall_affine {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f ↔
      ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS), IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) →
        ∀ (g : yonedaSheaf B S hS T ⟶ Y),
          IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_iff_exists_affineEtaleCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (4): a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed immersion if and only if there is a covering
`{Y_j ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM with every base change `X ×_Y Y_j ⟶ Y_j` a closed immersion.

Necessity takes the atlas of `Y` furnished by its being a formal algebraic space; sufficiency
is the descent step, which asks nothing of `f`, so in particular does not assume `f`
representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_exists_affineEtaleCover {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f ↔
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (Yi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (g : ∀ i, Yi i ⟶ Y),
        IsAffineEtaleCover B S hS Yi g ∧
          ∀ i, IsClosedImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd f (g i))
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasFlatClosedImmersionCover_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, condition (1) implies condition (5): a closed immersion `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` admits a morphism `Z ⟶ Y` of formal algebraic spaces,
representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, along
which the base change of `f` is a closed immersion.

The identity of `Y` serves: it is representable by algebraic spaces and étale, hence surjective
on points, and each of its base changes along a scheme-valued point of `Y` is an isomorphism
onto that point, so flatness and local finite presentation hold on every étale chart of it.
The base change of `f` along the identity is `f` itself up to the canonical isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatClosedImmersionCover_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    HasFlatClosedImmersionCover B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_of_hasFlatClosedImmersionCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, condition (5) implies condition (1): if there is a morphism `Z ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of
finite presentation along which the base change of `f` is a closed immersion, then `f` is a
closed immersion.

Surjectivity here is the source's, surjectivity on points; it is upgraded to a surjection of
sheaves by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallySurjective_of_isSurjective_of_flat`, and the descent
step then applies to the one-member family `{Z ⟶ Y}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_hasFlatClosedImmersionCover {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h : HasFlatClosedImmersionCover B S hS f) : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (5) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_iff_hasFlatClosedImmersionCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GHY**, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (5): a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` is a closed immersion if and only if there is a morphism
`Z ⟶ Y` of formal algebraic spaces, representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation, with `X ×_Y Z ⟶ Z` a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_iff_hasFlatClosedImmersionCover {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f ↔ HasFlatClosedImmersionCover B S hS f
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_of_mono_of_reduction_factors
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by
algebraic spaces and a monomorphism, and through which the inclusion `iY : Yred ⟶ Y` of a
reduction of `Y` factors. If `f` is locally of finite type, or `Y` is locally Noetherian, then `f`
is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_of_mono_of_reduction_factors {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) (hmono : Mono f)
    {Yred : FppfSheaf B S hS} {iY : Yred ⟶ Y} (hiY : IsReduction B S hS Y Yred iY)
    (r : Yred ⟶ X) (hr : r ≫ f = iY)
    (hfin : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f ∨ IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion B S hS f
declarations.comment: the reduction, its inclusion and the factorisation are data, as in Stacks 0GB8

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEtale_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `T` be a set of points
of `X`. If `f` is étale, then the induced morphism of completions `X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is
étale: it is representable by algebraic spaces and each of its base changes along a
scheme-valued point of its target is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsEtale B S hS f) :
    ∃ hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun ⦃A C : Space.AlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS⦄ (g : A ⟶ C) ↦
          Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T).hom hrep

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.eq_of_eq_on_openComplement_of_eq_on_completion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI1.** Let `X` and `W` be algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` locally Noetherian,
let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset and let `a, b : X ⟶ W` be morphisms over `S` which agree on
the open subspace `X ∖ T` and whose completions along `T` agree. Then `a = b`.

The equalizer `E` of `a` and `b` is an algebraic space whose projection `g : E ⟶ X` is a
monomorphism locally of finite type — Stacks 03HK — and the two hypotheses factor
`X ∖ T ⟶ X` and `X_{/T} ⟶ X` through `g`, so Stacks 0AR6 applied to `𝟙 X` and `g` gives a
section `v` of `g`. Since `g ≫ a = g ≫ b` by construction, `a = v ≫ g ≫ a = v ≫ g ≫ b = b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_eq_on_openComplement_of_eq_on_completion
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (hXnoeth : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) (a b : X ⟶ W)
    (hopen : (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι ≫ a =
      (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι ≫ b)
    (hcompletion :
      completionOfAlgebraicSpaceInclusion B S hS hX T ≫ upliftedMap B S hS hX hW a =
        completionOfAlgebraicSpaceInclusion B S hS hX T ≫ upliftedMap B S hS hX hW b) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morToModificationCompletion_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI3**, injectivity. Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let
`T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset with complementary open subspace `U ⊆ X`, and let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a
proper morphism of algebraic spaces whose base change `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` is an isomorphism. For every
algebraic space `W` over `S` a morphism `X ⟶ W` is determined by its restriction to `X'`
together with the morphism `X_{/T} ⟶ W` it induces.
declarations.statement:
theorem morToModificationCompletion_injective
    {X' X W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (_hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (hXnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsClosed T)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (_hfproper : IsProper B S hS f)
    (hfU : IsIso (pullback.snd f (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι)) :
    Function.Injective (morToModificationCompletion B S hS f T W)
declarations.comment: injectivity of the comparison map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.morToModificationCompletion_codRestrict_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI3.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`,
`T ⊆ |X|` a closed subset with complementary open subspace `U ⊆ X`, and `f : X' ⟶ X` a proper
morphism of algebraic spaces such that `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` is an isomorphism. For any algebraic space
`W` over `S` the map
`Mor_S(X, W) ⟶ Mor_S(X', W) ×_{Mor_S(X'_{/T}, W)} Mor_S(X_{/T}, W)`, sending `w` to its
restriction to `X'` and the morphism it induces on the completion `X_{/T}`, is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem morToModificationCompletion_codRestrict_bijective
    {X' X W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hW : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (hXnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsClosed T)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (hfproper : IsProper B S hS f)
    (hfU : IsIso (pullback.snd f (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι)) :
    Function.Bijective (Set.codRestrict (morToModificationCompletion B S hS f T W)
      {p | completionMap B S hS f T ≫ p.2 =
        (completionSubfunctor B S hS X' (pointsMap B S hS X' f ⁻¹' T)).ι ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight p.1 uliftFunctor.{u + 1}}
      (morToModificationCompletion_compatible B S hS f T W))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEtale_iff_isRepresentableEtale_of_overIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI4.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|` be
a closed subset and let `U ⊂ X` be the open subspace with `|U| = |X| ∖ T`. Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be
a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type and such that `f⁻¹U ⟶ U` is an
isomorphism, and let `g : W ⟶ X_{/T}` correspond to `f` under the equivalence of Stacks 0ARB,
that is, be isomorphic over `X_{/T}` to `f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X_{/T}`. Then `f` is étale if and
only if `g` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_iff_isRepresentableEtale_of_overIso
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXN : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (M : Space.FiniteTypeModification B S hS (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ))
    {W : FppfSheaf B S hS} (g : W ⟶ Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
    (e : Over.mk g ≅ Over.mk (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS M.obj.hom T)) :
    Space.IsEtale B S hS M.obj.hom ↔ IsRepresentableEtale B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.limitPreserving_contractionFunctor
declarations.doc:
For a contraction situation `c`, the functor `contractionFunctor c` is limit preserving: for
every cofiltered limit `V = lim V_λ` of affine locally Noetherian objects over `S`, the map
`colim F(V_λ) ⟶ F(V)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitPreserving_contractionFunctor (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) :
    LimitPreserving.{u, u + 1, u, u, u + 1, u} (LocallyNoetherianOver.toScheme B S hS)
      (contractionFunctor c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.contractionFunctor_satisfiesRS
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI6.** In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, Artin's functor `F` of Stacks 0GHA
satisfies the Rim–Schlessinger condition (RS): for every pushout `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` of spectra of
Artinian local rings of finite type over `S` along a closed immersion `X ⟶ X'`, every pair of
elements of `F` over `Y` and `X'` with the same restriction to `X` is the pair of restrictions of
exactly one element of `F(Y')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem contractionFunctor_satisfiesRS (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) :
    LocallyNoetherianOver.SatisfiesRS B S hS (contractionFunctor c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.finiteDimensional_artinianTangentSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI7.** In Situation 0GH8 the tangent spaces of the functor `F` of Stacks 0GHA are
finite dimensional: for every field `k` of finite type over `S`, every affine open
`Spec Λ ⊆ S` through which `Spec k ⟶ S` factors with `Λ → k` finite, and every
`x₀ ∈ F(Spec k)`, the predeformation category `𝓕_{F,k,x₀}` is a deformation category (so a
predeformation category whose functor of isomorphism classes satisfies (S2)), and its tangent
space, with the vector-space structure of Stacks 06IH these give it, is a finite dimensional
`k`-vector space.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_artinianTangentSpace
    (Λ k : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Field k] [Algebra Λ k] [Module.Finite Λ k]
    (iΛ : Spec (.of Λ) ⟶ S) (hiΛ : IsOpenImmersion iΛ) (x₀ : (contractionFunctor c).Elementsᵒᵖ)
    (hx₀ : (LocallyNoetherianOver.elementsToOver B S hS (contractionFunctor c)).obj x₀ =
      Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap Λ k)) ≫ iΛ)) :
    let D := predeformationCategory iΛ
      (LocallyNoetherianOver.elementsToOver B S hS (contractionFunctor c)) x₀ hx₀
    letI : Category D.carrier := D.category
    let hD := isDeformationCategory_predeformationCategory c Λ k iΛ hiΛ x₀ hx₀
    letI : Fact (IsPredeformationCategory (BasedCategory.ofFunctor D.projection).p) :=
      ⟨hD.predeformation⟩
    letI : Fact (SchlessingerConditionS2 (CategoryOfElements.π
        (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor D.projection) hD.predeformation.cofibered))) :=
      ⟨tangentConditionS2 hD⟩
    FiniteDimensional k (artinianTangentSpace Λ k
      (isomorphismClasses (BasedCategory.ofFunctor D.projection) hD.predeformation.cofibered))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.hasEffectiveFormalObjects
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0GH8 assume `X' ⟶ S` is separated. Then every formal object for the contraction
functor `F` is effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEffectiveFormalObjects (hX' : Space.IsSeparated B S hS (terminal.from c.X')) :
    LocallyNoetherianOver.HasEffectiveFormalObjects B S hS (contractionFunctor c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isOpenImmersion_smooth_of_isVersalAtCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GI9.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `V` a scheme locally of finite type
over `S`, `Z ⊆ |V|` closed, `W` a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space over `S` with `W_red`
locally of finite type over `S`, and `g : V_{/Z} ⟶ W` an adic morphism. If `v ∈ V` is a closed
point at which `g` is versal (Section 07XZ), then there is an open neighbourhood `U ⊆ V` of `v`
such that the restriction `U_{/Z} ⟶ W` of `g` is smooth in the sense of Bootstrap, Definition
03XZ.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_smooth_of_isVersalAtCompletion
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian S] (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hV : AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj V : Over S).hom)
    (Z : Set (Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj V))) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (W : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hW : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS W)
    (Wred : FppfSheaf B S hS) (ι : Wred ⟶ W) (_hι : IsReduction B S hS W Wred ι)
    (_hWred : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteTypeULift.{u + 1} B S hS (terminal.from Wred.obj))
    (g : Space.completionSheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj V) Z ⟶ W) (hg : IsAdicMorphism B S hS g)
    (v : ((Over.post B.inclusion).obj V : Over S).left) (hvc : IsClosed ({v} : Set _))
    (hvZ : v ∈ Space.pointsToScheme B S hS V '' Z)
    (hvers : IsVersalAtCompletion B S hS V Z W g v) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : U ⟶ V),
      IsOpenImmersion ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map i) ∧
      v ∈ Set.range ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map i) ∧
      ∃ hrep, Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ a ↦ Space.IsSmoothULift.{u + 1} B S hS a.hom)
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS (yoneda.map i) Z ≫ g).hom hrep
declarations.comment: an open neighbourhood `U` of the closed point `v` with `U_{/Z} ⟶ W` smooth in the sense of Bootstrap, Definition 03XZ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.contractionFunctor_hasOpenVersality
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0GH8 the functor `F` of Stacks 0GHA satisfies openness of versality:
for every scheme `V` locally of finite type over `S`, every `ξ ∈ F(V)` and every finite type point
`v₀ ∈ V` at which `ξ` is versal, there is an open neighbourhood of `v₀` in `V` at every finite type
point of which `ξ` is versal.
declarations.statement:
theorem contractionFunctor_hasOpenVersality (c : ContractionSituation B S hS) :
    LocallyNoetherianOver.HasOpenVersality B S hS (contractionFunctor c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.exists_solution_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GIB (Artin's theorem on contractions).** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme whose
local rings at finite type points are G-rings, `X'` an algebraic space locally of finite type over
`S`, `T' ⊆ |X'|` closed, `W` a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space over `S` with `W_red`
locally of finite type over `S`, and `g : X'_{/T'} ⟶ W` a formal modification (Situation 0GH8,
the data of `c`). If `X'` and `W` are separated over `S`, then there are a proper morphism
`f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S`, a closed subset `T ⊆ |X|` and an isomorphism
`a : X_{/T} ≅ W` such that (1) `T'` is the inverse image of `T` under `|f|`, (2) `f` maps
`X' ∖ T'` isomorphically onto `X ∖ T` (the open subspace `U` of the solution has `|U| = |X| ∖ T`),
and (3) `g = a ∘ f_{/T}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_solution_of_isSeparated (c : ContractionSituation B S hS)
    (hG : ∀ s : S, IsFiniteTypePoint s → IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s))
    (hX' : Space.IsSeparated B S hS (terminal.from c.X'))
    (hW : FormalSpace.IsSeparatedMorphism B S hS (terminal.from c.W)) :
    ∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (s : Solution c X),
      Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS s.U.toFunctor s.U.ι) = s.Tᶜ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.separatednessRemark
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0GH8, with the local rings of `S` at its finite type points G-rings
and **no separatedness assumed on `X'` or on `W`**:

1. the diagonal `Δ : F ⟶ F × F` of Artin's functor is representable (by schemes, a fortiori by
   algebraic spaces): the bootstrap of the remark, applying Artin's theorem in the separated case
   to the triples `E'`, `(E' ⟶ V)⁻¹Z`, `E'_{/Z} ⟶ E_W` of Stacks 0GHD;
2. "the proof of Lemma 0GI8 is the only place where separatedness of `X'` is used, and only to
   obtain `x' : V' ⟶ X'`": for every `X'` for which the morphisms `x'` exist (the algebraization
   property `HasCompletionAlgebraization`), Artin's theorem holds, with no separatedness of `X'`
   or `W`;
3. in particular Artin's theorem holds when `X'` alone is separated over `S`, `W` being arbitrary.

The solutions are the solutions of Stacks 0GIB whose open part `U` is the complement of `T` (the
corrected notion of Stacks 0GHB). The remark's closing sentences on quasi-separated `X'` rest on
Remark 0GHK, outside the Stacks project; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem separatednessRemark
    (hG : ∀ s : S, IsFiniteTypePoint s → IsGRing (S.presheaf.stalk s)) :
    (uliftYoneda.{u + 1} (C := LocallyNoetherianOver B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable
        (diag (contractionFunctor c)) ∧
      (c.HasCompletionAlgebraization → ∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (s : Solution c X), Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS s.U.toFunctor s.U.ι) = s.Tᶜ) ∧
      (Space.IsSeparated B S hS (terminal.from c.X') → ∃ (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (s : Solution c X), Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS s.U.toFunctor s.U.ι) = s.Tᶜ)
declarations.comment: the diagonal of F is representable with no separatedness of X' or W; the theorem holds for every X' admitting the morphisms x' of Lemma 0GI8, with no separatedness of X' or W; the theorem holds with X' separated and W arbitrary. The closing sentences on quasi-separated X' rest on Remark 0GHK (algebraization results of Bhatt and of Hall-Rydh outside the Stacks project), which the source does not state or prove

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.Analytification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GID.** The analytification data the remark posits, over a base `S` contained in
a big fppf site `B` and with values in a category `An` standing for the fictitious category
`An_S` of analytic spaces over `S`: an analytification `Y ↦ Y^an`, its rigid part
`Y ↦ Y^rig` with the inclusion `Y^rig ⟶ Y^an`, the notions of open immersion, closed
immersion and open complement in `An`, and the comparison morphisms
`can : (Y_{/Z})^rig ⟶ (Y ∖ Z)^an`, subject to the four requirements the remark imposes.

Nothing here is asserted to exist: this is the remark's fiction carried as a hypothesis, so
that what the remark deduces from it can be stated and proved. See the module documentation
for the two places where the encoding departs from the source — the two functors are total on
the ambient category of fppf sheaves rather than defined only on locally Noetherian formal
algebraic spaces, and `Y ↦ Y_red` is not an operation, property (b) being quantified over
reductions instead.
declarations.statement:
structure Analytification (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (An : Type v) [Category.{w} An]
