declarations.comment: the fictitious category of analytic spaces over S and the fictitious analytification functor, together with the four properties the remark requires of them: (a) that open immersions, closed immersions and open complements of closed immersions exist in An_S, (b) that the analytification of a reduction Y_red ⟶ Y is a closed immersion with Y^rig ⟶ Y^an as its open complement, (c) that for an algebraic space Y and a closed Z the analytification of Y_{/Z} ⟶ Y is an open immersion and induces an open immersion can : (Y_{/Z})^rig ⟶ (Y ∖ Z)^an, and (d) that the rigid part of a formal modification is an isomorphism. The remark's closing claim, that the resulting requirement is equivalent to compatibility condition (4), is not stated: the source makes it only under assumptions of faithfulness of the analytification functor that it does not formulate

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.AnalyticSquareCommutes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GID.** The requirement of the remark: that the square

```
        (V_{/Z})^rig  --can-->  (V ∖ Z)^an
            |                        |
  (g^rig)⁻¹ ∘ x̂^rig              (u')^an
            v                        v
      (X'_{/T'})^rig  --can-->  (X' ∖ T')^an
```

commute, for a triple `(Z, u', x̂)` satisfying conditions (1), (2), (3) and for analytification
data as the remark posits. The two horizontal morphisms are the comparison morphisms of
property (c), the right-hand column is the analytification of `u'`, and the left-hand column
is `x̂^rig` followed by the inverse of the isomorphism `g^rig` of property (d).

This is a requirement on the given data, and only that. Whether it is equivalent to
compatibility condition (4) is left open: the source asserts that equivalence only under
assumptions of faithfulness of the analytification functor which it does not state.
declarations.statement: def AnalyticSquareCommutes {V : BigFppfOver B S hS} (t : PreCompatibilityTriple c V) : Prop
declarations.comment: the requirement that the displayed square of analytic spaces commute: the comparison morphism can : (V_{/Z})^rig ⟶ (V ∖ Z)^an followed by the analytification of u' agrees with x̂^rig followed by the inverse of the isomorphism g^rig and then by can : (X'_{/T'})^rig ⟶ (X' ∖ T')^an. It is stated as a requirement on the posited analytification data, exactly as the source states it, and is not asserted to be equivalent to compatibility condition (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.isIso_rigFunctor_map_g_and_range_pointsMap_ι_U'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GID.** The remark's own observation that its requirement is well formed: in
Situation 0GH8 the morphism `g^rig : (X'_{/T'})^rig ⟶ W^rig` is an isomorphism, by property
(d) of the analytification data applied to the formal modification `g`, so that the composite
`(g^rig)⁻¹ ∘ x̂^rig` forming the left-hand column of the square exists; and `|U'| = |X'| ∖ T'`,
so that the bottom row of the square, which lands in the analytification of the open subspace
of `X'` complementary to `T'`, may be read as landing in `(X' ∖ T')^an`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_rigFunctor_map_g_and_range_pointsMap_ι_U' :
    IsIso (d.rigFunctor.map c.g) ∧
      Set.range (Space.pointsMap B S hS c.U'.toFunctor c.U'.ι) = c.T'ᶜ
declarations.comment: that the requirement is well formed, which is the remark's sentence "this makes sense as g^rig : (X'_{/T'})^rig ⟶ W^rig is an isomorphism and U' = X' ∖ T'": the first conjunct is the invertibility of g^rig, which is what lets the left-hand column of the square be formed as (g^rig)⁻¹ ∘ x̂^rig, and the second is that the point set of U' is the complement of T'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.analyticSquareCommutes_iff
declarations.doc:
The inverse-free form of the remark's requirement: the square commutes exactly when there
is a unique morphism `h : (V_{/Z})^rig ⟶ (X'_{/T'})^rig` with `h` followed by `g^rig` equal
to `x̂^rig` and with the square formed from `h` commutative.

This is the precise content of the remark's "this makes sense": the left-hand column of the
square is not given, it is the unique filler over `x̂^rig` along `g^rig`, and it exists
because `g^rig` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem analyticSquareCommutes_iff {V : BigFppfOver B S hS} (t : PreCompatibilityTriple c V) :
    AnalyticSquareCommutes c d t ↔
      ∃! h : d.rigFunctor.obj (Space.completionSheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj V) t.Z) ⟶
          d.rigFunctor.obj (Space.completionSheaf B S hS c.X' c.T'),
        h ≫ d.rigFunctor.map c.g = d.rigFunctor.map t.x ∧
          d.can (yoneda.obj V) (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V) t.Z t.isClosed_Z ≫
              d.anFunctor.map (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS t.u') =
            h ≫ d.can c.X' c.isAlgebraicSpace_X' c.T' c.isClosed_T'
declarations.comment: that the requirement is well formed, in the inverse-free form that carries the mathematical content of the remark's sentence "this makes sense as g^rig is an isomorphism": the square commutes exactly when there is a UNIQUE filler h over x̂^rig along g^rig making the square formed from h commute. The left-hand column of the source's square is not given data, it is that filler, and it exists and is unique precisely because g^rig is invertible by property (d). This is the substantive reading; the conjunction in AlgebraicGeometry.Artin.ContractionSituation.isIso_rigFunctor_map_g_and_range_pointsMap_ι_U' is the literal reading of the same sentence

registrations.name: RelSeries.length
registrations.comment: the length of a chain of prime ideals

declarations.name: Algebra.Smooth.prod_iff
declarations.doc:
**A product of two algebras is smooth if and only if both factors are.** Let `R` be a ring and
let `S = S' × S''` be a product of `R`-algebras. Then `S` is smooth over `R` if and only if both
`S'` and `S''` are smooth over `R`.

Each factor is the principal localization of `S` at one of the complementary idempotents
`(1, 0)` and `(0, 1)`, which is why the equivalence holds; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.Smooth.prod_iff (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (S' : Type*) [CommRing S']
    [Algebra R S'] (S'' : Type*) [CommRing S''] [Algebra R S''] :
    Algebra.Smooth R (S' × S'') ↔ Algebra.Smooth R S' ∧ Algebra.Smooth R S''
declarations.comment:
The product is the literal `S' × S''`, with the componentwise `Prod.algebra`
structure; the abstract form (an `S` with `S ≃ₐ[R] S' × S''`) follows by transport, via
`Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_equiv` and `Algebra.FinitePresentation.equiv`. The two factors are
allowed to lie in different universes, so this is not an instance of Mathlib's
`Algebra.FormallySmooth.pi_iff`; that lemma also settles only the formal smoothness half, the
finite presentation of each factor of a finitely presented product being the content added here.
See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBilinearPairing_iff_moduleObj_isBilinear
declarations.doc:
**Bilinear maps of sheaves of modules are bilinear maps of module objects.** Let `O` be a sheaf
of commutative rings. Its underlying sheaf of sets is a ring object in the category of sheaves of
sets, and the underlying sheaves of sets of `O`-modules `A`, `B`, `N` are module objects over it.
A map `q : A × B → N` of sheaves of sets is a bilinear map of sheaves of `O`-modules if and only if
it is a bilinear map of these module objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBilinearPairing_iff_moduleObj_isBilinear
    {A B N : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Tensor.ringSheaf O)}
    (q : moduleSheaf (Tensor.ringSheaf O) A ⨯ moduleSheaf (Tensor.ringSheaf O) B ⟶
      moduleSheaf (Tensor.ringSheaf O) N) :
    IsBilinearPairing (Tensor.ringSheaf O) q ↔
      letI := hasSheafCompose_forget₂_commRingCat.{w} J
      letI := sheafCommRingObj J O
      letI := sheafModuleObj J O A
      letI := sheafModuleObj J O B
      letI := sheafModuleObj J O N
      ModuleObj.IsBilinear (underlyingRingSheaf J O) (F := underlyingModuleSheaf J A)
        (G := underlyingModuleSheaf J B) (H := underlyingModuleSheaf J N) q
declarations.comment:
the fifth characterisation of the section: `O_X` is a ring object in the category
of sheaves of sets, `F`, `G`, `H` are module objects over it, and a bilinear map `F x G -> H` of
sheaves of modules is the same thing as a bilinear map of module objects over a ring object, the
notion `CategoryTheory.ModuleObj.IsBilinear` defined for module objects over a ring object in any
category with finite products (a cartesian monoidal category). The ring and module objects are
`Stacks.sheafCommRingObj` and `Stacks.sheafModuleObj`. Over an arbitrary site rather than only the
opens of a ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBilinearPairing_iff_forall_exists_linearMap
declarations.doc:
**Bilinearity is bilinearity on sections.** A map `q : A × B → N` of the underlying sheaves of
sets of three sheaves of modules over a sheaf of commutative rings `O` is a bilinear map of sheaves
of `O`-modules if and only if, for every object `U`, the induced map `A(U) × B(U) → N(U)` is an
`O(U)`-bilinear map of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBilinearPairing_iff_forall_exists_linearMap
    (q : moduleSheaf (Tensor.ringSheaf O) A ⨯ moduleSheaf (Tensor.ringSheaf O) B ⟶
      moduleSheaf (Tensor.ringSheaf O) N) :
    IsBilinearPairing (Tensor.ringSheaf O) q ↔
      ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, ∃ φ : A.val.obj U →ₗ[(Tensor.ringSheaf O).obj.obj U]
          B.val.obj U →ₗ[(Tensor.ringSheaf O).obj.obj U] N.val.obj U,
        ∀ (a : A.val.obj U) (b : B.val.obj U), φ a b = pairingApp (Tensor.ringSheaf O) q U a b
declarations.comment:
the definition of the section: a bilinear map `F x G -> H` of sheaves of
`O_X`-modules is a map of sheaves of sets such that for every open `U` the induced map
`F(U) x G(U) -> H(U)` is an `O_X(U)`-bilinear map of modules; here `IsBilinearPairing`, the
condition the rest of the section is phrased in, is shown to be exactly that, with `O_X(U)`-bilinear
meaning given by an `O_X(U)`-linear map `F(U) -> Hom(G(U), H(U))`. Over an arbitrary site rather
than only the opens of a ringed space

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBilinearPairing_iff_stalk
declarations.doc:
**The stalk characterisation of bilinearity.** A pairing of the underlying sheaves of sets
of three sheaves of modules on a topological space is bilinear if and only if the map it induces
on the stalks at a point is bilinear over the stalk of the sheaf of rings, at every point.

This is the third assertion of the section [Stacks, Tag 0GIG]. The forward direction is
`IsBilinearPairing.isBilinearPairingObj` and needs nothing of the space; the converse is
`isBilinearPairing_of_forall_sheafFiber` at the conservative family of points that a
topological space provides.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBilinearPairing_iff_stalk :
    IsBilinearPairing R q ↔ ∀ x : X, IsBilinearPairingObj R q (stalkTypeFunctor x)
declarations.comment:
the third characterisation of the section: a map of the underlying sheaves of sets
which induces a bilinear map of modules on the stalk at every point of `X` is bilinear, and
conversely. The stalk is taken in the shape the site gives it, the fibre functor at the point of
`Opens X` determined by `x`, which `Opens.pointFiberStalkFunctorIso` identifies with the ordinary
stalk; its module structure over the stalk of `O_X` is the one
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.moduleObjModule` transports. Over a not necessarily commutative sheaf of
rings. The forward direction is proved for every finite-product-preserving functor to types, as
`IsBilinearPairing.isBilinearPairingObj`, and the converse over any site with a conservative
family of points, as `isBilinearPairing_iff_forall_sheafFiber`; the points of a topological space
are such a family, so this statement carries no hypothesis of its own beyond the standing binders
of the section

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBilinearPairing_iff_forall_coyoneda
declarations.doc:
**The Yoneda characterisation of bilinearity.** A pairing of the underlying sheaves of sets
is bilinear if and only if the rule it induces on morphisms from an arbitrary sheaf of sets `S`
is bilinear over the ring of morphisms from `S` to the sheaf of rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBilinearPairing_iff_forall_coyoneda :
    IsBilinearPairing R q ↔
      ∀ S : Sheaf J (Type w), IsBilinearPairingObj R q (coyoneda.obj (op S))
declarations.comment:
the fourth characterisation of the section: a pairing is bilinear if and only if
for every sheaf of sets `S` the induced rule `Mor(S, F) x Mor(S, G) -> Mor(S, H)` is bilinear
over the ring `Mor(S, O_X)`. The ring and module structures on those morphism sets are the ones
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.ringObjRing` and `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.moduleObjModule` transport along
`Mor(S, -)`, which preserves finite products. Over an arbitrary site rather than only the opens
of a ringed space, and over a not necessarily commutative sheaf of rings. The forward direction
is `IsBilinearPairing.isBilinearPairingObj`; the converse needs only the single `S` which is the
source of each of the four squares, with the three arguments taken to be the projections out of
it

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsBilinearPairing
declarations.doc:
A morphism from the product of the underlying sheaves of sets of two sheaves of modules to
that of a third is **bilinear** when, on local sections, it is additive and compatible with
scalar multiplication in each of its two arguments. This is the condition defining
`Bilin_O(A × B, N)` in Stacks 18.26.
declarations.statement:
structure IsBilinearPairing (q : moduleSheaf R A ⨯ moduleSheaf R B ⟶ moduleSheaf R N) :
    Prop
declarations.comment:
the definition of the section: a bilinear map `F × G → H` of sheaves of
modules is a map of the underlying sheaves of sets whose induced map `F(U) × G(U) → H(U)` on
sections is `O_X(U)`-bilinear for every `U`. Over an arbitrary site rather than only the opens
of a ringed space, and over a not necessarily commutative sheaf of rings

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isBilinearPairing_iff_squares
declarations.doc: Bilinearity of a pairing is equivalent to the four commuting squares.
declarations.statement:
lemma isBilinearPairing_iff_squares :
    IsBilinearPairing R q ↔ addLeftSquare R q ∧ addRightSquare R q ∧
      smulLeftSquare R q ∧ smulRightSquare R q
declarations.comment:
the second characterisation of the section: a pairing is bilinear if and only if
certain diagrams of maps of sheaves of sets commute, imitating the usual axioms for bilinear
maps of modules. The diagram displayed in the section, for `f(x + y, z) = f(x, z) + f(y, z)`,
is `addLeftSquare`. Over an arbitrary site rather than only the opens of a ringed space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GIH.** In a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes whose transition morphisms are closed immersions, if all the structure
morphisms to a quasi-separated base are locally of finite type and the morphism induced on the
limit is an immersion, then the structure morphisms are immersions for all sufficiently large
indices.
`Nonempty I` is not a weakening: it is what makes `Filter.atTop` on the index a PROPER
filter. Over an empty index `atTop = ⊥` and the conclusion would be vacuously true, so this
hypothesis is what rules vacuity out. The source assumes it too — a directed limit is indexed
by a directed set, which is nonempty by convention.
declarations.statement:
lemma eventually_isImmersion {I : Type v} [Preorder I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Small.{u} I]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj S) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (f : c.pt ⟶ S)
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    [∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj (op i))]
    [∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj (op i))]
    [∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), IsClosedImmersion (D.map (homOfLE h).op)]
    [∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (t.app (op i))]
    (hcomm : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f)
    [IsImmersion f] :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsImmersion (t.app (op i))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeilCohomology.WeilRealization.exists_globalSections_isoClassEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GIJ.** Let `k` be a field and `F` a field of characteristic `0`. A Weil
cohomology theory (Definition 0FI2) is the same thing as a `ℚ`-linear symmetric monoidal functor
`G : M_k ⥤ graded F-vector spaces` (`Stacks.WeilCohomology.WeilRealization`) such that

1. `G(𝟏(1))` is nonzero only in degree `-2`, and
2. for every smooth projective `X` over `k` with `k' = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` the map
   `G(h(Spec k')) → G(h(X))` is an isomorphism in degree `0`
   (`Stacks.WeilCohomology.WeilRealization.GlobalSections`):

there is a bijection between isomorphism classes of such functors and isomorphism classes of
Weil cohomology theories, sending the class of `G` to the class of the Weil cohomology theory
`H^*(X) = G(h(X))` of Stacks 0FHK.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_globalSections_isoClassEquiv :
    ∃ e : Quotient ((isoSetoid k F).comap
          (Subtype.val : {G : WeilRealization k F // G.GlobalSections} → _)) ≃
        Quotient (WeilCohomologyTheory.isoSetoid k F),
      ∀ (G : {G : WeilRealization k F // G.GlobalSections}) (T : WeilCohomologyTheory k F),
        e (Quotient.mk _ G) = Quotient.mk _ T ↔
          (Quotient.mk (WeilDataAxioms.isoSetoid k F) G.1.toWeilDataAxioms =
            Quotient.mk _ T.toWeilDataAxioms)
declarations.comment:
a Weil cohomology theory is the same thing as a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor
G : M_k -> graded F-vector spaces with G(1(1)) nonzero only in degree -2 and
G(h(Spec k')) -> G(h(X)) an isomorphism in degree 0 for k' = Gamma(X, O_X): a bijection of
isomorphism classes, G corresponding to H^*(X) = G(h(X))

declarations.name: isFilteredColimitOfEtale_colim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GIM, Lemma 10.154.4.**

Let `I` be a directed set (a nonempty directed preorder). Let `𝓡, 𝓐 : I ⥤ CommRingCat`
be two functors (the systems `i ↦ R_i` and `i ↦ A_i`) and `α : 𝓡 ⟶ 𝓐` a natural
transformation (the structure maps `R_i → A_i`, whose naturality squares are the
required commutative squares with the transition maps).

Take colimits `R = colimit 𝓡` and `A = colimit 𝓐`; the induced structure map
`R → A` is `colimMap α`. If each `A_i = 𝓐.obj i` is a filtered colimit of étale
`R_i`-algebras (via the structure map `(α.app i).hom`), then `A` is a filtered
colimit of étale `R`-algebras (via the induced structure map `(colimMap α).hom`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFilteredColimitOfEtale_colim
    (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
    (𝓡 𝓐 : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (α : 𝓡 ⟶ 𝓐)
    (hetale : ∀ i, IsFilteredColimitOfEtaleHom (α.app i).hom) :
    IsFilteredColimitOfEtaleHom (colimMap α).hom

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Strict henselization and tensor products, quasi-finite case** (Stacks 0GIP (1)). Let
`D = B ⊗_A C` and let `P` be a prime of `D`, with contractions to `A`, `B`, `C`. Let `A^sh`,
`B^sh`, `C^sh`, `D^sh` be strict henselizations of the localizations of `A`, `B`, `C`, `D` at these
primes, with local ring maps forming a commutative square over the square `A → B, C → D`. If
`A → B` is of finite type and quasi-finite at `P ∩ B`, then
`B^sh ⊗_{A^sh} C^sh → D^sh` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_quasiFiniteAt
    {Ap : Type u} [CommRing Ap] [IsLocalRing Ap] [Algebra A Ap]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Ap (P.under A)]
    [Algebra Ap Ash] [IsScalarTower A Ap Ash] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ap Ash)]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Ap) (ResidueField Ash)] [IsHenselization Ap (ResidueField Ash) Ash]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Bp) (ResidueField Bsh)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Bsh)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Csh)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Csh Dsh)]
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt A (P.under B)] :
    Function.Bijective (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom Ash Bsh Dsh)
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom Ash Csh Dsh) fun _ _ => .all _ _)
declarations.comment:
(1).
The field `κ` is replaced by the prime `P = ker(D → κ)` of `D`: the statement is proved for all
strict henselizations `A^sh`, `B^sh`, `C^sh`, `D^sh` of the localizations at the contractions of `P`
and all local maps between them forming a commutative square over `A → B, C → D`, which includes
the maps of Lemma 04GU attached to the embeddings of the residue fields in `κ`. The isomorphism is
the bijectivity of `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` of the two maps into `D^sh`, and
`D = B ⊗_A C` is any `Algebra.IsPushout A B C D`. Quasi-finiteness at `P ∩ B` is
`Algebra.FiniteType A B` with
`Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt A (P.under B)`, as in Lemma 04GH. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_ind_quasiFinite
declarations.doc:
**Strict henselization and tensor products, colimit case** (Stacks 0GIP (2)). In the
situation of Lemma 0GIP, if `B` is a filtered colimit of quasi-finite `A`-algebras, then
`B^sh ⊗_{A^sh} C^sh → D^sh` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_ind_quasiFinite
    {Ap : Type u} [CommRing Ap] [IsLocalRing Ap] [Algebra A Ap]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Ap (P.under A)]
    [Algebra Ap Ash] [IsScalarTower A Ap Ash] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ap Ash)]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Ap) (ResidueField Ash)] [IsHenselization Ap (ResidueField Ash) Ash]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Bp) (ResidueField Bsh)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Bsh)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Csh)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Csh Dsh)]
    (hB : (ObjectProperty.ind.{u} fun X : CommAlgCat.{u} A =>
      Algebra.FiniteType A X ∧ Algebra.QuasiFinite A X) (CommAlgCat.of A B)) :
    Function.Bijective (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom Ash Bsh Dsh)
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom Ash Csh Dsh) fun _ _ => .all _ _)
declarations.comment:
(2).
The field `κ` is replaced by the prime `P = ker(D → κ)` of `D`: the statement is proved for all
strict henselizations `A^sh`, `B^sh`, `C^sh`, `D^sh` of the localizations at the contractions of `P`
and all local maps between them forming a commutative square over `A → B, C → D`, which includes
the maps of Lemma 04GU attached to the embeddings of the residue fields in `κ`. The isomorphism is
the bijectivity of `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` of the two maps into `D^sh`, and
`D = B ⊗_A C` is any `Algebra.IsPushout A B C D`.
"Filtered colimit of quasi-finite `A`-algebras" is
`ObjectProperty.ind` in `CommAlgCat A` of `Algebra.FiniteType A X ∧ Algebra.QuasiFinite A X`. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_ind_quasiFinite_localization
declarations.doc:
**Strict henselization and tensor products, local colimit case** (Stacks 0GIP (3)). In the
situation of Lemma 0GIP, if `B_{P ∩ B}` is a filtered colimit of quasi-finite algebras over
`A_{P ∩ A}`, then `B^sh ⊗_{A^sh} C^sh → D^sh` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_ind_quasiFinite_localization
    {Ap : Type u} [CommRing Ap] [IsLocalRing Ap] [Algebra A Ap]

    [Algebra Ap Ash] [IsScalarTower A Ap Ash] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ap Ash)]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Ap) (ResidueField Ash)] [IsHenselization Ap (ResidueField Ash) Ash]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField Bp) (ResidueField Bsh)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Bsh)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ash Csh)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Csh Dsh)]
    [Algebra Ap Bp] [Algebra A Bp] [IsScalarTower A Ap Bp] [IsScalarTower A B Bp]
    (hB : (ObjectProperty.ind.{u} fun X : CommAlgCat.{u} Ap =>
      Algebra.FiniteType Ap X ∧ Algebra.QuasiFinite Ap X) (CommAlgCat.of Ap Bp)) :
    Function.Bijective (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom Ash Bsh Dsh)
      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom Ash Csh Dsh) fun _ _ => .all _ _)
declarations.comment:
(3).
The field `κ` is replaced by the prime `P = ker(D → κ)` of `D`: the statement is proved for all
strict henselizations `A^sh`, `B^sh`, `C^sh`, `D^sh` of the localizations at the contractions of `P`
and all local maps between them forming a commutative square over `A → B, C → D`, which includes

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.IsHenselization.bijective_tensorProduct_lift_of_isIntegral
