declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimit_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_Γ_smallEtale_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GIS].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`K : I → D⁺(X_étale)` be a family of objects of the bounded below derived category of abelian
sheaves on the small étale site of `X` and let `a : ℤ` be such that `H^n(K i) = 0` for `n < a`
and all `i`, that is `(K i).IsGE a`. Then `RΓ(X, ⨁ i, K i) = ⨁ i, RΓ(X, K i)`.

Nothing is assumed: the one input of the argument beyond the injective resolutions bounded below
by `a` of [Stacks, Tag 07D9] and Leray's acyclicity lemma [Stacks, Tag 015E] is that each
`H^q_étale(X, -)` commutes with the direct sum, which is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_rightDerived_Γ_smallEtale`, and that
is where the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `X` are used.

The source states the lemma in `D(X_étale)`; its hypothesis places every `K i` in `D⁺`, and the
module docstring records why the statement is read there and why the index universe is
`max (u + 1) v`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimit_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_Γ_smallEtale_of_isGE
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] {I : Type (max (u + 1) v)}
    (K : I → DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}))
    (a : ℤ) (hK : ∀ i, (K i).IsGE a) :
    PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor K)
      (Sheaf.Γ X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus
declarations.comment:
RΓ(X, ⨁ K_i) = ⨁ RΓ(X, K_i) for a family of D⁺(X_étale) with common lower bound
a, on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. The global sections case of the machinery behind
Tag 0GIW; unlike that tag nothing is carried, the input that H^q_étale(X, -) commutes with direct
sums being `preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_rightDerived_Γ_smallEtale`. The index type lies in
Type (max (u+1) v), the universe at which the abelian sheaves on the small étale site are
Grothendieck abelian: the termwise direct sum of the resolutions is formed inside that category,
so the index universe and the Grothendieck universe are the same.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isSystemColimit_etaleHypercohomologyMap_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Étale cohomology of a bounded below complex pulled back to a limit of schemes**
([Stacks, Tag 0GIT]). Let `S` be a scheme, `X = lim X_i` the limit of a directed inverse system of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes over `S`, with structure morphisms `ι_i : X_i ⟶ S`,
`g : X ⟶ S` and affine transition morphisms, and `K ∈ D^+(S_étale)`. Then for every `p ∈ ℤ` the
pull back maps `H^p(X_i, K|_{X_i}) ⟶ H^p(X, K|_X)` exhibit `H^p(X, K|_X)` as the colimit of the
system of the `H^p(X_i, K|_{X_i})`. Here `K|_{X_i}` is the derived inverse image of `K` along
`ι_i`, and the transition maps are induced by the comparisons `f_{i'i}⁻¹ ι_i⁻¹ ≅ ι_{i'}⁻¹` and
`f_i⁻¹ ι_i⁻¹ ≅ g⁻¹` of inverse images along composites.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSystemColimit_etaleHypercohomologyMap_of_isLimit (ι : ∀ i, D.obj i ⟶ S)
    (hι : ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), D.map a ≫ ι j = ι i) (g : c.pt ⟶ S)
    (hg : ∀ i, c.π.app i ≫ ι i = g)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology S) Ab.{u + 1})) (p : ℤ) :
    IsSystemColimit
      (fun i => AddCommGrpCat.of (etaleHypercohomology (D.obj i)
        ((smallEtalePullbackAb (ι i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) p))
      (fun {i j} a => AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (etaleHypercohomologyMap (D.map a)
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryIsoComp _ _ _
          (smallEtalePullbackAbComp' (D.map a) (ι j) (ι i) (hι a).symm)).inv.app K.obj) p))
      (AddCommGrpCat.of (etaleHypercohomology c.pt
        ((smallEtalePullbackAb g).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) p))
      (fun i => AddCommGrpCat.ofHom (etaleHypercohomologyMap (c.π.app i)
        ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryIsoComp _ _ _
          (smallEtalePullbackAbComp' (c.π.app i) (ι i) g (hg i).symm)).inv.app K.obj) p))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.pullbackProjectionMap
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map of Stacks 0GIU**, `h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} K_i ⟶ R^p g_* K`, for
`K_0 ∈ D^+(X_{0, étale})`, `K_i` the pullback of `K_0` to `X_i` and `K` the pullback of `K_0` to
`X`: the derived comparison map `derivedProjectionMap` at `L = K_i`, `M = K` and
`κ = κ_i : R f_i^{-1} K_i ≅ K`.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackProjectionMap (K₀ : PlusAb (DX.obj i₀)) (K : PlusAb cX.pt) {i : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ i₀)
    (κ : (derivedPullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).obj (derivedLevelPullback a K₀) ≅ K) :
    (smallEtalePullbackAb (cS.π.app i)).obj
        ((homologyAb (DS.obj i) p).obj
          ((derivedPushforwardAb (γ.app i)).obj (derivedLevelPullback a K₀))) ⟶
      (homologyAb cS.pt p).obj
        ((derivedPushforwardAb (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS)).obj K)
declarations.comment: the comparison maps `h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} K_i ⟶ R^p g_* K` of the assertion, for all `p ∈ ℤ`, with `K_i` the derived pullback of `K_0 ∈ D^+(X_{0, étale})` to `X_i`, built from the derived base change comparison of Stacks 0F02 together with exactness of `h_i^{-1}`; their naturality in `K_0` is `derivedProjectionMap_naturality`. The colimit assertion `R^p g_* K = colim_{i ≥ 0} h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} K_i` is NOT proved, and cannot be: it is a formal consequence (by the dimension-shifting induction of the source over the triangle `H^a(K_0)[-a] → K_0 → τ_{≥ a+1}K_0`) of the colimit assertion of Stacks 0EYM, which the carrier `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.projectionMap` of that tag states in its own clause string is not proved; indeed the colimit itself cannot be formed, since that needs the cocycle condition of Stacks 0E47 which 0EYM's carrier also leaves open. EXTRA HYPOTHESIS: the pullback `K` of `K_0` to `X` and the isomorphisms `κ_i : R f_i^{-1} K_i ≅ K` are taken as data, as `ℱ` and `ι_i` are in 0EYM's carrier and as `K` is given data in the source; this is a generalization, since in the source's situation those data exist.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.derivedPullbackHigherDirectImageColimit
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a directed set, `g_i : X_i ⟶ S_i` an inverse system of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms of schemes with affine transition morphisms
`f_{i'i}`, `h_{i'i}`, and `g : X ⟶ S` its limit with projections `f_i`, `h_i`. Let `0 = i₀ ∈ I`,
`K_0 ∈ D^+(X_{0, étale})`, `K_i = R f_{i0}^{-1}K_0` its pullback to `X_i` for `i ≥ 0` and
`K = R f_0^{-1}K_0` its pullback to `X`. Then for every `p ∈ ℤ` the maps
`h_{i'i}^{-1}R^pg_{i, *}K_i ⟶ R^pg_{i', *}K_{i'}` (the derived base change maps of the
transition squares composed with `R^pg_{i', *}` of `R f_{i'i}^{-1}K_i ≅ K_{i'}`), pulled back to
`S`, satisfy the cocycle condition, the maps `h_i^{-1}R^pg_{i, *}K_i ⟶ R^pg_*K` (the derived base
change maps of the projection squares composed with `R^pg_*` of `R f_i^{-1}K_i ≅ K`) are
compatible with them, and they present `R^pg_*K = colim_{i ≥ 0} h_i^{-1}R^pg_{i, *}K_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPullbackHigherDirectImageColimit (K₀ : PlusAb (DX.obj (op i₀))) (p : ℤ) :
    (∀ {j j' j'' : (Set.Ici i₀)ᵒᵖ} (c : j ⟶ j') (c' : j' ⟶ j''),
        derivedPullbackTransition γ cS i₀ p K₀ (c ≫ c') =
          derivedPullbackTransition γ cS i₀ p K₀ c' ≫ derivedPullbackTransition γ cS i₀ p K₀ c) ∧
      (∀ {j j' : (Set.Ici i₀)ᵒᵖ} (c : j ⟶ j'),
        derivedPullbackTransition γ cS i₀ p K₀ c ≫ derivedPullbackLeg γ cX cS i₀ p K₀
            (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS) (fun j => limitMorphism_comp_π γ cX cS hcS _) j =
          derivedPullbackLeg γ cX cS i₀ p K₀ (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS)
            (fun j => limitMorphism_comp_π γ cX cS hcS _) j') ∧
      IsSystemColimit (derivedPullbackTerm γ cS i₀ p K₀)
        (fun {j j'} c => derivedPullbackTransition γ cS i₀ p K₀ (j := j) (j' := j') c)
        ((homologyAb cS.pt p).obj ((derivedPushforwardAb (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS)).obj
          ((derivedPullbackAb (cX.π.app (op i₀))).obj K₀)))
        (derivedPullbackLeg γ cX cS i₀ p K₀ (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS)
          (fun j => limitMorphism_comp_π γ cX cS hcS _))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.complexHigherDirectImageColimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GIV].** Let `I` be a directed set, `g_i : X_i ⟶ S_i` an inverse system of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphisms of schemes with affine transition morphisms
`f_{i'i}`, `h_{i'i}`, and `g : X ⟶ S` its limit with projections `f_i`, `h_i`. Let
`(ℱ_i^•, φ_{i'i})` be a system of complexes of abelian sheaves on the `X_{i, étale}`, with
`ℱ_i^n = 0` for `n < a` and all `i`, and `ℱ^• = colim f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^•`, presented by maps of
complexes `ι_i : f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^• ⟶ ℱ^•` compatible with the transition maps and presenting every
term `ℱ^n` as `colim f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^n`. Then for every `p ∈ ℤ` the maps
`h_i^{-1}R^pg_{i, *}ℱ_i^• ⟶ R^pg_*ℱ^•` (the derived base change maps of the projection squares
followed by `R^pg_*ι_i`) are compatible with the maps
`h_{i'i}^{-1}R^pg_{i, *}ℱ_i^• ⟶ R^pg_{i', *}ℱ_{i'}^•` of the system of the
`R^pg_{i, *}ℱ_i^•` and present `R^pg_*ℱ^• = colim_i h_i^{-1}R^pg_{i, *}ℱ_i^•`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexHigherDirectImageColimit (F : EtaleComplexSystem DX) (a : ℤ)
    [∀ i, (F.obj i).IsStrictlyGE a]
    (𝓕 : CochainComplex (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cX.pt) Ab.{u + 1}) ℤ)
    (ι : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, ((smallEtalePullbackAb (cX.π.app i)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj (F.obj i) ⟶ 𝓕)
    (hι : F.IsPullbackCocone cX ι)
    (hpres : ∀ n, IsPullbackColimitPresentation cX (𝓕.X n) (F.term n) (fun i => (ι i).f n))
    (p : ℤ) :
    haveI := F.isStrictlyGE_of_isPullbackColimitPresentation a hpres
    (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (c : i ⟶ j),
        (complexHigherDirectImageSystem γ p a F).pullbackDiagramMap cS (i := i) (j := j) c ≫
          complexLeg γ p a F cX cS hcS 𝓕 ι i = complexLeg γ p a F cX cS hcS 𝓕 ι j) ∧
      IsComplexHigherDirectImageColimit γ p a F cX cS hcS 𝓕 ι

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.complexProjectionMap
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map of Stacks 0GIV**, `h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i^• ⟶ R^p g_* ℱ^•`, for a
complex `ℱ_i^•` of abelian sheaves on `X_{i, étale}` vanishing in degrees `< a`, a complex `ℱ^•`
on `X_étale` vanishing in degrees `< a`, and a map of complexes
`ι_i : f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^• ⟶ ℱ^•`: the derived comparison map `derivedProjectionMap` at the classes of
the two complexes in the bounded below derived categories, with `κ` the comparison
`complexPullbackComparison`.
declarations.statement:
def complexProjectionMap (i : Iᵒᵖ)
    (F : CochainComplex (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology (DX.obj i)) Ab.{u + 1}) ℤ) [F.IsStrictlyGE a]
    (G : CochainComplex (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology cX.pt) Ab.{u + 1}) ℤ) [G.IsStrictlyGE a]
    (ι : complexPullbackObj cX i F ⟶ G) :
    (smallEtalePullbackAb (cS.π.app i)).obj
        ((homologyAb (DS.obj i) p).obj
          ((derivedPushforwardAb (γ.app i)).obj (plusComplexObj a F))) ⟶
      (homologyAb cS.pt p).obj
        ((derivedPushforwardAb (limitMorphism γ cX cS hcS)).obj (plusComplexObj a G))
declarations.comment: the comparison maps `h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i^• ⟶ R^p g_* ℱ^•` of the assertion, for all `p ∈ ℤ`, where `R^p g_*` of a complex is the degree-`p` cohomology of the total right derived direct image of its class in `D^+`; built from the derived base change comparison of Stacks 0F02, exactness of `h_i^{-1}`, and — for the pullback of the complex — the invertibility of the right-derived-functor unit of the exact functor `f_i^{-1}`. The uniform lower bound `a` of the source (`ℱ_i^n = 0` for `n < a`, `a` independent of `i`) is carried as `CochainComplex.IsStrictlyGE`; naturality is `derivedProjectionMap_naturality`. The colimit assertion `R^p g_*(colim f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^•) = colim_{i ≥ 0} h_i^{-1} R^p g_{i, *} ℱ_i^•` is NOT proved, and cannot be: it is a formal consequence (by the two spectral sequences of a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution, Stacks 015J) of the colimit assertion of Stacks 0EYM, which the carrier `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.projectionMap` of that tag states in its own clause string is not proved; indeed the colimit itself cannot be formed, since that needs the cocycle condition of Stacks 0E47 which 0EYM's carrier also leaves open. EXTRA HYPOTHESIS: the complex `ℱ^• = colim f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^•` and the maps of complexes `ι_i : f_i^{-1}ℱ_i^• ⟶ ℱ^•` are taken as data, as `ℱ` and `ι_i` are in 0EYM's carrier and as the colimit is given data in the source; this is a generalization, since in the source's situation those data exist. The transition maps `φ_{i'i}` and their cocycle condition are the data of the system; the transition form of the comparison map is `derivedTransitionMap`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimit_etaleModuleDerivedDirectImage_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GIW].** Let `Λ` be a ring, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes, let `K : I → D⁺(X_étale, Λ)` be a family of objects and
let `a : ℤ` be such that `H^n(K i) = 0` for `n < a` and all `i`, that is `(K i).IsGE a`. Then
`Rf_*(⨁ i, K i) = ⨁ i, Rf_*(K i)`.

The one input that is carried rather than used is `hsums`: that each ordinary higher direct
image `R^q f_*` on the small étale site commutes with the direct sum. That is
[Stacks, Tag 09Z1], which is not proved in this repository, so it appears here as a hypothesis,
in the shape in which the source cites it. Nothing else is assumed: that `f_*` itself commutes
with the direct sum is *proved* from `hsums` at `q = 0`, and the rest of the argument of the
source — the injective resolutions bounded below by `a` of [Stacks, Tag 07D9], the right
acyclicity of their termwise direct sum, and Leray's acyclicity lemma [Stacks, Tag 015E]
identifying `Rf_*` with the termwise image on each of them — is proved.

Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f` are the hypotheses under which the source's
proof invokes [Stacks, Tag 09Z1]; they are carried here even though the argument consumes them
only through `hsums`, so that the statement is the source's.

The source states the lemma in `D(X_étale)`; its hypothesis places every `K_i` in `D⁺`, and the
module docstring records why the statement is read there, why the coefficients are an arbitrary
ring, and why the index universe is `max (u + 1) r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimit_etaleModuleDerivedDirectImage_of_isGE
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    {I : Type (max (u + 1) r)}
    (hsums : ∀ p : ℕ, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
      ((etaleModuleDirectImage.{u, r} Λ f).rightDerived p))
    (K : I → DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X)) (a : ℤ)
    (hK : ∀ i, (K i).IsGE a) :
    PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor K) (etaleModuleDerivedDirectImage.{u, r} Λ f)
declarations.comment:
Rf_*(⨁ K_i) = ⨁ Rf_* K_i for a family of D⁺(X_étale, Λ) with common lower bound
a. Tag 09Z1, that each R^q f_* on the small étale site commutes with direct sums, is carried as
the hypothesis `hsums`, since it is not proved in this library; everything
else the source cites is proved. The index type lies in Type (max (u+1) r), the universe at
which the sheaves of Λ-modules on the small étale sites are Grothendieck abelian: the termwise
direct sum of the resolutions is formed inside those categories, so the index universe and the
Grothendieck universe are the same. For Λ a general ring.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.preservesColimit_etaleAbelianDerivedDirectImage_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GIW].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes, let `K : I → D(X_étale)` be a family of objects of the derived category of abelian
sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, and let `a : ℤ` be such that `H^n(K i) = 0` for `n < a`
and all `i`, that is `(K i).IsGE a`. Then `Rf_*(⨁ i, K i) = ⨁ i, Rf_*(K i)`: the unbounded
derived direct image `Rf_* : D(X_étale) ⥤ D(Y_étale)` preserves the direct sum of the family.

Nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses. That each `R^q f_*` commutes with direct sums
is `preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_rightDerived_etaleAbelianDirectImage`, where
quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f` are used.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimit_etaleAbelianDerivedDirectImage_of_isGE
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    {I : Type (max (u + 1) v)}
    (K : I → DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}))
    (a : ℤ) (hK : ∀ i, (K i).IsGE a) :
    PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor K) (etaleAbelianDerivedDirectImage.{u, v} f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSectionsViaBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GIX, the second map.** The canonical map
`RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K) ⟶ RΓ(X_s, K|_{X_s})`, natural in `K ∈ D(X_étale)`, defined as
the source defines it: from the derived base change map `i⁻¹Rf'_*(p⁻¹K) ⟶ Rf_{s,*}(K|_{X_s})` of
the left square

```
X_s ----> X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})
|f_s             |f'
v                v
s  ---i--> Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})
```

by taking global sections: it is the identification
`RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), -) ≅ RΓ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), Rf'_* -)`, restriction of derived
global sections along `i` (an isomorphism over the strictly henselian base), derived global
sections on `s` of the base change map, the identification `RΓ(s, Rf_{s,*} -) ≅ RΓ(X_s, -)`, and
the identification of the restriction of `p⁻¹K` to `X_s` with `K|_{X_s}`.

Every derived functor here is the total right derived functor on the whole unbounded homotopy
category; their existence is not assumed but supplied by the instances
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleGlobalSectionsAb_hasRightDerivedFunctor` and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.hasRightDerivedFunctor_smallEtalePushforwardAb` (abelian sheaves on a
small étale site have K-injective resolutions).
declarations.statement:
def strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSectionsViaBaseChange :
    smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s) ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (geometricFibreToSource f s) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (geometricFibre f s)
declarations.comment: the second map: global sections of the base change map for the left square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsViaBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GIX, the first map.** The canonical map
`(Rf_*K)_s ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K)`, natural in `K ∈ D(X_étale)`, defined as the
source defines it: from the derived base change map `j⁻¹Rf_*K ⟶ Rf'_*(p⁻¹K)` of the right square

```
X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) --p--> X
|f'                           |f
v                             v
Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ---j---> S
```

by taking global sections over the strict henselization: it is the comparison
`(Rf_*K)_s ⟶ RΓ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), j⁻¹Rf_*K)` of the stalk with derived sections over the
strict henselization (`AlgebraicGeometry.vanishingCyclesMap`, an isomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_vanishingCyclesMap_id`), derived global sections over the strict
henselization of the base change map, and the identification
`RΓ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), Rf'_* -) ≅ RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), -)`. The structure morphism `j` is
written `𝟙 ≫ j`, the form in which the comparison of the stalk with sections presents it.

Every derived functor here is the total right derived functor on the whole unbounded homotopy
category; their existence is not assumed but supplied by the instances
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleGlobalSectionsAb_hasRightDerivedFunctor` and
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.hasRightDerivedFunctor_smallEtalePushforwardAb` (abelian sheaves on a
small étale site have K-injective resolutions).
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsViaBaseChange :
    smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f ⋙ smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb s.hom ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s)
declarations.comment: the first map: global sections of the base change map for the right square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsViaBaseChange_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GIX, the composition clause.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and a
geometric point `s` of `S`, the composite of the two canonical maps

`(Rf_*K)_s ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K) ⟶ RΓ(X_s, K|_{X_s})`

obtained by taking global sections of the base change maps of the right and of the left square
(`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsViaBaseChange` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSectionsViaBaseChange`) is the usual base
change map `(Rf_*K)_s ⟶ RΓ(X_s, K|_{X_s})`: the identification of the stalk at `s` with global
sections on `s` of the inverse image, followed by global sections on `s` of the derived base change
map `s⁻¹Rf_*K ⟶ Rq_*(K|_{X_s})` of Stacks 0A2A for the cartesian square defining the geometric
fibre (`q : X_s ⟶ s` its structure morphism), and by the identification
`RΓ(s, Rq_* -) ≅ RΓ(X_s, -)` of Stacks 0D6H. This holds as an equality of natural transformations
on the whole unbounded derived category `D(X_étale)`; nothing is assumed of `f` or of `s`, and the
existence of the unbounded derived functors involved is supplied by instances, not assumed.

The two maps agree with the ones this library constructs directly
(`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_eq_baseChange` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSections_eq_baseChange`), whose composite is
computed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_comp_fibreSections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsViaBaseChange_comp :
    derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsViaBaseChange B hS f s ≫
        strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSectionsViaBaseChange B hS f s =
      Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f)
          (derivedGeometricStalkToPullbackSections s.hom) ≫
        (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv ≫
        Functor.whiskerRight (geometricFibreDerivedBaseChangeAb f s)
          (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections s.source) ≫
        (Functor.associator _ _ _).hom ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (geometricFibreToSource f s))
          (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsPushforwardIsoAb (geometricFibreToPoint f s)).hom
declarations.comment: the composition is the base change map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GIX, the map to the fibre.** The canonical map

`RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K) ⟶ RΓ(X_s, K|_{X_s})`

for an object `K` of the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of
`X`, natural in `K`, where `p : X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ X` is the projection.

It is the derived restriction map along the canonical morphism
`X_s ⟶ X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})` over `X`, after identifying the inverse image along that
morphism of `p⁻¹K` with the restriction of `K` to the geometric fibre.
declarations.statement:
def strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSections :
    smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s) ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (geometricFibreToSource f s) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (geometricFibre f s)
declarations.comment: the map to the fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GIX, the map from the stalk.** The canonical map

`(Rf_*K)_s ⟶ RΓ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹K)`

for an object `K` of the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of
`X`, natural in `K`, where `p : X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ X` is the projection.

The stalk of the derived direct image is a right derived functor of the stalk of the direct
image, the stalk functor having a right adjoint, so the map on sheaves
`AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsAb` extends uniquely to a map of
unbounded derived categories factoring it through the units.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections :
    smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f ⋙ smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb s.hom ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s)
declarations.comment: the map from the stalk

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GIY.** Let `X` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme, let
`x` be a geometric point of `X` and let `Λ` be a ring. The finite type locally constant sheaves of
`Λ`-modules on `X_étale` are equivalent to the finite `Λ`-modules endowed with a continuous
`π₁(X, x)`-action.

The source proves this by reducing to the case of an integral normal scheme along the
normalization `ν : X^ν → X`, which is a universal homeomorphism by Tag 0GIQ precisely because `X`
is irreducible and geometrically unibranch. That reduction is what is carried out here: the
geometric unibranchness is used to produce the universal homeomorphism, the equivalence of the
finite type locally constant module categories of `X` and `X^ν` is instantiated at it, the
isomorphism `π₁(X^ν, x^ν) ≅ π₁(X, x)` is obtained from the hypothesis that base change along `ν`
is an equivalence of finite étale covers — the content of Tag 0BQN — through Tag 0BQA part (2),
and the tag itself for the normalization is a hypothesis. See the module docstring for the gaps by
tag number.
declarations.statement:
public def finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModule
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) [IrreducibleSpace X.obj]
    (hX : IsGeometricallyUnibranch X.obj) (x : GeometricPoint X.obj)
    (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    [∀ V : SmallEtale B X.obj X.property,
      HasWeakSheafify ((SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property).over V) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    (hν : B.Contains (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj))
    [ConnectedSpace (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj)]
    [∀ V : SmallEtale B (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj) hν,
      HasWeakSheafify
        ((SmallEtale.topology B (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj) hν).over V)
        (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [(finiteEtaleBaseChange (Scheme.normalizationOfIrreducible X.obj)).IsEquivalence]
    (xν : GeometricPoint (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj))
    (hx : xν.map (Scheme.normalizationOfIrreducible X.obj) = x)
    (hinvariance : UniversalHomeomorphism (Scheme.normalizationOfIrreducible X.obj) →
      (FiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleCategory Λ (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≌
        FiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleCategory Λ
          (SmallEtale.topology B (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj) hν)))
    (hnormal : FiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleCategory Λ
        (SmallEtale.topology B (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj) hν) ≌
      FiniteTypeContinuousModule Λ
        (EtaleFundamentalGroup (Scheme.normalizationSchemeOfIrreducible X.obj) xν)) :
    FiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleCategory Λ (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≌
      FiniteTypeContinuousModule Λ (EtaleFundamentalGroup X.obj x)
declarations.comment: the equivalence, with the geometric input carried as hypotheses. Proved here: the source's reduction along the normalization — geometric unibranchness yields the universal homeomorphism of Tag 0GIQ, at which the hypothesis on the locally constant categories is instantiated; the fundamental group comparison is derived from the hypothesis that base change on finite étale covers along the normalization is an equivalence, which is the content of Tag 0BQN, by Tag 0BQA part (2); and the category of finite type continuous modules is transported along that comparison. Carried as hypotheses, none of them proved in this library: that base change on finite étale covers along a universal homeomorphism is an equivalence (Tag 0BQN, of which only faithfulness is available, the rest resting on Tag 0BTP), that a universal homeomorphism induces an equivalence of the finite type locally constant module categories (Tag 04DZ), the existence of a lift of the geometric point to the normalization, and the tag itself for the normalization, i.e. for an integral normal scheme (Tags 0BQM, 0BTD, 0BQI, 03RV, 0245, 03QW)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModuleUniv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GIY.** Let `X` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme, let
`x` be a geometric point of `X` and let `Λ` be a ring. The finite type locally constant sheaves of
`Λ`-modules on `X_étale` are equivalent to the finite `Λ`-modules endowed with a continuous
`π₁(X, x)`-action.

The functor sends a sheaf `F` to its monodromy module `colim_{(A, a)} F(A)` over the pointed
Galois covers of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public def finiteTypeLocallyConstantEquivContinuousModuleUniv (X : Scheme.{u}) [IrreducibleSpace X]
    (hX : IsGeometricallyUnibranch X) (x : GeometricPoint X) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] :
    Stacks.ConstantSheaf.FiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleCategory.{max (u + 1) r, u + 1, u, r} Λ
        X.smallEtaleTopology ≌
      Stacks.GroupCohomology.FiniteTypeContinuousModule.{r, u + 1, max (u + 1) r} Λ
        (EtaleFundamentalGroup X x)

declarations.name: Module.exists_relSeries_trivial_action_subquotient
declarations.doc:
A module over the group ring of a finite `ℓ`-group, annihilated by a power of `ℓ`,
has a finite filtration by group-ring submodules with trivial group action on every successive
quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_relSeries_trivial_action_subquotient
    (Λ H M : Type*) [CommRing Λ] [Group H] [Finite H]
    (ℓ n : ℕ) (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hH : IsPGroup ℓ H)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MonoidAlgebra Λ H) M]
    (hM : ∀ x : M, (ℓ ^ n) • x = 0) :
    ∃ X : RelSeries {p : Submodule (MonoidAlgebra Λ H) M ×
        Submodule (MonoidAlgebra Λ H) M |
      p.1 ≤ p.2 ∧ ∀ (g : H) (x : p.2),
        MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : Λ) • (x : M) - x ∈ p.1},
      X.head = ⊥ ∧ X.last = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_finiteModuleFiltration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJ0.** Let `S` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme, let
`ℓ` be a prime number, let `n ≥ 1`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let `F` be a finite type
locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `S_étale` annihilated by `ℓ ^ n`. Then there is a finite
étale morphism `f : T → S` of degree prime to `ℓ` such that `f⁻¹F` has a finite filtration whose
successive quotients are of the form `M_T` for finite `Λ`-modules `M`.

The filtration is a chain of subobjects of `f⁻¹F` running from the zero subobject to the whole
sheaf, each step having the constant sheaf of a finite `Λ`-module as its quotient.

The irreducibility and geometric unibranchness of `S` and the local constancy of `F` are the
hypotheses under which the dictionary `D` of Stacks Tag 0GIY is available. The annihilation of `F`
by `ℓ ^ n` is stated twice: on the sections of `F`, as `_hann`, because the source states it there,
and on the module the dictionary attaches to `F`, as the field `D.annihilated`, because that is the
form Tag 0GIZ consumes. Transporting the first to the second is part of Tag 0GIY and so is part of
what `D` carries; nothing here derives one from the other.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_finiteModuleFiltration {ℓ n : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    (_hn : 1 ≤ n) {Λ : Type v} [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace S] (_hS : IsGeometricallyUnibranch S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology S) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) v} Λ))
    (_hF : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant Λ (smallEtaleTopology S) F)
    (_hann : ∀ (U : S.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op U)), (ℓ ^ n) • x = 0)
    (D : FiniteModuleMonodromyDictionary Λ ℓ n s F) :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (d : ℕ), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d ∧ ¬ ℓ ∣ d ∧
      ∃ X : RelSeries (ConstantFiniteModuleStep Λ
          ((smallEtalePullbackModuleCat Λ f).obj F)),
        IsZero (Subobject.underlying.obj X.head) ∧ IsIso X.last.arrow
declarations.comment: granted hypothesis D, the Stacks 0GIY dictionary in finite-module form

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_finiteModuleFiltration_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJ0.** Let `S` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme, let
`ℓ` be a prime number, let `n ≥ 1`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let `F` be a finite type
locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `S_étale` annihilated by `ℓ ^ n`. Then there is a finite
étale morphism `f : T → S` of degree prime to `ℓ` such that `f⁻¹F` has a finite filtration whose
successive quotients are of the form `M_T` for finite `Λ`-modules `M`.

The filtration is a chain of subobjects of `f⁻¹F` running from the zero subobject to the whole
sheaf, each step having the constant sheaf of a finite `Λ`-module as its quotient. The degree of
`f` is the rank of the finite locally free morphism `f` (Tag 02KA).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_finiteModuleFiltration_general {ℓ n : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    (_hn : 1 ≤ n) {Λ : Type v} [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace S] (hS : IsGeometricallyUnibranch S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology S) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) v} Λ))
    (hF : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant Λ (smallEtaleTopology S) F)
    (hann : ∀ (U : S.Etale) (x : F.obj.obj (Opposite.op U)), (ℓ ^ n) • x = 0) :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (d : ℕ), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d ∧ ¬ ℓ ∣ d ∧
      ∃ X : RelSeries (ConstantFiniteModuleStep Λ
          ((smallEtalePullbackModuleCat Λ f).obj F)),
        IsZero (Subobject.underlying.obj X.head) ∧ IsIso X.last.arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_finiteEtale_primeToEll_constantModuleFiltration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 0GJ0.** Let `S` be an irreducible, geometrically unibranch scheme, let `ℓ` be a
prime number and `n ≥ 1`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let `F` be a finite type, locally
constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `S_étale` annihilated by `ℓ ^ n`. Then there is a finite étale
morphism `f : T ⟶ S` of degree `d` prime to `ℓ` such that `f⁻¹ F` has a finite filtration whose
successive quotients are of the form `M̲_T` for finite `Λ`-modules `M`.

The filtration is a chain of subobjects of `f⁻¹ F` from the zero subobject to the whole sheaf,
each step having the constant sheaf of a finite `Λ`-module as its quotient. The degree is the
rank `d` of `f` as a finite locally free morphism.

**The unibranch hypothesis of the source is necessary**: it cannot be dropped even for `S`
irreducible (a fortiori it cannot be replaced by connectedness). Let
`S` be the nodal cubic over an algebraically closed field `k`: it is irreducible but not
geometrically unibranch at the node, and its étale fundamental group is `ℤ̂`. It is `ℙ¹_k` with
`0` and `∞` glued, and the infinite chain of copies of `ℙ¹_k`, the `i`-th glued at `∞` to
the `(i+1)`-st at `0`, is an étale covering `S̃ ⟶ S` with deck group `ℤ`. Let
`Λ = 𝔽_ℓ[t, t⁻¹]`, a Noetherian domain annihilated by `ℓ`, and let `F = S̃ ×^ℤ Λ` be the sheaf of
`Λ`-modules obtained by letting the generator of `ℤ` act on `Λ` by multiplication by `t`. It is
locally constant (constant on `S̃`), of finite type (stalks `Λ`) and annihilated by `ℓ`. For
every finite étale `f : T ⟶ S` and every connected component `T₀` of `T` (a cycle of `m ≥ 1`
copies of `ℙ¹_k`), the pullback of `S̃` to `T₀` is the `ℤ`-cover with monodromy `m`, so
`Γ(T₀, f⁻¹ F) = {v ∈ Λ | t ^ m v = v} = 0`, `t ^ m - 1` being a nonzero divisor. A constant
subsheaf `M̲_{T₀}` of `f⁻¹ F|_{T₀}` therefore has `M ⊆ Γ(T₀, M̲) = 0`; by induction along a
filtration with constant successive quotients every term restricted to `T₀` is `0`, while
`f⁻¹ F|_{T₀}` has stalks `Λ ≠ 0`. So the conclusion fails for every finite étale `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtale_primeToEll_constantModuleFiltration {ℓ n : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    (_hn : 1 ≤ n) {Λ : Type r} [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace S] (hS : IsGeometricallyUnibranch S)
    (F : EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ S)
    (hF : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant Λ S.smallEtaleTopology F)
    (hann : ∀ (U : S.Etale) (y : F.obj.obj (op U)), (ℓ ^ n) • y = 0) :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (d : ℕ), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d ∧ ¬ ℓ ∣ d ∧
      ∃ X : RelSeries (ConstantFiniteModuleStep Λ ((etaleModuleInverseImage.{u, r} Λ f).obj F)),
        IsZero (Subobject.underlying.obj X.head) ∧ IsIso X.last.arrow
declarations.comment: the filtration after a finite étale cover of degree prime to ℓ, for S irreducible and geometrically unibranch

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.directImageExtensionByZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJ1.** For a cartesian square `j' ≫ f = g ≫ j` of schemes with `f`
finite and `j` an open immersion, `f_* ∘ j'_! ≅ j_! ∘ g_*` as functors from abelian sheaves on
`U_étale` to abelian sheaves on `Y_étale`.
declarations.comment: at the coefficients AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}, on Mathlib's small etale sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.extensionByZeroFinitePushforwardCartesianIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJ1.** For a cartesian square `g ≫ j = j' ≫ f` of schemes of a big étale site
with `f` finite and `j : V ⟶ Y` an open immersion, the functors `j_! ∘ g_*` and `f_* ∘ j'_!`
from abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `U` to abelian sheaves on the small étale site
of `Y` are naturally isomorphic.

The isomorphism is the mate, along the two extension-by-zero adjunctions, of the base change
identification `AlgebraicGeometry.abelianRestrictionPushforwardCartesianIso` of the
restriction functors; it is an isomorphism by the uniqueness characterisation of extension by
zero, whose stalk hypothesis is
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalk_pushforward_extensionByZero_isZero`, where finiteness of `f` is
used. The cartesian square is used twice: once for the base change identification, and once to
see that `j'` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
public def extensionByZeroFinitePushforwardCartesianIso [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)]
    [IsOpenImmersion (B.inclusion.map V.obj.hom)]
    (sq : IsPullback (B.inclusion.map U.obj.hom) (B.inclusion.map g) (B.inclusion.map f)
      (B.inclusion.map V.obj.hom)) :
    B.smallPushforward g AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
        abelianExtensionByZero B Y.1 Y.property V ≅
      abelianExtensionByZero B X.1 X.property U ⋙
        B.smallPushforward f AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkToSectionsAb_eq_smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb
declarations.doc:
**The specialization map is pullback by `t`.** Composed with the comparison
`F_{t ≫ p} ⟶ Γ(t, (t ≫ p)⁻¹F)` of Stacks 03Q1, the specialization map on stalks is the canonical
map `F_s ⟶ Γ(t, (t ≫ p)⁻¹F)` of Stacks 0GJN, which restricts the germ at `s` of a section over an
étale neighbourhood `W` along the composite `t ⟶ Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleStalkToSectionsAb_eq_smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb :
    etaleStalkToSectionsAb B S hS s t.hom =
      smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb B S hS s t ≫
        geometricStalkToPullbackSectionsAb (t.hom ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)
declarations.comment:
the specialization map is pullback by the geometric point of the strict
henselization, after the identification of the stalk at the specialized point with sections on
that point. The factorization of the left-hand side through sections over the strict
henselization itself is not proved here; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb_eq_sectionsRestrictionAb
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, `s` a geometric point of `S`, `p : Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ S` the
structure morphism of the strict henselization at `s`, and `t` a geometric point of
`Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})`, so that the image of `t ≫ p` is a specialization of the image of `s`. Use
the two identifications

`F_s = Γ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹F)`  and  `F_{t ≫ p} = Γ(t, t⁻¹p⁻¹F)`,

the first of which is Theorem 03Q9 applied to `id_S : S ⟶ S` and the second Lemma 03Q1. Then the
specialization map `sp : F_s ⟶ F_{t ≫ p}` of Stacks 0GJ2 *is* the map induced between them by
pullback of sections along `t`, that is, it is the composite of the first identification, the
restriction of sections along `t`, and the inverse of the second.

Here the first identification is `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkSectionsAbIso`, the second is
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricStalkPullbackSectionsAbIso`, and restriction of sections along `t` is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleSectionsRestrictionAb`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb_eq_sectionsRestrictionAb :
    smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb B S hS s t =
      (etaleStalkSectionsAbIso B S hS s).hom ≫
        smallEtaleSectionsRestrictionAb
            (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s) ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s) t.hom
            (t.hom ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)
            ((Category.assoc t.hom (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s))
                (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)).symm.trans
              (congrArg (fun y : t.source ⟶ strictHenselization B S hS s =>
                y ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s) (Category.comp_id t.hom))) ≫
          (geometricStalkPullbackSectionsAbIso
            (t.hom ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)).inv
declarations.comment: the specialization map is pullback of sections along `t`, read through the two identifications F_s = Γ(Spec 𝒪^sh_{S,s}, p⁻¹F) (03Q9 at the identity) and F_{t ≫ p} = Γ(t, t⁻¹p⁻¹F) (03Q1), both isomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkToSectionsAb_id_comp_sectionsRestrictionAb
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJ3, the displayed composite.** Let `S` be a scheme, `s` a geometric point of `S`,
`p : Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ S` the structure morphism of the strict henselization at `s`, and `t` a
geometric point of `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})`. Then the identification
`F_s = Γ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹F)` of Stacks 03Q9, followed by pullback of sections by `t`, is
the specialization map `sp : F_s ⟶ F_{t ≫ p}` followed by the identification
`F_{t ≫ p} = Γ(t, (t ≫ p)⁻¹F)` of Stacks 03Q1.

This is the source's displayed description of `sp` as pullback by `t`. The two identifications
are `AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkToSectionsAb` at the identity of the strict henselization and
`AlgebraicGeometry.geometricStalkToPullbackSectionsAb`; they are the canonical maps, which Stacks
03Q9 and 03Q1 assert are isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleStalkToSectionsAb_id_comp_sectionsRestrictionAb :
    etaleStalkToSectionsAb B S hS s (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s)) ≫
        smallEtaleSectionsRestrictionAb
          (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s) ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s) t.hom
          (t.hom ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)
          ((Category.assoc t.hom (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s))
              (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)).symm.trans
            (congrArg (fun y : t.source ⟶ strictHenselization B S hS s =>
              y ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s) (Category.comp_id t.hom))) =
      smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb B S hS s t ≫
        geometricStalkToPullbackSectionsAb (t.hom ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)
declarations.comment:
the displayed composite: the identification of the stalk at `s` with sections over
the strict henselization, followed by pullback by `t`, is the specialization map followed by the
identification of the stalk at the specialized point with sections on that point. The two
identifications are the canonical maps; this statement compares them and does not assert that
either is invertible. Invertibility is Stacks 03Q1 and Stacks 03Q9. Of these the library carries
03Q1 for `Type`-valued sheaves, as `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePullbackStalkIso`, and 03Q9 only
conditionally on the base being the spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring; neither is in
the abelian form and at the generality used here, so neither is applied.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_specializationMorphism_and_specialization_eq_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJ4.** Let `S` be a scheme, `s` a geometric point of `S`, and `t` a geometric
point of the strict henselization `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})`, with structure morphism
`p : Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}) ⟶ S`.

1. There is exactly one morphism `c : Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,t ≫ p}) ⟶ Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})` over `S`
   compatible with the given morphism `t` to `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})` and the canonical geometric
   point of `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,t ≫ p})`.
2. Taking global sections of abelian sheaves over the strictly henselian schemes
   `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s})` and `Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,t ≫ p})` is exact, and is the same as taking stalks
   at their canonical geometric points (lying over `s` and over `t ≫ p`). This is the source's
   reason that the equality signs below are valid.
3. For abelian sheaves `F` on the small étale site of `S`, the identifications
   `F_s = Γ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹F)` and `F_{t ≫ p} = Γ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,t ≫ p}), p⁻¹F)` are
   isomorphisms, and the specialization map `sp : F_s ⟶ F_{t ≫ p}` is pullback by `c`: the
   first identification followed by restriction of sections along `c` is `sp` followed by the
   second identification.
4. The same holds for objects `K` of the unbounded derived category `D(S_étale)`, with `RΓ` in
   place of `Γ` and the specialization map on derived stalks in place of `sp`: both
   identifications `K_s = RΓ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), K)` and
   `K_{t ≫ p} = RΓ(Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,t ≫ p}), K)` are isomorphisms, and `sp` is pullback by `c`.

Part (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_specializationMorphism`; part (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.preservesFiniteColimits_smallEtaleGlobalSections_strictHenselization` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_strictHenselizationSectionsToStalkAb`; the invertibility in (3) and
(4) is `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_etaleStalkToSectionsAb_id` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_vanishingCyclesMap_id`, the source's reason that global sections over a
strictly henselian scheme are exact and are the stalk at the closed point; the equations are
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleStalkToSectionsAb_id_comp_sectionsRestrictionAb_specializationMorphism`
and
`AlgebraicGeometry.vanishingCyclesMap_id_comp_derivedSectionsRestriction_specializationMorphism`.
The derivability instances that unbounded derived global sections on the two strict
henselizations are formed with are bound inside part (4); they hold for every scheme
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleGlobalSectionsAb_hasRightDerivedFunctor`), and part (4) is
proved for every choice of them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_specializationMorphism_and_specialization_eq_pullback
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s)) :
    (∃! c : strictHenselization B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)) ⟶
        strictHenselization B S hS s,
        c ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s =
            strictHenselizationToBase B S hS
              (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)) ∧
          geometricPointToStrictHenselization B S hS
              (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)) ≫ c = t.hom) ∧
      (PreservesFiniteColimits
          (Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B S hS s)) Ab.{u + 1}) ∧
        PreservesFiniteColimits (Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B S hS
          (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))) Ab.{u + 1}) ∧
        IsIso (strictHenselizationSectionsToStalkAb B S hS s) ∧
        IsIso (strictHenselizationSectionsToStalkAb B S hS
          (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))) ∧
      (IsIso (etaleStalkToSectionsAb B S hS s (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s))) ∧
        IsIso (etaleStalkToSectionsAb B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
          (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))) ∧
        etaleStalkToSectionsAb B S hS s (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s)) ≫
            smallEtaleSectionsRestrictionAb
              (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s) ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)
              (specializationMorphism B S hS s t)
              (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS
                  (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))) ≫
                strictHenselizationToBase B S hS
                  (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))
              (specializationMorphism_id_comp B S hS s t) =
          smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb B S hS s t ≫
            etaleStalkToSectionsAb B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
              (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS
                (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))) ∧
        ∀ [((Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B S hS s))
                Ab.{u + 1}).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙
              DerivedCategory.Qh).HasRightDerivedFunctor
              (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
                (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B S hS s))
                  Ab.{u + 1}) (.up ℤ))]
            [((Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B S hS
                    (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))
                  Ab.{u + 1}).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙
                DerivedCategory.Qh).HasRightDerivedFunctor
                (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
                  (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology (strictHenselization B S hS
                    (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))) Ab.{u + 1}) (.up ℤ))],
          IsIso (vanishingCyclesMap B S hS s (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s))) ∧
          IsIso (vanishingCyclesMap B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
            (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))) ∧
          vanishingCyclesMap B S hS s (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s)) ≫
              Functor.whiskerLeft
                  (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
                    (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s) ≫
                      strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
                  (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsRestriction
                    (specializationMorphism B S hS s t)) ≫
                (Functor.associator
                    (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
                      (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s) ≫
                        strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
                    (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (specializationMorphism B S hS s t))
                    (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselization B S hS
                      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))).inv ≫
                  Functor.whiskerRight (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIsoOfCompIso
                      (smallEtalePullbackAbCompIso (specializationMorphism B S hS s t)
                          (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS s) ≫
                            strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s) ≪≫
                        eqToIso (congrArg
                          (fun m : strictHenselization B S hS
                              (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)) ⟶ S =>
                            smallEtalePullbackAb m)
                          (specializationMorphism_id_comp B S hS s t)))).hom
                    (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselization B S hS
                      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))) =
            smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAb B S hS s t ≫
              vanishingCyclesMap B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
                (𝟙 (strictHenselization B S hS
                  (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))
declarations.comment: the whole remark: (1) the unique existence of `c`; (2) global sections over the two strictly henselian schemes are exact and are stalks at their closed geometric points; (3) on abelian sheaves, the identifications of the stalks at `s` and at `t ≫ p` with the sections over the two strict henselizations are isomorphisms, and `sp` is pullback by `c`; (4) the same on the unbounded derived category, with `RΓ`. The big etale site `B` with `hS` is a size device, not a source hypothesis.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_specializationMorphism
declarations.doc:
The specialization morphism of strict henselizations exists and is unique: a geometric point
`t` of the strict henselization at `s` determines exactly one morphism from the strict
henselization at the image of `t` in `S` to the strict henselization at `s` which lies over `S`
and carries the canonical geometric point of its source to `t`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_specializationMorphism (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s)) :
    let T := strictHenselization B S hS s
    let p := strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s
    let tS := t.map p
    ∃! c : strictHenselization B S hS tS ⟶ T,
      (c ≫ p = strictHenselizationToBase B S hS tS) ∧
      (geometricPointToStrictHenselization B S hS tS ≫ c = t.hom)
declarations.comment: specialization_morphism_of_strict_henselizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specializationMorphism
declarations.doc:
The specialization morphism of strict henselizations attached to a geometric point of the
strict henselization at `s`: the unique morphism over `S` from the strict henselization at the
image of that point in `S` to the strict henselization at `s` which carries the canonical
geometric point of its source to the given one.
declarations.statement:
public def specializationMorphism (s : GeometricPoint S)
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s)) :
    strictHenselization B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)) ⟶
      strictHenselization B S hS s
declarations.comment: specialization_morphism_of_strict_henselizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specializationMapOnSections
declarations.doc:
Specialization of a section along the canonical morphism of strict henselizations
determined by a geometric point `t` of the strict henselization at `s`: the pullback of global
sections along the specialization morphism.
declarations.statement:
public def specializationMapOnSections
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s))
    (hT : B.Contains (strictHenselization B S hS s))
    (hU : B.Contains (strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) :
    let p : (⟨strictHenselization B S hS s, hT⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme) :=
      ⟨strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s⟩
    haveI := smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B p
    let c : (⟨strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)), hU⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
      (⟨strictHenselization B S hS s, hT⟩ : B.Scheme) :=
      ⟨specializationMorphism B S hS s t⟩
    haveI := smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B c
    let G := ((smallEtaleBaseChange B p).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
      (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT)).obj F
    (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT) (Type (u + 1))).obj G ⟶
      (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B _ hU) (Type (u + 1))).obj
        (((smallEtaleBaseChange B c).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
          (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT)
          (SmallEtale.topology B _ hU)).obj G)
declarations.comment: specialization_map_on_sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.abelianSpecializationMapOnSections
declarations.doc:
Specialization along the canonical morphism of strict henselizations, as a natural
transformation of functors on abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public def abelianSpecializationMapOnSections
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s))
    (hT : B.Contains (strictHenselization B S hS s))
    (hU : B.Contains (strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))) :
    let p : (⟨strictHenselization B S hS s, hT⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme) :=
      ⟨strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s⟩
    haveI := smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B p
    let c : (⟨strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)), hU⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
      (⟨strictHenselization B S hS s, hT⟩ : B.Scheme) :=
      ⟨specializationMorphism B S hS s t⟩
    haveI := smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B c
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange B p).sheafPullback Ab.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT) ⋙
      Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT) Ab.{u + 1}) ⟶
    ((smallEtaleBaseChange B p).sheafPullback Ab.{u + 1}
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT) ⋙
      ((smallEtaleBaseChange B c).sheafPullback Ab.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT) (SmallEtale.topology B _ hU) ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B _ hU) Ab.{u + 1}))
declarations.comment: specialization_map_on_sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specializationMapOnSections_germ
declarations.doc:
The geometric germ of a specialized global section is the pullback of its germ on the first
strict henselization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem specializationMapOnSections_germ
    (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s))
    (hT : B.Contains (strictHenselization B S hS s))
    (hU : B.Contains (strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))
    (x : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))))
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) :
    let p : (⟨strictHenselization B S hS s, hT⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶ (⟨S, hS⟩ : B.Scheme) :=
      ⟨strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s⟩
    haveI := smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B p
    let c : (⟨strictHenselization B S hS
      (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)), hU⟩ : B.Scheme) ⟶
      (⟨strictHenselization B S hS s, hT⟩ : B.Scheme) :=
      ⟨specializationMorphism B S hS s t⟩
    haveI := smallEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous B c
    let G := ((smallEtaleBaseChange B p).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (SmallEtale.topology B S hS)
      (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT)).obj F
    let H := ((smallEtaleBaseChange B c).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
      (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT)
      (SmallEtale.topology B _ hU)).obj G
    ∀ σ : (Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B _ hT) (Type (u + 1))).obj G,
      ((smallEtalePullbackStalkIso B c x).hom.app G)
        ((globalSectionsToEtaleStalk B
          ↥(etaleLocalRing B S hS (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))) hU x H)
          (specializationMapOnSections B S hS s t hT hU F σ)) =
      (globalSectionsToEtaleStalk B ↥(etaleLocalRing B S hS s) hT
          (x.map (B.inclusion.map c)) G) σ
declarations.comment: specialization_map_on_sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparable_residueField_strictHenselizationToBase
declarations.doc:
The residue field at a point of the strict henselization at a geometric point is separable
over the residue field at the image of that point in the scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparable_residueField_strictHenselizationToBase (sbar : GeometricPoint S)
    (x : strictHenselization B S hS sbar) :
    let f := strictHenselizationToBase B S hS sbar
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f x))
      ((strictHenselization B S hS sbar).residueField x)
declarations.comment: the residue-field extension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_lift_toStrictHenselization_of_specializes
declarations.doc:
A geometric point over a generization lifts to the strict henselization at a geometric point
over the specialization, and the lifted point specializes to the canonical point of the strict
henselization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_lift_toStrictHenselization_of_specializes
    (t s : S) (hts : t ⤳ s) (tbar sbar : GeometricPoint S)
    (ht : tbar.LiesOver t) (hs : sbar.LiesOver s) :
    ∃ lift : tbar.source ⟶ strictHenselization B S hS sbar,
      (lift ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S hS sbar = tbar.hom) ∧
      (lift default ⤳ (geometricPointToStrictHenselization B S hS sbar) default)
declarations.comment: lifting the generic geometric point

registrations.name: geometricPointToStrictHenselization_comp
registrations.comment: compatibility of the special geometric point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specializationMapOnStalks_smallEtalePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJ6.** Let `g : S' ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `s'` be a
geometric point of `S'` and let `σ` be a geometric specialization of `s'`, and let `h` be the
canonical morphism of strict henselizations, characterized by lying over `g` and carrying the
canonical geometric point of its source to the canonical geometric point of its target. For a
sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `S` the specialization map of the inverse image `g⁻¹F`
from `s'` to `σ` is the specialization map of `F` from the image of `s'` to the image of `σ`,
under the identification of the stalks of an inverse image with the stalks of `F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem specializationMapOnStalks_smallEtalePullback (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    (S S' : B.Scheme) (g : S' ⟶ S) (s' : GeometricPoint S'.1)
    (σ : GeometricSpecialization B S'.1 S'.property s')
    (h : strictHenselization B S'.1 S'.property s' ⟶
      strictHenselization B S.1 S.property (s'.map (B.inclusion.map g)))
    (hbase : h ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B S.1 S.property (s'.map (B.inclusion.map g)) =
      strictHenselizationToBase B S'.1 S'.property s' ≫ B.inclusion.map g)
    (hpoint : geometricPointToStrictHenselization B S'.1 S'.property s' ≫ h =
      geometricPointToStrictHenselization B S.1 S.property (s'.map (B.inclusion.map g)))
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.1 S.property) (Type (u + 1))) :
    specializationMapOnStalks σ
          (((smallEtaleBaseChange B g).sheafPullback (Type (u + 1))
            (SmallEtale.topology B S.1 S.property)
            (SmallEtale.topology B S'.1 S'.property)).obj F).obj ≫
        (smallEtalePullbackStalkIso B g σ.target).hom.app F =
      (smallEtalePullbackStalkIso B g s').hom.app F ≫
        specializationMapOnStalks (σ.map g h hbase) F.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finite_etaleStalk_and_bijective_specializationMap
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme every quasi-compact open of which has finitely many irreducible components
and let `F` be a sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `S`. Then `F` is finite locally constant
if and only if all its stalks at geometric points are finite and all specialization maps between
those stalks are bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_finite_etaleStalk_and_bijective_specializationMap
    (hScomp : ∀ V : S.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set S) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) :
    Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteLocallyConstant (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) F ↔
      (∀ s : GeometricPoint S, Finite (etaleStalk B S hS s F.obj)) ∧
        ∀ (s : GeometricPoint S) (σ : GeometricSpecialization B S hS s),
          Function.Bijective (specializationMapOnStalks σ F.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsAb_comp_sectionsRestrictionAb
declarations.doc:
**The square on abelian sheaves.** The map `(f_*F)_s ⟶ Γ(X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}), p⁻¹F)`
of Stacks 0GIX at `s`, followed by restriction of sections along `id_X × c`, is the
specialization map `sp : (f_*F)_s ⟶ (f_*F)_{t ≫ p}` followed by the same map at `t ≫ p`.

Both sides are maps out of the stalk at `s` of the direct image, so it suffices to compare them
on the germ of a section over an étale neighbourhood `(V, w)` of `s`; there both are restriction
along `X ×_S Spec(𝒪^{sh}_{S,t ≫ p}) ⟶ X ×_S V` of the corresponding section of `F` over
`X ×_S V`, the two morphisms agreeing because `c` carries the canonical morphism from the strict
henselization into `V` to the one for the specialized neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsAb_comp_sectionsRestrictionAb :
    pushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsAb B hS f s ≫
        smallEtaleSectionsRestrictionAb (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s)
          (strictHenselizationBaseChangeSpecializationMap B hS f s t)
          (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f
            (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)))
          (strictHenselizationBaseChangeSpecializationMap_comp_toSource B hS f s t) =
      Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtalePushforwardAb f)
          (smallEtaleSpecializationStalkAb B S hS s t) ≫
        pushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSectionsAb B hS f
          (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))
declarations.comment: the square for an abelian sheaf `F`, in place of an object `K` of `D⁺(X_étale)`: the vertical identifications are those of Stacks 0GIX rather than their derived counterparts

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specializationStalk_comp_derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections
declarations.doc:
For `K` in `D(X_etale)`, the square whose top arrow is the specialization map `sp` on the
stalk of `Rf_*K` and whose verticals are the maps of Stacks 0GIX from those stalks to the global
sections over the base changes to the strict henselizations commutes, its bottom arrow being
pullback along `id_X × c`.  The verticals are the identifications of Theorem 03Q9 when `f` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `K` is bounded below; the square commutes for an arbitrary
morphism of schemes and an arbitrary object of `D(X_etale)`.  It is the square of
`derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_comp_sectionsSpecialization` read with
`sp` on top.
declarations.statement:
theorem specializationStalk_comp_derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections :
    Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f)
          (smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAbAt B S hS s t) ≫
        derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f
          (specializedGeometricPoint B S hS s t) =
      derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f s ≫
        strictHenselizationSectionsSpecializationAt B hS f s t
declarations.comment: the square, with `sp` on top and the maps of Stacks 0GIX as its verticals, proved for an arbitrary morphism of schemes and an arbitrary object of `D(X_etale)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_comp_sectionsSpecialization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJ9.** For `K` in `D(X_etale)` the specialization map on the stalk of `Rf_*K` at a
geometric point `s` of `S`, and pullback along `id_X × c` on global sections over the base change
to the strict henselization, form a commutative square with the two maps of Stacks 0GIX from
those stalks.

Read with `sp` vertical this is the left square of the diagram of Stacks 0GJ9; read with `sp`
horizontal it is the square of Stacks 0GJ8, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.specializationStalk_comp_derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections`.
It is proved here for an arbitrary morphism of schemes and an arbitrary object of `D(X_etale)`,
which is the generality Stacks 0GJ9 asserts it in.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_comp_sectionsSpecialization :
    derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f s ≫
        strictHenselizationSectionsSpecializationAt B hS f s t =
      Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f)
          (smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAbAt B S hS s t) ≫
        derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f
          (specializedGeometricPoint B S hS s t)
declarations.comment: the left square, whose verticals are the specialization map `sp` and pullback along `id_X × c`; the source states that in general no vertical map exists between the cohomologies of `K` on the two fibres, so the right-hand column carries no square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_comp_sectionsSpecialization_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, `s` a geometric point of `S` and `t` a geometric
point of the strict henselization of `S` at `s`. For `K` in the unbounded derived category
`D(X_étale)`, the maps of Stacks 0GIX from the stalks of `Rf_*K` at `s` and at the specialized
point `t ≫ p` to the derived global sections over the base changes of `X` to the two strict
henselizations form a commutative square with the specialization map `sp` on the left and pullback
along `id_X × c` on the right.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections_comp_sectionsSpecialization_unconditional
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X S : Scheme.{u}} (hS : B.Contains S) (f : X ⟶ S)
    (s : GeometricPoint S) (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS s)) :
    derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f s ≫
        strictHenselizationSectionsSpecializationAt B hS f s t =
      Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f)
          (smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAbAt B S hS s t) ≫
        derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f
          (specializedGeometricPoint B S hS s t)
declarations.comment: the left square for an arbitrary morphism of schemes and an arbitrary object of the unbounded `D(X_etale)`: its verticals are `sp` and pullback along `id_X × c`, its horizontals the maps of Stacks 0GIX, and the unbounded `Rf_*` and `RΓ` are built from K-injective resolutions; the source states that no vertical map exists in general between the cohomologies of `K` on the two fibres, so the right-hand column carries no square

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveStatements_iff_curveStatements_extensionByZero_of_dense
declarations.doc:
In Situation 0A52 let `j : X' → X` be the inclusion of a dense open subscheme. Then statements
(1) -- (8) hold for `F` if and only if they hold for `j_! j^{-1} F`.

The source assumes `F` constructible; that is not needed here, both sides being true for every
torsion `F` by Theorem 03SC (`j_! j^{-1} F` is a subsheaf of `F`, hence torsion). The direction
from `j_! j^{-1} F` to `F` is the dense-open reduction of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveStatements_of_curveStatements_extensionByZero_of_dense`.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveStatements_iff_curveStatements_extensionByZero_of_dense
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hF : Stacks.Torsion.torsionSheafProperty X.smallEtaleTopology F) :
    CurveStatements.{u, v, w} π F ↔ CurveStatements.{u, v, w} π
      ((extensionByZero.{u, v} j).obj ((etaleRestriction.{u, v} j).obj F))
declarations.comment: for every torsion sheaf F, not only constructible ones

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.module_finite_etaleCohomology_constantSheaf_of_coprime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJC, part (1).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `M` a finite
`Λ`-module annihilated by an integer `n > 0`, `k` an algebraically closed field and `X` a
separated scheme of finite type over `k` of dimension at most one. If `n` is prime to the
characteristic of `k`, then `H^q(X, M̲)` is a finite `Λ`-module for every `q`.

Here `X` is a scheme with a separated, locally of finite type and quasi-compact structure morphism
`π : X ⟶ Spec k`, the dimension is the Krull dimension of the underlying space, `M̲` is the
constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale` and `H^q(X, M̲)` is the `q`-th right derived functor
of global sections of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale`. "Prime to the characteristic" is read
with the exponential characteristic, so that it is no condition in characteristic zero.

The proof is the source's (`module_finite_etaleCohomology_constantSheaf`), with the input
Tag 03SC supplied by `curveTorsionCohomologyStatement_holds`.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_finite_etaleCohomology_constantSheaf_of_coprime
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsSeparated π] [LocallyOfFiniteType π] [QuasiCompact π] (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ) [Module.Finite Λ M] (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (hM : ∀ m : M, n • m = 0) (hnk : n.Coprime (ringExpChar k)) (q : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite Λ (((etaleModuleGlobalSections.{u, r} Λ X).rightDerived q).obj
      ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ)).obj M))
declarations.comment: part (1): n prime to char(k)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.module_finite_etaleCohomology_constantSheaf_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJC, part (2).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `M` a finite
`Λ`-module annihilated by an integer `n > 0`, `k` an algebraically closed field and `X` a

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.module_finite_cohomology_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJD**, granted Tag 03QP for sheaves of `Λ`-modules as the hypothesis
`h03QP`.

Let `Λ` be a ring, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of a big étale site whose underlying morphism
of schemes is finite, and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site of `X`. If
`H^q_étale(X, ℱ)` is a finite `Λ`-module, then so is `H^q_étale(Y, f_*ℱ)`.

The hypothesis `h03QP` is the general statement of part (2) of Stacks 03QP for sheaves of
`Λ`-modules: for *every* morphism of the big étale site with finite underlying morphism of
schemes, *every* sheaf of `Λ`-modules on its source and *every* positive degree, the higher
direct image vanishes. It is a different tag from the one being proved, it quantifies over all
of its own inputs, and it is instantiated only inside the proof, at `f` and `ℱ`. Nothing about
`H^q_étale(Y, f_*ℱ)` — the conclusion — is assumed.

The remaining hypotheses of the source statement (`Λ` Noetherian, `k` algebraically closed,
`X` and `Y` separated of finite type over `k` of dimension at most one) are not needed: the
source's proof does not use them, and neither does this one.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_finite_cohomology_pushforward
    [∀ Z : B.Scheme,
      HasSheafify (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)]
    [∀ Z : B.Scheme, HasInjectiveResolutions
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ))]
    [∀ (Z W : B.Scheme) (g : Z ⟶ W), (modulePushforward.{u, w} B Λ g).IsRightAdjoint]
    (h03QP : ∀ (Z W : B.Scheme) (g : Z ⟶ W), IsFinite (B.inclusion.map g) →
      ∀ (𝒢 : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ))
        (q : ℕ), 0 < q → IsZero (((modulePushforward.{u, w} B Λ g).rightDerived q).obj 𝒢))
    (hf : IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f))
    (ℱ : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ))
    (q : ℕ)
    (hfin : Module.Finite Λ (((moduleGlobalSections.{u, w} B Λ X).rightDerived q).obj ℱ)) :
    Module.Finite Λ (((moduleGlobalSections.{u, w} B Λ Y).rightDerived q).obj
      ((modulePushforward.{u, w} B Λ f).obj ℱ))
declarations.comment: granted Tag 03QP for sheaves of Λ-modules, as the hypothesis h03QP

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.module_finite_cohomology_pushforward_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJD.** Let `Λ` be a ring, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of a big étale
site whose underlying morphism of schemes is finite, and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the
small étale site of `X`. If `H^q_étale(X, ℱ)` is a finite `Λ`-module, then so is
`H^q_étale(Y, f_*ℱ)`.

The source states this for `Λ` Noetherian, `k` an algebraically closed field and `f` a finite
morphism of separated schemes of finite type over `k` of dimension at most one. None of that is
used by the source's proof, and none of it is assumed here: the source's statement is the special
case in which those hypotheses hold. The proof is the source's: the higher direct images
of `f` vanish (`isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isIntegralHom`, Stacks 03QP), so the
Leray spectral sequence collapses to `H^q_étale(X, ℱ) ≅ H^q_étale(Y, f_*ℱ)`
(`moduleCohomologyPushforwardIso`, Stacks 0733), and finiteness transports along it.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_finite_cohomology_pushforward_of_isFinite [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)]
    (ℱ : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w r} Λ))
    (q : ℕ)
    (hfin : Module.Finite Λ
      (((moduleGlobalSections.{u, max w r} B Λ X).rightDerived q).obj ℱ)) :
    Module.Finite Λ (((moduleGlobalSections.{u, max w r} B Λ Y).rightDerived q).obj
      ((modulePushforward.{u, max w r} B Λ f).obj ℱ))
