declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.module_finite_cohomology_iff_extensionByZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJE**, granted Tag 095L for sheaves of `Λ`-modules as the hypothesis
`h095L`, and the cohomology of `i_*i^{-1}ℱ` as the hypotheses `h0` and `hpos`.

Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, let `X` be a scheme, let `j : X' ⟶ X` be an open immersion and let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion whose image is the complement of the image of `j`. Let `ℱ` be
a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale`. If `H^0_étale(X, i_*i^{-1}ℱ)` is a finite `Λ`-module and
`H^q_étale(X, i_*i^{-1}ℱ) = 0` for `q > 0`, then for every `q`

  `H^q_étale(X, ℱ)` is a finite `Λ`-module  ↔  `H^q_étale(X, j_!j^{-1}ℱ)` is a finite
  `Λ`-module.

The hypothesis `h095L` is the general statement of Tag 095L for sheaves of `Λ`-modules: for
*every* scheme, *every* closed immersion into it, *every* open immersion onto the complement and
*every* sheaf of `Λ`-modules, the localization short complex exists and is short exact. It is a
different tag, it quantifies over all of its own inputs, it is instantiated only inside the
proof, and it says nothing about cohomology or finiteness.

The hypotheses `h0` and `hpos` are not a Stacks tag. They are the cohomological consequence of
the geometric hypotheses of the source — `X` separated of finite type of dimension at most one
over an algebraically closed field, `X'` dense, `ℱ` constructible — and are the part of Tag 0GJE
this declaration does **not** prove; see the implementation notes of this file for the chain of
four absent results they stand in for. They concern `i_*i^{-1}ℱ` only, and so are independent of
the conclusion, which concerns `ℱ` and `j_!j^{-1}ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_finite_cohomology_iff_extensionByZero
    {X Z X' : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : X' ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (hij : Set.range j.base = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ)
    (h095L : ∀ {W Z' U' : Scheme.{u}} (i' : Z' ⟶ W) (j' : U' ⟶ W) [IsClosedImmersion i']
        [IsOpenImmersion j'], Set.range j'.base = (Set.range i'.base)ᶜ →
      ∀ 𝒢 : Sheaf W.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w r} Λ),
        ∃ hz : (moduleExtensionByZeroAdj.{u, w, r} Λ j').counit.app 𝒢 ≫
            (moduleInverseImageDirectImageAdj.{u, w, r} Λ i').unit.app 𝒢 = 0,
          (openClosedModuleShortComplex.{u, w, r} Λ i' j' 𝒢 hz).ShortExact)
    (ℱ : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w r} Λ))
    (h0 : Module.Finite Λ ((moduleEtaleCohomology.{u, w, r} Λ X 0).obj
      ((moduleDirectImage.{u, w, r} Λ i).obj ((moduleInverseImage.{u, w, r} Λ i).obj ℱ))))
    (hpos : ∀ q, 0 < q → IsZero ((moduleEtaleCohomology.{u, w, r} Λ X q).obj
      ((moduleDirectImage.{u, w, r} Λ i).obj ((moduleInverseImage.{u, w, r} Λ i).obj ℱ))))
    (q : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite Λ ((moduleEtaleCohomology.{u, w, r} Λ X q).obj ℱ) ↔
      Module.Finite Λ ((moduleEtaleCohomology.{u, w, r} Λ X q).obj
        ((moduleExtensionByZero.{u, w, r} Λ j).obj
          ((moduleRestriction.{u, w, r} Λ j).obj ℱ)))
declarations.comment: granted 095L for Λ-module sheaves as h095L; closed part's cohomology as h0, hpos

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.TorsionModules.module_finite_cohomology_iff_extensionByZero_of_dense
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJE.** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `k` an algebraically closed
field, `X` a separated scheme of finite type over `k` of dimension at most one, `ℱ` a
constructible sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale`, and `j : X' ⟶ X` the inclusion of a dense open
subscheme. Then `H^q_étale(X, ℱ)` is a finite `Λ`-module if and only if
`H^q_étale(X, j_!j^{-1}ℱ)` is a finite `Λ`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem module_finite_cohomology_iff_extensionByZero_of_dense
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (Λ : Type r) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    (X : B.Scheme) (p : X.obj ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [IsSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X.obj ≤ 1)
    (ℱ : Sheaf X.obj.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ))
    (hℱ : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteModuleSheaf B X Λ ℱ)
    {X' : Scheme.{u}} (j : X' ⟶ X.obj) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (hdense : Dense (Set.range j.base)) (q : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite Λ ((moduleEtaleCohomology.{u, r, r} Λ X.obj q).obj ℱ) ↔
      Module.Finite Λ ((moduleEtaleCohomology.{u, r, r} Λ X.obj q).obj
        ((moduleExtensionByZero.{u, r, r} Λ j).obj
          ((moduleRestriction.{u, r, r} Λ j).obj ℱ)))

**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJI, part (1) (Tag 0GJJ).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `k` an
algebraically closed field, `X` a separated scheme of finite type over `k` of dimension at most
one, and `F` a constructible sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_étale` which is torsion prime to the
characteristic of `k`. Then `H^q_étale(X, F)` is a finite `Λ`-module for every `q`.

"Torsion prime to `char(k)`" is `Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion` of the underlying
abelian sheaf at the exponential characteristic of `k`: every local section is, locally, killed by
a positive integer prime to it. It implies that `F` is torsion, and in characteristic zero it is
exactly that. Constructibility is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.IsBigSiteConstructibleEtaleModule`
(Tag 03RW (3), read on the small étale site of Tag 021B of a big étale site `B` containing `X`).
declarations.statement:

    (F : EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X.obj) (hc : IsBigSiteConstructibleEtaleModule B X Λ F)
    (ht : Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion X.obj.smallEtaleTopology (ringExpChar k)
      ((etaleModuleForgetAb.{u, r} Λ X.obj).obj F)) (q : ℕ) :

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChangeDerived.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_limit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJL.** Let `(X_i, Y_i, S_i, T_i, f_i, h_i, e_i, g_i)` be an inverse system of
squares as in the setup of Stacks 0EZT, with limit square `(X, Y, S, T, f, h, e, g)`. Let
`0 ∈ I`, let `K_0` be an object of `D^+(T_{0, étale})`, let `K_i` be the pullback of `K_0` to
`T_i` for `i ≥ 0` and `K` the pullback of `K_0` to `T`. If `f_i^{-1}Rg_{i, *}K_i =
Rh_{i, *}e_i^{-1}K_i` for all `i ≥ 0`, then `f^{-1}Rg_*K = Rh_*e^{-1}K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_limit
    (w : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, h.app i ≫ f.app i = e.app i ≫ g.app i) (wL : hL ≫ fL = eL ≫ gL)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    {i₀ : Iᵒᵖ} (K₀ : PlusAb (DT.obj i₀)) (J : Type w₁) [Category.{w₂} J] (σ : J → Iᵒᵖ)
    (τ : ∀ j : J, σ j ⟶ i₀)
    (P : ∀ p : ℤ,
      ColimitPresentation f g h e cX cS cT cY fL gL hL eL w wL hfL K₀ J σ τ p)
    (hstage : ∀ (i : Iᵒᵖ) (a : i ⟶ i₀),
      IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb (f.app i) (g.app i) (h.app i) (e.app i) (w i)).app
        (stageObj K₀ a))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb fL gL hL eL wL).app (limitObj cT K₀))
declarations.comment: if the derived base change map of the `i`-th square is an isomorphism at `K_i` for all `i ≥ 0`, then the derived base change map of the limit square is an isomorphism at `K`, with `K_i` and `K` the derived inverse images of `K_0 ∈ D^+(T_{0, étale})` to `T_i` and to `T`. Both steps of the source's proof are carried out: the reduction to cohomology sheaves is `isIso_of_forall_isIso_derivedLimitComparison` and the colimit argument of Stacks 0EZT, with the reference to Stacks 0EYM replaced by one to Stacks 0GIU, is `isIso_derivedLimitComparison`. EXTRA HYPOTHESIS: the single bundled hypothesis `P` grants, in each degree `p`, the two instances of the colimit assertion of Stacks 0GIU that the source's proof cites — `H^p(Rg_*K) = colim_{i ≥ 0} s_i^{-1}H^p(Rg_{i, *}K_i)` and `H^p(Rh_*Re^{-1}K) = colim_{i ≥ 0} r_i^{-1}H^p(Rh_{i, *}Re_i^{-1}K_i)` — presented as in `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChange.isIso_higherBaseChangeMapAb_limit`, namely a diagram with terms identified with `derivedSourceTerm` resp. `derivedTargetTerm` and a colimit cocone with the stated vertex, together with the comparison of the two diagrams and its compatibility with terms and legs, which is the pasting of base change maps of Stacks 0E47. That colimit assertion is NOT available in this repository: `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitHigherDirectImage.pullbackProjectionMap`, the carrier of Stacks 0GIU, states in its own clause string that it is not proved and that the colimit cannot even be formed, both because the colimit assertion of Stacks 0EYM is unproved and because the cocycle compatibility of Stacks 0E47 is unavailable for the bounded below derived base change map. The hypothesis does not restate the goal: it says nothing about any base change map being invertible, only that the two sides are the asserted colimits and that the comparison maps assemble.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LimitBaseChangeDerived.isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_limit_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a directed set and let `(X_i, Y_i, S_i, T_i, f_i, h_i, e_i, g_i)` be an inverse
system of cartesian squares of schemes with affine transition morphisms and with `g_i`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, with limit square `(X, Y, S, T, f, h, e, g)`. Let `0 = i₀ ∈ I`,
let `K_0 ∈ D^+(T_{0, étale})`, let `K_i` be the pullback of `K_0` to `T_i` for `i ≥ 0` and `K` the
pullback of `K_0` to `T`. If the derived base change map
`f_i^{-1}Rg_{i, *}K_i ⟶ Rh_{i, *}e_i^{-1}K_i` is an isomorphism for all `i ≥ 0`, then so is
`f^{-1}Rg_*K ⟶ Rh_*e^{-1}K`.

The limit morphisms are any morphisms `f`, `g`, `h`, `e` satisfying the equations of the
projection squares.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb_limit_of_isLimit [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DX.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DS.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DT.map a)]
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (a : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (DY.map a)]
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact (g.app i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparated (g.app i)]
    (hsq : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsPullback (h.app i) (e.app i) (f.app i) (g.app i))
    (hcX : IsLimit cX) (hcS : IsLimit cS) (hcT : IsLimit cT) (hcY : IsLimit cY)
    (fL : cX.pt ⟶ cS.pt) (gL : cT.pt ⟶ cS.pt) (hL : cY.pt ⟶ cX.pt) (eL : cY.pt ⟶ cT.pt)
    (hfL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, fL ≫ cS.π.app i = cX.π.app i ≫ f.app i)
    (hgL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, gL ≫ cS.π.app i = cT.π.app i ≫ g.app i)
    (hhL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, hL ≫ cX.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ h.app i)
    (heL : ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, eL ≫ cT.π.app i = cY.π.app i ≫ e.app i)
    (i₀ : I) (K₀ : PlusAb (DT.obj (op i₀)))
    (hstage : ∀ (i : Iᵒᵖ) (a : i ⟶ op i₀),
      IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb (f.app i) (g.app i) (h.app i) (e.app i)
        (hsq i).w).app (stageObj K₀ a))) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedBaseChangeAb fL gL hL eL
      (LimitBaseChange.limitSquare_comm f g h e cX cS cT cY fL gL hL eL hcS hfL hgL hhL heL
        fun i => (hsq i).w)).app (limitObj cT K₀))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.vanishingCyclesMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN.** The canonical map `α_{K,x,t} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(T, K)` from the stalk at a geometric
point `x` of `X` of an object `K` of the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on the
small étale site of `X`, to the unbounded derived global sections of `K` on a scheme `T` over the
strict henselization `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`, natural in `K`.

For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` and a geometric point `t` of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}` the
variety of vanishing cycles of `f` at `x` is the fibre product
`F_{x,t} = t ×_{Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}} Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` over `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`, and the
displayed map of the source is this one for that `T` and the second projection; the construction
uses nothing about `T` beyond its morphism to the strict henselization.

Since the strict henselization is the initial étale neighbourhood of `x`, pulling back germs
along `T ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` gives the map `etaleStalkToSectionsAb` on abelian sheaves. The
stalk functor is exact, so its action on unbounded derived categories is a right derived functor
of itself, and the map on sheaves extends uniquely to one of derived categories.
declarations.statement:
def vanishingCyclesMap :
    smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb x.hom ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
          (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections T
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary scheme over the strict henselization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.vanishingCyclesMap_fac_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN.** On every complex of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, the
canonical map to the derived global sections over `T` factors the degreewise map on sheaves
through the unit of the derivation of global sections, read through the identifications of the
degreewise actions of the stalk and of inverse image with their actions on derived categories.

Since the degreewise action of the stalk functor is a right derived functor of itself, this
property determines the map.
declarations.statement:
theorem vanishingCyclesMap_fac_app
    (J : HomotopyCategory (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (.up ℤ)) :
    (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app J ≫
        (vanishingCyclesMap B X hX x q).app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj J) =
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((Stacks.DerivedFunctor.mapHomotopyCategoryOfComp
          (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom)
          (smallEtalePullbackAb
            (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x))
          (Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
          (etaleStalkToSectionsAb B X hX x q)).app J) ≫
        (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsUnit T).app
            (((smallEtalePullbackAb
              (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj J) ≫
          (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections T).map
            ((smallEtalePullbackAb
              (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app J)
declarations.comment: the derived map factors the map on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.vanishingCyclesFibreMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN.** The canonical map

`α_{K,x,t} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(F_{x,t}, K)`

from the stalk at a geometric point `x` of `X` of an object `K` of the unbounded derived category
of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, to the unbounded derived sections of `K` on the
variety of vanishing cycles `F_{x,t}` of a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` at `x` and a geometric point `t`
of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}`, natural in `K`.

The stalk of `K` at `x` is the derived sections of `K` over the strictly henselian
`Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`, and the map is pullback of cohomology along the projection
`F_{x,t} ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`.
declarations.statement:
def vanishingCyclesFibreMap :
    smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb x.hom ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (vanishingCyclesFibreToSource B hX hS f x t) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (vanishingCyclesFibre B hX hS f x t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDerivedStalkToSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN.** The canonical map `α_{K,x} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(T, K)` from the stalk at a geometric
point `x` of `X` of an object `K` of the unbounded derived category `D(X_étale)` of abelian
sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, to the unbounded derived global sections
`RΓ(T, K) = RΓ(T_étale, g⁻¹K)` of `K` on a scheme `T` over the strict henselization
`Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`, with `g : T ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x} ⟶ X` the structure morphism, natural in `K`.

The derived global sections on `T` are the total right derived functor of global sections on the
whole unbounded homotopy category, which exists by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleGlobalSectionsAb_hasRightDerivedFunctor`. Since the strict
henselization is the initial étale neighbourhood of `x`, pulling back germs along
`T ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` gives the map `etaleStalkToSectionsAb` on abelian sheaves; the stalk
functor is exact, so the map on sheaves extends uniquely to one of derived categories.
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDerivedStalkToSections_eq_restriction` identifies it with the
identification `K_x = RΓ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, K)` followed by pulling back cohomology along
`T ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleDerivedStalkToSections :
    smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb x.hom ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections T
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary scheme over the strict henselization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDerivedStalkToSections_fac_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN.** On every complex of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, the
canonical map to the derived global sections over `T` factors the degreewise map on sheaves
through the unit of the derivation of global sections, read through the identifications of the
degreewise actions of the stalk and of inverse image with their actions on derived categories.

Since the degreewise action of the stalk functor is a right derived functor of itself, this
property determines the map.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallEtaleDerivedStalkToSections_fac_app
    (J : HomotopyCategory (Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (.up ℤ)) :
    (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app J ≫
        (smallEtaleDerivedStalkToSections B X hX x q).app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj J) =
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((Stacks.DerivedFunctor.mapHomotopyCategoryOfComp
          (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom)
          (smallEtalePullbackAb
            (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x))
          (Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology T) Ab.{u + 1})
          (etaleStalkToSectionsAb B X hX x q)).app J) ≫
        (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsUnit T).app
            (((smallEtalePullbackAb
              (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ)).obj J) ≫
          (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections T).map
            ((smallEtalePullbackAb
              (q ≫ strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.inv.app J)
declarations.comment: the derived map factors the map on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkToVanishingCyclesFibreSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN.** The canonical map

`α_{K,x,t} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(F_{x,t}, K)`

from the stalk at a geometric point `x` of `X` of an object `K` of the unbounded derived category
`D(X_étale)` of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, to the unbounded derived sections
`RΓ(F_{x,t}, K) = RΓ((F_{x,t})_étale, g⁻¹K)` of `K` on the variety of vanishing cycles
`F_{x,t} = t ×_{Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}} Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` of a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` at `x` and a
geometric point `t` of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}`, with `g : F_{x,t} ⟶ X` the canonical morphism,
natural in `K`.

The derived global sections on `F_{x,t}` exist by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleGlobalSectionsAb_hasRightDerivedFunctor`. The stalk of `K` at
`x` is the derived sections of `K` over the strictly henselian `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDerivedStalkIsoStrictHenselizationSections`), and the map is
pullback of cohomology along the projection `F_{x,t} ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.stalkToVanishingCyclesFibreSections_eq_restriction`).
declarations.statement:
def stalkToVanishingCyclesFibreSections :
    smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb x.hom ⟶
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (vanishingCyclesFibreToSource B hX hS f x t) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (vanishingCyclesFibre B hX hS f x t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleDerivedStalkIsoStrictHenselizationSections
declarations.doc:
**The stalk is the derived sections over the strict henselization.** For every object `K` of
the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, the canonical
map `K_x ⟶ RΓ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, p⁻¹K)` is an isomorphism, natural in `K`: on sheaves it is
`F_x = Γ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, p⁻¹F)`, and global sections over the strictly henselian
`Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` are exact, so no boundedness of `K` is needed.
declarations.statement:
def smallEtaleDerivedStalkIsoStrictHenselizationSections :
    smallEtaleDerivedStalkAb x.hom ≅
      smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x) ⋙
        smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (strictHenselization B X hX x)
declarations.comment: `K_x = RΓ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, K)`, since `𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` is strictly henselian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkToVanishingCyclesFibreSections_eq_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJN: the map `α_{K,x,t}` is pullback of cohomology along
`F_{x,t} ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`.** The canonical map `α_{K,x,t} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(F_{x,t}, K)` at the
variety of vanishing cycles `F_{x,t} = t ×_{Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}} Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` is the
identification `K_x = RΓ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, K)` followed by restriction of unbounded derived
global sections along the second projection `F_{x,t} ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`, read through the
composition isomorphism of inverse images.
declarations.statement:
theorem stalkToVanishingCyclesFibreSections_eq_restriction :
    stalkToVanishingCyclesFibreSections B hX hS f x t =
      (smallEtaleDerivedStalkIsoStrictHenselizationSections B X hX x).hom ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x))
          (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsRestriction
            (vanishingCyclesFibreToStrictHenselization B hX hS f x t)) ≫
        (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight
            (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIsoOfCompIso
              (smallEtalePullbackAbCompIso (vanishingCyclesFibreToStrictHenselization B hX hS f x t)
                (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x))).hom
            (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (vanishingCyclesFibre B hX hS f x t))
declarations.comment: the map is obtained by pulling back cohomology along `F_{x,t} ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`, using `K_x = RΓ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, K)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.localAcyclicity_iff_isIso_vanishingCyclesFibreMap
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and let `K` be an object of `D(X_étale)`. The five
notions of the definition are, in terms of the canonical maps `α_{K,x,t} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(F_{x,t}, K)`
of [Stacks, Tag 0GJN]:

1. `f` is *locally acyclic at a geometric point `x` of `X` relative to `K`* when `α_{K,x,t}` is
   an isomorphism for every geometric point `t` of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}`;
2. `f` is *locally acyclic relative to `K`* when that holds at every geometric point `x` of `X`;
3. `f` is *universally locally acyclic relative to `K`* when for every morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` of
   schemes the base change `X ×_S S' ⟶ S'` is locally acyclic relative to the inverse image of
   `K`;
4. `f` is *locally acyclic* when for every geometric point `x` of `X` and every positive integer
   `n` prime to the characteristic of `κ(x)` it is locally acyclic at `x` relative to the
   constant sheaf `ℤ/nℤ`;
5. `f` is *universally locally acyclic* when every base change of `f` is locally acyclic.

The geometric points `t` are not assumed to be algebraic geometric points of
`Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}`: `GeometricPoint` asks only for a morphism from the spectrum of an
algebraically closed field.

The varieties of vanishing cycles are formed inside a big étale site, so clauses (1), (2) and
(4) carry one; clauses (3) and (5) quantify over all morphisms `g : S' ⟶ S` and over all big
étale sites containing `X ×_S S'` and `S'`, of which there is always at least one
(`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bigEtaleSite_contains_pullback`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem localAcyclicity_iff_isIso_vanishingCyclesFibreMap (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (hX : B.Contains X) (hS : B.Contains S) (f : X ⟶ S)
    (K : smallEtaleDerivedCategory X) :
    (∀ x : GeometricPoint X, IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX hS f K x ↔
        ∀ t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f)),
          IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app K)) ∧
      (IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K ↔
        ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X)
          (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f))),
          IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app K)) ∧
      (IsUniversallyLocallyAcyclicRelative f K ↔
        ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S) (B' : BigEtaleSite.{u})
          (hX' : B'.Contains (pullback f g)) (hS' : B'.Contains S')
          (x' : GeometricPoint (pullback f g))
          (t' : GeometricPoint
            (strictHenselization B' S' hS' (x'.map (pullback.snd f g)))),
          IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B' hX' hS'
              (pullback.snd f g) x' t').app
            ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (pullback.fst f g)).obj K))) ∧
      (IsLocallyAcyclic B hX hS f ↔
        ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X) (n : ℕ), 0 < n →
          (ringChar x.residueField = 0 ∨ n.Coprime (ringChar x.residueField)) →
            ∀ t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f)),
              IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app
                (smallEtaleConstantZModComplex X n))) ∧
      (IsUniversallyLocallyAcyclic f ↔
        ∀ (S' : Scheme.{u}) (g : S' ⟶ S) (B' : BigEtaleSite.{u})
          (hX' : B'.Contains (pullback f g)) (hS' : B'.Contains S')
          (x' : GeometricPoint (pullback f g)) (n : ℕ), 0 < n →
          (ringChar x'.residueField = 0 ∨ n.Coprime (ringChar x'.residueField)) →
            ∀ t' : GeometricPoint
              (strictHenselization B' S' hS' (x'.map (pullback.snd f g))),
              IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B' hX' hS'
                  (pullback.snd f g) x' t').app
                (smallEtaleConstantZModComplex (pullback f g) n)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.SmoothBaseChange.isUniversallyLocallyAcyclic_of_smooth_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Smooth morphisms are universally locally acyclic** ([Stacks, Proposition 0GJQ]). Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a smooth morphism of schemes. Then `f` is universally locally acyclic: for every
morphism `S' ⟶ S` and every big étale site containing `X ×_S S'` and `S'`, the base change
`X ×_S S' ⟶ S'` of `f` is locally acyclic there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyLocallyAcyclic_of_smooth_unconditional {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Smooth f] : IsUniversallyLocallyAcyclic f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicRelative_of_isLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJR.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and let `F` be a locally constant
abelian sheaf on `X_étale` whose stalk at every geometric point `x` is torsion with every element
order prime to the characteristic of the residue field at `x`. If `f` is locally acyclic, then
`f` is locally acyclic relative to `F`.

What is proved here is the dévissage: the reduction of the locally constant torsion coefficient
sheaf `F` to the constant sheaves `ℤ/nℤ` that local acyclicity speaks about. The stalk is written
as the filtered colimit of its finite subgroups, each of those splits as a finite direct sum of
cyclic groups of prime-to-`p` order, and local acyclicity is applied to each summand.

Four hypotheses are supplied rather than derived.

* `hdep` and `hconst` are the two facts about the strict henselization that the source's proof
  rests on, each stated in its own right. `hdep` is the consequence of
  `K_x = RΓ(Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}, K)` that the canonical map only sees the inverse image of `K` on
  `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}`; `hconst` is that a locally constant sheaf has constant inverse image
  there, with value its stalk.
* `hcolim` is Tag 03Q5 for the affine variety of vanishing cycles, in the form the argument
  consumes it: the iso-locus of the canonical map on constant coefficients is closed under
  filtered colimits of the coefficient group.
* `hadd` is additivity of unbounded derived global sections, which is formal but not an
  available instance.

See the module docstring for why `hcolim` cannot be stated as preservation of filtered
colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAcyclicRelative_of_isLocallyConstant
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X S : Scheme.{u}} (hX : B.Contains X) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (f : X ⟶ S)
    (hadd : ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X)
        (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f))),
      (smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections (vanishingCyclesFibre B hX hS f x t)).Additive)
    (hcolim : ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X)
        (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f))),
      ∀ {I : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I] (N : I ⥤ Ab.{u + 1})
        (c : Cocone N), IsColimit c →
        (∀ i, IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app
            (smallEtaleConstantComplexAb X (N.obj i)))) →
          IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app
            (smallEtaleConstantComplexAb X c.pt)))
    (hdep : ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X)
        (t : GeometricPoint (strictHenselization B S hS (x.map f)))
        (K K' : smallEtaleDerivedCategory X),
      ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).obj K ≅
          (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).obj K') →
      (IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app K) ↔
        IsIso ((vanishingCyclesFibreMap B hX hS f x t).app K')))
    (hconst : ∀ (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}),
        Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant X.smallEtaleTopology G →
        ∀ x : GeometricPoint X,
      (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}) 0).obj G) ≅
        (smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb (strictHenselizationToBase B X hX x)).obj
          (smallEtaleConstantComplexAb X ((smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).obj G)))
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1})
    (hFlc : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant X.smallEtaleTopology F)
    (hFtors : ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X) (a : (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).obj F),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧
        (ringChar x.residueField = 0 ∨ Nat.Coprime n (ringChar x.residueField)) ∧ n • a = 0)
    (hf : IsLocallyAcyclic B hX hS f) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}) 0).obj F)
declarations.comment: the dévissage from constant ℤ/nℤ coefficients to a locally constant prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion sheaf: the stalk is the filtered colimit of its finite subgroups and each of those is a finite direct sum of cyclic groups. The two strict-henselization inputs are hypotheses — `hdep`, that the canonical map depends only on the inverse image on Spec O^sh_{X,x}, and `hconst`, that a locally constant sheaf is constant there with value its stalk — as are `hcolim`, which is Tag 03Q5 for the affine variety of vanishing cycles, and `hadd`, additivity of RGamma

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicRelative_of_isLocallyConstant_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJR.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and let `F` be a locally constant
abelian sheaf on `X_étale` whose stalk at every geometric point `x` is torsion with every element
order prime to the characteristic of the residue field at `x`. If `f` is locally acyclic, then
`f` is locally acyclic relative to `F`.

What is proved here is the dévissage: the reduction of the locally constant torsion coefficient
sheaf `F` to the constant sheaves `ℤ/nℤ` that local acyclicity speaks about. The stalk is written
as the filtered colimit of its finite subgroups, each of those splits as a finite direct sum of
cyclic groups of prime-to-`p` order, and local acyclicity is applied to each summand.

No hypothesis is supplied rather than derived. The two facts about the strict henselization that
the source's proof rests on are both proved: that the canonical map only sees the inverse image of
`K` on `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{X,x}` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_vanishingCyclesFibreMap_app_iff_of_derivedPullbackIso`, and that a
locally constant sheaf has constant inverse image there, with value its stalk, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationDerivedPullbackConstantComplexIso`. Nor is the filtered
colimit step a hypothesis: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_vanishingCyclesFibreMap_app_constantComplex_of_isColimit`, Tag 03Q5 for
the variety of vanishing cycles, and neither is additivity of `RΓ` there, which is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleDerivedGlobalSections_additive`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicRelative_of_isLocallyConstant` is the same statement with
those four facts taken as hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAcyclicRelative_of_isLocallyConstant_unconditional
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) {X S : Scheme.{u}} (hX : B.Contains X) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (f : X ⟶ S)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1})
    (hFlc : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant X.smallEtaleTopology F)
    (hFtors : ∀ (x : GeometricPoint X) (a : (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).obj F),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧
        (ringChar x.residueField = 0 ∨ Nat.Coprime n (ringChar x.residueField)) ∧ n • a = 0)
    (hf : IsLocallyAcyclic B hX hS f) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology Ab.{u + 1}) 0).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicAt_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
For a cartesian square of schemes with `g` integral, an
object `K` of `D(X_étale)` and a geometric point `x'` of the fibre product with image `x` in `X`,
local acyclicity of `f` at `x` relative to `K` implies local acyclicity of `f'` at `x'` relative
to `(g')⁻¹K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyAcyclicAt_of_isIntegralHom [IsIntegralHom g]
    (h : IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX hS f K (x'.map g')) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX' hS' f' ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb g').obj K) x'
declarations.comment: integral base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicAt_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
For a cartesian square of schemes with `g` locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite, an
object `K` of `D(X_étale)` and a geometric point `x'` of the fibre product with image `x` in `X`,
local acyclicity of `f` at `x` relative to `K` implies local acyclicity of `f'` at `x'` relative
to `(g')⁻¹K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyAcyclicAt_of_locallyQuasiFinite [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite g] (h : IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX hS f K (x'.map g')) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX' hS' f' ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb g').obj K) x'
declarations.comment: locally quasi-finite base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicAt_of_limit
declarations.doc:
Let `{ Dᵢ }` be an inverse system of
schemes indexed by a cofiltered category, with affine transition morphisms, whose stages are
locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite over `S` compatibly with the transition
morphisms, let `S' = lim Dᵢ`, and let

```
X' --g'--> X
|f'        |f
S' --g---> S
```

be a cartesian square whose `g` is induced by the morphisms from the stages. For an object `K` of
`D(X_étale)` and a geometric point `x'` of `X'` with image `x` in `X`, local acyclicity of `f` at
`x` relative to `K` implies local acyclicity of `f'` at `x'` relative to `(g')⁻¹K`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyAcyclicAt_of_limit (p : ∀ i : I, D.obj i ⟶ S)
    (hp : ∀ i : I, c.π.app i ≫ p i = g) (hcompat : ∀ {i j : I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.map a ≫ p j = p i)
    [∀ i : I, LocallyOfFiniteType (p i)] [∀ i : I, LocallyQuasiFinite (p i)]
    (h : IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX hS f K (x'.map g')) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX' hS' f' ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb g').obj K) x'
declarations.comment: directed inverse limit base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicAt_strictHenselizationBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Local acyclicity survives base change to the strict henselization.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be
a morphism of schemes of a big étale site `B`, let `K` be an object of `D(X_étale)`, let `s` be a
geometric point of `S` and let `x` be a geometric point of the base change
`Y = X ×_S Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}` with image `y` in `X`. If `f` is locally acyclic at `y` relative to
`K`, then the projection `Y ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}` is locally acyclic at `x` relative to `K|_Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAcyclicAt_strictHenselizationBaseChange
    (x : GeometricPoint (strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s))
    (h : IsLocallyAcyclicAt B hX hS f K
      (x.map (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s))) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicAt B (contains_strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS hX f s)
      (contains_strictHenselization_of_contains B hS s)
      (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToStrictHenselization B hS f s)
      ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
        (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s)).obj K) x
declarations.comment: base change along the strict henselization at a geometric point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyAcyclicRelative_strictHenselizationBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Local acyclicity survives base change to the strict henselization.** If `f : X ⟶ S` is
locally acyclic relative to an object `K` of `D(X_étale)`, then the projection
`X ×_S Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s} ⟶ Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}` is locally acyclic relative to the restriction of
`K` to the base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAcyclicRelative_strictHenselizationBaseChange
    (hla : IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K) :
    IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B (contains_strictHenselizationBaseChange B hS hX f s)
      (contains_strictHenselization_of_contains B hS s)
      (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToStrictHenselization B hS f s)
      ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
        (strictHenselizationBaseChangeToSource B hS f s)).obj K)
declarations.comment: base change along the strict henselization at a geometric point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback_cospecializationUnit
declarations.doc:
Assume that isomorphy in unbounded derived categories of abelian sheaves on small étale sites
is detected on stalks (`hcons`) and that the stalks of `i⁻¹β_{K,s,t}` are canonical maps of
Tag 0GJN (`hcomp`). For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` which is locally acyclic relative to an
object `K` of `D(X_étale)`, the inverse image on the closed geometric fibre `X_s` of the
comparison `β_{K,s,t} : K|_Y ⟶ Rh_*(K|_{X_t})` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullback_cospecializationUnit
    (hla : IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K)
    (hcons : HasDerivedStalkConservativity.{u})
    (hcomp : HasCospecializationStalkComparison B) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
      (geometricFibreToStrictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s)).map
        (cospecializationUnit B hS f s t K))
declarations.comment: modulo derived-stalk conservativity and the stalk computation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback_cospecializationUnit_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GJU].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, `s` a geometric point of
`S`, `t` a geometric point of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}`, and `K` an object of `D(X_étale)` which is
bounded below and relative to which `f` is locally acyclic. Write `Y = X ×_S Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}`,
`h : X_t ⟶ Y` for the fibre over `t` and `i : X_s ⟶ Y` for the closed geometric fibre. Then the
inverse image `i⁻¹β_{K,s,t}` of the comparison `β_{K,s,t} : K|_Y ⟶ Rh_*(K|_{X_t})` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullback_cospecializationUnit_of_isGE (K : smallEtaleDerivedCategory X) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : K.IsGE m) (hla : IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
      (geometricFibreToStrictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s)).map
        (cospecializationUnit B hS f s t K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.specializationStalk_comp_baseChange_comp_cospecializationMap_of_isGE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GJV].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
schemes, `s` a geometric point of `S`, `t` a geometric point of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}`, and `K` an
object of `D(X_étale)` which is bounded below and relative to which `f` is locally acyclic, so
that the cospecialization map `cosp : RΓ(X_t, K) ⟶ RΓ(X_s, K)` is defined (Stacks 0GJU,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pullback_cospecializationUnit_of_isGE`). Then the square

```
(Rf_*K)_s ----------> RΓ(X_s, K)
   | sp                    ^ cosp
   v                       |
(Rf_*K)_t ----------> RΓ(X_t, K)
```

commutes: `sp` followed by the base change map of Stacks 0GIX at `t` and by `cosp` is the base
change map of Stacks 0GIX at `s`. Here `X_s` and `X_t` are the geometric fibres of `f` at `s` and
at the image of `t` in `S`, and the stalk of `Rf_*K` at `t` is taken at that image.
declarations.statement:
theorem specializationStalk_comp_baseChange_comp_cospecializationMap_of_isGE
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (K : smallEtaleDerivedCategory X) (m : ℤ)
    (hK : K.IsGE m) (hla : IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K) :
    haveI := isIso_pullback_cospecializationUnit_of_isGE B hX hS f s t K m hK hla
    (smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAbAt B S hS s t).app
          ((smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f).obj K) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f
          (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))).app K ≫
        (strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSections B hS f
          (t.map (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s))).app K ≫
        cospecializationMapGeometricFibre B hS f s t K =
      (derivedPushforwardStalkToStrictHenselizationSections B hS f s).app K ≫
        (strictHenselizationSectionsToFibreSections B hS f s).app K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_specializationStalk_and_cospecializationMap_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GJW].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes and `K` an object of
`D(X_étale)` such that

1. `K` is bounded below,
2. `f` is locally acyclic relative to `K`,
3. `f` is proper, and
4. `K` has torsion cohomology sheaves.

Then for every geometric point `s` of `S` and every geometric point `t` of `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,s}`
the specialization map `sp : (Rf_*K)_s ⟶ (Rf_*K)_t` is an isomorphism, and the cospecialization
map `cosp : RΓ(X_t, K) ⟶ RΓ(X_s, K)` — defined because `i⁻¹β_{K,s,t}` is an isomorphism (Tag
0GJU) — is an isomorphism.

The objects named in the statement, all defined in this library with no hypothesis beyond their
data:

* `smallEtaleDerivedCategory X` (`EtaleCohomology/DerivedEtale.lean`) is `D(X_étale)`, the derived
  category of abelian sheaves on the small étale site; `K.IsGE m` says `K` is bounded below.
* `IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K` (`LocalAcyclicity/Basic.lean`) is part (2) of
  Definition 0GJP: at every geometric point `x` of `X` and every geometric point `t` of
  `Spec 𝒪^{sh}_{S,f(x)}` the map `α_{K,x,t} : K_x ⟶ RΓ(F_{x,t}, K)` to the cohomology of the
  variety of vanishing cycles is an isomorphism; `B` is a big étale site containing `X` and `S`, a
  size device only.
* `Stacks.Torsion.torsionCohomologyProperty` (`CategoryTheory/Sites/Cohomology/Torsion/
  StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Cohomology/Torsion/DerivedCategoryOfTorsionSheaves.lean`) says every cohomology sheaf of `K` is torsion.
* `smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f` (`EtaleCohomology/StalkOfDerivedPushforward.lean`) is
  `Rf_*`, the total right derived functor of direct image; its existence is the proved instance
  `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.hasRightDerivedFunctor_smallEtalePushforwardAb`
  (`EtaleCohomology/SmallEtaleUnboundedDerivations.lean`), and that of `RΓ` the proved instance
  `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleGlobalSectionsAb_hasRightDerivedFunctor`
  (`EtaleCohomology/SmallEtaleDerivedGlobalSectionsExistence.lean`).
* `smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAbAt B S hS s t`
  (`EtaleCohomology/SpecializationMapAndFibres.lean`) is the specialization map
  `sp : (−)_s ⟶ (−)_t` on derived stalks, at the image of `t` in `S`.
* `cospecializationUnit B hS f s t K` (`LocalAcyclicity/CospecializationMap.lean`) is
  `β_{K,s,t} : K|_Y ⟶ Rh_*(K|_{X_t})`, and `geometricFibreToStrictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s`
  (`EtaleCohomology/StalkOfDerivedPushforward.lean`) is `i : X_s ⟶ Y`.
* `cospecializationMap B hS f s t K` (`LocalAcyclicity/CospecializationMapDerived.lean`) is the
  cospecialization map of Section 0GJT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_specializationStalk_and_cospecializationMap_of_isProper [IsProper f]
    (K : smallEtaleDerivedCategory X) (m : ℤ) (hK : K.IsGE m)
    (hla : IsLocallyAcyclicRelative B hX hS f K)
    (hKt : Stacks.Torsion.torsionCohomologyProperty.{u + 1} (smallEtaleTopology X) K) :
    IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedSpecializationStalkAbAt B S hS s t).app
        ((smallEtaleDerivedPushforwardAb f).obj K)) ∧
      ∃ _ : IsIso ((smallEtaleDerivedPullbackAb
          (geometricFibreToStrictHenselizationBaseChange B hS f s)).map
            (cospecializationUnit B hS f s t K)),
        IsIso (cospecializationMap B hS f s t K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.moduleTorsionSheafProperty_fShriekMod
declarations.doc:
A `Λ`-linear lift of the direct image with compact support sends torsion étale sheaves of
`Λ`-modules to torsion étale sheaves of `Λ`-modules: the lift is identified with `f_!` on
underlying abelian sheaves, and `f_!` preserves torsion there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleTorsionSheafProperty_fShriekMod
    (fShriekMod : ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B Y Λ)
    (hlift : fShriekMod ⋙ forgetModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B Y Λ ≅
      forgetModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ ⋙ fShriekFunctor.{u, max v r} B f)
    (F : ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ)
    (hF : moduleTorsionSheafProperty.{u, v, r} B X Λ F) :
    moduleTorsionSheafProperty.{u, v, r} B Y Λ (fShriekMod.obj F)
declarations.comment: the sheaf-level reduction: a `Λ`-linear lift of `f_!` preserves torsion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJX.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes and let `Λ` be
a ring. The functor `f_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⥤ D(Y_étale, Λ)` of Stacks 0F5N sends a complex with
torsion cohomology sheaves to a complex with torsion cohomology sheaves.

The `Λ`-linear lift of `f_!` is exact, so the cohomology of `f_! K` is `f_!` of the cohomology of
`K`; torsion of a sheaf of `Λ`-modules is torsion of its underlying abelian sheaf, which `hlift`
identifies with the image under `f_!` of the underlying abelian sheaf; and `f_!` preserves torsion
abelian sheaves, which Stacks 0GJX reads off the stalk description of `f_!` in Stacks 0F5F.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor
    (fShriekMod : ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B Y Λ)
    (hlift : fShriekMod ⋙ forgetModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B Y Λ ≅
      forgetModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ ⋙ fShriekFunctor.{u, max v r} B f)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ))
    (hK : moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty.{u, v, w, r} B X Λ K) :
    moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty.{u, v, w, r} B Y Λ
      ((moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor.{u, v, w, r} B Λ f fShriekMod hlift).obj K)
declarations.comment: general coefficient ring `Λ`: for a `Λ`-linear lift of `f_!`, the functor `f_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⥤ D(Y_étale, Λ)` of Tag 0F5N sends complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves to complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.moduleTorsionSheafProperty_fShriekMod_obj
declarations.doc:
The direct image with compact support with coefficients in a ring `Λ` sends torsion étale
sheaves of `Λ`-modules to torsion étale sheaves of `Λ`-modules: on underlying abelian sheaves it
is `f_!`, which preserves torsion by the stalk description of Stacks 0F5F.
declarations.comment: the sheaf-level input, for f_! with coefficients in Λ itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor_fShriekMod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GJX.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a locally quasi-finite morphism of schemes and let `Λ` be
a ring. The functor `f_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, Λ)` of Stacks 0F5N sends complexes with
torsion cohomology sheaves to complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves.

The functor `f_!` with coefficients in `Λ` is exact, so the cohomology of `f_! K` is `f_!` of the
cohomology of `K`; torsion of a sheaf of `Λ`-modules is torsion of its underlying abelian sheaf,
which is the image under `f_!` of the underlying abelian sheaf of the cohomology; and `f_!`
preserves torsion abelian sheaves, which the source reads off the stalk description of `f_!` in
Stacks 0F5F.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor_fShriekMod
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ))
    (hK : moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty.{u, v, w, r} B X Λ K) :
    moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty.{u, v, w, r} B Y Λ
      ((moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor.{u, v, w, r} B Λ f (fShriekMod.{u, v, r} B Λ f)
        (fShriekModForgetIso.{u, v, r} B Λ f)).obj K)
declarations.comment: f_! on D(X_étale, Λ) ⟶ D(Y_étale, Λ) sends complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves to complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.exists_nsmul_eq_zero_etaleStalk
declarations.doc: The stalk of a torsion abelian étale sheaf at a geometric point is a torsion abelian group.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_nsmul_eq_zero_etaleStalk (t : GeometricPoint S)
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hF : torsionSheafProperty (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) F)
    (g : ↑(etaleStalk B S hS t F.obj)) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ n • g = 0
declarations.comment: an input to the proof: the stalk of a torsion abelian étale sheaf at a geometric point is a torsion abelian group

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.torsionSheafProperty_of_forall_etaleStalk
declarations.doc:
An abelian étale sheaf whose stalks at all geometric points are torsion abelian groups is a
torsion abelian sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torsionSheafProperty_of_forall_etaleStalk
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hF : ∀ (t : GeometricPoint S) (g : ↑(etaleStalk B S hS t F.obj)),
      ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ n • g = 0) :
    torsionSheafProperty (SmallEtale.topology B S hS) F
declarations.comment: the stalk criterion used by the proof: an abelian étale sheaf whose stalks at all geometric points are torsion is a torsion abelian sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.torsionSheafProperty_fShriekFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
The direct image with compact support `f_!` of a locally quasi-finite morphism sends a torsion
abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `X` to a torsion abelian sheaf on the small étale site of
`Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torsionSheafProperty_fShriekFunctor_obj (F : AbelianSheaf.{u, v} B X)
    (hF : torsionSheafProperty (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) F) :
    torsionSheafProperty (SmallEtale.topology B Y.obj Y.property)
      ((fShriekFunctor.{u, v} B f).obj F)
declarations.comment: the abelian-sheaf case: `f_!` of a locally quasi-finite morphism sends a torsion abelian sheaf to a torsion abelian sheaf. The statement for a general coefficient ring is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.moduleTorsionCohomologyProperty_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJZ.** The cohomology with compact support
`RΓ_c(X, K) = RΓ(Spec k, Rf_! K)` of a bounded below complex of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the
small étale site of a separated finite type `k`-scheme `X`, through a compactification `j`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev compactlySupportedCohomology (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] :
    DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ)
declarations.comment: RΓ_c(X, K) = RΓ(Spec k, Rf_! K)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyTorsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJZ.** Cohomology with compact support on the subcategory
`D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)` of bounded below complexes with torsion cohomology sheaves, which is the
domain the source states the definition on.
declarations.statement:
abbrev compactlySupportedCohomologyTorsion (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] :
    (isTorsionPlus.{u, r} Λ X).FullSubcategory ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ)
declarations.comment: RΓ_c on D⁺_tors

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GJZ.** The compactly supported cohomology module
`H^i_c(X, K) = H^i(RΓ_c(X, K))`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] (i : ℤ) :
    DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) ⥤ ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ
declarations.comment: H^i_c(X, K) = H^i(RΓ_c(X, K))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyUnbounded
declarations.doc:
The cohomology with compact support `RΓ_c(X, K) = RΓ(Spec k, Rf_! K)` of an arbitrary
complex of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site of a separated finite type `k`-scheme
`X`, through a compactification `j`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev compactlySupportedCohomologyUnbounded (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] :
    DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ)
declarations.comment: RΓ_c(X, K) = RΓ(Spec k, Rf_! K) on D(X_étale, Λ)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyGroupUnbounded
declarations.doc:
The compactly supported cohomology module `H^i_c(X, K) = H^i(RΓ_c(X, K))` of an arbitrary
complex `K` in `D(X_étale, Λ)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev compactlySupportedCohomologyGroupUnbounded (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f))
    (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ] (i : ℤ) :
    DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) ⥤ ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ
declarations.comment: H^i_c(X, K) = H^i(RΓ_c(X, K)) on D(X_étale, Λ)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GK0**, the cohomology form, for a base change to a field. For a
cartesian square of schemes with `Y' = Spec k` (for instance a geometric point
`ȳ : Spec k ⟶ Y`, `k` separably closed), a compactification `j` of `X` over `Y` and
`K ∈ D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`: `RΓ(Spec k, g⁻¹ Rf_! K)`, which for `k` separably closed is the stalk
`(Rf_! K)_ȳ`, is the compactly supported cohomology `RΓ_c(X', (g')⁻¹ K)` of the fibre
`X' = X ×_Y Spec k`, computed with the base change of `j`.
declarations.statement:
def compactlySupportedCohomologyBaseChangeIso {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y X' : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Y} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of k)}
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [QuasiCompact f'] [IsSeparated f'] (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X))
    (hK : isTorsionPlus.{u, 0} Λ X K) :
    (etaleModuleDerivedGlobalSections.{u, 0} Λ (Spec (.of k))).obj
        ((etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus.{u, 0} Λ g).obj
          ((derivedLowerShriek.{u, 0} f j Λ).obj K)) ≅
      (compactlySupportedCohomology.{u, 0} k f' (j.baseChange sq) Λ).obj
        ((etaleModuleDerivedInverseImagePlus.{u, 0} Λ g').obj K)
declarations.comment: (Rf_! K)_ȳ ≅ RΓ_c(X_ȳ, K|_{X_ȳ}), with (Rf_! K)_ȳ = RΓ(Spec k, ȳ⁻¹ Rf_! K)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyUnboundedBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GK0**, the case of `D(X_étale, Λ)` for a torsion ring `Λ`. For a
cartesian square of schemes with `Y' = Spec k` (for instance a geometric point
`ȳ : Spec k ⟶ Y`, `k` separably closed), a compactification `j` of `X` over `Y`, a ring `Λ` with
`m = 0` in `Λ` for some `m > 0`, and an arbitrary `K ∈ D(X_étale, Λ)`:
`RΓ(Spec k, g⁻¹ Rf_! K)`, which for `k` separably closed is the stalk `(Rf_! K)_ȳ`, is the
compactly supported cohomology `RΓ_c(X', (g')⁻¹ K)` of the fibre `X' = X ×_Y Spec k`, computed
with the base change of `j`. Together with
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.compactlySupportedCohomologyBaseChangeIso` (the case of
`D⁺_tors(X_étale, Λ)`) this is the whole tag.
declarations.statement:
def compactlySupportedCohomologyUnboundedBaseChangeIso
    (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X)) :
    (etaleModuleDerivedGlobalSectionsUnbounded.{u, 0} Λ (Spec (.of k))).obj
        ((etaleModuleDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} Λ g).obj
          ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ).obj K)) ≅
      (compactlySupportedCohomologyUnbounded.{u, 0} k f' (j.baseChange sq) Λ).obj
        ((etaleModuleDerivedInverseImage.{u, 0} Λ g').obj K)
declarations.comment: (Rf_! K)_ȳ ≅ RΓ_c(X_ȳ, K|_{X_ȳ}) for K ∈ D(X_étale, Λ), Λ torsion

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.nonempty_compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup_zero_iso
declarations.doc:
The zeroth compactly supported cohomology group of a sheaf of `Λ`-modules `ℱ` on a `k`-scheme
`X`, placed in degree zero, is the group of global sections of the extension by zero `j_!ℱ` on a
compactification `j : X ⟶ X̄` of `X` over `k`.

This is the half of Tag 0GK1 that concerns Definition 0GJZ; the source's torsion hypothesis is not
used.  Tag 0GK1 itself is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.nonempty_addEquiv_compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup_zero_iso
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    (F : EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) :
    Nonempty ((compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup.{u, r} k f j Λ 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) 0).obj F) ≅
      (etaleModuleGlobalSections.{u, r} Λ j.space).obj
        ((etaleModuleExtensionByZero.{u, r} Λ j.immersion).obj F))
declarations.comment: the Definition 0GJZ side only: H^0_c(X, F) is H^0 of the extension by zero on a compactification

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.nonempty_addEquiv_compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GK1.** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a field `k`
and let `ℱ` be an abelian sheaf on `X_étale`, that is a sheaf of `ℤ`-modules. The group
`H⁰_c(X, ℱ)` of Definition 0GJZ, the zeroth cohomology of `RΓ_c(X, ℱ) = RΓ(Spec k, Rf_!ℱ)`
formed with a compactification `j : X ⟶ X̄`, agrees with the group `H⁰_c(X, ℱ)` of Definition
0F72 of sections of `ℱ` with support proper over `k`, the latter taken on the small étale site of
Tag 021B inside any big étale site `B` containing `X`, on which `ℱ` is read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.etaleModulesIntEquivalence`.

Both groups are `H⁰(X̄, j_!ℱ)`: the first by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.nonempty_compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup_zero_iso`, the second by Tags
0F75 and 0F73. The source's torsion hypothesis is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_addEquiv_compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup_zero
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (hX : B.Contains X)
    (F : EtaleModules.{u, 0} ℤ X) :
    Nonempty ((compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup.{u, 0} k f j ℤ 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (EtaleModules.{u, 0} ℤ X) 0).obj F) ≃+
      SmallEtale.compactlySupportedSections k X f B hX
        ((SmallEtale.etaleModulesIntEquivalence B X hX).functor.obj F))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isConstructible_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GK3**, granted the sheaf-level case. Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes which is locally quasi-finite and of finite presentation.
If a complex `K` of étale sheaves of `Λ`-modules on `X` lies in `D_c(X_étale, Λ)`, then
`f_! K` lies in `D_c(Y_étale, Λ)`, where `f_!` is the functor of Stacks 0F5N.

The proof is the source's reduction. A `Λ`-linear lift of the direct image with compact support
is exact, so it acts on the derived category termwise and `Hⁱ(f_! K) ≅ f_!(Hⁱ K)`; each `Hⁱ K` is
constructible by hypothesis, and constructibility of its image under `f_!` is `hShriekSheaf`.

`hShriekSheaf` is the sheaf-level form of this tag, quantified over every morphism of the big
étale site that is locally quasi-finite and of finite presentation, every `Λ`-linear lift of its
direct image with compact support and every sheaf of `Λ`-modules on its source; it mentions
neither `f`, nor `fShriekMod`, nor `K`. See "What is carried" in the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructible_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor
    (hShriekSheaf : ModuleFShriekConstructibleOnSheaves B Λ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, v, r} B X Λ)) (hK : IsConstructible B X Λ K) :
    IsConstructible B Y Λ ((moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor B Λ f fShriekMod hlift).obj K)
declarations.comment: the source's reduction of the tag to its sheaf-level case, which is carried as hShriekSheaf: granted that a Λ-linear lift of f_! takes constructible sheaves of Λ-modules to constructible sheaves for every locally quasi-finite morphism of finite presentation, the functor f_! of Stacks 0F5N on unbounded derived categories sends D_c into D_c. The step from sheaves to complexes, exactness of f_! and hence Hⁱ(f_! K) ≅ f_!(Hⁱ K), is proved

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isConstructible_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor_general
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GK3.** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes
which is locally quasi-finite and of finite presentation. The functor
`f_! : D(X_étale, Λ) ⥤ D(Y_étale, Λ)` of Stacks 0F5N, induced by the direct image with compact
support `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fShriekMod` with coefficients in `Λ`, sends
`D_c(X_étale, Λ)` into `D_c(Y_étale, Λ)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructible_moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor_general
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleSheaf.{u, u, u + 1} B X Λ)) (hK : IsConstructible B X Λ K) :
    IsConstructible B Y Λ ((moduleFShriekDerivedFunctor B Λ f (fShriekMod.{u, u, u + 1} B Λ f)
      (fShriekModForgetIso.{u, u, u + 1} B Λ f)).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProper_and_isProjective_normalizationOverField
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GK4.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme over `k` and let
`ν : X^ν ⟶ X` be the normalization morphism. Then `X^ν` is proper over `k`, and if `X` is
projective over `k` then `X^ν` is projective over `k`.

Projectivity of `X` is an implication inside the conclusion: the properness assertion holds at
the source's own hypotheses, with nothing assumed about projectivity. Over the affine base
`Spec k` projectivity and H-projectivity agree ([Stacks, Tag 01WB]), so the implication may be
read with either notion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProper_and_isProjective_normalizationOverField (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper p] :
    IsProper (normalizationOverField k p ≫ p) ∧
      (IsProjective p → IsProjective (normalizationOverField k p ≫ p))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_normalization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GK5], clauses (1) and (2), with the normalization smooth over `k'`.** Let `k`
be a field and let `X` be a scheme of finite type over `k` with `dim X ≤ 1`. There is a finite
purely inseparable extension `k'/k` such that the normalization of `X_{k'}` is smooth over `k'`.

Clauses (3), (4) and (5) of the source — the compactification `j` with dense image, the finite
separable extensions `k'_i/k'` and the smooth projective geometrically irreducible pieces over
them — are not established here; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_normalization (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Module.Finite k k')
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k'),
      Smooth (normalizationOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ≫
        pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p)
declarations.comment: clauses (1) and (2), with ν smooth over k'; clauses (3), (4), (5) not established

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_dense_openImmersion_smooth_projective_of_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GK5] for a reduced `X`.** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a reduced
separated scheme of finite type over `k` with `dim(X) ≤ 1`. There is a finite purely inseparable
extension `k'/k`, a finite family of schemes `Ȳᵢ` over `Spec k'`, and a dense open immersion `j`
from the normalization of `X_{k'}` into their disjoint union over `Spec k'`, such that each `Ȳᵢ`
is smooth, H-projective and geometrically irreducible of dimension at most one over a finite
separable extension `k'ᵢ/k'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_dense_openImmersion_smooth_projective_of_isReduced
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced X]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Module.Finite k k')
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k') (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (Ybar : ι → Scheme.{u})
      (sbar : (∐ Ybar) ⟶ Spec (.of k'))
      (K : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k' (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite k' (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable k' (K i))
      (rbar : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ Spec (.of (K i)))
      (j : normalizationSchemeOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ⟶ ∐ Ybar)
      (_ : IsOpenImmersion j),
      Dense (Set.range j.base) ∧
        j ≫ sbar = normalizationOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ≫
            pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p ∧
          (∀ i, rbar i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k' (K i)))
              = Sigma.ι Ybar i ≫ sbar) ∧
            ∀ i, Smooth (rbar i) ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism (rbar i) ∧
              GeometricallyIrreducible (rbar i) ∧ topologicalKrullDim (Ybar i : Type u) ≤ 1
declarations.comment: clauses (3), (4) and (5) -- the whole diagram -- for a REDUCED X. The source's first move is to replace X by its reduction; everything after that move is proved here. The normalization of X_{k'} is exhibited as a DENSE OPEN SUBSCHEME of the disjoint union of the compactifications Ybar_i (clause 3), each of which is SMOOTH, PROJECTIVE and GEOMETRICALLY IRREDUCIBLE of dimension at most one over a finite SEPARABLE extension k'_i/k' (clauses 4 and 5), and the diagram commutes over Spec k'. What is NOT covered: the reduction step, i.e. the case of an X that is not reduced.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_dense_openImmersion_smooth_projective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GK5].** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type
over `k` with `dim(X) ≤ 1`. There is a finite purely inseparable extension `k'/k` (clause 1) such
that the normalization of `X_{k'}` (clause 2) is a dense open subscheme (clause 3) of a finite
disjoint union of schemes `Ȳᵢ`, each smooth, H-projective and geometrically irreducible of
dimension at most one (clause 5) over a finite separable extension `k'ᵢ/k'` (clause 4), the whole
diagram commuting over `Spec k'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_dense_openImmersion_smooth_projective
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsSeparated p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [QuasiCompact p]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Module.Finite k k')
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k') (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (Ybar : ι → Scheme.{u})
      (sbar : (∐ Ybar) ⟶ Spec (.of k'))
      (K : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k' (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite k' (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable k' (K i))
      (rbar : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ Spec (.of (K i)))
      (j : normalizationSchemeOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ⟶ ∐ Ybar)
      (_ : IsOpenImmersion j),
      Dense (Set.range j.base) ∧
        j ≫ sbar = normalizationOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ≫
            pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p ∧
          (∀ i, rbar i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k' (K i)))
              = Sigma.ι Ybar i ≫ sbar) ∧
            ∀ i, Smooth (rbar i) ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism (rbar i) ∧
              GeometricallyIrreducible (rbar i) ∧ topologicalKrullDim (Ybar i : Type u) ≤ 1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_normalization_coproduct_smooth_projective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GK5] for a proper `X`.** Let `k` be a field and let `X` be proper over `k`
with `dim(X) ≤ 1`. There is a finite purely inseparable extension `k'/k` such that the
normalization of `X_{k'}` is a finite coproduct of schemes `Yᵢ`, each smooth, H-projective and
geometrically irreducible of dimension at most one over a finite separable extension `k'ᵢ/k'`,
compatibly with the structure morphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isPurelyInseparable_normalization_coproduct_smooth_projective
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper p]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : Module.Finite k k')
      (_ : IsPurelyInseparable k k') (ι : Type u) (_ : Finite ι) (Y : ι → Scheme.{u})
      (e : normalizationSchemeOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ≅ ∐ Y)
      (K : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Field (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra k' (K i))
      (_ : ∀ i, Module.Finite k' (K i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable k' (K i))
      (r : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Spec (.of (K i))),
      (∀ i, r i ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k' (K i))) =
          Sigma.ι Y i ≫ e.inv ≫
            normalizationOverField k' (pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ≫
              pullback.fst (spectrumMap k k') p) ∧
        ∀ i, Smooth (r i) ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism (r i) ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible (r i) ∧
          topologicalKrullDim (Y i : Type u) ≤ 1
declarations.comment: clauses (3), (4) and (5) for a PROPER X, where the open immersion j of clause (3) is an isomorphism and the compactifications Ybar_i are the components Y_i of the normalization themselves. Clauses (1) and (2) -- the finite purely inseparable k'/k and the normalization of X_{k'} -- are reproved here as part of the diagram. What the general separated case still needs is the compactification of Stacks 0BXW applied to X before k' is chosen, together with the identification of the normalization of X_{k'} with the open part of the normalization of that compactification.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSeparable_smooth_isProjectiveMorphism_geometricallyIrreducible
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GK5], clauses (4) and (5) at one component.** Let `Z` be a connected scheme,
smooth and proper over a field `k`, of dimension at most one. Then there is a finite separable
extension `K/k` and a morphism `r : Z ⟶ Spec K` over `k` which is smooth, H-projective and
geometrically irreducible, with `dim(Z) ≤ 1`.

The field is `K = Γ(Z, 𝒪_Z)` and the morphism is the canonical `Z ⟶ Spec Γ(Z, 𝒪_Z)`, exactly as
in the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isSeparable_smooth_isProjectiveMorphism_geometricallyIrreducible
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {Z : Scheme.{u}} (q : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper q] [Smooth q] [ConnectedSpace Z]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (Z : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra k K) (_ : Module.Finite k K)
      (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k K) (r : Z ⟶ Spec (.of K)),
      r ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)) = q ∧
        Smooth r ∧ IsProjectiveMorphism r ∧ GeometricallyIrreducible r ∧
        topologicalKrullDim (Z : Type u) ≤ 1
declarations.comment: clauses (4) and (5), at one component: for a CONNECTED scheme Z smooth and proper over a field k with dim Z <= 1 -- that is, for one of the compactified pieces Ybar_i of the diagram -- the field k'_i = Gamma(Z, O_Z) of clause (4) is a finite SEPARABLE extension of k, and Z is SMOOTH, PROJECTIVE and GEOMETRICALLY IRREDUCIBLE of dimension at most one over it, which is clause (5). The assembly of the diagram -- decomposing the normalization into its components and transporting along the open immersion j of clause (3) -- is not done here; clauses (1) and (2) are carried by AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isPurelyInseparable_smooth_normalization.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_curveDiagram_near_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GK7.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be separated and of finite presentation, and
let `η` be a generic point of an irreducible component of `S` such that `dim(X_η) ≤ 1`. Then
there are

1. an open neighbourhood `U` of `η`,
2. a finite, surjective, universally injective morphism `V ⟶ U`,
3. the base change `X_V = V ×_S X`, a pullback square over `V ⟶ U ⟶ S`,
4. a finite surjective morphism `ν : ∐ Yᵢ ⟶ X_V` and an open `W ⊆ X_V` such that `W` is dense
   in all fibres of `X_V ⟶ V`, `ν⁻¹(W) ∩ Yᵢ` is dense in all fibres of `Yᵢ ⟶ Tᵢ`, and
   `ν⁻¹(W) ⟶ W` is a thickening,
5. open immersions `jᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Ȳᵢ`,
6. finite étale morphisms `Tᵢ ⟶ V`,
7. surjective smooth morphisms `Yᵢ ⟶ Tᵢ`, and
8. smooth proper morphisms `Ȳᵢ ⟶ Tᵢ` with geometrically connected fibres of dimension at most
   one,

such that the diagram commutes: `jᵢ ≫ (Ȳᵢ ⟶ Tᵢ) = (Yᵢ ⟶ Tᵢ)` and the map `Yᵢ ⟶ X_V ⟶ V` is
`Yᵢ ⟶ Tᵢ ⟶ V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_curveDiagram_near_genericPoint {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsSeparated f]
    (hf : FinitePresentation f) (η : S) (hη : η ∈ genericPoints S)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber η) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (U : S.Opens) (_ : η ∈ U) (V : Scheme.{u}) (v : V ⟶ U.toScheme),
      IsFinite v ∧ Surjective v ∧ UniversallyInjective v ∧
      ∃ (XV : Scheme.{u}) (a : XV ⟶ X) (pV : XV ⟶ V), IsPullback a pV f (v ≫ U.ι) ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (T Y Ybar : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (t : ∀ i, T i ⟶ V) (q : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ T i)
        (qbar : ∀ i, Ybar i ⟶ T i) (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ Ybar i) (ν : (∐ Y) ⟶ XV) (W : XV.Opens),
        (∀ i, j i ≫ qbar i = q i) ∧ (∀ i, Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν ≫ pV = q i ≫ t i) ∧
        IsFinite ν ∧ Surjective ν ∧
        (∀ s : V, Dense ((pV.fiberι s) ⁻¹' (W : Set XV))) ∧
        (∀ i (s : T i), Dense (((q i).fiberι s) ⁻¹' ((Sigma.ι Y i ≫ ν) ⁻¹' (W : Set XV)))) ∧
        Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening (ν ∣_ W) ∧
        (∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)) ∧ (∀ i, IsFinite (t i) ∧ Etale (t i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Surjective (q i) ∧ Smooth (q i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsProper (qbar i) ∧ Smooth (qbar i) ∧
          (∀ s : T i, GeometricallyConnected ((qbar i).fiberToSpecResidueField s)) ∧
          ∀ s : T i, topologicalKrullDim ((qbar i).fiber s) ≤ 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeighting.comp_isOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
The restriction of a weighting to an open subscheme of the source is a
weighting of the restricted morphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsWeighting.mul_comp
declarations.doc:
The pointwise product of a weighting of `f` and the pullback of a weighting
of `g` is a weighting of `f ≫ g`.

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NodalFamilyCohomology.isIso_c_and_isIso_c_of_isPullback_of_isAtWorstNodal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GKA], part (a).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper and at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres. Then `f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S`, i.e. the comparison
`f.c : 𝒪_S ⟶ f_*𝒪_X` is invertible, and this holds after any base change: for every cartesian
square `X' ⟶ X`, `f' : X' ⟶ S'`, `S' ⟶ S`, the comparison `f'.c` is invertible.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0E0L]: `f` is flat and locally of finite presentation, being syntomic, and
geometrically reduced by `geometricallyReduced_of_isAtWorstNodal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_c_and_isIso_c_of_isPullback_of_isAtWorstNodal (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    [GeometricallyConnected f] (hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f) :
    IsIso f.c ∧ ∀ {X' S' : Scheme.{u}} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'},
      IsPullback g' f' f g → IsIso f'.c
declarations.comment: (a): `f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S`, as invertibility of `f.c`, and the same for every base change, stated for every cartesian square over `S`

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NodalFamilyCohomology.isFiniteLocallyFree_rightDerived_one_and_isIso_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GKA], part (b).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper and at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres. Then `R¹f_*𝒪_X` is a finite locally free
`𝒪_S`-module, and its formation commutes with any base change: over every quasi-compact and
quasi-separated open `V ⊆ S` (for instance every affine open, or `S` itself when `S` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated), for every cartesian square `X'' ⟶ f⁻¹(V)`, `X'' ⟶ Y''`,
`Y'' ⟶ V`, the canonical map `h^* R¹(f ∣_ V)_*𝒪 ⟶ R¹f''_* (h')^*𝒪` of [Stacks, Tag 0EX3] is an
isomorphism.

The base-change map of this library,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.topDirectImageBaseChangeMap`, is defined over a
quasi-compact quasi-separated base; commutation with base change is local on
the base, so asking it over every such open of `S` is the source's assertion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_rightDerived_one_and_isIso_baseChange (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    [GeometricallyConnected f] (hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
        (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived 1).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)) ∧
      ∀ (V : S.Opens) [CompactSpace V] [QuasiSeparatedSpace V] {X'' Y'' : Scheme.{u}}
        (h' : X'' ⟶ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (f'' : X'' ⟶ Y'') (h : Y'' ⟶ V)
        (sq : IsPullback h' f'' (f ∣_ V) h),
        IsIso (@Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.topDirectImageBaseChangeMap _ _
          (topDegreeSituation f hf V) (SheafOfModules.unit (f ⁻¹ᵁ V).toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
          (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AffineQcohPushforward.isQuasicoherent_unit _) h' f'' h
          (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeBaseChange.toShHom_comm_of_isPullback
            (S := topDegreeSituation f hf V) h' f'' h sq))
declarations.comment: (b): `R¹f_*𝒪_X` is finite locally free, and its formation commutes with any base change, read over every quasi-compact quasi-separated open of the base, where the base-change map of Tag 0EX3 is defined

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NodalFamilyCohomology.isZero_rightDerived_of_two_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GKA], part (c).** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper and at-worst-nodal of relative
dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres. Then `Rᵠf_*𝒪_X = 0` for every `q ≥ 2`.

The fibres have dimension one, so this is [Stacks, Tag 0E7D] at `d = 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_of_two_le (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [GeometricallyConnected f]
    (hf : IsAtWorstNodalOfRelativeDimensionOne f) (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).rightDerived q).obj
      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))
declarations.comment: (c): `Rᵠf_*𝒪_X = 0` for `q ≥ 2`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_extendScalars
declarations.doc:
Extension of scalars along a homomorphism of Noetherian rings preserves
constructibility on the small étale site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleModuleSheaf_extendScalars
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (R : Type r) (S : Type s) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
