    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (f : X.obj ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] :
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X.obj),
      (∀ q : ℤ, IsBigSiteConstructibleEtaleModule B X Λ
          ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K) ∧
        IsTorsionEtaleModule Λ X.obj ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) →
      ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ ((compactlySupportedCohomologyGroup.{u, 0} k f j Λ i).obj K)) ∧
    ((∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ (m : Λ) = 0) →
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X.obj),
        (∀ q : ℤ, IsBigSiteConstructibleEtaleModule B X Λ
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) →
        ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ
          ((compactlySupportedCohomologyGroupUnbounded.{u, 0} k f j Λ i).obj K))
declarations.comment: both cases: K in D+_{tors,c}(X, Λ), and K in D_c(X, Λ) when Λ is torsion (m = 0 in Λ for some m > 0; H^i_c on D(X, Λ) is compactlySupportedCohomologyGroupUnbounded); H^i_c through any compactification j of X over k

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_rightDerived_of_smooth_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a smooth proper morphism of schemes, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let
`F` be a finite type, locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules on
`X_étale` such that for every geometric point `x̄` of `X` the stalk `F_x̄` is annihilated by an
integer `n > 0` prime to the residue characteristic of `x̄`. Then `Rⁱ f_* F` is a finite type,
locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `S_étale` for every `i`.

Here `Rⁱ f_*` is the `i`-th right derived functor of the direct image of sheaves of `Λ`-modules
for the small étale topologies, `i : ℕ` (for `i < 0` it is zero); the stalk `F_x̄` is that of the
underlying abelian sheaf, and "prime to the residue characteristic" reads `n` coprime to the
characteristic of the residue field of `x̄`, a condition void in characteristic zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_rightDerived_of_smooth_of_isProper
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] [IsProper f] (Λ : Type) [CommRing Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (F : EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ X)
    (hF : IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u + 1, 0} X.smallEtaleTopology Λ F)
    (htors : ∀ x : GeometricPoint X, ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧
      (ringChar x.residueField = 0 ∨ n.Coprime (ringChar x.residueField)) ∧
      ∀ a : (smallEtaleStalkAb x.hom).obj ((etaleModuleForget Λ X).obj F), n • a = 0)
    (i : ℕ) :
    IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u + 1, 0} S.smallEtaleTopology Λ
      (((etaleModuleDirectImage.{u, 0} Λ f).rightDerived i).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedUpperShriek_homology_affineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GLK.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated finite type morphism of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, let `Λ` be a torsion ring (`n = 0` in `Λ` for some
`n ≥ 1`) and let `K ∈ D(Y_étale, Λ)`.  For `m ∈ ℤ` the cohomology sheaf `H^m(Rf^! K)` restricted
to `X_{affine, étale}` is the sheaf associated to the presheaf
`U ↦ Hom_Y(R(U ⟶ Y)_! Λ, K[m])`.

Here `Rf_! = R(fbar)_* ∘ j_!` is read off a compactification `j` of `f`, which exists by Nagata's
theorem ([Stacks, Tag 0F41]), and `Rf^!` is its right adjoint of [Stacks, Tag 0G2C].  The
identification holds for every compactification.  The functoriality of `R(U ⟶ Y)_! Λ` in `U` is
that of the discussion preceding the lemma, and the identification is one of presheaves: the
transition maps are those the source leaves to the reader.  The ring `Λ` lies in `Type`, the
universe in which [Stacks, Tag 0G2C] is available.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedUpperShriek_homology_affineEtale {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] :
    (∃ j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f), QuasiCompact j.immersion) ∧
      ∀ (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (K : DerivedCategory (EtaleModules.{u, 0} Λ Y))
        (m : ℤ),
        letI := DerivedUpperShriek.isLeftAdjoint_derivedLowerShriekUnbounded Λ n hn hΛ f j
        Nonempty ((presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1 + 1}).obj
            (affineEtaleLowerShriekHomPresheafUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ K m) ≅
          (affineEtaleAbelianRestriction.{u, 0} Λ X).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ m).obj
              ((derivedLowerShriekUnbounded.{u, 0} f j Λ).rightAdjoint.obj K)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSheafifiedHomIso
declarations.doc:
**The content of Stacks Tag 0GLK that does not depend on Stacks Tag 0BKV.** The
sheafification of the source's presheaf `U ↦ Hom_Y(R(U ⟶ Y)_! Λ, K[n])` on the small affine
étale site of `X` is the sheafification of `U ↦ Hom_X((j_U)_! Λ, Rf^! K[n])`.
declarations.statement:
def affineEtaleSheafifiedHomIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    {Uf : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ Y) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X)}
    (adjF : derivedLowerShriek.{u, r} f j Λ ⊣ Uf)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ Y)) (n : ℤ) :
    (presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r + 1}).obj
        (affineEtaleLowerShriekHomPresheaf.{u, r} f j Λ K n) ≅
      (presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r + 1}).obj
        (affineEtaleUpperShriekHomPresheaf.{u, r} Λ X (Uf.obj K) n)
declarations.comment: the comparison of the two sheafifications, which is the half of the tag not depending on Stacks 0BKV; Rf^! is an explicit right adjoint of Rf_!, its existence being Stacks 0G2C

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.affineEtaleSheafifiedHomIsoOfToBase
declarations.doc:
**The same comparison, with only the right adjoint of the proper pushforward assumed.**

`Rf_!` is the composite `R(fbar)_* ∘ Rj_!` of a compactification, and `Rj_!` has the right
adjoint `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleModuleDerivedExtensionByZeroAdj`, extension by zero along
the open immersion being exact. So the adjunction `Rf_! ⊣ Rf^!` is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedLowerShriekAdjunctionOfFactors` of a right adjoint `Ubar` of
`R(fbar)_*`, and `Rf^!` is `Ubar ⋙ Rj^{-1}`.
declarations.statement:
def affineEtaleSheafifiedHomIsoOfToBase {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    {Ubar : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ Y) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ j.space)}
    (adjToBase : etaleModuleDerivedDirectImage.{u, r} Λ j.toBase ⊣ Ubar)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ Y)) (n : ℤ) :
    (presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r + 1}).obj
        (affineEtaleLowerShriekHomPresheaf.{u, r} f j Λ K n) ≅
      (presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r + 1}).obj
        (affineEtaleUpperShriekHomPresheaf.{u, r} Λ X
          ((Ubar ⋙ etaleModuleDerivedRestriction.{u, r} Λ j.immersion).obj K) n)
declarations.comment: the comparison of the two sheafifications, assuming only a right adjoint of the proper pushforward R(fbar)_*; the right adjoint of Rj_! along the open immersion is constructed, not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.derivedUpperShriekHomologyAffineEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GLK.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated finite type morphism of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, let `Λ` be a ring, let `K` be an object of
`D⁺(Y_étale, Λ)` and let `n : ℤ`.  Let `Uf` be a right adjoint of `Rf_!`, so `Uf = Rf^!`.  Then
the cohomology sheaf `H^n(Rf^! K)`, restricted to the small affine étale site of `X`, is the
sheaf associated to the presheaf
```
U ↦ Hom_Y(R(U ⟶ Y)_! Λ, K[n])
```
The right adjoint `Uf` and the adjunction are data: the adjunction is what `Rf^!` is, and its
existence is Stacks Tag 0G2C.  The hypothesis `sheafifiedCohomology` is Stacks Tag 0BKV
together with the source's recollection `Hom_X(j_! Λ, M[n]) = H^n(U, M)`, at the single object
`M = Rf^! K`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedUpperShriekHomologyAffineEtale {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    {Uf : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ Y) ⥤
      DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X)}
    (adjF : derivedLowerShriek.{u, r} f j Λ ⊣ Uf)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ Y)) (n : ℤ)
    (sheafifiedCohomology :
      (presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r + 1}).obj
          (affineEtaleUpperShriekHomPresheaf.{u, r} Λ X (Uf.obj K) n) ≅
        (affineEtaleAbelianRestriction.{u, r} Λ X).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) n).obj
            (Uf.obj K))) :
    (presheafToSheaf (AffineEtale.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r + 1}).obj
        (affineEtaleLowerShriekHomPresheaf.{u, r} f j Λ K n) ≅
      (affineEtaleAbelianRestriction.{u, r} Λ X).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (EtaleModules.{u, r} Λ X) n).obj (Uf.obj K))
declarations.comment: with Rf^! taken as an explicit right adjoint of Rf_!, its existence being Stacks 0G2C, which is not proved in this library and is therefore an interface here; and with Stacks 0BKV supplied at the single object Rf^!K, the clauses of 0BKV in this library being stated for a RingedSite's SheafOfModules in the derived-sections presentation, which does not instantiate to Sheaf(X_etale, ModuleCat Λ) in the Hom((j_U)_!Λ, -) presentation

declarations.name: CompletionAdjunction.derivedCompleteModules_abelian_hasLimits_exact_hasColimits
declarations.doc:
The full subcategory of modules derived complete with respect to an ideal is abelian and has
all limits, and its inclusion into modules is exact and preserves limits. If the ideal is
finitely generated, the subcategory has all colimits and the inclusion has a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedCompleteModules_abelian_hasLimits_exact_hasColimits
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    let P : ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      fun M => IsDerivedCompleteModule I M
    let C := P.FullSubcategory
    let F : C ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := P.ι
    Nonempty (Abelian C) ∧
      HasLimitsOfSize.{u, u} C ∧
      PreservesLimitsOfSize.{u, u} F ∧
      exactFunctor C (ModuleCat.{u} A) F ∧
      (I.FG → HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} C ∧ F.IsRightAdjoint)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_isSolution_of_tower
declarations.doc:
A finite extension of a solution for an extension of discrete valuation rings is again a
solution.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSolution_of_tower
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL)
    (K₁ : Type uK₁) (K₂ : Type uK₂)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Field K₁] [Field K₂]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A K] [Algebra A L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra K L]
    [Algebra K K₁] [Algebra K₁ K₂] [Algebra K K₂]
    [Algebra A K₁] [Algebra A K₂]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [IsScalarTower A K K₁] [IsScalarTower A K K₂]
    [IsScalarTower K K₁ K₂] [IsScalarTower A K₁ K₂]
    [IsExtension A B]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Module.Finite K K₁] [Module.Finite K₁ K₂]
    (hsolution :
      ∃ D₁ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₁,
          max uL uK₁, uK₁, max uL uK₁} A B K L K₁,
        D₁.IsSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₁, max uL uK₁, uK₁, max uL uK₁,
          max uL uK₁}) :
    letI : Module.Finite K K₂ := Module.Finite.trans K₁ K₂
    ∃ D₂ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₂,
        max uL uK₂, uK₂, max uL uK₂} A B K L K₂,
      D₂.IsSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₂, max uL uK₂, uK₂, max uL uK₂,
        max uL uK₂}

declarations.name: IsNagataRing.of_isSeparable_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be an extension of discrete valuation rings, and let `K → L` be the induced
extension of their fraction fields. If `B` is Nagata and `L/K` is separable, then `A` is
Nagata.
declarations.statement:
theorem of_isSeparable_fractionRing
    (A B K L : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsExtension A B]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L] [Algebra A L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (hB : IsNagataRing B) (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension K L) :
    IsNagataRing A

declarations.name: exists_bound_finite_extension_ringEquiv_mod
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GLT**.
Let `A' ⊂ A` be an extension of rings and `f ∈ A'`, with `A` finite over `A'`, `f` a nonzerodivisor
on `A`, and `A'_f = A_f`. Then there is `n₀ > 0` such that for all `n ≥ n₀`: for every ring `B'`,
every nonzerodivisor `g ∈ B'`, and every ring isomorphism `φ' : A'/f^n A' ≃ B'/g^n B'` sending
the class of `f` to the class of `g`, there exist a finite ring extension `B' ⊂ B` and a ring
isomorphism `φ : A/fA ≃ B/gB` compatible with `φ'`, i.e. making the square of reduction maps
commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bound_finite_extension_ringEquiv_mod
    (A' : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing A'] [CommRing A] [Algebra A' A]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A' A))
    (f : A')
    [Module.Finite A' A]
    (hnzd : algebraMap A' A f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (hloc : LocalizationEq A' A f) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, 0 < n₀ ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
      ∀ (B' : Type w) [CommRing B'] (g : B') (_ : g ∈ nonZeroDivisors B')
        (hn : 1 ≤ n)
        (φ' : (A' ⧸ Ideal.span {f ^ n}) ≃+* (B' ⧸ Ideal.span {g ^ n})),
        φ' (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ f) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ g →
        ∃ (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra B' B),
          Function.Injective (algebraMap B' B) ∧
          Module.Finite B' B ∧
          ∃ φ : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap A' A f}) ≃+*
              (B ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap B' B g}),
            (φ : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap A' A f}) →+* _).comp
                (reductionMap A' A f n hn)
              = (reductionMap B' B g n hn).comp
                (φ' : (A' ⧸ Ideal.span {f ^ n}) →+* _)

declarations.name: exists_compatible_finite_extensions_of_quotient_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GLU**. The construction of `exists_bound_finite_extension_ringEquiv_mod` is
  functorial. Given a commutative square
of finite injective ring extensions satisfying its hypotheses, and a compatible square of
isomorphisms modulo a sufficiently large common power, the two constructed finite extensions
admit a map extending the given map of base rings. Both the square of extensions and the square
of the resulting isomorphisms modulo the nonzerodivisors commute. As in the construction
`B = g^{-t} N ⊆ B'_g` of `bSubalg`, each extension becomes an isomorphism after inverting the
corresponding image of `g`, and this image is a nonzerodivisor in the constructed ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_compatible_finite_extensions_of_quotient_equiv
    (A₁' : Type u₁) (A₁ : Type v₁) (A₂' : Type u₂) (A₂ : Type v₂)
    [CommRing A₁'] [CommRing A₁] [CommRing A₂'] [CommRing A₂]
    [Algebra A₁' A₁] [Algebra A₂' A₂]
    (iA₁ : Function.Injective (algebraMap A₁' A₁))
    (iA₂ : Function.Injective (algebraMap A₂' A₂))
    (a' : A₁' →+* A₂') (a : A₁ →+* A₂)
    (ha : a.comp (algebraMap A₁' A₁) = (algebraMap A₂' A₂).comp a')
    (f : A₁')
    (hfin₁ : Module.Finite A₁' A₁) (hfin₂ : Module.Finite A₂' A₂)
    (hnzd₁ : algebraMap A₁' A₁ f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A₁)
    (hnzd₂ : algebraMap A₂' A₂ (a' f) ∈ nonZeroDivisors A₂)
    (hloc₁ : LocalizationEq A₁' A₁ f)
    (hloc₂ : LocalizationEq A₂' A₂ (a' f)) :
    ∃ (n₀₁ : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n₀₁) (n₀₂ : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n₀₂),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (hnmax : max n₀₁ n₀₂ ≤ n),
      ∀ (B₁' : Type w₁) (B₂' : Type w₂) [CommRing B₁'] [CommRing B₂']
        (b' : B₁' →+* B₂') (g : B₁')
        (_ : g ∈ nonZeroDivisors B₁') (_ : b' g ∈ nonZeroDivisors B₂')
        (φ₁' : (A₁' ⧸ Ideal.span {f ^ n}) ≃+* (B₁' ⧸ Ideal.span {g ^ n}))
        (φ₂' : (A₂' ⧸ Ideal.span {(a' f) ^ n}) ≃+*
          (B₂' ⧸ Ideal.span {(b' g) ^ n})),
        φ₂'.toRingHom.comp
            (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.span {(a' f) ^ n}) a' (by
              apply Ideal.span_le.2
              rintro _ rfl
              change a' (f ^ n) ∈ Ideal.span {(a' f) ^ n}
              rw [map_pow]
              exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _))) =
          (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.span {(b' g) ^ n}) b' (by
            apply Ideal.span_le.2
            rintro _ rfl
            change b' (g ^ n) ∈ Ideal.span {(b' g) ^ n}
            rw [map_pow]
            exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _))).comp φ₁'.toRingHom →
        φ₁' (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ f) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ g →
        ∃ (B₁ : Type w₁) (_ : CommRing B₁) (_ : Algebra B₁' B₁)
          (B₂ : Type w₂) (_ : CommRing B₂) (_ : Algebra B₂' B₂),
          Function.Injective (algebraMap B₁' B₁) ∧ Module.Finite B₁' B₁ ∧
          Function.Injective (algebraMap B₂' B₂) ∧ Module.Finite B₂' B₂ ∧
          LocalizationEq B₁' B₁ g ∧ LocalizationEq B₂' B₂ (b' g) ∧
          algebraMap B₁' B₁ g ∈ nonZeroDivisors B₁ ∧
          algebraMap B₂' B₂ (b' g) ∈ nonZeroDivisors B₂ ∧
          ∃ (b : B₁ →+* B₂)
            (hb : b.comp (algebraMap B₁' B₁) = (algebraMap B₂' B₂).comp b')
            (φ₁ : (A₁ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap A₁' A₁ f}) ≃+*
              (B₁ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap B₁' B₁ g}))
            (φ₂ : (A₂ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap A₂' A₂ (a' f)}) ≃+*
              (B₂ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap B₂' B₂ (b' g)})),
            φ₂.toRingHom.comp
                (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.span {algebraMap A₂' A₂ (a' f)}) a (by
                  apply Ideal.span_le.2
                  rintro _ rfl
                  change a (algebraMap A₁' A₁ f) ∈
                    Ideal.span {algebraMap A₂' A₂ (a' f)}
                  rw [show a (algebraMap A₁' A₁ f) =
                    algebraMap A₂' A₂ (a' f) from DFunLike.congr_fun ha f]
                  exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _))) =
              (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.span {algebraMap B₂' B₂ (b' g)}) b (by
                apply Ideal.span_le.2
                rintro _ rfl
                change b (algebraMap B₁' B₁ g) ∈
                  Ideal.span {algebraMap B₂' B₂ (b' g)}
                rw [show b (algebraMap B₁' B₁ g) =
                  algebraMap B₂' B₂ (b' g) from DFunLike.congr_fun hb g]
                exact Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_singleton _))).comp
                φ₁.toRingHom ∧
            φ₁.toRingHom.comp (reductionMap A₁' A₁ f n (by omega)) =
              (reductionMap B₁' B₁ g n (by omega)).comp φ₁'.toRingHom ∧
            φ₂.toRingHom.comp (reductionMap A₂' A₂ (a' f) n (by omega)) =
              (reductionMap B₂' B₂ (b' g) n (by omega)).comp φ₂'.toRingHom

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_isSeparable_solution_of_isPurelyInseparable_finrank_eq_prime
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be an extension of discrete valuation rings with separable fraction-field
extension `L/K`, where `K` has prime characteristic `p`, and suppose that `B` is Nagata. If
`K → K₁ → K₂` is a tower of finite extensions, `K₂` is a solution for `A → B`, and
`K₂/K₁` is purely inseparable of degree `p`, then some separable extension `K₃/K₁`
is a solution for `A → B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparable_solution_of_isPurelyInseparable_finrank_eq_prime
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) (K : Type uK) (L : Type uL)
    (K₁ : Type uK₁) (K₂ : Type uK₂)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Field K₁] [Field K₂]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A K] [Algebra A L] [Algebra B L] [Algebra K L]
    [Algebra K K₁] [Algebra K₁ K₂] [Algebra K K₂]
    [Algebra A K₁] [Algebra A K₂]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [IsScalarTower A K K₁] [IsScalarTower A K K₂]
    [IsScalarTower K K₁ K₂] [IsScalarTower A K₁ K₂]
    [IsExtension A B]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Module.Finite K K₁] [Module.Finite K₁ K₂]
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) [CharP K p]
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension K L)
    (hB : IsNagataRing B)
    (hsolution :
      letI : Module.Finite K K₂ := Module.Finite.trans K₁ K₂
      ∃ D₂ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₂,
          max uL uK₂, uK₂, max uL uK₂} A B K L K₂,
        D₂.IsSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₂, max uL uK₂, uK₂, max uL uK₂,
          max uL uK₂})
    (hpi : IsPurelyInseparable K₁ K₂)
    (hdegree : Module.finrank K₁ K₂ = p) :
    ∃ (K₃ : Type uK₁) (_ : Field K₃) (_ : Algebra K₁ K₃) (_ : Algebra K K₃)
      (_ : Algebra A K₃) (_ : IsScalarTower K K₁ K₃) (_ : IsScalarTower A K K₃)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A K₁ K₃) (_ : Module.Finite K K₃),
      Algebra.IsSeparable K₁ K₃ ∧
        ∃ D₃ : IntegralClosureBaseChange.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₁,
            max uL uK₁, uK₁, max uL uK₁} A B K L K₃,
          D₃.IsSolution.{uA, uB, uK, uL, uK₁, max uL uK₁, uK₁, max uL uK₁,
            max uL uK₁}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.colimitOfRepresentable
declarations.doc:
A sheaf `F` of sets on a site `C` is the colimit of the sheafified representables
`h_{U_i}^#` along the diagram `indexingDiagram J F`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def colimitOfRepresentable : IsColimit (coconeOfRepresentable J F)
declarations.comment:
(main statement) Every sheaf of sets on a site is the colimit of the sheafified
  representables over its category of elements. The final clause, that the diagram may be
  taken to land in a given family of objects covering every object, is not covered.

declarations.name: Module.exists_localizedMap_away_surjective_of_localizedMap_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GLX, special case (I) `I = 0`**: if `φ` becomes surjective after localizing at `S`,
it is already surjective after localizing at a single `f ∈ S`.

Taking `φ` to be `(a₁, …, a_r) ↦ ∑ aⱼxⱼ` recovers the footnote's wording: if `x₁, …, x_r`
generate `S⁻¹M`, then they generate `M_f` for some `f ∈ S`.

The arbitrary-submonoid form of
`Module.exists_localizedMap_away_surjective_of_localizedMap_atPrime_surjective`, and it needs only
`Module.Finite` on the target — `Module.FinitePresentation`, which the bijective analogue
`exists_bijective_map_powers` requires, is not needed for surjectivity alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.exists_localizedMap_away_surjective_of_localizedMap_surjective
    {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (S : Submonoid R) [Module.Finite R M] (φ : N →ₗ[R] M)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective (LocalizedModule.map S φ)) :
    ∃ f ∈ S, Function.Surjective (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) φ)
declarations.comment:
the footnote's special case (I), `I = 0`; for the general statement see
  `Submodule.exists_mem_addIdeal_and_span_image_eq_top` below

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_mem_addIdeal_and_span_image_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GLX**: if `s` generates `S⁻¹(M/IM)` and `M` is finite, then `s` generates `M_f`
for some `f ∈ S + I`.

The proof does not follow the Stacks argument, which localizes twice — first at some `s ∈ S`,
then at some `g ∈ 1 + I_s` via Nakayama — and then glues the two into a single `f = ss' + is`,
a step the tag leaves as "details omitted". Instead it localizes **once**, at `T = S + I`.

That works because `T` is a submonoid (`Submonoid.addIdeal`) which absorbs `I` under addition,
so `I` lands in the Jacobson radical of `T⁻¹R` (`Ideal.map_addIdeal_le_ringJacobson`) and
Nakayama applies over `T` directly. Concretely: enlarge the hypothesis from `S` to `T`
(`Submodule.span_image_eq_top_iff` at both ends), strip the quotient, apply 00DV (4)
(`Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`) to get that `s` spans `T⁻¹M`, then descend to a
single `f ∈ T` by the `I = 0` case above. `S + I` is not an ad-hoc answer: it is exactly the
submonoid over which `I` becomes Jacobson.

Stated against arbitrary localization witnesses; see
`Submodule.exists_mem_addIdeal_and_span_image_mkLinearMap_eq_top` for the concrete reading. The
hypothesis is phrased over `S⁻¹R` rather than the tag's `S⁻¹(R/I)`; spans agree along the
surjection `S⁻¹R ↠ S⁻¹(R/I)`, so this is a simplification and not a weakening. As in 00DV (7),
`s` need not be finite — only `M` — and the tag's `x₁, …, x_r` is `s := Set.range x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.exists_mem_addIdeal_and_span_image_eq_top
    (S : Submonoid R) (I : Ideal R) [Module.Finite R M] (s : Set M)
    {Rₛ Qₛ : Type*} [CommRing Rₛ] [Algebra R Rₛ] [IsLocalization S Rₛ]
    [AddCommGroup Qₛ] [Module R Qₛ] [Module Rₛ Qₛ] [IsScalarTower R Rₛ Qₛ]
    (fQ : (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) →ₗ[R] Qₛ) [IsLocalizedModule S fQ]
    (hs : Submodule.span Rₛ (fQ '' (Submodule.Quotient.mk '' s)) = ⊤) :
    ∃ f ∈ S.addIdeal I, ∀ {Rf Mf : Type*} [CommRing Rf] [Algebra R Rf]
      [IsLocalization (Submonoid.powers f) Rf] [AddCommGroup Mf] [Module R Mf] [Module Rf Mf]
      [IsScalarTower R Rf Mf] (g : M →ₗ[R] Mf) [IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) g],
      Submodule.span Rf (g '' s) = ⊤

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_mem_addIdeal_and_span_image_mkLinearMap_eq_top
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0GLX**, in the concrete `LocalizedModule` model: the tag's literal `M_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Submodule.exists_mem_addIdeal_and_span_image_mkLinearMap_eq_top
    (S : Submonoid R) (I : Ideal R) [Module.Finite R M] (s : Set M)
    (hs : Submodule.span (Localization S)
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule R M)) ''
        (Submodule.Quotient.mk '' s)) = ⊤) :
    ∃ f ∈ S.addIdeal I, Submodule.span (Localization (Submonoid.powers f))
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M '' s) = ⊤

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.FlatNeighbourhood.isIso_tensorUnitMap_of_pow_smul_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GLY.** If a flat map of ring sheaves is an
isomorphism modulo an ideal `I`, then extension of scalars is an isomorphism on
every module annihilated by a power of `I`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_tensorUnitMap_of_pow_smul_eq_zero
    {O O' : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}} (f : O ⟶ O')
    (hf : IsFlatMap f)
    {I : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)}
    (i : I ⟶ RingModule O) [Mono i]
    (hquot : ∃ q : cokernel i ⟶
        cokernel (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} O).flip.obj
            (RestrictedRingModule f)).map i),
      IsIso q ∧ cokernel.π i ≫ q = (tensorUnitMap f (RingModule O)).val ≫
        cokernel.π (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} O).flip.obj
            (RestrictedRingModule f)).map i))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O))
    (hF : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (a : Fin n → I.val.obj X) (x : F.val.obj X),
      ((F.val.obj X).smul
        (show (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O).obj.obj X from
          (Finset.univ.prod (fun k ↦ show O.obj.obj X from (i.val.app X) (a k)) :
            O.obj.obj X))).asHom x = 0) :
    IsIso (tensorUnitMap f F).val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleSectionsPresheaf_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
For a sheaf `ℱ` on the small étale site of `S`, the rule
`(f : Y → S) ↦ Γ(Y_étale, f_étale⁻¹ℱ)` is a sheaf on the small pro-étale site of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.etaleSectionsPresheaf_isSheaf (S : Scheme.{u})
    (F : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S)
      ((Scheme.etaleSectionsPresheaf.{u, v} S).obj F)
declarations.comment: the formula is a sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleInverseImageIsoEtaleSectionsSheaf
declarations.doc:
The sheaf defined by the rule is the inverse image `ε⁻¹ℱ` of the morphism of sites
`ε : S_proétale → S_étale`, through the canonical comparison of two left adjoints of `ε_*`.
declarations.statement:
public def Scheme.proetaleInverseImageIsoEtaleSectionsSheaf :
    Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback S.etaleToProetale
        (Type (max (u + 1) v)) S.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) ≅

declarations.comment: the identification with ε⁻¹

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleSectionsFormulaIso
declarations.doc:
At a pro-étale object `f : Y → S`, the sheaf defined by the rule has as its sections the
global sections on the small étale site of `Y` of the inverse image `f_étale⁻¹ℱ`, naturally in
the étale sheaf `ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
public def Scheme.etaleSectionsFormulaIso (S : Scheme.{u}) (Y : S.ProEt) :
    Scheme.etaleSectionsSheaf.{u, v} S ⋙
        (sheafSections (Scheme.ProEt.topology S)
          (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj (Opposite.op Y) ≅
      Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} Y.hom ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ Y.left.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v))
declarations.comment: the formula for sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleInverseImageSectionsIso
declarations.doc:
The sections of `ε⁻¹ℱ` at a pro-étale object `f : Y → S` are the global
sections on the small étale site of `Y` of `f_étale⁻¹ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
public def Scheme.proetaleInverseImageSectionsIso (S : Scheme.{u}) (Y : S.ProEt) :
    Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback S.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) S.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) ⋙
        (sheafSections (Scheme.ProEt.topology S)
          (Type (max (u + 1) v))).obj (Opposite.op Y) ≅
      Stacks.EtaleCohomology.smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} Y.hom ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ Y.left.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v))
declarations.comment: the formula for sections

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0GM0.** The derived tensor product of two perfect objects of `D(A)` is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedTensorProduct
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (ULift.{v} R)))
    (hK : IsPerfect K) (hL : IsPerfect L) :
    IsPerfect ((derivedHomData (R := R)).tensor.obj (K, L))

declarations.name: ncard_irreducibleComponents_le_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X → Y` be a surjective, continuous map of topological spaces. If `X` has finitely
many irreducible components, then `Y` has finitely many irreducible components and their number
is at most that of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ncard_irreducibleComponents_le_of_surjective
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    (f : X → Y) (hf_cont : Continuous f) (hf_surj : Function.Surjective f)
    (hX : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite) :
    (irreducibleComponents Y).Finite ∧
      (irreducibleComponents Y).ncard ≤ (irreducibleComponents X).ncard

declarations.name: TopologicalSpace.exists_isConnected_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GM3.** Let `X` be a connected topological space with finitely many irreducible
components, more than one of them. Then some irreducible component `Z` may be deleted so
that the union of the remaining components is still connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isConnected_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff [ConnectedSpace X]
    (h_fin : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite)
    (h_gt : 1 < (irreducibleComponents X).ncard) :
    ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X,
      IsConnected (⋃₀ (irreducibleComponents X \ {Z}))

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.nonempty_iso_biproduct_singleFunctor_obj_homology_of_forall_ext_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**A bounded complex with no higher Ext between its cohomologies is the sum of them.**
Let `𝒜` be an abelian category and let `K` be an object of `D(𝒜)` whose cohomology vanishes
outside `[a, b]`. If `Ext^p_𝒜(H^i(K), H^j(K)) = 0` for all `p ≥ 2` and all `i > j`, then `K` is
isomorphic to the direct sum `⨁_{a ≤ i ≤ b} H^i(K)[-i]` of its cohomologies. The isomorphism
depends on choices of splittings, so only its existence is asserted. For `a = b` this is
`DerivedCategory.exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_biproduct_singleFunctor_obj_homology_of_forall_ext_eq_zero
    (K : DerivedCategory C) (a b : ℤ) [K.IsGE a] [K.IsLE b]
    (h : ∀ (i j : ℤ) (p : ℕ), j < i → 2 ≤ p →
      ∀ e : Abelian.Ext.{w'} ((homologyFunctor C i).obj K) ((homologyFunctor C j).obj K) p,
        e = 0) :
    Nonempty (K ≅ ⨁ fun i : Finset.Icc a b =>
      (singleFunctor C i.1).obj ((homologyFunctor C i.1).obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isKFlat_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GM5.** In the situation of Stacks 08DM — `E` strictly perfect, so that the
internal Hom complex `H = SheafHom(E, F)` represents `RSheafHom(E, F)` — the complex `H` is
K-flat as soon as `F` is.

For an acyclic `G` the argument is: `F` is K-flat and `G` is acyclic, so `Tot(G ⊗ F)` is
acyclic; the internal Hom complex out of a strictly perfect source into an acyclic complex is
acyclic, so the target of the Stacks 0BYR comparison
`Tot(G ⊗ SheafHom(E, F)) ⟶ SheafHom(E, Tot(G ⊗ F))` is acyclic; that comparison is a
quasi-isomorphism at a strictly perfect source, by the dévissage along the termwise split
stupid filtration of Homology, Section 0118 on the ringed site of the opens of `X`
in `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorHomInterchange_quasiIso_of_isFiniteFreeSummand`; hence
its source is acyclic too, and that source is the total complex K-flatness of `H` asks
about.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKFlat_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
    (E F : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ)
    (hE : {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (E.X i)}.Finite)
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ, RingedSite.IsFiniteFreeSummand (ringedSite Rc) (E.X i))
    (hF : IsKFlat Rc F) :
    IsKFlat Rc (sheafHomComplex Rc E F).obj
declarations.comment: the whole lemma on a ringed space: for E strictly perfect, written out as in Definition 20.46.1 -- hE is 'E^i is zero for all but finitely many i' and hterm is 'E^i is a direct summand of a finite free O_X-module for all i' -- and F K-flat (hF), the complex sheafHomComplex E F is K-flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isKFlat_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GM5 on a ringed site.** In the situation of Stacks 08DM — `E` with finitely many
nonzero terms, each a direct summand of a finite free module, so that the internal Hom complex
`SheafHom(E, F)` represents `RSheafHom(E, F)` — that complex is K-flat as soon as `F` is.

This is what makes the dual `SheafHom(P, O[0])` of a strictly perfect complex `P` usable as the
K-flat tensor factor in the invertibility criterion for the composition morphism of derived
internal Homs, and so is the input the local step of the third assertion of Stacks 08DQ needs on
the slices of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKFlat_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
    (E F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (hE : {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (E.X i)}.Finite)
    (hterm : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteFreeSummand X (E.X i))
    (hF : letI : X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u} := inferInstance
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O F) :
    letI : X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u} := inferInstance
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O (sheafHomComplex X E F).obj
declarations.comment: on a ringed site

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPullback.isIso_derivedPullbackSheafHomMap_of_hasFiniteTorDimensionOverInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Pullback of a derived internal hom along a morphism of finite tor dimension.** Let
`h : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of ringed spaces such that `𝒪_X` has finite tor dimension over
`h⁻¹𝒪_Y`. For a pseudo-coherent `K ∈ D(𝒪_Y)` and a locally bounded below `M ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, the
canonical map `Lh^*R𝓗om(K, M) ⟶ R𝓗om(Lh^*K, Lh^*M)` of Tag 08I3 is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackSheafHomMap_of_hasFiniteTorDimensionOverInverseImage
    (hh : HasFiniteTorDimensionOverInverseImage h)
    (K : DerivedCategory (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y))
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y) K)
    (M : DerivedCategory (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y))
    (hM : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow Y M) :
    IsIso (derivedPullbackSheafHomMap h K M)
declarations.comment: clause (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPullback.isIso_derivedPullbackSheafHomMap_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Pullback of a derived internal hom out of a perfect object.**  For a morphism of ringed
spaces `h : X ⟶ Y`, a perfect `K ∈ D(𝒪_Y)` and an arbitrary `M ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, the canonical map
`Lh^*R𝓗om(K, M) ⟶ R𝓗om(Lh^*K, Lh^*M)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackSheafHomMap_of_isPerfect
    (K : DerivedCategory (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y))
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := Y) K)
    (M : DerivedCategory (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y)) :
    IsIso (derivedPullbackSheafHomMap h K M)
declarations.comment: clause (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomPullback.isIso_derivedPullbackSheafHomMap_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Flat pullback of a derived internal hom out of a pseudo-coherent object.**  For a flat
morphism of ringed spaces `h : X ⟶ Y`, a pseudo-coherent `K ∈ D(𝒪_Y)` and a locally bounded below
`M ∈ D(𝒪_Y)`, the canonical map `Lh^*R𝓗om(K, M) ⟶ R𝓗om(Lh^*K, Lh^*M)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPullbackSheafHomMap_of_isPseudoCoherent (hh : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlat h)
    (K : DerivedCategory (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y))
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y) K)
    (M : DerivedCategory (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules Y))
    (hM : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow Y M) :
    IsIso (derivedPullbackSheafHomMap h K M)
declarations.comment: clause (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomStalk.isIso_stalkSheafHomMap_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GM8, case (1).**  For a ringed space `X`, a point `x ∈ X`, a perfect `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and
an arbitrary `M ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, the canonical map

`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, M)_x ⟶ RHom_{𝒪_{X,x}}(K_x, M_x)`

is an isomorphism.  Here `Y = {x}` is the one-point ringed space with structure sheaf `𝒪_{X,x}`,
and the map is the canonical map of Tag 08I3 along the flat inclusion `Y ⟶ X`, read through the
identification `D(𝒪_Y) ≌ D(𝒪_{X,x})` given by the stalk.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_stalkSheafHomMap_of_isPerfect
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X) K) :
    IsIso (stalkSheafHomMap X x (pointStalkPresentation X x) K M)
declarations.comment: case (1): K perfect, M arbitrary

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedInternalHomStalk.isIso_stalkSheafHomMap_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GM8, case (2).**  For a ringed space `X`, a point `x ∈ X`, a pseudo-coherent
`K ∈ D(𝒪_X)` and a locally bounded below `M ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, the canonical map

`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, M)_x ⟶ RHom_{𝒪_{X,x}}(K_x, M_x)`

is an isomorphism, the map being that of `isIso_stalkSheafHomMap_of_isPerfect`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_stalkSheafHomMap_of_isPseudoCoherent
    (hK : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X) K)
    (hM : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow X M) :
    IsIso (stalkSheafHomMap X x (pointStalkPresentation X x) K M)
declarations.comment: case (2): K pseudo-coherent, M locally bounded below

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.associatedSimplicialObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GM9.** The one-summand simplicial semi-representable object associated
to an augmented simplicial object of the site.
declarations.statement:
def associatedSimplicialObject :
    SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X))
declarations.comment: the associated simplicial object

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isHypercovering_associatedSimplicialObject_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GM9.** The simplicial semi-representable object over `X` associated to
an augmented simplicial object `U ⟶ X` is a hypercovering exactly when the augmentation in degree
zero, the degree-one morphism to `U₀ ×_X U₀`, and every higher matching morphism generate a
covering presieve of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHypercovering_associatedSimplicialObject_iff (J : Pretopology C) :
    IsHypercovering J (associatedSimplicialObject U a) ↔
      (Presieve.singleton (a.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) ∈ J X) ∧
      (Presieve.singleton (oneSimplexToFiberProduct U a) ∈
        J (pullback (a.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0)))
          (a.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))))) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Presieve.singleton (matchingMap U a n) ∈
        J ((((SimplicialObject.cosk n).obj (Over.lift U a)).obj
          (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk (n + 1)))).left)
declarations.comment: the covering characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isHypercovering_cech
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GMA.** The Čech object of a covering morphism is a hypercovering of
its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHypercovering_cech (J : Pretopology C) {U X : C} (f : U ⟶ X)
    (hf : Presieve.singleton f ∈ J.coverings X) :
    let : HasTerminal (Over X) := Over.over_hasTerminal X
    let : HasBinaryProducts (Over X) :=
      Over.ConstructProducts.over_binaryProduct_of_pullback
    let : HasFiniteProducts (Over X) := hasFiniteProducts_of_has_binary_and_terminal
    IsHypercovering J ((FormalCoproduct.incl (Over X)).obj (Over.mk f)).cech
declarations.comment: the hypercovering property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S` has finitely many irreducible components over
every quasi-compact open of every étale scheme chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hN : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_genericPoints_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GMC, representable case.** A flat morphism of schemes carries a
generic point of an irreducible component of its source to a generic point of an irreducible
component of its target. Equivalently, it carries codimension-zero points to
codimension-zero points, which is the second conclusion of Tag 0GMD.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_genericPoints_of_flat {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f]
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ genericPoints X) : f x ∈ genericPoints Y
declarations.comment: representable case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
A flat morphism of algebraic spaces takes points of codimension zero to points of codimension
zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_zero_of_isFlat
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (x : points B S hS X) (hx : localRingDimension B S hS x = 0) :
    localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS X f x) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_and_codimensionZero_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is flat and
locally of finite type, and assume `Y` satisfies the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0BB1. Then
`X` satisfies those conditions too, and for every point `x` of `X` of codimension zero the image
`f x` has codimension zero in `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_and_codimensionZero_of_isFlat_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFlat B S hS f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYfinite : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS Y) :
    HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS X ∧
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS X f x) = 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.pairDerivedSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GME.** The cartesian simplicial system of the derived category attached to a pair
`(K₀, α)`: in degree `n` the derived inverse image of `K₀` along the last vertex of `⦋n⦌`.
declarations.statement: def pairDerivedSystem (P : DerivedCocyclePair S) : SimplicialDerivedSystem S
declarations.comment: the simplicial system

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.pairDerivedSystem_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GME.** The object of the system in degree `n` is `f_{τⁿₙ}⁻¹K₀`, the derived
inverse image of `K₀` along the last vertex of `⦋n⦌`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pairDerivedSystem_obj (P : DerivedCocyclePair S) (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (S.pairDerivedSystem P).obj n =
      (derivedInverseImage S
        (SimplexCategory.const (SimplexCategory.mk 0) n (Fin.last n.len))).obj P.obj

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.pairDerivedSystem_cartesian
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0GME.** The system attached to a pair is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem pairDerivedSystem_cartesian (P : DerivedCocyclePair S) :
    (S.pairDerivedSystem P).Cartesian
declarations.comment: the system is cartesian

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.pairDerivedModuleSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMF.** The simplicial system of the derived category of modules attached to a pair
`(K₀, α)`: in degree `n` the derived pullback of `K₀` along the last vertex of `⦋n⦌`, with the
transition at `φ` given by pulling back to the image of the last vertex and transporting along
the edge to the last vertex. The cocycle condition of Stacks 0D9N is
`pairDerivedModuleTransition_comp`.

def pairDerivedModuleSystem (Pr : S.DerivedModuleCocyclePair O) :
    SimplicialDerivedModuleSystem S O
declarations.comment: the simplicial system

declarations.doc:

pullback of `K₀` along the last vertex of `⦋n⦌`.

theorem pairDerivedModuleSystem_obj (Pr : S.DerivedModuleCocyclePair O) (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (S.pairDerivedModuleSystem O Pr).obj n =
      (S.derivedTransitionPullback O
        (SimplexCategory.const (SimplexCategory.mk 0) n (Fin.last n.len))).obj Pr.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.CoveringGlueing.existsUnique_glueing
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, O_C)` be a ringed site with fibre products and `{U_i ⟶ X}_{i ∈ I}` a covering in
`C`. For `i ∈ I` let `E_i` be an object of `D(O_{U_i})` and for `i, j ∈ I` let
`ρ_{ij} : E_i|_{C/U_{ij}} ⟶ E_j|_{C/U_{ij}}` be an isomorphism in `D(O_{U_{ij}})`, where
`U_{ij} = U_i ×_X U_j`. Assume

1. the `ρ_{ij}` satisfy the cocycle condition on `U_i ×_X U_j ×_X U_k` for all `i, j, k ∈ I`,
2. `SheafExt^p_{O_{U_i}}(E_i, E_i) = 0` for all `p < 0` and `i ∈ I` (stated as the vanishing of
   the negative self-exts of `E_i|_{C/V}` for every object `V` over `U_i`), and
3. there exists a `t ∈ ℤ` such that `H^p(E_i) = 0` for `p < t` and all `i ∈ I`.

Then there exists a pair `(E, ρ_i)`, with `E` an object of `D(O_X)` and `ρ_i : E|_{U_i} ⟶ E_i`
isomorphisms in `D(O_{U_i})` compatible with the `ρ_{ij}`, and it is unique: two such pairs are
isomorphic by exactly one isomorphism compatible with the `ρ_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_glueing {X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}} [hX : HasPullbacks X.C] {X₀ : X.C}
    {ι : Type u} {U : ι → X.C} (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X₀) (E : ∀ i, LocalDerivedCategory.{0} X (U i))
    (ρ : ∀ i j, (derivedOverMap.{0} X (pullback.fst (f i) (f j))).obj (E i) ≅
      (derivedOverMap.{0} X (pullback.snd (f i) (f j))).obj (E j))
    (hf : Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows U f) ∈ X.J X₀)
    (hρ : IsCocycle f ρ)
    (hExt : ∀ (i : ι) {V : X.C} (a : V ⟶ U i) (n : ℤ), n < 0 →
      Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext ((derivedOverMap.{0} X a).obj (E i))
        ((derivedOverMap.{0} X a).obj (E i)) n))
    (hBound : ∃ t : ℤ, ∀ (i : ι) (n : ℤ), n < t →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj (E i))) :
    Nonempty (Glueing f E ρ) ∧
      ∀ A B : Glueing f E ρ, ∃! e : A.obj ≅ B.obj, ∀ i : ι,
        (derivedOverMap.{0} X (f i)).map e.hom ≫ (B.iso i).hom = (A.iso i).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_smooth_atlas_iff_forall_smooth_chart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMI, conditions (1) and (2).** One smooth surjective scheme chart whose
quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components suffices: then every smooth scheme
chart of the algebraic stack has that property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_atlas_iff_forall_smooth_chart (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
        (fun X : Scheme.{u} =>
          ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) 𝒳 ↔
      HasPropertyOnEverySchemeChart B S hS
        (fun X : Scheme.{u} =>
          ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) 𝒳
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forall_smooth_chart_iff_forall_space
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMI, conditions (2) and (3).** Every smooth scheme chart of the algebraic stack has
finitely many irreducible components over each of its quasi-compact opens exactly when every
algebraic space smooth over it satisfies the equivalent conditions of Tag 0BB1.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_smooth_chart_iff_forall_space (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnEverySchemeChart B S hS
        (fun X : Scheme.{u} =>
          ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) 𝒳 ↔
      ∀ (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
        (f : algebraicSpaceStack.{u, w} B S hS F hF ⟶ 𝒳),
        AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f →
          Space.HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.forall_smooth_chart_iff_finite_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMI, conditions (2) and (4).** Every smooth scheme chart of the algebraic stack has
finitely many irreducible components over each of its quasi-compact opens exactly when the space
of points of Tag 04XL of every quasi-compact algebraic stack smooth over it has finitely many
irreducible components.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_smooth_chart_iff_finite_irreducibleComponents
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    HasPropertyOnEverySchemeChart B S hS
        (fun X : Scheme.{u} =>
          ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) 𝒳 ↔
      ∀ (𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (f : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳),
        IsQuasiCompactStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴.val 𝒴.property →
          AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f →
            (@irreducibleComponents (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒴)
              (pointTopology B S hS 𝒴.val)).Finite
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIntegralHom_normalization_and_isTwoFibreProduct_normSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMJ.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S` satisfying the equivalent conditions
of Stacks 0GMI, and let `ν : 𝒳^ν ⟶ 𝒳` be its normalization (Stacks 0GMK). Then `ν` is integral
(Stacks 0CHU), and for every scheme `U` over `S` and every smooth 1-morphism `f : U ⟶ 𝒳`, every
2-fibre product `U ×_𝒳 𝒳^ν` is the normalization of `U`: it is represented by an algebraic space
isomorphic, over `U`, to the normalization `U^ν ⟶ U` of the scheme `U`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normSpace`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normSpaceProj`; Stacks 035N).

The finiteness of irreducible components of the quasi-compact opens of `U` that the
normalization of `U` needs is condition (2) of Stacks 0GMI for the smooth chart `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_normalization_and_isTwoFibreProduct_normSpace :
    AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom B S hS (normalization 𝒳 h𝒳) ∧
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒳)
        (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f)
        (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f (normalization 𝒳 h𝒳)) (_ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P),
        ∃ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
          (eV : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver P.pt.val.val.p
            (presheafOfCategories (V ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
          (e : V ≅ yoneda.obj (Space.normSpace B S hS U
            ((exists_smooth_atlas_iff_forall_smooth_chart B S hS 𝒳).1 h𝒳 U f hf))),
          e.hom ≫ yoneda.map (Space.normSpaceProj B S hS U
              ((exists_smooth_atlas_iff_forall_smooth_chart B S hS 𝒳).1 h𝒳 U f hf)) =
            representingMap B S hS P.pt.val (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U).val V (yoneda.obj U) eV
              (PresheafOfCategories.sliceElementsEquivalenceOver U) P.fst.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_isIntegralHom_and_isTwoFibreProduct_normSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMJ, in the existential form the source states.** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S`
satisfying the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0GMI admits an integral 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks `𝒳^ν ⟶ 𝒳` such that for every scheme `U` and smooth `U ⟶ 𝒳` every 2-fibre product
`U ×_𝒳 𝒳^ν` is the normalization of `U`. The witness is the normalization of Stacks 0GMK.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIntegralHom_and_isTwoFibreProduct_normSpace :
    ∃ (𝒳ν : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (ν : 𝒳ν ⟶ 𝒳),
      AlgebraicStacks.IsIntegralHom B S hS ν ∧
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒳)
        (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f)
        (P : Bicategory.TwoCommSq f ν) (_ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct P),
        ∃ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V)
          (eV : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver P.pt.val.val.p
            (presheafOfCategories (V ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
          (e : V ≅ yoneda.obj (Space.normSpace B S hS U
            ((exists_smooth_atlas_iff_forall_smooth_chart B S hS 𝒳).1 h𝒳 U f hf))),
          e.hom ≫ yoneda.map (Space.normSpaceProj B S hS U
              ((exists_smooth_atlas_iff_forall_smooth_chart B S hS 𝒳).1 h𝒳 U f hf)) =
            representingMap B S hS P.pt.val (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U).val V (yoneda.obj U) eV
              (PresheafOfCategories.sliceElementsEquivalenceOver U) P.fst.hom
declarations.comment: the existential form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_normalizationChartSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMJ, the fibre-product assertion at the presenting chart.**  For a groupoid in
algebraic spaces `(U, R, s, t, c)` presenting `𝒳 = [U/R]` and a normalized groupoid `N` for it,
the square formed by the normalization 1-morphism `ν : [U^ν/R^ν] ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 046Q and the
canonical projection `𝒮_U ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 044R is a 2-fibre product with apex `𝒮_{U^ν}`; that
is, `𝒳^ν ×_𝒳 U = U^ν`.

This is the assertion of Stacks 0GMJ that the source obtains from `R^ν = R ×_{s, U} U^ν` by
citing Stacks 04ZN, and the proof here is that citation: the cartesian source square is the field
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.NormalizationGroupoid.isPullback_source` of the normalized groupoid, and
Stacks 04ZN is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isTwoFibreProduct_functorialitySquare_of_isPullback`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isTwoFibreProduct_normalizationChartSquare
    (N : NormalizationGroupoid C S hS G) :
    Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct (functorialitySquare N.hom)
declarations.comment: the fibre product with a presenting chart is the normalization of the chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIntegralHom_quotientStackMapHom_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMJ, the 1-morphism `𝒳^ν ⟶ 𝒳` and its integrality.** Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a
groupoid in algebraic spaces whose quotient stack is `𝒳 = [U/R]`, and let `N` be a normalized
groupoid for it. Then the 1-morphism `ν : [U^ν/R^ν] ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 046Q induced by the
morphism of groupoids `(U^ν, R^ν) ⟶ (U, R)` is integral in the sense of Stacks 04XB.

The source's argument is exactly this one: `U^ν ⟶ U` is integral, it is the base change of `ν`
along the presenting chart, and integrality descends. The base-change identification is
Stacks 04ZN and is carried; integrality of `U^ν ⟶ U` is Stacks 0BB4, part (2), and is proved in
this library. See the partial-coverage section of the module documentation for every hypothesis
and the result it stands for.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_quotientStackMapHom_normalization
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (N : NormalizationGroupoid C S hS G)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS (quotientStackMapHom N.hom).hom)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq (quotientStackProjectionHom G) (quotientStackMapHom N.hom))
    (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hQfst : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS Q.fst.hom)
    {𝒜 𝒞 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver C S hS)}
    (a : 𝒜 ⟶ 𝒞) (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS a.hom)
    (p : Q.pt.val ⥤ᵇ 𝒜.val) (q : (liftedObjectSpace G).val ⥤ᵇ 𝒞.val)
    [Functor.IsEquivalence p.toFunctor] [Functor.IsEquivalence q.toFunctor]
    (α : BasedFunctor.comp p a.hom ≅ BasedFunctor.comp Q.fst.hom q)
    (eF : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒜.val.p (presheafOfCategories (N.data.space ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eG₀ : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒞.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G.objects.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (hrep : representingMap C S hS 𝒜 𝒞 N.data.space G.objects.obj eF eG₀ a = N.data.hom) :
    IsIntegralHom C S hS (quotientStackMapHom N.hom) hf
declarations.comment: integrality of ν; the normalized groupoid, Stacks 04ZP and the 04ZN form of the base change are hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isIntegralHom_quotientStackMapHom_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMJ in the existential form the source states it.** For a groupoid in algebraic
spaces with a normalized groupoid, there is a category fibred in groupoids `𝒳^ν` over the big
fppf site together with an integral 1-morphism `𝒳^ν ⟶ [U/R]`.

The witnesses are the quotient stack `[U^ν/R^ν]` of Stacks 044Q and the 1-morphism of
Stacks 046Q, so the existential is inhabited by the source's own construction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIntegralHom_quotientStackMapHom_normalization
    {G : GroupoidInAlgebraicSpaces C S hS B} (N : NormalizationGroupoid C S hS G)
    (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS (quotientStackMapHom N.hom).hom)
    (Q : Bicategory.TwoCommSq (quotientStackProjectionHom G) (quotientStackMapHom N.hom))
    (hQ : Bicategory.IsTwoFibreProduct Q)
    (hQfst : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS Q.fst.hom)
    {𝒜 𝒞 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver C S hS)}
    (a : 𝒜 ⟶ 𝒞) (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS a.hom)
    (p : Q.pt.val ⥤ᵇ 𝒜.val) (q : (liftedObjectSpace G).val ⥤ᵇ 𝒞.val)
    [Functor.IsEquivalence p.toFunctor] [Functor.IsEquivalence q.toFunctor]
    (α : BasedFunctor.comp p a.hom ≅ BasedFunctor.comp Q.fst.hom q)
    (eF : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒜.val.p (presheafOfCategories (N.data.space ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (eG₀ : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
      𝒞.val.p (presheafOfCategories (G.objects.obj ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (hrep : representingMap C S hS 𝒜 𝒞 N.data.space G.objects.obj eF eG₀ a = N.data.hom) :
    ∃ (𝒳ν : CatFiberedInGroupoids (BigFppfOver C S hS))
      (ν : 𝒳ν ⟶ quotientStackCFG C S hS G)
      (hν : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces C S hS ν.hom),
      IsIntegralHom.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} C S hS ν hν
declarations.comment: the existence assertion, witnessed by [U^ν/R^ν] and the 1-morphism of Stacks 046Q

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMK, the normalization of an algebraic stack.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack
satisfying the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0GMI. Its *normalization* is the morphism
`ν : 𝒳^ν ⟶ 𝒳` constructed in the proof of Stacks 0GMJ: for a presentation `𝒳 ≃ [U/R]`
(Stacks 04T3), `𝒳^ν = [U^ν/R^ν]` is the quotient stack of the normalized groupoid, and `ν` is the
1-morphism `[U^ν/R^ν] ⟶ [U/R]` of Stacks 046Q induced by the morphism of groupoids
`(U^ν, R^ν) ⟶ (U, R)`, followed by the presentation.

Every ingredient is constructed from `𝒳` and the hypothesis of Stacks 0GMI: the normalization
`U^ν` (Stacks 07U4), the cartesian square `R^ν = U^ν ×_{U, s} R`, the groupoid structure and its
smoothness are those of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.normalizationGroupoid`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def normalization (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun X : Scheme.{u} =>
        ∀ V : X.Opens, IsCompact (V : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) 𝒳) :
    normalizationStack 𝒳 h𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMK, the normalization of an algebraic stack.** For a groupoid in algebraic spaces
`(U, R, s, t, c)` presenting `ð³ = [U/R]`, and a normalized groupoid `N` for it, the
*normalization* of `𝒳` is the 1-morphism `ν : 𝒳^ν ⟶ 𝒳` of Stacks 046Q induced by the
morphism
of groupoids `(U^Î½, R^Î½) â¶ (U, R)`, with `ð³^Î½ = [U^Î½/R^Î½]` the quotient stack
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.normalizationStack` of the normalized groupoid.

This is the morphism constructed in Stacks 0GMJ, named: the body is the construction
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackMapHom` of the source's proof, so nothing is chosen out of
the existential of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isIntegralHom_quotientStackMapHom_normalization`. Its
integrality is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIntegralHom_quotientStackMapHom_normalization`, which
applies to it unchanged.

The hypothesis of Stacks 0GMI on `ð³` is not a separate assumption, for the reason given in the
coverage notes of this module's documentation: it is carried inside `N`, whose
normalization data of the object space contains condition (1) of Stacks 0GMI for the presenting
chart through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.finite_irreducibleComponents_of_chart`. The
equivalences of Stacks 0GMI are stated for `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks`, and
exhibiting a quotient stack there is Stacks 04TK, which this library does not have, so no 0GMI
condition can be stated at this presentation.
declarations.comment: the normalization ν : 𝒳^ν ⟶ 𝒳 at a presenting smooth groupoid, with the normalized groupoid as data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAmpleFamily_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GML.** A quasi-compact regular scheme whose diagonal is affine has an
ample family of invertible modules.

The family is `{𝒪_X(D x)}` indexed by the points of `X`, where `D x` is the effective Cartier
divisor whose support is the complement of a dense affine open around `x`, supplied by Tag 0EGJ;
the required section of `𝒪_X(D x)` is the canonical section `1_{D x}`, whose nonvanishing locus
is exactly that affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmpleFamily_of_isRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X))] (hX : IsRegular X) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (L : I → X.Modules), X.IsAmpleFamily L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsAmpleFamily.hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GMM].** A scheme carrying an ample family of invertible modules has the
resolution property.

The ample family supplies a finite covering of `X` by affine opens `U k = X_{s k}`, the
nonvanishing loci of global sections `s k` of positive tensor powers `M k` of members of the
family.  The image of evaluation at `s k`, a morphism `M k ^∨ ⟶ 𝒪_X` out of the invertible,
hence finite locally free, dual, is a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals whose vanishing
locus is the complement of `U k`, and it is a quotient of `M k ^∨`.  The substantial direction
of [Stacks, Tag 0F89] then gives the resolution property.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.IsAmpleFamily.hasResolutionProperty {ι : Type v} {X : Scheme.{u}}
    {L : ι → X.Modules} (hL : X.IsAmpleFamily L) : HasResolutionProperty X

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isQuasiCompact_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc: Quasi-compactness of a sheaf of sets passes along a surjection `φ : F ⟶ G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_of_isLocallySurjective {F G : Sheaf J (Type max u v)} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : IsLocallySurjective φ) (hF : IsQuasiCompact F) :
    IsQuasiCompact G

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isQuasiCompact_sheafifiedYoneda_of_isLocallySurjective
declarations.doc:
If `f : U ⟶ V` sheafifies to a surjection `h_U^# ⟶ h_V^#` of sheafified representables and
`h_U^#` is quasi-compact, then so is `h_V^#`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_sheafifiedYoneda_of_isLocallySurjective {U V : C} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (hf : IsLocallySurjective ((sheafifiedYoneda J).map f))
    (hU : IsQuasiCompact ((sheafifiedYoneda J).obj U)) :
    IsQuasiCompact ((sheafifiedYoneda J).obj V)

declarations.name: Sheaf.quasiCompact_coproduct_fin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GMQ, Lemma 7.17.6.**

Let `C` be a site and let `n ≥ 1`. If `F : Fin n → Sh(C)` is a finite family of
quasi-compact sheaves (quasi-compact objects of the topos `Sh(C)` in the sense of
`Sheaf.QuasiCompact`), then their coproduct `∐ F` in `Sh(C)` is quasi-compact.

The family is indexed by `Fin n` with `n ≥ 1`, the `0`-indexed form of the family
`F_1, …, F_n` of the informal statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem Sheaf.quasiCompact_coproduct_fin
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (F : Fin n → Sheaf J (Type max u v))
    [HasCoproduct F]
    (hF : ∀ i, Sheaf.QuasiCompact (F i)) :
    Sheaf.QuasiCompact (∐ F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.injective_and_bijective_colimit_post_globalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMR.** Let `C` be a site and `F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Type max u v)` a filtered diagram
of sheaves of sets. For the canonical map
`Ψ = colimit.post F (Γ J _) : colim_i Γ(C, F i) ⟶ Γ(C, colim_i F i)`:

1. if every transition map `F.map f` is a monomorphism, then `Ψ` is injective;
2. if the topos `Sh(C)` is quasi-compact (Stacks 0D07), then `Ψ` is injective;
3. if the topos `Sh(C)` is quasi-compact and every transition map is a monomorphism, then `Ψ`
   is bijective;
4. if there is a set `S` of sheaves such that every sheaf `G` surjecting onto the final sheaf
   admits a map `K ⟶ G` from some `K ∈ S` which itself surjects onto the final sheaf, and such
   that `K ⨯ K` is quasi-compact for every `K ∈ S`, then `Ψ` is bijective.

The four conjuncts are the four parts of the source, in order.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_and_bijective_colimit_post_globalSections {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {I : Type w₁} [Category.{w₂} I] [IsFiltered I]
    [HasColimitsOfShape I (Type max u v)] (F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Type max u v)) :
    ((∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), Mono (F.map f)) →
        Function.Injective (colimit.post F (Γ J (Type max u v)))) ∧
      (J.IsQuasiCompactTopos → Function.Injective (colimit.post F (Γ J (Type max u v)))) ∧
      (J.IsQuasiCompactTopos →
        (∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), Mono (F.map f)) →
        Function.Bijective (colimit.post F (Γ J (Type max u v)))) ∧
      ((∃ S : Set (Sheaf J (Type max u v)),
          (∀ G : Sheaf J (Type max u v),
              IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from G) →
                ∃ K ∈ S, Nonempty (K ⟶ G) ∧ IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from K)) ∧
            ∀ K ∈ S, IsQuasiCompact (K ⨯ K)) →
        Function.Bijective (colimit.post F (Γ J (Type max u v))))
declarations.comment: Global sections of a filtered colimit of sheaves of sets.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_prodLift_absolute
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2)(c) of Stacks 0GMS for the fppf site of a quasi-separated algebraic stack**, in
the shape
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf` consumes as its
hypothesis `h_product`: for two objects `x`, `x'` of the site lying over affine schemes there is a
finite family of such objects, with a morphism to `x` and a morphism to `x'` from each, whose
sheafified representables jointly cover `h_x^# ⨯ h_{x'}^#`.

The family has one member, as in the source. It is the object the quadruple of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_quadruple_dominating` classifies, with the two morphisms that
quadruple classifies, and the covering assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.isLocallySurjective_prodLift_fppfTopology_of_exists_quadruple_dominating_base`.
Quasi-compactness of the 2-fibre product, which is what produces the quadruple, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.isQuasiCompactStack_twoFibreProductAlgebraicStack_objectMorphism_absolute`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_prodLift_absolute
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (h𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    ∀ U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val, ∀ U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
            Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
              prod.lift ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)).map (p i))
                ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)).map (q i)))
declarations.comment: condition (2)(c) for the fppf site of a quasi-separated algebraic stack, with the collection B of Stacks 0GQV: the objects of the site lying over affine schemes; the family produced has one member, as in the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_prodLift_etale_absolute
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2)(c) of Stacks 0GMS for the étale site of a quasi-separated algebraic stack**,
in the shape
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_etale` consumes as its
hypothesis `h_product`: for two objects `x`, `x'` of the étale site lying over affine schemes
there is a finite family of such objects, with a morphism to `x` and a morphism to `x'` from each,
whose sheafified representables jointly cover `h_x^# ⨯ h_{x'}^#`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_prodLift_associatedTopology_absolute`
at the big étale
topology, its fibre-lifting hypothesis discharged by **Stacks 06XH** part (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etaleCovering_fibre_lift`, which reads the fibre lifts of a
surjective smooth 1-morphism off an *étale* covering of the base. The affine smooth presentation
of **Stacks 04YC** is smooth and surjective, which is exactly what that tag asks for, so the
étale case needs nothing of the presentation beyond what the fppf case needs — in particular no
affine étale presentation of a quasi-compact algebraic stack. The family has one member, as in the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_prodLift_etale_absolute
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (h𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    ∀ U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val, ∀ U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
            Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
              prod.lift
                ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                  (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (p i))
                ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                  (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (q i)))

there is a finite family of such objects, with a morphism to `x` and a morphism to `x'` from each,
