declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.exists_set_isLocallySurjective_and_isQuasiCompact_prod_self
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMS, case (2).** Let `C` be a site and `B ⊆ Ob(C)` a set of objects such that

* (a) there are finitely many `U₁, …, U_m ∈ B` with `∐_j h_{U_j}^# ⟶ *` surjective,
* (b) every covering of a member of `B` is refined by a finite covering by members of `B`,
* (c) for `U, U' ∈ B` there are finitely many `V_1, …, V_m ∈ B` with morphisms `V_k ⟶ U` and
  `V_k ⟶ U'` for which `∐_k h_{V_k}^# ⟶ h_U^# ⨯ h_{U'}^#` is surjective.

Then the hypotheses of part (4) of Stacks 0GMR are satisfied, with
`S = CategoryTheory.Sheaf.coveringSetOfObjects J B` the set of finite coproducts of the sheafified
representables of members of `B`.

The two clauses are `exists_mem_coveringSetOfObjects` and
`isQuasiCompact_prod_self_of_mem_coveringSetOfObjects`; the latter consumes (b) and (c) through
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isQuasiCompactObject_of_exists_finite_refinement` and
`isQuasiCompact_prod_sheafifiedYoneda_of_isLocallySurjective`. The existential over `S` is the
shape in which Stacks 0GMR (4) states its hypothesis, and `S` is pinned to the set the source
displays rather than merely asserted to exist.

Cases (1) and (3) of the remark are not proved here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_set_isLocallySurjective_and_isQuasiCompact_prod_self {B : Set C}
    (ha : ∃ (ι : Type max u v) (_ : Finite ι) (U : ι → C), (∀ i, U i ∈ B) ∧
      IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from (∐ fun i => (sheafifiedYoneda J).obj (U i))))
    (hb : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ 𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{max u v} U, 𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J U →
      ∃ (𝒱 : PreZeroHypercover.{max u v} U) (_ : 𝒱.Hom 𝒰),
        𝒱.sieve₀ ∈ J U ∧ Finite 𝒱.I₀ ∧ ∀ i, 𝒱.X i ∈ B)
    (hc : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ U' ∈ B, ∃ (ι : Type max u v) (_ : Finite ι) (V : ι → C)
      (a : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (b : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'), (∀ i, V i ∈ B) ∧
        IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc fun i =>
          prod.lift ((sheafifiedYoneda J).map (a i)) ((sheafifiedYoneda J).map (b i)))) :
    ∃ S : Set (Sheaf J (Type max u v)),
      (∀ G : Sheaf J (Type max u v), IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from G) →
          ∃ K ∈ S, Nonempty (K ⟶ G) ∧ IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from K)) ∧
        ∀ K ∈ S, IsQuasiCompact (K ⨯ K)
declarations.comment: case (2)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.derivedExtensionScalarsAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMT.** Derived extension of scalars along a homomorphism of commutative rings is
left adjoint to derived restriction of scalars. The extension functor may be any model equipped
with the total-left-derived universal property, since uniqueness of left derived functors
identifies it with the model computed by K-flat resolutions.
declarations.statement:
public def derivedExtensionScalarsAdjunction
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] (f : R →+* A)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wR} (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} A)] :
    letI : (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uA, max uR uA uM} f).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max uR uM, uR, uA} f).isLeftAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uR uA uM, uR, uA} f).IsRightAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max uR uM, uR, uA} f).isRightAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uR uA uM, uR, uA} f).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj.{max uR uM, uR, uA} f).isLeftAdjoint
    ∀ (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R))
      (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} A)))
    (comparison : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uA, max uR uA uM} f).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    [F.IsLeftDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))],
    F ⊣ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uR uA uM, uR, uA} f).mapDerivedCategory

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.pullbackTensorFunctor_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GMU.** If `F` is an `𝒪_X`-module flat over `Y`, then the functor
`G ↦ f^*G ⊗_{𝒪_X} F` is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackTensorFunctor_exact (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver f F) :
    exactFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Y))
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) (pullbackTensorFunctor f F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isColimit_sheafHomCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GMV.** Let `F` be an `O_X`-module of finite presentation on a ringed
space and let `G = colim_λ G_λ` be a filtered colimit of `O_X`-modules. Then the canonical
cocone of internal homs over `SheafHom_{O_X}(F, G)`, whose legs are the postcomposition maps
induced by the colimit inclusions, is a colimit cocone; that is, the canonical map
`colim_λ SheafHom_{O_X}(F, G_λ) ⟶ SheafHom_{O_X}(F, G)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimit_sheafHomCocone [F.IsFinitePresentation] [IsFiltered K]
    (c : Cocone D) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (H : ∀ j, SheafHom Rc F (D.obj j)) (Hc : SheafHom Rc F c.pt) :
    IsColimit (sheafHomCocone F D c H Hc)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_desc_sheafHomCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GMV**, in comparison-map form: for `F` of finite presentation and a
filtered diagram, the canonical map from any colimit of the internal homs
`SheafHom_{O_X}(F, G_λ)` to `SheafHom_{O_X}(F, colim_λ G_λ)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_desc_sheafHomCocone [F.IsFinitePresentation] [IsFiltered K]
    (c : Cocone D) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (H : ∀ j, SheafHom Rc F (D.obj j)) (Hc : SheafHom Rc F c.pt)
    (t : Cocone (sheafHomDiagram F D H)) (ht : IsColimit t) :
    IsIso (ht.desc (sheafHomCocone F D c H Hc))

declarations.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationTensorIso
declarations.doc:
Sheafification commutes with the tensor product of presheaves of modules: there is an
isomorphism `F⁺ ⊗_{O⁺} G⁺ ≅ (F ⊗_{p,O} G)⁺`, natural in both presheaves of modules, where the
left-hand tensor product is the sheafification of the objectwise tensor product of the two sheaves
of sections.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafificationTensorIso :
    Functor.prod (moduleSheafification.{v, u, w, z} J a)
          (moduleSheafification.{v, u, w, z₁} J a) ⋙
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u, v, w, z, z₁} Osharp)) ≅
      Functor.uncurry.obj (tensorBifunctor.{v, u, w, z, z₁} O) ⋙
        moduleSheafification.{v, u, w, max z z₁} J a

declarations.name: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationTensorIso_hom_unit_tmul
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `sheafificationTensorIso` sends the image, under the unit exhibiting the tensor
product sheaf as a sheafification, of a pure tensor of two sheafification-unit images to the
sheafification-unit image of the original pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma sheafificationTensorIso_hom_unit_tmul (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : F.obj U) (y : G.obj U) :
    Hom.app ((sheafificationTensorIso.{v, u, w, z, z₁} J a).hom.app (F, G)).val U
        (Hom.app ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
            (R := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Osharp)
            (𝟙 (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Osharp).obj)).unit.app
            (tensorObj (((moduleSheafification.{v, u, w, z} J a).obj F)).val
              (((moduleSheafification.{v, u, w, z₁} J a).obj G)).val)) U
          (Hom.app (moduleSheafificationUnit.{v, u, w, z} J a F) U x ⊗ₜ
            Hom.app (moduleSheafificationUnit.{v, u, w, z₁} J a G) U y)) =
      Hom.app (moduleSheafificationUnit.{v, u, w, max z z₁} J a (tensorObj F G)) U (x ⊗ₜ y)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.pullbackInternalHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMX.** The canonical map `f^* Hom_{O_D}(F, G) ⟶ Hom_{O_C}(f^*F, f^*G)` attached
to a morphism of ringed sites: the transpose, under the correspondence of Stacks 03EO, of the
pullback of the evaluation morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackInternalHomMap :
    (ringedSitePullback f).obj ((internalHomSecondFunctor Y.J Y.O F).obj G) ⟶
      (internalHomSecondFunctor X.J X.O ((ringedSitePullback f).obj F)).obj
        ((ringedSitePullback f).obj G)
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.adjointPullbackInternalHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMX.** The map `Hom_{O_D}(F, G) ⟶ f_* Hom_{O_C}(f^*F, f^*G)` displayed in the
source: the adjoint of `pullbackInternalHomMap` under the adjunction `f^* ⊣ f_*` of
Stacks 03D7.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointPullbackInternalHomMap :
    (internalHomSecondFunctor Y.J Y.O F).obj G ⟶
      (ringedSitePushforward f).obj
        ((internalHomSecondFunctor X.J X.O ((ringedSitePullback f).obj F)).obj
          ((ringedSitePullback f).obj G))
declarations.comment: the adjoint map

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.tensorEvaluation_pullbackInternalHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMX.** The canonical map is compatible with evaluation: tensoring it with `f^*F`
and then evaluating `Hom_{O_C}(f^*F, f^*G)` gives the pulled-back evaluation of
`Hom_{O_D}(F, G)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorEvaluation_pullbackInternalHomMap :
    tensorEvaluation X.O ((ringedSitePullback f).obj F) ((ringedSitePullback f).obj G)
        (pullbackInternalHomMap f F G) =
      pullbackEvaluation f F G
declarations.comment: compatibility of the canonical map with evaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.toposPullbackInternalHomMap_compOf
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map is compatible with composition, with the composite supplied as
data.** Let `φ : X ⟶ Y` and `ψ : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of ringed topoi between the
topoi of three ringed sites, let `χ : X ⟶ Z` play the role of their composite and let `τ` be a
comparison of the geometric direct images carrying the composite structure map to the structure
map of `χ`. Then the canonical map

`χ^* Hom_{O_Z}(F, G) ⟶ Hom_{O_X}(χ^*F, χ^*G)`

is the canonical map of `ψ` pulled back along `φ`, followed by the canonical map of `φ`, read
through the comparison of pullbacks attached to `(χ, τ)` at `Hom_{O_Z}(F, G)`, at the source of
the internal Hom sheaf — through `internalHomPre`, the comparison in the first variable — and at
its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem toposPullbackInternalHomMap_compOf
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf Z.O)) :
    toposPullbackInternalHomMap χ F G =
      toposPullbackCompComparisonOf φ ψ χ τ hτ ((internalHomSecondFunctor Z.J Z.O F).obj G) ≫
        (toposPullback φ).map (toposPullbackInternalHomMap ψ F G) ≫
          toposPullbackInternalHomMap φ ((toposPullback ψ).obj F) ((toposPullback ψ).obj G) ≫
            (internalHomPre X.O (toposPullbackCompComparisonOf φ ψ χ τ hτ F)).app
                ((toposPullback φ).obj ((toposPullback ψ).obj G)) ≫
              (internalHomSecondFunctor X.J X.O ((toposPullback χ).obj F)).map
                (toposPullbackCompComparisonInvOf φ ψ χ τ hτ G)
declarations.comment:
compatibility of the canonical map with composition, for a composite given as
data

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.toposPullbackInternalHomMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks 0GMX is compatible with composition.** For morphisms of ringed
topoi `φ : X ⟶ Y` and `ψ : Y ⟶ Z` between the topoi of three ringed sites and sheaves of
`O_Z`-modules `F`, `G`, the canonical map

`(ψ ∘ φ)^* Hom_{O_Z}(F, G) ⟶ Hom_{O_X}((ψ ∘ φ)^*F, (ψ ∘ φ)^*G)`

of the composite is the canonical map of `ψ` pulled back along `φ`, followed by the canonical
map of `φ`, read through the comparison of pullbacks along a composite at `Hom_{O_Z}(F, G)`, at
the source of the internal Hom sheaf — through `internalHomPre`, the comparison in the first
variable — and at its target.

This is the law the localization square of Stacks 04J0 reduces to, and it is proved by the route
the source's Remark 18.27.3 indicates: `tensorEvaluation_injective` turns it into an identity
between two morphisms out of `(ψ ∘ φ)^*Hom_{O_Z}(F, G) ⊗_{O_X} (ψ ∘ φ)^*F`, where
`tensorEvaluation_comp` and `tensorEvaluation_comp_internalHomPre_comp_map` read the composite
route off and `toposPullbackEvaluationExchange` assembles the four inputs — the exchange of
tensorings `sheafTensor_exchange_three`, the pulled-back tensor--evaluation composite
`toposPullback_tensorEvaluation`, the naturality
`toposPullbackCompComparisonInv_naturality_pullbackTensorIso` transported along the two readings
of the inner pulled-back evaluation, and the composition law of Stacks 03EL
`pullbackTensorIso_inv_app_toposCompHom` with the comparison of pullbacks cancelled off it by
`cancelWhisker`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toposPullbackInternalHomMap_comp
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf Z.O)) :
    toposPullbackInternalHomMap (toposCompHom φ ψ) F G =
      toposPullbackCompComparison φ ψ ((internalHomSecondFunctor Z.J Z.O F).obj G) ≫
        (toposPullback φ).map (toposPullbackInternalHomMap ψ F G) ≫
          toposPullbackInternalHomMap φ ((toposPullback ψ).obj F) ((toposPullback ψ).obj G) ≫
            (internalHomPre X.O (toposPullbackCompComparison φ ψ F)).app
                ((toposPullback φ).obj ((toposPullback ψ).obj G)) ≫
              (internalHomSecondFunctor X.J X.O ((toposPullback (toposCompHom φ ψ)).obj F)).map
                (toposPullbackCompComparisonInv φ ψ G)
declarations.comment: compatibility of the canonical map with composition

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.toposPullbackInternalHomMap_naturality
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks 0GMX is functorial in its first variable.** For a morphism
`c : F' ⟶ F` of sheaves of `O_Y`-modules the square built from the canonical maps at `F` and at
`F'` and from the comparison `internalHomPre` in the first variable on the two sites commutes.

This is the "functoriality of Remark 18.27.3" that the proof of Stacks 0GN2 cites. By
`tensorEvaluation_injective` it is an identity between two morphisms out of a tensor product,
and there it is the naturality of the comparison of Stacks 03EL in its second variable: both
sides become the pulled-back evaluation of `Hom_{O_Y}(F, G)` precomposed with `c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toposPullbackInternalHomMap_naturality
    {F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := Y.J)) Y.O)}
    (c : F' ⟶ F) :
    toposPullbackInternalHomMap φ F G ≫
        (internalHomPre X.O ((toposPullback φ).map c)).app ((toposPullback φ).obj G) =
      (toposPullback φ).map ((internalHomPre Y.O c).app G) ≫
        toposPullbackInternalHomMap φ F' G
declarations.comment: functoriality of the canonical map in the first variable

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.pullbackInternalHomNatural
declarations.doc:
**The canonical maps of Stacks 0GMX are functorial in the first variable.** For a morphism
`c : F' ⟶ F` of sheaves of `O_D`-modules the square built from the canonical maps at `F` and at
`F'` and from the comparison `internalHomPre` on the two sites commutes.

This is the "functoriality of Remark 18.27.3" that the proof of Stacks 0GN2 cites. It is
`toposPullbackInternalHomMap_naturality` at the morphism of ringed topoi of `f`, the two
readings of the canonical map agreeing by `toposPullbackInternalHomMap_ringedToposHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackInternalHomNatural
    {F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := Y.J)) Y.O)}
    (c : F' ⟶ F) :
    pullbackInternalHomMap f F G ≫
        (internalHomPre X.O ((ringedSitePullback f).map c)).app
          ((ringedSitePullback f).obj G) =
      (ringedSitePullback f).map ((internalHomPre Y.O c).app G) ≫
        pullbackInternalHomMap f F' G
declarations.comment: first-variable functoriality, for a morphism of ringed sites

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.ringedSite_sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft_mono_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMY, part (1).** Precomposition along an epimorphism is a monomorphism of
internal Hom sheaves, which is the initial zero of the target sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringedSite_sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft_mono_of_epi
    {F₁ F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)}
    (g : F₁ ⟶ F) [Epi g] :
    Mono (sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft X.J X.O (G := G) g)
declarations.comment: exact_first_argument

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.ringedSite_sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft_exact_of_exact_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GMY, part (1).** A right-exact sequence of sheaves of modules becomes exact at
the middle term after applying internal Hom in the first argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem ringedSite_sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft_exact_of_exact_epi
    (S : ShortComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hS : S.Exact) [Epi S.g] :
    ∃ h : sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft X.J X.O (G := G) S.g ≫
        sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft X.J X.O (G := G) S.f = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft X.J X.O (G := G) S.g)
        (sheafInternalHomObjMapLeft X.J X.O (G := G) S.f) h).Exact
declarations.comment: exact_first_argument

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.internalHomSecondFunctor_preservesFilteredColimits
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site, internal Hom out of a module of finite presentation commutes with filtered
colimits: the canonical map `colim_λ Hom_O(F, G_λ) ⟶ Hom_O(F, colim_λ G_λ)` is an isomorphism
for every filtered diagram `λ ↦ G_λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomSecondFunctor_preservesFilteredColimits
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := X.J)) X.O))
    [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (K : Type u) [Category.{u} K] [IsFiltered K] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape K (internalHomSecondFunctor.{u, u, u, u} X.J X.O F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.coyoneda_preservesColimitsOfShape_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN0.** On a ringed site satisfying the hypothesis of Stacks 0GMR part (4), Hom out
of a module `F` of finite presentation commutes with filtered colimits:

`colim_λ Hom_O(F, G_λ) = Hom_O(F, colim_λ G_λ)`.

The site hypothesis is the one the source attaches to the statement; it is needed already for
`F = O`, where the assertion is that global sections commute with the colimit. Stacks 0GMS
records sufficient conditions for it, one of which is applied in
`coyoneda_preservesColimitsOfShape_of_coveringSet` below.
declarations.statement:
theorem coyoneda_preservesColimitsOfShape_of_isFinitePresentation
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) [F.IsFinitePresentation]
    (K : Type u) [Category.{u} K] [IsFiltered K]
    (hX : ∃ S : Set (Sheaf X.J (Type u)),
      (∀ H : Sheaf X.J (Type u), Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from H) →
          ∃ L ∈ S, Nonempty (L ⟶ H) ∧ Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from L)) ∧
        ∀ L ∈ S, Sheaf.IsQuasiCompact (L ⨯ L)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape K (coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op F))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.FlatSheafification.isFlat_sheafification_of_locally_objectwise_flat
declarations.doc:
If a presheaf of modules is objectwise flat after passing to a covering of every object,
then its associated sheaf is flat.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFlat_sheafification_of_locally_objectwise_flat
    {O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{w}} {Osharp : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w}}
    (a : O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w} ⟶
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Osharp).obj)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J a]
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J a]
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{z} (O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w}))
    (hF : ∀ U : C,
      ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U),
        Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U ∧
          ∀ i, Module.Flat (O.obj (Opposite.op (X i))) (F.obj (Opposite.op (X i)))) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat
      ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification
        (R := Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Osharp)
        a).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.doc:
Flat pullback commutes with the canonical internal-Hom map for a module which is locally
finitely presented. This statement uses a single universe for the site and coefficients.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite
    [F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite]
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMapULift
      f.ringedToposHom.fSharpInverseImage) : IsIso (pullbackInternalHomMap f F G)
declarations.comment:
the isomorphism under the source's own hypotheses: `F` of finite presentation in
the local sense of Tag 03DL and `f` flat; stated for a site and coefficients in one universe

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN2, for a globally finitely presented `F`.** Let
`f : (C, O_C) ⟶ (D, O_D)` be a flat morphism of ringed sites and let `F`, `G` be sheaves of
`O_D`-modules with `F` presented, over the whole site `D`, as the cokernel of a morphism between
finite coproducts of copies of `O_D`. Then the canonical map

`f^* Hom_{O_D}(F, G) ⟶ Hom_{O_C}(f^*F, f^*G)`

of Stacks 0GMX is an isomorphism.

Flatness is the hypothesis `hf`, that `O_C` is flat as an `f⁻¹O_D`-module, which is the
definition of a flat morphism of Tag 04JB. It enters through the left exactness of `f^*`
(Tag 04JC, `preservesFiniteLimits_ringedSitePullback_of_isFlat`), because that is what makes
`F ↦ f^* Hom_{O_D}(F, G)` carry the finite colimit presenting `F` to a limit of internal Hom
sheaves; the other composite needs only that `f^*` is a left adjoint. The continuity of internal
Hom in its first variable is Tag 03EN, `preservesFiniteColimits_internalHomFirstMate`, and the
remaining two inputs the source's proof names are `pullbackInternalHomNatural`, the
first-variable functoriality of the canonical map of Stacks 0GMX, and
`isIso_toposPullbackInternalHomMap_structureSheaf`, its invertibility at the structure sheaf.

The presentation of `F` is a global one, not the local finite presentation of Tag 03DL that the
source assumes: `ι`, `κ`, `hP`, `hQ`, `a`, `b`, `hab` and `hF` exhibit `F` as a cokernel of a
morphism between finite coproducts of copies of the structure sheaf over the whole site `D`.
That is strictly stronger than finite presentation, so the statement here is the global special
case of Stacks 0GN2; the local case is reduced to it by
`PullbackInternalHomFinitePresentation.isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap_of_isFinitePresentationOnSite`,
which states the source's own hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMapULift
      f.ringedToposHom.fSharpInverseImage)
    {n m : ℕ} {P Q : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)}
    (ι : Fin n → (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) ⟶ P))
    (κ : Fin m → (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O) ⟶ Q))
    (hP : Limits.IsColimit (Limits.Cofan.mk P ι))
    (hQ : Limits.IsColimit (Limits.Cofan.mk Q κ))
    (a : Q ⟶ P) (b : P ⟶ F) (hab : a ≫ b = 0)
    (hF : Limits.IsColimit (Limits.CokernelCofork.ofπ b hab)) :
    IsIso (pullbackInternalHomMap f F G)
declarations.comment:
the isomorphism, for a global rather than local (Tag 03DL) finite presentation
of F

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN2 for `F` the structure sheaf.** Let `f : (C, O_C) ⟶ (D, O_D)` be a morphism of
ringed sites and `G` a sheaf of `O_D`-modules. The canonical map

`f^* Hom_{O_D}(O_D, G) ⟶ Hom_{O_C}(f^*O_D, f^*G)`

of Stacks 0GMX is an isomorphism.

The structure sheaf is finitely presented, and at it both sides of the canonical map are
identified with `f^*G`: the inputs are the identification `f^*O_D = O_C` of Stacks 03D6 and the
identity `Hom_O(O, -) = id` of Stacks 03EM. Flatness of `f` is not used — the source needs it
only to carry a presentation of a general `F` across the pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackInternalHomMap_structureSheaf :
    IsIso (pullbackInternalHomMap f
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := Y.J)) Y.O)) G)
declarations.comment: the isomorphism for F the structure sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ColimitsOfCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN3.** Let `C` be a site and let `S` be a set of sheaves of sets on `C` such that

1. some `K ∈ S` surjects onto the final sheaf,
2. every surjection `G ⟶ K` onto a member of `S` admits a map `K' ⟶ G` from a member of `S` whose
   composite to `K` is surjective,
3. every pair of members of `S` is covered by a member of `S` mapping onto their product,
4. the equalizer of every pair of maps between members of `S` is covered by a member of `S`, and
5. every member of `S` is quasi-compact.

Then `colim_λ H^p(C, F_λ) ⟶ H^p(C, colim_λ F_λ)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`, for every
filtered diagram `F` of abelian sheaves.

The proof is the source's induction on the degree. The base case is Stacks 0GMR (4), as
`isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_zero`; the step is the long exact cohomology
sequence of a functorial injective embedding of the diagram, as
`isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_succ`, whose acyclicity input is
`isZero_rightDerived_globalSections_colimit_of_isIso`. That input needs cohomology over the self
powers `K^r` of a `K ∈ S` to commute with the colimit in the degrees already known, which is
Stacks 07A0 (`isIso_colimit_post_extFunctorObj_freeAbelianSheafOn`) applied to Stacks 0GN3 on the
localized site `C/K^r`, available because `C/K^r` again carries such a set
(`Stacks.Cohomology.CoveringSet.exists_localized_coveringSet`). The induction is therefore strong
in the degree and generalised over the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections
    (S : Set (Sheaf J (Type u)))
    (h_terminal : ∃ K ∈ S, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from K))
    (h_lift : ∀ {G K : Sheaf J (Type u)} (f : G ⟶ K), K ∈ S →
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f →
        ∃ K' ∈ S, ∃ g : K' ⟶ G, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (g ≫ f))
    (h_product : ∀ K ∈ S, ∀ K' ∈ S,
      ∃ K'' ∈ S, ∃ f : K'' ⟶ K ⨯ K', Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f)
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {K K' : Sheaf J (Type u)} (a b : K ⟶ K'), K ∈ S → K' ∈ S →
      ∃ K'' ∈ S, ∃ f : K'' ⟶ equalizer a b, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f)
    (h_quasiCompact : ∀ K ∈ S, Sheaf.IsQuasiCompact K)
    (p : ℕ) {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Ab.{u})) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F ((Sheaf.Γ J (Ab.{u})).rightDerived p))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ColimitsOfCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_coveringSet
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN3 for an arbitrary site.** Let `C` be a site with objects in `Type u₁` and
morphisms in `Type v`, and let `S` be a set of sheaves of sets on `C` with sections at the join
`max u₁ v` of those two universes, such that

1. some `K ∈ S` surjects onto the final sheaf,
2. every surjection `G ⟶ K` onto a member of `S` admits a map `K' ⟶ G` from a member of `S` whose
   composite to `K` is surjective,
3. every pair of members of `S` is covered by a member of `S` mapping onto their product,
4. the equalizer of every pair of maps between members of `S` is covered by a member of `S`, and
5. every member of `S` is quasi-compact.

Then `colim_λ H^p(C, F_λ) ⟶ H^p(C, colim_λ F_λ)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`, for every
filtered diagram `F` of abelian sheaves with sections at that same universe.

Unlike `isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections`, the site need not be a `SmallCategory`:
its objects and morphisms may live in different universes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_coveringSet
    (S : Set (Sheaf J (Type max u₁ v)))
    (h_terminal : ∃ K ∈ S, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (terminal.from K))
    (h_lift : ∀ {G K : Sheaf J (Type max u₁ v)} (f : G ⟶ K), K ∈ S →
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f →
        ∃ K' ∈ S, ∃ g : K' ⟶ G, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (g ≫ f))
    (h_product : ∀ K ∈ S, ∀ K' ∈ S,
      ∃ K'' ∈ S, ∃ f : K'' ⟶ K ⨯ K', Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f)
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {K K' : Sheaf J (Type max u₁ v)} (a b : K ⟶ K'), K ∈ S → K' ∈ S →
      ∃ K'' ∈ S, ∃ f : K'' ⟶ equalizer a b, Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective f)
    (h_quasiCompact : ∀ K ∈ S, Sheaf.IsQuasiCompact K)
    (p : ℕ) {I : Type max u₁ v} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Ab.{max u₁ v})) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F ((Sheaf.Γ J (Ab.{max u₁ v})).rightDerived p))
declarations.comment: for a site whose objects and morphisms need not share a universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift
declarations.doc:
**Condition (4) of Stacks 0GN4 for the fppf site of an algebraic stack quasi-separated over a
quasi-separated base scheme**, in the shape
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf` consumes as its
hypothesis `h_equalizer`: for two objects `x`, `x'` of the site lying over affine schemes and two
morphisms `a, b : x ⟶ x'` there is a finite family of objects lying over affine schemes, each with
a morphism to `x` equalizing `a` and `b`, whose sheafified representables jointly cover the
equalizer of `h_a^#` and `h_b^#`.

The family has one member, as in the source: the object the dominating object of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_graph_dominating` classifies, with the equalizing morphism it
classifies. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift_associatedTopology` at the big fppf
topology of `B`, its fibre-lifting hypothesis discharged by **Stacks 06QA**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_fibre_lift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift :
    ∀ {x x' : 𝒳.val.val.obj} (a b : x ⟶ x'),
      x ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val → x' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ x) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ a = p i ≫ b),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift
              (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)).map a)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)).map b)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)).map (p i)) (by
                simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using
                  congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)).map (hp i)))
declarations.comment: condition (4) for the fppf site of an algebraic stack quasi-separated over a quasi-separated base scheme, with the collection B of Stacks 0GQV: the objects of the site lying over affine schemes; the family produced has one member, as in the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift_etale
declarations.doc:
**Condition (4) of Stacks 0GN4 for the étale site of an algebraic stack quasi-separated over a
quasi-separated base scheme**, in the shape
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_etale` consumes as its
hypothesis `h_equalizer`: for two objects `x`, `x'` of the étale site lying over affine schemes and
two morphisms `a, b : x ⟶ x'` there is a finite family of such objects, each with a morphism to `x`
equalizing `a` and `b`, whose sheafified representables jointly cover the equalizer of `h_a^#` and
`h_b^#`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift_associatedTopology` at the big étale
topology, its fibre-lifting hypothesis discharged by **Stacks 06XH** part (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etaleCovering_fibre_lift`, which reads the fibre lifts of a
surjective smooth 1-morphism off an *étale* covering of the base. The affine smooth presentation of
**Stacks 04YC** is smooth and surjective, which is exactly what that tag asks for, so the étale
case needs nothing of the presentation beyond what the fppf case needs — in particular no affine
étale presentation of a quasi-compact algebraic stack. The family has one member, as in the
source.

The fppf statement is the same result at
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.topology`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift`, where
**Stacks 06QA** discharges the hypothesis instead.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift_etale
    (hqsS : QuasiSeparatedSpace S) (h𝒳 : IsQuasiSeparatedOver.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) :
    ∀ {U U' : 𝒳.val.val.obj} (u v : U ⟶ U'),
      U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val → U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳.val) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ u = p i ≫ v),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift
              (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map u)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map v)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (p i)) (by
                simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using
                  congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                    (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (hp i)))
declarations.comment: condition (4) for the étale site of an algebraic stack quasi-separated over a quasi-separated base scheme, with the collection B of Stacks 0GQV: the objects of the site lying over affine schemes; the family produced has one member, as in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ColimitsOfCohomology.isQuasiCompact_of_finiteCoproductSheafifiedYoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN4, quasi-compactness assertion.** If every covering of every `U ∈ B` is refined by
a finite covering family with sources in `B` — condition (2) — then every finite coproduct of
sheafified representables of objects of `B` is a quasi-compact sheaf.

Condition (2) makes each `U ∈ B` a quasi-compact object of the site, hence each `h_U^#` a
quasi-compact sheaf by Stacks 0D06, and a finite coproduct of quasi-compact sheaves is
quasi-compact by Stacks 0GMQ. The empty coproduct is handled separately, being initial.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_of_finiteCoproductSheafifiedYoneda {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (B : Set C)
    (h_refine : ∀ U ∈ B, HasFiniteCoverRefinementsFrom J B U)
    {K : Sheaf J (Type max u v)} (hK : K ∈ FiniteCoproductSheafifiedYoneda J B) :
    Sheaf.IsQuasiCompact K
declarations.comment: quasi-compactness assertion

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ColimitsOfCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_finite_covers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN4, the criterion.** Let `C` be a small site and `B ⊆ Ob(C)`, and assume

1. for some `n ≥ 0` and `U_1, …, U_n ∈ B` the map `∐_i h_{U_i}^# ⟶ *` is surjective,
2. every covering of a `U ∈ B` is refined by a finite covering family with sources in `B`,
3. for any `U, U' ∈ B` there are finitely many `V_i ∈ B` with maps to both for which
   `∐_i h_{V_i}^# ⟶ h_U^# ⨯ h_{U'}^#` is surjective, and
4. for any `a, b : U ⟶ U'` between members of `B` there are finitely many `V_i ∈ B` with maps to
   `U` equalizing `a` and `b` for which `∐_i h_{V_i}^# ⟶ Equalizer(h_a^#, h_b^#)` is surjective.

Then `colim_λ H^p(C, F_λ) ⟶ H^p(C, colim_λ F_λ)` is an isomorphism in every degree, for every
filtered diagram of abelian sheaves.

The proof checks the five hypotheses of Stacks 0GN3 for the set `S` of finite coproducts of
sheafified representables of objects of `B`. Hypotheses (1), (3) and (4) of Stacks 0GN3 come from
(1), (3) and (4) here, after rewriting a coproduct of pairings as a map out of a coproduct and
distributing a coproduct over a product. Hypothesis (2), the lifting property for a surjection
`G ⟶ K` with `K ∈ S`, is obtained by applying (2) to the sieve of local liftings of the
tautological section of each summand of `K`: this produces a finite covering of each summand by
objects of `B` over which the surjection splits, and the resulting coproduct is again in `S`.
Hypothesis (5) is `isQuasiCompact_of_finiteCoproductSheafifiedYoneda`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_finite_covers
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (B : Set C)
    (h_terminal : ∃ (m : ℕ) (U : Fin m → C),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ B) ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i => terminal.from ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).obj (U i))))
    (h_refine : ∀ U ∈ B, HasFiniteCoverRefinementsFrom J B U)
    (h_product : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ U' ∈ B,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → C),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ B) ∧ ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc fun i =>
            prod.lift ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (p i))
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (q i))))
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {U U' : C} (a b : U ⟶ U'), U ∈ B → U' ∈ B →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → C),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ B) ∧ ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ a = p i ≫ b),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map a)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map b)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (p i)) (by
              simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (hp i))))
    (n : ℕ) {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Ab.{u})) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F ((Sheaf.Γ J (Ab.{u})).rightDerived n))
declarations.comment: criterion

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ColimitsOfCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_covers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN4 for an arbitrary site.** Let `C` be a site with objects in `Type u₁` and
morphisms in `Type v`, let `B ⊆ Ob(C)`, and assume

1. for some `n ≥ 0` and `U_1, …, U_n ∈ B` the map `∐_i h_{U_i}^# ⟶ *` is surjective,
2. every covering of a `U ∈ B` is refined by a finite covering family with sources in `B`,
3. for any `U, U' ∈ B` there are finitely many `V_i ∈ B` with maps to both for which
   `∐_i h_{V_i}^# ⟶ h_U^# ⨯ h_{U'}^#` is surjective, and
4. for any `a, b : U ⟶ U'` between members of `B` there are finitely many `V_i ∈ B` with maps to
   `U` equalizing `a` and `b` for which `∐_i h_{V_i}^# ⟶ Equalizer(h_a^#, h_b^#)` is surjective.

Then `colim_λ H^p(C, F_λ) ⟶ H^p(C, colim_λ F_λ)` is an isomorphism in every degree, for every
filtered diagram of abelian sheaves with sections at the join `max u₁ v` of the two universes of
the site.

The small-site form of the tag asks for `SmallCategory C`, that is for the objects and the morphisms
of the site to live in one universe, which the sites of algebraic geometry do not satisfy. Here
the site is arbitrary, every sheaf of sets and every abelian coefficient living at the join of its
two universes.

The proof is the source's: it checks the five hypotheses of Stacks 0GN3 for the set `S` of finite
coproducts of sheafified representables of objects of `B`, and concludes by
`isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_coveringSet`, the form of Stacks 0GN3 for an
arbitrary site. Hypotheses (1), (3) and (4) of Stacks 0GN3 come from (1), (3) and (4) here, after
rewriting a coproduct of pairings as a map out of a coproduct and distributing a coproduct over a
product. Hypothesis (2), the lifting property for a surjection `G ⟶ K` with `K ∈ S`, is obtained
by applying (2) to the sieve of local liftings of the tautological section of each summand of `K`:
this produces a finite covering of each summand by objects of `B` over which the surjection
splits, and the resulting coproduct is again in `S`. Hypothesis (5) is
`isQuasiCompact_of_finiteCoproductSheafifiedYoneda`, which is already general.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_covers
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (B : Set C)
    (h_terminal : ∃ (m : ℕ) (U : Fin m → C),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ B) ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i => terminal.from ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).obj (U i))))
    (h_refine : ∀ U ∈ B, HasFiniteCoverRefinementsFrom J B U)
    (h_product : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ U' ∈ B,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → C),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ B) ∧ ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc fun i =>
            prod.lift ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (p i))
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (q i))))
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {U U' : C} (a b : U ⟶ U'), U ∈ B → U' ∈ B →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → C),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ B) ∧ ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ a = p i ≫ b),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map a)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map b)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (p i)) (by
              simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda J).map (hp i))))
    (n : ℕ) {I : Type max u₁ v} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Ab.{max u₁ v})) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F ((Sheaf.Γ J (Ab.{max u₁ v})).rightDerived n))
declarations.comment: criterion, for a site whose objects and morphisms need not share a universe

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ModuleBaseChange.isIso_degreewiseComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GN5].**  Let

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
S' --g---> S
```

be a cartesian square of schemes with `f` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let `G` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_{S'}`-module flat over `S` and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then
the degreewise comparison

`Φ(R ⁱ f_* F) ⟶ R ⁱ f'_*(Ψ F)`

of the two coefficient functors `Φ : M ↦ g^*M ⊗ G` and `Ψ : F ↦ (g')^*F ⊗ (f')^*G` is an
isomorphism in every degree `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_degreewiseComparison_app (H : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S'.toRingedSpace)) [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hG : AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOver g.toLRSHom.toShHom G)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (i : ℕ) :
    IsIso ((degreewiseComparison H G hG i).app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedTensorBaseChange.tensorBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**The left-to-right map of [Stacks, Tag 0GN5]** attached to a commutative square of ringed
spaces:

`G ⊗^L_{𝒪_{S'}} Lg^*Rf_*F ⟶ Rf'_*(L(f')^*G ⊗^L_{𝒪_{X'}} L(g')^*F)`.

It is the adjunction unit `G ⟶ Rf'_*L(f')^*G` of Stacks 079W in the first tensor factor and the
derived base change map of Stacks 08HY in the second, followed by the relative cup product of
Stacks 0B68 for `f'`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorBaseChangeMap (G : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S')))
    (F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S'.sheaf).obj G).obj
        ((derivedPullback g).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj F)) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f').obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.sheaf).obj ((derivedPullback f').obj G)).obj
          ((derivedPullback g').obj F))
declarations.comment: the canonical map from left to right, in the derived category

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedTensorBaseChange.tensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_left
declarations.doc: The map of [Stacks, Tag 0GN5] is natural in the derived module on the base `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_left
    {G G' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S'))} (w : G ⟶ G')
    (F : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S'.sheaf).map w).app
          ((derivedPullback g).obj ((derivedPushforward f).obj F)) ≫
        tensorBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq G' F =
      tensorBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq G F ≫
        (derivedPushforward f').map
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.sheaf).map ((derivedPullback f').map w)).app
            ((derivedPullback g').obj F))
declarations.comment: naturality of the canonical map in the module on the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedTensorBaseChange.tensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_right
declarations.doc: The map of [Stacks, Tag 0GN5] is natural in the derived module on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_right
    (G : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S')))
    {F F' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))} (u : F ⟶ F') :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S'.sheaf).obj G).map
          ((derivedPullback g).map ((derivedPushforward f).map u)) ≫
        tensorBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq G F' =
      tensorBaseChangeMap g' f' f g sq G F ≫
        (derivedPushforward f').map
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.sheaf).obj ((derivedPullback f').obj G)).map
            ((derivedPullback g').map u))
declarations.comment: naturality of the canonical map in the module upstairs

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedTensorBaseChange.schemeTensorBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**The left-to-right map of [Stacks, Tag 0GN5]** for the cartesian square of schemes of
[Stacks, Tag 02KF]:

`G ⊗^L_{𝒪_{S'}} Lg^*Rf_*F ⟶ Rf'_*(L(f')^*G ⊗^L_{𝒪_{X'}} L(g')^*F)`.

It is the map above at the underlying ringed spaces.
declarations.statement:
def schemeTensorBaseChangeMap (H : IsPullback g' f' f g) (G : DerivedCategory S'.Modules)
    (F : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj G).obj
        ((derivedPullback g.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
          ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F)) ⟶
      (derivedPushforward f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
            ((derivedPullback f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)).obj
          ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F))
declarations.comment: the canonical map from left to right, for a cartesian square of schemes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedTensorBaseChange.schemeTensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_left
declarations.doc:
The map of [Stacks, Tag 0GN5] for a cartesian square of schemes is natural in the derived
module on the base `S'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_left (H : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    {G G' : DerivedCategory S'.Modules} (w : G ⟶ G') (F : DerivedCategory X.Modules) :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map w).app
          ((derivedPullback g.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
            ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F)) ≫
        schemeTensorBaseChangeMap H G' F =
      schemeTensorBaseChangeMap H G F ≫
        (derivedPushforward f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map
            ((derivedPullback f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).map w)).app
              ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj F))
declarations.comment: naturality for a cartesian square of schemes, in the module on the base

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedTensorBaseChange.schemeTensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_right
declarations.doc:
The map of [Stacks, Tag 0GN5] for a cartesian square of schemes is natural in the derived
module on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTensorBaseChangeMap_naturality_right (H : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (G : DerivedCategory S'.Modules) {F F' : DerivedCategory X.Modules} (u : F ⟶ F') :
    ((derivedTensorProductFunctor S'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj G).map
          ((derivedPullback g.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
            ((derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).map u)) ≫
        schemeTensorBaseChangeMap H G F' =
      schemeTensorBaseChangeMap H G F ≫
        (derivedPushforward f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).map
          (((derivedTensorProductFunctor X'.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
            ((derivedPullback f'.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj G)).map
              ((derivedPullback g'.toLRSHom.toShHom).map u))
declarations.comment: naturality for a cartesian square of schemes, in the module upstairs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN7 for the big site, and clause (1) of Stacks 06VE for it.**  For every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}` the functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU, from
the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪`-modules on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ`, is fully
faithful.

The two tags assert one thing of one functor, and the clause strings record the scope this
declaration proves — on **one source line**, because a tag registry that reads the attributes
matches a second `stacks` clause only when it is on the same line as the first, and two clause
strings plus the attribute syntax do not fit in a hundred characters unless both are short.  The
0GN7 string therefore no longer ends `; small site S_τ untreated`: that is information about
*where else the tag is registered*, not about the scope proved, and
`big site (Sch/S)_τ, every τ` already states the scope exactly.  The other registrations are
named in the last paragraph below.

06VE's first functor is `QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, whose target is
`Mod` — which is the target below on the nose, `SheafOfModules` over the structure sheaf of
`(Sch/S)_τ` — so clause (1) of 06VE needs no reading through a subcategory.  0GN7 spells the
same functor with target `QCoh((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, and that too is the same statement: full
faithfulness of a functor into a category is full faithfulness into any full subcategory
containing its image, and the image does land in `QCoh` by Stacks 03DV (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`.

What is **not** claimed by either tag here is the source's second functor,
`QCoh(𝒪_S) → Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)` into the *small* site of `S` for `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}` — a different
construction, Definition 03DU (4).  It is claimed elsewhere, and 0GN7 quantifies over nothing
beyond these: Definition 03DU gives a small site only at `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}`, so this
declaration together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallZariskiRealFullyFaithful.lean`)
and `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh'`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallEtaleLocalBijectivity.lean`) is
every functor the lemma speaks of.  At `τ = Zariski` the *sections*-defined form of the functor
carries the tag too, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedSheafFunctor`.

(The small étale functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallEtaleRingedSite.lean`, and its full
faithfulness rests on `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.unitIsoOnQuasicoherent` of
`SmallEtaleLocalBijectivity.lean`, which proves
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.UnitIsoOnQuasicoherent` with no hypothesis.)
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh (τ : SiteKind) :
    (baseAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS τ).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: big site (Sch/S)_τ, every τ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh'
declarations.doc:
**The small étale half of Stacks 0GN7 and of Stacks 06VE (1), with no hypothesis at all**:
the functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = étale`, from the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪`-modules on `S_étale`, is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh' :
    (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: small site at τ = étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GN7 for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, and clause (1) of Stacks 06VE for it.**
The functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` of Definition 03DU (4) at `τ = Zariski` — the pullback of sheaves of
modules along the morphism of ringed sites `(S_Zar, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` of Remark 03FH, with the
coefficient sheaf `T/S ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` of Definition 03DU (2) — from the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪`-modules on the small Zariski site, is fully faithful.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh` (the big
site, every `τ`) and `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh'` (the
small site at `τ = étale`) this completes the covering set of 0GN7: Definition 03DU gives a small
site only for `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale}`, so those three statements are every functor the lemma
quantifies over.

0GN7 spells the target `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` where this is `Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, and that is the same
statement for the same reason as at `τ = étale` and on the big site: full faithfulness of a
functor into a category is full faithfulness into any full subcategory containing its image, and
the image lands in `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` by Stacks 03DV (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.isQuasicoherentOnSite_associatedModule_of_isQuasicoherent`;
the corestriction itself is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcohOnSite` below.  06VE's second
functor has target `Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)`, which is the target here with nothing to read through.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh :
    (associatedModuleQcoh B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: small site at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GN7] for the small site at `τ = Zariski`, for the functor the source
defines**: the assignment `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ` of [Stacks, Tag 03DU] (4) — the sheaf of `𝒪`-modules on
`S_Zar` whose sections over `f : T → S` are `Γ(T, f^*𝓕)`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor` — is fully faithful on the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules.

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh` is the same statement for the
*pullback*-defined functor of [Stacks, Remark 03FH]; this is it read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor`, which identifies
the two.  Both are 0GN7 at `τ = Zariski`, and the source's own statement is about the sections
description, so the clause is only about the object the source names once this form exists.

0GN7 spells the target `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` where this is `Mod(S_Zar, 𝒪)`; that is the same
statement for the reason recorded on
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh`, full faithfulness into a
category being full faithfulness into any full subcategory containing the image, and the image
landing in `QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪)` by [Stacks, Tag 03DV] (2).

**This is also clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 06VE] at `τ = Zariski` for the sections-defined
functor**, that clause being the same assertion of full faithfulness; its second functor has
target `Mod(S_τ, 𝒪)`, which is the target here with nothing to read through.  The two attributes
sit together for the same reason they do on
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallZariski.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh` for the pullback-defined
functor.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulAssociatedSheafFunctor :
    (associatedSheafFunctor B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: small site at τ = Zariski, for the SECTIONS-defined functor 𝓕 ↦ 𝓕ᵃ of Definition 03DU (4) — SmallZariski.associatedSheafFunctor, whose value at 𝓕 is SmallZariski.associatedModuleOfSections. The same clause for the pullback-defined functor of Remark 03FH is fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh; the two functors are identified by associatedModuleQcohIsoAssociatedSheafFunctor

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.bijective_associatedModuleMap_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
On a site of schemes over `S` whose coverings are fpqc coverings of schemes, the map
`φ ↦ φᵃ` is bijective on morphisms of quasi-coherent modules on `S`, with **no affineness
assumption on `S`**, as soon as the arrows factoring through an object with affine underlying
scheme cover every object and the site contains an object `X₀` with invertible structure morphism
receiving a morphism from every object.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_associatedModuleMap_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
    (hfpqc : ∀ ⦃T : C⦄ (R : Presieve T), R ∈ K T →
      Presieve.map (toOver ⋙ Over.forget S) R ∈
        Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} ((toOver ⋙ Over.forget S).obj T))
    (hcover : ∀ X : C, Sieve.coverByImage
      (ObjectProperty.ι (fun Y : C ↦ IsAffine (toOver.obj Y).left)) X ∈ K.toGrothendieck X)
    (X₀ : C) [IsIso (toOver.obj X₀).hom] (hterm : ∀ X : C, Nonempty (X ⟶ X₀))
    (M N : S.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] [N.IsQuasicoherent] :
    Function.Bijective fun φ : M ⟶ N => associatedModuleMap S toOver φ
declarations.comment: the lemma over a base that is NOT assumed affine, on a site of schemes over S presented by a precoverage K and a functor toOver : C -> Over S. The two registrations that stood before this one are at particular sites and neither covers this presentation: Stacks.Descent.fullyFaithfulAssociatedModuleQcoh' is the small site at a topology tau (StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/SmallEtaleLocalBijectivity.lean:717) and Stacks.Descent.fullyFaithfulBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh is the big site (Sch/S)_tau (StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/BaseFullyFaithful.lean:211); the abstract presentation has neither the objScheme/objRestrict apparatus of the second nor a functor out of S.Opens as the first uses, so neither transfers. WHAT IS REMOVED relative to the affine-base case Stacks.Sites.bijective_associatedModuleMap is exactly IsAffine S, and nothing else: both sheaf conditions of bijective_associatedModuleMap_of_isPrestack are discharged here, the presheaf of morphisms by isPrestackOver_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage and the associated presheaf by isSheaf_associatedPresheaf_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage, the latter being the SECOND assertion of Stacks 03OJ. CARRIED: hcover, that the arrows factoring through an object with affine underlying scheme cover every object. That is a real hypothesis and not a restatement of the conclusion, but it is NOT supplied by condition (2) of Stacks 03OJ -- condition (2) yields covering only at the class Stacks.Sites.OverAffineOpen, of objects whose structure morphism has image inside an affine open, and at that class the local half of this lemma is BLOCKED: the required agreement of two Gamma(T,O)-linear maps on all of Gamma(g^+M, top) needs AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.span_range_pullbackSection_eq_top at W = top, which needs T affine, and that file's own documentation records that both of its affineness hypotheses are needed and that the statement is false for U affine and V arbitrary. So hcover at the AFFINE class is what this form asks for, and supplying it from Stacks 03OJ's conditions is the open problem that the third assertion of that tag now rests on. The full and faithful forms of this clause are full_ and faithful_associatedModuleFunctor_of_mem_fpqcPrecoverage below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isFlatMapULift_inverseImageStructureMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNA.**  The morphism of ringed sites `ε = id_{small, étale, Zar} : S_étale → S_Zar`
is flat: `𝒪_{S_étale}` is a flat module over `ε⁻¹𝒪_{S_Zar}`, the flatness being asserted for
the structure map `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.inverseImageStructureMap` of `ε` in
inverse-image form.

This is also the first assertion of **Stacks 08H8**, which states exactly that the `ε` of
Equation 75.4.0.1 — `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toZariskiRingedToposHom`, carrying Stacks
08H7 — is a flat morphism of ringed sites, and cites Descent, Lemma 35.10.1, which is 0GNA,
for it.  The second assertion of 08H8, exactness of `ε^*`, is carried by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.exactFunctor_pullbackModules_toZariski`.  The third, the
implication `ε^*𝓕 = 0 ⟹ 𝓕 = 0`, is *not* carried by this statement and is not available in
the library; the attribute clause records that scope.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNB (2).**  A colimit of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a
scheme is quasi-coherent; the shape is indexed at the size of the scheme, as in Stacks 06VE (3)
on the same site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isColimit {K : Type u} [SmallCategory K]
    {D : K ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS)}
    (hD : ∀ k, (D.obj k).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) {c : Cocone D} (hc : IsColimit c) :
    c.pt.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (2): colimits

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNB (1).**  A direct sum of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of
a scheme is quasi-coherent.
declarations.comment: part (1): direct sums

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isColimit_cokernelCofork
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNB (3), the cokernel half.**  A cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:

    (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)

**Stacks 0GNB (3), the kernel half.**  A kernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₁
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNB (4), the case in which the quotient and the middle term are quasi-coherent.**
The kernel term of a short exact sequence of `𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme is
quasi-coherent when the other two are.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₁
    {T : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS))} (hT : T.ShortExact)
    (h₂ : T.X₂.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (h₃ : T.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    T.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (4): the case of the sub, from the kernel clause

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₃
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNB (4), the case in which the sub and the middle term are quasi-coherent.**
The quotient term of a short exact sequence of `𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme
is quasi-coherent when the other two are.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₃

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₂
declarations.doc:
**The third case of Stacks 0GNB (4): the middle term of a short exact sequence of
`𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme is quasi-coherent when the outer two are.**

The source derives this case not from clause (3) but from Stacks 06VE (10), and on this site the
two are the same statement, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_essImage_associatedModuleQcoh`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₂ (hC : C.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : C.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (h₃ : C.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
      (R := AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.structureSheaf B S hS) C.X₂
declarations.comment: clause (4), third case: the middle term of a short exact sequence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Clause (6) of Stacks 0GNB.**  The internal Hom `𝓗om_𝒪(𝓕, 𝓖)` of two `𝒪`-modules on the
small étale site of a scheme `S` is quasi-coherent when `𝓕` is of finite presentation — Stacks
03DL (7) — and `𝓖` is quasi-coherent.

Quasi-coherence is local on the site (Stacks 03DN), so it is enough to produce a covering family
of the final object on whose members the restriction of the internal Hom is quasi-coherent, and
the objects carrying a finite global presentation of `𝓕` form one, by the finite-presentation
hypothesis itself.  On such an object the conclusion is
`isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf_of_hasFiniteGlobalPresentation` of this namespace.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf (hF : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (internalHomSheaf B S hS F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: clause (6): the internal Hom out of a module of finite presentation is quasi-coherent, small site at τ = étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.tensorSheaf_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**The tensor product clause of Stacks 0GNB.**  The tensor product of two quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorSheaf_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS))
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
        (commRingStructureSheaf B S hS))).obj (F, G))
declarations.comment: tensor_products

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₂_all
declarations.doc:
**Clause (4) of Stacks 0GNC on the big `τ`-site of a scheme, at every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`.**  Given a short exact sequence
`0 → 𝓕₁ → 𝓕₂ → 𝓕₃ → 0` of `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_τ` with `𝓕₁` and `𝓕₃` quasi-coherent, the
middle term `𝓕₂` is quasi-coherent.

The source's three steps are
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModule/BaseExtensionClosure.lean`.  Of the two
hypotheses they carried, essential surjectivity of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is Descent, Proposition 03DX (1) and
is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseQuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`, and right
exactness of restriction to `S_Zar` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.epi_baseRestrictModule_map_all` above.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_shortExact_X₂_all (hC : C.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : C.X₁.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (h₃ : C.X₃.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
      (R := AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf B S hS τ) C.X₂
declarations.comment: part (4), big site at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderExtensions_baseIsQuasicoherentOnSite_all
declarations.doc:
Quasi-coherence of `𝒪`-modules on the big `τ`-site of a scheme is closed under extensions, at
every `τ`.  This is clause (4) of Stacks 0GNC in the shape
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderExtensions` records; it has no hypothesis, so it is
safe as an instance.
declarations.comment: part (4), big site at every τ, as a closure-under-extensions instance

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC, part (5).**  The tensor product of two quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on the big
`τ`-site of a scheme `S` is quasi-coherent, for each of the five topologies.

The tensor product is the one of Stacks 0GMW, the sheafification of the objectwise tensor
product of the underlying presheaves of modules.  The statement is the quasi-coherent clause of
Stacks 03L6 on a ringed site,
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorLocalProperties.tensorSheaf_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, read at this
site: the two factors are globally presented on the members of two covering families, the
objects admitting an arrow into a member of each again cover, and over such an object the
tensor product of two globally presented modules is globally presented.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (baseRingedSite B S hS τ).O))
    [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite F] [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite G] :
    SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
      ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
        (FibredSite.baseStructureSheaf B S hS τ))).obj (F, G))
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC, part (6).**  The internal hom `𝓗om_𝒪(𝓕, 𝓖)` of Stacks 03EM is quasi-coherent
on the big `τ`-site of a scheme `S`, for each of the five topologies, when `𝓕` and `𝓖` are
quasi-coherent and `𝓕` is finite locally free.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent`, the statement for an
arbitrary ringed site, with its two sheafification hypotheses on the slice sites discharged:
every slice of the big category of schemes over `S` is essentially small, so abelian presheaves
on it have a sheafification whose weak equivalences are the locally bijective maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (baseRingedSite B S hS τ).O))
    [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite F] [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite G]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u + 1} F] :
    (RingedSite.internalHomSheaf (baseRingedSite B S hS τ) F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (6)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc: Internal Hom from a finite locally free quasi-coherent sheaf is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    [∀ U : X.C, HasWeakSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{w, v, u} F] :
    (internalHomSheaf X F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: internal_hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_baseIsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC (2) on the big `τ`-site of `S`, at every `τ` and with no hypothesis**:
quasi-coherence of `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_τ` is closed under colimits of shape `K`, for `K` at
an arbitrary universe.

This is the transfer the source performs with Lemma 06VE, carried out at every `τ`: the
quasi-coherent modules of `(Sch/S)_τ` are the essential image of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, which is fully
faithful (Stacks 0GN7) and preserves colimits (Stacks 06VE (3)) out of `QCoh(𝒪_S)`, where the
colimits exist and are quasi-coherent; so they are closed under those colimits.  That the
essential image is *all* the quasi-coherent modules is the essential-surjectivity half of
Descent, Proposition 03DX (1) at `(Sch/S)_τ`, and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseQuasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule`.
declarations.comment: part (2), big site at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, unconditionally, for an index category K at an arbitrary universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_discrete_baseIsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC (1) on the big `τ`-site of `S`, at every `τ` and with no hypothesis**: a
direct sum of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_τ` is quasi-coherent.  A direct sum is a
colimit over a discrete index category, which is how the source argues it.
declarations.comment: part (1), big site at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_walkingParallelPair_baseIsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC (3) on the big `τ`-site of `S`, at every `τ` and with no hypothesis**: the
cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_τ` is quasi-coherent.  A
cokernel is a colimit over `CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingParallelPair`, and the source obtains
clause (3) from clause (2) in exactly this way.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_walkingParallelPair_baseIsQuasicoherentOnSite
    (τ : SiteKind) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf B S hS τ)).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape
      WalkingParallelPair
declarations.comment: part (3), big site at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, unconditionally

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_isQuasicoherentOnSite_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC (2)** for `τ = fppf`: a colimit of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on the big fppf
site of a scheme `S` is quasi-coherent.

`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_baseIsQuasicoherentOnSite`, the
`τ`-indexed form of the clause, at `τ = .fppf`; the statement here is the one about the fppf
structure sheaf itself, and the two agree because
`FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf B S hS .fppf = structureSheaf B S hS` holds by `rfl`.
This is the transfer the source performs with Lemma 06VE: the colimit is formed in `QCoh(𝒪_S)`,
where it exists and is quasi-coherent, and carried up by `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`, which preserves colimits
and whose essential image is exactly the quasi-coherent modules of the site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_isQuasicoherentOnSite_unconditional
    (K : Type u) [Category.{u} K] :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (structureSheaf B S hS)).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape K
declarations.comment: part (2), big site at τ = fppf
