declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC (1)** for `τ = fppf`: a direct sum of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on the big
fppf site of a scheme `S` is quasi-coherent.  A direct sum is a colimit over a discrete index
category, which is how the source argues it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_discrete_isQuasicoherentOnSite_unconditional
    (I : Type u) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (structureSheaf B S hS)).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
declarations.comment: part (1), big site at τ = fppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_walkingParallelPair_isQuasicoherentOnSite_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNC (3)** for `τ = fppf`: the cokernel of a morphism of quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the big fppf site of a scheme `S` is quasi-coherent.  A cokernel is a colimit
over `CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingParallelPair`, and the source obtains clause (3) from
clause (2) in exactly this way.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_walkingParallelPair_isQuasicoherentOnSite_unconditional :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (structureSheaf B S hS)).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair
declarations.comment: part (3), big site at τ = fppf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site whose slices admit sheafification of abelian sheaves, the internal Hom of
Stacks 03EM from a finite locally free quasi-coherent module to a quasi-coherent module is
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
    [∀ U : X.C, HasWeakSheafify (X.J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : X.C, (X.J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] [G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{w, v, u} F] :
    (X.internalHomSheaf F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: internal_hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.hasColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (1), the existence half**, with no hypothesis: the category of quasi-coherent
`𝒪`-modules on the big fppf site of `S` has all colimits indexed at the size of the site.

`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.hasColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite'` with its
essential-surjectivity hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.quasicoherentIsEssImageAssociatedModule'`.
declarations.comment: part (1), existence: QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, O) has colimits indexed at the size of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.preservesColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_ι_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (1), the agreement with `Mod((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`**, with no hypothesis: a colimit
of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf` is the colimit of the same diagram taken in all
`𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.preservesColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_ι'` with its
essential-surjectivity hypothesis discharged.
declarations.comment: part (1), agreement: the colimits of QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, O) are the colimits taken in Mod((Sch/S)_fppf, O)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.preservesColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_ι_comp_restrictTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (1), the agreement with `Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`**, over every shape indexed at the
size of the site: the colimits of `QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)` are the colimits taken in
`Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, at every one of the five topologies and for an arbitrary diagram.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.hasColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_fppf` and
`…preservesColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_ι_fppf` this is the source's clause (1): the
colimits exist and agree with those computed in `Mod((Sch/S)_Zar, 𝒪)`,
`Mod((Sch/S)_étale, 𝒪)` and `Mod((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`.
declarations.comment: part (1), agreement: the colimits of QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, O) are the colimits taken in Mod((Sch/S)_tau, O), for every one of the five topologies and for an arbitrary diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_restrictTopology_iff
declarations.doc:
**Descent, Lemma 0GNE (3), the parenthetical.**  A quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module `𝓕` on the big
fppf site of `S` is finite locally free there if and only if its reading as an `𝒪`-module on
`(Sch/S)_τ` is finite locally free, for every one of the five topologies — in particular for the
étale and the Zariski topology, which are the two the source names alongside fppf.

The source's proof is run unchanged: `𝓕 = 𝓗ᵃ` by the essential surjectivity half of Descent,
Proposition 03DX (1) at `τ = fppf`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.essImage_associatedModuleQcoh_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`), and
both sides are then compared with "`𝓗` is finite locally free on `S`" by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_baseAssociatedModule_iff`, the reading
on `(Sch/S)_τ` of `𝓗ᵃ` being `𝓗ᵃ` computed on `(Sch/S)_τ` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.restrictTopologyAssociatedModuleIso`.

The `if` half needs no quasi-coherence and no reduction at all: it is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_of_comparisonPushforward`, valid for an
arbitrary module and an arbitrary pair of topologies.  Quasi-coherence is used only for the
`only if` half, and it is the hypothesis the source's clause carries.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_restrictTopology_iff (τ : SiteKind)
    (𝓕 : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS))
    (h𝓕 : SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u} 𝓕) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite 𝓕 ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj 𝓕)
declarations.comment: part (3), the parenthetical: finite local freeness agrees at τ = fppf, étale and Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.restrictTopology_internalHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (3), the agreement, at the big sites of a scheme.**  For arbitrary `𝒪`-modules
`𝓕`, `𝓖` on `(Sch/S)_fppf`, the internal hom `𝓗om_𝒪(𝓕, 𝓖)` computed in `Mod((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`
and read for the coarser topology *is* the internal hom of the readings computed in
`Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`, at every one of the five topologies — so in particular the Zariski, étale
and fppf values of the source's statement agree.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.coarsenModules_internalHomSheaf`, the statement for an
arbitrary ringed site read with a coarser topology, at `(Sch/S)_fppf` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology_le_fppf`: the ringed site `(Sch/S)_fppf` read
with the `τ`-topology is `(Sch/S)_τ`, the structure sheaves having the same underlying presheaf
and a sheaf condition that is a proposition.

An *equality* of sheaves of modules, not an isomorphism: the internal hom of Stacks 03EM is a
construction on presheaves of modules and the topology enters only in the proof that the result
is a sheaf, so there is nothing to compare.  No quasi-coherence and no finite local freeness are
needed for the agreement; they are the hypotheses of the quasi-coherence clause below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem restrictTopology_internalHomSheaf (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf B S hS)) :
    (restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj
        (RingedSite.internalHomSheaf (baseRingedSite B S hS .fppf) F G) =
      RingedSite.internalHomSheaf (baseRingedSite B S hS τ)
        ((restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj F) ((restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (3), the internal homs computed on (Sch/S)_fppf and on (Sch/S)_tau agree, for arbitrary O-modules, at every one of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (3), the quasi-coherence of the common value**, on the big `τ`-site of `S` for
every `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, with finite local freeness in the sense of
Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL (2) — the sense in which the source's part (3) states it.

At `τ = fppf` this is the source's "the common value is an object of `QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`";
the agreement of the values computed at the five topologies, which is what makes "the common
value" a legitimate phrase, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.restrictTopology_internalHomSheaf` above, an equality of sheaves
of modules and not merely an isomorphism.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf` — Stacks 0GNC on
the big `τ`-site — with its finite-local-freeness hypothesis supplied from the 03DL (2) form by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite`, whose two
sheafification hypotheses on the slices of the big site are the instances
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.hasSheafify_baseOver` and
`…wEqualsLocallyBijective_baseOver`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_internalHomSheaf_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
    (τ : SiteKind)
      (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (baseRingedSite B S hS τ).O))
    [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite F] [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite G]
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite F) :
    (RingedSite.internalHomSheaf (baseRingedSite B S hS τ) F G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (3), quasi-coherence of the common value, on the big tau-site for every one of the five topologies, with finite local freeness in the sense of Modules on Sites 03DL (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.tensorAgreementQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (2), the agreement, at the source's own scope.**  For an **arbitrary** pair
`𝓕`, `𝓖` of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf`, the tensor product `𝓕 ⊗_𝒪 𝓖` computed
in `Mod((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`, read for the coarser topology, *is* the tensor product computed in
`Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)` — at every one of the five topologies, so in particular the Zariski, étale
and fppf values of the source's statement agree.

`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.tensorAgreementAssociatedModule` is this for `𝓕 = 𝓗^a` and
`𝓖 = 𝓘^a`; the reduction of an arbitrary pair to that case is Stacks 03DX (1) at `τ = fppf`
together with the functoriality of the tensor product in both arguments — see the implementation
notes.  The comparison itself is the same one, the inverse of the unit of "sheafify for fppf" ⊣
"read an fppf sheaf for `τ`", so this is not a transported isomorphism but the canonical one
with its invertibility now known at every quasi-coherent pair.
declarations.statement:
def tensorAgreementQuasicoherentOnSite
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj
        ((Functor.uncurry.obj (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
            (FibredSite.baseStructureSheaf B S hS .fppf))).obj (F, G)) ≅
      (Functor.uncurry.obj
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (FibredSite.baseStructureSheaf B S hS τ))).obj
        ((restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj F, (restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (2), the tensor products computed on (Sch/S)_fppf and on (Sch/S)_tau agree, for an arbitrary pair of quasi-coherent O-modules on (Sch/S)_fppf, at every one of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorRestrictTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (2), the quasi-coherence of the common value, at the source's own scope.**  For
an arbitrary pair of quasi-coherent `𝒪`-modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf`, the common value of the
tensor products — the right-hand side of
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.tensorAgreementQuasicoherentOnSite` — is quasi-coherent on
`(Sch/S)_τ`, at every one of the five topologies; at `τ = fppf` this is the source's "the common
value is an object of `QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`".

By the reduction it is the reading of `(𝓗 ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓘)^a`, which is quasi-coherent by Stacks
01CE (3) and Stacks 03DV at every `τ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorRestrictTopology
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((Functor.uncurry.obj
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (FibredSite.baseStructureSheaf B S hS τ))).obj
      ((restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj F,
        (restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj G)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (2), quasi-coherence of the common value, for an arbitrary pair of quasi-coherent O-modules on (Sch/S)_fppf, at every one of the five topologies

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorLeftFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (2), the comparison.**  The tensor product of two sheaves of modules for the
finer topology is the sheafification, for the finer topology, of their tensor product taken for
the coarser one.  Both are sheafifications of the objectwise tensor product of the two
underlying presheaves of modules, which does not mention a topology, so this is one component
of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafificationFactorization`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorLeftFactorization :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (J := J) (R)).obj F).obj G ≅
      (comparisonPullback.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (J := K) ((commRingOfLe h R))).obj
            ((comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj F)).obj
          ((comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj G))
declarations.comment: part (2), the tensor product for the finer topology is the sheafification of the one for the coarser topology, for an arbitrary pair of topologies on one category

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorLeftAgreement
declarations.doc:
**Towards Stacks 0GNE (2), the agreement.**  The tensor product computed for the finer
topology, read for the coarser one, is the tensor product computed for the coarser topology, as
soon as the latter is already a sheaf for the finer topology — which is what invertibility of
the unit at it says.

`hunit` is a hypothesis the source does not have, and the clause string of the `stacks`
attribute below says so: what is proved here is the implication.  It is discharged at the big
sites of a scheme, by Stacks 06VE (7), in
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isIso_comparisonUnit_tensorRestrictTopology`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/QuasiCoherentTopologiesTwo/BigSiteTensorAgreement.lean`),
and the 0GNE (2) attribute for the clause without that hypothesis sits there, on
`…tensorAgreementQuasicoherentOnSite`, which is this declaration with `hunit` supplied for an
arbitrary pair of quasi-coherent modules on `(Sch/S)_fppf` — note that the arbitrary pair is
reached by widening `hunit`, so the isomorphism it returns is still this canonical one.  The
half of part (2) that needs no hypothesis at all is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.tensorLeftFactorization`, which carries the tag here.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorLeftAgreement
    (hunit : IsIso ((comparisonAdjunction.{u, v, w, m} h
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).unit.app
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (J := K) ((commRingOfLe h R))).obj
          ((comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj F)).obj
        ((comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj G)))) :
    (comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (J := J) (R)).obj F).obj G) ≅
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (J := K) ((commRingOfLe h R))).obj
          ((comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj F)).obj
        ((comparisonPushforward.{u, v, w, m} h ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := J)) R)).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (2), the two tensor products agree once the coarser one is a sheaf for the finer topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.coarsenModules_internalHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (3), the agreement clause.**  The internal hom of two sheaves of modules
computed on a ringed site, read for a coarser topology, *is* the internal hom of their readings
computed for the coarser topology.

This is the source's own argument for part (3): the internal hom of Stacks 03EM is a
construction on presheaves of modules, and the topology enters only in the proof that the
result is a sheaf, which needs the sheaf condition on the target alone.  So no comparison map
is involved — the two sheaves of modules have the same underlying presheaf of modules, and
their sheaf conditions are propositions.
declarations.statement:
theorem coarsenModules_internalHomSheaf (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    {J' : GrothendieckTopology X.C} (h : J' ≤ X.J)
    (A B : SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (coarsenModules X h).obj (internalHomSheaf X A B) =
      internalHomSheaf (X.ofLE h) ((coarsenModules X h).obj A)
        ((coarsenModules X h).obj B)
declarations.comment: part (3), the internal homs computed for two topologies agree, for arbitrary sheaves of modules on a ringed site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.restrictTopologyAssociatedModuleIso
declarations.doc:
**The key to Stacks 0GNE.**  The functor `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` is given by the same formula for every
`τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`: the associated module of a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-module on `(Sch/S)_τ` is the associated module on `(Sch/S)_fppf`, read for the coarser
topology.

Every clause of the source's lemma is deduced from this, which is why it carries the tag: the
source's proof of all three parts is "the equivalence of Proposition 03DX is given by the same
formula independent of the choice of the topology", applied to a colimit, to a tensor product
and to an internal hom.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictTopologyAssociatedModuleIso (τ : SiteKind) (F : S.Modules)
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (restrictTopology B S hS τ).obj ((associatedModule B S hS).obj F) ≅
      (baseAssociatedModule B S hS τ).obj F
declarations.comment: the key to the proof: the associated-module functor is given by one formula for all five topologies, so its values for the five topologies agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isColimitMapCoconeBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNE (1), the comparison with the modules of `(Sch/S)_τ`, every `τ`.**  A colimit
of a diagram of quasi-coherent modules on `S` is carried by `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a` to a colimit in
`Mod((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪)`.  Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.restrictTopologyAssociatedModuleIso`, which identifies the
vertex at `τ` with the vertex at fppf read for the coarser topology, this says that the
colimits computed in the five module categories agree.

The source states the clause for a diagram in `QCoh((Sch/S)_fppf, 𝒪)`, and reduces it to a
diagram in `QCoh(𝒪_S)` by the essential surjectivity of `𝓕 ↦ 𝓕^a`; the diagram here is the
reduced one.  That reduction is now available, and the clause for an arbitrary diagram is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.preservesColimitsOfSize_quasicoherentOnSite_ι_comp_restrictTopology`
(`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/QuasiCoherentTopologiesTwo/BigSiteColimitAgreement.lean`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimitMapCoconeBaseAssociatedModuleQcoh
    {D : K ⥤ (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory}
    {c : Cocone D} (hc : IsColimit c) :
    IsColimit ((baseAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS τ).mapCocone c)
declarations.comment: part (1), the colimit of a diagram of associated modules computed in Mod((Sch/S)_τ, O), for every one of the five topologies

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.internalHomSheaf_isQuasicoherent
registrations.comment: part (3), quasi-coherence of the common value

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.coinductionAdjunction_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GNF.**  The unit of the forgetful--coinduction adjunction at a quasi-coherent
module `(𝓕, α)` on a groupoid scheme is, on underlying modules, the unit of the
pullback--pushforward adjunction along the source followed by the direct image of the inverse
of the descent morphism:
`𝓕 ⟶ s_* s^* 𝓕 ⟶ s_* t^* 𝓕`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coinductionAdjunction_unit_app (M : QuasicoherentModule G) :
    ((coinductionAdjunction G).unit.app M).hom =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction G.source.left).unit.app M.module ≫
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).map (inv M.alpha)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension
declarations.doc:
A functor on finitely presented modules has an extension to all modules which preserves
filtered colimits.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def filteredColimitExtension
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{max u v, max u v} B]
    (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (FinitelyPresentedModuleCat.{u, max u v} A) B) :
    FilteredColimitExtension A F
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: ModuleCat.FilteredColimitExtension.existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
Two filtered-colimit-preserving extensions are related by a unique natural isomorphism
compatible with their specified identifications on finitely presented modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem FilteredColimitExtension.existsUnique_iso
    {F : CategoryTheory.Functor (FinitelyPresentedModuleCat.{u, max u v} A) B}
    (E₁ E₂ : FilteredColimitExtension A F) :
    ∃! e : CategoryTheory.Iso E₁.functor E₂.functor,
      Functor.whiskerLeft (finitelyPresentedModule.{u, max u v} A).ι e.hom =
        (CategoryTheory.Iso.trans E₁.iso E₂.iso.symm).hom
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension_additive
declarations.doc:
A filtered-colimit-preserving extension of an additive functor from finitely presented
modules is additive.
declarations.statement:
public lemma filteredColimitExtension_additive
    (E : FilteredColimitExtension A F) [F.Additive] :
    E.functor.Additive
declarations.comment: additivity

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension_preservesCoproducts
declarations.doc:
A filtered-colimit-preserving extension of an additive functor from finitely presented
modules preserves arbitrary direct sums.
declarations.statement:
public lemma filteredColimitExtension_preservesCoproducts
    (E : FilteredColimitExtension A F) [F.Additive]
    (J : Type (max u v)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) E.functor
declarations.comment: arbitrary direct sums

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension_functor_additive
declarations.doc:
The extension of a right exact functor on finitely presented modules to all modules is
additive.
declarations.statement:
public lemma filteredColimitExtension_functor_additive :
    (filteredColimitExtension A G).functor.Additive
declarations.comment: additivity

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension_functor_preservesFiniteColimits
declarations.doc:
The extension of a right exact functor on finitely presented modules to all modules is
right exact.
declarations.statement:
public lemma filteredColimitExtension_functor_preservesFiniteColimits :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (filteredColimitExtension A G).functor
declarations.comment: right exactness

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension_functor_preservesCoproducts
declarations.doc:
The extension of a right exact functor on finitely presented modules to all modules
commutes with arbitrary direct sums.
declarations.statement:
public lemma filteredColimitExtension_functor_preservesCoproducts (J : Type (max u v)) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) (filteredColimitExtension A G).functor
declarations.comment: arbitrary direct sums

declarations.name: ModuleCat.filteredColimitExtension_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
If filtered colimits commute with kernels in the target, the filtered-colimit extension
of a left exact functor on finitely presented modules is left exact.
declarations.statement:
public lemma filteredColimitExtension_preservesFiniteLimits
    [IsCoherentRing A] (E : FilteredColimitExtension A F) [HasKernels B]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F]
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{max u v, max u v} B]
    [∀ (J : Type (max u v)) [Category.{max u v} J] [IsFiltered J],
      ∀ {X Y : J ⥤ B} (f : X ⟶ Y),
        PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) (colim : (J ⥤ B) ⥤ B)] :
    PreservesFiniteLimits E.functor
declarations.comment: left exactness

declarations.name: ModuleCat.rightExactFunctor_additive
declarations.doc: A right exact functor on finitely presented modules is automatically additive.
declarations.statement:
public lemma rightExactFunctor_additive (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [Ring A]
    [Category.{w} B] [Preadditive B] [HasFiniteBiproducts B]
    (F : FPModule A ⥤ᵣ B) : F.obj.Additive
declarations.comment: automatic additivity

declarations.name: ModuleCat.tfae_iso_tensorFunctor_preserves_colimits_isLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
A functor between module categories is tensoring with a bimodule iff it is right exact and
commutes with arbitrary direct sums; these are also equivalent to preserving all colimits and
to having a right adjoint.
declarations.statement:
public lemma tfae_iso_tensorFunctor_preserves_colimits_isLeftAdjoint
    (F : ModuleCat.{u} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) :

          Nonempty (tensorFunctorOverInt A B K ≅ F),
        PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧
          ∀ J : Type u, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F,

        F.IsLeftAdjoint ]

declarations.name: ModuleCat.moduleTensorFunctor_comp
declarations.doc:
The tensor product over the middle algebra represents the composite of two tensor functors. The
equation on pure tensors records the canonical action of `A ⊗[R] C`, and the functor isomorphism
includes naturality in the input `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
public lemma moduleTensorFunctor_comp
    (K : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) (K' : ModuleCat.{u} (B ⊗[R] C)) :
    letI : Module A K := Module.compHom K
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := A) (B := B))
    letI : Module B K := Module.compHom K
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := A) (B := B)).toRingHom
    letI : Module B K' := Module.compHom K'
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := B) (B := C))
    letI : Module C K' := Module.compHom K'
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := B) (B := C)).toRingHom
    ∃ inst : Module (A ⊗[R] C) (K ⊗[B] K'),
      letI : Module (A ⊗[R] C) (K ⊗[B] K') := inst
      (∀ (a : A) (c : C) (k : K) (k' : K'),
        (a ⊗ₜ[R] c) • (k ⊗ₜ[B] k') = (a • k) ⊗ₜ[B] (c • k')) ∧
      Nonempty
        ((moduleTensorFunctor R A C).obj
            (ModuleCat.of (A ⊗[R] C) (K ⊗[B] K')) ≅
          ((moduleTensorFunctor R A B).obj K ⋙
            (moduleTensorFunctor R B C).obj K'))

declarations.name: ModuleCat.tensorFunctor_exact_iff_flat
declarations.doc:
Tensoring with an `A ⊗[R] B`-module `K` is an exact functor from `A`-modules to `B`-modules if
and only if `K` is flat as an `A`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorFunctor_exact_iff_flat
    (R A B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (K : ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) :
    exactFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ModuleCat.{u} B) (tensorFunctor R A B K) ↔
      Module.Flat A ((restrictScalars
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom (R := R) (A := A) (B := B))).obj K)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.exists_ringEquiv_invertible_iso_extensionTensorFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GP0.** Every equivalence between categories of modules is extension
of scalars along an isomorphism of the rings, followed by tensoring with an invertible module.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_ringEquiv_invertible_iso_extensionTensorFunctor
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (F : ModuleCat.{u} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) [F.IsEquivalence] :
    ∃ (e : A ≃+* B) (L : ModuleCat.{u} B),
      Module.Invertible B L ∧ Nonempty (F ≅ extensionTensorFunctor A B e L)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.exists_algEquiv_invertible_iso_extensionTensorFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GP1.** An equivalence of module categories linear over the base
ring is extension of scalars along an algebra isomorphism, followed by tensoring with an
invertible module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_algEquiv_invertible_iso_extensionTensorFunctor
    (R : Type v) (A B : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B]
    (F : ModuleCat.{u} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} B) [F.IsEquivalence]
    [F.Linear R] :
    ∃ (e : A ≃ₐ[R] B) (L : ModuleCat.{u} B),
      Module.Invertible B L ∧
        Nonempty (F ≅ extensionTensorFunctor A B e.toRingEquiv L)

declarations.name: ModuleCat.torsionFreeQuotient_scalarValue
declarations.doc:
For any monoidal structure on torsion-free quotient, conjugating the image of
each scalar endomorphism of the monoidal unit gives that same scalar endomorphism.
This expresses that the induced scalar map is the identity in every module universe.
declarations.statement:
public theorem torsionFreeQuotient_scalarValue
    (h : torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}.Monoidal) (a : ℤ) :
    letI : torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}.Monoidal := h
    (Functor.Monoidal.εIso torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}).hom ≫
      torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}.map
        (a • (𝟙 (𝟙_ (ModuleCat.{u} ℤ)))) ≫
      (Functor.Monoidal.εIso torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}).inv =
        a • (𝟙 (𝟙_ (ModuleCat.{u} ℤ)))
declarations.comment: part (5): induced scalar map is the identity

declarations.name: ModuleCat.torsionFreeQuotient_scalar_action

    torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}.map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (a • (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[ℤ] M))) =
      ModuleCat.ofHom (a • (LinearMap.id :
        torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}.obj M →ₗ[ℤ]
          torsionFreeQuotientFunctor.{u}.obj M))
declarations.comment: part (5): scalar endomorphisms on all modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_kernel_natTrans_isIso_whiskerLeft_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GPA.**  Let `R` be a ring, let `X` and `Y` be schemes over `R` with `X` quasi-compact
with affine diagonal, and let `F : QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be `R`-linear, right exact and
commute with arbitrary direct sums.  Then there are a quasi-coherent module `K` on `X ×_R Y` and a
natural transformation `t : F ⟶ F_K` such that `t ∘ f_* : F ∘ f_* ⟶ F_K ∘ f_*` is an
isomorphism for every morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` whose source is an affine scheme.

The kernel is `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineChartKernels.glued` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.openKernelSystem`, glued from the kernels of `F ∘ j_{U,*}` over the affine
opens `U` of `X`, and `t` is `AlgebraicGeometry.kernelTransform`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_kernel_natTrans_isIso_whiskerLeft_pushforward [CompactSpace X.left]
    [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal (terminal.from X.left))]
    (hF : rightExactLinearCoproductFunctor R X Y F) :
    ∃ (K : Scheme.QuasicoherentModules (pullback X.hom Y.hom))
      (t : F ⟶ quasicoherentIntegralTransform R X Y K),
      ∀ (X' : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X'] (f : X' ⟶ X.left),
        letI : IsAffineHom f :=
          Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeCechComplex.isAffineHom_of_isAffine_source f
        IsIso (Functor.whiskerLeft (quasicoherentPushforward f) t)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_iso_quasicoherentIntegralTransform_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPB.**  Let `R` be a ring and let `X` and `Y` be schemes over `R`,
with `X` quasi-compact with affine diagonal.  A functor `F : QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` is
isomorphic to the integral transform `F_K = pr_{2,*}(pr_1^*(−) ⊗ K)` of a quasi-coherent module
`K` on `X ×_R Y` if and only if

1. `F` is `R`-linear (in particular additive) and commutes with arbitrary direct sums,
2. `F ∘ j_*` is right exact for the inclusion `j : U ⟶ X` of every affine open `U`
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.PreservesFiniteColimitsAfterAffineOpens`), and
3. `0 ⟶ F(F) ⟶ F(G) ⟶ F(H)` is exact for every short exact sequence
   `0 ⟶ F ⟶ G ⟶ H ⟶ 0` of quasi-coherent modules whose sequences of stalks are split short
   exact sequences of `𝒪_{X,x}`-modules (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsStalkwiseSplitLeftExact`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_quasicoherentIntegralTransform_iff
    (F : Scheme.QuasicoherentModules X.left ⥤ Scheme.QuasicoherentModules Y.left) :
    letI : Linear R (SheafOfModules.{u} X.left.ringCatSheaf) := modulesLinear R X
    letI : Linear R (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.left.ringCatSheaf) := modulesLinear R Y
    (∃ K : Scheme.QuasicoherentModules (pullback X.hom Y.hom),
        Nonempty (F ≅ quasicoherentIntegralTransform R X Y K)) ↔
      ∃ _ : F.Additive, F.Linear R ∧ (∀ I : Type u, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F) ∧
        PreservesFiniteColimitsAfterAffineOpens R X F ∧ IsStalkwiseSplitLeftExact F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentIntegralTransformConvolutionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPC.**  Let `R` be a ring and let `X`, `Y`, `Z` be schemes over `R`,
with `X` quasi-compact with affine diagonal and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated.  Let `K`
be a quasi-coherent kernel on `X ×_R Y` and `L` a quasi-coherent kernel on `Y ×_R Z` in
category (2) of Tag 0FZH, that is, flat over `Y` with vanishing higher direct images, so that its
integral transform `F_L : QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Z)` is `R`-linear, exact and commutes with direct
sums.  Then

`F_L ∘ F_K ≅ F_{pr_{13,*}(pr_{12}^*K ⊗ pr_{23}^*L)}`

as functors `QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Z)`.

This is the source's statement for exact functors `F` and `G` with kernels `K` and `L`
(`G ∘ F ≅ F_L ∘ F_K`), in greater generality: nothing is assumed of `K`, and of `Y` only
quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.  That, when `K` is of category (2) as well, the
convolution is up to isomorphism the kernel of category (2) which Tag 0FZH attaches to `G ∘ F` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_integralTransformExactKernel_iso_convolutionKernel`.

Exactness of `F_L` cannot be dropped.  Let `E` be an elliptic curve over a field `k` with origin
`o`, let `C = E ∖ {e}` for a point `e ≠ o`, `R = Γ(C, 𝒪_C)`, `X = E ×_k C` over `R`, `Y = Spec R`,
`Z = Spec k` the point `o` of `C`, `L = 𝒪_Z` on `Y ×_R Z = Z`, and `K = 𝒪(Δ - {o} × C)` on
`X ×_R Y = X`, with `Δ` the graph of `C ⊆ E`.  The fibre of `K` over `c ∈ C` is `𝒪_E(c - o)`,
nontrivial of degree zero for `c ≠ o`, so `Γ(X, K)`, a torsion-free `R`-module with zero generic
fibre, vanishes and `F_L(F_K(𝒪_X)) = 0`.  But `X ×_R Y ×_R Z = E`, the convolution kernel is
`K|_{E × {o}} ≅ 𝒪_E`, and `F_{K * L}(𝒪_X) = Γ(E, 𝒪_E) = k`.  Here `F_L = - ⊗_R k` is not left
exact.
declarations.comment: the composition formula F_L ∘ F_K ≅ F_{pr13,*(pr12^*K ⊗ pr23^*L)} as a natural isomorphism of functors QCoh(O_X) to QCoh(O_Z), for L a kernel of category (2) of 0FZH (so F_L is R-linear, exact and commutes with direct sums), K arbitrary, X quasi-compact with affine diagonal and Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinitelyPresentable_iff_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPE.**  A quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme is a categorically compact object of the category of quasi-coherent modules if and only if
it is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinitelyPresentable_iff_isFinitePresentation
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    IsFinitelyPresentable.{u} F ↔ F.obj.IsFinitePresentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_nonzero_hom_of_supp_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPF.** If the support of a nonzero quasi-coherent module on an
affine scheme is contained in that of a finitely presented module, then there is a nonzero
morphism from the latter to the former.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_hom_of_supp_subset
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    (F E : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] [E.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hE : ¬ IsZero E)
    (hsupp : SheafOfModules.supp E ⊆ SheafOfModules.supp F) :
    ∃ f : F ⟶ E, f ≠ 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportContained_eq_serreCoproductClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPG.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, the
quasi-coherent modules supported on the support of a finitely presented module are exactly
the smallest Serre subcategory containing it and closed under arbitrary direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportContained_eq_serreCoproductClosure (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (F : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (R := X.ringCatSheaf) F] :
    (fun E : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ↦
        IsSupportedOn E.obj F) =
      serreCoproductClosure
          (C := (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
        ⟨F, by
        constructor
        exact ⟨(SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.exists_quasicoherentData F).choose⟩⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentSupportedOn_isSerreClass
declarations.doc:
Quasi-coherent modules supported on a fixed subset of a scheme form a Serre subcategory of
the category of all quasi-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
public instance quasicoherentSupportedOn_isSerreClass (X : Scheme.{u}) (Z : Set X) :
    (quasicoherentSupportedOn X Z).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: the full subcategory of modules supported on `Z` is a Serre subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentRestriction_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GPH].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let `U` be
a quasi-compact open whose complement is the closed subset `Z`.  Restriction along `U ↪ X`
exhibits `QCoh(𝒪_U)` as the localization of `QCoh(𝒪_X)` at the morphisms whose kernel and
cokernel are supported on `Z`, that is, as the Serre quotient of `QCoh(𝒪_X)` by the full
subcategory of quasi-coherent modules supported on `Z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasicoherentRestriction_isLocalization (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Z : Set X) (U : X.Opens) (hUZ : (U : Set X) = Zᶜ)
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) :
    (quasicoherentRestriction U.ι).IsLocalization
      (quasicoherentSupportedOn X Z).isoModSerre
declarations.comment: restriction is the localization at the supported Serre subcategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentSupportedQuotientEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GPH].** The equivalence `QCoh(𝒪_X)/𝒜 ≌ QCoh(𝒪_U)` induced by restriction,
where `𝒜` is the Serre subcategory of quasi-coherent modules supported on the closed complement
`Z` of the quasi-compact open `U`, and `QCoh(𝒪_X)/𝒜` is the Serre quotient, that is the
localization of `QCoh(𝒪_X)` at the morphisms that are isomorphisms modulo `𝒜`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quasicoherentSupportedQuotientEquivalence (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Z : Set X) (U : X.Opens)
    (hUZ : (U : Set X) = Zᶜ) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) :
    (quasicoherentSupportedOn X Z).isoModSerre.Localization ≌
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: the induced equivalence from the quotient category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentSupportedQuotientEquivalenceFunctorIso
declarations.doc:
The equivalence `QCoh(𝒪_X)/𝒜 ≌ QCoh(𝒪_U)` of [Stacks, Tag 0GPH] is the one induced by the
restriction functor: composing it with the quotient functor gives back restriction.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quasicoherentSupportedQuotientEquivalenceFunctorIso (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (Z : Set X) (U : X.Opens)
    (hUZ : (U : Set X) = Zᶜ) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) :
    (quasicoherentSupportedOn X Z).isoModSerre.Q ⋙
        (quasicoherentSupportedQuotientEquivalence X Z U hUZ hU).functor ≅
      quasicoherentRestriction U.ι
declarations.comment: the equivalence is induced by the restriction functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineOfModuleCategory.isAffine_of_quasicoherentModules_equivalent_moduleCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPI.** A quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme whose category
of quasi-coherent modules is equivalent to the category of modules over a commutative ring
is affine.

The commutativity of `R` is a reading of the tag's `a ring`. It is used through the separator
`P`, whose endomorphism ring must be commutative for the rank of `P` to be forced to be `1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffine_of_quasicoherentModules_equivalent_moduleCat
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R]
    (e : ModuleCat.{u} R ≌
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    IsAffine X
declarations.comment: `[CommRing R]` reads the tag's `a ring`: the rank-one step needs `End P` commutative. For noncommutative `R` the conclusion still holds by Morita equivalence (`Mod (M₂ k) ≌ Mod k`), but that rank-one step fails outright.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineOfModuleCategory.isAffine_of_quasicoherentModules_equivalence_moduleCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPI**, with the equivalence written in the orientation of the source:
a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme whose category of quasi-coherent modules is equivalent
to the category of modules over a commutative ring is affine.

As for the mirror form, the commutativity of `R` is a reading of the tag's `a ring`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffine_of_quasicoherentModules_equivalence_moduleCat
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R]
    (e : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    IsAffine X
declarations.comment: the hypothesis in the orientation of the source, `QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ Mod R`; `[CommRing R]` reads the tag's `a ring`, exactly as for the mirror form `isAffine_of_quasicoherentModules_equivalent_moduleCat`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeIso_invertible_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
If `X` and `Y` are affine schemes and
`F : QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` is an equivalence, then there are an isomorphism of schemes
`f : Y ≅ X` and an invertible `Γ(Y, ⊤)`-module `L` such that `F` is inverse image along `f`
followed by tensoring with `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_schemeIso_invertible_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
    (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) [F.IsEquivalence] :
    ∃ (f : Y ≅ X) (L : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(Y, ⊤)), Module.Invertible Γ(Y, ⊤) L ∧
      Nonempty (F ≅ (quasicoherentModulesEquivOfSchemeIso f).symm.functor ⋙
        affineTensorFunctor Y L)
declarations.comment:
affine case: for `X` and `Y` affine, with the tensoring by the invertible module
  read on `ModuleCat Γ(Y, ⊤)` through the affine comparison
  `AlgebraicGeometry.affineQuasicoherentModulesEquiv` rather than as the tensor product of
  sheaves of `𝒪_Y`-modules.  This is the form in which the Tag 0GP0 argument produces the
  conclusion; the source's own sheaf-level form is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_quasicoherentEquivalence`, proved from
  this one in the same file.  What is NOT proved here is the general quasi-compact
  quasi-separated case; its local form, steps 3 to 8 of the source's argument, is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation`, and
  what remains beyond that is step 2 and the gluing step 9 that the source itself omits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
If `X` and `Y` are affine schemes and `F : QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` is an equivalence, then there
are an isomorphism of schemes `f : Y ≅ X` and an invertible sheaf `L` of `𝒪_Y`-modules such
that `F` is inverse image along `f` followed by `- ⊗_{𝒪_Y} L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
    (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) [F.IsEquivalence] :
    ∃ (f : Y ≅ X) (L : SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf),
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2 L ∧
        Nonempty (F ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf) ≅
          pullbackTensorFunctor f.hom L)
declarations.comment:
affine case: for `X` and `Y` affine.  The invertible object is a sheaf of
  `𝒪_Y`-modules, invertible in the sense of Tag 01CS
  (`Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible`), and the tensoring is `- ⊗_{𝒪_Y} L`.  Two deviations
  from the source statement.  First, the general quasi-compact quasi-separated case is not
  proved; its local form, steps 3 to 8 of the source's argument, is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation`,
  which quotes this theorem for its affine input, and what remains beyond that is step 2 (the
  existence of a finitely presented module supported on the complement of a given affine open)
  and the gluing step 9 that the source itself omits.  Second, the comparison of functors is
  stated after
  forgetting quasi-coherence, i.e. between functors into all `𝒪_Y`-modules, so that the
  statement does not depend on quasi-coherence being stable under inverse image and tensor
  product; since the inclusion of the quasi-coherent modules is fully faithful and
  quasi-coherence is invariant under isomorphism, nothing of the source's content is lost

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPJ.**  Let `X` and `Y` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes
and let `e : QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence of their categories of quasi-coherent
modules.  Then there are an isomorphism of schemes `g : Y ≅ X` and an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module
`M` with `e(𝓕) ≅ g^*𝓕 ⊗ M`, naturally in the quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕`.

The module is `e(𝒪_X)`; the isomorphism is the one glued from the reconstruction charts.  As in
the affine case the comparison of functors is stated after forgetting quasi-coherence, between
functors into all `𝒪_Y`-modules, which loses nothing because the inclusion of the quasi-coherent
modules is fully faithful and quasi-coherence is invariant under isomorphism.

Nothing is assumed beyond the equivalence and quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the
two schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (e : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    ∃ (g : Y ≅ X) (M : Y.Modules),
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2 M ∧
        Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf) ≅
          pullbackTensorFunctor g.hom M)
declarations.comment: the tag IN FULL, for `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated: an equivalence of the categories of quasi-coherent modules gives an isomorphism of schemes `g : Y ≅ X`, an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `M`, and a NATURAL isomorphism `e(𝓕) ≅ g^*𝓕 ⊗ M`. No cover, no affineness and no further hypothesis of any kind beyond qcqs. The scheme half is `exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` and the module half `isInvertible_map_quasicoherentUnit_of_quasicoherentEquivalence`, both already unconditional; what is new is the comparison of functors, which the Stacks source dismisses with "We omit the details".  It is glued from the per-chart comparisons `chartComparisonIso` by `exists_natIso_of_chartComparison`, whose agreement hypothesis is discharged by the rigidity `natIso_eq_of_app_unit_eq_of_iso` once the comparisons are normalised at `𝒪_X`; the normalisation is `chartComparisonIso_hom_app_quasicoherentUnit` and it is automatic, because the module is `e(𝒪_X)` and the identification of its restriction with the chart's `L` is `restrictMapUnitIsoOfChartIso`, built from the same `α` and `β`. As in the affine case the comparison is stated after forgetting quasi-coherence, between functors into all `𝒪_Y`-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPJ in its global form.**  Let `X` and `Y` be quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes and let `e : QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence.  Let `U i` be an
affine open cover of `X` and let `G i` be a finitely presented quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose
support is the complement of `U i`.  Then there are opens `V i ⊆ Y` which **cover `Y`** and are
each affine and quasi-compact, and for each `i` an equivalence `F_i : QCoh(𝒪_{U i}) ≌
QCoh(𝒪_{V i})` compatible with `e` and the two restrictions, an isomorphism of schemes
`f_i : V i ≅ U i` and an invertible sheaf `L_i` of `𝒪_{V i}`-modules such that `F_i` is inverse
image along `f_i` followed by `- ⊗_{𝒪_{V i}} L_i`.

The chart `V i` is the complement of the support of `e.functor.obj (G i)`, as in
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation`; what
is new here is that these opens cover `Y`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenCover_of_supportedCorrespondence`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hUaff : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hUcover : IsOpenCover U)
    (G : ι → (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
    [∀ i, SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (G i).obj]
    (hG : ∀ i, supportSet (G i).obj = (U i : Set X)ᶜ) :
    ∃ V : ι → Y.Opens, IsOpenCover V ∧
      ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i) ∧ IsCompact (V i : Set Y) ∧
        ∃ (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (U i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
          (f : (V i).toScheme ≅ (U i).toScheme)
          (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf),
          F.IsEquivalence ∧
            Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (V i).toScheme.presheaf
              (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 L ∧
            Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ quasicoherentRestriction (V i).ι ≅
              quasicoherentRestriction (U i).ι ⋙ F) ∧
            Nonempty (F ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
                (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ≅
              pullbackTensorFunctor f.hom L)
declarations.comment: the GLOBAL form — `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, no affineness and no restriction to a single open `U`. Steps 3 to 8 together with the covering assertion of step 9, which is PROVED here and no longer hypothesised: `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenCover_of_supportedCorrespondence` shows the opens `V_U` cover `Y`, and `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_gluedQuasicoherentFunctor_restrictIso` runs the functor-level gluing with that hypothesis discharged. The module `G` of step 2 is a hypothesis here, one per member of the cover; it need not be, and `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isAffineOpenCover` below is this statement with `G` and `hG` deleted, the module produced instead as `𝒪_X/I` for the Tag 01PH ideal. The per-chart data IS glued downstream: the `f_U` into one isomorphism `Y ≅ X` by `exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalSchemeIso.lean`) and the `L_U` into one invertible `𝒪_Y`-module by `exists_isOpenCover_invertibleModule_restrictIso_of_isAffineOpenCover` (`ReconstructionGlobalModule.lean`). The single natural isomorphism `e(F) ≅ g^*F ⊗ M` comparing `e` with that glued pair — the stated conclusion of 0GPJ, which the source dismisses with "We omit the details" — is `exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalComparison.lean`). As in the affine case the comparison of functors is stated after forgetting quasi-coherence, between functors into all `𝒪_V`-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isAffineOpenCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPJ in its global form, with step 2 discharged.**  Let `X` and `Y` be
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, let `e : QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence and
let `U i` be an affine open cover of `X`.  Then there are opens `V i ⊆ Y` which **cover `Y`** and
are each affine and quasi-compact, and for each `i` an equivalence
`F_i : QCoh(𝒪_{U i}) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_{V i})` compatible with `e` and the two restrictions, an
isomorphism of schemes `f_i : V i ≅ U i` and an invertible sheaf `L_i` of `𝒪_{V i}`-modules such
that `F_i` is inverse image along `f_i` followed by `- ⊗_{𝒪_{V i}} L_i`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation` with its
hypotheses `G` and `hG` *deleted*: the modules are produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinitePresentation_supportSet_eq_compl`.  Only the affine open cover
of `X` is given.

The module family is kept opaque, by `choose` against the single-index statement above, for the
reason recorded in the implementation notes: handing over an explicit composite instead makes
the conclusion unfold definitionally once per index and per conjunct.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isAffineOpenCover {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hUaff : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hUcover : IsOpenCover U) :
    ∃ V : ι → Y.Opens, IsOpenCover V ∧
      ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i) ∧ IsCompact (V i : Set Y) ∧
        ∃ (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (U i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
          (f : (V i).toScheme ≅ (U i).toScheme)
          (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf),
          F.IsEquivalence ∧
            Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (V i).toScheme.presheaf
              (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 L ∧
            Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ quasicoherentRestriction (V i).ι ≅
              quasicoherentRestriction (U i).ι ⋙ F) ∧
            Nonempty (F ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
                (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ≅
              pullbackTensorFunctor f.hom L)
declarations.comment: the GLOBAL form with step 2 DISCHARGED — `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, an affine open cover `U i` of `X`, and no module hypothesised. The `G i` is `𝒪_X/I i` for the finite type ideal sheaf `I i` of Tag 01PH, finitely presented by `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheafQuotient.isFinitePresentation_structureQuotient` and with support `V(I i)` by `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheafQuotient.supp_structureQuotient`. Steps 2 to 8 and the covering assertion of step 9 are therefore all proved. The per-chart data IS glued downstream: the `f_i` into one isomorphism `Y ≅ X` by `exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalSchemeIso.lean`) and the `L_i` into one invertible `𝒪_Y`-module by `exists_isOpenCover_invertibleModule_restrictIso_of_isAffineOpenCover` (`ReconstructionGlobalModule.lean`). The single natural isomorphism `e(F) ≅ g^*F ⊗ M` comparing `e` with that glued pair — the stated conclusion of 0GPJ, which the Stacks source dismisses with "We omit the details" — is `exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalComparison.lean`). As in the affine case the comparison of functors is stated after forgetting quasi-coherence, between functors into all `𝒪_V`-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isInvertible_map_quasicoherentUnit_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The image of the structure sheaf under an equivalence of categories of quasi-coherent
modules is invertible.**  Let `X` and `Y` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes and let
`e : QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence.  Then `e(𝒪_X)` is an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module.

Invertibility of a module on a scheme is local on the base
(`Stacks.Modules.isInvertible_of_isInvertible_restrict_isOpenCover`), the opens `V i` of the
reconstruction cover `Y`, and over each of them `e(𝒪_X)` is the invertible sheaf `L i` of that
chart by `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictMapUnitIsoOfChartIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertible_map_quasicoherentUnit_of_quasicoherentEquivalence :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2
      (e.functor.obj (quasicoherentUnit X)).obj
declarations.comment: the MODULE half of the tag's conclusion, unconditionally: `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and an equivalence `e` of their categories of quasi-coherent modules make `e(𝒪_X)` an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module. No cover, no affineness and no further hypothesis of any kind beyond qcqs. This identifies WHICH module the tag's `L` is and proves it invertible: were the tag's comparison `e(F) ≅ f^*F ⊗ L` available, `F = 𝒪_X` would give `L ≅ f^*𝒪_X ⊗ L ≅ e(𝒪_X)`, so no other module can serve. The statement is not an existential — `∃ L, IsInvertible L` is satisfied by `𝒪_Y` and would say nothing — it names the module. The per-chart invertible sheaves `L i` of the reconstruction are its restrictions (`restrictMapUnitIsoOfChartIso`), which is also what supplies the transition data the gluing of `ReconstructionGluedModule.lean:197` asks for; that gluing run on the reconstruction's own charts is `exists_isOpenCover_invertibleModule_restrictIso_of_isAffineOpenCover` below. The SCHEME half is `exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalSchemeIso.lean:324`). The comparison of functors — 0GPJ also asserts `e(F) ≅ f^*F ⊗ L` naturally in `F` — is NOT produced here: it is `exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalComparison.lean`), glued from the per-chart `chartComparisonIso` (`ReconstructionGlobalNatIso.lean`) by `exists_natIso_of_chartComparison` (`ReconstructionChartGlue.lean`), the two comparisons over a common affine open being made equal by the rigidity `natIso_eq_of_app_unit_eq_of_iso` (`ReconstructionChartRigidity.lean`) once they are normalised at `𝒪_X` (`chartComparisonIso_hom_app_quasicoherentUnit`). Nothing below assumes any of it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_invertibleModule_restrictIso_of_isAffineOpenCover
declarations.doc:
**The global form of [Stacks, Tag 0GPJ] with the per-chart invertible sheaves glued into one
invertible module.**  Let `X` and `Y` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, let
`e : QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence and let `U i` be an affine open cover of `X`.
Then there are opens `V i` covering `Y`, each affine, and for each `i` an equivalence
`F i : QCoh(𝒪_{U i}) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_{V i})` compatible with `e` and the two restrictions, an
isomorphism of schemes `f i : V i ≅ U i` and an invertible sheaf `L i` of `𝒪_{V i}`-modules with
`F i` inverse image along `f i` followed by `- ⊗ L i` — **and a single invertible `𝒪_Y`-module
`M` whose restriction to each `V i` is `L i`**.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isAffineOpenCover` with the
families pulled out of the per-index existential, together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invertibleModule_of_isOpenCover_of_overlapCompatible` run on those
charts.  The three transition hypotheses of the gluing are
`AlgebraicGeometry.transOfRestrictIso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.transOfRestrictIso_resLE` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.transOfRestrictIso_trans` for the module `e(𝒪_X)`, which restricts to each
`L i` by `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictMapUnitIsoOfChartIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenCover_invertibleModule_restrictIso_of_isAffineOpenCover {κ : Type u}
    (U : κ → X.Opens) (hUaff : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) (hUcover : IsOpenCover U) :
    ∃ (V : κ → Y.Opens)
      (F : ∀ i, (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (U i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
      (f : ∀ i, (V i).toScheme ≅ (U i).toScheme)
      (L : ∀ i, SheafOfModules.{u} (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (M : Y.Modules),
      IsOpenCover V ∧ (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i)) ∧ (∀ i, (F i).IsEquivalence) ∧
        (∀ i, Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (V i).toScheme.presheaf
          (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 (L i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ quasicoherentRestriction (V i).ι ≅
          quasicoherentRestriction (U i).ι ⋙ F i)) ∧
        (∀ i, Nonempty (F i ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (V i).toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ≅
          pullbackTensorFunctor (f i).hom (L i))) ∧
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2 M ∧
        ∀ i, Nonempty (Scheme.Modules.restrict M (V i).ι ≅ L i)
declarations.comment: the GLOBAL form with the per-chart invertible sheaves GLUED into one invertible `𝒪_Y`-module: `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, an affine open cover `U i` of `X`, and no further hypothesis. The chart data is `exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isAffineOpenCover` (`ReconstructionGlobalForm.lean:236`) with the families pulled out of the per-index existential; what is new is the last conjunct, a SINGLE invertible `𝒪_Y`-module restricting to every `L i`. It is `exists_invertibleModule_of_isOpenCover_of_overlapCompatible` (`ReconstructionGluedModule.lean:197`) run on these charts, its transition data being `transOfRestrictIso` for the module `e(𝒪_X)`, which restricts to each `L i` by `restrictMapUnitIsoOfChartIso`. The SCHEME half of the tag is `exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalSchemeIso.lean:324`). The comparison of functors `e(F) ≅ f^*F ⊗ M`, naturally in `F`, is NOT produced here: it is `exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalComparison.lean`), and it is stated for the module `e(𝒪_X)` rather than for the `M` glued here — taking `e(𝒪_X)` is what makes the per-chart comparisons agree at `𝒪_X`, because then the identification of its restriction with `L i` is `restrictMapUnitIsoOfChartIso`, built from the same `α i` and `β i`. Nothing in this statement assumes it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The scheme half of [Stacks, Tag 0GPJ] with no cover hypothesised.**  Two quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes with equivalent categories of quasi-coherent modules are isomorphic.

This is the statement above with the affine open cover of `X` deleted: `X` is covered by its own
affine opens, `AlgebraicGeometry.iSup_affineOpens_eq_top`, and that family is indexed by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.affineOpens`, a type in the same universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_schemeIso_of_quasicoherentEquivalence {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (e : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory) :
    Nonempty (Y ≅ X)
declarations.comment: the SCHEME HALF of the tag's conclusion, unconditionally: `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and an equivalence of their categories of quasi-coherent modules give an isomorphism of schemes `Y ≅ X`. No cover, no affineness, no invertible module and no further hypothesis of any kind beyond qcqs. This is the step the Stacks source dismisses with "We omit the details", carried out: the charts are matched (`ReconstructionGlobalForm.lean`), they cover `Y` (`ReconstructionCover.lean:164`), they agree on overlaps in both directions (`ReconstructionOverlapCompatible.lean:256`, `ReconstructionGlobalSchemeIso.lean:223`) because the matched pair is rigid (`ReconstructionRigidity.lean:141`), and they glue (`ReconstructionGluedIso.lean:113`). The MODULE half — 0GPJ also asserts a single invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `L` with `e(F) ≅ f^*F ⊗ L` — is NOT produced here: it is `isInvertible_map_quasicoherentUnit_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalModule.lean`), the module being `e(𝒪_X)`, and the comparison of functors is `exists_natIso_pullbackTensorFunctor_of_quasicoherentEquivalence` (`ReconstructionGlobalComparison.lean`). Nothing in this statement assumes either

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPJ, steps 3 to 8: the local form of the proposition.**  Let `X` and
`Y` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes and let `e : QCoh(𝒪_X) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_Y)` be an
equivalence.  Let `U ⊆ X` be an affine open and let `G` be a finitely presented quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module whose support is the complement of `U`.  Then there is a quasi-compact open
`V ⊆ Y` — namely the complement of the support of `e.functor.obj G` — which is affine, and there
are an equivalence `F_U : QCoh(𝒪_U) ≌ QCoh(𝒪_V)` compatible with `e` and the two restrictions, an
isomorphism of schemes `f_U : V ≅ U` and an invertible sheaf `L_U` of `𝒪_V`-modules such that
`F_U` is inverse image along `f_U` followed by `- ⊗_{𝒪_V} L_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isFinitePresentation (U : X.Opens)
    (hUaff : IsAffineOpen U)
    (G : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (R := X.ringCatSheaf) G.obj]
    (hG : supportSet G.obj = (U : Set X)ᶜ) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen V ∧ IsCompact (V : Set Y) ∧
      ∃ (F : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ⥤
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
        (f : V.toScheme ≅ U.toScheme) (L : SheafOfModules.{u} V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf),
        F.IsEquivalence ∧
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible V.toScheme.presheaf V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.2 L ∧
          Nonempty (e.functor ⋙ quasicoherentRestriction V.ι ≅
            quasicoherentRestriction U.ι ⋙ F) ∧
          Nonempty (F ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι
              (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) ≅
            pullbackTensorFunctor f.hom L)
declarations.comment: steps 3 to 8 only: the statement LOCALIZED at one affine open `U ⊆ X`, with the module `G` of step 2 given as a hypothesis. This is the per-chart building block; the statement over a whole cover is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenCover_schemeIso_invertibleSheaf_of_isAffineOpenCover`, where the covering of `Y` is proved (`AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenCover_of_supportedCorrespondence`) and `G` is produced rather than hypothesised, so nothing in this clause is left open by this file alone. Step 9's descent datum is available too: `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictionSquareFunctor` makes `F_U` explicit with `rfl` section formulas (the localization lift has no formula on sections, which is why it is rebuilt), and `AlgebraicGeometry.ReconstructionGlue.glueData` is a complete `FunctorGlueData`, all five fields, its covering hypothesis discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_gluedQuasicoherentFunctor_restrictIso`. What remains open for 0GPJ as a whole is the gluing of the per-chart `f_U` and `L_U` into a single isomorphism `Y ≅ X` and a single invertible `𝒪_Y`-module, which the source dismisses with "We omit the details".  As in the affine case the comparison of functors is stated after forgetting quasi-coherence, between functors into all `𝒪_V`-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentModuleFunctors.exists_iso_pullbackTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPK.** Let `X` and `Y` be Noetherian schemes and let
`F : Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence of categories. Then there are an isomorphism of
schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` and an invertible `𝒪_Y`-module `ℒ` with `F(𝓕) = f^*𝓕 ⊗ ℒ`, naturally in the
coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕`. The corresponding description of an equivalence of the categories of
quasi-coherent modules is Tag 0GPJ, available here as
`exists_iso_pullbackTensor_quasicoherent`; the coherent case follows from it by extending `F` to
the quasi-coherent modules. Nothing is hypothesised.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_pullbackTensor {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (F : CoherentModules X.ringCatSheaf ⥤ CoherentModules Y.ringCatSheaf) [F.IsEquivalence] :
    ∃ (f : Y ≅ X) (L : Y.Modules),
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2 L ∧
      Nonempty (coherentToModules X ⋙ pullbackTensor f.hom L ≅ F ⋙ coherentToModules Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentModuleFunctors.exists_iso_pullbackTensor_over_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GPL.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `X` and `Y` be Noetherian
schemes over `R`, and let `F : Coh(𝒪_X) ⥤ Coh(𝒪_Y)` be an equivalence of categories which is
linear over `R`. Then the isomorphism of schemes `f : Y ≅ X` and the invertible `𝒪_Y`-module
`ℒ` of Tag 0GPK with `F(𝓕) = f^*𝓕 ⊗ ℒ` may be chosen with `f` a morphism of schemes over `R`,
that is with `f ≫ (X → Spec R) = (Y → Spec R)`.

Nothing is hypothesised. Tag 0GPK is unconditional, so the content here is only the refinement
over `R`: `R`-linearity of `F` forces `f` to be a morphism over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_pullbackTensor_over_base (X Y : Over (Spec (.of R)))
    [IsNoetherian X.left] [IsNoetherian Y.left]
    (F : CoherentModules X.left.ringCatSheaf ⥤ CoherentModules Y.left.ringCatSheaf)
    [F.IsEquivalence] :
    letI : Linear R (SheafOfModules.{u} X.left.ringCatSheaf) := modulesLinear R X
    letI : Linear R (SheafOfModules.{u} Y.left.ringCatSheaf) := modulesLinear R Y
    F.Linear R →
      ∃ (f : Y.left ≅ X.left) (L : Y.left.Modules),
        Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.left.presheaf Y.left.ringCatSheaf.2 L ∧
        Nonempty (coherentToModules X.left ⋙ pullbackTensor f.hom L ≅
          F ⋙ coherentToModules Y.left) ∧
        f.hom ≫ X.hom = Y.hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidQuasicoherentPullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GPM.**  Let `f : (U, R, s, t, c) ⟶ (U', R', s', t', c')` be a morphism of
groupoids in algebraic spaces over `A` such that `f : U ⟶ U'` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, the square formed by `f : R ⟶ R'`, the target morphisms `t, t'` and
`f : U ⟶ U'` is cartesian, and `s'` is flat.  Then pushforward `(ℱ, α) ↦ (f_*ℱ, f_*α)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidQuasicoherentPushforward`) is a functor from the
quasi-coherent modules on `(U, R, s, t, c)` to those on `(U', R', s', t', c')`, and it is right
adjoint to the inverse image functor of Stacks 0442
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.groupoidQuasicoherentPullback`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentModule.forgetAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GPP.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces with `s` (and hence
`t = s ∘ i`) flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.  For a quasi-coherent `𝒪_U`-module `𝒢` the
module `s_*t^*𝒢` carries a canonical isomorphism `α : t^*s_*t^*𝒢 ⟶ s^*s_*t^*𝒢` making
`(s_*t^*𝒢, α)` a quasi-coherent module on `(U, R, s, t, c)`; this defines the functor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentModule.cofree`, and it is right adjoint to the forgetful
functor `(ℱ, β) ↦ ℱ`.
declarations.statement: def forgetAdjunction : forgetQuasicoherent G ⊣ cofree G hsflat hsqc hsqs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentModule.forgetAdjunction_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GPQ.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces with `s` flat,
quasi-compact and quasi-separated (then so is `t = s ∘ i`), and let
`forgetQuasicoherent G ⊣ cofree G` be the adjunction of Stacks 0GPP between the forgetful functor
`(ℱ, β) ↦ ℱ` and `𝒢 ↦ (s_*t^*𝒢, α)`.  The unit of this adjunction at a quasi-coherent module
`(ℱ, β)` on the groupoid is

`ℱ ⟶ s_*s^*ℱ ⟶ s_*t^*ℱ`,

the unit of the adjunction `s^* ⊣ s_*` at `ℱ` followed by the direct image along `s` of the
inverse of `β : t^*ℱ ⟶ s^*ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetAdjunction_unit_app (M : QuasicoherentModule B S hS G) :
    ((forgetAdjunction G hsflat hsqc hsqs).unit.app M).hom =
      (modulePullbackAdjunction B S hS G.source).unit.app M.F.obj ≫
        (modulePushforward B S hS G.source).map (inv M.alpha)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_intersectionPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GPR.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, let
`F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `G` be an `𝒪_Y`-module and let `φ : G ⟶ f^*F` be a map
of `𝒪_Y`-modules.  Assume that `φ` is injective, that `f` is quasi-compact, quasi-separated,
flat and surjective, that `X` and `Y` are locally Noetherian, and that `G` is coherent.  Then
`F ∩ f_*G`, the fibre product of `F ⟶ f_*f^*F ⟵ f_*G`, is a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.

The two direct images `f_*G` and `f_*f^*F` are quasi-coherent by Stacks 03M9, so `F ∩ f_*G` is
quasi-coherent.  Its inverse image `f^*(F ∩ f_*G)` is a quasi-coherent submodule of `G`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mono_intersectionPushforwardAdj`, hence coherent by Stacks 07UD, and
coherence descends along `f` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_isCoherent_modulePullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_intersectionPushforward (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (φ : G ⟶ (modulePullback B S hS f).obj F) (mono : Mono φ)
    (quasiCompact : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom)
    (quasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (flat : IsFlat B S hS f.hom) (surjective : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom)
    (X_noetherian : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (Y_noetherian : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (F_qcoh : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (G_coherent : IsCoherent B S hS Y.1 Y.2 G) :
    IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 (intersectionPushforward B S hS f φ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.QuasicoherentModule.exists_filtered_diagram_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GPS.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `B` such that
`U` and `R` are Noetherian and `s` and `t` are flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.  Then every
quasi-coherent module `(ℱ, β)` on `(U, R, s, t, c)` is a filtered colimit of coherent modules: it
is the colimit of a diagram, indexed by a filtered category, of quasi-coherent modules on
`(U, R, s, t, c)` whose underlying `𝒪_U`-modules are coherent.

The diagram is indexed by the coherent submodules `ℋ` of `ℱ`, and its term at `ℋ` is the fibre
product of the unit `(ℱ, β) ⟶ (s_*t^*ℱ, α)` of Stacks 0GPP with `(s_*t^*ℋ, α) ⟶ (s_*t^*ℱ, α)`.
By the description of the unit in Stacks 0GPQ its underlying module is `ℱ ∩ s_*t^*ℋ`, which is
coherent by Stacks 0GPR.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_filtered_diagram_isCoherent (terminal_mem : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (objects_noetherian : IsNoetherian B S hS terminal_mem G.objects.1)
    (arrows_noetherian : IsNoetherian B S hS terminal_mem G.arrows.1)
    (source_flat : IsFlat B S hS G.source.hom)
    (source_quasiCompact : IsQuasiCompact B S hS G.source.hom)
    (source_quasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS G.source.hom)
    (target_flat : IsFlat B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_target_quasiCompact : IsQuasiCompact B S hS G.target.hom)
    (_target_quasiSeparated : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS G.target.hom)
    (M : QuasicoherentModule B S hS G) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentModule B S hS G) (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj M),
      (∀ i, IsCoherent B S hS G.objects.1 G.objects.2 (D.obj i).F.obj) ∧
        Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk M φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne
declarations.doc:
Isomorphism classes of square-zero extensions of an `A`-algebra `B` by a `B`-module `N`
are canonically equivalent to `Ext¹_B(NL_{B/A}, N)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] :
    SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.IsomorphismClasses.{uA, uA, uB, uN,
        max uB uN}
        (algebraExtensionProblem A B N) ≃
      naiveCotangentExtOne A B N

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne_sub
declarations.doc:
The classification sends the difference between two square-zero extensions to the
canonical obstruction class comparing them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne_sub
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    (X Y : (algebraExtensionProblem A B N).CompatibleExtension.{max uB uN}) :
    squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne A B N
        (Quotient.mk
          (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid
            (algebraExtensionProblem A B N)) Y) -
      squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne A B N
      (Quotient.mk
        (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid
          (algebraExtensionProblem A B N)) X) =
      (obstructionClass (comparisonDiagram X Y)).1
declarations.comment: canonical difference

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne_split_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The canonical classification sends the split square-zero extension to zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne_split_eq_zero
    (A : Type uA) (B : Type uB) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (N : Type uN) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N] :
    squareZeroAlgebraExtensionClassesEquivExtOne A B N
      (Quotient.mk
        (SquareZeroExtensionProblem.CompatibleExtension.isomorphicSetoid
          (algebraExtensionProblem A B N)) (splitAlgebraExtension A B N)) = 0
declarations.comment: split extension

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.exists_lift_and_cotangentMap_to_squareZeroKernel
declarations.doc:
A polynomial presentation of an algebra lifts through every square-zero extension, and the
restriction of the lift to the relation ideal factors `B`-linearly through `J / J²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_and_cotangentMap_to_squareZeroKernel
    {ι : Type w} (P : Algebra.Generators A B ι) (E : Algebra.Extension A B)
    (hE : E.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) :
    letI := Algebra.Extension.squareZeroKerModule E hE
    ∃ (f : P.toExtension.Hom E) (l : P.toExtension.Cotangent →ₗ[B] E.ker),
      ∀ x : P.toExtension.ker,
        (l (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.mk x) : E.Ring) = f.toRingHom x
declarations.comment: lift_and_factor

declarations.name: Stacks.Deformation.extensionClass_eq_conormalCokernelClass
declarations.doc:
