declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAffineHom_of_comp_of_isAffineHom_relativeDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQE.** Let

```text
  𝒳 ----f----> 𝒴
    \         /
     a       b
      \     /
       >  𝒵 <
```

be a 2-commutative triangle of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`, the commutativity being
the 2-isomorphism `comm : a ≅ f ≫ b`. If `a` is affine and the relative diagonal `Δ_b` is affine
in the sense of Properties of Stacks, Section 04XB, then `f` is affine.

*Reading the statement.* The unqualified `IsAffineHom`, in the hypothesis `ha` on `a` and in the
conclusion on `f`, elaborates to `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom`, the notion
of an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks of **Stacks 0CHQ** (registered in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.AffineMorphism`). It is by definition the conjunction
`IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS q.hom.hom ∧ Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS q.hom` for `q = a`
and for `q = f`, so it includes representability by algebraic spaces: `a` is assumed, and `f` is
concluded, to be representable by algebraic spaces and affine in the sense of Stacks 04XB, exactly
as in the source. The 1-morphism `relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS b` is the relative
diagonal `Δ_b : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴 ×_{b, 𝒵, b} 𝒴`, `y ↦ (y, y, id)`. The hypothesis `hΔ` on it is written
with the qualified `Stack.IsAffineHom`, the condition of Stacks 04XB alone, without
representability; it is weaker than the source's hypothesis that `Δ_b` is affine, and loses
nothing, since `Δ_b` is representable by algebraic spaces unconditionally by Stacks 04XS part (1)
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_relativeDiagonal_of_isAlgebraicStack`).

This is the source's proof. The 1-morphism `f` is 2-isomorphic to `Γ_f ≫ pr₂`, where
`Γ_f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴` is the graph of `f` over `𝒵` (Stacks 050I) and
`pr₂ : 𝒳 ×_𝒵 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒴` is the second projection of the canonical 2-fibre product of the cospan
`(a, b)`. The projection is a base change of `a`, hence affine by **Stacks 0CHR**; the graph is
affine by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAffineHom_graph`, which carries the hypothesis on `Δ_b`
along the base-change square of **Stacks 04Z1**; and **Stacks 0CHS** composes the two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_of_comp_of_isAffineHom_relativeDiagonal
    {𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (a : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒵) (b : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒵) (comm : a ≅ f ≫ b)
    (ha : IsAffineHom B S hS a)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B S hS (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B S hS b).hom) :
    IsAffineHom B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_iff_restrictMapToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQF, isomorphisms.**  Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `x_i : U_i → 𝒳`, `i ∈ I`,
flat objects with `∐ x_i : ∐ U_i → 𝒳` surjective.  An arrow `φ` of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is an
isomorphism if and only if each restriction `φ_i = φ|_{(U_i)_{étale}}` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_iff_restrictMapToSmallEtale :
    IsIso φ ↔ ∀ i, IsIso (restrictMapToSmallEtale B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        (x i)
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _).map φ.hom.val))
declarations.comment: isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.epi_iff_restrictMapToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQF, surjectivity.**  Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `x_i : U_i → 𝒳`,
`i ∈ I`, flat objects with `∐ x_i : ∐ U_i → 𝒳` surjective.  An arrow `φ` of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is
surjective (an epimorphism of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`) if and only if each restriction
`φ_i = φ|_{(U_i)_{étale}}` is surjective as a map of sheaves on `(U_i)_{étale}`, i.e. locally
surjective for the étale topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_iff_restrictMapToSmallEtale :
    Epi φ ↔ ∀ i, Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (SmallEtale.topology E (𝒳.val.val.p.obj (x i)).left.1
        (contains_base B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (x i)))
      (restrictMapToSmallEtale B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (x i)
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _).map φ.hom.val))
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mono_iff_restrictMapToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQF, injectivity.**  Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `x_i : U_i → 𝒳`, `i ∈ I`,
flat objects with `∐ x_i : ∐ U_i → 𝒳` surjective.  An arrow `φ` of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is injective (a
monomorphism of the abelian category `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`) if and only if each restriction
`φ_i = φ|_{(U_i)_{étale}}` is injective on all sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_iff_restrictMapToSmallEtale :
    Mono φ ↔ ∀ i V, Function.Injective ((restrictMapToSmallEtale B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (x i) ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf _).map φ.hom.val)).app V)
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictedFppfModulesHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQH.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact (`hqc`), quasi-separated (`hqs`)
1-morphism of algebraic stacks which is representable by algebraic spaces (`hrep`). Let `ℱ` be in
`LQCoh^{fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` (`hF`), and let `y : V ⟶ 𝒴` be an object of `𝒴` over a scheme `V`. Then:

* the 2-fibre product `U = V ×_𝒴 𝒳` is represented by an algebraic space;
* for every such presentation `eU` of `U` by an algebraic space, with `f' : U ⟶ V` the base
  change of `f` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.baseChangeSpacesHom`), and for every `i`,
  `(Rⁱf_*ℱ)|_{V_étale} ≅ Rⁱf'_{small,*}(ℱ|_{U_étale})`.

Here `Rⁱf_*` is the higher direct image of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, in the fppf topology. `(-)|_{V_étale}` reads
an fppf module on the étale site (`stackModulesEtaleComparison`), pulls it back along `y` and
restricts it to the small étale site of `V` (`π_{V,*}`, Stacks 073M). `(-)|_{U_étale}` does the
same along the projection `U ⟶ 𝒳`. `f'_{small,*}` is the direct image of the small étale sites
of the algebraic spaces `U` and `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictedFppfModulesHigherDirectImage {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS}
    (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hrep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom)
    (F : StackModules B S hS .fppf 𝒳) (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, t, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F)
    {V : BigFppfOver B S hS} (y : schemeStack.{u, t} B S hS V ⟶ 𝒴) :
    (∃ U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U ∧
      Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (U ⋙ typeToCat)).p)) ∧
    ∀ (U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
      (eU : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
        (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val.val.p
        (presheafOfCategories (U ⋙ typeToCat)).p) (i : ℕ),
      Nonempty ((AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules
          (Space.projectionRingedToposHom B S hS (yoneda.obj V)
            (schemeStack.{u, t} B S hS V).val.val.p
            (schemeStack.{u, t} B S hS V).val.isFiberedInGroupoids
            (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V) (schemeStackEquivalenceOver B S hS))).obj
          ((stackModuleInverseImage B S hS .etale y).obj
            ((stackModulesEtaleComparison B S hS 𝒴).obj
              ((fppfModulesHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj F))) ≅
        (Space.smallEtaleHigherDirectImage
            (baseChangeSpacesHom B S hS f y (yoneda.obj V) (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS V)
              (schemeStackEquivalenceOver B S hS) U hU eU) i).obj
          ((AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules
            (Space.projectionRingedToposHom B S hS U
              (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val.val.p
              (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).pt.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
              hU eU)).obj
            ((stackModuleInverseImage B S hS .etale
              (twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS f y).fst).obj
              ((stackModulesEtaleComparison B S hS 𝒳).obj F))))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, at the module universe u of the schemes: for f : X -> Y quasi-compact, quasi-separated and representable by algebraic spaces, F in LQCoh^fbc(O_X) (the flat base change property read on sheaves, Stacks 0762) and an object y : V -> Y over a scheme V, the 2-fibre product U = V x_Y X is an algebraic space, and for every presentation of it and every i, (R^i f_* F)|_{V_etale} = R^i f'_{small,*}(F|_{U_etale}), with R^i f_* the fppf higher direct image of Mod(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictedHigherDirectImageChartIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQH.** For an object `y : V ⟶ 𝒴` of `𝒴`, with `𝒱` the category fibred in
groupoids of that object, `𝒰 = 𝒱 ×_𝒴 𝒳` the 2-fibre product — presented by the *algebraic
space* `F = U`, because `f` is representable by algebraic spaces — and `f' : 𝒰 ⥤ 𝒱` the base
change of `f`, inducing a morphism `U ⟶ V` on presenting algebraic spaces
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.inducedAlgebraicSpacesHom`):

```text
(R^i f_* ℱ)|_{V_étale} ≅ R^i f'_{small,*}(ℱ|_{U_étale}),
```

naturally in the complex `ℱ` of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. On the left, `R^i f_* ℱ` is `H^i` of the total
right derived direct image `RfStack`, and `(-)|_{V_étale}` is inverse image along `𝒱 ⥤ 𝒴`
followed by the restriction `π_{V,*}` of Stacks 073M. On the right, `(-)|_{U_étale}` is derived
inverse image along `𝒰 ⥤ 𝒳` followed by `π_{U,*}`, and `R^i f'_{small,*}` is `H^i` of the total
right derived direct image `RfSpace` of the small étale sites of the algebraic spaces `U`
and `V`.

The chain is the source's: `hDg` and `bc` are its reduction to the representable case, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictedDerivedDirectImageIso` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedPushforwardOfExactCompHomologyFunctorIso` are its
appeal to Stacks 075N. See the implementation notes of this file for what each hypothesis is
and where the source's hypotheses on `f` and on `ℱ` are consumed.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictedHigherDirectImageChartIso
    (Dy : DerivedCategory
        (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS p𝒴 h𝒴 .etale).Modules ⥤
      DerivedCategory (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS q hq .etale).Modules)
    (Dy' : DerivedCategory
        (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS p𝒳 h𝒳 .etale).Modules ⥤
      DerivedCategory (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS p hp .etale).Modules)
    (i : ℤ)
    (hDy : Dy ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS q hq .etale).Modules i ≅
        DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS p𝒴 h𝒴 .etale).Modules i ⋙
          Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules
            (FibredSite.ringedToposMorphism B S hS q p𝒴 hq h𝒴 y hy .etale).toModulesHom)
    (bc : RfStack ⋙ Dy ≅ Dy' ⋙ Rf) :
    RfStack ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (FibredSite.associatedRingedTopos B S hS p𝒴 h𝒴 .etale).Modules i ⋙
        Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules
            (FibredSite.ringedToposMorphism B S hS q p𝒴 hq h𝒴 y hy .etale).toModulesHom ⋙
          RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules
            (projectionRingedToposHom B S hS G q hq hG eG) ≅
      Dy' ⋙ RingedToposHom.derivedPushforwardOfExact
            (projectionRingedToposHom B S hS F p hp hF eF) ⋙
        RfSpace ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ⟨G, hG⟩).Modules i
declarations.comment:
(R^i f_*F)|_{V_etale} = R^i f'_{small,*}(F|_{U_etale}) for the base change f' of
  f along an object y : V -> Y of Y, with U = V x_Y X an ALGEBRAIC SPACE (f is representable by
  algebraic spaces, so U need not be a scheme) and f'_{small,*} the direct image of the small
  etale sites of algebraic spaces; stated for every i and naturally in the complex of
  O_X-modules, with R^i the i-th cohomology of the total right derived direct image, which is
  what composes with Tag 075N. PROVED here from four inputs, two of which are themselves
  assumed, and all named: (1) `bc`, the BASE CHANGE isomorphism of the 2-cartesian square in
  derived form, which is Tag 075H -- carried in this library only for ABELIAN sheaves
  (`abelianHigherDirectImageBaseChangeIso`), the module-coefficient statement
  `nonempty_moduleHigherDirectImageBaseChangeIso` being itself conditional on a linearity
  hypothesis that is 075H's own module-coefficient assertion, so the module case is ASSUMED;
  (2) `hDg`, that the derived inverse image along the chart is computed degreewise, which is
  exactness of the inverse image of sheaves of modules; (3) Tag 075N, via
  `restrictedDerivedDirectImageIso`, which is now UNCONDITIONAL -- four inputs that carrier used
  to ask for are gone: Tag 073N itself, the 2-isomorphism of the two legs of the square, is
  PROVED, as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.restrictionRingedSquareInducedAlgebraicSpaces`, out of
  invertibility of the comparison map of equation 075M
  (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_restrictedDirectImageComparison`) and its structure-sheaf
  compatibility; exactness of the module-level restrictions pi_{U,*}, pi_{V,*} is PROVED, as
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_pushforwardModules_projectionRingedToposHom`;
  Tag 093Y for degreewise f_* is no longer needed, the unit of the exact pi_{V,*} being
  invertible; and the condition the composition criterion consumes at the leg f_small . pi_U is
  PROVED, as
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardComputesDerived_smallEtaleRingedToposHom`, out of the
  unconditional Tag 0D6E for a morphism of ringed topoi;
  and (4) the commutation of H^i with an exact direct image, which IS proved here
  (`derivedPushforwardOfExactCompHomologyFunctorIso`). The source's
  remaining hypotheses are consumed rather than restated: representability of f by algebraic
  spaces is `hF`,`eF`,`hG`,`eG`, the presentations that make the right-hand side exist;
  quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness enter only through `hf`; and F in LQCoh^fbc, whose
  role (Tag 0771 part (4)(a)) is to license computing R^i f_* in the etale topology, is built
  into the statement, every site here being the etale one, so the conclusion is stated for an
  arbitrary complex of O_X-modules and contains that case. The reduction of Tag 0771 part (3)
  is not needed and not used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.stacks0GQI
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQI.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`.  The
direct image restricts to a functor `f_* : LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineLqcohSheafFbcPushforward`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fppfModulesPushforward` on objects and morphisms by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineLqcohSheafFbcPushforwardCompιIso`), and

1. `f_*` is exact: a sequence of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` which is short exact in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` goes to a
   sequence short exact in `Mod(𝒪_𝒴)`;
2. `f_*` commutes with direct sums (indexed by any `ι : Type u`);
3. `Rⁱf_* F = 0` for every `i > 0` and `F` in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

Modules are on the fppf sites at the module universe `u` of the schemes; `LQCoh^fbc` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacks0GQI :
    (∀ Sq : ShortComplex (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory,
        (Sq.map (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).ι).ShortExact →
        (Sq.map (affineLqcohSheafFbcPushforward B E h S hS f hf ⋙
          (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒴).ι)).ShortExact) ∧
      (∀ ι : Type u, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι)
        (affineLqcohSheafFbcPushforward B E h S hS f hf)) ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < i → ∀ F : fppfModules B S hS 𝒳,
        lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F →
          IsZero ((fppfModulesHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj F))
declarations.comment: all three assertions, unconditionally, for an affine 1-morphism f, on the fppf sites at module universe u: f_* restricts to LQCoh^fbc(O_X) -> LQCoh^fbc(O_Y); (1) it is exact (short exact sequences of LQCoh^fbc, read in Mod, go to short exact sequences); (2) it commutes with direct sums; (3) R^i f_* F = 0 for i > 0 and F in LQCoh^fbc(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.shortExact_map_etaleModuleDirectImage_of_isZero_higherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Assertion (1) of Stacks 0GQI from assertion (3)**, which is the source's own deduction.

Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be an affine 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` and suppose the higher
direct images `Rⁱf_*` vanish in positive degrees on `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.  Then `f_*` carries a
short exact sequence of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_étale` whose outer terms lie in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` to
a short exact sequence of `𝒪_𝒴`-modules on `𝒴_étale`; that is, `f_*` is exact on
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

The vanishing in positive degrees is right acyclicity for `f_*`, by **Stacks 015C** and left
exactness of the right adjoint `f_*`, and **Stacks 015D** part (1) turns right acyclicity of the
outer terms into short exactness of the image.  Affineness is what discharges `hvan` and is
consumed nowhere in the deduction, which is why the binder is written `_hf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_etaleModuleDirectImage_of_isZero_higherDirectImage (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (_hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS f)
    (hvan : ∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < i → ∀ ℱ : etaleModulesOfHomSource B S hS f,
      IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChangeUnivLE B E h S hS
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
          (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) ℱ.val →
        IsZero ((etaleModuleHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj ℱ))
    (Sq : ShortComplex (etaleModulesOfHomSource B S hS f)) (hSq : Sq.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChangeUnivLE B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) Sq.X₁.val)
    (h₃ : IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChangeUnivLE B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) Sq.X₃.val) :
    (Sq.map (etaleModuleDirectImage B S hS f)).ShortExact
declarations.comment:
ASSERTION (1) ONLY, exactness of f_*, on the ETALE reading of LQCoh^fbc (Tag
0771 part (4)(a), the agreement with the source's default fppf reading, is absent here). It is
DEDUCED from assertion (3) exactly as the source deduces it, through Tag 015D, and
that deduction is the content of this declaration; the positive-degree vanishing is the
hypothesis hvan and is NOT proved anywhere in this repository. Assertion (2), commutation with
direct sums, and assertion (3) itself are NOT delivered by this file: see the module's
implementation notes, and note that `stacks0GQI_of_objectwise_of_preservesDirectSums`
deliberately carries NO attribute because its direct-sums conjunct is returned verbatim from
its own hypothesis. Stated as preservation of short exact sequences rather than as an exact
functor between the subcategories because Tag 0771 part (2) is absent, so LQCoh^fbc is not
known to be a weak Serre subcategory and hence not known abelian; only the OUTER terms are
required to lie in LQCoh^fbc, which is weaker than the source's hypothesis. AFFINENESS IS THE
BINDER `_hf` AND IS CONSUMED NOWHERE: given the vanishing, this implication holds for an
arbitrary 1-morphism, so it is a generalisation of the tag's assertion (1), not a weakening.
The blocking input for the rest is Tag 03DW, the etale-site analogue of Tag 01XC, which is
absent from the whole repository and also blocks Tags 073H and 03M9

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_lqcohFbcCoheratorPullbackComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQJ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a flat morphism of algebraic stacks.  Then
`Q_𝒳 ∘ f^* = f^* ∘ Q_𝒴`, with `Q_𝒳` and `Q_𝒴` the coherators of **Stacks 0778**: the canonical
comparison `f^* Q_𝒴(𝓕) ⟶ Q_𝒳(f^*𝓕)` is an isomorphism for every `𝓕` in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lqcohFbcCoheratorPullbackComparison (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) :
    IsIso (lqcohFbcCoheratorPullbackComparison B E h S hS f)
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison f^* ∘ Q_𝒴 ⟶ Q_𝒳 ∘ f^*, the mate of i ∘ f^* = f^* ∘ i under the adjunctions of Stacks 0778, is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_restrict_coheratorAdjunction_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQK.** Let `x` be an object of an algebraic stack `𝒳` lying over a scheme `U` such
that `x : U → 𝒳` is flat, and let `𝓕` be in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.  Then `Q(𝓕)|_{U_ét} = 𝓕|_{U_ét}`:
the restriction to the small étale site of `U` of the adjunction map `Q(𝓕) ⟶ 𝓕` of the coherator
of **Stacks 0778** is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_restrict_coheratorAdjunction_counit (F : Stack.fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F)
    (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hx : flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val x) :
    IsIso ((restrictModuleFunctorToSmallEtale B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids x (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).map
        ((coheratorAdjunction B S hS 𝒳).counit.app F).val)
declarations.comment: Q(F)|_{U_ét} = F|_{U_ét} for x : U → 𝒳 flat and F in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳): the restriction of the adjunction map Q(F) → F to U_ét is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLimitKernelForkCoherator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (3), the kernel in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.** For a map `φ : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓖` of
quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack, `Q(Ker(i φ))`, the coherator of the kernel computed
in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, with its map to `𝓕`, is the kernel of `φ` in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.comment: part (3), the second half: Q(Ker φ), with its map to 𝓕, is the kernel of φ in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), for the coherator Q of Stacks 0778

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.lqcohSheafFbc_kernel_quasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (3), the kernel in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.** For a map `φ : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓖` of quasi-coherent
modules on an algebraic stack, the kernel of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` lies in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`, `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` being a weak Serre subcategory containing `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
(**Stacks 0771** (2)). Its coherator is the kernel of `φ` in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isLimitKernelForkCoherator`).
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbc_kernel_quasicoherentInclusion {F G : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳}
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳
      (kernel ((quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).map φ))
declarations.comment: part (3), the first half: the kernel computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of a map of quasi-coherent modules lies in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.lqcohSheafFbc_image_quasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (2), corrected, the image in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.** For a map `φ : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓖` of
quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack, the image of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` lies in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`: it is the kernel of `𝓖 ⟶ Coker(φ)`. It need not be quasi-coherent: part (2)
as printed is refuted by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ImageCounterexample.not_forall_isQuasicoherentOnSite_image`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbc_image_quasicoherentInclusion {F G : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳}
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳
      (Abelian.image ((quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).map φ))
declarations.comment: part (2), corrected, the first half: the image computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of a map of quasi-coherent modules lies in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳); it need not be quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coheratorImageIsImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (2), corrected, the image in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.** For a map `φ : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓖` of
quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack, `Q(Im φ)`, the coherator of the image computed in
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, is the image of `φ` in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`: the epimorphism `𝓕 ⟶ Im φ` lies in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`, where `Q` is right exact (**Stacks 0779** (3)), and `Q` keeps
`Im φ ⟶ 𝓖` a monomorphism. Part (2) as printed, with `Im φ` itself quasi-coherent, is refuted by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ImageCounterexample.not_forall_isQuasicoherentOnSite_image`.
declarations.statement:
def coheratorImageIsImage {F G : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    IsImage (Abelian.coreflectorImageMonoFactorisation (coheratorAdjunction B S hS 𝒳) φ)
declarations.comment: part (2), corrected, the second half: Q(Im φ) is the image of φ in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), for the coherator Q of Stacks 0778

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ImageCounterexample.not_forall_isQuasicoherentOnSite_image
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (2), fails as written.** It is not true that for every map `φ` of
quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack the image of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is
quasi-coherent: multiplication by `2` on `𝒪` over `Spec ℤ` is a counterexample. The corrected
part (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.lqcohSheafFbc_image_quasicoherentInclusion`
(the image lies in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`) together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coheratorImageIsImage` (its coherator is the image in
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isQuasicoherentOnSite_image :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (F G : AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳)
      (φ : F ⟶ G),
      (Abelian.image
        ((AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).map φ)).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (2) as printed is false, and the inclusion QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is not exact in general: for multiplication by 2 on 𝒪 over Spec ℤ the image computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is not quasi-coherent (it vanishes on Spec 𝔽₂ while its would-be module 2ℤ ⊗ 𝔽₂ does not); the corrected part (2) is lqcohSheafFbc_image_quasicoherentInclusion and coheratorImageIsImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isColimitCokernelCoforkMapQuasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (1).**  Let `φ : 𝓕 → 𝓖` be a map of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.  The
cokernel of `φ` in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, included into `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` together with its projection, is a
cokernel of `φ` in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.

So the cokernel computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is the image of a quasi-coherent module — which is the
quasi-coherence half of the clause, recorded separately as
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherent_cokernel_quasicoherentInclusion` — and it is the
cokernel in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.  The proof is the right exactness of the inclusion, which is how the
source gets the clause.
declarations.statement:
def isColimitCokernelCoforkMapQuasicoherentInclusion
    {F G : quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS p hp} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ
      ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)).ι.map (cokernel.π φ))
      (by simp only [← Functor.map_comp, cokernel.condition, zero_comp, Functor.map_zero]) :
      Cofork ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)).ι.map φ) 0)
declarations.comment: part (1): the cokernel of a map of quasi-coherent modules computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is the inclusion of the cokernel computed in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), over the closure of quasi-coherence under colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherent_cokernel_quasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (1), the quasi-coherence half.**  The cokernel of a map of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is quasi-coherent, because it is isomorphic to the
inclusion of the cokernel computed in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.comment: part (1), the quasi-coherence half: the cokernel computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of a map of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent, over the closure of quasi-coherence under colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLimitKernelForkFlatBaseChangeQuasicoherator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (3), second half.**  Let `φ : 𝓕 → 𝓖` be a map of quasi-coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules and let `Ker(i φ)` be its kernel inside `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.  Then `Q(Ker(i φ))`,
with the map `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoheratorKernelι` to `𝓕`, is a kernel of `φ` in
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.

The proof is formal: `Q` is a right adjoint, so it preserves the kernel, and `Q ∘ i` is the
identity because the inclusion is fully faithful; transporting the kernel of `Q(i φ)` along that
identification gives the kernel of `φ`.

That `Ker(φ)` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` lies in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` is the first half of the clause and
is **Stacks 0771** part (2); it is not available, and it enters here only as the instance
hypothesis that the kernel exists in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
def isLimitKernelForkFlatBaseChangeQuasicoherator
    {F G : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS p hp} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    [HasKernel ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E h S hS p hp hinc).map φ)] :
    IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι
      (quasicoheratorKernelι B E h S hS p hp hinc hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep φ)
      (quasicoheratorKernelι_comp B E h S hS p hp hinc hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep φ))
declarations.comment: part (3), second half: Q(Ker φ) is the kernel of φ in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), over the existence of Ker φ inside LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) — the first half of the clause, which is Stacks 0771 part (2) and is not available

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.preservesFiniteColimits_quasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, the right exactness of the inclusion.** The inclusion
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` of the quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack is right exact.
declarations.comment: the inclusion QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is right exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isColimitCokernelCoforkQuasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (1).** Let `φ : 𝓕 → 𝓖` be a map of quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic
stack `𝒳`. The cokernel of `φ` in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, included into `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` with its projection, is a
cokernel of `φ` in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`: the cokernel computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is the cokernel in
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
def isColimitCokernelCoforkQuasicoherentInclusion
    {F G : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ
      ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
            .fppf)).ι.map (cokernel.π φ))
      (by simp only [← Functor.map_comp, cokernel.condition, zero_comp, Functor.map_zero]) :
      Cofork ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          .fppf)).ι.map φ) 0)
declarations.comment: part (1): the cokernel computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of a map of quasi-coherent modules is the cokernel computed in QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasicoherent_cokernel_quasicoherentInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL, part (1), the quasi-coherence half.** The cokernel computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` of a
map of quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_cokernel_quasicoherentInclusion
    {F G : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids} (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids .fppf))
      (cokernel ((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          .fppf)).ι.map φ))
declarations.comment: part (1), the quasi-coherence half: the cokernel computed in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of a map of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.instAbelianQuasicoherentModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQL**: `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is abelian, for every algebraic stack `𝒳` (also **Stacks 06WV**
part (2)). It is coreflective in the weak Serre subcategory `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, with
the coherator, right exact there, as coreflector.
declarations.statement: instance instAbelianQuasicoherentModules : Abelian (quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: the category QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) is abelian, for every algebraic stack 𝒳

registrations.name: preservesFiniteColimits_quasicoherentInclusion
registrations.comment: the inclusion QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is right exact, over the closure of quasi-coherence under colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isMonoidal_lqcohSheafFbc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (ii).** `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` is closed under the tensor product of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules
(**Stacks 0771** (6)) and contains `𝒪_𝒳`: it is a monoidal subcategory of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMonoidal_lqcohSheafFbc :
    (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).IsMonoidal
declarations.comment: (ii): LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) is closed under the tensor product, a monoidal subcategory of Mod(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.lqcohSheafFbcInclusionBraided
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (iii), the inclusion `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`**: a functor of symmetric
monoidal categories, for the tensor product of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules and the structure it induces on
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.comment: (iii): the inclusion LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is a functor of symmetric monoidal categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentToLqcohSheafFbcBraided
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (iii), the inclusion `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`**: a functor of symmetric
monoidal categories, for the structures both inherit from `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.comment: (iii): the inclusion QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) is a functor of symmetric monoidal categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coheratorBraided
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (iv).** The coherator `Q : LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) → QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is a functor of
symmetric monoidal categories. Its comparison `Q(𝓕) ⊗ Q(𝓖) → Q(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)` is the adjoint transpose
of the tensor product `Q(𝓕) ⊗ Q(𝓖) → 𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖` of the two counits, the south-west arrow of the
triangle of the source, and it is invertible because `Q` inverts that tensor product of counits
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_coherator_map_tensorHom_counit`).
declarations.comment: (iv): the coherator Q : LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) → QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) is a functor of symmetric monoidal categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_coheratorTensorComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (iv), the tensor comparison.** For `𝓕, 𝓖` in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` the canonical
map `Q(𝓕) ⊗ Q(𝓖) → Q(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)`, the adjoint transpose of the tensor product of the two counits,
is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_coheratorTensorComparison
    (F G : (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory) :
    letI := isMonoidal_lqcohSheafFbc B S hS 𝒳 E h
    letI := (lqcohSheafFbcCoheratorAdjunction B S hS 𝒳 E h).rightAdjointLaxMonoidal
    IsIso (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ
      ((lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).ι ⋙ coherator B S hS 𝒳) F G)
declarations.comment: (iv): the canonical map Q(F) ⊗ Q(G) → Q(F ⊗ G) is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coheratorTensorIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (iv), the isomorphism `Q(𝓕) ⊗ Q(𝓖) ≅ Q(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)`** of the symmetric monoidal
functor `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coheratorBraided`; its forward map is the
canonical comparison (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coheratorTensorIso_hom`).
declarations.statement:
def coheratorTensorIso
    (F G : (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory) :
    letI := isMonoidal_lqcohSheafFbc B S hS 𝒳 E h
    (coherator B S hS 𝒳).obj F.obj ⊗ (coherator B S hS 𝒳).obj G.obj ≅
      (coherator B S hS 𝒳).obj (F ⊗ G).obj
declarations.comment: (iv): the isomorphism Q(F) ⊗ Q(G) ≅ Q(F ⊗ G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isQuasicoherentOnSite_sheafTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (i).** The tensor product `𝓕 ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} 𝓖` of two quasi-coherent modules on an
algebraic stack is quasi-coherent (**Stacks 06WV** part (5)). The tensor product is the tensor
product sheaf, the sheafification of the objectwise tensor product, on the fppf site of `𝒳`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_tensorSheaf` at the fppf site of the
algebraic stack, which is essentially small.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_sheafTensor (F G : Stack.fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor (FibredSite.structureSheaf B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids .fppf)).obj F).obj G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: (i): the tensor product of two quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic stack is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentInclusionBraided
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM, (iii), the first inclusion into `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.** `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is a symmetric
monoidal category for the tensor product of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules, and the inclusion
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is a functor of symmetric monoidal categories.
declarations.statement: def quasicoherentInclusionBraided : (quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).Braided
declarations.comment: (iii): the inclusion QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) → Mod(𝒪_𝒳) is a functor of symmetric monoidal categories

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQM.** The tensor product of two quasi-coherent sheaves of modules on a site is
quasi-coherent.

Each factor is presented on some family covering the final object. The two families are refined
by the objects carrying a morphism into a member of each, which again covers the final object:
given an object, the first family covers it, each member of that cover is covered by the second
family, and every object of the resulting cover maps to a member of both. On such an object the
two presentations restrict, their tensor product presents the tensor product of the restrictions
by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.tensorPresentation`, and that is the restriction of
`F ⊗_𝒪 G` by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorProduct.tensorSheafificationOverIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_tensorSheaf'
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w} (structureSheaf 𝒪 h𝒪))
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
        ⟨𝒪, Presheaf.isSheaf_of_isSheaf_comp _ (𝒪) (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)
          (h𝒪)⟩).obj (F)).obj (G))).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: tensor products of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules_val
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQN**, the first assertion, on underlying presheaves of modules.  The internal
Hom of two sheaves of modules on the associated fppf site of a category fibred in groupoids has
the same underlying presheaf of modules whether it is computed on the associated fppf site or
on any of the five associated sites; the source's case is the étale one.

The internal Hom of Stacks 03EM is built from the presheaves of modules underlying its two
arguments and from the presheaf of rings underlying the structure sheaf, and none of the three
depends on the topology, so the two presheaves of modules are equal on the nose.
declarations.statement:
public theorem internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules_val (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)) :
    ((ringedSite B S hS p hp τ).internalHomSheaf
        (restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ F)
        (restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ G)).val =
      ((ringedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).internalHomSheaf F G).val
declarations.comment: the two internal Homs have the same presheaf of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.isSheaf_internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQN**, the first assertion, on the sheaf condition.  The internal Hom computed on
one of the five associated sites of a category fibred in groupoids is a sheaf for the
associated *fppf* topology, so it is an object of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` and not merely of
`Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`.

By Stacks 03EM the internal Hom is a sheaf for any topology for which its target is one, and
the target here is a sheaf for the associated fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSheaf_internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p .fppf)
      ((ringedSite B S hS p hp τ).internalHomSheaf
        (restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ F)
        (restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ G)).val.presheaf
declarations.comment: the common value is a sheaf for the fppf topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQN**, the first assertion.  The internal Hom of two sheaves of modules on the
associated fppf site of a category fibred in groupoids, computed on one of the five associated
sites, agrees as an object of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` with the one computed on the associated fppf site; the
source's case is the étale one.

This is the conjunction of the two statements above: the underlying presheaves of modules are
equal, and the common presheaf is a sheaf for the associated fppf topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules_eq (τ : SiteKind)
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)) :
    (⟨((ringedSite B S hS p hp τ).internalHomSheaf
          (restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ F)
          (restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ G)).val,
        isSheaf_internalHomSheaf_restrictSiteModules.{u, v, w, m} B S hS p hp τ F G⟩ :
        SheafOfModules.{max v w m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp .fppf)) =
      (ringedSite B S hS p hp .fppf).internalHomSheaf F G
declarations.comment: the two internal Homs agree as objects of Mod(𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.fppfInternalHom_presheaf_eq_etaleInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQN**, the agreement of the two internal Homs at module universe `u`.  The internal
Hom `SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G)` computed in `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` and the one computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`
have the same underlying presheaf of abelian groups, for arbitrary modules `F` and `G` on the fppf
site; the source states it for `F` of finite presentation and `G` quasi-coherent.

Both are the internal Hom of Stacks 03EM read in the universe `u` of the module sections, and
that construction depends only on the underlying presheaves of `F`, `G` and of the structure
sheaf, none of which changes with the topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem fppfInternalHom_presheaf_eq_etaleInternalHom (F G : Stack.fppfModules B S hS 𝒳) :
    (fppfInternalHom B S hS 𝒳 F G).val.presheaf =
      (etaleInternalHom B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        (FibredSite.restrictSiteModules B S hS _ _ .etale F)
        (FibredSite.restrictSiteModules B S hS _ _ .etale G)).val.presheaf
declarations.comment: the agreement of the internal Homs of Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳) and Mod(𝒪_𝒳), for arbitrary F and G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of `hom(F, G)`** (Stacks 0GQN): for `H` quasi-coherent,
`Hom_𝒳(H, hom(F, G)) = Hom_𝒳(H ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} F, G)`.  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentHomOfEquiv` at the coherator; it holds for
arbitrary `F` and `G`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentHomEquiv (F G : Stack.fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (H : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳) :
    (H ⟶ quasicoherentHom B S hS 𝒳 F G) ≃
      (fppfTensor B S hS 𝒳 ((quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).obj H) F ⟶ G)
declarations.comment: the universal property of hom(F, G) = Q(SheafHom(F, G)), for arbitrary F and G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfInternalHom_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQN**, the membership clause: for `F` an `𝒪_𝒳`-module of finite presentation and `G`
a quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module on an algebraic stack, the internal Hom `SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G)`,
whose two computations agree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.fppfInternalHom_presheaf_eq_etaleInternalHom`, is an
object of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.  It is Stacks 0771 (7) applied to `G ∈ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⊆ LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfInternalHom_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (F G : Stack.fppfModules B S hS 𝒳) [F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite]
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 (fppfInternalHom B S hS 𝒳 F G)
declarations.comment: the common value SheafHom(F, G) is an object of LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳), for F of finite presentation and G quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentHomFlatPullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQP.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a flat morphism of algebraic stacks, `F` an
`𝒪_𝒴`-module of finite presentation and `G` a quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒴`-module. Then
`f^* hom(F, G) = hom(f^* F, f^* G)`, with `hom` the quasi-coherent internal Hom
`hom(F, G) = Q(SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒴}(F, G))` of Stacks 0GQN.

The isomorphism is the composite of `f^* Q_𝒴 = Q_𝒳 f^*` (Stacks 0GQJ, at
`SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒴}(F, G)`, which lies in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)` by Stacks 0GQN) with `Q_𝒳` of
`f^* SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒴}(F, G) = SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒳}(f^* F, f^* G)`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentHomFlatPullbackIso (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (F G : Stack.fppfModules B S hS 𝒴) [F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite]
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (quasicoherentPullback B S hS f).obj (quasicoherentHom B S hS 𝒴 F G) ≅
      quasicoherentHom B S hS 𝒳 ((fppfModulesPullback B S hS f).obj F)
        ((fppfModulesPullback B S hS f).obj G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_app_quasicoherentDirectImageOfEtale_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQQ.**  Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks over `S`, let `y` be a flat object of `𝒴` and let `ℱ` be an object of
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.  Then the canonical comparison from the sections at `y` of the quasi-coherent direct
image of **Stacks 077A** to the sections at `y` of the étale direct image is invertible:

`(f_*ℱ)(y) = (f_{QCoh,*}ℱ)(y)` and `(R^i f_*ℱ)(y) = (R^i f_{QCoh,*}ℱ)(y)`.

The comparison is the component at `y` of the counit `ε : i Q(𝓖) ⟶ 𝓖` of the adjunction of
**Stacks 0778** at `𝓖 = D(i ℱ)`, whose domain is `i` of the composite of **Stacks 077A** by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange_quasicoherentDirectImageOfEtale_obj`.
Both halves of the source are covered at once: `D` is the étale direct image for the first and
its `i`-th right derived functor for the second.

The hypotheses `hker` and `hcoker` are **Stacks 0779** part (2) read at the presheaf level; see
"Carried versus proved" in the module documentation for why the library's part (2) does not
discharge them.  Everything else is proved, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_app_of_isParasitic`.  The two hypotheses on `f` are named `_hqc`
and `_hqs` because the argument does not consume them: they are the source's, and they stand
behind the carried data `D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_app_quasicoherentDirectImageOfEtale_counit
    (_hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (_hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (D : locallyQuasicoherentFlatBaseChangeModules.{u, u + 1, u} B E h S hS
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) ⥤
      locallyQuasicoherentFlatBaseChangeModules.{u, u + 1, u} B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
        𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids)
    (F : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom))
    (hker : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒴 .etale
      (kernel ((flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
        𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids hinc hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).counit.app
          (D.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E h S hS
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
            (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) hincX).obj F))).hom.val))
    (hcoker : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒴 .etale
      (cokernel ((flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
        𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids hinc hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).counit.app
          (D.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E h S hS
            (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
            (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) hincX).obj F))).hom.val))
    (y : 𝒴.val.val.obj) (hy : flatObject B S hS 𝒴.val y) :
    IsIso (((flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
      𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids hinc hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).counit.app
        (D.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E h S hS
          (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
          (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) hincX).obj F))).hom.val.app
            (op y))
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison, namely the counit of Stacks 0778, is invertible on sections over a flat object: both (f_*F)(y) = (f_{QCoh,*}F)(y) and (R^i f_*F)(y) = (R^i f_{QCoh,*}F)(y), never an unspecified isomorphism. Carried: the middle étale direct image of Stacks 077A on LQCoh^fbc, as data D exactly as in 0GQX; and hker, hcoker, which are Stacks 0779 part (2), its library form needing Stacks 0771 part (2) to reach this reading

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.bijective_coheratorAdjunction_counit_directImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQQ.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks, `y` an object of `𝒴` such that `y : V → 𝒴` is flat, and `𝓕` a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-module.  Then `(f_*𝓕)(y) = (f_{QCoh,*}𝓕)(y)` and `(Rⁱf_*𝓕)(y) = (Rⁱf_{QCoh,*}𝓕)(y)` for
all `i`: the adjunction maps `f_{QCoh,*}𝓕 = Q(f_*𝓕) ⟶ f_*𝓕` and
`Rⁱf_{QCoh,*}𝓕 = Q(Rⁱf_*𝓕) ⟶ Rⁱf_*𝓕` of the coherator are bijective on sections at `y`.  Both
`f_*𝓕` and `Rⁱf_*𝓕` lie in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)`, so the kernels and cokernels of those maps are
parasitic by **Stacks 0779** part (2), and vanish at `y`.  For `i < 0` both sides are zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_coheratorAdjunction_counit_directImage (F : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (y : 𝒴.val.val.obj) (hy : flatObject B S hS 𝒴.val y) :
    Function.Bijective (((coheratorAdjunction B S hS 𝒴).counit.app
        ((fppfModulesPushforward B S hS f).obj ((quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).obj F))).val.app
          (op y)) ∧
      ∀ i, Function.Bijective (((coheratorAdjunction B S hS 𝒴).counit.app
        ((fppfModulesHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj
          ((quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳).obj F))).val.app (op y))
declarations.comment: (f_*F)(y) = (f_{QCoh,*}F)(y) and (R^i f_*F)(y) = (R^i f_{QCoh,*}F)(y) for f qcqs, y flat and F quasi-coherent: the adjunction maps of the coherator are bijective at y; i ≥ 0, both sides vanishing for i < 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.directImageNaiveCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**The naive relative cup product in degree `0`** (Stacks 0FPJ), the right vertical arrow `c`
of Stacks 0GQR: `f_*𝓕 ⊗ f_*𝓖 ⟶ f_*(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)`, adjoint to the comparison of Stacks 03EL
followed by the counit of `f^* ⊣ f_*` in each factor. It is
`Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeZeroCupProduct.naiveRelativeCupProduct` at this morphism of ringed
topoi.
declarations.statement:
def directImageNaiveCupProduct (M N : quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS p hp) :
    (fppfSheafTensor B S hS q hq).obj
        ((fppfPushforwardModules B S hS p q hp hq F hF).obj
            ((quasicoherentModulesInclusion B S hS p hp).obj M),
          (fppfPushforwardModules B S hS p q hp hq F hF).obj
            ((quasicoherentModulesInclusion B S hS p hp).obj N)) ⟶
      (fppfPushforwardModules B S hS p q hp hq F hF).obj
        ((quasicoherentModulesInclusion B S hS p hp).obj
          ((quasicoherentSheafTensor B S hS p hp).obj (M, N)))
declarations.comment: the vertical arrow c on the right, the naive relative cup product in degree 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**The left vertical arrow of Stacks 0GQR**,
`f_{QCoh,*}𝓕 ⊗ f_{QCoh,*}𝓖 ⟶ f_{QCoh,*}(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)`, for a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks: `Q(c)` precomposed with the comparison `Q(A) ⊗ Q(B) ⟶ Q(A ⊗ B)` of Remark 0GQM
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentCupProduct_eq`). Here
`f_{QCoh,*} = Q ∘ f_* ∘ i`, with `f_*` the direct image of the morphism of ringed topoi `f`
induces and `Q` the coherator `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coherator` of `𝒴`.
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow, Q applied to c through the comparison of Remark 0GQM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.map_quasicoherentCupProduct_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQR.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks and let `𝓕`, `𝓖` be quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. The square

```
f_{QCoh,*}𝓕 ⊗ f_{QCoh,*}𝓖 ───→ f_*𝓕 ⊗ f_*𝓖
        │                              │ c
        ↓                              ↓
f_{QCoh,*}(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖) ─────────→ f_*(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)
```

commutes: the left vertical arrow
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentCupProduct`, the comparison of
Remark 0GQM followed by `Q(c)`) followed by the counit `Q ⟶ id` at `f_*(𝓕 ⊗ 𝓖)` equals the top
arrow (`i` commuting with `⊗`, then the counit at `f_*𝓕` and at `f_*𝓖`) followed by the naive
relative cup product `c` (`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.directImageNaiveCupProduct`). `f_*` is
the direct image along the morphism of ringed topoi `f` induces, and `Q` is the coherator
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.coherator` of `𝒴`, which takes no input.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_quasicoherentCupProduct_comp_counit
    (_hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (_hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (𝓕 𝓖 : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳) :
    (i𝒴).map (quasicoherentCupProduct B S hS f 𝓕 𝓖) ≫
        (adjQ).counit.app ((fStar).obj ((i𝒳).obj ((tensorQ𝒳).obj (𝓕, 𝓖)))) =
      (tensorIso𝒴).hom.app ((Q𝒴).obj ((fStar).obj ((i𝒳).obj 𝓕)),
          (Q𝒴).obj ((fStar).obj ((i𝒳).obj 𝓖))) ≫
        (tensor𝒴).map ((adjQ).counit.app ((fStar).obj ((i𝒳).obj 𝓕)) ×ₘ
          (adjQ).counit.app ((fStar).obj ((i𝒳).obj 𝓖))) ≫
        cupC 𝓕 𝓖
declarations.comment: commutativity of the diagram, for a quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentCupProduct_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQR, functoriality of the left vertical arrow** in `𝓕` and `𝓖`, for a
quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentCupProduct_natural
    (_hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (_hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    {𝓕 𝓕' 𝓖 𝓖' : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳} (a : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕') (b : 𝓖 ⟶ 𝓖') :
    (tensorQ𝒴).map ((fQCoh).map a ×ₘ (fQCoh).map b) ≫ quasicoherentCupProduct B S hS f 𝓕' 𝓖' =
      quasicoherentCupProduct B S hS f 𝓕 𝓖 ≫ (fQCoh).map ((tensorQ𝒳).map (a ×ₘ b))
declarations.comment: the construction is functorial in F and G: the left vertical arrow

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentNaiveCupProduct_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQR, functoriality of the naive relative cup product `c`** in `𝓕` and `𝓖`, for a
quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentNaiveCupProduct_natural
    (_hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (_hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    {𝓕 𝓕' 𝓖 𝓖' : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳} (a : 𝓕 ⟶ 𝓕') (b : 𝓖 ⟶ 𝓖') :
    (tensor𝒴).map ((fStar).map ((i𝒳).map a) ×ₘ (fStar).map ((i𝒳).map b)) ≫ cupC 𝓕' 𝓖' =
      cupC 𝓕 𝓖 ≫ (fStar).map ((i𝒳).map ((tensorQ𝒳).map (a ×ₘ b)))
declarations.comment: the construction is functorial in F and G: the arrow c

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeZeroCupProduct.naiveRelativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**The naive relative cup product in degree zero**, the map
`f_*F ⊗_{O_D} f_*G ⟶ f_*(F ⊗_{O_C} G)` adjoint to the comparison of Tag 03EL followed by the
counit of `f^* ⊣ f_*` in each tensor factor.
declarations.statement:
def naiveRelativeCupProduct
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    (Functor.uncurry.obj (sheafTensor.{u', v', w', w', w'} Y.O)).obj
          ((pushforwardModules f).obj F, (pushforwardModules f).obj G) ⟶
      (pushforwardModules f).obj
        ((Functor.uncurry.obj (sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} X.O)).obj (F, G))
declarations.comment: the vertical arrow c on the right, for a morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeZeroCupProduct.quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct
declarations.doc:
The naive relative cup product in degree zero carried through the comparison attached to the
adjunction `adj : i ⊣ Q` and the tensor comparison `α`: the canonical map
`A(Q(f_*F), Q(f_*G)) ⟶ Q(f_*F ⊗ f_*G)` followed by `Q` applied to `c`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    A.obj (Q.obj ((pushforwardModules f).obj F), Q.obj ((pushforwardModules f).obj G)) ⟶
      Q.obj ((pushforwardModules f).obj
        ((Functor.uncurry.obj (sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} X.O)).obj (F, G)))
declarations.comment: the left vertical arrow, over an adjunction with a tensor comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeZeroCupProduct.map_quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**The square commutes.**  Going right along the upper horizontal
arrow — the comparison `α` followed by the counit of `adj` in each tensor factor — and then down
`c` agrees with going down the left vertical arrow and then right along the counit of `adj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct_comp_counit
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :
    i.map (quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct f adj A α F G) ≫
        adj.counit.app ((pushforwardModules f).obj
          (((sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} X.O).obj F).obj G)) =
      α.app (Q.obj ((pushforwardModules f).obj F), Q.obj ((pushforwardModules f).obj G)) ≫
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (sheafTensor.{u', v', w', w', w'} Y.O)).map
            (adj.counit.app ((pushforwardModules f).obj F) ×ₘ
              adj.counit.app ((pushforwardModules f).obj G)) ≫
          naiveRelativeCupProduct f F G
declarations.comment: commutativity of the diagram, over an adjunction with a tensor comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DegreeZeroCupProduct.quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct_natural
declarations.doc: **The construction is functorial in the two modules.**
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct_natural
    {F F' G G' : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)}
    (u : F ⟶ F') (v : G ⟶ G') :
    A.map (Q.map ((pushforwardModules f).map u) ×ₘ Q.map ((pushforwardModules f).map v)) ≫
        quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct f adj A α F' G' =
      quasicoherentRelativeCupProduct f adj A α F G ≫
        Q.map ((pushforwardModules f).map
          ((Functor.uncurry.obj (sheafTensor.{u, v, w, w, w} X.O)).map (u ×ₘ v)))
declarations.comment: functoriality in the two modules, over an adjunction with a tensor comparison

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesFiniteLimits_etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImageFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQS, part (1), the left exact half.** The functor
`a : ℱ ↦ f^*ℱ|_{U_étale}` preserves finite limits.

Limits of sheaves of modules are computed in presheaves, where restriction along a functor is
pointwise, so this holds for the direct image along any continuous functor of ringed sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImageFunctor
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hr : r.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (eU : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver p
      (presheafOfCategories (U.1 ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (f : 𝒰 ⥤ 𝒳) (hf : p.IsFibredOneMorphism r f) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImageFunctor B S hS p r hp hr eU f hf)
declarations.comment: part (1), the left exact half: a preserves finite limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exactFunctor_etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImageFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQS, part (1).** The functor `a : Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod(U_étale, 𝒪_U)`,
`ℱ ↦ f^*ℱ|_{U_étale}`, is exact.

The source's two reasons are the continuity and the cocontinuity of the functor `U_étale ⥤ 𝒳`
along which the restriction is taken: `f^{-1}` is restriction along the 1-morphism `f` and
`·|_{U_étale}` is restriction along `u_U`, and both functors are continuous and cocontinuous, so
Stacks 04BD (2) applies to their composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImageFunctor [EssentiallySmall.{u} 𝒳]
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hr : r.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (eU : StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver p
      (presheafOfCategories (U.1 ⋙ typeToCat)).p)
    (f : 𝒰 ⥤ 𝒳) (hf : p.IsFibredOneMorphism r f) :
    exactFunctor (inheritedEtaleModules B S hS r hr)
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS U))
      (etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImageFunctor B S hS p r hp hr eU f hf)
declarations.comment: part (1): the functor a from all modules on the étale site of the stack to all modules on the small étale site of the algebraic space is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.spaceChartRestrictionCoheratorInternalHomIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQT.** Let `f : 𝒰 ⟶ 𝒳` be a flat 1-morphism of algebraic stacks with `𝒰` the
algebraic stack of an algebraic space `U`, and let `d : ℱ ↦ f^*ℱ|_{U_étale}` be the restriction of
Stacks 0GQS. For `𝒪_𝒳`-modules `ℱ` and `𝒢` with `ℱ` quasi-coherent,
`d(hom(ℱ, 𝒢)) = 𝓗om_{𝒪_U}(d(ℱ), d(𝒢))`, where `hom(ℱ, 𝒢) = Q(𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(ℱ, 𝒢))` is the
object of Stacks 0GQN.
declarations.statement:
def spaceChartRestrictionCoheratorInternalHomIso (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳))
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    spaceChartRestriction B S hS 𝒳 U hU f (coheratorInternalHom B S hS 𝒳 F G) ≅
      Space.smallEtaleInternalHomSmall B S hS U hU (spaceChartRestriction B S hS 𝒳 U hU f F)
        (spaceChartRestriction B S hS 𝒳 U hU f G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_associatedTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQV at any one of the sites of Stacks 06TP, from all four conditions of
Stacks 0GN4.** Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of a scheme
`S` contained in a big fppf site, let `τ` be a topology on the underlying category of schemes of
`B`, give the total category of `𝒳` the topology it inherits from `τ` localized at `S`
(Stacks 06TP), and assume of the collection `affineObjects` of its objects lying over affine
schemes that

1. finitely many of them have sheafified representables jointly covering the final sheaf,
2. every covering sieve of a member of it contains a finite covering family by members of it,
3. the product of the sheafified representables of two of them is covered by a finite coproduct of
   sheafified representables of members of it, and
4. the equalizer of the sheafified representables of two parallel morphisms between members of it
   is covered by such a finite coproduct.

Then `colim_i H^p(𝒳, F_i) ⟶ H^p(𝒳, colim_i F_i)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`, for every
filtered diagram `F` of abelian sheaves on that site.

This is the site-theoretic step of the source's proof, and the source takes it at two values of
`τ`: the big fppf topology and the big étale topology. Nothing below uses which topology was
chosen — the step is an instance of
`Stacks.Cohomology.ColimitsOfCohomology.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_of_covers`,
the form of Stacks 0GN4 for a site whose objects and morphisms do not share a universe, and the
site of a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of `S` does not, its objects
lying in `Type (u + 1)` and its morphisms in `Type u`. Coefficients, sheaves of sets and the index
category of the diagram all live at the join `u + 1` of those two universes.

So the two assertions of the source differ only in the four conditions fed to this result. Its
fppf and étale instances are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf`, where condition (2)
is discharged, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_etale`, where none of the
four is; see "What is proved and what is assumed" in the module docstring for the state of each
condition in each topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_associatedTopology
    (τ : GrothendieckTopology B.Schemes)
    (h_terminal : ∃ (m : ℕ) (U : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i => terminal.from
            ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).obj (U i))))
    (h_refine : ∀ x ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳,
      HasFiniteCoverRefinementsFrom (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)
        (affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) x)
    (h_product : ∀ U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳, ∀ U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            prod.lift ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).map (p i))
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).map (q i))))
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {U U' : 𝒳.val.obj} (a b : U ⟶ U'),
      U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳 → U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳 →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ a = p i ≫ b),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift
              (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).map a)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).map b)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).map (p i)) (by
                simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using
                  congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ)).map
                    (hp i))))
    (p : ℕ) {I : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ) Ab.{u + 1}) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F
      ((Sheaf.Γ (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p τ) Ab.{u + 1}).rightDerived p))
declarations.comment: the site-theoretic step, at an arbitrary one of the five topologies of Stacks 06TP, hence for the fppf and the étale assertion alike; all four conditions of 0GN4 are assumed here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQV in the fppf topology, from conditions (1), (3) and (4) of Stacks 0GN4.** Let `𝒳`
be a category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of a scheme `S` contained in a big
fppf site, give its total category the fppf topology of Stacks 06TP, and assume of the collection
`affineObjects` of its objects lying over affine schemes that

1. finitely many of them have sheafified representables jointly covering the final sheaf,
3. the product of the sheafified representables of two of them is covered by a finite coproduct of
   sheafified representables of members of it, and
4. the equalizer of the sheafified representables of two parallel morphisms between members of it
   is covered by such a finite coproduct.

Then `colim_i H^p(𝒳, F_i) ⟶ H^p(𝒳, colim_i F_i)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`, for every
filtered diagram `F` of abelian fppf sheaves on `𝒳`.

Condition (2) of Stacks 0GN4 is not assumed: it holds for every category fibred in groupoids, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFiniteCoverRefinementsFrom_fppfTopology`. Conditions (1), (3) and (4)
are what the source derives from quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of an algebraic stack;
see "What is proved and what is assumed" in the module docstring for the state of each, and
`Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf_of_isQuasiCompactStack` below for the
form of this result in which (1) too is discharged.

This is the fppf instance of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_associatedTopology`, the
site-theoretic step taken at an arbitrary topology; the fppf topology of Stacks 06TP is that
construction at `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.topology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf
    (h_terminal : ∃ (m : ℕ) (U : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i => terminal.from
            ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).obj (U i))))
    (h_product : ∀ U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳, ∀ U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            prod.lift ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).map (p i))
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).map (q i))))
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {U U' : 𝒳.val.obj} (a b : U ⟶ U'),
      U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳 → U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳 →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ a = p i ≫ b),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift
              (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).map a)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).map b)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).map (p i)) (by
                simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using
                  congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳)).map (hp i))))
    (p : ℕ) {I : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) Ab.{u + 1}) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F
      ((Sheaf.Γ (fppfTopology B S hS 𝒳) Ab.{u + 1}).rightDerived p))
declarations.comment: the site-theoretic step for the fppf site; conditions (1), (3) and (4) of 0GN4 are assumed here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_etale
declarations.doc:
**The second assertion of Stacks 0GQV: the same statement in the étale topology**, from
conditions (1), (3) and (4) of Stacks 0GN4. Let `𝒳` be a category fibred in groupoids over the
big fppf category of a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site, give its total category the
*étale* topology of Stacks 06TP — the one it inherits from the big étale topology
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleTopology` of Stacks 03FF localized at `S` — and assume of the collection
`affineObjects` of its objects lying over affine schemes those three conditions. Then
`colim_i H^p(𝒳, F_i) ⟶ H^p(𝒳, colim_i F_i)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`, for every
filtered diagram `F` of abelian étale sheaves on `𝒳`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_associatedTopology` at the
big étale topology, and it is the shape in which the source's second assertion — "the same is true
for abelian sheaves on `𝒳_étale` taking cohomology in the étale topology" — becomes a statement of
this library.

Condition (2) of Stacks 0GN4 is not assumed, exactly as in the fppf case: it holds for every
category fibred in groupoids, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFiniteCoverRefinementsFrom_etaleTopology`, whose geometric input is
**Stacks 0218** where the fppf proof uses Stacks 021P. Condition (1) is likewise available for
the étale site, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isAffineObject_isLocallySurjective_terminal_from_etale`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack`
`.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_etale_of_isQuasiCompactStack`
is the form of this result in which it too is discharged. Conditions (3) and (4) remain open for
the étale site; see "What is proved and what is assumed" in the module docstring for the state of
each of the four.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_etale
    (h_terminal : ∃ (m : ℕ) (U : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i => terminal.from
            ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
              (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).obj (U i))))
    (h_product : ∀ U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳, ∀ U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳,
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U'),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            prod.lift ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (p i))
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (q i))))
    (h_equalizer : ∀ {U U' : 𝒳.val.obj} (a b : U ⟶ U'),
      U ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳 → U' ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳 →
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (V : Fin m → 𝒳.val.obj),
        (∀ i, V i ∈ affineObjects B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃ (p : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U) (hp : ∀ i, p i ≫ a = p i ≫ b),
          Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Limits.Sigma.desc fun i =>
            equalizer.lift
              (f := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map a)
              (g := (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map b)
              ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (p i)) (by
                simpa only [Functor.map_comp] using
                  congrArg (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                    (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))).map (hp i))))
    (p : ℕ) {I : Type (u + 1)} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B)) Ab.{u + 1}) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F
      ((Sheaf.Γ (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.p (etaleTopology B))
        Ab.{u + 1}).rightDerived p))
declarations.comment: the second assertion, in the étale topology: the site-theoretic step for the étale site of Stacks 06TP; conditions (1), (3) and (4) of 0GN4 are assumed here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf_of_isQuasiCompactStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GQV in the fppf topology for a quasi-compact algebraic stack, from conditions (3) and
(4) of Stacks 0GN4.** Let `𝒴` be a quasi-compact algebraic stack over a scheme `S` contained in a
big fppf site and assume of the collection `affineObjects` of the objects of its fppf site lying
over affine schemes that

3. the product of the sheafified representables of two of them is covered by a finite coproduct of
   sheafified representables of members of it, and
4. the equalizer of the sheafified representables of two parallel morphisms between members of it
   is covered by such a finite coproduct.

Then `colim_i H^p(𝒴, F_i) ⟶ H^p(𝒴, colim_i F_i)` is an isomorphism in every degree `p`, for every
filtered diagram `F` of abelian fppf sheaves on `𝒴`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf` with its
condition (1) discharged from quasi-compactness by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_isAffineObject_isLocallySurjective_terminal_from`. The hypothesis
is stated for an `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks` rather than for a bare category fibred
in groupoids because that is what Stacks 04YC and Stacks 075S are about; the conclusion is the one
of the previous result at the underlying category fibred in groupoids.

Conditions (3) and (4) are the two the source derives from quasi-separatedness of `𝒴`, and both
are available: (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_prodLift` and (4) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fin_affineObjects_isLocallySurjective_equalizerLift`, each for a
stack quasi-separated over a quasi-separated base scheme. They are hypotheses here because this
statement asks nothing of quasi-separatedness — no hypothesis of it appears, the two conditions
standing in for it — so this is not the full assertion of Stacks 0GQV, whose hypotheses are
quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness alone. That assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_globalSections_fppf_of_isQuasiCompact`,
in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/ColimitsOfCohomologyEqualizerAffineCover.lean`. See
"What is proved and what is assumed" in the module docstring.

    (𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
