    IsQuasicoherentFiniteTypeModule B S hS 𝒳 M
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tfae_coherenceConditions
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_coherenceConditions (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)) :
    [IsQuasicoherentFiniteTypeModule B S hS 𝒳 M, M.IsFinitePresentationOnSite,
      IsCoherentOnNoetherianSpaceCharts.{u, u, t} B S hS 𝒳 M,
      IsCoherentOnSomeFlatSpaceChart.{u, u, t} B S hS 𝒳 M].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR6.**  A module on the big fppf site of an algebraic stack `𝒳` is *coherent* when
it satisfies the conditions of Stacks 0GR5: it is quasi-coherent of finite type, condition (1),
and of finite presentation, condition (2).
declarations.comment: coherence, as conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 0GR5 jointly

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.coherentModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR6.**  The category `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)` of coherent modules on an algebraic stack `𝒳`: the
full subcategory of the `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on the big fppf site of `𝒳` cut out by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCoherent`.
declarations.comment: the category Coh(O_X) of coherent modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentModule_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR7, the structure-sheaf clause.**  On a locally Noetherian algebraic stack the
module `𝒪_𝒳` is coherent: on any site the structure sheaf viewed as a module over itself is the
coproduct of one copy of itself, hence of finite presentation.

Local Noetherianity is the hypothesis of the source and is not used; see the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentModule_unit (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS)
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳) :
    IsCoherentModule B S hS 𝒳 (SheafOfModules.unit _)
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf of the stack is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentModule_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR7, the finite locally free clause.**  On a locally Noetherian algebraic stack
every finite locally free `𝒪_𝒳`-module is coherent: the covering witnessing finite local freeness
already carries a finite global presentation on each of its members.

Local Noetherianity is the hypothesis of the source and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentModule_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS)
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl))
    (hM : M.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite) :
    IsCoherentModule B S hS 𝒳 M
declarations.comment: finite locally free modules on the stack are coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentModule_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc: On a locally Noetherian algebraic stack every invertible `𝒪_𝒳`-module is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentModule_of_isInvertible (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS)
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl))
    (hM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible
      (structureSheaf B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl).obj
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        B.topology le_rfl).property M) :
    IsCoherentModule B S hS 𝒳 M
declarations.comment: invertible modules on the stack are coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentModule_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR8.**  For a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of locally Noetherian algebraic stacks, the
inverse image `f^*` sends coherent modules on `𝒴` to coherent modules on `𝒳`.

Coherence is Stacks 0GR5(2), finite presentation on the fppf site, and the inverse image of
modules along a 1-morphism preserves it.  Local Noetherianity of the two stacks is the hypothesis
of the source and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentModule_modulePullback (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (_h𝒴 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒴)
    (M : SheafOfModules.{max (u + 1) m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
      𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl))
    (hM : IsCoherentModule B S hS 𝒴 M) :
    IsCoherentModule B S hS 𝒳
      ((modulePullback B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids f.hom.hom.toFunctor f.hom.hom.w
        B.topology le_rfl).obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_abelian_coh
declarations.doc:
The category of coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules is abelian, for a locally Noetherian algebraic stack
`𝒳`. Its kernels are the `Q(Ker φ)` and its cokernels are computed in
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.relKernelData_coherentModules`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_abelian_coh
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳) :
    Nonempty (Abelian (Coh.{u, u, w} B S hS 𝒳))
declarations.comment: the category Coh(O_X) of coherent modules on a locally Noetherian algebraic stack is abelian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesFiniteLimits_preservesFiniteColimits_coh_qcoh
declarations.doc:
The inclusion `Coh(𝒪_𝒳) → QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is exact, for a locally Noetherian algebraic stack `𝒳`:
it preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Here `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is the full subcategory of
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` of the quasi-coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_preservesFiniteColimits_coh_qcoh
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits
        (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE (FlatFppf.relKernelData_coherentModules h𝒳).le) ∧
      PreservesFiniteColimits
        (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE (FlatFppf.relKernelData_coherentModules h𝒳).le)
declarations.comment: the inclusion functor Coh(O_X) → QCoh(O_X) is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_coherator_image
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` be a map of coherent modules on a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`Im φ = Ker(𝒢 ⟶ Coker φ)` its image computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`. Then `Q(Im φ)` is coherent and
`Q(Im φ) ⟶ Im φ ⟶ 𝒢` is the image of `φ` in `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)`, i.e. a kernel in `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)` of the cokernel
`𝒢 ⟶ Coker φ`, which is coherent.

`Im φ` itself need not be coherent
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_not_isCoherent_image_of_isCoherent`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_coherator_image
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (FlatFppf.ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)}
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G) (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    ∃ (hC : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 (cokernel φ))
      (hK : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 ((FlatFppf.lowerShriekInverseImageCoherator B S hS 𝒳).obj
        (kernel (cokernel.π φ)))),
      Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι
        (f := ((coherentModules.{u, u, w} B S hS 𝒳).homMk (cokernel.π φ) :
          (⟨G, hG⟩ : Coh B S hS 𝒳) ⟶ ⟨cokernel φ, hC⟩))
        ((coherentModules.{u, u, w} B S hS 𝒳).homMk
          ((FlatFppf.coheratorCounit B S hS 𝒳).app (kernel (cokernel.π φ)) ≫
            kernel.ι (cokernel.π φ)) : (⟨_, hK⟩ : Coh B S hS 𝒳) ⟶ ⟨G, hG⟩)
        (by ext1; exact (FlatFppf.isRelKernel_coherator_kernel B S hS 𝒳 (cokernel.π φ)).1)))
declarations.comment: part (2), corrected reading: the image computed in Mod(O_X) need not be coherent (exists_not_isCoherent_image_of_isCoherent); Q(Im φ) is coherent and is the image of φ in Coh(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR9, part (1).**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a
map of coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.  The cokernel of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is a coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-module.

Coherence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCoherent`, the reading of Stacks 0GR6 as the conjunction
of the conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 0GR5 this library states.  On a locally Noetherian
algebraic stack that conjunction is condition (2) alone, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_iff_isCoherentModule`, so the clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentModule_cokernel`; local Noetherianity is used, in that
reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_cokernel
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G) (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 (cokernel φ)
declarations.comment: part (1): the cokernel computed in Mod(O_X) of a map of coherent modules (Stacks 0GR6) is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentOnSite_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR9, part (1).**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.  The cokernel of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is
coherent.

Coherence is the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8) on the big fppf ringed site of `𝒳`, and
the content is Stacks 01BY (3) there: the cokernel projection is locally surjective and the
image of `φ` is of finite type, which bounds both the generators and the relations of the
quotient.  Local Noetherianity is the hypothesis of the source and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_cokernel
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite F) (hG : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite G)
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite (cokernel φ)
declarations.comment: part (1), the cokernel, with coherence read as the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8) rather than as Stacks 0GR6, whose four conditions this library does not identify

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentOnSite_kernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR9, part (3).**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.  The kernel of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is
coherent, hence is already the kernel of `φ` inside the coherent modules.

Coherence is the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8) on the big fppf ringed site of `𝒳`, and
the content is Stacks 01BY (3) there: the kernel is of finite type by Stacks 01BY (2) and is a
subsheaf of the coherent source, so Stacks 01BY (1) applies.  The source states the clause for
coherence in the sense of Stacks 0GR6, where the kernel may fail to be coherent and the
coherator of Stacks 0778 is needed; see the module documentation.  Local Noetherianity is the
hypothesis of the source and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_kernel
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite F) (hG : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite G)
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite (kernel φ)
declarations.comment: part (3), the kernel, with coherence read as the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8): under that reading Ker(φ) is itself coherent and is the kernel inside the coherent modules, so the coherator Q of the source's formulation is not needed — the source's own clause for Stacks 0GR6-coherence, that Ker(φ) lies in LQCoh^fbc and that Q(Ker(φ)) is coherent, is not proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentOnSite_image
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR9, part (2).**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.  The image of `φ` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is
coherent.

The abelian image is the kernel of the projection onto the cokernel, so this is the kernel
clause applied to `𝒢 ⟶ Coker(φ)`, whose target is coherent by the cokernel clause.  Local
Noetherianity is the hypothesis of the source and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_image
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite F) (hG : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite G)
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite (Abelian.image φ)
declarations.comment: part (2), the image, with coherence read as the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8) rather than as Stacks 0GR6, whose four conditions this library does not identify

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherentOnSite_imageSubobject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR9, part (2), for the categorical image.**  The image of a map of coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules formed as `CategoryTheory.Limits.image` is coherent, being isomorphic to the
abelian image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_imageSubobject
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite F) (hG : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite G)
    (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite (image φ)
declarations.comment: part (2) for the categorical image, with coherence read as the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8) rather than as Stacks 0GR6

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_abelian_cohOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GR9, the abelian-category clause.**  The category of coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on a
locally Noetherian algebraic stack is abelian.

The structure is the one a full subcategory of an abelian category closed under kernels,
cokernels and finite products carries; the kernel and cokernel closure are parts (3) and (1)
above and the product closure comes from the extension clause Stacks 0GRA.  Coherence is the
sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8); local Noetherianity is the hypothesis of the source and
is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_abelian_cohOnSite
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳) :
    Nonempty (Abelian (CohOnSite.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳))
declarations.comment: the abelian-category clause, with coherence read as the sectionwise condition of Stacks 03DL(8) rather than as Stacks 0GR6, whose four conditions this library does not identify

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.kernel_mem_lqcohFbc_and_isCoherent_coherator_kernel
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules, and let `Ker φ` be its kernel computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`. Then

* `Ker φ` is in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`: read as an étale sheaf of modules, it is locally
  quasi-coherent (Stacks 06WJ) and has the flat base change property (Stacks 0762, with the
  inverse image of sheaves of modules on the small étale sites); and
* `Q(Ker φ)` is coherent and `Q(Ker φ) ⟶ Ker φ ⟶ ℱ` is a kernel of `φ` in `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)`.

Here `Q = g_!g^{-1}` with its counit is the coherator: composing with `Q(K) ⟶ K` is a bijection on
maps out of quasi-coherent modules
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.bijective_comp_coheratorCounit`). The source's remark that
`Ker φ` may not be coherent is not part of the assertion. The small étale sites are those of a
big étale site `E` with the same cutoff as the big fppf site `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem kernel_mem_lqcohFbc_and_isCoherent_coherator_kernel
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (FlatFppf.ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)}
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G) (φ : F ⟶ G) :
    (IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (kernel φ).val ∧
      HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE.{u, u + 1, u, u} B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        (etaleModuleOfFppf B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (kernel φ))) ∧
    ∃ hK : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳
        ((FlatFppf.lowerShriekInverseImageCoherator B S hS 𝒳).obj (kernel φ)),
      Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι
        (f := ((coherentModules.{u, u, w} B S hS 𝒳).homMk φ : (⟨F, hF⟩ : Coh B S hS 𝒳) ⟶ ⟨G, hG⟩))
        ((coherentModules.{u, u, w} B S hS 𝒳).homMk
          ((FlatFppf.coheratorCounit B S hS 𝒳).app (kernel φ) ≫ kernel.ι φ) :
            (⟨_, hK⟩ : Coh B S hS 𝒳) ⟶ ⟨F, hF⟩)
        (by ext1; exact (FlatFppf.isRelKernel_coherator_kernel B S hS 𝒳 φ).1)))
declarations.comment: part (3): the kernel Ker(φ) computed in Mod(O_X) of a map of coherent modules is in LQCoh^fbc(O_X) -- locally quasi-coherent and with the flat base change property, the latter read with the inverse image of sheaves of modules as in the source -- and Q(Ker φ) is coherent and is the kernel of φ in Coh(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_X₂_of_kernel_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRA.**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack, let `φ : ℱ₁ ⟶ ℱ₂` be a
kernel of `ψ : ℱ₂ ⟶ ℱ₃` and let `ℱ₃` be a cokernel of `φ` along `ψ`.  If `ℱ₁` and `ℱ₃` are
coherent then so is `ℱ₂`.

Coherence is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCoherent`, the notion of Stacks 0GR6.  On a locally
Noetherian algebraic stack it is finite presentation on the big fppf site, condition (2) of
Stacks 0GR5, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_iff_isCoherentModule`, which is where local
Noetherianity of `𝒳` enters; the content is then that finite presentation on a ringed site is
closed under extensions.  The exactness is given as a kernel fork and a cokernel cofork, so
nothing is assumed about the category of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCoherent_X₂_of_kernel_cokernel
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F₁ F₂ F₃ : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    {φ : F₁ ⟶ F₂} {ψ : F₂ ⟶ F₃} (hz : φ ≫ ψ = 0)
    (hφ : IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι φ hz)) (hψ : IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ ψ hz))
    (h₁ : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F₁) (h₃ : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F₃) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F₂
declarations.comment: extensions of coherent modules, exactness as a kernel fork and a cokernel cofork

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentFiniteTypeModule_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRB, part (1).**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and let
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` be a surjective map of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules.  If `ℱ` is coherent then so
is `𝒢`.

Coherence is condition (1) of Stacks 0GR5, that the module be quasi-coherent and of finite type;
see the module documentation.  Quasi-coherence of `𝒢` is the hypothesis of the source, which
takes `φ` to be a map of quasi-coherent modules, and what is proved is that `𝒢` is of finite
type: the condition 03DL(5) is inherited by quotients over an arbitrary ringed site.
Surjectivity is `CategoryTheory.Epi`, which for a morphism of sheaves of modules is local
surjectivity, by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.EpiMono.epi_iff_isLocallySurjective`.  Local
Noetherianity is the hypothesis of the source and is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentFiniteTypeModule_of_epi
    (_h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl)}
    (φ : F ⟶ G) [Epi φ]
    (hF : IsQuasicoherentFiniteTypeModule B S hS 𝒳 F)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsQuasicoherentFiniteTypeModule B S hS 𝒳 G
declarations.comment:
part (1): a quotient of a coherent module by a surjection of quasi-coherent
modules is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isCoherent_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRB, part (1).** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a surjective map of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. If `ℱ` is coherent, so is `𝒢`.

Surjectivity is `CategoryTheory.Epi` in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, i.e. local surjectivity; an epimorphism of
`QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is one of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.epi_hom_of_epi_qcoh`), so
this is also the statement for surjections in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`. Coherence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCoherent` (Stacks 0GR6). Finite type passes to quotients and, on a
locally Noetherian stack, a quasi-coherent module of finite type is coherent (Stacks 0GR5).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_epi
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)} (φ : F ⟶ G) [Epi φ]
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G
declarations.comment: part (1): if F is coherent and φ : F → G is a surjection of quasi-coherent modules then G is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSerreClass_coh_qcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRB: `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)` is a Serre subcategory of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`**, for a locally
Noetherian algebraic stack `𝒳`. Here `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is the full subcategory of the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules on the big fppf site, with the abelian structure
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianQCoh` (its kernels are the `Q(Ker φ)`, its cokernels are
computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`), and `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)` is cut out by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsCoherent`
(Stacks 0GR6). `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass` is the Serre-subcategory condition:
a coherent zero object, and closure under subobjects, quotients and extensions in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSerreClass_coh_qcoh
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳) :
    letI := FlatFppf.abelianQCoh 𝒳
    (FlatFppf.cohInQCoh 𝒳).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: Coh(O_X) is a Serre subcategory of QCoh(O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_image_qcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRB, part (2).** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules with `ℱ` coherent. Then the image of `φ` is
coherent.

The image is the image of `φ` in the abelian category `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianQCoh`), which is the reading of Stacks 0GQL (2) the
source's Remark sets up; it is a quotient of `ℱ` in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`. The image computed in
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` need not be quasi-coherent, already for `2 : 𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪` on `Spec ℤ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_not_isCoherent_image_of_isCoherent`), so it is not the object of
the clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_image_qcoh
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : (FlatFppf.qcohModules 𝒳).FullSubcategory} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F.obj) :
    letI := FlatFppf.abelianQCoh 𝒳
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 (Limits.image φ).obj
declarations.comment: part (2): if F is coherent then the image of φ : F → G in QCoh(O_X) is coherent; the image computed in Mod(O_X) need not be quasi-coherent (exists_not_isCoherent_image_of_isCoherent)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_of_isParasitic_kernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRB, part (3).** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and
`φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. If `𝒢` is coherent and `Ker(φ)` is parasitic
(Stacks 0773), then `ℱ` is coherent.

Here `Ker(φ)` is the kernel computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, as in Stacks 0GR9 and 0GQL. The variant with
the kernel taken in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_of_isParasitic_kernel_qcoh`.
On sections over a flat object the map `φ` is injective, its kernel there vanishing; so over a
flat object lying over a Noetherian affine scheme the sections of `ℱ` form a submodule of a finite
module, which suffices on a locally Noetherian stack
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isCoherent_of_moduleFinite_sections`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_isParasitic_kernel
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (FlatFppf.ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)}
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (φ : F ⟶ G) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G)
    (hK : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 .fppf (kernel φ).val) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F
declarations.comment: part (3): if G is coherent and Ker(φ), computed in Mod(O_X), is parasitic, then F is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_of_isParasitic_kernel_qcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRB, part (3), with the kernel taken in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`.** Let `𝒳` be a locally
Noetherian algebraic stack and `φ : ℱ ⟶ 𝒢` a map of quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. If `𝒢` is
coherent and the kernel of `φ` in the abelian category `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianQCoh`, kernel `Q(Ker φ)`) is parasitic, then `ℱ` is
coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_isParasitic_kernel_qcoh
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : (FlatFppf.qcohModules 𝒳).FullSubcategory} (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hG : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G.obj) :
    letI := FlatFppf.abelianQCoh 𝒳
    IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 .fppf (kernel φ).obj.val → IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F.obj
declarations.comment: part (3), the kernel read in QCoh(O_X): if G is coherent and the kernel of φ in QCoh(O_X) is parasitic, then F is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.coherentFlatPresentationEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRC.** Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack, let `U` be an algebraic
space and let `f : U → 𝒳` be surjective, locally of finite presentation and flat.  Let
`(U, R, s, t, c)` be the groupoid in algebraic spaces of Stacks 04T4, `R` representing
`U ×_𝒳 U`.  Then the equivalence `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ≅ QCoh(𝒪_{[U/R]}) ≅ QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)` of Sheaves
on Stacks, Section 06WU, and Stacks 06WT
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.SelfIntersection.quasicoherentFlatPresentationEquivalence`) sends
coherent modules to coherent modules and vice versa, i.e. induces an equivalence
`Coh(𝒪_𝒳) ≅ Coh(U, R, s, t, c)`.

`Coh(𝒪_𝒳)` is the category of coherent modules of Stacks 0GR6 and `Coh(U, R, s, t, c)` that of
Groupoids in Spaces, Section 0GPN.  The equivalence is the restriction of
`quasicoherentFlatPresentationEquivalence` to these full subcategories, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.coherentPresentationEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coherentFlatPresentationEquivalence
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (hlfp : AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS f)
    (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    Coh.{u, u, t} B S hS 𝒳 ≌
      Space.QuasicoherentModule.Coh B S hS (flatPresentationGroupoid B S hS 𝒳 F hF f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_internalHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRD for the internal Hom of Stacks 03EM, with a finite locally free first
argument.**  Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack, let `ℱ` be a finite locally free
`𝒪_𝒳`-module and let `𝒢` be a coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module.  Then the internal Hom
`𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(ℱ, 𝒢)` on the big fppf site of `𝒳` is a coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module.

Two things separate this from Stacks 0GRD, and the attribute names both.  The source's object is
not this internal Hom but its image `hom(ℱ, 𝒢) = Q(𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(ℱ, 𝒢))` under the quasi-coherator,
and forming it needs Stacks 0GQN, which this library does not have; and the source asks only
that `ℱ` be coherent, where this asks that it be finite locally free — a strengthening, since a
finite locally free module on a locally Noetherian algebraic stack is coherent by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite`.  See the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_internalHomSheaf (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (ℱ 𝒢 : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl))
    (hℱ : ℱ.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite) (h𝒢 : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 𝒢) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳
      ((FibredSite.ringedSite B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        SiteKind.fppf).internalHomSheaf ℱ 𝒢)
declarations.comment: the internal Hom of Stacks 03EM, for a finite locally free first argument; conditional on Stacks 0GQN for the passage to the quasi-coherator's value hom(F, G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_internalHomSheafSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRD for the internal Hom of Stacks 03EM, with the tag's own hypothesis on `ℱ`.**
Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack, let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module in the sense
of Stacks 0GR6 and let `𝒢` be coherent in the sectionwise sense of Stacks 03DL(8).  Then the
internal Hom `𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(ℱ, 𝒢)` is a coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module in the sense of Stacks 0GR6.

Two things still separate this from Stacks 0GRD, and the attribute names both; but the
hypothesis on the *first* argument is now the source's own, where
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isCoherent_internalHomSheaf` asks it to be finite locally free.  What
remains is the hypothesis on the second argument, strengthened from Stacks 0GR6-coherence to the
sectionwise coherence of Stacks 03DL(8) — it is the coherence that
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherentOnSite_piFin` and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isCoherentOnSite_kernel` are closed under, and it implies but is not
implied by Stacks 0GR6-coherence, see
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.CoherenceNotionComparison` — and the source's object,
which is not this internal Hom but its image under the quasi-coherator; see the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_internalHomSheafSmall (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS)
    [hsm : EssentiallySmall.{u} 𝒳.val.val.obj]
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    (ℱ 𝒢 : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl))
    (hℱ : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 ℱ)
    (h𝒢 : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite 𝒢) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳
      (@RingedSite.internalHomSheafSmall.{u, u, u + 1, u}
        (FibredSite.ringedSite B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          SiteKind.fppf) hsm ℱ 𝒢)
declarations.comment: the coherence of the internal Hom of Stacks 03EM itself, for a first argument satisfying the source's own condition of coherence in the sense of Stacks 0GR6; the condition on the second argument is strengthened to the sectionwise coherence of Stacks 03DL(8), which implies Stacks 0GR6-coherence and is not implied by it; and the source's object is the image hom(F, G) of this one under the quasi-coherator of Stacks 0GQN, which is not this statement's object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isCoherent_coheratorInternalHom
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack and `ℱ`, `𝒢` coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. Then the
internal hom `hom(ℱ, 𝒢) = Q(𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(ℱ, 𝒢))` is a coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_coheratorInternalHom
    (h𝒳 : HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T) 𝒳)
    {F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (ambientRingStructureSheaf B S hS 𝒳)}
    (hF : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 F) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 G) :
    IsCoherent B S hS 𝒳 (coheratorInternalHom B S hS 𝒳 F G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFiltered_coherentSubobject_and_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRF.**  Let `𝒳` be a Noetherian algebraic stack.  Every quasi-coherent
`𝒪_𝒳`-module `ℱ` is the filtered colimit of its coherent submodules: the coherent subobjects of `ℱ`
in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` form a filtered (nonempty and directed) partially ordered set, and `ℱ` with the
inclusions is the colimit in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of the diagram of their underlying modules.

"Submodule" means subobject in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, the category the source works in.  Read as subsheaves
of `ℱ` on the big fppf site the statement is false (`k[x, x⁻¹]` on `𝔸¹_k` has no nonzero coherent
subsheaf: it vanishes over `Spec k[x]/(x)`); see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_coherentSubobject_and_isColimit (h𝒳 : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳)
    (F : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳) :
    IsFiltered (CoherentSubobject B S hS 𝒳 F) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (coherentSubobjectCocone B S hS 𝒳 F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_fpqc_of_isQuasiAffineHom_diagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRH.** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` with quasi-affine diagonal satisfies descent
for fpqc coverings: it is a stack for the fpqc topology of the big fppf site over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStack_fpqc_of_isQuasiAffineHom_diagonal
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hΔ : IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS (diagonal.{u, u, u} B S hS 𝒳)) :
    𝒳.val.p.IsStack
      ((Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.comap (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).toGrothendieck)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isMorSheaf_fpqc_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**The full-faithfulness half of Stacks 0GRH**: condition (2) of the fpqc stack condition for
an algebraic stack. For every scheme `U` over `S` and all objects `x`, `y` of the fibre of an
algebraic stack `𝒳` over `U`, the presheaf `Mor(x, y)` of Stacks 02ZB is a sheaf for the fpqc
topology on the localization at `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorSheaf_fpqc_of_isAlgebraicStack
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x y : 𝒳.val.p.Fiber U) :
    haveI : 𝒳.val.p.IsFibered := 𝒳.isFiberedInGroupoids.isFibered
    𝒳.val.p.IsMorSheaf
      ((Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.comap (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).toGrothendieck) U x y
declarations.comment:
the full-faithfulness half of the proof: condition (2) of the fpqc stack
  condition, that the presheaves Mor(x, y) = Isom(x, y) of an algebraic stack are sheaves for the
  fpqc topology. No hypothesis on the diagonal is carried: representability of the diagonal by
  algebraic spaces, which every algebraic stack has, already suffices for this half, so the
  quasi-affine diagonal of the source and the ind-quasi-affine diagonal of its footnote are both
  dropped. The essential-surjectivity half, effectivity of fpqc descent data, is not formalized.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.existsUnique_tensorExtension_coherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRJ.** Let `𝒳` and `𝒴` be Noetherian algebraic stacks.  Any right exact tensor
functor `F' : Coh(𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ Coh(𝒪_𝒴)` — additive, preserving finite colimits, and a functor of
monoidal categories (Stacks 0FFL) — extends to a right exact tensor functor
`F : QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ QCoh(𝒪_𝒴)` commuting with all (small) colimits, in particular with direct
sums: there is an identification `e` of the restriction of `F` to `Coh(𝒪_𝒳)` with `F'`
(followed by the inclusion of `Coh(𝒪_𝒴)`), compatible with the tensor structures.  The extension
is unique up to unique isomorphism: for any other functor `G` commuting with filtered colimits and
identification `e'`, there is a unique isomorphism `F ≅ G` restricting to `e' ⁻¹ ∘ e` on coherent
modules, and it is compatible with any tensor structure on `G` for which `e'` is.

The input "every quasi-coherent module is a filtered colimit of coherent ones" is Stacks 0GRF
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFiltered_coherentSubobject_and_isColimit`), in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ind_coherentQuasicoherent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_tensorExtension_coherent
    (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳)
    (h𝒴 : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒴) :
    haveI := coherentQuasicoherent_isMonoidal B S hS 𝒳 h𝒳.2.2
    haveI := coherentQuasicoherent_isMonoidal B S hS 𝒴 h𝒴.2.2
    ∀ (F' : (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory ⥤
        (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒴).FullSubcategory) [F'.Additive]
      [PreservesFiniteColimits F'] (hF' : F'.TensorStructure),
      ∃ (F : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
          𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids ⥤
          FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
            𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids)
        (e : (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒳).ι ⋙ F ≅ F' ⋙ (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒴).ι)
        (hF : F.TensorStructure),
        (F.Additive ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits F ∧ PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} F ∧
          (hF.restrict (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒳)).IsCompatible
            (hF'.compι (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒴)) e) ∧
        ∀ (G : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
            𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids ⥤
            FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u, u} B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
              𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids),
          PreservesFilteredColimitsOfSize.{u, u} G →
            ∀ (e' : (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒳).ι ⋙ G ≅
                F' ⋙ (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒴).ι),
              ∃! φ : F ≅ G, Functor.whiskerLeft (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒳).ι φ.hom =
                  (e ≪≫ e'.symm).hom ∧
                ∀ hG : G.TensorStructure,
                  (hG.restrict (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒳)).IsCompatible
                    (hF'.compι (coherentQuasicoherent B S hS 𝒴)) e' →
                    hF.IsCompatible hG φ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_ringHom_tensorFunctor_comp_quasicoherentPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRK.**  Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack with affine diagonal, `R` a ring and
`F : QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod_R` a right exact tensor functor (additive, preserving finite colimits, lax
symmetric monoidal) which commutes with direct sums.  Let `g : U ⟶ 𝒳` be a morphism with `U` an
affine scheme, with ring of global functions `A`.  Then `g` is affine, and

1. `C = F(g_{QCoh,*}𝒪_U)` is a commutative `R`-algebra
   (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineTensorAlgebra` with its `CommRing` and `Algebra R`
   instances), and
2. there is a ring map `φ : A → C`

such that `F ∘ g_{QCoh,*}` sends `M` to `M ⊗_A C` seen as an `R`-module: both as a functor
`Mod_A ⥤ Mod_R` through `M ↦ M~`, and as a functor `QCoh(𝒪_U) ⥤ Mod_R` through
`N ↦ Γ(U, N)`, which is how `QCoh(𝒪_U)` is `Mod_A`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.tildeCounitIso`).

"Affine diagonal" is absolute, as in the source (Morphisms of Stacks, Definition 050D): it is the
diagonal of the view of `𝒳` over the terminal scheme `Spec ℤ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers`), which lies in every big fppf site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.contains_terminalScheme`).  That `g` is affine is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isAffineHom_of_isAffineHom_diagonal_viewOverIntegers`
(Stacks 0GQE over `Spec ℤ`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ringHom_tensorFunctor_comp_quasicoherentPushforward
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
      (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
        (AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳).val))
    (hUaff : IsAffineOver B S hS U) (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒳) :
    ∃ hg : AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS g,
      ∃ φ : schemeGlobalRing U →+* affineTensorAlgebra g hg F,
        Nonempty (tildeQuasicoherent.{u, w} U ⋙ affineQuasicoherentPushforward g hg ⋙ F ≅
          ModuleCat.extendScalars φ ⋙
            ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R (affineTensorAlgebra g hg F))) ∧
        Nonempty (affineQuasicoherentPushforward g hg ⋙ F ≅
          quasicoherentGlobalSections.{u, w} U ⋙ ModuleCat.extendScalars φ ⋙
            ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R (affineTensorAlgebra g hg F)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_affineTensorAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRL.**  Let `𝒳` be a Noetherian algebraic stack with affine diagonal, `R` a ring and
`F : QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod_R` a right exact tensor functor (additive, preserving finite colimits,
symmetric monoidal) which commutes with direct sums.  Let `g : U ⟶ 𝒳` be a flat and surjective
morphism from an affine scheme `U`.  Then `g` is affine, and the structure map `R ⟶ C` of the
commutative `R`-algebra `C = F(g_{QCoh,*}𝒪_U)` of Stacks 0GRK
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.affineTensorAlgebra`) is universally injective.

"Affine diagonal" is absolute, as in Stacks 0GRK: the diagonal of the view of `𝒳` over the
terminal scheme `Spec ℤ` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers`).  The proof
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.universallyInjective_affineTensorAlgebra_of_coherentGeneration` with
Stacks 0GRF (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isFiltered_coherentSubobject_and_isColimit`,
in the form `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ind_coherentQuasicoherent`) as its input.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_affineTensorAlgebra
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
      (diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
        (AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳).val))
    (h𝒳 : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳) (hUaff : IsAffineOver B S hS U)
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (F : AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳 ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R) [F.Braided]
    [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteColimits F] [∀ J : Type u, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F]
    (g : schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U ⟶ 𝒳) (hflat : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS g) :
    ∃ hg : AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS g,
      Algebra.UniversallyInjective R (affineTensorAlgebra g hg F)

declarations.name: Algebra.faithfullyFlat_of_flat_selfTensor_of_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
A universally injective ring map whose two self-base-change coprojections are flat is
faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem faithfullyFlat_of_flat_selfTensor_of_universallyInjective
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] {C : Type u} [CommRing C] [Algebra B C]
    (hleft : ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : C →ₐ[B] C ⊗[B] C).toRingHom).Flat)
    (_hright : ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : C →ₐ[B] C ⊗[B] C).toRingHom).Flat)
    (hBC : Algebra.UniversallyInjective B C) :
    (algebraMap B C).FaithfullyFlat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_tensorPushforwardMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRN, corrected: one leg affine.** Let `a : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` be an affine (Stacks 0CHQ),
quasi-compact, quasi-separated and flat 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and `b : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` one which
is representable (by schemes), quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For the projection
`f = pr₁ ≫ a : 𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` of the canonical 2-fibre product, the canonical map
`μ : a_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒴 ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} b_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒵 ⟶ f_{QCoh,*}𝒪_{𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.tensorPushforwardMap`, `s ⊗ t ↦ pr₁^*s · pr₂^*t`) is an
isomorphism in `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`; here `g_{QCoh,*} = quasicoherentDirectImage g`, `⊗` is the tensor
product sheaf of Stacks 0GQM and `𝒪 = 𝟙_`.

Relative to the source: `a` is in addition affine. Without it the statement is false
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.not_forall_nonempty_tensorPushforwardUnits_iso`: for the
two disjoint punctured planes `V`, `W` of `Spec k[x,y,z,w]/(xz,xw,yz,yw)` the right hand side is
`0` and the left hand side has global sections `Γ(V, 𝒪) ⊗ Γ(W, 𝒪) = k`); the source's proof
breaks at reading off `H⁰` of the derived tensor product, which needs `H¹(V, 𝒪) = 0` and
flatness of `Γ(V, 𝒪)` over the base. With `a` affine, `a_*𝒪` is computed by `Γ(V, 𝒪)` with `V`
affine and flat over the base, and the last step is flat base change of `H⁰`. Flatness of `b`,
and representability of `a` beyond what affineness gives, are not needed and are dropped.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_tensorPushforwardMap (ha : AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS a)
    (haqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS a) (haqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS a)
    (haf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS a)
    (hbr : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor b.hom))
    (hbqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS b) (hbqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS b) :
    IsIso (tensorPushforwardMap a b)
declarations.comment: corrected (one leg affine): for a : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳 affine, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and flat and b : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳 representable, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical map a_{QCoh,*}O_𝒴 ⊗ b_{QCoh,*}O_𝒵 ⟶ f_{QCoh,*}O_{𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵} is an isomorphism. Added relative to the source: a affine (as printed the tag is false, not_forall_nonempty_tensorPushforwardUnits_iso: two disjoint punctured planes, where H¹(V,O) ≠ 0 and Γ(V,O) is not flat over the base, so H⁰ of the derived tensor product is not the tensor product). Affineness makes a_*O be Γ(V,O) with V affine and flat over the base, so the last step is flat base change of H⁰. Dropped: flatness of b (not needed)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.nonempty_iso_tensorPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRN, corrected (one leg affine), the asserted isomorphism**
`a_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒴 ⊗ b_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒵 ≅ f_{QCoh,*}𝒪_{𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵}`, under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_tensorPushforwardMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_tensorPushforward (ha : AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineHom B S hS a)
    (haqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS a) (haqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS a)
    (haf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS a)
    (hbr : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor b.hom))
    (hbqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS b) (hbqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS b) :
    Nonempty ((quasicoherentDirectImage B S hS a).obj (𝟙_ _) ⊗
        (quasicoherentDirectImage B S hS b).obj (𝟙_ _) ≅
      (quasicoherentDirectImage B S hS
        ((twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS a b).fst ≫ a)).obj (𝟙_ _))
declarations.comment: corrected (one leg affine), the asserted isomorphism a_{QCoh,*}O_𝒴 ⊗ b_{QCoh,*}O_𝒵 ≅ f_{QCoh,*}O_{𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵}, for a affine, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and flat and b representable, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; see isIso_tensorPushforwardMap for the added hypothesis (a affine) and why it is needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.not_forall_nonempty_tensorPushforwardUnits_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRN, as printed, is false.** It is not true that for all 1-morphisms
`a : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳`, `b : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` of algebraic stacks which are representable (by schemes),
quasi-compact, quasi-separated and flat,
`a_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒴 ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} b_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒵 ≅ f_{QCoh,*}𝒪_{𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵}` for the projection
`f : 𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` of the 2-fibre product; not even an abstract isomorphism exists in general.

The counterexample: `X = Spec A`, `A = k[x, y, z, w] / (xz, xw, yz, yw)` the union of two planes
meeting at the origin, viewed as an algebraic stack over itself, and `a`, `b` the open immersions
of the punctured planes `V = D(z) ∪ D(w)` and `W = D(x) ∪ D(y)`. They are disjoint, so the right
hand side is `0`, while on global sections the left hand side is
`Γ(V, 𝒪) ⊗_A Γ(W, 𝒪) = k[z, w] ⊗_A k[x, y] = k`. Here `quasicoherentDirectImage` is
`f_{QCoh,*}` of Stacks 077A, `⊗` the tensor product of `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` of Stacks 0GQM (the local
instance `fppfModulesMonoidal`, the tensor product sheaf) and `𝟙_` the structure sheaf. The
source's proof breaks at its last step: the
Künneth formula (**Lemma 0FLQ**) computes `Rf_*𝒪 = Ra_*𝒪 ⊗^𝐋 Rb_*𝒪`, and reading off `H⁰` of the
right hand side as `a_*𝒪 ⊗ b_*𝒪` needs `H¹(V, 𝒪) = 0` or flatness; here `H¹(V, 𝒪) ≠ 0` (a punctured
plane) and `Γ(V, 𝒪) = A / (x, y)` is not flat over `A`. The same failure occurs with `a = b` the
open immersion `D(x) ∪ D(z) → Spec k[x, y, z, w] / (xy - zw)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.TensorPushforwardCounterexample.not_injective_lmul'_coneSections`). The
statement holds when one leg is affine
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.isIso_tensorPushforwardMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_nonempty_tensorPushforwardUnits_iso :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (𝒳 𝒴 𝒵 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (a : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳) (b : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳),
      Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor a.hom) →
      IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS a → AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS a →
      AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS a →
      Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒳.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor b.hom) →
      IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS b → AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS b →
      AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS b →
      Nonempty ((quasicoherentDirectImage B S hS a).obj (𝟙_ _) ⊗
          (quasicoherentDirectImage B S hS b).obj (𝟙_ _) ≅
        (quasicoherentDirectImage B S hS
          ((twoFibreProductSquareAlgebraicStacks B S hS a b).fst ≫ a)).obj (𝟙_ _))
declarations.comment: as printed it is false: a counterexample at X = Spec A, A = k[x,y,z,w]/(xz,xw,yz,yw), with a, b the open immersions of the two punctured planes D(z) ∪ D(w) and D(x) ∪ D(y); the 2-fibre product is empty so f_{QCoh,*}O = 0, while a_{QCoh,*}O ⊗ b_{QCoh,*}O ≠ 0 since Γ(V,O) ⊗_A Γ(W,O) = k (H¹(V,O) ≠ 0 and Γ(V,O) is not A-flat)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `μ`.**  For 1-morphisms `a : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳`, `b : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` of
algebraic stacks and a 2-fibre product square `sq` over the cospan `(a, b)` with apex
`𝒫 = 𝒴 ×_𝒳 𝒵` and projection `f = sq.fst ≫ a`, the map

`μ : a_{QCoh, *}𝒪_𝒴 ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} b_{QCoh, *}𝒪_𝒵 ⟶ f_{QCoh, *}𝒪_𝒫`

given by the tensor product of the two relative pullback maps
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentRelativePullbackMap` along the legs `sq.fst` and `sq.snd`,
followed by the comparison of **Remark 0GQR** attached to the coherator of
**Lemma 0778** at the relative cup product `cup`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap :
    FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorObj B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property
        ((flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed
            hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj
          (aStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.property
            hincY).obj (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.property))))
        ((flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed
            hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj
          (bStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒵.val.property
            hincZ).obj (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒵.val.val.p
              𝒵.val.property)))) ⟶
      (flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed hpres
          hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj
        (fStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS sq.pt.val.val.p
          sq.pt.val.property hincP).obj
            (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS sq.pt.val.val.p sq.pt.val.property)))
declarations.comment: THE CANONICAL MAP ONLY, NOT THE ASSERTION. This is μ : a_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒴 ⊗ b_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒵 ⟶ f_{QCoh,*}𝒪_𝒫, built from the two relative pullback maps of Stacks 06UM and the comparison of Remark 0GQR. Its INVERTIBILITY, which is what the tag asserts, is NOT PROVED here: the étale-local step (the content of Cohomology of Stacks Section 103.12, namely Lemma 0GQH plus the scheme-level Künneth of Lemma 0FLQ) does not compose with the stack-level QCoh monoidal product without further infrastructure. The reduction lemmas below that conclude invertibility from invertibility after a reflecting functor are deliberately left UNTAGGED, being instances of CategoryTheory.isIso_of_reflects_iso rather than content of this tag

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap_eq_coheratorCupProduct
declarations.doc:
**`μ` is the comparison of Remark 0GQR at a single map out of a tensor product.**  Tensoring
the two relative pullback maps and then applying the comparison of the coherator is the same as
applying the comparison to the relative cup product precomposed with those two maps on
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap_eq_coheratorCupProduct :
    (quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap B E hE S hS a b sq hincX hincY hincZ hincP hclosed hpres hls
        hlsD hwp hsep
        aStar bStar fStar hlqY prStarY adjPrY cmpY hlqZ prStarZ adjPrZ cmpZ
        TLQ tcmp cup) =
      coheratorCupProduct (flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
          𝒳.val.property hincX
      hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep)
        (Functor.uncurry.obj (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorBifunctor B S hS
      𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property)) TLQ tcmp
        (TLQ.map ((locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap B E hE S hS hincY hincP aStar fStar
      sq.fst hlqY prStarY adjPrY cmpY) ×ₘ
            (locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap B E hE S hS hincZ hincP bStar fStar
      sq.snd hlqZ prStarZ adjPrZ cmpZ)) ≫ cup)
declarations.comment: the identification of μ with Q of the relative cup product precomposed with the two relative pullback maps on LQCoh^fbc, i.e. that applying the coherator commutes with tensoring the two maps of Stacks 06UM in

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.map_quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**The diagram of Remark 0GQR commutes at `μ`.**  The inclusion of **Lemma 0778** applied to
`μ`, followed by the counit of the coherator adjunction, is the comparison `tcmp` of
**Lemma 0GQM** followed by the counit in each tensor factor and then by the relative cup product
precomposed with the two relative pullback maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap_comp_counit :
    (quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX).map
          (quasicoherentTensorPushforwardMap B E hE S hS a b sq hincX hincY hincZ hincP hclosed
              hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep
        aStar bStar fStar hlqY prStarY adjPrY cmpY hlqZ prStarZ adjPrZ cmpZ
        TLQ tcmp cup) ≫
        (flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX
      hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).counit.app
          (fStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS sq.pt.val.val.p sq.pt.val.property
              hincP).obj
        (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS sq.pt.val.val.p sq.pt.val.property))) =
      tcmp.app ((flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed
          hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj (aStar.obj
            ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.property hincY).obj
                (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.property))),
          (flatBaseChangeQuasicoherator B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX hclosed hpres
              hls hlsD hwp hsep).obj (bStar.obj
            ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒵.val.property hincZ).obj
                (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒵.val.property)))) ≫
        TLQ.map ((flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property
            hincX
      hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).counit.app
              (aStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.property
                  hincY).obj
                (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.property))) ×ₘ
            (flatBaseChangeQuasicoheratorAdjunction B E hE S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.property hincX
      hclosed hpres hls hlsD hwp hsep).counit.app
              (bStar.obj ((quasicoherentToFlatBaseChange B E hE S hS 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒵.val.property
                  hincZ).obj
                (FibredSite.quasicoherentTensorUnit B S hS 𝒵.val.val.p 𝒵.val.property)))) ≫
          (TLQ.map ((locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap B E hE S hS hincY hincP aStar fStar
      sq.fst hlqY prStarY adjPrY cmpY) ×ₘ
              (locallyQuasicoherentStructurePullbackMap B E hE S hS hincZ hincP bStar fStar
      sq.snd hlqZ prStarZ adjPrZ cmpZ)) ≫ cup)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the diagram of Remark 0GQR at μ, over the same carried data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.eq_and_exists_iso_pointPullbackTransportIso_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRP.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack with affine diagonal and `B` a ring. Let
`f₁, f₂ : Spec B ⟶ 𝒳` be two morphisms, given as points `x₁`, `x₂` of `𝒳` over `Spec B`, with
structure morphisms `q₁, q₂ : Spec B ⟶ S`, and let `t : f₁^* ≅ f₂^*` be an isomorphism of the
tensor functors `f_i^* : QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod_B`
    (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.pointPullback`,
a braided monoidal additive functor; `t` is monoidal). Then `q₁ = q₂`, and there is a 2-arrow
`f₁ ⟶ f₂`, an isomorphism `a : x₁ ≅ x₂` lying over the identity of `Spec B`, inducing `t`.

"Affine diagonal" is absolute, as in the source (Morphisms of Stacks, Definition 050D): it is the
diagonal of the view of `𝒳` over `Spec ℤ`,
    `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers`.
The structure morphisms to `S` are not assumed equal: that they agree is part of the conclusion,
read off from the functions `B ⟶ Γ(x_i, 𝒪)` which `t` preserves (it is monoidal). The form with
equal structure morphisms is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_iso_pointPullbackTransportIso_eq_of_over`.

The proof does not follow the source's chart and descent, but takes the chart `g = f₁ : Spec B ⟶ 𝒳`
itself (affine, the diagonal being affine): with `W_i = Spec B ×_{f_i, 𝒳, f₁} Spec B` and
`g_*𝒪 = g_{QCoh,*}𝒪_{Spec B}`, `f_i^*(g_*𝒪) = Γ(W_i)`, and `t` gives a ring isomorphism
`Γ(W₂) ⟶ Γ(W₁)` over both copies of `B` (it is monoidal and natural, the multiplication of
`g_*𝒪` being `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.affineDirectImageMul`), hence an arrow
`W₁ ⟶ W₂`; the image of the identity 2-arrow of `f₁` in `W₁` is the 2-arrow `f₁ ≅ f₂`. That it
induces `t` follows from naturality of `t` and the units `M ⟶ g_* g^* M`. This is the content of
Stacks 0GRK (the algebra `C = F(g_{QCoh,*}𝒪_U)` with its map `A ⟶ C`) for the point pullbacks,
computed directly.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_and_exists_iso_pointPullbackTransportIso_eq
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
      (Stack.diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
        (AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳).val))
    {q₁ q₂ : B.obj hR ⟶ B.obj hS} {x₁ x₂ : 𝒳.val.val.obj}
    (hx₁ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₁ = Over.mk q₁) (hx₂ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₂ = Over.mk q₂)
    (t : pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₁ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁) ≅
      pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₂ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)) [NatTrans.IsMonoidal t.hom] :
    q₁ = q₂ ∧ ∃ (a : x₁ ≅ x₂) (ha : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (𝒳.val.val.p.map a.hom) ≫
        (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂).hom = (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁).hom),
      pointPullbackTransportIso B S hS 𝒳 (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁) (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)
        a ha = t
declarations.comment: points over possibly different structure morphisms; they agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exists_iso_pointPullbackTransportIso_eq_of_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRP, with equal structure morphisms** (the source's statement). Let `𝒳` be an
algebraic stack with affine diagonal (over `Spec ℤ`), `B` a ring and `f₁, f₂ : Spec B ⟶ 𝒳` two
morphisms over `S`, given as points `x₁`, `x₂` of `𝒳` lying over the same object `Spec B ⟶ S` of
the site. Every isomorphism `t : f₁^* ≅ f₂^*` of the tensor functors
`f_i^* : QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod_B` is induced by a 2-arrow `f₁ ⟶ f₂`: an isomorphism `a : x₁ ≅ x₂` of
the fibre over `Spec B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_pointPullbackTransportIso_eq_of_over
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
      (Stack.diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
        (AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳).val))
    {q : B.obj hR ⟶ B.obj hS} {x₁ x₂ : 𝒳.val.val.obj}
    (hx₁ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₁ = Over.mk q) (hx₂ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₂ = Over.mk q)
    (t : pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₁ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁) ≅
      pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₂ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)) [NatTrans.IsMonoidal t.hom] :
    ∃ (a : x₁ ≅ x₂) (ha : 𝒳.val.val.p.map a.hom = eqToHom (hx₁.trans hx₂.symm)),
      pointPullbackTransportIso B S hS 𝒳 (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁) (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)
        a (toScheme_map_comp_overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁ hx₂ a ha) = t
declarations.comment: the source's form, with equal structure morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.existsUnique_pointPullback_iso_of_tensorFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRQ.** Let `𝒳` be a Noetherian algebraic stack with affine diagonal (over
`Spec ℤ`, as in the source), `R` a ring (with `Spec R` in the site) and `F : QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod_R` a
right exact tensor functor (additive, preserving finite colimits, braided monoidal) which commutes
with direct sums. Then `F` comes from a unique morphism `Spec R ⟶ 𝒳`:

1. there are a point `x` of `𝒳` over `Spec R` (lying over some `q : Spec R ⟶ S`) and an
   isomorphism of tensor functors `e : F ≅ x^*`;
2. if `e₁ : F ≅ x₁^*` and `e₂ : F ≅ x₂^*` are two such, over `q₁` and `q₂`, then `q₁ = q₂` and
   there is a unique 2-arrow `a : x₁ ≅ x₂` over the identity of `Spec R` whose induced isomorphism
   `x₁^* ≅ x₂^*` is `e₁⁻¹ ≫ e₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_pointPullback_iso_of_tensorFunctor
    (h𝒳 : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
      (Stack.diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
        (viewOverIntegers B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳).val))
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (hR : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
    (F : quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳 ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R) [F.Additive] [F.Braided]
    [PreservesFiniteColimits F] [∀ J : Type u, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F] :
    (∃ (q : B.obj hR ⟶ B.obj hS) (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hx : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x = Over.mk q)
        (e : F ≅ pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx)), NatTrans.IsMonoidal e.hom) ∧
    ∀ {q₁ q₂ : B.obj hR ⟶ B.obj hS} {x₁ x₂ : 𝒳.val.val.obj}
      (hx₁ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₁ = Over.mk q₁) (hx₂ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₂ = Over.mk q₂)
      (e₁ : F ≅ pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₁ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁))
      (e₂ : F ≅ pointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₂ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)),
      NatTrans.IsMonoidal e₁.hom → NatTrans.IsMonoidal e₂.hom →
      q₁ = q₂ ∧ ∃ (a : x₁ ≅ x₂) (ha : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (𝒳.val.val.p.map a.hom) ≫
          (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂).hom = (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁).hom),
        pointPullbackTransportIso B S hS 𝒳 (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁) (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)
            a ha = e₁.symm ≪≫ e₂ ∧
          ∀ (b : x₁ ≅ x₂) (hb : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (𝒳.val.val.p.map b.hom) ≫
              (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂).hom = (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁).hom),
            pointPullbackTransportIso B S hS 𝒳 (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁)
              (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂) b hb = e₁.symm ≪≫ e₂ → b = a
declarations.comment: the morphism Spec R ⟶ 𝒳 is a point over Spec R in the site; uniqueness is up to the unique 2-arrow inducing the given isomorphism of tensor functors

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.existsUnique_coherentPointPullback_iso_of_tensorFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GRR.** Let `𝒳` be a Noetherian algebraic stack with affine diagonal (over `Spec ℤ`,
as in the source), `R` a Noetherian ring (with `Spec R` in the site) and
`F : Coh(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ Mod^{fg}_R` a right exact tensor functor (additive, preserving finite colimits,
braided monoidal). Then `F` comes from a unique morphism `Spec R ⟶ 𝒳`:

1. there are a point `x` of `𝒳` over `Spec R` (lying over some `q : Spec R ⟶ S`) and an
   isomorphism of tensor functors `F ≅ x^*|_{Coh}`;
2. if `E₁ : F ≅ x₁^*|_{Coh}` and `E₂ : F ≅ x₂^*|_{Coh}` are two such, over `q₁` and `q₂`, then
   `q₁ = q₂` and there is a 2-arrow `a : x₁ ≅ x₂` over the identity of `Spec R` inducing
   `E₁⁻¹ ≫ E₂` on coherent modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_coherentPointPullback_iso_of_tensorFunctor
    (h𝒳 : IsNoetherianStack.{u, w, w'} B S hS 𝒳)
    (hΔ : Stack.IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
      (Stack.diagonal.{u, u, u + 1} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) (contains_terminalScheme B)
        (AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers B S hS (contains_terminalScheme B) 𝒳).val))
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (hR : B.Contains (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
    (F : Coh.{u, u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ⥤ FGModuleCat.{u} R) [F.Additive] [F.Braided]
    [PreservesFiniteColimits F] :
    (∃ (q : B.obj hR ⟶ B.obj hS) (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) (hx : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x = Over.mk q)
      (E : F ≅ coherentPointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx)),
        NatTrans.IsMonoidal E.hom) ∧
    ∀ {q₁ q₂ : B.obj hR ⟶ B.obj hS} {x₁ x₂ : 𝒳.val.val.obj}
      (hx₁ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₁ = Over.mk q₁) (hx₂ : 𝒳.val.val.p.obj x₂ = Over.mk q₂)
      (E₁ : F ≅ coherentPointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₁ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁))
      (E₂ : F ≅ coherentPointPullback B S hS 𝒳 x₂ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂)),
      NatTrans.IsMonoidal E₁.hom → NatTrans.IsMonoidal E₂.hom →
      q₁ = q₂ ∧ ∃ (a : x₁ ≅ x₂) (ha : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map
          (𝒳.val.val.p.map a.hom) ≫ (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂).hom =
            (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁).hom),
        Functor.whiskerLeft (coherentQuasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳)
            (pointPullbackTransportIso B S hS 𝒳 (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₁)
              (overSpecIso B S hS 𝒳 hx₂) a ha).hom =
          (coherentPointPullbackCompIso B S hS 𝒳 x₁ _).inv ≫
            Functor.whiskerRight (E₁.inv ≫ E₂.hom)
              (forget₂ (FGModuleCat.{u} R) (ModuleCat.{u} R)) ≫
              (coherentPointPullbackCompIso B S hS 𝒳 x₂ _).hom
declarations.comment: the morphism Spec R ⟶ 𝒳 is a point over Spec R in the site; uniqueness is up to a 2-arrow inducing the given isomorphism of tensor functors

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ColimitCofinality.sections_commute_colimit_of_cofinality
declarations.doc:
**(Stacks 0GS0.) Sections commute with colimits along ordinals of large enough cofinality.**

Let `𝒮` be a site (a small category `C` with covering families carrying explicit index sets and
satisfying axioms (1)–(3); in particular all fiber products `U_i ×_X U_j` exist). Let `β` be an
ordinal and `F : β.ToType ⥤ Sh(C)` a system of sheaves over `β` (a `β`-indexed direct system of
sheaves of sets), whose colimit in `Sh(C)` exists (`Sh(C)` is cocomplete, Definition 3). Suppose
the cofinality of `β` is large enough for `𝒮` (the pointwise bound `|I| < cf β` for every covering
family). Then for every object `U` the canonical comparison map `c_U` is a bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem sections_commute_colimit_of_cofinality
    {β : Ordinal.{u}} (F : β.ToType ⥤ 𝒮.Sheaf) [HasColimit F]
    (hβ : 𝒮.CofinalityLargeEnough β) (U : C) :
    Function.Bijective (⇑(𝒮.colimSectionsComparison F U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LimitFPObjectDescent.exists_isLimit_finiteType_arrow
declarations.doc:
A morphism between quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes is a limit of morphisms between
schemes of finite type over `ℤ`, with affine transition morphisms on sources and targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_finiteType_arrow
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirectedOrder I)
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Arrow Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D),
      (∀ i,
        LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from (D.obj i).left) ∧
          QuasiCompact (terminal.from (D.obj i).left)) ∧
      (∀ i,
        LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from (D.obj i).right) ∧
          QuasiCompact (terminal.from (D.obj i).right)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j),
        IsAffineHom (D.map g).left ∧ IsAffineHom (D.map g).right) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧ Nonempty (c.pt ≅ Arrow.mk f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isFinite_of_henselianPair
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GS2 for a finite morphism.** If `(A, I)` is a henselian pair and `f : X ⟶ Spec A` is
finite, then base change to the closed fibre `X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ I) ⟶ X` is an equivalence on
finite étale covers.

A finite morphism is affine, so `X.isoSpec` presents `X` as `Spec Γ(X, ⊤)` with `Γ(X, ⊤)` a finite,
hence integral, `A`-algebra, and the statement becomes the affine core
`isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_specMap_algebraMap_of_henselianPair`.  The two differences
between the two base-change morphisms are absorbed by the transport lemmas: the pullback along a
composite is rebracketed by `pullbackRightPullbackFstIso`, and a pullback projection along the
isomorphism `X.isoSpec.hom` is itself that isomorphism's inverse precomposed with an isomorphism.

This is the case of Tag 0GS2 in which properness is used only through finiteness: no
algebraization — neither Grothendieck existence nor Artin approximation — enters.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isFinite_of_henselianPair
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : HenselianPair A I)
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsFinite f] :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: for a finite morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec A`, which is the case of a proper `f` in which no algebraization is needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianPair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GS2.** Let `(A, I)` be a henselian pair and let `X` be a proper scheme
over `A`, with closed fibre `X₀ = X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ I)`. Then base change
`FÉt_X ⥤ FÉt_{X₀}, U ↦ U ×_X X₀` is an equivalence of categories.

Essential surjectivity is `essSurj_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianPair`, applied to
every scheme finite étale over `X` (each again proper over `A`); full faithfulness follows from it
by `isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianPair_of_essSurj`, as in the
source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianPair (A : Type u)
    [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : HenselianPair A I) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange (pullback.fst f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the full statement: any henselian pair `(A, I)` and any proper `X` over `Spec A`, with nothing granted or assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasRelativeApproximation_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Relative approximation over `Spec ℤ`, on any big fppf site.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `Spec ℤ` is the limit of a directed inverse
system of morphisms of quasi-separated algebraic spaces of finite type over `Spec ℤ` with affine
transition morphisms. It is built on an enlargement of the site on which `X` and `Y` have small
atlases, and descended.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasRelativeApproximation_of_isQuasiCompactSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X Y : (BigFppfOver B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ Y)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ X)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ Y)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hZ X)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hZ Y) :
    HasRelativeApproximation B hZ f

declarations.name: comap_ne_bot_of_localization_or_discrete_fibers
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a map of domains. Suppose that it is a localization of an étale
map; or that it is flat and a localization of an unramified, quasi-finite, or integral
map; or that it is flat and its fibers have no nontrivial specializations; or that it
maps the generic point to the generic point and its fibers have no nontrivial
specializations; or that exactly one point of `Spec(B)` maps to the generic point of
`Spec(A)`. Then every nonzero ideal of `B` has nonzero contraction to `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_ne_bot_of_localization_or_discrete_fibers
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain A] [IsDomain B]
    [Algebra A B]
    (h :
      (∃ (T : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra A T) (_ : Algebra T B)
          (_ : IsScalarTower A T B), Algebra.Etale A T ∧
            ∃ M : Submonoid T, IsLocalization M B) ∨
      (Module.Flat A B ∧
        ∃ (T : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra A T) (_ : Algebra T B)
          (_ : IsScalarTower A T B), Algebra.Unramified A T ∧
            ∃ M : Submonoid T, IsLocalization M B) ∨
      (Module.Flat A B ∧
        ∃ (T : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra A T) (_ : Algebra T B)
          (_ : IsScalarTower A T B), Algebra.QuasiFinite A T ∧
            ∃ M : Submonoid T, IsLocalization M B) ∨
      (Module.Flat A B ∧
        ∃ (T : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing T) (_ : Algebra A T) (_ : Algebra T B)
          (_ : IsScalarTower A T B), Algebra.IsIntegral A T ∧
            ∃ M : Submonoid T, IsLocalization M B) ∨
      (Module.Flat A B ∧ NoNontrivialSpecializationsInFibers A B) ∨
      ((⊥ : Ideal B).comap (algebraMap A B) = ⊥ ∧
        NoNontrivialSpecializationsInFibers A B) ∨
      (∃! q : Ideal B, q.IsPrime ∧ q.comap (algebraMap A B) = ⊥)) :
    ∀ J : Ideal B, J ≠ ⊥ → J.comap (algebraMap A B) ≠ ⊥

declarations.name: exists_etale_isLocalization_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GS6.** An injective, essentially finite type local map from a geometrically
unibranch local domain is a localization of an étale map when its target maximal ideal is
extended from the source and its residue-field extension is separable.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_isLocalization_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    (hinjective : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hunibranch : IsGeometricallyUnibranch A)
    (hmaximal : Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B)
    (hseparable : Algebra.IsSeparable (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C)
      (_ : Algebra C B) (_ : IsScalarTower A C B) (M : Submonoid C),
        Algebra.Etale A C ∧ IsLocalization M B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_unramifiedAt_of_specializes_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite type with `Y` integral,
and let `x : X` be a point whose image is a point where `Y` is geometrically unibranch. If `f`
is unramified at `x` and `x` is a specialization of a point lying over the generic point of `Y`,
then `f` is étale at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_of_unramifiedAt_of_specializes_genericPoint
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral Y] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] {x x' : X}
    (hy : IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt Y (f x))
    (hxx' : x' ⤳ x) (hx' : f x' = genericPoint Y)
    (hunramified : UnramifiedAt f x) :
    EtaleAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_of_unramified_of_dominant_component
declarations.doc:
An unramified morphism from a connected scheme to an integral geometrically unibranch scheme
is étale as soon as one irreducible component of its source dominates the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_of_unramified_of_dominant_component
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral Y] [Unramified f] [ConnectedSpace X]
    (hY : IsGeometricallyUnibranch Y)
    (hdom : ∃ Z : irreducibleComponents X, closure (f '' (Z : Set X)) = Set.univ) :
    Etale f
declarations.comment: etaleness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.irreducibleSpace_of_unramified_of_dominant_component
declarations.doc:
The source of an unramified morphism from a connected scheme to an integral geometrically
unibranch scheme is irreducible as soon as one of its irreducible components dominates the
target.
declarations.statement:
theorem irreducibleSpace_of_unramified_of_dominant_component
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral Y] [Unramified f] [ConnectedSpace X]
    (hY : IsGeometricallyUnibranch Y)
    (hdom : ∃ Z : irreducibleComponents X, closure (f '' (Z : Set X)) = Set.univ) :
    IrreducibleSpace X
declarations.comment: irreducibility

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_left_of_comp_etaleAt_of_specializes_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
If a composite `f ≫ g` is étale at `x`, the intermediate scheme is integral and
geometrically unibranch at `f x`, and `x` is a specialization of a point whose image under `f` is
the generic point, then `f` is étale at `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_left_of_comp_etaleAt_of_specializes_genericPoint
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIntegral Y] {x x' : X}
    (hy : IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt Y (f x)) (hcomp : EtaleAt (f ≫ g) x)
    (hxx' : x' ⤳ x) (hx' : f x' = genericPoint Y) :
    EtaleAt f x
declarations.comment: first factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_right_of_comp_etaleAt_of_specializes_genericPoint
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_left_of_comp_etaleAt_of_specializes_genericPoint`, the second factor
is étale at the image of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_right_of_comp_etaleAt_of_specializes_genericPoint
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIntegral Y] {x x' : X}
    (hy : IsGeometricallyUnibranchAt Y (f x)) (hcomp : EtaleAt (f ≫ g) x)
    (hxx' : x' ⤳ x) (hx' : f x' = genericPoint Y) :
    EtaleAt g (f x)
