declarations.comment: second factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etale_left_of_comp_etale_of_dominant_components
declarations.doc:
If a composite `f ≫ g` is étale, the intermediate scheme is integral and geometrically
unibranch, and every irreducible component of the source dominates it, then `f` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_left_of_comp_etale_of_dominant_components
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIntegral Y]
    (hY : IsGeometricallyUnibranch Y) (hcomp : Etale (f ≫ g))
    (hdom : ∀ C : irreducibleComponents X, closure (f '' (C : Set X)) = Set.univ) :
    Etale f
declarations.comment: first factor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_right_of_comp_etale_of_dominant_components
declarations.doc:
Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.etale_left_of_comp_etale_of_dominant_components`, the second factor is étale
at every point in the image of the first.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleAt_right_of_comp_etale_of_dominant_components
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIntegral Y]
    (hY : IsGeometricallyUnibranch Y) (hcomp : Etale (f ≫ g))
    (hdom : ∀ C : irreducibleComponents X, closure (f '' (C : Set X)) = Set.univ) :
    ∀ y ∈ Set.range f, EtaleAt g y
declarations.comment: second factor

declarations.name: exists_etale_away_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch_of_isUnramifiedAt
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a ring map from a domain, and let `q` be a prime of `B` lying over a prime
`p` of `A`. If `Aₚ` is geometrically unibranch, the map is unramified at `q`, and the canonical
map `Aₚ → B_q` is injective, then some principal localization `B_g`, with `g ∉ q`, is étale
over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_away_of_isGeometricallyUnibranch_of_isUnramifiedAt
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsDomain A]
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] [q.LiesOver p]
    (hgeom : IsGeometricallyUnibranch (Localization.AtPrime p))
    (hunram : ∃ f : B, f ∉ q ∧ Algebra.Unramified A (Localization.Away f))
    (hinj : letI := Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p q
      Function.Injective
        (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q))) :
    ∃ g : B, g ∉ q ∧ Algebra.Etale A (Localization.Away g)

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_mem_maximalIdeal_bijective_algebraMap_quotient_span_pow
declarations.doc:
**An étale local homomorphism is an isomorphism modulo powers of a principal ideal.** Let
`(R, m_R) → (S, m_S)` be a local homomorphism of local rings such that `S` is the localization
of an étale `R`-algebra `T` at a prime `q`, and such that the residue field extension
`κ(m_R) → κ(m_S)` is surjective, hence an isomorphism. Then there is `t ∈ m_R` such that
`R/tⁿR → S/tⁿS` is an isomorphism for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.exists_mem_maximalIdeal_bijective_algebraMap_quotient_span_pow
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (S : Type v) [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] (T : Type w) [CommRing T] [Algebra R T]
    [Algebra.Etale R T] [Algebra T S] [IsScalarTower R T S] (q : Ideal T) [q.IsPrime]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime S q]
    (hres : Function.Surjective (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap R S))) :
    ∃ t ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R, ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
      (algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {t ^ n}) (S ⧸ (Ideal.span {t ^ n}).map (algebraMap R S)))
declarations.comment:
The hypothesis `t ∈ m_R` and the conclusion are the source's; the map shown
bijective is the canonical `R/tⁿR → S/tⁿS`. Stated for all `n : ℕ` (the case `n = 0` is the zero
ring), with `κ(m_R) → κ(m_S)` merely surjective (equivalent, as it is injective automatically),
and with the étale algebra `T` and the prime `q` as hypotheses rather than an existential.

declarations.name: essentiallyOfFinitePresentation_and_finitePresentation_of_flat_of_valuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GSE.** Let `A` be a valuation ring, `B` an essentially-of-finite-type
`A`-algebra, and `M` a `B`-module.  If `B` is flat over `A`, then `A → B` is essentially of
finite presentation.  If `M` is finite over `B` and flat over `A`, then `M` is finitely presented
over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallyOfFinitePresentation_and_finitePresentation_of_flat_of_valuationRing
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B] [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M] :
    (Module.Flat A B → (algebraMap A B).EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) ∧
      (Module.Flat A M → Module.Finite B M → Module.FinitePresentation B M)

declarations.name: Module.Flat.injective_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal_of_valuationRing
declarations.doc:
**The injectivity half of Stacks 0GSG.** Let `A` be a valuation ring, let `A → B` be a local
homomorphism of local rings which is essentially of finite type, and let `u : N → M` be a map of
finite `B`-modules with `M` flat over `A`. If `ū : N/𝔪_A N → M/𝔪_A M` is injective then `u` is
injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal_of_valuationRing
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} {N : Type u₃} {M : Type u₄}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N] [Module.Finite B N]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M] [Module.Finite B M]
    [Module.Flat A M]
    (u : N →ₗ[B] M)
    (hu : Function.Injective
      (Submodule.mapQ (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A N))
        (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) (u.restrictScalars A)
        (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal A) (u.restrictScalars A)))) :
    Function.Injective u
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: Module.Flat.flat_quotient_range_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal_of_valuationRing
declarations.doc:
**The cokernel half of Stacks 0GSG.** Let `A` be a valuation ring, let `A → B` be a local
homomorphism of local rings which is essentially of finite type, and let `u : N → M` be a map of
finite `B`-modules with `M` flat over `A`. If `ū : N/𝔪_A N → M/𝔪_A M` is injective then `M/u(N)`
is flat over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_quotient_range_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal_of_valuationRing
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} {N : Type u₃} {M : Type u₄}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N] [Module.Finite B N]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M] [Module.Finite B M]
    [Module.Flat A M]
    (u : N →ₗ[B] M)
    (hu : Function.Injective
      (Submodule.mapQ (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A N))
        (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) (u.restrictScalars A)
        (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal A) (u.restrictScalars A)))) :
    Module.Flat A (M ⧸ LinearMap.range u)
declarations.comment: flatness of the cokernel

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.exists_valuation_base_change_generic_component
declarations.doc:
A valuation-ring base change through a prescribed generic point of a component of
the fibre of the integral closure of a point.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_valuation_base_change_generic_component
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (y : X)
    (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hY : Y = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure ({y} : Set X)))
    (s : S) (x : X)
    (ξ : (Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber s)
    (hξ : closure ({ξ} : Set ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber s)) ∈
      irreducibleComponents ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber s))
    (hx : Y.subschemeι ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiberι s ξ) = x) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsDomain A) (_ : ValuationRing A)
      (g : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S),
      g (genericPoint (Spec (.of A))) = f y ∧
      g (closedPoint A) = s ∧
      (let X' := (pullback f g : Scheme.{u})
       let p : X' ⟶ X := pullback.fst f g
       let q : X' ⟶ Spec (.of A) := pullback.snd f g
       let Z : X'.IdealSheafData := Y.comap p
       let j : Z.subscheme ⟶ X' := Z.subschemeι
       ∃ η : (j ≫ q).fiber (genericPoint (Spec (.of A))),
         closure ({η} : Set ((j ≫ q).fiber (genericPoint (Spec (.of A))))) ∈
           irreducibleComponents ((j ≫ q).fiber (genericPoint (Spec (.of A)))) ∧
         p (j ((j ≫ q).fiberι (genericPoint (Spec (.of A))) η)) = y ∧
         (let y' : X' := j ((j ≫ q).fiberι (genericPoint (Spec (.of A))) η)
          let Y' : X'.IdealSheafData :=
            Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ({y'} : Set X'))
          IsIntegral Y'.subscheme ∧
          ∃ ξ' : (Y'.subschemeι ≫ q).fiber (closedPoint A),
            closure ({ξ'} : Set ((Y'.subschemeι ≫ q).fiber (closedPoint A))) ∈
              irreducibleComponents ((Y'.subschemeι ≫ q).fiber (closedPoint A)) ∧
            p (Y'.subschemeι ((Y'.subschemeι ≫ q).fiberι (closedPoint A) ξ')) = x))

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_fiber_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Fibre dimension at a generic point of the fibre of a closure.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally
of finite type, `F` a quasi-coherent finite type `𝒪_X`-module and `y` a point of `Ass_{X/S}(F)`.
Let `Y` be the reduced closed subscheme supported on the closure of `y`. At a generic point `x`
of an irreducible component of the fibre of `Y` over `s` at whose image `F` is flat over `S`, the
local dimension of that fibre equals the dimension of the fibre of `Y` over `f y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDimAt_fiber_eq_fiber_of_flat
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (y : X) (hy : y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F) (s : S) :
    let Y := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (⟨closure ({y} : Set X), isClosed_closure⟩ : Closeds X)
    let g : Y.subscheme ⟶ S := Y.subschemeι ≫ f
    ∀ x : g.fiber s,
      (∃ Z : irreducibleComponents (g.fiber s), IsGenericPoint x (Z : Set (g.fiber s))) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (Y.subschemeι (g.fiberι s x)) →
      topologicalKrullDimAt (g.fiber s) x = topologicalKrullDim (g.fiber (f y))
declarations.comment: the fibre dimension equality

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.mem_relativeAssassin_of_isGenericPoint_fibre_closure
declarations.doc:
**Relative associated points at generic points of the fibres of a closure.** Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, `F` a quasi-coherent finite type `𝒪_X`-module and `y` a
point of `Ass_{X/S}(F)`. Let `Y` be the reduced closed subscheme supported on the closure of `y`
and let `ξ` be a generic point of an irreducible component of the fibre of `Y` over a point `s`
of `S`. If `F` is flat over `S` at the image of `ξ` in `X`, that image lies in
`Ass_{X/S}(F)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_relativeAssassin_of_isGenericPoint_fibre_closure
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (y : X) (hy : y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F)
    (Y : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hY : Y = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ({y} : Set X)))
    (s : S) (ξ : (Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber s)
    (hξ : closure ({ξ} : Set ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber s)) ∈
      irreducibleComponents ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiber s))
    (hflat : IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F
      (Y.subschemeι ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiberι s ξ))) :
    Y.subschemeι ((Y.subschemeι ≫ f).fiberι s ξ)
      ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F
declarations.comment: the relative assassin conclusion

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.isDominant_closureSubschemeMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the reduced closure of a point to the reduced closure
of its image is dominant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDominant_closureSubschemeMap
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (y : X) :
    let Y := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure ({y} : Set X))
    let T := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure ({f y} : Set S))
    let h : Y.subscheme ⟶ T.subscheme :=
      Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeMap Y T f (by
        rw [Scheme.IdealSheafData.map_vanishingIdeal]
        apply le_of_eq
        apply congrArg Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        apply Closeds.ext
        change closure ({f y} : Set S) = closure (f '' closure ({y} : Set X))
        exact ((closure_image_closure f.continuous).trans (by simp)).symm)
    IsDominant h
declarations.comment: dominance of the canonical map

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.relativeDimension_closureSubschemeMap
declarations.doc:
If the module is flat at component-generic fibre points, the canonical map
from the reduced closure of a relative associated point to the reduced closure
of its image has constant relative dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimension_closureSubschemeMap
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (y : X) (hy : y ∈ Stacks.Divisors.relativeAssassin f F) :
    let Y := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure ({y} : Set X))
    let T := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
      (Closeds.closure ({f y} : Set S))
    let h : Y.subscheme ⟶ T.subscheme :=
      Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeMap Y T f (by
        rw [Scheme.IdealSheafData.map_vanishingIdeal]
        apply le_of_eq
        apply congrArg Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
        apply Closeds.ext
        change closure ({f y} : Set S) = closure (f '' closure ({y} : Set X))
        exact ((closure_image_closure f.continuous).trans (by simp)).symm)
    (∀ t : T.subscheme, ∀ x : h.fiber t,
      (∃ Z : irreducibleComponents (h.fiber t),
        IsGenericPoint x (Z : Set (h.fiber t))) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F
        (Y.subschemeι (h.fiberι t x))) →
    let hh : LocallyOfFiniteType h := by
      have : LocallyOfFiniteType (h ≫ T.subschemeι) := by
        rw [Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeMap_subschemeι]
        infer_instance
      exact locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp h T.subschemeι
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType h := hh
    ∃ d : ℕ, RelativeDimension h d
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.relativeDimension_of_isGenericPoint_of_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GSK, first set of hypotheses.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite
type with `X` integral of generic point `ξ`, and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of
finite type whose support is all of `X` and which is flat over `S` at every generic point of
every fibre. If the transcendence degree of `κ(ξ)` over `κ(f ξ)` is `d`, then `f` has relative
dimension `d` in the sense of Tag 02NJ.

Only the irreducibility of `X` is used, not its reducedness, and the flatness hypothesis is the
one the source's last sentence allows; flatness of `F` over `S` everywhere, which the source's
list asks for, gives it as `fun s z _ => hF _`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimension_of_isGenericPoint_of_trdeg (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hsupp : SheafOfModules.supp F = Set.univ)
    (hflat : ∀ (s : S) (z : f.fiber s), z ∈ genericPoints (f.fiber s) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (f.fiberι s z))
    (ξ : X) (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ (Set.univ : Set X)) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : letI := (f.residueFieldMap ξ).hom.toAlgebra
      Cardinal.toENat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f ξ)) (X.residueField ξ)) = (d : ℕ∞)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f d
declarations.comment: first set of hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeAssassin.relativeDimension_of_dense_fiber_of_component_dim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GSK, second set of hypotheses.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite
type and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type whose support is all of `X` and
which is flat over `S` at every generic point of every fibre. If the fibre over a point `η` of
`S` is dense in `X` and every irreducible component of that fibre has dimension `d`, then `f` has
relative dimension `d` in the sense of Tag 02NJ.

The source asks in addition that `S` be irreducible with `η` its generic point, which is what
makes the density plausible; the argument uses only the density itself, so that hypothesis is
dropped here and the source's statement is the case of an irreducible `S` and its generic
point. The flatness hypothesis is again the weakened one of the source's last sentence.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeDimension_of_dense_fiber_of_component_dim (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType]
    (hsupp : SheafOfModules.supp F = Set.univ)
    (hflat : ∀ (s : S) (z : f.fiber s), z ∈ genericPoints (f.fiber s) →
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsFlatOverAt f.toLRSHom.toShHom F (f.fiberι s z))
    (η : S) (hdense : Dense (f ⁻¹' ({η} : Set S))) (d : ℕ)
    (hdim : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents (f.fiber η), topologicalKrullDim Z = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeDimension f d
declarations.comment: second set of hypotheses

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isSaturated_and_isCompatibleWithTriangulation_inverseImage_ι_and_isLocalizedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a pre-triangulated category, let `P` be a full pre-triangulated subcategory of `C`,
and let `W` be a saturated multiplicative system of morphisms of `C` compatible with the
triangulated structure. Then `W ∩ Arrows(P)`, i.e. `W.inverseImage P.ι`, is a saturated
multiplicative system on `P` compatible with the triangulated structure, and if every object of `C`
admits a resolution by `P` — a morphism `s : X' ⟶ X` in `W` with `X'` in `P` — then the inclusion
of `P` induces an equivalence `(W ∩ Arrows(P))⁻¹P ⥤ W⁻¹C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSaturated_and_isCompatibleWithTriangulation_inverseImage_ι_and_isLocalizedEquivalence
    (hW : W.IsSaturated) [W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation] :
    (W.inverseImage P.ι).IsSaturated ∧
      (W.inverseImage P.ι).IsCompatibleWithTriangulation ∧
      (({ functor := P.ι, map := le_rfl } :
            LocalizerMorphism (W.inverseImage P.ι) W).HasLeftResolutions →
        ({ functor := P.ι, map := le_rfl } :
          LocalizerMorphism (W.inverseImage P.ι) W).IsLocalizedEquivalence)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.extClass_comp_extClass_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**Vanishing of a Yoneda product of two extension classes.** Let `0 → A → Z → B → 0` and
`0 → B → Z' → C → 0` be short exact sequences in an abelian category `𝒜`, with classes
`[Z] ∈ Ext^1_𝒜(B, A)` and `[Z'] ∈ Ext^1_𝒜(C, B)`. Then the Yoneda product
`[Z] ∘ [Z'] ∈ Ext^2_𝒜(C, A)` is zero if and only if there is a commutative diagram with exact
rows and columns

```
                 0             0
                 ↓             ↓
  0 →   A   →    Z     →       B      →  0
      ‖ 1 ‖      ↓             ↓
  0 →   A   →    W     →       Z'     →  0
                 ↓             ↓
                 C   → ‖ 1 ‖ → C
                 ↓             ↓
                 0             0
```

in `𝒜`, i.e. if and only if `0 → A → Z → B → 0` is the restriction along `B → Z'` of an
extension `0 → A → W → Z' → 0` of `Z'` by `A`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.DerivedFunctor.eta_commutes_shift_but_not_triangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GSN.** The cone triangle of multiplication by `f` on `A` in degree
one is distinguished. Its eta cone is homotopic to zero. If `f` is not a unit,
the first eta arrow is not invertible and the image triangle is not distinguished.
The compatible shift comparison is the fixed multiplication-by-`f` map
`etaShiftIso_one_hom_app_f_val`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eta_commutes_shift_but_not_triangulated
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    let g := etaCounterexampleMap.{u, v} f hf
    let q := HomotopyCategory.quotient (FTorsionFreeModule.{u, v} f) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
    let T := CochainComplex.mappingCone.triangleh g
    T ∈ distTriang (HomotopyCategory (FTorsionFreeModule.{u, v} f) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      IsZero ((etaHomotopyFunctor f).obj (q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone g))) ∧
      (¬ IsUnit f →
        ¬ IsIso ((etaHomotopyFunctor f).map (q.map g)) ∧
        (etaHomotopyFunctor f).mapTriangle.obj T ∉
          distTriang (HomotopyCategory (FTorsionFreeModule.{u, v} f) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaComplex.FractionalPowerBockstein.powerBocksteinOperator_eq_connectingHom_comp_reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GSP.** For the actual fractional power ideals in `A[1/f]`, the Bockstein
operator for the successive-quotient row equals the connecting morphism of the unquotiented
row followed by cohomology of the canonical reduction `fⁱ⁺¹A → fⁱ⁺¹A/fⁱ⁺²A`, after
tensoring both rows with `M`. The definitions above formally identify every object and map
with the power-ideal diagram in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerBocksteinOperator_eq_connectingHom_comp_reduction
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (hM : ∀ n, IsSMulRegular (M.X n) f)
    (i n : ℤ) :
    ∃ (hUpper : (powerIdealShortComplex M f i).ShortExact)
      (hLower : (successivePowerQuotientShortComplex M f i).ShortExact),
      powerBocksteinOperator M f i n hLower =
        hUpper.δ n (n + 1) (by simp [ComplexShape.up]) ≫
          HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
            ((tensorWithCochainComplex M).map
              (cokernel.π (fractionalPowerInclusion f (i + 1)))) (n + 1)

declarations.name: EtaPow.Bockstein.bocksteinComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GSQ.** The complex `Hᵇ(M/f)` has term
`Hⁱ(M ⊗ fⁱA/fⁱ⁺¹A)` in degree `i` and the canonical Bockstein map as its differential.
declarations.statement:
def bocksteinComplex (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (hM : ∀ n, IsSMulRegular (M.X n) f) :
    CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.BaseChange.algebraMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.** If `f` is a nonzerodivisor in `A` and `A → B` is flat, then its image
`g = algebraMap A B f` is a nonzerodivisor in `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem algebraMap_mem_nonZeroDivisors (f : A) [Module.Flat A B] (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    (algebraMap A B f) ∈ nonZeroDivisors B
declarations.comment: g is a nonzerodivisor

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.BaseChange.isSMulRegular_baseChange_X
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.** For `A → B` flat and `M^•` a complex of `f`-torsion free `A`-modules, each
base-changed term `M^i ⊗_A B` is `g`-torsion free, where `g = algebraMap A B f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSMulRegular_baseChange_X (f : A) [Module.Flat A B] (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat A) ℤ)
    (hM : ∀ i, IsSMulRegular (M.X i) f) (i : ℤ) :
    IsSMulRegular (B ⊗[A] (M.X i : Type _)) (algebraMap A B f)
declarations.comment: the base change is g-torsion free

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.BaseChange.etaBaseChangeTerm_eq_fetaTerm
declarations.doc:
**Statement 3.** With the identification of Definition 4,
`η_f M^• ⊗_A B = η_g (M^• ⊗_A B)` as complexes of `g`-torsion free `B`-modules.

This is the equality, for every `i ∈ ℤ`, of two `B`-submodules of the common ambient module
`(M^i ⊗_A B)_g = LocalizedModule (powers g) (B ⊗_A M^i)`:

* the base change `(η_f M)^i ⊗_A B` (`etaBaseChangeTerm f M i`), and
* the degree-`i` term `(η_g (M^• ⊗_A B))^i` of the décalage of the base-changed complex,
  `fetaTerm g (d^i ⊗ id_B) i`.

The second conjunct records compatibility with the differentials: the localized base-changed
differential `d^i ⊗ id_B` carries the degree-`i` term into the degree-`(i+1)` term, exhibiting
the equality as an equality of *subcomplexes*.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaBaseChangeTerm_eq_fetaTerm (f : A) [Module.Flat A B] (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat A) ℤ)
    (i : ℤ) :
    (etaBaseChangeTerm f M i
        = fetaTerm (algebraMap A B f)
            (LinearMap.baseChange B (M.d i (i + 1)).hom) i) ∧
      Submodule.map (fLoc (algebraMap A B f) (LinearMap.baseChange B (M.d i (i + 1)).hom))
          (fetaTerm (algebraMap A B f) (LinearMap.baseChange B (M.d i (i + 1)).hom) i)
        ≤ fetaTerm (algebraMap A B f) (LinearMap.baseChange B (M.d (i + 1) (i + 1 + 1)).hom) (i +
            1)
declarations.comment: eta commutes with the base change

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.GoodBaseChange.isIso_etaBaseChangeMap_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**More on Algebra, Tag 0GSR as an isomorphism of complexes.**  Let `A → B` be a flat map of
commutative rings, let `f ∈ A` with image `g = algebraMap A B f`, and let `K` be a cochain
complex of `A`-modules.  Then the canonical comparison

`B ⊗_A (η_f K) ⟶ η_g (B ⊗_A K)`

is an isomorphism of complexes of `B`-modules: the décalage commutes with flat base change.

The tag itself, `Stacks.Eta.BaseChange.etaBaseChangeTerm_eq_fetaTerm`, states this as an
equality of `B`-submodules of one ambient localization in each degree; what is added here is
that the comparison realizing that equality is a degreewise bijection, which is
`Stacks.Eta.GoodBaseChange.bijective_psiTermMap_of_flat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_etaBaseChangeMap_of_flat (f : A) [Module.Flat A B]
    (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) :
    IsIso (etaBaseChangeMap (B := B) f K)
declarations.comment: the comparison `B ⊗_A (η_f K) ⟶ η_g (B ⊗_A K)` is an isomorphism of complexes, for a flat ring map and an arbitrary cochain complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Eta.DeterminantalIdeal.pow_mul_idealI_eq_of_derived_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GSS.** Let `f` be a nonzerodivisor and let `M` and `N` be bounded complexes of
finite free modules representing isomorphic objects of the derived category. If `m` and `n`
are nonnegative integers such that
`m + ∑_{j ≥ i} (-1)^(j-i) rank(Mʲ) = n + ∑_{j ≥ i} (-1)^(j-i) rank(Nʲ)`,
then `fᵐ I_i(M, f) = fⁿ I_i(N, f)` as ideals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pow_mul_idealI_eq_of_derived_iso
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A)
    (M N : BoundedComplex A) (i : ℤ) (m n : ℕ)
    (hMN : Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj M.toCochainComplex ≅
      (DerivedCategory.Q).obj N.toCochainComplex))
    (hEuler : (m : ℤ) + M.tailEulerCharacteristic i =
      (n : ℤ) + N.tailEulerCharacteristic i) :
    Ideal.span {f ^ m} * idealI M f i = Ideal.span {f ^ n} * idealI N f i

declarations.name: idealI_unit_mul_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GST (Lemma 15.98.2).** Let `A` be a commutative ring, `f ∈ A` a nonzerodivisor,
and `u ∈ A` a unit. For a bounded complex `M^•` of finite free `A`-modules and every `i ∈ ℤ`,
`I_i(M^•, f) = I_i(M^•, u·f)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealI_unit_mul_eq (C : BoundedComplex A) (f : A) (u : Aˣ) (i : ℤ) :
    idealI C f i = idealI C ((u : A) * f) i

declarations.name: map_idealI_eq_idealI_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GSU (Lemma 15.98.3).** Let `φ : A → B` be a ring map, `f` a
nonzerodivisor in `A`, `C = M^•` a bounded complex of finite free `A`-modules,
and assume `g = φ(f)` is a nonzerodivisor in `B`. Then for every `i ∈ ℤ`, the
extension of `I_i(M^•, f)` along `φ` equals `I_i(M^• ⊗_A B, g)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_idealI_eq_idealI_baseChange {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
    (f : A) (C : BoundedComplex A) (i : ℤ) :
    Ideal.map φ (idealI C f i) = idealI (C.baseChange φ) (φ f) i

declarations.name: Stacks.DeterminantalIdeal.FreeHomology.localized_idealI_eq_span_pow_of_free_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GSV.** If the localization at `p` of every cohomology module of a bounded
complex `M` of finite free modules is free, then for every degree the localization of
`I_i(M, f)` is generated by a power of the nonzerodivisor `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localized_idealI_eq_span_pow_of_free_homology
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) (M : BoundedComplex A)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime p)
      (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl
        ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i).obj
          M.toCochainComplex))) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ,
      Ideal.map (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p)) (idealI M f i) =
        Ideal.span {(algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime p) f) ^ n}

declarations.name: Stacks.Decalage.DirectSumIdeal.etaDirectSumIdeal_eq_of_derived_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GSW.** If `M` and `N` are bounded complexes of finite free modules representing
isomorphic objects in the derived category and every `I_i(M, f)` is principal, then their
direct-sum ideals `J_i(-, f)` in `A / fA` agree in every degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaDirectSumIdeal_eq_of_derived_iso
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (f : A) (hf : IsRegular f)
    (M N : BoundedComplex A)
    (hMN : Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj M.toCochainComplex ≅
      (DerivedCategory.Q).obj N.toCochainComplex))
    (_hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (idealI M f i).IsPrincipal) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, etaDirectSumIdeal M f i = etaDirectSumIdeal N f i

declarations.name: FiniteLengthEndomorphism.det_exact
declarations.doc: Determinant is multiplicative in an equivariant short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem det_exact (M₁ : Type v₁) (M₂ : Type v₂) (M₃ : Type v₃)
    [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
    [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃]
    (h₁ : IsFiniteLength R M₁) (h₂ : IsFiniteLength R M₂) (h₃ : IsFiniteLength R M₃)
    (φ₁ : Module.End R M₁) (φ₂ : Module.End R M₂) (φ₃ : Module.End R M₃)
    (f : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃) (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hexact : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (hfφ : f.comp φ₁ = φ₂.comp f) (hgφ : g.comp φ₂ = φ₃.comp g) :
    det R h₂ φ₂ = det R h₁ φ₁ * det R h₃ φ₃
declarations.comment: multiplicativity of the residue-field determinant

declarations.name: FiniteLengthEndomorphism.trace_exact
declarations.doc: Trace is additive in an equivariant short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem trace_exact (M₁ : Type v₁) (M₂ : Type v₂) (M₃ : Type v₃)
    [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
    [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃]
    (h₁ : IsFiniteLength R M₁) (h₂ : IsFiniteLength R M₂) (h₃ : IsFiniteLength R M₃)
    (φ₁ : Module.End R M₁) (φ₂ : Module.End R M₂) (φ₃ : Module.End R M₃)
    (f : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃) (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hexact : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (hfφ : f.comp φ₁ = φ₂.comp f) (hgφ : g.comp φ₂ = φ₃.comp g) :
    trace R h₂ φ₂ = trace R h₁ φ₁ + trace R h₃ φ₃
declarations.comment: additivity of the residue-field trace

declarations.name: FiniteLengthEndomorphism.charpoly_exact
declarations.doc: Characteristic polynomial is multiplicative in an equivariant short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem charpoly_exact (M₁ : Type v₁) (M₂ : Type v₂) (M₃ : Type v₃)
    [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module R M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂] [Module R M₂]
    [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module R M₃]
    (h₁ : IsFiniteLength R M₁) (h₂ : IsFiniteLength R M₂) (h₃ : IsFiniteLength R M₃)
    (φ₁ : Module.End R M₁) (φ₂ : Module.End R M₂) (φ₃ : Module.End R M₃)
    (f : M₁ →ₗ[R] M₂) (g : M₂ →ₗ[R] M₃) (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hexact : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (hfφ : f.comp φ₁ = φ₂.comp f) (hgφ : g.comp φ₂ = φ₃.comp g) :
    charpoly R h₂ φ₂ = charpoly R h₁ φ₁ * charpoly R h₃ φ₃
declarations.comment: multiplicativity of the residue-field characteristic polynomial

declarations.name: FiniteLengthEndomorphism.multiplication_det_eq_norm_pow_length
declarations.doc:
For a local homomorphism of local rings with finite residue-field extension, the determinant
over the source residue field of multiplication by `u` on a finite-length target module is the
appropriate power of the residue-field norm of `u`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem multiplication_det_eq_norm_pow_length
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (R' : Type v) [CommRing R'] [IsLocalRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')]
    [Module.Finite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R')]
    (M' : Type w) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module R' M'] [IsScalarTower R R' M']
    (hM' : IsFiniteLength R' M') (u : R') :
    let hM : IsFiniteLength R M' := Module.length_ne_top_iff.mp <| by
      rw [IsLocalRing.length_restrictScalars R R' M']
      exact WithTop.mul_ne_top (Module.length_ne_top_iff.mpr hM') (by
        rw [Module.length_eq_finrank]
        exact ENat.natCast_ne_top _)
    FiniteLengthEndomorphism.det R hM
        ((LinearMap.lsmul R' M' u).restrictScalars R) =
      Algebra.norm (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) (IsLocalRing.residue R' u) ^
        (Module.length R' M').toNat

declarations.name: FiniteLengthEndomorphism.map_det_pow_eq_det_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GT0.** Under a flat local homomorphism `R → S` whose closed fibre has finite
length `m`, the determinant of a finite-length module endomorphism after scalar extension is the
image in the residue field of `S` of the original determinant raised to the power `m`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem map_det_pow_eq_det_baseChange
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)] [Module.Flat R S]
    (m : ℕ)
    (hm : Module.length S
      (S ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) = m)
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (hM : IsFiniteLength R M) (phi : Module.End R M) :
    ∃ hMS : IsFiniteLength S (S ⊗[R] M),
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap R S)
          (FiniteLengthEndomorphism.det R hM phi ^ m) =
        FiniteLengthEndomorphism.det S hMS (LinearMap.baseChange S phi)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
declarations.doc:
**The finite free cohomology locus of a derived object.** These are the points at which every
cohomology stalk `H^i(E)_x` is a finite free `𝒪_{X, x}`-module.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) : Set X.carrier
declarations.comment: the locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.subset_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GT1, maximality.** Every open set over which all the cohomology sheaves of a derived
object are finite locally free is contained in the finite free cohomology locus: finite local
freeness near a point makes the cohomology stalks there finite free.
declarations.statement:
theorem subset_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (V : Opens X.carrier)
    (hV : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOver
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) i).obj E) V) :
    (V : Set X.carrier) ⊆ cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E
declarations.comment: maximality of the locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isOpen_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GT1, openness.** On a ringed space whose structure-sheaf stalks are local rings,
the finite free cohomology locus of a perfect object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules is
open: near a point of the locus the object is computed by a strictly perfect complex, whose
opcycles are then free on a neighbourhood, and over such a neighbourhood all the cohomology
stalks are again finite free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
    [hloc : ∀ x : X.carrier, IsLocalRing (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk x))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X))
    (hE : IsPerfect E) : IsOpen (cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E)
declarations.comment: openness of the locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
declarations.doc:
The set of points at which every cohomology sheaf of an object of `D(𝒪_X)` has a
finite free stalk.
declarations.comment: the locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isOpen_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
declarations.doc: The locus where all cohomology stalks of a perfect object are finite free is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus
    {X : RingedSpace.{u, v}}
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (structureSheafStalk X x)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, v} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, v} X)) (hE : IsPerfect E) :
    IsOpen (cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E)
declarations.comment: openness

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isFiniteLocallyFree_homology_restrict_locus
declarations.doc:
On the finite free locus of a perfect object every cohomology sheaf is finite locally
free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_homology_restrict_locus
    {X : RingedSpace.{u, v}}
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (structureSheafStalk X x)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, v} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, v} X)) (hE : IsPerfect E)
    (i : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteLocallyFree
      ((restrictModules X
        ⟨cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E,
          isOpen_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E hE⟩).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, v} X) i).obj E))
declarations.comment: finite locally free

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.le_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
An open set on which all cohomology sheaves of a perfect object are finite locally free is
contained in its finite free locus; together with the previous result this says the locus is
the largest such open set.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
    {X : RingedSpace.{u, v}}
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (structureSheafStalk X x)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, v} X)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, v} X)) (hE : IsPerfect E)
    (V : Opens X)
    (hV : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteLocallyFree
      ((restrictModules X V).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, v} X) i).obj E))) :
    V ≤ ⟨cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E,
      isOpen_cohomologyFiniteFreeLocus E hE⟩
declarations.comment: maximality

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.isInvertible_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular
declarations.doc:
**Condition (1) of Stacks 0GT3 implies condition (2).** An ideal sheaf locally generated by
a nonzerodivisor is invertible as an `O_X`-module. There is no hypothesis on the stalks of the
structure sheaf: this half of the tag holds on every ringed space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertible_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular
    {I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ} (i : I ⟶ 𝒪) (h : IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X i) :
    Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X).property I
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.isLocallyGeneratedByRegular_of_isInvertible
declarations.doc:
**Condition (2) of Stacks 0GT3 implies condition (1) when the stalks are local rings.** An
invertible ideal sheaf on a ringed space all of whose stalks `O_{X,x}` are local rings is
locally generated by a nonzerodivisor. The hypothesis on the stalks is the one the tag requires
and cannot be dropped: without it an invertible module need not be locally free of rank one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocallyGeneratedByRegular_of_isInvertible
    [∀ x : X.carrier, IsLocalRing (ringStalk X x)]
    {I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ} (i : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono i]
    (h : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X).property I) :
    IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X i
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1) when the stalks are local rings

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.Situation
declarations.doc:
**Situation 0GT4.** A sheaf of ideals `ι : I ⟶ O_X` on a ringed space which is locally
generated by a nonzerodivisor: every point has an open neighbourhood `U` carrying a section `f`
of `I` which generates `I|_U` and acts injectively on `O_U`.
declarations.statement: public structure Situation

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.idealTorsionFree_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT5.** For an ideal sheaf locally generated by a
nonzerodivisor, the following are equivalent: `F[I] = 0`; `F[I^n] = 0` for every
`n ≥ 1`; multiplication `I ⊗ F ⟶ F` is injective; multiplication by every local
generator is injective; and every stalk generator is a nonzerodivisor on the stalk of
`F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idealTorsionFree_tfae
    {I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ} (i : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono i]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (C := Opens X)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology X) I 1]
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) :
    List.TFAE [
      IsIdealTorsionFree X i F,
      IsIdealPowerTorsionFree X i F,
      Mono (idealTensorMultiplication X i F),
      ∀ (U : Opens X) (f : I.val.obj (op U)),
        GeneratesIdealOn X U f → IsGeneratorRegularOn X i F U f,
      IsStalkwiseGeneratorRegular X i F]

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.etaStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT6.** At a generator `f` of the ideal stalk `I_x`, the stalk of the
sheaf-theoretic décalage `η_I F` is isomorphic, as a complex of modules over the local ring
`O_{X,x}`, to the ordinary décalage `η_f` of the complex of stalks.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def etaStalkIso
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory.mk X.presheaf X.IsSheaf))).property I]
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X n))
    (x : X) (f : ringStalk X x)
    (hf : GeneratesStalkIdeal X ι x f) :
    stalkComplex X x (etaObj X I ι F hF) ≅
      EtaComplex.etaObject f (stalkComplex X x F)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.etaStalkIso_hom
declarations.doc:
In degree `n`, the comparison of Tag 0GT6 is the normalized ideal-power map applied to the
first projection of the defining fibre product, read inside the localization.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaStalkIso_hom
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory.mk X.presheaf X.IsSheaf))).property I]
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ n : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X n))
    (x : X) (f : ringStalk X x)
    (hf : GeneratesStalkIdeal X ι x f) (n : ℤ) :
    (etaStalkIso X I ι F hF x f hf).hom.f n ≫
      ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.subtype (EtaComplex.term f (stalkComplex X x F) n)) =
    (stalkModuleFunctor X x).map
      (pullback.fst (idealPowerMap X I n (F.d n (n + 1)))
        (idealPowerIncl X I ι n (F.X (n + 1)))) ≫
      (idealPowerStalkComparison X I ι (F.X n) x f hf).map n
declarations.comment: generator-normalized degreewise map

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Bockstein.bockstein_comp_bockstein
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT8.** Consecutive Bockstein operators compose to zero,
`β^{i+1} ∘ β^i = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bockstein_comp_bockstein
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.sheaf)).property I]
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)) (i : ℤ) :
    bocksteinOperator X I ι M i ≫ bocksteinOperator X I ι M (i + 1) = 0
declarations.comment: square-zero Bockstein maps

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Bockstein.bocksteinComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT8.** The Bockstein complex `H^•(M/I)` of an object `M` of
`D(O_X)`: the integer-indexed complex whose `i`-th term is `H^i(M ⊗^L I^i/I^{i+1})` and whose
differentials are the Bockstein operators.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bocksteinComplex
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.sheaf)).property I]
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)) : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ
declarations.comment: the Bockstein complex

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Reduction.reductionComparisonQ
declarations.doc:
The canonical arrow `η_I F ⊗ O_X/I ⟶ H^•(F/I)` in `D(O_X)`, for a termwise `I`-torsion-free
complex `F`: the image under `DerivedCategory.Q` of the canonical morphism of complexes
`Reduction.reductionComparisonChainMap` from the reduction of the décalage to the chain-level
Bockstein complex.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def reductionComparisonQ
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (Oₓ).property I]
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ k : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X k)) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (etaModIdealComplex X I ι F hF) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (bocksteinChainComplex X I ι F hF)
declarations.comment: the canonical arrow in D(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Reduction.isIso_reductionComparisonQ_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT9.**  In Situation 0GT4, on a complex `F` of `I`-torsion-free
`O_X`-modules, the canonical arrow

`η_I F ⊗ O_X/I ⟶ H^•(F/I)`

of `D(O_X)` is invertible.  The inputs are those of the situation: the ideal is locally generated
by a nonzerodivisor and `F` is termwise `I`-torsion-free, which is what Lemma 20.55.6 provides for
an arbitrary object of `D(O_X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_reductionComparisonQ_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (Oₓ).property I]
    (hregl : Stacks.IdealTorsion.IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X ι)
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ k : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X k)) :
    IsIso (reductionComparisonQ X I ι F hF)
declarations.comment: in Situation 0GT4: the canonical arrow of D(O_X) is invertible

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Reduction.reductionComparisonQIsoOfRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT9.**  The canonical isomorphism

`η_I F ⊗ O_X/I ≅ H^•(F/I)` in `D(O_X)`,

in Situation 0GT4, as an explicit isomorphism.  This is the tag's own
conclusion: "there is a canonical isomorphism".

The forward map is `DerivedCategory.Q.map` of the named chain map `reductionComparisonChainMap`,
and `reductionComparisonQIsoOfRegular_hom` says so by `rfl`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def reductionComparisonQIsoOfRegular
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (Oₓ).property I]
    (hregl : Stacks.IdealTorsion.IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X ι)
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
    (hF : ∀ k : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X k)) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (etaModIdealComplex X I ι F hF) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (bocksteinChainComplex X I ι F hF)
declarations.comment: in Situation 0GT4: the canonical isomorphism in D(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Reduction.exists_isIso_reductionComparisonQ_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GT9, at the tag's own quantifier.**  In Situation 0GT4, for an
arbitrary object `M` of `D(O_X)` there is a complex `F` of `I`-torsion-free `O_X`-modules with
`Q F ≅ M` on which the canonical arrow

`η_I F ⊗ O_X/I ⟶ H^•(F/I)`

is invertible.  This is the tag read with its own "let `M` be an object of `D(O_X)`": the
representative is produced by the proof.  Its existence is
`Eta.torsionFreeResolutions_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular` composed with the essential
surjectivity of `DerivedCategory.Q`, and the invertibility is
`isIso_reductionComparisonQ_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isIso_reductionComparisonQ_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [Mono ι]
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj (Oₓ).property I]
    (hregl : Stacks.IdealTorsion.IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X ι)
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ)) :
    ∃ (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) ℤ)
      (hF : ∀ k : ℤ, IsIdealTorsionFree X ι (F.X k)),
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ M) ∧ IsIso (reductionComparisonQ X I ι F hF)
declarations.comment: in Situation 0GT4, for an arbitrary object of D(O_X): a termwise I-torsion-free representative exists and the canonical arrow is invertible on it

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.isFiniteFreeStalkOfRank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTA, in Situation 0GT4.**  Let
`ι : I ⟶ O_X` be an ideal sheaf locally generated by a section that is a nonzerodivisor on
`O_X`, let `M` be an object of `D(O_X)` and let `x` be a point of `X`.  If the stalk `H^n(M)_x`
is finite free of rank `r` over `O_{X,x}`, then so is `H^n(Lη_I M)_x`.

The proof applies `isFiniteFreeStalkOfRank_homology_leta`: the derived décalage is
`derivedEtaOfRegular`, the functor of Tag 0F8Q built from the situation, the torsion-free
resolutions are `torsionFreeResolutions_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular`, and the freeness of
rank one of `I_x` is `isFiniteFreeStalkOfRank_one_of_isLocallyGeneratedByRegular`.  The
invertibility of `I` comes from the implication (1) ⟹ (2) of Tag 0GT3.  The statement holds at
every point `x`, and the degree `n` may be negative.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFiniteFreeStalkOfRank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [monoIncl : Mono ι]
    (hregl : IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X ι)
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ))
    (x : X) (n : ℤ) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : IsFiniteFreeStalkOfRank X
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) n).obj M) x r) :
    IsFiniteFreeStalkOfRank X
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) n).obj
        ((@derivedEtaOfRegular X I ι monoIncl hregl).obj M)) x r
declarations.comment: in Situation 0GT4: if H^n(M)_x is finite free of rank r over O_{X,x}, then so is H^n(Lη_I M)_x, where Lη_I is derivedEtaOfRegular, the functor of Tag 0F8Q for that situation; the uniqueness of the rank over a nonzero stalk is rank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.IdealTorsion.Eta.rank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTA, the clause "of the same rank", in Situation 0GT4 itself.**  Let
`ι : I ⟶ O_X` be an ideal sheaf locally generated by a section that is a nonzerodivisor on
`O_X`, let `M` be an object of `D(O_X)` and let `x` be a point of `X` at which the stalk
`O_{X,x}` is nonzero.  If `H^n(M)_x` is finite free of rank `r` and `H^n(Lη_I M)_x` is finite
free of rank `s`, then `s = r`.

Together with `isFiniteFreeStalkOfRank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular` this is the complete source
statement: that statement supplies the finite
freeness of `H^n(Lη_I M)_x` at the rank of `H^n(M)_x`, and this one that no other rank is
possible, which is what makes "the same rank" a determinate assertion.  The nonvanishing of
`O_{X,x}` enters only here, through `IsFiniteFreeStalkOfRank.rank_eq`: over the zero ring every
module is free of every rank.
declarations.statement:
public theorem rank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular_eq
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) (ι : I ⟶ 𝒪) [monoIncl : Mono ι]
    (hregl : IsLocallyGeneratedByRegular X ι)
    (M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ))
    (x : X) [Nontrivial (ringStalk X x)] (n : ℤ) (r s : ℕ)
    (hr : IsFiniteFreeStalkOfRank X
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) n).obj M) x r)
    (hs : IsFiniteFreeStalkOfRank X
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} Oₓ) n).obj
        ((@derivedEtaOfRegular X I ι monoIncl hregl).obj M)) x s) :
    s = r
declarations.comment: the clause `of the same rank`, in Situation 0GT4: the ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor and the derived décalage is derivedEtaOfRegular, the functor of Tag 0F8Q for that situation; the condition O_{X,x} ≠ 0 is Nontrivial on the stalk of the structure sheaf, and the finite freeness itself is isFiniteFreeStalkOfRank_homology_derivedEtaOfRegular

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isImmersion_baseChange_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
If a locally finite type morphism becomes an immersion over the inverse limit,
it becomes an immersion at a later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isImmersion_baseChange_of_isLimit
    {I : Type v} [Category.{w} I] [IsCofiltered I] [EssentiallySmall.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left]
    [IsImmersion ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (hi : i ⟶ i₀),
      IsImmersion ((Over.pullback (D.map hi)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.hasResolutionProperty_of_surjective_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTC.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjective finite locally free morphism of
schemes and `X` has the resolution property, then so does `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_surjective_isFiniteLocallyFree {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [Surjective f] [Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree f] [HasResolutionProperty X] :
    HasResolutionProperty Y

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_mem_ideal_transcendental_residue
declarations.doc:
An ideal avoiding finitely many incomparable prime ideals contains an element whose image is
transcendental over each of the prescribed subfields of the residue fields.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_ideal_transcendental_residue
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (ι : Type*) [Finite ι]
    (p : ι → PrimeSpectrum R)
    (k : ∀ i, Subfield (p i).asIdeal.ResidueField)
    (hinc : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ¬ (p i).asIdeal ≤ (p j).asIdeal)
    (htrans : ∀ i, ¬ Algebra.IsAlgebraic (k i) (p i).asIdeal.ResidueField)
    (J : Ideal R) (hJ : ∀ i, ¬ J ≤ (p i).asIdeal) :
    ∃ x ∈ J, ∀ i, Transcendental (k i)
      (algebraMap R (p i).asIdeal.ResidueField x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_specMapAeval_pow_add_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTF.** If the morphism to the affine line determined by `a` has
fibres of dimension at most `d`, then so does the morphism determined by `a ^ n + b`, for every
sufficiently large exponent `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eventually_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_specMapAeval_pow_add_le
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (d : ℕ) (a b : S)
    (ha : ∀ q : Spec (.of (Polynomial R)),
      topologicalKrullDim ((specMapAeval a).fiber q) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
      ∀ q : Spec (.of (Polynomial R)),
        topologicalKrullDim ((specMapAeval (a ^ n + b)).fiber q) ≤
          (d : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial_of_relativeDimension_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTG.** Let `R → S` be a finite type ring map and let `d` bound the
maximum `Algebra.relativeDimension R S` of the dimensions of the fibres of `Spec S → Spec R`.
Then there is a quasi-finite `R`-algebra map `R[t_1, …, t_d] → S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial_of_relativeDimension_le
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : Algebra.relativeDimension R S ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ φ : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →ₐ[R] S,
      φ.toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ φ.toRingHom.QuasiFinite
declarations.comment:
The maximum of the dimensions of the fibres is `Algebra.relativeDimension R S`
(Tag 00QD) and is bounded by, rather than equal to, the natural number `d`; the two are
equivalent, and the inequality is what covers `Spec S = ∅`, where the maximum is `⊥`.
Quasi-finiteness is Mathlib's `RingHom.QuasiFinite`, which asks only for finite fibres, so the
finite type of the map is a separate conjunct.

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial_of_relativeDimension_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTG**, in the source's form: `d` *is* the maximum of the dimensions of
the fibres of `Spec S → Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_quasiFinite_mvPolynomial_of_relativeDimension_eq
    {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : Algebra.relativeDimension R S = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ∃ φ : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →ₐ[R] S,
      φ.toRingHom.FiniteType ∧ φ.toRingHom.QuasiFinite
declarations.comment:
The source's form, with `d` equal to the maximum
`Algebra.relativeDimension R S` (Tag 00QD) of the dimensions of the fibres. Quasi-finiteness is
Mathlib's `RingHom.QuasiFinite`, which asks only for finite fibres, so the finite type of the map
is a separate conjunct.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCompletelyDecomposed
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is **completely decomposed** if every point of the target is the
image of a point at which the induced map on residue fields is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: def IsCompletelyDecomposed {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily
declarations.doc:
A family of morphisms of schemes with a common target is **completely decomposed** if the
induced morphism from the coproduct of the source schemes is completely decomposed.
declarations.statement:
def IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    {X : I → Scheme.{u}} {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: family

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompletelyDecomposed_comp
declarations.doc:
The composite of two completely decomposed morphisms of
schemes is completely decomposed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCompletelyDecomposed_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsCompletelyDecomposed f) (hg : IsCompletelyDecomposed g) :
    IsCompletelyDecomposed (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompletelyDecomposedFamily_comp
declarations.doc:
Composing a completely decomposed family with a completely
decomposed family over each of its sources gives a completely decomposed family indexed by the
dependent sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCompletelyDecomposedFamily_comp {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I]
    {J : I → Type w} [∀ i, Small.{u} (J i)] {X : I → Scheme.{u}}
    {X' : ∀ i, J i → Scheme.{u}} {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y)
    (g : ∀ i j, X' i j ⟶ X i) (hf : IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily f)
    (hg : ∀ i, IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily (g i)) :
    IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily
      (fun ij : Σ i, J i => g ij.1 ij.2 ≫ f ij.1)
declarations.comment: families

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompletelyDecomposed_pullback
declarations.doc:
A completely decomposed morphism remains completely
decomposed after arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCompletelyDecomposed_pullback
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsCompletelyDecomposed f) :
    IsCompletelyDecomposed (pullback.snd f g)
declarations.comment: morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompletelyDecomposedFamily_pullback
declarations.doc:
A completely decomposed family of morphisms remains completely decomposed after arbitrary
base change.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCompletelyDecomposedFamily_pullback
    {I : Type v} [Small.{u} I] {X : I → Scheme.{u}} {Y Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily f) :
    IsCompletelyDecomposedFamily (fun i ↦ pullback.snd (f i) g)
declarations.comment: family

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_immersion_cover_with_sections
declarations.doc:
A completely decomposed morphism locally of finite presentation over a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated base has a finite surjective cover by immersions
of finite presentation on each of which the morphism admits a section.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_immersion_cover_with_sections
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsCompletelyDecomposed f)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (Z : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (g : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ Y),
      Surjective (Sigma.desc g) ∧
        (∀ i, IsImmersion (g i)) ∧
        (∀ i, FinitePresentation (g i)) ∧
        (∀ i, ∃ s : Z i ⟶ pullback f (g i),
          s ≫ pullback.snd f (g i) = 𝟙 (Z i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isCompletelyDecomposed_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTM.** Let a scheme be the limit of a cofiltered inverse system of
schemes with affine transition morphisms, and let a locally finitely presented morphism over one
stage have quasi-compact, quasi-separated target. If its base change to the limit is completely
decomposed, then its base change to some later stage is completely decomposed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompletelyDecomposed_baseChange_of_limitBaseChange
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (S : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (S.map g)]
    (c : Cone S) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (S.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    (hf : IsCompletelyDecomposed ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left) :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      IsCompletelyDecomposed ((Over.pullback (S.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleFamilyRelativeAmple.exists_isAmpleFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0GTP.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes. If `Y` has an ample family of
invertible modules and there is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module ample relative to `f`, then `X` has an
ample family of invertible modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmpleFamily {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) {I : Type v} (N : I → Y.Modules)
    (hN : Y.IsAmpleFamily N)
    (hL : ∃ (L : X.Modules) (_ : IsInvertibleModule X L),
      Stacks.RelativeAmple.IsRelativelyAmple f L) :
    ∃ (J : Type v) (M : J → X.Modules), X.IsAmpleFamily M

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleFamilyRelativeAmple.exists_isAmpleFamily_of_isAffineHom_or_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GTQ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine or quasi-affine morphism of schemes. If `Y` has
an ample family of invertible modules, then so does `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmpleFamily_of_isAffineHom_or_isQuasiAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsAffineHom f ∨ IsQuasiAffineHom f) {I : Type v} (N : I → Y.Modules)
    (hN : Y.IsAmpleFamily N) :
    ∃ (J : Type v) (M : J → X.Modules), X.IsAmpleFamily M

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleFamilyCartier.exists_isAmpleFamily_of_isAmpleOnComplement_cover
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GTS].** Let `X` be a scheme, let `D 0, …, D (m-1)` be effective Cartier
divisors on `X` and `L 0, …, L (m-1)` invertible `𝒪_X`-modules such that the divisors have empty
common intersection (every point lies in the complement of some `D i`) and `L i` restricted to
`X ∖ D i` is ample. Then `X` has an ample family of invertible modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmpleFamily_of_isAmpleOnComplement_cover {m : ℕ}
    (D : Fin m → X.IdealSheafData) (L : Fin m → X.Modules)
    (hD : ∀ i, Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (D i))
    (hL : ∀ i, Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 (L i))
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ (D i).support.compl)
    (hample : ∀ i, IsAmpleOnComplement (D i) (L i)) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (N : J → X.Modules), X.IsAmpleFamily N

declarations.name: Stacks.DenseOpenAdmissibleBlowup.exists_isCompact_dense_admissibleBlowup_isAmpleFamily
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GTT].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme with finitely
many irreducible components. There exist a quasi-compact dense open `U ⊆ X` and a `U`-admissible
blowup `X' ⟶ X` such that `X'` has an ample family of invertible modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isCompact_dense_admissibleBlowup_isAmpleFamily
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [Finite (irreducibleComponents X)] :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) ∧ Dense (U : Set X) ∧
      ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f : X' ⟶ X), Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup U f ∧
        ∃ (J : Type u) (N : J → X'.Modules), X'.IsAmpleFamily N

declarations.name: Stacks.BlowupAmpleFamily.exists_finitePresentation_proper_completelyDecomposed_isAmpleFamily
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GTU].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. There is a
morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` which is of finite presentation, proper and completely
decomposed ([Stacks, Tag 0GTI]) and such that `Y` has an ample family of invertible modules.

The reduction to a base of finite type over `ℤ` is
`exists_finitePresentation_proper_completelyDecomposed_isAmpleFamily_of_finiteTypeCase`, and the
case of such a base, which is Noetherian, is
`exists_finitePresentation_proper_completelyDecomposed_isAmpleFamily_of_isNoetherian`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_proper_completelyDecomposed_isAmpleFamily
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X), FinitePresentation f ∧ IsProper f ∧
      IsCompletelyDecomposed f ∧ ∃ (J : Type u) (N : J → Y.Modules), Y.IsAmpleFamily N

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEta_isQuasicoherent_and_affineComparison
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GTV].** Let `X` be a scheme and let `D ⊆ X` be an effective Cartier divisor
with ideal sheaf `I ⊆ 𝒪_X`. The functor `Lη_I : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 0F8Q] sends
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into itself: if every cohomology sheaf `H^n(K)` of `K` is quasi-coherent, so is
every cohomology sheaf of `Lη_I K`.
Moreover, if `X = Spec(A)` is affine and `D = V(f)` — the ideal of `D` in `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)` is
generated by `f` — then the functor `Lη_f` on `D(A)` of [Stacks, Tag 0F7R] and the functor `Lη_I`
correspond via the equivalence `(-)^~ : D(A) ≌ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` of [Stacks, Tag 06Z0]:
`(-)^~ ⋙ Lη_I ≅ Lη_f ⋙ (-)^~`.

The functor `Lη_f` is defined because `f` is a nonzerodivisor, which follows from the
hypotheses (`Stacks.Divisors.Eta.mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ideal_top_eq_span`).
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedEta_isQuasicoherent_and_affineComparison :
    (∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (D : X.IdealSheafData) [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D]
        (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules),
        (∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj K).IsQuasicoherent) →
          ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj
            ((derivedEtaData D).functor.obj K)).IsQuasicoherent) ∧
      ∀ (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (D : (Spec R).IdealSheafData)
        [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D] (f : GammaTop R)
        (hf : D.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top (Spec R)⟩ = Ideal.span {f}),
        Nonempty (derivedTildeGamma R ⋙ (derivedEtaData D).functor ≅
          Stacks.Eta.DerivedDescent.moduleDerivedEta f
              (mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ideal_top_eq_span R D hf) ⋙
            derivedTildeGamma R)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.chartDecalage_of_derivedEta
declarations.doc:
**The derived décalage of a triple on its affine charts with principal determinantal
ideals**, for every triple `(X, D, M)` and every derived décalage `Lη_I` of its divisor: on such
a chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` the restriction of `Lη_I M` to `U` is the complex of `𝒪_U`-modules
associated with `η_f M^•`, as a roof of quasi-isomorphisms.  The comparison is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.nonempty_restrictModules_derivedEta_iso`,
which holds on every affine chart.  For the derived décalage
`Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData` of a triple at the standard model this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.chartDecalage`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartDecalage_of_derivedEta (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d})
    (E : Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta S.D) : ChartDecalage S E
declarations.comment: the second assertion, on an affine chart with principal determinantal ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isPerfect_derivedEtaData_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GTW].** Let `X, D, I, M` be as in Situation 0F8S. If `(X, D, M)` is a good
triple, then `Lη_I M` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Here `Lη_I` is the derived décalage of
tag 0F8Q and `M` is read in the model of `D(𝒪_X)` in which it is constructed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedEtaData_obj (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d})
    (hS : IsGoodTriple S) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.X.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedEtaData S.D).functor.obj S.standardM)
declarations.comment: Lη_I M is perfect for a good triple (X, D, M); Lη_I is Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData, and M is carried to its model of D(𝒪_X) by the canonical equivalence of localizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodTriple.isPerfect_derivedEta_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTW.**  Let `X`, `D`, `I`, `M` be as in Situation 0F8S.  If `(X, D, M)` is a
good triple, then `Lη_I M` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isPerfect_derivedEta_obj`, whose
comparison on affine charts is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.chartDecalage_of_derivedEta` and whose charts off the
divisor are
`ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_chart_isPrincipal_determinantalIdeal_of_notMem_supportSet`.
The derived décalage is any `Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta` of the divisor at the model of
`D(𝒪_X)` the triple carries; for a triple at the standard model it may be taken to be
`Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsGoodTriple.isPerfect_derivedEta_obj (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d})
    (E : Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta S.D) (hS : IsGoodTriple S) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.X.toRingedSpace) (E.functor.obj S.M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isPerfect_derivedEta_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GTW].** Let `X`, `D`, `I`, `M` be as in Situation 0F8S. If `(X, D, M)` is a
good triple, then `Lη_I M` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

The functor `Lη_I` is the hypothesis `E` (tag 0F8Q) and the affine-chart comparison is the
hypothesis `hcomp` (the second assertion of tag 0GTV); `hoff` supplies at the points off `D`
the charts with principal determinantal ideals that good-triple-ness supplies at the points of
`D`. See the module documentation for why each is carried.

Perfectness of a complex is local, so it is enough that, around every point of `X`, a
representative of `Lη_I M` restricts to a perfect complex. A chart with principal determinantal
ideals is such an open: by `hcomp` another representative restricts to a complex joined by a
roof of quasi-isomorphisms to the complex coming from the algebraic décalage of the chart, which
is strictly perfect by the translation of tag 0F7W, and the two representatives are joined by a
roof which restricts to the chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedEta_obj (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d})
    (E : Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta S.D)
    (hS : IsGoodTriple S)
    (hoff : ∀ x ∉ S.D.supportSet, ∃ C : AffineChart S,
      x ∈ (C.U : Set S.X) ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal)
    (hcomp : ChartDecalage S E) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.X.toRingedSpace) (E.functor.obj S.M)
declarations.comment: granted Stacks 0F8Q as the hypothesis E, bundled as Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta, and the second assertion of Stacks 0GTV as the hypothesis hcomp; neither is proved in this library. The hypothesis hoff supplies the affine charts with principal determinantal ideals at the points off D, which the source leaves implicit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isPerfect_derivedEta_obj_of_isGoodTriple
declarations.doc:
If `(X, D, M)` is a good triple, then `Lη_I M` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, for every
functor `Lη_I` with the properties of tag 0F8Q and every affine-chart comparison of the shape of
the second assertion of tag 0GTV.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedEta_obj_of_isGoodTriple (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d})
    (E : Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta S.D)
    (hS : IsGoodTriple S)
    (hcomp : ChartDecalage S E) :
    RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := S.X.toRingedSpace) (E.functor.obj S.M)
declarations.comment: perfectness of Lη_I M for a good triple, proved for every functor Lη_I with the properties Stacks 0F8Q gives it --- the structure Stacks.Divisors.Eta.DerivedEta, realized for the ideal sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor by Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData --- and for every affine-chart comparison of the shape of Stacks 0GTV's second assertion read at an affine open of X

declarations.name: Stacks.BlowUpComplexes.exists_isLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree_derivedEta
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GTX.**  Let `X` be a scheme, `D ⊆ X` an effective Cartier divisor
with ideal sheaf `ℐ`, and `M` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, and assume `(X, D, M)` is a good
triple.  If `M` is represented by a locally bounded complex of finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules, then so is `Lη_ℐ M`.

The representing complex for `Lη_ℐ M` is the chain-level décalage `η_ℐ ℳ^•` of the given one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree_derivedEta (X : Scheme.{u})
    (D : X.IdealSheafData) (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D)
    (M : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hM : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) M)
    (hgood : IsGoodTriple
      { X := X, D := D, isEffectiveCartierDivisor := hD, M := M, isPerfect := hM })
    (hrep : ∃ ℳ : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ,
      Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree ℳ ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ℳ ≅ M)) :
    ∃ 𝒬 : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ,
      Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree 𝒬 ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj 𝒬 ≅
          (@Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData X D hD).functor.obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.isAdmissibleBlowup_blowUpToBase_blowupCentreIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, the admissibility assertion over an affine chart.**  Over an affine chart
`(U, A, f, M^•)` the morphism `b` of the tag is the blowing up of `U` in the product
`∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of the determinantal ideals of the chart, and that blowing up is a
`(U \ D)`-admissible blowing up: the centre is of finite presentation and its support, being
contained in that of `D ∩ U`, is disjoint from `U \ D`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdmissibleBlowup_blowUpToBase_blowupCentreIdealSheaf (C : AffineChart S) :
    Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup
      ((C.U : S.X.Opens).ι ⁻¹ᵁ S.D.support.compl)
      (AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf)
declarations.comment: the admissibility assertion over an affine chart: the blowing up of the chart in the product of its determinantal ideals, which is what `b` restricts to there, is a `(U \ D)`-admissible blowing up

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.isGoodOver_chartBlowupToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, clause (1) over an affine chart.**  Let `(U, A, f, M^•)` be an affine
chart for the triple `(X, D, M)` and let `b_U : U' ⟶ U` be the blowing up of `U` in the product
`∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of its determinantal ideals.  Then the composite `U' ⟶ U ⟶ X` is good for the
triple: the pullback of `D` along it is defined, and the pulled-back triple
`(U', b_U⁻¹(D ∩ U), Lb_U^*M)` is a good triple.

Every point of `U'` lies in an affine open `V` on which all the finitely many inverse images
`I_i(M^•, f)𝒪_{U'}` are principal, these being effective Cartier divisors by
`AffineChart.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_determinantalIdealSheaf`; the degrees in which `M^•`
vanishes contribute the unit ideal.  By part (1) of Stacks tag 0F8T such a `V` carries the
pulled-back chart `(V, Γ(U', V), f|_V, M^• ⊗_A Γ(U', V))`, and by part (2) of that tag its
determinantal ideals are exactly those inverse images.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGoodOver_chartBlowupToBase (C : AffineChart S) :
    S.IsGoodOver C.chartBlowupToBase
declarations.comment: clause (1) over an affine chart: the triple pulled back along the blowing up of the chart in the product of its determinantal ideals --- which is what `b` restricts to over the chart --- is a good triple, and the pullback of `D` along it is defined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.existsUnique_lift_chartBlowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, clause (2) over an affine chart.**  Let `(U, A, f, M^•)` be an affine chart
for the triple `(X, D, M)` and let `b_U : U' ⟶ U` be the blowing up of `U` in the product
`∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of its determinantal ideals.  Every morphism `h : Y ⟶ U` whose composite with
the inclusion of `U` is good for the triple factors through `b_U` in exactly one way.

The inverse image of the centre along `h` is an effective Cartier divisor by
`AffineChart.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_comap_blowupCentreIdealSheaf`, so the universal property of
blowing up, Stacks tag 0806, applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_lift_chartBlowup (C : AffineChart S) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (b : Y ⟶ (C.U : S.X.Opens).toScheme)
    (hgood : S.IsGoodOver (b ≫ (C.U : S.X.Opens).ι)) :
    ∃! k : Y ⟶ blowUp C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf,
      k ≫ blowUpToBase C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf = b
declarations.comment: clause (2) over an affine chart: a morphism to the chart whose composite with the inclusion of the chart is good for the triple factors uniquely through the blowing up of the chart in the product of its determinantal ideals, which is what `b` restricts to there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isAdmissibleBlowup_morphismRestrict_goodBlowupToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, the quasi-compact-open admissibility assertion.**  In Situation 0F8S let
`b : X' ⟶ X` be the morphism of tag 0GTY and let `W ⊂ X` be a quasi-compact open.  Then
`b|_{b⁻¹(W)} : b⁻¹(W) ⟶ W` is a `W \ D`-admissible blowing up.

The centre is `AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.gluedNormalizedCentre`, glued from
the normalized centres of the charts of a finite cover of `W` by chart domains; it is of finite
presentation and supported on the divisor, and over each chart of the cover the restriction of
`b` is the blowing up in it, so the identification descends to `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdmissibleBlowup_morphismRestrict_goodBlowupToBase
    (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d}) (W : S.X.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set S.X)) :
