    Stacks.Blowup.IsAdmissibleBlowup (W.ι ⁻¹ᵁ S.D.support.compl)
      (S.goodBlowupToBase ∣_ W)
declarations.comment: the quasi-compact-open admissibility assertion: for a quasi-compact open `W ⊂ X` the restriction `b|_{b^{-1}(W)} : b^{-1}(W) ⟶ W` of the morphism of the tag is a `W \ D`-admissible blowing up. The centre is glued from the normalized determinantal products of the charts of a finite cover of `W`, with the product taken over a finite degree window containing the supports of those finitely many charts' complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.existsUnique_isGoodBlowup
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY: the existence and uniqueness assertion.**  In Situation 0F8S there is a
morphism `b : X' ⟶ X` such that

1. the pullback `D' = b⁻¹D` is defined and `(X', D', Lb^*M)` is a good triple, and
2. every morphism `h : Y ⟶ X` for which `h⁻¹D` is defined and `(Y, h⁻¹D, Lh^*M)` is a good triple
   factors uniquely through `b`,

and any morphism with those two properties is identified with it by a unique isomorphism over
`X`.

The morphism is `AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.goodBlowupToBase`, obtained by
blowing up each affine chart in the product of its determinantal ideals and gluing over the basis
of chart domains; the uniqueness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodBlowup.existsUnique_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_isGoodBlowup :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (b : X' ⟶ S.X), S.IsGoodBlowup b ∧
      ∀ (X'' : Scheme.{u}) (b' : X'' ⟶ S.X), S.IsGoodBlowup b' →
        ∃! e : X'' ≅ X', e.hom ≫ b = b'
declarations.comment: the existence and uniqueness assertion: there is a morphism `b : X' ⟶ X` whose pullback of `D` is defined and makes the pulled-back triple good, through which every morphism to `X` with defined pullback of `D` and good pulled-back triple factors uniquely, and any two such morphisms are identified by a unique isomorphism over `X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.existsUnique_iso_preimage_blowUp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY: the affine-chart description of `b`.**  Over an affine chart
`(U, A, f, M^•)` for the triple, the restriction `b⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` of the morphism of the tag is the
blowing up of `U` in the product `∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of the determinantal ideals of the chart: there
is exactly one isomorphism `b⁻¹(U) ≅ U'` over `U` between the two.

Both morphisms have the two conditions of the tag over `U` — the restriction of `b` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodBlowupOver.restrict`, the blowing up of the
chart by `AffineChart.isGoodBlowupOver_chartBlowupToBase` — so they are identified by a unique
isomorphism over `X`, and over `U` that is the same thing.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_preimage_blowUp (C : AffineChart S) :
    ∃! e : (S.goodBlowupToBase ⁻¹ᵁ (C.U : S.X.Opens)).toScheme ≅
        AlgebraicGeometry.blowUp C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf,
      e.hom ≫ AlgebraicGeometry.blowUpToBase C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf =
        S.goodBlowupToBase ∣_ (C.U : S.X.Opens)
declarations.comment: the affine-chart description: over an affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` the restriction `b⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` of the morphism of the tag is the blowing up of `U` in the product of the determinantal ideals `I_i(M^•, f)` of the chart, by a unique isomorphism over `U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.blowupCentre_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, the centre of the blowup over an affine chart: finite type.**  The
product of the determinantal ideals is finitely generated, being a finite product of finitely
generated ideals.  Finite type of the centre is the condition under which the blowup in it is
proper and, with
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.pow_mem_blowupCentre`, admissible away
from the divisor.
declarations.statement: theorem blowupCentre_fg (C : AffineChart S) : C.blowupCentre.FG
declarations.comment: the centre `∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of the blowup over an affine chart is of finite type; for the blowup in it over an affine chart --- its admissibility, the goodness of the pulled-back triple and its universal property --- see `ChartBlowupAdmissible.lean` and `ChartBlowupUniversal.lean`, and for the morphism `b : X' ⟶ X` glued from them see `GoodBlowupTag.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.AffineChart.pow_mem_blowupCentre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, the centre of the blowup over an affine chart: supported on the
divisor.**  The power `f ^ (∑ᵢ rᵢ)` of the equation of `D ∩ U` lies in the product of the
determinantal ideals, since `f ^ rᵢ` lies in the `i`-th factor.  Hence the closed subscheme cut
out by the centre is contained in `D ∩ U`, so the centre is disjoint from `U \ D`: this is the
condition that makes the blowup of the chart in it a `(U \ D)`-admissible blowing up.
declarations.statement:
theorem pow_mem_blowupCentre (C : AffineChart S) :
    C.f ^ (∑ i ∈ C.complex.bounded.toFinset, C.complex.rank i) ∈ C.blowupCentre
declarations.comment: the centre `∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of the blowup over an affine chart contains a power of the equation of the divisor, hence is supported on it; for the blowup in it over an affine chart --- its admissibility, the goodness of the pulled-back triple and its universal property --- see `ChartBlowupAdmissible.lean` and `ChartBlowupUniversal.lean`, and for the morphism `b : X' ⟶ X` glued from them see `GoodBlowupTag.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isGoodBlowup_id
declarations.doc:
**The existence assertion of Stacks tag 0GTY for a triple that is already good.**  If `𝟙 X`
is good for `(X, D, M)` then it has both properties (1) and (2) of the tag: property (1) is the
hypothesis, and every morphism `h : Y ⟶ X` factors through `𝟙 X` uniquely, by `h` itself.
declarations.statement: theorem isGoodBlowup_id (h : S.IsGoodOver (𝟙 S.X)) : S.IsGoodBlowup (𝟙 S.X)
declarations.comment: the morphism `b`, in the case where `𝟙 X` is good for the triple: the identity of `X` then has both properties of the tag, so `b` may be taken to be `𝟙 X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodBlowup.existsUnique_iso
declarations.doc:
**The uniqueness assertion of Stacks tag 0GTY.**  Two morphisms to `X` with properties (1)
and (2) are identified by a unique isomorphism over `X`.

Each factors through the other by (2), and the two composites are identities by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodBlowup.eq_id_of_comp_eq`; an isomorphism
over `X` is determined by its underlying morphism, which (2) pins down.
declarations.comment: the uniqueness assertion: any two morphisms to `X` with properties (1) and (2) of the tag are identified by a unique isomorphism over `X`, which is what it means for the morphism the tag describes to be unique

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodBlowup.isIso_of_isGoodOver_id
declarations.doc:
A morphism with properties (1) and (2) of Stacks tag 0GTY over a triple for which `𝟙 X` is
already good is an isomorphism.  By
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isGoodBlowup_id` the identity also has those
properties, so the two are identified over `X` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodBlowup.existsUnique_iso`.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_of_isGoodOver_id (hb : S.IsGoodBlowup b) (h : S.IsGoodOver (𝟙 S.X)) : IsIso b
declarations.comment: the morphism `b` over a triple for which `𝟙 X` is good: any morphism with the two properties of the tag is then an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_isPullback_blowUpToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTY, over an affine chart.**  For every affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` of the
triple, the part `b⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` of `b` over `U` is the blowing up of `U` in the product
`∏ᵢ I_i(M^•, f)` of the determinantal ideals of the chart: there is a morphism from that blowup
to `X'` making the square with `b` and the inclusion of `U` Cartesian.

The chart need not be one of those used to glue `X'`: the blowup of any chart has the universal
property over its domain, and so does the part of `b` over it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_blowUpToBase (S : ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d})
    (C : AffineChart S) :
    ∃ e : blowUp C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf ⟶ S.goodBlowup,
      IsPullback e (blowUpToBase C.blowupCentreIdealSheaf) S.goodBlowupToBase
        (C.U : S.X.Opens).ι
declarations.comment: over every affine chart, b is the blowing up in the product of the determinantal ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_comap_eq_bot_of_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal
declarations.doc:
**More on Flatness, Tag 0GTZ: the finite presentation of the closed immersion and part
(1).**  Let `(X, D, M)` be a good triple as in Situation 0F8S and let `T ⊆ D` be a closed
subscheme whose ideal over `D ∩ U` is the total obstruction ideal `J(M^•, f)` of Tag 0F81 for
every affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` with principal determinantal ideals.  Then the closed
immersion `i : T → D` is locally of finite presentation, and `T` scheme-theoretically contains
`D ∩ W`, where `W ⊆ X` is the maximal open over which the cohomology sheaves of `M` are locally
free: the inverse image of the ideal sheaf of `T` on `D ∩ W` is zero.

`T` is a variable of this statement; the subscheme itself is glued from the local closed
subschemes cut out by `J(M^•, f)` along a cover of `D` by good charts in
`AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_isGoodChartOpen_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal`,
which combines with this theorem into the existential assertion of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_comap_eq_bot_of_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal :
    LocallyOfFinitePresentation T.subschemeι ∧
      T.comap (S.D.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ S.locallyFreeLocus).ι = ⊥
declarations.comment: the finite presentation of the closed immersion `i : T → D` and part (1), at a closed subscheme `T` of `D` cutting out the obstruction ideal of Tag 0F81 on every good affine chart; such a `T` is constructed, and the tag stated existentially, in AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_isGoodChartOpen_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal of GoodTripleSubschemeExistence.lean. Parts (2) and (3), which concern `Li^*Lη_I M`, rest on identifying it over a good chart with the chart-local décalage, for which the affine comparison of Tag 08DW is proved and the remaining ingredient is the chart-level form of Tag 0GTV's second assertion recorded as AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.ChartDecalage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.isFiniteLocallyFree_etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTZ, part (2).**  Let `(X, D, M)` be a triple, let `b : X' ⟶ X` be a
morphism along which the pullback `D'` of the divisor is defined and the pulled-back triple
`(X', D', Lb^*M)` is good, and let `T ⊆ D'` be the closed subscheme cut out on every chart with
principal determinantal ideals by the obstruction ideal of More on Algebra, Tag 0F81.  Then the
cohomology sheaves of `Lj^*Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M` are finite locally free, `j : T ⟶ X'` being the
inclusion.

On a chart with principal determinantal ideals they are the sheaves of the cohomology modules of
`η_f M^• ⊗_A C`, `C = (A ⧸ fA) ⧸ J(M^•, f)`, which are finite projective by Tag 0F81; such charts
cover `T`, the pulled-back triple being good.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteLocallyFree_etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology
    (hS : (S.pullback b hb).IsGoodTriple)
    (hT : ∀ C : AffineChart (S.pullback b hb), (∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal) →
      T.ideal C.divisorAffineOpen = C.obstructionIdeal) (n : ℤ) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u}
      (S.etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology b hb
        (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hb).D.subschemeι) n)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.finiteLocallyFreeRank_etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology_eq_fiberRank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 0GTZ, part (3).**  In the situation of
`isFiniteLocallyFree_etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology`, at a point `t ∈ T` whose image in `X'`
lies in the locally free locus of `Lb^*M`, the rank of `H^n(Lj^*Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M)` at `t` is the
rank of `H^n(Lb^*M)` at the image of `t`.

Around that image there is a chart with principal determinantal ideals inside the locally free
locus; its cohomology modules are finite projective, so the décalage has the same cohomology
(More on Algebra, Tag 0F7P) and its cohomology commutes with base change to `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFreeRank_etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology_eq_fiberRank
    (hS : (S.pullback b hb).IsGoodTriple)
    (hT : ∀ C : AffineChart (S.pullback b hb), (∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal) →
      T.ideal C.divisorAffineOpen = C.obstructionIdeal) (n : ℤ) (t : T.subscheme)
    (ht : (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hb).D.subschemeι) t ∈
      (S.pullback b hb).locallyFreeLocus) :
    @Scheme.Modules.finiteLocallyFreeRank T.subscheme
        (S.etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology b hb
          (T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hb).D.subschemeι) n)
        (S.isFiniteLocallyFree_etaDerivedPullbackRestrictHomology hS hT n) t =
      Scheme.Modules.fiberRank ((S.pullback b hb).cohomologySheaf n)
        ((T.subschemeι ≫ (S.pullback b hb).D.subschemeι) t)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_isGoodChartOpen_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal
declarations.doc:
**More on Flatness, Tag 0GTZ: the closed subscheme `T` of `D` exists, the closed immersion
`i : T ⟶ D` is of finite presentation, and `T` contains `D ∩ W` scheme-theoretically.**  Let
`(X, D, M)` be a good triple as in Situation 0F8S.  There is a closed subscheme `T ⊆ D` whose
ideal over `D ∩ U` is the total obstruction ideal `J(M^•, f)` of More on Algebra, Tag 0F81 for
every affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` with principal determinantal ideals; the closed immersion
`i : T ⟶ D` is locally of finite presentation; and the inverse image on `D ∩ W` of the ideal
sheaf of `T` is zero, where `W ⊆ X` is the maximal open over which the cohomology sheaves of `M`
are locally free.

`T` is `goodChartSubscheme`, glued from the chart-local obstruction ideals by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofAffineFamily`; the two properties are
`locallyOfFinitePresentation_and_comap_eq_bot_of_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGoodChartOpen_ideal_eq_obstructionIdeal (hS : S.IsGoodTriple) :
    ∃ T : S.D.subscheme.IdealSheafData,
      (∀ C : AffineChart S, (∀ i : ℤ, (C.determinantalIdeal i).IsPrincipal) →
          T.ideal C.divisorAffineOpen = C.obstructionIdeal) ∧
        LocallyOfFinitePresentation T.subschemeι ∧
          T.comap (S.D.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ S.locallyFreeLocus).ι = ⊥
declarations.comment: the existence of the closed immersion `i : T ⟶ D` of finite presentation, and part (1). `T` is glued from the obstruction ideals of Tag 0F81 on the good affine charts by AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofAffineFamily. Parts (2) and (3) concern `Li^*Lη_I M`: over and above the affine comparison of Tag 08DW they need the chart-level comparison AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.ChartDecalage, and part (3) then reads off Tag 0GTA --- formalized in both halves in StacksFrontier.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.EtaSheafStalk --- at the points part (1) supplies, `i` being an isomorphism over `D` intersected with the locally free locus

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.exists_subscheme_isClosedImmersion_etaPullbackHomology
declarations.doc:
**More on Flatness, Tag 0GTZ.**  Let `X`, `D`, `I`, `M` be as in Situation 0F8S.  If
`(X, D, M)` is a good triple, then there exists a closed immersion `i : T ⟶ D` of finite
presentation such that

1. `T` scheme theoretically contains `D ∩ W`, where `W ⊆ X` is the maximal open over which the
   cohomology sheaves of `M` are locally free: the ideal sheaf of `T` vanishes on `D ∩ W`;
2. the cohomology sheaves of `Li^*(Lη_I M)` are (finite) locally free; and
3. for every point `t ∈ T` with image `x = i(t) ∈ W`, the rank of `H^n(M)_x` over `𝒪_{X, x}`
   and the rank of `H^n(Li^*(Lη_I M))_t` over `𝒪_{T, t}` agree, for every `n`.

The closed subscheme `T ⊆ D` is cut out by the ideal sheaf `obstructionIdealSheaf`, which on a
good affine chart `(U, A, f, M^•)` is the total obstruction ideal `J(M^•, f)` of More on Algebra,
Tag 0F81; these ideals glue because they do not depend on the chart (Tag 0GSW, flat base
change, and `etaTotalDirectSumIdeal_unit_mul`).  A closed immersion is quasi-compact and
separated, so being of finite presentation is being locally of finite presentation, which holds
because the obstruction ideals are finitely generated.  Here `Li^*(Lη_I M)` is the derived
pullback along `T ⟶ D ⟶ X` of the derived décalage of `M`, and its `n`-th cohomology sheaf is
`etaPullbackHomology`; `W` is `ComplexAndDivisorSituation.locallyFreeLocus`, the open of the
points at which every cohomology sheaf of `M` has a finite free stalk, which by Stacks 0GT1 is
the maximal open over which these sheaves are finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subscheme_isClosedImmersion_etaPullbackHomology (hS : S.IsGoodTriple) :
    ∃ T : S.D.subscheme.IdealSheafData,
      IsClosedImmersion T.subschemeι ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation T.subschemeι ∧
      T.comap (S.D.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ S.locallyFreeLocus).ι = ⊥ ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Scheme.Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
        (S.etaPullbackHomology (T.subschemeι ≫ S.D.subschemeι) n)) ∧
      ∀ t : T.subscheme, S.D.subschemeι (T.subschemeι t) ∈ S.locallyFreeLocus → ∀ n : ℤ,
        Module.finrank (S.X.presheaf.stalk (S.D.subschemeι (T.subschemeι t)))
            ((S.objectHomology n).presheaf.stalk (S.D.subschemeι (T.subschemeι t))) =
          Module.finrank (T.subscheme.presheaf.stalk t)
            ((S.etaPullbackHomology (T.subschemeι ≫ S.D.subschemeι) n).presheaf.stalk t)
declarations.comment: the existence of the closed immersion i : T → D of finite presentation together with parts (1), (2) and (3); locally free in (2) is proved in the stronger form finite locally free, and part (3) is stated for every degree n

declarations.name: Stacks.BlowUpComplexes.exists_isLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree_etaDerivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GU0.**  Let `(X, D, M)` be a triple as in Situation 0F8S and let
`b : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism along which the pullback `D' = b⁻¹D` of the effective Cartier divisor
is defined and makes the pulled-back triple `(X', D', Lb^*M)` good — the two conditions that
Stacks tag 0GTY's morphism satisfies.  If `M` is represented by a locally bounded complex of
finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules, then `Q = Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M` is represented by a locally bounded
complex of finite locally free `𝒪_{X'}`-modules.

The pullback `b^*ℳ^•` of a representative of `M` is a locally bounded complex of finite locally
free `𝒪_{X'}`-modules representing `Lb^*M`, so tag 0GTX applies to the pulled-back triple.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree_etaDerivedPullback
    (S : AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.{u, d}) {X' : Scheme.{u}} (b : X' ⟶ S.X)
    (hD : Stacks.Divisors.IsPullbackDefined b S.D)
    (hgood : AlgebraicGeometry.ComplexAndDivisorSituation.IsGoodTriple (S.pullback b hD))
    (hrep : ∃ ℳ : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} S.X.toRingedSpace) ℤ,
      Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree ℳ ∧
        Nonempty ((@DerivedCategory.Q _ _ _ S.hasDerivedCategory).obj ℳ ≅ S.M)) :
    ∃ 𝒬 : CochainComplex X'.Modules ℤ,
      Stacks.Chow.IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree 𝒬 ∧
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj 𝒬 ≅
          (Stacks.Divisors.Eta.derivedEtaData (S.D.comap b)).functor.obj
            (S.derivedPullbackObject b))
declarations.comment: for every `b` along which `b⁻¹D` is defined and the pulled-back triple is good, in particular the morphism of Tag 0GTY (`goodBlowupToBase`); `Q` is stated directly as `Lη_{ℐ'}Lb^*M`

declarations.name: Stacks.Length.map_norm_pow_length_eq_prod_norm_pow_length
declarations.doc:
Let `A → S` be a flat local homomorphism of local rings with `m = length_S(S / 𝔪_A S)`, let
`B` be a local `A`-algebra along a local homomorphism with `κ(B) / κ(A)` finite, and let
`π`, `u ∈ B` with `B / πB` of finite length. Then, writing `T = S ⊗_A B`,

`(Norm_{κ(B)/κ(A)}(ū) ^ length_B(B / πB)) ^ m
  = ∏_𝔮 Norm_{κ(T_𝔮)/κ(S)}(ū) ^ length_{T_𝔮}(T_𝔮 / πT_𝔮)`,

the product running over the maximal ideals of `T` and the left-hand side being read in `κ(S)`
through `κ(A) → κ(S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_norm_pow_length_eq_prod_norm_pow_length
    {A : Type u} {S : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing S] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing S] [IsLocalRing B]
    [Algebra A S] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A S)]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A S]
    [Fintype (MaximalSpectrum (S ⊗[A] B))]
    [Module.Finite (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum (S ⊗[A] B),
      IsLocalHom (algebraMap S (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))]
    [∀ q : MaximalSpectrum (S ⊗[A] B),
      Module.Finite (ResidueField S) (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))]
    (π u : B) (hM : IsFiniteLength B (B ⧸ Ideal.span {π}))
    {m : ℕ} (hm : Module.length S (S ⧸ extendedMaximalIdeal A S) = m) :
    ResidueField.map (algebraMap A S)
      ((Algebra.norm (ResidueField A) (residue B u) ^
        (Module.length B (B ⧸ Ideal.span {π})).toNat) ^ m) =
      ∏ q : MaximalSpectrum (S ⊗[A] B),
        Algebra.norm (ResidueField S)
          (residue (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            ((algebraMap (S ⊗[A] B) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
              (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight u))) ^
            (Module.length (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
            (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal ⧸
              Ideal.span {(algebraMap (S ⊗[A] B) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
                (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight π))})).toNat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyFiniteDirectSum
declarations.doc:
The subgroup of pointwise families whose support meets every quasi-compact open subset of
the scheme in a finite set.
declarations.statement:
def locallyFiniteDirectSum (X : Scheme.{u}) (T : Set X) (G : T → Type v)
    [∀ x, AddCommGroup (G x)] : AddSubgroup (∀ x, G x)
declarations.comment: locally_finite_direct_sum

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseCycleEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU2.** The group of `k`-cycles is the locally finite direct sum of the degree-zero
Milnor K-groups of the residue fields at the points of relative dimension `k`.
declarations.statement: def pointwiseCycleEquiv (k : ℤ) : CycleGroup C p k ≃+ PointwiseCycleGroup C p k
declarations.comment: the pointwise description of cycles

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseCycleEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU2.** Under the pointwise description of cycles, the degree-zero Milnor K-class at
a point of relative dimension `k` is the coefficient of the cycle there.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseCycleEquiv_apply (k : ℤ) (c : CycleGroup C p k)
    (x : pointsOfDimension C p k) :
    milnorKTheoryZeroAddEquiv (X.residueField x.1) ((pointwiseCycleEquiv C p k c).1 x) =
      c.1 x.1
declarations.comment: the coordinate identification with integer coefficients

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU3.** The divisor differential from pointwise Milnor K₁-chains at the points of
relative dimension `k + 1` to pointwise Milnor K₀-chains at the points of relative dimension `k`:
each Milnor K₁-class is read as a nonzero rational function on the closure of its point, and the
differential is the locally finite sum of the pushed-forward principal divisors, transported to
the pointwise description of cycles of Stacks 0GU2.
declarations.statement:
def pointwiseDivisorDifferential (k : ℤ) :
    PointwiseKOneGroup C p k →+ PointwiseCycleGroup C p k
declarations.comment: pointwise_divisor_differential

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_spec
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0GU3.** The divisor differential satisfies the coordinatewise divisor formula.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseDivisorDifferential_spec (k : ℤ) :
    IsPointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k)
declarations.comment: pointwise_divisor_differential

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_pointwiseDivisorDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU3.** There is a homomorphism from pointwise Milnor K₁-chains to pointwise Milnor
K₀-chains satisfying the coordinatewise divisor formula.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pointwiseDivisorDifferential (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ d : PointwiseKOneGroup C p k →+ PointwiseCycleGroup C p k,
      IsPointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k d
declarations.comment: pointwise_divisor_differential

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseChowClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU3.** The class in the Chow group `A_k(X)` of a locally finite family of
degree-zero Milnor K-classes at the points of relative dimension `k`: the cycle it names,
modulo rational equivalence.
declarations.statement: def pointwiseChowClass (k : ℤ) : PointwiseCycleGroup C p k →+ chowGroup C p k
declarations.comment: the map from pointwise cycles to the Chow group

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseChowClass_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU3.** Every class in the Chow group `A_k(X)` is the class of a pointwise Milnor
K₀ chain: the chain attached to any cycle representing it.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseChowClass_surjective (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Surjective (pointwiseChowClass C p k)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the presentation

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_range_eq_ker_pointwiseChowClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU3.** The presentation of the Chow group is exact in the middle: a pointwise
Milnor K₀-chain is a pointwise divisor exactly when the cycle it names is rationally equivalent
to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseDivisorDifferential_range_eq_ker_pointwiseChowClass (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k).range = (pointwiseChowClass C p k).ker
declarations.comment: exactness of the presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsEnvelope
declarations.doc: An **envelope** is a proper, completely decomposed morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEnvelope {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEnvelope_comp
declarations.doc: The composite of two envelopes of schemes is an envelope.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEnvelope_comp {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsEnvelope f) (hg : IsEnvelope g) : IsEnvelope (g ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEnvelope_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc: Envelopes of schemes are stable under arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
instance isEnvelope_isStableUnderBaseChange :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) ↦ IsEnvelope f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.envelope_chow_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Pushing a class on `Y ×_X Y` forward along the two projections, taking the difference and
pushing forward along `f` gives zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem envelope_chow_comp_eq_zero (γ : chowGroup C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) k) :
    properChowPushforward C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k)
        (properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k
            (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
              (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k) γ -
          properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
            (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k
            (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
              (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
              (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k) γ) = 0
declarations.comment: the composite of the two maps is zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.envelope_chow_exact
declarations.doc:
For an envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` a class in
`A_k(Y)` pushes forward to zero in `A_k(X)` exactly when it is the difference of the pushforwards
of a single class in `A_k(Y ×_X Y)` along the two projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem envelope_chow_exact (hcd : IsCompletelyDecomposed f) (β : chowGroup C (f ≫ sX) k) :
    properChowPushforward C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k) β = 0 ↔
      ∃ γ : chowGroup C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) k,
        β = properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k
              (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
                (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k) γ -
            properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
              (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k
              (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
                (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
                (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k) γ
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.envelope_chow_exactSequence
declarations.doc:
For an envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` with the two projections `p, q : Y ×_X Y ⟶ Y` of its fibre
square, the sequence

  `A_k(Y ×_X Y) --(p_* - q_*)--> A_k(Y) --f_*--> A_k(X) ⟶ 0`

is exact for every `k ∈ ℤ`: the composite of the two maps is zero, a class killed by `f_*` is a
difference `p_* γ - q_* γ`, and `f_*` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem envelope_chow_exactSequence (hcd : IsCompletelyDecomposed f) :
    (∀ γ : chowGroup C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) k,
        properChowPushforward C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
          (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k)
          (properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k
              (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
                (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k) γ -
            properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
              (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k
              (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
                (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
                (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k) γ) = 0) ∧
      (∀ β : chowGroup C (f ≫ sX) k,
        properChowPushforward C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
            (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k) β = 0 ↔
          ∃ γ : chowGroup C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) k,
            β = properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX)
                  (pullback.fst f f) rfl k
                  (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
                    (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.fst f f) rfl k) γ -
                properChowPushforward C (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX)
                  (pullback.snd f f) (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k
                  (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C
                    (pullback.fst f f ≫ f ≫ sX) (f ≫ sX) (pullback.snd f f)
                    (pullback_snd_comp_eq_pullback_fst_comp f sX) k) γ) ∧
      Function.Surjective (properChowPushforward C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k
        (properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence C (f ≫ sX) sX f rfl k))
declarations.comment: the exact sequence of Chow groups of an envelope

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU9.** The three locally finite direct sums of Milnor K-groups of the tag form a
complex: the tame-symbol differential followed by the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3 is the
zero homomorphism.

This is the assertion of the tag. By
`Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary_of_forall` it suffices to
check it one point of relative dimension `k + 2` and one point of relative dimension `k` at a
time, which is `Stacks.Chow.finsum_pointClosureOrdBoundaryTerm_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k).comp (pointwiseMilnorBoundary C p k) = 0
declarations.comment: the complex of the tag: the composite of the tame-symbol differential of the tag with the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3 is the zero homomorphism, so the three locally finite direct sums of Stacks 0GU2 -- the degree-two, degree-one and degree-zero Milnor K-groups of the residue fields at the points of relative dimension k + 2, k + 1 and k -- form a complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU9.** The complex of the tag, packaged as a short complex of abelian groups: the
degree-two Milnor K-chains at the points of relative dimension `k + 2`, the degree-one chains at
the points of relative dimension `k + 1` and the degree-zero chains at the points of relative
dimension `k`, with the tame-symbol differential and the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3.
Its `zero` field is
`Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_comp_pointwiseMilnorBoundary`.
declarations.statement: def pointwiseMilnorShortComplex (k : ℤ) : ShortComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the complex of the tag, assembled as a short complex of abelian groups out of the three locally finite direct sums of Stacks 0GU2 and the two differentials, the vanishing of whose composite is its defining property

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorBoundary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GU9.** The first differential of the complex of the tag: the homomorphism from the
locally finite direct sum of the degree-two Milnor K-groups at the points of relative dimension
`k + 2` to the locally finite direct sum of the degree-one Milnor K-groups at the points of
relative dimension `k + 1` whose coefficient at `x'` is the sum, over the points `x` of relative
dimension `k + 2` specializing to `x'`, of the tame-symbol boundaries
`∂_{𝒪_{closure {x}, x'}}` of the classes of the chain.
declarations.statement:
def pointwiseMilnorBoundary (k : ℤ) :
    PointwiseKTwoGroup C p k →+ PointwiseKOneGroup C p k
declarations.comment: the first differential of the complex of the tag, as a homomorphism of the locally finite direct sums of Stacks 0GU2: the degree-two Milnor K-chain group at the points of relative dimension k + 2 maps to the degree-one chain group at the points of relative dimension k + 1 by the rule whose coefficient at a point x' is the sum, over the points x of relative dimension k + 2 specializing to x', of the tame-symbol boundary of the class at x along the one-dimensional local ring of the closure of x at x'; both the finiteness of that sum and the local finiteness of the resulting family are proved, so the rule is a well defined additive map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.milnorKTwoTameSymbol
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GU9.** The tame symbol `∂_A` of a one-dimensional Noetherian local
domain `A` with fraction field `K`, descended along the presentation of Milnor K-theory to a
homomorphism `K₂ᴹ(K) ⟶ K₁ᴹ(κ(A))`. This is the local component of the first differential of the
complex of the tag, the one written `∂_{𝒪_{W_x, x'}}` there.
declarations.statement:
def milnorKTwoTameSymbol (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) :
    MilnorKTheory K 2 →+ MilnorKTheory (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) 1
declarations.comment: the construction of the local component of the first differential: the tame symbol of a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, descended to a homomorphism from the degree-two Milnor K-group of its fraction field to the degree-one Milnor K-group of its residue field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sum_localMilnorBoundaryOrder_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GU9.** Let `A` be a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain with
fraction field `K` and let `α` be a class in the degree-two Milnor K-group of `K`. Summing, over
the height-one primes `𝔮` of `A`, the order along `A / 𝔮` of the tame-symbol boundary of `α` at
`𝔮` gives zero.

This is the vanishing which the tag's argument reduces the composite of its two differentials to:
at a point `x''` of `δ`-dimension `k` lying on the integral closed subscheme `W` with generic
point `x` of `δ`-dimension `k + 2`, the ring `A` is `𝒪_{W, x''}`, its height-one primes are the
intermediate points `x'` of `δ`-dimension `k + 1`, and the summand at `𝔮` is the coefficient
`ord_{𝒪_{closure {x'}, x''}}(∂_{𝒪_{W, x'}}(α))`. The source reduces to a pure symbol by
additivity and linearity before appealing to Stacks 0EAX; here the reduction is carried out, so
the statement holds for every class of the Milnor K-group and not only for a pure symbol.
declarations.statement:
theorem sum_localMilnorBoundaryOrder_eq_zero (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (α : MilnorKTheory (FractionRing A) 2) :
    (∑ᶠ q : {q : Ideal A // q.IsPrime ∧ q.height = 1},
      localMilnorBoundaryOrder hdim q α) = 0
declarations.comment: the vanishing of the composite of the two differentials in its local algebraic form: for a two-dimensional Noetherian local domain, the orders along the quotients of the tame-symbol boundaries of an arbitrary degree-two Milnor K-class of the fraction field, summed over the height-one primes, give zero -- this is the displayed sum of the tag's proof, with the reduction to a pure symbol discharged; the fraction field is realized as `FractionRing A`, and the geometric indexing of that sum by the intermediate points, the locally finite chain groups and the three-term complex itself are not formalized here

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseMilnorBoundary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA for the first differential and the restriction map.** Restriction of locally
finite Milnor K-chains to an open subscheme commutes with the tame-symbol differential of
Stacks 0GU9: the square formed by the two differentials and the two restriction maps, in Milnor
degrees two and one, commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem milnorChainComap_pointwiseMilnorBoundary (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseMilnorBoundary C (j ≫ p) k).comp
        (milnorChainComap C p j (injective_base_of_isOpenImmersion j)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_openImmersion j) (k + 2) 2) =
      (milnorChainComap C p j (injective_base_of_isOpenImmersion j)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_openImmersion j) (k + 1) 1).comp
        (pointwiseMilnorBoundary C p k)
declarations.comment: the compatibility of the restriction map of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag with the FIRST boundary map of the complex of Stacks 0GU9, the tame-symbol differential: for an open immersion j into a scheme locally of finite type over a Chow situation, restriction of locally finite Milnor K-chains to the open subscheme carries the tame-symbol differential in relative dimensions k + 2 and k + 1 to the tame-symbol differential of the open subscheme. The companion square for the extension-by-zero map from the closed complement is Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorBoundary_milnorChainExtend. The two squares for the SECOND boundary map, the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3, are Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential and Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend; the six-term exact sequence the snake lemma yields from all four is Stacks.Chow.milnorChowLocalization_exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorBoundary_milnorChainExtend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA for the first differential and the extension-by-zero map.** Extension by zero
of locally finite Milnor K-chains from a closed subscheme commutes with the tame-symbol
differential of Stacks 0GU9.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseMilnorBoundary_milnorChainExtend (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseMilnorBoundary C p k).comp
        (milnorChainExtend C p i (injective_base_of_isClosedImmersion i)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_closedImmersion i) inferInstance (k + 2) 2) =
      (milnorChainExtend C p i (injective_base_of_isClosedImmersion i)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_closedImmersion i) inferInstance (k + 1) 1).comp
        (pointwiseMilnorBoundary C (i ≫ p) k)
declarations.comment: the compatibility of the extension-by-zero map of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag with the FIRST boundary map of the complex of Stacks 0GU9, the tame-symbol differential: for a closed immersion i into a scheme locally of finite type over a Chow situation, extension by zero of locally finite Milnor K-chains from the closed subscheme carries its tame-symbol differential in relative dimensions k + 2 and k + 1 to the tame-symbol differential of the ambient scheme. The companion square for the restriction map to the open complement is Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseMilnorBoundary. The two squares for the SECOND boundary map, the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3, are Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential and Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend; the six-term exact sequence the snake lemma yields from all four is Stacks.Chow.milnorChowLocalization_exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA for the second differential and the restriction map.** Restriction of locally
finite Milnor K-chains to an open subscheme commutes with the divisor differential of
Stacks 0GU3: the square formed by the two differentials and the two restriction maps, in Milnor
degrees one and zero, commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C (j ≫ p) k).comp
        (milnorChainComap C p j (injective_base_of_isOpenImmersion j)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_openImmersion j) (k + 1) 1) =
      (milnorChainComap C p j (injective_base_of_isOpenImmersion j)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_openImmersion j) k 0).comp
        (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k)
declarations.comment: the compatibility of the restriction map of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag with the SECOND boundary map of the complex of Stacks 0GU9, the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3: for an open immersion j into a scheme locally of finite type over a Chow situation, restriction of locally finite Milnor K-chains to the open subscheme carries the divisor differential in relative dimensions k + 1 and k to the divisor differential of the open subscheme. The companion square for the extension-by-zero map from the closed complement is Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA for the second differential and the extension-by-zero map.** Extension by zero
of locally finite Milnor K-chains from a closed subscheme commutes with the divisor differential
of Stacks 0GU3.
declarations.statement:
theorem pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend (k : ℤ) :
    (pointwiseDivisorDifferential C p k).comp
        (milnorChainExtend C p i (injective_base_of_isClosedImmersion i)
          (bijective_residueFieldMap_closedImmersion i) inferInstance (k + 1) 1) =

          (bijective_residueFieldMap_closedImmersion i) inferInstance k 0).comp

declarations.comment: the compatibility of the extension-by-zero map of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag with the SECOND boundary map of the complex of Stacks 0GU9, the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3: for a closed immersion i into a scheme locally of finite type over a Chow situation, extension by zero of locally finite Milnor K-chains from the closed subscheme carries its divisor differential in relative dimensions k + 1 and k to the divisor differential of the ambient scheme. The companion square for the restriction map to the open complement is Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalizationComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA.** The degreewise localization sequence of locally finite Milnor K-chains: the
chains on the closed subscheme `Y`, on `X` and on the open subscheme `U`, with extension by zero
from `Y` and restriction to `U`.
declarations.statement:
def milnorChainLocalizationComplex (hcomp : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ)
    (m : ℤ) (n : ℕ) : ShortComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the degreewise localization sequence of the tag, for one relative dimension m and one Milnor degree n: the locally finite direct sums of Stacks 0GU2 for the closed subscheme, the ambient scheme and the complementary open subscheme, together with the extension-by-zero map from the closed subscheme and the restriction map to the open subscheme, as a short complex of abelian groups; its compatibility with the two boundary maps of Stacks 0GU9, and the six-term exact sequence the snake lemma yields from it, are proved not here but in Stacks.Chow.milnorChowLocalization_exact, Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseMilnorBoundary, Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorBoundary_milnorChainExtend, Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential and Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalizationSplitting
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA.** The degreewise localization sequence is split: restriction to `Y` is a
retraction of the extension by zero from `Y`, extension by zero from `U` is a section of the
restriction to `U`, and the two composites add up to the identity.
declarations.comment: the splitting of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag: restriction to the closed subscheme retracts the extension by zero from it, extension by zero from the open subscheme sections the restriction to it, and the two resulting idempotents of the chains on the ambient scheme add up to the identity

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalization_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA.** The degreewise localization sequence is short exact: it is split, and a
split short complex is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem milnorChainLocalization_shortExact
    (hcomp : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) (m : ℤ) (n : ℕ) :
    (milnorChainLocalizationComplex C p i j hcomp m n).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the short exactness of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag, in one relative dimension and one Milnor degree: extension by zero from the closed subscheme is injective, restriction to the open subscheme is surjective, and the image of the first is the kernel of the second

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalization_shortExact_degrees
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA.** The three split short exact sequences of the tag, for `i = 2, 1, 0`: the
locally finite direct sums of degree-`i` Milnor K-groups at the points of relative dimension
`k + i`, for the closed subscheme, the ambient scheme and the complementary open subscheme. By
`Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalizationComplex_X₂_two`,
`Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalizationComplex_X₂_one` and
`Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalizationComplex_X₂_zero` the middle terms are the three groups that
carry the complex of Stacks 0GU9.
declarations.statement:
theorem milnorChainLocalization_shortExact_degrees
    (hcomp : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) (k : ℤ) :
    (milnorChainLocalizationComplex C p i j hcomp (k + 2) 2).ShortExact ∧
      (milnorChainLocalizationComplex C p i j hcomp (k + 1) 1).ShortExact ∧
      (milnorChainLocalizationComplex C p i j hcomp k 0).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the three split short exact sequences of the tag, for i = 2, 1 and 0: for an open subscheme and a closed subscheme with complementary underlying set, the sequence of locally finite direct sums of the degree-i Milnor K-groups of the residue fields at the points of relative dimension k + i is short exact and split; the middle terms are exactly the three groups carrying the complex of Stacks 0GU9. Only the sequences themselves are proved here; their compatibility with the two boundary maps of that complex is proved in Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseMilnorBoundary, Stacks.Chow.pointwiseMilnorBoundary_milnorChainExtend, Stacks.Chow.milnorChainComap_pointwiseDivisorDifferential and Stacks.Chow.pointwiseDivisorDifferential_milnorChainExtend, and the six-term exact sequence the snake lemma yields from them is Stacks.Chow.milnorChowLocalization_exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChowGroupOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA.** The first higher Chow group `CH^M_k(X, 1)` of the tag: the homology in the
middle of the complex of Stacks 0GU9, that is, the degree-one Milnor K-chains killed by the
divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3 modulo those coming from a degree-two Milnor K-chain under
the tame-symbol differential. The superscript of the tag distinguishes this group from the higher
Chow groups of the literature.
declarations.statement: def milnorChowGroupOne (k : ℤ) : Type u
declarations.comment: the definition of the tag: the first higher Chow group CH^M_k(X, 1) is the homology in the middle of the complex of Stacks 0GU9, formed as the degree-one Milnor K-chains killed by the divisor differential of Stacks 0GU3 modulo the image of the tame-symbol differential of Stacks 0GU9, the latter lying in the former because that composite is the zero homomorphism; the localization property of the tag, namely the degreewise split short exact sequences attached to an open subscheme with reduced closed complement together with the six-term exact sequence the snake lemma yields from them, is not proved here but in Stacks.Chow.milnorChainLocalization_shortExact_degrees and Stacks.Chow.milnorChowLocalization_exact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.milnorChowLocalization_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUA.** The six-term exact sequence

`CH^M_k(Y, 1) ⟶ CH^M_k(X, 1) ⟶ CH^M_k(V, 1) ⟶ CH_k(Y) ⟶ CH_k(X) ⟶ CH_k(V) ⟶ 0`

attached to an open subscheme `V` of `X` and a closed immersion `i : Y ⟶ X` with complementary
image. The first three maps are those induced by the extension-by-zero and restriction maps of
the degreewise localization sequence of the tag, together with the connecting map
`Stacks.Chow.milnorChowBoundary`; the last two are the proper pushforward and the restriction to
an open subscheme of Stacks 02RX, whose exactness and surjectivity are
`Stacks.Chow.exact_chowPushforward_chowGroupOpensRestrict` and
`Stacks.Chow.surjective_chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem milnorChowLocalization_exact (k : ℤ) :
    Function.Exact (milnorChowGroupOneExtend C p i k) (milnorChowGroupOneComap C p V k) ∧
      Function.Exact (milnorChowGroupOneComap C p V k) (milnorChowBoundary C p i V hcomp k) ∧
      Function.Exact (milnorChowBoundary C p i V hcomp k)
        (chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C (i ≫ p) p i rfl k) ∧
      Function.Exact (chowPushforwardOfIsClosedImmersion C (i ≫ p) p i rfl k)
        (chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion C p V k) ∧
      Function.Surjective (chowGroupOpensRestrictOfIsOpenImmersion C p V k)
declarations.comment: the six-term exact sequence of the tag, the main claim of the remark: for an open subscheme V of a scheme X locally of finite type over a Chow situation and a closed immersion i of Y into X whose image is the complement of V, the sequence of the first higher Chow groups of Y, X and V, followed by the Chow groups of Y, X and V and ending in zero, is exact. The first two maps are induced on the first higher Chow groups of Stacks 0GU9 by the extension-by-zero and restriction maps of the degreewise localization sequence of the tag; the third is the connecting map of the snake lemma, formed from the splitting of that sequence; the last two are the proper pushforward along the closed immersion and the restriction to the open subscheme of Stacks 02RX

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullbackChow_bijective_of_isAffineSpaceBundle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUB.** Let `(S, δ)` be as in Situation 02QL, let `Y` be locally of finite type over
`S`, let `r ≥ 0` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes such that every point of `Y` lies in
an open `V ⊆ Y` with `f⁻¹(V) ≅ V × 𝔸^r` as schemes over `V`. Then flat pullback

  `f^* : CH_k(Y) ⟶ CH_{k+r}(X)`

is an isomorphism for every `k`. The morphism `f` is locally of finite type, flat and of relative
dimension `r` because it is so locally on `Y`; these are not hypotheses but consequences of the
local triviality, recorded through `letI`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullbackChow_bijective_of_isAffineSpaceBundle (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sY : Y ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) (r : ℕ)
    (hbundle : IsAffineSpaceBundle f r) (k : ℤ) :
    letI := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isAffineSpaceBundle f r hbundle
    letI := flat_of_isAffineSpaceBundle f r hbundle
    Function.Bijective (flatPullbackChowOfRelativeDimension C (f ≫ sY) sY f rfl r
      (relativeDimension_of_isAffineSpaceBundle f r hbundle) k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_bivariantRestriction_eq_of_isEnvelope
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUC.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type over the base
of chapter 42, let `g : Y' ⟶ Y` be an envelope and write `X' = X ×_Y Y'`. Let
`c' ∈ A^p(X' ⟶ Y')`. If the two restrictions `res₁(c') = res₂(c')` in
`A^p(X' ×_X X' ⟶ Y' ×_Y Y')` agree, then there is a unique `c ∈ A^p(X ⟶ Y)` whose restriction
`res(c)` along `g` is `c'`.

Bivariant classes are taken against the Gysin system of the first Chern class of an invertible
module.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_bivariantRestriction_eq_of_isEnvelope (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    {X Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] (sY : Y ⟶ C.S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (comm : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (envelope : IsEnvelope g) (p : ℤ) :
    letI : IsProper g := envelope.isProper
    ∀ c' : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst f g ≫ sX) (g ≫ sY)
        (pullback.snd f g) (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C sX sY f comm g) p,
      envelopeDescentRes₁ C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f comm g p
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) c' =
        envelopeDescentRes₂ C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f comm g p
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) c' →
      ∃! c : BivariantClass C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f comm p,
        bivariantRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX sY f comm g p
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) c = c'

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_of_restriction_eq_totalChernClassComplexLocallyBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUD, uniqueness for the total Chern class.** Let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and
let `H` be an envelope presentation of it, Stacks 0F9E (1), whose source is quasi-compact. Two
families `c, d` of Chow cohomology classes of `X` whose restrictions along the envelope of `H`
are the coefficients of the total Chern class `c(P)` of the presenting complex are equal.

The existence of such a family is **not** proved: see the implementation notes of this file. The
hypothesis is taken at the single presentation `H` rather than at every presentation of `E`, so
this is stronger than the uniqueness clause of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_restriction_eq_totalChernClassComplexLocallyBounded
    (H : EnvelopePresentation E) [LocallyOfFiniteType H.f] [CompactSpace H.Y]
    {R : ChowCohomologySeriesRing C G (H.f ≫ sX)} (D : TotalChernClassSeries C G (H.f ≫ sX) R)
    {c d : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyComponent C G sX (p : ℤ)}
    (hc : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      (totalChernClassComplexLocallyBounded C G (H.f ≫ sX) D H.P H.locallyBounded).1 p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (d p) =
      (totalChernClassComplexLocallyBounded C G (H.f ≫ sX) D H.P H.locallyBounded).1 p) :
    c = d
declarations.comment: the uniqueness half for the total Chern class c(E), read on the coefficients of the series of Tag 0ESZ; the existence of the classes is not constructed here, and the hypothesis is taken at one envelope presentation rather than at all of them, which is stronger

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_of_restriction_eq_powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUD, uniqueness for the power sums.** Let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `H`
be an envelope presentation of it, Stacks 0F9E (1), whose source is quasi-compact. Two families
`c, d` of Chow cohomology classes of `X` whose restrictions along the envelope of `H` are the
classes `P_p(P)` of the presenting complex are equal.

The existence of such a family is **not** proved: see the implementation notes of this file. The
hypothesis is taken at the single presentation `H` rather than at every presentation of `E`, so
this is stronger than the uniqueness clause of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_restriction_eq_powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded
    (H : EnvelopePresentation E) [LocallyOfFiniteType H.f] [CompactSpace H.Y]
    (W : PowerSumClassRule C G (H.f ≫ sX))
    {c d : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyComponent C G sX (p : ℤ)}
    (hc : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded C G (H.f ≫ sX) W H.P H.locallyBounded p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (d p) =
      powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded C G (H.f ≫ sX) W H.P H.locallyBounded p) :
    c = d
declarations.comment: the uniqueness half for the power sums P_p(E), the classes of Tag 0ESZ; the existence of the classes is not constructed here, and the hypothesis is taken at one envelope presentation rather than at all of them, which is stronger

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.eq_of_restriction_eq_chernCharacterComplexLocallyBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUD, uniqueness for the Chern character.** Let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let
`H` be an envelope presentation of it, Stacks 0F9E (1), whose source is quasi-compact. Two
families `c, d` of rational Chow cohomology classes of `X` whose restrictions along the envelope
of `H` are the components `ch_p(P) = P_p(P)/p!` of the Chern character of the presenting complex
are equal.

The existence of such a family is **not** proved: see the implementation notes of this file. The
hypothesis is taken at the single presentation `H` rather than at every presentation of `E`, so
this is stronger than the uniqueness clause of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_restriction_eq_chernCharacterComplexLocallyBounded
    (H : EnvelopePresentation E) [LocallyOfFiniteType H.f] [CompactSpace H.Y]
    (W : PowerSumClassRule C G (H.f ≫ sX))
    {c d : ∀ p : ℕ, rationalChowCohomologyComponent C G sX (p : ℤ)}
    (hc : ∀ p : ℕ, rationalChowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      ((Nat.factorial p : ℚ)⁻¹) ⊗ₜ[ℤ]
        powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded C G (H.f ≫ sX) W H.P H.locallyBounded p)
    (hd : ∀ p : ℕ, rationalChowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (d p) =
      ((Nat.factorial p : ℚ)⁻¹) ⊗ₜ[ℤ]
        powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded C G (H.f ≫ sX) W H.P H.locallyBounded p) :
    c = d
declarations.comment: the uniqueness half for the Chern character ch(E), read componentwise as ch_p = P_p/p! with the classes P_p of Tag 0ESZ; the existence of the classes is not constructed here, and the hypothesis is taken at one envelope presentation rather than at all of them, which is stronger

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_perfectPowerSum
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the power sums.** Let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose Chern
classes are defined. For every `p` there is a unique class `P_p(E) ∈ A^p(X)` whose restriction
along the envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` of every presentation `(f, 𝓔^•)` of `E` is the class `P_p(𝓔^•)`
of Lemma 0ESZ, which on the locus where the terms have constant ranks is `∑ (-1)^n P_p(𝓔^n)`
(`Stacks.Chow.res_complexPowerSum_complexRankLocus`). The class is
`Stacks.Chow.perfectPowerSumComponent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_perfectPowerSum (p : ℕ) :
    ∃! x : chowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (p : ℤ),
      ∀ H : EnvelopePresentation E,
        chowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX H.f (p : ℤ)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) x =
          complexPowerSumComponent C (H.f ≫ sX) H.locallyBounded p
declarations.comment: P_p(E): the unique class of A^p(X) restricting along the envelope of every presentation (f, E^bullet) of E to P_p(E^bullet), independent of f and E^bullet

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_perfectChernCharacter
declarations.doc:
**Uniqueness of the Chern character.** Let `E` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose Chern
classes are defined. For every `p` there is a unique class `ch_p(E) ∈ A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐` whose rational
restriction along the envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` of every presentation `(f, 𝓔^•)` of `E` is the
component `ch_p(𝓔^•) = P_p(𝓔^•)/p!` of the Chern character of `𝓔^•` (Lemma 0ESZ). The class is
`Stacks.Chow.perfectChernCharacterComponent`, and the family `(ch_p(E))_p` is
`ch(E) ∈ ∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(X) ⊗ 𝐐`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_perfectChernCharacter (p : ℕ) :
    ∃! x : rationalChowCohomologyComponent C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (p : ℤ),
      ∀ H : EnvelopePresentation E,
        rationalChowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX H.f (p : ℤ)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C) x =
          complexChernCharacterComponent C (H.f ≫ sX) H.locallyBounded p
declarations.comment: ch(E): for every p the unique class of A^p(X) ⊗ Q restricting along the envelope of every presentation (f, E^bullet) of E to ch_p(E^bullet) = P_p(E^bullet)/p!, independent of f and E^bullet

registrations.name: Stacks.Chow.existsUnique_forall_res_eq_complexChern
registrations.comment: c(E): the unique class of the product of the A^p(X), p ≥ 0, restricting along the envelope of every presentation (f, E^bullet) of E to c(E^bullet), independent of f and E^bullet

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_envelope
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUE (1).** If some envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` has `Lf^*E` isomorphic to a locally
bounded complex of finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-modules, then the Chern classes of `E` are
defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_of_envelope {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsEnvelope f) (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (P : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ)
    (hP : IsLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree P)
    (hrep : Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)) :
    HasDefinedChernClasses E
declarations.comment: clause (1): the envelope condition of Tag 0F9E (1) itself

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_bounded_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUE (2).** If `E` is represented by a bounded complex of finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-modules, then the Chern classes of `E` are defined: the identity of `X` is an envelope and
`L(𝟙 X)^* ≅ 𝟭`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_of_bounded_isFiniteLocallyFree {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (P : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.bounded X.Modules P)
    (hflf : ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree
      (R := structureSheafOfRings X.toRingedSpace) (P.X n))
    (hrep : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅ E)) :
    HasDefinedChernClasses E
declarations.comment: clause (2): a bounded complex of finite locally free modules representing `E`

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUE (5).** If `E` is isomorphic to the derived pullback of an object `E'` whose
Chern classes are defined, then the Chern classes of `E` are defined: the base change of an
envelope of `E'` is an envelope, and the degreewise pullback of a locally bounded complex of
finite locally free modules is one again and computes the derived pullback.

At `i = Iso.refl` this is the well-definedness that clause (2) of Stacks 0FAC presupposes when it
writes `c_p(Lg^*E)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_of_derivedPullback {X X' : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ X')
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (E' : DerivedCategory X'.Modules)
    (hE' : HasDefinedChernClasses E')
    (i : E ≅ (Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      g.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E') :
    HasDefinedChernClasses E
declarations.comment: clause (5): `E` is the derived pullback of an object whose Chern classes are defined

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_isCompact_irreducibleComponents
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GUE] clause (3).** Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X`
be locally of finite type over `S` with quasi-compact irreducible components, and let `E` be a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then the Chern classes of `E` are defined: there is an envelope
`f : Y ⟶ X` such that `Lf^*E` is isomorphic in `D(𝒪_Y)` to a locally bounded complex of finite
locally free `𝒪_Y`-modules.

`X` is locally Noetherian, the base being locally Noetherian and `X` locally of finite type over
it, so `Stacks.Chow.exists_isEnvelope_sigma_of_isCompact_irreducibleComponents` supplies an
envelope `∐ W ⟶ X` whose summands are Noetherian — hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated —
with the resolution property and affine diagonal. Then
`Stacks.Chow.exists_isLocallyBoundedFiniteLocallyFree_iso_derivedPullback_sigma` represents
`Lf^*E`, which is clause (1) of the source.

Every hypothesis is a hypothesis of the source: the Chow situation, `X` locally of finite type
over its base, `E` perfect, and quasi-compactness of the irreducible components of `X`. Local
Noetherianity, the envelope, the summands' resolution property and affine diagonal, and the
complex are all derived.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_of_isCompact_irreducibleComponents
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    (hqc : ∀ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsCompact Z)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hE : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    HasDefinedChernClasses E
declarations.comment: clause (3): the irreducible components of X are quasi-compact.  The conclusion is the full one: the Chern classes of E are defined, i.e. there is an envelope f : Y -> X with Lf^*E isomorphic in D(O_Y) to a locally bounded complex of finite locally free O_Y-modules, which is Tag 0F9E (1). The hypotheses are exactly the source's: the base situation of Tag 02QL, X locally of finite type over its base, E perfect, and the irreducible components of X quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_compactSpace
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GUE] clause (4).** Let `(S, δ)` be the base situation of chapter 42, let `X`
be locally of finite type over `S` and quasi-compact, and let `E` be a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_X)`. Then the Chern classes of `E` are defined: there is an envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` such that
`Lf^*E` is isomorphic in `D(𝒪_Y)` to a locally bounded complex of finite locally free
`𝒪_Y`-modules.

`X` is Noetherian, the base being locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated, so
[Stacks, Tag 0GTU] gives an envelope `f : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` carrying an ample family of invertible
modules; `Y` is Noetherian because `f` is proper, has the resolution property by
`Stacks.Chow.hasResolutionProperty_of_isAmpleFamily_of_isNoetherian`, and therefore has affine
diagonal by the Noetherian case of [Stacks, Tag 0F8C]. Then
`Stacks.Chow.hasDefinedChernClasses_of_resolutionProperty_envelope` applies.

Every hypothesis is a hypothesis of the source: the Chow situation, `X` locally of finite type
over its base, perfectness of `E`, and quasi-compactness of `X`. Quasi-separatedness,
Noetherianity, the envelope, the ample family, the resolution property and the affine diagonal
are all derived.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasDefinedChernClasses_of_compactSpace
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    [CompactSpace X] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) E) :
    HasDefinedChernClasses E
declarations.comment: clause (4): X is quasi-compact.  The conclusion is the full one: the Chern classes of E are defined, i.e. there is an envelope f : Y ⟶ X with Lf^*E isomorphic in D(O_Y) to a locally bounded complex of finite locally free O_Y-modules, which is Tag 0F9E (1). The hypotheses are exactly the source's: the base situation of Tag 02QL, X locally of finite type over its base, E perfect, and X quasi-compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.powerSumClass_eq_of_envelopePresentation_modification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUF, the characteristic class clause, for the power sums.** Let `E` be an object of
`D(𝒪_X)` and let `H` be an envelope presentation of it, Stacks 0F9E (1), with presenting complex
`ℰ_Y^• = H.P` vanishing outside the degrees `w, …, w + k`. Let `a : W' ⟶ Y` be the lift to the
envelope of a modification of a morphism `g : W ⟶ X`, as produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsEnvelope.exists_properBirational_modification`, so that the morphism
`g' : W' ⟶ X` of the source is `a ≫ H.f`.

If a family `c` of Chow cohomology classes of `X` restricts along the envelope to the power sums
of the presenting complex — which is this repository's expression for `c` being the family of
power sum classes `P_p(E)` of `E`, and is the hypothesis of
`Stacks.Chow.eq_of_restriction_eq_powerSumClassComplexLocallyBounded` — then its restriction
along `g' = a ≫ H.f` is the power sum class of the pulled back complex `a^*ℰ_Y^•`:

  `res_{g'}(P_p(E)) = P_p(a^*ℰ_Y^•)`.

This is the source's chain
`res_{g'}(c_p(E)) = res_a(res_f(c_p(E))) = res_a(c_p(ℰ_Y^•)) = c_p(a^*ℰ_Y^•)`. See the
implementation notes of this file for what stands in for `c_p(E)`, why the power sums and not the
total Chern class, and what the statement does not deliver.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerSumClass_eq_of_envelopePresentation_modification (H : EnvelopePresentation E)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType H.f] {V : Scheme.{u}} (a : V ⟶ H.Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType a]
    (W : PowerSumClassRule C G (H.f ≫ sX)) (Wa : PowerSumClassRule C G (a ≫ (H.f ≫ sX)))
    (hW : PowerSumClassRule.IsBaseChangeCompatible C G (H.f ≫ sX) a hgys W Wa)
    (w : ℤ) (k : ℕ)
    (hflf : ∀ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
      Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := H.Y.ringCatSheaf)
        (H.P.X (w + (i : ℤ))))
    {c : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyComponent C G sX (p : ℤ)}
    (hc : ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      powerSumClassComplex C G (H.f ≫ sX) W H.P w k p)
    (p : ℕ) :
    chowCohomologyRestriction C G sX (a ≫ H.f) (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      powerSumClassComplex C G (a ≫ (H.f ≫ sX)) Wa
        (((Scheme.Modules.pullback a).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj H.P)
        w k p
declarations.comment: the characteristic class clause res(c_p(E)) = c_p(E^bullet), in the power sum reading P_p of Tag 0ESZ, for the lift a : W' -> Y of the modification to the envelope, so that res is along the g' = a . f of the tag. CARRIED: the family P_p(E) itself, which this repository does not construct -- it is taken as a family restricting along the envelope to P_p of the presenting complex, the hypothesis of the Tag 0GUD uniqueness theorems and the only expression here for 'c is the family of Chern classes of E'; the base change compatibility of the power sum data, which Stacks.Chow.PowerSumClassRule does not record; and the identification of a^*E_Y^. with a representative of L(g')^*E. NOT DELIVERED: the total Chern class reading, which needs the multiplicativity of the restriction map, Tag 0FE0 hence Tag 0B6Y, not formalized here; and the refinement that on an integral W' the pulled back complex has terms of constant rank. The geometric half of the tag is Stacks 0GUF on AlgebraicGeometry.IsEnvelope.exists_properBirational_modification

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chernCharacter_eq_of_envelopePresentation_modification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUF, the characteristic class clause, for the Chern character.** The Chern
character reading of `res(c_p(E)) = c_p(ℰ^•)`: for a family `c` of rational Chow cohomology
classes of `X` restricting along the envelope of a presentation to the components
`ch_p(ℰ_Y^•) = P_p(ℰ_Y^•)/p!`, the restriction of `c p` along `g' = a ≫ H.f` is `ch_p(a^*ℰ_Y^•)`.

The hypothesis is the one of `Stacks.Chow.eq_of_restriction_eq_chernCharacterComplexLocallyBounded`,
the Stacks 0GUD uniqueness theorem for the Chern character, read at a bounded window; see the
implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem chernCharacter_eq_of_envelopePresentation_modification (H : EnvelopePresentation E)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType H.f] {V : Scheme.{u}} (a : V ⟶ H.Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType a]
    (W : PowerSumClassRule C G (H.f ≫ sX)) (Wa : PowerSumClassRule C G (a ≫ (H.f ≫ sX)))
    (hW : PowerSumClassRule.IsBaseChangeCompatible C G (H.f ≫ sX) a hgys W Wa)
    (w : ℤ) (k : ℕ)
    (hflf : ∀ i ∈ Finset.range (k + 1),
      Stacks.FiniteLocallyFree.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := H.Y.ringCatSheaf)
        (H.P.X (w + (i : ℤ))))
    {c : ∀ p : ℕ, rationalChowCohomologyComponent C G sX (p : ℤ)}
    (hc : ∀ p : ℕ, rationalChowCohomologyRestriction C G sX H.f (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      chernCharacterComplexComponent C G (H.f ≫ sX) W H.P w k p)
    (p : ℕ) :
    rationalChowCohomologyRestriction C G sX (a ≫ H.f) (p : ℤ) hgys (c p) =
      chernCharacterComplexComponent C G (a ≫ (H.f ≫ sX)) Wa
        (((Scheme.Modules.pullback a).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj H.P)
        w k p
declarations.comment: the characteristic class clause res(c_p(E)) = c_p(E^bullet), in the Chern character reading ch_p = P_p/p! of Tag 0ESZ, for the lift a : W' -> Y of the modification to the envelope, so that res is along the g' = a . f of the tag. CARRIED: the family ch_p(E) itself, which this repository does not construct -- it is taken as a family restricting along the envelope to ch_p of the presenting complex, the hypothesis of the Tag 0GUD uniqueness theorem; the base change compatibility of the power sum data; and the identification of a^*E_Y^. with a representative of L(g')^*E. NOT DELIVERED: the total Chern class reading, which needs the multiplicativity of the restriction map, Tag 0FE0 hence Tag 0B6Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.exists_properBirational_res_perfectChernClass_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUF.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base and let `E` be an object of
`D(𝒪_X)` whose Chern classes are defined. For `g : W ⟶ X` locally of finite type with `W`
integral there are an integral scheme `W'` and a proper birational morphism `b : W' ⟶ W` such
that, for `g' = b ≫ g`, the derived pullback `L(g')^*E` is represented by a bounded complex `ℰ^•`
of finite locally free `𝒪_{W'}`-modules of constant ranks `ρ`, and

  `res_{g'}(c_p(E)) = c_p(ℰ^•)` in `A^p(W')` for every `p`,

where `c_p(E)` is the degree-`p` component of the total Chern class `c(E)` of Stacks 0F9E (2) and
`c_p(ℰ^•)` that of `∏_n c(ℰ^n)^{(-1)^n}`.

Perfectness of `E` is not used: the Chern classes being defined is the only hypothesis on `E`
the construction needs.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_properBirational_res_perfectChernClass_eq (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses E)
    {W : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral W] (g : W ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType g] :
    ∃ (W' : Scheme.{u}) (b : W' ⟶ W) (_ : IsIntegral W') (_ : IsProper b),
      IsBirational b ∧
      ∃ (ℰ : CochainComplex W'.Modules ℤ) (ρ : ℤ →₀ ℕ)
        (hρ : ∀ n,
          AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} (ℰ.X n) (ρ n)),
        (∃ lo hi : ℤ, ∀ n, (n < lo ∨ hi < n) → IsZero (ℰ.X n)) ∧
        Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          (b ≫ g).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj ℰ) ∧
        ∀ p : ℕ, chowCohomologyRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) sX (b ≫ g) (p : ℤ)
            (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
            (perfectChernClass C sX hE p) =
          complexChernBounded C ((b ≫ g) ≫ sX) ℰ ρ hρ p
declarations.comment: the full lemma: an integral W' with b : W' -> W proper birational, a bounded complex E^bullet of finite locally free O_{W'}-modules of constant ranks representing L(g')^*E for g' = b . g, and res_{g'}(c_p(E)) = c_p(E^bullet) in A^p(W') for the Chern classes c_p(E) of Tag 0F9E (2), Stacks.Chow.perfectChernClass. The perfectness of E is not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsEnvelope.exists_properBirational_modification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUF**, the modification and the factorization. Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be an envelope and
let `g : W ⟶ X` be a morphism with `W` integral. Then there are an integral scheme `W'`, a
proper birational morphism `b : W' ⟶ W` and a morphism `a : W' ⟶ Y` with `b ≫ g = a ≫ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsEnvelope.exists_properBirational_modification {X Y W : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : Y ⟶ X} (hf : IsEnvelope f) (g : W ⟶ X) [IsIntegral W] :
    ∃ (W' : Scheme.{u}) (b : W' ⟶ W) (a : W' ⟶ Y),
      IsIntegral W' ∧ IsProper b ∧ IsBirational b ∧ b ≫ g = a ≫ f
declarations.comment: existence of the proper birational modification factoring through an envelope

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassOfClosedCover_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUG, for the Chern classes.** In the situation of Stacks 0F9H, with `E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂}`
finite locally free of rank `< p` in degree `0`, let `q : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type,
let `X' = X'₁ ∪ X'₂` with `X'_j = X_j ×_X X'`, and let `E'₂ = (X'₂ ⟶ X₂)^* E₂`. Then `E'₂`
satisfies the hypotheses of Stacks 0F9H for this cover, and the class `c'_p(E'₂) ∈ A^p(X'₂ ⟶ X')`
constructed by Stacks 0F9H from `X' = X'₁ ∪ X'₂` and `E'₂` is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of
`c'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)`.

The restriction is a class for `X₂ ×_X X' ⟶ X'` whose source carries the structure morphism
`X₂ ×_X X' ⟶ X₂ ⟶ S`, while the class of Stacks 0F9H at `X'` carries `X'₂ ⟶ X' ⟶ S`; the two are
equal, and the restriction is read with the second one by `Stacks.Chow.bivariantTransport` along
the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClassOfClosedCover_baseChange
    (hres : ∃ M : (pullback i₁ i₂).Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E₂ ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (pullback i₁ i₂).Modules 0).obj M)) :
    localizedChernClassOfClosedCover C (q ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₁ q) (pullback.snd i₂ q)
        (range_pullbackSnd_union_range_pullbackSnd i₁ i₂ hcover q)
        (hasDefinedChernClasses_baseChange i₂ hE₂ q) p
        (exists_iso_single_baseChange i₁ i₂ p q hres) =
