      bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst i₂ q ≫ i₂ ≫ sX)
        (pullback.snd i₂ q ≫ q ≫ sX) (q ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₂ q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl q)
        (pullback.snd i₂ q) rfl (Iso.refl _) (Category.id_comp _) (p : ℤ)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
        (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl q (p : ℤ)
          (localizedChernClassOfClosedCover C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE₂ p hres))
declarations.comment: the classes c'_p: c'_p(E'₂) built from X' = X'₁ ∪ X'₂ and E'₂ is the restriction of c'_p(E₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUG, for the classes `P_p`.** In the situation of Stacks 0F9H, with `E₂` perfect
and `E₂|_{X₁ ∩ X₂}` zero, let `q : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type, let `X' = X'₁ ∪ X'₂` with
`X'_j = X_j ×_X X'`, and let `E'₂ = (X'₂ ⟶ X₂)^* E₂`. Then `E'₂` satisfies the hypotheses of
Stacks 0F9H for this cover, and the class `P'_p(E'₂) ∈ A^p(X'₂ ⟶ X')` constructed by Stacks 0F9H
from `X' = X'₁ ∪ X'₂` and `E'₂` is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of `P'_p(E₂) ∈ A^p(X₂ ⟶ X)`,
read with the structure morphism `X'₂ ⟶ X' ⟶ S` as in
`Stacks.Chow.localizedChernClassOfClosedCover_baseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover_baseChange
    (perfect : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := X₂.toRingedSpace) E₂)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (pullback.snd i₁ i₂).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E₂)) :
    localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover C (q ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₁ q) (pullback.snd i₂ q)
        (range_pullbackSnd_union_range_pullbackSnd i₁ i₂ hcover q)
        (hasDefinedChernClasses_baseChange i₂ hE₂ q) p (isPerfect_baseChange i₂ q perfect)
        (isZero_baseChange i₁ i₂ q hzero) =
      bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst i₂ q ≫ i₂ ≫ sX)
        (pullback.snd i₂ q ≫ q ≫ sX) (q ≫ sX) (pullback.snd i₂ q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl q)
        (pullback.snd i₂ q) rfl (Iso.refl _) (Category.id_comp _) (p : ℤ)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
        (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C (i₂ ≫ sX) sX i₂ rfl q (p : ℤ)
          (localizedPowerSumOfClosedCover C sX i₁ i₂ hcover hE₂ p perfect hzero))
declarations.comment: the classes P'_p: P'_p(E'₂) built from X' = X'₁ ∪ X'₂ and E'₂ is the restriction of P'_p(E₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.gysinAtInfinityClass_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUH.** Let `X` be locally of finite type over the base of chapter 42, let
`b : W ⟶ 𝐏¹_X` be proper and an isomorphism over `𝐀¹_X`, and let `C ∈ A⁰(W_∞ ⟶ X)` be the class
of Stacks 0F9J. Let `q : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type and let
`b' : W' = W ×_{𝐏¹_X} 𝐏¹_{X'} ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` be the base change of `b`, with fibre at infinity
`i'_∞ : W'_∞ ⟶ W'` (the base change of `i_∞`). Then `b'` is again proper and an isomorphism over
`𝐀¹_{X'}`, and the class `C' ∈ A⁰(W'_∞ ⟶ X')` constructed as in Stacks 0F9J using `b'` is the
restriction `res(C)` of Remark 0F9Z.

The restriction is a class for the chosen fibre product `W_∞ ×_X X' ⟶ X'`; it is read as a class
for `W'_∞ ⟶ X'` along the canonical identification `W_∞ ×_X X' ≅ W'_∞` over `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinAtInfinityClass_baseChange
    (hA : IsIso (pullback.snd b (projectiveLineAffineChart f))) :
    haveI := hA
    gysinAtInfinityClass C (q ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b q) inferInstance =
      bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
        (pullback.fst (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) q ≫
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f))
        (modificationProjectionAtInfinity (q ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b q) ≫ (q ≫ f))
        (q ≫ f) (pullback.snd (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f) f
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) rfl q)
        (modificationProjectionAtInfinity (q ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b q)) rfl
        (baseChangedInfinityIso f b q) (baseChangedInfinityIso_hom_comp f b q) 0
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
        (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f) f
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) rfl q 0 (gysinAtInfinityClass C f b hA))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinity_baseChange_cap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUH, on cap operations**, conditional on the construction of Stacks 0F9J for both
modifications and its compatibility with base change.

For every test scheme `g : T ⟶ X'` locally of finite type, `C' ∩ α = C ∩ α` after the canonical
identification `W_∞ ×_X T ≅ W'_∞ ×_{X'} T` of the two base changes of the fibre at infinity. This
is the form the source's proof produces; the equality of bivariant classes asserted by the tag is
`Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinity_eq_bivariantTransport_bivariantRestriction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinAtInfinity_baseChange_cap
    (hlift : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (q ≫ f)) k),
      P'.lift g k α =
        chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
          (modificationBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
          (modificationBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' η hη g)
          (modificationBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' η hη g) (k + 1)
          (P.lift (g ≫ q) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc g q f).symm k α)))
    (hgysinStep : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (β : chowGroup C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q)) (k + 1)),
      P'.gysinStep g k
          (chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
            (modificationBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
            (modificationBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' η hη g)
            (modificationBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' η hη g) (k + 1) β) =
        chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
          (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
          (modificationInfinityBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' θ hθ g)
          (modificationInfinityBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' θ hθ g) k
          (P.gysinStep (g ≫ q) k β))
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
    (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (q ≫ f)) k) :
    D'.bivariantClass.cap g k α =
      chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
        (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
        (modificationInfinityBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' θ hθ g)
        (modificationInfinityBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' θ hθ g) (k - 0)
        (D.bivariantClass.cap (g ≫ q) k
          (chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc g q f).symm k α))
declarations.comment: on cap operations: given the construction of Stacks 0F9J as a presentation of each cap operation by a lift and a Gysin step, and the compatibility of each of those two factors with the base change (the source's `a similar statement holds for flat pullback and i_infty^*`), the class constructed from the base-changed modification caps as the original one does

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinity_eq_bivariantTransport_bivariantRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUH.** In the setting of Stacks 0F9J let `q : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type and
let `b' : W' ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` and `i'_∞ : W'_∞ ⟶ W'` be the base changes of `b` and `i_∞`. Then the
class `C' ∈ A⁰(W'_∞ ⟶ X')` constructed as in Stacks 0F9J using `b'` is the restriction (Remark
0F9Z) of `C`: it equals `Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction` of `C` along `q`, carried along the
identification `W_∞ ×_X X' ≅ W'_∞` by `Stacks.Chow.bivariantTransport`.

The transport is needed only because `Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction` produces a class for the
chosen fibre product `W_∞ ×_X X' ⟶ X'`, whereas `C'` is a class for `W'_∞ ⟶ X'`; the tag
identifies the two silently. Both constructions are the library's own.

The hypotheses are the base-change witnesses `η`, `θ`, the construction of Stacks 0F9J for both
modifications, and the compatibility of each of its two factors with the base change; see the
implementation notes of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Chow.GysinAtInfinityBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinAtInfinity_eq_bivariantTransport_bivariantRestriction
    (hgys : G.IsNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso)
    (hlift : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (α : chowGroup C (g ≫ (q ≫ f)) k),
      P'.lift g k α =
        chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
          (modificationBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
          (modificationBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' η hη g)
          (modificationBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' η hη g) (k + 1)
          (P.lift (g ≫ q) k (chowGroupCongr C (Category.assoc g q f).symm k α)))
    (hgysinStep : ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ X') [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (k : ℤ)
        (β : chowGroup C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q)) (k + 1)),
      P'.gysinStep g k
          (chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
            (modificationBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
            (modificationBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' η hη g)
            (modificationBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' η hη g) (k + 1) β) =
        chowPushforwardOfIso C (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver f b (g ≫ q))
          (modificationInfinityBaseChangeOver (q ≫ f) b' g)
          (modificationInfinityBaseChangeComparison C f b q b' θ hθ g)
          (modificationInfinityBaseChangeComparison_comp_base C f b q b' θ hθ g) k
          (P.gysinStep (g ≫ q) k β)) :
    D'.bivariantClass =
      bivariantTransport C G
        (pullback.fst (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) q ≫
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f))
        (modificationProjectionAtInfinity (q ≫ f) b' ≫ (q ≫ f)) (q ≫ f)
        (pullback.snd (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f) f
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) rfl q)
        (modificationProjectionAtInfinity (q ≫ f) b') rfl θ hθ 0 hgys
        (bivariantRestriction C G (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f) f
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) rfl q 0 hgys D.bivariantClass)
declarations.comment: given the construction of Stacks 0F9J as a presentation of each cap operation by a lift and a Gysin step, and the compatibility of each of those two factors with the base change (the source's `a similar statement holds for flat pullback and i_infty^*`), together with the isomorphism case of Stacks 02TA for the Gysin system that Stacks 0F9Z needs

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.gysinAtInfinityClass_restrictedModification_eq_bivariantRestriction
declarations.doc:
In the setting of Stacks 0F9J let `q : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type and let
`b' : W' = W ×_{𝐏¹_X} 𝐏¹_{X'} ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` and `i'_∞ : W'_∞ ⟶ W'` be the base changes of `b` and
`i_∞` (`Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.baseChangedModification`). Then the class
`C' ∈ A⁰(W'_∞ ⟶ X')` of Stacks 0F9J for `b'` is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of `C`: it equals
`Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction` of `C` along `q`, carried along the canonical identification
`W_∞ ×_X X' ≅ W'_∞` by `Stacks.Chow.bivariantTransport`.
declarations.statement:
theorem gysinAtInfinityClass_restrictedModification_eq_bivariantRestriction :
    gysinAtInfinityClass C (q ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b q)
        (isIso_restrictedModification_affineChart f b q hA) =
      bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
        (pullback.fst (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) q ≫
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f))
        (modificationProjectionAtInfinity (q ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b q) ≫ (q ≫ f))
        (q ≫ f) (pullback.snd (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f) f
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) rfl q)
        (modificationProjectionAtInfinity (q ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b q)) rfl
        (restrictedModificationInfinityIso f b q)
        (restrictedModificationInfinityIso_hom_projection f b q) 0
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
        (bivariantRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C)
          (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b ≫ f) f (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b) rfl
          q 0 (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
          (gysinAtInfinityClass C f b hA))
declarations.comment: the class C' of Lemma 0F9J for the base change b' is the restriction of C

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.localizedChernClassAtInfinity_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUI, for the Chern classes.** In the situation of Stacks 0F9K, with `Q|_T` finite
locally free of rank `< p` in degree `0`, let `q : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism locally of finite type.
Let `Z' = Z ×_X X'`, `b' : W' = W ×_{𝐏¹_X} 𝐏¹_{X'} ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` and `T' = T ×_{W_∞} W'_∞ ⊆ W'_∞`
be the base changes of `Z`, `b` and `T`, and let `Q' = (W' ⟶ W)^*Q`. Then `b'`, `Q'` and `T'`
satisfy the assumptions of Stacks 0F9K, and the class `c'_p(Q') ∈ A^p(Z' ⟶ X')` constructed as in
Stacks 0F9K using `b'`, `Q'` and `T'` is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of
`c'_p(Q) ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`.

The restriction is a class for `Z' ⟶ X'` whose source carries the structure morphism
`Z' ⟶ Z ⟶ S`, while the class constructed at `X'` carries `Z' ⟶ X' ⟶ S`; the two are equal, and
the restriction is read with the second one by `Stacks.Chow.bivariantTransport` along the
identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChernClassAtInfinity_baseChange
    (hV : ∀ w, (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b).base w ∉ Set.range jZ.base →
      w ∈ Set.range iV.base)
    (hres : RestrictionIsLocallyFreeOfRankLT f b iV Q p) :
    localizedChernClassAtInfinity C (haveI := hA; isIso_baseChangedModification_chart f b q)
        (pullback.snd jZ q)
        (hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedPullback (pullback.fst b (familyBaseChange f q)) hQ)
        (baseChange_mem_range f b jZ iV q hV)
        (restrictionIsLocallyFreeOfRankLT_baseChange f b iV q hres) =
      bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst jZ q ≫ jZ ≫ f)
        (pullback.snd jZ q ≫ q ≫ f) (q ≫ f) (pullback.snd jZ q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (jZ ≫ f) f jZ rfl q) (pullback.snd jZ q) rfl
        (Iso.refl _) (Category.id_comp _) (p : ℤ)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
        (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C (jZ ≫ f) f jZ rfl q (p : ℤ)
          (localizedChernClassAtInfinity C hA jZ hQ hV hres))
declarations.comment: the classes c'_p: c'_p(Q') built as in Stacks 0F9K from b', Q' and T' is the restriction of c'_p(Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.GysinAtInfinity.localizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUI, for the classes `P_p`.** In the situation of Stacks 0F9K, with `Q|_T` zero,
let `q : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism locally of finite type. Let `Z' = Z ×_X X'`,
`b' : W' = W ×_{𝐏¹_X} 𝐏¹_{X'} ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` and `T' = T ×_{W_∞} W'_∞ ⊆ W'_∞` be the base changes of
`Z`, `b` and `T`, and let `Q' = (W' ⟶ W)^*Q`. Then `b'`, `Q'` and `T'` satisfy the assumptions of
Stacks 0F9K, and the class `P'_p(Q') ∈ A^p(Z' ⟶ X')` constructed as in Stacks 0F9K using `b'`,
`Q'` and `T'` is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of `P'_p(Q) ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`, read with the structure
morphism `Z' ⟶ X' ⟶ S` as in `localizedChernClassAtInfinity_baseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity_baseChange
    (perfect : RingedSpace.IsPerfect.{u, u + 1} (X := W.toRingedSpace) Q)
    (hV : ∀ w, (modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b).base w ∉ Set.range jZ.base →
      w ∈ Set.range iV.base)
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      iV.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj (restrictionAtInfinity f b Q))) :
    localizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity C (haveI := hA; isIso_baseChangedModification_chart f b q)
        (pullback.snd jZ q)
        (hasDefinedChernClasses_derivedPullback (pullback.fst b (familyBaseChange f q)) hQ)
        (RingedSpace.KFlatDerivedPullback.isPerfect_derivedPullback _ Q perfect)
        (baseChange_mem_range f b jZ iV q hV) (isZero_restriction_baseChange f b iV q hzero)
        (p := p) =
      bivariantTransport C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.fst jZ q ≫ jZ ≫ f)
        (pullback.snd jZ q ≫ q ≫ f) (q ≫ f) (pullback.snd jZ q)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (jZ ≫ f) f jZ rfl q) (pullback.snd jZ q) rfl
        (Iso.refl _) (Category.id_comp _) (p : ℤ)
        (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
        (bivariantRestrictionOfInvertible C (jZ ≫ f) f jZ rfl q (p : ℤ)
          (localizedPowerSumClassAtInfinity C hA jZ hQ perfect hV hzero (p := p)))
declarations.comment: the classes P'_p: P'_p(Q') built as in Stacks 0F9K from b', Q' and T' is the restriction of P'_p(Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction_modificationPowerSum
declarations.doc:
In the setting of Stacks 0F9K let `h : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type, let
`b' : W' = W ×_{𝐏¹_X} 𝐏¹_{X'} ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` and `Z' = Z ×_X X'` be the base changes, and set
`Q' = (W' ⟶ W)^* Q`. Then the class `P'_p(Q') ∈ A^p(Z' ⟶ X')` constructed as in Stacks 0F9K from
`b'`, `Q'` and any closed `T' ⊆ W'_∞` with the properties used there (for instance the base change
of `T`) is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of `P'_p(Q) ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestriction_modificationPowerSum
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b w ∉ Set.range z → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hT' : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity (h ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b h) w ∉
      Set.range (pullback.snd z h) → w ∈ Set.range t')
    (hzero : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q))
    (hzero' : IsZero ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
      (t' ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity (h ≫ f)
        (baseChangedModification f b h)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
      ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (pullback.fst b (familyBaseChange f h)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q))) :
    bivariantClassCongrBase C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.snd z h)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (z ≫ f) f z rfl h).symm rfl
        (hv := pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (z ≫ f) f z rfl h) (hv' := rfl) p
        (bivariantRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (z ≫ f) f z rfl h p
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
          (modificationPowerSum C f b hA z t hQ p hT hzero)) =
      modificationPowerSum C (h ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b h)
        (isIso_restrictedModification_affineChart f b h hA) (pullback.snd z h) t'
        (hQ.derivedPullback (pullback.fst b (familyBaseChange f h))) p hT' hzero'
declarations.comment: the case of P'_p: the class P'_p(Q') of Lemma 0F9K for the base change is the restriction of P'_p(Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.bivariantRestriction_modificationChernClass
declarations.doc:
In the setting of Stacks 0F9K let `h : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type, let
`b' : W' = W ×_{𝐏¹_X} 𝐏¹_{X'} ⟶ 𝐏¹_{X'}` and `Z' = Z ×_X X'` be the base changes, and set
`Q' = (W' ⟶ W)^* Q`. Then the class `c'_p(Q') ∈ A^p(Z' ⟶ X')` constructed as in Stacks 0F9K from
`b'`, `Q'` and any closed `T' ⊆ W'_∞` with the properties used there (for instance the base change
of `T`) is the restriction (Remark 0F9Z) of `c'_p(Q) ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bivariantRestriction_modificationChernClass
    (hT : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity f b w ∉ Set.range z → w ∈ Set.range t)
    (hT' : ∀ w, modificationProjectionAtInfinity (h ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b h) w ∉
      Set.range (pullback.snd z h) → w ∈ Set.range t')
    (hrank : ∃ M : T.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (t ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity f b).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M))
    (hrank' : ∃ M : T'.Modules, IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLT M p ∧
      Nonempty ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
        (t' ≫ modificationInclusionAtInfinity (h ≫ f)
          (baseChangedModification f b h)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj
        ((Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPullback
          (pullback.fst b (familyBaseChange f h)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Q) ≅
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)) :
    bivariantClassCongrBase C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (pullback.snd z h)
        (pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (z ≫ f) f z rfl h).symm rfl
        (hv := pullbackSnd_comp_structureMorphism_eq C (z ≫ f) f z rfl h) (hv' := rfl) p
        (bivariantRestriction C (gysinSystemOfInvertible C) (z ≫ f) f z rfl h p
          (gysinSystemOfInvertible_isNaturalUnderBaseChangeIso C)
          (modificationChernClass C f b hA z t hQ p hT hrank)) =
      modificationChernClass C (h ≫ f) (baseChangedModification f b h)
        (isIso_restrictedModification_affineChart f b h hA) (pullback.snd z h) t'
        (hQ.derivedPullback (pullback.fst b (familyBaseChange f h))) p hT' hrank'
declarations.comment: the case of c'_p: the class c'_p(Q') of Lemma 0F9K for the base change is the restriction of c'_p(Q)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation
declarations.doc:
The standing situation for the localized Chern classes and localized Chern character components
of chapter 42 of the Stacks Project: a scheme locally of finite type over the base, a closed
subscheme, a perfect object of the derived category of the ambient scheme which away from the
closed subscheme is zero or a finite locally free module of rank below the chosen degree (the data
`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedChernData`), and one of the four finiteness alternatives of the source.
declarations.statement: structure LocalizedSituation extends LocalizedChernData.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedChernSituation
declarations.doc:
The standing situation for the localized Chern classes and localized Chern character
components of chapter 42 of the Stacks Project: a scheme locally of finite type over the base, a
closed subscheme, a perfect object of the derived category of the ambient scheme which away from
the closed subscheme is zero or a finite locally free module of rank below the chosen degree, and
one of four finiteness alternatives.
declarations.statement: structure LocalizedChernSituation

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedChernData.localizedPowerSum
declarations.doc:
**The localized class `P_p(Z ⟶ X, E) ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)` when the Chern classes of `E` are
defined** (Remark 0GUK), when `E|_{X ∖ Z}` is zero, for every degree `p`: the unique class whose
restriction along the envelope `g : Y ⟶ X` of a presentation of `E` by a locally bounded complex of
finite locally free modules is the class `P_p(Z ×_X Y ⟶ Y, Lg^*E)` of Stacks 0FB2 (Stacks 0GUC).
In Situation 0GUJ it is the class of Stacks 0FB2
(`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.localizedPowerSum_toLocalizedChernData`).
declarations.statement:
def localizedPowerSum (hE : HasDefinedChernClasses D.E) (h : D.IsZeroOnComplement) (p : ℕ) :
    BivariantClass D.base (gysinSystemOfInvertible D.base) (D.i ≫ D.a) D.a D.i rfl p
declarations.comment: P_p(Z → X, E) in A^p(Z → X) for E perfect with E|_{X ∖ Z} zero whose Chern classes are defined, by descent (0GUC) of the classes of 0FB2 along an envelope; in Situation 0GUJ it is the class of 0FB2 (localizedPowerSum_toLocalizedChernData)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedChernData.localizedChern
declarations.doc:
**The localized Chern class `c_p(Z ⟶ X, E) ∈ A^p(Z ⟶ X)` when the Chern classes of `E` are
defined** (Remark 0GUK), when `E|_{X ∖ Z}` is finite locally free of rank `< p` in degree `0`: the
unique class whose restriction along the envelope `g : Y ⟶ X` of a presentation of `E` is the class
`c_p(Z ×_X Y ⟶ Y, Lg^*E)` of Stacks 0FB2 (Stacks 0GUC). In Situation 0GUJ it is the class of
Stacks 0FB2 (`Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.localizedChern_toLocalizedChernData`).
declarations.comment: c_p(Z → X, E) in A^p(Z → X) for E perfect with E|_{X ∖ Z} finite locally free of rank < p in degree 0 whose Chern classes are defined, by descent (0GUC) of the classes of 0FB2 along an envelope; in Situation 0GUJ it is the class of 0FB2 (localizedChern_toLocalizedChernData)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedChernData.localizedChernChar
declarations.doc:
**The localized Chern character `ch(Z ⟶ X, E) = ∑_p P_p(Z ⟶ X, E)/p!` when the Chern classes
of `E` are defined** (Definition 0FB5 (1) and Remark 0GUK), when `E|_{X ∖ Z}` is zero, as an
element of `∏_{p ≥ 0} A^p(Z ⟶ X) ⊗ 𝐐`.
declarations.comment: the localized Chern character ch(Z → X, E) = Σ_p P_p(Z → X, E)/p! of 0FB5 (1) for E perfect with E|_{X ∖ Z} zero whose Chern classes are defined

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.localizedPowerSum_toLocalizedChernData
declarations.doc:
**In Situation 0GUJ the class of Remark 0GUK is the class `P_p(Z ⟶ X, E)` of Stacks 0FB2**:
both restrict to `P_p(Z ×_X Y ⟶ Y, Lg^*E)` along an envelope (Stacks 0FB3), and the uniqueness
in Stacks 0GUC applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedPowerSum_toLocalizedChernData (h : S.IsZeroOnComplement) (p : ℕ) :
    S.toLocalizedChernData.localizedPowerSum S.hasDefinedChernClasses_E h p =
      S.localizedPowerSum h p
declarations.comment: the extension agrees with the definition: in Situation 0GUJ the class P_p(Z → X, E) of the remark is the class of 0FB2

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.localizedChern_toLocalizedChernData
declarations.doc:
**In Situation 0GUJ the class of Remark 0GUK is the class `c_p(Z ⟶ X, E)` of Stacks 0FB2**,
as `Stacks.Chow.LocalizedSituation.localizedPowerSum_toLocalizedChernData`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedChern_toLocalizedChernData (h : S.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLTOnComplement) :
    S.toLocalizedChernData.localizedChern S.hasDefinedChernClasses_E h =
      S.localizedChern h
declarations.comment: the extension agrees with the definition: in Situation 0GUJ the class c_p(Z → X, E) of the remark is the class of 0FB2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_integralSchemeCover_finiteEtaleOverDenseOpen_and_refining
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GUL.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over a scheme `S` such that `|X|` has finitely many irreducible components. Then

1. there is a surjective integral morphism to `X` from the presheaf represented by an object of
   the big fppf site — a scheme over `S` — which is finite étale over a quasi-compact open
   subspace of `X` with dense point set, and
2. given a surjective étale morphism `p : V ⟶ X` from an algebraic space, such a cover can be
   chosen so that it factors through `p` on a representable open subspace neighbourhood of
   every one of its points.

Clause (2) for a cover `p` is reduced to a chart `c : h_{V₀} ⟶ V`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsIntegralSchemeCoverRefining_of_comp_chart`); for the chart
`c ≫ p` the induction gives a cover étale over a dense open
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsIntegralSchemeCoverEtaleRefining_of_isEtale`), which is upgraded
to one finite étale over a quasi-compact dense open
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsIntegralSchemeCoverRefining_of_etaleRefining`). Clause (1) is
clause (2) at the identity of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integralSchemeCover_finiteEtaleOverDenseOpen_and_refining
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (hcomp : (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite) :
    ExistsIntegralSchemeCoverFiniteEtaleOverDenseOpen B S hS X ∧
      ∀ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V →
        ∀ p : V ⟶ X, IsSurjective B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS p →
          ExistsIntegralSchemeCoverRefining B S hS p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLimit_finite_finitePresentation_fixedOnOpen
declarations.doc:
An integral morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, which is finite and of finite presentation over a quasi-compact open subspace `V`
of `Y` (that is, `f⁻¹(V) = X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is), is the limit of a directed inverse system, indexed by
a nonempty directed preorder in the universe of the schemes, of algebraic spaces `D i` with
morphisms `t i : D i ⟶ Y` finite and of finite presentation, the limiting cone `p` having vertex
`X` and lying over `Y`; and for every `i` the square formed by `X ×_Y V ⟶ X ⟶ D i`, `X ×_Y V ⟶ V`,
`t i` and `V ⟶ Y` is cartesian, that is `f⁻¹(V) ⟶ f_i⁻¹(V)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_finite_finitePresentation_fixedOnOpen
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (V : Subfunctor Y) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS V.toFunctor)
    (hfVfinite : IsFinite B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι))
    (hfVfp : IsFinitePresentation B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι)) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirectedOrder I)
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
      (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D) (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y),
      (∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsFinite B S hS (t.app i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsFinitePresentation B S hS (t.app i)) ∧
      (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X p)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsPullback (pullback.fst f V.ι ≫ p.app i) (pullback.snd f V.ι) (t.app i) V.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteSchemeCover_finiteEtaleOverDenseOpen_and_refining
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GUN.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over a scheme `S` such that `|X|` has finitely many irreducible components. Then

1. there is a surjective, finite and finitely presented morphism `f : h_Y ⟶ X` from the
   presheaf represented by an object `Y` of the big fppf site — a scheme over `S` — and a
   quasi-compact open subspace `U ⊆ X` with dense point set over which `f` is finite étale, and
2. given a surjective étale morphism `p : V ⟶ X` from an algebraic space, such a cover can be
   chosen so that it factors through `p` on a representable open subspace neighbourhood of
   every one of its points.

Clause (2) for `p` is reduced to an affine chart `h_A ⟶ V`, where it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteSchemeCover_refining_of_isAffine`; clause (1) is clause (2)
at the identity of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteSchemeCover_finiteEtaleOverDenseOpen_and_refining
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (hcomp : (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite) :
    (∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X) (U : Subfunctor X),
      IsFiniteSchemeCoverFiniteEtaleOverDenseOpen B S hS Y f U) ∧
    ∀ (V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS V →
      ∀ p : V ⟶ X, IsSurjective B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS p →
        ∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X) (U : Subfunctor X),
          IsFiniteSchemeCoverFiniteEtaleOverDenseOpen B S hS Y f U ∧
            FactorsZariskiLocallyThrough B S hS p Y f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteEtaleCoverStratification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUP.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space. There are
`t ≥ 0` and closed subspaces `X ⊇ Z₀ ⊇ Z₁ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ Z_t = ∅` with each `Z_i ⟶ X` of finite
presentation and `Z₀ ⊆ X` a thickening, such that for each `i < t` there is a scheme `Y_i` and a
surjective, finite and finitely presented morphism `Y_i ⟶ Z_i` which is finite étale over the
open subspace `Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1}` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFiniteEtaleCoverStep`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteEtaleCoverStratification (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (Z : ℕ → Subfunctor X),
      (∀ i, IsClosedSubspace B S hS (Z i)) ∧ (∀ i, IsFinitePresentation B S hS (Z i).ι) ∧
      (∀ i, Z (i + 1) ≤ Z i) ∧ IsThickening B S hS ⟨X, hX⟩ (Z 0) ∧
      IsEmpty (points B S hS (Z t).toFunctor) ∧
      ∀ i < t, IsFiniteEtaleCoverStep B S hS (Z i) (Z (i + 1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isRelativelyAmple_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUQ.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces is quasi-affine if and only if
the structure sheaf `𝒪_X` is `f`-relatively ample.

Quasi-affineness of Stacks 03WL is identified with its representable form by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_tfae_of_isAlgebraicSpace`, and that form quantifies
over exactly the cartesian squares relative ampleness does; on each of them the equivalence is
the scheme-level Stacks 0891 in the shape
`Stacks.AmplePullback.isRelativelyAmple_iff_isQuasiAffineHom_of_iso_unitModule`, applied through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.baseChangeUnitModuleIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_iff_isRelativelyAmple_unit {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom ↔
      IsRelativelyAmple B S hS f
        (SheafOfModules.unit
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUS.** An algebraic space has the *resolution property* when every
quasi-coherent module of finite type on it is a quotient of a finite locally free module.
declarations.statement:
class HasResolutionProperty (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_cover_hasResolutionProperty_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme with `Y` quasi-compact, and
let `L` be an `f`-ample module on `X`.  Then there is an affine scheme `V` over the base with a
surjective étale morphism `g` to `Y`, and a cartesian square presenting the fibre product
`V ×_Y X` as a scheme `U`, such that the base change of `L` to `U` is ample and `U` has the
resolution property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_etale_cover_hasResolutionProperty_of_isRelativelyAmple
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y} {L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2}
    (hL : IsRelativelyAmple B S hS f L) (hY : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.1),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf g ∧
        IsEtale B S hS g ∧
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : U ⟶ V) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.1),
          IsPullback p (yoneda.map q) f.hom g ∧
            (∃ hinv : Stacks.Ample.IsInvertibleModule ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
                (baseChangeModule B S hS L U p),
              @Stacks.Ample.IsAmple ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
                (baseChangeModule B S hS L U p) hinv) ∧
            _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
declarations.comment:
the first step of the proof: an affine surjective étale chart of the target over
which the scheme fibre product carries an ample module and has the resolution property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isRelativelyAmple
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUT.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` such
that `Y` is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and has the resolution property, and such that there
is an `f`-ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L`.  Then `X` has the resolution property.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteLocallyFree_epi_of_isRelativelyAmple` packaged as
the class `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasResolutionProperty` of Stacks 0GUS.

The hypotheses are exactly the tag's.  `hLinv` is part of hypothesis (2): Stacks 0D31 defines an
`f`-ample module to be invertible, and in this tree `IsRelativelyAmple` records invertibility only
of the base changes of `L` to the scheme charts, so it is carried separately.  `hZ` is needed only
to state `IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated`, this tree's spelling of quasi-separatedness of `Y`.
Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `f` are *derived* from `hL` by Stacks 0D34 and 03KK,
not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isRelativelyAmple (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (L : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hLinv : IsInvertibleModule X L) (hL : IsRelativelyAmple B S hS f L)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (hYres : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteLocallyFree_modulePullback_hom_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**The step of the proof of Stacks 0GUU which produces the finite locally free module on the
source.**  In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteLocallyFree_epi_submodule_modulePushforward` the pullback
`f^*ℰ` is again finite locally free, and the map `ℰ ⟶ f_*ℱ` — the epimorphism onto the submodule
`𝒢` followed by its inclusion — transposes along `f^* ⊣ f_*` to a map `ψ : f^*ℰ ⟶ ℱ`.

This is the source's sentence *"Then the corresponding maps `f^*ℰ_i ⊗ ℒ^{⊗ n_i} → ℱ` are going to
be jointly surjective"* at `ℒ = 𝒪_X`, up to that surjectivity: the module and the map exist, and
`ψ` is characterized by its transpose being `φ ≫ 𝒢.ι`.  Finite local freeness of `f^*ℰ` is
Stacks 03DL under pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteLocallyFree_modulePullback_hom_of_hasResolutionProperty
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hfqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (hYres : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (V : SmallEtale B S hS Y.1) (hV : IsAffine (chartScheme V))
    (σ : α → ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F).val.obj (op V)) :
    ∃ (G : ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F).Submodule)
      (E : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)
      (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite E)
      (φ : E ⟶ G.toSheafOfModules), Epi φ ∧ (∀ x ∈ s, σ x ∈ G.obj (op V)) ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite ((modulePullback B S hS f).obj E) ∧
        ∃ ψ : (modulePullback B S hS f).obj E ⟶ F,
          (modulePullbackAdjunction B S hS f).homEquiv E F ψ = φ ≫ G.ι
declarations.comment:
the step of the proof producing the finite locally free module on the target and
its transpose on the source, for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism: the sections of the
direct image over an affine chart of the target lie in the image submodule

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**The reduction of the affine case of Stacks 0GUU to its quasi-affine case.**  An affine
morphism of algebraic spaces is quasi-affine: its base change to an affine test object is
represented by an affine, hence quasi-affine, scheme.

This is why Stacks 0GUU may assume `f` quasi-affine throughout: its two hypotheses, affine and
quasi-affine, are one hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiAffineHom_of_isAffineHom {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f) : IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f
declarations.comment:
the reduction of the hypothesis: the affine case of the statement is its
quasi-affine case, an affine morphism of algebraic spaces being quasi-affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_etale_cover_hasResolutionProperty_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**The chart step of the proof of Stacks 0GUU.** For `f : X ⟶ Y` a
quasi-affine morphism of algebraic spaces with `Y` quasi-compact there are an affine scheme `V`
over the base with a surjective étale morphism to `Y` and a cartesian square presenting the
fibre product `V ×_Y X` as a scheme `U` with the resolution property.

This is the source's sentence *"Choose an affine scheme `V` and a surjective étale morphism
`V → Y`.  Set `U = V ×_Y X`"*, with the properties of `U` that the rest of the proof reads off
it: `𝒪_U` is ample on `U` because `f` is quasi-affine and `V` is affine (Stacks 0GUQ and
Stacks 01VK), so `U` has the resolution property by Stacks 0F87.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_etale_cover_hasResolutionProperty_of_isQuasiAffineHom
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (g : yoneda.obj V ⟶ Y.1),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf g ∧
        IsEtale B S hS g ∧
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : U ⟶ V) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.1),
          IsPullback p (yoneda.map q) f.hom g ∧
            _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.HasResolutionProperty
              ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U)
declarations.comment:
the chart step of the proof: an affine surjective étale chart of the target over
which the scheme fibre product has the resolution property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUU, the quasi-affine case.**  For `f : X ⟶ Y` a quasi-affine morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` with `Y` quasi-compact, quasi-separated and carrying the resolution property, `X`
has the resolution property.

This is the source's reduction: by Stacks 0GUQ the structure sheaf of `X` is `f`-ample
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativelyAmple_unit_of_isQuasiAffineHom`) and invertible
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInvertibleModule_unit`), so this is Stacks 0GUT,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isRelativelyAmple`, at `L = 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isQuasiAffineHom (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (hYres : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: the quasi-affine case; the affine case is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isAffineHom`, and the two together are the tag's "affine or quasi-affine"

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUU, the affine case.**  For `f : X ⟶ Y` an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` with `Y` quasi-compact, quasi-separated and carrying the resolution property, `X` has the
resolution property.

An affine morphism of algebraic spaces is quasi-affine
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiAffineHom_of_isAffineHom`), so this is the quasi-affine case.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isAffineHom (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (hYres : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2
declarations.comment: the affine case; the quasi-affine case is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_source_of_isQuasiAffineHom`, and the two together are the tag's "affine or quasi-affine"

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_of_isSurjective_isFiniteLocallyFree_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUV, with no further input.**  For `f : X ⟶ Y` a surjective finite locally free
morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, if `X` has the resolution property then so does
`Y`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_of_isSurjective_isFiniteLocallyFree_of_dualTwist`
with its hypothesis `hdual` discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.directImageDualDescent`, which
is proved outright for every morphism of algebraic spaces.  Its hypotheses are therefore exactly
the tag's: `f` surjective, `f` finite locally free, and `X` having the resolution property.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_of_isSurjective_isFiniteLocallyFree_unconditional (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f.hom) (hflf : IsFiniteLocallyFree B S hS f)
    (hX : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isBlowupAlong_isIso_strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp_of_isProper_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ A` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `U ⊆ A` be an open subspace.
Assume that `A` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, that `U` is quasi-compact, that `f` is proper
and that `f⁻¹(U) ⟶ U` (the restriction `X ×_A U ⟶ U`) is an isomorphism. Then there is a
`U`-admissible blowup `b : A' ⟶ A` -- the blowup of `A` in a closed subspace `Z` of finite
presentation whose points avoid those of `U` -- such that the strict transform of `X` with
respect to `b` maps isomorphically to `A'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isBlowupAlong_isIso_strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp_of_isProper_unconditional
    {A X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ A) (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS A.1)
    (hAqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS A.1)
    (hAqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal A.1)
    (hUqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS U.1.toFunctor)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hiso : IsIso (pullback.snd f.hom U.1.ι)) :
    ∃ (A' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (b : A' ⟶ A) (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS A.1),
      IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z.1.ι ∧
        Disjoint (subspacePointSet B S hS A.1 U.1) (subspacePointSet B S hS A.1 Z.1) ∧
          IsBlowupAlong B S hS Z b ∧
            IsIso (strictTransformSpaceToBlowUp B S hS f b (Z.1.preimage b.hom)).hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_isSurjective_isEtale_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUY, the existence of the chart `V → X`.** A quasi-compact algebraic space over
`S` admits a surjective étale morphism from an affine scheme of the site, surjectivity being
the point-set notion of Stacks 03ME.

This is the parenthetical claim of the source that such a chart exists: Stacks 03H6 gives a
chart whose every represented base change is a surjective morphism of schemes, and Stacks
03H5 identifies that with surjectivity on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_isSurjective_isEtale_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hX : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.1),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
        IsSurjective B S hS φ ∧ IsEtale B S hS φ
declarations.comment: the existence of the affine surjective étale chart of the situation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ResolutionPropertyDescentSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUY.** The choices fixed in the situation of the source for a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space `X` over `S`: an affine scheme `V` of the site with a
surjective étale morphism `φ : V → X`, a factorization of `φ` into an open immersion
`j : V → Y` into an algebraic space `Y` followed by a finite morphism `π : Y → X`, and a
finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Y` with `|V(ℐ)| = |Y| ∖ |j(V)|`.

A chart `V` as in the first clause exists by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_affine_isSurjective_isEtale_of_isQuasiCompactSpace`.
declarations.statement:
structure ResolutionPropertyDescentSituation (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
declarations.comment: the data chosen in the situation, and the conditions imposed on it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_epi_biproduct_idealSheafPowPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GUZ.**  In the situation of Stacks 0GUY — a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
algebraic space `X`, a surjective étale `φ : V ⟶ X` from an affine scheme factored as an open
immersion `j : V ⟶ Y` followed by a finite `π : Y ⟶ X`, and a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Y` with `V(ℐ) = Y ∖ j(V)` — assume `X` Noetherian.  Then every coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `ℱ` admits, for some `r ≥ 0` and integers `n_1, …, n_r ≥ 0`, a surjection

`⨁_{i = 1}^{r} π_*(ℐ^{n_i}) ⟶ ℱ`

of `𝒪_X`-modules.  This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_epi_biproduct_idealSheafPowPushforward_of_le` at `N = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_biproduct_idealSheafPowPushforward (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F) :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (n : Fin r → ℕ)
      (_ : HasBiproduct fun i =>
        idealSheafPowPushforward B S hS (D.piHom B S hS hZ X hqc hqs) D.I (n i))
      (σ : (⨁ fun i => idealSheafPowPushforward B S hS (D.piHom B S hS hZ X hqc hqs) D.I (n i)) ⟶
        F), Epi σ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_epi_modulePushforwardIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GV0, the direction from the resolution property.**  In the situation of
Stacks 0GUY with `X` Noetherian, if `X` has the resolution property then `π_*ℐ` is the quotient
of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module: there are a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module `E` and an
epimorphism `E ⟶ π_*ℐ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_epi_modulePushforwardIdeal
    (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (hRP : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    ∃ (E : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
      (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite E)
      (p : E ⟶ modulePushforwardIdeal B S hS hZ X hqc hqs D), Epi p
declarations.comment: the direction from the resolution property: `π_*ℐ` is coherent by Stacks 07UH, so the resolution property of the Noetherian `X` exhibits it as the quotient of a finite locally free module. The converse direction is not claimed; its input Stacks 0GUZ, the powers `ℐ^n` of a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals on an algebraic space, and the closure of finite local freeness under tensor powers and finite direct sums are all absent from the library, as the module documentation records

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_epi_modulePushforwardIdeal
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space, `φ : V ⟶ X` a surjective
étale morphism from an affine scheme factored as an open immersion `j : V ⟶ Y` followed by a
finite `π : Y ⟶ X`, and `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Y` a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with
`V(ℐ) = Y ∖ j(V)`, and assume `X` is Noetherian. Then `X` has the resolution property if and only
if `π_*ℐ` is the quotient of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_epi_modulePushforwardIdeal
    (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ↔
      ∃ (E : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite E)
        (p : E ⟶ modulePushforwardIdeal B S hS hZ X hqc hqs D), Epi p
declarations.comment: the whole statement, both directions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ResolutionPropertyDescentSituation.exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_epi_idealDirectImage_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GV1, the implication from the resolution property.**  In the situation of Stacks
0GUY, if the algebraic space `X` has the resolution property then `π_*ℐ` is the quotient of a
finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite_epi_idealDirectImage_of_hasResolutionProperty
    (hX : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    ∃ (E : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
      (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite E)
      (f : E ⟶ idealDirectImage B S hS hZ sit), Epi f
declarations.comment: the implication from the resolution property of `X` to `π_*ℐ` being the quotient of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module; the reverse implication, whose proof in the source reduces to the Noetherian case Stacks 0GV0, is not proved — see the module documentation for the inputs it needs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_epi_idealDirectImage
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 0GUY — `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space
over `S`, `V` an affine scheme with a surjective étale `φ : V ⟶ X` factored as an open immersion
`j : V ⟶ Y` followed by a finite `π : Y ⟶ X`, and `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Y` a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf
of ideals with `|V(ℐ)| = |Y| ∖ |j(V)|` — the algebraic space `X` has the resolution property if
and only if `π_*ℐ` is the quotient of a finite locally free `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_iff_exists_epi_idealDirectImage
    (sit : ResolutionPropertyDescentSituation B S hS hZ X hqc hqs) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ↔
      ∃ (E : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (_ : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite E)
        (p : E ⟶ sit.idealDirectImage B S hS hZ), Epi p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasResolutionProperty_limitAlgebraicSpace_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GV2.**  Let `X = lim X_i` be the limit of a cofiltered system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms.  Then `X` has the
resolution property if and only if some `X_i` has it.

The system is indexed by a cofiltered category, which contains the directed systems of the
source; the bounds `hSize` and `hHomSize` on the index are those under which the limit of the
presheaves `D` is an algebraic space of the big fppf site (`limitAlgebraicSpace`, Stacks 07SF).

If `X_i` has the resolution property, so does `X`, by the affine case of Stacks 0GUU along the
affine projection `X ⟶ X_i`.  Conversely, the proof is the source's; see the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasResolutionProperty_limitAlgebraicSpace_iff
    (hqc : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hqs : ∀ i, IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (D.obj i)) :
    HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS
        (limitAlgebraicSpace B S hS D hSize hHomSize hD hAffine).1
        (limitAlgebraicSpace B S hS D hSize hHomSize hD hAffine).2 ↔
      ∃ i, HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS (D.obj i) (hD i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_viewOverIntegers_diag_of_hasResolutionProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GV3.**  Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over a
scheme `S` with the resolution property.  Then `X` has affine diagonal over `ℤ`: the diagonal of
`X` viewed as an algebraic space over `Spec ℤ` is an affine morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_viewOverIntegers_diag_of_hasResolutionProperty
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (hXres : HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS X hX) :
    IsAffineHom B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ (diag (viewOverIntegers B S hS hZ X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_closedFiltration_admissibleBlowups_resolutionProperty_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GV6 for an algebraic space over an arbitrary base scheme, with no hypothesis
beyond the tag's own.**  For a quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic space `X` over a scheme
`S` of the site there are closed subspaces `Z₀ ⊇ Z₁ ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ Z_t` of `X`, each of finite
presentation over `X`, with `Z₀ ⊆ X` a thickening, with `Z_t` carrying no points, and with a
`(Z_i ∖ Z_{i+1})`-admissible blowing up of `Z_i` whose source has the resolution property for
every `i < t`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_closedFiltration_admissibleBlowups_resolutionProperty`
with its hypothesis `h0GV5` discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_exists_isQuasiCompact_dense_isAdmissibleBlowup_`
`hasResolutionProperty`, read over the terminal scheme.

**The index direction, and an erratum in the source.**  The tag's statement reads "for each
`i = 0, …, t - 1` there exists a `(Z_i ∖ Z_{i - 1})`-admissible blowing up", with the chain
`X ⊃ Z_0 ⊃ Z_1 ⊃ ⋯ ⊃ Z_t = ∅`.  That index cannot be meant.  The chain gives `Z_i ⊆ Z_{i - 1}`,
so `Z_i ∖ Z_{i - 1}` is empty for every `i ≥ 1`, and at `i = 0` it names a `Z_{-1}` the statement
never introduces.  A `∅`-admissible blowing up is one whose centre is disjoint from `∅`, that is
any blowing up at all, so the literal reading collapses the clause to "some blowing up of `Z_i`
has the resolution property" — strictly weaker than intended.  The tag's own proof settles it:
its induction produces blowing ups admissible with respect to `Z_{1, i} ∖ Z_{1, i + 1}`.  So the
sets meant are the strata `Z_i ∖ Z_{i + 1}`, which partition `Z_0`, and that is what is proved
here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closedFiltration_admissibleBlowups_resolutionProperty_unconditional
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (Z : ℕ → Subfunctor X.1) (hZ : ∀ i, IsClosedSubspace B S hS (Z i)),
      (∀ i, IsFinitePresentation B S hS (Z i).ι) ∧
      (∀ i, Z (i + 1) ≤ Z i) ∧
      IsThickening B S hS X (Z 0) ∧
      IsEmpty (points B S hS (Z t).toFunctor) ∧
      ∀ i < t, ∃ (U : OpenSubspaces B S hS (Z i).toFunctor) (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
          (f : Y ⟶ (⟨(Z i).toFunctor, (hZ i).1⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)),
        Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.1.toFunctor (U.1.ι ≫ (Z i).ι)) =
            subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 (Z i) \ subspacePointSet B S hS X.1 (Z (i + 1)) ∧
          IsAdmissibleBlowup B S hS U f ∧
          HasResolutionProperty.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2

declarations.name: ClosedPointSpace
declarations.doc: The space of closed points of the prime spectrum of `R`, with its induced topology.
declarations.statement: abbrev ClosedPointSpace (R : Type u) [CommRing R]

declarations.name: ClosedPointResidueField
declarations.doc: The residue field at a closed point `x` of `Spec(R)`.
declarations.statement: abbrev ClosedPointResidueField {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (x : ClosedPointSpace R)

declarations.name: ClosedPointFiber
declarations.doc: The fibre `M(x) = M / xM` of an `R`-module at a closed point `x`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev ClosedPointFiber {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (x : ClosedPointSpace R)

declarations.name: sectionAt
declarations.doc: The canonical image `s(x)` of a module element `s` in the fibre at `x`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev sectionAt {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (x : ClosedPointSpace R) (s : M) : ClosedPointFiber M x

declarations.name: finiteDimensional_fiber
declarations.doc:
The fibre of a finite module at a closed point is finite-dimensional over the
residue field at that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_fiber
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (x : ClosedPointSpace R) :
    FiniteDimensional (ClosedPointResidueField x) (ClosedPointFiber M x)

declarations.name: canonicalKernel
declarations.doc:
The canonical subspace `B(x)` of the fibre: the common kernel of all fibre
functionals induced by `R`-linear maps `M → R`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def canonicalKernel {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (x : ClosedPointSpace R) :
    Submodule (ClosedPointResidueField x) (ClosedPointFiber M x)

declarations.name: CanonicalQuotient
declarations.doc: The canonical quotient `V(x) = M(x) / B(x)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev CanonicalQuotient {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (x : ClosedPointSpace R)

declarations.name: canonical_exact_and_splits_iff_linearIndependent
declarations.doc:
The canonical sequence `0 → B(x) → M(x) → V(x) → 0` is short exact.
Moreover, a finite family of elements of `M` splits off a free direct summand after
inverting an element outside `x` if and only if its images in `V(x)` are linearly
independent.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonical_exact_and_splits_iff_linearIndependent
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M] (x : ClosedPointSpace R) :
    Function.Injective (canonicalKernel M x).subtype ∧
      Function.Exact (canonicalKernel M x).subtype (canonicalKernel M x).mkQ ∧
      Function.Surjective (canonicalKernel M x).mkQ ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (s : Fin r → M),
        (∃ f : R, f ∉ x.1.asIdeal ∧ SplitsAfterInverting f s) ↔
          LinearIndependent (ClosedPointResidueField x)
            (fun i ↦ (canonicalKernel M x).mkQ (sectionAt x (s i)))

declarations.name: pi_canonicalQuotient_mkQ_sectionAt_surjective
declarations.doc:
At finitely many distinct closed points, every family of values in the canonical quotients
`V(x)` is induced by a single element of the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem pi_canonicalQuotient_mkQ_sectionAt_surjective
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    {ι : Type w} [Finite ι] (x : ι → ClosedPointSpace R) (hx : Function.Injective x) :
    Function.Surjective fun s : M ↦
      fun i ↦ (canonicalKernel M (x i)).mkQ (sectionAt (x i) s)

declarations.name: exists_section_dependentLocus_subset_union_of_card_add_le_finrank
declarations.doc:
Suppose that the dependent locus of `h` sections of a finitely presented module is contained
in a closed set `F` of the Noetherian space of closed points. If every canonical quotient `V(y)`
has dimension at least `h + k`, then one can choose a further section with arbitrary prescribed
values at finitely many distinct points of `F`. The new dependent locus is contained in `F`
together with a closed set all of whose irreducible components have codimension at least `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_section_dependentLocus_subset_union_of_card_add_le_finrank
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M] [NoetherianSpace (ClosedPointSpace R)]
    {h k : ℕ} (sections : Fin h → M) (F : Set (ClosedPointSpace R)) (hF : IsClosed F)
    (hsections :
      {y | ¬LinearIndependent (ClosedPointResidueField y)
        (fun i ↦ (canonicalKernel M y).mkQ (sectionAt y (sections i)))} ⊆ F)
    {ι : Type w} [Finite ι] (x : ι → ClosedPointSpace R) (hx : Function.Injective x)
    (hxF : ∀ i, x i ∈ F) (v : ∀ i, CanonicalQuotient M (x i))
    (hdim : ∀ y : ClosedPointSpace R,
      h + k ≤ Module.finrank (ClosedPointResidueField y) (CanonicalQuotient M y)) :
    ∃ (s : M) (F' : Set (ClosedPointSpace R)),
      (∀ i, (canonicalKernel M (x i)).mkQ (sectionAt (x i) s) = v i) ∧
        IsClosed F' ∧
        {y | ¬LinearIndependent (ClosedPointResidueField y)
          (fun i ↦ (canonicalKernel M y).mkQ
            (sectionAt y ((Fin.snoc sections s : Fin (h + 1) → M) i)))} ⊆ F ∪ F' ∧
        ∀ Z : IrreducibleCloseds (ClosedPointSpace R),
          Maximal (fun W : IrreducibleCloseds (ClosedPointSpace R) ↦
            (W : Set (ClosedPointSpace R)) ⊆ F') Z →
            (k : ℕ∞) ≤ codimension Z

declarations.name: exists_linearEquiv_prod_of_local_free_summand_rank_gt_dimension
declarations.doc:
Let `M` be a finitely presented module over a commutative ring whose Noetherian space of
closed points has dimension at most `d`. If at every closed point the localization of `M` has
a free direct summand of some rank strictly greater than `d`, then a rank-one free summand
splits from `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_linearEquiv_prod_of_local_free_summand_rank_gt_dimension
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.FinitePresentation R M] [NoetherianSpace (ClosedPointSpace R)]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (ClosedPointSpace R) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hlocal : ∀ x : ClosedPointSpace R,
      ∃ r : ℕ, d < r ∧
        ∃ s : Fin r → LocalizedModule x.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M,
          ∃ p : LocalizedModule x.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M →ₗ[Localization x.1.asIdeal.primeCompl]
              (Fin r → Localization x.1.asIdeal.primeCompl),
            p.comp (Fintype.linearCombination (Localization x.1.asIdeal.primeCompl) s) =
              LinearMap.id) :
    ∃ N : Submodule R M, Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] R × N)

declarations.name: countablyGenerated_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVD**. Let `R → S` be a faithfully flat ring map and let `M` be an `R`-module.
If the base change `S ⊗[R] M` is countably generated as an `S`-module, then `M` is countably
generated as an `R`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem countablyGenerated_of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (h : Module.CountablyGenerated S (S ⊗[R] M)) :
    Module.CountablyGenerated R M

declarations.name: eilenberg_swindle
declarations.doc:
**Eilenberg's lemma / Eilenberg swindle (Stacks Tag 0GVF).**
Let `R` be a ring and `P`, `Q`, `F` left `R`-modules with `P ⊕ Q ≅ F`, where `F` is a
free left `R`-module that is not finitely generated. Then `P ⊕ F ≅ F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eilenberg_swindle {R : Type*} [Ring R] (P Q F : Type*) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] [Module.Free R F]
    (h : Nonempty ((P × Q) ≃ₗ[R] F)) (hnfg : ¬ Module.Finite R F) :
    Nonempty ((P × F) ≃ₗ[R] F)

declarations.name: exists_free_prod_of_projective
declarations.doc:
A projective module is a direct summand of a free module with a free complementary
summand.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_free_prod_of_projective
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Projective R P] :
    ∃ (F : Type (max u v)) (_ : AddCommGroup F) (_ : Module R F)
      (_ : Module.Free R F), Module.Free R (P × F)

declarations.name: exists_finite_free_summand_containing_zero_prod
declarations.doc:
For an element `s` of a projective module `P`, there is a finite free module `F` and a
finite free direct summand of `F × P` containing `(0, s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_free_summand_containing_zero_prod
    {R : Type u} [Ring R] {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Projective R P] (s : P) :
    ∃ (F : Type (max u v)) (_ : AddCommGroup F) (_ : Module R F)
      (_ : Module.Finite R F) (_ : Module.Free R F),
      ∃ (K : Submodule R (F × P)) (_ : Module.Finite R K) (_ : Module.Free R K),
        (0, s) ∈ K ∧ ∃ K' : Submodule R (F × P), IsCompl K K'

declarations.name: exists_mem_add_unimodular
declarations.doc:
If `P` is projective and has infinite rank after localization at every maximal ideal, then
an element which generates `P` together with `M` can be modified by an element of `M` to become
unimodular.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_add_unimodular
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Projective R P] (M : Submodule R P) (s : P)
    (hR : IsNoetherianRing (R ⧸ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)))
    (hP : ∀ p : MaximalSpectrum R,
      ¬ Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
        (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl P))
    (hspan : Submodule.span R {s} ⊔ M = ⊤) :
    ∃ m ∈ M, ∃ φ : P →ₗ[R] R, φ (s + m) = 1

declarations.name: exists_finite_isStablyFree_summand_containing
declarations.doc:
Every element of a projective module of infinite rank at all maximal ideals lies in a finite
stably free direct summand, provided the quotient by the Jacobson radical is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_isStablyFree_summand_containing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Projective R P] (s : P)
    (hR : IsNoetherianRing (R ⧸ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)))
    (hP : ∀ p : MaximalSpectrum R,
      ¬ Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
        (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl P)) :
    ∃ M : Submodule R P,
      Module.Finite R M ∧ Module.IsStablyFree R M ∧ s ∈ M ∧
        ∃ M' : Submodule R P, IsCompl M M'

declarations.name: free_of_countablyGenerated_projective_of_localization_not_finite
declarations.doc:
A countably generated projective module over a commutative ring is free if the quotient by
the Jacobson radical is Noetherian and every localization at a maximal ideal has infinite
rank.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_of_countablyGenerated_projective_of_localization_not_finite
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Projective R P]
    (hR : IsNoetherianRing (R ⧸ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal R)))
    (hP : Module.CountablyGenerated R P)
    (hPinf : ∀ p : MaximalSpectrum R,
      ¬ Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
        (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl P)) :
    Module.Free R P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit
declarations.doc:
The colimit of a directed system of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` whose transition
morphisms are representable thickenings -- equivalently, closed immersions inducing isomorphisms
on reductions -- is an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, provided it satisfies the
set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {I : Type (u + 1)} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hthick : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      MorphismProperty.relative (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)) (D.map f))
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) (e : X ≅ colimit D)
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: granting the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS for the colimit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_of_cofinal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVM.** The colimit of a directed system of affine formal algebraic spaces over
`S` whose transition morphisms are representable thickenings -- equivalently, closed immersions
inducing isomorphisms on reductions -- is an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, provided
the index set has a cofinal family `ι : K → I` indexed by a set `K` which is not too large
(`u`-small, of cardinality below the cofinality of the size cutoff of the site; every countable
`K` qualifies).

The size bound is the proviso of observation (1) of Remark 0AIS. For a colimit
`X = colim X_λ` of a system as in Definition 0AI7, the source notes that `U = ∐_λ X_λ ⟶ X` is a
surjection of fppf sheaves, and that "if `U` is representable by an object of `(Sch/S)_fppf`"
then the set-theoretic condition is satisfied, which "is always the case if `Λ` is countable"
(Sets, Lemma 000R). Being `u`-small of cardinality below the cofinality of the size cutoff,
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.AdmitsCoproductIndex`, is what makes a coproduct of objects of
the site indexed by `K` an object of the site; every countable `K` qualifies
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.admitsCoproductIndex_of_countable`). It is asked only of a
cofinal family, which has the same colimit. Because the stages here are affine formal algebraic
spaces rather than affine schemes, each stage `X_{ι k}` is replaced by an object `U_k` of the
site surjecting onto it, as in observation (3) of Remark 0AIS, and `∐_k U_k` is the object of
the site that the proviso asks for. The bound cannot be dropped: see
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_of_cofinal (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {I : Type (u + 1)} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i))
    (hthick : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      MorphismProperty.relative (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
        (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
          (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)) (D.map f))
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) (e : X ≅ colimit D)
    {K : Type v} [Small.{u} K] [B.AdmitsCoproductIndex K] (ι : K → I)
    (hι : ∀ i, ∃ k, i ≤ ι k) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: corrected form: the printed statement is false for an index set as large as the size cutoff of the site, the colimit then failing the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS (AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit); stated, under the source's hypotheses, for an index with a cofinal family whose index is admissible for coproducts in the site, the proviso of Stacks 0AIS observation (1) that the coproduct of the stages be representable by an object of the site (always the case for a countable index), and with the set-theoretic condition derived, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVM needs a size bound on the index set.** Over a nonempty scheme `S` of the site
it is not the case that the colimit of every directed system of affine formal algebraic spaces
over `S` along representable thickenings is an affine formal algebraic space: the colimit of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.sqZeroSheafDiagram`, for a residue field of `S` and an index set
as large as the size cutoff of the site, does not satisfy the set-theoretic condition of
Remark 0AIS. This is where the proviso of observation (1) of Remark 0AIS fails: each stage has
one point, so the coproduct of the stages has as many points as the index, which is as large as
the size cutoff, while an object of the site has fewer points than the cutoff.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) [Nonempty S] :
    ¬ ∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
      (D : I ⥤ Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))),
      (∀ i, IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i)) →
      (∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
        MorphismProperty.relative (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
          (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
            (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)) (D.map f)) →
      ∀ (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))), (X ≅ colimit D) →
        IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: the statement as printed is false: over any nonempty S, the directed system Spec(k + k^μ) of affine schemes along thickenings, indexed by the finite subsets μ of a set as large as the size cutoff of the site, has a colimit failing the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS, the coproduct of its stages not being an object of the site as the proviso of Stacks 0AIS observation (1) requires; the corrected form is AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_of_cofinal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_closedImmersions_of_admissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVN**, in the form its proof establishes. Let `E` be a directed system of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` whose transition morphisms are representable thickenings —
equivalently, by Stacks 0GVL, closed immersions inducing isomorphisms on reductions — indexed by
a type admitting coproducts in the site (every countable index does). Then a sheaf isomorphic to
its colimit is a formal algebraic space over `S`.

The bound is forced: the source's proof never checks the set-theoretic condition of
Definition 0AIM for the colimit, Remark 0AIS (1) and (3) give it only for an index "not too
large (for example countable)", and without a bound the conclusion is false,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_closedImmersions`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_closedImmersions_of_admissible
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] [Small.{u} Λ]
    [B.AdmitsCoproductIndex Λ] (E : Λ ⥤ FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hform : ∀ i : Λ, IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (E.obj i))
    (hthick : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (g : i ⟶ j),
      Space.IsRepresentableThickeningULift.{u + 1} B S hS (E.map g).hom)
    (Z : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hZ : Nonempty (Z ≅ colimit E)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z
declarations.comment: corrected form: the index is required to admit coproducts in the site (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.AdmitsCoproductIndex, e.g. any countable index), the caveat of Remark 0AIS (1) and (3) that the source's proof leaves unchecked; without such a bound the statement is false, by AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_closedImmersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_closedImmersions_of_satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVN, corrected per the recorded erratum.** Let `E` be a directed system of formal
algebraic spaces over `S`, indexed by an arbitrary directed set, whose transition morphisms are
representable thickenings — equivalently, by Stacks 0GVL, closed immersions inducing
isomorphisms on reductions. A sheaf `Z` isomorphic to its colimit which satisfies the
set-theoretic condition of Remark 0AIS is a formal algebraic space over `S`.

The set-theoretic condition is the only hypothesis beyond those of the source, and it cannot be
dropped
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_closedImmersions`).
