The chart system of the source's proof is constructed from an atlas of one stage by the étale
lifting of Stacks 0DEG/0DEE and its stages are affine by Stacks 0DE8
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_of_setTheoretic`, with
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineOfSurjectiveClosedImmersion`); for an index admitting
coproducts in the site the condition is itself a theorem,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_closedImmersions_of_admissible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_closedImmersions_of_satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)]
    (E : Λ ⥤ FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hform : ∀ i : Λ, IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (E.obj i))
    (hthick : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (g : i ⟶ j),
      Space.IsRepresentableThickeningULift.{u + 1} B S hS (E.map g).hom)
    (Z : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hZset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS Z)
    (hZ : Nonempty (Z ≅ colimit E)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z
declarations.comment: corrected form per the recorded erratum: for an arbitrary directed index, the colimit of a system of formal algebraic spaces along closed immersions inducing isomorphisms on reductions (representable thickenings, Stacks 0GVL) is a formal algebraic space provided the colimit satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Remark 0AIS; that condition cannot be dropped, AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_closedImmersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVQ.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`,
let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be a closed subset. Then the
completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` — the fppf sheaf whose sections over an object `U` of the
big fppf site of `S` are the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with `f(|U|) ⊆ T` — is an affine formal
algebraic space over `S`.

Nothing is assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses. The affine presentation is
`exists_affinePresentation_completionSheafULift` and the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS
is `satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheafULift`.

The two steps the source cites in general form are proved here: that a closed subset of
`|X_red|` is a closed subset of `|X|` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction.isClosed_image_pointsMapULift`, and that
`X_{/T} = colim (X_λ)_{/T}` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionSheafULiftIsoColimitCompletion`.

The reduction is supplied as data satisfying `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction`
rather than constructed, since Stacks 0AIN — the existence of a reduction — is not available
in this library; this is how Stacks 0GVT is stated here as well, and it needs no choice.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVR.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` and let
`T ⊆ |X_red|` be a closed subset, for a reduction `i : X_red ⟶ X` of `X`. Then the functor
`X_{/T}` on the big fppf site of `S` sending `U` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with
`f(|U|) ⊆ T` is a formal algebraic space: it is an fppf sheaf, and as such a formal algebraic
space over `S`. It is the completion `completionAlong i T` of Stacks 0GVS, which is a formal
algebraic space as well.

The functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSubfunctorULift` of `X` along the image of
`T` in `|X|`. Nothing is assumed: the sheaf property is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSheaf_completionSubfunctorULift`, the atlas of Definition 0AIM is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheafULift` with its affine
charts from Stacks 0GVQ, and the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS is
`satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheafULift_of_satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition`.
A reduction exists by Stacks 0AIN, and the statement holds for every one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionFunctor {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T) :
    ∃ h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (Space.completionSubfunctorULift B S hS X.obj
          (Space.pointsMapULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj i.hom '' T)).toFunctor,
      IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS ⟨_, h⟩ ∧
        IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (completionAlong i T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVR.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` with
reduction `i : X_red ⟶ X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed. The completion `X_{/T}` of `X`
along `T` — the fppf sheaf attached to the functor sending `U` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X`
with `f(|U|) ⊆ T` — is a formal algebraic space over `S`: the completions of the charts of `X`
along the inverse images of `T` form an atlas as in Definition 0AIM, each of them affine formal
by clause (1) of Stacks 0GVV, each representable étale over `X_{/T}` as a base change of a
chart of `X`, and jointly surjective because the charts of `X` are.

The closed subset `T` of `|X_red|` enters the completion through its image in `|X|`, which is
closed because the inclusion of a reduction is a homeomorphism on points:
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction.isClosed_image_pointsMapULift`. The set-theoretic
condition `hset` of Stacks 0AIS is the only hypothesis beyond the tag's own; see the section
"What is assumed" of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionAlong' {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (completionAlong i T)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: the whole statement for the tag's own hypotheses — `X` a formal algebraic space and `T` closed in `|X_red|` — from one carried hypothesis, `hset`, the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS for the completion, which this library carries by standing convention on the library's Stacks 0AJ1 (`isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover`, StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/EtaleCover.lean) and Stacks 0GVM (`isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit`, StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/DirectedColimit.lean), the condition being part of the definition of a formal algebraic space used here and not following from the conditions on the members of a covering family. Nothing else: the affine case, clause (1) of Stacks 0GVV, is proved — `completionOfAffineIsAffine`; and closedness of `T` is the tag's own, in `|X_red|`, the inclusion of a reduction being a homeomorphism on points (`IsReduction.isHomeomorph_pointsMapULift`) and hence carrying `T` to a closed subset of `|X|`, which is where the proof uses it (`IsReduction.isClosed_image_pointsMapULift`). `hi` supplies the reduction as data because Stacks 0AIN is unavailable in this library, the convention of the library's Stacks 0GVQ and 0GVT

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionAlong
registrations.comment: the completion of a formal algebraic space along a closed subset of its reduction, defined for an arbitrary morphism into the space and an arbitrary subset of the points of its source

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionAlong
registrations.comment: the completion of a formal algebraic space along a closed subset of its reduction, defined for an arbitrary morphism into the space and an arbitrary subset of the points of its source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosed_preimage_pointsMapULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVT.** The inverse image `T' = |f_red|⁻¹ T` of a closed subset `T ⊆ |X_red|` is a
closed subset of `|X'_red|`, since the morphism of reductions is continuous on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_preimage_pointsMapULift {Xred' Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (fred : Xred' ⟶ Xred) (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj)) :
    letI := Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj
    letI := Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred'.obj
    IsClosed T →
      IsClosed (Space.pointsMapULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred'.obj fred.hom ⁻¹' T)
declarations.comment: the closed subset `T'`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPullback_completionAlongMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVT.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`T ⊆ |X_red|` be a closed subset and let `T' = |f_red|⁻¹ T ⊆ |X'_red|`. Then the square formed
by `X'_{/T'} ⟶ X'`, `X_{/T} ⟶ X`, the morphism of completions and `f` is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_completionAlongMap {X' X Xred' Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (_hX' : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i' : Xred' ⟶ X'} {i : Xred ⟶ X} (hi' : IsReduction B S hS X' Xred' i')
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (_hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T) :
    IsPullback
      (completionAlongInclusion i'
        (Space.pointsMapULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred'.obj (reductionMap hi' hi f).hom ⁻¹' T))
      (completionAlongMap hi' hi f T)
      f
      (completionAlongInclusion i T)
declarations.comment: the cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isReduction_completionAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVU.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B`, let `X` be a formal
algebraic space over `S` with reduction `i : X_red ⟶ X`, and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be a closed
subset. The reduction of the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` is the reduced induced closed
subspace `Z` of `X_red` corresponding to `T`: the canonical morphism `Z ⟶ X_{/T}` exhibits `Z`
as the reduction of the completion.

The conclusion contains the mapping property: every morphism to `X_{/T}` from a reduced
algebraic space over `S` factors uniquely through `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduction_completionAlong (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X (sheafOfAlgebraicSpace B S hS Xred₀ hXred₀) i)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS Xred₀)) (hT : IsClosed T) :
    IsReduction B S hS (completionAlong i (liftedPointSet B S hS hXred₀ T))
      (reducedSubspaceSheaf B S hS hXred₀ T hT)
      (reducedSubspaceToCompletionAlong B S hS hXred₀ T hT)
declarations.comment: with the reduction of `X` written as the universe lift of an algebraic space over `S`, the form in which the reduced induced closed subspace of Stacks 03IQ is available; that costs no generality, by `Space.exists_uliftFunctor_iso_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_completionAlong
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, let
`i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed with `|X_red| \ T`
quasi-compact. If `X` is countably indexed then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`.

It takes as hypothesis `hspf : CompletionOfCountablyIndexedIsCountableSpf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_completionAlong {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hqc : @IsCompact _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) Tᶜ)
    (hspf : CompletionOfCountablyIndexedIsCountableSpf B S hS) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (3): if `|X_red| \ T` is quasi-compact and `X` is countably indexed then so is `X_{/T}`, countably indexed being `IsCountablyIndexed` (Stacks 0AIJ, StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/CountablyIndexed.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own countable-indexing hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data rather than choosing one from Stacks 0AIN (the convention of the library's Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`, `hqc` is the tag's own quasi-compactness of `|X_red| \ T`, stated as compactness of `Tᶜ` for the point topology `Space.pointTopologyULift` since this library has no quasi-compactness predicate for formal algebraic spaces, and `hspf` is the source's own step producing the weakly admissible ring `lim A/J_{m,n}` with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero — condition (2) of Stacks 0AN1 — quantified over its own space, reduction and subset. The step from `hspf` to the conclusion is Stacks 0AN1, (2) ⇒ (1) (`isCountablyIndexedAffine_of_hasCountableWeakPresentation`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_completionAlong
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, let
`i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed with `|X_red| \ T`
quasi-compact. If `X` is adic\* then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`.

It takes as hypotheses `hideal : CompletionOfAdicStarIsCompletionAlongFGIdeal` and the
set-theoretic condition `hset` on `X_{/T}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_completionAlong {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsAdicStar B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hqc : @IsCompact _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) Tᶜ)
    (hideal : CompletionOfAdicStarIsCompletionAlongFGIdeal B S hS)
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (completionAlong i T)) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (4): if `|X_red| \ T` is quasi-compact and `X` is adic* then so is `X_{/T}`, adic* being `IsAdicStar` (Stacks 0AID (4), StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/Affine/Types.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own adic* hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data rather than choosing one from Stacks 0AIN (the convention of the library's Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`, `hqc` is the tag's own quasi-compactness of `|X_red| \ T`, stated as compactness of `Tᶜ` for the point topology `Space.pointTopologyULift` since this library has no quasi-compactness predicate for formal algebraic spaces, `hideal` is the source's own step identifying `X_{/T}` with the completion of an affine scheme along the finitely generated ideal `J = (f_1,...,f_r) + I`, quantified over its own space, reduction and subset, and `hset` is the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS on the completion, carried where Stacks 0GVM (`isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit`) carries it and needed to transport the conclusion back along the isomorphism. The step from `hideal` to the conclusion is Stacks 0GXX (3) (`isAdicStar_completionAlongIdeal`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_completionAlong
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, let
`i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed. If `X` is Noetherian
then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`. No quasi-compactness of `|X_red| \ T` is
assumed.

It takes as hypotheses `hideal : CompletionOfNoetherianIsCompletionAlongNoetherianIdeal` and the
set-theoretic condition `hset` on `X_{/T}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_completionAlong {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hideal : CompletionOfNoetherianIsCompletionAlongNoetherianIdeal B S hS)
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (completionAlong i T)) :
    IsNoetherian B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (5): if `X` is Noetherian then so is `X_{/T}`, Noetherian being `IsNoetherian` (Stacks 0AID (5), StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/Affine/Types.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own Noetherian hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data rather than choosing one from Stacks 0AIN (the convention of the library's Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`, `hideal` is the source's own step identifying `X_{/T}` with the completion of a Noetherian affine scheme along an ideal, quantified over its own space, reduction and subset, and `hset` is the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS on the completion, carried where Stacks 0GVM (`isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit`) carries it and needed to transport the conclusion back along the isomorphism. There is deliberately NO quasi-compactness hypothesis: the source notes it is automatic here. The step from `hideal` to the conclusion is Stacks 0GXX (4) (`isNoetherian_completionAlongIdeal`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, let
`i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed with `|X_red| \ T`
quasi-compact. If `X` is countably indexed then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`:
it admits a presentation indexed by `ℕ` by affine schemes along thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_completionAlong' {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hqc : @IsCompact _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) Tᶜ) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (3): if `|X_red| \ T` is quasi-compact and `X` is countably indexed then so is `X_{/T}`, countably indexed being `IsCountablyIndexed` (Stacks 0AIJ, StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/CountablyIndexed.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own countable-indexing hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data rather than choosing one from Stacks 0AIN (the convention of Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`, `hqc` is the tag's own quasi-compactness of `|X_red| \ T`, stated as compactness of `Tᶜ` for the point topology `Space.pointTopologyULift` since this library has no quasi-compactness predicate for formal algebraic spaces. Nothing else: the source's step producing the weakly admissible ring `lim A/J_{m,n}` with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero — condition (2) of Stacks 0AN1 — is not needed at all. The proof goes through condition (1) directly: `isCountablyIndexed_completionSheafULift`, which gets a countable directed presentation of `X_{/T}` from a countable one of `X` and turns it into a sequential one by Stacks 0AII (`isCountablyIndexed_iff_exists_countable_presentation`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, let
`i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed with `|X_red| \ T`
quasi-compact. If `X` is adic\* then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`: it is
presented by an adic topological ring with a finitely generated ideal of definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_completionAlong' {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsAdicStar B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hqc : @IsCompact _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) Tᶜ) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (4): if `|X_red| \ T` is quasi-compact and `X` is adic* then so is `X_{/T}`, adic* being `IsAdicStar` (Stacks 0AID (4), StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/Affine/Types.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own adic* hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data because Stacks 0AIN is unavailable in this library (the convention of Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`, and `hqc` is the tag's own quasi-compactness of `|X_red| \ T`, stated as compactness of `Tᶜ` for the point topology `Space.pointTopologyULift` since this library has no quasi-compactness predicate for formal algebraic spaces. NOTHING ELSE: the source's own step `X_{/T} = Spf (lim A/J^n)` for a finitely generated `J` is PROVED (`exists_fg_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso_completionSheafULift`). Nothing in the chain asks anything of `Spec A` -- no structure morphism to `S` and no site-membership -- exactly as the source asks nothing: the affines of the site cutting out the powers of `J` are quotients of the STAGE rings `A/K`. The set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS is not assumed. The step from `X_{/T} = Spf (lim A/J^n)` to the conclusion is the ring half of Stacks 0GXX (`isAdic_adicCompletion`, `isIdealOfDefinition_map_adicCompletion`, `isWeaklyAdmissible_adicCompletion`) together with clause (2) of this tag (`hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionAlong'`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`, let
`i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed. If `X` is Noetherian
then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`: it is presented by a topological ring which
is both Noetherian and adic.
declarations.comment: clause (5): if `X` is Noetherian then so is `X_{/T}`, Noetherian being `IsNoetherian` (Stacks 0AID (5), StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/Affine/Types.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own Noetherian hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data because Stacks 0AIN is unavailable in this library (the convention of Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), and `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`. NOTHING ELSE: the source's own step `X_{/T} = Spf (lim A/J^n)` for a Noetherian `A` is PROVED (`exists_fg_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso_completionSheafULift`). Nothing in the chain asks anything of `Spec A` -- no structure morphism to `S` and no site-membership. There is deliberately NO quasi-compactness hypothesis: it is automatic here, which is `isCompact_of_isNoetherianRing` (the point space of `X` is the prime spectrum of a quotient of the Noetherian presenting ring, hence a Noetherian space). The set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS is not assumed. The step from `X_{/T} = Spf (lim A/J^n)` to the conclusion is Stacks 0316 for the Noetherianness of the adic completion together with the ring half of Stacks 0GXX (`isAdic_adicCompletion`) and clause (2) of this tag (`hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionAlong'`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks 0GVV.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a McQuillan affine formal
algebraic space over `S`, let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be
closed. Then the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` is again McQuillan, that is satisfies
condition (4) of Stacks 0AIC: it is an affine formal algebraic space some presentation of which
by affine thickenings has all its section-ring projections surjective.

Nothing is assumed beyond the tag's own hypotheses. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionSheafULift` in the
source's spelling `X_{/T}` for a closed subset `T` of the points of a reduction; the source's
step — write `X = Spf(A)` and observe that `X_{/T} ⟶ X ⟶ Spec(A)` satisfies condition (2) of
Stacks 0AIC — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_completionSheafULift`, and the
geometric content it rests on is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionClosedSubscheme_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace`: a
closed immersion of an object of the site into `X_{/T}` is a closed immersion into `X`.
declarations.comment: clause (2): if `X` is McQuillan so is `X_{/T}`, with McQuillan read as `HasSomeSurjectivePresentation` (condition (4) of Stacks 0AIC, registered for Stacks 0AID at StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalSpace/Affine/Types.lean). Carried hypotheses: `hX` is the tag's own McQuillan hypothesis on `X`, `hi` supplies the reduction as data because Stacks 0AIN is unavailable in this library (the convention of the library's Stacks 0GVT and 0GB8), and `hT` is the tag's own closedness of `T` in `|X_red|`. Nothing else: the source's step producing condition (2) of Stacks 0AIC for the completion is proved — `hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_completionSheafULift`, resting on `completionClosedSubscheme_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace`; and the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS on the completion is proved — `satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheafULift`. The step from condition (2) to the conclusion is Stacks 0AIC, (2) ⇒ (5) ⇒ (4).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionOfAffineIsAffine
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0GVV**, in the ambient spelling
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.CompletionOfAffineIsAffine`: the completion of an affine formal
algebraic space over `S` along a closed set of its points is again an affine formal algebraic
space, for every such space and every such set at once. It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionAlong'` (Stacks 0GVQ) with
the reduction removed from the statement: the completion is formed along a closed set of points
of the space itself, which is what the consumers of clause (1) in this library — the
base-changed charts of Stacks 0GVR and Stacks 0GVW — supply, and so no `hred` is needed.

Nothing is assumed. The affine presentation is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affinePresentation_completionSheafULift` and the
set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheafULift`.
declarations.statement: theorem completionOfAffineIsAffine : CompletionOfAffineIsAffine' B S hS
declarations.comment: clause (1), in the ambient spelling `CompletionOfAffineIsAffine`, quantified over the affine formal algebraic space and over the closed subset of its own points. No hypotheses beyond the tag's own: the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS on the completions is proved — `satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheafULift`; the commutation of completion with directed colimits of fppf sheaves is proved — `completionSheafULiftIsoColimitCompletion`; Stacks 0AIY at the affine stages is `isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheafULift_affineStageSheaf`. No `hred` is needed, the ambient spelling mentioning no reduction. Clause (1) is Stacks 0GVQ, whose registration stays on `isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionAlong'` above

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyCountablyIndexed_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 0GVW.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a formal algebraic space
over `S`, let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed such that
the inclusion `|X_red| \ T ⟶ |X_red|` of the open subspace with points `|X_red| \ T` is
quasi-compact. If `X` is locally countably indexed then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X`
along `T`.

The open subspace `|X_red| \ T` is the subfunctor of the sections of `X_red` with point-set
image in `Tᶜ`, and the hypothesis `hqc` is quasi-compactness of its inclusion in the sense of
Stacks 03HE; see the section "The source's quasi-compactness hypothesis" of this file. It is
transferred to the charts by `complementCompactOnCharts_of_isQuasiCompactULift`, and the
statement follows from
`isLocallyCountablyIndexed_completionAlong_of_complementCompactOnCharts`. Nothing else is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyCountablyIndexed_completionAlong' {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsLocallyCountablyIndexed B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (Space.completionSubfunctorULift B S hS Xred.obj Tᶜ).ι) :
    IsLocallyCountablyIndexed B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (1): if the complement of `T` is quasi-compact and `X` is locally countably indexed then so is `X_{/T}` (`IsLocallyCountablyIndexed`, Stacks 0AKY). Binders are exactly the source's data: `T` closed in `|X_red|`, and quasi-compactness (Stacks 03HE, `Space.IsQuasiCompactULift`) of the inclusion of the open subspace `|X_red| \ T` (the subfunctor of sections with point-set image in `Tᶜ`). The set-theoretic condition of 0AIS is proved (0GVR), clause (1) of 0GVV is proved (`completionOfAffineIsAffine`), clause (3) of 0GVV is proved (`isCountablyIndexed_completionAlong'`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks 0GVW.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a formal algebraic space
over `S`, let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed such that
the inclusion `|X_red| \ T ⟶ |X_red|` of the open subspace with points `|X_red| \ T` is
quasi-compact. If `X` is locally adic\* then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`.

The hypothesis `hqc` is read as for clause (1), `isLocallyCountablyIndexed_completionAlong'`.
Nothing else is assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAdicStar_completionAlong' {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS X) {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i)
    (T : Set (Space.pointsULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopologyULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj) T)
    (hqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (Space.completionSubfunctorULift B S hS Xred.obj Tᶜ).ι) :
    IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS (completionAlong i T)
declarations.comment: clause (2): if the complement of `T` is quasi-compact and `X` is locally adic* then so is `X_{/T}` (`IsLocallyAdicStar`, Stacks 0AKY). Binders are exactly the source's data: `T` closed in `|X_red|`, and quasi-compactness (Stacks 03HE, `Space.IsQuasiCompactULift`) of the inclusion of the open subspace `|X_red| \ T` (the subfunctor of sections with point-set image in `Tᶜ`). The set-theoretic condition of 0AIS is proved (0GVR), clause (4) of 0GVV is proved (`isAdicStar_completionAlong'`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionAlong'
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of Stacks 0GVW.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a formal algebraic space
over `S`, let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X` and let `T ⊆ |X_red|` be closed. If `X` is
locally Noetherian then so is the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T`: the completions of the
charts of `X` along the inverse images of `T` form an atlas as in Definition 0AIM, and each of
them is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space by clause (5) of Stacks 0GVV. No
quasi-compactness hypothesis is needed, the source observing that it holds automatically
because `|X_red|` is then the spectrum of a Noetherian ring.

Nothing is assumed beyond the source's hypotheses: the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS
for `X_{/T}` is `satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionAlong_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`
(Stacks 0GVR), and clause (5) of Stacks 0GVV is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_completionAlong'`.
declarations.comment: clause (3): if `X` is locally Noetherian then so is `X_{/T}` (`IsLocallyNoetherian`, Stacks 0AKY); deliberately NO quasi-compactness hypothesis, as in the source. Binders are exactly the source's data: `T` closed in `|X_red|`. The set-theoretic condition of 0AIS is proved (0GVR), clause (5) of 0GVV is proved (`isNoetherian_completionAlong'`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasiSober_points_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVX.** The space of points of Stacks 04XL of a locally Noetherian algebraic stack
over `S` is quasi-sober in the sense of Stacks 004X: every irreducible closed subset of it has a
generic point.

Local Noetherianity is read as the atlas condition of Stacks 04YF, which supplies a smooth
surjective 1-morphism from the algebraic stack of a locally Noetherian scheme `U` of the site.
The point space of that algebraic stack is the topological space of `U`, hence is quasi-sober and
locally Noetherian, and the chart is continuous, open and surjective on points, so quasi-sobriety
passes to `|𝒳|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiSober_points_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hN : Stack.HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian X) 𝒳) :
    letI := Stack.pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val
    QuasiSober (Stack.points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_specializes_spacePointMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GVZ.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `f : U ⟶ 𝒳` be a smooth
1-morphism from an algebraic space `U` over `S`, let `x' ⤳ x` be a specialization of points of
`|𝒳|` and let `u` be a point of `|U|` with `f(u) = x`. If the point `x'` admits a quasi-compact
field-valued representative — one of the equivalent conditions of **Stacks 0DTK** for the pair
`(𝒳, x')` — then there is a specialization `u' ⤳ u` in `|U|` with `f(u') = x'`.

Smoothness of `f` enters twice. It makes `|U| ⟶ |𝒳|` an open map (**Stacks 06R7**), which is
what puts `u` in the closure of the fibre of `|U| ⟶ |𝒳|` over `x'`: an open neighbourhood of `u`
missing that fibre would have open image containing `x` but not `x'`. And it is what makes the
base change of the 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` of the representative an algebraic space over the
affine chart, so that the fibre is the image, on points, of an affine scheme quasi-compact over
the chart; **Stacks 02JQ** then produces the specialization inside that fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_specializes_spacePointMap_eq
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
    (f : fibredCategory B S hS U ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hf : HasPropertyOnSomeSmoothDiagram B S hS
      (fun _ _ h => Space.IsSmooth B S hS h) f)
    {x x' : points B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property} (hxx' : x' ⤳ x)
    (hx' : ∃ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳.val,
      pointClass B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property p = x' ∧
        IsQuasiCompactFieldValuedPoint B S hS 𝒳 p)
    (u : Space.points B S hS U) (hu : spacePointMap B S hS U 𝒳 f.hom u = x) :
    ∃ u' : Space.points B S hS U, u' ⤳ u ∧
      spacePointMap B S hS U 𝒳 f.hom u' = x'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsDecent
declarations.doc:
A category fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` — in particular an algebraic
stack — is *decent* when every one of its points admits a quasi-compact field-valued
representative.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsDecent : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDecent_of_isQuasiCompact_diagonal
declarations.doc: **An algebraic stack whose absolute diagonal is quasi-compact is decent.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_isQuasiCompact_diagonal
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hΔ : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ
      (relativeDiagonalAlgebraicStacks B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ
        (structureMorphism B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ
          (AlgebraicStacks.viewOverIntegers B S hS hZ 𝒳)))) :
    IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val
declarations.comment: quasi-compact diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDecent_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**A quasi-separated algebraic stack is decent.** If `𝒳` is quasi-separated in the absolute
sense, then every point of `𝒳` has a field-valued representative which is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_isQuasiSeparated (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (h𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳) :
    IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val
declarations.comment: quasi-separated case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDecent_of_representable_or_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GW3.** The source of a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S` with decent target
is decent as soon as the 1-morphism is representable by schemes, or is representable by algebraic
spaces and quasi-separated.

The argument is the source's.  Fix a point `x` of `𝒳`; decency of `𝒴` supplies a *quasi-compact*
field-valued representative `q` of the image of `x`, and the 1-morphism `g : Spec k ⟶ 𝒴` it
determines is quasi-compact (**Stacks 050T**).  Form the 2-fibre product `P` of `g` and `f`
(**Stacks 04T2**); its second projection is quasi-compact as a base change of `g`
(**Stacks 050V**), and by **Stacks 04XH** the pair consisting of the point of `Spec k` named by
`q` and of `x` lifts to a point `w` of `P`.  Any field-valued representative `p` of `w` then has
quasi-compact 1-morphism — in the representable case because `P` is the stack of a scheme, in the
quasi-separated case because the composite of that 1-morphism with the *first* projection is
quasi-compact and the first projection is quasi-separated, so **Stacks 050Y** cancels it — and the
field-valued point of `𝒳` it induces represents `x` with quasi-compact 1-morphism by
**Stacks 050W**.

Unlike the source, no appeal to **Stacks 0DTK** is needed: the representative is chosen
downstream rather than tested, so only the existential form of decency is ever used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_representable_or_quasiSeparated
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (h𝒴 : IsDecent B S hS 𝒴.val)
    (hf : Stacks.RepresentableMorphism.IsRepresentableMorphism 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒴.val.val.p
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom) ∨
      (IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f.hom.hom ∧
        AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)) :
    IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDecent_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GW4.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `f` is
quasi-compact and surjective and `𝒳` is decent, then `𝒴` is decent.

Let `y` be a point of `𝒴`. Surjectivity of `f` is surjectivity of the map on points
(**Stacks 04ZS**), so `y` is the image of a point `x` of `𝒳`, and decency of `𝒳` supplies a
field-valued representative `p` of `x` whose 1-morphism `Spec k ⟶ 𝒳` is quasi-compact
(**Stacks 050T**). The image field-valued point `f ∘ p` has the same base, represents `y`, and
its 1-morphism is the composite of that of `p` with `f`, hence quasi-compact by **Stacks 050W**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_isSurjective
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    IsDecent B S hS 𝒴.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isDecent_of_isGerbeOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GW5.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`. If `f`
exhibits `𝒳` as a gerbe over `𝒴` (**Stacks 06QC**) and `𝒳` is decent (**Stacks 0GW1**), then `𝒴`
is decent.

By **Stacks 06R9** `f` is a universal homeomorphism (**Stacks 0CI7**), hence quasi-compact,
through `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasiCompactMorphism_of_universalHomeomorphism`; surjectivity
of `f` comes from the gerbe condition directly, by the surjectivity clause of **Stacks 06QI**.
With both in hand the conclusion is **Stacks 0GW4**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_isGerbeOver
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbeOver.{u, w} B S hS f)
    (h𝒳 : IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val) :
    IsDecent B S hS 𝒴.val

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.t0Space_points_of_isDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GW7.** The space of points of a decent algebraic stack over `S` is Kolmogorov: two
points of `|𝒳|` with the same open neighbourhoods are equal.

Two such points `x₁`, `x₂` have the same closure `C`, and `x₁, x₂ ∈ C`. Choose a smooth chart
`φ : |U| → |𝒳|` by a scheme, surjective on points, and inside the nonempty closed set `φ ⁻¹' C`
choose a point `u` maximal for specialization, which the sobriety of `|U|` provides. Decency
feeds **Stacks 0GVZ** the quasi-compact field-valued representative it asks for, so every
specialization `x' ⤳ φ u` with `x' ∈ C` lifts to a specialization `u' ⤳ u` with `u' ∈ φ ⁻¹' C`;
maximality of `u` forces `u' = u` and hence `x' = φ u`. Applied to `x₁` and to `x₂`, both of
which specialize to `φ u` because `φ u ∈ C`, this gives `x₁ = φ u = x₂`.
declarations.statement:
theorem t0Space_points_of_isDecent
    (𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hdecent : IsDecent B S hS 𝒳) :
    T0Space (points B S hS 𝒳.val 𝒳.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.stacksSober_and_isLocallyNoetherianSpace_points
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GW8.** The space of points of Stacks 04XL of a decent, locally Noetherian
algebraic stack over `S` is a sober, locally Noetherian topological space.

Soberness is Kolmogorov together with quasi-soberness. The Kolmogorov half is Stacks 0GW7,
which decency supplies; the quasi-sober half is Stacks 0GVX and local Noetherianity of the
space is Stacks 0DQI, part (1), both from the locally Noetherian smooth chart of Stacks 04YF.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksSober_and_isLocallyNoetherianSpace_points
    (𝒳 : Stack.AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hdecent : Stack.IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hN : Stack.HasPropertyOnSomeSchemeAtlas B S hS
      (fun X : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian X) 𝒳) :
    StacksSober (Stack.points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property) ∧
      IsLocallyNoetherianSpace (Stack.points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.stacksSober_points_of_isDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GW9.** Let `𝒳` be a decent algebraic stack over `S` such that the inertia projection
`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is quasi-compact. Then the space of points `|𝒳|` is sober.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksSober_points_of_isDecent (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hd : IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    @StacksSober (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsIntegral
declarations.doc:
An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` is *integral* when it is reduced, it is
decent, its inertia projection `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is quasi-compact, and its space of points `|𝒳|` is
irreducible.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsIntegral (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.stacksSober_and_exists_openSubstack_isGerbeOver_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GWC.** Let `𝒳` be an integral algebraic stack over `S` (**Stacks 0GWB**). Then
1. `|𝒳|` is sober (Stacks 004X), irreducible, and has a unique generic point;
2. there is an open substack `𝒰 ⊆ 𝒳` which is a gerbe over an integral scheme `U`: a 1-morphism
   from `𝒰` to the algebraic stack of `U` making `𝒰` a gerbe over it (**Stacks 06QC**).

The two parts are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.stacksSober_irreducibleSpace_existsUnique_isGenericPoint_of_isIntegral`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_openSubstack_isGerbeOver_isIntegral`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stacksSober_and_exists_openSubstack_isGerbeOver_of_isIntegral
    (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) (h𝒳 : IsIntegral B S hS 𝒳) :
    (letI := pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val;
      StacksSober (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) ∧
        IrreducibleSpace (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳) ∧
          ∃! x : AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳, IsGenericPoint x Set.univ) ∧
      ∃ (𝒰 : OpenSubstack 𝒳) (U : BigFppfOver B S hS),
        AlgebraicGeometry.IsIntegral ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
          ∃ f : 𝒰.toAlgebraicStack ⟶ schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U,
            AlgebraicStacks.IsGerbeOver B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIntegral_of_isReducedStack_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GWD.** An algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` which is reduced and quasi-separated and
whose space of points `|𝒳|` is irreducible is integral in the sense of Stacks 0GWB.

Two of the four conditions of Stacks 0GWB are hypotheses. Decency is Stacks 0GW2 for a
quasi-separated algebraic stack. Quasi-compactness of the inertia projection `I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` holds
because that 1-morphism is the base change of the absolute diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` along
itself, and `Δ` is quasi-compact since `𝒳` is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_of_isReducedStack_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hred : IsReducedStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated.{u, w} B S hS hZ 𝒳)
    (hirr : @IrreducibleSpace (points B S hS 𝒳.val.val 𝒳.val.property)
      (pointTopology B S hS 𝒳.val)) :
    IsIntegral.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.bijective_pointClosure_and_bijective_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GWE.** Let `𝒳` be a decent algebraic stack over `S` whose inertia projection
`I_𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳` is quasi-compact. Then the map `x ↦ closure {x}` from the points of `𝒳` to the
irreducible closed subsets of `|𝒳|` is bijective, and so is the map `𝒵 ↦ |𝒵|` from the integral
closed substacks of `𝒳` to the irreducible closed subsets of `|𝒳|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_pointClosure_and_bijective_support
    (hd : IsDecent B S hS 𝒳.val)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism.{u, w} B S hS (inertiaProjectionAlgebraicStacks B S hS 𝒳)) :
    Function.Bijective (pointClosure B S hS 𝒳) ∧
      Function.Bijective (IntegralClosedSubstack.support (𝒳 := 𝒳))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_negative_epimorphic_lift_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWG.** A map of bounded derived objects whose target has zero
cohomology in degree `b` can be killed by a map from a negative object in degree `b` which
surjects onto the degree-`b` cohomology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_negative_epimorphic_lift_comp_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (hA : ∀ Y : A, ∃ (N : A) (p : N ⟶ Y), Epi p ∧ Subsingleton (Y ⟶ N))
    (X X' : DerivedCategory.Bounded A) (f : X ⟶ X') (b : ℤ)
    (hX' : IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A b).obj X'.obj)) :
    ∃ (N : A) (g : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A b).obj N ⟶ X.obj),
      Epi ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso A b).inv.app N ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A b).map g) ∧
      Subsingleton (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A b).obj X.obj) ⟶ N) ∧
      g ≫ (DerivedCategory.Bounded.ι.map f) = 0
declarations.comment: the case `X' = 0`, with no condition on the composition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_negative_epimorphic_lift_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWG.** A map of bounded derived objects whose target has zero
cohomology in degree `b` can be killed by a map from a negative object in degree `b` which
surjects onto the degree-`b` cohomology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_negative_epimorphic_lift_comp_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (hA : ∀ Y : A, ∃ (N : A) (p : N ⟶ Y), Epi p ∧ Subsingleton (Y ⟶ N))
    (X X' : DerivedCategory.Bounded A) (f : X ⟶ X') (b : ℤ)
    (hX' : IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A b).obj X'.obj)) :
    ∃ (N : A) (g : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor A b).obj N ⟶ X.obj),
      Epi ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso A b).inv.app N ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A b).map g) ∧
      Subsingleton (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor A b).obj X.obj) ⟶ N) ∧
      g ≫ (DerivedCategory.Bounded.ι.map f) = 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.FiberedMor
declarations.doc:
A morphism of fibred categories `(𝒞/U, Over.forget U) ⟶ (𝒮, p)`, i.e. an object of
the category `Mor_{Fib/𝒞}(𝒞/U, 𝒮)` of Stacks Definition 02XP(2) with source the slice
fibration. It is a functor over `𝒞` — a `BasedFunctor` between the based categories
attached to `Over.forget U` and to `p`, so the underlying functor `Over U ⥤ 𝒮` commutes
strictly with the projections to `𝒞` — which in addition preserves strongly Cartesian
morphisms.

Since the slice projection `Over.forget U` is a fibration in which every morphism
`g : a ⟶ b` of `Over U` is strongly Cartesian over its underlying `𝒞`-arrow
`g.left = (Over.forget U).map g`, the preservation condition specialises to the
unconditional requirement that `toFunctor.map g` be strongly Cartesian over `g.left`.
declarations.statement:
structure FiberedMor (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (U : 𝒞) extends
    BasedCategory.ofFunctor (Over.forget U) ⥤ᵇ BasedCategory.ofFunctor p

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.fibYonedaEvaluation
declarations.doc:
The evaluation, or "2-Yoneda", functor
`ev_U : Mor_{Fib/𝒞}(𝒞/U, 𝒮) ⥤ 𝒮_U`, `G ↦ G 1_U`.

On objects it sends a morphism of fibred categories `G` to its value at the terminal
object `1_U = (U, 𝟙 U)` of `𝒞/U`, which lies in the fibre over `U` because
`G ⋙ p = Over.forget U`. On a 2-morphism `t` it returns the component of `t` at `1_U`,
which lies over `𝟙 U` and is therefore a morphism of the fibre.
declarations.statement: def fibYonedaEvaluation (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (U : 𝒞) : FiberedMor p U ⥤ p.Fiber U

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.fibYonedaEvaluation_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The 2-Yoneda lemma for fibred categories (Stacks 0GWI).** For a fibred category
`p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞` and an object `U : 𝒞`, the evaluation functor
`ev_U : Mor_{Fib/𝒞}(𝒞/U, 𝒮) ⥤ 𝒮_U`, `G ↦ G 1_U`, is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem fibYonedaEvaluation_isEquivalence (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) [p.IsFibered] (U : 𝒞) :
    (fibYonedaEvaluation p U).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: InternalHom
declarations.doc:
**Definition 1 (Internal hom).**
An internal hom on a monoidal category `C` consists of a bifunctor
`hom : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ C ⥤ C` (contravariant in the first variable, covariant in the second)
together with, for all objects `X, Y, Z`, a bijection
`Φ X Y Z : Mor(X, hom(Y, Z)) ≃ Mor(X ⊗ Y, Z)` that is natural in `X`, in `Y`, and
in `Z`.

This is the opening clause of Stacks 0GWJ: `C` *has an internal hom* if for every pair `X, Y`
there is an object `hom(X, Y)` with `Mor(X, hom(Y, Z)) = Mor(X ⊗ Y, Z)` functorially in
`X, Y, Z`.
declarations.statement: structure InternalHom (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C]

declarations.name: InternalHom.ev
declarations.doc:
**Construction of (1) Evaluation.**
`ev_{X,Y} := Φ (id_{hom(X,Y)})`, the image of the identity under `Φ`.
declarations.statement: def ev (X Y : C) : ih.homObj X Y ⊗ X ⟶ Y

declarations.name: InternalHom.comp
declarations.doc:
**Construction of (2) Composition.**
`c_{X,Y,Z}` is the image under `Φ⁻¹` (using `X` as the tensoring object) of the
composite `hom(Y,Z) ⊗ hom(X,Y) ⊗ X → hom(Y,Z) ⊗ Y → Z` given by
`(id ⊗ ev_{X,Y})` followed by `ev_{Y,Z}`.
declarations.statement: def comp (X Y Z : C) : ih.homObj Y Z ⊗ ih.homObj X Y ⟶ ih.homObj X Z

declarations.name: InternalHom.tensorLeftMor
declarations.doc:
**Construction of (3) Tensor on the left.**
`t_{X,Y,Z}` is the image under `Φ⁻¹` of `id_Z ⊗ ev_{X,Y} : Z ⊗ hom(X,Y) ⊗ X → Z ⊗ Y`.
declarations.statement: def tensorLeftMor (X Y Z : C) : Z ⊗ ih.homObj X Y ⟶ ih.homObj X (Z ⊗ Y)

declarations.name: InternalHom.coev
declarations.doc:
**Construction of (4) Unit / coevaluation.**
`η_{X,Y} := ρ_Y⁻¹ ≫ (id_Y ⊗ u_X) ≫ t_{X,X,Y}`.
declarations.statement: def coev (X Y : C) : Y ⟶ ih.homObj X (Y ⊗ X)

declarations.name: InternalHom.internalCurryMor
declarations.doc:
**Construction of (5) Internalized currying (symmetric case).**
`d_{X,Y,Z}` is the image under `Φ⁻¹` (using `hom(X,Y)` as the tensoring object) of the
composite `hom(Y,Z) ⊗ X ⊗ hom(X,Y) → hom(Y,Z) ⊗ hom(X,Y) ⊗ X → hom(Y,Z) ⊗ Y → Z`,
where the first arrow uses the braiding `σ_{X, hom(X,Y)}`.
declarations.statement:
def internalCurryMor [BraidedCategory C] (X Y Z : C) :
    ih.homObj Y Z ⊗ X ⟶ ih.homObj (ih.homObj X Y) Z

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SiteGlueing.canonicalEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GWK.** For a site `C`, with no smallness hypothesis and with sheaves of sets
valued in an arbitrary universe, the category of sheaves on `C` is equivalent to the category of
absolute glueing data, via the functor sending a sheaf to its canonical absolute glueing data.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def canonicalEquivalence : Sheaf J (Type w) ≌ GlueingData.{w} J

declarations.name: TotalTensorComplex.homotopyCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of cochain complexes of modules over a commutative ring is symmetric
monoidal under the total tensor product. Its associator and Koszul braiding are induced from the
corresponding canonical constraints on complexes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    ∃ sC : SymmetricCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ),
      (∀ (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n),
        HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L p q n h ≫
            (sC.toBraidedCategory.braiding K L).hom.f n =
          ((p * q).negOnePow : ℤˣ) •
            ((β_ (K.X p) (L.X q)).hom ≫
              HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj L K q p n (by simpa [add_comm] using h))) ∧
      letI := sC
      ∃ mK : MonoidalCategory
          (HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)),
        letI := mK
        ∃ sK : SymmetricCategory
            (HomotopyCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)),
          letI := sK
          Nonempty
            (HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).Braided

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.MonoidalClosed.cochainComplex_symmetricMonoidalClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GWQ**.
Cochain complexes of modules over a commutative ring form a symmetric monoidal closed category.
The concrete Hom complexes, with pre- and postcomposition on morphisms, form a bifunctor
naturally isomorphic to the internal Hom bifunctor. Under this isomorphism, the closed-structure
adjunction, after applying the symmetry `K ⊗ L ≅ L ⊗ K`, is the canonical currying isomorphism of
Hom complexes. Moreover, a degree-zero cochain is the cochain of a unique morphism of complexes
if and only if its differential vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem cochainComplex_symmetricMonoidalClosed (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    ∃ (s : SymmetricCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)),
      letI := s
      ∃ (closed : MonoidalClosed (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)),
        letI := closed
        ∃ (H : (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)ᵒᵖ ⥤
            CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ ⥤ CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
          (hObj : ∀ (L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ),
            (H.obj (Opposite.op L)).obj M = HomComplexR R L M),
          (∀ (L M N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : M ⟶ N),
            (H.obj (Opposite.op L)).map f =
              eqToHom (hObj L M) ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R L M N f ≫ eqToHom (hObj
                L N).symm) ∧
          (∀ (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ L),
            (H.map f.op).app M =
              eqToHom (hObj L M) ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R K L M f ≫ eqToHom (hObj
                K M).symm) ∧
          ∃ e : MonoidalClosed.internalHom ≅ H,
            (∀ (L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : Cochain L M 0),
                (∃! φ : L ⟶ M, Cochain.ofHom φ = f) ↔ δ 0 1 f = 0) ∧
            ∀ (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
                (φ : K ⟶ HomComplexR R L M),
              Cochain.ofHom
                  ((s.toBraidedCategory.braiding K L).hom ≫
                    MonoidalClosed.uncurry
                      (φ ≫ eqToHom (hObj L M).symm ≫ (e.app (Opposite.op L)).inv.app M)) =
                (Stacks.HomComplex.Currying.curryIso K L M).hom.f 0 (Cochain.ofHom φ)

declarations.name: TotalTensorComplex.cochainComplex_symmetricMonoidalCategory
declarations.doc:
The category of cochain complexes of modules over a commutative ring, with tensor product
given by the total complex of the degreewise tensor product, is symmetric monoidal. On the
summand of bidegree `(p, q)`, its braiding is the ordinary symmetry of tensor products multiplied
by the Koszul sign `(-1)^(p*q)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cochainComplex_symmetricMonoidalCategory (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    ∃ s : SymmetricCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ),
      ∀ (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n),
        HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj K L p q n h ≫
            (s.toBraidedCategory.braiding K L).hom.f n =
          ((p * q).negOnePow : ℤˣ) •
            ((β_ (K.X p) (L.X q)).hom ≫
              HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj L K q p n (by simpa [add_comm] using h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp_surjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWS.** If `f` is surjective, `f ≫ g` is locally
quasi-finite, and `g` is locally of finite type, then `g` is locally quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp_surjective
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [Surjective f]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ g)]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite (f ≫ g)]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] :
    LocallyQuasiFinite g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_hom_of_punctured_and_stalk
declarations.doc:
Morphisms from a scheme are glued uniquely from its punctured complement and the local
scheme at a closed point, when the target is locally of finite presentation over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_hom_of_punctured_and_stalk
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (fX : X ⟶ S) (fY : Y ⟶ S)
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation fY] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    let U : X.Opens := ⟨({x} : Set X)ᶜ, hx.isOpen_compl⟩
    ∀ (_hU : QuasiCompact U.ι)
      (a : U.toScheme ⟶ Y) (b : Spec (X.presheaf.stalk x) ⟶ Y),
      a ≫ fY = U.ι ≫ fX →
      b ≫ fY = X.fromSpecStalk x ≫ fX →
      pullback.fst U.ι (X.fromSpecStalk x) ≫ a =
        pullback.snd U.ι (X.fromSpecStalk x) ≫ b →
      ∃! f : X ⟶ Y,
        (f ≫ fY = fX) ∧ (U.ι ≫ f = a) ∧ (X.fromSpecStalk x ≫ f = b)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag05JXGeneral.universallyClosed_tfae_essentiallyFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWV.**  Over a Nagata base `S`, for a quasi-compact `f : X ⟶ Y` with
`X` and `Y` locally of finite type over `S`, universal closedness, closedness of every
finite-dimensional affine-space base change, and the essentially-finite-type one-dimensional
extension test are equivalent.

Three of the four edges come from the Nagata files; the fourth, `2 ⇒ 1`, is Stacks `05JX`
(3) ⇒ (1), proved in `Basic.lean` for an arbitrary quasi-compact morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_tfae_essentiallyFiniteType
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : X ⟶ S) (hY : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ hY = hX) (hS : IsNagataScheme S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType hX] [LocallyOfFiniteType hY] [QuasiCompact f] :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed f,
       ∀ n : ℕ, IsClosedMap (AffineSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) f),
       HasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeExtension f hY]

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NagataValuativeCriterion.isSeparated_iff_hasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeUniqueness
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWW.**  Over a Nagata base `S`, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` between schemes
locally of finite type over `S` is separated if and only if the lift in every one-dimensional
finite-type test diagram is unique.

Uniqueness for a separated morphism holds because `Spec (Frac 𝒪_{C,c}) ⟶ Spec 𝒪_{C,c}` is
dominant and `Spec 𝒪_{C,c}` is reduced.  Conversely the extension condition for the diagonal of
`f` follows from the assumed uniqueness, and tag `0GWV` turns it into universal closedness of the
diagonal, which for an immersion means that it is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_hasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeUniqueness
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : X ⟶ S) (hY : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ hY = hX) (hS : IsNagataScheme S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType hX] [LocallyOfFiniteType hY] :
    IsSeparated f ↔ HasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeUniqueness f hY

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NagataValuativeCriterion.isSeparated_iff_hasAtMostOneLiftOverPuncturedCurves
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWW.**  Let `S` be a Nagata scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism
of schemes locally of finite type over `S`.  Then `f` is separated if and only if, for every
normal integral scheme `C` of finite type over `S`, every closed point `c ∈ C` with
`dim 𝒪_{C,c} = 1`, and every commutative square over `S` with `C \ {c} ⟶ X` along the top and
`C ⟶ Y` along the bottom, at most one `Spec 𝒪_{C,c} ⟶ X` makes the induced square from
`Spec (Frac 𝒪_{C,c}) ⟶ Spec 𝒪_{C,c}` to `f` commute.

This is `isSeparated_iff_hasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeUniqueness`, whose condition is
equivalent to this one by `hasAtMostOneLiftOverPuncturedCurves_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_iff_hasAtMostOneLiftOverPuncturedCurves
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : X ⟶ S) (hY : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ hY = hX) (hS : IsNagataScheme S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType hX] [LocallyOfFiniteType hY] :
    IsSeparated f ↔ HasAtMostOneLiftOverPuncturedCurves hX hY f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.NagataValuativeCriterion.isProper_iff_hasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GWX.**  Over a Nagata base `S`, a quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`
between schemes locally of finite type over `S` is proper if and only if every one-dimensional
finite-type test diagram admits exactly one lift.

This is formal from tags `0GWV` and `0GWW` and the definition of a proper morphism as one that is
locally of finite type, separated and universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_iff_hasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeLift
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : X ⟶ S) (hY : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : f ≫ hY = hX) (hS : IsNagataScheme S)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType hX] [LocallyOfFiniteType hY] [QuasiCompact f] :
    IsProper f ↔ HasEssentiallyFiniteTypeValuativeLift f hY

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.stalkHomology_isZero_iff_hom_residueFieldSkyscraper_subsingleton
declarations.doc:
For a bounded complex with coherent cohomology, stalk cohomology above `b`
vanishes exactly when all maps to the residue-field skyscraper in those degrees vanish.
declarations.statement:
public theorem stalkHomology_isZero_iff_hom_residueFieldSkyscraper_subsingleton
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (x : X)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf)]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Bounded (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ,
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj K.obj).IsCoherent)
    (b : ℤ) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero (OXModule.stalk
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj K.obj) x)) ↔
    (∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      Subsingleton (K.obj ⟶
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) i).obj
          (residueFieldSkyscraper X x)))

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedVarieties.Orlov.essImage_of_agree_on_zeroDimensional
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X`, `Y` be proper schemes over `k` with
`X` regular. Let `F, G : D_perf(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_perf(𝒪_Y)` be `k`-linear exact functors such that
(1) `F(𝓕) ≅ G(𝓕)` for every coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` with `dim Supp(𝓕) = 0`, and (2) `F` is
fully faithful. Then the essential image of `G` is contained in the essential image of `F`.

The coherent module `𝓕` is read in `D_perf(𝒪_X)` placed in degree zero; the hypothesis asks for
the isomorphism for every proof that it is perfect, which is automatic on a regular scheme
(`isPerfect_single_of_isCoherent`).
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_of_agree_on_zeroDimensional (hX : IsRegular X.left)
    (F G : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left ⥤ PerfectDerivedCategory Y.left)
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] [F.Linear k] [G.CommShift ℤ] [G.IsTriangulated]
    [G.Linear k]
    (hagree : ∀ (M : X.left.Modules), M.IsCoherent →
      topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp M) = 0 →
      ∀ (hM : IsPerfect (X := X.left.toRingedSpace)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules 0).obj M)),
        Nonempty (F.obj (⟨_, hM⟩ : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left) ≅
          G.obj (⟨_, hM⟩ : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left)))
    (hFF : Nonempty F.FullyFaithful) (E : PerfectDerivedCategory X.left) :
    F.essImage (G.obj E)

declarations.name: RingHom.isTaut_completion

    letI : UniformSpace A := IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A
    letI : IsUniformAddGroup A := isUniformAddGroup_of_addCommGroup
    RingHom.IsTaut (UniformSpace.Completion.coeRingHom :
      A →+* UniformSpace.Completion A)

declarations.name: RingHom.isTaut_comp

declarations.name: RingHom.isTaut_completedTensorProduct_baseChange
declarations.doc: Completed tensor-product base change preserves a taut homomorphism.

declarations.name: RingHom.isWeaklyPreAdmissible_of_isTaut

Weak pre-admissibility ascends along a continuous taut homomorphism of

Pre-admissibility ascends along a continuous taut homomorphism of linearly topologized

    (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C) (hf_continuous : Continuous f)

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdic
declarations.doc:
A linearly topologized ring is *weakly pre-adic* if the closures of the powers of some
ideal are open and form a neighborhood basis at zero.
declarations.statement:
public class IsWeaklyPreAdic (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdic
declarations.doc:
A linearly topologized ring is *weakly adic* if it is weakly pre-adic, complete, and
separated. Completeness uses the canonical uniformity of its additive topological group.
declarations.statement:
public class IsWeaklyAdic (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] : Prop extends IsWeaklyPreAdic A, T2Space A
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.weaklyPreAdic_tfae
declarations.doc: The four equivalent characterizations of a weakly pre-adic linearly topologized ring.
declarations.statement:
public lemma weaklyPreAdic_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A] :
    List.TFAE
      [ TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdic A,
        HasTautPreAdicSource.{u, max u v} A,
        TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible A ∧
          ∃ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧
            (∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → IsOpen ((I ^ n).topologicalClosure : Set A)),
        TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible A ∧
          (∀ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I →
            ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → IsOpen ((I ^ n).topologicalClosure : Set A)) ]
declarations.comment: weakly_pre_adic_characterizations

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isLinearTopology_completion

declarations.statement:

    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A] :
    letI : UniformSpace A := IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A
    letI : IsUniformAddGroup A := isUniformAddGroup_of_addCommGroup
    IsLinearTopology (UniformSpace.Completion A) (UniformSpace.Completion A)
declarations.comment: completion_weakly_adic

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isWeaklyAdic_completion
declarations.doc: The completion of a weakly pre-adic linearly topologized ring is weakly adic.
declarations.statement:
public instance isWeaklyAdic_completion (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A] [TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdic A] :
    letI : UniformSpace A := IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A
    letI : IsUniformAddGroup A := isUniformAddGroup_of_addCommGroup
    TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdic (UniformSpace.Completion A)
declarations.comment: completion_weakly_adic

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isAdmissible_of_isWeaklyAdic

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_countable_basis_open_ideals
declarations.doc:
A weakly adic linearly topologized ring has a countable fundamental system of open
ideals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_countable_basis_open_ideals (A : Type*) [CommRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdic A] :
    ∃ I : ℕ → Ideal A, (∀ n : ℕ, IsOpen (I n : Set A)) ∧
      (𝓝 (0 : A)).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True) (fun n ↦ (I n : Set A))
declarations.comment: weakly_adic_countable_basis

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_fg_isAdic_of_fg_closure_powers_basis
declarations.doc:
A complete linearly topologized ring whose topology is the fundamental system given by the
closures of the powers of a finitely generated ideal is adic with a finitely generated ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_fg_isAdic_of_fg_closure_powers_basis
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [T2Space A]
    [hcomplete : @CompleteSpace A (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A)]
    (I : Ideal A) (hIfg : I.FG)
    (hopen : ∀ n : ℕ, IsOpen ((I ^ n).topologicalClosure : Set A))
    (hbasis : (𝓝 (0 : A)).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True)
      (fun n ↦ ((I ^ n).topologicalClosure : Set A))) :
    ∃ J : Ideal A, J.FG ∧ _root_.IsAdic J

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_fg_isAdic_of_quotient_closure_sq_finite
declarations.doc:
A weakly adic ring with an ideal of definition `I` for which
`I / closure(I ^ 2)` is finite has a finitely generated ideal defining its topology.
declarations.statement:

    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdic A]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition I)
    [Module.Finite A
      (I ⧸ Submodule.comap I.subtype (I ^ 2).topologicalClosure)] :
    ∃ J : Ideal A, J.FG ∧ _root_.IsAdic J

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isWeaklyPreAdic_of_isTaut

The target of a continuous taut homomorphism from a weakly pre-adic linearly topologized
