declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isCountablyGenerated_nhds_zero_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
declarations.doc:
A countable fundamental system of open ideals descends along a continuous taut map
whose induced maps on quotients by open ideals are faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCountablyGenerated_nhds_zero_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hφ_taut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hφ_quotient : ∀ (I : Ideal A), IsOpen (I : Set A) →
      (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.closure (I.map φ)) φ
        (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (fun _ hx ↦ subset_closure hx))).FaithfullyFlat)
    (hB : (nhds (0 : B)).IsCountablyGenerated) :
    (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isWeaklyPreAdmissible_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
declarations.doc:
Weak pre-admissibility descends along a taut map when the induced
maps on quotients by open ideals and their closed extensions are faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isWeaklyPreAdmissible_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B)
    (hφ_taut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hφ_quotient : ∀ I : Ideal A, IsOpen (I : Set A) →
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I := I) (Ideal.closure (I.map φ)) φ (by
        exact Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp
          (show I.map φ ≤ Ideal.closure (I.map φ) from
            fun _ hx ↦ subset_closure hx))).FaithfullyFlat)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdmissible B) :
    TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdmissible A

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isPreAdmissible_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
declarations.doc:
Pre-admissibility descends along a continuous taut homomorphism when all of the induced maps
on quotients by open ideals and their closed extensions are faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPreAdmissible_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ) (hφ_taut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hφ_quotient : ∀ (I : Ideal A), IsOpen (I : Set A) →
      (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.closure (I.map φ)) φ
        (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (fun _ hx ↦ subset_closure hx))).FaithfullyFlat)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible B) :
    TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible A

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isWeaklyPreAdic_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
declarations.doc:
Weak pre-adicness descends along a continuous taut homomorphism when all maps on the
corresponding quotients by open ideals are faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isWeaklyPreAdic_of_isTaut_of_faithfullyFlat_quotient
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ) (hφ_taut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hquot : ∀ I : Ideal A, IsOpen (I : Set A) →
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I := I) (Ideal.closure (I.map φ)) φ (by
        exact Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp
          (show I.map φ ≤ Ideal.closure (I.map φ) from
            fun _ hx ↦ subset_closure hx))).FaithfullyFlat)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdic B) : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyPreAdic A

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_fg_ideal_of_definition_of_taut
declarations.doc:
Adicness with a finitely generated ideal of definition descends along a continuous taut
homomorphism when all the induced maps modulo open ideals are faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fg_ideal_of_definition_of_taut
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    [@CompleteSpace A (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A)] [T2Space A]
    [@CompleteSpace B (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace B)] [T2Space B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (_hφ : Continuous φ) (_htaut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (_hquot : ∀ I : Ideal A, IsOpen (I : Set A) →
      (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.closure (I.map φ)) φ
        (Ideal.le_comap_of_map_le
          (show I.map φ ≤ Ideal.closure (I.map φ) from subset_closure))).FaithfullyFlat)
    (_hB : ∃ J : Ideal B, _root_.IsAdic J ∧ J.FG) :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, _root_.IsAdic I ∧ I.FG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_iff_of_isSurjective_of_isRepresentableFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S`
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and flat. Then `X` is countably indexed
and classical if and only if `Y` is.

The countably indexed half is Stacks 0AKS. For the classical half, a presenting ring `A` of `Y`
with a continuous taut homomorphism `A → C` to a presenting ring of `X` whose maps on quotients
by open ideals are faithfully flat is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isTaut_faithfullyFlat_presentingRing_of_surjective_flat`,
and pre-admissibility descends along it by Stacks 0GXN.
declarations.statement: alias isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_iff_of_isSurjective_of_isRepresentableFlat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_iff_of_surjective_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S`
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and flat. Then `X` is countably indexed
and classical if and only if `Y` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_iff_of_surjective_flat {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hflat : IsRepresentableFlat B S hS f) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X ∧ IsClassical B S hS X ↔
      IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y ∧ IsClassical B S hS Y
declarations.comment: the equivalence, at the source's own hypotheses. Stacks 0AKN is the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`; the countably indexed half of the forward implication is `isCountablyIndexed_target_of_surjective_flat`, the presenting ring of the target with its continuous taut homomorphism to that of the source is `exists_isTaut_faithfullyFlat_presentingRing_of_surjective_flat`, and pre-admissibility descends along it by Stacks 0GXN; the reverse implication is clause (3) of Stacks 0AKP, the library's `isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_of_relative_isAffineHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_iff_of_surjective_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S`
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and flat. Then `X` is weakly adic if
and only if `Y` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAdic_iff_of_surjective_flat {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hflat : IsRepresentableFlat B S hS f) :
    IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X ↔ IsWeaklyAdic B S hS Y
declarations.comment: the equivalence, at the source's own hypotheses. Stacks 0AKN is the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`; the presenting ring of the target with its continuous taut homomorphism to that of the source is `exists_isTaut_faithfullyFlat_presentingRing_of_surjective_flat`, which takes countable indexing of the source from item (5) of Stacks 0AIK. The forward implication is the library's Stacks 0GXP and the reverse one is clause (4) of Stacks 0AKP, the library's `isWeaklyAdic_of_relative_isAffineHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_iff_of_surjective_flat'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S`
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and flat. Then `X` is weakly adic if
and only if `Y` is.
declarations.statement: alias isWeaklyAdic_iff_of_surjective_flat'
declarations.comment: the equivalence, at the source's own hypotheses. The presenting ring of the target together with the continuous taut homomorphism to the source's, which is Stacks 0AN0, the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5 and the identification of Stacks 0AMZ, is the library's `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace``.exists_isTaut_faithfullyFlat_presentingRing_of_surjective_flat`, which takes countable indexing of the source from item (5) of Stacks 0AIK; Stacks 0AKN is the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`. The forward implication is the library's Stacks 0GXP and the reverse one is clause (3) of Stacks 0AKQ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXU.** The completion `X^∧_Z` of an algebraic space `X` over `S` along a closed
subspace `Z`: the fppf sheafification of the union of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of `Z`
in `X`, which is their colimit in fppf sheaves.
declarations.statement:
def completionSubspace (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (Z : Subfunctor X.1) :
    Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: the completion along a closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_completionSubspaceMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXV.** Completion along a closed subspace is compatible with base change: for a
morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` and a subfunctor `Z` of `X`, in the source a
closed subspace, the square formed by the completion of `X'` along `Z' = f⁻¹(Z) = X' ×_X Z`,
the completion of `X` along `Z` and the two ambient sheaves is a cartesian square of fppf
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_completionSubspaceMap {X' X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (Z : Subfunctor X.1) :
    IsPullback
      (completionSubspaceToAmbient B S hS X' (Z.preimage f.hom))
      (completionSubspaceMap B S hS f Z)
      (sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS f.hom)
      (completionSubspaceToAmbient B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: the square is cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_completionSubspaceMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXV.** For a morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` and a subfunctor
`Z` of `X`, in the source a closed subspace, the induced morphism of completions
`(X')^∧_{f⁻¹(Z)} ⟶ X^∧_Z` is representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_completionSubspaceMap
    {X' X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X' ⟶ X) (Z : Subfunctor X.1) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (completionSubspaceMap B S hS f Z).hom
declarations.comment: representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isReduction_completionSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXW.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed
subspace. The reduction of the completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is `Z_red`: the composite
`Z_red ⟶ Z ⟶ X^∧_Z` exhibits `Z_red` as the reduction of the completion.

The hypothesis is that the canonical morphism `Z ⟶ X^∧_Z` is a representable thickening. That
is exactly what it is: `Z = Z_0` is a stage of the colimit presentation of `X^∧_Z` by the
infinitesimal neighbourhoods of `Z`, whose transition morphisms are thickenings, so Stacks
0AI9 applies. The library has Stacks 0AI9 only for a colimit of *affine* objects of the site,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isThickening_colimitι`, which is why the property is carried
here as a hypothesis; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduction_completionSubspace
    (hc : Space.IsRepresentableThickeningULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (closedSubspaceToCompletionSubspace B S hS hX Z hZ).hom) :
    IsReduction B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS ⟨X, hX⟩ Z)
      (reductionOfClosedSubspaceSheaf B S hS hX Z hZ)
      (reductionInclusion B S hS hX Z hZ ≫
        closedSubspaceToCompletionSubspace B S hS hX Z hZ)
declarations.comment: the whole statement, under the additional hypothesis that the canonical morphism `Z ⟶ X^∧_Z` is a representable thickening; that is Tag 0AI9 for a colimit of algebraic spaces, which is available here only for a colimit of affine objects of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isReduction_completionSubspace'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXW.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed
subspace. The reduction of the completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is `Z_red`: the composite
`Z_red ⟶ Z ⟶ X^∧_Z` exhibits `Z_red` as the reduction of the completion.

Both morphisms are representable thickenings — the first because `Z_red` is a closed subspace
of `X` contained in `Z` with the same point set, the second by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableThickeningULift_toCompletionSubspace` — and
`Z_red` is a reduced algebraic space, so the composite exhibits it as the reduction.

This is the unconditional form of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isReduction_completionSubspace`, which takes the
representability of `Z ⟶ X^∧_Z` as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReduction_completionSubspace' :
    IsReduction B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS ⟨X, hX⟩ Z)
      (reductionOfClosedSubspaceSheaf B S hS hX Z hZ)
      (reductionInclusion B S hS hX Z hZ ≫
        closedSubspaceToCompletionSubspace B S hS hX Z hZ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_completionAlongIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXX (1).** For an affine scheme `X = Spec A` over `S` and the closed subscheme
`Z ⊆ X` of an ideal `I ⊆ A`, the completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is a weakly adic affine
formal algebraic space: it is the formal spectrum of the `I`-adic completion of `A`, whose
topology is given by the closures of the powers of the ideal generated by `I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isWeaklyAdic_completionAlongIdeal (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (f : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (I : Ideal A) :
    IsWeaklyAdic B S hS (completionAlongIdeal B S hS f hA I)
declarations.comment: clause (1): weakly adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdic_and_iso_formalSpectrum_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXX (2).** If `I` is finitely generated then the completion `X^∧_Z` of
`X = Spec A` along the closed subscheme `Z` of `I` is `Spf (A^∧)` for the `I`-adic completion
`A^∧` of `A`: the topology of `A^∧` is the adic topology of the ideal `I A^∧`, and `X^∧_Z` is
the formal spectrum of `A^∧`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdic_and_iso_formalSpectrum_adicCompletion (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (f : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    _root_.IsAdic (Ideal.map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A)) I) ∧
      Nonempty (completionAlongIdeal B S hS f hA I ≅
        formalSpectrum (adicCompletionQuotientSystem B S hS f hA I))
declarations.comment: clause (2): formal spectrum of the adic completion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_completionAlongIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXX (3).** If `I` is finitely generated — equivalently, if the closed subscheme
`Z ⊆ X = Spec A` of `I` is of finite presentation over `X` — then the completion `X^∧_Z` is an
adic\* affine formal algebraic space: it is presented by the `I`-adic completion of `A`, which
is adic with the finitely generated ideal of definition `I A^∧`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdicStar_completionAlongIdeal (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (f : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS (completionAlongIdeal B S hS f hA I)
declarations.comment: clause (3): adic star

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_completionAlongIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXX (4).** For an affine scheme `X = Spec A` over `S` with `A` Noetherian and the
closed subscheme `Z ⊆ X` of an ideal `J ⊆ A`, the completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is a
Noetherian affine formal algebraic space: it is presented by the `J`-adic completion of `A`,
which is a Noetherian ring by Stacks 0316 and which is adic with the finitely generated ideal
of definition `J A^∧` by Stacks 0GXX (2), the ideal `J` being finitely generated because `A` is
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_completionAlongIdeal {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (str : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (J : Ideal A) :
    IsNoetherian B S hS (completionAlongIdeal B S hS str hA J)
declarations.comment: clause (4): Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyWeaklyAdic_completionSubspace_of_isClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXY (1).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace. The completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is *locally weakly
adic*.

The completions of the affine étale charts of `X` along the inverse images of `Z` form an atlas
of `X^∧_Z` (Stacks 0GXV), each is the completion of an affine scheme along an ideal, hence
weakly adic by Stacks 0GXX (1), and `X^∧_Z` satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Stacks
0AIS by `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSubspace`.
declarations.comment: part (1): locally weakly adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSubspace_of_isClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXY (2).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace such that `Z ⟶ X` is of finite presentation. The completion
`X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is *locally adic\**.

As in clause (1), with the members of the atlas adic\* by Stacks 0GXX (3): finite presentation
of `Z ⟶ X` makes the ideal cutting out the inverse image of `Z` on an affine chart finitely
generated, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fg_closedChartIdeal_of_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAdicStar_completionSubspace_of_isClosedSubspace {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (Z : Subfunctor X.1) (hZ : Space.IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z)
    (hZfp : Space.IsFinitePresentation B S hS Z.ι) :
    IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: part (2): locally adic star

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionSubspace_of_isClosedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXY (3).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space
over `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace. The completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is
*locally Noetherian*.

As in clause (1), with the members of the atlas Noetherian by Stacks 0GXX (4),
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_completionAlongIdeal`: local Noetherianness of `X`
is local in the étale topology (Stacks 03E8), so every étale chart of `X` is a locally
Noetherian scheme and its ring of regular functions is Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_completionSubspace_of_isClosedSubspace {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (Z : Subfunctor X.1) (hZ : Space.IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z)
    (hXN : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1
      (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: part (3): locally Noetherian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyWeaklyAdic_completionSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXY (1).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace. The completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is *locally weakly
adic*: the completions of the affine charts of `X` along the inverse images of `Z` form an
atlas of `X^∧_Z`, and each of them is a weakly adic affine formal algebraic space by Stacks
0GXX (1).

The charts of `X` and the identification of their completions with completions of affine
schemes along ideals are carried as hypotheses, as is the set-theoretic condition of Stacks
0AIS; see the section "What is assumed" of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyWeaklyAdic_completionSubspace
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Z : Subfunctor X.1)
    {Ix : Type (u + 1)} (Xi : Ix → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hf : ∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ q ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom).hom hfi)
    (hcov : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
          Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i ↦ Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom))
    (hchart : ∀ i, ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (str : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
      (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (J : Ideal A),
      Nonempty (Space.completionSubspace B S hS (Xi i) (Z.preimage (f i).hom) ≅
        completionAlongIdeal B S hS str hA J))
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)) :
    IsLocallyWeaklyAdic B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: part (1): locally weakly adic; charts and 0AIS condition assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXY (2).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace with `Z ⟶ X` of finite presentation. The completion `X^∧_Z` of
`X` along `Z` is *locally adic\**: the completions of the affine charts of `X` along the
inverse images of `Z` form an atlas of `X^∧_Z`, and each of them is an adic\* affine formal
algebraic space by Stacks 0GXX (3), finite presentation of `Z ⟶ X` saying on an affine chart
`Spec A` that the ideal cutting out the inverse image of `Z` is finitely generated.

The charts of `X` and the identification of their completions with completions of affine
schemes along finitely generated ideals are carried as hypotheses, as is the set-theoretic
condition of Stacks 0AIS; see the section "What is assumed" of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAdicStar_completionSubspace
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Z : Subfunctor X.1)
    {Ix : Type (u + 1)} (Xi : Ix → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hf : ∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ q ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom).hom hfi)
    (hcov : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
          Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i ↦ Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom))
    (hchart : ∀ i, ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (str : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
      (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (J : Ideal A), J.FG ∧
      Nonempty (Space.completionSubspace B S hS (Xi i) (Z.preimage (f i).hom) ≅
        completionAlongIdeal B S hS str hA J))
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)) :
    IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: part (2): locally adic star; charts and 0AIS condition assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GXY (3).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space
over `S` and let `Z ⊆ X` be a closed subspace. The completion `X^∧_Z` of `X` along `Z` is
*locally Noetherian*: the completions of the affine charts of `X` along the inverse images of
`Z` form an atlas of `X^∧_Z`, and each of them is presented by the adic completion of the
Noetherian chart ring, which is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition by Stacks
0GXX (2).

The charts of `X` and the identification of their completions with completions of Noetherian
affine schemes along ideals are carried as hypotheses, as is the set-theoretic condition of
Stacks 0AIS; see the section "What is assumed" of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_completionSubspace
    {X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (Z : Subfunctor X.1)
    {Ix : Type (u + 1)} (Xi : Ix → AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hf : ∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ q ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom).hom hfi)
    (hcov : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
          Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i ↦ Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (f i).hom))
    (hchart : ∀ i, ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (str : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
      (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (J : Ideal A) (_ : IsNoetherianRing A),
      Nonempty (Space.completionSubspace B S hS (Xi i) (Z.preimage (f i).hom) ≅
        completionAlongIdeal B S hS str hA J))
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS (Space.completionSubspace B S hS X Z)
declarations.comment: part (3): locally Noetherian; charts and 0AIS condition assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.StrictlyHenselian.subsingleton_H_of_degreeOne_kernel_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring all of whose local rings are strictly henselian and let `F` be an abelian
sheaf on the small étale site of `Spec R`. If for all `f, g ∈ R` the kernel of

`H¹(D(f + g), F) ⟶ H¹(D(f(f + g)), F) ⊕ H¹(D(g(f + g)), F)`

is zero, then `H^q(Spec R, F) = 0` for every `q > 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_H_of_degreeOne_kernel_eq_zero
    (hlocal : ∀ x : Spec (CommRingCat.of R), StrictlyHenselianLocalRing
      ↥((Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).presheaf.stalk x))
    (F : Sheaf (MayerVietoris.topology (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (h₁ : ∀ f g : R, ∀ y : (opensCohomology F 1).obj (op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f + g))),
      (opensCohomology F 1).map
          (homOfLE (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_mul_le_right f (f + g))).op y = 0 →
      (opensCohomology F 1).map
          (homOfLE (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen_mul_le_right g (f + g))).op y = 0 → y = 0)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1} F q)

declarations.name: exists_monic_adjoinRoot_isUnit_sub_mul_root
declarations.doc:
A monogenic extension in which `a - b y` is a unit, when `a` and `b`
are coprime and `a` is a root of unity modulo `b`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_monic_adjoinRoot_isUnit_sub_mul_root
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (a b : A)
    (hab : IsCoprime a b)
    (ha : IsOfFinOrder (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {b}) a)) :
    ∃ P : A[X], P.Monic ∧ Function.Injective (algebraMap A (AdjoinRoot P)) ∧
      IsUnit (algebraMap A (AdjoinRoot P) a -
        algebraMap A (AdjoinRoot P) b * AdjoinRoot.root P)

declarations.name: localizationMap_X
declarations.doc: The canonical map sends `t` to `Φ(s)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationMap_X
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (π : A) (ℓ : ℕ) (Φ : A[X])
    (hΦ : (C π * X + 1) ^ ℓ = C (π ^ ℓ) * Φ + 1) :
    localizationMap A π ℓ Φ hΦ
      (algebraMap A[X] (Localization.Away (C (π ^ ℓ) * X + 1)) X) =
      aeval (algebraMap A[X] (Localization.Away (C π * X + 1)) X) Φ
declarations.comment: the canonical substitution map on the generator

declarations.name: localization_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_power_eq
declarations.doc:
For `Φ` monic of positive degree, the target localization is obtained from
the source localization by adjoining the target variable as a root of the
monic equation `Φ(s) - t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_isAdjoinRootMonic_of_power_eq
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (π : A) (ℓ : ℕ) (Φ : A[X])
    (hΦ : (C π * X + 1) ^ ℓ = C (π ^ ℓ) * Φ + 1)
    (hMonic : Φ.Monic) (hDegree : 0 < Φ.natDegree) :
    ∃ h : @IsAdjoinRootMonic (Localization.Away (C (π ^ ℓ) * X + 1))
        (Localization.Away (C π * X + 1)) _ _
        (localizationMap A π ℓ Φ hΦ).toRingHom.toAlgebra
        (Φ.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away (C (π ^ ℓ) * X + 1))) -
          C (algebraMap A[X] (Localization.Away (C (π ^ ℓ) * X + 1)) X)),
      @IsAdjoinRoot.map (Localization.Away (C (π ^ ℓ) * X + 1))
        (Localization.Away (C π * X + 1)) _ _
        (localizationMap A π ℓ Φ hΦ).toRingHom.toAlgebra _
        (@IsAdjoinRootMonic.toIsAdjoinRoot
          (Localization.Away (C (π ^ ℓ) * X + 1))
          (Localization.Away (C π * X + 1)) _ _
          (localizationMap A π ℓ Φ hΦ).toRingHom.toAlgebra _ h) X =
        algebraMap A[X] (Localization.Away (C π * X + 1)) X
declarations.comment: the monic presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MultiplicativeDeformation.isogenyOnPoints_add
declarations.doc: The map `f` is a morphism of group schemes: it is additive on points.
declarations.statement:
theorem isogenyOnPoints_add {R : Type v} [CommRing R] [Algebra A R]
    (x y : DeformedPoint (ζ - 1) R) :
    isogenyOnPoints ℓ ζ hsplit (x + y)
      = isogenyOnPoints ℓ ζ hsplit x + isogenyOnPoints ℓ ζ hsplit y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MultiplicativeDeformation.constantPoint_add
declarations.doc:
The points `σ_i` form a homomorphism from `ℤ/ℓℤ` to the `A`-points of `G^{(ζ - 1)}`, as in
`σ_i +_G σ_j = σ_{i + j}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantPoint_add
    (hsplit : ∏ k : ZMod ℓ, (X - C (ζ ^ k.val)) = X ^ ℓ - 1)
    (i j : ZMod ℓ) :
    constantPoint ℓ ζ hζ (i + j) = constantPoint ℓ ζ hζ i + constantPoint ℓ ζ hζ j

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MultiplicativeDeformation.isogenyOnPoints_constantPoint
declarations.doc:
The composition of `ℤ/ℓℤ → G^{(ζ - 1)}` with `f` is trivial: the points `σ_i` lie in the
kernel of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isogenyOnPoints_constantPoint (i : ZMod ℓ) :
    isogenyOnPoints ℓ ζ hsplit (constantPoint ℓ ζ hζ i) = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MultiplicativeDeformation.kernelCoordinateRing_algEquiv_pi
declarations.doc:
Exactness at `G^{(ζ - 1)}`: for `ℓ` prime, the closed immersion of the constant group scheme
of `ℤ/ℓℤ` into the kernel of `f` which sends `i` to `σ_i` is an isomorphism. Dually, the
`A`-algebra map from the coordinate ring of the kernel to the functions on `ℤ/ℓℤ` sending `s`
to `i ↦ σ_i` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem kernelCoordinateRing_algEquiv_pi (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) :
    ∃ e : kernelCoordinateRing ℓ ζ hsplit ≃ₐ[A] (ZMod ℓ → A),
      ∀ i : ZMod ℓ,
        e (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (coordinateGenerator (ζ - 1))) i = sigmaPoint ℓ ζ i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MultiplicativeDeformation.isogeny_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc: Exactness at `G^{((ζ - 1) ^ ℓ)}`: the morphism `f` is faithfully flat.
declarations.statement: theorem isogeny_faithfullyFlat : (isogeny ℓ ζ hsplit).toRingHom.FaithfullyFlat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.MultiplicativeDeformation.exists_shortExactSequence_of_groupSchemes
declarations.doc:
The short exact sequence `0 → ℤ/ℓℤ → G^{(ζ - 1)} → G^{((ζ - 1) ^ ℓ)} → 0` is a sequence of
group schemes over `Spec A`, not merely a sequence of groups of `A`-points. The left-hand group
scheme is the constant group scheme of `ℤ/ℓℤ`; the right-hand map is the scheme morphism dual
to the explicitly specified algebra homomorphism `isogeny`. The coordinate of the left-hand map
is pinned to the points `σ_i`, and the pullback square says that it identifies the constant
group scheme with the kernel.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExactSequence_of_groupSchemes (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) :
    ∃ (g : Grp (Over (Spec (.of A)))) (h : Grp (Over (Spec (.of A))))
      (i : constantGroupScheme (Multiplicative (ZMod ℓ)) (Spec (.of A)) ⟶ g) (f : g ⟶ h),
      ∃ (eg : g.X ≅ (Spec (.of (coordinateRing (ζ - 1)))).asOver (Spec (.of A)))
        (eh : h.X ≅ (Spec (.of (coordinateRing ((ζ - 1) ^ ℓ)))).asOver (Spec (.of A))),
        (((eg.inv ⊗ₘ eg.inv) ≫ MonObj.mul (X := g.X) ≫ eg.hom).left =
          (pullbackSpecIso A (coordinateRing (ζ - 1)) (coordinateRing (ζ - 1))).hom ≫
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (comultiplication (ζ - 1)).toRingHom)) ∧
        (((eh.inv ⊗ₘ eh.inv) ≫ MonObj.mul (X := h.X) ≫ eh.hom).left =
          (pullbackSpecIso A (coordinateRing ((ζ - 1) ^ ℓ))
            (coordinateRing ((ζ - 1) ^ ℓ))).hom ≫
            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (comultiplication ((ζ - 1) ^ ℓ)).toRingHom)) ∧
        (CategoryTheory.IsPullback i.hom.hom (toUnit _)
          f.hom.hom (MonObj.one : (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of A)))) ⟶ h.X)) ∧
        (Flat f.hom.hom.left ∧ Surjective f.hom.hom.left) ∧
        (eg.inv ≫ f.hom.hom ≫ eh.hom).left =
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (isogeny ℓ ζ hsplit).toRingHom) ∧
        (∀ j : ZMod ℓ,
          (Spec.preimage
            (constantComponentOver (A := A) ℓ (Multiplicative.ofAdd j) ≫
              i.hom.hom ≫ eg.hom).left).hom
            (coordinateGenerator (ζ - 1)) = sigmaPoint ℓ ζ j)

declarations.name: surjective_precomp_localizationMap_of_isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed
declarations.doc:
Every point of the target of the monogenic map lifts over an absolutely
integrally closed `A`-algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_precomp_localizationMap_of_isAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (π : A) (ℓ : ℕ) (Φ : A[X])
    (hΦ : (C π * X + 1) ^ ℓ = C (π ^ ℓ) * Φ + 1)
    (hMonic : Φ.Monic)
    (hDegree : 0 < Φ.natDegree)
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [Algebra A R]
    (hR : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed R) :
    Function.Surjective (fun g : Localization.Away (C π * X + 1) →ₐ[A] R =>
      g.comp (localizationMap A π ℓ Φ hΦ))

declarations.name: exists_isUnit_one_add_mul_of_comaximal
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be absolutely integrally closed and `π ∈ R` with `1 + π` of finite order. For
comaximal ideals `I` and `J` of `R` there is `s ∈ I` with `s - 1 ∈ J` and `1 + π s` a unit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isUnit_one_add_mul_of_comaximal
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (hR : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed R) (π : R) (hπ : IsOfFinOrder (1 + π))
    (I J : Ideal R) (hIJ : I + J = ⊤) :
    ∃ s : R, IsUnit (1 + π * s) ∧ s ∈ I ∧ s - 1 ∈ J

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.AbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed.subsingleton_H_constantSheaf_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GY7.** Let `R` be an absolutely integrally closed ring and let `M` be a finite
abelian group. Then `H^i_étale(Spec R, M) = 0` for `i > 0`.

This is `subsingleton_H_constantSheaf_of_finite` read on Mathlib's small étale site of `Spec R`,
to which the one-universe model used there is a dense subsite.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_H_constantSheaf_smallEtale (hR : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed R)
    (M : AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) [Finite M] (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1}
      ((constantSheaf (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).smallEtaleTopology
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj M) q)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.AbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed.subsingleton_H_constantSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GY7, with the degree-zero gluing hypothesis `hsub` carried.** Let `R` be an
absolutely integrally closed ring and let `M` be a finite abelian group. Then the étale
cohomology of `Spec R` with coefficients in the constant sheaf `M` vanishes in every positive
degree, provided every section of that constant sheaf over `D(f(f + g)) ∩ D(g(f + g))` is a
difference of sections over `D(f(f + g))` and over `D(g(f + g))`.

This is weaker than Stacks 0GY7, which carries no such hypothesis. In the source, the gluing
statement is where finiteness of `M` is used, through the group-scheme argument of Stacks 0GY4,
0GY5 and 0GY6; here it is a hypothesis, and `[Finite M]` is therefore not used by the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_H_constantSheaf (hR : IsAbsolutelyIntegrallyClosed R)
    (M : AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) [Finite M]
    (hsub : ∀ f g : R,
      SectionsSub ((constantSheaf (MayerVietoris.topology (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj M)
        (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (f * (f + g))) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (g * (f + g))))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u + 1}
      ((constantSheaf (MayerVietoris.topology (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj M) q)
declarations.comment: assuming degree-zero sections over an overlap are differences (hypothesis hsub)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_iso_preadditiveYoneda_of_generating_of_factorsThroughSigma
declarations.doc:
**Brown representability**, weak version: let `𝒟` be a triangulated category with direct
sums and let `E : ι → 𝒟` be a family of objects such that every nonzero object of `𝒟` receives a
nonzero morphism from some `E i`, and such that every morphism from some `E i` to a countable
direct sum `∐ X`, `X : ℕ → 𝒟`, factors through a direct sum `∐ fun n ↦ E (j n)` of members of
the family via a direct sum of morphisms `E (j n) ⟶ X n`. Then a contravariant cohomological
functor `H : 𝒟ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` which transforms direct sums into products is representable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_preadditiveYoneda_of_generating_of_factorsThroughSigma
    {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] [Preadditive D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D] [IsTriangulated D]
    [HasCoproducts.{max w v} D] {ι : Type w} (E : ι → D)
    (hE : ∀ X : D, ¬ IsZero X → ∃ (i : ι) (f : E i ⟶ X), f ≠ 0)
    (hE' : ∀ (X : ℕ → D) (i : ι) (α : E i ⟶ ∐ X), ∃ (j : ℕ → ι) (β : ∀ n, E (j n) ⟶ X n)
      (γ : E i ⟶ ∐ fun n ↦ E (j n)), α = γ ≫ Limits.Sigma.map β)
    (H : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.IsHomological]
    [∀ J : Type (max w v), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) H] :
    ∃ X : D, Nonempty (preadditiveYoneda.obj X ≅ H)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_of_generating_of_factorsThroughSigma
declarations.doc:
Let `D` be a triangulated category with direct sums and let `E : ι → D` be a family of
objects satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of weak Brown representability
[Stacks, Tag 0GYG]: every nonzero object of `D` receives a nonzero morphism from some `E i`, and
every morphism from some `E i` to a countable direct sum `∐ X`, `X : ℕ → D`, factors through a
direct sum `∐ fun n ↦ E (j n)` of members of the family via a direct sum of morphisms
`E (j n) ⟶ X n`. Let `F : D ⥤ D'` be an exact functor of triangulated categories which transforms
direct sums into direct sums. Then `F` has a right adjoint `G`, which is again exact: the
adjunction `F ⊣ G` is a triangulated adjunction for a (unique) `Functor.CommShift ℤ` structure
on `G`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_of_generating_of_factorsThroughSigma
    (F : D ⥤ D') [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ α : Type (max w v), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete α) F]
    {ι : Type w} (E : ι → D)
    (hE : ∀ X : D, ¬ IsZero X → ∃ (i : ι) (f : E i ⟶ X), f ≠ 0)
    (hE' : ∀ (X : ℕ → D) (i : ι) (α : E i ⟶ ∐ X), ∃ (j : ℕ → ι) (β : ∀ n, E (j n) ⟶ X n)
      (γ : E i ⟶ ∐ fun n ↦ E (j n)), α = γ ≫ Limits.Sigma.map β) :
    ∃ (G : D' ⥤ D) (adj : F ⊣ G) (_ : G.CommShift ℤ), adj.IsTriangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.SubcomplexEnlargement.exists_enlargements_killing_kernel_and_covering_image
declarations.doc:
Compatible subcomplexes of quasi-isomorphic complexes after derived base change can be
enlarged, with a bound depending only on the ring map, so that the kernel defect vanishes and the
image defect is covered in every degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_enlargements_killing_kernel_and_covering_image
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v},
      letI : (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max v (max u w)} f).IsLeftAdjoint :=
        ModuleCat.instIsLeftAdjointExtendScalars.{u, v, max u w} f
      let E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ℤ ⥤
          CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) ℤ :=
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max v (max u w)} f).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      let G : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ℤ ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) :=
        E ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} B)
      ∀ (T : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B))
        (α : DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ⋙ T ⟶ G)
        [T.IsLeftDerivedFunctor α
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
        (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ℤ)
        (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) ℤ),
      ∀ (b : E.obj M ⟶ N),
      IsIso (α.app M ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} B)).map b) →
      ∀ (M₁ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ℤ)
        (N₁ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) ℤ)
        (m₁ : M₁ ⟶ M) (n₁ : N₁ ⟶ N) [Mono m₁] [Mono n₁]
        (b₁ : E.obj M₁ ⟶ N₁),
      E.map m₁ ≫ b = b₁ ≫ n₁ →
      ∃ (M₂ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A) ℤ)
        (N₂ : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) ℤ)
        (m₂ : M₂ ⟶ M) (n₂ : N₂ ⟶ N) (_ : Mono m₂) (_ : Mono n₂)
        (m₁₂ : M₁ ⟶ M₂) (n₁₂ : N₁ ⟶ N₂) (_ : Mono m₁₂) (_ : Mono n₁₂)
        (b₂ : E.obj M₂ ⟶ N₂),
      m₁₂ ≫ m₂ = m₁ ∧ n₁₂ ≫ n₂ = n₁ ∧ E.map m₂ ≫ b = b₂ ≫ n₂ ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ,
        let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) i
        kernel.ι (H.map (α.app M₁ ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} B)).map b₁)) ≫
          H.map (T.map
            ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} A)).map m₁₂)) = 0) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ,
        let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v w} B) i
        imageSubobject (H.map
          ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} B)).map n₁₂)) ≤
          imageSubobject (H.map (α.app M₂ ≫
            (DerivedCategory.Q (C := ModuleCat.{max u v w} B)).map b₂))) ∧
      Cardinal.mk ((Σ i : ℤ, M₂.X i) ⊕ (Σ i : ℤ, N₂.X i)) ≤
        max (Cardinal.lift.{w} κ)
          (Cardinal.mk ((Σ i : ℤ, M₁.X i) ⊕ (Σ i : ℤ, N₁.X i)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MittagLefflerCohomology.cohomology_transitionImage_stable_uniformly_of_powerCohomologyGradedACC
declarations.doc:
If the whole graded module `⨁ₙ Hᵖ⁺¹(X, Iⁿ𝓕ₙ₊₁)` satisfies graded ACC, there is a single
lag `c` such that, for every `i`, the image of `Hᵖ(F_(i+c+1)) → Hᵖ(F_(i+1))` is already the
stable image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomology_transitionImage_stable_uniformly_of_powerCohomologyGradedACC
    (I : Ideal A) (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, w} A X) (p : ℕ)
    (hquotient : IsQuotientTower.{u, v, w} I F)
    (hACC : PowerCohomologyHaveGradedACC.{u, v, w} I F (p + 1)) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (i m : ℕ) (h : i + c ≤ m),
      transitionImage (F ⋙ cohomology.{u, v, w} (A := A) (X := X) p)
        i m ((Nat.le_add_right i c).trans h) =
      transitionImage (F ⋙ cohomology.{u, v, w} (A := A) (X := X) p)
        i (i + c) (Nat.le_add_right i c)
declarations.comment: uniform stabilization (footnote)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MittagLefflerCohomology.isMittagLeffler_cohomology_of_powerCohomologyGradedACC
declarations.doc:
If the whole graded module `⨁ₙ Hᵖ⁺¹(X, Iⁿ𝓕ₙ₊₁)` satisfies graded ACC, the degree-`p`
cohomology tower of an ideal-power quotient system satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMittagLeffler_cohomology_of_powerCohomologyGradedACC
    (I : Ideal A) (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, w} A X) (p : ℕ)
    (hquotient : IsQuotientTower.{u, v, w} I F)
    (hACC : PowerCohomologyHaveGradedACC.{u, v, w} I F (p + 1)) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical
      (F ⋙ cohomology.{u, v, w} (A := A) (X := X) p)
declarations.comment: Mittag-Leffler condition

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MittagLefflerCohomology.cohomology_transitionImage_stable_uniformly
declarations.doc:
Under the same hypotheses, there is a single lag `c` such that, for every
`i`, the image of `Hᵖ(F_(i+c+1)) → Hᵖ(F_(i+1))` is already the stable image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomology_transitionImage_stable_uniformly
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Small.{v} A] (I : Ideal A)
    {X : Type w} [TopologicalSpace X]
    [UnivLE.{max w v, v}]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, w} A X) (p : ℕ)
    (hquotient : IsQuotientTower.{u, v, w} I F)
    (hACC : StableImagesHaveGradedACC.{u, v, w} I F (p + 1)) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ (i m : ℕ) (h : i + c ≤ m),
      transitionImage (F ⋙ cohomology.{u, v, w} (A := A) (X := X) p)
        i m ((Nat.le_add_right i c).trans h) =
      transitionImage (F ⋙ cohomology.{u, v, w} (A := A) (X := X) p)
        i (i + c) (Nat.le_add_right i c)
declarations.comment: uniform stabilization (footnote)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.MittagLefflerCohomology.isMittagLeffler_cohomology_of_stableImagesGradedACC
declarations.doc:
If the stable images in degree `p + 1` satisfy graded ACC, the
degree-`p` cohomology tower of an ideal-power quotient system satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMittagLeffler_cohomology_of_stableImagesGradedACC
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Small.{v} A] (I : Ideal A)
    {X : Type w} [TopologicalSpace X]
    [UnivLE.{max w v, v}]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, w} A X) (p : ℕ)
    (hquotient : IsQuotientTower.{u, v, w} I F)
    (hACC : StableImagesHaveGradedACC.{u, v, w} I F (p + 1)) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical
      (F ⋙ cohomology.{u, v, w} (A := A) (X := X) p)
declarations.comment: Mittag-Leffler condition

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.QuotientTowers.cohomologyTowerLimit_topology_eq_adic
declarations.doc:
For a quotient tower of sheaves `F` whose stable images satisfy ACC over `gr_I(A)`, the
inverse-limit topology on `lim Hᵖ(X, F_n)` equals the `I`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomologyTowerLimit_topology_eq_adic
    [Small.{v} A] [UnivLE.{max w v, v}]
    (I : Ideal A) (X : Type w) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, w} A X) (p : ℕ)
    (hquotient : IsQuotientTower.{u, v, w} I F)
    (hACC : StableImagesHaveGradedACC.{u, v, w} I F p) :
    CohomologyTowerLimit.limitTopology (fun n => cohomologyModule.{u, v, w} F p n)
        (cohomologyTransition.{u, v, w} F p) =
      I.adicModuleTopology
        (CohomologyTowerLimit (fun n => cohomologyModule.{u, v, w} F p n)
          (cohomologyTransition.{u, v, w} F p))
declarations.comment: the same conclusion under the stronger ACC hypothesis on the ambient graded

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.QuotientTowers.cohomologyTowerLimit_topology_eq_adic
declarations.doc:
For a quotient tower of sheaves `F` whose stable images satisfy ACC over `gr_I(A)`, the
inverse-limit topology on `lim Hᵖ(X, F_n)` equals the `I`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomologyTowerLimit_topology_eq_adic
    [Small.{v} A] [UnivLE.{max w v, v}]
    (I : Ideal A) (X : Type w) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleSheaf.{u, v, w} A X) (p : ℕ)
    (hquotient : IsQuotientTower.{u, v, w} I F)
    (hACC : StableImagesHaveGradedACC.{u, v, w} I F p) :
    CohomologyTowerLimit.limitTopology (fun n => cohomologyModule.{u, v, w} F p n)
        (cohomologyTransition.{u, v, w} F p) =
      I.adicModuleTopology
        (CohomologyTowerLimit (fun n => cohomologyModule.{u, v, w} F p n)
          (cohomologyTransition.{u, v, w} F p))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AdicInverseSystems.exists_uniform_stable_image
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GYQ**, the footnote: the images of `Hᵖ(C, F_k) → Hᵖ(C, Fᵢ)` are the
stable image already at `k = i + c`, for one `c` independent of `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_stable_image (hacc : WellFoundedGT (GradedSubmodule hF p)) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ i k : ℕ, ∀ h : i + c ≤ k,
      transitionImage (F ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, r, w} O p) i k (by omega) =
        transitionImage (F ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, r, w} O p) i (i + c) (by omega)
declarations.comment: the uniform shift of the footnote

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AdicInverseSystems.isMittagLefflerCategorical_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GYQ.** For an inverse system of sheaves of modules on a site with
`Fₙ = Fₙ₊₁/IⁿFₙ₊₁`, the ascending chain condition on the graded submodules of
`⨁ₙ H^(p+1)(C, IⁿFₙ₊₁)` implies that the inverse system `n ↦ Hᵖ(C, Fₙ)` satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLefflerCategorical_cohomology (hacc : WellFoundedGT (GradedSubmodule hF p)) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical (F ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, r, w} O p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AdicInverseSystems.isMittagLefflerCategorical_cohomology_of_stableImages
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GYR.** For an inverse system of sheaves of modules on a site with
`Fₙ = Fₙ₊₁/IⁿFₙ₊₁`, the ascending chain condition on the graded submodules of `⨁ₙ Nₙ`, where
`Nₙ = ⋂_{m ≥ n} Im(H^(p+1)(C, IⁿF_m) → H^(p+1)(C, IⁿFₙ))`, implies that the inverse system
`n ↦ Hᵖ(C, Fₙ)` satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLefflerCategorical_cohomology_of_stableImages
    (hacc : WellFoundedGT (StableGradedSubmodule hF p)) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical (F ⋙ globalModuleCohomology.{u, v, r, w} O p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AdicInverseSystems.limitTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GYS.** For an inverse system of sheaves of modules on a site with
`Fₙ = Fₙ₊₁/IⁿFₙ₊₁`, the ascending chain condition on `⨁ₙ Hᵖ(C, IⁿFₙ₊₁)` as a graded
`⨁ₙ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹`-module implies that the limit topology on `lim Hᵖ(C, Fₙ)` is the `I`-adic
topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology (hF : IsAdicQuotientSystem O I F) (p : ℕ)
    (hACC : HasGradedACC O I F hF p) :
    Stacks.AdicLimit.towerLimit.limitTopology
        (fun n => ((cohomologySystem O F p).obj (op n) : Type _))
        (cohomologyTransition O F p) =
      I.adicModuleTopology (cohomologyLimit O F p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AdicInverseSystems.limitTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology_of_stableImages
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0GYT.** For an inverse system of sheaves of modules on a site with
`Fₙ = Fₙ₊₁/IⁿFₙ₊₁`, the ascending chain condition on `⨁ₙ Nₙ` as a graded `⨁ₙ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹`-module,
where `Nₙ = ⋂_{m ≥ n} Im(Hᵖ(C, IⁿF_m) → Hᵖ(C, IⁿFₙ))`, implies that the limit topology on
`lim Hᵖ(C, Fₙ)` is the `I`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem limitTopology_eq_adicModuleTopology_of_stableImages
    (hF : IsAdicQuotientSystem O I F) (p : ℕ) (hACC : HasStableGradedACC O I F hF p) :
    Stacks.AdicLimit.towerLimit.limitTopology
        (fun n => ((cohomologySystem O F p).obj (op n) : Type _))
        (cohomologyTransition O F p) =
      I.adicModuleTopology (cohomologyLimit O F p)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianObjects.IsCartesian
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(O)` has cartesian derived sections if for every morphism `U → V` of `C` the
canonical derived base-change comparison `RΓ(V, K) ⊗^L_{O(V)} O(U) ⟶ RΓ(U, K)` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCartesian (K : Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.DMod.{0} O) : Prop
declarations.comment: cartesian-object condition

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianObjects.cartesianDerivedModules
declarations.doc:
The full subcategory `QC(O) ⊆ D(O)` consisting of the objects with cartesian derived
sections.
declarations.statement: abbrev cartesianDerivedModules : Type _
declarations.comment: the full subcategory QC(O)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.isQC_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GYW**, strict fullness: the cartesian objects form a subcategory of `D(O)` closed
under isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
instance isQC_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms (IsQC.{w} bc)
declarations.comment: strictly full

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.isQC_isSaturated
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0GYW**, saturation: a direct summand of a cartesian object is cartesian.
declarations.statement: instance isQC_isSaturated : ObjectProperty.IsSaturated (IsQC.{w} bc)
declarations.comment: saturated

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.isQC_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GYW**, triangulatedness: the cartesian objects form a triangulated subcategory of
`D(O)`.
declarations.statement: instance isQC_isTriangulated : ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated (IsQC.{w} bc)
declarations.comment: triangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.isQC_isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GYW**, direct sums: a direct sum of cartesian objects, indexed by an arbitrary
type, is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
instance isQC_isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (J : Type j) :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (IsQC.{w} bc) (Discrete J)
declarations.comment: arbitrary direct sums

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianSubcategory.isCartesian_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GYW, strict fullness.** The cartesian objects of `D(O)` are closed under isomorphism,
so `QC(O)` is a strictly full subcategory of `D(O)`.
declarations.statement:
instance isCartesian_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms (Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianObjects.IsCartesian
      O hO)
declarations.comment: strictly full

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianSubcategory.isCartesian_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GYW, saturation.** The cartesian objects of `D(O)` are closed under direct summands, so
`QC(O)` is a saturated (thick) subcategory of `D(O)`.
declarations.statement:
instance isCartesian_isSaturated :
    ObjectProperty.IsSaturated (Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianObjects.IsCartesian O hO)
declarations.comment: saturated

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianSubcategory.isCartesian_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GYW, triangulatedness.** `QC(O)` is a triangulated subcategory of `D(O)`: for each
`a : V ⟶ U` the comparison maps are the components of a shift-compatible natural transformation
between triangulated functors, `- ⊗^L_{O(V)} O(U)` being triangulated as a left adjoint of a
triangulated functor, and the locus where such a transformation is invertible is triangulated.
declarations.statement:
instance isCartesian_isTriangulated :
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated (Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianObjects.IsCartesian O hO)
declarations.comment: triangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianSubcategory.isCartesian_isClosedUnderCoproducts_of_smallSite
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GYW, arbitrary direct sums.** `QC(O)` is closed under direct sums indexed by an
arbitrary type. Discarding the zero summands leaves an index type small in the module universe,
because `D(O)` is locally small there by tag 079Q, and both `RΓ(V, -) ⋙ (- ⊗^L_{O(V)} O(U))` and
`RΓ(U, -)` preserve direct sums of that size — the first as a left adjoint, the second as the
derived functor of the exact evaluation. Stated for a small site, the standing smallness
convention of the source.
declarations.statement:
instance isCartesian_isClosedUnderCoproducts_of_smallSite {C : Type} [SmallCategory C]
    (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{0}) (hO : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : O.obj U), x * y = y * x) (J : Type j) :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape
      (Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.CartesianObjects.IsCartesian O hO) (Discrete J)
declarations.comment: arbitrary direct sums

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_subcomplex_containing_sections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GYX in the presheaf model.** There is a cardinal, depending only on the category
and its presheaf of rings, such that every family of prescribed sections of a complex of
`O`-modules is contained in a subcomplex whose number of sections is bounded by the maximum of
that cardinal and the size of the family.

This is the transport of
`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.exists_subcomplex_containing_sections_of_size_le` across the
equivalence between sheaves of modules on the chaotic site and presheaves of modules, which
preserves monomorphisms and identifies the two counts of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subcomplex_containing_sections (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ RingCat.{r}) :
    ∃ kappa : Cardinal.{max u v r w},
      ∀ (F : CochainComplex (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) ℤ)
        (Omega : ∀ (i : ℤ) (U : C), Set ((F.X i).obj (op U))),
        ∃ (H : CochainComplex (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O) ℤ) (inclusion : H ⟶ F),
          Mono inclusion ∧
            (∀ (i : ℤ) (U : C) (x : (F.X i).obj (op U)), x ∈ Omega i U →
              ∃ y : (H.X i).obj (op U), (inclusion.f i).app (op U) y = x) ∧
            complexSectionSize.{w} O H ≤ max kappa (presheafSectionFamilySize.{w} Omega)
declarations.comment: presheaf model

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.exists_subcomplex_containing_sections_of_size_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GYX.** There is a cardinal, depending only on the category and its sheaf of
rings, such that every family of prescribed sections of a complex is contained in a
subcomplex whose size is bounded by the maximum of that cardinal and the size of the
family.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subcomplex_containing_sections_of_size_le
    (R : Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) RingCat.{r}) :
    ∃ kappa : Cardinal.{max u v m r},
      ∀ (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} R) ℤ)
        (Omega : ∀ (i : ℤ) (U : C), Set ((F.X i).val.obj (op U))),
        ∃ (H : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} R) ℤ) (inclusion : H ⟶ F),
          Mono inclusion ∧
            (∀ (i : ℤ) (U : C) (x : (F.X i).val.obj (op U)), x ∈ Omega i U →
              ∃ y : (H.X i).val.obj (op U), (inclusion.f i).val.app (op U) y = x) ∧
            complexSectionSize H ≤ max kappa (sectionFamilySize Omega)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.exists_small_quasiIso_subcomplex_presheaf
declarations.doc:
There is a cardinal, depending only on the category and its sheaf of rings, such that every
complex of presheaves of modules representing a derived object contains a quasi-isomorphic
subcomplex bounded by that cardinal and the size of the derived object.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_quasiIso_subcomplex_presheaf :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v r w},
      ∀ (F : CochainComplex (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} R.obj) ℤ)
        (K : DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} R.obj)),
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ K) →
          ∃ (H : CochainComplex (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} R.obj) ℤ) (f : H ⟶ F),
            Mono f ∧ QuasiIso f ∧
              QuasiCoherentEquivalence.complexSectionSize.{w} R.obj H ≤
                max κ (QuasiCoherentEquivalence.derivedObjectSize.{w} R.obj K)
declarations.comment: presheaf model

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.exists_small_quasiIso_subcomplex
declarations.doc:
There is a cardinal, depending only on the category and its sheaf of rings, such that every
representative of a derived object contains a quasi-isomorphic subcomplex bounded by that cardinal
and the size of the derived object.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_quasiIso_subcomplex :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v m r},
      ∀ (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} R) ℤ)
        (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{m} R)),
        Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F ≅ K) →
          ∃ (H : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} R) ℤ) (f : H ⟶ F),
            Mono f ∧ QuasiIso f ∧
              complexSectionSize H ≤
                max κ (derivedObjectSize R K)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_cardinal_small_nonzero_map_and_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GYZ.** Let `C` be a category, regarded as a site with the chaotic topology, and let
`O` be a presheaf of commutative rings on `C`. There is a cardinal `κ` such that

1. every nonzero object `K` of `QC(O)` receives a nonzero morphism from an object of `QC(O)` of
   size at most `κ`, and
2. every morphism `α : E ⟶ ⨁_n K_n` of `QC(O)` with `|E| ≤ κ` factors through a morphism
   `⨁_n E_n ⟶ ⨁_n K_n` induced by morphisms `E_n ⟶ K_n` of `QC(O)` with `|E_n| ≤ κ`.

Conclusion (1) is `exists_nonzero_map_of_size_le_of_cartesianEnlargement` fed with
`exists_hasCartesianEnlargement`. Conclusion (2) comes from its analogue for `D(O)`,
`exists_factorization_of_sum_of_derivedObjectSize_le`, by replacing each of the summands it
produces with a cartesian object of the same size bound, which is
`exists_small_cartesian_factorization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cardinal_small_nonzero_map_and_factorization (bc : BaseChangeData.{w} O)
    (hO : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : O.obj V), x * y = y * x) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v r w},
      (∀ K : QC.{w} bc, ¬ IsZero K.obj →
          ∃ (E : QC.{w} bc) (f : E ⟶ K), f ≠ 0 ∧ derivedObjectSize.{w} O E.obj ≤ κ) ∧
        (∀ (E : QC.{w} bc) (K : ℕ → QC.{w} bc) (α : E.obj ⟶ ∐ fun n => (K n).obj),
          derivedObjectSize.{w} O E.obj ≤ κ →
          ∃ (E' : ℕ → QC.{w} bc) (f : ∀ n, E' n ⟶ K n)
            (β : E.obj ⟶ ∐ fun n => (E' n).obj),
            (∀ n, derivedObjectSize.{w} O (E' n).obj ≤ κ) ∧
              α = β ≫ Limits.Sigma.map fun n => (QCι.{w} bc).map (f n))
declarations.comment: both conclusions, at one cardinal, for a presheaf of commutative rings

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_factorization_of_sum_of_derivedObjectSize_le
declarations.doc:
**Conclusion (2) of Stacks 0GYZ with the cartesianness demand dropped.** There is a cardinal
`κ₀`, depending only on the category and its presheaf of rings, such that for every cardinal `κ`
above it, every morphism from an object of `D(O)` of size at most `κ` into a countable direct sum
factors through a direct sum of objects of size at most `κ` mapping to the summands.

The conclusion is stated at every `κ ≥ κ₀` rather than at `κ₀` alone — which is the source's
form, recovered by taking `κ = κ₀` — because the hypothesis and the conclusion both read `≤ κ`,
so the property is monotone in neither direction and the form at a single cardinal cannot be
combined with conclusion (1) at one cardinal, as Stacks 0GYZ asserts it is.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_of_sum_of_derivedObjectSize_le :
    ∃ κ₀ : Cardinal.{max u v r w}, ∀ κ : Cardinal.{max u v r w}, κ₀ ≤ κ →
      ∀ (E : DMod.{w} O) (K : ℕ → DMod.{w} O) (α : E ⟶ ∐ K),
        derivedObjectSize.{w} O E ≤ κ →
        ∃ (E' : ℕ → DMod.{w} O) (f : ∀ n, E' n ⟶ K n) (β : E ⟶ ∐ E'),
          (∀ n, derivedObjectSize.{w} O (E' n) ≤ κ) ∧ α = β ≫ Limits.Sigma.map f
declarations.comment: part (2) for D(O) in place of QC(O): cartesianness dropped from the source and from the summands

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_nonzero_map_of_derivedObjectSize_le
declarations.doc:
**Every nonzero object of `D(O)` receives a nonzero morphism from an object of size at most
`singleGeneratorBound O`.** This is the detection step of conclusion (1) of Stacks 0GYZ with the
cartesianness demand dropped from both objects: the subcomplex produced by
`exists_small_subcomplex_detecting_nonzero` is used as the source as it stands, with no
enlargement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_map_of_derivedObjectSize_le (K : DMod.{w} O) (hK : ¬ IsZero K) :
    ∃ (E : DMod.{w} O) (f : E ⟶ K),
      f ≠ 0 ∧ derivedObjectSize.{w} O E ≤ singleGeneratorBound.{w} O
declarations.comment: part (1) for D(O) in place of QC(O): cartesianness dropped from both objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GZ0] part (3) on `D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪)`.** Let `S` be a scheme and let
`(S_affine, 𝒪)` be its small affine Zariski site read with the chaotic topology. An exact functor
`F : D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪) ⥤ D'` of triangulated categories which transforms direct sums into
direct sums has a right adjoint `G`, which is again exact: the adjunction `F ⊣ G` is a
triangulated adjunction for a `Functor.CommShift ℤ` structure on `G`.

No hypothesis is carried: no compact generation, and no quasi-compactness or
quasi-separatedness. The two inputs are [Stacks, Tag 0GZ0] part (3) for the cartesian objects,
which is Brown representability without compact generation, and the identification of
`D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪)` with `QC(S_affine, 𝒪)`, which is the comparison (4) ≃ (5) of
[Stacks, Tag 0GZZ] in the sharp form
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineChaotic_isQC_eq_hasQuasicoherentCohomology`: on the chaotic site
the two subcategories of `D(S_affine, 𝒪)` are equal, not merely equivalent.

This is the abstract input of the Stacks proof of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E], but on the affine site;
nothing here is a statement about `D_QCoh(𝒪_S)`, and Tag 0A9E does not follow. See the coverage
note of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherent
    {D' : Type u'} [Category.{max (u + 1) w} D'] [HasZeroObject D'] [Preadditive D']
    [HasShift D' ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D' n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D']
    (F : (qcohCohomologyProperty.{w} (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS)).FullSubcategory ⥤ D')
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ α : Type (max (u + 1) w), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete α) F] :
    ∃ (G : D' ⥤
        (qcohCohomologyProperty.{w} (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS)).FullSubcategory)
      (adj : F ⊣ G) (_ : G.CommShift ℤ), adj.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: part (3) on D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪) of an arbitrary scheme, through the equality of that subcategory with QC(S_affine, 𝒪) which is the comparison (4) ≃ (5) of Stacks 0GZZ

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_iso_preadditiveYoneda_of_isHomological_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GZ0] part (2).** Let `C` be a category with the chaotic topology, let `O` be a
presheaf of commutative rings on `C` and let `bc` be derived base-change data for `O`. Every
contravariant cohomological functor on `QC(O)` which transforms direct sums into products is
representable.

This is weak Brown representability [Stacks, Tag 0GYG] applied to the generating family
`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_small_generating_family`, which is
[Stacks, Tag 0GYZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_preadditiveYoneda_of_isHomological_unconditional
    (hO : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : O.obj V), x * y = y * x)
    (H : (QC.{w} bc)ᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v r w}) [H.IsHomological]
    [∀ J : Type (max u v r w), PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) H] :
    ∃ K : QC.{w} bc, Nonempty (preadditiveYoneda.obj K ≅ H)
declarations.comment: part (2), for a presheaf of commutative rings

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0GZ0] part (3).** Let `C` be a category with the chaotic topology, let `O` be a
presheaf of commutative rings on `C` and let `bc` be derived base-change data for `O`. An exact
functor `F : QC(O) ⥤ D'` of triangulated categories which transforms direct sums into direct sums
has a right adjoint `G`, which is again exact: the adjunction `F ⊣ G` is a triangulated adjunction
for a `Functor.CommShift ℤ` structure on `G`.

This is Brown representability in the form [Stacks, Tag 0GYH] applied to the generating family
`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_small_generating_family`, which is
[Stacks, Tag 0GYZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint
    (hO : ∀ (V : Cᵒᵖ) (x y : O.obj V), x * y = y * x)
    {D' : Type u'} [Category.{max u v r w} D'] [HasZeroObject D'] [Preadditive D']
    [HasShift D' ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D' n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D']
    (F : QC.{w} bc ⥤ D') [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ α : Type (max u v r w), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete α) F] :
    ∃ (G : D' ⥤ QC.{w} bc) (adj : F ⊣ G) (_ : G.CommShift ℤ), adj.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: part (3), for a presheaf of commutative rings

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_QCι
declarations.doc:

exact right adjoint. The inclusion is exact and transforms direct sums into direct sums, because
`QC(O)` is a triangulated subcategory closed under direct sums ([Stacks, Tag 0GYW]), so this is the

    ∃ (G : DMod.{w} O ⥤ QC.{w} bc) (adj : QCι.{w} bc ⊣ G) (_ : G.CommShift ℤ),
      adj.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: part (4), for a presheaf of commutative rings

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_of_preservesCoproducts

`F : QC(O) ⥤ D` of triangulated categories which transforms direct sums into direct sums has a
right adjoint `G`, and `G` is again exact: the adjunction `F ⊣ G` is triangulated for a (unique)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.PullbackPreservesQuasiCoherent.isQC_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Derived pullback along a morphism of ringed topoi on chaotic sites carries cartesian
objects to cartesian objects.** If the derived sections of `K` are cartesian then so are the
derived sections of `Lg^*K`, the cartesian condition on either side being taken with respect to
the derived base changes along the restriction homomorphisms of the structure sheaf there.

**Stacks 0GZ1.** **Derived pullback along a morphism of ringed topoi carries cartesian
objects to cartesian objects.** If the derived sections of `K` are cartesian then so are the
derived sections of `Lg^*K`, the cartesian condition on either side being taken with respect to
the derived base changes along the restriction homomorphisms of the structure sheaf there.

The derived pullback is supplied as data, together with the computation of its derived sections
of Stacks 0D6D, in the same way that
