declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_tateResolution_koszulPowers
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GZ4.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `f₁, …, f_r ∈ R`. Write `K_m` for the Koszul
divided power algebra `R⟨ξ₁, …, ξ_r⟩` with `ξᵢ` of degree one and `d(ξᵢ) = fᵢ^m`, and `K_M → K_m`
for the transition map `ξᵢ ↦ fᵢ^(M-m) ξᵢ`. Then for every `n` there is an `N ≥ n` and maps
`K_N → A → R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)` and `A → K_n` such that `(A, d, γ)` is a divided power
differential graded algebra as in Definition 09PJ, `A → R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)` is a
quasi-isomorphism, the composition `K_N → A → R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)` is the canonical map, the
composition `K_N → A → K_n` is the transition map, `A₀ = R → R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)` is the canonical
surjection, `A` is a graded divided power polynomial algebra over `R` with finitely many
generators in each degree, and `A → K_n` is a homomorphism of differential graded `R`-algebras
compatible with divided powers inducing the canonical map
`R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N) → R/(f₁^n, …, f_r^n)` on homology in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_tateResolution_koszulPowers [IsNoetherianRing R] (f : Fin r → R) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (hN : n ≤ N) (A : GradedDPAlgebra.{u, u} R) (d : A.carrier →ₗ[R] A.carrier)
        (ι : R →ₐ[R] A.carrier) (ε : A.carrier →ₐ[R] R ⧸ koszulPowerIdeal f N)
        (α : ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R) →ₐ[R] A.carrier)
        (β : A.carrier →ₐ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R)),
      -- (1) `(A, d, γ)` is as in Definition 09PJ
      IsDifferentialGradedAlgebra A.grade d ∧ IsCompatibleWithDifferential A.gamma d ∧
      -- (6) a graded divided power polynomial algebra over `R`, degreewise finitely generated
      (∃ P : GradedDividedPowerPolynomial A.grade A.gamma ι, ∀ i : ℕ, Finite (P.indices i)) ∧
      -- (5) `A₀ = R`, and `A₀ → R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)` is the canonical surjection
      Function.Injective ι ∧
      (∀ a : A.carrier, a ∈ A.grade 0 ↔ ∃ c : R, ι c = a) ∧
      (∀ c : R, ε (ι c) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (koszulPowerIdeal f N) c) ∧
      -- (2) `ε` is a quasi-isomorphism onto `R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)`
      Function.Surjective ε ∧
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (a : A.carrier), 0 < k → a ∈ A.grade k → ε a = 0) ∧
      (∀ a : A.carrier, ε (d a) = 0) ∧
      (∀ a : A.carrier, a ∈ A.grade 0 → ε a = 0 → ∃ b ∈ A.grade 1, d b = a) ∧
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (a : A.carrier), a ∈ A.grade (k + 1) → d a = 0 →
        ∃ b ∈ A.grade (k + 2), d b = a) ∧
      -- `α : K_N → A` is a morphism of differential graded divided power algebras
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (x : ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R)),
        x ∈ exteriorGrade R (Fin r → R) k → α x ∈ A.grade k) ∧
      (∀ x, α (koszulPowerDifferential f N x) = d (α x)) ∧
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (x : ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R)),
        x ∈ positiveEvenPart (exteriorGrade R (Fin r → R)) →
          α ((exteriorDividedPowerStructure R r).dpow k x) = A.gamma.dpow k (α x)) ∧
      -- (7) `β : A → K_n` is a morphism of differential graded divided power algebras
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (a : A.carrier), a ∈ A.grade k → β a ∈ exteriorGrade R (Fin r → R) k) ∧
      (∀ a, β (d a) = koszulPowerDifferential f n (β a)) ∧
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (a : A.carrier), a ∈ positiveEvenPart A.grade →
        β (A.gamma.dpow k a) = (exteriorDividedPowerStructure R r).dpow k (β a)) ∧
      -- (3) the composition `K_N → A → R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N)` is the canonical map
      (∀ x, ε (α x) = koszulPowerAugmentation f N x) ∧
      -- (4) the composition `K_N → A → K_n` is the transition map
      (∀ x, β (α x) = koszulPowerTransitionHom f N n x) ∧
      -- (7) `β` is the identity of `R` in degree zero, hence induces the canonical map
      -- `R/(f₁^N, …, f_r^N) → R/(f₁^n, …, f_r^n)` on homology in degree zero
      (∀ c : R, β (ι c) = algebraMap R (ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R)) c) ∧
      (∀ a : A.carrier, a ∈ A.grade 0 →
        koszulPowerAugmentation f n (β a) =
          Ideal.Quotient.factor (koszulPowerIdeal_le_of_le f hN) (ε a))

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exists_koszulTateProIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GZ5.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `f₁, …, f_r ∈ R`. Write `K_m` for the Koszul
divided power algebra of the `m`-th powers and `K_M → K_m` for its transition maps. Then there
is a sequence of exponents `1 = n₀ < n₁ < n₂ < ⋯`, cofinal in `ℕ`, and for each `i` maps
`K_{nᵢ₊₁} → Aᵢ → R/(f₁^{nᵢ₊₁}, …, f_r^{nᵢ₊₁})` and `Aᵢ → K_{nᵢ}` as in Tag 0GZ4, such that with
`Aᵢ₊₁ → Aᵢ` the composite `Aᵢ₊₁ → K_{nᵢ₊₁} → Aᵢ` the ladder commutes and the two inverse systems
`(K_n)` and `(Aᵢ)` are pro-isomorphic as differential graded `R`-algebras with compatible divided
powers: the composite `K_{nᵢ₊₁} → Aᵢ → K_{nᵢ}` is the Koszul transition map, and the composite
`Aᵢ₊₁ → K_{nᵢ₊₁} → Aᵢ` is the Tate transition map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_koszulTateProIso (f : Fin r → R) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ → ℕ) (stage : ∀ i : ℕ, KoszulTateStage f (n i)),
      n 0 = 1 ∧ StrictMono n ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, ∃ i : ℕ, k ≤ n i) ∧
      (∀ i : ℕ, (stage i).topPower = n (i + 1)) ∧
      -- the upper square of the ladder commutes
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (x : ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R)),
        (stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) ((stage (i + 1)).up x) =
          (stage i).up (koszulPowerTransitionHom f (n (i + 2)) (n (i + 1)) x)) ∧
      -- the lower square of the ladder commutes
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (a : (stage (i + 1)).A.carrier),
        (stage i).down ((stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) a) =
          koszulPowerTransitionHom f (n (i + 1)) (n i) ((stage (i + 1)).down a)) ∧
      -- the composite `K_{nᵢ₊₁} → Aᵢ → K_{nᵢ}` is the transition map of the Koszul system
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (x : ExteriorAlgebra R (Fin r → R)),
        (stage i).down ((stage i).up x) =
          koszulPowerTransitionHom f (n (i + 1)) (n i) x) ∧
      -- the composite `Aᵢ₊₁ → K_{nᵢ₊₁} → Aᵢ` is the transition map of the Tate system
      (∀ i : ℕ, (stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) =
        ((stage i).up).comp ((stage (i + 1)).down)) ∧
      -- the transition maps of the Tate system are maps of differential graded `R`-algebras
      -- with compatible divided powers
      (∀ (i k : ℕ) (a : (stage (i + 1)).A.carrier), a ∈ (stage (i + 1)).A.grade k →
        (stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) a ∈ (stage i).A.grade k) ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (a : (stage (i + 1)).A.carrier),
        (stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) ((stage (i + 1)).d a) =
          (stage i).d ((stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) a)) ∧
      (∀ (i k : ℕ) (a : (stage (i + 1)).A.carrier),
        a ∈ positiveEvenPart (stage (i + 1)).A.grade →
          (stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) ((stage (i + 1)).A.gamma.dpow k a) =
            (stage i).A.gamma.dpow k ((stage (i + 1)).proTransition (stage i) a))

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.exact_degreeZeroHomology_oddVariableExtension
declarations.doc:
Multiplication by the cycle followed by the inclusion into the degree-one
extension is right exact on degree-zero homology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exact_degreeZeroHomology_oddVariableExtension
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] [IsStrictlyGradedComm 𝒜]
    (dA : A →ₗ[R] A) [IsDifferentialGradedAlgebra 𝒜 dA]
    (f : A) (hf_grade : f ∈ 𝒜 0)
    (dExt : OddVariableExtension 𝒜 1 →ₗ[R] OddVariableExtension 𝒜 1)
    [IsDifferentialGradedAlgebra (OddVariableExtension.grade 𝒜 1) dExt]
    (hdExt : ∀ x : A, dExt (OddVariableExtension.inclusion 𝒜 1 x) =
      OddVariableExtension.inclusion 𝒜 1 (dA x))
    (hT : dExt (OddVariableExtension.generator 𝒜 1) =
      OddVariableExtension.inclusion 𝒜 1 f) :
    LinearMap.range (mulOnDegreeZeroHomology 𝒜 dA f hf_grade) =
      LinearMap.ker (toExtensionOnDegreeZeroHomology 𝒜 dA dExt hdExt)
declarations.comment: degree_one

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.surjective_degreeZeroHomology_oddVariableExtension
declarations.doc: The inclusion onto degree-zero homology of the extension is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_degreeZeroHomology_oddVariableExtension
    {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] [IsStrictlyGradedComm 𝒜]
    (dA : A →ₗ[R] A)
    (dExt : OddVariableExtension 𝒜 1 →ₗ[R] OddVariableExtension 𝒜 1)
    (hdExt : ∀ x : A, dExt (OddVariableExtension.inclusion 𝒜 1 x) =
      OddVariableExtension.inclusion 𝒜 1 (dA x)) :
    Function.Surjective
      (toExtensionOnDegreeZeroHomology 𝒜 dA dExt hdExt)
declarations.comment: degree_one

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.evenVariableSpectralSequence_degree_two
declarations.doc:
**The spectral sequence of a degree-two divided-power variable, Tag 0GZ6 part (2).**

Let `(A, dA)` be a strictly graded-commutative differential graded algebra, let `f` be a cycle of
degree `1 = 2 - 1`, and let `A⟨T⟩` be the extension by a divided-power variable of degree two with
`dT = f`, with the differential of Tag 09PM. Filtering `A⟨T⟩` by `Fᵖ = ⨁_{n ≤ p} A T⁽ⁿ⁾` gives a
spectral sequence, and this records the four assertions of the tag:

* its first page in the bidegree with filtration index `i` and total degree `2 i + q` is the
  degree-`q` homology of `A`, by an isomorphism carrying the class of a degree-`q` cycle `ξ` to
  the page class of the representative `ξ T⁽ⁱ⁾`;
* that bidegree is `(i, j)` with `j - i = q`, so the first page in the bidegree `(i, j)` is
  `H_{j - i}(A) · T⁽ⁱ⁾`, as the tag writes it;
* its first differential sends the class of `ξ T⁽ⁱ⁺¹⁾` to the class of
  `(signRingHom 𝒜 1 ξ * f) T⁽ⁱ⁾ = ((-1) ^ q • (ξ f)) T⁽ⁱ⁾`, that is, it is multiplication by `f`
  with the Koszul sign of the degree of `ξ`;
* it converges, the filtration being finite in every degree, and abuts to the homology of the
  complex of `A⟨T⟩`, whose degree-`k` term is the degree-`k` homology of `A⟨T⟩`.

The sign of the first differential is the one of `evenPolynomialDifferential_monomial`; the tag
writes `f ξ` unsigned, which is the same up to the unit `(-1) ^ q` of the coefficient ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem evenVariableSpectralSequence_degree_two (hf_grade : f ∈ 𝒜 1) (hf_cycle : dA f = 0)
    (h0 : ∀ p : P, algebraMap P A p ∈ 𝒜 0) :
    letI : IsDifferentialGradedAlgebra (EvenVariableAlgebra.grade 𝒜 2)
        (evenPolynomialDifferential 𝒜 dA f) :=
      evenPolynomialDifferential_two_isDGA 𝒜 dA f hf_grade hf_cycle
    (∀ i q : ℕ, ∃ e : coefficientHomology 𝒜 dA h0 q ≃ₗ[P]
          ((evenVariableSpectralSequence 𝒜 dA f h0).page 1 le_rfl).X
            (filtrationBidegree true (i : ℤ) ((2 * i + q : ℕ) : ℤ)),
        ∀ ξ : ↥(coefficientCycles 𝒜 dA h0 q),
          e (Submodule.Quotient.mk ξ) = evenVariablePageOneRep 𝒜 dA f h0 i q ξ) ∧
      (∀ i q : ℕ, filtrationBidegree true (i : ℤ) ((2 * i + q : ℕ) : ℤ) =
          ((i : ℤ), (i : ℤ) + q)) ∧
      (∀ (i q : ℕ) (ξ : ↥(coefficientCycles 𝒜 dA h0 q)),
          ((evenVariableSpectralSequence 𝒜 dA f h0).page 1 le_rfl).d
              (filtrationBidegree true ((i + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ((2 * (i + 1) + q : ℕ) : ℤ))
              (filtrationBidegree true (i : ℤ) ((2 * i + (q + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ))
              (evenVariablePageOneRep 𝒜 dA f h0 (i + 1) q ξ) =
            evenVariablePageOneRep 𝒜 dA f h0 i (q + 1)
              ⟨signRingHom 𝒜 1 (ξ : A) * f,
                signRingHom_mul_mem_coefficientCycles 𝒜 dA f h0 hf_grade hf_cycle q ξ⟩ ∧
            signRingHom 𝒜 1 (ξ : A) * f = (-1 : R) ^ q • ((ξ : A) * f)) ∧
      ((evenVariableFiltrationData 𝒜 dA f h0).Converges ∧
        HomologicalSpectralSequenceAbutsTo (evenVariableSpectralSequence 𝒜 dA f h0)
          (fun n => (evenVariableCochainComplex 𝒜 dA f h0).homology (-n)) ∧
        ∀ k : ℕ, Nonempty ((evenVariableCochainComplex 𝒜 dA f h0).homology (-(k : ℤ)) ≅
          ModuleCat.of P (evenVariableHomology 𝒜 dA f h0 k)))
declarations.comment: degree_two

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.range_mulOnGradeHomology_eq_ker_toExtension
declarations.doc:

    [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] [IsStrictlyGradedComm 𝒜] (dA : A →ₗ[R] A)

declarations.name: Koszul.exists_derivedComparisonArrow
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0GZ7.** *"For all `n ≥ t ≥ 1` there exists an `N > n` and a map
`K_t → K_n ⊗_R K_t` in `D(K_N, d)` whose composition with the multiplication map is the
transition map (in either direction)."*

Both composites are asserted: postcomposition with the multiplication map
`μ_n : K_n ⊗_R K_t → K_t` is the transition map `K_t → K_t`, which is the identity, and
precomposition with the multiplication map `μ_N : K_N ⊗_R K_t → K_t` is the transition map
`τ_{N,n} ⊗ id`. Here `K_t` carries the left `K_N`-action through `τ_{N,t}` and `K_n ⊗_R K_t`
carries it through `ξᵢ ↦ fᵢ^{N-n} ξᵢ ⊗ 1`; left differential graded modules are recorded as
right modules over the graded opposite algebra.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedComparisonArrow (f : Fin r → R) {n t : ℕ} (ht : 1 ≤ t) (htn : t ≤ n) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (hnN : n < N),
      ∃ σ : (powDerived f N).obj (powRestrictedModule f ht (htn.trans hnN.le)) ⟶
            (powDerived f N).obj (powTensorRestrictedModule f t (ht.trans htn) hnN.le),
        σ ≫ (powDerived f N).map (powMulHom f ht htn hnN.le) =
            CategoryStruct.id
              ((powDerived f N).obj (powRestrictedModule f ht (htn.trans hnN.le))) ∧
          (powDerived f N).map (powMulBaseHom f ht (htn.trans hnN.le)) ≫ σ =
            (powDerived f N).map (powTransitionTensorHom f t (ht.trans htn) hnN.le)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.Chaotic.QC
declarations.doc:
**The full subcategory `QC(A, d)` of `D(A, d)`**: an object `X` lies in it when, for every
right differential graded `A`-module `M` computing `X` and every morphism `U → V` of the chaotic
site `C`, the canonical map

`RΓ(V, X) ⊗^𝐋_{A(V)} A(U) ⟶ RΓ(U, X)`

is an isomorphism of `D(A(U), d)`. The derived sections `RΓ(U, X)` are the sections `M(U)` over
`U` of such a module, which is what they are on a chaotic site, and the canonical map is the
adjoint transpose of restriction of sections under the adjunction between derived extension of
scalars along `A(V) ⟶ A(U)` and derived restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement: def QC : ObjectProperty (derivedCategory.{t, a, a} A)
declarations.comment: the full subcategory QC(A, d) of D(A, d)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.Chaotic.qc_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isSaturated_isTriangulated_isClosedUnderCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZA.** *Let `C` be a category, viewed as a site with the chaotic topology, let `O`
be a sheaf of rings on `C` and let `(A, d)` be a sheaf of differential graded `O`-algebras. The
subcategory `QC(A, d)` is a strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory of `D(A, d)`
preserved by arbitrary direct sums.*

Here `D(A, d)` is the derived category `SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory`
of Tag 0FT5 with its triangulated structure of Tag 0FT4, and `QC(A, d)` is
`SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.Chaotic.QC` of Tag 0GZ9. The four conjuncts are, in
order: strict fullness (closure under isomorphisms), saturation (closure under direct summands),
triangulatedness, and closure under the direct sums indexed by an arbitrary type of the universe
of the modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem qc_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isSaturated_isTriangulated_isClosedUnderCoproducts :
    (QC A).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ (QC A).IsSaturated ∧ (QC A).IsTriangulated ∧
      ∀ J : Type (max u v), (QC A).IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete J)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.qc_chaoticDerivedPullback_chaotic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZC.** Let `u : C' ⥤ C` be a functor of categories with the chaotic topology,
`g : (Sh(C'), O') → (Sh(C), O)` the induced morphism of ringed topoi together with
`σ : g⁻¹O ⟶ O'`, and `φ : g^*A → A'` a map of sheaves of differential graded `O'`-algebras. Then
the derived pullback `Lg^* : D(A, d) ⥤ D(A', d)` maps `QC(A, d)` into `QC(A', d)`.

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.ChaoticExtension.isEquivalence_qcRestriction
declarations.doc:
*Let `C, O, A` be as in Section 0GZ8. Let `C' ⊂ C` be a full subcategory with the following
property: for every `U ∈ Ob(C)` the category `U/C'` of arrows `U → U'` is cofiltered. Denote
`O', A'` the restrictions of `O, A` to `C'`. Then restriction induces an equivalence
`QC(A, d) → QC(A', d)`.*

Here `C` carries the chaotic topology, `O` is a sheaf of commutative rings and `A` a sheaf of
differential graded `O`-algebras on it; the full subcategory `C'` is `P.FullSubcategory` for a
property `P` of objects, `U/C'` is `StructuredArrow U P.ι`, `O'` is
`SheafOfModules.restrictRingSheaf P.ι O` and `A'` is `A.restrict P.ι`. `QC(A, d)` is the full
subcategory `Chaotic.QC A` of `D(A, d)` of Definition 0GZ9, and the functor is restriction
`D(A, d) ⥤ D(A', d)`, the functor induced by restriction of differential graded modules, which is
exact. That functor is the literal restriction up to the canonical isomorphism
`restriction_sectionModuleIso : (M|_{C'})(U') ≅ M(F U')` (read over `A'(U') = A(F U')`), natural
in `M` by `restriction_sectionModuleIso_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_qcRestriction [∀ U : C, IsCofiltered (StructuredArrow U P.ι)] :
    (qcRestriction P.ι A).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.Chaotic.qc_derivedExtension_iff_and_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZF.** Let `C` be a category with the chaotic topology, `O` a sheaf of rings on it
and `φ : A ⟶ B` a homomorphism of sheaves of differential graded `O`-algebras which induces an
isomorphism on cohomology sheaves. Then the equivalence `D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)`, `M ↦ M ⊗^𝐋_A B`, of
Tag 0FTZ induces an equivalence `QC(A, d) ⥤ QC(B, d)`.

The three conjuncts are: an object `M` of `D(A, d)` lies in `QC(A, d)` exactly when `M ⊗^𝐋_A B`
lies in `QC(B, d)`, so that the functor induces a functor `QC(A, d) ⥤ QC(B, d)`; that functor
lies over derived extension of scalars; and it is an equivalence.

The source's functor `M ↦ M ⊗^𝐋_A B` is defined only for a homomorphism `φ` preserving `1`,
since `B` is made a left `A`-module through `φ`; so `PreservesOne` is implicit in the
statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem qc_derivedExtension_iff_and_isEquivalence :
    (∀ M : derivedCategory.{u, u, u} A, QC B ((derivedExtension φ hφ).obj M) ↔ QC A M) ∧
      qcDerivedExtension φ hφ hqis ⋙ QCι B = QCι A ⋙ derivedExtension φ hφ ∧
      (qcDerivedExtension φ hφ hqis).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.SystemProHom.isEquivalence_qcPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZH.** **Let `(A_n)` and `(B_n)` be inverse systems of differential graded
`R`-algebras, and let `φ : (A_n) → (B_n)` be a morphism of pro-objects, given by a representative
`(m(·), A_{m(n)} → B_n)`. If `φ` is an isomorphism of pro-objects, then the functor
`QC(𝒜) ⥤ QC(ℬ)` it induces is an equivalence.**

Here the index category is a linearly ordered type `ι` with finite lower sets, the source's `ℕ`
being an instance, `𝒜` and `ℬ` are the sheaves of differential graded algebras on the chaotic site
`ι` with the constant sheaf of rings `R` attached to the two systems, and the functor is the
derived pullback of Tag 0GZC along the morphism of chaotic sites given by the representative,
restricted to the quasi-coherent objects of Definition 24.33.1. That `φ` is an isomorphism of
pro-objects is `IsProIso`: a representative of a morphism of pro-objects in the other direction
whose composites with `φ` agree with the transition maps after restriction to a further stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_qcPullback (φ : SystemProHom A B) (hφ : φ.IsProIso) :
    φ.qcPullback.IsEquivalence

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.nonempty_iso_of_proIsoDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZI.** Let `(A_n)` be an inverse system of differential graded algebras over `R`,
let `(N_n)` and `(N'_n)` be inverse systems of left differential graded modules over it which are
pro-isomorphic in the derived category, and let `(M_n)` be an inverse system of differential
graded `(A_n, B)`-bimodules. Then the derived limits of the two towers
`n ↦ M_n ⊗^𝐋_{A_n} N_n` and `n ↦ M_n ⊗^𝐋_{A_n} N'_n` of `D(B, d)` are isomorphic, although not
canonically. With `B` concentrated in degree zero with `B^0 = R` this is the source's
`R lim (M_n ⊗^𝐋_{A_n} N_n) = R lim (M_n ⊗^𝐋_{A_n} N'_n)` in `D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_of_proIsoDerived {S : AlgebraSystem R}
    {B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R} {N N' : ModuleSystem S} (p : ProIsoDerived N N')
    (M : BimoduleSystem S B)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (M.tower N).obj (op n)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (M.tower N').obj (op n)] (K K' : derivedCategory' B)
    (hK : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit (M.tower N) K)
    (hK' : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit (M.tower N') K') :
    Nonempty (K ≅ K')

declarations.name: Koszul.powBaseTensorBalanceDerivedObjIso
declarations.doc:
**The first step of the proof of Tag 0GZJ, one index at a time:**
`M_m ⊗_{K_m}^𝐋 (K_m ⊗_R K_t) ≅ M_m ⊗_R^𝐋 K_t` in `D(B, d)`, for `m = b + k`.

Both sides are computed by their plain tensor products, because `K_m ⊗_R K_t` and `K_t` are
orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules, and the plain tensor products are identified by
`Koszul.powBaseTensorBalanceObjIso`.
declarations.comment: the identification M_n ⊗^𝐋_R K_t = M_n ⊗^𝐋_{K_n} (K_n ⊗_R K_t), objectwise

declarations.name: Koszul.nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_powBaseTensorBalance
declarations.doc:
**The first step of the proof of Tag 0GZJ, passed to derived limits:**
`R lim (M_m ⊗_R^𝐋 K_t) = R lim (M_m ⊗_{K_m}^𝐋 (K_m ⊗_R K_t))` in `D(B, d)`.

The isomorphism is not canonical — a derived limit is pinned only up to a non-unique isomorphism
— so the conclusion is stated for an arbitrary derived limit of each tower. This is Tag 0H9L
applied to the pro-isomorphism `Koszul.powBaseTensorBalanceProIso`.

Replacing `K_m ⊗_R K_t` by `K_t` on the right-hand side, which turns this into the statement of
Tag 0GZJ, is the second step of the source's proof and is not done here.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_powBaseTensorBalance
    [HasProduct fun k : ℕ =>
      (powBaseTensorDerivedTensorTower f t hb bimod bimodTrans).tower.obj (op k)]
    [HasProduct fun k : ℕ =>
      (powBaseDegreeZeroDerivedTensorTower f t hb bimod bimodTrans).tower.obj (op k)]
    (K K' : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory' B)
    (hK : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit
      (powBaseTensorDerivedTensorTower f t hb bimod bimodTrans).tower K)
    (hK' : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit
      (powBaseDegreeZeroDerivedTensorTower f t hb bimod bimodTrans).tower K') :
    Nonempty (K ≅ K')
declarations.comment: the identification M_n ⊗^𝐋_R K_t = M_n ⊗^𝐋_{K_n} (K_n ⊗_R K_t), passed to R lim

declarations.name: Koszul.nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_powKoszulTensorBalance
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring, let `f₁, …, f_r ∈ R` and let `K_n` be the Koszul complex on `f₁^n, …, f_r^n`
viewed as a differential graded `R`-algebra. Let `(M_n)` be an object of `D(ℕ, (K_n))`. Then for
every `t ≥ 1` `R lim (M_n ⊗_R^𝐋 K_t) = R lim (M_n ⊗_{K_n}^𝐋 K_t)`.

The isomorphism is not canonical, so the conclusion is stated for an arbitrary derived limit of
each tower. With `B` concentrated in degree zero with `B^0 = R` the target `D(B, d)` is the
source's `D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_powKoszulTensorBalance
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (M.tower (powRestrictedModuleSystem f ht)).obj (op n)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ =>
      (powBaseDegreeZeroDerivedTensorTower f t ht M.obj bimodTrans).tower.obj (op n)]
    (K K' : derivedCategory' B)
    (hK : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit (M.tower (powRestrictedModuleSystem f ht)) K)
    (hK' : Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit
      (powBaseDegreeZeroDerivedTensorTower f t ht M.obj bimodTrans).tower K') :
    Nonempty (K ≅ K')
declarations.comment: R lim (M_n ⊗^𝐋_R K_t) = R lim (M_n ⊗^𝐋_{K_n} K_t)

declarations.name: Koszul.powProIsoDerived
declarations.doc:
**The second step of the proof of Tag 0GZJ:** the system `({}_{t+n}K_t)` and the system
`(K_{t+n} ⊗_R K_t)` of left differential graded modules over the Koszul algebras are
pro-isomorphic in the derived category.

The indices are the multiples of `t`, the comparison maps are those of Tag 0GZ7
(`Koszul.powComparisonArrow`), the maps in the other direction are the multiplication maps, and
the two composition identities are the two composites of Tag 0GZ7.
declarations.statement:
def powProIsoDerived :
    ProIsoDerived (powRestrictedModuleSystem f ht) (powBaseTensorModuleSystem f ht)
declarations.comment: the pro-isomorphism of ({}_nK_t) with (K_n ⊗_R K_t) in the derived category

declarations.name: Koszul.idealPowKoszulDerivedCompleteEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZK.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ R` an ideal, with generators
`f₁, …, f_r`. Let `𝒜` be the sheaf of `R`-algebras on the chaotic site of the natural numbers of
the inverse system `R / I ^ n`, and `ℬ` the sheaf of differential graded `R`-algebras of the
inverse system of Koszul algebras on `f₁ ^ n, …, f_r ^ n` (both indexed so that the stage `n`
carries the exponent `n + 1`). Then the three categories `QC(𝒜)`, `QC(ℬ)` and the full
subcategory `D_comp(R, I)` of derived complete objects of `D(R)` are canonically equivalent:
`QC(𝒜) ≌ QC(ℬ)` along the pro-isomorphisms of the quotient and Koszul–Tate systems and the
quasi-isomorphism of the Tate resolution (Tags 0GZH, 0GZF, 0GZ5), and `QC(ℬ) ≌ D_comp(R, I)` by the
derived global sections, with quasi-inverse `K ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_R ℬ`.
declarations.statement:
def idealPowKoszulDerivedCompleteEquivalences [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R) {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → R) (generators : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    ((Chaotic.QC (liftedIdealPowSheafAlgebra.{u} I)).FullSubcategory ≌
      (Chaotic.QC (liftedPowSheafAlgebra.{u} f)).FullSubcategory) ×
    ((Chaotic.QC (liftedPowSheafAlgebra.{u} f)).FullSubcategory ≌
      (derivedCompleteObjects I).FullSubcategory)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_affine_finitePresentation_image_not_finiteUnionLocallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZM.** A finite-presentation morphism of affine schemes can take a locally closed
subset to a set that is not a finite union of locally closed subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_finitePresentation_image_not_finiteUnionLocallyClosed :
    ∃ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y) (T : Set X),
      IsAffine X ∧ IsAffine Y ∧ FinitePresentation f ∧
        IsLocallyClosed T ∧ ¬ IsFiniteUnionLocallyClosed (f.base '' T)

declarations.name: ChaoticQCoh.quasiCoherent_iff_canonicalMap_isIso
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag `0GZN`, Lemma 18.24.3: A sheaf of `O`-modules `F` on the chaotic
site `C` is quasi-coherent if and only if for every morphism `f : U ⟶ V` of `C`
the canonical map `c_f : F(V) ⊗_{O(V)} O(U) ⟶ F(U)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiCoherent_iff_canonicalMap_isIso :
    QuasiCoherent O F ↔ ∀ ⦃U V : C⦄ (f : U ⟶ V), IsIso (canonicalMap O F f)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent_iff_canonicalMap_isIso
declarations.doc:
A module sheaf on a chaotic site is quasi-coherent precisely when its
canonical base-change maps are isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherent_iff_canonicalMap_isIso
    (hX : X.J = ⊥) :
    F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∀ ⦃U V : X.C⦄ (f : U ⟶ V), IsIso (canonicalMap X F f)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ChaoticFlatQuasicoherent.isQuasicoherentOnSite_isWeakSerreClass
declarations.doc:
Quasi-coherent modules on a chaotic site with flat restrictions form a
weak Serre subcategory of all sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
public instance isQuasicoherentOnSite_isWeakSerreClass
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, r}) [Fact (X.J = ⊥)]
    [Fact (∀ {U V : X.Cᵒᵖ} (a : V ⟶ U),
      RingHom.Flat (X.O.obj.map a).hom)] :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) :
        ObjectProperty (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.TopCohomology.isQuasicoherentOnSite_topHomology
declarations.doc:
**Quasi-coherence of the top cohomology module.**  Let `C` be a category viewed as a site
with the chaotic topology and let `O` be its sheaf of rings.  If `M` is an object of `QC(O)`
and `b` is an integer such that `H^i(M) = 0` for all `i > b`, then `H^b(M)` is a quasi-coherent
module on `(C, O)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_topHomology (hJ : J = ⊥) (bc : BaseChangeData.{w} R.obj)
    (M : DMod.{w} R.obj) (hM : IsQC.{w} bc M) (b : ℤ)
    (hvan : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} R.obj) i).obj M)) :
    ∃ hsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (PresheafOfModules.{max u v r w} R.obj) b).obj M).presheaf,
      (⟨_, hsh⟩ : SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} R).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentCohomology.isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Quasi-coherent cohomology under flat restrictions.** Let `C` be a category viewed as a
site with the chaotic topology, let `O` be its sheaf of rings, and assume that for every
morphism `U → V` of `C` the restriction homomorphism `O(V) → O(U)` is flat.  Then an object of
`D(O)` lies in `QC(O)` exactly when all of its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, that is,
`QC(O) = D_QCoh(O)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQC_iff_hasQuasicoherentCohomology (X : RingedSite.{u, v, r}) (hX : X.J = ⊥)
    (hflat : ∀ {U V : X.Cᵒᵖ} (a : V ⟶ U), RingHom.Flat (X.O.obj.map a).hom)
    (bc : BaseChangeData.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj)
    (K : DMod.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).obj) :
    IsQC.{w} bc K ↔ hasQuasicoherentCohomology.{w} X K

declarations.name: Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.ChaoticComparison.cartesianEquivalenceOfLocallyKFlatAcyclic
declarations.doc:
Let `C` carry a Grothendieck topology `τ`, let `τ'` be the chaotic topology on `C` and let `O`
be a `τ`-sheaf of rings with commuting sections. Assume hypothesis (2) of the source: for every
object `U` of `C` and every K-flat complex `M^•` of `O(U)`-modules the canonical map
`M^• ⟶ RΓ((C/U)_τ, (M^• ⊗_{O(U)} O_U)^#)` is a quasi-isomorphism. Then `ε^*` and `Rε_*` are
mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between `QC(O)` and the full subcategory of `D(C_τ, O_τ)`
consisting of the objects `K` with `Rε_*K` in `QC(O)`.

Hypothesis (1) of the source, that `τ'` is the chaotic topology, is structural here: a module on
`(C_τ', O_τ')` *is* a presheaf of `O`-modules, `ε_*` is the forgetful functor and `ε^*` is
`τ`-sheafification. Hypothesis (2) is `IsLocallyKFlatAcyclic`, read on the localized site
`(C/U, τ)`. The commutativity `hO` gives the canonical base-change datum
`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.PullbackQuasiCoherentBaseChange.baseChangeDataOfComm`; the cartesian
condition does not depend on the choice of datum.

The objects and the morphisms of `C` and the section rings lie in independent universes `u`, `v`
and `r`, and the modules in `max u v r w`; the site therefore need not be small, as is the case
for the associated affine site of a category fibred in groupoids (Stacks 0H0J).
declarations.statement:
def cartesianEquivalenceOfLocallyKFlatAcyclic (h2 : IsLocallyKFlatAcyclic.{w} R hO) :
    (IsCartesianPushforward.{w} R
          (baseChangeDataOfComm.{r, v, u, w} R.obj hO)).FullSubcategory ≌
      QC.{w} (baseChangeDataOfComm.{r, v, u, w} R.obj hO)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zariski_affineToBigRingedToposEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZU, Zariski site.** The affine-to-big morphism of ringed topoi over the big
Zariski site of `S` is an equivalence of ringed topoi: its inverse image is an equivalence and
its structure morphism is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem zariski_affineToBigRingedToposEquivalence
    (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    let f := affineToBigRingedToposHom.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u, w}
      (BigAffineZariski.topology B S hS) (BigZariskiOver.topology B S hS)
      (BigAffineZariski.inclusion B S hS)
      (uliftRingSheaf.{w} (commStructureSheaf S (BigZariskiOver.topology B S hS)
        (Over.post B.inclusion) (BigZariskiOver.structure_isSheaf B S hS)))
    f.toToposHom.inverseImage.IsEquivalence ∧ IsIso f.fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: Zariski site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffineFppf_isRestrictedAssociatedModule_of_isRestrictionOfQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZV, (7) ⇒ (8) at `τ = fppf`**, with the uniqueness of `𝒢` included. The module
`𝓜` on `(Sch/S)_fppf` given by condition (7) is quasi-coherent, hence isomorphic to `𝒢^a` for a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithfulBigAffineAssociatedModuleQcohOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZV, the uniqueness of `𝒢` in condition (8), at every `τ`.** The functor
`𝒢 ↦ 𝒢^a|_{(Aff/S)_τ}` from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪_Aff`-modules on
`(Aff/S)_τ` is fully faithful: it is Stacks 0GN7 for the big `τ`-site followed by the Comparison
Lemma for sheaves of modules on the dense subsite of affine objects.  No part of Descent,
Proposition 03DX is used.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulBigAffineAssociatedModuleQcohOf (τ : SiteKind) :
    (bigAffineAssociatedModuleQcohOf B S hS τ).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (8) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffine_iso_of_associatedModuleQcohOf_restriction_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZV, the uniqueness of `𝒢` in condition (8) at every `τ`**, read as a uniqueness
statement: two quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules whose associated modules have isomorphic
restrictions to `(Aff/S)_τ` are isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bigAffine_iso_of_associatedModuleQcohOf_restriction_iso (τ : SiteKind)
    (G₁ G₂ : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
    (e : (bigAffineAssociatedModuleQcohOf B S hS τ).obj G₁ ≅
      (bigAffineAssociatedModuleQcohOf B S hS τ).obj G₂) :
    Nonempty (G₁.obj ≅ G₂.obj)
declarations.comment: (8) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.statement:
public theorem bigAffine_isRestrictionOfQuasicoherentOf_of_isRestrictedAssociatedModuleOf
    (τ : SiteKind) (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (bigAffineRingedSiteOf B S hS τ).O))
    (hF : BigAffineFppf.IsRestrictedAssociatedModuleOf B S hS τ F) :
    BigAffineFppf.IsRestrictionOfQuasicoherentOf B S hS τ F
declarations.comment: (8) ⇒ (7) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffine_isRestrictionOfQuasicoherentOf_of_canonicalMap_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZV, (1) ⇒ (7) at every `τ`.** A sheaf of `𝒪_Aff`-modules on `(Aff/S)_τ` all of
whose base-change maps `𝓕(U') ⊗_{𝒪(U')} 𝒪(U) ⟶ 𝓕(U)` are isomorphisms corresponds, under the
equivalence of ringed topoi of Stacks 0GZU, to a quasi-coherent module on `(Sch/S)_τ`.

The three inputs are the quasi-coherence conjunct of condition (2)–(6) at `τ`; the existence of
an ambient lift, by the Comparison Lemma at `τ`; and the quasi-coherence of that lift, by the
reflection of quasi-coherence along the dense subsite.
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (7) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffine_isIso_canonicalMapOf_of_isRestrictionOfQuasicoherentOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZV, (7) ⇒ (1) at every `τ`.** The restriction to `(Aff/S)_τ` of the quasi-coherent
module given by condition (7) is quasi-coherent, hence cartesian by Stacks 0H04.
declarations.comment: (7) ⇒ (1) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffine_isRestrictedAssociatedModuleOf_of_canonicalMap_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZV, (1) ⇒ (8) at every `τ`**, with the uniqueness of `𝒢` included.

A cartesian sheaf of modules on `(Aff/S)_τ` satisfies the fppf sheaf axiom, so it is a sheaf of
modules on `(Aff/S)_fppf` with the same underlying presheaf, where (1) ⇒ (8) is proved as
`AlgebraicGeometry.bigAffineFppf_isRestrictedAssociatedModule_of_canonicalMap_isIso`.  Reading
the resulting isomorphism back for `τ` and applying Stacks 0GNE to its right-hand side gives
condition (8) at `τ`; the uniqueness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithfulBigAffineAssociatedModuleQcohOf`.
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (8) at every τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}, existence and uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.doc:

declarations.doc:

    BigAffineFppf.IsRestrictedAssociatedModule B S hS F
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (8) at τ = fppf, existence and uniqueness of 𝒢

public theorem bigAffineFppf_isSheaf_and_isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineEtale_isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_canonicalMap_isIso
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules on the small affine étale site of `S` is quasi-coherent on the ringed site
`(S_{affine, étale}, 𝒪_affine)` exactly when all of its base-change maps
`𝓕(U') ⊗_{𝒪(U')} 𝒪(U) ⟶ 𝓕(U)` are isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallAffineEtale_isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_canonicalMap_isIso
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallAffineEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O)) :
    F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔
      ∀ ⦃U V : SmallAffineEtale B S hS⦄ (f : U ⟶ V),
        IsIso (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalMap (smallAffineEtaleRingedSite B S hS) F f)
declarations.comment: (1) ⇔ (2) at τ = étale, for a sheaf of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithfulSmallAffineEtaleAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZX, the uniqueness of `𝒢` in condition (4) at `τ = étale`.**  The functor
`𝒢 ↦ 𝒢ᵃ|_{S_{affine, étale}}` from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the `𝒪_affine`-modules on
`S_{affine, étale}` is fully faithful: it is Stacks 0GN7 at `τ = étale` followed by the
Comparison Lemma for sheaves of modules on the dense subsite of affine objects.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulSmallAffineEtaleAssociatedModuleQcoh :
    (smallAffineEtaleAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (4) at τ = étale, uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineEtale_iso_of_associatedModuleQcoh_restriction_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZX, the uniqueness of `𝒢` in condition (4) at `τ = étale`**, read as a
uniqueness statement: two quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules whose associated modules have isomorphic
restrictions to the small affine étale site of `S` are isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineEtale_iso_of_associatedModuleQcoh_restriction_iso
    (G₁ G₂ : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
    (e : (smallAffineEtaleAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).obj G₁ ≅
      (smallAffineEtaleAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).obj G₂) :
    Nonempty (G₁.obj ≅ G₂.obj)
declarations.comment: (4) at τ = étale, uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineZariski_exists_isQuasicoherentOnSite_restriction_iso
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules on the small affine Zariski site of `S` which is quasi-coherent on the
ringed site `(S_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪_affine)` is the restriction of a quasi-coherent `𝒪`-module on
`(S_Zar, 𝒪)`, i.e. corresponds to one under the equivalence of ringed topoi (0GZW).
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineZariski_exists_isQuasicoherentOnSite_restriction_iso
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallAffineZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O))
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ∃ N : SheafOfModules.{u} (SmallZariski.structureSheaf B S hS), N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
      Nonempty ((smallAffineZariskiModuleRestriction B S hS).obj N ≅ F)
declarations.comment: (2) ⇒ (3) at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineZariski_essImage_associatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules `𝓕` on the small affine Zariski site of `S` which is quasi-coherent on the
ringed site `(S_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪_affine)` comes from a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝒢` by the
procedure of Descent, Section 35.8: it is in the essential image of
`𝒢 ↦ 𝒢ᵃ|_{S_{affine, Zar}}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineZariski_essImage_associatedModuleQcoh
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallAffineZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O))
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).essImage F
declarations.comment: (4) at τ = Zariski, existence of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineZariski_exists_associatedModuleQcoh_restriction_iso
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of modules `𝓕` on the small affine Zariski site of `S` all of whose base-change maps
`𝓕(U') ⊗_{𝒪(U')} 𝒪(U) ⟶ 𝓕(U)` are isomorphisms is isomorphic to `𝒢ᵃ|_{S_{affine, Zar}}` for a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝒢`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineZariski_exists_associatedModuleQcoh_restriction_iso
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (smallAffineZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O))
    (hF : ∀ ⦃U V : SmallAffineZariski B S hS⦄ (f : U ⟶ V),
      IsIso (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalMap (smallAffineZariskiRingedSite B S hS) F f)) :
    ∃ G : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty ((smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (4) at τ = Zariski, existence of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_smallAffineZariskiModuleRestrictionQcoh
declarations.doc:
The equivalence of ringed topoi (0GZW) induces an equivalence
`QCoh(S_Zar, 𝒪) ≌ QCoh(S_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪_affine)` between the categories of quasi-coherent
modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_smallAffineZariskiModuleRestrictionQcoh :
    (smallAffineZariskiModuleRestrictionQcoh B S hS).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: (2) ⇔ (3) at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcohOnSite
declarations.doc:
The functor `𝒢 ↦ 𝒢ᵃ|_{S_{affine, Zar}}` is an equivalence from the quasi-coherent
`𝒪_S`-modules onto the quasi-coherent modules on the ringed site `(S_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪_affine)`:
every such module comes from a `𝒢`, and from a unique one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEquivalence_smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcohOnSite :
    (smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcohOnSite B S hS).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: (2) ⇔ (4) at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcohEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The equivalence of categories `QCoh(𝒪_S) ≌ QCoh(S_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪_affine)` whose functor
is `𝒢 ↦ 𝒢ᵃ|_{S_{affine, Zar}}`.
declarations.comment: (2) ⇔ (4) at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithfulSmallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh
declarations.doc:
The functor `𝒢 ↦ 𝒢ᵃ|_{S_{affine, Zar}}` from the quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules to the
`𝒪_affine`-modules on `S_{affine, Zar}` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def fullyFaithfulSmallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh :
    (smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (4) at τ = Zariski, uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineZariski_iso_of_associatedModuleQcoh_restriction_iso
declarations.doc:
Two quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-modules whose associated modules have isomorphic restrictions to the
small affine Zariski site of `S` are isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineZariski_iso_of_associatedModuleQcoh_restriction_iso
    (G₁ G₂ : (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
    (e : (smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).obj G₁ ≅
      (smallAffineZariskiAssociatedModuleQcoh B S hS).obj G₂) :
    Nonempty (G₁.obj ≅ G₂.obj)
declarations.comment: (4) at τ = Zariski, uniqueness of 𝒢

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineZariski_isIso_restrictionBaseChange_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZX, condition (4) implies condition (1) at `τ = Zariski`.** The presheaf `𝒢ᵃ` of
Descent, Section 35.8 attached to a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝒢` has all its base-change
comparisons `𝒢ᵃ(U') ⊗_{𝒪(U')} 𝒪(U) ⟶ 𝒢ᵃ(U)` isomorphisms on the small affine Zariski site
of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineZariski_isIso_restrictionBaseChange_associatedModule
    (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (G : S.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] {X Y : (SmallAffineZariski B S hS)ᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsIso (Stacks.PresheafOfModules.restrictionBaseChange
      (R := (smallAffineZariskiRingedSite B S hS).O.obj)
      (associatedModulePresheaf S G (smallAffineZariskiToOver B S hS)) f)
declarations.comment: (4) ⇒ (1) at τ = Zariski

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineEtale_isIso_restrictionBaseChange_associatedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZX, condition (4) implies condition (1) at `τ = étale`.** The presheaf `𝒢ᵃ` of
Descent, Section 35.8 attached to a quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝒢` has all its base-change
comparisons `𝒢ᵃ(U') ⊗_{𝒪(U')} 𝒪(U) ⟶ 𝒢ᵃ(U)` isomorphisms on the small affine étale site
of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallAffineEtale_isIso_restrictionBaseChange_associatedModule
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (G : S.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] {X Y : (SmallAffineEtale B S hS)ᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsIso (Stacks.PresheafOfModules.restrictionBaseChange
      (R := (smallAffineEtaleRingedSite B S hS).O.obj)
      (associatedModulePresheaf S G (smallAffineEtaleToOver B S hS)) f)
declarations.comment: (4) ⇒ (1) at τ = étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZZ, the equivalence of (4) and (5).** For a scheme `S`, the derived category of
modules on the small affine site `S_affine` with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves is
canonically equivalent to the category `QC(S_affine, 𝒪)` of quasi-coherent objects of the
derived category.

The equivalence is realized inside `D(S_affine, 𝒪)`, by
`smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC_functor_comp_ι`; the two subcategories are in
fact equal, by `smallAffineChaotic_isQC_eq_hasQuasicoherentCohomology`.

For a scheme in `Scheme.{0}` both sides are triangulated subcategories of `D(S_affine, 𝒪)`, by
`smallAffineChaotic_qcohCohomologyProperty_isTriangulated`, so the comparison is then an exact
equivalence of triangulated categories. None of the other four comparisons of Stacks 0GZZ is
proved; see the coverage note of this file.
declarations.statement:
def smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC
    (bc : BaseChangeData.{w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS).O).obj) :
    (qcohCohomologyProperty.{w} (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS)).FullSubcategory ≌
      QC.{w} bc
declarations.comment: the equivalence (4) ≃ (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC_functor_comp_ι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZZ, the equivalence of (4) and (5), as a commuting triangle.** The comparison
`D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪) ≌ QC(S_affine, 𝒪)` is the canonical one: it commutes with the inclusions
of both sides into `D(S_affine, 𝒪)`.
declarations.statement:
def smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC_functor_comp_ι
    (bc : BaseChangeData.{w}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS).O).obj) :
    (smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC.{w} B S hS bc).functor ⋙ QCι.{w} bc ≅
      (qcohCohomologyProperty.{w} (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS)).ι
declarations.comment: the equivalence (4) ≃ (5) is the canonical one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineChaotic_qcohCohomologyProperty_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZZ, triangulatedness of (4) and (5).** For a scheme in `Scheme.{0}`,
`D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪)` is a triangulated subcategory of `D(S_affine, 𝒪)`: it is the same
subcategory as `QC(S_affine, 𝒪)`, which is triangulated by Stacks 0GYW.

Together with `smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC` and
`smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC_functor_comp_ι` this makes the comparison of (4)
and (5) an exact equivalence of triangulated categories, both sides being triangulated
subcategories of `D(S_affine, 𝒪)` and the comparison commuting with the two inclusions.

The restriction to `Scheme.{0}` comes from the input: the library constructs derived base
change only over a structure sheaf with values in `RingCat.{0}`; see
`smallAffineChaoticBaseChangeData`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallAffineChaotic_qcohCohomologyProperty_isTriangulated :
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
      (qcohCohomologyProperty.{0} (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B₀ S₀ hS₀))
declarations.comment: (4) and (5) are triangulated, for a scheme in `Scheme.{0}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallAffineChaotic_qcohCohomologyProperty_isTriangulated_univ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZZ, triangulatedness of (4) and (5).** For an arbitrary scheme `S`,
`D_QCoh(S_affine, 𝒪)` is a triangulated subcategory of `D(S_affine, 𝒪)`: it is the same
subcategory as `QC(S_affine, 𝒪)`, which is triangulated by Stacks 0GYW.

Together with `smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC` and
`smallAffineChaoticDerivedQuasiCoherentEquivQC_functor_comp_ι` this makes the comparison of (4)
and (5) an exact equivalence of triangulated categories, both sides being triangulated
subcategories of `D(S_affine, 𝒪)` and the comparison commuting with the two inclusions.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallAffineChaotic_qcohCohomologyProperty_isTriangulated_univ :
    ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated
      (qcohCohomologyProperty.{w} (smallAffineChaoticRingedSite B S hS))
declarations.comment: (4) and (5) are triangulated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.nonempty_quasicoherentDerived_linearTriangulatedEquivalences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0GZZ.** Let `X` be a scheme, and let `Sch_Zar` be a big Zariski site containing it.
There are canonical exact equivalences between the following triangulated categories:

1. `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, the complexes of `𝒪_X`-modules on the ringed space `(X, 𝒪_X)` with
   quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves;
2. `D_QCoh(X_Zar, 𝒪)`, the same on the small Zariski site `X_Zar` of Topologies, Definition 020T
   (the open immersions `U → X` of `Sch_Zar`), with its structure sheaf `U ↦ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)` and
   quasi-coherence in the sense of Modules on Sites, Definition 03DL;
3. `D_QCoh(X_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪)`, the same on the category of affine opens of `X` with the
   Zariski topology;
4. `D_QCoh(X_affine, 𝒪)`, the same on the category of affine opens of `X` with the chaotic
   topology, where modules are presheaves of modules;
5. `QC(X_affine, 𝒪)`, the full subcategory of `D(X_affine, 𝒪)` of Cohomology on Sites,
   Definition 0GYV: the objects `K` for which `RΓ(V, K) ⊗^L_{𝒪(V)} 𝒪(U) ⟶ RΓ(U, K)` is an
   isomorphism for all `U ⟶ V`, formed with the derived base change of
   `AlgebraicGeometry.affineChaoticBaseChangeData`.

Formally: the five subcategories are triangulated subcategories of their ambient derived
categories, and there are equivalences of triangulated categories (an equivalence whose functor
commutes with the shifts and preserves distinguished triangles)
`(2) ≌ (1)`, `(1) ≌ (3)`, `(4) ≌ (3)` and `(4) ≌ (5)`, which are the canonical ones: each lies,
through the inclusions of the subcategories, over the canonical functor of the source, namely
derived restriction along the identification of modules of Descent, Remark 03FG; derived
restriction to the affine opens; the identification of presheaves with sheaves for the chaotic
topology followed by `Lε^*` for the morphism of ringed sites
`ε : (X_{affine, Zar}, 𝒪) ⟶ (X_affine, 𝒪)` of Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 07A8; and the identity
of `D(X_affine, 𝒪)`.

The derived categories of sheaves of modules are taken at the standard model
`HasDerivedCategory.standard`, the one the change of topology of Stacks 07A8 is constructed at;
those of presheaves of modules at the model of
`Stacks.ModulesOnACategory.QuasiCoherentEquivalence.DMod`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Scheme.nonempty_quasicoherentDerived_linearTriangulatedEquivalences :
    letI := SmallZariski.abelianModules B X hX
    letI := SmallZariski.derivedCategoryModel B X hX
    haveI := Scheme.isWeakSerreClass_isQuasicoherent_ringCatSheaf X
    haveI := SmallZariski.isWeakSerreClass_isQuasicoherentOnSite B X hX
    haveI := SmallZariski.additive_restrictModuleEquivalence B X hX
    -- the five subcategories are triangulated
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).IsTriangulated ∧
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
        (SmallZariski.structureSheaf B X hX))).IsTriangulated ∧
    (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u, u, u, u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.affineZariskiRingedSite.O))).IsTriangulated ∧
    (qcohCohomologyProperty.{u} X.affineChaoticRingedSite).IsTriangulated ∧
    (isQCProperty.{u} (affineChaoticBaseChangeData.{u} X)).IsTriangulated ∧
    -- `(2) ≃ (1)`, over derived restriction along Descent, Remark 03FG
    (∃ e : LinearTriangulatedEquivalence ℤ
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          (SmallZariski.structureSheaf B X hX))).FullSubcategory
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty (e.equivalence.functor ⋙
          (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).ι ≅
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
          (SmallZariski.structureSheaf B X hX))).ι ⋙
          (SmallZariski.restrictModuleEquivalence B X hX).functor.mapDerivedCategory)) ∧
    -- `(1) ≃ (3)`, over derived restriction to the affine opens
    (∃ e : LinearTriangulatedEquivalence ℤ
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory
        X.affineOpensQuasicoherentDerivedCategory,
      Nonempty (e.equivalence.functor ⋙
          (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u, u, u, u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.affineZariskiRingedSite.O))).ι ≅
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).ι ⋙
          X.affineOpensModuleRestrictionEquivalence.functor.mapDerivedCategory)) ∧
    -- `(4) ≃ (3)`, over sheafification for the chaotic topology followed by `Lε^*`
    (∃ e : LinearTriangulatedEquivalence ℤ
        (qcohCohomologyProperty.{u} X.affineChaoticRingedSite).FullSubcategory
        X.affineOpensQuasicoherentDerivedCategory,
      Nonempty (e.equivalence.functor ⋙
          (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u, u, u, u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.affineZariskiRingedSite.O))).ι ≅
        (qcohCohomologyProperty.{u} X.affineChaoticRingedSite).ι ⋙
          X.affineChaoticSheafPresheafEquivalence.inverse.mapDerivedCategory ⋙
            X.affineCoarseningDerivedPullback)) ∧
    -- `(4) ≃ (5)`, over the identity of `D(X_affine, 𝒪)`
    (∃ e : LinearTriangulatedEquivalence ℤ
        (qcohCohomologyProperty.{u} X.affineChaoticRingedSite).FullSubcategory
        (QC.{u} (affineChaoticBaseChangeData.{u} X)),
      Nonempty (e.equivalence.functor ⋙ QCι.{u} (affineChaoticBaseChangeData.{u} X) ≅
        (qcohCohomologyProperty.{u} X.affineChaoticRingedSite).ι))
